# iOS browse audit — all findings (358)

Audit of the iOS app's browse screens (Live TV, Movies, Series, detail pages, Search, Settings, playlist list, TV guide, M3U), 2026-10-02. 28 review lenses; every finding was checked by an independent verifier. When the verdict is "partly", the **corrected claim** and **corrected fix** describe the real problem and replace the finder's text. One refuted finding is left out.

The fixes landed in commit c525141 ("feat(ios): make browsing feel native and fluid"). This file is the source material for `ios-browse-native-handoff.md`; line numbers refer to the code **before** that commit.
Each finding has the finder's text, then the independent verifier's verdict. When the verdict is "partly", the **corrected claim** and **corrected fix** are what counts; where they contradict the finder, follow the verifier.


---

## haptics-touch-feedback-1 — Xtream channel, movie and series cards have no context menu: a long press is just a slow tap, and a live channel can only be favourited from inside the player

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category grid, All Channels, Movies home, Movies category grid, Series home, Series category grid, Favorites, Search results
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:429-458, 1159-1182`, `Views/VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-704`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:311-322, 423-434, 650-659`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:109-118, 134-144, 160-170`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475`, `Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:122-135`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:159-179`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Which actions the menus carry beyond favourite / download / hide category: a direct Play or Resume on movie cards (needs the play logic of MovieDetailView.swift:190-266 extracted), the channel schedule entry on live cards, and whether favourited cards also get a visible badge.

**What the user perceives:** Holding a poster or a channel logo does nothing until the finger lifts, then the normal tap fires: shots iphone-light/M06-movie-card-long-press.png shows the movie detail and iphone-dark/L08-live-card-long-press.png shows the player after a 1.3 s press. There is no way to favourite, download or inspect anything from a list. To favourite a live channel on an Xtream playlist the user must start the stream and use the player star; to un-favourite one from the Favorites grid they must play it again. Hiding a category is only possible through a swipe inside the category-picker sheet.

**Mechanism (finder):** There are exactly two contextMenu sites outside the player: the M3U card (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446) and DownloadButton (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:82). LiveStreamCard (LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457), the NavigationLink-wrapped VODStreamCard (VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-704) and SeriesCard (SeriesView.swift:311-322, 423-434, 650-659) carry none, so the system long-press recognizer never engages and the Button fires on touch-up. The only DBFavorite writers are the detail screens and the live player shell (MovieDetailView.swift:324, SeriesView.swift:1257, LiveStreamsView.swift:1167). HiddenCategoryStore.setHidden has a single caller, the swipe action at CategoryPickerSheet.swift:125. The M3U side already proves the pattern scales to thousands of cards and the empty-state copy even teaches it (favorites.empty.message: "Long press a channel...").

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add Views/Components/CatalogContextMenus.swift with small menu-content views and attach them with .contextMenu on the Button / NavigationLink (outside the label, as M3UChannelsView.swift:446 does).
1) Favourite state without per-card queries: add an Xtream favourite store mirroring Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:8-67 (one ValueObservation per playlist publishing Set<Int> per type). Existing writers keep writing DBFavorite; the observation picks them up.
2) Menu content as views so nothing but a struct init runs per card body (the contextMenu closure is non-escaping and runs on every card body):
   struct FavoriteMenuButton: View { let id: Int; let type: String; let playlistId: UUID
     @ObservedObject private var store = XtreamFavoriteStore.shared
     var body: some View { let fav = store.isFavorite(id, type)
       Button { Task { await store.toggle(id, type, playlistId) } } label: { Label(fav ? L("favorites.remove") : L("favorites.add"), systemImage: fav ? "star.slash" : "star") } } }
3) Items: live card = Play (existing onStreamSelected), favourite, channel schedule (present the already written but unused ChannelEPGSheet through a callback next to onStreamSelected; the Equatable shelf rows ignore closures, LiveStreamsView.swift:344-349); movie card = favourite + download (generalise M3UDownloadMenuItems, DownloadButton.swift:211-281, building the URL inside its body); series card = favourite; shelf header = Hide category (HiddenCategoryStore.shared.setHidden). All labels exist already (favorites.add/remove, download.action/cancel/delete, category_picker.hide, epg.guide.title), so no new strings.
4) Preview: keep the default lift, add .contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous)) so the platter is rounded. No custom preview: movie metadata is only fetched when the detail opens (MovieDetailView.swift:99-103), a preview would cost one panel request per long press.
5) Do not offer Share / Copy link: Xtream stream URLs embed the account credentials.
No iOS 26 API involved; nothing to fall back from.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0); View.contentShape(_:_:eoFill:) with ContentShapeKinds.contextMenuPreview (iOS 15.0); View.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) (deliberately not used) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read the code. Outside the player there are exactly two contextMenu sites (grep): Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446 and Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:82. LiveStreamCard (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:429-458) is a Button + .buttonStyle(.plain) with no menu; the VOD cards are NavigationLinks with no menu (Views/VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-704), same for series (Views/SeriesView.swift:311-322, 423-434, 650-659) and the Favorites grids (Views/FavoritesView.swift:109-118, 134-144, 160-170). DBFavorite writers are only Views/MovieDetailView.swift:320-324, Views/SeriesView.swift:1253-1257 and the live player shell Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:1149-1171, so an Xtream live channel really can only be (un)favourited by starting the stream. HiddenCategoryStore.setHidden has one UI caller, Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:125 (Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:42 toggle() has no caller). ChannelEPGSheet (Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:159-179) is defined and never instantiated. Screenshots iphone-light/M06-movie-card-long-press.png (movie detail opened) and iphone-dark/L08-live-card-long-press.png (player opened, 404) show the long press acting as a tap; shots/README.txt says the same. No comment or history marks the absence as deliberate; the M3U card got the menu, the Xtream cards never did. Minor inaccuracies: favorites.empty.message ("Long press a channel...") is only used by Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:31, the Xtream FavoritesView uses favorites.empty.live/movie/series, so the copy does not teach it on Xtream; and the M3U comment at M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450 ("menu is rebuilt on every open") is wrong, the menuItems closure is non-escaping and runs with the card body, so the M3U label can be stale. The finding's design (state read inside a menu-item View) avoids that.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Xtream live, movie and series cards (shelves, category grids, All Channels, Favorites, search rows) have no context menu, so a long press is a slow tap; an Xtream live channel can only be favourited or un-favourited from inside the player. The M3U card already has a menu, so the two playlist kinds behave differently. (The "Long press a channel" empty-state copy is M3U-only.)

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with these adjustments. (1) Menu items as small View structs attached with .contextMenu on the Button / NavigationLink at the call sites (playlist is in scope there). The in-memory XtreamFavoriteStore (one ValueObservation, Set<Int> per type, tracked from DashboardView the way M3UDashboardView.swift:86 calls track) is the robust option because the label is correct on the first frame; a no-new-store alternative is @Query<IsFavoriteRequest> (Models/Requests.swift:268) inside the menu button, exactly like M3UDownloadMenuItems uses @Query, at the cost of one frame with the default false. (2) Before rolling out, confirm once with a print in the menu-item body that it is evaluated only when the menu is presented, not per card. (3) Movie download item: generalise M3UDownloadMenuItems with id DownloadManager.idFor(vod:streamId:) and PlaybackURLBuilder(playlist:).movieURL(streamId:containerExtension:). (4) Channel schedule item: show only when epgSnapshot != nil and EPGChannelKey.forXtream(stream) is non-nil; epg.guide.title ("TV Guide") is the wrong label for one channel's schedule, so either add a new key in all ten .strings files (additive only; those files hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys) or leave the item out of the first pass. Play label: epg.detail.play_channel exists for live, detail.watch for the rest. (5) Hide category on shelf headers is a product decision: the only un-hide path is the swipe in the category picker. (6) Keep .contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous)), no custom preview, no Share / Copy link. Optionally switch the M3U card's favourite item to the same View so its label cannot go stale. No iOS 26 API, no fallback needed.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9867-9870: @available(iOS 13.0, macOS 10.15, tvOS 14.0, *) extension View { nonisolated public func contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems) -> some View } (closure is non-escaping, as the finding says). :9873-9876: contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) iOS 16.0 (not used). SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3986-4000: ContentShapeKinds, iOS 15.0, with static let contextMenuPreview (unavailable only on macOS/watchOS). SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13328-13336: @available(iOS 15.0, ...) func contentShape<S>(_ kind: ContentShapeKinds, _ shape: S, eoFill: Bool = false). All below the iOS 18 deployment target.

**Regression risks:** Per-card cost must stay at a struct init: do not add @ObservedObject / @Query to the card itself (the M3U comment at M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450 records that observing the store in the card re-rendered thousands of cards). Do not put the new callback into the Equatable == of the shelf rows (LiveStreamsView.swift:344-349). A favourite removed from the Favorites grid makes the card vanish while the menu dismisses (expected). Hiding a category from a shelf header has no undo nearby. UI tests that tap posters must still pass; the tour shots M06 / L08 will change by design.

**How to verify:** UI test: press(forDuration: 1.0) on a movie poster and a live card, assert app.buttons["Add to Favorites"] exists and neither the detail nor the player opened; toggle and assert the Favorites grid updates. With a large catalog put a print / Self._printChanges in the menu-item body and in LiveStreamCard: scrolling and toggling a favourite must not log per card.

## haptics-touch-feedback-2 — Cards, shelf headers and detail buttons answer a press in three different ways and the artwork itself never reacts

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category grids, Favorites, Watch history, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367, 457`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:337-348, 445`, `Views/VODView.swift:315-326, 345, 418-429, 462, 704`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:292-303, 322, 394-405, 434, 650-659`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:134-144, 160-170`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:210-251, 264-267, 281-284, 392-399, 443-465`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:78-81`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Only the look: scale and dim amounts, and whether the detail action buttons keep the custom gradient with a press state or move to system button styles.

**What the user perceives:** Touching a poster or channel logo gives no sign that the app registered the finger: no dim, no shrink, no highlight shape. The same series poster dims when pressed in a category grid or in Favorites but not in the home shelf; movie posters never do. The big blue Watch Now button, Restart, Trailer and Download on the detail screens also stay visually inert while held. This reads as a tap delay even though the action fires on time.

**Mechanism (finder):** Three press behaviours coexist. (a) .buttonStyle(.plain): live card LiveStreamsView.swift:457, M3U card M3UChannelsView.swift:445, movie shelves VODView.swift:345 and 462, movie grid VODView.swift:704, series shelves SeriesView.swift:322 and 434, history grid WatchHistoryListView.swift:201, detail CTA DetailComponents.swift:251, secondary and trailer buttons :267 and :284, DownloadButton.swift:81, season chips DetailComponents.swift:465. Plain adds no background, shape or scale; the labels are bitmaps or explicitly coloured (white CTA text DetailComponents.swift:230, .foregroundColor(.primary) titles VODView.swift:534), so there is nothing for it to restyle. (b) No style at all, i.e. the default borderless style: series grid SeriesView.swift:650-659, both Favorites grids FavoritesView.swift:134 and 160, every shelf header (LiveStreamsView.swift:356, VODView.swift:315 and 418, SeriesView.swift:292 and 394, M3UChannelsView.swift:337): whole label dims and takes the tint (headers render accent blue in iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png). (c) No button: Continue Watching cards, episode rows, EPG cells use onTapGesture (separate findings). The exact plain-style dimming should be confirmed once in the simulator; whatever it is, it is not the same as (b).

**Proposed fix (finder):** One shared style file, Views/Components/PressStyles.swift, used everywhere a custom label is a button:
  struct CardPressStyle: ButtonStyle {
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
      configuration.label
        .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed && !reduceMotion ? 0.96 : 1)
        .opacity(configuration.isPressed ? 0.8 : 1)
        .animation(configuration.isPressed ? .easeOut(duration: 0.1) : .spring(response: 0.28, dampingFraction: 0.7), value: configuration.isPressed)
    }
  }
  extension ButtonStyle where Self == CardPressStyle { static var cardPress: CardPressStyle { .init() } }
plus a DimPressStyle (opacity only) for rows, chips and the detail buttons. Replace every .plain listed above, and add .buttonStyle(.cardPress) to SeriesView.swift:650 and FavoritesView.swift:134/160 so they stop being the odd ones out. NavigationLink honours ButtonStyle, so nothing else changes.
Scrolling: it must be a ButtonStyle driven by configuration.isPressed. The enclosing ScrollView delays content touches and cancels the press as soon as a pan starts, so a flick across a shelf never flashes cards while a deliberate press shrinks after roughly 0.15 s, which is how App Store and TV cards behave. Do not build it from DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) or onLongPressGesture(pressing:): both compete with the shelf pan.
Context menus: keep .contextMenu on the Button / NavigationLink, outside the style. When the long press is recognised the system cancels the button touch, isPressed drops, the card springs back and the system lift takes over; keep the scale small (0.96) so the two do not read as a double bounce.
Optional, iOS 26 only: the detail CTA could become .buttonStyle(.glassProminent) behind if #available(iOS 26, *), falling back to DimPressStyle on iOS 18.

**APIs:** ButtonStyle / ButtonStyleConfiguration.isPressed (iOS 13.0); EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion (iOS 13.0); PrimitiveButtonStyle.glassProminent (optional) (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The inconsistency is real in code. .buttonStyle(.plain): LiveStreamsView.swift:457, M3UChannelsView.swift:445, VODView.swift:345/462/704, SeriesView.swift:322/434, WatchHistoryListView.swift:201, DetailComponents.swift:251/267/284/465, DownloadButton.swift:81. No style (automatic = borderless outside a List): SeriesView.swift:650-659, FavoritesView.swift:134-144 and 160-170, shelf headers LiveStreamsView.swift:356, VODView.swift:315 and 418, SeriesView.swift:292 and 394, M3UChannelsView.swift:337. iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows the headers in accent blue with a dim-blue chevron although the label says .foregroundStyle(.primary) (hierarchical styles resolve against the button tint), which proves the default tinted style is in effect there; ContinueWatchingRow.swift:43 uses .plain for the same kind of header. onTapGesture instead of a button: ContinueWatchingRow.swift:50, SeriesView.swift:1449, EPGGuideRowViews.swift:24, ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:63. So the same SeriesCard is styled differently in the shelf (:322/:434 plain) and in the grid (:650 default). What the code cannot prove is the perception claim: PlainButtonStyle is documented as possibly applying a pressed effect, and whether .plain leaves a bitmap poster completely inert and whether the default style dims the whole poster on iOS 18 / 26 needs one recording (the finding itself hedges this). Also not addressed: inside a ScrollView the button touch is delayed, so on a quick tap isPressed is true for about a frame; a style keyed only on isPressed will show almost nothing on quick taps and helps only on presses longer than about 0.15 s. No comment or history marks any of the three styles as a deliberate choice.

**Corrected claim:** Custom-labelled buttons use three press treatments (.plain, the default tinted style, and onTapGesture with none), so the same card is styled differently between shelf and grid, and shelf headers pick up the accent tint on four screens but not on Continue Watching. Whether .plain posters show no reaction at all, and how strongly the default-styled ones dim, is unverified. The big custom buttons (gradient Watch Now with explicit white text, secondary buttons, season chips) have no designed pressed state.

**Corrected fix:** One shared file Views/Components/PressStyles.swift with CardPressStyle (scale 0.96-0.97 + slight dim) and DimPressStyle (opacity only), applied to every site listed, including SeriesView.swift:650 and FavoritesView.swift:134/160. Corrections: (a) read accessibilityReduceMotion in a private View returned from makeBody rather than as @Environment on the ButtonStyle struct; (b) quick taps: either accept that only deliberate presses animate, or hold the pressed look for a minimum time (e.g. an inner View with @State that sets on press and releases after about 0.12 s); decide after watching it in the simulator; (c) shelf headers: give them DimPressStyle too and make the colour explicit; turning the blue headers primary is a visible change, so it is the owner's call; (d) leave the detail CTA's gradient and add only the press state; .glassProminent is a look change and a separate decision (if adopted: if #available(iOS 26, *) { .buttonStyle(.glassProminent) } else { DimPressStyle }, in a @ViewBuilder helper because the branches have different types). Keep .contextMenu outside the styled button.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10441-10451: @available(iOS 13.0, ...) public struct ButtonStyleConfiguration { public let role: ButtonRole? (iOS 15); public let label: Label; public let isPressed: Bool }. SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:18334: EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion: Bool { get } (iOS 13). SwiftUI.swiftinterface:3444-3447: @available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, *) extension PrimitiveButtonStyle where Self == GlassProminentButtonStyle { static var glassProminent } (optional, must be gated; iOS 18 fallback = DimPressStyle). PlainButtonStyle (:8850) and BorderlessButtonStyle (:1514) are iOS 13 PrimitiveButtonStyles; their pressed rendering is not visible in the interface.

**Regression risks:** UI tests find cards via app.staticTexts["Midnight Horizon"] / ["Northern Lights"] and app.buttons with a combined label (ScreensUITests.swift:78-93, UserFlowsUITests.swift:47-58, 62-69); a custom ButtonStyle should keep the same accessibility shape but run them. Replacing the default style on SeriesView.swift:650 / FavoritesView.swift:134, 160 removes the tint environment: check that no label relied on it. A scale animation plus the context-menu lift can read as a double bounce. The style must stay a ButtonStyle (no DragGesture / onLongPressGesture) so shelf and page pans keep working. The Equatable shelf rows are unaffected.

**How to verify:** Before the change, record on the simulator (iOS 26 and an iOS 18 runtime): press and hold about 1 s, and quick tap, on a Movies shelf poster (.plain), a Series category-grid poster (default), a Favorites poster and the Watch Now button; compare frames for any opacity or colour change. That settles the perception claim. After the change, the same recording must show identical feedback on all of them, a flick across a shelf must not flash cards, and the existing UI tests must pass.

## haptics-touch-feedback-3 — Episode rows are not buttons: the thumbnail and the row padding are dead, only the text column reacts, and nothing highlights

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1476`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping an episode's thumbnail, the most natural target, does nothing. The episode starts only when the finger lands on the title or plot text. The row gives no pressed feedback, and VoiceOver reads the texts without announcing a button.

**Mechanism (finder):** EpisodeDetailRow is an HStack of thumbnail ZStack, text VStack and DownloadButton (SeriesView.swift:1390-1473). The tap is attached to the text VStack only: .contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } at :1448-1451. The CachedImage stack at :1391-1414 has no gesture; it is 50 x 75 pt on iPhone and 100 x 150 pt on iPad (PosterMetrics episodeThumbWidth/Height, Views/PosterMetrics.swift:40-41). The 16 pt / 12 pt row padding (:1474-1475) is outside the gesture as well. onTapGesture adds neither a pressed state nor the button trait.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make thumbnail + text one Button and leave DownloadButton as its sibling (buttons must not nest):
  HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
    Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } label: {
      HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { thumbnail; textColumn }
        .contentShape(Rectangle())
    }
    .buttonStyle(.dimPress)            // shared style from the press-state finding
    if let remoteURL { DownloadButton(...) }
  }
Optionally add .contextMenu { Play from beginning; download items } on the Button. No new API.

**APIs:** Button + ButtonStyle (iOS 13.0); View.contentShape(_:eoFill:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1476: the row is an HStack of the thumbnail ZStack (:1391-1414, no gesture), the text VStack (:1416-1451) and DownloadButton (:1453-1472). The only tap handler is .contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture on the text VStack (:1448-1451); grep finds no other gesture on the row or in EpisodesPanel (:1294-1352). Row padding (:1474-1475) is outside it. Thumbnail size: PosterMetrics.swift:40-41 scaled(100) x scaled(150), layoutScale clamps to 0.5 on phones (PosterMetrics.swift:9-14), so 50 x 75 pt on iPhone and up to 100 x 150 pt on iPad; its placeholder icon is play.rectangle.fill, which invites the tap. History shows this is a regression, not a decision: in fe55017 (native/ios/.../SeriesView.swift:~968-972) the whole row was Button(action: { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) }) { HStack { thumbnail; text } }; when DownloadButton was added as a sibling the Button became an onTapGesture on the text column only. No comment explains leaving the thumbnail out. onTapGesture gives no pressed state and no button trait.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Since the download button was added to episode rows, only the text column starts the episode; the thumbnail (50 x 75 pt on iPhone, up to 100 x 150 pt on iPad) and the row padding are dead, there is no pressed state, and VoiceOver does not announce a button. The text column is still most of the row width on iPhone, so the miss is worst on iPad.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: outer HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } label: { HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { thumbnail; textColumn } ... }; if let remoteURL { DownloadButton(...) } }. Two additions: move the leading 16 pt and vertical 12 pt padding inside the Button label before .contentShape(Rectangle()) so the padding the finding calls dead becomes tappable (keep the trailing padding outside, after DownloadButton); and use the shared dim style if the press-style finding is adopted, otherwise .buttonStyle(.plain), which already restores the pre-regression behaviour. Remove the old .contentShape/.onTapGesture from the text column. The episode context menu is optional and can wait.

**API check:** Button and ButtonStyle: iOS 13 (ButtonStyleConfiguration at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10441-10451). SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13251: @inlinable nonisolated public func contentShape<S>(_ shape: S, eoFill: Bool = false) -> some View where S : Shape, iOS 13. No iOS 26 API.

**Regression risks:** DownloadButton must stay a sibling, not nested, or its tap and its context menu (DownloadButton.swift:78-82) break. With a non-plain style the title (:1417-1419, .foregroundStyle(.primary)) and the accent 'remaining' label would resolve against the button tint; a custom ButtonStyle or .plain avoids that. The divider inset (PosterMetrics.episodeRowDividerLeading) and the row height must not change when the padding moves inside the label. The watchHistory @Query capture is unchanged.

**How to verify:** UI test with a fixture that has one loaded season (the demo fixture has seasonsLoaded: false): tap the thumbnail coordinate of the first episode row and assert the player appears; assert the row is in app.buttons; tap the download button and assert the player did not open. Manually on iPad: tap the thumbnail and the row's top and bottom edge.

## haptics-touch-feedback-4 — Live results in Search and every Downloads row use a plain button inside a List: no row highlight and only the icon and text are tappable

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search, Downloads
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:154-163, 309-326`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:181-204, 206-232, 235-261`

**What the user perceives:** In the same result list, movie and series rows highlight under the finger and react anywhere across the row, while live-channel rows show nothing and ignore taps to the right of the channel name. In Downloads a tap in the empty middle of a row does nothing and no row ever highlights.

**Mechanism (finder):** SearchView.swift:156-162 wraps ResultRow in Button { playLive(item) }.buttonStyle(.plain). A plain (or borderless) button opts out of List's row-wide tap handling and selection highlight, so the hit area is the label's own content; ResultRow (SearchView.swift:316-324) is an HStack without Spacer, frame(maxWidth:) or contentShape. The sibling rows are NavigationLinks (SearchView.swift:180-187, 205-212) and get the system highlight. DownloadsView.swift:182-187 has the same Button + .plain; its label contains a Spacer (:257) that is not hit-testable without a contentShape. The app already uses the right pattern elsewhere: default-style Button with a primary foreground in ContentView.swift:211-242, CategoryPickerSheet.swift:103-120 and LanguagePickerSection.swift:37-56.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Remove .buttonStyle(.plain) at SearchView.swift:162 and DownloadsView.swift:187 and tint the label instead (.foregroundStyle(.primary) on ResultRow / row(item)); List then draws its own highlight and takes the whole row. In DownloadsView, rows whose primary action is empty (downloading and queued, :208-209) should not be wrapped in a Button at all, so they do not highlight for nothing; give every row a .contextMenu mirroring the swipe actions at :188-203 (cancel or delete). Search rows can reuse the menus from the context-menu finding.

**APIs:** Button in List with the automatic button style (iOS 13.0); View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code confirms the setup: Views/SearchView.swift:156-162 is Button { playLive(item) } label: { ResultRow(...) }.buttonStyle(.plain) inside a List, while the movie and series rows are NavigationLinks (:180-187, :205-212). ResultRow (:309-326) is an HStack with no Spacer, no frame(maxWidth:) and no contentShape, so with .plain the hit area is the icon plus the text block and List draws no row highlight. Views/DownloadsView.swift:181-187 is the same Button + .plain; its label (:235-261) has a Spacer (:257) and no contentShape, so the gap between text and the trailing icon is not hit-testable. The comment at :178-179 says the whole row is meant to be the button, so the dead gap is not intended. The mechanism is standard SwiftUI List behaviour (plain / borderless opt a button out of the row-wide tap and highlight); I am confident from code, but it was not exercised. The fix has a concrete error: it tells you to put .foregroundStyle(.primary) on the label. Inside a default-styled (tinted) button the hierarchical .primary resolves against the tint: iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows shelf headers written with .foregroundStyle(.primary) (LiveStreamsView.swift:366) rendered accent blue. The patterns the finding cites use the concrete colour instead: ContentView.swift:242 .foregroundColor(.primary) on the Button (white in iphone-dark/P01-playlist-list.png) and CategoryPickerSheet.swift:107. In DownloadsView the row also uses hierarchical .secondary (:249, :271, :302-316), which would turn tinted as well unless a concrete colour is set at the label root.

**Corrected claim:** Live rows in Search and all Downloads rows are .plain buttons inside a List: they get no system row highlight, and only the label's own content is tappable (right of the channel name in Search; the gap between text and trailing icon in Downloads). Movie and series rows in the same search list are NavigationLinks and behave like native rows.

**Corrected fix:** Remove .buttonStyle(.plain) at SearchView.swift:162 and DownloadsView.swift:187 and set a concrete colour on the Button: .foregroundStyle(Color.primary) (or .foregroundColor(.primary) as ContentView.swift:242 does), not .foregroundStyle(.primary). Check after the change that the hierarchical .secondary texts in DownloadsView (:249, :271, :302-316) and ProgressView still render grey and not tinted. In DownloadsView do not wrap downloading / queued rows in a Button (their primary action is empty, :208-209) and add a .contextMenu mirroring the swipe actions (:188-203). If the owner wants no highlight, the minimal alternative is to keep .plain and add .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading).contentShape(Rectangle()) to the labels; that fixes the hit area only.

**API check:** Button in List with the automatic style: iOS 13, no specific declaration to check. contextMenu(menuItems:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9867-9870, iOS 13.0. contentShape(_:eoFill:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13251, iOS 13. foregroundStyle / foregroundColor are long-standing; the difference between hierarchical .primary and Color.primary inside a tinted button is behavioural and is evidenced by screenshots L01 (blue) versus P01 (primary).

**Regression risks:** Text and icons turning accent blue if the hierarchical style is used as written in the finding. test_search_openingLiveResult_presentsPlayerWithoutKeyboard (UserFlowsUITests.swift:293-311) taps app.staticTexts["World News 24"]; the movie rows prove a default-styled row still exposes the static text, but run it. The 'N more results' buttons (SearchView.swift:164-169) are already default-styled and unaffected. Swipe actions in Downloads must stay on the row for both the Button and the non-Button variants.

**How to verify:** UI test: search 'World News', tap the live cell at normalized offset (0.9, 0.5), assert the player opens (fails today if the mechanism is as described, passes after). In Downloads with one completed item, tap the middle gap of the row and assert playback starts. Screen recording: live rows highlight grey like movie rows, text stays primary / secondary in light and dark.

## haptics-touch-feedback-5 — Continue Watching cards use onTapGesture: no pressed state, no button trait, and a single item cannot be removed from history

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U Channels, Watch history
- Code: `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:46-57, 64-110`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:70-75, 98-118, 154-203`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether removing a single item from history is wanted, and its wording (the sketch reuses the existing Delete label to avoid new strings).

**What the user perceives:** The first row of every tab, the one used most, is the least responsive: the card does not react to a press and a long press does nothing. A title watched by accident stays in the row until the whole history is wiped with the trash button.

**Mechanism (finder):** ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52 renders HistoryCard(item:).onTapGesture { onPlay(item) }: a plain VStack (:68-108) with no Button, so no isPressed, no .isButton trait, and VoiceOver gets title and subtitle as loose texts. Neither this row nor HistoryCardGridItem (WatchHistoryListView.swift:154-203) has a context menu; the only removal path is the clear-all alert at WatchHistoryListView.swift:98-118.

**Proposed fix (finder):** ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53:
  ForEach(historyItems) { item in
    Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item) }
      .buttonStyle(.cardPress)
      .contextMenu {
        Button { onPlay(item) } label: { Label(L("detail.watch"), systemImage: "play") }
        Button(role: .destructive) { Task { try? await AppDatabase.shared.write { db in _ = try DBWatchHistory.deleteOne(db, key: item.id) } } } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") }
      }
  }
Same menu on HistoryCardGridItem (WatchHistoryListView.swift:71). The @Query rows update by themselves (RecentWatchHistoryRequest). Existing strings only (detail.watch, common.delete).

**APIs:** Button + ButtonStyle (iOS 13.0); View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53 renders HistoryCard(item:).onTapGesture { onPlay(item) }; HistoryCard (:64-110) is a plain VStack, so there is no Button, no isPressed, no button trait. The row is the first shelf on Live (LiveStreamsView.swift:213), Movies (VODView.swift:65), Series (SeriesView.swift:66) and M3U (M3UChannelsView.swift:157). HistoryCardGridItem (WatchHistoryListView.swift:154-203) is a Button with .plain and no context menu; the only removal path is the clear-all alert (:98-118) and clearHistory (:130-152). No comment or history marks the tap gesture or the missing single delete as deliberate. The fix compiles against the code base: watchHistory has a text primary key id (Database/AppDatabase.swift:159-160), GRDB has TableRecord.deleteOne(_ db:, key:) (GRDB/Record/TableRecord.swift:601; deleteOne(db, id:) at :676 also works since DBWatchHistory is Identifiable), AppDatabase.shared.write is used the same way in Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:44, and RecentWatchHistoryRequest (Models/Requests.swift:399-429) is a ValueObservation, so the row updates by itself. detail.watch and common.delete exist in en.lproj. Not stated in the finding: the watchHistory row is also the resume position and the source of the progress bars, so deleting it resets that item; for series each episode is its own row, so deleting the latest one makes the series fall back to the previously watched episode.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Continue Watching cards are tap gestures, not buttons (no pressed state, no button trait), and neither the shelf nor the history grid can remove a single item; only the whole history can be cleared. Removing a row also discards that title's resume position and progress bar.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: wrap HistoryCard in Button { onPlay(item) } with the shared card press style (or .buttonStyle(.plain) if the press-style finding is not adopted) and add .contextMenu { Watch; destructive remove } on the Button; the same menu on HistoryCardGridItem at WatchHistoryListView.swift:71. Use DBWatchHistory.deleteOne(db, id: item.id). The Button part is a plain fix. The remove item is a product decision: it resets resume and progress for that title, and 'Delete' is ambiguous next to downloads; a dedicated string means ten additive lines in Localizable.strings, which also hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys (leave those untouched).

**API check:** Button / ButtonStyle iOS 13 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10441-10451). contextMenu(menuItems:) iOS 13.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9867-9870). GRDB (checkout, not SDK): public static func deleteOne(_ db: Database, key: some DatabaseValueConvertible) throws -> Bool at GRDB/Record/TableRecord.swift:601, and deleteOne(_ db:, id:) at :676. No iOS 26 API.

**Regression risks:** Deleting the row removes the resume position (WatchHistoryRequest), the poster progress bars (WatchProgressMapRequest) and, for series, changes which episode LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest resumes. If the item is playing in the mini player the next progress save re-creates the row. HistoryCard's title has no explicit colour (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:95-97): with the default button style it would turn accent blue, so use a custom ButtonStyle or .plain. The row is a non-lazy HStack of at most 10 items, so there is no performance concern.

**How to verify:** Unit test: insert two watchHistory rows, deleteOne by id, assert the other remains and RecentWatchHistoryRequest emits one row. UI test: seed two rows, long-press the first Continue Watching card, tap the remove item, assert one card remains; assert the cards are in app.buttons. Manually: after removing a half-watched movie its poster progress bar disappears and the detail offers Watch Now instead of resume.

## haptics-touch-feedback-6 — The download button ignores taps in three of its five states; cancel and delete exist only behind an undiscoverable long press, and the compact variant is about 29 x 28 pt

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:77-83, 101-123, 145-174, 176-202`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1453-1471`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:147-162`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the pill while it says Queued, Downloading 43 % or Completed does nothing at all. To stop a download the user has to guess that a long press opens a menu. In episode rows the target is a small icon chip next to a much larger dead thumbnail.

**Mechanism (finder):** primaryAction() only acts for .idle and .failed; .downloading, .queued and .completed break out (DownloadButton.swift:195-200, the comments say cancel and delete live in the context menu at :82 and :145-174). The compact label is a footnote glyph with 8 pt / 6 pt padding (:101-114), roughly 29 x 28 pt, used for every episode row (SeriesView.swift:1470).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make the menu the tap target whenever there is no primary action, the pattern of the system download controls:
  var body: some View {
    switch state {
    case .idle, .failed:
      Button(action: primaryAction) { labelContent }.buttonStyle(.dimPress).contextMenu { contextMenuItems }
    case .queued, .downloading, .completed:
      Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent }.buttonStyle(.plain)
    }
  }
and give the compact label .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).contentShape(Rectangle()) outside its background so the chip keeps its look. contextMenuItems already returns the right items per state.

**APIs:** Menu(content:label:) (iOS 14.0); Menu(content:label:primaryAction:) (alternative for the idle state) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift. The claim is accurate: body is Button(action: primaryAction).buttonStyle(.plain).contextMenu{...} (:77-83), and primaryAction() breaks out for .downloading, .queued and .completed (:195-200), with Turkish comments saying cancel/delete live in the context menu. So three of five states have a dead tap. The compact label is a footnote-semibold glyph with 8 pt / 6 pt padding (:101-114), roughly 32 x 28 pt, used for every episode row (Views/SeriesView.swift:1453-1471, compact: true). History: the behaviour dates from the monorepo import (d2489f9); no comment or commit gives a reason beyond 'use the context menu', so it is not protected earlier work.

Three corrections:
1. 'Cancel and delete exist only behind a long press' is overstated. Views/DownloadsView.swift:188-198 offers both as swipe actions. They are only hidden on the detail screens.
2. The fix uses .buttonStyle(.dimPress), which does not exist. A grep over the whole app target finds no dimPress or DimPress symbol; the only custom ButtonStyle is the private MoreMenuButtonStyle in PlayerView.swift:5205. As written the fix does not compile unless another finding introduces that style.
3. .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44) outside the chip background is not layout-neutral. The chip sits in HStack(alignment: .top) next to the episode text (SeriesView.swift:1389, 1453), so it would take about 12 pt of text width and drop about 8 pt.

The 'dead thumbnail' remark is true (the tap gesture is only on the text VStack, SeriesView.swift:1447-1451) but is a separate issue.

**Corrected claim:** On movie and series detail, the download pill does nothing when tapped in the Queued, Downloading and Completed states. Cancel and delete are reachable there only through a long-press context menu (they also exist as swipe actions in the Downloads screen). The compact episode-row variant is about 32 x 28 pt, under the 44 pt minimum.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the Button + contextMenu for .idle and .failed, with the existing .buttonStyle(.plain) (use a press-dimming style only if another accepted finding adds one; .dimPress does not exist today).

For .queued, .downloading and .completed, return Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent }.buttonStyle(.plain), so a tap opens Cancel or Delete. contextMenuItems already yields the right items per state.

For the compact target, enlarge the hit area without moving layout: on the compact label apply .padding(8).contentShape(Rectangle()).padding(-8) instead of a 44 pt min frame. The overlap with the neighbouring text tap area resolves to the download control because it is the later HStack sibling.

No iOS 26 API is involved, so no availability guard or fallback is needed.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7129-7132: @available(iOS 14.0, macOS 11.0, tvOS 17.0, *) extension Menu { nonisolated public init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content, @ViewBuilder label: () -> Label) }. Found.
SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7140-7143: @available(iOS 15.0, ...) Menu.init(content:label:primaryAction:). Found, not needed.
View.contextMenu(menuItems:) at :9870 (non-escaping builder). Found.
View.contentShape(_:eoFill:) is present in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface (:13251 / :13336, iOS 13).
.buttonStyle(.dimPress): not in the SDK and not in the code base.

**Regression risks:** The body switches between Button and Menu, so the control's identity changes on idle -> queued; any future animation on the pill would restart there.
The Menu label re-renders on every progress tick while the menu is open. If the download completes while it is open, the item changes from Cancel to Delete under the finger (the same hazard exists today in the context menu).
Menu applies its own tint and press dimming to the label unless .buttonStyle(.plain) is kept, and on iOS 26 the menu morphs out of the label; check the pill looks unchanged in both states.
The enlarged compact hit area overlaps the episode text tap area by 8 pt; confirm a tap near the chip does not start playback.

**How to verify:** Simulator with a reachable stream: start a download from movie detail and from an episode row. Tap the pill while Queued or Downloading: a menu with Cancel must open. After completion, a tap must offer Delete. Long-press in the idle state must still show the Download item.
Compare screenshots of movie detail (M07) and an episode row before and after: the pill and chip must not move.
In the episode row, tap 6 pt outside the chip's visible edge and assert the menu opens (or the download starts) and playback does not.

## haptics-touch-feedback-7 — Several primary touch targets are well under 44 pt: shelf headers, filter and day chips, season chips, Show more, the settings header refresh glyph

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U Channels, Search, TV Guide, Series detail, Movie detail, Settings
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:355-370`, `Views/VODView.swift:314-329, 417-432`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:291-306, 393-408`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:336-355`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44`, `Views/SearchView.swift:25-44`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:104-123`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:391-400, 443-465`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:170-181`

**What the user perceives:** Opening a category from a shelf means hitting a single line of text; taps slightly above or below scroll or do nothing. Search filter chips, guide day chips and season chips need a careful tap. In Settings a tiny refresh arrow sits in a section header.

**Mechanism (finder):** Shelf header: the NavigationLink label is only Text(.headline) plus a chevron, with the Spacer outside the link (LiveStreamsView.swift:355-369 and the four copies): about 22 pt high and as wide as the name, yet it is the only route to the category grid (iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png). Continue Watching header: Spacer inside a .plain label without contentShape (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:33-43), about 28 pt. Search chips: subheadline + 7 pt padding = about 32-34 pt (SearchView.swift:31-38, measured in iphone-light/Q03-search-results-mi.png). Guide day chips: caption + 6 pt = about 26-28 pt (EPGGuideView.swift:112-116, iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png). Season chips about 38 pt (DetailComponents.swift:448-452). Show more / less: footnote text only, about 18 pt (DetailComponents.swift:392-399). Settings: Button { Image(arrow.clockwise) } inside a Section header (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:174-179), about 16 pt, duplicating pull-to-refresh (:397) and Try Again (:235).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Grow hit areas without moving pixels.
Shelf headers (5 files) and Continue Watching: put the Spacer inside the label and add .frame(minHeight: 44).contentShape(Rectangle()), then take the added 22 pt back from the surrounding spacing (VStack spacing 10 -> 0 and the shelf's .padding(.vertical, 6)).
Chips: after the capsule background add .frame(minHeight: 44).contentShape(Rectangle()) on the label and reduce the strip's own vertical padding by the same amount (SearchView.swift:43 from 10 to 4, EPGGuideView.swift:121 from 8 to 0; season bar DetailComponents.swift:470).
Show more: .frame(minHeight: 44, alignment: .leading).contentShape(Rectangle()) with the block's spacing reduced.
Settings: remove the header glyph (pull-to-refresh and the Try Again row already cover it).

**APIs:** View.contentShape(_:eoFill:) (iOS 13.0); View.frame(minWidth:idealWidth:maxWidth:minHeight:...) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The sizes are real, from code and screenshots.
- Shelf headers: the NavigationLink label is only Text(.headline) plus a chevron, with the Spacer outside the link (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:355-369; VODView.swift:316-329 and 418-431; SeriesView.swift:293-306 and 394-407; M3UChannelsView.swift:337-349). That is about 22 pt high and as wide as the title (iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png). It is the only route to the category grid: LiveCategoryDetailView( is constructed only at LiveStreamsView.swift:357, and the toolbar category picker only scrolls (pendingScrollTarget, :145-147).
- Continue Watching header: .buttonStyle(.plain) with a Spacer inside the label and no contentShape (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44), so only the title2 text and chevron are hittable, about 28 pt.
- Search chips: subheadline + 7 pt padding (SearchView.swift:31-38), about 32 pt in iphone-light/Q03.
- Guide day chips: caption + 6 pt (EPGGuideView.swift:112-116), about 26 pt in iphone-dark/L06.
- Season chips: subheadline + 9 pt, about 38 pt (DetailComponents.swift:448-452).
- Show more: footnote text only, about 18 pt (DetailComponents.swift:396-404).
- Settings header glyph: a bare Image(arrow.clockwise) button in a Section header (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:170-181).
None of these is deliberate; no comment or commit explains the small targets.

Corrections to the fix:
1. Compensating by zeroing the VStack spacing and the shelf's .padding(.vertical, 6) is not layout-neutral at the edges. The first and last shelf lose 6 pt of outer padding while the header gains 11 pt, so the first header moves about 5 pt. The 'not more than a point' criterion fails there.
2. The search strip arithmetic is off by a point per side (a 34 pt chip needs 5 pt of padding, not 4).
3. A simpler pattern needs no compensation: .padding(.vertical, k).contentShape(Rectangle()).padding(.vertical, -k) on the label.
4. Removing the settings glyph is a product decision. The glyph is shown only once the info has loaded (:173), exactly when the Try Again row (:233-237) is not visible, so pull-to-refresh (:397) would become the only way to refresh.

The settings edit is about 180 lines from the TipJarRow() line (:355), so the tip-jar work stays intact.

**Corrected claim:** Several frequently used targets outside the player are under 44 pt high: shelf title links (about 22 pt, and the only route to a category grid), the Continue Watching title (about 28 pt, text only), search filter chips (about 32 pt), guide day chips (about 26 pt), season chips (about 38 pt), Show more / less (about 18 pt) and the settings header refresh glyph (about 16-20 pt).

**Corrected fix:** Enlarge hit areas without changing layout, using padding + contentShape + negative padding on the tappable label.
- Shelf headers (LiveStreamsView.swift:358, VODView.swift:319 and 421, SeriesView.swift:296 and 397, M3UChannelsView.swift:340): on the label HStack add .padding(.vertical, 11).contentShape(Rectangle()).padding(.vertical, -11). Widening the link to the full row (Spacer inside the label) is optional; Apple's shelf headers keep the title + chevron as the target.
- Continue Watching (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:33): same modifier with 8 pt. Its Spacer is already inside the label, so this also makes the full width tappable.
- Chips: 6 pt for search (SearchView.swift:31), 9 pt for guide days (EPGGuideView.swift:112), 3 pt for seasons (DetailComponents.swift:448). The strips' own vertical padding (10 / 8 / 4 pt) already contains the overflow.
- Show more (DetailComponents.swift:396): 13 pt.
- Settings glyph: either keep it with .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).contentShape(Rectangle()), like the eye button at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:218-219, or remove it. Removal is the owner's call. Leave the TipJarRow() line untouched.

No iOS 26 API is involved.

**API check:** View.contentShape(_:eoFill:): present in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface (:13251 / :13336 extension blocks, iOS 13.0).
View.padding(_:_:) and View.frame(minWidth:...minHeight:...): iOS 13.0 core API, already used in this code base (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:218-219 uses .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).contentShape(Rectangle())).
No iOS 26-only API involved.

**Regression risks:** Expanded hit areas overlap neighbours. A shelf header's area reaches 1 pt into the card strip below (cards win as the later sibling) and 11 pt into the gap above. Chip areas stay inside their strip's padding.
A full-width header target sits between two card rows, so tap attribution near the edges should be checked.
The shelf rows' Equatable conformance and .equatable() wrapping are untouched.
If the settings glyph is removed, users lose the only visible refresh for subscription info.
The settings file carries the tip-jar WIP; the edit must not reflow the About section.

**How to verify:** Screenshots before and after for Live home, Movies home, Search, TV Guide and series detail must be pixel-identical (the negative-padding variant does not move layout).
Simulator UI test: tap 10 pt below a shelf title's baseline and assert the category screen pushes; tap 8 pt above a day chip's top edge and assert the day changes.
Accessibility Inspector audit: no hit region under 44 pt for these elements.
Repeat at the largest Dynamic Type size to confirm nothing clips.

## haptics-touch-feedback-8 — The M3U long-press menu is built when the card renders, not when it opens: the favourite label goes stale and every card body parses its stream URL

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels, M3U group grid, M3U Favorites
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475`, `Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:37-63`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:205-222`

**What the user perceives:** Long-press a channel, choose Add to Favorites, long-press it again: the menu still says Add to Favorites with an empty star, and choosing it now removes the favourite. The label only corrects itself after the card happens to re-render.

**Mechanism (finder):** contextMenu takes a non-escaping builder (SDK: func contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems)), so the closure runs during M3UChannelCard.body. let isFavorite = M3UFavoriteStore.shared.isFavorite(channelId:) at M3UChannelsView.swift:451 is therefore captured at card-render time; the comment at :447-450 assumes it is read on every menu opening. The card deliberately does not observe the store and its parent row is Equatable (:326-330), so nothing re-runs the body after a toggle except the once-a-minute EPG snapshot. toggle() decides from the database (M3UFavoriteStore.swift:42-63), so the stale label and the action disagree. The same closure also runs M3UParser.sanitizedURL and M3UStreamClassifier.classify (:460-461) for every card body during scrolling.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Move the whole menu into a view whose body is only evaluated when the menu is presented, the way M3UDownloadMenuItems already works (DownloadButton.swift:207-222):
  private struct M3UChannelMenu: View {
    let channel: DBM3UChannel
    @ObservedObject private var favorites = M3UFavoriteStore.shared
    var body: some View {
      let fav = favorites.isFavorite(channelId: channel.id)
      Button { Task { await favorites.toggle(channel: channel) } } label: { Label(fav ? L("favorites.remove") : L("favorites.add"), systemImage: fav ? "star.slash" : "star") }
      if let url = M3UParser.sanitizedURL(from: channel.url) { /* classify + M3UDownloadMenuItems as today */ }
    }
  }
  ... .contextMenu { M3UChannelMenu(channel: channel) }
The card body then only constructs one struct. Keep the card itself free of store observation.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (non-escaping builder) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real. The SDK declares contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems) with a non-escaping builder, so the closure at Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475 runs inside M3UChannelCard.body. That means let isFavorite = M3UFavoriteStore.shared.isFavorite(...) (:451) is evaluated when the card renders, not when the menu opens.

The comment at :447-450 assumes the opposite ('the menu is rebuilt on every opening'). git log -S on that comment gives 0ab5bcd (2026-07-22), which replaced @ObservedObject favorites on the card with this one-shot read to stop thousands of cards re-rendering. The non-observation is deliberate; the staleness is its unintended side effect.

Nothing re-runs the card body after a toggle:
- The card observes only \.epgSnapshot (:415).
- Shelf rows are Equatable and wrapped in .equatable() (:171-179, :326-330).
- M3UChannelsView and M3UGroupDetailView do not observe M3UFavoriteStore; only M3UDashboardView, M3UFavoritesView and M3UPlayerShell do.
- Lazy containers keep created cards alive.
toggle() decides from the database (Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:42-63), so after one toggle the label says the opposite of what the tap does.

Two scope notes:
- M3U Favorites is not really affected: there the card leaves the grid when unfavourited (M3UFavoritesView recomputeKey).
- The 'every card body parses its URL' sub-claim is true (:460-461) but costs a few microseconds per card (URL(string:) plus two lowercased() calls; Networking/M3UParser.swift:149-160, M3UChannelsView.swift:955-967). It is not a perceptible scroll cost.

The fix matches the existing M3UDownloadMenuItems pattern (DownloadButton.swift:207-222), which already relies on menu content being evaluated on presentation.

Severity lowered to low: M3U playlists only, and only on a second long-press of the same card in the same visit.

**Corrected claim:** On the M3U Channels shelves and the group grid, the favourite item of the long-press menu is computed when the card renders. After a toggle the label and icon stay stale (the menu says Add to Favorites for a channel that is already a favourite, and choosing it removes it) until the card is rebuilt. The per-card URL parse in the same closure is real but negligible.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: move the menu content into a small View, private struct M3UChannelMenu { let channel: DBM3UChannel; @ObservedObject private var favorites = M3UFavoriteStore.shared }. Its body builds the favourite Button from favorites.isFavorite(channelId:) and the existing sanitizedURL / classify / M3UDownloadMenuItems branch. Use .contextMenu { M3UChannelMenu(channel: channel) }.

Keep M3UChannelCard itself free of store observation (the 0ab5bcd optimisation) and update the comment at :447-450.

Keep the @ObservedObject in the menu view, not a plain read. It stays correct whether SwiftUI builds menu content lazily or eagerly; that laziness is assumed by the existing code, not verified here.

No iOS 26 API is involved.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9870: nonisolated public func contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems) -> some View where MenuItems : View. The builder is non-escaping, which confirms it runs during the card body. iOS 13.0.
@ObservedObject and ObservableObject are plain SwiftUI/Combine, already used by M3UDownloadMenuItems (DownloadButton.swift:221).

**Regression risks:** If SwiftUI instantiated context-menu content eagerly, every realised card's menu view would subscribe to M3UFavoriteStore and re-evaluate on each toggle. Those bodies are far cheaper than the card bodies 0ab5bcd protected, but it would partly reintroduce that cost, so measure it.
The card must not gain an @ObservedObject.
M3UFavoritesView reuses the same card via M3UGroupGridContent and gets the new menu too; behaviour there is unchanged.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test on an M3U fixture playlist: long-press a channel in a shelf, tap Add to Favorites, long-press the same card again, assert Remove from Favorites with star.slash. Repeat in the group grid.
Put a temporary counter or Self._printChanges() in M3UChannelMenu.body and M3UChannelCard.body. Scroll about 500 cards without opening a menu and toggle one favourite: expect zero menu-body evaluations for unopened cards and zero card-body evaluations from the toggle.

## haptics-touch-feedback-9 — Outside the player the app is haptically silent: favourite toggles, custom chip selection, sync results and errors give no feedback

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Search, TV Guide, Settings, Add playlist, Dashboard
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:73-92, 315-332`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:867-888, 1249-1264`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:438-477`, `Views/SearchView.swift:25-44`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:104-123`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44, 512-536`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40, 321-344`, `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:112-116`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:135-139`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:138-155`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:91-108`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether destructive confirmation alerts should carry a warning haptic at all (Apple's own alerts are silent); everything else follows system conventions.

**What the user perceives:** The player ticks and thumps like a system app, the rest of the app feels flat: starring a movie swaps an icon silently, selecting a season or a search filter has no click, a 20-second catalog refresh ends without any signal, and a failed load only shows an alert.

**Mechanism (finder):** The only two sensoryFeedback sites are in the player timeline (Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:231-233); there is no UIFeedbackGenerator outside player files. Custom controls that replace system ones lose the system's own haptics: the capsule chips (DetailComponents.swift:443-465, SearchView.swift:28-39, EPGGuideView.swift:109-118) stand in for segmented or scope controls; the star toggles are plain toolbar buttons (MovieDetailView.swift:87-90, SeriesView.swift:881-886).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use SwiftUI sensoryFeedback (already used by the player), attached to the screen content rather than to toolbar items:
1) Favourite toggle: @State private var favoriteTaps = 0, incremented in the star action; .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: favoriteTaps) on the root Group at MovieDetailView.swift:73 and SeriesView.swift:867; add .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)) on the star image. Do not trigger on isFavorite itself: the @Query starts at its default false (Models/Requests.swift:270) and would buzz when a favourited title opens.
2) Chip selection: .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: selectedId) { old, _ in old != nil } on DetailSeasonTabBar (the first assignment is programmatic); .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: selectedFilter) at SearchView.swift:24; .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: model.selectedDay) on the day picker.
3) Long operations: on the settings Form, .sensoryFeedback(trigger: isSyncing) { was, now in was && !now ? (syncError == nil ? .success : .error) : nil } (PlaylistSettingsView; M3U variant tests showError).
4) Errors: .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: showError) { _, shown in shown } next to the alerts at AddPlaylistView.swift:112 and AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:135; .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: contentStore.loadError) { old, new in old == nil && new != nil } next to DashboardView.swift:138 (covers failed pull-to-refresh, which writes loadError in PlaylistContentStore.swift:202 and :217) and the M3U twin.
5) Destructive confirmations (optional): .sensoryFeedback(.warning, trigger: flag) { _, shown in shown } beside the alerts at WatchHistoryListView.swift:110, PlaylistSettingsView.swift:373/381, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:262/270, ContentView.swift:117.
Leave silent on purpose: plain taps and navigation, pull-to-refresh (the system refresh control already ticks), Toggle, system Menu / Picker, swipe actions and context menus (all have system haptics). All APIs are iOS 17, no availability guard needed.

**APIs:** View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) (iOS 17.0); View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:condition:) (iOS 17.0); View.sensoryFeedback(trigger:_:) returning SensoryFeedback? (iOS 17.0); SensoryFeedback.selection / .success / .warning / .error / .impact(weight:intensity:) (iOS 17.0); ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The factual part holds. A grep for sensoryFeedback and *FeedbackGenerator across the app target finds only Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:231-233, PlayerView.swift and PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:211/222, all player surfaces. Nothing in browsing, search, settings or the add-playlist flows emits a haptic of its own.

The cited controls are as described:
- Star toggles are plain toolbar buttons with an instant icon swap (MovieDetailView.swift:85-91, SeriesView.swift:879-887).
- Chips are custom capsule buttons (DetailComponents.swift:443-465, SearchView.swift:28-39, EPGGuideView.swift:109-118).
- syncContents ends silently (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:512-536).
- IsFavoriteRequest.defaultValue is false (Models/Requests.swift:269-270), so the warning not to trigger on isFavorite itself is correct.

The proposals are technically sound:
- All triggers are Equatable (String?, Date, the String-backed SearchFilter enum, Bool).
- syncError and isSyncing are set in the same MainActor.run block (:530-533), so the feedback closure sees the final error state.
- In the M3U variant the catch sets showError before the defer clears isSyncing (M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:321-343).

What needs correcting:
1. The mechanism 'custom controls lose the system's own haptics' is weak. UISegmentedControl and search scope bars give no haptic on iOS 18, so the chips lose nothing there. Chip haptics are an addition, not a restoration.
2. This is polish and mostly a product decision, not a defect. Apple uses haptics sparingly and its alerts are silent. Severity is low.
3. Triggering on selectedId / selectedDay also fires on programmatic changes after the first (for example the Now toolbar button calling selectDay at EPGGuideView.swift:345, or onSelectFilter from the results at SearchView.swift:62). A tap counter incremented in the chip action, as proposed for the star, is more precise.
4. On M3U settings, item 3 (sync result) and an error-alert haptic would both fire for one failure; use only one.

The settings edits are far from the TipJarRow() lines (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:355, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:233) and leave the tip work intact.

**Corrected claim:** Outside the player the app adds no haptics of its own. Favourite toggles, long catalog syncs and failed loads complete without tactile confirmation; system controls (Toggle, pull-to-refresh, context menus) still carry theirs. This is a polish gap and largely a product decision. The custom chips do not lose any system haptic on iOS 18.

**Corrected fix:** Keep it to a few meaningful events, using sensoryFeedback (iOS 17, no availability guard needed).
1. Favourite star: add @State favoriteTaps, incremented in the star action. Put .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: favoriteTaps) on the root Group (MovieDetailView.swift:73, SeriesView.swift:867) and .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)) on the star Image. Do not trigger on isFavorite.
2. Sync result: on the PlaylistSettingsView Form, .sensoryFeedback(trigger: isSyncing) { was, now in was && !now ? (syncError == nil ? .success : .error) : nil }. The M3U variant tests showError and must not also get a separate error-alert haptic.
3. Failures: .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: showError) { _, shown in shown } beside the alerts at AddPlaylistView.swift:112 and AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:135; .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: contentStore.loadError) { old, new in old == nil && new != nil } at DashboardView.swift:138 and its M3U twin.
4. Chip selection (optional, owner's call): if wanted, drive .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: chipTaps) from a counter incremented in the chip Button actions, not from selectedId / selectedDay / selectedFilter.
5. Drop the warning haptic on destructive confirmation alerts; system alerts are silent.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1981-1988, @available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, visionOS 26.0, *):
- func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T) where T : Equatable
- func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (_ oldValue: T, _ newValue: T) -> Bool)
- func sensoryFeedback<T>(trigger: T, _ feedback: @escaping (_ oldValue: T, _ newValue: T) -> SensoryFeedback?)
All three found.
SensoryFeedback statics at :842-855: success, warning, error, selection, impact, impact(weight:intensity:), impact(flexibility:intensity:). Found, iOS 17.
ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:) at :4578-4580, @available(iOS 17.0, ...). Found.
The iOS 26-only SensoryFeedback.selection(_:) / press / release (:871-875) are not used.

**Regression risks:** Over-buzzing: a trigger bound to a value fires on programmatic changes too, so use tap counters or old/new conditions.
A sync-result haptic also fires when a sync is started indirectly (the filter change at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:504) and may fire while the user is on another tab.
Double feedback on the M3U settings error path if both the sync-result and error-alert variants are added.
The settings files carry the tip-jar WIP; add modifiers only on the Form.
No performance impact.

**How to verify:** Device only (the simulator has no Taptic Engine).
- Star and unstar a movie and a series: one light tap each.
- Open an already-favourited title: no buzz on appear.
- Run Re-download All Content with network (success) and in airplane mode (error): exactly one haptic each.
- Fail an add-playlist validation: one error haptic.
- If chip haptics are adopted: switch seasons and search filters (one tick per tap), and confirm no tick when a series detail first selects its season.

## haptics-touch-feedback-10 — TV Guide touch handling is hand-rolled: a channel tap gives no feedback, the schedule hides behind a silent 0.5 s hold, programme cells and schedule rows do not highlight

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: TV Guide, Channel schedule
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:18-30, 133-170`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:202-216, 398-424`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:56-66`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether a channel tap in the M3U guide should play like on Xtream.

**What the user perceives:** In the guide nothing responds to the finger. Tapping a channel starts playback with no highlight; holding it for half a second suddenly pushes a schedule screen with no lift, haptic or menu, so the feature is effectively hidden. Programme cells and the rows of the channel schedule open a sheet without ever highlighting. On an M3U playlist the same channel tap opens the schedule instead of playing.

**Mechanism (finder):** EPGChannelColumnCell attaches LongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.5).exclusively(before: TapGesture()) (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169): no pressed state, no haptic at recognition, no accessibility action for the long-press branch, no button trait. Programme cells use .onTapGesture (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:24-26), and the sheet is presented only after an awaited database read (EPGGuideView.swift:412-424). ChannelEPGDetailView rows are .contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture inside a List (:59-64), so the List never highlights them. playChannel falls back to the schedule when row.liveStream is nil, i.e. for M3U (EPGGuideView.swift:398-402).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Channel cell: replace the composed gesture with Button(action: onTap) { cell }.buttonStyle(.dimPress).contextMenu { Button(play); Button(schedule) } (labels exist: epg.detail.play_channel, epg.guide.title). The context menu is the native long press: lift, haptic, VoiceOver actions. Keep the Equatable conformance (closures are already ignored, :139-141) and keep the .offset(x: bodyOffsetX) outside the cell as today.
Programme cells: Button with the dim style instead of onTapGesture; present the sheet immediately with the programme at hand and load the detail fields inside the sheet.
Schedule list: Button { selected = programme } label: { row(programme) } with .foregroundStyle(.primary) so the plain List highlights the row.
M3U guide: decide whether a channel tap should play there too (M3UPlayerShell exists).

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0); Button + ButtonStyle (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The code is as described.
- EPGChannelColumnCell attaches LongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.5).exclusively(before: TapGesture()) (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169). There is no pressed state, no haptic, no button trait and no accessibility action for the long-press branch, so the schedule push (EPGGuideView.swift:206) is invisible to VoiceOver and gives no cue to sighted users.
- Programme cells use .onTapGesture (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:24-26).
- ChannelEPGDetailView rows use .contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture inside a List (ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:59-63), so the List never highlights them.
- playChannel falls back to the schedule when row.liveStream is nil, i.e. for M3U (EPGGuideView.swift:398-402).
The composed gesture dates from 1cce013 / 654cefc with no rationale, so it is not protected performance work. The Equatable conformances and the sticky .offset(x: bodyOffsetX) are the deliberate parts and the fix can keep them.

Corrections to the fix:
1. .buttonStyle(.dimPress) does not exist anywhere in the app target; a press-dimming ButtonStyle must be added or supplied by another finding.
2. contextMenu { Button(play); Button(schedule) } cannot be unconditional. M3U rows have liveStream == nil (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:10) and EPGGuideRow carries no DBM3UChannel, so Play is impossible there without new plumbing.
3. 'epg.guide.title' is "TV Guide" (en.lproj/Localizable.strings:508), the name of the screen the user is already on. No schedule string exists, so a new key is needed in all ten languages. That touches the Localizable.strings files holding the uncommitted tip keys: append only.
4. Do not present the sheet first and load details inside it. programmeDetails is one keyed fetchOne on the reader (EPG/EPGStore.swift:303-312), a few milliseconds, and presenting first would make the description pop in. The missing press highlight is the real gap.
5. Empty cells (cell.programme == nil) must not become buttons.

**Corrected claim:** In the TV Guide, a channel tap plays with no press feedback, and the channel schedule is reachable only through a silent 0.5 s custom long press with no lift, haptic, button trait or VoiceOver action. Programme cells and channel-schedule rows open their sheet without a highlight. On M3U playlists the channel tap opens the schedule because the guide row has no playable channel.

**Corrected fix:** Channel cell (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:143-170): replace the composed gesture with Button(action: onTap) { existing HStack } using a small press-dimming ButtonStyle (new, or the shared one if another finding adds it), plus .contextMenu.
- The menu shows 'Play channel' (epg.detail.play_channel) only when row.liveStream != nil, and a schedule item with a new localized key (for example epg.channel.schedule) appended to the ten Localizable.strings files without touching the tip keys.
- Add .contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)) because the cell has a material background.
- Keep the Equatable conformance and keep .frame/.offset(x: bodyOffsetX)/.zIndex outside the cell.

Programme cells: wrap only cells with a programme in Button { onTap(programme) } with the same style. Leave empty cells as plain views. Keep the awaited programmeDetails read before presenting.

Schedule list (ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:59-63): Button { selected = programme } label: { row(programme) } with .foregroundStyle(.primary), keeping .id(rowID(programme)) on the row.

M3U guide: leave tap = schedule until the owner decides. Play needs the DBM3UChannel carried in EPGGuideRow or looked up in M3UContentStore, plus M3UPlayerShell.

No iOS 26 API is involved.

**API check:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9870, iOS 13.0. Found.
Button, ButtonStyle and ButtonStyleConfiguration.isPressed: iOS 13 core API, already used by MoreMenuButtonStyle (PlayerView.swift:5205-5208).
View.contentShape(_:_:eoFill:) with ContentShapeKinds.contextMenuPreview: the contentShape overloads are present in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface (:13251 / :13336); the kinds overload is iOS 15. I did not print that declaration line, so re-grep 'contextMenuPreview' before use.
.buttonStyle(.dimPress): not in the SDK and not in the code base.

**Regression risks:** The guide is performance-sensitive (the comments on the scroll-sync hang and the Equatable rows). A Button per programme cell adds a gesture and style per cell on row creation; rows are lazy and Equatable so scrolling should not re-render them, but creation cost on fast vertical flings must be measured.
Buttons inside the two-axis ScrollView must not steal or delay the pan.
The context-menu lift comes from a cell that is offset by bodyOffsetX; the preview could animate from the un-offset position or show a broken material snapshot.
Adding a localization key touches the WIP Localizable.strings files.
VoiceOver gains a button trait and menu actions; existing UI tests do not reference the guide cells (grep found none).

**How to verify:** EPGGuidePerformanceTests must stay green.
Simulator, large guide: scroll diagonally and fling vertically, compare hitch rate before and after in Instruments, and confirm pans starting on a channel or programme cell still scroll.
Long-press a channel after scrolling horizontally by several hours: the lifted preview must come from the pinned column position and look correct in light and dark.
UI test: long-press a guide channel and assert the menu items (Play absent on an M3U fixture); tap a schedule row and assert the row highlights and the sheet opens.
VoiceOver: the channel cell reads as a button and exposes the schedule action.
