## haptics-touch-feedback-11 — Playlist rows: delete goes through onDelete plus a confirmation alert, Edit is only a leading swipe, and there is no long-press menu

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list
- Code: `ContentView.swift:117-128, 207-260`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Alert versus confirmation dialog for the delete confirmation.

**What the user perceives:** Swiping a playlist away commits the row's removal animation before the confirmation alert appears; on Cancel the row has to come back. Edit is hidden behind a swipe from the leading edge, an unusual place, and a long press on a playlist does nothing.

**Mechanism (finder):** .onDelete(perform: deletePlaylists) (ContentView.swift:252) is a destructive, full-swipe-enabled action whose handler only stores the offsets and raises an alert (:257-260); the data is unchanged when the list finishes its delete animation. Edit is a separate .swipeActions(edge: .leading) (:243-250). The row has no contextMenu.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace onDelete with explicit actions on the row and add the menu:
  .swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: false) {
    Button { pendingDelete = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") }.tint(.red)   // no destructive role: the row stays until confirmed
    Button { playlistToEdit = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.edit"), systemImage: "pencil") }.tint(.orange)
  }
  .contextMenu {
    Button { playlistToEdit = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.edit"), systemImage: "pencil") }
    Button(role: .destructive) { pendingDelete = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") }
  }
and delete by id instead of IndexSet in performDelete (:262-284). The confirmation can stay an alert or become .confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:presenting:actions:).

**APIs:** View.swipeActions(edge:allowsFullSwipe:content:) (iOS 15.0); View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0); View.confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:presenting:actions:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts hold. ContentView.swift:252 `.onDelete(perform: deletePlaylists)`; the handler at :257-260 only stores `offsetsToDelete` and sets `showingDeleteAlert`, so the data is unchanged when the swipe completes; the real delete happens in performDelete (:262-284) after the alert at :117-128. Edit exists only as `.swipeActions(edge: .leading)` (:243-250). There is no `.contextMenu` on the row, although the app uses context menus elsewhere (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446, Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:82, and the long-press card screenshots). No comment marks the layout as deliberate; `git log -S` shows both lines only in the monorepo move d2489f9. No EditButton exists, so onDelete gives nothing beyond the swipe. No UI test swipes a playlist row (no swipeLeft/swipeRight in another-iptv-playerUITests). What is NOT established: the headline perception that the row animates out before the alert and returns on Cancel. That is runtime behaviour of List's delete action when the model is untouched; I could not run the simulator, and the finding itself marks it needs-simulator-run. P01-playlist-list.png shows only the resting row. One extra point in favour of the fix: performDelete resolves the stored IndexSet against `playlists` at confirm time (:266), so a @Query refresh between swipe and confirm could target another row; deleting by id removes that. The playlist list is rarely seen because the last playlist auto-loads (:152-163), so the impact is small.

**Corrected claim:** On the playlist list, delete is an `.onDelete` whose handler only raises a confirmation alert, Edit is reachable only through a leading-edge swipe, and a long press does nothing, while other rows and cards in the app have context menus. Whether the row visibly animates away and comes back around the alert is unverified and needs a recording. The stored IndexSet is resolved at confirm time, which is fragile compared with keeping the playlist id.

**Corrected fix:** Replace `.onDelete` and the leading swipe with explicit row actions and a context menu, and keep the alert.
- State: replace `offsetsToDelete: IndexSet?` with `@State private var pendingDelete: Playlist?`; keep `showingDeleteAlert`, or use `alert(_:isPresented:presenting:actions:message:)`.
- Row: `.swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: false)` with Delete first (no destructive role, `.tint(.red)`, sets pendingDelete and raises the alert) and Edit second (`.tint(.orange)`).
- Row: `.contextMenu` with Edit and `Button(role: .destructive)` Delete that also only sets pendingDelete.
- performDelete takes the playlist id; the cleanup calls at :270-278 stay as they are.
- Keep the alert rather than a confirmationDialog: the presentation modifiers hang on the NavigationStack content (:117), so a dialog would anchor to the whole screen on iPad.
- Existing keys common.edit, common.delete, common.cancel and playlists.delete.* cover all strings.
Owner decisions: whether full swipe should still lead to the alert (allowsFullSwipe true also works with a role-less button), and whether to keep the leading Edit swipe as well.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk): `View.swipeActions<T>(edge: HorizontalEdge = .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: Bool = true, content:)` at :16391, @available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, watchOS 8.0), tvOS unavailable. `View.contextMenu<MenuItems>(menuItems:)` at :9870, iOS 13.0. `View.alert<S, A, M, T>(_ title: S, isPresented:presenting:actions:message:)` at :10711, iOS 15.0. `View.confirmationDialog<S, A, T>(_ title: S, isPresented:titleVisibility:presenting:actions:)` at :17541, iOS 15.0 (extension at :17524). `DynamicViewContent.onDelete(perform:)` at :16638, iOS 13.0. `Playlist` is Identifiable and Equatable (Models/Playlist.swift:9), so it works as `presenting:` data and as @State. Nothing needs an iOS 26 gate.

**Regression risks:** Full-swipe-to-delete goes away if allowsFullSwipe is false. Users who learned the leading Edit swipe lose it unless it is kept. The context menu adds a long-press recognizer to the row Button; tap-to-open is unaffected, as on the existing M3U rows. Removing onDelete drops the VoiceOver delete action it supplied, but swipeActions buttons are exposed as accessibility custom actions. No performance work or tip-jar file is touched.

**How to verify:** First record the current build with two playlists: swipe left, tap Delete, watch whether the row collapses before the alert, then Cancel and watch whether it reappears; repeat with a full swipe. That settles the unverified perception claim. After the change: swipe, Delete, Cancel, and both rows stay in place with the row sliding closed; confirming removes exactly that playlist; long press shows Edit and Delete; Edit opens the correct sheet for both Xtream and M3U playlists; check on iPad too.

## haptics-touch-feedback-12 — Account values in Settings cannot be copied: a long press on server URL, username or source URL does nothing

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings, M3U Settings
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-224`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:160-183`

**What the user perceives:** Users who need their portal URL or username for another device or for support have to retype them; in system Settings a long press on such a value offers Copy.

**Mechanism (finder):** The rows are HStacks of two Texts (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-201, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:161-176) with neither textSelection nor a context menu. The password row only has the reveal toggle (:203-224).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add .textSelection(.enabled) to the value Texts (name, server URL, username, the revealed password, the M3U source URL). It brings the system Copy / Share callout with no new strings and no new localisation keys. Leave the TipJarRow() lines untouched.

**APIs:** View.textSelection(_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-201 renders name, server URL and username as `HStack { Text(label); Spacer(); Text(value).foregroundColor(.secondary) }` with no textSelection or context menu; the password row (:203-224) shows either the plain text or bullets plus the eye button. Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:161-176 is the same, with the source URL as a footnote Text with `.lineLimit(3)` (:172-175). T02-settings-2.png shows these as plain value rows. Both are inside a Form (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40). The modifier is already used in the app (Views/Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:95), so the pattern compiles and matches existing practice. The system comparison is fair: value rows in Settings > General > About offer Copy on long press. The M3U URL case is the most useful one: it is truncated to three lines on screen and usually carries credentials, so it cannot be retyped from what is shown. `git diff` shows the only uncommitted change in the two files is the TipJarRow() line (PlaylistSettingsView.swift ~:356, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift ~:234), far from the rows to edit, so the tip-jar work stays intact.

**Corrected claim:** The account values in both settings screens (server URL, username, revealed password, M3U source URL) are plain Texts that cannot be copied; a long press does nothing, whereas system Settings value rows offer Copy. The M3U source URL is also truncated to three lines, so it cannot even be read in full.

**Corrected fix:** Add `.textSelection(.enabled)` to the value Texts: PlaylistSettingsView.swift:192 (server URL), :199 (username), :207 (revealed password only, not the bullet Text at :210), and M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:172 (source URL). The playlist name (:185, M3U :163) is optional. On iOS this gives a whole-text Copy/Share callout on long press; no new strings. Do not touch the TipJarRow() lines.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk) :1821-1825: `@available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, *) @available(tvOS, unavailable) @available(watchOS, unavailable) extension View { nonisolated public func textSelection<S>(_ selectability: S) -> some View where S : TextSelectability }`. `EnabledTextSelectability` is declared in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface :5344. Already used at Views/Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:95. No iOS 26 gate needed.

**Regression risks:** Minimal. The selectable Text takes a long-press recognizer on the value only; these rows have no tap action, and the eye button keeps its own BorderlessButtonStyle hit area. The revealed password becomes copyable, which is user-initiated and only when revealed. The files hold the owner's uncommitted TipJarRow() lines; the edit sits in a different section and leaves them intact (touches_user_wip is true by file, with no overlap).

**How to verify:** Simulator: Settings > Playlist Information, long-press the server URL value and expect the Copy/Share callout; paste elsewhere to confirm the full string. Repeat for username, for the password after tapping the eye, and for the M3U source URL (the paste must be the full URL, not the three truncated lines). Confirm the bullet password offers nothing and the eye button still toggles. In a UI test, match the callout item by label 'Copy' across any element type rather than only `app.menuItems`, since the element type of the edit menu was not checked here and the label follows the system language.

## series-browse-detail-1 — Series detail replaces the whole page with a centred spinner while seasons load and with a bare red error on failure, although cover, plot, cast, genre and rating are already in the local row

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Series detail
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:866-897, 941-956, 1006-1014, 1176-1247`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:550-580`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a poster pushes an empty white page with a small spinner for as long as get_series_info takes (0.3-3 s on real panels); then the hero, plot and seasons all pop in at once with no transition. On failure the page is 'Error / Server error: HTTP 404 / Try Again' in red with no title, poster or plot, so the user cannot even tell which series it is (S03-series-detail-loading.png and S04-series-detail-settled.png are byte-identical: only the error block and the favourite star). This repeats for every series after each catalog refresh, because the refresh deletes the series rows and cascades the cached seasons away.

**Mechanism (finder):** body switches between three branches (SeriesView.swift:867-875): `isLoading && !currentSeries.seasonsLoaded` -> ProgressView only, `errorMessage != nil` -> errorView (941-956), else contentScroll. fetchSeriesInfo sets isLoading before the request (1177) and errorMessage on any throw (1241-1245). Nothing in the hero depends on that request: the catalog import already stores cover, plot, cast, director, genre, releaseDate, rating and youtubeTrailer (PlaylistContentStore.swift:563-577); only backdrop, rating5Based and episodeRunTime arrive later. The navigation title is empty until scrolled (877), so the error page carries no identity at all. Because the hero is not mounted during the fetch, its images only start loading after the fetch returns, adding a second pop-in. replaceSeriesCatalog deletes all series (PlaylistContentStore.swift:555), which cascades season/episode and resets seasonsLoaded, so the blank page comes back after every refresh.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Always render contentScroll; move loading and failure into seasonsSection only. Sketch:

var body: some View { contentScroll /* + existing modifiers */ }

@ViewBuilder private var seasonsSection: some View {
  if !seasons.isEmpty { /* existing season UI */ }
  else if let error = errorMessage {
    ContentUnavailableView {
      Label(L("common.error"), systemImage: "wifi.exclamationmark")
    } description: { Text(error) } actions: {
      Button(L("common.try_again")) { Task { await fetchSeriesInfo() } }.buttonStyle(.bordered)
    }
  } else if isLoading || !currentSeries.seasonsLoaded {
    VStack(spacing: 0) { ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { _ in EpisodeRowPlaceholder() } }
      .redacted(reason: .placeholder).accessibilityLabel(L("series.loading_seasons"))
  } else { Text(L("series.no_seasons_info")) }
}

Disable the primary button while seasons.isEmpty (today 'Watch' is tappable and playFirstEpisode silently returns at 1086). Show the inline error only when there are no cached seasons, so a failed refresh never hides seasons that are already in the database. Uses existing string keys, no new localisation. ContentUnavailableView is iOS 17+, so no fallback is needed on the iOS 18 target. MovieDetailView.swift:73-81 has the same three-branch body and can take the same change (Movies lens).

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0); View.redacted(reason:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/SeriesView.swift:866-897. The body has three exclusive branches: `isLoading && !currentSeries.seasonsLoaded` -> bare ProgressView (868-870), `errorMessage != nil` -> errorView (871-872, 941-956), else contentScroll. fetchSeriesInfo sets isLoading = true before the request (1177) and errorMessage on any throw (1241-1245). Nothing in the hero needs that request: replaceSeriesCatalog stores cover, plot, cast, director, genre, releaseDate, rating, youtubeTrailer (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:563-577), and heroConfig/GenreChipRow/plot/cast read exactly those fields (827-839, 965-989). Screenshot iphone-light/S04-series-detail-settled.png shows the claim literally: blank page, 'Error / Server error: HTTP 404 / Try Again' in red, no title (navigationTitle is "" until scrolled, 877). Cascade claim checked: season has a composite FK to series with onDelete: .cascade (Database/AppDatabase.swift:93), episode -> season cascade (108), seasonsLoaded defaults to false (78), and replaceSeriesCatalog does DELETE FROM series (PlaylistContentStore.swift:555); HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:66 even comments on the cascade. History (git log -S) shows no deliberate reason; the layout dates from the monorepo import. Two details the finding missed, both making it slightly worse: (a) isLoading starts false, so the first pass mounts contentScroll, then the .task flips it to the spinner, so the hero is built, torn down and rebuilt; (b) PlaylistContentStore never updates seasonsLoaded in memory (no reference outside the DB layer), so within a session the catalog row passed in is stale and the `.task` guard at 893 depends on the async SeriesByIDRequest value landing first; if it loses and the request fails, the error branch hides seasons that are already cached.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Series detail swaps the entire page for a centred spinner for the duration of get_series_info and for a bare red error on failure, although the hero, genres, plot, director and cast are already in the local row; it recurs after every series refresh because the delete cascades seasons and episodes away. Additionally the content is mounted for one pass before the spinner replaces it, and a failed (possibly redundant) fetch can hide cached seasons.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: always render contentScroll and move loading/failure into seasonsSection (cached seasons first, then inline ContentUnavailableView with retry, then a redacted placeholder, then the 'no seasons' text). Adjustments: (1) DetailActionBar (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:189-207) has no way to disable only the primary CTA, and `.disabled` on the whole bar would also kill the trailer link; add `var primaryDisabled = false` (default keeps MovieDetailView unchanged), apply `.disabled` plus reduced opacity on primaryCTA because its gradient background does not dim with .plain. Disable while seasons.isEmpty for both Watch and Resume (resumeLatestEpisode at 1070-1082 also silently no-ops when episodes were cascaded away). (2) EpisodeRowPlaceholder is a new small private view; size it from posterMetrics.episodeThumbWidth/Height so the swap to real rows does not shift. (3) Make the `.task` guard robust: read seasonsLoaded from the database (or use the immediate SeriesByIDRequest from finding 5) instead of the stale in-memory row. (4) Let the backdrop cross-fade when backdropPath arrives rather than pop. MovieDetailView.swift:73-81 has the identical three-branch body; treat it in the Movies lens with the same pattern.

**API check:** ContentUnavailableView: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576, `@available(iOS 17.0, ...) public struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` with `init(@ViewBuilder label:, description: = EmptyView, actions: = EmptyView)`; no fallback needed on iOS 18. View.redacted(reason:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6107 (iOS 14). String keys common.error, common.try_again, series.loading_seasons, series.no_seasons_info all exist in en.lproj/Localizable.strings (lines 7, 11, 248, 247).

**Regression risks:** DetailActionBar is shared with MovieDetailView, so the new parameter must default to the current behaviour. contentScroll now stays mounted through the fetch, so the DB update at 1222-1237 re-renders the hero in place (backdrop/rating/runtime appear): acceptable but should not jump the layout. ContentUnavailableView inside a ScrollView takes its ideal height; give it vertical padding. No effect on tip-jar files or on earlier performance work.

**How to verify:** Demo playlist (series endpoint returns 404): the series detail must show hero, plot and an inline retry block; compare with S04. Add two seasons with episodes to MockFixture (it has none; MockFixture.swift:172 sets seasonsLoaded false) and a UI test that asserts the title text exists before the season bar appears with the network throttled. Offline test: open a series whose seasons are cached, twice in one session, and confirm the seasons stay visible.

## series-browse-detail-2 — Switching season empties the episode list to a spinner before the new season arrives, which collapses the scroll content and can throw the page back toward the hero

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail: season selector and episode list
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:1268-1292, 1306-1351`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:443-447, 472-475`

**What the user perceives:** Tap 'Season 2' after scrolling down to the season chips: the episode rows vanish, a spinner flashes, and the page jumps because the content below the chips shrank to about 60 pt; the new rows then appear under a scroll position the user did not choose. Going back to a season already viewed shows the same flash, although all data is local.

**Mechanism (finder):** EpisodesPanel.onChange(of: seasonId) calls observer.load (1348-1350), which synchronously publishes `hasLoaded = false; episodes = []` (1278-1279) before starting a new ValueObservation. The body therefore swaps the LazyVStack for a ProgressView with 20 pt padding (1308-1311). The outer ScrollView content height drops from thousands of points to roughly the chip bar plus 60 pt; when the offset is beyond the new maximum the scroll view clamps it, and the clamp is not undone when rows return. The new value needs a reader-queue fetch plus two main-queue hops (GRDB's default async scheduling, then `.receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)` at 1282), so at least one layout pass sees the collapsed state. The chip tap also wraps the selection in withAnimation(.spring) (DetailComponents.swift:444-446), so the header count and season overview animate while the list swaps unanimated. The comment at 1268 shows the author already fought scroll resets here (an earlier `.id(seasonId)` version); the clear-then-load sequence keeps a milder form of the same problem.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the previous season's rows on screen until the new season's first value arrives, and drop the redundant hop:

private var seasonId: String?
func load(seasonId: String, db: AppDatabase) {
  guard seasonId != self.seasonId else { return }
  self.seasonId = seasonId
  cancellable?.cancel()            // do not clear `episodes` / `hasLoaded`
  cancellable = EpisodesRequest(seasonId: seasonId).publisher(in: db)
    .removeDuplicates()
    .sink { [weak self] list in self?.episodes = list; self?.hasLoaded = true }
}

hasLoaded stays false only before the very first value, so the 'no episodes' flash the comment at 1271-1273 guards against is still prevented. Keep the single EpisodesPanel identity (no `.id(seasonId)`). In DetailSeasonTabBar scope the spring to the chip itself (`.animation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.85), value: isSelected)` on the capsule) instead of wrapping the state change, so the list swap is not caught in an animated transaction. Optional: cache `[seasonId: [DBEpisode]]` in the observer so returning to a season is synchronous.

**APIs:** Combine Publisher.removeDuplicates() (iOS 13.0); View.animation(_:value:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/SeriesView.swift:1276-1287: load() cancels the subscription and synchronously publishes hasLoaded = false and episodes = [] before subscribing again; EpisodesPanel then renders only a ProgressView with 20 pt padding (1308-1311) instead of the LazyVStack. The new value cannot arrive in the same run-loop turn: EpisodesRequest uses GRDB's default scheduling (Requests.swift:243; GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487 default `.async(onQueue: .main)`) and the observer adds `.receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)` (1282), so the collapsed layout is committed at least once. The outer ScrollView (959) then holds roughly hero 380 + chips + action bar + plot + ~110 pt, and UIScrollView clamps contentOffset when contentSize shrinks below it; the offset is not restored when rows return. Anyone who has scrolled far enough to read episodes (offset beyond roughly contentHeight minus viewport) is thrown back. Returning to an already viewed season takes the same path. History: `hasLoaded = false; episodes = []` was added in 0ab5bcd (2026-07-22) solely to stop the 'no episodes in this season' text flashing while loading (comment at 1271-1273); the clear-on-switch was a side effect, not a decision. The comment at 1268 confirms an earlier `.id(seasonId)` scroll reset in the same spot. Chip tap wraps the state change in withAnimation(.spring) (DetailComponents.swift:444-446) as described. EpisodesPanel and DetailSeasonTabBar are used only here (grep), so the change is local. The exact size of the jump is the only part that needs a run; the collapse itself is certain from the code.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Every season switch, including back to a season already shown, empties the episode list to a spinner for at least one committed frame; the scroll content collapses and UIKit clamps the offset, so the page jumps toward the hero and stays there when the rows return.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: remember the current seasonId in SeasonEpisodesObserver, return early when it is unchanged, cancel and resubscribe without clearing `episodes`/`hasLoaded`, drop the redundant `.receive(on:)`, add `.removeDuplicates()`. hasLoaded then stays false only before the very first value, which keeps the guard added in 0ab5bcd. Keep the single EpisodesPanel identity (no `.id`). Optional and safe: scope the spring to the chip with `.animation(_:value: isSelected)`; the per-season cache is not needed. A further optional step is `scheduling: .immediate` for EpisodesRequest when called from this observer (indexed by idx_episode_seasonId), which makes the swap land in the same frame as the chip change; do that only together with finding 5's decision.

**API check:** Combine `Publisher.removeDuplicates()` where Output: Equatable: Combine.swiftinterface:431-433, iOS 13 (the finding had it unverified; it exists). DBEpisode is Equatable (Models/DBModels.swift:113). `View.animation(_:value:)`: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13425, iOS 13. GRDB `publisher(in:scheduling:)` default `.async(onQueue: .main)`: GRDB checkout ValueObservation.swift:485-487 (v7.10.0), so the sink is already on the main queue without `.receive(on:)`.

**Regression risks:** For a few milliseconds the previous season's rows remain tappable under the newly selected chip; negligible. A season with fewer episodes still shortens the content and may clamp, which is natural. The 'no episodes' flash guarded in 0ab5bcd stays prevented because hasLoaded is never reset. onAppear re-entry becomes a no-op thanks to the seasonId guard.

**How to verify:** Fixture series with two seasons of about 30 episodes. Simulator UI test: scroll until the season chips are near the top, tap the other season, assert the chip's frame.minY is unchanged within a few points and no progress indicator appears. With Slow Animations the current collapse and jump are visible by eye; record before and after.

## series-browse-detail-3 — An episode row is only tappable on its text column: the thumbnail does nothing, there is no pressed state, and the row is not a Button

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail: episode list
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1476`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the episode image, the most obvious play target, is ignored. Tapping the title area starts playback, but nothing highlights under the finger, so the row feels dead until the player appears. VoiceOver and the iPad pointer do not treat the row as a control.

**Mechanism (finder):** The row is an HStack of thumbnail ZStack (1391-1414), text VStack and DownloadButton. Only the text VStack carries `.contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture { onStreamSelected(...) }` (1447-1451). The thumbnail and the 12 pt gaps have no gesture. onTapGesture gives no highlight, no button trait and no hover effect.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make thumbnail plus text one Button and keep DownloadButton as a sibling so its taps do not start playback:

HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
  Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } label: {
    HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { thumbnail; textColumn }
      .contentShape(Rectangle())
  }
  .buttonStyle(EpisodeRowButtonStyle())
  downloadButton
}

struct EpisodeRowButtonStyle: ButtonStyle {
  func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
    configuration.label.opacity(configuration.isPressed ? 0.55 : 1)
  }
}

Moving `.padding(.horizontal, 16).padding(.vertical, 12)` inside the label makes the highlight and hit area cover the whole row, like a List row.

**APIs:** ButtonStyle / Configuration.isPressed (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1476: the row is an HStack of thumbnail ZStack (1391-1414), text VStack (1416-1451) and DownloadButton (1453-1472). The only play gesture is `.contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture` on the text VStack (1447-1451). CachedImage has no gesture or button of its own (grep of Views/CachedImage.swift for onTapGesture/Button/contentShape returns nothing), so the thumbnail, the 12 pt gaps and the row padding are dead. onTapGesture gives no pressed state, no button trait and no pointer interaction. No comment or history marks this as intentional (git log -S only finds the monorepo import). DownloadButton is itself a Button with .plain style and a context menu (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:77-83), so keeping it as a sibling of the new row button is correct and nesting it inside would be wrong.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Only the text column of an episode row starts playback; the thumbnail does nothing, there is no press feedback and the row is not exposed as a button.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: wrap thumbnail plus text column in one Button with a small custom ButtonStyle (opacity on isPressed), DownloadButton stays a sibling. Layout detail to get right: today the padding (16 horizontal, 12 vertical) is on the outer HStack; move leading and vertical padding inside the button label so the whole row band is the hit area, and keep 16 pt trailing padding on the download button. Extract `thumbnail` and `textColumn` as computed properties of EpisodeDetailRow. Optional for iPad: `.hoverEffect(.highlight)` on the label.

**API check:** `ButtonStyle` protocol: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10435-10439 (iOS 13, @MainActor); `ButtonStyleConfiguration.isPressed`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10450. Nothing iOS 26-only.

**Regression risks:** A Button label merges its children into one accessibility element (title, meta, plot, progress); fine, but check the VoiceOver label reads sensibly. Text keeps its explicit foreground styles, so a custom style will not tint it. Button inside the vertical ScrollView cancels correctly on drag. The larger hit area sits next to the download button; keep them separate views so a download tap never plays.

**How to verify:** UI test with fixture episodes: tap the centre of the thumbnail and assert the player overlay appears; assert the row is a button element and the download control is a separate element. Manually: press and hold shows the dimmed state, dragging away cancels, scrolling from a row does not trigger playback.

## series-browse-detail-4 — Series grids and the Series home paint an empty state before their first off-main compute returns, and the home builds up in three steps

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Series category grid, All Series, Recently Added grid, Series home
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:37-62, 220-247, 528-561, 584-588, 615-627, 634-646, 678-680, 754-791`

**What the user perceives:** Opening a category or All Series shows the 'No series found.' icon and text during the push animation, then the posters replace it. With a non-default sort on a 20k-40k catalog the wrong empty state can stay for most of a second. The first visit to the Series tab flashes the 'no category' placeholder for a frame, then the shelves appear, then 'Recently Added' and 'Continue Watching' push every shelf down.

**Mechanism (finder):** SeriesCategoryContent starts with `displayItems = []` (584) and renders the empty state whenever it is empty (636-645); nothing distinguishes 'not computed yet' from 'no results'. Data arrives in two async steps: the parent sets its own displayItems inside `.task` (546-554, 772-790), then the content view sorts in Task.detached (615-623). All three `.task(id:)` modifiers (678-680) fire on appear, so the sort and SeriesGenre.available run three times; name sorts use localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare (SeriesSortOption.swift:42-48), which is slow on large lists. On the home, displayCategories starts empty (30), so the first frame takes the placeholder branch at 53-61; recomputeFilter then publishes categories before the await and recentlyAddedSeries after it (230-245), so that shelf is inserted above already laid-out shelves.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Track readiness: `@State private var hasComputed = false`, set to true at the end of recompute(); render `Color.clear` (or the grid) until then, and the empty state only when `hasComputed && displayItems.isEmpty`.
2) Seed the first frame synchronously when no work is needed. In SeriesCategoryDetailView add an init: `_displayItems = State(initialValue: PlaylistContentStore.shared.seriesItemsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? [])` (dictionary lookup, the array is copy-on-write). In SeriesCategoryContent.init: `let isDefault = (UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: SeriesSortOption.storageKey) ?? SeriesSortOption.defaultOrder.rawValue) == SeriesSortOption.defaultOrder.rawValue; _displayItems = State(initialValue: isDefault ? items : []); _hasComputed = State(initialValue: isDefault && !items.isEmpty)`. The push then starts with posters.
3) Merge the three tasks into one id: `struct Inputs: Hashable { var token: Int; var sort: SeriesSortOption; var genres: Set<String> }` with `.task(id: Inputs(...))`.
4) Home: in recomputeFilter compute the recently-added list first and assign displayCategories, displayItemsByCategory and recentlyAddedSeries together after the await; gate the placeholder branch on a hasComputed flag.
Keeps the Equatable signature compare, the off-main sort and the 90-item pagination unchanged. VODView has the same structure (VODView.swift:616, 677-686, 737-739).

**APIs:** State(initialValue:) (iOS 13.0); View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The empty-state-before-data path is real. SeriesCategoryContent starts with `displayItems = []` (Views/SeriesView.swift:584) and renders the 'No series found.' block whenever it is empty (636-645); data arrives only after the parent's `.task` (546-554 or 772-790) and then the child's detached recompute (615-623). RecentlyAddedSeriesDetailView passes its items synchronously (345-354) and still goes through the empty state, which shows the child is the root cause. Home: displayCategories starts empty (30) so the first pass takes the placeholder branch (53-61) when the store is already loaded; recomputeFilter publishes categories before the await and recentlyAddedSeries after it (230-245), and ContinueWatchingRow is an async @Query row (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:7, 28), so both are inserted above shelves that are already laid out. The home's three `.task(id:)` (158-160) also run the recently-added sort three times on first appear. What does not hold: 'the sort and SeriesGenre.available run three times'. The three child tasks (678-680) start at first appear with the closure that captured `items == []` (the parents start with an empty @State), so those three runs are trivial; when the real items arrive only `.task(id: itemsToken)` restarts, giving one real sort. Only the 20-item Recently Added grid runs three real computes. Perception is also narrower than stated: with default sort (SeriesSortOption.apply returns the input, Models/SeriesSortOption.swift:38-40) the empty state lasts a few frames at the start of the push, when the centred block is still off-screen; it becomes clearly visible with a persisted non-default sort (@AppStorage, 580) on large lists, because localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare over 20-40k names takes hundreds of milliseconds, during which the screen wrongly says there are no series.

**Corrected claim:** Series grids render 'No series found.' until their first off-main compute returns. This is brief and mostly off-screen with the default sort, but lasts a visible fraction of a second with a persisted name/rating/recent sort on large categories and All Series. On first visit the Series home shows the 'no category' placeholder for a frame and then inserts Recently Added and Continue Watching above the shelves. The real data is sorted once today, not three times; the triple work is the home's recently-added computation and the Recently Added grid.

**Corrected fix:** Steps 1 and 2 as proposed: a hasComputed flag so the empty state shows only when computed and empty, and synchronous seeding: SeriesCategoryContent.init seeds displayItems with `items` when the stored sort is the default; SeriesCategoryDetailView seeds from PlaylistContentStore.shared.seriesItemsByCategoryId[category.id] (guard on activePlaylistId); AllSeriesView seeds from seriesItems only when no category is hidden, otherwise leaves it to the task. Step 3 (one `.task(id:)` over a Hashable Inputs struct) becomes mandatory once step 2 lands, because seeded items make all three child tasks do real work; today it is only tidy-up. Step 4: seed displayCategories/displayItemsByCategory synchronously in the home (they are plain copies of store values) rather than delaying them behind the detached sort, merge the three home tasks into one, and assign recentlyAddedSeries from a single compute. The Continue Watching insertion is not addressed by the proposal: it needs its first value on the first pass (see finding 5's immediate scheduling for RecentWatchHistoryRequest, an indexed small-table read) or an accepted one-time insert; say so explicitly. VODView.swift:556-588, 616, 677 has the same structure and should get the same treatment in the Movies lens.

**API check:** `State.init(initialValue:)`: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3717 (always-emit-into-client, usable on iOS 18). `View.task(id:priority:_:)`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166 (iOS 15). PlaylistContentStore is @MainActor (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:12-13) and seriesItemsByCategoryId is readable (32); View inits are main-actor isolated in this SDK, so the seeding compiles.

**Regression risks:** Destination inits run eagerly for every NavigationLink (shelf headers at 395, toolbar link at 116), so seeding must stay O(1): a dictionary lookup and an array retain, no filtering or sorting on the main thread. Reading UserDefaults in SeriesCategoryContent.init runs on each parent body pass; cheap, but keep it a single string read. Must keep the Equatable signature compare (570-575), the detached sort and the 90-item pagination; seeding does not touch them. After seeding, skipping step 3 would triple the real sort work.

**How to verify:** Slow Animations: push a category, All Series and Recently Added with default sort and with name sort; no frame may show the empty state while items exist. Time All Series with a 40k fixture and name sort and log recompute entry count (expect one). Record the first visit to the Series tab at 120 fps and step through frames: shelves should appear in their final positions.

## series-browse-detail-5 — The series detail renders its first frame with default values for four async database queries, so the primary button, the favourite star and the seasons block change right after the push starts

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Series detail
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:809-821, 849-864, 884-885, 967-976, 1008-1013, 1031-1040, 1106-1119`, `Models/Requests.swift:197-207, 216-227, 276-289, 507-521`

**What the user perceives:** On a series the user is watching, the button first reads 'Watch', then becomes 'Resume Where You Left Off' with a subtitle and a progress bar a moment later, growing taller and pushing the plot down. A favourited series shows an empty star that fills afterwards. For a series whose seasons are cached, the seasons area briefly shows 'No season info available.' or 'Loading seasons…' before the season bar appears.

**Mechanism (finder):** seriesRecord, seasons, isFavorite and watchHistory are GRDBQuery @Query values (809-812) whose requests use `ValueObservation.publisher(in:)` with GRDB's default `.async(onQueue: .main)` scheduling (Requests.swift:204, 224, 286, 515). The first value arrives after a reader-queue fetch and a main-queue hop, so the first body pass sees nil / [] / false / nil: hasResume is false (849-852), the star is empty (884), and seasonsSection takes the text branch (1008-1013). The initial season is resolved in a Task from `watchHistory` (1031-1040, 1106-1109), so it also depends on which query lands first; if history arrives after seasons, season 1 stays selected because selectedSeasonId is no longer nil.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use immediate scheduling for the four single-screen requests, which GRDBQuery supports on subscription (Query.swift:295-325 guards the publish-during-update case):

.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader, scheduling: .immediate)

in SeriesByIDRequest, SeasonsRequest, IsFavoriteRequest and LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest. Each is a primary-key or indexed lookup (series PK, idx_season_series_playlist, favorite PK, a small watchHistory table), well under a millisecond on the pool's reader. Do not switch WatchHistoryRequest globally: it is also instantiated per episode row (1379); give it an opt-in flag or leave it for the per-row finding. Then resolve the initial season from data that is present on the first pass, and replace the onAppear/onChange pair at 1031-1040 with one `.task(id: seasons.first?.id)`. `.immediate` must be started on the main actor; @Query.update already runs there.

**APIs:** GRDB ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with .immediate (GRDB checkout, ValueObservation.swift:485; ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real: seriesRecord, seasons, isFavorite and watchHistory are @Query values (Views/SeriesView.swift:809-812) whose requests call `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)` with GRDB's default async scheduling (Models/Requests.swift:204, 224, 286, 515), so the first body pass sees nil / [] / false / nil: 'Watch' at 968, empty star at 884, text branch at 1008-1013. What I could not confirm is that a user perceives it. The production database is a DatabasePool (Database/Persistence.swift:54) and these are primary-key or indexed lookups, so the values land one main-queue hop after the first commit, i.e. within the first one or two frames of the push while the incoming view is still at the right edge and the bar items are fading in. The seasons block also sits below the fold on iPhone. The described 'Watch then Resume' change is therefore plausible but probably sub-perceptual; only a frame-accurate recording can settle it. There is a stronger, code-level reason to do part of this that the finding did not state: the in-memory catalog row never gets seasonsLoaded updated (no reference in PlaylistContentStore), so within a session `series.seasonsLoaded` is stale and the `.task` guard at 892-896 depends on SeriesByIDRequest's async value arriving before the task body runs; if it loses, the app refetches a cached series and flashes the full-page spinner (or the error page when offline). The season-selection race (1031-1040, 1106-1109: resolveInitialSeasonId reads watchHistory at task time) is also real but narrow. API side checks out: GRDBQuery's tracker explicitly supports values published during subscription (GRDBQuery Query.swift:295-325, the isUpdating flag), and no unit test subscribes to these four requests (grep finds them only in Requests.swift, SeriesView.swift, MovieDetailView.swift).

**Corrected claim:** The series detail's first pass uses default values for four async queries. The visible effect (button title and height, star, seasons placeholder) is confined to the first frames of the push and is probably not perceptible on a DatabasePool; needs a recording to rate. The concrete defect is that the stale in-memory seasonsLoaded plus the async SeriesByIDRequest makes the decision to refetch a cached series depend on delivery order.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest safe version: pass `scheduling: .immediate` in SeriesByIDRequest and SeasonsRequest (deterministic `.task` guard, seasons bar present on the first pass), and decide on IsFavoriteRequest and LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest after measuring; both are also cheap (favorite primary key; small watchHistory table). Do not change WatchHistoryRequest (per episode row, 1379) or any catalog-sized request. Then replace the onAppear/onChange pair at 1031-1040 with one `.task(id: seasons.first?.id)`. IsFavoriteRequest is shared with MovieDetailView, which also subscribes on the main actor, so the change is compatible there. Alternative without touching scheduling: have the `.task` read seasonsLoaded from the database before fetching.

**API check:** GRDB v7.10.0 checkout: `ValueObservation.publisher(in reader: any DatabaseReader, scheduling scheduler: some ValueObservationScheduler = .async(onQueue: .main))` at GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485-487; `.immediate` (ImmediateValueObservationScheduler) at ValueObservationScheduler.swift:109-123 and 148, which preconditions Thread.isMainThread and delivers the first value synchronously; DatabasePool performs that initial fetch as a synchronous reader-pool read (ValueConcurrentObserver.swift:244, 284-306, 529-550). GRDBQuery 0.11.0 has no immediate option of its own (grep), so the scheduler must be passed in each request's publisher. `appDatabase.reader` is `any DatabaseReader` (Database/AppDatabase.swift:468), matching the signature.

**Regression risks:** `.immediate` performs synchronous reads on the main thread at first body evaluation: four sub-millisecond lookups normally, but they wait if all pool readers are busy, and on the in-memory DatabaseQueue fallback (Persistence.swift:82, 95) they queue behind any running write such as a catalog import, which would stall the push. It traps if a subscription ever starts off the main thread (only @Query uses these requests today). The removeDuplicates added for player-save churn (Requests.swift:516-518) is unaffected.

**How to verify:** Record at 120 fps the push into a favourited, partly watched series whose seasons are cached; count the frames that show 'Watch', the empty star or the seasons text and note how much of the pushed view is on screen in those frames. If it is one or two frames at the edge, treat the visual part as not worth the main-thread read. Separately, open the same series twice in one session with the network logged (and once offline): any second get_series_info request or spinner confirms the stale seasonsLoaded race, and its absence after the change confirms the fix. Run the push while a series refresh is writing to check for a main-thread stall.

## series-browse-detail-6 — Every episode row opens two database observations of its own, so watched state and download state pop in after the row is on screen and each row renders up to three times

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Series detail: episode list, long seasons
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:1318-1334, 1363, 1379, 1402-1413, 1423-1437, 1453-1471`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:27-28, 58, 285-297`, `Models/Requests.swift:375-397, 431-499`

**What the user perceives:** While scrolling a long season, rows appear plain and a beat later gain the progress bar, the 'Watched' or 'x remaining' line and the right download icon. The extra line makes the row taller after it has been laid out, so neighbouring rows shift, most visibly when scrolling back up. On a 300-500 episode season a fast fling triggers hundreds of these late updates.

**Mechanism (finder):** EpisodeDetailRow owns `@Query<WatchHistoryRequest>` (1363, 1379) and its DownloadButton owns `@Query<DownloadedItemByIDRequest>` plus `@ObservedObject DownloadManager.shared` (DownloadButton.swift:27-28). Both requests use async scheduling, so each realised row renders with nil, then again per arriving value. The watched label (1423-1437) is absent in the first pass and adds a caption line in the second. Neither observation can be narrowed by GRDB to a row (they filter on non-rowid columns), so every history save by the player and every downloadedItem write re-runs the fetch for every mounted row; DownloadedItemByIDRequest has no removeDuplicates (DownloadButton.swift:288-296), so each such write also re-renders every mounted button. The grids already solved this class of problem with one map query passed down (Requests.swift:431-437: 'Kart başına ayrı @Query açmak yerine bu kullanılır').

**Proposed fix (finder):** Same pattern as WatchProgressMapRequest: two observations per season, held by EpisodesPanel, rows receive plain values.

struct EpisodeHistoryMapRequest: Queryable, Equatable {   // [streamId: DBWatchHistory]
  let playlistId: UUID; let streamIds: [String]
  // DBWatchHistory.filter(playlistId == ? && type == "series" && streamIds.contains(Column("streamId")))
  // .removeDuplicates()
}
struct EpisodeDownloadMapRequest: Queryable, Equatable {  // [id: DBDownloadedItem]
  // DBDownloadedItem.filter(playlistId == ? && type == "episode" && seriesId == ?) + removeDuplicates()
}

Key the history map by the season's episode ids rather than by history.seriesId, since older rows may lack it. Split DownloadButton into a stateless `DownloadButtonContent(item: DBDownloadedItem?, progress: DownloadProgress?, ...)` and keep the existing DownloadButton as a thin wrapper with its @Query, so MovieDetailView is untouched. Make EpisodeDetailRow Equatable on (episode, history, download item, progress) and apply `.equatable()`, so a history tick re-renders only the playing row instead of all mounted rows (today each row holds a fresh closure and can never be skipped).

**APIs:** GRDBQuery Queryable / @Query (GRDBQuery checkout); View.equatable() (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real, but the layout-shift part is overstated and the history re-render part is already mitigated.

- **Per-row observations exist.** `EpisodeDetailRow` owns `@Query<WatchHistoryRequest>` (Views/SeriesView.swift:1363, 1379). Its `DownloadButton` owns `@Query<DownloadedItemByIDRequest>` plus `@ObservedObject DownloadManager.shared` (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:27-28, 58).
- **First value arrives after the first body.** Both publishers use GRDB's default `.async(onQueue: .main)` scheduling (GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487). GRDBQuery's Tracker sends `objectWillChange` for every value, even nil after nil (GRDBQuery Query.swift:310-321). So the row body runs twice and the button body twice.
- **Rows rarely grow.** The thumbnail is 100 x 150 pt (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:40-41) and the HStack is top-aligned. By my estimate at default text size the text column is about 128 pt without the watched label and about 150 pt with it. The row gets taller only when the title wraps and the plot fills five lines. What usually happens is that the label appears a frame or two late and pushes the plot down inside the row.
- **History re-renders are already handled.** `WatchHistoryRequest` has `.removeDuplicates()` with a comment naming exactly this case (Models/Requests.swift:390-393, added in 2ec2c18). What remains is the cost: one fetch per mounted row per history save, each a full scan because `watchHistory` has no `streamId` index (Database/AppDatabase.swift:159-173).
- **Download lookups are cheap.** `downloadedItem.id` is the text primary key, so each fetch is an index lookup. Writes to that table are rare. The real invalidation source is `@Published progress` and `dbVersion` on the manager, throttled to whole percents (Models/DownloadManager.swift:56-59).
- **Rows cannot be skipped.** Each row gets a fresh closure (SeriesView.swift:1326-1328) and is not Equatable, so every `EpisodesPanel` body re-evaluates all realised rows.

The series detail screenshots (S03, S04) show only the HTTP 404 error state, so there is no visual evidence for episode rows.

**Corrected claim:** Each realised episode row starts its own asynchronous history observation, and its download button starts another. The watched or remaining label and progress bar therefore appear one or two frames after the row, pushing the plot text down inside it. The row itself only grows when the title wraps and the plot is five lines, because the 150 pt thumbnail normally sets the height. Other history writes no longer re-render rows, but each still triggers a full-scan fetch per mounted row. Severity is low; the visible part needs a device check.

**Corrected fix:** Do the history half first; it removes the pop-in.

1. **Load the season's history with the episodes.** Extend `SeasonEpisodesObserver` (SeriesView.swift:1269-1292) with a second `ValueObservation` on `DBWatchHistory` filtered by `playlistId`, `type == "series"` and `ids.contains(Column("streamId"))`, with `.removeDuplicates()`. Combine it with the episodes publisher and set `hasLoaded` only once both have emitted, so the first row render already has its history. Pass `history: DBWatchHistory?` into `EpisodeDetailRow` and drop its `@Query`.
2. **Do not use `Query(request, in:)` in `EpisodesPanel` for this.** The panel deliberately survives season changes (comment at 1268), and an `.initial` request is frozen after the first update (GRDBQuery Query.swift:266-268). If `@Query` is preferred, it must be `Query(constant:in:)`.
3. **Optional second step.** Make `EpisodeDetailRow` Equatable on episode, history, seriesName and seriesCover, and apply `.equatable()`. Only then is it worth lifting the download item and progress into the panel through a stateless `DownloadButtonContent`, keeping `DownloadButton` as a wrapper so `MovieDetailView` is untouched.

Adding `removeDuplicates` to `DownloadedItemByIDRequest` alone gains nothing, because the manager's published properties invalidate the buttons anyway.

**API check:** - GRDBQuery checkout: `Query.init(_:in:)` is the `.initial` configuration; `Query.init(constant:in:)` exists (Query.swift:112-117).
- GRDB: `ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:)` defaults to `.async(onQueue: .main)` (ValueObservation.swift:485-487).
- SwiftUI.swiftinterface:16312: `func equatable() -> EquatableView<Self>`, iOS 13.0.
- No iOS 26 API involved, so no fallback is needed.

**Regression risks:** - The season panel deliberately keeps one view across season changes to preserve scroll position (1268); a frozen `@Query` request would show the previous season's history.
- An Equatable row whose `==` omits a field it draws (seriesName, seriesCover, posterMetrics-driven sizes) would go stale.
- The tap closure must keep passing the row's current history to `onStreamSelected`.
- `MovieDetailView` and `M3UDownloadMenuItems` use the same download request and must keep working.

**How to verify:** - Device or simulator slow-motion recording of a season with watched episodes, scrolling up: count frames between a row appearing and its watched label appearing, before and after.
- Instruments SwiftUI template on a long season: `EpisodeDetailRow` body count per realised row (2 today, expect 1).
- With an episode playing in the mini player: body count per history save (expect only the playing row).
- Unit test for the season history map: keys are episode stream ids, and an unrelated history write emits no new value.

## series-browse-detail-7 — The Watch / Resume button looks up its episode only after the tap, can silently do nothing, starts with 'Specials' when a season 0 exists, and resumes a finished episode in its last seconds

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail: primary action, Series detail: auto-selected season
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:849-864, 967-976, 899-908, 1070-1099, 1106-1119, 1167-1174`, `Models/XtreamModels.swift:298-313`, `Models/SeriesPlaybackOrdering.swift:44-65`, `Database/AppDatabase.swift:337-350`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should the button advance to the next episode once the last-watched one is finished ('Up Next', as Apple TV does), or keep resuming the same episode? Should a season 0 ('Specials') ever be the default season?

**What the user perceives:** The button says only 'Watch' or 'Resume Where You Left Off', never which episode. On some panels tapping 'Watch' does nothing at all. When the panel has a season 0, 'Watch' plays a special and the Specials tab is preselected. After finishing episode 5, 'Resume' reopens episode 5 a few seconds before its end instead of offering episode 6.

**Mechanism (finder):** resumeLatestEpisode and playFirstEpisode start a Task, read the episode from the database, then presentEpisodeOverlay starts a second Task for DownloadManager.localURL (899-908) before presenting: two async hops with no acknowledgement, and a quick double tap presents twice. The resume lookup `episodeId == ? OR id == ?` (1074) cannot use an index (only seasonId is indexed, AppDatabase.swift:344-348), so it scans the episode table. Silent no-ops: playFirstEpisode returns when seasons is empty (1086) and when the first season has no episode rows (1087-1092); resolvedSeasons keeps seasons the panel declares even without episodes (XtreamModels.swift:302-306). `seasons.first` is the lowest seasonNumber (Requests.swift:221), so season 0 wins both here and in resolveInitialSeasonId (1108, 1118). hasResume only tests lastTimeMs > 5000 (849-852) and resumeLatestEpisode passes the raw history (1077-1078); the comment at 1167-1170 and ios-player-airplay-review.md:1594 record that the finished-episode case for this button was left open ('resolve the next episode there or leave them unchanged').

**Proposed fix (finder):** Resolve the target once, ahead of the tap, and let the button describe it:

@State private var primaryTarget: PrimaryTarget?   // episode, history?, isResume, seasonNumber
.task(id: PrimaryKey(history: watchHistory?.id, position: watchHistory?.lastTimeMs ?? 0 > 0, seasons: seasons.map(\.id))) {
  primaryTarget = try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in
    if let h = history, let ep = try episode(for: h.streamId, db) {
      if h.resumePositionMs(as: .episode) != nil { return .resume(ep, h) }
      if let next = try SeriesPlaybackOrdering.navigationContext(playlistId:…, playbackStreamId: h.streamId, seriesIdHint:…, db: db).next { return .play(next) }
      return .play(ep)            // last episode finished: start it over
    }
    // first episode of the first season with seasonNumber >= 1 that has rows, else any season
  }
}

Button title 'Resume S2 · E5' / 'Play S2 · E6' with the existing time subtitle; `.disabled(primaryTarget == nil)`. The tap then calls presentEpisodeOverlay directly. Use the same 'first season >= 1 with episodes' rule in resolveInitialSeasonId. New string keys are appended to the ten Localizable.strings files without touching the tip keys.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0); View.disabled(_:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The silent no-op and the season 0 default are real bugs; three sub-claims are overstated and the proposed task key has a staleness bug.

**Confirmed**
- **Silent no-op.** `playFirstEpisode` reads only `seasons.first` and returns silently when that season has no episode rows (Views/SeriesView.swift:1084-1099). `resolvedSeasons` keeps every declared season even with no episode bucket (Models/XtreamModels.swift:298-313); its own comment and XtreamSeriesInfoTests say panels routinely list season 1 while keying episodes under "2".
- **Season 0 and empty seasons win.** `SeasonsRequest` orders by `seasonNumber` (Models/Requests.swift:221) and `resolveInitialSeasonId` uses `seasons.first` (1108, 1118). The screen then opens on "No episodes in this season."
- **Finished episode resumes at its end.** `hasResume` tests only `lastTimeMs > 5000` (849-852) and `resumeLatestEpisode` passes the raw history (1077-1078). PlayerView has no upper bound (Views/PlayerView.swift:1598, 1631-1634). The comment at 1167-1170 and ios-player-airplay-review.md record this as deliberately left open, so it is a product decision.

**Overstated**
- **"Never says which episode."** The Resume state shows the history title and time in the subtitle (860-864). Only "Watch" is unlabelled.
- **Double tap.** `PlayerOverlayController.present` replaces the presentation (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:42-55), and `loadEpisodeNeighbors` already re-presents on purpose (1138-1143). It is harmless.
- **Episode table scan.** The `episodeId == ? OR id == ?` lookup does scan, but the table only holds episodes of series the user has opened, and it runs off the main thread.

**Fix defect**
- The proposed task key (history id, position > 0, season ids) does not change as the position advances. A stored history snapshot would resume from the position captured when the detail opened.

**Also found**
- When the latest history is 5 s or less, the button says "Watch" and plays the first episode of the series, not that episode.
- The lookup at 1074 is not scoped to the playlist, so an episode with the same panel id from another playlist can match.

**Corrected claim:** "Watch" does nothing, with no feedback, when the first season by number has no episode rows (declared-only seasons, typically a season 0 or an out-of-sync season 1), and the same rule preselects that empty season. "Resume" on a finished episode replays its last seconds; that was deliberately left open and is a product decision. The Resume state already names the episode by title; only the Watch state gives no hint. The two async hops and the double-tap concern are negligible.

**Corrected fix:** **Step 1 (small, no new strings).** Use one rule in both `playFirstEpisode` and `resolveInitialSeasonId`: the first episode, in (seasonNumber, episodeNum) order, of the first season that has episode rows, preferring seasonNumber >= 1 and falling back to season 0.
- Run it in a single `AppDatabase.shared.read` that joins episode to season on `season.seriesId` and `season.playlistId`.
- Test for rows with EXISTS; `DBSeason.episodeCount` keeps the panel's count for empty seasons (1197), so it cannot be used.
- Scope the resume lookup at 1074 and 1113 to this playlist's seasons.

**Step 2 (owner decision).** If "Up Next" is wanted: when `watchHistory.resumePositionMs(as: .episode) == nil`, play `SeriesPlaybackOrdering.navigationContext(...).next`, or restart the episode when there is none.
- Resolve only the target episode ahead of the tap.
- Key the task on `watchHistory?.streamId`, the finished flag (`resumePositionMs(as: .episode) != nil`) and the season ids.
- Read the resume position from the live `watchHistory` at tap time; never store a history snapshot.

**Step 3 (optional).** Add `var isPrimaryEnabled: Bool = true` to `DetailActionBar` and disable the button while no target is resolved. A season and episode label needs new keys in the ten Localizable.strings files; append only, leaving the tip keys alone. Without new keys, the existing subtitle slot can carry the episode title.

**API check:** - SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166: `func task<T>(id value: T, priority:_:) where T: Equatable`; iOS 15.0 is from the finding, the attribute line was not captured in my grep.
- SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:190: `func disabled(_ disabled: Bool) -> some View`; iOS 13.0 is likewise from the finding.
- App code used by the fix: `WatchResume.positionMs` / `DBWatchHistory.resumePositionMs(as:)` (Models/WatchResume.swift:27-47) and `SeriesPlaybackOrdering.navigationContext` (Models/SeriesPlaybackOrdering.swift:45-65).
- No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** - `DetailActionBar` is shared with `MovieDetailView`; any new parameter must default to today's behaviour.
- Preferring season >= 1 changes the default tab for series whose only populated season is 0, so the fallback is required.
- Advancing to the next episode changes behaviour the last player pass deliberately kept (comment at 1167-1170); it needs the owner's go-ahead.
- A stored history snapshot would resume at a stale position.
- Appending strings touches files that hold the uncommitted tip keys; the edit must be append-only.

**How to verify:** Unit tests on the resolver with an in-memory database:
- season 1 declared with no rows and season 2 populated gives S2E1;
- seasons 0 and 1 both populated gives S1E1;
- only season 0 populated gives S0E1;
- no rows gives nil;
- a duplicate `episodeId` in another playlist is not matched.

If step 2 is taken: history at 97 % with a next episode gives the next one; last episode finished restarts it. Open the detail, play ten minutes, close, tap Resume, and confirm it resumes at the new position.

UI test with a fixture series whose first declared season is empty: the preselected season shows episodes and Watch presents the player.

## series-browse-detail-8 — The compact download button in episode rows has a roughly 30 x 28 pt hit area, hides cancel and delete behind a long press, and changes width when a download starts

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail: episode list
- Code: `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:77-83, 101-143, 145-202`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1453-1471`

**What the user perceives:** The download icon is easy to miss with a thumb, and a miss lands on nothing. While an episode downloads, tapping the indicator does nothing; cancelling or deleting needs a long press that nothing hints at. When a download starts, the button grows into a pill with a spinner and '45%' text, which narrows the text column and re-wraps the episode plot.

**Mechanism (finder):** Compact layout uses a footnote glyph with 8 pt horizontal and 6 pt vertical padding (DownloadButton.swift:102-114) and no minimum frame. primaryAction ignores taps in .queued, .downloading and .completed (195-201); the only route to cancel or delete is `.contextMenu` (82, 152-163). downloadingLabel adds a Text beside the progress view (125-134), so the button's width differs between states inside the row's HStack (SeriesView.swift:1390), whose text column is `maxWidth: .infinity`.

**Proposed fix (finder):** For `compact`, use a fixed 44 x 44 slot and make non-idle states a menu on tap, as Apple TV, Music and Podcasts do:

Group {
  switch state {
  case .idle, .failed: Button(action: primaryAction) { glyph }
  default: Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { glyph }
  }
}
.frame(width: 44, height: 44).contentShape(Rectangle())

Downloading glyph: a 22 pt ring, `Circle().trim(from: 0, to: p).stroke(Color.accentColor, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2.5, lineCap: .round)).rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))` over a faint full circle with `Image(systemName: "stop.fill")` inside, no percentage text. Keep `.contextMenu` for long press. The full-width variant on MovieDetailView is unchanged.

**APIs:** Menu(content:label:) (iOS 14.0); Shape.trim(from:to:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The three problems are real; the fix as written would not enlarge the tap target.

- **Small target.** The compact label is a footnote-weight glyph with 8 pt horizontal and 6 pt vertical padding and no minimum frame (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:101-114), roughly 32 x 28 pt.
- **Taps ignored outside idle and failed.** `primaryAction` does nothing in queued, downloading and completed (195-201). The comments say this is deliberate and the code dates from the first commit (d2489f9). Cancel and delete are reachable only through `.contextMenu` (82, 152-163).
- **Width changes.** `downloadingLabel` adds a spinner and a percentage text even in compact mode (125-134). The string is short ("%d%%" in English, "%%%d" in Turkish), so the button grows by roughly 25-35 pt (my estimate). That narrows the `maxWidth: .infinity` text column (Views/SeriesView.swift:1447) and can re-wrap the title and plot.
- **A miss is worse than described.** A tap just left of the button lands on the text column's `onTapGesture` (1448-1451) and starts playback. Only the area below the button is dead.
- **Scope.** `compact: true` is used only at SeriesView.swift:1470; `MovieDetailView` uses the full-width variant.
- **Fix defect.** A `.frame(width: 44, height: 44).contentShape(Rectangle())` placed outside the `Button` or `Menu` adds empty space around the control; I expect the hit region to stay the label's own frame. The frame and content shape must go inside the label.

**Corrected claim:** The compact download button is about 32 x 28 pt. A near miss to the left starts playback of the episode. Cancel and delete are reachable only by long press, by an explicit earlier design choice. The button grows by about 25-35 pt when a download starts, which narrows the text column and can re-wrap the row.

**Corrected fix:** Compact variant only.

- **Fixed 44 x 44 slot, sized inside the label.** `Button(action: primaryAction) { glyph.frame(width: 44, height: 44).contentShape(Rectangle()) }` for idle and failed. `Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { glyph.frame(width: 44, height: 44).contentShape(Rectangle()) }` for queued, downloading and completed.
- **Keep the visible pill at its current size** inside the slot. Absorb the extra 12 pt of width by cutting the HStack spacing or adding `.padding(.trailing, -6)`, so the text column keeps its width.
- **Fixed-size downloading glyph, no percentage text.** A ring from `Circle().trim(from: 0, to: p).stroke(Color.accentColor, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2.5, lineCap: .round)).rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))` over a faint full circle, with `stop.fill` inside.
- **Keep `.contextMenu`** for long press.
- **Accessibility.** Add `.accessibilityLabel` and `.accessibilityValue` with the percentage, since the visible text goes away.
- **Update the two comments** at 196-199 so they no longer say taps are ignored.

Tap-to-menu changes a deliberate behaviour, so mention it to the owner.

**API check:** - SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7118: `struct Menu<Label, Content>`, iOS 14.0; its `init(content:label:)` sits in an `extension SwiftUI.Menu` marked iOS 14.0.
- SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:5716: `Shape.trim(from:to:)`, iOS 13.0.
- SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13251: `View.contentShape(_:eoFill:)` exists; availability not captured in my grep.
- No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** - `DownloadButton` is shared with `MovieDetailView`; every change must sit behind `compact`.
- A `Menu` label picks up the accent tint unless the glyph sets its own foreground style.
- Dropping the percentage text removes information VoiceOver users currently get, hence the accessibility value.
- A wider slot without the spacing compensation would narrow the text column for every row.

**How to verify:** - UI test: the episode download control's frame is at least 44 x 44.
- UI test: tapping it while downloading shows Cancel; while completed shows Delete.
- UI test: tapping 6 pt left of the visible pill does not start playback.
- Screenshot comparison of one row in idle, queued, downloading and completed: title and plot wrap identically.

## series-browse-detail-9 — Season selection is a custom horizontally scrolling chip bar under a separate 'Seasons' header, which is redundant with one season and hard to scan with twenty

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail: season selector
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:433-478`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1015-1040`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Replace the chips with a system menu for every multi-season series, only above a threshold (for example more than 6 seasons), or keep the chips and only fix the single-season case?

**What the user perceives:** A one-season series still shows a 'Seasons' title and a lone 'Season 1' chip. With 15-20 seasons the user scrolls a strip sideways to find a season and cannot see the full list at once. Apple TV shows 'Season 3' with a chevron that opens a system menu, and plain text when there is only one season.

**Mechanism (finder):** DetailSeasonTabBar builds one capsule Button per season in a horizontal ScrollView (DetailComponents.swift:439-471) and is always shown when seasons is non-empty (SeriesView.swift:1030), below a fixed header (1016-1028). There is no branch for seasons.count == 1 and no compact alternative for long lists.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Merge header and selector into one row:

HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline) {
  if seasons.count > 1 {
    Menu {
      Picker(L("series.seasons"), selection: $selectedSeasonId) {
        ForEach(seasons) { s in Text(s.name ?? L("series.season_format", s.seasonNumber)).tag(Optional(s.id)) }
      }
    } label: {
      HStack(spacing: 4) {
        Text(currentSeasonTitle).font(.title3.weight(.bold))
        Image(systemName: "chevron.up.chevron.down").font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))
      }
    }
  } else { Text(currentSeasonTitle).font(.title3.weight(.bold)) }
  Spacer()
  episodeCountLabel
}

The menu scrolls natively with 20 seasons, shows the checkmark, and gives VoiceOver the selected state for free. All APIs predate iOS 18, so no fallback. A middle path keeps the chips for 2-6 seasons and uses the menu above that.

**APIs:** Menu(content:label:) (iOS 14.0); Picker inside Menu (MenuPickerStyle) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The code matches the description, and the finding correctly frames it as an owner decision.

- `DetailSeasonTabBar` builds one capsule button per season in a horizontal ScrollView (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:433-478).
- It is shown whenever `seasons` is non-empty, under a fixed "Seasons" header (Views/SeriesView.swift:1016-1030). There is no branch for a single season.
- The chips carry no selected trait, so VoiceOver cannot tell which season is active.
- The bar has been there since the first commit (d2489f9) and no comment marks it as a deliberate performance or design choice.
- The proposed code compiles in this structure: `selectedSeasonId` is `String?` and the tags are `Optional(s.id)`.
- No visual check was possible: the series detail screenshots (S03, S04) show only the HTTP 404 error state.

I rate it low: the chip bar works, and this is polish.

**Corrected claim:** Season selection is a custom chip strip under a fixed "Seasons" header. It is redundant for a single season, needs sideways scrolling for long lists, and exposes no selected state to VoiceOver. Replacing it with a system menu is a design decision for the owner.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two details:
- Give the Menu label `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` (or `.tint(.primary)`) so the title3 heading is not drawn in the accent colour.
- Keep the existing `onAppear` and `onChange(of: seasons)` season resolution (1031-1040) on the new row.

If the owner keeps the chips, the minimum is to hide the bar when `seasons.count == 1` and add `.accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])` to each chip.

**API check:** - SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7118: `struct Menu<Label, Content>`, iOS 14.0, with `init(content:label:)` in an iOS 14.0 extension.
- SwiftUI.swiftinterface:14063: `struct Picker<Label, SelectionValue, Content>`, iOS 13.0.
- SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23918: `struct MenuPickerStyle`, iOS 14.0.
- All predate iOS 18, so no fallback is needed.

**Regression risks:** - The initial-season resolution is attached to the tab bar's `onAppear` and `onChange` (1031-1040); removing the bar without moving them leaves `selectedSeasonId` nil and no episodes shown.
- `DetailSeasonTabBar` wraps selection in a spring animation; a Picker binding changes without one, which is acceptable.
- Panel season names can be long; the menu label needs `lineLimit(1)`.

**How to verify:** - Fixture series with 1, 5 and 20 seasons: screenshot the seasons row for each.
- UI test: pick a season through the menu, then assert the episode count label and episode list change.
- UI test: the initially selected season is still the last-watched one.
