## image-pipeline-5 — LazyImage throws away and reloads its image on every onAppear and has no working way to lower priority off-screen, so tiles can blink back to gray after backgrounding and off-screen cells compete equally with visible ones

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Category grids, All Movies / All Channels, Home shelves, Favorites, EPG guide, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:62-94`

**What the user perceives:** Return to the app after using another one, open a movie and go back (or switch tab and back): posters that were on screen turn gray and pop in again. During a fast scroll the tiles the user stops on wait behind requests for tiles that already left the screen. The detail hero waits behind a grid that is still loading.

**Mechanism (finder):** - NukeUI's LazyImage calls `viewModel.load(request)` on every onAppear (NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:165-171). `FetchImage.load` begins with `reset()`, which cancels the task and clears the displayed image (FetchImage.swift:103-106, 240-249), then looks in the memory cache.
- While the entry is in memory this is invisible. After the cache was trimmed to 10 % on backgrounding (Nuke/Caching/Cache.swift:150-160), cleared on memory pressure (Cache.swift:49-53) or evicted, a visible image is replaced by the placeholder and fetched again.
- For .shelf, .grid and .high the app passes `.onDisappear(nil)` (CachedImage.swift:80), so off-screen requests keep .normal priority until SwiftUI destroys the cell. `.high` never cancels either.
- The comment at CachedImage.swift:75-79 is right about `.lowerPriority`, and the cause is visible in the source: LazyImage sets `viewModel.priority = .veryLow` on disappear (LazyImage.swift:173-181) and nothing sets it back; `load()` then applies that stored priority to every later request (FetchImage.swift:116-118).
- All requests are created with the default .normal priority (CachedImage.swift:111-122), including the hero.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace LazyImage inside CachedImage with a thin view over NukeUI.FetchImage (same public init, so no call site changes; about 50 lines in CachedImage.swift):
```swift
@StateObject private var model = FetchImage()
...
.onAppear {
  model.transaction = Transaction(animation: .easeOut(duration: 0.18))
  model.priority = (loadProfile == .standard || loadProfile == .high) ? .high : .normal  // also raises a running task
  guard model.imageContainer == nil, !model.isLoading else { return }   // keep what is already shown
  model.load(url.map(makeRequest))
}
.onDisappear {
  if loadProfile == .standard || loadProfile == .high { model.cancel() } else { model.priority = .low }
}
.onChange(of: requestKey) { _, _ in model.load(url.map(makeRequest)) }   // requestKey: url + size + mode + profile
```
`FetchImage.priority`'s didSet updates the running ImageTask (FetchImage.swift:67-69), so priority drops when a cell leaves and comes back when it returns, without the stuck state. A failed load is retried on the next appear, as today.
If this refactor is not wanted now, one line still helps: pass `priority: .high` in `CachedImage.request` for .standard and .high so detail images jump the grid backlog. Priority is not part of the memory-cache key (Nuke/Internal/ImageRequestKeys.swift:8-32), so prefetch matching is unaffected.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** NukeUI.FetchImage (init, load(_: ImageRequest?), priority, transaction, imageContainer, isLoading, cancel()) (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, NukeUI/FetchImage.swift:11-250); ImageRequest.init(url:processors:priority:options:userInfo:) / ImageRequest.Priority.high (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, Nuke/ImageRequest.swift:156-171, 287-293); ImageTask.priority (settable while running) (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, Nuke/ImageTask.swift:27-30, 186-197)

**Verifier reasons:** The source-level mechanisms are confirmed. LazyImage calls `viewModel.load(context?.request)` on every onAppear (NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:165-171); `FetchImage.load` starts with `reset()`, which cancels the task and clears `imageContainer` (FetchImage.swift:103-106, 240-249) before the memory lookup (120-129). With the entry in memory this is invisible; after the background trim to 15 MB / 150 entries (Nuke/Caching/Cache.swift:150-160, about 50 grid posters at 2x), a memory warning (Cache.swift:49-53) or eviction, a displayed image is replaced by the placeholder and loaded again. The stuck-priority explanation matches the app's comment at CachedImage.swift:75-79: LazyImage sets `viewModel.priority = .veryLow` on disappear (LazyImage.swift:173-181), nothing restores it, and `load` applies it to every later request (FetchImage.swift:116-118). Grid and shelf profiles pass `.onDisappear(nil)` (CachedImage.swift:80) and every request is .normal (111-122), including the hero. Limits of the claim: returning from background alone does not re-fire onAppear, so tiles blink only when backgrounding (or memory pressure, or eviction by large prefetches) is followed by a pop or tab switch; how often SwiftUI re-fires onAppear for lazy-grid cells there, and how long off-screen cells stay alive during a fling, was not observed (the finding itself marks this as needing a simulator run). The 'no cancel' behaviour for .shelf/.grid/.high is deliberate (profile docs at CachedImage.swift:41-51, comment 75-79); the proposal keeps it for shelf and grid but silently changes .high to cancel. The proposed code has a real bug: after `model.cancel()` FetchImage never clears `isLoading` (FetchImage.swift:229-236) and the closure API delivers no completion after a cancel (Nuke/Pipeline/Deprecated.swift:62-64), so the guard `guard model.imageContainer == nil, !model.isLoading else { return }` returns forever on the next appear and the image never loads for any profile that cancels (detail poster, history cards, the hero under the proposal).

**Corrected claim:** LazyImage clears and reloads its image on every onAppear. When the memory cache no longer holds the entry (trimmed to about 50 posters on backgrounding, emptied on memory warning, or evicted), tiles that were already on screen turn gray and load again after a pop or a tab switch. Off-screen cells of the grid and shelf profiles keep their requests at the same priority as visible ones for as long as SwiftUI keeps the cell alive, and LazyImage's own lowerPriority option cannot be used because the lowered priority is never restored. How often this is visible depends on SwiftUI's onAppear and cell-lifetime behaviour and needs a simulator run.

**Corrected fix:** Replace LazyImage inside CachedImage with a thin view over `@StateObject private var model = FetchImage()` (same public init, no call-site changes), with the guard corrected: onAppear sets `model.transaction` and `model.priority` (.high for .standard and .high, .normal otherwise; the didSet also re-raises a running task), then `guard model.imageContainer == nil else { return }`; for the non-cancelling profiles additionally `if model.isLoading { return }`; otherwise `model.load(makeRequest(url:))`. Never rely on `isLoading` after a cancel. onDisappear: `.standard` cancels as today; `.shelf` and `.grid` set `model.priority = .low`; keep `.high` non-cancelling as today (lower its priority) unless the owner wants the change. Reload on `.onChange(of: requestKey)` with an Equatable key of url, width, height, contentMode and loadProfile (ImageRequest itself is not Equatable). Keep the existing `if let url` branch so a nil URL shows the placeholder without a load. If the refactor is not wanted now, the one-line step stands on its own: pass `priority: .high` in `CachedImage.request` for .standard and .high so detail images are served before the grid backlog; the prefetcher overrides priority and priority is not part of the cache or task keys. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, NukeUI/FetchImage.swift: `@MainActor public final class FetchImage: ObservableObject` (10-11), `public init()` (93), `public func load(_ request: ImageRequest?)` (103), `public var priority: ImageRequest.Priority? { didSet { priority.map { imageTask?.priority = $0 } } }` (67-69), `public var transaction` (37), `@Published public private(set) var imageContainer` (29), `@Published public private(set) var isLoading` (32; not reset by `cancel()`, 229-236), `public func cancel()` (229), `public func reset()` (240). `ImageRequest.init(url:processors:priority:options:userInfo:)` (Nuke/ImageRequest.swift:156-162), `enum Priority { veryLow, low, normal, high, veryHigh }` (287-288). `ImageTask.priority` is settable while running (ImageTask.swift:29-32, 188-198). Memory and task keys exclude priority (Internal/ImageRequestKeys.swift:8-57). SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827 has `View.onChange(of:initial:_:)` with the two-parameter action, available from iOS 17 (below the iOS 18 target).

**Regression risks:** With the guard as originally written, images never load after a cancel and re-appear. Keeping the displayed image across onAppear means a cell reused for another item must reload through the request-key onChange; a wrong key shows a stale poster. Each alive cell keeps holding its decoded image, as today. Changing .high to cancel alters a documented profile behaviour. The wrapper replaces LazyImage's `onChange(of: context)`; the comparison must still include the Resize size or rotation and iPad resizing will keep an image decoded for the old size. The wrapper must keep using `CachedImage.request` so prefetch and render keys stay equal (0ab5bcd).

**How to verify:** Simulator: open All Movies, background the app and return, push a detail and pop, then switch tab and back; before the change count tiles that turn gray, after it none may. Repeat after Debug > Simulate Memory Warning. Log onAppear/onDisappear of CachedImage cells during a pop, a tab switch and a fling to learn how often onAppear re-fires and how long off-screen cells live. Unit test for the wrapper with `ImagePipeline.Delegate.imageTaskCreated` as a counter: appear, disappear, appear on a .grid image creates exactly one ImageTask; on a .standard image that was cancelled mid-load the second appear creates a new task and the image arrives. With signposts enabled, confirm on a fling that requests of cells that left the screen drop to low priority and visible ones are served first.

## image-pipeline-6 — Opening a detail screen re-downloads and re-decodes the poster the user just tapped at two new sizes, showing a gray block with a large glyph first; the blurred fallback backdrop decodes the poster at full hero size at 3x only to blur it

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:26-32, 47-72, 103-110`, `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:109-123, 138-147`, `another-iptv-player/Views/PosterMetrics.swift:34-35`

**What the user perceives:** Tap a poster that is fully loaded in the grid: on the detail screen the small poster and the whole 380 pt header start as gray placeholders (the header with a film glyph about 100 pt tall), then the images cut in. On iPad, rotating the detail screen flashes the header gray again.

**Mechanism (finder):** - Nuke's memory key includes the resize target (Nuke/Internal/ImageRequestKeys.swift:8-32).
- On iPhone the grid and shelf decode the poster at 200x300 px (PosterMetrics.swift:16-20, layoutScale 0.5, 2x cap).
- The hero poster asks for 118x176 px (DetailComponents.swift:103-110): a different key, so a miss.
- The backdrop asks for width x 380 pt at up to 3x, about 1206x1140 px, with .high (DetailComponents.swift:51-59): another miss.
- When there is no backdropPath, the poster URL is used at that hero size and then blurred with radius 28 at 55 % opacity (DetailComponents.swift:26-32, 61-62). Screenshots iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png and iphone-dark/M07-movie-detail.png show the result is a soft colour wash for which a 200x300 source would be enough.
- The backdrop decode size follows the live GeometryReader width (line 53), so each width change is a new request, which makes LazyImage reset to the placeholder (NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:151-153).
- .high gets no fade (CachedImage.swift:87-93).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Let CachedImage decode at a size independent of its display frame: add optional `decodeWidth` / `decodeHeight` parameters that default to width / height and feed them to `CachedImage.request`.
In DetailHero:
1. Poster: `decodeWidth: metrics.categoryGridPosterWidth, decodeHeight: metrics.categoryGridPosterHeight`. With .fill this is the same key as VODStreamCard / SeriesCard in shelves and grids, so it is a synchronous memory hit, and it is also sharper than today's 118 px.
2. Backdrop: always draw the grid-size poster, blurred, as an instant underlay (memory hit, no placeholder glyph). When a real backdropURL exists, put it on top and let it fade in.
3. Give the real backdrop a decode size that does not follow the live width, for example the longer window side in pixels capped at 2048, so rotation does not reload it.
4. Optional: pre-blur the underlay once with `ImageProcessors.GaussianBlur(radius:)` instead of a live `.blur(radius: 28)` that sits under the per-frame `.visualEffect` parallax.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** ImageProcessors.Resize(size:unit:contentMode:crop:upscale:) (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, Nuke/Processing/ImageProcessors+Resize.swift:32 (already used)); ImageProcessors.GaussianBlur(radius:) (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, Nuke/Processing/ImageProcessors+GaussianBlur.swift:21-27)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real, but three details need correcting.

What holds:
- The hero poster is a different cache key from the card the user tapped. It is built at `seriesDetailHeroWidth` x `seriesDetailHeroHeight` with `.fill` and the `.standard` profile (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:103-110), which is 59x88 pt = 118x176 px on iPhone. Cards use 100x150 pt = 200x300 px (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:16-20, Views/VODView.swift:503-509).
- Nuke's memory key compares processors, and the Resize identifier contains the size (Nuke/Internal/ImageRequestKeys.swift:8-32, Nuke/Processing/ImageProcessors+Resize.swift:65).
- The backdrop request follows the live `GeometryReader` width (DetailComponents.swift:50-59). A width change gives a new Resize size, so `LazyImageContext` differs (it compares processors), `.onChange(of: context)` calls `viewModel.load`, and `FetchImage.load` starts with `reset()` (NukeUI/LazyImage.swift body; NukeUI/FetchImage.swift:103-128). The view goes back to the placeholder.
- The placeholder is a systemGray6 block with a glyph of `min(w,h) * 0.28`, about 106 pt for the 380 pt hero (Views/CachedImage.swift:138-147).
- Non-`.standard` profiles get no animation (CachedImage.swift:87-93), so the backdrop cuts in.
- `FetchImage.load` does a synchronous memory lookup, so equal keys would give a first-frame hit.
- No comment or history marks any of this as deliberate: `git log -S'backdropIsFallback'` shows only the import commit d2489f9.

Corrections:
1. "Decodes the poster at about 1206x1140" is overstated. Resize runs with `upscale: false` (CachedImage.swift:114-120), so a typical 600x900 poster is kept at source size (about 2.1 MB). Only larger originals reach about 1206x1809 px (about 8.7 MB for a 2000x3000 source).
2. The hero is not what the user sees for most of a first open. Both detail views swap in a full-screen `ProgressView` while metadata loads (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:74-76, Views/SeriesView.swift:868-870; `isLoading` starts false, so the hero mounts for a frame, is replaced, then remounts). The gray placeholders show on that first frame and again when the hero comes back.
3. Step 4 of the fix works against step 2. Adding `GaussianBlur` makes a new key. Nuke reuses the cached Resize result as an intermediate (Nuke/Tasks/TaskLoadImage.swift:56) but applies the blur asynchronously on the processing queue, so the underlay is no longer a first-frame hit.

Screenshot iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png confirms the fallback renders as a soft colour wash. No iPad detail screenshot exists yet, so the rotation flash is from code only.

**Corrected claim:** Opening a detail screen requests the tapped poster again under two new cache keys, 118x176 px for the hero poster and width x 380 pt at up to 3x for the backdrop. Both miss the memory cache, so each shows a gray placeholder (the backdrop with a glyph of about 106 pt) before the image arrives, and the backdrop cuts in without a fade.

Because the backdrop key follows the live width, a width change such as iPad rotation or a split-view resize reloads it through the placeholder.

The blurred fallback is decoded at up to hero size, bounded by the source size, although a grid-size bitmap would be enough for a 28 pt blur.

On a first open the effect is partly masked by the full-screen loading spinner that replaces the hero while metadata loads.

**Corrected fix:** Keep steps 1 to 3 and drop step 4.

1. Add optional `decodeWidth` / `decodeHeight` to `CachedImage`, defaulting to `width` / `height`, and pass them to `CachedImage.request`.
2. Hero poster: decode at `categoryGridPosterWidth` x `categoryGridPosterHeight` with `.fill`. Profiles `.standard`, `.shelf` and `.grid` share the same 2x cap, so the key equals the shelf and grid card key.
3. Backdrop: always draw the grid-size poster as the underlay with the existing live `.blur(radius: 28)` and 0.55 opacity. When `backdropURL` exists, draw it on top and let it fade in. That layer needs a profile that animates, or a small change to the `.transaction` block, because `.high` disables animation today. When `posterURL` is nil, keep the current gradient.
4. Give the real backdrop a decode size that does not depend on the live width, for example the longer window side in pixels capped at 2048.
5. Do not pre-blur with `ImageProcessors.GaussianBlur`; keep the live blur.

No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** - `ImageProcessors.Resize(size:unit:contentMode:crop:upscale:)`: found at Nuke/Processing/ImageProcessors+Resize.swift:32, Nuke 13.0.1, already in use.
- `ImageProcessors.GaussianBlur(radius:)`: found at Nuke/Processing/ImageProcessors+GaussianBlur.swift:21-27. It is a vImage box blur and is not recommended here.
- `ImagePipeline.Cache.makeImageCacheKey(for:)`: public, Nuke/Pipeline/ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:192.
- `FetchImage.load` synchronous memory lookup: NukeUI/FetchImage.swift, `if let image = pipeline.cache[request]`.
- No SwiftUI API beyond what DetailComponents.swift already uses.

**Regression risks:** - On iPad the hero poster would be held at 400x600 px instead of 236x352 px. This costs nothing extra when the card is already cached, and about 0.9 MB when the detail is opened from search or history.
- The underlay adds a second image layer under the per-frame `.visualEffect` parallax; a blurred 402x380 pt layer is cheap.
- A fixed backdrop decode size changes the key once and does not affect prefetch.
- The hero poster's tap-to-enlarge and the stroke overlay must stay on the display frame, not the decode size.
- The new parameters must default to today's values so the player's `CachedImage` call sites (Views/PlayerView.swift:4823, 5417, 5602) are unchanged.

**How to verify:** 1. Unit test: `ImagePipeline.shared.cache.makeImageCacheKey(for:)` for the hero-poster request equals the key for `CachedImage.request(url:width: categoryGridPosterWidth, height: categoryGridPosterHeight, contentMode: .fill, loadProfile: .grid)`.
2. Simulator, Slow Animations on: open a movie whose metadata is already loaded from a grid where the poster is visible. The first frame of the detail must show the poster and the blurred header with no glyph.
3. iPad: rotate the detail screen and toggle the sidebar. The header must not flash gray.

## image-pipeline-7 — The same image URL is decoded at up to eight different sizes across screens, so moving between screens produces cache misses and new downloads for artwork that is already in memory

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category grid, EPG guide, EPG programme sheet, Search, Downloads, Continue watching, Watch history
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:102-136`, `another-iptv-player/Views/PosterMetrics.swift:16-41`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:317`, `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:148`, `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:36`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DownloadsView.swift:237-242`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77`, `another-iptv-player/Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169`

**What the user perceives:** A channel logo that is visible on Live TV home loads again in its category grid, again in the TV guide and again in search. Each new screen starts gray for content the user was just looking at.

**Mechanism (finder):** The decode size is always the display size times scale (CachedImage.swift:125-136) and is part of the cache key.
Channel logo on iPhone:
- shelf 112 px (PosterMetrics.liveShelfIcon)
- grid 180 px (liveGridIconSize)
- guide 64 px (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:148)
- search and programme sheet 88 px (SearchView.swift:317, EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:36)
Movie poster:
- shelf and grid 200x300
- search 88x88 fit
- hero 118x176
- hero fallback about 1206x1140
- continue watching 320x180
- history 320x190
- downloads 112x112
- full-screen viewer at original size
Each size is a separate memory entry and needs the original bytes again. Those come from URLCache at best and from the network otherwise (see the thumbnail-cache finding).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Introduce two canonical decode buckets in CachedImage.swift and make small consumers use them, with display size separate from decode size (the same `decodeWidth` / `decodeHeight` parameters as in the detail-hero finding):
- logo bucket = PosterMetrics.liveGridIconSize square, .fit. Use it for the Live shelf, Live grid, EPG guide column, search rows, programme sheet and M3U cards.
- poster bucket = categoryGridPosterWidth x Height, .fill. Use it for the hero poster, search rows and downloads rows.
A 180 px logo costs about 130 KB, so the 150 MB cache still holds more than 1,000. Scaling a 180 px bitmap down to a 32 pt cell is a factor below 2 on a 3x screen and looks fine.
Prefetch call sites keep using CachedImage.request with the same bucket, so prefetch and render keys still match.
Leave continue-watching and history (16:9) and the hero backdrop as their own sizes.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** ImagePipeline.Cache.makeImageCacheKey(for:) (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:192 (for the key-equality test))

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real, but the proposed buckets would cost far more memory on iPad than the finding states and partly reverse the deliberate small-decode tuning.

What holds:
- The decode target is always display size times scale (Views/CachedImage.swift:125-136) and is part of the Resize identifier, so it is part of the memory key (Nuke/Internal/ImageRequestKeys.swift:8-32).
- Call sites I re-read, with iPhone sizes at layoutScale 0.5:
  - Live shelf 56 pt = 112 px (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:410-414)
  - Live grid 90 pt = 180 px (LiveStreamsView.swift:680)
  - Guide 32 pt = 64 px (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:148)
  - Search and programme sheet 44 pt = 88 px (Views/SearchView.swift:317, Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:36)
  - Downloads 56 pt (Views/DownloadsView.swift:237-242)
  - Continue watching 160x90 and history 160x95 (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77, Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169)
- Each is a separate key, so Live home to category grid, or to the guide, is a miss for every logo.
- A miss needs the original data again. The pipeline has no `DataCache`, only the `URLCache` behind `DataLoader.defaultConfiguration` (CachedImage.swift:19-37), so a miss costs a network round trip whenever the host's headers are not cacheable.
- Grid and shelf profiles have no fade (CachedImage.swift:87-93), so the reload shows as gray then a cut.

What does not hold:
1. The memory figures are iPhone-only. On iPad, layoutScale is 1.0 and `liveGridIconSize` is 180 pt = 360 px, about 518 KB per logo, so 150 MB holds about 290 logos, not "more than 1,000". A 32 pt guide cell would hold a 360 px bitmap against 64 px today. That is about 32 times the memory and a 5.6x minification on screen, which aliases wordmark logos. The "factor below 2" statement is true only on iPhone.
2. The poster bucket for search and downloads rows multiplies memory per row by about 11 on iPhone (59x88 px to 200x300 px) and about 24 on iPad (400x600 px, 0.92 MB per row). The benefit is small, because search results are rarely posters the user has just seen.
3. Small shelf and guide decodes are deliberate. The profile comment says "Yatay raf: küçük decode" (CachedImage.swift:45-46), and the 2x cap and the prefetch/render key match came in commit 0ab5bcd.

How long the gray flash lasts depends on `URLCache` hits and cannot be read from code. The demo screenshots (13 channels, opaque photos) say nothing about it.

**Corrected claim:** The same artwork URL is requested under several different decode sizes, so moving between screens misses the memory cache: Live shelf 112 px, Live grid 180 px, guide 64 px, search and programme sheet 88 px on iPhone.

The miss most often seen is Live home to a category grid or the TV guide, where every logo reloads through a gray placeholder with no fade. Each miss needs the original bytes again, from `URLCache` when the host allows caching and from the network otherwise.

Poster variants in search, downloads, continue watching and history are also separate keys, but they matter much less because those screens rarely show artwork the user has just looked at.

**Corrected fix:** Narrow the change to channel logos and cap the bucket in pixels.

1. Add `decodeWidth` / `decodeHeight` to `CachedImage` (the same parameters as in image-pipeline-6).
2. Define one logo decode side in `PosterMetrics`, for example `min(ceil(liveGridIconSize * min(scale, 2)), 192...256 px)`. The exact cap is an owner decision between iPad grid sharpness and memory.
3. Use it for the Live shelf, Live grid and All Channels, M3U cards, live rows in search, and the programme sheet. Pass the same values at the matching `ListImagePrefetch.start` call sites so prefetch and render keys stay equal.
4. Guide column: join the bucket on iPhone only, or leave it at 64 px. Do not hold 360 px bitmaps for 32 pt cells on iPad.
5. Posters: only the hero poster shares the grid key (covered by image-pipeline-6). Leave search, downloads, continue-watching and history decodes small.

If a disk cache for image data is added by another finding, re-measure before doing this; a miss then costs a few milliseconds and this change may not be worth the memory.

No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** - `ImagePipeline.Cache.makeImageCacheKey(for:)`: public, Nuke/Pipeline/ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:192.
- `ImageProcessors.Resize`: Hashable; its identifier includes size, content mode, crop and upscale (Nuke/Processing/ImageProcessors+Resize.swift:16-66).
- No SwiftUI or UIKit API is involved.

**Regression risks:** - Undoes part of the deliberate small-decode tuning for shelves and the guide, raising memory per logo: about 2.6 times for shelf logos, up to 32 times for guide logos on iPad without a pixel cap.
- Larger logos fill the 150 MB cache sooner and evict posters, and the count limit of 1500 is reached sooner on large channel lists.
- Any call site whose prefetch size is not updated together with its render size decodes every image twice. `ListImagePrefetch` builds requests through `CachedImage.request`, so both must receive the same decode size.
- Strong minification of a large bitmap in small cells can alias.

**How to verify:** 1. Unit test: for one URL, the requests built for the Live shelf card, the Live grid card and the search live row produce equal `ImageCacheKey`s, and each prefetch request equals its render request.
2. Device with a real playlist: load Live home, push a category and open the guide. Count placeholder frames before and after with a screen recording stepped frame by frame.
3. Instruments Allocations on iPad with a 5k-channel guide: compare image cache cost (`ImageCache.totalCost`) and eviction before and after.

## image-pipeline-8 — Channel logos lose their tile when they load, and search and downloads rows letterbox portrait posters inside a 44/56 pt square

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category grid, All Channels, M3U channels, EPG guide, Search results, Downloads, Continue watching, Watch history
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:66-82, 138-147`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:434-441`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:422-429`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:317-318`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DownloadsView.swift:237-243`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77`, `another-iptv-player/Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Tile colour for logos: adaptive systemGray6 as in the placeholder, or a fixed dark tile in both appearances because most IPTV logos are drawn for dark TV interfaces. Also whether logos get the 10 % inset.

**What the user perceives:** While loading, every channel is a rounded gray tile. When a real logo (transparent PNG, wide wordmark) arrives, the tile disappears and the logo floats on the page background, so tiles in one row have different visible shapes. Dark logos vanish on the black background in dark mode and white logos vanish in light mode. In search results a movie poster is a narrow strip with square corners inside an invisible 44 pt square. In Continue Watching, a live channel's logo is cropped to 16:9.

**Mechanism (finder):** - The gray fill exists only in `placeholder` (CachedImage.swift:138-147). The loaded branch is just `image.resizable().aspectRatio(contentMode:)` with no background (lines 67-70), so in .fit mode the area around the image, and any transparency inside it, shows the screen background.
- The clip shape is applied to the outer frame, not to the image, so a letterboxed image keeps square corners. iphone-light/Q03-search-results-mi.png shows this: about 29x44 pt posters with sharp corners.
- SearchView.swift:317 and DownloadsView.swift:237-242 use one square .fit frame for both logos and 2:3 posters.
- HistoryCard and HistoryCardGridItem use .fill at 160x90 for every type, including type == "live" logos (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77, WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169).
- The demo data uses opaque square photos as logos (Database/MockFixture.swift:83), so the screenshots cannot show the transparent case; that part is from code.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. CachedImage.swift: in .fit mode keep the tile under the loaded image and inset the image by about 10 %:
```swift
ZStack { tile; image.resizable().aspectRatio(contentMode: .fit).padding(min(width, height) * 0.1) }
```
.fill posters are unchanged, since they cover the tile.
2. SearchView ResultRow and the DownloadsView row: for movies and series use a 2:3 frame (for example 40x60, .fill, corner radius 6); keep the square .fit tile for live channels.
3. HistoryCard / HistoryCardGridItem: `contentMode: item.type == "live" ? .fit : .fill`.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** SwiftUI.RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:style:) (iOS 13+, SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:10354)

**Verifier reasons:** All three visual problems are real, but fix 1 as written changes the player's artwork and does not solve the contrast problem it describes.

What holds:
- The loaded branch is only `image.resizable().aspectRatio(contentMode:)` with no background (Views/CachedImage.swift:66-70). The gray tile exists only in `placeholder` (138-147).
- `LiveStreamCard` and `M3UChannelCard` put nothing behind the image (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:434-441, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:422-429). In `.fit` mode a transparent or non-square logo therefore sits directly on the page background, and the clip is on the outer frame (CachedImage.swift:81-82), so a letterboxed image keeps square corners.
- Search rows use one 44x44 `.fit` frame for logos and 2:3 posters (Views/SearchView.swift:317-318). Screenshot iphone-light/Q03-search-results-mi.png shows the result: posters about 29x44 pt with sharp corners.
- Downloads rows use the same pattern at 56x56 (Views/DownloadsView.swift:237-243). The downloads screenshot is empty, so that part is from code.
- `HistoryCard` and `HistoryCardGridItem` use `.fill` at 160x90 and 160x95 for every type, while the same code branches on `item.type == "live"` for the icon (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77, Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169). Live logos are therefore cropped.
- The transparent-logo case cannot be seen in screenshots: the demo logos are opaque 200x200 photos (Database/MockFixture.swift:83, iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png). It follows directly from the code.

Corrections:
1. Fix 1 edits `CachedImage` for every `.fit` consumer. That includes three call sites in the out-of-scope player (Views/PlayerView.swift:4823, 5417, 5602), which would gain a gray tile and a 10 % inset.
2. An adaptive systemGray6 tile gives consistent shapes but does not make dark logos visible in dark mode or white logos visible in light mode, because the tile is nearly the same tone as the background. Only a fixed tile colour changes contrast, and that is the owner's decision.

**Corrected claim:** While loading, a channel is a rounded gray tile. Once the logo loads, the tile is gone: transparent or non-square logos sit directly on the page background, so tiles in one row have different visible shapes and logos close to the background colour are hard to see.

Search and downloads rows letterbox 2:3 posters inside a 44 or 56 pt square with square corners; the search case is confirmed by screenshot.

Continue Watching and Watch History crop live-channel logos to 16:9.

**Corrected fix:** 1. `CachedImage`: add an opt-in parameter, for example `showsTile: Bool = false`. When it is true and the mode is `.fit`, draw the rounded tile under the loaded image and inset the image by about 10 %:
```swift
ZStack { tile; image.resizable().aspectRatio(contentMode: .fit).padding(min(width, height) * 0.1) }
```
Turn it on in `LiveStreamCard`, `M3UChannelCard`, the guide's channel cell, live rows in search, the programme sheet, and live history cards. Leave the default off so the player's call sites are unchanged.
2. Search `ResultRow` and the downloads row: use a 2:3 `.fill` frame (about 40x60, corner radius 6) for movies, series and episodes, and the square tile for live channels. The search row's separator inset and row height need a check after the change.
3. `HistoryCard` and `HistoryCardGridItem`: `contentMode: item.type == "live" ? .fit : .fill`, with the tile on.

Decision for the owner: tile colour (adaptive systemGray6 for shape consistency only, or a fixed tone for contrast) and whether logos get the inset.

No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** - `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:style:)`: found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface at line 10354, `@inlinable public init(cornerRadius: CoreFoundation.CGFloat, style: SwiftUICore.RoundedCornerStyle = .continuous)`, on `@frozen public struct RoundedRectangle : SwiftUICore.Shape` (line 10347). Available since iOS 13 and already used in CachedImage.swift.
- `ZStack`, `padding` and `aspectRatio(contentMode:)` are already in use in this file.

**Regression risks:** - If the tile is applied globally rather than opt-in, the player's artwork changes; the opt-in parameter avoids that.
- The inset makes opaque square logos slightly smaller inside the tile, which changes the look of the demo and of playlists with full-bleed logos.
- A taller poster thumbnail changes the row height and separator inset in search and downloads lists.
- The Equatable shelf rows and the prefetch keys are not affected, because the decode size does not change.

**How to verify:** 1. Add two demo channels with transparent PNG logos (one dark wordmark, one white wordmark) to the mock fixture.
2. Screenshot Live home, a category grid, the TV guide and Continue Watching in light and dark, before and after.
3. Re-shoot Q03 for the search rows, and the downloads list with one movie and one episode.
4. Open the player's channel list and the audio-only artwork and confirm they look as before.

## image-pipeline-9 — Every image is decoded at full source size and then redrawn smaller; Nuke 13's thumbnail option would downsample during decode

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All image surfaces, Live category grid, All Channels, M3U channels, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:102-123`

**What the user perceives:** On fast scrolls through channel lists whose logos are large PNGs (1000-2000 px is common), images arrive later than the network explains and the device warms up. On older devices memory spikes during scrolling.

**Mechanism (finder):** `CachedImage.request` attaches `ImageProcessors.Resize` (CachedImage.swift:111-122). In Nuke 13 the default decoder then only wraps the data (`UIImage(data:)`, Nuke/Decoding/ImageDecoders+Default.swift:177-183), and the Resize processor draws the full-size image into a new CGContext (Nuke/Internal/Graphics.swift:30-45, 133-145). That means a complete full-resolution decode plus a second buffer for every image, two at a time (processing queue, ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:175). A 2000x3000 poster costs about 24 MB transient to produce a 240 KB thumbnail. The work is off the main thread, so this is throughput and memory, not a main-thread stall. Nuke's own doc says thumbnails are 'significantly more efficient, especially in terms of memory usage, than image resizing' (Nuke/ImageRequest.swift:117-123).

**Proposed fix (finder):** In `CachedImage.request` replace the processor with the thumbnail option, same target size and mode:
```swift
var request = ImageRequest(url: url)
request.thumbnail = ImageRequest.ThumbnailOptions(size: target, unit: .pixels, contentMode: nukeMode)
return request
```
- It uses CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex (Graphics.swift:360-387), never upscales, bakes in EXIF orientation, and the result is already decoded (no separate decompression step: Nuke/Decoding/ImageDecoding.swift:58-60).
- The thumbnail options are part of the memory key and the disk key (ImageRequestKeys.swift:12-30, ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:204). Prefetch and render both go through this function, so they stay equal.
- Thumbnail decoding runs on `imageDecodingQueue`, which defaults to 1 concurrent task (ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:169). Set `$0.imageDecodingQueue = TaskQueue(maxConcurrentOperationCount: 2)` in the pipeline setup to keep today's parallelism.
- The sizes and the 2x cap stay exactly as they are (deliberate tuning at CachedImage.swift:125-136).
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** ImageRequest.thumbnail / ImageRequest.ThumbnailOptions(size:unit:contentMode:) (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, Nuke/ImageRequest.swift:123-126, 422-426); ImagePipeline.Configuration.imageDecodingQueue (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:169)

**Verifier reasons:** The claim and the fix both stand; only the severity is lower than stated.

Mechanism, re-read in the Nuke 13.0.1 checkout:
- `CachedImage.request` attaches only `ImageProcessors.Resize` (Views/CachedImage.swift:111-122).
- Without `thumbnail`, the default decoder is synchronous and just wraps the data in `UIImage(data:scale:)` (Nuke/Decoding/ImageDecoders+Default.swift, `isAsynchronous` and `_decode`).
- Resize then draws the full `cgImage` into a new context of the target size (Nuke/Internal/Graphics.swift, `byResizing` and `draw(inCanvasWithSize:)`). That forces a full-resolution decode on the processing queue, which runs 2 at a time (Nuke/Pipeline/ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:175).
- With `thumbnail` set, the decoder calls `makeThumbnail`, which uses `CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex` with a max pixel size computed from the flexible size and content mode. It never upscales, bakes in orientation, and decodes immediately (the default options). The decoder marks the result with `isThumbnailKey`, so the separate decompression step is skipped (Nuke/Decoding/ImageDecoding.swift).
- Nuke's own documentation on `ImageRequest.thumbnail` says thumbnails are significantly more efficient than `ImageProcessors.Resize`.
- `thumbnail` is part of `MemoryCacheKey`. `ListImagePrefetch` builds its requests through `CachedImage.request` (Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift:31-39), so prefetch and render keys stay equal.
- Thumbnail decoding moves to `imageDecodingQueue`, default 1 (Nuke/Tasks/AsyncPipelineTask.swift:51-54, Configuration.swift:169), so the proposed bump to 2 is needed to keep today's parallelism.

Nothing in comments or history says Resize was chosen over thumbnails; `git log -S'thumbnail'` on CachedImage.swift is empty. The 2x cap and the sizes are untouched by the fix. No other code builds requests with Resize; the full-screen viewer loads by URL (Views/Components/ZoomableImageView.swift:33). No unit test references `CachedImage`.

Severity is low rather than medium. The work is already off the main thread, and for typical sources (TMDB 600x900 posters, logos of a few hundred pixels) the saving is a few milliseconds and about 2 MB transient per image. It becomes significant only for playlists that serve originals of 2000 px and more. Nuke also already caps a single decode at 64 MB (`maximumDecodedImageSize`, Configuration.swift:128-133).

One behaviour change the finding did not mention: `LazyImageContext` equality compares image ID, priority, processors and options but not `thumbnail` (NukeUI/LazyImage.swift, `LazyImageContext.==`). A mounted `CachedImage` whose size changes while its URL stays the same will no longer reload. That removes the rotation flash on the detail backdrop, but an image can stay at its old decode size after a window resize until the view is recreated.

**Corrected claim:** Every image is fully decoded at source resolution and then redrawn at the target size by `ImageProcessors.Resize`. For large sources that costs a full-size transient bitmap per image, two at a time. The work is off the main thread, so the effect is throughput, heat and memory on playlists that serve large originals, not a main-thread stall. For typical 600x900 posters and small logos the gain is modest.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed. In `CachedImage.request`:
```swift
var request = ImageRequest(url: url)
request.thumbnail = ImageRequest.ThumbnailOptions(size: target, unit: .pixels, contentMode: nukeMode)
return request
```
In the pipeline setup add `$0.imageDecodingQueue = TaskQueue(maxConcurrentOperationCount: 2)`.

Keep the sizes and the 2x cap as they are.

If a mounted image must reload when only its size changes, add `.id(...)` on the size at that call site; for the detail backdrop the new behaviour is the better one.

No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** - `ImageRequest.thumbnail`: `public var thumbnail: ThumbnailOptions?`, Nuke/ImageRequest.swift:123-126.
- `ImageRequest.ThumbnailOptions.init(size:unit:contentMode:)`: `public init(size: CGSize, unit: ImageProcessingOptions.Unit = .points, contentMode: ImageProcessingOptions.ContentMode = .aspectFill)`, ImageRequest.swift:422-426. Default options are createThumbnailFromImageIfAbsent, createThumbnailFromImageAlways, createThumbnailWithTransform and shouldCacheImmediately (ImageRequest.swift:457-462).
- `ImagePipeline.Configuration.imageDecodingQueue`: `public var imageDecodingQueue = TaskQueue(maxConcurrentOperationCount: 1)`, Configuration.swift:169.
- `TaskQueue`: `public final class TaskQueue: Sendable` with `public init(maxConcurrentOperationCount:)`, Nuke/Internal/TaskQueue.swift:13 and 66.
- `ImagePipeline.Configuration.isSignpostLoggingEnabled`: public static, Configuration.swift (for the measurement).

**Regression risks:** - Every memory-cache key changes once; this is harmless because the cache is memory-only.
- Size-only changes on a mounted view no longer trigger a reload, because `LazyImageContext` ignores `thumbnail`.
- Thumbnails skip `preparingForDisplay`. They are decoded, but the pixel format is whatever ImageIO produced, so check that Core Animation does not copy or convert images on the main thread at commit time.
- Requests for one URL at different sizes no longer share one decoded original; each size decodes from the shared data. That is cheaper per decode, but there is one decode per size.
- Animated GIF logos behave as today: first frame only, with the data kept in the container.

**How to verify:** 1. Unit test: decode a 2000x3000 JPEG fixture and a 1024x1024 transparent PNG through the new request. Assert the pixel size matches the Resize path within 1 px, that alpha is kept, and that an image smaller than the target is not upscaled.
2. Unit test: the prefetch request and the render request for the same card produce equal `ImageCacheKey`s.
3. Device: Instruments Allocations and Time Profiler with Nuke signposts on, scrolling All Channels and All Movies on a playlist with large artwork, before and after. Compare peak transient memory and decode time per image.
4. In the same trace, check for image copies on the main thread during commits.

## image-pipeline-10 — The 150 MB memory cache holds only about 156 posters on iPad, less than two grid pages, so scrolling back in a grid reloads what was just shown

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Category grids (iPad), All Movies (iPad), Movies home (iPad), Series home (iPad)
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:26-29`, `another-iptv-player/Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-20`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: How much memory the image cache may take on devices with 6 GB or more, given the player's own needs for 4K/HDR. 320 MB is a proposal, not a measured value.

**What the user perceives:** On iPad, scroll two pages down a movie grid and back up: the top rows are gray again and pop back in. On iPhone the same cache holds about 625 posters and the effect is much rarer.

**Mechanism (finder):** - `costLimit = 150 MB`, `countLimit = 1500` (CachedImage.swift:27-29).
- On iPad, layoutScale is 1.0 (PosterMetrics.swift:9-14), so a grid or shelf poster is 200x300 pt at 2x = 400x600 px, about 0.96 MB decoded (cost = bytesPerRow x height, Nuke/Caching/ImageCache.swift:107-117). 150 MB / 0.96 MB is about 156 entries.
- One grid page is 90 cells (VODView.swift:626), about 86 MB.
- One home shelf prefetches 32 posters, about 31 MB (VODView.swift:397), so five shelves fill the cache.
- An entry larger than 10 % of the limit (15 MB) is never stored (Nuke/Caching/Cache.swift:47, 100-103).
- The limit was set for a good reason (comment at CachedImage.swift:26: an unlimited cache filled RAM), but it is the same number on a 3 GB iPhone and a 16 GB iPad. The value dates from the initial import (git log -S'costLimit = 150' shows only d2489f9).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Scale the limit with the device and keep a hard cap, in CachedImage.swift:
```swift
let ram = ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory
memoryCache.costLimit = ram >= 6 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 ? 320 * 1024 * 1024 : 150 * 1024 * 1024
```
Nuke still empties the cache on memory pressure (Cache.swift:49-53) and trims it on background, so the player keeps its headroom. Do this together with the prefetch reduction, which removes most of the churn, and the thumbnail disk cache, which makes the remaining misses cheap.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** ImageCache.costLimit / countLimit / entryCostLimit (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, Nuke/Caching/ImageCache.swift:26-49)

**Verifier reasons:** The arithmetic is roughly right, but the limit is not the main cause of the churn, and the proposed fix does not help the iPads most likely to hit it.

What holds:
- `costLimit` is 150 MB and `countLimit` 1500 (Views/CachedImage.swift:27-29). Cost is `bytesPerRow * height` (Nuke/Caching/ImageCache.swift, `cost(for:)`).
- On iPad layoutScale is 1.0 (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-14), so a poster is 200x300 pt at 2x = 400x600 px = 960,000 bytes. 150 MiB divided by that is about 164 entries; the finding says 156, which is close enough.
- Posters whose source is not 2:3 cost more, because `crop` is false.
- An entry at or above 10 % of the limit is never stored, and the cache empties on memory pressure (Nuke/Caching/Cache.swift, `set` and the memory-pressure handler).

Corrections:
1. In a grid, 164 posters is about 30 rows of 5, which is roughly 10 to 14 screenfuls on iPad. "Two pages" in the finding means two 90-item pagination pages (Views/VODView.swift:626), not two screens. Reloading after that distance is ordinary behaviour.
2. The case reached quickly is the home screen. Every shelf prefetches 32 posters when it appears (VODView.swift:395-398, 476-488), about 29 MB per shelf on iPad, while only 4 to 6 are visible. Five to six shelves, about two screens, fill the cache and evict the first shelves. The prefetch head count is the driver, not the limit.
3. The 150 MB value is a deliberate cut. Nuke's default is 15 % of RAM capped at 768 MB (ImageCache.swift, `defaultCostLimit`), and the comment at CachedImage.swift:26 says an uncapped cache filled RAM. Raising it is a product decision set against the player's memory needs.
4. The proposed test `physicalMemory >= 6 * 1024^3` will not match devices sold as 6 GB, because iOS reports less than the nominal size; I state this from platform knowledge and did not measure it here. It also leaves 3 and 4 GB iPads, the common base models, at 150 MB, so they see no change.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad a poster decodes to 400x600 px (about 0.92 MiB), so the 150 MB memory cache holds about 164 posters.

The visible effect is on Movies and Series home: each shelf prefetches 32 posters, so scrolling past five or six shelves evicts the first ones, and scrolling back two screens shows them reloading.

In category grids the same eviction needs a scroll of 10 or more screenfuls. iPhone holds about 640 posters and is rarely affected.

**Corrected fix:** 1. First reduce the shelf prefetch head count to roughly what one screen width shows plus a small margin. That belongs to the prefetch finding and removes most of the churn on every iPad, including 3 and 4 GB models.
2. Then decide whether to raise the limit. If the owner agrees, make it proportional and capped rather than a 6 GiB threshold:
```swift
let ram = Int(ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory)
memoryCache.costLimit = min(max(150 * 1024 * 1024, ram / 25), 320 * 1024 * 1024)
```
(4 % of RAM, floor 150 MB, cap 320 MB.) If a threshold is preferred, use 5 GiB so devices sold as 6 GB qualify.
3. Keep `countLimit`. Both numbers are proposals to be measured, not measured values.

No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** - `ImageCache.costLimit`, `countLimit`, `entryCostLimit`: public vars, Nuke/Caching/ImageCache.swift:26-49.
- `ImageCache.defaultCostLimit`: public static, 15 % of RAM capped at 768 MB, same file.
- Memory-pressure and enter-background trimming: Nuke/Caching/Cache.swift (init and `registerForEnterBackground`).
- `ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory`: Foundation, `UInt64`; Nuke uses it the same way.

**Regression risks:** - A larger image cache takes headroom from the player during 4K and HDR playback. Nuke empties the cache on a memory warning, but jetsam can come before the warning is handled.
- The existing limit is deliberate earlier work, so raising it must be the owner's call.
- A proportional limit makes memory behaviour differ per device, which makes bug reports harder to reproduce.

**How to verify:** Device only (iPad, 4 GB and 8 GB if available):
1. Movies home: scroll down six shelves and back to the top. Count shelves that show placeholders, before and after the prefetch change and again after the limit change.
2. All Movies: scroll three pagination pages down and back up; count placeholder rows.
3. Log `ImageCache.totalCost` and `totalCount` at those points.
4. With the cache full, start a 4K HDR stream and watch Xcode's memory gauge for warnings or a jetsam kill.
5. Print `ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory` on each test device to settle the threshold.

## image-pipeline-11 — The full-screen poster viewer opens to a black screen with a spinner although the thumbnail is already in memory, shows nothing on failure, and never cancels its download

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail poster viewer, Series detail poster viewer
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/ZoomableImageView.swift:25-45`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/FullscreenImageViewer.swift:8-14`, `another-iptv-player/Views/MovieDetailView.swift:93-95, 126-128`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the poster cuts to black with a white spinner, then the image appears at once. In Photos or the App Store the picture is on screen from the first frame and only sharpens. If the load fails, the user is left on a black screen with only a close button.

**Mechanism (finder):** - `ImagePipeline.shared.loadImage(with: url)` (ZoomableImageView.swift:33) requests the original with no processors. That key is never in the memory cache, because every other site uses a resized key.
- Nothing is shown until the full download and decode finish.
- The returned ImageTask is discarded, so dismissing the viewer does not cancel the download.
- On failure the loader is removed and nothing replaces it (lines 35-43).
- The completion is already delivered on the main actor in Nuke 13, so the extra `DispatchQueue.main.async` only adds a frame; this API is marked soft-deprecated (Nuke/Pipeline/Deprecated.swift:36-40).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. Give ZoomableImageView an optional `placeholder: UIImage?`. DetailHero passes the cached thumbnail, read synchronously with `ImagePipeline.shared.cache[CachedImage.request(url:..., grid metrics...)]?.image`.
2. Set it on the UIImageView and lay out before starting the load; show the spinner only when there is no placeholder.
3. Keep the task in the Coordinator and cancel it in `dismantleUIView`.
4. On failure keep the placeholder; if there is none, show a 'photo' symbol and call onDismiss on tap.
5. Load with `ImagePipeline.shared.imageTask(with: ImageRequest(url: url, priority: .veryHigh))` and await `.image`.
The zoom navigation transition for this cover belongs to the transitions lens.

**APIs:** ImagePipeline.Cache.subscript(request:) (synchronous memory lookup) (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:29-40); ImagePipeline.imageTask(with:) / ImageTask.image / ImageTask.cancel() (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, ImagePipeline.swift:139; ImageTask.swift:176)

**Verifier reasons:** The problem is real, but two parts of the fix would not work as written.

What holds:
- Views/Components/ZoomableImageView.swift:33 calls `ImagePipeline.shared.loadImage(with: url)` with no processors and discards the returned ImageTask. Nothing is shown until completion (lines 26-30 add only a white spinner over Color.black, FullscreenImageViewer.swift:9).
- On failure the loader is removed and nothing replaces it (lines 35-43).
- No other site loads an unprocessed request: the only other pipeline user is CachedImage, which always adds a Resize processor (Views/CachedImage.swift:111-122). So the original key is absent from the memory cache on the first open.
- Nuke/Pipeline/Deprecated.swift:37-40 marks the API soft-deprecated, and line 73 already hops to main, so the extra `DispatchQueue.main.async` at ZoomableImageView.swift:34 is redundant.
- Both call sites exist: Views/MovieDetailView.swift:93-95 and Views/SeriesView.swift:889-891.

What needs correcting:
- The thumbnail in memory is not under "grid metrics". The tapped poster is rendered at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:103-110 with `metrics.seriesDetailHeroWidth/Height`, contentMode .fill and the default `.standard` profile. A grid-metrics key only hits if the user happened to arrive from a category grid and the entry was not evicted; it misses from shelves, search, history and favourites.
- On iPhone layoutScale is 0.5 (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:13), so that thumbnail is about 59x88 pt, 118x176 px (see iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png). It will be very soft full-screen. When the item has no backdrop, the same poster URL is also cached at hero size under the `.high` profile (DetailComponents.swift:26-28, 51-58), which is a much better placeholder.
- "Set it on the UIImageView and lay out before starting the load" is a no-op: in makeUIView the scroll view bounds are zero and `updateLayout` returns early at ZoomableImageView.swift:87. Today layout only happens because the async completion arrives after sizing. A synchronous placeholder needs a real layout hook.
- "Never in the memory cache" is true only for the first open; after one successful load the original sits under the unprocessed key.
- The pipeline has no Nuke DataCache but uses DataLoader's URLCache (CachedImage.swift:19-24), so the original bytes are often on disk and the black gap is usually short. Severity stays low.

No history explains the current behaviour as deliberate: `git log -S'ZoomableImageView'` shows only the monorepo move d2489f9.

**Corrected claim:** The poster viewer (movie and series detail) shows black plus a white spinner until the unprocessed original is fetched and decoded, even though a resized copy of the same poster is in the memory cache under the hero-poster key (`.standard`, seriesDetailHero metrics, .fill) and, when there is no backdrop, under the `.high` hero-backdrop key. On failure only the close button remains on a black screen. The ImageTask is discarded, so dismissing does not cancel the download. The gap is usually short when URLCache holds the bytes; it is long on a slow network or a cache miss.

**Corrected fix:** 1. Add `placeholder: UIImage?` to ZoomableImageView. FullscreenImageViewer resolves it synchronously from `ImagePipeline.shared.cache[...]?.image`, trying in order:
   - the unprocessed `ImageRequest(url:)` (second open);
   - the `.high` hero-backdrop key, if the hero width is passed along;
   - the hero-poster key: `CachedImage.request(url:, width: metrics.seriesDetailHeroWidth, height: metrics.seriesDetailHeroHeight, contentMode: .fill, loadProfile: .standard)`.
   Expose that last request from a small static helper next to DetailHero so the two cannot drift.
2. Drive layout from a real hook: a small UIScrollView subclass whose `layoutSubviews` calls `coordinator.updateLayout` when the bounds size changes. Do not rely on makeUIView or updateUIView. This also fixes stale layout after rotation.
3. Show the spinner only when there is no placeholder.
4. Hold the ImageTask in the Coordinator and cancel it in `static func dismantleUIView(_:coordinator:)`.
5. On failure keep the placeholder; with none, show a `photo` symbol and keep the close button.
6. Replace the soft-deprecated call with `ImagePipeline.shared.imageTask(with: ImageRequest(url: url, priority: .veryHigh))`, await `.image` in a Task owned by the Coordinator, and drop the extra `DispatchQueue.main.async`.
No iOS 26 API; works on iOS 18.

**API check:** Nuke 13.0.1 checkout:
- `ImagePipeline.Cache.subscript(request: ImageRequest) -> ImageContainer?` at Sources/Nuke/Pipeline/ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:29; synchronous memory lookup.
- `ImageContainer.image: UIImage` at Sources/Nuke/ImageContainer.swift:34.
- `nonisolated public func imageTask(with request: ImageRequest) -> ImageTask` at Sources/Nuke/Pipeline/ImagePipeline.swift:139.
- `ImageTask.image { get async throws(ImagePipeline.Error) }` at Sources/Nuke/ImageTask.swift:79; `ImageTask.cancel()` at :176.
- `ImageRequest.init(url:processors:priority:options:userInfo:)` at Sources/Nuke/ImageRequest.swift:156.
- `loadImage(with:completion:)` soft-deprecated at Sources/Nuke/Pipeline/Deprecated.swift:37-40.

SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22608: `@MainActor @preconcurrency static func dismantleUIView(_ uiView: Self.UIViewType, coordinator: Self.Coordinator)`, with a default implementation at :22636.

**Regression risks:** - A wrong placeholder key fails silently: the lookup returns nil and behaviour is as today.
- The placeholder and the final image have the same aspect ratio (Resize uses crop: false), so there is no layout jump on swap. Confirm zoom scale is reset or preserved when the image is swapped.
- A layoutSubviews hook must not reset the frame while zoomed (zoomScale != 1) or during the drag-to-dismiss transform.
- The uncached original can be large; it lands in the 150 MB memory cache as today, so nothing changes there.
- Touches no player files and no tip-jar files.

**How to verify:** - Simulator with Network Link Conditioner on 3G, movie detail, tap the poster: the first frame of the cover must show the soft poster, then sharpen; no black frame.
- Repeat for an item without a backdrop and for a series.
- Offline with a cold URLCache: the placeholder stays and no spinner hangs.
- Rotate while the viewer is open: the image re-centres.
- Unit test: dismantleUIView cancels the stored task (task.state == .cancelled).

## image-pipeline-12 — A failed image looks exactly like one that is still loading and is only retried when the cell happens to re-appear; nothing retries when the connection comes back

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Category grids, Movies home, Series home, EPG guide, Search
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:66-74, 138-147`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether missing or failed channel logos should show a channel-name monogram instead of the generic 'tv' glyph. This is a design choice.

**What the user perceives:** After a network drop, the tiles on screen stay gray until the user scrolls them away and back. Channels with no logo, a broken logo and a logo still downloading all show the same gray 'tv' glyph, so the user cannot tell whether to wait.

**Mechanism (finder):** - The content closure only checks `state.image` (CachedImage.swift:67-73); `state.error` and `state.isLoading` (NukeUI/LazyImageState.swift:12-38) are ignored, and the nil-URL case uses the same placeholder (line 84).
- Nuke does not retry by itself. The only retry is LazyImage's reload on the next onAppear (NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:165-171).
- `waitsForConnectivity = false` (CachedImage.swift:23) makes requests fail immediately when offline, which is right for scrolling but leaves visible cells failed.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. Retry visible failures when the app becomes active or the network returns. With the FetchImage-backed wrapper from the re-appear finding, observe `scenePhase` in CachedImage and call `model.load(request)` when `model.result` is a failure. If network-path monitoring is wanted, drive it from the app's existing reachability source or a single shared NWPathMonitor.
2. Optional, visual: give the three states different looks: loading = plain tile; no URL or failed logo = channel-name monogram instead of the generic glyph; failed poster = glyph. This needs a `fallbackText` parameter at the two channel-card call sites.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** NukeUI.LazyImageState.error / isLoading / result (Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, NukeUI/LazyImageState.swift:12-38); SwiftUI.EnvironmentValues.scenePhase (iOS 14+ (not re-checked in the swiftinterface for this audit; verify before use))

**Verifier reasons:** The retry gap is real, but narrower than described, and the fix leans on something this code base does not have.

What holds:
- Views/CachedImage.swift:66-74 branches only on `state.image`; failure, loading and the nil-URL case (line 84) all draw the same placeholder (138-147).
- Nuke does not retry. LazyImage reloads only in `onAppear` (NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:165-171), and `FetchImage.load` resets and re-requests (NukeUI/FetchImage.swift:103-155).
- `waitsForConnectivity = false` (CachedImage.swift:23) makes offline requests fail at once. `git log -S'waitsForConnectivity'` shows only the monorepo move, so there is no recorded rationale, but the file header comment (lines 7-8) is about dead hosts and it is part of the request tuning.
- Nothing in scope re-triggers image loads on foreground or network return: no NWPathMonitor or reachability type anywhere in the app; the only foreground observers are in EPG/EPGStore.swift:76 and the out-of-scope PlayerView.

What needs correcting:
- "Only retried when the cell happens to re-appear" understates the existing triggers. onAppear fires again on scroll and, as I understand SwiftUI's behaviour (not run here), also on tab switch and on return from a pushed detail. The true gap is background to foreground and network return while staying on one screen, plus dismissal of the in-window player overlay.
- The fix depends on "the FetchImage-backed wrapper from the re-appear finding", which is another finding and may not be adopted. With LazyImage as it stands, the view model is a private @StateObject and cannot be told to reload.
- "The app's existing reachability source" does not exist.
- "Failed looks like loading" as a native-feel defect is weak: Apple's own apps show the same neutral placeholder for both. The monogram idea is a product decision, and it touches more than "two channel-card call sites": `iconName: "tv"` appears in four in-scope places (LiveStreamsView.swift:439, M3UChannelsView.swift:427, EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:148, EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:36) and two in the out-of-scope PlayerView.

Evidence is code only, and this is an edge case after a network drop, so severity stays low.

**Corrected claim:** Images that fail (offline, timeout) are retried only when their LazyImage gets another onAppear. Returning from background, the network coming back while the user stays on the same screen, or closing the in-window player do not retry, so visible tiles stay as gray placeholders until the user scrolls or navigates. Loading, failed and no-URL states share one placeholder; that is how Apple's apps behave too, and changing it is a design choice, not a defect.

**Corrected fix:** Self-contained, no dependency on another finding:
1. In CachedImage add `@State private var failed = false` and `@State private var retryToken = 0`.
2. Attach `.onCompletion { if case .failure = $0 { failed = true } }` and `.id(retryToken)` to the LazyImage.
3. Add `.onChange(of: scenePhase)`: when the phase becomes `.active` and `failed` is true, clear `failed` and increment `retryToken`. Only failed cells remount; loaded cells are untouched.
4. Optional second trigger: one shared `NWPathMonitor` (Network framework, first-party) publishing an epoch on the unsatisfied-to-satisfied transition, observed the same way. Create it new; there is no existing source.
5. Keep `waitsForConnectivity = false` and all request tuning as they are.
6. If the FetchImage wrapper from the other finding is adopted, call `model.load(request)` instead of the `.id` remount.
Monogram for missing channel logos: owner decision, separate from the retry; if adopted it covers the four in-scope `tv` sites.

**API check:** - `EnvironmentValues.scenePhase: SwiftUI.ScenePhase`, `@available(iOS 14.0, ...)`, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5567-5569. The finder had left this unverified; it is present.
- `State: Sendable where Value: Sendable`, SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:15923, so capturing the Bool state in the `@MainActor @Sendable` completion closure is fine (target is Swift 5 mode with MainActor default isolation).
- Nuke 13.0.1: `LazyImage.onCompletion(_:)` at Sources/NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:129; `LazyImageState.result / error / isLoading` at Sources/NukeUI/LazyImageState.swift:12-38; `FetchImage.load(_ request:)` at Sources/NukeUI/FetchImage.swift:103.
- NWPathMonitor: not checked in the SDK; it is not in the three interface locations given. Verify before use.

**Regression risks:** - CachedImage is instantiated in every shelf and grid cell. Two @State values and a scenePhase dependency make every visible CachedImage body re-evaluate on each phase change; that is cheap but must not break the Equatable shelf rows (environment invalidation bypasses the parent's Equatable check, which is what is wanted here).
- Dead logo hosts are common (CachedImage.swift:7-8); each foreground will re-hit them for the visible failed cells only, bounded by 4 connections per host and the 10 s timeout.
- Do not apply `.id` to all cells or switch to `waitsForConnectivity = true`; either would undo the request tuning or cause re-mount flicker.
- The `.id` remount resets the 0.12 s fade for `.standard` cells, which is harmless.

**How to verify:** Simulator or device:
- Airplane mode, open Movies (gray tiles), re-enable the network, background and foreground the app without scrolling: failed tiles must fill within a few seconds and already-loaded tiles must not flicker.
- Instruments (SwiftUI template): confirm a scenePhase change re-evaluates only CachedImage bodies, not shelf rows.
- Count requests in Network instruments after a foreground with 20 visible dead-logo cells: at most 20 new requests.

## image-pipeline-13 — Decode scale is read from UIScreen.main, which the iOS 26 SDK marks deprecated, and PosterMetrics still carries two unused prefetch-size helpers

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All image surfaces
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:125-136`, `another-iptv-player/Views/PosterMetrics.swift:52-68, 75-79`

**What the user perceives:** Nothing visible today. This is upkeep: `UIScreen.main` is now formally deprecated, and the dead helpers describe a prefetch key scheme the app no longer uses, which invites someone to reintroduce mismatched keys.

**Mechanism (finder):** - `UIScreen.main.scale` is used at CachedImage.swift:130, 133 and PosterMetrics.swift:54, 63; `UIScreen.main.bounds` at PosterMetrics.swift:77.
- UIScreen.h:57 in the iPhoneSimulator26.0 SDK declares `mainScreen` API_DEPRECATED ios(2.0, 26.0) and points to trait collections.
- `prefetchCategoryDecodePixelSize()` and `prefetchShelfDecodePixelSize()` (PosterMetrics.swift:52-68) have no callers since commit 0ab5bcd moved prefetch onto CachedImage.request.

**Proposed fix (finder):** - Read the scale once from the trait system, the same way Nuke does (Nuke/Internal/Graphics.swift:327): `static let decodeScale = max(1, min(UITraitCollection.current.displayScale, 2))` in CachedImage, and the same with 3 for .high. It must be one shared value so that prefetch and render keys stay equal.
- Delete the two dead helpers in PosterMetrics.
- The `UIScreen.main.bounds` uses for layout (PosterMetrics.swift:77, DashboardView.swift:38, M3UDashboardView.swift:17) belong to the iPad adaptivity lens.
No iOS 26-only API; works on iOS 18.

**APIs:** UITraitCollection.displayScale (iOS 8+, UIKit.framework/Headers/UITraitCollection.h:48); UIScreen.main (deprecated) (API_DEPRECATED ios(2.0, 26.0), UIKit.framework/Headers/UIScreen.h:57); SwiftUI.EnvironmentValues.displayScale (alternative) (iOS 13+, SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:17074)

**Verifier reasons:** The facts are right, but half of the fix carries more risk than benefit and none of it is user-visible.

What holds:
- `UIScreen.main.scale` at Views/CachedImage.swift:129, 133 and Views/PosterMetrics.swift:54, 63; `UIScreen.main.bounds` at PosterMetrics.swift:77.
- UIKit.framework/Headers/UIScreen.h:57 declares `mainScreen` `API_DEPRECATED(..., ios(2.0, 26.0), ...)`.
- `prefetchCategoryDecodePixelSize()` and `prefetchShelfDecodePixelSize()` (PosterMetrics.swift:52-68) have no callers in the app, unit tests or UI tests. `git show 0ab5bcd -- Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift` shows their only call site being replaced by `CachedImage.request`.

What needs correcting:
- With the deployment target at 18.0 (project.pbxproj) the compiler emits no deprecation warning for an API deprecated in 26.0. Nothing changes for the user or the build today.
- The proposed `max(1, min(UITraitCollection.current.displayScale, 2))` is not equivalent. UITraitCollection.h:48 documents displayScale as "unspecified: 0.0" and `currentTraitCollection` is thread-local (UITraitCollection.h:238-240). If the static is first evaluated where the trait is unspecified, the clamp silently pins the whole session to 1x decode and every poster is blurry. `UIScreen.main.scale` cannot fail that way.
- Prefetch and render keys already share one code path (`CachedImage.request` -> `downsamplePixelSize`, CachedImage.swift:102-136), so the "one shared value" goal is already met.
- The dead helpers also hard-code `.aspectFill`-era assumptions; deleting them is safe and removes a trap.
- The finder's own verification step (temporarily raising the deployment target) would edit project.pbxproj, which carries the owner's uncommitted tip-jar changes.

**Corrected claim:** PosterMetrics carries two prefetch-size helpers that have had no callers since 0ab5bcd. Separately, the decode scale is read from `UIScreen.main`, which the iOS 26 SDK marks deprecated; with the deployment target at 18.0 this produces no warning and no behaviour change. Neither item affects what the user sees.

**Corrected fix:** 1. Delete `prefetchCategoryDecodePixelSize()` and `prefetchShelfDecodePixelSize()` from Views/PosterMetrics.swift (lines 52-68). Zero-risk.
2. Leave `UIScreen.main.scale` in CachedImage for now. Replace it when the deployment target moves to 26 or when the iPad-adaptivity work threads a real window/trait context through.
3. If it is replaced earlier, never clamp an unspecified scale up to 1: read `let s = UITraitCollection.current.displayScale` once on the main actor and use it only when `s > 0`, and add a unit test asserting it equals the screen scale on a 3x and a 2x simulator.
4. `UIScreen.main.bounds` (PosterMetrics.swift:77, DashboardView.swift:38, M3UDashboardView.swift:17) stays with the iPad-adaptivity lens.

**API check:** - UIKit.framework/Headers/UIScreen.h:57: `@property(class, nonatomic, readonly) UIScreen *mainScreen API_DEPRECATED("Use a UIScreen instance found through context instead ..., or for properties like UIScreen.scale with trait equivalents, use a traitCollection found through context.", ios(2.0, 26.0), tvos(9.0, 26.0), visionos(1.0, 26.0))`.
- UIKit.framework/Headers/UITraitCollection.h:48: `@property (nonatomic, readonly) CGFloat displayScale; // unspecified: 0.0`.
- UITraitCollection.h:240: `@property (class, nonatomic, strong) UITraitCollection *currentTraitCollection API_AVAILABLE(ios(13.0), tvos(13.0))`, documented thread-local at :238.
- SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:17074: `EnvironmentValues.displayScale: CGFloat`.
- Nuke uses the same trait read at Sources/Nuke/Internal/Graphics.swift:327.

**Regression risks:** - Deleting the helpers: none; no callers in any target.
- Replacing the scale source: if it resolves to 0 and is clamped to 1, all images decode at 1x for the session. If prefetch and render ever read different sources, the cache keys diverge and every image decodes twice, undoing the 0ab5bcd key-matching work.
- Do not verify by editing the deployment target in project.pbxproj; that file holds the owner's uncommitted tip-jar changes.

**How to verify:** - After deleting the helpers: the app and both test targets build; grep shows no remaining references.
- If the scale source is changed: unit test that `CachedImage.request(url:, width: 100, height: 150, contentMode: .fit, loadProfile: .grid)` carries a 200x300 px Resize on both a 3x and a 2x simulator, and that a ListImagePrefetch request for the same parameters produces an equal processor.
- To see the deprecation warning without touching the project file, pass IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=26.0 as a build-setting override on the xcodebuild command line.
