## swiftui-invalidation-1 — Pull-to-refresh on Live TV, Movies and Series updates the store but never the shelves, because the views recompute only when streamsLoaded flips and the scoped reload does not flip it

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Live/Movies/Series category detail, All Channels / All Movies / All Series, Search results
- Code: `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:210-220, 234-278 (scoped reload, streamsLoaded untouched) vs 287-318 (full reload toggles it)`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17, 105-107, 247, 509, 734`, `Views/VODView.swift:29-31, 97, 157-159, 575, 834`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:30-32, 98, 158-160, 547, 773`, `Views/SearchView.swift:246-248`

**What the user perceives:** The user pulls down on Live TV / Movies / Series, the spinner runs for the whole network sync (seconds on a big panel), and when it ends the screen is exactly as before: newly added channels, films or categories do not appear until the app is relaunched, a category is hidden/unhidden, or a search is typed. Pull-to-refresh feels broken.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each home view renders from a @State snapshot (displayCategories / displayItemsByCategory, LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17) that is rebuilt only by .task(id: debouncedQuery), .task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded) and .task(id: hiddenIds) (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107; VODView.swift:157-159; SeriesView.swift:158-160). The refreshable action calls refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only:) (LiveStreamsView.swift:247), whose reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) replaces liveCategories/liveStreams/liveStreamsByCategoryId (PlaylistContentStore.swift:247-249, 259-261, 271-273) but never touches streamsLoaded. The body re-evaluates (the store published) but none of the three task ids changed, so recomputeFilter() does not run and the Equatable shelf rows compare equal. The same key is used by the pushed category/All screens (LiveStreamsView.swift:509, 734; VODView.swift:575, 834; SeriesView.swift:547, 773) and by SearchResultsView (SearchView.swift:248). The full reload used by Settings ▸ Refresh all works only because reloadFromDatabase sets streamsLoaded false then true (PlaylistContentStore.swift:295, 317). The scoped variant arrived in 1cce013 (git log -S'only type: CatalogContentType'); no test covers it (grep of another-iptv-playerTests finds no refreshFromNetwork/streamsLoaded).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give the store an O(1) per-type change signal and key the tasks on it instead of on the boolean. PlaylistContentStore: add `@Published private(set) var liveRevision = 0` (and vodRevision, seriesRevision), bumped as the LAST assignment wherever that type's arrays are replaced (loadPlaylist phase 2, reloadFromDatabase, the three scoped cases, clearLists). Views: replace `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` with `.task(id: CatalogToken(loaded: contentStore.streamsLoaded, revision: contentStore.liveRevision))` where `struct CatalogToken: Equatable { let loaded: Bool; let revision: Int }` (12 call sites listed above; SearchResultsView keys on the sum of the three). Bump once per reload, after the arrays are in place, so recompute runs once on the final data. Do not 'fix' it by toggling streamsLoaded in the scoped path: that would flip isStreamsLoading on every shelf (LiveStreamsView.swift:235) and re-render all of them twice. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166))

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed from code. The three home views render from @State snapshots rebuilt only by .task(id: debouncedQuery / contentStore.streamsLoaded / hiddenIds) (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, Views/VODView.swift:157-159, Views/SeriesView.swift:158-160). The refreshable action calls refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only:) (LiveStreamsView.swift:247, VODView.swift:97, SeriesView.swift:98), whose scoped reload replaces the categories/streams/byCategory arrays (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:247-249, 259-261, 271-273) and never touches streamsLoaded; the full reload does toggle it (295, 317). So after a pull none of the three task ids changes, recomputeFilter() does not run, and the Equatable shelf rows keep the old items. History: the scoped variant came in 1cce013 (2026-07-24); before it the full path toggled the flag, so this is a regression, not a deliberate choice. No test references PlaylistContentStore at all (grep of another-iptv-playerTests and UITests is empty).

Corrections: (1) 'until the app is relaunched' is overstated. .task is tied to appearance, so the stale snapshot is rebuilt the next time the home view re-appears (switching tab and back, or pushing a category and popping). The visible defect is 'spinner ends, nothing changes until the user navigates away and back' - still a correctness bug but shorter-lived than claimed. Not run on a simulator; reasoned from .task lifecycle. (2) Scope: only the three home screens have .refreshable; category/All grids and Search are affected only if they are on screen when a refresh started earlier lands. (3) There are 10 .task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded) sites (3 Live, 3 Movies, 3 Series, 1 Search), not 12. (4) The proposed unit test cannot be written as described: PlaylistContentStore has a private init and reads AppDatabase.shared directly.

**Corrected claim:** After a pull-to-refresh on Live TV, Movies or Series the store holds the new catalog but the shelves on screen keep the old snapshot, because the scoped reload does not change any of the three .task ids. The screen catches up only when the view re-appears (tab switch, push and pop), when a category is hidden/unhidden, or when a search is typed. Pushed category/All grids and Search results are affected only when a refresh lands while they are showing. Regression from 1cce013; untested.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: add per-type revision counters to PlaylistContentStore (@Published private(set) var liveRevision/vodRevision/seriesRevision), bumped as the last assignment wherever that type's arrays are replaced (loadPlaylist phase 2, reloadFromDatabase, the three scoped cases, clearLists), and key the 10 .task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded) sites on an Equatable token of (streamsLoaded, revision); Search keys on all three. Do not bump in applyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:164-178), otherwise every first open of a movie detail would recompute the Movies home. Do not toggle streamsLoaded in the scoped path (it flips isStreamsLoading on every shelf, LiveStreamsView.swift:235, and flashes Search's loading state, SearchView.swift:225). Known remaining limit, deliberate and unchanged: the grids' cheap signature (count + first + last id, LiveStreamsView.swift:534-539 and 555-561) will not notice a refresh that changes only middle items of a pushed grid.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:) found at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166, @available(iOS 15.0, ...), requires T: Equatable - a small Equatable token struct is valid. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Each scoped reload triggers one extra recompute of the affected tab (off-main filtering already in place). If the revision is bumped before the arrays are assigned, the recompute reads old data - it must be the last assignment. Bumping in applyVODMetadata would add a recompute per movie-detail open. Three more @Published properties add no extra view updates because they change in the same turn as the arrays.

**How to verify:** UI test with the mock fixture: insert a liveStream row for the demo playlist, pull to refresh on Live TV, assert the new card exists without leaving the screen (today it should appear only after switching tab and back - check that too, it confirms the corrected scope). A unit test needs either AppDatabase.shared pointed at a test database or an injectable database in the store; as written the store cannot be built against an in-memory database.

## swiftui-invalidation-2 — Fifteen browse views subscribe to PlayerOverlayController with @EnvironmentObject although they only call present()/dismiss(), so every player open, minimize, expand and close re-evaluates every mounted browse screen in the first frame of the player animation

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Series detail, Movie detail, Search, Favorites, Downloads, EPG guide, M3U channels, Mini player dock/expand
- Code: `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:17-22, 54-55, 75, 91, 98`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:124, 182`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:9, 472, 693`, `Views/VODView.swift:9`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:11, 800, 1053-1063, 1319-1328`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:19`, `Views/SearchView.swift:138`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:10`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:9`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:8`, `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:15`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:10, 491`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:12`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a channel or episode, pulling the player down into the mini card, expanding it and closing it all start with a small stutter, and the stutter grows with how much is mounted underneath: worst on a series detail with a long season open, or after several tabs have been visited.

**Mechanism (finder):** ObservableObject has no per-property tracking: @EnvironmentObject invalidates the view on every objectWillChange whether or not body reads anything. A grep for `playerOverlay.` outside DashboardView/M3UDashboardView finds only present(...) and dismiss() calls (no view reads presentation, mode or pendingPresentation), so the subscription is pure cost. present() publishes twice (PlayerOverlayController.swift:54-55), minimize/expand/dismiss once each (75, 91, 98). Each publish re-runs the body of LiveStreamsView, VODView, SeriesView (every visited tab stays mounted in the TabView), SearchResultsView, and whatever is pushed: MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView, FavoritesView, category screens, EPGGuideView. SeriesDetailView is the expensive one: its body hands EpisodesPanel a fresh closure (SeriesView.swift:1053-1063), EpisodesPanel hands each EpisodeDetailRow a fresh closure (1319-1328), so every materialized episode row (CachedImage + DownloadButton with a material background) re-evaluates. All of that lands in the same transaction that starts the 0.14 s overlay fade or the mini-card morph.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Hand the controller to browse views as a plain environment value, which does not subscribe. Add next to the existing keys: `private struct PlayerOverlayControllerKey: EnvironmentKey { static let defaultValue: PlayerOverlayController? = nil }` plus `var playerOverlayController: PlayerOverlayController?` on EnvironmentValues. DashboardView/M3UDashboardView: `.environment(\.playerOverlayController, playerOverlay)` (a class reference compares by pointer, so the value is stable across root re-evaluations). In the 15 sites replace `@EnvironmentObject private var playerOverlay: PlayerOverlayController` with `@Environment(\.playerOverlayController) private var playerOverlay` and call `playerOverlay?.present(...)`. The controller class itself is not changed. Side benefit: the explicit re-injection for the Downloads sheet (DashboardView.swift:182) and the 'No ObservableObject found' crash class go away, since custom environment values flow into sheets. Larger alternative, same effect: make the controller @Observable (iOS 17+, below the iOS 18 target, no fallback needed) and read it with @Environment(PlayerOverlayController.self); that touches the out-of-scope controller file and DashboardView's @StateObject, so I would not start there.

**APIs:** EnvironmentKey / EnvironmentValues custom key (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12560)); @Observable macro (alternative only) (iOS 17.0+ (Observation.swiftinterface:11)); View.environment(_:) for Observable objects (alternative only) (iOS 17.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:14667))

**Verifier reasons:** Subscription facts confirmed. 15 @EnvironmentObject PlayerOverlayController declarations exist (grep: DownloadsView:9, FavoritesView:10, MovieDetailView:19, SearchView:138, LiveStreamsView:9/472/693, VODView:9, M3UChannelsView:10/491, EPGProgrammeDetailSheet:15, EPGGuideView:8, M3UFavoritesView:12, SeriesView:11/800). All reads of presentation/mode/pendingPresentation are in DashboardView and M3UDashboardView (7 + 6 + 1 hits, all accounted for there); the other views only call present()/dismiss(). @EnvironmentObject invalidates its view on every objectWillChange regardless of what body reads, so each overlay publish re-runs those bodies. No out-of-scope player file uses the environment object, so the injection can be replaced.

Corrections: (1) present() assigns two @Published properties in the same main-thread turn (PlayerOverlayController.swift:54-55); SwiftUI coalesces them into one update, so it is one body run per view per event, not two. (2) The 'side benefit' is wrong: .sheet at DashboardView.swift:173 is attached outside the injection at line 124, so the sheet content does not see it - that is why line 182 re-injects. A custom environment value has the same scoping; dropping line 182 would give DownloadsView nil. (3) With an optional key, a missing injection turns today's loud crash into a silent no-op tap (playerOverlay?.present does nothing). (4) LiveStreamsView will still re-evaluate after this fix: DashboardView owns the @StateObject and re-runs on every overlay publish, and LiveStreamsView never compares equal because its @State initial value is a new class instance per init (LiveStreamsView.swift:25, class at 1220). So 'after it none do' in how_to_verify is wrong for LiveStreamsView unless finding 3 part 4 is also done. (5) SeriesDetailView writes selectedEpisode on tap and in the onDismiss callback (SeriesView.swift:916, 1061), so present/dismiss may re-run it anyway; the gain there is mainly minimize/expand. (6) Perceptibility is not shown: row views short-circuit (.equatable(), Array == identity fast path), so the cost is a handful of home/detail bodies plus the materialized episode rows. 'Stutter' is plausible on a long season but unmeasured.

**Corrected claim:** Fifteen browse views subscribe to PlayerOverlayController through @EnvironmentObject although they only call present()/dismiss(), so each player open, minimize, expand and close re-runs the body of every mounted subscriber once (the two publishes in present() coalesce). The cost is real but small per view; the largest is a series detail with a long season open, where every materialized episode row re-evaluates. Whether it produces a visible hitch has to be measured.

**Corrected fix:** Custom environment key as proposed (PlayerOverlayControllerKey with an optional class value; 15 declarations become @Environment(\.playerOverlayController)), with three changes: (a) keep the Downloads-sheet injection at DashboardView.swift:182, rewritten as .environment(\.playerOverlayController, playerOverlay) - it cannot be dropped; (b) do not let a missing injection fail silently: route calls through a small helper that does assertionFailure in debug when the value is nil; (c) pair it with making LivePlaybackModelMemo a @StateObject (see finding 3), otherwise Live TV home keeps re-evaluating on every overlay event. .environmentObject(playerOverlay) at DashboardView.swift:124 and M3UDashboardView.swift:83 can then be removed (nothing else reads it). No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** EnvironmentKey: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12560, @available(iOS 13.0). Its default _valuesEqual (iOS 16+, 12566-12573) is used for non-Equatable values; an Optional class reference compares by pointer, so the value is stable across root re-evaluations. Environment<Value>.init(_ keyPath:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:11450/11458, iOS 13.0. View.environment(_:_:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3096, iOS 13.0. EnvironmentObject struct at 4686 (the line the finding cited for something else in finding 4).

**Regression risks:** A screen reached without the injection (the Downloads sheet if line 182 is dropped, or any future sheet attached outside the dashboard ZStack) would silently ignore play taps instead of crashing. No change to the controller class or to PlayerView identity. Views that are presented as sheets from inside the TabView (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet) inherit the value as they inherit the object today.

**How to verify:** Self._printChanges() in VODView, SeriesView, SeriesDetailView, MovieDetailView: no prints on minimize/expand after the change (LiveStreamsView still prints until the memo is a @StateObject). Instruments SwiftUI template, View Body count in the minimize transaction over a 50-episode season, before and after, to decide whether the gain is perceptible. UI test: start playback from the Downloads sheet opened via the download-warning alert, to prove the sheet injection still works.

## swiftui-invalidation-3 — DashboardView observes the whole catalog store and the whole EPG store at the root and rebuilds the player's environment closures on every evaluation, so tab switches, EPG minute ticks and catalog publishes re-run the docked player's body

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Tab switching with the mini player docked, Live TV home, Dashboard root, M3U dashboard
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:6-8, 26-34, 46-124, 130, 138-155`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:8-11, 58-64, 84, 91-108`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:25, 1219-1228`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:16-32, 197-199, 212-214`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:49-51, 163-167, 463-470`, `Views/PlayerView.swift:218-222 (readers of the closures; hand-off reference only)`

**What the user perceives:** With a channel playing in the mini card, switching tabs is not as crisp as without it; once a minute, and whenever a movie detail finishes loading or a pull-to-refresh progresses, there is a small hitch even though nothing visible changes.

**Mechanism (finder):** DashboardView.body re-evaluates for (a) any of the 15 @Published properties of PlaylistContentStore (DashboardView.swift:6) although it renders only the load-error alert (138-155): during pull-to-refresh the three loadingMessage publishes (PlaylistContentStore.swift:212-219) are rendered nowhere because the shelves are on screen; (b) any EPGStore publish (line 7): the minute snapshot (EPGStore.swift:163-167), four or five refreshState phases and lastSuccess per guide refresh (463-470), of which it needs only snapshot (line 130); (c) every tab switch, because tabBinding's getter reads selectedTab and the setter writes @AppStorage savedTab (26-34). Each evaluation creates new closures for \.playerOverlayDismiss / Minimize / Expand (98-104). Closures do not compare equal, so the environment readers in PlayerViewImpl (PlayerView.swift:218-222) are invalidated and the player's large body runs, which is exactly what last week's rework avoids for playback ticks. Each evaluation also resolves 17 L() strings and re-evaluates LiveStreamsView: its `@State private var playbackModelMemo = LivePlaybackModelMemo()` (LiveStreamsView.swift:25) allocates a new class instance in every init, so the view value should never compare equal to the previous one (verify with _printChanges; VODView/SeriesView have only value-type state and are skipped). Typing in Search does not hit the root: only $globalSearchText is used (line 79), keep that.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Move each observation to the smallest thing that renders it; DashboardView keeps only the @StateObject. (1) `private struct EPGSnapshotEnvironment: ViewModifier { @ObservedObject private var epgStore = EPGStore.shared; func body(content: Content) -> some View { content.environment(\.epgSnapshot, epgStore.snapshot) } }` replaces lines 7 and 130; refreshState publishes then re-run a one-line modifier and nothing below it (EPGSnapshot == is a version compare). (2) `CatalogLoadErrorAlert: ViewModifier` owning `@ObservedObject contentStore` and the alert of lines 138-155; DashboardView calls PlaylistContentStore.shared directly in .task. (3) Move the TabView with selectedTab, savedTab and globalSearchText into a child `DashboardTabs(playlist:onDismiss:)`, and the inner overlay ZStack (lines 92-122, verbatim, so PlayerView's identity rules in the comments stay true) into `PlayerOverlayHost` with `@ObservedObject var controller`. Tab switches then re-run only DashboardTabs; the three closures are rebuilt only when the overlay itself publishes, when the player must update anyway. (4) LiveStreamsView: create the memo without changing the view value, e.g. keep one box per playlist in a static cache or make it a lazily filled property of a small @StateObject. Same split for M3UDashboardView. Alternative for (1)+(2): convert PlaylistContentStore/EPGStore to @Observable (iOS 17+) for per-property tracking; larger change, same result for the root.

**APIs:** ViewModifier with DynamicProperty members (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:15360)); View.environment(_:_:) (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface)); @Observable macro (alternative only) (iOS 17.0+ (Observation.swiftinterface:11))

**Verifier reasons:** Confirmed parts: DashboardView observes the whole PlaylistContentStore and EPGStore (Views/DashboardView.swift:6-7) but renders only the load-error alert (138-155) and passes the snapshot (130). Each body run builds new closures for \.playerOverlayDismiss/Minimize/Expand (98-104); they capture self and item, and EnvironmentKey's default _valuesEqual cannot treat a freshly allocated closure context as equal, so PlayerViewImpl's readers (Views/PlayerView.swift:218-222) are invalidated on every DashboardView evaluation while a player is mounted. LiveStreamsView's @State initial value is a new instance of a final class per init (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:25, 1220-1228), so the view value differs on every parent evaluation. M3UDashboardView has the same shape (8-10, 58-64, 84).

Corrections: (1) PlayerViewImpl reads \.epgSnapshot itself (PlayerView.swift:225), so the minute tick re-runs it whatever the dashboard does; the 'after: none print for EPG ticks' expectation is wrong for the player and cannot be met from in-scope files. (2) The cost is one PlayerViewImpl body plus one LiveStreamsView body per tab switch / catalog publish while a player is docked. That is low; the finding's own wording is 'small hitch'. No measurement supports a perceptible difference. (3) Tab switch re-running DashboardView.body rests on selectedTab being read through the Binding getter and the @AppStorage write; likely, but confirm with _printChanges. (4) The proposed four-part restructure is larger than needed and moves code that carries explicit identity warnings (DashboardView.swift:105-121).

**Corrected claim:** While a player is mounted, every DashboardView evaluation (tab switch, any catalog-store publish such as pull-to-refresh progress or movie metadata, any EPG-store publish) rebuilds the three overlay closures and so re-runs the player's body once; Live TV home also re-evaluates each time because its memo @State defeats value comparison. The per-minute EPG tick re-runs the player anyway through its own snapshot read. Impact is small and unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest change that removes the mechanism: (a) move the inner overlay ZStack (DashboardView.swift:92-121, verbatim, same modifier order) into a small PlayerOverlayHost view with @ObservedObject var controller; keep .zIndex(10_000) at the call site. DashboardView re-evaluations then produce an equal host value and the closures are rebuilt only when the controller itself publishes. Same in M3UDashboardView. (b) Make LivePlaybackModelMemo conform to ObservableObject (no @Published) and hold it with @StateObject, so LiveStreamsView compares equal; a tap-time fill still does not invalidate the view. Optional and lower value: the EPGSnapshotEnvironment and CatalogLoadErrorAlert modifiers and a DashboardTabs child, which only reduce how often the now-cheap root body runs. The @Observable conversion of the stores is not needed.

**API check:** ViewModifier protocol: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:15360 (iOS 13.0). View.environment(_:_:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3096 (iOS 13.0). EnvironmentKey._valuesEqual default and Equatable-constrained variants: 12563-12580 (iOS 16.0) - closures fall to the default comparison, EPGSnapshot? uses its version-only ==. StateObject: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:14575, storage .initially(() -> ObjectType) (14578) - a capture-free initializer thunk compares equal across inits, which is what makes (b) work. @Observable not needed.

**Regression risks:** The overlay host sits next to deliberate PlayerView identity rules (no if/else around item.root, unconditional ignoresSafeArea, animation keyed on presentation != nil). Moving it must be verbatim; a changed modifier order or a conditional wrapper would remount PlayerView and tear playback or AirPlay down. zIndex must stay effective on the ZStack child. The memo change must keep 'fill from a tap does not invalidate' (LiveStreamsView.swift:1218-1219) - true as long as the class publishes nothing.

**How to verify:** Debug build with Self._printChanges() in DashboardView, LiveStreamsView and PlayerViewImpl: dock the mini player, switch tabs, pull to refresh, open a movie detail for the first time. Before: all three print; after: DashboardView may still print, LiveStreamsView and PlayerViewImpl must not (PlayerViewImpl will still print at minute boundaries because of its own snapshot read). Then the 30 existing UI tests plus a manual check of open, minimize, expand, source switch and AirPlay continuity. Instruments body counts for PlayerViewImpl during a tab switch decide whether this was worth doing.

## swiftui-invalidation-4 — Every channel card reads the EPG snapshot itself, so the once-a-minute snapshot swap re-evaluates the full body of every card the lazy stacks keep alive

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category detail, All Channels, Favorites (Live), M3U channels, M3U group detail
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:408-445, 446-451`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:163-167, 389-392`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:27-35, 41-80`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:62-98`

**What the user perceives:** On Live TV screens there is a short hitch at every minute boundary (and again when a guide refresh or the short-EPG fallback finishes). It is barely noticeable on the home shelves and becomes a visible dropped-frame burst after scrolling far into a long channel grid.

**Mechanism (finder):** EPGStore publishes a new EPGSnapshot every minute on purpose so the progress capsules advance (EPGStore.swift:163-167). LiveStreamCard and M3UChannelCard declare @Environment(\.epgSnapshot) on the card (LiveStreamsView.swift:427; M3UChannelsView.swift:415), so the invalidated unit is the whole card: Button, CachedImage (a new ImageRequest plus Resize processor per body, CachedImage.swift:66, 96-98), the name Text, and EPGChannelKey.forXtream (trim + lowercased allocation, EPGComponents.swift:28-30). This happens for every card that exists, not only visible ones; the code base already records that lazy stacks keep thousands of cards alive (M3UChannelsView.swift:446-451, the reason the favourites store is not observed per card). The paginated grids grow by 90 cards per page, so a scrolled All Channels grid re-runs hundreds to thousands of full card bodies in one frame, once a minute. Cards of channels without guide data pay the same although their output cannot change.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the per-minute publish (it is deliberate) and shrink what it invalidates: move the environment read into a leaf. `struct EPGNowNextSlot: View { let channelKey: String?; let width: CGFloat; @Environment(\.epgSnapshot) private var snapshot; var body: some View { if let snapshot { EPGNowNextLine(nowNext: snapshot[channelKey], width: width, reserveSpace: true) } } }` and in both cards delete the @Environment property and replace the `if let snapshot` block with `EPGNowNextSlot(channelKey: EPGChannelKey.forXtream(stream), width: width)` (forM3U in the M3U card). A snapshot swap then re-runs only the leaf (one dictionary lookup, a Text and two capsules) and the card body, image request included, is untouched. FavoritesView reuses LiveStreamCard and benefits automatically. No behaviour change.

**APIs:** @Environment(\.keyPath) in a leaf view (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4686))

**Verifier reasons:** LiveStreamCard and M3UChannelCard declare @Environment(\.epgSnapshot) on the card (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:427, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:415). EPGStore publishes a new snapshot version every minute on purpose (EPG/EPGStore.swift:163-167) and EPGSnapshot equality is version-only (EPG/EPGModels.swift:138), so every card that exists re-runs its whole body once a minute, and again after ensureShortEPG or a guide refresh. The code base itself records that lazy stacks keep thousands of cards alive (M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450). Other readers of the key are the player and ChannelEPGDetailView only.

Two detail corrections that do not change the fix: (1) the 'new ImageRequest plus Resize per body' cost is not supported: the request is built in CachedImage.body (Views/CachedImage.swift:66, 96-98), not in the card body, and a CachedImage with unchanged inputs is not expected to re-run. (2) The M3U card is the more expensive one, for a reason the finding missed: .contextMenu's builder is non-escaping and runs during body, so each minute every alive M3U card also runs M3UParser.sanitizedURL and M3UStreamClassifier.classify (M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475). The cited SDK line for Environment (4686) is actually EnvironmentObject; Environment is at 11450.

**Corrected claim:** Every channel card reads the EPG snapshot itself, so the per-minute snapshot swap re-runs the full body of every card the lazy stacks keep alive; on M3U cards that includes the eagerly built context menu (URL sanitizing and stream classification per card). The cost grows with how far the user has scrolled; a visible hitch at the minute boundary is plausible on long lists but unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: move the read into a leaf, EPGNowNextSlot(channelKey:width:) with @Environment(\.epgSnapshot), rendering EPGNowNextLine(nowNext: snapshot[channelKey], width: width, reserveSpace: true) only when the snapshot is non-nil; delete the property from both cards and pass EPGChannelKey.forXtream(stream) / forM3U(channel). An empty leaf contributes no child to the VStack, so spacing and height are unchanged in the nil case.

**API check:** Environment<Value> property wrapper: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:11450, init(_ keyPath:) at 11458, @available(iOS 13.0). contextMenu(menuItems:) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9870 takes a non-escaping () -> MenuItems builder, confirming it runs with the card body. No iOS 26 API.

**Regression risks:** None for layout. One thing to check rather than assume: the progress capsule computes its fraction from Date() inside EPGNowNextLine.body (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:73) while the line's inputs can be equal between ticks; confirm the capsule still advances each minute before and after the change (the leaf keeps today's behaviour either way). FavoritesView reuses LiveStreamCard and follows automatically.

**How to verify:** Self._printChanges() or a signpost counter in LiveStreamCard.body and M3UChannelCard.body: scroll All Channels several pages, wait for a minute boundary; before, one line per alive card, after, none. Instruments Hitches around the boundary on a device with a real guide while scrolling. Watch one capsule across two minute boundaries to confirm it still moves.

## swiftui-invalidation-5 — Live shelves grow by 32 pt per row when the first EPG snapshot replaces nil, shortly after the catalog appears, on every launch of a playlist that has a guide

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category detail, M3U channels
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397, 451-454`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:439-442`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:83-100, 159-162`, `EPG/EPGModels.swift:145`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:130-137`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:84-90`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:48-51, 66-68`

**What the user perceives:** Live TV opens, the channel shelves appear, and a moment later every shelf gets taller and everything below the first row shifts down as the programme line pops in. It reads as a layout jump right when the user starts to scroll.

**Mechanism (finder):** The card adds the now/next line only when the environment snapshot is non-nil (`if let snapshot = epgSnapshot`, LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454); with nil there is no reserved space, which is what iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows (labels directly followed by the next shelf header). The Live shelf has no fixed height (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397; the Movies shelf does, VODView.swift:467), so the line adds reservedHeight 22 + spacing 10 to every row. The snapshot is nil at launch and is reset to nil in setActivePlaylist (EPGStore.swift:88), which DashboardView calls only after loadPlaylist has finished both phases (DashboardView.swift:131-135); the first tick then needs loadSourceStatus plus rebuildResolution (reads every liveStream row, every epgChannel row and DISTINCT channelKey over epgProgramme, EPGStore.swift:211-245) before it publishes. So the shelves are on screen with the short layout for a few hundred milliseconds to a second, then all jump. EPGNowNextLine already takes care that placeholder and populated line have the same height (EPGComponents.swift:48-51); the gap is only the nil phase.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Publish a non-nil placeholder as soon as a guide is expected, so the line is reserved from the first frame the shelves render. EPGStore.setActivePlaylist: instead of `snapshot = nil` use `snapshot = Self.expectsGuide(playlist) ? .empty : nil` (EPGSnapshot.empty already exists, EPGModels.swift:145, and is unused), with `expectsGuide` = xtream && epgEnabled, or m3u && effectiveEPGURL != nil; in tick() keep the placeholder instead of nil for the `dict.isEmpty && !configured` case when expectsGuide is true (EPGStore.swift:159-162). DashboardView/M3UDashboardView: call `epgStore.setActivePlaylist(playlist)` before `await contentStore.loadPlaylist(playlist)`; keep refreshIfStale after the load as today (its comment about the wanted-channel set still holds; reload() only reads). Playlists without a guide keep the compact layout. Version 0 → 1 still invalidates the cards once, but with no geometry change.

**APIs:** none beyond existing project types (EPGSnapshot.empty) (n/a)

**Verifier reasons:** The jump is real. Cards add the now/next line only when the environment snapshot is non-nil (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:439-442), the Live shelf has no fixed height (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397), and EPGStore.setActivePlaylist sets snapshot = nil (EPG/EPGStore.swift:88) then needs loadSourceStatus + rebuildResolution (full liveStream, epgChannel and DISTINCT epgProgramme reads, 211-245) + the first tick before publishing. The dashboard calls it right after loadPlaylist returns (Views/DashboardView.swift:131-135), so cards render compact, then every row grows by 22 + 10 pt. EPGSnapshot.empty exists and is unused (EPG/EPGModels.swift:145). The screenshot iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows the compact layout, consistent with a nil snapshot; it does not show the jump itself.

Corrections: (1) Scope is wider than 'a playlist that has a guide'. recordAttempt writes an epgSource row on the first refresh attempt, success or not (EPG/EPGRefreshCoordinator.swift:36, 280-287), and configured is true whenever that row exists (EPGStore.swift:106-111). So from the second launch on, every Xtream playlist with EPG enabled (the default, Models/Playlist.swift:23) publishes a non-nil, possibly empty snapshot and jumps, guide data or not. (2) The reorder is not needed and has a cost: loadPlaylist ends with streamsLoaded = true and returns to the same main-actor task with no suspension before setActivePlaylist runs, so a placeholder set inside setActivePlaylist already lands in the same update as the cards. Calling it before loadPlaylist would build the alias map before a first-run catalog bootstrap has written liveStream rows, and contradicts the comment at DashboardView.swift:133-134. (3) 'Playlists without a guide keep the compact layout' and 'must stay identical to L01' do not hold for the demo playlist or any Xtream playlist with EPG enabled: they will reserve the blank line from the first launch (today they get it from the second).

**Corrected claim:** On every launch of an Xtream playlist with EPG enabled (after the first refresh attempt), and of an M3U playlist with a guide URL, the Live shelves render compact and then every row grows by 32 pt when the first snapshot replaces nil, a few hundred milliseconds after the cards appear - whether or not the guide has data.

**Corrected fix:** Change only EPGStore: in setActivePlaylist use snapshot = expectsGuide(playlist) ? .empty : nil, with expectsGuide = (xtream && epgEnabled) || (m3u && effectiveEPGURL != nil), remember that flag, and in tick() leave the placeholder in place instead of assigning nil in the 'dict.isEmpty && !configured' branch when the flag is true. Keep the call order in DashboardView and M3UDashboardView as it is. Optional follow-up: the streams-loading placeholder height (LiveStreamsView.swift:374, icon + 30) is shorter than a populated row, so rows still change height once when the cards arrive; passing a 'reserves guide line' Bool into the Equatable row would let it match (do not make the row read the snapshot, that would re-run every shelf each minute). Product decision for the owner: whether a playlist whose guide never loaded should carry the blank line at all; the fix keeps today's steady-state behaviour.

**API check:** No SDK API involved; EPGSnapshot.empty (EPG/EPGModels.swift:145, version 0) and the existing \.epgSnapshot key only. Equality is version-only, so setting .empty repeatedly does not invalidate, and the first real tick (version >= 1) invalidates the cards once with no geometry change.

**Regression risks:** Xtream playlists with EPG enabled and no source row yet (first launch, mock fixture) change from compact to reserved-line layout immediately, so UI-test screenshots of the demo Live shelves change. Readers that index the snapshot (PlayerView.swift:230, LiveStreamsView.swift:1056/1066, EPGStore.swift:382) behave the same with an empty dictionary; nothing treats non-nil as 'guide loaded'. If the early call before loadPlaylist were kept as originally proposed, first-run alias resolution could be built against an empty liveStream table.

**How to verify:** Seed a guide for the mock playlist, then in a UI test record the frame of the second shelf header when the first card appears and again 3 s later; y must not change (today it moves by 32 pt). Repeat on a second launch with EPG enabled but no programme rows to confirm the wider scope. Check the same on the M3U channels screen. Confirm with a playlist that has EPG switched off that the layout stays compact.

## swiftui-invalidation-6 — Opening a movie detail for the first time copies the whole movie catalog on the main thread and invalidates every catalog observer, and the mutation does not even reach the shelves it was written for

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Movies home, All Movies, Dashboard root
- Code: `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:27, 31, 161-178`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:33-35, 74-76, 99-103, 303-306`, `Views/VODView.swift:157-159, 556, 575, 596-599, 616`, `Models/DBModels.swift:DBVODStream (20 stored fields) and VODWithCategory at 180-184`

**What the user perceives:** On a large catalog, a movie detail that is opened for the first time hitches at the moment its plot, cast and backdrop arrive (a few dropped frames; noticeable if the user is already scrolling or swiping back). Shelves are not re-rendered, but everything observing the store re-evaluates.

**Mechanism (finder):** fetchMovieInfo ends with PlaylistContentStore.shared.applyVODMetadata(saved) on the main actor (MovieDetailView.swift:303-306). Inside, `vodStreams.firstIndex(where:)` is a linear scan and `vodStreams[i] = ...` goes through @Published's get/set, so the array is copied in full while the wrapper still holds the old buffer: about 312 bytes per VODWithCategory (20 fields in DBVODStream plus categoryName), i.e. roughly 47 MB allocated, copied with a retain per heap string and the old buffer released, for 150k movies. I estimate 20-40 ms on the main thread; then the bucket array and the category dictionary are copied the same way (PlaylistContentStore.swift:170-176). The two objectWillChange emissions re-run DashboardView, LiveStreamsView, VODView, SeriesView, SearchResultsView and any pushed category/All screen. Answer to the audit question: no shelf re-renders, because shelves render from @State snapshots keyed on streamsLoaded and are Equatable (VODView.swift:157-159, 400-411) and the grid has the signature compare added for this storm (596-599). For the same reason the stated purpose (comment at PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-163: avoid a refetch and spinner flash on re-entry) is not served for shelf and grid entries: they keep passing the pre-mutation copy with metadataLoaded == false (VODView.swift:452, 693). Only paths that read the store at tap time see the update.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Decide from the database row instead of mutating the catalog. MovieDetailView: `.task { let pid = playlist.id, sid = movie.streamId; let stored = try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in try DBVODStream.filter(Column("streamId") == sid && Column("playlistId") == pid).fetchOne(db) }; if stored?.metadataLoaded != true { await fetchMovieInfo() } }` and delete the applyVODMetadata call and function. The point lookup is the same one VODByIDRequest already runs; isLoading is only set inside fetchMovieInfo, so there is no spinner flash on re-entry, and this works for every entry point including shelves. If an in-memory hint is still wanted, keep a non-published `private var vodMetadataLoadedIds = Set<Int>()` in the store (O(1), no publish, cleared in clearLists). Either way the O(n) copy and the store-wide invalidation disappear. This replaces earlier deliberate work with something that meets its stated goal more completely; nothing visible is lost because shelves never showed the patched copy.

**APIs:** GRDB QueryInterfaceRequest.fetchOne(_:) via AppDatabase.read (GRDB checkout, already used at Models/Requests.swift:256-259); View.task(priority:_:) (iOS 15.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5163))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-178, Views/MovieDetailView.swift:20-35, 72-103, 268-313, Views/VODView.swift:28-31, 157-159, 165-190, 400-411, 548-604, Models/DBModels.swift:36-63, Database/AppDatabase.swift:55-66. (1) Cost: vodStreams is @Published (PlaylistContentStore.swift:27); `vodStreams[i] = ...` goes through the wrapper's get/set, so the temporary shares the buffer with the stored value and the element write triggers a full copy-on-write of the array, then the old buffer is destroyed, all on the main actor (MovieDetailView.swift:303-306). DBVODStream has 21 stored fields (about 312 bytes) plus categoryName, so the estimate of roughly 45-50 MB copied for 150k films is right in order of magnitude; I could not measure the 20-40 ms figure but it is plausible. The bucket copy is one category; the dictionary copy is only as large as the number of categories, i.e. negligible (the finding overstates that part). (2) Invalidation: every @ObservedObject of the store re-runs body; the owner already met this storm, see the comment at VODView.swift:596-599 ('applyVODMetadata's @Published storm ... froze All Movies for seconds'), and mitigated it at the grid. (3) Stated purpose not served: the home shelves render from @State snapshots filled only in recomputeFilter (VODView.swift:165-179, re-run only on streamsLoaded / query / hidden changes), and VODCategoryDetailView.displayItems is filled only in recomputeItems (VODView.swift:575-588). So a mounted shelf or grid keeps handing MovieDetailView the pre-mutation copy with metadataLoaded == false; only newly pushed category/All screens and new searches read the patched store. Extra point the finding did not make: on re-entry with a stale copy, whether the detail refetches depends on a race between the first value of @Query<VODByIDRequest> (asynchronous ValueObservation, Requests.swift:254-263; GRDBQuery Tracker stores it when it arrives, Query.swift:300-318) and `.task` (MovieDetailView.swift:99-103). If .task wins, the network call, the DB update and the whole-catalog copy run again on every open, not only the first; code alone cannot say which wins. History: applyVODMetadata was added in 0ab5bcd (bulk '95 findings' commit) and is called from exactly one place. The mutation is deliberate earlier work, but the proposed replacement meets its documented goal for every entry point, so removing it does not undo an optimisation. Nothing else depends on the patched in-memory copy: VODSortOption sorts by name, rating and added, not by metadata-only fields.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands. Refinements: the dictionary copy is negligible, the cost is the vodStreams array copy plus destruction of the old buffer; and the cost can recur on every re-entry from a shelf or a mounted grid (stale metadataLoaded == false), depending on whether the detail's @Query delivers before .task runs.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: in MovieDetailView.task read the row first and call fetchMovieInfo() only when it is missing metadata, then delete applyVODMetadata and its call. vodStream's primary key is (streamId, playlistId) (AppDatabase.swift:55-66), so the lookup is an index hit: `let stored = try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in try DBVODStream.filter(Column("streamId") == sid && Column("playlistId") == pid).fetchOne(db) }`. Keep the comment at VODView.swift:596-599 accurate (drop the applyVODMetadata reference; the signature compare is still useful for other store publishes). The optional non-published Set<Int> hint is not needed.

**API check:** View.task(priority:_:) found at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5162, @available(iOS 15.0). GRDB QueryInterfaceRequest.fetchOne via AppDatabase.shared.read is already used with the identical expression at MovieDetailView.swift:217-219 and Requests.swift:256-259. No iOS 26-only API involved.

**Regression risks:** First open: the content is visible for one DB hop longer before the full-screen spinner replaces it (today the spinner comes one runloop turn after appear), so the content -> spinner -> content sequence is unchanged in kind. A newly pushed category or search result no longer carries plot/genre in memory until the next catalog reload, which no list screen displays. VODPlayerShell queues already carry catalog copies, so nothing changes there.

**How to verify:** XCTest measure of applyVODMetadata on a synthetic 150k-row store to confirm the size of the stall before deleting it. Then: open a film from a home shelf, go back, open the same film from the same shelf with the network blocked: stored plot and cast must appear with no spinner and no error (this also settles the @Query-versus-.task race, which today decides whether a second request is made). Log getVODInfo calls to confirm one request per film.

## swiftui-invalidation-7 — The dashboard is fed from a one-time copy of the Playlist row, so settings changes never reach it: the Xtream adult-content toggle resyncs with the old flag, and stale copies written back overwrite other settings

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U), EPG settings, M3U channels pull-to-refresh
- Code: `ContentView.swift:6, 17, 43-64, 145-163`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:40, 460-465, 496-505, 512-524`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:463`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:57-63, 94-104, 158-165`, `Models/M3UImporter.swift:25-31`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:205-219`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:329-337, 393-400`, `EPG/PanelTimeZoneResolver.swift:55-60`, `EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:273-282 (existing column-scoped pattern)`

**What the user perceives:** Turning 'Filter adult content' on in an Xtream playlist starts a full catalog download and changes nothing; it only applies after relaunching the app and refreshing again. In an M3U playlist, an EPG URL entered in Settings silently disappears after the next pull-to-refresh in the same session. Toggling the EPG switch can undo an adult-filter change made a moment earlier (the switch still shows the new state until relaunch).

**Mechanism (finder):** ContentView observes the playlist table with @Query (line 6) but renders the dashboard from `@State selectedPlaylist` (17), assigned only when a playlist is picked or auto-loaded (161, 167); the onChange handler only calls attemptAutoLoad, which returns immediately after the first run (145-157). Every view below therefore keeps the Playlist value from launch. Consequences in code: (1) PlaylistSettingsView.saveFilterSetting saves `updated` and then calls syncContents(), which passes the view's stale `playlist` (519) to syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal, where `let filterAdult = playlist.filterAdultContent` (PlaylistContentStore.swift:463) is the old value. (2) Every whole-row `updated.save(db)` built from a stale copy writes all its other columns back: XtreamEPGSettingsSection.saveEnabled (EPGSettingsSections.swift:158-161) reverts filterAdultContent; saveFilterSetting reverts epgEnabled; fetchAuthInfo (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:460-465) and PanelTimeZoneResolver.persist (55-60) rewrite the launch copy on each run while the timezone is new; M3UImporter.replace(playlist:) (25-31), called from pull-to-refresh (M3UChannelsView.swift:214-218) and Settings ▸ refresh (M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:333-337), wipes an epgURLOverride saved through M3UEPGSettingsSection, which keeps its own private copy (57-63). The code base already identified this hazard once and fixed it locally: CatchupURLResolver.persistStyle 'Writes only the timeshiftStyle column. Saving the caller's snapshot would write its other, possibly stale columns back' (273-282).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Two small parts. (a) Keep the dashboard on the live row: in ContentView's `.onChange(of: playlists)` add `if let current = selectedPlaylist, let fresh = newList.first(where: { $0.id == current.id }), fresh != current { selectedPlaylist = fresh }` (Playlist is Equatable; `.task(id: playlist.id)` in the dashboards is keyed on the id and does not re-run; shelf rows compare playlist.id only). (b) Make each settings write column-scoped, following CatchupURLResolver.swift:278-281: e.g. `try Playlist.filter(key: id).updateAll(db, [Column("epgEnabled").set(to: enabled)])`, likewise filterAdultContent, serverTimezone, epgURLOverride, and in M3UImporter.replace update only m3uEpgURL/serverURL. In saveFilterSetting pass the new value explicitly: `await syncContents(using: updated)`, because the running function still holds the old struct even after (a). M3UEPGSettingsSection can then drop its private @State copy of the playlist. None of this touches the TipJarRow line or the tip strings.

**APIs:** GRDB QueryInterfaceRequest.updateAll(_:_:) with Column.set(to:) (GRDB checkout: QueryInterfaceRequest.swift:1064, 1919; used at EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:280-281); View.onChange(of:initial:_:) (iOS 17.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read ContentView.swift:6-17, 41-65, 140-170; Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:37-41, 448-472, 496-536; Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:447-471, 474-510; Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:57-104, 113-165; Models/M3UImporter.swift:20-31; Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:205-219; Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:320-362, 393-404; Models/M3UContentStore.swift:80-91; EPG/PanelTimeZoneResolver.swift:55-61; EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:262-283; Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:227-300; Models/Playlist.swift. The mechanism is real. selectedPlaylist is assigned only at ContentView.swift:161 and 167; onChange(of: playlists) only calls attemptAutoLoad, which returns after the first run (153). (1) Xtream adult filter: saveFilterSetting writes `updated` and then calls syncContents(), which passes the view's `playlist` (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:519); syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal reads `playlist.filterAdultContent` (PlaylistContentStore.swift:463), the launch value. A full catalog download runs and filters with the old flag. Tab pull-to-refresh uses the same stale copy (480). (2) Whole-row saves from stale copies: XtreamEPGSettingsSection.saveEnabled (EPGSettingsSections.swift:158-161), fetchAuthInfo (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:460-465, which runs on every Settings .task/refresh while the launch copy has a different or nil serverTimezone, so simply returning to the Settings tab can revert a filter change), PanelTimeZoneResolver.persist (55-60) and M3UImporter.replace (25-31) all write every column of the launch copy back, including timeshiftStyle, which CatchupURLResolver.persistStyle was written specifically to protect (273-282). (3) M3U: an epgURLOverride saved by M3UEPGSettingsSection is wiped by the next pull-to-refresh or Settings refresh. Additional consequence not in the finding: in an M3U playlist the adult filter itself is undone by pull-to-refresh, because M3UImporter.replace saves the stale flag and reloadIfActive(playlist:) copies it into the store (M3UContentStore.swift:82). What needs correcting is the M3UImporter part of the fix: replace() is also the insert path for a new playlist and the save path for an edited one (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-302; the doc comment at M3UImporter.swift:5 says add and refresh share it). Updating only m3uEpgURL/serverURL there would insert channels for a playlist row that does not exist (foreign-key failure) and would drop name/URL edits. History: selectedPlaylist handling dates from the monorepo move (d2489f9); no comment marks the one-time copy as intentional.

**Corrected claim:** As stated, plus: on M3U the adult filter is reverted by the next pull-to-refresh in the same session, and the whole-row saves also revert timeshiftStyle and serverTimezone. The Settings tab's own .task (fetchAuthInfo) is one of the writers that reverts earlier toggles while the launch copy's serverTimezone differs from the panel's.

**Corrected fix:** (a) As proposed: in ContentView.onChange(of: playlists), after attemptAutoLoad, replace selectedPlaylist with the fresh row when it differs (same optional case, so the ZStack transition does not fire; .task(id: playlist.id) and the Equatable rows key on the id). (b) Column-scoped writes with Playlist.filter(key:).updateAll for epgEnabled, filterAdultContent, serverTimezone (both writers) and epgURLOverride; pass the new value explicitly into the sync (`syncContents(using: updated)`), and pass `updated` to EPGStore calls as today. (c) M3UImporter.replace must stay an upsert: inside the transaction, `if try Playlist.exists(db, key: pid) { try Playlist.filter(key: pid).updateAll(db, [Column("name").set(to: playlist.name), Column("serverURL").set(to: clearServerURL ? "" : playlist.serverURL), Column("m3uEpgURL").set(to: epgURL)]) } else { try updated.insert(db) }`. That keeps add and edit working and stops refresh from touching epgURLOverride, filterAdultContent, epgEnabled and timeshiftStyle. (d) The M3U refresh callers should reload the store with the fresh row (or let reloadIfActive read filterAdultContent from the database) so the in-memory filter flag is not reset. Keeping M3UEPGSettingsSection's private @State copy is harmless; dropping it is optional. The TipJarRow line and tip strings are not touched.

**API check:** GRDB QueryInterfaceRequest.updateAll(_:onConflict:_:) at GRDB/QueryInterface/Request/QueryInterfaceRequest.swift:1064-1166; ColumnExpression.set(to:) at the same file:1919; TableRecord.filter(key:) at TableRecord+QueryInterfaceRequest.swift:477; TableRecord.exists(_:key:) at Record/TableRecord.swift:471. The updateAll + set(to:) form is already compiled in this project at EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:279-281. View.onChange(of:initial:_:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827, iOS 17.0+, already used at ContentView.swift:145. Playlist is Equatable (Models/Playlist.swift:9). No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** (a) makes every dashboard child receive a new Playlist value when any column changes (for example timeshiftStyle persisted during a catch-up probe, or serverTimezone on first Settings open): one extra body pass for the tab roots; shelf rows compare playlist.id only and @Query requests are keyed on the id, so nothing re-subscribes. @State seeded from the playlist in initialisers (filterAdultContent, epgEnabled toggles) is not re-seeded, which is the desired behaviour. The M3UImporter change is the risky part: it must keep insert for new playlists and name/URL updates for edits, see (c). Column-scoped updates no longer re-insert a playlist that was deleted meanwhile, which is the safer behaviour CatchupURLResolver already documents. PlaylistSettingsView.swift and M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift carry the owner's uncommitted TipJarRow line; the edits are in other functions.

**How to verify:** Unit tests on an in-memory AppDatabase: save epgURLOverride, call M3UImporter.replace with the pre-save Playlist value, assert the override and filterAdultContent survive; call replace for a brand-new playlist and for an edited name, assert insert and rename still work; toggle epgEnabled from a stale copy and assert filterAdultContent, serverTimezone and timeshiftStyle are unchanged. Manual or UI test with the mock fixture: enable the adult filter in Xtream settings and check the adult-named category disappears without relaunch; on M3U enable the filter, pull to refresh, check it stays applied.

## swiftui-invalidation-8 — Every DownloadButton observes the whole DownloadManager, so each percent of any running download re-evaluates every mounted episode button

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail (episode list), Movie detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:27-28, 61-75, 77-143, 285-296`, `Models/DownloadManager.swift:39-41, 56-59, 566-572`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1453-1471`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:147-157`

**What the user perceives:** While an episode or film is downloading, scrolling a season's episode list stutters at a steady rhythm: once per percent, which on a fast connection is several times a second.

**Mechanism (finder):** DownloadButton holds `@ObservedObject private var manager = DownloadManager.shared` (line 27). The manager publishes `progress` once per whole percent of each active task (DownloadManager.swift:566-572; the throttle is deliberate and good) and bumps `dbVersion` after every DB write (41). Each publish re-runs the body of every DownloadButton that exists: one per materialized EpisodeDetailRow (SeriesView.swift:1453-1471) plus the movie one. A body builds the material-backed label, evaluates the contextMenu builder, computes `state` twice and resolves two L() strings (DownloadButton.swift:77-143), although only the single button whose id is downloading can change. dbVersion has no reader anywhere outside the manager (grep), so those publishes are pure invalidation. DownloadedItemByIDRequest also lacks removeDuplicates (285-296), so any write to the downloads table re-publishes to every button.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Observe the manager only where a fraction is drawn. DownloadButton: delete the @ObservedObject, call DownloadManager.shared in primaryAction and the context menu, change `case downloading(Double)` to `case downloading`, and render `DownloadingLabel(id: id, compact: compact)` for it: `private struct DownloadingLabel: View { let id: String; let compact: Bool; @ObservedObject private var manager = DownloadManager.shared; var body: some View { let p = manager.progress[id]?.fraction ?? 0; /* existing downloadingLabel(progress:) content */ } }`. Idle, queued, completed and failed buttons then never re-evaluate for progress; status changes still arrive through the per-id @Query. Add `.removeDuplicates()` to DownloadedItemByIDRequest's publisher (DBDownloadedItem is Equatable, DBModels.swift:200), like the history requests already do. DownloadsView keeps observing the manager; it shows the progress.

**APIs:** @ObservedObject in a leaf view (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8008)); Combine Publisher.removeDuplicates() (iOS 13.0+; already used at Models/Requests.swift:393)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:9-28, 61-143, 176-200, 285-296; Models/DownloadManager.swift:38-41, 56-59, 553-572; Views/SeriesView.swift:1318-1319, 1453-1471; Views/MovieDetailView.swift:143-157; Models/DBModels.swift:200-224. The mechanism is real: every DownloadButton holds @ObservedObject DownloadManager.shared (DownloadButton.swift:27), the manager publishes `progress` once per whole percent per task (566-572) and `dbVersion` after each write (eleven sites, all inside the manager; grep finds no reader), so each publish re-runs the body of every materialised button in the episode LazyVStack. The owner knows this cost: the comment at DownloadManager.swift:56-59 says each publish re-renders all DownloadButtons and the percent throttle was the deliberate mitigation. What does not hold up is the perceived effect. A body here is a Button, one small label and a context-menu builder; the output is unchanged for every button except the downloading one, so SwiftUI re-evaluates and discards. For 20-50 episodes that is well under a frame, at most 100 times per download. 'Stutters at a steady rhythm' is asserted, not shown; I would expect it only on very long seasons (hundreds of materialised rows) with a very fast download. The download table is not written per percent (only status changes and total bytes once), so removeDuplicates on DownloadedItemByIDRequest saves a handful of re-renders per download.

**Corrected claim:** Each percent of any running download, and each downloads-table write, re-evaluates the body of every materialised DownloadButton although only one can change. The work is small per button; a visible hitch while scrolling is plausible only for very long episode lists and is unmeasured. This is invalidation hygiene, not a demonstrated stutter.

**Corrected fix:** The proposed fix stands and is small: remove @ObservedObject from DownloadButton, use DownloadManager.shared directly in primaryAction and the context menu, make the state case payload-free, and draw the percentage in a private leaf view that alone observes the manager. Add .removeDuplicates() to DownloadedItemByIDRequest (Optional<DBDownloadedItem> is Equatable). Leave dbVersion and DownloadsView alone: DownloadsView observes the manager and may rely on those publishes.

**API check:** ObservedObject at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8008, @available(iOS 13.0). Combine Publisher.removeDuplicates() at Combine.swiftinterface:433 (iOS 13.0), already used at Models/Requests.swift:393. No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Low. The button's status still comes from its per-id @Query, so idle -> queued -> downloading -> completed transitions are unaffected. The leaf must read progress[id] with the same fallback of 0 so the label does not flash an empty value between the DB status change and the first progress publish. M3UDownloadMenuItems has the same @ObservedObject but only exists while a context menu is open; no change needed.

**How to verify:** Self._printChanges() in DownloadButton with a season open and one download running: before, one line per mounted button per percent; after, none. To settle whether it was ever perceptible: Instruments SwiftUI template (or Hitches) on a device while scrolling a 100+ episode season during a fast download, before and after.

## swiftui-invalidation-9 — M3U: the dashboard root observes the favourites store it never renders, and two views detect catalog changes by comparing the full 310k-element channel array on the main thread

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U channels, M3U group detail, M3U dashboard root, M3U player favourite button
- Code: `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:8-10, 58-64, 86`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:137-140, 514`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:17-19, 80-91, 109-113`, `Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:11, 28-34`

**What the user perceives:** On a large M3U playlist, a pull-to-refresh that finds nothing new ends with a visible freeze just as the spinner should disappear. Toggling a favourite (from the player or a card menu) re-evaluates the whole dashboard root and the player.

**Mechanism (finder):** (1) M3UDashboardView declares `@ObservedObject private var favorites = M3UFavoriteStore.shared` (line 9) but uses it only to call favorites.track(playlistId:) in .task (86). Each favouriteIds publish (M3UFavoriteStore.swift:32-34) re-runs the root body, which rebuilds the three player environment closures (58-64) and so invalidates the player, on top of the legitimate observers (M3UFavoritesView, the player shell). (2) M3UChannelsView and M3UGroupDetailView use `.onChange(of: store.channels)` (M3UChannelsView.swift:137, 514). Array == is O(1) while the buffer is the same, but reloadIfActive always installs a newly fetched array (M3UContentStore.swift:84-87, 110): when the playlist did not change, the comparison walks all channels and compares every string field of DBM3UChannel before concluding 'equal'. For the 310k-channel case the store's own header mentions, that is on the order of 100 ms on the main thread, once per view that has the modifier, inside the update pass that ends the refresh. LiveCategoryContent documents the same trap and avoids it with an O(1) token (LiveStreamsView.swift:553-561).

**Proposed fix (finder):** (1) M3UDashboardView: remove the property and call `M3UFavoriteStore.shared.track(playlistId: playlist.id)` in the task; apply the same root split as for DashboardView (EPG snapshot modifier, alert modifier) so `store` is not observed at the root either. (2) M3UContentStore: add `@Published private(set) var revision = 0`, incremented last in apply(channels:grouping:) and in clearLists(); replace both `.onChange(of: store.channels)` with `.onChange(of: store.revision)`. Behaviour difference: an unchanged refresh now re-applies the (identical) snapshot, which the Equatable shelf rows absorb with element compares bounded to materialized shelves, instead of one whole-catalog compare.

**APIs:** View.onChange(of:initial:_:) (iOS 17.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:8-10, 52-110; Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:11-35; Models/M3UContentStore.swift:17-19, 44-91, 105-113; Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:8, 137-140, 144-148, 205-219, 327-331, 487-515; Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:553-561; Models/DBModels.swift DBM3UChannel. (1) Confirmed but negligible: `favorites` in M3UDashboardView is used only at line 86 for track(playlistId:), so each favouriteIds publish re-runs the root body and rebuilds the environment closures for the player overlay. That is one body pass per user tap on a star, and the player shell observes the favourites store legitimately anyway; a user cannot perceive it. Removing the property is correct and free. (2) Confirmed in mechanism, narrower in scope: onChange(of: store.channels) compares arrays on every body pass. Array == returns immediately on count mismatch and on identical buffers, so the full walk happens only when reloadIfActive installs a freshly fetched array with the same count (M3UContentStore.swift:84-87): a pull-to-refresh or Settings refresh of an unchanged playlist (or one whose first difference is far down the list). Then every element's fourteen fields are compared on the main thread, once per mounted view with the modifier (M3UChannelsView always, M3UGroupDetailView when pushed). At the 310k size the store's header names that is tens of milliseconds, at ordinary M3U sizes (10-50k) a few. It happens once, at the end of an operation that already took seconds. The code base's own O(1) token pattern (LiveStreamsView.swift:553-561, same comment about O(n) equality) supports the fix. The 'apply the same root split as for DashboardView' sentence depends on another finding that is not in this set; it cannot be judged here and is not needed for either part.

**Corrected claim:** M3UDashboardView observes the favourites store without rendering from it (harmless extra body pass per favourite toggle). M3UChannelsView and M3UGroupDetailView detect catalog reloads with full array equality, which costs a whole-catalog compare on the main thread only when a refresh returns a list of unchanged length; perceptible only on very large playlists.

**Corrected fix:** (1) Delete the `favorites` property from M3UDashboardView and call M3UFavoriteStore.shared.track(playlistId: playlist.id) in the task. Drop the root-split sentence from this finding. (2) Add `@Published private(set) var revision = 0` to M3UContentStore, incremented in apply(channels:grouping:) and clearLists(); replace both .onChange(of: store.channels) with .onChange(of: store.revision). An unchanged refresh then re-applies the snapshot and the Equatable shelf rows compare items per materialised shelf (M3UChannelsView.swift:327-331) instead of one whole-catalog compare.

**API check:** View.onChange(of:initial:_:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827, iOS 17.0+, already used at the two sites. @Published / ObservableObject are Combine, already used by the store. No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Low. After the change an unchanged refresh runs recomputeFilter where today it is skipped; with a playlist that has one giant group (no group-title, everything under the ungrouped key) the shelf row's `items ==` then walks that group, so the worst case is no better than today, never worse. An active search is re-applied after refresh, which is what the existing comment at M3UChannelsView.swift:138 intends. Increment revision after the three assignments so the onChange closure reads the new groups.

**How to verify:** XCTest measure of == on two separately fetched 310k DBM3UChannel arrays to size the stall. Unit test that reloadIfActive and loadPlaylist change `revision`. Device: pull-to-refresh on a large unchanged M3U playlist and watch the spinner dismissal with the Hitches instrument, before and after.

## swiftui-invalidation-10 — Playback does reach the browse grids: each rounded watch-progress change re-evaluates the whole poster grid body instead of the one bar that moved

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail / All Movies, Series category detail / All Series, Favorites
- Code: `Models/Requests.swift:438-457, 484-498`, `Views/VODView.swift:608, 614-616, 691-708`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:578, 649-661`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:15-16, 133-146, 159-171`, `Views/PlayerView.swift:1678-1684 (10 s save cadence; reference only)`

**What the user perceives:** With an episode playing in the mini card, a long Series grid (or Favorites) hitches slightly every 10 to 20 seconds while scrolling; with a film it is about once a minute.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODCategoryContent, SeriesCategoryContent and FavoritesView own `@Query<WatchProgressMapRequest>` (VODView.swift:608; SeriesView.swift:578; FavoritesView.swift:15-16). The request already rounds to 0.01 and removes duplicates (Requests.swift:443-457, 495), which cuts a two-hour film to about one change per 72 s; for a 22-minute episode, 1% is 13 s, so most 10 s saves still change the map (series key = seriesId, value = latest episode). Each change re-runs the grid body: `Array(displayItems.prefix(visibleCount).enumerated())` is rebuilt (O(visibleCount), which grows by 90 per page scrolled, VODView.swift:691; SeriesView.swift:649) and the ForEach content closure runs again for every alive cell, creating a new NavigationLink and destination closure each, although at most one card's bar moved. The ContinueWatchingRow of the playing type also updates on every save; that one is legitimate (its own bar moves) and cheap (10 cards).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Deliver the map through the environment and read it in a leaf, the pattern the EPG snapshot already uses. `struct WatchProgressScope: ViewModifier { @Query<WatchProgressMapRequest> private var map: [String: Double]; init(playlistId: UUID, type: String) { _map = Query(WatchProgressMapRequest(playlistId: playlistId, type: type), in: \.appDatabase) }; func body(content: Content) -> some View { content.environment(\.watchProgressMap, map) } }` applied by the three grids in place of their @Query; VODStreamCard/SeriesCard replace the `watchProgress: Double?` parameter with `progressKey: String?` and draw the existing bar inside `PosterProgressBar(key:width:)`, which holds `@Environment(\.watchProgressMap)`. A change then re-runs only the small leaves; the grid body and ForEach are untouched. Shelf cards pass nil as today.

**APIs:** GRDBQuery @Query inside a ViewModifier (GRDBQuery checkout (Query is a DynamicProperty, Sources/GRDBQuery/Query.swift)); EnvironmentKey / EnvironmentValues custom key (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12560))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Models/Requests.swift:432-498; Views/VODView.swift:490-545, 590-722; Views/SeriesView.swift:566-670; Views/FavoritesView.swift:12-26, 126-172; Views/PlayerView.swift:1679-1686 (cadence comment only); Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:5-18; Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:420-428. The mechanism is as described: the grids own @Query<WatchProgressMapRequest>, so a changed map re-runs the grid body, rebuilds Array(displayItems.prefix(visibleCount).enumerated()) and re-invokes the ForEach content for live cells. The frequency figures check out: the map is rounded to 0.01 and de-duplicated (Requests.swift:443-457, 495), saves come every 10 s, so a 22-minute episode changes about every 13 s and a two-hour film about every 72 s. But the rounding and removeDuplicates are the owner's deliberate fix for exactly this ('comparing the exact fraction made the map differ on every save and re-rendered each grid'), and what remains is one body pass of a paginated grid every 13-72 s, only while something is playing in the mini card and the user is on one of these grids. The cards whose inputs did not change do not re-run their bodies. Nothing in the code shows this reaches a dropped frame; it would need a grid scrolled many pages deep (visibleCount in the thousands). The proposed environment-plus-leaf design is sound and matches the existing epgSnapshot pattern (EPGComponents.swift:5-18, read in the card at LiveStreamsView.swift:427), but it changes the VODStreamCard/SeriesCard interface used by shelves, grids, Favorites and search for a gain that is not demonstrated. For FavoritesView it brings nothing: that grid is not paginated, favourites are few, and the screen holds two maps (vod and series), so a single environment key would have to be applied per grid.

**Corrected claim:** While a film or episode plays in the mini card, each 1% step of its progress re-runs the body of a mounted Movies or Series poster grid (O(visibleCount) array rebuild plus content closures for live cells) to move one bar. This is the residue left after the deliberate rounding fix; a perceptible hitch is unproven and likely only for grids scrolled many pages deep.

**Corrected fix:** Measure first; do not change the cards on this evidence. If measurement shows a hitch, apply the proposed WatchProgressScope modifier and leaf bar to VODCategoryContent and SeriesCategoryContent only (wrap the grid inside their body so the modifier's @Query, not the grid's, receives the change), keep the existing `watchProgress: Double?` parameter for Favorites and other callers, and leave FavoritesView as it is. A cheaper first step, if any is wanted, is to stop rebuilding the enumerated array on every pass by keeping it in @State alongside displayItems.

**API check:** EnvironmentKey at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12560 (iOS 13.0+); custom EnvironmentValues key pattern already compiled at Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:5-18. ViewModifier at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:15360. GRDBQuery Query is a DynamicProperty (Sources/GRDBQuery/Query.swift) and is usable inside a ViewModifier. No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Changing the card signature touches shelves, grids, Favorites and search call sites; a missed call site silently loses its progress bar. Two progress maps on one screen (Favorites) would collide on a single environment key. The custom == on VODCategoryContent/SeriesCategoryContent and the pagination must stay untouched. WatchProgressMapRequest's rounding and removeDuplicates must stay as they are.

**How to verify:** Self._printChanges() in SeriesCategoryContent while an episode plays in the mini card to confirm one body pass per changed save. Then Instruments (SwiftUI template or Hitches) on a device: All Series scrolled 30+ pages with an episode playing; record the body duration at each progress change. Only if it exceeds a frame is the refactor justified; repeat after the change and compare M04-movies-all.png style screens for identical bars.
