## swiftui-invalidation-11 — Changing the language re-creates the entire view tree: the user is thrown from Settings to the last content tab, navigation stacks reset, the docked player is destroyed and the catalog is re-read from SQLite

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings ▸ Language, Dashboard root, Mini player
- Code: `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:51-67`, `Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:37-39`, `ContentView.swift:17-18, 134-137, 152-163`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:8, 16-23, 131-137, 200-216`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-152`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:65-88`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Which behaviour the owner wants after a language change: (a) rebuild but return to Settings (recommended, small), (b) also keep the docked player alive across the change, or (c) replace the in-app picker with the system per-app language setting.

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a language makes the screen blank for a moment and then shows Live TV (or Movies/Series), not the language list the user was on, so the new checkmark is never seen. Anything playing in the mini card stops. On a big catalog the shelves show placeholders again while the whole catalog is reloaded.

**Mechanism (finder):** AppRootView applies `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:59-66); the comment explains why: L() strings are resolved at body time and only a few views observed the manager. The id change discards all state below it: ContentView's selectedPlaylist and hasAttemptedAutoLoad (ContentView.swift:17-18) reset, so the blank 'initial check' branch shows (134-137) until the @Query answers and attemptAutoLoad re-selects the last playlist; DashboardView is new, so selectedTab comes from restoreInitialTab(), which by design never restores Settings (DashboardView.swift:200-216), and the @StateObject PlayerOverlayController (line 8) is a new instance, which tears the presented player down; `.task(id: playlist.id)` runs again and loadPlaylist re-fetches all three catalogs and flips streamsLoaded false → true (PlaylistContentStore.swift:128-152) although the data is already in memory; new home views start with empty @State, so they pass through their empty-state branch (LiveStreamsView.swift:79-87) before the first recompute.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the rebuild (it is the reliable way to re-resolve every L() string) and make it land where the user was. Smallest version: LocalizationManager sets a one-shot flag when selectedLanguage changes; DashboardTab.restoreInitialTab() consumes it and returns .settings; loadPlaylist returns early when activePlaylistId == playlist.id && streamsLoaded (nothing in the catalog depends on the language except the 'Uncategorized' label, which can be re-labelled in place). Optional: lift the PlayerOverlayController above the `.id` boundary so playback survives. The alternative is the system route: drop the in-app list and open the app's page in Settings (per-app language), which relaunches the app the way every Apple app behaves. Touches another_iptv_playerApp.swift only inside AppRootView; the TipStore line in App.init stays as is.

**APIs:** View.id(_:) (iOS 13.0+ (existing usage)); UIApplication.openSettingsURLString (system-route alternative) (iOS 8.0+ (UIKit headers, UIApplication.h))

**Verifier reasons:** Core claim holds from code. another_iptv_playerApp.swift:62-66 puts `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` on ContentView; LanguagePickerSection.swift:38 assigns `manager.selectedLanguage = lang.code`, so every state below the id is discarded. The rebuild is deliberate (comment at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:51-55; introduced in 0ab5bcd) and should stay.

Confirmed consequences:
- ContentView.swift:17-18 `selectedPlaylist` / `hasAttemptedAutoLoad` reset. PlaylistRequest.defaultValue is nil (Models/Requests.swift:7) and GRDB's `publisher(in:scheduling:)` defaults to `.async(onQueue: .main)` (GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487), so the blank branch (ContentView.swift:134-137) renders for at least one frame before attemptAutoLoad (152-163) re-selects the playlist.
- Views/DashboardView.swift:22 seeds selectedTab from restoreInitialTab(), which clamps to a content tab (206-216). The user lands on Live TV / Movies / Series and the pushed Language list is gone.
- Views/DashboardView.swift:8 `@StateObject PlayerOverlayController` is new, so a docked player is removed. Teardown is clean: PlayerView.swift:1343-1351 onDisappear saves history and calls player.teardown().
- `.task(id: playlist.id)` (DashboardView.swift:131-137) re-runs loadPlaylist, which re-reads categories and all three catalogs and flips streamsLoaded false then true (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:128-152).

Corrections:
1. "Shelves show placeholders again" is wrong. clearLists() only runs when activePlaylistId differs (PlaylistContentStore.swift:106-109), so the in-memory arrays stay populated during the re-read. The shelf placeholder needs `items.isEmpty && isStreamsLoading` (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:372-374). What happens instead: one first-pass frame of the 'no category' empty state (LiveStreamsView.swift:79-87, because displayCategories @State is empty, isLoading is false and activePlaylistId matches), then three recomputeFilter passes (LiveStreamsView.swift:106, 278-294), plus a transient second copy of the catalog in memory. SearchView would show its loading branch while streamsLoaded is false (Views/SearchView.swift:225).
2. Scope is incomplete. M3U playlists have the same problem: Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:123 hosts LanguagePickerSection, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:14 has `@State selectedTab = 0` and :11 its own @StateObject PlayerOverlayController, and M3UContentStore.loadPlaylist (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:43-68) always sets isLoading and re-fetches and re-groups.
3. The 'optional: lift PlayerOverlayController above the .id' step does not keep playback alive. The player view is rendered inside DashboardView's ZStack (DashboardView.swift:92-113), below the id. Its identity and its controller StateObject die regardless; a surviving controller would re-mount `item.root` as a new PlayerView and start a second stream while the first is tearing down, which is a connection-limit collision on Xtream panels. Keeping playback would mean moving the overlay host itself above the id, which restructures the out-of-scope player hand-off.
4. 'Only the Uncategorized label depends on language' understates it. Every orphan row carries `categoryName = L("content.uncategorized")` baked in at fetch time (PlaylistContentStore.swift:376, 390, 404), and the synthetic category name is baked in at :429. An early return leaves these in the old language until the next reload; relabelling in place means walking up to 150k rows.
5. The one-shot flag needs two guards the finding does not mention. `selectedLanguage.didSet` fires even when the already-selected language is tapped, with no id change and no rebuild, so an unguarded flag would stay armed and send a later, unrelated dashboard entry to Settings. And DashboardView.init runs on every ContentView body pass, so consume-in-init is fragile.
6. The proposed unit test is not possible as written: DashboardTab is a `private enum` (DashboardView.swift:190).
7. The minimal fix does not need to touch another_iptv_playerApp.swift (its only uncommitted change is the TipStore line in App.init) or either settings view, so it does not touch the owner's tip-jar work.

Adjacent, not part of this finding and intent not checked in history: loadPlaylist does not apply mergeUncategorized / appendingUncategorized (PlaylistContentStore.swift:144-152) while reloadFromDatabase does (:301-316). Today a language change after a pull-to-refresh therefore also drops the synthetic Uncategorized shelf.

Screenshots (76 PNGs, three variants) contain no language-change capture, so they say nothing about this behaviour.

**Corrected claim:** Changing the in-app language changes the `.id` on the app root (deliberate, so every L() string re-resolves) and rebuilds the whole tree. The screen is blank for a frame or more while the playlist @Query re-answers. The user is then dropped on the last content tab (Xtream) or on Channels (M3U) instead of Settings, with all navigation stacks, search text and scroll positions reset. A docked or fullscreen player is torn down (progress is saved through PlayerView.onDisappear). The Xtream catalog is re-read from SQLite off the main thread although it is already in memory. Shelves do not go back to placeholders, because the in-memory data stays in place; the cost is one first-frame empty state on the landing tab, repeated recompute passes and a transient second catalog copy. The M3U dashboard is affected the same way and M3UContentStore.loadPlaylist re-fetches and re-groups too.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the `.id` rebuild.

1. LocalizationManager: add a plain (not @Published) `static var returnToSettingsAfterRebuild = false`. Set it in `selectedLanguage.didSet` only when `oldValue != selectedLanguage`.
2. DashboardView.init: seed selectedTab with `.settings` when the flag is set, otherwise `restoreInitialTab()`. Read the flag without consuming it and clear it in the dashboard's `.onAppear`. Do not write savedTab, so the next cold launch still restores the content tab.
3. M3UDashboardView: same change. Turn `@State selectedTab = 0` into an init-seeded state that starts at 1 when the flag is set, and clear the flag in `.onAppear`.
4. Optional, and of little visible value once the user lands on Settings (content tabs are lazy and not mounted during the reload): at the top of PlaylistContentStore.loadPlaylist, before loadToken is replaced, return early when `activePlaylistId == playlist.id && streamsLoaded && loadError == nil`. Accept that 'Uncategorized' labels stay in the old language until the next refresh or launch, or skip the early return. An M3U equivalent would be `activePlaylistId == playlist.id && !channels.isEmpty`.
5. Drop the 'lift PlayerOverlayController above the id' step. Either accept that the player closes on a language change (a system per-app language change also relaunches the app), or treat keeping playback as a separate, larger change to the player hand-off.

None of this touches another_iptv_playerApp.swift, the TipJarRow() lines or the tip strings, so touches_user_wip is false.

Owner decision: (a) rebuild and return to Settings (recommended); (b) the system per-app language route via UIApplication.openSettingsURLString. I did not verify (b) on iOS 26: from memory, the per-app Language row only appears when the device has more than one preferred language, and existing stored `app.selected_language` overrides would need migrating.

**API check:** - `View.id(_:)`: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:18608, `@inlinable nonisolated public func id<ID>(_ id: ID) -> some SwiftUICore.View where ID : Swift.Hashable`, in the base View extension (iOS 13+). Existing usage; the fix adds no new call.
- `UIApplicationOpenSettingsURLString` (Swift: UIApplication.openSettingsURLString): UIKit Headers/UIApplication.h:613, `API_AVAILABLE(ios(8.0)) NS_SWIFT_NONISOLATED`. Found, so the finding's `verified_in_sdk: false` can be true. Only needed for the system-route alternative.
- `protocol View` is `@preconcurrency @MainActor` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13881) and the app target sets SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:578, 619), so reading a static on the @MainActor LocalizationManager from DashboardView.init or DashboardTab.restoreInitialTab compiles without extra annotations.
- No iOS 26-only API is involved, so no availability gate or fallback is needed.

**Regression risks:** - If the flag is set without the `oldValue != selectedLanguage` guard, tapping the current language arms it with no rebuild, and the next dashboard entry (for example after returning to the playlist list) opens on Settings.
- Consume-in-init is fragile because DashboardView.init runs on every ContentView body pass; use peek in init and clear in onAppear.
- The loadPlaylist early return changes the 'Try again' buttons (DashboardView.swift:151, LiveStreamsView.swift:77, VODView.swift:50, SeriesView.swift:51) from a DB re-read to a no-op when a pull-to-refresh failed with the catalog loaded. That is equivalent in effect today, since loadPlaylist never retried the network in that state, but keep the `loadError == nil` condition or leave this step out.
- The early return leaves old-language 'Uncategorized' strings in memory.
- Initial selection of the Settings tab must not write savedTab; the existing tabBinding setter already only persists content tabs.
- Lifting only the overlay controller, as the original proposes, would start a second player instance during teardown. Do not do it.
- No deliberate performance work (Equatable shelf rows, off-main filtering) is touched.

**How to verify:** UI test in another-iptv-playerUITests, for an Xtream and an M3U playlist: open Settings, open Language, pick another language. Assert the Settings tab is selected, its navigation title is in the new language and the Language row shows the new name. Then relaunch and assert a content tab is restored, not Settings.

Manual:
1. Tap the already-selected language, go back to the playlist list, re-enter the playlist: it must open on the content tab.
2. Change language with the mini player docked: the player closes, and the item's resume position is present in Continue Watching.
3. If the early return is adopted, on a 100k+ catalog: put a signpost or log in PlaylistContentStore.loadPlaylist and confirm no fetch*Data read runs after a language change, then switch to Live TV and confirm shelves render immediately.

To unit-test the tab seed, DashboardTab would have to become internal.

## navigation-architecture-1 — Twelve pushed browse screens hide the tab bar while sibling pushes (Favorites, movie/series detail, Downloads) keep it, so the bar disappears and reappears inside one stack and tab switching is impossible from every grid

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live category detail, All Channels, Movies category / All Movies / Recently Added, Series category / All Series / Recently Added, Watch history, M3U group detail, M3U favorites, TV Guide, iPad top tab bar
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:380, 563, 822`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:502`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:63`, `another-iptv-player/Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:82`, `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:85`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:45`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should the TV Guide stay full-height with the tab bar hidden (1 site) or follow the same rule as the grids? Should the bar minimise on scroll on iOS 26, given the custom mini player card docks above it?

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a category header on Movies makes the tab bar vanish (iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png, iphone-dark/L03-live-category-detail.png). On iPad the whole top tab pill is gone (ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png). A film opened from the home shelf keeps the bar (iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png), as do Favorites (iphone-light/L04-favorites-live.png, ipad-light/M03-favorites-movies.png) and Downloads (iphone-light/T05-downloads.png). So the same stack shows, hides and shows the bar again depending on which screen is on top, and from any grid the user cannot change tab or reach Search without backing out first. Apple's TV, Music and App Store keep the tab bar on every browse push and hide it only for playback.

**Mechanism (finder):** .toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar) sits on 12 destinations (lines above). MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView, FavoritesView (Views/FavoritesView.swift:56-58), DownloadsView and LanguagePickerListView do not set it. Favorites differs between playlist types: Xtream shows the bar, M3U hides it (Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:63). No comment or commit message gives a reason (git log -S: initial import and 654cefc). Two points I could not run and that need a simulator pass on the installed 18.1 and 26.0 runtimes: (1) the preference is per destination, so a detail pushed from a hidden-bar grid should bring the bar back and hide it again on pop; (2) the hide is not tied to the push the way UIKit's hidesBottomBarWhenPushed is, so on an interactive back-swipe the bar is expected to return when the pop commits instead of tracking the finger. Side effect outside this lens: the mini card reserves a fixed 49pt for a tab bar on compact width (Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:478) even on these screens.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Delete the modifier at the 11 browse sites (LiveStreamsView 497/722, VODView 380/563/822, SeriesView 357/535/761, M3UChannelsView 502, M3UFavoritesView 63, WatchHistoryListView 82). Keep it on EPGGuideView:51 only if the owner wants the guide immersive. To win back the vertical space on iOS 26, let the system collapse the bar while scrolling, on both TabViews:

struct TabBarMinimizeOnScroll: ViewModifier {
  func body(content: Content) -> some View {
    if #available(iOS 26, *) { content.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown) } else { content }
  }
}
// DashboardView.swift:85, M3UDashboardView.swift:45
.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable).modifier(TabBarMinimizeOnScroll())

iOS 18 fallback: the standard always-visible tab bar, no extra code.

**APIs:** View.toolbar(_:for:) (existing usage; current spelling is toolbarVisibility(_:for:)) (iOS 16.0 / toolbarVisibility iOS 18.0); View.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:) (iOS 26.0); TabBarMinimizeBehavior.onScrollDown (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read all sites. `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` occurs exactly 12 times: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722; Views/VODView.swift:380, 563, 822; Views/SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761; Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:502; Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:63; Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:82; Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51. MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView, FavoritesView (Views/FavoritesView.swift:56-58), DownloadsView and LanguagePickerListView do not set it, so Xtream Favorites keeps the bar and M3U Favorites hides it. No comment sits next to any site; `git log -S` shows only the initial import (d2489f9), 654cefc (new flat browse views copied the pattern) and 1cce013 (EPG guide). No commit message gives a reason, so this is not documented deliberate work. Screenshots agree: iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png has no tab bar, iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png and iphone-light/L04-favorites-live.png have it, ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png has lost the whole top tab pill while ipad-light/L06-favorites.png keeps it next to the back button. The mini card supports the change: Views/PlayerView.swift:1948-1966 always reserves MiniPlayerMetrics.tabBarAllowance (49pt, Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:478) on compact width, so on the hidden-bar grids the card floats above an empty strip today. One citation is wrong: ipad-light/M03-favorites-movies.png does not exist (ipad-light has only L01-L06); ipad-light/L06-favorites.png shows the same thing. The two points the finder marked as unverified (bar returns on a detail pushed from a grid; bar does not track an interactive back-swipe) remain unverified. They are not needed for the verdict: home > grid hides the bar and home > detail keeps it, which is already inconsistent.

**Corrected claim:** Eleven pushed browse screens (plus the TV Guide) hide the tab bar while sibling pushes in the same stacks (Xtream Favorites, movie/series detail, Downloads, Language) keep it. On those grids the user cannot switch tab or reach Search, the iPad top tab pill disappears, and the docked mini card floats above an empty 49pt strip. The original claim stands; replace the non-existent screenshot reference with ipad-light/L06-favorites.png.

**Corrected fix:** Delete `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` at the 11 browse sites (LiveStreamsView 497/722, VODView 380/563/822, SeriesView 357/535/761, M3UChannelsView 502, M3UFavoritesView 63, WatchHistoryListView 82). Leave EPGGuideView:51 until the owner decides. Ship this alone first. Treat `tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)` behind `if #available(iOS 26, *)` (fallback: plain always-visible bar) as a separate, optional product decision, because the mini card keeps a fixed 49pt allowance and would sit above a collapsed bar. The removal itself is also a product choice the owner should confirm: the grids lose the bottom strip they have today.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk): `func toolbar(_ visibility: Visibility, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...)` iOS 16.0, soft-deprecated (deprecated: 100000.0, renamed toolbarVisibility(_:for:)); `toolbarVisibility(_:for:)` iOS 18.0. `nonisolated public func tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_ behavior: TabBarMinimizeBehavior) -> some View` @available(iOS 26.0, ...). `public struct TabBarMinimizeBehavior : Hashable, Sendable` iOS 26.0 with `static let onScrollDown` @available(iOS 26.0, *), unavailable on macOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS. All three found as declared by the finder.

**Regression risks:** (1) WatchHistoryListView:83 and M3UFavoritesView:45 use `.searchable` with default placement. With the bar visible the field should sit in the navigation drawer as it does on FavoritesView (iphone-light/L04), but that needs a look on both runtimes. (2) Grids lose bottom height on iOS 18 (opaque 49pt bar); on iOS 26 content scrolls under the floating bar. (3) If minimise-on-scroll is added, the mini card will hover 49pt above a collapsed bar; the card geometry is out of scope and must not be changed for this. (4) No UI test depends on the bar being hidden (tests only use app.tabBars to select tabs). No deliberate performance work is touched.

**How to verify:** UI test on the 18.x and 26.0 simulators: push Movies > category, All Movies, Recently Added, Series equivalents, Live category, All Channels, history, M3U group and M3U favorites, and assert app.tabBars.firstMatch exists and is hittable (iPad: the top tab pill). Screen-record push, pop and interactive back-swipe from grid to detail and back to confirm the bar no longer appears and disappears. Check the search field position on WatchHistoryListView and M3UFavoritesView. Dock the mini card over a grid and confirm it rests 12pt above the bar.

## navigation-architecture-2 — Tab roots carry three to four unlabelled glyph buttons in the navigation bar, two of them NavigationLinks, where a native app shows one primary action and a More menu

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U Channels home
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:108-138`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:112-133`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:113-134`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:64-94`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:231-241`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Which single action stays visible per tab: TV Guide on Live TV is the obvious one; on Movies and Series it could be the category picker or nothing. Touches the ten Localizable.strings files only to add one key; the tip keys stay as they are.

**What the user perceives:** Live TV shows four icons in one glass capsule that takes about 58% of the bar width (iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png: star, guide, grid, list). Movies and Series show three (iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png). None has a text label: square.grid.2x2 means "All Movies", list.bullet.indent means "Jump to category". Once scrolled, the inline title is pushed to the leading edge beside the capsule (iphone-light/L02-live-home-scrolled.png). On iPad the system already spills two of them into an automatic overflow "..." (ipad-light/L01-live-home.png). TV, Music and App Store roots carry one item.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each root adds its own ToolbarItems with Image-only labels (LiveStreamsView.swift:109-137, VODView.swift:113-132, SeriesView.swift:114-133, M3UChannelsView.swift:65-93), and DashboardNavigationModifier adds the Favorites star on top (DashboardView.swift:232-240). Guide, All and Favorites are view-based NavigationLinks placed in the toolbar; the category picker is a Button that opens a sheet. All use the deprecated .navigationBarTrailing placement. Because the labels are bare Images, the iPad overflow menu has no titles to show other than the accessibility labels, and the Xtream star has none at all (DashboardView.swift:234-238).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Per root: keep at most one primary item (TV Guide on Live TV / M3U) and move the rest into one Menu with text labels. Pushes from a menu need no router, a Bool-driven destination is enough:

@State private var showAll = false
@State private var showFavorites = false
.toolbar {
  ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarTrailing) {   // Live TV only
    Button { showGuide = true } label: { Label(L("epg.guide.title"), systemImage: "calendar.day.timeline.left") }
  }
  if #available(iOS 26, *) { ToolbarSpacer(.fixed, placement: .topBarTrailing) }
  ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarTrailing) {
    Menu {
      Button { showingCategoryPicker = true } label: { Label(L("list.jump_to_category"), systemImage: "list.bullet.indent") }
      Button { showAll = true } label: { Label(L("browse.all_live"), systemImage: "square.grid.2x2") }
      Button { showFavorites = true } label: { Label(L("favorites.title"), systemImage: "star") }
    } label: { Label(L("common.more"), systemImage: "ellipsis") }
  }
}
.navigationDestination(isPresented: $showAll) { AllLiveView(playlist: playlist) }

The Favorites entry moves out of DashboardNavigationModifier into the same menu. Needs one new string key (common.more) in the ten Localizable.strings files. iOS 18 fallback: the same toolbar without ToolbarSpacer (items sit side by side as plain bar buttons).

**APIs:** Menu (iOS 14.0); View.navigationDestination(isPresented:destination:) (iOS 16.0); ToolbarSpacer(_:placement:) with SpacerSizing.fixed (iOS 26.0); ToolbarItemPlacement.topBarTrailing (navigationBarTrailing is marked deprecated: "use topBarTrailing instead") (iOS 14.0); ToolbarContentBuilder.buildLimitedAvailability (if #available inside .toolbar) (iOS 17.5)

**Verifier reasons:** Code is as described. Live root: three image-only ToolbarItems (guide link, All link, category button) at Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:108-138, plus the Favorites star added by DashboardNavigationModifier (Views/DashboardView.swift:231-241), which has no accessibilityLabel (lines 234-238). VODView.swift:112-133 and SeriesView.swift:113-134 add two each; M3UChannelsView.swift:64-94 adds three. All use `.navigationBarTrailing`. Screenshots confirm: iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows four glyphs in one glass capsule spanning about 57% of the bar width; iphone-light/L02-live-home-scrolled.png shows the inline title pushed to the leading edge beside a three-glyph capsule; ipad-light/L01-live-home.png shows the star plus a system overflow "...". What does not hold as a defect: several icons in one shared glass capsule is the standard iOS 26 toolbar look, and "one primary action plus a More menu" is a design preference, not a system rule. Moving Favorites (today one tap, accent-coloured) into a menu costs discoverability. The claim that the iPad overflow has no titles is unverified: there is no screenshot of the opened overflow, and whether NavigationLinks work from inside it is unknown. The concrete, verifiable problems are narrower: ambiguous unlabelled glyphs (square.grid.2x2 for All, list.bullet.indent for Jump to category), the missing label on the Xtream star, and bar crowding on Live TV.

**Corrected claim:** The tab roots put three (Movies, Series, M3U) or four (Live TV) image-only items in the trailing bar group. Two glyphs are ambiguous, the Xtream Favorites star has no accessibility label, and on Live TV the group takes more than half the bar and forces the inline title to the leading edge when scrolled. This is a clarity and crowding issue and a product decision, not a deviation from a system rule.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest version: (a) replace the bare Images with `Label(L(key), systemImage:)` so VoiceOver and any overflow get real titles, and add the missing label to the star in DashboardNavigationModifier; (b) switch to `.topBarTrailing`; (c) fold only the two secondary actions (All, Jump to category) into one `Menu`, pushing All through `.navigationDestination(isPresented:)`, and carry over the existing `.disabled(...)` conditions; (d) keep Favorites, and TV Guide on Live/M3U, as visible items, separated from the menu on iOS 26 with `if #available(iOS 26, *) { ToolbarSpacer(.fixed, placement: .topBarTrailing) }` (iOS 18 fallback: items side by side). Result: Live 4 to 3 items, Movies/Series 3 to 2. Moving Favorites into the menu as the finder proposes is an owner decision. Needs one new key (common.more does not exist in en.lproj/Localizable.strings; add to all ten files without touching the tip keys). Update another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:52 (`navigationBars.buttons["star.fill"]`) if the star's identifier changes.

**API check:** `Menu` iOS 14. `navigationDestination(isPresented:destination:)` @available(iOS 16.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1546). `public struct ToolbarSpacer : ToolbarContent, CustomizableToolbarContent` @available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *) with `init(_ sizing: SpacerSizing = .flexible, placement: ToolbarItemPlacement = .automatic)`; `SpacerSizing.fixed` iOS 26.0. `ToolbarItemPlacement.topBarTrailing` @available(iOS 14.0), @backDeployed(before: iOS 17.0); `navigationBarTrailing` is soft-deprecated ("use topBarTrailing instead"). `ToolbarContentBuilder.buildLimitedAvailability(_ content: any ToolbarContent)` @available(iOS 17.5), so `if #available` inside `.toolbar` compiles at the iOS 18 deployment target. All found.

**Regression risks:** A real test depends on the star: ScreensUITests.swift:52 `test_moviesTab_starToolbarButton_opensFavoritesScreen` looks up `navigationBars.buttons["star.fill"]`; adding a label or moving the star changes that identifier. Hiding Favorites in a menu lowers discoverability of a core IPTV feature. DashboardNavigationModifier is also applied to Settings (type nil) and must keep working. The ten Localizable.strings files hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys: append only. No performance work is affected (toolbars sit on the roots, outside the Equatable shelf rows).

**How to verify:** Screenshots of the four roots on iPhone and iPad, light and dark, at rest and scrolled, before and after. On iPad open the system overflow before the change to see what titles it shows and whether its links navigate. UI test: reach All, Favorites, TV Guide and the category sheet by label. VoiceOver pass over the bar items.

## navigation-architecture-3 — "Go to detail" from the player writes into the @State of the screen that started playback, so it lands off-screen or nowhere once that screen is gone or another tab is selected

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Player hand-back to Movies / Series detail, Downloads sheet, Docked mini player with a different tab selected
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:161-163, 231-243`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:162-164, 181-193`, `another-iptv-player/Views/MovieDetailView.swift:96-98, 206-228`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DownloadsView.swift:134-139, 400-427`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:12, 125-129`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the title in the player closes the player and shows nothing in these cases. Deterministic: playback started from the Downloads sheet. Situational: the user minimised the player, switched tab or popped the screen it started from, expanded again and tapped the title. In the other-tab case the detail is pushed inside the tab where playback began, which the user is not looking at.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each entry point builds an onNavigateToDetail closure that sets its own pendingMovieDetail / pendingSeriesDetail, consumed by a navigationDestination(item:) on that same view (VODView.swift:231-243 and 161; SeriesView.swift:181-193 and 162; MovieDetailView.swift:206-228 and 96; DownloadsView.swift:400-427 and 134-139). The player calls the closure and then dismisses itself (Views/PlayerView.swift:3158-3164, read for the hand-off only). The Downloads sheet is closed as soon as a presentation starts (DashboardView.swift:125-129), which removes the DownloadsView whose state the closure writes to. Nothing can select the right tab because selectedTab is private state of DashboardView (DashboardView.swift:12). MovieDetailView additionally returns early with a plain dismiss when the target is its own film (MovieDetailView.swift:211-214), which is only correct while that detail is still on top.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give the dashboard one owner for "show this detail", next to PlayerOverlayController:

@MainActor final class DashboardRouter: ObservableObject {
  @Published var selectedTab: DashboardTab
  @Published var paths: [DashboardTab: NavigationPath] = [:]
  func reveal(_ route: BrowseRoute, in tab: DashboardTab) {
    selectedTab = tab
    paths[tab, default: NavigationPath()].append(route)
  }
}

The closures in VODView, SeriesView, MovieDetailView and DownloadsView become router.reveal(.movie(...), in: .movies) / router.reveal(.series(...), in: .series). The six item-based destinations and their pending* state go away. This is the first consumer of the path-bound stacks in the router finding; it can ship with only the detail routes migrated. Whether the player then closes or minimises is a player decision and out of this lens.

**APIs:** NavigationStack(path:root:) with NavigationPath (iOS 16.0); View.navigationDestination(for:destination:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed in code. Each entry point builds a closure that writes its own @State and consumes it with its own navigationDestination(item:): Views/VODView.swift:231-243 with :161; Views/SeriesView.swift:181-193 with :162; Views/MovieDetailView.swift:206-228 with :96; Views/DownloadsView.swift:400-427 with :134-139. The player calls the closure and then always dismisses itself (Views/PlayerView.swift:3158-3164, read for the hand-off only). `selectedTab` is private @State (Views/DashboardView.swift:12), so nothing selects the owning tab: after minimise > switch tab > expand > tap title, the detail is pushed in a stack the user is not looking at and playback is gone. Sheet case: DashboardView.swift:125-129 closes the Downloads sheet as soon as a presentation starts, so the DownloadsView whose state the closure writes to no longer exists and the write is dropped. Scope correction: that sheet is only reachable from the "go to downloads" button of the download-warning alert (DashboardView.swift:163-166). The normal Downloads entry is a push inside Settings (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:89), where the hand-back works while Settings is selected. So "deterministic" is true only for a rare path. The MovieDetailView early return (lines 211-214) is as described. Fix corrections: (1) `DashboardTab` is a private enum (DashboardView.swift:190) and must be made internal. (2) The claim that it "can ship with only the detail routes migrated" is unsafe: appending to a bound path while view-based pushes (category grids, All, Favorites) are on top is undocumented behaviour. (3) Always revealing in the Movies/Series tab changes behaviour for playback started from Search or Favorites, where pushing in the visible stack is what the user expects. (4) PlayerOverlayController.swift is in the excluded Views/Player* set, so a separate router object is the right home.

**Corrected claim:** "Go to detail" from the player writes into the @State of the screen that started playback. If another tab is selected the detail is pushed off-screen in the origin tab; if the origin screen is gone (the alert-driven Downloads sheet, or a popped detail) nothing appears. In both cases the player has already closed. This is situational, not a common path.

**Corrected fix:** Add a dashboard-level `DashboardRouter: ObservableObject` (owned by DashboardView next to playerOverlay, injected as an environment object, DashboardTab made internal) and have the four closures call `router.reveal(...)` instead of setting local pending* state. Push onto the currently selected tab's stack when it is Live/Movies/Series/Search; switch to Movies or Series only when the visible tab is Settings or the origin was the sheet. Before choosing between (a) path-bound stacks with a value route and (b) a router-published pending item consumed by the root's existing navigationDestination(item:), run a simulator check of what happens when the tab has view-based pushes on top. If (a) is chosen, migrate that tab's category/all/recent links in the same change. Keep MovieDetailView's same-film shortcut only when that detail is the top of the visible stack. No iOS 26 API involved.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `NavigationStack.init(path: Binding<NavigationPath>, root:)` and `init(path: Binding<Data>, root:)` (typed collection) @available(iOS 16.0) (lines 14989-14992). `struct NavigationPath` iOS 16.0. `navigationDestination(for:destination:)` iOS 16.0 (line 1544). `navigationDestination(item:destination:)` iOS 17.0 (line 1552), already used in the code base. All found. DBVODStream, DBSeries and DBCategory are Hashable (Models/DBModels.swift:4, 34, 66), so they can be route payloads.

**Regression risks:** Mixing a bound path with the 27 view-based links can pop or reorder screens in ways that are not documented. A router that publishes per-tab paths re-evaluates DashboardView.body on every push; it already re-evaluates on contentStore and playerOverlay changes, so this is not a new cost class, but `item.root` must keep its identity so PlayerView is not remounted. The hand-off closures are passed into the *PlayerShell structs and PlayerView (out of scope): only the closure bodies may change, not the player side. No conflict with the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** UI tests: (1) start a film from Continue Watching in Movies, minimise, select Series, expand, tap the title; assert a movie detail is visible. (2) Trigger the download-warning alert, choose Go to downloads, play a downloaded film from the sheet, tap the title; assert the detail is visible. (3) Play from Search > detail with a queue, skip to the next film, tap the title; assert the detail appears in the visible stack. (4) Repeat (1) with a category grid pushed in Movies to see where the detail lands. Unit test for the router.

## navigation-architecture-4 — Choosing a language rebuilds the whole app through .id(selectedLanguage) at the root: the user is thrown from Settings > Language to the last content tab, a playing mini player is torn down and the catalog is reloaded

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Settings > App Language, Mini player, All tabs
- Code: `another-iptv-player/another_iptv_playerApp.swift:56-68`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:8, 14, 16-23, 131-137, 200-216`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:11, 14`, `another-iptv-player/ContentView.swift:17-18, 134-138, 152-163`, `another-iptv-player/Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:9-11, 37-39`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Touches another_iptv_playerApp.swift, which carries the uncommitted TipStore.shared.startObservingTransactions() line in init; only AppRootView changes. The two settings views are not edited: the destination is registered in the dashboards and the link lives in LanguagePickerSection.swift.

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a language in the list does not move the checkmark in place. The screen blanks for a moment and comes back on Live TV, Movies or Series, whichever content tab was used last. Anything playing in the mini player stops. Every tab is back at its root with search text and scroll position gone. In iOS Settings the list stays where it is and the tick moves.

**Mechanism (finder):** AppRootView applies .id(localization.selectedLanguage) to ContentView (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:62-66). A new id destroys all state below it. ContentView.selectedPlaylist goes back to nil and is restored asynchronously from UserDefaults, with the placeholder background shown in between (ContentView.swift:134-138, 152-163). DashboardView.init restores the tab with restoreInitialTab(), which by design never returns Settings (DashboardView.swift:22, 201, 215); M3U restarts at tab 0 (M3UDashboardView.swift:14). PlayerOverlayController is a @StateObject of the dashboard (DashboardView.swift:8, M3UDashboardView.swift:11), so the presentation and its PlayerView are released. .task(id: playlist.id) runs again and re-reads categories and all three catalogs from the database plus the EPG staleness check (DashboardView.swift:131-137, Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-151). The comment at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:51-55 explains why the id exists (most screens resolve L() without observing the manager); that goal can be kept with a narrower scope.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. another_iptv_playerApp.swift: drop the .id line, keep .environment(\.locale) and .environment(\.layoutDirection).
2. DashboardView and M3UDashboardView: observe LocalizationManager and put the id on the TabView only:
   TabView(selection: tabBinding) { ... }
     .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)
     .id(localization.selectedLanguage)
   Bars, tab titles and all browse content are rebuilt in the new language and direction; selectedTab, playerOverlay, globalSearchText and the catalog task survive because they live above the id.
3. Bind the Settings stack so the Language screen is still on top after the rebuild:
   @State private var settingsPath: [SettingsRoute] = []
   NavigationStack(path: $settingsPath) { PlaylistSettingsView(...)
     .navigationDestination(for: SettingsRoute.self) { _ in LanguagePickerListView() } }
   LanguagePickerSection.swift:9 becomes NavigationLink(value: SettingsRoute.language) { ... }.
The playlist list needs no id: the language can only be changed inside a dashboard and the list is re-inserted on exit. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** View.id(_:) (iOS 13.0); NavigationStack(path:root:) with a typed collection path (iOS 16.0); NavigationLink(value:label:) (iOS 16.0); View.navigationDestination(for:destination:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed. another_iptv_playerApp.swift:62-66 applies `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` to ContentView. A new id resets ContentView state: `selectedPlaylist` returns to nil (ContentView.swift:17), the @Query result starts nil so the placeholder shows (ContentView.swift:134-138), then attemptAutoLoad restores the playlist (ContentView.swift:152-163). DashboardView.init restores the tab with restoreInitialTab(), which never returns Settings (Views/DashboardView.swift:22, 201, 206-216); M3U restarts at tab 0 (Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:14). `playerOverlay` is a @StateObject of each dashboard (DashboardView.swift:8, M3UDashboardView.swift:11), so a docked player is released. `.task(id: playlist.id)` runs again (DashboardView.swift:131-137) and loadPlaylist re-reads categories and all three catalogs even for the same playlist; it only skips the loading flag (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-151) and flips streamsLoaded false then true, which re-runs every shelf filter. The picker sets the language at Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:38. The id is deliberate: it was added in 0ab5bcd (2026-07-22, "in-app language switch now refreshes the whole UI (incl. RTL)") and the comment at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:51-55 explains that L() is not observed. The proposed fix keeps that goal for everything inside the TabView, so it narrows the earlier work rather than undoing it. LanguagePickerSection is used only in the two settings views (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:128, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:123), both inside a dashboard, so the playlist list needs no id. Severity lowered: a language change is close to a once-per-install action.

**Corrected claim:** The original claim stands. Add: the root id is deliberate (0ab5bcd) and its purpose, refreshing every L() string and the layout direction, must be preserved; the user-visible cost is paid only on the rare language change.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with three additions. (1) Drop `.id` in AppRootView but keep `.environment(\.locale)` and `.environment(\.layoutDirection)`; only AppRootView changes in that file, the uncommitted `TipStore.shared.startObservingTransactions()` line in init stays. (2) Both dashboards observe LocalizationManager and put `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` on the TabView only; selectedTab, playerOverlay, globalSearchText and the catalog task live above it and survive. (3) Bind the Settings stack in both dashboards to `@State var settingsPath: [SettingsRoute]`, register `.navigationDestination(for: SettingsRoute.self)` there, and change LanguagePickerSection.swift:9 to `NavigationLink(value: SettingsRoute.language)`; the two settings view files are not edited. Additions: the player overlay sits outside the id, so text it has already rendered stays in the old language until its body next re-evaluates (acceptable for the mini card; check the expanded chrome, read-only for this lens). DashboardView's own alerts pick up new strings because it now observes the manager. Re-check the Arabic switch for a mirrored tab bar and navigation bar. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:18608 `@inlinable nonisolated public func id<ID>(_ id: ID) -> some View where ID : Hashable` (iOS 13). SwiftUI.swiftinterface:14992 `NavigationStack.init(path: Binding<Data>, root:)` for a typed MutableCollection/RandomAccessCollection/RangeReplaceableCollection path, iOS 16.0. `NavigationLink.init<P>(value: P?, label:) where P : Hashable` iOS 16.0 (line 10609). `navigationDestination(for:destination:)` iOS 16.0 (line 1544). All found.

**Regression risks:** This narrows deliberate work from 0ab5bcd. Anything outside the TabView that caches a localized string (the player overlay, a Downloads sheet opened at the time) will not refresh until re-rendered. The RTL switch must still mirror the UIKit-backed tab bar when only the TabView is rebuilt. All tab stacks and their state still reset on a language change, as today; only Settings is restored through the path. The value-based language link needs the destination registered in both dashboards or it becomes a dead row. another_iptv_playerApp.swift carries uncommitted tip-jar work in init; do not touch it.

**How to verify:** UI test: Settings > App Language > Deutsch; assert the language list is still on screen, the tick is on Deutsch and the title is translated. Repeat with a mini player docked and assert it is still present and playing. Switch to Arabic and compare screenshots for a right-to-left tab bar, navigation bar and back-swipe edge. Log PlaylistContentStore.loadPlaylist to confirm it no longer runs on a language change. Repeat on an M3U playlist. Run on both the 18.x and 26.0 runtimes.

## navigation-architecture-5 — All seven NavigationStacks are created without a path and 27 links are view-based, so nothing outside a screen can push, pop or restore; the per-cell cost of the eager destinations turns out to be small

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort L · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series, Search, Settings, M3U Channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:50, 57, 64, 71, 78, 234`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:28, 38`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:114-116, 315-317, 334-336, 418-420, 451-453, 692-694`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:115-117, 292-294, 311-313, 394-396, 423-425, 650`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:110-112, 119-121, 356-358`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:66-68, 75-77, 337-339`, `another-iptv-player/Views/FavoritesView.swift:134, 160`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:180-182, 205-207`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-32`

**What the user perceives:** Three things a native tab app does are out of reach today: jumping from the player to a detail in the right tab (see the hand-back finding), staying on the same screen after a language change, and coming back to the same place after relaunch. Whether re-tapping the selected tab pops to root and scrolls to top was not runnable here and has to be checked; where the tab bar is hidden it cannot be tried at all.

**Mechanism (finder):** NavigationStack { } appears five times in DashboardView and twice in M3UDashboardView, never with a path. 27 NavigationLink { Destination } sites build their destination value during the cell's body; six more pushes go through navigationDestination(item:) with a private @State each (VODView:161, SeriesView:162, MovieDetailView:96, DownloadsView:134 and 137, EPGGuideView:63). View-based pushes are not represented in a bound path, so even adding a path later cannot pop them. Cost count requested by the brief: MovieDetailView.init creates 3 @Query wrappers (MovieDetailView.swift:24-31), SeriesDetailView.init 4 (SeriesView.swift:814-821), FavoritesView.init 5 (FavoritesView.swift:18-26), WatchHistoryListView.init 1. In GRDBQuery a Query init only stores an Environment key path and the request enum; the tracker is a @StateObject created when the view is installed (GRDBQuery/Sources/GRDBQuery/Query.swift:73-79), and EPGGuideView's view model sits behind StateObject's autoclosure (EPGGuideView.swift:37-39). So no observation, allocation or I/O starts per cell; what a cell pays is a copy of a roughly 22-field DBVODStream plus Playlist and three request structs. The reason to change is control, not scroll speed. On re-tap: both installed runtimes contain an internal reselection hook (SwiftUI.ReselectionTraitState and View.onReselect, found with nm in the 18.1 and 26.0 simulator SwiftUI binaries; not in the public interface), which suggests the system handles pop-to-root and scroll-to-top for plain NavigationStack plus ScrollView roots, but that is a simulator check, not a code fact.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Introduce one route type and bind one path per tab in DashboardView / M3UDashboardView:

enum BrowseRoute: Hashable {
  case liveCategory(DBCategory), allLive, guide
  case vodCategory(DBCategory), allVOD, recentVOD, movie(DBVODStream, queue: QueueRef)
  case seriesCategory(DBCategory), allSeries, recentSeries, series(DBSeries)
  case favorites(type: String), history(type: String?)
}
NavigationStack(path: router.binding(for: .movies)) {
  VODView(playlist: playlist)
    .dashboardNavigation(...)
    .navigationDestination(for: BrowseRoute.self) { BrowseDestination(route: $0, playlist: playlist) }
}
// cells
NavigationLink(value: BrowseRoute.movie(item.stream, queue: queueRef)) { VODStreamCard(...) }

Register the destination once at each stack root (inside dashboardNavigation), never inside a lazy container. Do not put the play queue array into the route: Array hashing would walk every 22-field element on each push; carry a reference box hashed by identity or a queue descriptor. Keep the .equatable() shelf rows as they are; value links make their bodies lighter. Order of work: detail routes first (unblocks the hand-back fix), then category / all / recent, then toolbar and settings links. After migration the re-tap rule is one line in tabBinding's setter if the system does not already do it: if newTab == selectedTab { router.popToRoot(newTab) }.

**APIs:** NavigationStack(path: Binding<NavigationPath>, root:) (iOS 16.0); NavigationLink(value:label:) (iOS 16.0); View.navigationDestination(for:destination:) (iOS 16.0); NavigationPath (append, removeLast, isEmpty) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The facts are right. Seven tab stacks are created without a path (Views/DashboardView.swift:50, 57, 64, 71, 78; Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:28, 38). grep finds 29 NavigationLink lines, 2 of them comments, so 27 view-based links. Six navigationDestination(item:) sites exist (VODView:161, SeriesView:162, MovieDetailView:96, DownloadsView:134 and 137, EPGGuideView:63). The cost analysis is also right: GRDBQuery's `Query.init(_:in:)` only stores an Environment key path and the request, and the tracker is `@StateObject private var tracker = Tracker()` behind StateObject's autoclosure (GRDBQuery/Sources/GRDBQuery/Query.swift:21, 74-80), so eager destinations start no observation or I/O per cell. The comment at Views/VODView.swift:444-447 shows the per-shelf queue was already hoisted out of the cell on purpose. What does not hold is the framing as a finding in its own right: by the finder's own analysis there is no scroll or frame cost, and the user-visible consequences are exactly findings 3 and 4. State restoration after relaunch is not something the owner asked for. Re-tap-to-root is unverified: the evidence is private symbols found with nm, which says nothing about behaviour. The proposed BrowseRoute is also incomplete: WatchHistoryListView is built by a caller closure carrying an onPlay closure (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:19, 30-32) and RecentlyAddedVODDetailView takes an items array (Views/VODView.swift:315-317); neither can be expressed as the payload-free cases `history(type:)` / `recentVOD` without moving play logic out of VODView and SeriesView. A whole-app migration at effort L conflicts with the "smallest change" rule.

**Corrected claim:** The tab stacks are unbound and all 27 links are view-based. This has no measurable per-cell cost and is not perceivable on its own. It is the structural reason behind two real problems (the player hand-back and the language-change reset) and should be scoped to what those need, not treated as a separate app-wide defect.

**Corrected fix:** Do not schedule the full BrowseRoute migration as its own item. Fold the minimum into the other two findings: a typed `[SettingsRoute]` path for the Settings stack (finding 4) and whatever the simulator check in finding 3 shows is needed for a reliable "reveal detail" (a router, with path-bound Movies/Series/Search stacks only if required). If a tab is migrated, migrate all of its links in one step so a bound path and view-based pushes are not mixed, register navigationDestination(for:) once at the stack root outside lazy containers, keep the `.equatable()` shelf rows and the per-shelf queue hoisting, and carry the queue as a descriptor or identity-hashed box. Leave history and recently-added destinations view-based unless their play closures are moved first. Add a manual pop-to-root on re-tap only if the simulator shows the system does not already do it.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `NavigationStack.init(path: Binding<NavigationPath>, root:)` iOS 16.0 (line 14991); `struct NavigationPath` with count, isEmpty, init() iOS 16.0 (line 5999); `NavigationLink.init<P>(value: P?, label:)` iOS 16.0 (line 10609); `navigationDestination(for:destination:)` iOS 16.0 (line 1544). All found. The reselection hook the finder mentions is not in the public interface and cannot be relied on. Model payloads are Hashable (Models/DBModels.swift:4, 34, 66); Playlist is only Equatable (Models/Playlist.swift:9), so it cannot go into a route.

**Regression risks:** Large surface: 27 links across the Equatable shelf rows and paginated grids that were tuned earlier. A route that carries the queue array would hash every element on push, and a route payload that changes identity could defeat the shelf rows' Equatable short-circuit. Partial migration mixes a bound path with view-based pushes, with undocumented results. Destinations that take closures (history onPlay) would need play logic moved, which touches the player hand-off.

**How to verify:** Settle the open question on the current build first, on the 18.x and 26.0 simulators: push Movies > film detail (tab bar visible), tap the selected tab again and record whether the stack pops to root; tap once more and record whether the shelf list scrolls to top; repeat on iPad with the top tab pill. If any tab is migrated: UI tests for push, back and pop-to-root, plus an Instruments SwiftUI trace of a shelf scroll on a real catalog comparing body counts before and after.

## navigation-architecture-6 — Favorites is a filled accent star in each tab's toolbar that pushes one cross-type screen into whichever tab you are in; the same glyph toggles a favourite on detail screens

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV / Movies / Series home toolbar, Favorites, M3U Favorites, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:52, 59, 66, 231-241`, `another-iptv-player/Views/FavoritesView.swift:37-44, 56-58, 134, 160`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:74-83`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:61-63`, `another-iptv-player/Views/MovieDetailView.swift:86-91`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:880-887`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Is Favorites per tab (scoped to the tab's type) or one global Library with History and Downloads? The second changes the tab line-up.

**What the user perceives:** A filled blue star in a navigation bar reads as "this is favourited", and on the detail screens the star is exactly that toggle (iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png). On the tab roots the same star is a doorway (iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png). Behind it is a screen titled Favorites with a Live TV / Movies / Series switch, pushed inside the current tab: the Series tab can show live favourites and push a movie detail into the Series stack (iphone-light/L04-favorites-live.png shows Series selected in the tab bar). Each of the three tabs keeps its own copy with its own segment and search text.

**Mechanism (finder):** DashboardNavigationModifier adds NavigationLink(destination: FavoritesView(playlist:initialType:)) with a tinted star.fill and no accessibility label to every content tab (DashboardView.swift:232-240; the M3U twin has a label, M3UChannelsView.swift:82). FavoritesView always offers all three types through a segmented Picker (FavoritesView.swift:37-44) and pushes MovieDetailView / SeriesDetailView into the hosting stack (lines 134, 160). The two favourites screens disagree on chrome: Xtream uses a large title and keeps the tab bar (FavoritesView.swift:56-57), M3U uses an inline title and hides it (M3UFavoritesView.swift:62-63).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest change: move the entry into the More menu from the toolbar finding as a labelled item with the outline glyph (Label(L("favorites.title"), systemImage: "star")), so the filled star keeps one meaning. Scope the screen to the tab it was opened from: pass the type, drop the segmented Picker for that entry and title it with the type (or keep the Picker only when opened from Search). Give both favourites screens the same title mode and tab bar rule. Larger option, owner's call: one Library destination that holds Favorites, History and Downloads, as a sidebar section on iPad and a tab on iPhone in place of Settings, with Settings behind a gear in Library.

**APIs:** Menu / Label (iOS 14.0); TabSection (iPad sidebar grouping, only for the Library option) (iOS 18.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Facts check out in code. Views/DashboardView.swift:232-240 puts NavigationLink(destination: FavoritesView(playlist:initialType:)) with Image("star.fill") + foregroundStyle(Color.accentColor) and no accessibilityLabel on the three content tabs; the M3U twin has the label (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:82). FavoritesView always shows the three-way segmented Picker (Views/FavoritesView.swift:37-44) and pushes MovieDetailView / SeriesDetailView into the hosting stack (134, 160). Chrome differs: FavoritesView.swift:56-57 is large title and has no .toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar), M3UFavoritesView.swift:62-63 is inline and hides the tab bar. Screenshots iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png and iphone-dark/M01 show the blue filled star next to two monochrome glyphs.

Corrections: (1) The 'same glyph, two meanings' collision is weaker than stated. On detail screens the favourited state is a YELLOW star.fill and the unfavourited state a primary outline star (MovieDetailView.swift:86-91, SeriesView.swift:880-887; iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png shows the outline). The root doorway is accent-blue. Same symbol, different colour, different screen level. (2) iphone-light/L04-favorites-live.png is not evidence of cross-type leakage: the shots README says L03-L06 in iphone-light were captured on the Series tab by mistake, and the segment shown is Series, i.e. the screen opened on the hosting tab's own type exactly as initialType intends. The cross-type reach is real only if the user moves the segment. (3) 'No accessibility label' is true in code, but an SF Symbol image gets a system default description, so VoiceOver is not silent; it is just not the app's own L("favorites.title") (the app has an in-app language switch, so the system string can be in the wrong language). (4) The first step of the fix depends on a 'More menu' from another finding that is not in this set, so it cannot be judged standalone. (5) Scoping Favorites per tab vs. one cross-type screen is a product decision, not a defect: the current design (one screen, segment preselected to the current tab) is coherent. History gives no reason either way (initialType dates from the first import, d2489f9 / fe55017).

Not in the finding but visible and in the same screen: the Picker's .background(.ultraThinMaterial) (FavoritesView.swift:44) paints a grey band from the top of the screen down to below the segmented control, against a black/white content area (iphone-dark/M09-favorites-movies.png, iphone-light/L04). No other pushed list has that band.

**Corrected claim:** The Favorites entry on the three Xtream tab roots is a tinted, filled star without the app's own accessibility label, while the M3U entry has one; the Xtream and M3U favourites screens disagree on title mode and tab-bar visibility, and the Xtream one alone keeps the tab bar among pushed list screens and draws a material band behind its segmented control. Whether Favorites should be scoped to the tab it was opened from (or become a Library destination) is a product decision, not a defect; the doorway star (accent blue) and the detail toggle (yellow when on, outline when off) are already distinguishable by colour.

**Corrected fix:** Small, standalone, no dependency on other findings: in DashboardView.swift:234-238 drop the accent foregroundStyle so the glyph is a normal monochrome bar item (keep star.fill or switch to the outline "star", both already used in the code base) and add .accessibilityLabel(L("favorites.title")) as M3UChannelsView.swift:82 does. In FavoritesView.swift remove .background(.ultraThinMaterial) from the Picker (or move the Picker into the scroll content) and apply the same title mode and tab-bar rule as the other pushed list screens (they use .large + .toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar), e.g. VODView.swift:379-380); make M3UFavoritesView.swift:62 use the same title mode. If a More menu is introduced by the toolbar finding, move the entry there as Label(L("favorites.title"), systemImage: "star"). Per-tab scoping (dropping the Picker) and the Library tab are owner decisions; do not do them as part of a fix.

**API check:** Menu and Label: present in SwiftUI.swiftinterface, iOS 14. TabSection: 'public struct TabSection<Header, Content, Footer, SelectionValue>' @available(iOS 18.0, ...) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:16071-16072 (only needed for the Library option). accessibilityLabel, toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar), navigationBarTitleDisplayMode are already used in the code base. SF Symbol names cannot be checked in the interface files; "star" and "star.fill" are both already rendered by the app.

**Regression risks:** Hiding the tab bar on Favorites changes where the docked mini player sits on that screen, same as on the other pushed lists; check with the mini player docked. Removing the material behind the Picker changes how the segmented control looks when grid content scrolls under it (it is a sibling above the ScrollView in a VStack, so content does not actually scroll under it; safe). If the entry moves into a Menu, a NavigationLink inside a Menu in a toolbar is unreliable with destination-based links; it would need a state-driven navigationDestination. Dropping the Picker would strand users who use one tab to reach all favourites.

**How to verify:** Screenshots of the three roots and of Favorites (light and dark, iOS 18.1 and 26.0) before and after. VoiceOver or an XCUITest that finds the bar button by the label L("favorites.title"). With a mini player docked, open Favorites and check the card position against a category grid.

## navigation-architecture-7 — Entering a playlist slides the dashboard in like a push, but there is no back button or back-swipe; the only way out is a row at the top of Settings

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list, Dashboard entry and exit, Settings > Back to Playlists
- Code: `another-iptv-player/ContentView.swift:42-69, 130-133, 165-170`, `another-iptv-player/Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:45-54`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:41-50`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:224, 248-250`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Cross-fade context switch (steps 1 and 2, ContentView only) or an in-dashboard playlist switcher menu (step 3)? Step 3 would not touch the settings views; removing the Settings row afterwards would touch the two files that hold the TipJarRow line.

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a playlist row (which shows a disclosure chevron, iphone-light/P01-playlist-list.png) moves the dashboard in from the trailing edge, the motion of a push. Nothing on the dashboard leads back: no back button, no edge swipe. The exit is Settings tab > first row "Back to Playlists" (iphone-light/T01-settings-1.png), after which the dashboard slides out to the trailing edge like a pop.

**Mechanism (finder):** ContentView switches between the list and the dashboard with an if/else inside a ZStack; the dashboard uses .transition(.asymmetric(insertion: .move(edge: .trailing), removal: .move(edge: .trailing))) and the list fades (ContentView.swift:66-69, 130-133), driven by withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) (lines 48, 58, 166). It is not a navigation push, so there is no interactive pop. onDismiss is passed into dashboardNavigation for every tab but the modifier never uses it (DashboardView.swift:224, 248-250), so no bar-level affordance exists. On exit, unload() and setActivePlaylist(nil) run synchronously right after the animated state change (ContentView.swift:48-53, 58-62), publishing a dozen store changes into the dashboard while it is still sliding out; whether that shows as a hitch with a large catalog needs a device.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Treat it as a context switch, not a level in a hierarchy. In ContentView.swift only:
1. Replace the move transition with a non-directional one on both branches, e.g. .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .scale(scale: 0.98))), so the motion no longer promises a back gesture.
2. Release the catalog when the removal has finished:
   withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) { selectedPlaylist = nil } completion: {
     if selectedPlaylist == nil { PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload(); EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil) }
   }
   (the guard covers a new selection made during the animation; same for the M3U branch).
3. Optional, owner's call: a playlist switcher reachable from the tab roots, a leading toolbar Menu added in dashboardNavigation that lists the playlists with a checkmark plus "Manage Playlists...", using the onDismiss that is already passed in. Switching in place then needs .id(playlist.id) on the dashboard.

**APIs:** withAnimation(_:completionCriteria:_:completion:) (iOS 17.0); AnyTransition.opacity / scale / combined(with:) (iOS 13.0); ToolbarItemPlacement.topBarLeading with Menu (option 3) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts are right. ContentView.swift:42-69 switches list/dashboard with if/else in a ZStack; the dashboard branch has .transition(.asymmetric(insertion: .move(edge: .trailing), removal: .move(edge: .trailing))) (66-69), the list branch fades (130-133), driven by withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) (48, 58, 166). It is not a navigation push, so there is no back button or interactive pop. The playlist rows draw their own chevron.right (ContentView.swift:235-237; iphone-light/P01-playlist-list.png), which reinforces the push promise. DashboardNavigationModifier stores onDismiss (DashboardView.swift:224) and never uses it; the only exits are the first row in PlaylistSettingsView.swift:45-54 and M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:41-50 (iphone-light/T01-settings-1.png). unload() and setActivePlaylist(nil) run synchronously after the animated state change (ContentView.swift:52-53, 61-62); unload() clears every list (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:183-190) and setActivePlaylist(nil) sets snapshot = nil (EPG/EPGStore.swift:83-89), which changes the \.epgSnapshot environment of the whole dashboard (DashboardView.swift:130). History: the transition and the settings row date from the first import (git log -S'move(edge: .trailing)' -> d2489f9 / fe55017), no comment marks them as deliberate.

Corrections: (1) Severity. The last playlist is auto-restored on launch without animation (ContentView.swift:152-163), so a user with one playlist sees this transition once; it is not on the browse path the owner asked about. Low, not medium. (2) The exit hitch is described imprecisely. The store mutations happen in the same main-thread turn as the tap, before the first animation frame, so the cost (freeing 100k+ model structs, re-evaluating three hidden tab roots, the environment change) shows as a delay before the slide starts, not as store changes 'while it is still sliding out'. The visible tab at that moment is always Settings, which does not render the catalog, so there is no visible content flash. Whether the delay is perceptible needs a device. (3) Step 1 (cross-fade + scale) is a taste change, not a defect fix, and it carries its own risk: it applies group opacity to a UIKit-backed TabView whose bars are glass/material on iOS 26 and blur on iOS 18, and materials under an animated parent alpha commonly render flat or pop; the current move transition does not have that problem. It also leaves the row chevron promising a push. (4) Step 2 compiles and is sound: the completion guard on selectedPlaylist == nil covers re-selection inside 0.3 s, loadPlaylist clears lists itself when the id differs (PlaylistContentStore.swift:106-109) and loadToken guards late loads.

**Corrected claim:** The playlist list -> dashboard switch is a custom slide that looks like a push but offers no back affordance; the only exit is a row in Settings, and the onDismiss passed to every tab root is unused. This is a discoverability and consistency issue on a rarely used path (the last playlist is auto-restored), not a browsing-fluidity issue. On exit, the catalog and EPG state are torn down synchronously in the tap handler, which with a large catalog may delay the start of the exit animation; this is unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** Do step 2 only as the fix: in both onDismiss closures in ContentView.swift use withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) { selectedPlaylist = nil } completion: { if selectedPlaylist == nil { PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload() /* or M3UContentStore */; EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil) } }. Keep the existing transition unless a recording on iOS 18.1 and 26.0 shows the cross-fade looks clean with the tab bar and nav bar materials; if the owner wants the push promise removed cheaply, removing the hand-drawn chevron.right from the playlist rows (ContentView.swift:235-237) does that with no transition change. The in-dashboard playlist switcher (leading toolbar Menu using the already-plumbed onDismiss) is the most native answer but is an owner decision and a separate piece of work; it must not remove the Settings row in the same change (those two files hold the uncommitted TipJarRow line).

**API check:** withAnimation with completion: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:10277-10282 '@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *) public func withAnimation<Result>(_ animation: Animation? = .default, completionCriteria: AnimationCompletionCriteria = .logicallyComplete, _ body: () throws -> Result, completion: @escaping () -> Void) rethrows -> Result' (originally defined in SwiftUI, moved to SwiftUICore in 26). Fine for the iOS 18 target, no fallback needed. AnyTransition.opacity / .scale / combined(with:) are iOS 13 and already used (ContentView.swift:131, DashboardView.swift:111). ToolbarItemPlacement.topBarLeading / Menu exist (topBarTrailing is already used at MovieDetailView.swift:86).

**Regression risks:** Deferring unload by 0.3 s keeps the catalog and the EPG minute timer alive slightly longer; harmless. If the completion never fires (animations disabled in UI tests, Reduce Motion does not disable it) the catalog would stay in memory on the playlist list; with .logicallyComplete it fires even when the animation is skipped, but the existing UI test that returns to the list should assert a later re-entry still loads. With a docked mini player, the player subtree is removed with the dashboard: a scale/opacity transition would scale and fade the video surface instead of translating it (see the comment at DashboardView.swift:109-111 about video surfaces and geometry). Cross-fading glass/blur bars can look broken mid-fade. Settings files must not be restructured (tip-jar WIP).

**How to verify:** Device with a real catalog (50k+ movies): Instruments Hangs / Animation Hitches over 'Back to Playlists', measuring tap-to-first-frame before and after step 2. Simulator recording of enter and exit on iOS 18.1 and 26.0 if the transition is changed, looking at the tab bar and nav bar materials frame by frame, once with a mini player docked. UI test: Settings > Back to Playlists returns to the list, re-entering loads the catalog, and selecting another playlist within the animation does not end with an empty dashboard.
