## navigation-architecture-8 — Multi-select filters in the sort menu are plain Buttons, so the menu closes after every genre, file type or flag and has to be reopened for each one

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category / All Movies, Series category / All Series, Live category / All Channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:750-770`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:691-711`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:642-667`

**What the user perceives:** Picking three genres in All Series takes three round trips: open the menu, tap, menu closes, grid jumps to top, open again. System menus that hold several switches (Files view options, Mail filters) stay open while the user ticks them, and VoiceOver announces them as on/off.

**Mechanism (finder):** The sort part is a native Menu { Picker } and is fine (iphone-light/M05-movies-sort-menu.png). The filter part builds Buttons that swap between Label(text, systemImage: "checkmark") and Text (VODView.swift:752-761, SeriesView.swift:693-702, LiveStreamsView.swift:643-660). A Button in a Menu always dismisses it and carries no selected trait.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use Toggle rows and keep the menu open for that section:

Section(L("filter.genre")) {
  ForEach(genres, id: \.self) { genre in
    Toggle(genre, isOn: Binding(
      get: { genreFilter.contains(genre) },
      set: { on in if on { genreFilter.insert(genre) } else { genreFilter.remove(genre) } }))
  }
}
.menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled)

Same shape for file types and for the two live flags. The off-main recompute and the paginated grid stay untouched. Deployment target covers the API; no fallback needed.

**APIs:** View.menuActionDismissBehavior(_:) (iOS 16.4); Toggle inside Menu (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read all three menus. VODView.swift:750-770, SeriesView.swift:691-711 and LiveStreamsView.swift:642-667 build the multi-select rows as Button whose label swaps between Label(text, systemImage: "checkmark") and Text; the sort part above is a real Picker. A Button action in a Menu dismisses it, so each additional genre / file type / flag needs a re-open, and the rows carry no selected state for VoiceOver. iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png shows the Filter section rendered as plain rows without the leading checkmark column the Picker rows have. Each toggle also resets the grid: recompute() sets visibleCount back to the first page (SeriesView.swift:~625) and VOD scrolls to the top on fileTypeFilter change (VODView.swift:724-728), so the round trip is as described. Nothing in comments or history marks the Buttons as deliberate (introduced with 654cefc, the sort/filter feature). The proposed change does not touch the deliberate performance work: the genre and file-type lists are precomputed from the full source and held in @State (SeriesView.swift genres, VODView.swift:621 fileTypes), so the rows are stable while the menu is open, and recompute stays off-main via .task(id:).

Small corrections to the fix, not to the claim: put .menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled) on the toggles (the ForEach), not on the whole Section, so the destructive 'Clear' button still closes the menu; and for Live use a Binding over the OptionSet (get: filter.contains(.catchup), set: insert/remove). One thing only a run can settle: the menu's own label switches between line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle and .circle.fill when the first filter goes on (VODView.swift:773, SeriesView.swift:714, LiveStreamsView.swift:670) and the Menu lives in a ToolbarItem; if UIKit rebuilds the bar button item on that label change the open menu would close on the first toggle.

**Corrected claim:** Multi-select filters in the sort/filter menu on category and All grids (genres, file types, live catch-up / EPG flags) are plain Buttons with a hand-made checkmark, so the menu closes after every selection, the grid resets, and the rows have no on/off state for assistive tech.

**Corrected fix:** Replace the Buttons with Toggle rows bound to the existing @State sets (Binding get: contains, set: insert/remove; for Live, a Binding over LiveStreamFilter.contains / insert / remove), and apply .menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled) to the ForEach of toggles only, leaving the 'Clear' Button with the default dismissing behaviour. Keep the Picker for sort, the .task(id:) recompute and the pagination untouched. If the simulator run shows the menu closing on the first toggle because the toolbar label symbol changes, keep the label symbol constant while open (e.g. drive the fill variant from a value that is updated on menu dismissal) or accept the constant outline symbol.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13737-13738 '@available(iOS 16.4, macOS 13.3, tvOS 16.4, watchOS 9.4, *) nonisolated public func menuActionDismissBehavior(_ behavior: MenuActionDismissBehavior) -> some View'; 13741-13748 'public struct MenuActionDismissBehavior : Equatable' with 'static let automatic / enabled' and 'static let disabled' (@available tvOS 17.0, macOS unavailable, watchOS unavailable; available on iOS). Below the iOS 18 target, no availability check needed. Toggle is iOS 13 and is rendered as a checkable item inside Menu.

**Regression risks:** With the menu staying open, every toggle restarts the off-main recompute and re-diffs the open menu; with dozens of genres the menu content must update in place (expected on iOS 18/26, to be confirmed). The 'Clear' row appears and disappears while the menu is open, which resizes it. The toolbar label symbol change on first toggle may dismiss the menu (see reasons). VOD scrolls the grid to the top behind the open menu on each change; harmless. No effect on Equatable shelf rows, pagination or prefetch.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 18.1 and 26.0: All Series with the demo genres, open the menu, tap two genres, assert the menu is still presented, both rows show the checkmark and the grid count changed; then tap Clear and assert the menu closes. Repeat on a Live category for the two flags. The demo catalog has one movie file type, so the VOD section needs a fixture with two container extensions. VoiceOver: rows announce a selected/checked state.

## navigation-architecture-9 — Only the selected content tab survives a relaunch; the navigation path, the Settings / Search tab and the M3U tab are always reset

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort L · risk medium
- Screens: Relaunch after the system ended the app in the background, All tabs
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:10-12, 26-34, 190-217`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:13-14`, `another-iptv-player/ContentView.swift:22, 152-163`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Is deep restoration wanted at all? It is a nicety, depends on the router work, and a restored detail must cope with a catalog that changed since.

**What the user perceives:** A user reading a series detail who switches to another app and comes back after iOS reclaimed memory lands on the tab root, with the season choice and scroll position gone. The playlist and the content tab are kept.

**Mechanism (finder):** The last playlist id and the last content tab are stored in UserDefaults (ContentView.swift:22, 158-162; DashboardView.swift:11, 197-216), app-wide rather than per scene. Settings and Search are deliberately not restored (DashboardView.swift:25, 200-201) and M3U always starts on Channels (M3UDashboardView.swift:13-14). There is no @SceneStorage anywhere, and with path-less stacks there is nothing that could be stored.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Only after the router finding. Make the routes Codable by carrying ids instead of model copies, then persist per scene:

@SceneStorage("dashboard.paths") private var storedPaths: Data?
// on scenePhase == .background
storedPaths = try? JSONEncoder().encode(router.paths.compactMapValues { $0.codable })
// on init, after the tab restore
NavigationPath(codableRepresentation)

Destinations resolve their model by id from PlaylistContentStore or the database and show the existing loading state until streamsLoaded. Keep the synchronous tab restore in DashboardView.init as it is. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** SceneStorage<Data?> (iOS 14.0); NavigationPath.codable / NavigationPath(_: CodableRepresentation) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The description of the current behaviour is accurate: lastPlaylistId and the content tab are in UserDefaults (ContentView.swift:22, 158-162; DashboardView.swift:11, 197-216), Settings/Search are deliberately not restored (comments at DashboardView.swift:10, 25, 200), there is no @SceneStorage or NavigationPath anywhere (grep: only five navigationDestination(item:) sites and 29 destination-closure NavigationLinks), so nothing below the tab root can be restored.

Why this is not confirmed as a defect: (1) The M3U part is moot. M3UDashboardView has exactly two tabs, Channels and Settings (M3UDashboardView.swift:27-43), so 'always starts on Channels' is the same rule the Xtream dashboard applies (Settings is never restored); nothing is lost. (2) 'App-wide rather than per scene' has no practical consequence: the built Info.plist does declare UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes = true, but the catalog, EPG and favourites stores are process-wide singletons with one active playlist (PlaylistContentStore.shared, EPGStore.shared), so two windows cannot hold different playlists anyway. (3) It is not a native-feel gap in the sense of the request: the owner asked for fluid browsing, and restoring a deep stack after a cold relaunch is a nicety, as the finding itself says in decision_needed. (4) The fix is larger and riskier than rated. It presupposes a router that does not exist: every one of the 29 NavigationLink(destination:) sites would have to become value-based first, including those inside the deliberately Equatable shelf rows and paginated grids (e.g. the comment at VODView.swift:444 about building the queue once per shelf, which a value route must preserve), and each restored destination has to wait for PlaylistContentStore.loadPlaylist (async DB load of 100k+ rows) and tolerate ids that no longer exist after a sync. The models are already Codable + Hashable (Models/DBModels.swift:15, 34, 66), so the 'ids instead of model copies' step is optional, but that does not shrink the router work. Effort is L, not M.

**Corrected claim:** After a cold relaunch the app restores the playlist and the last content tab but not the navigation stack inside the tab. That is a consequence of destination-based NavigationLinks and is consistent across Xtream and M3U; Settings/Search not being restored is deliberate. Deep-stack restoration is an optional enhancement, not a defect.

**Corrected fix:** none for this pass. Revisit only if a value-based router is adopted for other reasons; then persisting NavigationPath.codable per tab in @SceneStorage on scenePhase == .background is a small add-on, with destinations resolving by id and falling back to the tab root when the id is gone or the catalog has not loaded.

**API check:** SceneStorage: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7036-7037 '@available(iOS 14.0, ...) @frozen @propertyWrapper public struct SceneStorage<Value> : DynamicProperty'. NavigationPath: 'public var codable: NavigationPath.CodableRepresentation?' (6007), 'public init(_ codable: NavigationPath.CodableRepresentation)' (6014), 'public struct CodableRepresentation : Codable' (6018), iOS 16.0. All below the iOS 18 target. The snippet in the finding is pseudo-code ('router.paths.compactMapValues { $0.codable }' encodes a dictionary of optional representations and 'NavigationPath(codableRepresentation)' needs a decoded value); it would need a real implementation.

**Regression risks:** Converting the links to value-based routes touches the Equatable shelf rows, the per-shelf queue construction and the paginated grids, i.e. the deliberate performance work; a careless navigationDestination(for:) placement inside lazy containers breaks navigation. Restoring into a detail before the catalog load finishes can show an empty or stale detail, and a restored detail for an item removed by a sync needs a fallback. Restoring while a player hand-off is expected (the overlay is not restored) can confuse users who left from the player.

**How to verify:** If ever implemented: UI test that pushes Series > detail, backgrounds, terminates and relaunches the app and asserts the detail is on screen once streams are loaded; unit test encoding/decoding a path of each route kind; a test with a route whose id no longer exists asserting a fall-back to the tab root.

## navigation-architecture-10 — Tab roots force the navigation bar background to stay visible and sibling screens disagree on large versus inline titles

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV / Movies / Series / Settings roots, M3U Channels root, Favorites vs M3U Favorites, Recently Added vs Watch history
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:80-81, 229-230, 242-243`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:32-33`, `another-iptv-player/Views/FavoritesView.swift:57`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:62`, `another-iptv-player/Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:81`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:379`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Large or inline for the pushed grid screens; either is defensible as long as it is one rule.

**What the user perceives:** On iOS 18 the tab roots are expected to show a permanent bar material and hairline behind the large title even at the top of the list, while the pushed grids have the usual transparent bar at rest, so the bar changes character on every push and pop. The same kind of screen also switches title style: Favorites is large on Xtream and inline on M3U; Recently Added is large while Watch history, reached from the neighbouring shelf header, is inline.

**Mechanism (finder):** .toolbar(.visible, for: .navigationBar) and .toolbarBackground(.visible, for: .navigationBar) are applied to every tab root (DashboardView.swift:242-243, M3UDashboardView.swift:32-33) and to no pushed screen; they date from the first import with no stated reason. The iOS 26 screenshots show no extra band (iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png), so the visible effect is on iOS 18 and was not captured. Title modes are set per screen with no rule: large at DashboardView.swift:230, FavoritesView.swift:57 and VODView.swift:379; inline at M3UFavoritesView.swift:62 and WatchHistoryListView.swift:81.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Remove the two modifiers from DashboardNavigationModifier and M3UDashboardView so the roots use the system scroll-edge behaviour on both OS versions. Pick one title rule and apply it: large on tab roots; one mode for every "list of things" push (category, all, recently added, history, favourites); inline for detail, guide, downloads and language. No new API.

**APIs:** View.toolbarBackground(_:for:) (to be removed; renamed toolbarBackgroundVisibility in the SDK) (iOS 16.0, soft-deprecated); View.navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(_:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Two claims in one finding; they fare differently.

Title modes (confirmed by code): pushed list screens are large almost everywhere: LiveStreamsView.swift:496, 721; VODView.swift:379, 562, 821; SeriesView.swift:356, 534, 760; M3UChannelsView.swift:501; FavoritesView.swift:57. The two outliers are WatchHistoryListView.swift:81 (.inline, reached from the shelf header next to Recently Added, which is large at VODView.swift:379) and M3UFavoritesView.swift:62 (.inline, against FavoritesView.swift:57 large). So a rule already exists in practice (list pushes are large, detail / guide / downloads / language are inline) and only two screens break it; 'no rule' overstates it. Related and unmentioned: FavoritesView is also the only pushed list that does not hide the tab bar.

Forced bar background (plausible, not verified): .toolbar(.visible, for: .navigationBar) and .toolbarBackground(.visible, for: .navigationBar) are on the tab roots only (DashboardView.swift:242-243, M3UDashboardView.swift:32-33). git log -S shows them in the very first import (fe55017, native/ios/.../DashboardView.swift:151-152) with no comment, and nothing outside the player hides the navigation bar today (grep for navigationBarHidden / hidden, for: .navigationBar is empty), so .toolbar(.visible, ...) is a no-op leftover. On the iOS 26 screenshots there is no band at rest or scrolled (iphone-dark/M01-movies-home.png, M02-movies-home-scrolled.png, iphone-light/M01), so on iOS 26 the modifier has no visible effect. The described iOS 18 effect (permanent bar material and hairline behind the large title, most visible in dark mode as grey on black) matches how toolbarBackground(.visible) behaves on iOS 16-18, but no iOS 18 screenshot exists and I was not allowed to run the simulator; the finding itself marks it needs-simulator-run. The iOS 18.1 runtime is installed (CoreSimulator volume iOS_22B81), so it can be settled. It also cannot be excluded without a run that the modifier masks a large-title / search-field flicker on the shelf roots on iOS 18.

**Corrected claim:** Two pushed list screens break the app's own title rule: Watch history and M3U Favorites are inline while every other pushed list (categories, All, Recently Added, Xtream Favorites) is large. Separately, the tab roots force the navigation bar background visible; on iOS 26 this has no visible effect, and on iOS 18 it probably shows a permanent bar material and hairline behind the large title that pushed screens do not have, which still has to be confirmed with an iOS 18.1 screenshot.

**Corrected fix:** Title modes: set WatchHistoryListView.swift:81 and M3UFavoritesView.swift:62 to .large to match the existing rule (smallest change; switching all list pushes to inline instead is the owner's call). Bar background: first capture each tab root at rest and scrolled on the iOS 18.1 runtime, light and dark. If the band is there, remove .toolbarBackground(.visible, for: .navigationBar) and the no-op .toolbar(.visible, for: .navigationBar) from DashboardView.swift:242-243 and M3UDashboardView.swift:32-33, then re-capture and scroll the shelf roots with the search field to confirm no title/search flicker appears. If iOS 18.1 shows no band, leave the lines alone.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10051-10055 'nonisolated public func toolbarBackground(_ visibility: Visibility, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...)' @available(iOS, introduced: 16.0, deprecated: 100000.0, renamed: "toolbarBackgroundVisibility(_:for:)"); 10057-10058 toolbarBackgroundVisibility is iOS 18.0. 18670-18674 'nonisolated public func navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(_ displayMode: NavigationBarItem.TitleDisplayMode)' iOS 14.0. The fix only removes or changes arguments of calls that already compile.

**Regression risks:** Removing the forced background on iOS 18 makes the root bar transparent at the scroll edge; the shelf roots are ScrollView/LazyVStack with a search field, so check for large-title collapse flicker and for content showing through the status bar area while the player overlay animates. Making Watch history and M3U Favorites large adds a taller header above a .searchable field on those screens; check the first row position and, for M3U Favorites, the ContentUnavailableView centring. No interaction with the tip-jar files.

**How to verify:** iOS 18.1 simulator (runtime 22B81 is installed): screenshots of Live TV, Movies, Series, Settings and M3U Channels roots at rest and scrolled, light and dark, before and after removing the modifiers; the thing to look for is a material band with hairline behind the large title at rest. Repeat on 26.0 to confirm no change. Then push Watch history and M3U Favorites and compare the title against Recently Added / Favorites.

## live-tv-browse-1 — The Live home rebuilds its shelves only when streamsLoaded flips, so a cold launch shows "No category found." while channels load and pull-to-refresh leaves the old list on screen

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category detail, All Channels
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:63-107, 235, 242-249, 278-294, 509, 734`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:127-152, 210-220, 234-249`

**What the user perceives:** (a) Cold launch or playlist switch with Live as the starting tab: the spinner shows for an instant, then a tv.slash icon with "No category found." stays until all three catalogs (live, movies, series) have been read from SQLite, then the shelves pop in. On a 100k+ catalog that is a second or more of a false empty state. (b) Pull to refresh: the spinner runs through the network sync and ends, but the list is unchanged. New or removed channels appear only after leaving the tab and coming back. The jump-to-category sheet already lists the new categories (it reads the store directly), and picking a new one scrolls nowhere.

**Mechanism (finder):** displayCategories / displayItemsByCategory are @State, filled only by recomputeFilter(), which three .task(id:) modifiers run: debouncedQuery, contentStore.streamsLoaded and the hidden ids (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107). (a) loadPlaylist phase 1 publishes the categories and sets isLoading = false while streamsLoaded stays false (PlaylistContentStore.swift:132-137). No task key changes, so the body falls through to the empty branch (LiveStreamsView.swift:79-87). Phase 2 awaits live, VOD and series together (PlaylistContentStore.swift:144) before streamsLoaded becomes true. The isStreamsLoading shelf placeholder (LiveStreamsView.swift:235, 372-375) is therefore never reached on the cold path, although the store comment at line 137 says the UI shows categories at once. (b) The scoped refresh used by .refreshable (LiveStreamsView.swift:247) ends in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only: .live), which replaces liveCategories / liveStreams / liveStreamsByCategoryId without touching streamsLoaded (PlaylistContentStore.swift:238-249). Nothing re-runs recomputeFilter, and playbackModelMemo keeps the old queue.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add a revision counter to the store and key the Live recomputes on it.

PlaylistContentStore: `@Published private(set) var liveRevision = 0`, incremented wherever the live lists are assigned (phase 1 at line 132, phase 2 at 146-147, reloadFromDatabase at 292 and 311-312, scoped reload at 247-249, clearLists).

LiveStreamsView.swift:106, 509 and 734: `.task(id: contentStore.liveRevision) { await recomputeFilter() }` in place of the streamsLoaded key.

LiveStreamsView.swift:66: treat `!contentStore.streamsLoaded && contentStore.loadError == nil` as loading, so the empty state can only show for a catalog that really has no categories.

Result: categories appear right after phase 1 with shelf placeholders, and pull-to-refresh updates the shelves when it ends. No new API, no iOS 18 fallback needed.

**Verifier reasons:** Both halves of the claim hold from the code; one part of the fix needs correcting.

(a) Cold launch. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17 keep displayCategories / displayItemsByCategory in @State, filled only by recomputeFilter() (278-315), which runs from three .task(id:) keys (105-107): debouncedQuery, contentStore.streamsLoaded, hidden ids. Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:132-137 (phase 1) assigns liveCategories, re-assigns streamsLoaded = false (value unchanged, so the task key does not change) and sets isLoading = false. The body then reaches the tv.slash / "No category found." branch (LiveStreamsView.swift:79-87) because displayCategories is still empty, isLoading is false and activePlaylistId matches. It stays until line 152 sets streamsLoaded = true, which happens only after live, VOD and series have all been read (line 144). The isStreamsLoading placeholder (235, 372-375) is therefore unreachable on this path, contrary to the store comment at 137.

(b) Pull to refresh. LiveStreamsView.swift:247 calls refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only: .live), which ends in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only:) (PlaylistContentStore.swift:238-249). That replaces the three live collections and never touches streamsLoaded, so no task key changes and the @State copies stay stale. History shows this is a regression, not a design: commit 1cce013 changed the call from refreshFromNetwork(playlist:) (the full reload toggles streamsLoaded false then true, lines 295 and 317) to the scoped variant.

Same pattern exists in Views/VODView.swift:158, 575, 834 and Views/SeriesView.swift:159, 547, 773, so Movies and Series have the same two defects.

Fix correction: the proposed line-66 condition `!streamsLoaded && loadError == nil` can spin forever. If phase 1 throws, loadError is set and streamsLoaded stays false; the DashboardView alert's OK button (Views/DashboardView.swift:146-148) sets loadError = nil, after which the condition is permanently true with no retry affordance.

**Corrected claim:** The Live home (and, by the same pattern, the Movies and Series homes) copies the catalog into @State only when streamsLoaded flips. On a cold launch or playlist switch the starting tab shows the "No category found." empty state for the whole of phase 2 (all three catalogs read from SQLite) before shelves appear. After a pull to refresh, which since commit 1cce013 uses a scoped reload that never touches streamsLoaded, the shelves, the playback queue memo, a pushed category detail and All Channels keep the pre-refresh data until the view is recreated; the category picker reads the store directly and so shows categories the list cannot scroll to.

**Corrected fix:** 1. PlaylistContentStore: add `@Published private(set) var liveRevision = 0` (and vodRevision / seriesRevision for parity), incremented wherever that type's collections are assigned: phase 1 (132-134), phase 2 (146-151), reloadFromDatabase (292-294, 308-316), the scoped reload (247-249, 259-261, 271-273) and clearLists.

2. Key the recomputes on the revision instead of streamsLoaded: LiveStreamsView.swift:106, 509, 734 (and the six VOD / Series sites).

3. Do not use `!streamsLoaded && loadError == nil` as the loading test. Track which revision the view has resolved instead: `@State private var resolvedRevision: Int?`, set at the end of recomputeFilter to the revision captured at its start. Show the spinner while `contentStore.isLoading || playlist.id != activePlaylistId || resolvedRevision != contentStore.liveRevision`; show the empty state only when the current revision has been resolved and produced nothing. This also removes the one-frame empty flash between the revision bump and the task running, and cannot hang after an error.

4. Optional: in loadPlaylist phase 2, assign each type as its own read finishes instead of awaiting all three together, so Live does not wait for a 150k-row VOD read.

**API check:** No new API. View.task(id:priority:_:) is declared in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166 (inlinable, iOS 15+), already used at all the sites involved.

**Regression risks:** After phase 1 the home will show category headers with empty shelf placeholders (LiveStreamsView.swift:374, height liveShelfIcon + 30) that are shorter than loaded shelves, so content shifts once when streams land; this is addressed by item 3 of live-tv-browse-2. Each scoped reload publishes three collections plus the counter; the recompute must stay keyed on the counter alone so it runs once. recomputeFilter resets playbackModelMemo, which is correct after a refresh. The Equatable shelf rows and off-main filtering are untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit tests on PlaylistContentStore: liveRevision increases after loadPlaylist phase 1, after phase 2 and after reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only: .live). UI test: insert a channel into the demo database, pull to refresh on Live, assert the new tile exists without leaving the tab. Cold path: delay phase 2 behind a launch argument and assert the text "No category found." never exists; also force a phase-1 error, dismiss the alert with OK and assert no endless spinner.

## live-tv-browse-2 — LiveStreamCard has no fixed height: it grows 32 pt when the EPG snapshot arrives after launch and varies with the caption's line count, so shelves jump and grid rows are jagged

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category detail, All Channels, Favorites (Live)
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:372-375, 433-455, 597-613`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:48-68`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:130-137`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:83-100, 156-167`

**What the user perceives:** With EPG on (the default for Xtream), the shelves appear and, a moment later, every card gains a programme line: each shelf grows and everything below slides down, sometimes under the finger. On the first EPG download this happens in the middle of browsing. In the category, All Channels and Favorites grids a tile whose name wraps to two lines sits about 8 pt higher than its one-line neighbours (iphone-dark/L03-live-category-detail.png and L05-live-all-channels.png: "Morning Update", "Cinema Channel", "Discovery Stories").

**Mechanism (finder):** The EPG line is only laid out once a snapshot exists: `if let snapshot = epgSnapshot { EPGNowNextLine(..., reserveSpace: true) }` (LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454). The snapshot is nil until DashboardView calls epgStore.setActivePlaylist, which it does after `await contentStore.loadPlaylist` (DashboardView.swift:131-136). The store then needs three more database reads before the first tick publishes (EPGStore.swift:94-99). When it arrives every card grows by the VStack spacing (10) plus reservedHeight (22, EPGComponents.swift:51). reserveSpace only equalises cards with and without a current programme, not the nil-to-non-nil transition. The name uses `.lineLimit(2)` without reserving two lines (LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449), and LazyVGrid centres each cell vertically in its row (GridItem default alignment, line 597-599). The loading placeholder is a third height, `liveShelfIcon + 30` (line 374).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. LiveStreamsView.swift:446: `.lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true)`. This fixes the grid alignment and makes shelf height independent of names.

2. Decide the EPG line from a value known on the first frame. Add an environment value `epgLineReserved: Bool`, injected in DashboardView next to epgSnapshot: `epgStore.snapshot != nil || UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: "epg.hasNowIndex.\(playlist.id)")`. EPGStore.tick writes the key when it publishes a non-empty index. Card: `if epgLineReserved { EPGNowNextLine(nowNext: epgSnapshot?[key], width: width, reserveSpace: true) }`. Only the very first EPG download still shifts once.

3. Replace the Color.clear placeholder (line 374) with four or five LiveStreamCards built from a placeholder stream, `.redacted(reason: .placeholder).allowsHitTesting(false)`, so the loading height equals the loaded height by construction.

The Equatable shelf row and the snapshot's version equality stay as they are.

**APIs:** View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16.0); View.redacted(reason:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Both layout problems are real; the persisted-flag part of the fix has the wrong trigger and the scope misses the M3U twin.

EPG growth: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454 lays out EPGNowNextLine only when the environment snapshot is non-nil. Views/DashboardView.swift:131-136 calls epgStore.setActivePlaylist only after `await contentStore.loadPlaylist`, which returns when streamsLoaded is already true, so the cards are always on screen first. EPG/EPGStore.swift:94-99 then needs three more database reads (source row, rebuildResolution which reads every liveStream row plus DISTINCT channelKey over the guide, then tick) before publishing. Each card then grows by the VStack spacing 10 (line 433) plus reservedHeight 22 (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:51), 32 pt per shelf, cumulative down the page. The comment at EPGComponents.swift:48-50 shows earlier work equalised only the populated and blank states of an existing snapshot. EPG is on by default (Models/Playlist.swift:23).

Name line: `.lineLimit(2)` at LiveStreamsView.swift:446 reserves nothing, and the grid's GridItem (597-599) uses default centre alignment. iphone-dark/L03-live-category-detail.png and L05-live-all-channels.png show the two-line tiles ("Morning Update", "Cinema Channel", "Discovery Stories") sitting about 8 pt higher than their neighbours.

Corrections:
- The store publishes a non-nil snapshot whenever `configured` is true, even with an empty index (EPGStore.swift:159-167), and configured is true once any refresh attempt has written a source row (EPG/EPGRefreshCoordinator.swift:282-284 writes one on failure too). A flag written only for a non-empty index would mispredict a configured playlist with no current programmes and the shift would remain.
- The flag must also be cleared in tick's nil branch, otherwise a stale true reserves a blank line permanently.
- Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:431-442 has the identical card and Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:84-88 the identical ordering.
- Item 3 only matters once live-tv-browse-1 makes the placeholder reachable.

**Corrected claim:** LiveStreamCard (and the identical M3UChannelCard) has no stable height. On every cold launch of a playlist whose EPG has been attempted at least once, the shelves render without the programme line and each grows 32 pt when the snapshot arrives a few database reads later; on the first EPG download the same jump happens in the middle of browsing. Separately, the name line does not reserve two lines, so in the category, All Channels and Favorites grids a tile with a two-line name sits about 8 pt above its one-line neighbours (visible in iphone-dark L03 and L05).

**Corrected fix:** 1. LiveStreamsView.swift:446 and M3UChannelsView.swift:434: `.lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true)`. One-line names get a blank second line; grid rows and shelf heights become uniform.

2. Add an environment Bool `epgLineReserved`, injected next to epgSnapshot in DashboardView and M3UDashboardView: `epgStore.snapshot != nil || UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: "epg.lineReserved.<playlist.id>")`. EPGStore.tick writes the key (only when it changes) to true whenever it publishes a snapshot, empty index included, and to false in the `dict.isEmpty && !configured` branch. Both cards: `if epgLineReserved { EPGNowNextLine(nowNext: epgSnapshot?[key], width: width, reserveSpace: true) }`. To avoid the one remaining shift on the very first download, the Xtream dashboard may also OR in `playlist.epgEnabled`. Remove the key when a playlist is deleted.

3. Dependent on live-tv-browse-1: replace the Color.clear placeholder at LiveStreamsView.swift:374 with real cards built from a placeholder DBLiveStream, `.redacted(reason: .placeholder).allowsHitTesting(false)` (or `.hidden()` if no skeleton look is wanted), so loading and loaded heights match by construction.

The Equatable shelf row and the snapshot's version equality stay as they are.

**API check:** View.lineLimit(_ limit: Int, reservesSpace: Bool): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8856, @available(iOS 16.0, macOS 13.0, tvOS 16.0, watchOS 9.0, *). View.redacted(reason: RedactionReasons): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6107, in an extension marked @available(iOS 14.0, macOS 11.0, tvOS 14.0, watchOS 7.0, *). Both below the iOS 18 target; no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** Every shelf and grid row becomes one caption line taller for one-line names, so slightly fewer rows per screen. The reserved line adds 32 pt of blank space on playlists whose EPG is configured but empty; that already happens today once the snapshot arrives, the change only moves it to the first frame. If tick's nil branch does not clear the flag, blank space would persist after EPG data is removed. Environment propagation through the Equatable shelf row already works for epgSnapshot, so the new value needs no change to that earlier work.

**How to verify:** Compare L03 / L05 screenshots: icons of one grid row share a top edge. UI test with EPG demo data: record minY of the second shelf header right after launch and again after 3 s on a second launch, assert equal. Unit test: tick sets the persisted flag for a configured playlist with an empty index and clears it when unconfigured and empty. On a device with a large guide, screen-record a cold launch and check that no shelf moves after first appearing.

## live-tv-browse-3 — Opening a category or All Channels flashes "No channel found." before the grid appears, and with a stored A-Z sort it stays for the whole sort

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live category detail, All Channels
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:469, 512-523, 547, 567-577, 584-596, 629-631, 697, 738-752`, `Models/LiveSortOption.swift:40-53`

**What the user perceives:** During the push, the incoming screen first shows a magnifying glass with "No channel found.", then swaps to the grid. For a small category it is a flicker. For All Channels on a large catalog with Name (A-Z) remembered, it reads as "this list is empty" for as long as the sort takes, which on tens of thousands of channels is likely a noticeable fraction of a second.

**Mechanism (finder):** Two async hops stand between the push and the first real content. The parent's displayItems starts empty (LiveStreamsView.swift:469, 697) and is filled by a .task after the first render (512-516, 738-752). The child LiveCategoryContent has its own displayItems, also empty (547), filled only after a Task.detached round trip (567-577). The body shows the empty state whenever displayItems.isEmpty (586-595), so "not computed yet" and "no results" look the same. The three .task(id:) at 629-631 each run recompute on first appear, so the work and the prefetch run three times. The sort compares with localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare per comparison (LiveSortOption.swift:45-51), which is slow for large arrays.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. Seed the parent synchronously. LiveCategoryDetailView gets an init that sets `_displayItems = State(initialValue: PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? [])`.

2. In LiveCategoryContent make the result optional and skip the hop for the identity case:
`@State private var computed: [LiveStreamWithCategory]?`
`let shown = computed ?? (isFilterActive ? [] : items)`
Show the empty state only when `computed != nil && shown.isEmpty`. While `computed == nil && isFilterActive` show a centred ProgressView. In recompute, when the sort is default and the filter empty, assign `computed = items` without Task.detached.

3. Collapse the three tasks into one keyed on a small Hashable struct (itemsToken, sortOption, filter.rawValue).

4. Use `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` when the parent has a query and `ContentUnavailableView(L("list.no_channel"), systemImage: "tv.slash")` otherwise; the magnifying glass is wrong for a category that is simply empty.

Pagination, itemsToken and the off-main sort stay.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real, but one sub-claim is wrong and the fix does not work for All Channels as written.

Real: LiveCategoryDetailView.displayItems and AllLiveView.displayItems start empty (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:469, 697) and are filled by .task after the first render (512-516, 738-752). LiveCategoryContent has its own displayItems (547), filled only after a Task.detached round trip (567-577), and its body shows the magnifying-glass "No channel found." state whenever that array is empty (586-595). With default order this lasts roughly two to three frames at the start of the push; whether that is visible needs a recording. With a remembered A-Z sort (@AppStorage, line 543) it lasts for the whole sort; Models/LiveSortOption.swift:45-51 calls localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare per comparison, which for 30k channels is about 450k locale-aware comparisons.

Wrong: "the work and the prefetch run three times". The three .task(id:) at 629-631 do all fire on first appear, but at that moment items is still empty, so they sort nothing; only the itemsToken task re-runs when items arrive. It would become true only after the proposed synchronous seeding.

Missed: recompute() has no cancellation check after the detached await (571-576). Switching from A-Z back to Default while a large A-Z sort is running lets the slow stale result overwrite the fast new one, leaving the grid sorted A-Z while the menu says Default.

Fix problems:
- For AllLiveView the parent's items are still empty when the child first resolves, so `computed = items` yields a resolved-empty state and the same false message. The child cannot tell "parent not ready" from "parent has nothing".
- LiveCategoryContent's == (534-539) compares only playlist, count, first and last id; any new loading or query input must be added to it, or SwiftUI will skip the update from loading to loaded-empty.
- NavigationLink destinations are built eagerly (LiveStreamsView.swift:119-120 for All Channels, 356-357 per shelf row), so an init seed must be O(1). The dictionary lookup for a category is; filtering all channels by hidden categories in AllLiveView.init would not be.

**Corrected claim:** Opening a category or All Channels renders the "No channel found." empty state before the grid, because "not computed yet" and "no results" are the same state in both the parent and LiveCategoryContent. With default order this is a few frames at the start of the push. With a remembered A-Z / Z-A sort it lasts as long as the off-main sort, which on a catalog of tens of thousands of channels is a visible false "empty" message. The same code can also show a stale sort result, because recompute() does not check cancellation after its detached await.

**Corrected fix:** 1. LiveCategoryContent gains `isResolving: Bool` and `searchQuery: String`, both included in its == function. AllLiveView passes isResolving = true until its first recompute finishes; LiveCategoryDetailView seeds its @State in init from `PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? []` (O(1)) and passes false.

2. In LiveCategoryContent: `@State private var computed: [LiveStreamWithCategory]?`; `let shown = isFilterActive ? computed : items`. Show a centred ProgressView while `isResolving || shown == nil`; show the empty state only when resolved and empty. When sort is default and no filter is set, render items directly and skip Task.detached; still reset visibleCount and prefetch.

3. Replace the three tasks with one keyed on a Hashable struct (itemsToken, sortOption, filter.rawValue) and add `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` after the detached await.

4. Empty state: `ContentUnavailableView.search(text: searchQuery)` when a query is active, else `ContentUnavailableView(L("list.no_channel"), systemImage: "tv.slash")`. Both forms are already used in the app (Views/DownloadsView.swift:77, Views/SearchView.swift:241, Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:40).

Pagination, itemsToken and the off-main sort stay. Speeding up the A-Z sort itself (precomputed keys) is a separate optional step.

**API check:** ContentUnavailableView: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17575, @available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *). `public static func search(text: Swift.String)`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17625, in the extension at 17620-17621 with the same iOS 17.0 availability. View.task(id:priority:_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166. No iOS 26-only API; no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** If == is not extended with the new inputs, the grid can stay on the spinner for an empty result. After seeding, the three existing tasks would each sort a non-empty list on first appear, so collapsing them is required, not optional. ContentUnavailableView.search uses system-provided strings rather than L(), as the two existing call sites already do. LiveCategoryContent's Equatable wrapper, itemsToken and pagination are deliberate performance work and must be kept.

**How to verify:** UI test: push a category and All Channels, assert the static text "No channel found." never exists during the transition for a non-empty list. Unit or UI test: set A-Z, then Default in quick succession on a large synthetic list and assert the final order is the default one. Device: slow-motion screen recording of All Channels on a 30k catalog with A-Z remembered, before and after; also measure the default-order case to see whether the two-to-three-frame flash is visible at all.

## live-tv-browse-4 — Channel tiles have no context menu: a channel cannot be favourited or un-favourited from any list, and the per-channel schedule is unreachable from browsing

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category detail, All Channels, Favorites (Live)
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459, 1146-1182`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:158-179`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:102-124`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457`

**What the user perceives:** Touch and hold on a channel does nothing native; on release playback just starts (iphone-dark/L08-live-card-long-press.png shows the player after a long press). The only way to favourite a channel is to start it and tap the star in the player, and the only way to remove one from Favorites is the same. The channel schedule screen can only be opened by a half-second press on the channel column inside the guide.

**Mechanism (finder):** LiveStreamCard is a plain Button with no .contextMenu (LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457). Live favourites are written only by LivePlayerShell.toggleFavorite (1159-1182). ChannelEPGSheet (ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:159) has no call site anywhere in the app. The M3U card already has a context menu with a favourite toggle (M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457), so the Xtream side is the gap.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add `.contextMenu { ... } preview: { ... }` to LiveStreamCard with Play, Add to / Remove from Favorites, and Schedule.

Favourite state: a small in-memory index (`Set<Int>` of live stream ids for the active playlist, fed by one ValueObservation on `SELECT streamId FROM favorite WHERE playlistId = ? AND type = 'live'`), read when the menu is built and not observed by the cards. That is the reasoning the M3U card documents at M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450. Move the insert / delete from LivePlayerShell.toggleFavorite into a shared static helper and call it from both places; the shell's behaviour does not change.

Schedule: the screen owns `@State var scheduleChannel` and presents the existing ChannelEPGSheet; the card receives an action closure.

Preview: a compact card with logo, full channel name and the current programme with its time range from epgSnapshot. This also gives long names a place to be read in full.

All three APIs are available at the deployment target; no fallback needed.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) (iOS 16.0); View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The gap is exactly as described; three details of the fix need changing.

Confirmed: LiveStreamCard is a plain Button with no context menu (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457); iphone-dark/L08-live-card-long-press.png shows the player after a long press. A search for DBFavorite writes outside PlayerView finds live favourites written only in LivePlayerShell.toggleFavorite (1159-1182); Views/FavoritesView.swift:102-124 has no removal affordance. ChannelEPGSheet (Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:159) has no call site; the schedule is reached only through the 0.5 s LongPressGesture on the guide's channel column (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:160, Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:206). The M3U card has a menu with a favourite toggle (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457).

Corrections:
- contextMenu's menuItems closure is non-escaping, so it runs when the card body is evaluated, not when the menu opens. A value read inline from an unobserved index (the M3U pattern the finding points to) can show a stale label after a toggle until the card re-renders. The code base's other precedent is the right one: a small View inside the menu that owns its own observation, as M3UDownloadMenuItems does (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:206-222).
- No new index or ValueObservation is needed: IsFavoriteRequest(streamId:playlistId:type:) already exists (Models/Requests.swift:269-289).
- Presenting ChannelEPGSheet as a sheet lets playback start behind it. EPGProgrammeDetailSheet's Play button dismisses only itself before presenting the overlay (Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:82-84, 127), and the overlay sits below system sheets (Views/DashboardView.swift:125-128 documents this for Downloads).
- There is no localized string for "Schedule"; a new key is needed in all ten Localizable.strings files, which also hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys. Adding a key leaves them intact.

**Corrected claim:** Xtream channel tiles have no context menu. A channel can be added to or removed from favourites only from inside the player, the Favorites > Live grid offers no way to remove an entry, and the per-channel schedule screen is reachable only by a half-second press on the channel column inside the guide. The M3U card already has a favourite menu, so the gap is on the Xtream side.

**Corrected fix:** Add `.contextMenu { ... } preview: { ... }` to LiveStreamCard with Play, a favourite toggle and Schedule.

Favourite toggle: a small menu-item view, e.g. `LiveFavoriteMenuItem(playlistId:streamId:)`, holding `@Query<IsFavoriteRequest>` and showing L("favorites.add") / L("favorites.remove") (both keys exist). Its write goes through a shared static helper that does exists-then-delete-else-insert in one write; LivePlayerShell.toggleFavorite may call the same helper but its behaviour must not change.

Schedule: push ChannelEPGDetailView with `navigationDestination(item:)` on the owning screens, as EPGGuideView.swift:63-66 does, instead of presenting ChannelEPGSheet. DBLiveStream is Hashable, so it can be the item. Channel key: `EPGStore.shared.storedKey(idKey:nameKey:) ?? "#stream:<id>"`, as EPGStore.swift:356-358 does. If a sheet is preferred, it must close when playerOverlay.presentation changes. The card takes the action as a closure; the shelf row's == already ignores closures.

Preview (optional): logo, full channel name, current programme and time range from epgSnapshot.

Which actions the menu carries is the owner's call; the mechanism above is the fix.

**API check:** View.contextMenu<M, P>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> M, @ViewBuilder preview: () -> P): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9876, @available(iOS 16.0, macOS 13.0, tvOS 16.0, *), watchOS unavailable; both closures non-escaping. View.contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems): line 9870, iOS 13.0. View.navigationDestination<D, C>(item: Binding<D?>, destination: @escaping (D) -> C) where D: Hashable: line 1552, @available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *). View.sensoryFeedback<T>(_:trigger:): line 1983, @available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, visionOS 26.0, *); listed by the finding but not needed. All at or below the iOS 18 target; no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** LivePlayerShell keeps its favourite star in local @State refreshed only on channel change (LiveStreamsView.swift:782, 966, 1146-1157); toggling a favourite from a list while that channel is docked in the mini player leaves the shell's star stale until the next channel change. Fixing that means touching out-of-scope player code. A long press no longer starts playback on release, which is the intended native behaviour. The menu must not make cards observe a favourites store, or one toggle re-renders every realised card (the reason documented at M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450). New string key must be added to all ten languages without disturbing the uncommitted tip keys.

**How to verify:** UI test: press the first channel for 1 s, assert "Add to Favorites" exists, tap it, open Favorites > Live TV and assert the channel is listed; press it there, tap "Remove from Favorites", assert it is gone; reopen the menu on the home card and assert the label has flipped. UI test: Schedule opens the channel schedule, tapping Play on a programme shows the player with nothing covering it. Unit test for the shared toggle helper (insert, delete, idempotent).

## live-tv-browse-5 — On iPhone the channel tiles are 56 pt (shelves) and 90 pt (grids), too narrow for real channel names and for the EPG line; a list-style row would fit the content

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort L · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category detail, All Channels, Favorites (Live)
- Code: `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-14, 26-28`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:433-455, 597-613`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:53-68`, `EPG/EPGModels.swift:118-129`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should channel lists on iPhone default to rows (logo, name, what is on now with progress) instead of square tiles, and may shelf tiles grow to about 72 pt?

**What the user perceives:** Shelf captions hyphenate short demo names ("Motor-sport HD" in iphone-light/L01-live-home.png). Real names such as "TR: BEIN SPORTS 1 FHD" lose the part that tells channels apart. With EPG the programme title gets the same 58 pt (90 pt in grids) in caption2: roughly 10 to 15 characters, no end time, no next programme. Catch-up channels look like any other, although a catch-up filter exists. In grids, 90 pt tiles float in about 118 pt columns, leaving three columns with wide gutters (iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** layoutScale is clamped to 0.5 on every iPhone (short side 375 to 440 divided by 834, PosterMetrics.swift:10-13), so liveShelfIcon is 56, the label 58 and the grid tile 90 (lines 26-28). The adaptive GridItem minimum equals the tile's fixed size, so leftover column width becomes gutter (LiveStreamsView.swift:597-599). EPGNowNextLine is one caption2 line limited to the tile width (EPGComponents.swift:55-63). EPGNowNext.next is never filled, by design, because fetching it for every channel each minute was most of the rebuild cost (EPGModels.swift:118-123).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest step (S, no decision needed): give iPhone shelves a floor, `liveShelfIcon = max(72, scaled(112))` and label = icon + 8, and add a small clock.arrow.circlepath corner badge when `stream.tvArchive == 1`.

Worthwhile step (L): add a list presentation inside LiveCategoryContent for category detail, All Channels, Favorites > Live and inline search results. Row: 44 pt logo, name (.body, one line), current programme (.subheadline, secondary, one line) with "until HH:mm" from now.stop, a 3 pt progress bar, a catch-up glyph. Build it as a second branch of the same view (LazyVStack of rows) so the off-main sort, the pagination, itemsToken and the Equatable wrapper are untouched. Add a "View as: List / Grid" Picker to the existing sort menu, stored with @AppStorage, defaulting to list on compact width and grid on regular. Home shelves stay.

"Next programme" is left to the context-menu preview and the schedule screen, since the snapshot deliberately does not carry it.

**Verifier reasons:** The observations hold; one number and the scope of the large step are off, and both steps are design decisions.

Confirmed: Views/PosterMetrics.swift:10-13 and 26-28 give a 56 pt shelf icon, 58 pt label and 90 pt grid tile on a 402 pt wide iPhone. iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows nearly every demo name wrapping to two lines and "Motor-sport HD" hyphenated. The adaptive GridItem minimum equals the fixed tile size (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:597-599), so 370 pt of usable width becomes three 118 pt columns holding 90 pt tiles (iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png). EPGNowNextLine is one caption2 line at tile width (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:55-63). EPGNowNext.next is deliberately unfilled (EPG/EPGModels.swift:118-123). No card shows catch-up availability. ipad-light/L01-live-home.png shows the iPad layout (112 pt) has none of these problems. History shows the metrics date from the original import with no comment marking 56 pt as a deliberate choice.

Corrections:
- The scale is not clamped to 0.5 on every iPhone: 430 and 440 pt wide models get 0.516 and 0.528, so 58-59 pt icons and 93-95 pt tiles. The conclusion is unchanged.
- LiveCategoryContent serves only the category detail and All Channels. Favorites > Live has its own LazyVGrid (Views/FavoritesView.swift:102-124) and the Live home's inline search renders shelves (LiveStreamsView.swift:210-241). A list mode inside LiveCategoryContent would not reach either.
- liveShelfIcon / liveShelfLabelWidth are shared with the M3U shelves (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:368-369, 399-400) and M3UGroupDetailView has its own grid (574-583), so both steps touch or should mirror M3U.
- The small step changes the density of the landing screen, so it is also a decision, not a neutral fix.

**Corrected claim:** On iPhone, live channel tiles are 56-59 pt in shelves and 90-95 pt in grids. Short demo names already wrap and hyphenate at that width, real IPTV names and the one-line programme title are cut to about ten characters, grids show three columns with wide gutters because the tile does not fill its column, and catch-up channels are not marked. iPad is unaffected. This is a density and presentation choice rather than a defect, so the remedy is the owner's decision.

**Corrected fix:** Decision A (S): give iPhone shelves a floor, `liveShelfIcon = max(72, scaled(112))`, label width = icon + 8, and add a small clock.arrow.circlepath badge on the icon when `stream.tvArchive > 0` (the predicate LiveStreamFilter uses). This applies to Xtream and M3U shelves alike and shows about one tile fewer per row and fewer shelves per screen.

Decision B (L): a row presentation (logo, name on one line, current programme with "until HH:mm" from now.stop, thin progress bar, catch-up glyph) as a second branch inside LiveCategoryContent, with a List / Grid picker in the existing sort menu stored in @AppStorage, defaulting to list on compact width. That covers category detail and All Channels including their search. Favorites > Live and M3UGroupDetailView need the same row view wired in separately; the Live home's inline search stays as shelves unless changed separately.

Smaller alternative for the gutters alone: size the grid tile to the column instead of a fixed 90 pt.

The off-main sort, pagination, itemsToken, the Equatable wrapper and the now-only EPG snapshot stay untouched.

**API check:** No new API is required by either step. Picker, Menu, LazyVStack and @AppStorage are already used in the same file (LiveStreamsView.swift:543, 634-674).

**Regression risks:** Decision A changes shelf height and density on the landing screen and on M3U shelves; prefetch sizes follow automatically because they read the same metric (LiveStreamsView.swift:412-413, M3UChannelsView.swift:399-400), and thumbnails are re-decoded once at the new size. Decision B adds a second layout to keep in step with sort, filter, pagination and the context menu from live-tv-browse-4, and risks drift between the Xtream and M3U screens if only one side gets it. Rows that show progress re-render on the per-minute snapshot, as tiles do today.

**How to verify:** Screenshots on a 402 pt iPhone with long real-world channel names and EPG demo data, before and after, checking that name and programme title are readable. For decision B, UI tests that sort, filter, search and pagination behave the same in both layouts, and a scroll-performance check on a 30k-channel list in list mode.

## live-tv-browse-6 — The player's channel order ignores the sort and filter the user sees in the grid, and All Channels hands the whole catalog over as one section

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live category detail, All Channels, hand-off into the player
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:474-491, 543-547, 567-577, 602-610, 699-717, 1253-1290`

**What the user perceives:** Sort All Channels by name, tap a channel, press next in the player: the next channel is not the next tile but the next one in provider order, and the channel panel lists provider order too. With "Catch-up available" on, next and previous land on channels the list had filtered out. On a large catalog the first tap in All Channels also hesitates before the player appears.

**Mechanism (finder):** The sorted and filtered array is LiveCategoryContent's private @State (LiveStreamsView.swift:547, 572-574), but the tap closure is built by the parent from its own unsorted displayItems (474 and 486 for the category, 699 and 706-711 for All Channels). In All Channels the parent also maps the entire catalog on every tap and passes it as a single section "all". LiveChannelPanelSectionCache.resolve then treats that section as the current one and builds it inline (1284-1290), so the 1,500-channel inline limit (1256) never protects this path: every channel gets a URL(string:) on the main thread at the tap.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Change the callback so the grid reports what it shows:
`var onStreamSelected: ((DBLiveStream, [LiveStreamWithCategory]) -> Void)?`
LiveCategoryContent passes its displayItems. The parents build the queue from that array and memoise it in a reference box like LivePlaybackModelMemo, cleared when the content reports a new result.

For All Channels in default order with no filter, pass per-category sections (the same shape LiveStreamsView.livePlaybackModel builds at lines 29-36, filtered for hidden ids), so the panel cache's per-category path and its off-main completion apply. With a sort or filter active, one section in visible order is correct.

LivePlayerShell itself is not changed.

**Verifier reasons:** Order and filter mismatch: confirmed from code. LiveCategoryContent keeps the sorted and filtered list in its own @State (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:543-547, 567-577) and renders from it (602), but passes the parent's closure straight to the card (609). Both parents build queue and panel sections from their own unsorted, unfiltered displayItems (474, 485-486 for a category; 699, 706-711 for All Channels). LivePlayerShell steps prev/next through `queue` (844-847, 1083-1089) and the panel shows `sections` (825-828). The sort is a persisted @AppStorage (543), so once chosen the mismatch is permanent. Not deliberate: `currentStreams` predates the sort (git log -S: d2489f9), the sort arrived in 654cefc without touching the hand-off, and no comment explains it.

Performance sub-claim: mechanism is real, effect is overstated. A single section "all" does bypass the 1,500 limit, because resolve() builds the section holding the current channel inline whatever its size (1284-1290). A host micro-benchmark of the same mapping (String(streamId) + URL(string:) per channel, swiftc -O, Mac) took about 10 ms for 30,000 channels and under 1 ms for the map(\.stream) copy. That is one or two frames on a phone, not a visible hesitation, except on catalogs well above 100k.

Fix part 2 is wrong. PlaylistContentStore.liveStreams is ordered by global `liveStream.sortIndex` (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:368-377), not grouped by category. A queue built as sections.flatMap in category-list order would again differ from the grid order, which is the defect being fixed.

**Corrected claim:** In Live category detail and All Channels, the player's prev/next order and its channel panel use the parent's unsorted, unfiltered list, while the grid shows LiveCategoryContent's sorted and filtered list. With a name sort or the catch-up / has-EPG filter active, next and previous go to channels that are not the neighbouring tiles, including channels the filter removed. Separately, All Channels re-maps the whole catalog on every tap and builds the panel for it inline; this costs roughly 10-30 ms per 30k channels and is a minor inefficiency, not a perceivable stall at normal sizes.

**Corrected fix:** Let the grid report what it shows, and keep the queue in visible order in every case.

1. In LiveCategoryContent keep a reference box (same idea as LivePlaybackModelMemo) holding `streams: [DBLiveStream]?`, cleared in recompute() (567-577) and filled lazily on the first tap from `displayItems.map(\.stream)`.
2. Change the callback to `((DBLiveStream, [DBLiveStream]) -> Void)?` and wrap the card's callback: `{ stream, _ in onStreamSelected?(stream, memo.streams) }`. LiveStreamCard keeps its signature; it always passes nil history.
3. LiveCategoryDetailView and AllLiveView use that array for both `queue` and the single section. The same buffer is then reused across taps, so the panel cache's `entry.streams == section.streams` check (1335-1339) is O(1) and the second tap maps nothing.

Drop the per-category-sections step for All Channels. If the first-tap inline build ever shows up in a profile, address it in LiveChannelPanelSectionCache (cap the inline build of an over-limit current section) as a separate change. LivePlayerShell is not changed.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. Code-base facts checked: LiveCategoryContent is only constructed at Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:477 and 702, so the callback signature change has two call sites. Its Equatable `==` (534-539) ignores the closure, which stays valid because the array is passed at call time rather than captured.

**Regression risks:** The `.equatable()` shelf/grid optimisation must stay: do not add the visible array to `==`. The memo must be a reference box, not value @State, or filling it in the tap handler invalidates the grid. With a search query active the parent already sorts by relevance and the child then applies the user's sort; the reported array covers both. Favourites, search, guide and history call sites of LivePlayerShell are untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit test on a pure function (items, sort, filter) -> queue: Z-A returns reversed names; catch-up filter returns only tvArchive > 0. UI test with demo data: Live > a category > sort Name Z-A, tap the first tile, press next, assert the player title equals the second tile's label; open the channel panel and assert the first row equals the first tile. Optional: Time Profiler on a 30k-channel playlist, tap in All Channels, check LivePlayerShell.init self time before and after.

## live-tv-browse-7 — In the guide, a programme's title is anchored to the block's start, so long programmes and "no information" rows look like blank bars at the current time

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: EPG guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:19-29, 37-60`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:311-314, 391-397`

**What the user perceives:** The guide opens at the current time. A film that started two hours ago is an empty block: its title sits at the block's left edge, scrolled out of view. Channels without data are completely blank bars (iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png: every row is empty although each holds a "No information" cell whose label is at 00:00).

**Mechanism (finder):** EPGProgrammeCell lays its label out leading-aligned inside a cell positioned by absolute x (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:21-23, 40-51). Nothing keeps the label inside the visible part of the cell. The filler cell for a channel without data spans the whole day from x = 0 (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:311-314, 395-397).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Clamp the label to the visible leading edge without any state, inside EPGProgrammeCell:

```swift
label.visualEffect { content, proxy in
    let hidden = pinnedLeading - proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal)).minX
    return content.offset(x: min(max(0, hidden), max(0, proxy.size.width - 44)))
}
```

`pinnedLeading` is metrics.channelColumnWidth. Apply it only when `cell.width > metrics.hourWidth` (and to the filler cells), which keeps the number of geometry-dependent effects to a few per row. The existing clipShape clips the overflow. The rows stay Equatable on layout version; the effect needs no body re-evaluation.

**APIs:** View.visualEffect(_:) (iOS 17.0); CoordinateSpaceProtocol.scrollView(axis:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Problem confirmed from code and screenshot. EPGChannelRowView places each cell at an absolute x (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:19-29) and EPGProgrammeCell aligns its label to the cell's leading edge (40-51, 54-58). Nothing ties the label to the visible part. A channel without data gets one filler from x = 0 across the whole day (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:311-314, 395-397; layout(for:) at 335-337). The guide opens at now minus half an hour (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:351-356). In iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png, taken at 10:20, every row is a blank bar: no "No information" text is visible anywhere. No comment or history marks this as deliberate (rows date from 1cce013).

Two corrections to the fix:
1. Threshold. The default position puts now minus 30 min at the leading edge, so any programme that began more than 30 minutes ago has its title cut or hidden. A 60-minute programme is exactly hourWidth (150 pt) wide and fails `cell.width > metrics.hourWidth`, so the most common case is not fixed.
2. Placement. `proxy.size.width - 44` is only the right clamp when the effect is applied to the full-cell frame. Applied to the bare VStack or Text, proxy.size is the text's own width and a short title in a long block never moves.

**Corrected claim:** In the guide, programme titles and the "No information" label are anchored to the cell's start. At the default scroll position, every programme that started more than about 30 minutes ago shows a truncated or missing title, and channels without data are fully blank bars.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the stateless approach, with two changes.

Inside EPGProgrammeCell, insert the effect between the existing `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` and `.background(...)` in both branches, so the proxy is the cell and the background does not move:

```swift
.visualEffect { [pinnedLeading] content, proxy in
    let hidden = pinnedLeading - proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal)).minX
    return content.offset(x: min(max(0, hidden), max(0, proxy.size.width - 44)))
}
```

Pass `pinnedLeading: metrics.channelColumnWidth` from EPGChannelRowView (metrics is already part of its `==`). Capture the value, not self: the closure is @Sendable.

Apply it to every cell at least 64 pt wide (the threshold the cell already uses for its time line, line 44) and to filler cells, not only to cells wider than an hour. That is most cells of each visible row, so the scroll-smoothness check on a device is a required step, not optional. If it costs frames, fall back to cells of 45 minutes or more.

No availability guard needed (iOS 17 API, target iOS 18).

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk):
- `nonisolated public func visualEffect(_ effect: @escaping @Sendable (EmptyVisualEffect, GeometryProxy) -> some VisualEffect) -> some View`, @available(iOS 17.0, ...) (line 16286).
- `extension CoordinateSpaceProtocol where Self == NamedCoordinateSpace { public static func scrollView(axis: Axis) -> Self; public static var scrollView }`, @available(iOS 17.0, ...) (line 19272).
- `extension VisualEffect { public func offset(x: CGFloat = 0, y: CGFloat = 0) -> some VisualEffect }`, @available(iOS 17.0, ...) (line 968).
- GeometryProxy is Sendable (line 7990).
All found, all below the iOS 18 target.

**Regression risks:** The guide's scroll performance is deliberate work: rows are Equatable on layout version and the two scrollers are synced by hand (EPGGuideView.swift:11-27, 321-340). The effect adds one geometry-dependent closure per affected cell per scroll frame; each row holds all of its day's cells (the ZStack is not lazy horizontally), so about 30 cells times the visible rows. The closure is trivial math and needs no body pass, but it is unmeasured. A title longer than the remaining visible part is clipped by the existing clipShape instead of ending in an ellipsis. Tap targets do not move (visual effects do not affect hit testing), which is what is wanted. Right-to-left (Arabic) needs a look: the row already uses unmirrored `.offset(x:)`.

**How to verify:** Needs a simulator or device run. (1) Screenshot at the default position with EPG data containing a three-hour programme, a one-hour programme that began 45 minutes ago, and a channel without data: all three labels sit just right of the channel column. (2) Scroll horizontally: the label stays pinned until 44 pt of the cell remain, then leaves with the cell. (3) Instruments > Animation Hitches on a device with a few thousand channels with data, horizontal and diagonal flicks, before and after; hitch time ratio must not rise.

## live-tv-browse-8 — The guide lists every channel of the playlist, including hidden categories and channels that have no guide data

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: EPG guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-263, 311-314, 335-337`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:284-285, 740-745`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should the guide hide channels without guide data by default (with a toggle to show them)? Respecting hidden categories is a plain fix.

**What the user perceives:** Categories the user hid in the category picker are back in the guide. On a provider where a few thousand of tens of thousands of channels carry guide data, the guide is mostly empty rows that have to be scrolled or collapsed past, category by category.

**Mechanism (finder):** buildRows maps PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreams with no hidden-category filter (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:253-263). The Live home and All Channels both filter (LiveStreamsView.swift:284-285, 745). A channel without programmes for the day gets the shared emptyLayout (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:335-337) and is listed like any other.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Plain fix: in buildRows drop streams whose categoryId is in `HiddenCategoryStore.shared.hiddenIds(playlistId:type: "live")`.

Product step: after rebuildLayouts, list by default only rows whose channelKey has an entry in `layouts` for the selected day. Add a "Show channels without guide data" Toggle (@AppStorage) to the existing toolbar Menu (EPGGuideView.swift:262-268). When the filter leaves nothing, show a ContentUnavailableView with a "Show all channels" action. recomputeItems already derives header counts from the rows it is given, so the counts follow.

**Verifier reasons:** buildRows maps PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreams with no hidden filter (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-263), and neither Views/EPG nor EPG references HiddenCategoryStore at all (grep; `git log -S'hiddenIds'` on those folders is empty). Live home filters categories (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:284-285), All Channels filters streams (740-745), search filters too (Views/SearchView.swift:256). So hidden categories reappear only in the guide. That is an omission, not a choice.

Listing channels without data is deliberate: the comment at EPGGuideViewModel.swift:113-115 introduces the shared emptyLayout precisely to carry them cheaply, and tapping the channel column plays the channel (EPGGuideView.swift:398-410). The finding correctly labels hiding them as a product decision.

Two gaps in the plain fix, neither changes the verdict:
- The M3U branch (264-274) has the same omission. M3U hidden groups are stored under type "m3u" with the group title as id (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:5, 27; ungrouped channels use M3UContentStore.ungroupedLabel).
- Hiding the synthetic "Uncategorized" category (id `__uncategorized__`, Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:358-360) is not matched by a raw categoryId check, because those streams carry nil or an orphan id. All Channels has the same gap today (745).

**Corrected claim:** The guide ignores hidden categories on both Xtream and M3U playlists, so categories the user hid on Live TV come back in the guide. It also lists every channel regardless of guide data; that part is a deliberate design and changing it is a product decision.

**Corrected fix:** Plain fix, in buildRows:
- Xtream: read `HiddenCategoryStore.shared.hiddenIds(playlistId: playlist.id, type: "live")` and drop streams whose categoryId is in it. To honour a hidden "Uncategorized", also drop streams whose categoryId is nil, empty or not in `liveCategories` when the set contains `PlaylistContentStore.uncategorizedCategoryId`.
- M3U: read type `M3UChannelsView.hiddenCategoryType` and drop channels whose group title (or `M3UContentStore.ungroupedLabel` when empty) is in it.
Both stores are @MainActor like the view model. The picker cannot be opened while the guide is on screen, so no observation is needed.

Product step (owner decides): default to rows with an entry in `layouts` for the selected day, with a toggle in the existing toolbar Menu. If adopted: keep the day picker visible and put the ContentUnavailableView in the grid area only; let a search query bypass the filter so a channel can always be found by name; call recomputeItems() after `layouts` is assigned (331); expect the row set to change on day switches.

**API check:** No new SDK API for the plain fix. `HiddenCategoryStore.hiddenIds(playlistId:type:) -> Set<String>` exists (Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:18). For the product step: Toggle, @AppStorage and ContentUnavailableView with actions are already used in this file set (EPGGuideView.swift:81-93).

**Regression risks:** Plain fix: none beyond the row set shrinking; collapsed-category persistence keys are unaffected. playChannel still hands the player the full catalog through xtreamLiveQueue() (EPGGuideView.swift:405), so prev/next can still reach hidden categories; that is existing behaviour and out of scope. Product step: with no EPG downloaded, or on a day the feed does not cover, the default guide would be empty; the empty state and the "show all" action must cover that.

**How to verify:** Unit test on EPGGuideViewModel (or an extracted static row builder): hidden live category ids are absent from rows; hiding `__uncategorized__` removes nil and orphan-category streams; the M3U variant with a hidden group. UI test: hide a category in the Live picker, open the guide, assert its header is absent. The effort and risk above rate the plain fix; the product step is M.
