## live-tv-browse-9 — Opening the guide builds a row for every channel on the main thread at the start of the push

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: EPG guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:19-29, 138-173, 218-233, 249-278, 288`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:54-57`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the guide icon on a large playlist: the push animation hitches or stalls briefly, then the spinner shows, then the grid. Not measured; the cost is proportional to the channel count.

**Mechanism (finder):** EPGGuideViewModel is @MainActor and load() starts from the view's .task on the first frame of the push (EPGGuideView.swift:54-57). buildRows runs synchronously for every live channel: two normalizeChannelKey calls (trim and lowercase), storedKey lookups, URL(string:), category trimming, and displayName.lowercased() in the row initialiser (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:28, 254-263). rebuildSections, recomputeItems and `Set(rows.map(\.channelKey))` (line 288) follow, also on the main actor. Only the programme query and the cell layout are off-main (318-327).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Move the row build off the main actor. Make it `nonisolated static func buildRows(entries:resolution:hidden:) -> (rows, sections, wantedKeys)` and run it with Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated), the same pattern rebuildLayouts already uses. It needs a copy of the alias map: add a read-only `resolutionSnapshot` accessor to EPGStore and replicate the four lines of storedKey as a static function. Assign rows, sections and items once when it returns. Cache the result in the view model keyed on the catalog revision and hidden ids so load() after a forced refresh does not rebuild it.

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed. EPGGuideViewModel is @MainActor (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:66) and load() runs buildRows() synchronously (218-221) from the view's .task (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:54-57). Per channel: two normalizeChannelKey calls (trim + lowercase, EPG/EPGConstants.swift:46-50), up to two dictionary lookups (EPG/EPGStore.swift:259-264), URL(string:), two trims in category(), an interpolated id and displayName.lowercased() (28). Then rebuildSections, recomputeItems and `Set(rows.map(\.channelKey))` (288), all on main. Only the programme query and cell layout are off-main (294-296, 318-327).

Measured on the host: a faithful replica of the Xtream row build (swiftc -O, Mac) took about 54 ms for 30,000 channels plus about 17 ms for sections, items and the key set; about 24 ms in total for 10,000. Phones will be at or above that, so roughly 70-200 ms on main at the start of the push for a 30k playlist. Real, but borderline rather than a clear hang.

The finding misses the worse case. The M3U branch first runs `M3UContentStore.shared.channels.filter { isLiveChannel($0) }` (265, 280-283) on main: a trim, URL(string:), path lowercasing and six substring checks for every entry of the playlist, VOD included. The store documents 310K+ entry playlists (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:7). That is a second-scale stall.

Fix corrections:
- The project sets SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj). EPGGuideRow has an explicit init (19-29), which is therefore main-actor isolated and cannot be called from a nonisolated static builder until the struct is marked `nonisolated` (as EPGProgramme already is, EPG/EPGModels.swift:63). `category(id:name:)` (193) needs `nonisolated` too.
- The proposed cache key does not exist: PlaylistContentStore has no catalog revision (grep). A cache keyed on catalog and hidden ids would also be wrong after an EPG refresh, because channelKey depends on EPGStore's alias map, which reload() rebuilds.

**Corrected claim:** Opening the guide builds all channel rows, sections and items on the main thread at the start of the push. For Xtream this is about 70 ms per 30,000 channels on a Mac host (more on a phone). For M3U it additionally URL-parses and classifies every playlist entry on the main thread, which on the documented 300k-entry playlists is a stall of a second or more.

**Corrected fix:** Move the build off the main actor, both branches, no cache.

1. Mark `EPGGuideRow` as `nonisolated struct ... Sendable` and make `category(id:name:)` `nonisolated private static` (L() is already nonisolated).
2. Add `nonisolated static func makeRows(xtream entries: [LiveStreamWithCategory], aliases: [String: String], hidden: Set<String>)` and an M3U twin that also does the isLiveChannel filter (M3UParser and M3UStreamClassifier.classify are already nonisolated). Return rows, ordered sections and the wanted-key set in one value.
3. Add a read-only `var resolutionSnapshot: [String: String]` to EPGStore and inline the four lines of storedKey in the static builder.
4. In load(): capture the inputs on main, run the builder in Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) as rebuildLayouts already does (318), check `generation == loadGeneration` after the await, then assign rows, orderedSections and items once. Store the task so cancelLoading() can cancel it.

A forced refresh simply runs the builder again off-main; that is correct because the alias map may have changed.

**API check:** No SDK API beyond Task.detached, already used at EPGGuideViewModel.swift:318. Code-base facts: EPGConstants is `nonisolated enum` (EPG/EPGConstants.swift:9); `nonisolated func L(_:)` (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:127); `nonisolated enum M3UParser` (Networking/M3UParser.swift:61); `nonisolated static func classify` (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:955); EPGStore.resolution is private (EPG/EPGStore.swift:54), so the accessor is needed.

**Regression risks:** State ordering: `rows.isEmpty` decides between .notConfigured and .empty (223-230) and must be evaluated after the awaited build. The generation guard must cover the new await, or a day switch or refresh during the build can apply stale rows. searchQuery.didSet calls recomputeItems (93-98) and must tolerate empty sections while the first build is in flight. Combining with the hidden-category fix (live-tv-browse-8) is natural: pass the hidden set into the builder.

**How to verify:** XCTest measure on the static builders with 30,000 synthetic Xtream streams and 300,000 synthetic M3U entries. Device: Instruments Hangs + Time Profiler while pushing the guide on a large Xtream playlist and on a large M3U playlist, before and after; main-thread time in EPGGuideViewModel.load should drop to the assignment only. Whether the Xtream case is visible as a hitch in the push (the animation itself runs in the render server) can only be settled on a device; the M3U case is large enough not to need that.

## live-tv-browse-10 — The guide's channel column cuts names to about eight hyphenated characters, and each category header draws its separator as a vertical hairline in the middle

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: EPG guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:101-123, 143-157`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:197-212`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:35`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Guide channel column on iPhone: logo only (name as fallback) or a narrower name column?

**What the user perceives:** iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png: "World New...", "Busi-ness...", "Morn-ing U...", "Foot-ball L...". Real names with a country prefix and a quality suffix cannot be told apart. The column still takes 104 of 402 pt, so less than two hours of programmes are visible. In the same screenshot a thin vertical line runs through the middle of the "News", "Sports" and "Entertainment" headers, and the headers have no bottom separator.

**Mechanism (finder):** Column: 104 pt holds 8 pt padding, a 32 pt logo, 8 pt spacing and about 48 pt of caption text with lineLimit(2) (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:144-156, EPGComponents.swift:209). The metrics are created with `compact: true` at both sites (EPGGuideView.swift:35, EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309), so iPad gets the same column.

Header: the `Divider()` in `.overlay(alignment: .bottom)` sits inside the Button's label (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:101-121). The rendering is consistent with the divider taking the vertical orientation there: a full-height line, centred horizontally by the .bottom alignment. The identical overlay outside a button (EPGGuideView.swift:163) renders as a horizontal line.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Header (plain fix, S): replace the Divider with `Rectangle().fill(Color(.separator)).frame(height: 1 / displayScale)` using `@Environment(\.displayScale)`, or attach the overlay outside the Button.

Column, option A: logo-first cell on compact width. A 44 pt logo centred in a 64 pt column; the name is shown only when there is no logo (three lines of caption2 with minimumScaleFactor(0.8)). The full name goes into the accessibility label and the context-menu preview.
Column, option B: keep the name, stack a 24 pt logo above two lines of caption2 in an 88 pt column.

Either way choose `compact` from horizontalSizeClass and pass the one metrics value into the view model instead of constructing it twice.

**Verifier reasons:** Both observations confirmed by code and by iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png (cropped and inspected).

Column: 104 pt minus 16 pt padding, a 32 pt logo and 8 pt spacing leaves about 48 pt for two lines of caption (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:144-156; Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:206-212). The screenshot shows "World New...", "Busi-ness...", "Morn-ing U...", "Foot-ball L...", "Motor-sport...". `EPGGuideMetrics(compact: true)` is hard-coded at both sites (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:35; Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309), so the regular values (172 pt column) are never used; history shows it has been so since 1cce013 with no explaining comment.

Header: a 1-pixel vertical line runs the full height of each category header at exactly half the screen width (x = 603 of 1206 px), and the header has no bottom rule. That matches a vertical Divider centred by `.overlay(alignment: .bottom)` inside the Button label (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:101-121). The same overlay on the axis row outside a button (EPGGuideView.swift:163) draws a horizontal rule in the same screenshot. The cause (the button label giving the divider a horizontal-stack context) is inferred, not proven; the explicit-height Rectangle fix does not depend on it.

Corrections to the fix:
- Option A shows the name only when iconURL is nil. IPTV logo URLs often exist but fail to load; those rows would show a placeholder icon with no name at all.
- Choosing `compact` from horizontalSizeClass also switches hourWidth (150 vs 180), which the view model bakes into the precomputed cell frames (309-310, 318-326). The class flips on rotation of large iPhones and on iPad window resizes, so every flip would need a layout rebuild and a scroll re-position.

**Corrected claim:** The guide's channel column leaves about 48 pt for the name, so most names are hyphenated and truncated after roughly eight characters, on iPad too because the compact metrics are hard-coded. Each category header draws its separator as a vertical hairline through its middle instead of a rule along its bottom.

**Corrected fix:** Header (plain fix): replace the Divider at EPGGuideRowViews.swift:121 with `Rectangle().fill(Color(.separator)).frame(height: 1 / displayScale)` in the same bottom overlay, with `@Environment(\.displayScale) private var displayScale` in EPGCategoryHeader.

Column (owner decides):
- Option B is the safe default: logo above two lines of caption2 in a column of about 88 pt, name always present.
- Option A (logo only) is acceptable only if the name is also shown whenever the logo is missing or fails to load, which needs a load-failure signal from CachedImage; otherwise failed logos leave anonymous rows.

Size class: vary only `channelColumnWidth` (and the cell arrangement) with horizontalSizeClass and keep hourWidth identical in both classes. Then the view model's precomputed layouts stay valid across rotation and resizing and it can keep constructing its own metrics. If a wider hour on iPad is wanted, hourWidth must be passed into rebuildLayouts and the layouts rebuilt on class change; that is a larger change.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface: `EnvironmentValues.displayScale: CGFloat` found (line 17074). UIColor.separator is existing UIKit API (iOS 13). `minimumScaleFactor`, `lineLimit` and `horizontalSizeClass` are long-standing and already used in the code base. Nothing iOS 26-only.

**Regression risks:** EPGChannelColumnCell is Equatable on row + metrics so the sticky offset can update without rebuilding cells (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:130-141); keep that, and keep metrics a value that compares equal across scroll frames. The column width also feeds the corner cell, the sticky offsets and the header width (EPGGuideView.swift:133, 207, 243), so it must come from the one metrics value. If the pinned-title fix (live-tv-browse-7) lands, its pinned edge is the same channelColumnWidth. The header fix alone is S with no known risk.

**How to verify:** Re-take L06 on iPhone (dark and light) and on iPad: no vertical hairline, a bottom rule under each header, channel names readable. Rotate an iPhone Pro Max and resize an iPad window with the guide open: programme cells stay aligned with the time axis and the now-line. Check a channel whose logo URL returns 404 still shows its name.

## live-tv-browse-11 — Typing in the Live search field keeps the shelf layout, so results are spread over horizontally scrolling rows, next to a Search tab that lists the same channels differently

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Search tab
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93-105, 226-240, 296-309, 744-749`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:77-83`, `Views/SearchView.swift:126-128, 151-171`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Keep the inline search field on the Live tab (with flat results), or remove it in favour of the Search tab?

**What the user perceives:** Searching "sport" on the Live tab leaves one horizontal row per matching category. A category whose name matches shows all of its channels. Results have to be hunted in two directions. The Search tab shows the same channels as a vertical list, with a different matching rule. On iPad two magnifier buttons sit in the same top bar (ipad-light/L01-live-home.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** recomputeFilter filters per category and keeps the category structure (LiveStreamsView.swift:296-309); contentList renders the same LiveCategoryShelfRow list for results (226-240). Channel matching here uses CatalogTextSearch.matches, while the Search tab uses localizedCaseInsensitiveContains on tokens (SearchView.swift:126-128). The dashboard already has a system search tab (DashboardView.swift:77-83).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest step: when debouncedQuery is not empty, render flat results with the existing LiveCategoryContent instead of contentList, built exactly like AllLiveView.recompute (LiveStreamsView.swift:744-749: filter hidden, match on channel name, sortLiveByRelevance, off the main thread). Shelves stay for the idle state. The player queue then follows the visible order.

Product question: with a system Search tab present, the per-tab field duplicates it. Apple's own tab apps keep search in the search tab. If the inline field stays, it should at least share one matching function with the Search tab.

**Verifier reasons:** The problem is real. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:296-309 filters per category and keeps the category structure; a category-name match keeps all of its channels (line 302). Results render through the same shelf list (226-240), and the ContinueWatchingRow (213-224) stays above them while searching, which the finding did not mention. The two matching rules differ: Live uses CatalogTextSearch.matches (Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:21-30, folds case, diacritics and punctuation, locale-invariant), while the Search tab uses localizedCaseInsensitiveContains per token (Views/SearchView.swift:126-128), which has the Turkish I/i problem that the CatalogTextSearch comment at lines 9-12 describes. ipad-light/L01-live-home.png shows two magnifiers in one top bar (tab bar search and the collapsed inline field). git log -S'catMatch' only returns the monorepo move d2489f9, and no comment marks the shelf search as deliberate. The fix needs correcting in five places. (1) VODView.swift:201-204, SeriesView.swift:254-257 and M3UChannelsView.swift:228-258 use the identical shelf-search pattern, so changing Live alone makes the tabs inconsistent. (2) LiveCategoryContent brings its own toolbar item (LiveStreamsView.swift:624-628) and applies the app-wide sort (543); with a name sort saved, results are not in relevance order. (3) The queue handed to the player comes from the parent's pre-sort array, as in AllLiveView (699, 706), so "queue follows the visible order" only holds with default sort and no filter. (4) A flat channel-name match drops the current category-name match, which is a behaviour change. (5) An if/else swap of contentList for a grid destroys the shelves ScrollView, so the scroll position is lost when search is cancelled.

**Corrected claim:** On the Live home (and equally on Movies, Series and the M3U channels home), typing in the inline search field keeps the shelf layout: one horizontal row per matching category, the whole category when its name matches, and the Continue Watching row still on top. The Search tab lists the same channels as a vertical list with a different and weaker matching function. On iPad both search entry points show as magnifiers in the same top bar.

**Corrected fix:** Product decision first: keep the per-tab inline field or rely on the Search tab. If it stays, apply one pattern to all four homes (Live, VOD, Series, M3U). While debouncedQuery is non-empty, show a flat result grid computed off-main as in AllLiveView.recompute (LiveStreamsView.swift:744-749) and hide ContinueWatchingRow. Keep the shelves ScrollView mounted (put the results in an overlay or ZStack above it, not an if/else swap) so its scroll position survives cancelling. Either reuse LiveCategoryContent and accept its sort/filter toolbar item and saved sort during search, or add a parameter that disables its toolbar and sort for the search use. Build the playback queue and a single section from the flat results and reset playbackModelMemo. Decide whether a category-name match should still surface (for example as a row linking to that category). Independently, make SearchView.search call CatalogTextSearch.matches so both entry points match identically; that also fixes the Turkish-locale miss in the Search tab.

**API check:** No new API is needed. Already in use here: searchable(text:isPresented:prompt:), Tab(_:systemImage:value:role:) with role .search (DashboardView.swift:77). tabViewSearchActivation and searchToolbarBehavior exist in the iOS 26 SwiftUI interface but the fix does not rely on them.

**Regression risks:** Loss of shelf scroll position if the views are swapped instead of layered. A sort/filter button appearing in the Live home toolbar during search on iPad. Saved name sort overriding relevance order. Category-name matches disappearing. Inconsistent tabs if only Live changes. The Equatable shelf rows and off-main filtering must stay for the idle state. playbackModelMemo must be rebuilt from the flat results or the player queue will be wrong.

**How to verify:** UI test on demo data: type a channel name in the Live search field; assert no category header and no Continue Watching row, and that results are in one vertical grid. Cancel search and assert the shelves return at the previous scroll offset. Tap a result and step next/previous to confirm the queue matches the visible order with default sort. Unit test: SearchView matching and CatalogTextSearch.matches agree for "HISTORY" vs "history" under a tr_TR locale and for diacritics. iPad screenshot to settle the two-magnifier question.

## live-tv-browse-12 — Every horizontal scroll frame in the guide re-evaluates the whole EPGGuideView body, because the pinned column and headers are positioned from @State

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: EPG guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:13-27, 104-123, 151-158, 185-188, 204-209, 238-248, 292-295, 323-340, 426-432`

**What the user perceives:** Expected, not measured: horizontal panning in the guide is less smooth than vertical scrolling on 120 Hz devices, and on a fast flick the time axis trails the grid by a frame.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each horizontal offset change writes bodyOffsetX (EPGGuideView.swift:185-188), which the body reads at 155, 208 and 247. So the body re-runs per frame: the day picker with nine Calendar computations and date formatting per chip (104-123, 426-432), the toolbar, and the row closure for every realised row, including a Date() per row for nowLineX (219, 292-295). EPGChannelRowView is skipped thanks to its Equatable wrapper, which is the part already done right. The time axis is a second ScrollView driven through a ScrollPosition binding (134-145, 323-340), so it follows its source one update late.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Stage 1 (S): extract the day picker into an Equatable subview (inputs: selectedDay and the day list) and compute nowLineX once per body.

Stage 2 (M): pin the channel cell and the category header without state:

```swift
.visualEffect { content, proxy in
    content.offset(x: -proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal)).minX)
}
```

Keep the axis now-line in a small subview that observes its own offset object, so EPGGuideView.body no longer depends on the scroll offset. Check on device that taps on the pinned cell still land; if hit-testing does not follow the effect, keep the current offset.

Stage 3 (L, optional): make the time axis the pinned header of `LazyVStack(pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders])` inside the body scroller. One scroller, and positions / reportedOffsets / activeScroller / programmaticTargetX / lastSyncX go away. The current latch design fixed a hang (comment at lines 20-23), so it stays until stage 3 is proven on device.

**APIs:** View.visualEffect(_:) (iOS 17.0); CoordinateSpaceProtocol.scrollView(axis:) (iOS 17.0); PinnedScrollableViews / LazyVStack(pinnedViews:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The per-frame body invalidation is real in code. Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:185-187 writes bodyOffsetX on every horizontal offset change, and body reads it eagerly in the axis overlay (151-158) and in the row and header builders (208, 247). Each pass re-runs the day picker (104-123; availableDays at EPGGuideViewModel.swift:127-130 does nine calendar date additions, plus per-chip calendar checks and formatting at 426-432), the toolbar, and the row closure for each realised row, including Calendar.isDateInToday and Date() via nowLineX (290-295). EPGChannelRowView is skipped through .equatable() (217). Two things need correcting. First, the perceptible effect is unmeasured: the per-pass work is small, and nothing in the code proves a hitch or a one-frame axis lag, so only a device trace can settle it. Second, stage 2 does not achieve what it states. propagate() also writes positions[followerID] on every frame of a user pan (336-338), and positions is read in body through hBinding (138, 180, 297-302). So body would still be invalidated per frame after bodyOffsetX is removed, for as long as the two-scroller sync exists. History: the latch and sync came with 1cce013 as a hang fix, and the shared-offset now-line came with 654cefc to stop drift; both are deliberate and must be kept until a single-scroller design is proven. EPGChannelColumnCell conforms to Equatable but is not wrapped in .equatable() at 204.

**Corrected claim:** Every horizontal scroll frame in the guide invalidates EPGGuideView.body. The causes are two @State values read in body: bodyOffsetX (pinned column, headers, axis now-line) and the positions dictionary that drives the follower scroller. The work per pass is the day picker, the toolbar and the closures of the realised rows; the programme strips are skipped. Whether this costs frames on a 120 Hz device, and whether the axis trails the grid, is unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** Measure first. Then:

Stage 1 (S): extract the day picker into an Equatable subview (inputs: selectedDay and the day list), compute nowLineX once per grid pass and pass it into the rows, and add .equatable() to EPGChannelColumnCell.

Stage 2 (M): move both scrollers and all sync state (positions, reportedOffsets, bodyOffsetX, lastSyncX, activeScroller, programmaticTargetX) into a dedicated grid subview, so the outer view (searchable, toolbar, day picker, sheet, navigationDestination) is no longer invalidated. Make the channel row and the header row Equatable view structs (row, layout.version, metrics, nowX). Pin the channel cell and header with `.visualEffect { content, proxy in content.offset(x: max(0, -proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal)).minX)) }`; the max(0, ...) keeps today's clamp during leading rubber-band. Keep the axis now-line on the shared offset inside the grid subview.

Stage 3 (L, optional, device-proven only): a single scroller with the time axis as a pinned section header. This is the only step that removes the per-frame positions writes. Keep the latch design until it is proven.

**API check:** SwiftUICore interface: `nonisolated public func visualEffect(_ effect: @escaping @Sendable (EmptyVisualEffect, GeometryProxy) -> some VisualEffect) -> some View`, @available(iOS 17.0). `extension CoordinateSpaceProtocol where Self == NamedCoordinateSpace { public static func scrollView(axis: Axis) -> Self }`, iOS 17.0. `VisualEffect.offset(x:y:)` is present. `PinnedScrollableViews`, iOS 14.0, and `LazyVStack.init(alignment:spacing:pinnedViews:content:)` are present. Already used by the screen: onScrollGeometryChange(for:of:action:) and onScrollPhaseChange, both iOS 18.0. visualEffect has a precedent in this code base at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:63. All are within the iOS 18 deployment target, so no availability guard is needed.

**Regression risks:** The active-scroller latch and the programmatic-target guard fixed a main-thread hang and a now-line drift (commits 1cce013, 654cefc); restructuring the sync can bring either back. Whether taps on a cell moved by visualEffect land where it is drawn must be checked on device. Row structs that are Equatable while ignoring closures keep stale closures; that is safe today because the closures only capture the row and the model. A pinned section header inside a two-axis ScrollView is unproven. Jump-to-now and day switching depend on applyProgrammaticOffset setting bodyOffsetX.

**How to verify:** On a ProMotion iPhone and an iPad with a playlist of several thousand channels with EPG: Instruments SwiftUI template plus Hitches during a 5-second horizontal pan and a hard flick. Record the body count of EPGGuideView per second, the hitch time ratio, and main-thread time per frame; compare with a vertical pan on the same screen. Use a 240 fps screen recording to see whether the axis labels and the pinned column trail the programme cells. Repeat after each stage. Manually check the now-line alignment between axis and rows, jump-to-now, day switching, and taps on the pinned channel cell.

## live-tv-browse-13 — Guide cells give no touch feedback and the channel schedule hides behind a custom half-second long-press

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: EPG guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:20-27, 158-169`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:204-206, 398-402`

**What the user perceives:** Nothing in the guide reacts visibly to a touch: channel cells and programme blocks do not highlight. The schedule opens after a 0.5 s press with no haptic, no lift and no preview, and nothing hints that it exists. For M3U playlists the same tap opens the schedule instead of playing.

**Mechanism (finder):** The channel cell attaches `LongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.5).exclusively(before: TapGesture())` with .gesture (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169). Programme cells use .onTapGesture (24-26). Neither is a Button, so there is no pressed state and no button trait. playChannel falls back to the schedule when there is no live stream (EPGGuideView.swift:398-402).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Channel cell: `Button(action: onTap) { ... }.buttonStyle(.plain)` plus `.contextMenu { Play; Schedule; Add to Favorites } preview: { ... }`, sharing the menu from the tile finding. The Equatable conformance stays.

Programme cell: a Button with a small ButtonStyle that lightens the fill while configuration.isPressed.

Device check for both the old and the new version: a vertical drag that starts on the channel column must scroll the guide. A gesture attached with .gesture to scroll content is a known source of swallowed drags, and the column is where a left thumb starts.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169 attaches `LongPressGesture(minimumDuration: 0.5).exclusively(before: TapGesture())` with .gesture to a plain HStack: there is no pressed state, no haptic, no button trait, and nothing hints at the long press. Programme cells use .onTapGesture (24-26) and also have no pressed state. That matters more because showProgramme awaits a database read before the sheet appears (EPGGuideView.swift:412-424), so a tap gives no immediate response. The M3U fallback is real and commented as deliberate (EPGGuideView.swift:398-402). One piece of history the finding missed: until 654cefc the cell was `Button(action: onTap) ... .buttonStyle(.plain).simultaneousGesture(LongPressGesture()...)`, and that commit replaced it with the exclusive gesture. So the Button was removed on purpose, most likely because tap and long press both fired. The proposed Button plus contextMenu does not bring that back, because no custom long-press gesture competes with the button; it must not be combined with any LongPressGesture. Whether the current .gesture swallows vertical drags that start on the channel column cannot be decided from code.

**Corrected claim:** The original claim stands. Addition: the channel cell was a Button until commit 654cefc and was deliberately changed to an exclusive long-press/tap gesture, so the fix must use the system context menu and not a custom long press beside a Button.

**Corrected fix:** Channel cell: `Button(action: onTap) { ... }.buttonStyle(.plain)` with `.contextMenu { Play (when row.liveStream != nil); Schedule } preview: { ... }` inside EPGChannelColumnCell.body, keeping the Equatable conformance and removing the LongPressGesture entirely. A Favorites item is optional and makes the change M, since it needs the DBFavorite read and write. For M3U rows the tap keeps opening the schedule and the menu offers Schedule only.

Programme cell: use a Button with a small pressed-state ButtonStyle only for cells that have a programme, and measure vertical scrolling afterwards, because each realised row builds dozens of cells. The cheaper alternative is to keep .onTapGesture and add .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton).

**API check:** SwiftUI interface: `nonisolated public func contextMenu<M, P>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> M, @ViewBuilder preview: () -> P) -> some View where M : View, P : View`, @available(iOS 16.0, macOS 13.0, tvOS 16.0, *). Button, ButtonStyle and PlainButtonStyle are iOS 13. No availability guard is needed.

**Regression risks:** Re-adding a custom long press next to the Button would restore the double-fire that 654cefc removed. Turning every programme cell into a Button raises the cost of creating a row during vertical scrolling in large guides. The context menu lift on a cell that is pinned by an offset and has a material background should be checked for a correct preview frame. EPGChannelColumnCell equality ignores closures; the menu actions must only use the row, as today.

**How to verify:** UI test: tap a channel cell and assert the player opens (Xtream). Long-press and assert a menu with Schedule appears and opens ChannelEPGDetailView, and that the player did not also open. Device, old and new build: start a vertical drag and a horizontal drag on the channel column and on a programme cell and confirm the guide scrolls both ways. Instruments hitch rate for a vertical flick through a large guide, before and after the programme-cell Button. VoiceOver: channel and programme cells are announced as buttons.

## live-tv-browse-14 — In the sort and filter menu the filters are buttons that swap in a checkmark icon, each choice closes the menu, and a spinner sits at the end of every long grid although nothing is loading

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live category detail, All Channels
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:543-545, 579-582, 616-620, 634-674`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should the catch-up / EPG filter be remembered like the sort, or stay per visit?

**What the user perceives:** iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png: the sort rows have the system checkmark, the two filters are plain text rows. Turning on both filters takes two trips into the menu. VoiceOver does not announce them as on or off. The filter is forgotten when leaving the screen, while the sort is remembered app-wide. Scrolling fast to the end of a page shows a spinner that suggests a network load.

**Mechanism (finder):** The filters are Buttons that switch between Label(..., systemImage: "checkmark") and Text (LiveStreamsView.swift:643-660). filter is @State (545) while sortOption is @AppStorage (543). The ProgressView is shown whenever visibleCount < displayItems.count (616-620), but loadMore is a synchronous counter bump (579-582).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use toggles, which menus render with the native checkmark and selected state:

```swift
Section(L("filter.title")) {
    Toggle(L("filter.catchup"), isOn: binding(.catchup))
    Toggle(L("filter.has_epg"), isOn: binding(.hasEPG))
}
.menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled)
```

The sort Picker stays as it is. Replace the spinner with an invisible sentinel, `Color.clear.frame(height: 1).onAppear(perform: loadMore)`; pagination itself is kept. Whether the filter should persist like the sort is the owner's call.

**APIs:** View.menuActionDismissBehavior(_:) (iOS 16.4); Toggle (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Menu part confirmed. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:643-660 builds the two filters as Buttons that swap between `Label(..., systemImage: "checkmark")` and Text, so the mark lands in the icon column and not in the selection column the sort Picker uses (iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png shows the Picker checkmark and two plain rows). Each Button tap closes the menu by default. filter is @State (545) and the sort is @AppStorage (543); the comment at 544 calls the filter screen-local, so that is deliberate and a product choice. The pattern exists only here (grep for formSymmetricDifference). Spinner part is overstated and its fix is wrong. loadMore is synchronous (579-582), but the per-item onAppear at index >= visibleCount - 15 (611) extends the page before the tail is reached, so the ProgressView (616-620) is on screen for a frame or two at most on a very hard flick or a scroll-bar drag. It does not sit at the end of every long grid. The proposed sentinel, `Color.clear.frame(height: 1).onAppear(perform: loadMore)`, would be a sibling of the LazyVGrid directly inside ScrollView, which is not a lazy container. Its onAppear fires once when it is inserted, not when it scrolls into view, so it would load page two immediately and then never fire again.

**Corrected claim:** In the Live sort and filter menu the two filters are buttons that swap in a checkmark icon instead of using the menu's selection state, each choice closes the menu, and the filter is per visit while the sort is remembered (the latter by design). The end-of-grid ProgressView can flash briefly on a very fast scroll although nothing is loading; this is a minor cosmetic point.

**Corrected fix:** Replace the two Buttons with `Toggle(L("filter.catchup"), isOn: ...)` and `Toggle(L("filter.has_epg"), isOn: ...)`, using a small Binding helper over the OptionSet (get: filter.contains(x); set: insert or remove). Apply `.menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled)` to those two toggles only, so the sort Picker and Clear filter still close the menu. Keep the Picker and the Clear button. For the spinner: delete the ProgressView block (616-620) and keep the per-item onAppear trigger as the only pagination driver; do not add a sentinel outside the lazy grid. Persisting the filter is the owner's decision.

**API check:** SwiftUI interface: `@available(iOS 16.4, macOS 13.3, tvOS 16.4, watchOS 9.4, *) nonisolated public func menuActionDismissBehavior(_ behavior: MenuActionDismissBehavior) -> some View`. `MenuActionDismissBehavior.disabled` is declared with `@available(tvOS 17.0, *)` and unavailable on macOS and watchOS; it is available on iOS from 16.4. `public struct Toggle<Label> : View` is iOS 13. No availability guard is needed.

**Regression risks:** With the menu staying open, the Clear filter row appears and disappears while the menu is visible, so the menu changes height; check that this looks acceptable, or show Clear always and disable it. The grid recomputes behind the open menu on each toggle (task keyed on filter.rawValue, line 631); that already runs off-main. Removing the spinner changes nothing functionally. Pagination and the Equatable signature stay untouched.

**How to verify:** UI test on a category with catch-up channels: open the menu, switch both filters, assert the menu is still open after each, assert both rows report a selected state, then dismiss and assert the grid is filtered. Screenshot of the menu with one filter on, in iOS 18 and iOS 26 simulators. Manual: flick to the end of All Channels with a large playlist and confirm that pages keep loading and no spinner is shown.

## live-tv-browse-15 — In the category picker, tapping a hidden category closes the sheet and does nothing, and hiding is only possible by an unannounced swipe

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Category picker sheet, Live TV home
- Code: `Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:64-81, 101-136`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:139-149, 250-258`

**What the user perceives:** A tap on a row in the "Hidden" section dismisses the sheet and the list does not move. Nothing tells the user that a swipe hides or shows a category. Counts are custom grey chips. There is a tall blank band between the search field and the first row (iphone-dark/L07-live-category-picker.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** row() calls onSelect(entry.id) for hidden rows too (CategoryPickerSheet.swift:103-105). LiveStreamsView turns that into proxy.scrollTo of an id that is not in displayCategories, which is a no-op (LiveStreamsView.swift:145-148, 250-254). Hide and show exist only as a swipe action (CategoryPickerSheet.swift:122-135). The count is a hand-built capsule (111-118).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Hidden rows: make the tap unhide the category (`hiddenStore.setHidden(false, ...)` inside withAnimation) instead of calling onSelect. Add a `.contextMenu` with the same Hide / Show action as the swipe, and a one-line section footer that mentions it. Replace the capsule with the list row badge, `.badge(entry.count)`, which gives the standard secondary trailing count. Tighten the top gap with `.contentMargins(.top, 0, for: .scrollContent)`. The single-pass partition stays.

**APIs:** View.badge(_:) (Int) (iOS 15.0); View.contentMargins(_:_:for:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The dead tap is confirmed. Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:103-105 calls onSelect for hidden rows too. All four callers close the sheet and set a scroll target (LiveStreamsView.swift:145-148, VODView.swift:140-143, SeriesView.swift:136 onward, M3UChannelsView.swift:107-110), and scrollTo is a no-op because hidden categories are not in the shelf list (LiveStreamsView.swift:285 and 250-254; M3UChannelsView.swift:26-29). Hide and show exist only as a swipe action (CategoryPickerSheet.swift:122-135): setHidden has no other call site and there is no hint string. The count is a hand-built capsule (111-118), visible in iphone-dark/L07-live-category-picker.png. Three corrections. (1) `.badge(entry.count)` shows nothing for a count of 0, and counts are 0 while streams are still loading (LiveStreamsView.swift:50) or for empty categories; the Text overload keeps the zero. (2) The gap under the search field is the system inset-grouped top inset, not a layout bug. Tightening it is a taste choice, and the owner made that same choice in the tip-jar work (Views/Components/TipJarView.swift:99-100, with a value of 8). (3) Making a tap on a hidden row unhide it is a product decision, not the only correct fix. The fix lives in the shared sheet, so it changes the Movies, Series and M3U pickers as well, which is the desired scope.

**Corrected claim:** In the shared category picker (Live, Movies, Series, M3U), tapping a row in the Hidden section closes the sheet and scrolls nowhere. Hiding and showing is reachable only through an unannounced swipe. Counts are a custom capsule and not the list badge. The space under the search field is the system default inset.

**Corrected fix:** In CategoryPickerSheet.row: for hidden rows, do not call onSelect. Either unhide in place (`withAnimation { hiddenStore.setHidden(false, ...) }`, sheet stays open) or disable the row's tap; the owner chooses. Add `.contextMenu` with the same Hide/Show action as the swipe (only when hidingEnabled) and a one-line section footer that mentions it. Replace the capsule with `.badge(Text("\(entry.count)"))` so zero counts still show. Optionally add `.contentMargins(.top, 8, for: .scrollContent)` to match the value already used in TipJarView. Keep the single-pass partition and the swipe action.

**API check:** SwiftUI interface: `@available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, *) extension View { nonisolated public func badge(_ count: Int) -> some View; nonisolated public func badge(_ label: Text?) -> some View }`. `@available(iOS 17.0, ...) nonisolated public func contentMargins(_ edges: Edge.Set = .all, _ length: CGFloat?, for placement: ContentMarginPlacement = .automatic) -> some View`. contextMenu(menuItems:) is iOS 13 and the preview variant is iOS 16. No availability guard is needed.

**Regression risks:** The footer needs a new key in all ten Localizable.strings files, which carry the owner's uncommitted tip keys; the change must be additive only. The sheet is shared by four screens, so each picker should be rechecked. The M3U group picker passes already filtered displayGroups as entries. A badge on a row whose label is a Button with an explicit primary colour should be checked visually in light and dark. Unhide-on-tap changes stored state from a plain tap; it is reversible by swipe.

**How to verify:** UI test: hide a category by swipe, tap it in the Hidden section, assert the sheet is still open and the row is back in the visible section (or, if the owner picks the disabled variant, that nothing happens and the sheet stays). Long-press a row and assert the Hide/Show menu item. Open the picker while streams are loading and assert zero counts are still displayed. Screenshot comparison with iphone-dark/L07-live-category-picker.png and the Series picker, light and dark.

## live-tv-browse-16 — Category headers on the Live home render in the accent colour although the code asks for .primary, next to a label-coloured "Continue Watching" header

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Confirm label-coloured shelf headers are wanted; the current blue is a side effect, but the owner may have grown used to it.

**What the user perceives:** Every category name is blue with a pale blue chevron (L01-live-home.png in all three variants). On a real playlist that is hundreds of blue links competing with the channel logos. "Continue Watching" on the same screen is a bold label-coloured title. Shelf titles in Apple's TV, Music and App Store apps are label-coloured with a grey chevron.

**Mechanism (finder):** The header is a NavigationLink without a button style. Inside its label `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:366) resolves to the primary level of the tint, not the label colour, and `.tertiary` on the chevron to a tint shade. ContinueWatchingRow adds `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (line 43) and gets the label colour, with .title2 bold instead of .headline.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add `.buttonStyle(.plain)` to the header NavigationLink, use one shared header style for both rows (for example `.font(.title3.weight(.semibold))`, chevron `.secondary`), and give the label `.contentShape(Rectangle())`. The same lines exist in VODView.swift:325, SeriesView.swift:302 and M3UChannelsView.swift:347.

**Verifier reasons:** The problem and the mechanism are real; the list of sites and one piece of evidence need correcting.

What stands:
- Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367 is a NavigationLink with no button style inside a ScrollView/LazyVStack. Its label sets `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` on the HStack (366) and `.tertiary` on the chevron (364). Both are HierarchicalShapeStyle levels, which resolve against the current foreground style. Under the default button style that is the tint, so the title renders blue and the chevron pale blue.
- Screenshots confirm it: iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png and ipad-light/L01-live-home.png (News / Sports / Entertainment / Kids in system blue with a pale blue chevron), and iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png and S01-series-home.png for the sibling shelves.
- The blue is not a brand choice: Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset/Contents.json has no colour value, so it is the default system blue.
- It is not deliberate: git blame puts lines 356-367 in the initial commit fe55017 ("feat: native ios app"), there is no comment beside them, and writing `.primary` shows the intent was label colour.
- Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44 has the same label structure plus `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (43), with `.title2.weight(.bold)` (35) and horizontal padding 20 (44) against `.headline` and padding 16 on the shelves (LiveStreamsView.swift:361, 370). Both rows sit in the same ScrollView (LiveStreamsView.swift:213 and 225-239).

Corrections:
1. The site list is incomplete. The finding names VODView.swift:325 and SeriesView.swift:302, which are the Recently Added shelves. The movie and series category shelves are Views/VODView.swift:418-429 and Views/SeriesView.swift:394-405. There are six sites in all: LiveStreamsView.swift:356, VODView.swift:315 and 418, SeriesView.swift:292 and 394, M3UChannelsView.swift:337.
2. The Continue Watching comparison is from code only. No screenshot shows that row, because the demo data has no watch history.
3. iphone-light/L01-live-home.png actually shows the Series tab (mis-captured), so "L01 in all three variants" is loose; it shows the same defect on Series.
4. The proposed common font (`.title3.weight(.semibold)`) is a design choice, not part of the fix.

**Corrected claim:** On every home screen (Live TV, Movies, Series, M3U channels) the shelf headers, both category names and Recently Added, render in the tint colour (default system blue) with a pale blue chevron, although the code asks for `.primary` / `.tertiary`. The cause is that the header NavigationLink has no button style, so the hierarchical styles resolve against the tint. Six sites: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367, Views/VODView.swift:315-326 and 418-429, Views/SeriesView.swift:292-303 and 394-405, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:337-348. The Continue Watching header on the same screens (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44) uses `.buttonStyle(.plain)` and so is label-coloured. It also uses a different font (.title2 bold against .headline) and a different leading inset (20 against 16), so one screen can show two header styles with misaligned leading edges. Apple's TV, Music and App Store apps use label-coloured shelf titles with a grey chevron.

**Corrected fix:** Minimal fix: add `.buttonStyle(.plain)` to the header NavigationLink at all six sites (LiveStreamsView.swift:367, VODView.swift:326 and 429, SeriesView.swift:303 and 404, M3UChannelsView.swift:348). Add `.contentShape(Rectangle())` to the label HStack so the 6pt gap between title and chevron stays tappable. Keep `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` and `.tertiary`; under the plain style they resolve to label colours.

Optional: extract one small shared view (for example `ShelfHeaderLabel(title:)`) and use it at all six sites and in ContinueWatchingRow, so font, chevron and leading inset are defined once. If so, align ContinueWatchingRow's horizontal padding (20) with the shelves (16).

Product decisions for the owner, not fixes: which font the shared header uses (.headline as now, .title3 semibold, or .title2 bold), and whether to keep blue headers on purpose. If blue is wanted, leave the code as it is.

**API check:** All three APIs exist from iOS 13, so no availability gate is needed for the iOS 18 target.
- SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8486-8488: `@available(iOS 13.0, ...) extension View { nonisolated public func buttonStyle<S>(_ style: S) -> some View where S : PrimitiveButtonStyle }`
- SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8843-8850: `@available(iOS 13.0, ...) extension PrimitiveButtonStyle where Self == PlainButtonStyle { static var plain: PlainButtonStyle }` and `@available(iOS 13.0, ...) public struct PlainButtonStyle : PrimitiveButtonStyle`
- SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13251: `@inlinable nonisolated public func contentShape<S>(_ shape: S, eoFill: Bool = false) -> some View where S : Shape`
- SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6675-6682: `ShapeStyle where Self == HierarchicalShapeStyle { static var primary / secondary / tertiary }`, which is why they follow the button tint.
`.buttonStyle(.plain)` is already used on NavigationLinks in the same files (VODView.swift:345, SeriesView.swift:322, ContinueWatchingRow.swift:43).

**Regression risks:** - The headers lose the one visual cue that they are tappable apart from the chevron. That matches Apple's shelves, but it is the owner's call.
- Pressed feedback changes from the default fade to the plain style's dimming.
- No effect on the earlier performance work: the change is inside the shelf rows' bodies, and their Equatable conformance and `.equatable()` call sites (LiveStreamsView.swift:337-349, 237) are untouched.
- The UI tests tap headers as buttons (another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:315, 347, 371: `app.buttons["News"]`, `["Action"]`, `["Drama"]`). A plain-styled NavigationLink is still a button, so they should keep matching; rerun to confirm.
- If the font is also unified, shelf height changes slightly; check the shelf loading placeholder heights and M3UChannelsView's trailing count label (M3UChannelsView.swift:350-352, `.firstTextBaseline` alignment).
- Does not touch the tip-jar files.

**How to verify:** After the change, recapture L01 (Live), M01 (Movies) and S01 (Series) on iPhone light and dark and on iPad, plus the M3U channels home. Shelf titles should be label-coloured (black / white) with a grey chevron.

Seed one watch-history entry so Continue Watching appears, then check that its header and the shelf headers share colour and leading edge.

Tap a header on its text, on the chevron and in the gap between them; each should push the category detail. Rerun ScreensUITests to confirm `app.buttons["News"]`, `["Action"]` and `["Drama"]` still resolve.

## transitions-motion-1 — Movie and series detail swap their whole content for a full-screen spinner (or error) one frame after the push, then everything pops back in

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:73-81, 99-103, 164-175, 268-270, 303-311`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:866-875, 892-896, 1007-1013, 1176-1178, 1240-1245`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:318-341`

**What the user perceives:** Tap a poster whose metadata is not cached yet: the detail slides in showing hero, title and Play for one frame, flips to an empty page with a centred spinner while still sliding, and when the panel answers the page reappears with genre chips, plot and cast inserted in one hard cut. The genre chip row lands between the hero and the Play button, so the button moves down ~45 pt just when the thumb is going for it. If the request fails, the whole page (poster, title, Play, Download) is replaced by an error (S03-series-detail-loading.png shows exactly that: only 'Error / Server error: HTTP 404 / Try Again').

**Mechanism (finder):** The first body pass has isLoading == false, so contentScroll renders (MovieDetailView.swift:79-80). The .task at :99-103 then calls fetchMovieInfo(), whose first statement is isLoading = true (:269); the body condition `isLoading && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded` (:74) now replaces the entire screen with ProgressView. Everything needed for the first screen (name, poster, rating, stream URL) is already in `movie`; only plot/genre/cast/backdrop depend on the request. Series does the same at SeriesView.swift:868-870 / :1177. On completion isLoading = false (:305, :1240) brings contentScroll back and the @Query record adds GenreChipRow (:130), DetailPlotBlock (:164-167) and the info blocks without any transaction, i.e. as layout jumps. errorMessage replaces the page the same way (:77-78, SeriesView.swift:871-872).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Never swap the page; make metadata additive.
1) body: always render contentScroll. Drop the `isLoading && !metadataLoaded` branch and turn the error into a non-blocking inline row under the action bar (retry button), so Play/Download stay usable.
2) Keep the primary button where it is: give GenreChipRow a fixed-height slot (or move it below DetailActionBar) so its arrival cannot move the CTA.
3) Placeholder while loading instead of nothing: `if isLoading && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded { DetailPlotBlock(plot: String(repeating: "placeholder ", count: 24)).redacted(reason: .placeholder) }`.
4) Animate the arrival once, on the container: `VStack { ... }.animation(.smooth(duration: 0.3), value: currentMovie.metadataLoaded)` (series: value: currentSeries.seasonsLoaded) so new blocks fade in and the ones below slide instead of jumping.
No iOS 26 API involved; nothing to gate.

**APIs:** View.redacted(reason:) (iOS 14.0 (SwiftUICore swiftinterface)); Animation.smooth(duration:extraBounce:) (iOS 17.0); View.animation(_:value:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/MovieDetailView.swift. `isLoading` starts false (:14), so the first body pass takes the `contentScroll` branch (:79-80). The `.task` (:99-103) calls `fetchMovieInfo()`, whose first statement is `isLoading = true` (:269); `isLoading && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded` (:74) then replaces the whole screen with `ProgressView` for the duration of the `get_vod_info` request. Everything on the first screen (name, poster, rating, playback URL from `PlaybackURLBuilder`, :143-146) comes from the `movie` parameter and needs no request. On failure `errorMessage` replaces the page (:77-78, :106-121), so Play and Download disappear although the stream URL is known. Series is the same: Views/SeriesView.swift:868-872, :892-896, :1177, :1240-1245. Screenshot iphone-light/S03-series-detail-loading.png shows exactly this page: only 'Error / Server error: HTTP 404 / Try Again', no hero, no title, no Watch button. History: the branch dates from the first native commit (fe55017); the only related deliberate work is `applyVODMetadata` (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-178), which avoids repeat fetches for movies and is not touched by the fix. Two corrections to the description, neither changes the verdict: (a) today the page comes back as one hard cut from spinner to full page (the Group's if/else rebuilds the ScrollView), so the 'Play button moves ~45 pt under the thumb' effect does not exist yet; it would appear once the content is always rendered, which is why point 2 of the fix matters. (b) For series, genre, plot, cast and director are already in the catalog row (PlaylistContentStore.swift:563-578), so only the seasons depend on the request and SeriesView.swift:1008-1013 already has a 'loading seasons' placeholder; the full-screen spinner is even less justified there.

**Corrected claim:** Movie and series detail render their full content for one frame, then replace the whole page with a centred spinner for as long as get_vod_info / get_series_info takes, then cut back to the full page. A failed request replaces the whole page with an error, removing Play and Download even though playback does not need the metadata. For movies only plot, genre, cast, director, backdrop and trailer depend on the request; for series only the seasons do.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with these additions. (1) Always render `contentScroll`; drop the spinner branch and show the error as an inline row with a retry button (movies: under the action bar; series: in place of `seasonsSection`). (2) Keep the primary button still: moving `GenreChipRow` below `DetailActionBar` is the smallest change; a fixed-height slot leaves a permanent gap for titles without genres. This is a layout choice for the owner. Note the trailer button (DetailComponents.swift:254-270) also arrives late inside the action bar and pushes Download down. (3) The redacted plot placeholder is optional; a small inline progress row where the plot will appear is enough and avoids a collapse when a title has no plot. (4) `.animation(.smooth(duration: 0.3), value: currentMovie.metadataLoaded)` on the VStack (series: `seasons.isEmpty`, since seasons arrive through their own @Query). (5) Series only: with the page always visible, the Watch button is tappable before seasons exist and `playFirstEpisode()` silently returns (SeriesView.swift:1086). Disable the primary action, or show progress in it, while `seasons.isEmpty && !hasResume`. No iOS 26 API, nothing to gate.

**API check:** SwiftUICore swiftinterface: `nonisolated public func redacted(reason: SwiftUICore.RedactionReasons) -> some View` at line 6107, in an extension marked @available(iOS 14.0, ...). `@_alwaysEmitIntoClient public static func smooth(duration: Foundation.TimeInterval = 0.5, extraBounce: Swift.Double = 0.0) -> SwiftUICore.Animation` at line 13314; the enclosing extension is @available(iOS 13.0) (line 13286) and the body calls `spring(duration:bounce:)`, so the finding's 'iOS 17.0' is not what the interface states, but either way it is below the iOS 18 target. `func animation<V>(_ animation: Animation?, value: V) -> some View where V: Equatable` at line 13425, iOS 13.0. All three found.

**Regression risks:** `applyVODMetadata` and the `metadataLoaded` guard in `.task` must stay, or every revisit refetches. The container animation also animates the hero switching from blurred poster fallback to the real backdrop (DetailComponents.swift:61-62); this looks intended but should be watched once. The series Watch button needs the guard in point 5 or it becomes a dead tap during loading. Nothing here touches the Equatable rows, pagination or the tip-jar files.

**How to verify:** UI test with get_vod_info / get_series_info stubbed to answer after 2 s: immediately after the push the primary button exists, is hittable, and has the same frame before and after the response; no element with the `detail.loading_movie` / `detail.loading_series` text ever exists. Second run with the stub returning 404: hero, title and primary button still exist and an inline retry is present. Frame-step a 120 Hz screen recording of the push to confirm there is no spinner frame.

## transitions-motion-2 — On launch the home tabs show 'No category found' between the two catalog load phases, and the phase-1 skeleton that was built for this never appears

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:64-91, 105-107, 278-294, 372-374`, `Views/VODView.swift:37-62, 157-159, 166-177, 434-436`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:38-63, 158-160, 220-232, 410-412`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-152`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:141-149`

**What the user perceives:** Cold start with a real catalog: spinner, then the empty-state icon with 'No category found.' for as long as the streams take to load from SQLite (seconds with 100k+ rows), then all shelves appear at once. On the first visit to each other tab the same empty state flashes for a frame before the shelves replace it. With the 13-channel demo data the window is too short to see, so the screenshots do not show it.

**Mechanism (finder):** loadPlaylist publishes categories first and sets isLoading = false on purpose ('UI kategorilerle hemen gösterilir', PlaylistContentStore.swift:132-137), then loads streams and sets streamsLoaded = true (:152). The tabs render from @State displayCategories, which is only filled by recomputeFilter(), and that only runs from .task(id: debouncedQuery / contentStore.streamsLoaded / hiddenIds) (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, VODView.swift:157-159, SeriesView.swift:158-160). streamsLoaded is false before and after phase 1 (:135 assigns false again), so no task re-fires when the categories land. Body then evaluates: displayCategories.isEmpty, isLoading == false, activePlaylistId == playlist.id, loadError == nil -> the last else branch, the 'live.empty.no_category' empty state (LiveStreamsView.swift:79-87). The reserved-height rows for 'streams still loading' (LiveStreamsView.swift:373-374, VODView.swift:435-436) are therefore unreachable on the initially selected tab. The one-frame flash on a first tab visit is the same branch: displayCategories is still [] in the first body pass because .task runs after the first commit. The M3U screen already avoids this by seeding synchronously in .onAppear (M3UChannelsView.swift:141-149).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Key the recompute on the catalog phase instead of streamsLoaded alone, e.g. in each tab: `private var catalogPhase: Int { var h = Hasher(); h.combine(contentStore.activePlaylistId); h.combine(contentStore.vodCategories.count); h.combine(contentStore.streamsLoaded); return h.finalize() }` and `.task(id: catalogPhase) { await recomputeFilter() }` (O(1), replaces the streamsLoaded task). Phase 1 then shows category headers over the already implemented reserved rows, and phase 2 fills posters in place with no layout change.
2) Seed the unfiltered state before the first commit, like M3U: `.onAppear { if displayCategories.isEmpty, debouncedQuery.isEmpty, playlist.id == contentStore.activePlaylistId { displayCategories = visibleCategories; displayItemsByCategory = contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId } }` (dictionary/array copies are COW, no catalog copy).
3) Only show the empty state when it is true: `contentStore.streamsLoaded && contentStore.vodCategories.isEmpty` or an active query with no hit; otherwise keep the spinner.
Does not touch the Equatable rows, the off-main filter or pagination.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism checked in code. `displayCategories` is @State and only `recomputeFilter()` fills it (Views/VODView.swift:166-177, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:278-293, Views/SeriesView.swift:220-231). It runs only from `.task(id:)` keyed on `debouncedQuery`, `contentStore.streamsLoaded` and the hidden-id set (VODView.swift:157-159, LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, SeriesView.swift:158-160). `loadPlaylist` publishes the categories, assigns `streamsLoaded = false` (already false) and `isLoading = false` (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:132-137), so none of the three ids changes at phase 1. Body then has `displayCategories.isEmpty`, `isLoading == false`, matching playlist id and no error, and falls into the last branch: the `live.empty.no_category` empty state (VODView.swift:52-60, LiveStreamsView.swift:79-87, SeriesView.swift:52-60). It stays until `streamsLoaded = true` (:152). The reserved-height rows (VODView.swift:434-436, LiveStreamsView.swift:372-374, SeriesView.swift:410-412) have existed since the first native commit (fe55017), as has the comment 'UI kategorilerle hemen gösterilir', so phase-1 display was intended and never wired up. SearchView already guards the same window on purpose (Views/SearchView.swift:225-227), which supports reading this as an oversight. What I could not settle from code: the claim assumes the tab's first `recomputeFilter()` runs before phase 1 finishes. The tab tasks and DashboardView's `.task` (Views/DashboardView.swift:131-132) are created in the same appear pass, and phase 1 needs two database round trips back to the main actor, so the tab tasks should win, but that is a scheduling argument, not a measurement. The duration of the window (phase 2: three full-table reads plus `Dictionary(grouping:)`, PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-151) is also unmeasured; the demo data hides it. The one-frame flash on a first visit to another tab follows from the same branch (first body pass has `displayCategories == []`, `.task` runs after the first commit). The fix needs three corrections, below.

**Corrected claim:** On entering a playlist the selected home tab shows the 'No category found' empty state from the end of catalog phase 1 (categories) until phase 2 (streams) completes, because nothing re-runs `recomputeFilter()` when the categories land; the reserved-height loading rows built for this window are not reached during the initial load. On the first visit to each other tab the same empty state is drawn for the first body pass. How long the launch window lasts on a real catalog has to be measured.

**Corrected fix:** 1) Trigger: the proposed hash of (activePlaylistId, categories.count, streamsLoaded) fixes phase 1 but still misses reloads that keep the count. The scoped pull-to-refresh (`reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:)`, PlaylistContentStore.swift:234-278) replaces categories and streams without touching `streamsLoaded`, so today the shelves keep showing the pre-refresh copy until a search or a tab re-mount. Use one counter instead: `@Published private(set) var catalogRevision = 0` in PlaylistContentStore, incremented once after each batch of list assignments (phase 1, phase 2, `reloadFromDatabase`, the scoped reload, `clearLists`), and `.task(id: contentStore.catalogRevision) { await recomputeFilter() }` in the three tabs in place of the `streamsLoaded` task. The category and All wrappers (VODView.swift:575, :834 and the Series/Live equivalents) should use the same id. Do not bump it in `applyVODMetadata`. 2) Seed before the first commit: `visibleCategories` does not exist in these views. Write it out: `.onAppear { guard displayCategories.isEmpty, debouncedQuery.isEmpty, playlist.id == contentStore.activePlaylistId else { return }; let hidden = hiddenStore.hiddenIds(playlistId: playlist.id, type: "vod"); displayCategories = contentStore.vodCategories.filter { !hidden.contains($0.id) }; displayItemsByCategory = contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId }`. In LiveStreamsView also reset `playbackModelMemo.model = nil` as `recomputeFilter` does (:292). 3) Empty state only when true: show the spinner branch while `!contentStore.streamsLoaded && contentStore.vodCategories.isEmpty`; show 'no category' only when `streamsLoaded` and the store's category list is empty, or a query has no hit. Leaves the Equatable rows, off-main search filter and pagination as they are.

**API check:** SwiftUI swiftinterface line 5166: `@inlinable nonisolated public func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) -> some View where T: Equatable`, in an extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, ...). SwiftUICore line 11055: `func onAppear(perform action: (() -> Void)? = nil) -> some View`, iOS 13. Both found. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Phase 1 now renders category headers over reserved rows, and phase 2 fills them. The VOD and Series reserved height equals the loaded shelf height (`shelfRowTotalHeight` in both branches), but the Live reserved height is `liveShelfIcon + 30` (LiveStreamsView.swift:374) while the loaded row has no fixed height (:382-397); check that the Live shelves do not shift when the channels arrive. 'Recently Added' and 'Continue Watching' are still inserted above the skeleton when phase 2 lands (see finding 4). `recomputeFilter` will run one extra time per load phase; in VOD/Series each run also starts the detached recents sort, so keep that guarded on `streamsLoaded`. A revision bump from `applyVODMetadata` would re-run every recompute on each detail visit and undo the Equatable-row work, so leave it out.

**How to verify:** Seed a large database (or add a DEBUG delay before PlaylistContentStore.swift:144) and run a UI test from playlist tap to first shelf: assert no static text with the `live.empty.no_category` string ever exists, and that category header texts exist before the first poster cell. Record the screen once without the fix to confirm the empty state really appears on the selected tab and for how long; that settles the task-ordering assumption. Unit test: `catalogRevision` changes at phase 1, at phase 2 and after a scoped reload. Separate check for the scoped-refresh observation: pull to refresh on Movies after the server catalog changed and confirm whether the shelves update without leaving the tab.

## transitions-motion-3 — Category, 'All' and Recently Added grids are pushed in showing their empty state ('No movie' / 'No channel') and the grid pops in afterwards

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Series category detail, All Series, Live category detail, All Channels
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:556-589, 616-624, 653-668, 675-687, 737-739, 815-854`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:528-561, 584-588, 615-627, 634-646, 678-680, 754-791`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:469-523, 547-549, 567-577, 584-596, 629-631, 697-752`

**What the user perceives:** Opening a category: the incoming page carries the grey film icon with 'No movie' (or the magnifier with 'No channel') while it slides in, then the poster grid replaces it. With a small category it is a flicker at the leading edge of the push; on 'All Movies' with a six-figure catalog the empty state is on screen for most of the push animation before the grid appears.

**Mechanism (finder):** Two chained asynchronous hops stand between the push and the first cell, and the default for both is 'empty'. Wrapper: @State displayItems = [] (VODView.swift:556) is filled by recomputeItems() from .task (:574-575), i.e. after the first commit. Content: VODCategoryContent has its own @State displayItems = [] (:616) that is filled only by recompute() through Task.detached (sort, file-type scan, queue map, :657-661) started from .task(id: itemsToken) (:737). Until that lands, body takes the `displayItems.isEmpty` branch (:677-686), which is the user-facing empty state, not a neutral 'not computed yet' state. AllVODView adds a detached hidden-category filter over the whole catalog in front (:846-851). Series and Live are structured identically (SeriesView.swift:636-645, LiveStreamsView.swift:586-595).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Separate 'not computed yet' from 'empty', and use the data that is already in memory for the first frame.
- Content views: `@State private var hasComputed = false`; set true at the end of recompute(). Render `let shown = hasComputed ? displayItems : (sortOption == .defaultOrder && fileTypeFilter.isEmpty ? items : [])`; when shown is empty and !hasComputed draw `Color.clear` (keeps the system background, no icon), and only show the empty state when hasComputed.
- Category wrappers: seed before the first commit, `.onAppear { if displayItems.isEmpty { displayItems = contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? [] } }` (O(1), copy-on-write). With default sort the grid is then in the very first frame of the push.
- All* wrappers cannot seed synchronously when hidden categories exist; they just get the neutral state until the detached filter returns.
Pagination, the off-main sort and the Equatable signature compare stay as they are (hasComputed is internal @State, so it does not go into ==). A tap in the first few milliseconds gets an empty play queue (single-film playback) until recompute sets streamQueue; acceptable, or pass `items.map(\.stream)` lazily at tap time.

**APIs:** View.onAppear(perform:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed in code. Wrapper: `@State displayItems = []` (Views/VODView.swift:556) is filled by `recomputeItems()` from `.task` (:574-575), i.e. after the first commit. Content: `VODCategoryContent` has its own `@State displayItems = []` (:616), filled only by `recompute()` through `Task.detached` (:653-668) from `.task(id: itemsToken)` (:737). Until both hops land, body takes `displayItems.isEmpty` (:677-686), which is the user-facing 'No movie' state. `AllVODView` puts a detached filter over the whole catalog in front (:838-854), and the content then maps the full result to a play queue (:660). Live and Series are built the same way (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:469, :547, :567-577, :586-595, :738-752; Views/SeriesView.swift:528, :584-588, :615-627, :636-645). The comments next to this code explain the off-main work and pagination as deliberate (VODView.swift:596-599, :614-626, :843-845); none of them explains using the empty state as the 'not computed yet' state. Two corrections. Scope: for a normal category the empty state lasts two to three frames at the very start of the push, when the incoming page has barely moved, so I rate that part low; the All screens on a six-figure catalog are where it is clearly visible, and how long is unmeasured. Fix: the proposed `hasComputed` flag inside the content view does not cover the All screens. The content's `.task(id: itemsToken)` runs on mount with `items == []`, sets `hasComputed = true`, and the empty state is back on screen while the wrapper's detached filter is still running.

**Corrected claim:** Category, All and Recently Added grids render their empty state until two chained asynchronous steps finish. For an ordinary category this is a flicker in the first frames of the push; on All Movies / All Series / All Channels with a large catalog the 'No movie' / 'No channel' state stays visible for a noticeable part of the push before the grid appears.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the off-main sort, the pagination and the cheap `==`. (a) Category wrappers: seed synchronously, `.onAppear { if displayItems.isEmpty, playlist.id == contentStore.activePlaylistId { displayItems = contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? [] } }` (O(1), copy-on-write). (b) Content views: add `var isResolving: Bool = false` as an input, include it in `==`, and pass `true` from the All wrappers until their first detached result is assigned (a wrapper-level `@State private var hasResult = false`). Inside, keep `@State private var hasComputed = false`, set at the end of `recompute()` only when `!isResolving`. Render `let shown = hasComputed ? displayItems : (sortOption == .defaultOrder && fileTypeFilter.isEmpty ? items : [])`; when `shown` is empty and (`isResolving` or `!hasComputed`) draw `Color.clear`; show the empty state only when computed and not resolving. Use `shown` for the ForEach, and guard `loadMore()` on `shown.count`. (c) Until `streamQueue` is set, pass `shown.map(\.stream)` only when the list is small, or accept single-item playback for a tap in the first milliseconds. (d) While there, add `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` after the detached call in LiveStreamsView.swift:571-574 and SeriesView.swift:619-623; VOD already has it (:662). No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** SwiftUICore swiftinterface line 11055: `@inlinable nonisolated public func onAppear(perform action: (() -> Swift.Void)? = nil) -> some View`, in an extension available from iOS 13.0. Found. Nothing else from the SDK is needed.

**Regression risks:** `isResolving` must be part of the Equatable signature or the content view will not re-render when it flips. Rendering `items` directly before the first compute means the first 90 cells are built once from `items` and again from `displayItems`; with default sort the ids and order are identical so SwiftUI keeps the cells, but with a persisted non-default sort (`@AppStorage`, VODView.swift:610) the seed path must stay empty, as written. The seeded wrapper state must still be replaced by `recomputeItems()` when a search is active.

**How to verify:** UI test: tap a category header and assert the `vod.empty.no_movie` / `series.empty.no_series` / `list.no_channel` text never exists while the first grid cell appears. Repeat for All Movies with a large seeded catalog and with hidden categories set, and once with a non-default sort stored. Measure with a 120 Hz screen recording how many frames the empty state is visible today on All Movies; that number decides whether the category-detail part is worth more than the seed line.
