## transitions-motion-4 — Home shelves are shoved down after first paint: 'Continue Watching' and 'Recently Added' are inserted above them late, and again after every search cancel

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, Live TV home, M3U channels
- Code: `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:21-28`, `Models/Requests.swift:399-425`, `Views/VODView.swift:65-80, 175-194`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:66-81, 229-248`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:213-224`

**What the user perceives:** The first category shelf is drawn at the top, then jumps down by about 200 pt when the Continue Watching row appears, and on Movies/Series jumps a second time by a full shelf height when Recently Added arrives 100-300 ms later on a big catalog. Cancelling a search repeats the second jump every time.

**Mechanism (finder):** ContinueWatchingRow renders nothing while historyItems is empty (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:28). Its @Query uses GRDB's default scheduler for publishers, .async(onQueue: .main) (Requests.swift:420; GRDB ValueObservation.swift:487), so the first value arrives after the first frame and the row is inserted above the LazyVStack. Recently Added: recomputeFilter assigns displayCategories and displayItemsByCategory first (VODView.swift:176-177) and only then awaits a detached filter + sort of the whole catalog (:180-191); the shelf (:78-80) is inserted when that returns. With a query active recentlyAddedVODs is cleared (:194), so every return to the unfiltered list re-sorts the catalog and re-inserts the shelf. There is also no Task.isCancelled check after that await, so a cancelled run can put the shelf back above search results.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Continue Watching in the first frame: give RecentWatchHistoryRequest an opt-in immediate first value (see the @Query finding for the request change) and use it in ContinueWatchingRow (limit 10, indexed on lastWatchedAt).
2) Recently Added in one layout pass: compute first, assign together, and memoise so search-cancel is free:
`if q.isEmpty { let recents = await recentlyAdded(visible: visibleCatIds)   // cached on (vodStreams.count, hidden set)
  guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
  displayCategories = allCats; displayItemsByCategory = allByCategory; recentlyAddedVODs = recents; return }`
The short wait on the very first load is covered by the phase-1 skeleton from the launch finding. Same change in SeriesView.swift:229-246.

**APIs:** GRDB ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with .immediate (GRDB checkout in SourcePackages (ValueObservation.swift:485-487, ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148); not an Apple SDK API)

**Verifier reasons:** `ContinueWatchingRow` renders nothing while `historyItems` is empty (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:28) and its request uses `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)` (Models/Requests.swift:420), whose default in the GRDB checkout (v7.10.0) is `scheduling: .async(onQueue: .main)` (GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485-487). The row is only mounted in the content branch (Views/VODView.swift:65, SeriesView.swift:66, LiveStreamsView.swift:213, M3UChannelsView.swift:157), so its first value always arrives after the shelves' first frame and it is inserted above the LazyVStack. Recently Added: `recomputeFilter` assigns `displayCategories` and `displayItemsByCategory` (VODView.swift:176-177) and only then awaits a detached filter, timestamp parse and full sort of the catalog (:180-191); the shelf (:78-80) is inserted when that returns. With a query active the list is cleared (:194), so every return to the unfiltered list repeats the sort and the insertion. `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` (:160) makes both insertions hard jumps. There is no `Task.isCancelled` check after the await at :180-191, unlike the search path at :212, so a superseded run can assign the shelf after a newer run has cleared it. Series is identical (SeriesView.swift:229-248). I found no comment or commit that presents this ordering as deliberate. Scope note: the Continue Watching jump happens once per mount of the content branch (first display of a tab, or after an empty search result), not on every search cancel; the repeated jump is the Recently Added shelf. How large the delay is on a real catalog is unmeasured.

**Corrected claim:** The home shelves move down after first paint: the Continue Watching row is inserted one frame late on each mount of the content branch, and on Movies and Series the Recently Added shelf is inserted after an off-main sort of the whole catalog, on first load and again after every search cancel. A superseded recompute can also put Recently Added back above search results.

**Corrected fix:** 1) Recently Added in one layout pass, as proposed: for an empty query compute the recents first, `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }`, then assign `displayCategories`, `displayItemsByCategory` and `recentlyAddedVODs` together. Memoise the recents on the catalog revision (or `vodStreams.count`) plus the hidden set so a search cancel is free. Skip the sort while `!contentStore.streamsLoaded`. Same in SeriesView.swift:229-246. 2) Continue Watching in the first frame, two options. (a) As proposed: an opt-in `immediate` flag on `RecentWatchHistoryRequest` that passes `scheduling: .immediate`, used only by ContinueWatchingRow (limit 10, `index_watchHistory_lastWatchedAt` exists, Database/AppDatabase.swift:173). This is a synchronous read on the main thread; see the risks. (b) No synchronous read: hoist the `@Query` into the home view so the subscription starts while the spinner is still showing and pass the items down; the shelf rows are Equatable so the extra parent updates are cheap. 3) If the phase-1 skeleton from finding 2 is adopted, Recently Added and Continue Watching will still be inserted above the skeleton when the streams land; assign them in the same pass as the phase-2 items so it is one layout change that coincides with the posters filling in.

**API check:** Not Apple SDK API. GRDB checkout: `public func publisher(in reader: any DatabaseReader, scheduling scheduler: some ValueObservationScheduler = .async(onQueue: .main)) -> DatabasePublishers.Value<Reducer.Value>` (ValueObservation.swift:485-487). `.immediate` is `ImmediateValueObservationScheduler` (ValueObservationScheduler.swift:109-150); it raises a fatal error if the observation is not started on the main thread. GRDBQuery 0.11.0 subscribes inside `Tracker.update` and handles a value delivered synchronously during the view update (Sources/GRDBQuery/Query.swift:251-309); its own docs use `scheduling: .immediate` (Documentation.docc/Extensions/Queryable.md:29).

**Regression risks:** Option 2a reads on the main thread during a view update. The app uses a `DatabasePool` with the default five readers (Database/Persistence.swift:54; GRDB Configuration.swift:360), and catalog phase 2 holds three of them for its whole duration (PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-142), which is exactly when this row would mount if the skeleton fix lands. If the pool is exhausted the main thread waits. In the in-memory fallback (`DatabaseQueue`, Persistence.swift:82) a synchronous read waits behind a running catalog write. Computing recents before assigning the categories delays the first shelf paint by the sort time on the first load only; the memo removes it afterwards. Keep `.removeDuplicates()` on the request (Requests.swift:425).

**How to verify:** UI test with watch history and a large seeded catalog: read the frame of the first category header as soon as it exists and again after 1 s; they must be equal. Repeat after typing a query and cancelling search. Type a query while the first recents sort is still running and assert the Recently Added title does not exist above the results. Unit test for the memoised recents helper. With option 2a, check Instruments (Hangs) during launch on a large catalog for main-thread waits in the row's read.

## transitions-motion-5 — Every @Query delivers its first value one frame late, so screens open in their default state: outlined star, 'Watch now', and the empty state on Favorites, History and Downloads

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Favorites, Watch history, Downloads
- Code: `Models/Requests.swift:210-228, 269-290, 292-317, 375-397, 399-425`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:20-31, 86-91, 132-141`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:809-821, 884-885, 967-976, 1007-1013`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:215-239`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:126-130, 152-156`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:51-57`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:68-75`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:58, 283-297`

**What the user perceives:** During the push into a favourited, half-watched film the star is drawn empty and turns yellow a moment later; the big button says 'Watch now', then changes to 'Resume 12:34' and grows by a progress bar, moving the Download button and plot. Favorites, Watch history and Downloads open with 'no favourites' / 'no history' / 'no downloads' for a frame before their content appears. On a series the season bar and the episode list arrive in two further steps.

**Mechanism (finder):** All requests build their publisher with `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)` (e.g. Requests.swift:286, :389, :420), which in GRDB defaults to scheduling: .async(onQueue: .main). GRDBQuery therefore renders the first body with Queryable.defaultValue (false / nil / []) and the real value arrives after the first commit. The views treat the default as a real state: star image (MovieDetailView.swift:88-89), CTA title/subtitle/progress (:133-136, DetailComponents.swift:234-239 adds a ProgressView row), `displayedVODs.isEmpty` -> emptyState (FavoritesView.swift:128-129), `items.isEmpty` -> ContentUnavailableView (WatchHistoryListView.swift:52-57, DownloadsView.swift:70-75).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Opt-in synchronous first value for screen-level queries (one small indexed read at subscription, on the main actor, which is where GRDBQuery subscribes):
`struct IsFavoriteRequest: Queryable, Equatable { ...; var immediate = false
  func publisher(in db: AppDatabase) -> AnyPublisher<Bool, Never> {
    let obs = ValueObservation.tracking { ... }
    let p = immediate ? obs.publisher(in: db.reader, scheduling: .immediate).eraseToAnyPublisher()
                      : obs.publisher(in: db.reader).eraseToAnyPublisher()
    return p.catch { _ in Just(false) }.eraseToAnyPublisher() } }`
Set immediate: true only at MovieDetailView.swift:29-30, SeriesView.swift:818-820, ContinueWatchingRow.swift:22, FavoritesView.swift:21-23, WatchHistoryListView.swift:27, DownloadsView.swift:24. Leave the per-row queries asynchronous (EpisodeDetailRow at SeriesView.swift:1379, DownloadButton.swift:58): a synchronous read per scrolling row would be wrong; those should get their value from one per-season map handed down by EpisodesPanel, the pattern already used for WatchProgressMapRequest (VODView.swift:497, :608). Default behaviour of every other call site is unchanged.

**APIs:** GRDB ValueObservationScheduler.immediate (GRDB checkout in SourcePackages (ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148, requires start on the main actor); not an Apple SDK API); GRDBQuery @Query / Queryable (GRDBQuery checkout (Query.swift:250-300 subscribes in update and handles synchronous delivery))

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is as described. Every request builds its publisher with `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)` (Models/Requests.swift:204, :224, :261, :286, :313, :389, :420), and GRDB's default for publishers is `.async(onQueue: .main)` (GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487). GRDBQuery therefore renders the first body with `defaultValue` and the real value arrives after the first commit. The views treat the default as real state: star (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:88-89, Views/SeriesView.swift:884-885), CTA title, subtitle and progress row (MovieDetailView.swift:133-136, Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:234-239), and the empty states (Views/FavoritesView.swift:103-104, :128-129, :154-155; Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:52-57; Views/DownloadsView.swift:70-75). The fix's API exists and GRDBQuery supports it. Where I disagree is perception and severity. All five surfaces are entered by a push or a sheet. The wrong state is on screen for the first frame or two of that transition, when the incoming page has barely started to move, and is then replaced. I do not think a user sees the star or the 'no favourites' text in that window on an idle device; only a frame-stepped recording can say. It becomes visible when the main thread or the reader pool is busy. The series season bar and episode list arriving in further steps is real (SeriesView.swift:1030-1040, :1053) but lands below the fold on iPhone. The evidence is code only and the user-visible effect is unproven, so I do not confirm at medium.

**Corrected claim:** Every @Query delivers its first value after the first commit, so detail, Favorites, Watch history and Downloads render one or two frames in their default state at the start of the push or sheet presentation. Mechanically true; whether it is visible in normal use is unproven and is most likely limited to moments when the main thread or the database readers are busy.

**Corrected fix:** The opt-in `immediate` flag is sound and is what GRDBQuery's documentation recommends. Narrow it to where it changes layout or behaviour: `IsFavoriteRequest` and `WatchHistoryRequest` / `LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest` on the two detail screens, and `VODByIDRequest` / `SeriesByIDRequest`. The by-id requests are the most useful: with the record available in the first body pass, the `.task` guard (`!currentSeries.seasonsLoaded`, SeriesView.swift:892-895) reads the stored flag instead of the stale in-memory copy. There is no series counterpart to `applyVODMetadata`, so a series opened twice in one session may refetch `get_series_info`; that depends on task ordering and should be checked in a run. Favorites, Watch history (limit 500, WatchHistoryListView.swift:27) and Downloads can stay asynchronous; if their first-frame empty state turns out to be visible, render nothing until the first value instead of adding synchronous reads of whole lists. Keep per-row queries asynchronous, as the finding says. Keep `.removeDuplicates()` where it is (Requests.swift:393, :425).

**API check:** Not Apple SDK API. GRDB v7.10.0 checkout: `publisher(in reader: any DatabaseReader, scheduling scheduler: some ValueObservationScheduler = .async(onQueue: .main))` (ValueObservation.swift:485-487); `static var immediate: ImmediateValueObservationScheduler` (ValueObservationScheduler.swift:124-150), precondition: started on the main thread. Both scheduler choices return the same `DatabasePublishers.Value<T>` type, so the proposed ternary compiles. GRDBQuery 0.11.0: `Tracker.update` subscribes during the dynamic-property update and suppresses `objectWillChange` for values delivered synchronously (Query.swift:290-309), so the first body sees the fetched value.

**Regression risks:** Each immediate query is a synchronous read on the main thread during a view update. With the `DatabasePool` (five readers by default, Database/Persistence.swift:54) it waits if all readers are taken; catalog phase 2 holds three for its whole duration (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-142). In the in-memory fallback (`DatabaseQueue`, Persistence.swift:82) it waits behind any running write, including a full catalog sync. A detail screen with four or five immediate queries performs them one after another before its first frame. Calling an immediate publisher off the main thread is a fatal error, which matters for unit tests of the requests.

**How to verify:** Record at 120 Hz the push into a favourited, half-watched film and into Favorites with content, on a device with a large catalog, and frame-step: count the frames in which the outlined star, 'Watch now' or the empty state are visible and how far the page has slid in by then. If it is one frame at the edge, leave the lists alone. For the series refetch: log `get_series_info` calls and open the same series twice in one session. After the change: unit test that the first value arrives synchronously inside `sink` when `immediate` is true, and Instruments (Hangs) on a push during catalog load to confirm no main-thread wait.

## transitions-motion-6 — The detail hero re-decodes a poster that is already on screen, and the backdrop goes blurred poster -> grey placeholder -> real backdrop in hard cuts

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:26-32, 46-73, 101-110`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:62-93, 102-136`, `Views/VODView.swift:503-510`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:475-482`

**What the user perceives:** The poster the user just tapped is missing on the detail page for the first frames (grey tile, then a 0.12 s fade), and the 380 pt area behind it is empty, then a blurred poster cuts in. When the metadata request returns, the blurred image is replaced by a flat grey rectangle with a film icon and after that the real backdrop appears with no fade. It reads as three separate flashes at the top of the screen (M07-movie-detail.png shows the settled blurred-fallback state).

**Mechanism (finder):** Nuke's memory-cache key contains the Resize processor (CachedImage.swift:111-121). The shelf/grid card requests shelfPosterWidth x shelfPosterHeight, .fill (VODView.swift:503-510); the hero poster requests seriesDetailHeroWidth x seriesDetailHeroHeight (DetailComponents.swift:103-110) and the fallback backdrop requests full width x 380 at up to 3x with profile .high (:51-59). Both are cache misses for an image that is decoded in memory, so they go back to URLCache/disk and decode again during the push. Profile .high gets `t.animation = nil` (CachedImage.swift:87-93), so the large image cuts in. When metadata sets backdropPath, the same CachedImage gets a new URL; LazyImage's onChange calls FetchImage.load, whose reset() clears imageContainer (NukeUI FetchImage.swift:239-248), so the placeholder (CachedImage.swift:138-147) is drawn between the two images, now without the blur because backdropIsFallback flipped (:61-62).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Reuse the cached bitmap for the hero poster: add `var requestSize: CGSize? = nil` to CachedImage and build the ImageRequest from it when set; in DetailHero pass `requestSize: CGSize(width: metrics.shelfPosterWidth, height: metrics.shelfPosterHeight)` with `loadProfile: .shelf`. shelfPoster* equals categoryGridPoster* (PosterMetrics.swift:16-20) and .shelf/.grid/.standard share the 2x pixel size, so shelves, grids and Favorites all hit synchronously (FetchImage.load checks `pipeline.cache[request]` first) and the poster is in the first frame. Entry from search rows is a miss and loads as today.
2) Build the backdrop as two layers instead of one URL that changes: bottom = the same shelf-keyed poster, blurred (it is blurred at radius 28 anyway, so the full-width 3x decode is wasted work); top = the real backdrop only when backdropURL != nil, loaded with Nuke's own transaction so only a network/disk arrival fades and a memory hit stays instant:
`LazyImage(request: req, transaction: Transaction(animation: .easeOut(duration: 0.3))) { state in if let image = state.image { image.resizable().aspectRatio(contentMode: .fill).transition(.opacity) } }`
The blurred layer stays underneath, so there is never a placeholder between the two. The comment at CachedImage.swift:65 warns about custom LazyImage transactions in lists; this is one image per screen, check the console once.
Grid and shelf profiles are untouched.

**APIs:** NukeUI LazyImage.init(request:transaction:content:) (Nuke checkout in SourcePackages (LazyImage.swift:83-91; FetchImage.swift:36 'Animation isn't used when the image is available in the memory cache'); not an Apple SDK API); AnyTransition/Transition .opacity (iOS 13.0 / iOS 17.0 (Transition protocol))

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:26-73,101-122, Views/CachedImage.swift:62-136, Views/VODView.swift:490-545, Views/PosterMetrics.swift:16-35, Views/MovieDetailView.swift:58-104, Views/SeriesView.swift:823-897, NukeUI FetchImage.swift (load/reset) and LazyImage.swift, Nuke Internal/ImageRequestKeys.swift:8-31.

What holds:
- The memory-cache key includes the processor list (ImageRequestKeys.swift:13,30) and Resize's identifier includes the pixel size, so the hero poster (seriesDetailHeroWidth x Height = scaled 118x176, DetailComponents.swift:103-110) and the fallback backdrop (full width x 380, .high, :51-59) are both misses for a poster already decoded at the shelf size (scaled 200x300, VODView.swift:503-510). The pipeline has no dataCache (CachedImage.swift:31-37), so a miss goes back to URLCache/network plus a new decode.
- The hero poster uses the default .standard profile, and CachedImage.swift:87-93 forces easeIn 0.12 s on every change in that subtree, so it fades in even when it would be a memory hit. .high gets animation nil, so the backdrop cuts in.
- A request change on a live LazyImage calls FetchImage.load, whose reset() sets imageContainer = nil, so the placeholder (CachedImage.swift:138-147) is drawn in between, unblurred because backdropIsFallback flips at the same time (DetailComponents.swift:61-62).

What needs correcting (mechanism): on a first visit the hero does not survive the metadata arrival. Both detail views replace the whole ScrollView with a full-screen ProgressView as soon as .task sets isLoading (MovieDetailView.swift:74-76 and 99-103; SeriesView.swift:868-870 and 892-896). The real first-visit sequence is: hero with blurred fallback or its placeholder for a frame or two, then spinner, then a brand-new hero whose LazyImage starts on the backdrop URL (grey placeholder with icon), then a hard cut to the backdrop. The described same-CachedImage URL swap only happens where the hero survives: series revisits (PlaylistContentStore has applyVODMetadata at :164 but no series equivalent, so the passed `series` is stale and the @Query row arrives after frame 0), and everywhere once the spinner swap is removed. On a movie revisit backdropPath is already in the catalog copy, so there is no blurred fallback at all, only placeholder then cut.

The perception (poster missing in the first frames, grey placeholder before the backdrop, no fade) is real on all paths. M07-movie-detail.png shows only the settled fallback state; the demo data cannot show the timing. No comment or history marks any of this as deliberate.

**Corrected claim:** The detail hero requests the tapped poster at two new sizes (hero tile and full-width .high fallback backdrop), so neither hits the memory cache: the poster tile starts as a grey placeholder and fades in over 0.12 s. The real backdrop always appears after an unblurred grey placeholder and with a hard cut. On a first visit this is preceded by the full-screen spinner swap, which destroys and rebuilds the hero; the same-view URL swap (FetchImage.reset) is the mechanism only on series revisits and once the spinner swap is gone.

**Corrected fix:** Keep both parts, with these adjustments.
1) Add `requestSize: CGSize? = nil` to CachedImage and build the ImageRequest from it when set. In DetailHero pass the shelf size (metrics.shelfPosterWidth x shelfPosterHeight) and `loadProfile: .shelf`. The .shelf profile is required, not optional: .standard would still fade a memory hit over 0.12 s (CachedImage.swift:88-89) and cancels on disappear.
2) Backdrop as two layers. Bottom: the same shelf-keyed poster, blurred, at 0.55 opacity. Top: only when backdropURL != nil, a direct NukeUI LazyImage built with CachedImage.request(..., loadProfile: .high), `transaction: Transaction(animation: .easeOut(duration: 0.3))`, content showing only state.image with .transition(.opacity). DetailComponents.swift then needs `import NukeUI`. Keep the visualEffect parallax on the container so both layers move together.
3) Sequence it with the finding that removes the full-screen spinner swap. Without that, the first visit still replaces the hero with a spinner and only revisits benefit.
Shelf and grid profiles, prefetch keys and CachedImage.swift:87-93 stay untouched.

**API check:** NukeUI (checkout 13.0.1, not an Apple SDK): `public init(request: ImageRequest?, transaction: Transaction = Transaction(animation: nil), @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (LazyImageState) -> Content)` at Sources/NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:78-87. FetchImage.load does the synchronous `pipeline.cache[request]` lookup and calls handle(result:) outside withTransaction for memory hits; network/disk completions run inside `withTransaction(self.transaction)`, so only real arrivals fade. `CachedImage.request(url:width:height:contentMode:loadProfile:)` already exists as a static (CachedImage.swift:102-123). AnyTransition.opacity is iOS 13. No iOS 26-only API involved.

**Regression risks:** - The blurred poster layer stays composited under an opaque backdrop while the parallax effect moves it. Cheap, but check scrolling the detail on an older device; it can be dropped via LazyImage.onCompletion if it costs frames.
- CachedImage.swift:65 warns that a custom LazyImage transaction caused 'multiple LazyImageContext updates per frame' console warnings in lists. This is one image per screen, but check the console once.
- Entries whose source artwork used another size (search rows, Continue Watching) stay a miss and load as today, at a slightly larger decode than the hero tile needs.
- Behaviour change, for the better: a dead backdrop URL (common on IPTV panels) now leaves the blurred poster instead of a permanent grey placeholder.
- Does not touch the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Unit test: the request built for the hero poster with requestSize has the same imageID and processors as the one VODStreamCard/SeriesCard builds, and ImagePipeline.shared.cache[request] is non-nil after the shelf has rendered. Simulator with a throttled network (Network Link Conditioner), screen recording stepped frame by frame: push a movie and a series from a shelf, a grid and Favorites; the poster must be present in the first frame of the push and there must be no grey rectangle between the blurred poster and the backdrop. Repeat on a revisit and with a backdrop URL that 404s.

## transitions-motion-7 — Poster to detail is a plain push; the iOS 18 zoom navigation transition fits the shelf and grid structure but should only be enabled after the detail's first frame is stable

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, Movies category detail, Series category detail, All Movies, All Series, Favorites, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:333-345, 450-462, 502-526, 691-704`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:310-322, 422-434, 474-498, 649-659`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:133-144, 159-170`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:63-70`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Adopt zoom for artwork navigation or keep the standard push. Zoom adds a system pull-down / pinch dismiss on the detail page, which takes over the pull at the top of the scroll view, so the hero's overscroll stretch (DetailComponents.swift:63-70) would mostly stop being reachable.

**What the user perceives:** Tapping artwork slides a new page in from the right, as for any list row. In TV, Photos and the App Store on iOS 18/26 artwork grows into its page and the page shrinks back into the artwork on dismiss, including an interactive pull-down.

**Mechanism (finder):** All poster links are closure-based NavigationLinks inside LazyHStack / LazyVGrid cells (VODView.swift:451-462, :692-704; SeriesView.swift:423-434, :650-659) with no navigationTransition, so the stack uses the default push.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Deployment target is 18.0, so no availability check is needed.
Where things go: one `@Namespace private var posterZoom` per container view that builds both the label and the destination: VODCategoryShelfRow, RecentlyAddedVODShelf, VODCategoryContent, SeriesCategoryShelfRow, RecentlyAddedSeriesShelf, SeriesCategoryContent, FavoritesView. A namespace per shelf keeps a film that is in 'Recently Added' and in its category shelf unambiguous; @Namespace is view state, so the Equatable shelf rows are unaffected.
`NavigationLink {
  MovieDetailView(playlist: playlist, movie: item.stream, queue: queue)
    .navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID: item.stream.streamId, in: posterZoom))
} label: {
  VODStreamCard(..., zoomSource: (item.stream.streamId, posterZoom))
}`
and inside the card, on the poster ZStack only (VODView.swift:502-526), not on the title text: `.matchedTransitionSource(id: id, in: ns) { $0.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)) }` (8 = CachedImage's default radius). Search result rows (44 pt thumbnails) and the programmatic navigationDestination(item:) entries keep the standard push.
Lazy cells on pop: the tapped cell cannot scroll away while it is covered, and neither applyVODMetadata nor the detail's own queries re-run the home/grid recompute tasks, so the source normally still exists. If it does not (rotation re-layout, a refresh that rebuilt the grid, memory pressure), there is no matched source and the system dismisses without a target frame instead of failing; that path must be looked at on the simulator rather than assumed.
Preconditions: the two detail findings above (no spinner swap, poster present in the first frame), otherwise the zoom lands on a blank page. Reduce Motion is handled by the system. If navigation is later moved to value-based links, hoist one namespace per tab into the environment and use (shelfID, streamID) as the source id.

**APIs:** View.navigationTransition(_:) (iOS 18.0); NavigationTransition.zoom(sourceID:in:) (iOS 18.0 (unavailable on macOS)); View.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:configuration:) (iOS 18.0; configuration supports clipShape(RoundedRectangle) only)

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/VODView.swift:331-349,444-466,490-545,688-709, Views/SeriesView.swift:647-661, Views/FavoritesView.swift:131-175, Views/MovieDetailView.swift:72-104, Views/SeriesView.swift:866-897, Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:63-70.

What holds: every poster link is a closure-based NavigationLink in a LazyHStack/LazyVGrid cell with no navigationTransition, so the push is the default one. The three zoom APIs exist at iOS 18.0, so no availability check is needed. The compile shape is right (closure destination plus a source on the label), and an @Namespace on the Equatable shelf rows is harmless.

Why it is not a defect:
- A plain push is itself system-standard for catalog browsing. To my knowledge Apple's TV and Music apps and App Store list rows push product pages; zoom is what Photos and card-style content use. I cannot check Apple's apps from this environment, so treat the 'TV does this' premise as unverified. This is an optional enhancement and a product decision, which the finding's own decision_needed admits.

Risks the finding understates:
1) Both detail views swap to a full-screen ProgressView right after appearing on a first visit (MovieDetailView.swift:74-76, SeriesView.swift:868-870). The zoom would land on a spinner. The finding lists this as a precondition; it is a hard blocker.
2) The claim that the source cell normally still exists is not established for paginated grids. VODCategoryContent, SeriesCategoryContent and LiveCategoryContent run three `.task(id:)` (VODView.swift:737-739, SeriesView.swift:678-680). `.task` restarts when the covered screen reappears on pop, and recompute unconditionally sets visibleCount back to one page of 90 (VODView.swift:666, SeriesView.swift:625). A source beyond item 90 can therefore vanish during the zoom-out. I could not run this; it must be checked.
3) From Favorites, un-starring inside the detail removes the source cell through the favorites query (FavoritesView.swift:133-144, 159-170).
4) The zoom's pull-down dismiss competes with the hero's overscroll stretch (DetailComponents.swift:63-70), as the finding says.

No card has a context menu today (the only .contextMenu is in DownloadButton), so there is no conflict there.

**Corrected claim:** Poster to detail uses the standard push, which is itself system-standard for catalog apps. The iOS 18 zoom navigation transition is available and structurally possible here, but it is an optional enhancement and a product decision, not a native-feel defect. It is blocked by the detail spinner swap and by the unverified page reset of the paginated grids on reappear.

**Corrected fix:** Do not schedule this as a fix. If the owner wants zoom:
- First land the detail first-frame work (no spinner swap, poster in the first frame) and make the grid recompute idempotent on reappear (skip it when sort, filter and the items token are unchanged, so visibleCount is not reset on pop).
- Trial it on one surface first, the Movies category grid (VODCategoryContent). Use one @Namespace in the container, `.navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID: item.stream.streamId, in: ns))` on the destination, and `.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:) { $0.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)) }` on the poster ZStack of VODStreamCard, passed through an optional parameter and a small ViewModifier.
- Check it on iOS 18.0 and 26.0 before rolling out to shelves, Series and Favorites.
- Decide at the same time whether to drop the hero overscroll stretch.
Search rows and the programmatic navigationDestination(item:) entries keep the push. Otherwise: none.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface (iOS 26.0 SDK):
- `@available(iOS 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 18.0, watchOS 11.0, visionOS 2.0, *) nonisolated public func navigationTransition(_ style: some NavigationTransition) -> some View` (line 8947).
- `@available(iOS 18.0, tvOS 18.0, watchOS 11.0, visionOS 2.0, *) @available(macOS, unavailable) public static func zoom(sourceID: some Hashable, in namespace: Namespace.ID) -> ZoomNavigationTransition` (line 8974).
- `@available(iOS 18.0, ...) nonisolated public func matchedTransitionSource(id: some Hashable, in namespace: Namespace.ID, configuration: (EmptyMatchedTransitionSourceConfiguration) -> some MatchedTransitionSourceConfiguration) -> some View` (line 14903).
- MatchedTransitionSourceConfiguration offers `clipShape(_ shape: RoundedRectangle)`, `shadow(color:radius:x:y:)` and `background(_ style: Color)`; the generic clipShape/background overloads are marked unavailable.
All three are usable at the 18.0 deployment target without #available.

**Regression risks:** - Zoom landing on the spinner or error page: S04-series-detail-settled.png shows the series detail replaced by a full-page error on the demo data.
- Source cell missing on pop: grid page reset on reappear, un-favoriting from Favorites, rotation re-layout, refresh.
- Loss of the hero overscroll stretch to the pull-down dismiss.
- Possible interaction with the large-title plus always-visible search drawer bars on the grid screens and with the docked mini player overlay.
- A source nested in LazyHStack inside LazyVStack inside `.equatable()` shelf rows is not a combination I could verify without a run.
- ScreensUITests navigation paths.
- Does not touch the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 18.0 and 26.0, iPhone and iPad, with a catalog larger than one grid page (>90 items):
- Push and pop from a shelf, from a grid cell beyond item 90, and from Favorites after un-starring in the detail.
- Interrupted and cancelled pull-down, edge-swipe and pinch dismissals.
- Pop after rotating on the detail; with the mini player docked; with Reduce Motion on.
- First visit to an item whose metadata is not loaded: the zoom must not land on a spinner.
- Separately, on today's build: scroll four pages into All Movies, open a movie, go back, and record whether the grid keeps its position. This settles the visibleCount reset question.

## transitions-motion-8 — Switching season empties the episode list to a spinner for at least a frame, which collapses the page height and can throw the scroll position upward

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:1268-1287, 1306-1317, 1345-1350`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:443-446`, `Models/Requests.swift:230-246`

**What the user perceives:** Tap another season while looking at episodes: the list disappears, a small spinner shows, the new episodes pop in. When the user was scrolled into the list, the page is momentarily too short for that offset, so the content jumps up and the new season starts somewhere else than where the user was looking.

**Mechanism (finder):** The season chip sets selectedId inside withAnimation(.spring) (DetailComponents.swift:444-446). EpisodesPanel.onChange(of: seasonId) calls observer.load (SeriesView.swift:1348-1350), which first publishes hasLoaded = false and episodes = [] (:1278-1279); body then replaces the LazyVStack of rows with a ProgressView of about 60 pt (:1308-1311). The new rows come back through the default asynchronous ValueObservation plus an extra .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main) hop (:1280-1282), so at least one frame with the collapsed height is committed, and they arrive outside any animation. The comment at :1268 documents an earlier scroll-reset fix (dropping .id(seasonId)); this is the remaining half of that problem. Exact size of the jump depends on offset and needs a run to measure.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the old rows until the new ones exist, and get the new ones in the same update:
- SeasonEpisodesObserver.load: do not reset `episodes` / `hasLoaded` when a season is already shown (reset only on the very first load); subscribe with an immediate first value and without the receive(on:) hop: `ValueObservation.tracking { ... }.publisher(in: db.reader, scheduling: .immediate)` (season episode lists are small and idx_episode_seasonId exists, AppDatabase.swift:345).
- Make the swap a cross-fade driven by the chip tap: `.onChange(of: seasonId) { _, id in withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.25)) { observer.load(seasonId: id, db: appDatabase) } }`; rows have per-season ids, so they get the default opacity transition, and the page height animates from one list height to the other instead of collapsing.

**APIs:** GRDB ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with .immediate (GRDB checkout in SourcePackages; not an Apple SDK API); Animation.smooth(duration:extraBounce:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/SeriesView.swift:1268-1351 and 1006-1067, Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:433-477, Models/Requests.swift:230-246, Database/Persistence.swift:54-55, Database/AppDatabase.swift:345 and 468.

Mechanism, verified in code:
- The chip tap sets selectedId inside withAnimation(.spring) (DetailComponents.swift:444-446).
- EpisodesPanel.onChange(of: seasonId) calls observer.load (SeriesView.swift:1348-1350).
- load publishes hasLoaded = false and episodes = [] (:1278-1279), and body replaces the LazyVStack with a ~60 pt ProgressView (:1308-1311).
- The new rows come back through GRDB's default `.async(onQueue: .main)` scheduling (Requests.swift:243) plus an extra `.receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)` hop (:1282). At least one layout pass with the collapsed content height is unavoidable.

History supports the claim. `git show 0ab5bcd` (the earlier bulk fix pass) added `hasLoaded = false` and `episodes = []` to load(), to stop the 'no episodes' text flashing during the first load. Before that commit a season switch kept the old rows until the new ones arrived. That is the design the comment at :1268 describes, and it is what the proposed fix restores. The reset on a season switch is a side effect of that commit, not a decision.

Perception: the season bar is not pinned, so the user taps it while it is on screen with episodes below. The collapsed page is shorter than the current offset for almost any bar position in the upper part of the screen, so the scroll view clamps and the new season then appears with the bar pushed down. The spinner itself may be shorter than one display frame on a fast read; the clamp is the lasting effect. Its exact size needs one simulator run, but the mechanism matches the scroll-reset symptom the :1268 comment already records.

Fix check: EpisodesRequest's only caller is this observer, the database is a DatabasePool (a main-thread read does not wait on writers), and idx_episode_seasonId exists.

**Corrected claim:** Switching season resets the episode list to an empty/loading state before the new rows arrive asynchronously. The page height collapses for at least one layout pass, which can clamp the scroll offset and briefly show a spinner. The reset was introduced by commit 0ab5bcd as a side effect of a first-load flicker fix; the original observer kept the old rows.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two precisions.
1) In SeasonEpisodesObserver.load, do not clear `episodes`/`hasLoaded` when a season is already shown; keep the hasLoaded gate only for the very first load, which preserves 0ab5bcd's intent. Deliver the first value synchronously: either give EpisodesRequest.publisher `scheduling: .immediate` (Models/Requests.swift:243, it has no other caller) or build the ValueObservation inline in the observer. Drop `.receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)`. load() must stay main-thread only: it is only called from onAppear/onChange today, and marking the class @MainActor makes that explicit.
2) Treat the cross-fade (`withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.25))` around load in onChange) as optional. Ship the synchronous swap first, then judge on the simulator whether animating rows inside the LazyVStack looks right. If the chip's spring leaks into the row swap, wrap the load in a non-animated transaction instead.

**API check:** GRDB (SourcePackages checkout, not an Apple SDK):
- `public func publisher(in reader: any DatabaseReader, scheduling scheduler: some ValueObservationScheduler = .async(onQueue: .main)) -> DatabasePublishers.Value<Reducer.Value>` at GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485-487.
- `public static var immediate: ImmediateValueObservationScheduler` at ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148. Its immediateInitialValue() has a GRDBPrecondition(Thread.isMainThread); later values are delivered with DispatchQueue.main.async.
SwiftUICore.swiftinterface: `@_alwaysEmitIntoClient public static func smooth(duration: Foundation.TimeInterval = 0.5, extraBounce: Swift.Double = 0.0) -> Animation` at line 13314, in an extension annotated iOS 13.0 and emitted into the client. Fine at the 18.0 target (the finding's 'iOS 17.0' is the documented availability).

**Regression risks:** - .immediate is a fatal error if load() is ever called off the main thread.
- The first fetch becomes a synchronous main-thread read. Negligible for one season with the index and a DatabasePool, but the in-memory DatabaseQueue fallback (Persistence.swift:82-96) would wait behind a running write.
- The 'no episodes in this season' text must still not flash on first load: keep hasLoaded for that case.
- If the animation is added, rows could slide oddly inside the LazyVStack.
- A shorter new season still clamps the scroll position legitimately.
- The onChange(of: observer.episodes) prefetch at SeriesView.swift:1335-1338 keeps working.

**How to verify:** Simulator, a series with two long seasons: scroll until the season bar is near the top, tap the other season, and assert in a UI test that the season bar's frame is unchanged and no activity indicator appears in between. Record before and after to see the clamp. Unit test (the observer has to become internal): after load(seasonId:) returns on the main thread, `episodes` already holds the new season and hasLoaded is true. Also re-check the first open of a series: no 'no episodes' flash.

## transitions-motion-9 — Changing sort or filter in a grid is handled three different ways and never as one transition: Movies animates a scroll while the new order lands mid-flight, Series and Live keep the old scroll offset

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Series category detail, All Series, Live category detail, All Channels
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:653-668, 688-730, 737-739`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:615-627, 647-671, 678-680`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577, 600-621, 629-631`

**What the user perceives:** Movies: pick another sort while scrolled down; the grid starts gliding to the top in the old order and at some point during or after the glide every poster changes at once. Series and Live: the same menu action replaces the items under the finger and the list stays at the old offset (or snaps to the new bottom because only 90 items are rendered again), so the user is left in the middle of a differently ordered list.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODCategoryContent starts an animated scrollTo(gridTopID) in onChange(of: sortOption / fileTypeFilter) (VODView.swift:719-728) and, independently, a detached recompute from .task(id:) (:738-739) whose result is assigned without animation whenever it finishes (:663-666): two unsynchronised events. SeriesCategoryContent and LiveCategoryContent have no ScrollViewReader at all (SeriesView.swift:647-671, LiveStreamsView.swift:600-621) and their recompute resets visibleCount to one page (:625, :575).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Treat a sort/filter change as one content replacement, the way Photos and Files do it: quick cross-fade of the whole grid, new content starts at the top. Do not animate the per-item diff: only the first `visibleCount` (90) items are in the ForEach, most cells would fly in from or out to positions outside that window, and at 10k+ items the old and new first pages rarely share items.
In all three content views:
`@State private var generation = 0
// recompute(animated:) after the detached work and the isCancelled guard:
withAnimation(animated ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : nil) {
  displayItems = result; visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count); generation &+= 1 }
...
ScrollView { LazyVGrid { ... } }.id(generation).transition(.opacity)`
A new identity starts at the top by itself, so the ScrollViewReader and both withAnimation(.easeOut(0.25)) blocks at VODView.swift:719-728 go away. Call with animated: true from the sortOption / filter tasks and animated: false from the itemsToken task (search-as-you-type must not animate, but should also restart at the top). Posters of the new first page come from the memory cache or the existing prefetch (:667).

**APIs:** View.id(_:) (iOS 13.0); View.transition(_:) with .opacity (iOS 13.0); withAnimation(_:_:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/VODView.swift:592-740, Views/SeriesView.swift:564-681, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:526-632; `git log -S'gridTopID'` gives a single commit, 654cefc, which added the sort/filter feature.

What holds:
- Movies fires an animated proxy.scrollTo(gridTopID) in onChange(of: sortOption / fileTypeFilter) (VODView.swift:719-728) and, separately, a detached recompute whose result is assigned without animation whenever it finishes (:653-668). These are two unsynchronised events.
- Series and Live have no scroll handling at all (SeriesView.swift:647-671, LiveStreamsView.swift:600-621). Their recompute resets visibleCount to 90 (:625, :575), so the user either stays at the old offset in a differently ordered list or is clamped to the end of the first page.
- No comment explains the difference. It is an omission from 654cefc, not a decision.

What is wrong in the fix:
1) recompute is driven by three `.task(id:)` modifiers and all three run on first appearance (VODView.swift:737-739 and the equivalents). Bumping `generation` in every recompute rebuilds the ScrollView three times on appear, and 'animated: true from the sort/filter tasks' would cross-fade the grid during the push.
2) `.task` also restarts when the screen reappears after a pop from a detail. With `.id(generation)` every return from a movie would rebuild the grid at the top and lose the scroll position. Today's unconditional `visibleCount = min(pageSize, count)` on each recompute has the same weakness; I could not run this, so it needs checking.
3) Replacing the ScrollView identity tears down all cells and in-flight image requests and puts two grids on screen during the fade, when only a position reset is needed.
4) The 'Photos and Files do it this way' precedent is not something I can verify. A consistent reset to the top is defensible on its own; the cross-fade is taste.

Severity: the Movies glide is 0.25 s and mostly a polish issue. The Series/Live behaviour (left mid-list after choosing, say, 'Top rated') is the real defect.

**Corrected claim:** After a sort or filter change Movies scrolls to the top with an animation that is not synchronised with the content swap, while Series and Live do not reset the position at all and can leave the user at the old offset or clamped to the end of the first 90 items. The three grids should behave the same: new order, start at the top, in one update.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the view identity; make the reset part of the same state update as the content swap, and only when the inputs really changed.
- In each of the three content views add `@State private var scrollPosition = ScrollPosition(edge: .top)` and `.scrollPosition($scrollPosition)` on the ScrollView.
- Keep a small applied-inputs key (sort, filter, itemsToken) in @State. In recompute, after the detached work and an isCancelled guard (Series and Live lack the guard today): if the key equals the last applied key, return without touching displayItems or visibleCount. Otherwise assign displayItems, set visibleCount to one page, call `scrollPosition.scrollTo(edge: .top)` and store the key.
- This removes the triple recompute on appear and the reset on return from a detail, and lets VODView.swift:688 and 719-728 (the ScrollViewReader and both withAnimation blocks) go.
- Search-as-you-type goes through itemsToken and also restarts at the top, without animation.
- A cross-fade is optional and a taste decision for the owner; if wanted, wrap only the sort/filter-initiated assignment in a short withAnimation. Do not use `.id(generation)`.

**API check:** Finding's APIs: View.id(_:), View.transition(_:), withAnimation are iOS 13 and exist, but the `.id(generation)` design is not recommended.
Corrected fix:
- SwiftUICore.swiftinterface line 688: `@available(iOS 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 18.0, watchOS 11.0, visionOS 2.0, *) public struct ScrollPosition : Sendable`.
- `public init(idType: (some Hashable & Sendable).Type = Never.self, edge: Edge)` (iOS 18.0).
- `public mutating func scrollTo(edge: Edge)` at line 726 (iOS 18.0).
- SwiftUI.swiftinterface line 22734: `@available(iOS 18.0, ...) nonisolated public func scrollPosition(_ position: Binding<ScrollPosition>, anchor: UnitPoint? = nil) -> some View`.
All usable at the 18.0 deployment target without #available.

**Regression risks:** - Must not undo the deliberate performance work: Equatable content views, itemsToken, off-main sort, pagination all stay.
- The applied-key guard changes when recompute runs. `fileTypes`/`genres` and the prefetch must still be computed on the first run and when items change.
- The scrollPosition binding is written once when the user starts scrolling, which re-evaluates the grid body once. Cheap, but check on a 10k+ list.
- scrollTo(edge: .top) with a large title and an always-visible search drawer: confirm the title expands cleanly and does not jump.
- With the finding's original `.id(generation)` fix: position lost on every return from a detail, triple rebuild on appear, cancelled image loads.

**How to verify:** Simulator with a catalog larger than three pages, per grid (Movies, Series, Live; category and All):
1) Scroll three pages down, pick another sort: the first cell of the new order is visible and hittable, with no scroll glide (UI test plus recording).
2) Type in the search field: the first match is visible.
3) Scroll three pages down, open a detail, go back: the position is kept. Run this on today's build first, to establish whether the visibleCount reset on reappear is a live bug.
4) First push of the grid: no fade and no second layout.
M05-movies-sort-menu.png and L04-live-category-sort-menu.png show the menus to drive.

## transitions-motion-10 — Blanket `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` on the Movies and Series home roots strips every system animation from those two tabs; Live TV and M3U run without it

- Verdict: **undecidable** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home, Series home
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:160`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:161`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93-149`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:87-93`

**What the user perceives:** Expected on iPad (ipad-light screenshots show the sidebar toggle of .sidebarAdaptable): toggling the sidebar, rotating or resizing in Split View animates the Live TV shelves to their new width, while Movies and Series snap to the final layout under the animating bars. Not confirmed on a device.

**Mechanism (finder):** The modifier sits after .toolbar / .sheet / .searchable / the tasks and before .navigationDestination (VODView.swift:160, SeriesView.swift:161), so its scope is the home shelf tree of that tab. What it does not suppress: the push (UIKit, and destinations are hosted outside this subtree), sheet presentation (presentations only honour disablesAnimations), the search bar activation (UISearchController), and CachedImage, which sets its own transaction further in (CachedImage.swift:87-93). What it could suppress from the app's own code: nothing, because no state write in these views is wrapped in withAnimation except the jump-to-category scroll (VODView.swift:102), which reads the transaction at call time. What is left are system-initiated animated transactions flowing into the subtree: size changes (rotation, sidebar, Split View), safe-area and keyboard inset changes, and a list diff that happens inside the system's search dismiss animation (onChange(of: isSearchActive) at :154-156 clears the query). The line dates from the first native commit (git log -S finds only fe55017 / d2489f9) with no comment; LiveStreamsView and M3UChannelsView have the same structure without it.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Remove both lines and compare Movies/Series against Live on: search activate and cancel, pull to refresh, hide a category, rotation, iPad sidebar toggle. If the shelf diff then animates on search cancel (the one thing it plausibly guarded against), suppress exactly that on the LazyVStack only: `.transaction(value: debouncedQuery) { $0.animation = nil }`, which applies the mutation only when the filter changes and leaves size and inset animations alone. CachedImage.swift:87-93 stays (deliberate: cache hits must not fade).

**APIs:** View.transaction(value:_:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/VODView.swift:112-164, Views/SeriesView.swift:161 (via grep), Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:242-256, Views/DashboardView.swift:46-123, ContentView.swift withAnimation sites (via grep); `git log -S'$0.animation = nil'` shows the line dates from the first native commit (6e8bd95 / fe55017, moved by d2489f9).

Facts that hold: the modifier exists only on the Movies and Series home roots (VODView.swift:160, SeriesView.swift:161). LiveStreamsView and the M3U views do not have it. It has no comment.

Why this cannot be settled from code:
- I found no state write inside the scoped subtree that runs under an animation. recomputeFilter runs from async `.task(id:)` (VODView.swift:157-159). The only withAnimation is the scrollTo at :102.
- DashboardView.swift:121's `.animation` is scoped to the player ZStack, not the TabView.
- So the only candidates are system-driven transactions: rotation, sidebar or Split View resize, search-bar inset changes. Whether SwiftUI content inside a UIKit-animated container visibly snaps cannot be derived from code. The shelves are leading-aligned full-width rows, for which a snap and an animated resize look nearly identical.
- The finding itself says 'Not confirmed on a device' and calls its own title claim ('strips every system animation') into question by listing what the modifier does not suppress.
- It is equally unknown what the line guarded against. One thing code cannot tell: whether it also kills the animated jump-to-category scroll at VODView.swift:102, which Live performs at LiveStreamsView.swift:252.

The evidence is too weak to confirm and not strong enough to refute.

**Corrected claim:** Movies and Series home carry an uncommented `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` from the first commit that Live TV and M3U lack. Whether it has any user-visible effect, or still guards anything, is unknown. It is an inconsistency worth one comparison run, not an established defect.

**Corrected fix:** None until measured. If the recordings show a visible difference in Live's favour and nothing regresses, remove the two lines. If only the search-cancel shelf diff then animates, scope the suppression with `.transaction(value: debouncedQuery) { $0.animation = nil }` on the LazyVStack. If there is no visible difference, leave the lines and add a comment, or remove them purely for consistency at the owner's discretion.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:
- `@inlinable nonisolated public func transaction(_ transform: @escaping (inout Transaction) -> Void) -> some View` (line 17633, iOS 13.0).
- `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *) @_alwaysEmitIntoClient nonisolated public func transaction(value: some Equatable, _ transform: @escaping (inout Transaction) -> Void) -> some View` (line 17638).
Both usable at the 18.0 target.

**Regression risks:** Removing an unexplained guard could re-enable animated shelf diffs during search activate/cancel, pull to refresh, hiding a category, or the playlist-to-dashboard transition (ContentView's withAnimation). CachedImage.swift:87-93 is separate and must stay. Does not touch the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Record Movies and Live TV side by side on the current build, then Movies again with the line removed.
- iPad: sidebar toggle, rotation, Split View resize. Do the shelves snap on Movies while Live animates?
- iPhone: search activate and cancel with a non-empty query; pull to refresh; hide a category; the jump-to-category scroll from the category picker (is it animated on Movies today, as it is on Live?); entering the dashboard from the playlist list with Movies as the restored tab.
The finding stands only if at least one of these shows a visible difference.

## transitions-motion-11 — Jump-to-category animates a 0.25 s scroll across any number of lazy shelf rows and resets its trigger with a 0.3 s asyncAfter timer

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:139-149, 250-258`, `Views/VODView.swift:100-108, 134-144`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:101-109, 135-145`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:189-198`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:75-80`

**What the user perceives:** Pick a category far down in the picker (L03-live-category-picker.png: the sheet covers only the lower half, the list above stays visible): while the sheet slides away, the list behind it streaks through every shelf in between in a quarter of a second, and the destination shelf's posters can arrive late.

**Mechanism (finder):** onSelect sets pendingScrollTarget in the same update that dismisses the sheet; onChange wraps proxy.scrollTo(target, anchor: .top) in withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.25)) (LiveStreamsView.swift:252-254 and the three siblings). In a LazyVStack an animated offset change passes through the intermediate offsets, so the rows that fly by are instantiated, each with a LazyHStack of cards, an onAppear prefetch of up to 32 posters (VODView.swift:468-470) and image requests that are deliberately not cancelled on disappear for the shelf profile (CachedImage.swift:75-80). Hundreds of categories in 0.25 s is several rows per frame on the main thread during the sheet dismissal. The reset `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.3) { pendingScrollTarget = nil }` only exists so that picking the same category again fires onChange; it is a timer standing in for an event. Movies and Series additionally sit under the blanket nil-animation transaction, so the four screens may not even behave alike.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Section jumps are instantaneous in the system (index bar in Contacts and Music); the sheet dismissal is the transition.
`.onChange(of: pendingScrollTarget) { _, target in
  guard let target else { return }
  pendingScrollTarget = nil                      // reset in place, no timer
  var t = Transaction(); t.disablesAnimations = true
  withTransaction(t) { proxy.scrollTo(target, anchor: .top) }
}`
Same four sites. If a visible glide is wanted for near targets, that needs the current position (scrollPosition(id:)) and is a larger change.

**APIs:** Transaction.disablesAnimations (iOS 13.0); withTransaction(_:_:) (iOS 13.0); ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo(_:anchor:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code re-read: all four sites are identical. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:250-258, Views/VODView.swift:100-108, Views/SeriesView.swift:101-109, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:189-198 run `withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.25)) { proxy.scrollTo(target, anchor: .top) }` followed by `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(.now() + 0.3) { pendingScrollTarget = nil }`. The sheet sets the target in the same closure that dismisses it (LiveStreamsView.swift:145-148, VODView.swift:140-143, M3UChannelsView.swift:107-110). CategoryPickerSheet uses `.presentationDetents([.medium, .large])` (Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:97) and iphone-dark/L07-live-category-picker.png shows the list visible above the half-height sheet, so the scroll is visible while the sheet leaves. History: the code predates the monorepo move (d2489f9) and has no comment calling the animation deliberate; the only comment (M3UChannelsView.swift:194) explains the reset, confirming the timer exists only to re-arm onChange.

What stands: an animated jump realizes the rows visible at each sampled frame, and every realized shelf row fires an onAppear prefetch of up to 32 posters (VODView.swift:468-470, 476-487; same pattern at LiveStreamsView.swift:410, SeriesView.swift:452, M3UChannelsView.swift:397). Nothing in the app ever calls stopPrefetching (grep: zero hits), ListImagePrefetch runs 3 concurrent requests into the memory cache (Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift:9-13) and shelf-profile LazyImages are not cancelled on disappear (Views/CachedImage.swift:75-80). A jump over 300 categories therefore leaves a backlog of up to a few thousand poster downloads/decodes for shelves the user never looked at, sharing 4 connections per host (CachedImage.swift:20) with the destination shelf. That is a real, code-evident cost independent of any frame-time measurement.

What needs correcting: (1) not every shelf in between is instantiated - only those visible at the 15-30 frames the animation samples (roughly 60-150 rows for a far jump), so 'every shelf' is overstated. (2) The main-thread hitch during the sheet dismissal is plausible but unmeasured. (3) Whether VOD/Series already jump without animation because of `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` (VODView.swift:160, SeriesView.swift:161) cannot be decided from code: scrollTo is an imperative call under withAnimation, the view-level transaction modifier may or may not strip it. (4) The proposed reset `pendingScrollTarget = nil` inside its own onChange mutates the observed value during the callback; it probably works (second invocation hits the nil guard) but is the classic source of the 'onChange(of:) action tried to update multiple times per frame' runtime warning. A reset that cannot re-enter is as small and safer.

**Corrected claim:** Jump-to-category animates a 0.25 s scroll to an arbitrarily distant lazy shelf row while the half-height picker sheet is dismissing. The rows sampled along the way (tens to ~150 for a far target, not every row) are realized, and each one enqueues a 32-poster prefetch that is never cancelled, so a far jump leaves a multi-thousand-image backlog competing with the destination shelf's posters; a main-thread hitch during the dismissal is plausible but unmeasured. The trigger is re-armed by a 0.3 s asyncAfter timer rather than an event. Movies/Series may already behave differently from Live/M3U because of their blanket nil-animation transaction (not decidable from code).

**Corrected fix:** Make the jump instantaneous and drop the timer, at the same four sites:
`.onChange(of: pendingScrollTarget) { _, target in
  guard let target else { return }
  var t = Transaction(); t.disablesAnimations = true
  withTransaction(t) { proxy.scrollTo(target, anchor: .top) }
}`
and re-arm the trigger where the picker is opened instead of inside onChange: in the four toolbar buttons (LiveStreamsView.swift:130, VODView.swift:125, SeriesView.swift:126, M3UChannelsView.swift:86) write `pendingScrollTarget = nil; showingCategoryPicker = true`. Selecting the same category twice then always goes nil -> id, with no timer and no state write inside the onChange callback. No iOS 26 API involved, so no fallback needed. Instant versus animated is a small taste call for the owner; instant matches system index jumps.

**API check:** Transaction.disablesAnimations: `public var disablesAnimations: Swift.Bool` in `extension SwiftUICore.Transaction`, @available(iOS 13.0) (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13856-13871). withTransaction: `public func withTransaction<Result>(_ transaction: Transaction, _ body: () throws -> Result) rethrows -> Result` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6003, iOS 13). ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo: `public func scrollTo<ID>(_ id: ID, anchor: UnitPoint? = nil) where ID : Hashable` inside `@available(iOS 14.0) public struct ScrollViewProxy` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:19361-19364). All found; nothing iOS 26-only.

**Regression risks:** An unanimated scrollTo to a far, never-realized LazyVStack row relies on estimated row heights; empty categories render a short Text instead of a shelf (VODView.swift:434-442), so the landing offset should be checked for a far target (header must be at the top, not a row off). Does not touch the Equatable shelf rows, prefetch tuning or CachedImage's deliberate no-cancel behaviour. If the reset were kept inside onChange as originally proposed, watch for the multiple-updates-per-frame console warning.

**How to verify:** Seed 300+ categories. UI test: open picker, choose the last category, assert its header is hittable within 1 s; scroll away, choose the same category again, assert it is reached again (covers re-arming). On device: Instruments Hitches during the jump before/after, and count Nuke prefetch task starts (os_signpost or a debug counter in ListImagePrefetch.start) for one far jump before/after. Also record Movies vs Live TV before the change to see whether they currently differ.

## transitions-motion-12 — Detail toolbar changes are hard cuts: the title pops in at the scroll threshold despite withAnimation, and the favourite star swaps images after a database round trip

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:83-92, 180-186, 315-332`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:877-888, 996-1002, 1249-1264`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:1159-1182`

**What the user perceives:** Scrolling a detail page, the film name appears in the bar at one exact offset and disappears again at the same offset, with no fade. Tapping the star changes outline to filled yellow a moment after the tap, with no symbol animation. While the page is at the top, the screen has no title at all (back-stack menu entry and VoiceOver screen title are empty).

**Mechanism (finder):** The title is switched by changing the string: `.navigationTitle(showNavTitle ? currentMovie.name : "")` (MovieDetailView.swift:83, SeriesView.swift:877). The state write is wrapped in withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.18)) (:184, :1000), but nothing in SwiftUI's render tree depends on showNavTitle; the navigation item's title is set through UIKit, which does not cross-fade a string change, so the animation has no effect. The star is `Image(systemName: isFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star")` driven by the @Query (:88-89), with no content transition, and toggleFavorite only writes to the database (:315-332), so the UI changes when the asynchronous observation comes back.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Title: keep a constant navigation title and fade a principal item, which is a SwiftUI view and does animate:
`.navigationTitle(currentMovie.name)
.toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) {
  Text(currentMovie.name).font(.headline).lineLimit(1)
    .opacity(showNavTitle ? 1 : 0)
    .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: showNavTitle)
    .accessibilityHidden(true) } }`
and set showNavTitle without withAnimation. The existing onScrollGeometryChange threshold stays.
Star: optimistic local state as LivePlayerShell already does (LiveStreamsView.swift:1159-1182) plus symbol transitions:
`Image(systemName: shownFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star")
  .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
  .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: favoriteTapCount)
  .animation(.default, value: shownFavorite)`
Drive the bounce from a tap counter, not from isFavorite, so the late first @Query value cannot bounce the star when the screen opens. Whether symbol effects are carried through the bar button bridging inside a toolbar item has to be confirmed on the simulator; if not, the same Image in the principal/hero area is the fallback.

**APIs:** ToolbarItemPlacement.principal (iOS 14.0); ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:) with .replace (iOS 17.0); View.symbolEffect(_:options:value:) with .bounce (iOS 17.0); View.contentTransition(_:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts confirmed. Title: `.navigationTitle(showNavTitle ? currentMovie.name : "")` (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:83) and `.navigationTitle(showNavTitle ? currentSeries.name : "")` (Views/SeriesView.swift:877); showNavTitle is read nowhere else (grep), so the `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.18))` at MovieDetailView.swift:184 / SeriesView.swift:1000 has nothing in the SwiftUI render tree to animate. The title is empty until contentOffset.y > 240, so the pushed screen has no title for the back-stack menu when another detail is pushed from it (MovieDetailView.swift:96-98). Star: `Image(systemName: isFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star")` driven only by `@Query<IsFavoriteRequest>` (MovieDetailView.swift:21, 88-89; SeriesView.swift:811, 884-885), no contentTransition/symbolEffect anywhere outside LoadingProcessView (grep), and toggleFavorite only writes to the DB (MovieDetailView.swift:315-332, SeriesView.swift:1249-1264); the UI changes when the ValueObservation (Models/Requests.swift:269-290) comes back. LivePlayerShell does have the optimistic pattern with rollback (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:1159-1182). No comment or history marks any of this as deliberate (both lines date from d2489f9).

What I could not confirm: (a) that the bar title really hard-cuts on iOS 18 and on the iOS 26 bar - very likely for a UIKit title string change, but it is a runtime behaviour; the screenshots (iphone-dark/M07, M08) cannot show it because the demo page is too short to pass 240 pt. (b) The star delay is one DB write plus one observation hop, normally a frame or two; it only becomes clearly visible when the writer is busy (e.g. a catalog refresh in progress). So 'a moment after the tap' is usually subtle. (c) Whether `.contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))` and `.symbolEffect(.bounce, value:)` survive bar-button bridging inside the iOS 26 glass button, and whether a `.principal` item gets its own glass capsule on iOS 26, need a simulator look (the finder says so too). Severity is polish, not medium. Also a latent bug the fix should cover: toggleFavorite reads `isFavorite` inside the write, so a double tap before the query returns runs two inserts.

**Corrected claim:** On Movie and Series detail the bar title is produced by swapping the navigationTitle string between "" and the name at a 240 pt threshold; the surrounding withAnimation cannot animate it, so it most likely cuts in and out (to be confirmed on iOS 18 and 26), and the screen has no title at all while at the top. The favourite star has no symbol transition and no optimistic state: it changes only after the DB write and observation round trip, which is normally near-instant but lags when the database writer is busy.

**Corrected fix:** Title: `.navigationTitle(currentMovie.name)` (constant) plus
`ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Text(currentMovie.name).font(.headline).lineLimit(1).opacity(showNavTitle ? 1 : 0).animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: showNavTitle).accessibilityHidden(true) }`
and set showNavTitle without withAnimation; keep the onScrollGeometryChange threshold. Same in SeriesDetailView. On iOS 26 check on the simulator that the principal item is drawn without a glass capsule; if it gets one, add `.sharedBackgroundVisibility(.hidden)` to that ToolbarItem behind `if #available(iOS 26, *)` (iOS 18 fallback: plain item, no glass exists there).
Star: add `@State private var favoriteOverride: Bool?` and `@State private var favoriteTaps = 0`; `let shownFavorite = favoriteOverride ?? isFavorite`; on tap set `favoriteOverride = !shownFavorite`, bump favoriteTaps, write using that captured value (not `isFavorite`), clear the override on failure, and clear it in `.onChange(of: isFavorite) { favoriteOverride = nil }`. Label: `Image(systemName: shownFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star").contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)).symbolEffect(.bounce, value: favoriteTaps).animation(.default, value: shownFavorite)`. If the simulator shows the symbol effects are dropped by the bar-button bridge, keep the optimistic state (that part is certain) and drop the effects.

**API check:** ToolbarItemPlacement.principal: `public static let principal` in `@available(iOS 14.0) struct ToolbarItemPlacement` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:6097-6101). ContentTransition.symbolEffect: `public static func symbolEffect<T>(_ effect: T, options: SymbolEffectOptions = .default) -> ContentTransition where T : ContentTransitionSymbolEffect, T : SymbolEffect`, @available(iOS 17.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4578-4580); ReplaceSymbolEffect iOS 17 (Symbols.swiftinterface:228-229). View.symbolEffect(_:options:value:): `where T : DiscreteSymbolEffect, U : Equatable`, @available(iOS 17.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4474-4481); BounceSymbolEffect iOS 17 (Symbols.swiftinterface:57-58). View.contentTransition(_:): in `extension View` under @available(iOS 16.0) (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:16098). onScrollGeometryChange (already used): iOS 18.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13688-13689). ToolbarContent.sharedBackgroundVisibility(_:): @available(iOS 26.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5789-5794) - only needed if the principal item gets glass. Also present: `ToolbarItemPlacement.title` (iOS 14 back-deployed, resolves to `._title` on iOS 26 and `.principal` below, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:6167-6174) as an alternative placement.

**Regression risks:** A constant navigationTitle changes what the back-stack menu and VoiceOver announce (intended). A principal item replaces the system title view, so the title no longer truncates/animates the system way and could collide with wide trailing items on small phones (lineLimit(1) covers it). Optimistic star must be cleared when the query catches up or the star can stick in the wrong state after a failed write; SeriesDetailView's toggle is async and called from a Task (SeriesView.swift:881-883), keep that shape. Outside the player scope and outside the tip-jar WIP.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 18.x and 26.0, with a detail page long enough to scroll past 240 pt (the demo page is too short): screen-record the scroll before/after and step frames to see whether the title cuts or fades, and whether the principal item shows a glass capsule on 26. Record a star tap to see whether replace/bounce render inside the bar button. UI test: navigation bar identifier/title equals the film name immediately after push; star image changes in the same run-loop turn as the tap; double tap leaves exactly zero or one DBFavorite row.
