## transitions-motion-13 — Download state changes rebuild the button and resize it; in episode rows the compact button grows from an icon to 'spinner + 12%' and re-wraps the row text

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Series detail, Movie detail, Downloads
- Code: `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:85-99, 101-123, 125-143`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1416-1472`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:79-116, 264-305`

**What the user perceives:** Starting an episode download: the small arrow button turns into a wider pill with a spinner and a percentage, the title and plot next to it lose width and can re-wrap, and the width changes again at 10% and 100%. Idle, queued, downloading and done are four different shapes with cuts between them. In Downloads the progress bar advances in steps and a finished item jumps from one section to another.

**Mechanism (finder):** labelContent is a switch that returns different view types per state (DownloadButton.swift:87-98) with no transition. The compact idle label is icon-only (:102-109), the downloading label is ProgressView + Text(percent) (:126-133), so its intrinsic width differs and changes with the digit count; EpisodeDetailRow gives the text column maxWidth .infinity next to it (SeriesView.swift:1447, :1453-1471). `ProgressView(value:).progressViewStyle(.circular)` (:127-129) is an indeterminate spinner on iOS, so the only progress indication is the text. DownloadsView's linear ProgressView gets a new value once per percent with no animation (DownloadsView.swift:292-293), and rows move between sections through the @Query with no transaction (:80-115).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Compact variant: fixed footprint and symbol transitions, like the App Store / TV download control.
`ZStack { switch state {
  case .idle: Image(systemName: "arrow.down.circle")
  case .queued: Image(systemName: "clock")
  case .downloading(let p): Circle().trim(from: 0, to: p).stroke(.tint, style: .init(lineWidth: 2.5, lineCap: .round)).rotationEffect(.degrees(-90)).overlay(Image(systemName: "stop.fill").font(.system(size: 8))).animation(.linear(duration: 0.3), value: p)
  case .completed: Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle.fill")
  case .failed: Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill") } }
.contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)).frame(width: 44, height: 32)`
Full-width variant: keep the layout, add `.contentTransition(.numericText(value: p))` and `.animation(.default, value: Int(p * 100))` to the percent text.
DownloadsView: `.animation(.linear(duration: 0.3), value: fraction)` on the bar and `.animation(.default, value: items.map(\.downloadStatus))` on the List so rows move between sections instead of jumping (download lists are short).

**APIs:** ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:) with .replace (iOS 17.0); ContentTransition.numericText(value:) (iOS 17.0); Shape.trim(from:to:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Problem confirmed from code. Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:85-99 is a switch returning different view trees per state with no transition and no animation. Compact idle/queued/completed/failed are icon-only with 8 pt padding (:101-123); downloading is `ProgressView + Text(L("download.downloading_format", Int(progress*100)))` (:125-143; the format is "%d%%" in en/de and "%%%d" in tr), so the compact button is roughly twice as wide while downloading and grows again at 10% and 100%. In EpisodeDetailRow the text column is `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` directly beside the button in the same HStack (Views/SeriesView.swift:1416-1472), so title and the 5-line plot lose width and can re-wrap. The downloading label also drops the stroke overlay the other states have (:139-142 vs :119-122), another small cut. DownloadManager publishes once per whole percent (Models/DownloadManager.swift:566-571), DownloadsView's linear bar takes that value with no animation (Views/DownloadsView.swift:290-293), and rows move between status sections straight from the @Query with no transaction (:79-116). `ProgressView(value:).progressViewStyle(.circular)` showing an indeterminate spinner on iOS matches Apple's documented behaviour but is a runtime fact I could not check here.

The fix needs correcting. (1) `ZStack { switch state { case .idle: Image(...) case .queued: Image(...) ... } }.contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))` will not produce a replace transition: each switch branch is a different view identity, so SwiftUI inserts/removes views instead of changing one Image's symbol, and a content transition also needs an animated transaction, which the @Query-driven change does not have. It has to be one Image whose systemName changes plus `.animation(_, value:)` on an Equatable state key (the private State enum is not Equatable today). (2) A `stop.fill` glyph inside the ring implies tap-to-cancel, but primaryAction deliberately ignores taps while downloading/queued (DownloadButton.swift:195-197, cancel is in the context menu). Showing stop without wiring it is misleading; wiring it is a behaviour change the owner must decide. (3) The proposal silently drops the material pill + stroke of the compact button; that is a visual redesign, not required to fix the width jump.

**Corrected claim:** The compact episode download button changes intrinsic width between states (icon-only versus spinner + percentage, widening again at 10% and 100%), which re-flows the episode title/plot beside it; all state changes of DownloadButton are un-animated view swaps; the Downloads list's progress bar steps once per percent and rows hop between status sections without animation. The circular ProgressView most likely renders as an indeterminate spinner on iOS (documented behaviour, verify on simulator).

**Corrected fix:** Smallest change that removes the layout jump: give the compact variant a fixed footprint and keep the percentage out of it. In compact mode render one symbol view, `Image(systemName: iconName).contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))` where iconName is derived from state (arrow.down.circle / clock / checkmark.circle.fill / exclamationmark.triangle.fill; hidden while downloading), overlay a determinate ring while downloading: `Circle().trim(from: 0, to: p).stroke(.tint, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2.5, lineCap: .round)).rotationEffect(.degrees(-90)).animation(.linear(duration: 0.3), value: p)` over a faint full `Circle().stroke(.quaternary, lineWidth: 2.5)`, all inside `.frame(width: 32, height: 28)` within the existing padding/material pill, and drive it with `.animation(.default, value: stateKey)` where stateKey is a small Equatable enum/Int derived from state. Keep the existing background/stroke. Do not add a stop glyph unless the owner decides tap should cancel (product decision; today cancel is context-menu only). Add an accessibilityValue with the percentage since the text disappears in compact mode.
Full-width variant: keep layout; on the percent Text add `.contentTransition(.numericText(value: progress))` and `.animation(.default, value: Int(progress * 100))`; add the missing stroke overlay to downloadingLabel so the outline does not blink.
DownloadsView: `.animation(.linear(duration: 0.3), value: fraction)` on the linear ProgressView and `.animation(.default, value: items.map(\.downloadStatus))` on the List (DownloadStatus is a String-raw enum, so the array is Equatable). All APIs are iOS 17 or older; no iOS 26 gate needed.

**API check:** ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:): @available(iOS 17.0), `where T : ContentTransitionSymbolEffect, T : SymbolEffect` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4578-4580); ReplaceSymbolEffect iOS 17 (Symbols.swiftinterface:228-229). ContentTransition.numericText(value:): `@available(iOS 17.0) public static func numericText(value: Swift.Double) -> ContentTransition` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:16088-16089); the argument is Double, matching `progress`. Shape.trim(from:to:): `@inlinable nonisolated public func trim(from startFraction: CGFloat = 0, to endFraction: CGFloat = 1) -> some Shape` in `extension Shape`, iOS 13 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:5716). CircularProgressViewStyle: `@available(iOS 14.0) public struct CircularProgressViewStyle` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5011-5012); the interface says nothing about determinate rendering on iOS, so the spinner claim rests on documentation.

**Regression risks:** Every DownloadButton observes DownloadManager.shared (DownloadButton.swift:27), so a per-row `.animation(value:)` keyed on progress re-runs for all visible episode rows on each percent tick of any download - key the animation on the row's own state/percent only. Animating the Downloads List on status changes also animates section insertion/removal; check it does not fight the swipe-to-delete animation. Removing the percentage text from the compact button loses information unless the ring is clearly determinate. MovieDetailView.swift:147 uses the full-width variant and must look unchanged at rest.

**How to verify:** UI test with a stubbed slow download in Series detail: record the episode title's frame in idle, queued, downloading (5%, 15%, 100%) and completed; it must be identical. Screen-record one download start-to-finish in Series detail and in Downloads on iOS 18 and 26; step through frames at the idle->queued->downloading->completed changes to confirm the symbol replace actually animates. Check on simulator what the current circular ProgressView(value:) draws.

## transitions-motion-14 — Playlist list to dashboard uses a hand-made 0.3 s easeInOut slide, and leaving the dashboard frees the whole catalog on the main thread while that slide is running

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list, Dashboard
- Code: `ContentView.swift:42-69, 130-133, 165-170`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:37-48, 183-190`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:46-48`

**What the user perceives:** Choosing a playlist slides the dashboard in with a symmetric ease curve that feels mechanical next to the system's spring push (no parallax, no back swipe). 'Back to playlists' can stutter at the start of the slide-out with a large catalog.

**Mechanism (finder):** The switch is an if/else in a ZStack with .transition(.move(edge: .trailing)) and withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) (ContentView.swift:48, :58, :66-69, :166). SwiftUI transitions are evaluated per frame on the main thread, unlike a UIKit push that runs in the render server. On exit, PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload() is called synchronously right after the animation starts (:59-62); clearLists() drops nine catalog collections (PlaylistContentStore.swift:37-48) and the hidden tabs react by clearing their @State copies, so several hundred thousand model values are released on the main thread during the frames of the transition. The first frames of the dashboard and the start of loadPlaylist also fall into the slide-in.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest change, keeping the structure:
`@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
private var switchAnimation: Animation { reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .smooth(duration: 0.4) }
// exit
withAnimation(switchAnimation) { selectedPlaylist = nil } completion: {
  guard selectedPlaylist == nil else { return }   // a new playlist may have been opened meanwhile; unload() also clears loadToken
  PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload(); EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil) }
// transition
.transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .trailing))`
Same for the M3U branch (:46-54). Replacing the root switch by a real navigation push or cover is a structural question for the navigation lens.

**APIs:** withAnimation(_:completionCriteria:_:completion:) (iOS 17.0); Animation.smooth(duration:extraBounce:) (iOS 17.0); EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts confirmed: the root switch is an if/else inside a ZStack with `.transition(.asymmetric(insertion: .move(edge: .trailing), removal: .move(edge: .trailing)))` and `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3))` (ContentView.swift:42-69, 165-170); on exit `PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload()` / `M3UContentStore.shared.unload()` and `EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil)` run synchronously right after the withAnimation block (ContentView.swift:48-53, 58-62); unload() clears nine @Published collections plus four other published fields on the main actor (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:37-48, 183-190). The unload was added deliberately for memory (commit 0ab5bcd, comment at ContentView.swift:51 and PlaylistContentStore.swift:180-182), so it must stay; only its timing is in question.

Mechanism corrections: (1) 'Back to playlists' lives in the Settings tab (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:46-48), so the view sliding out is a Form and the catalog tabs are off screen. Their `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` (e.g. LiveStreamsView.swift:96) is tied to appearance and most likely does not re-run while the tab is hidden, so the claim that the hidden tabs clear their @State copies during the slide is unsupported; those copies are released when the dashboard is torn down at the end of the transition. (2) unload() executes in the same run-loop turn as the withAnimation call, i.e. before the first frame of the slide is committed. Its cost (a dozen objectWillChange sends to every observing view of the still-alive dashboard plus the release of the flat arrays; the per-category buffers stay alive while tab @State still holds them) therefore shows up as tap-to-motion latency at the start, not as dropped frames spread across the slide. How large it is at 150k movies cannot be read from code. (3) 'easeInOut feels mechanical next to the system spring' is taste with no evidence; `.smooth(duration: 0.4)` is not the system push either, and a longer animation is not obviously better. The real non-native aspect (no back swipe, no real push) is structural and correctly left to the navigation lens.

Fix check: `withAnimation(_:completionCriteria:_:completion:)` exists (iOS 17) and deferring the unload is low-risk, but the proposed guard `guard selectedPlaylist == nil else { return }` skips the unload entirely when the user opens another playlist within the animation window; if that playlist is of the other kind (Xtream -> M3U or the reverse) the old store keeps its whole catalog in memory for the session, undoing the deliberate memory work. loadPlaylist only replaces the same store (PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-112).

**Corrected claim:** Leaving the dashboard runs the catalog unload (a dozen @Published changes and the release of the flat catalog arrays) synchronously on the main thread in the same turn that starts the 0.3 s slide-out, so with a large catalog the slide can start late; the rest of the catalog memory is freed on the main thread when the dashboard is torn down at the end of the slide. The magnitude needs a device measurement. The hand-made easeInOut .move transition itself is a stylistic choice; the curve is not a defect on its own.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the transition and curve as they are (changing the curve is an optional product/taste decision). Defer only the unload:
`withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) { selectedPlaylist = nil } completion: {
  // A playlist of the same kind reopened meanwhile owns the store again (unload() would clear its loadToken).
  if selectedPlaylist?.kind != .xtream { PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload() }   // Xtream branch
  if selectedPlaylist == nil { EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil) }
}`
and in the M3U branch `if selectedPlaylist?.kind != .m3u { M3UContentStore.shared.unload() }` with the same EPG guard (use whatever the non-M3U kind case is called; ContentView.swift:45 only shows `.m3u`). This keeps the memory release in every path, including a quick switch to a playlist of the other kind. iOS 17 API, no iOS 26 gate needed. If a Reduce Motion variant is wanted, see transitions-motion-15.

**API check:** withAnimation with completion: `@available(iOS 17.0, ...) public func withAnimation<Result>(_ animation: Animation? = .default, completionCriteria: AnimationCompletionCriteria = .logicallyComplete, _ body: () throws -> Result, completion: @escaping () -> Void) rethrows -> Result` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:10277-10282). Animation.smooth: `@_alwaysEmitIntoClient public static func smooth(duration: TimeInterval = 0.5, extraBounce: Double = 0.0) -> Animation` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13314; iOS 17 extension) - found, but not needed by the corrected fix. EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion: `public var accessibilityReduceMotion: Bool { get }` in an iOS 13 extension (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:18334). View.transition has both `transition(_ t: AnyTransition)` (@_disfavoredOverload) and the iOS 17 generic `transition<T: Transition>` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19751-19756); a ternary of `.opacity` and `.move(edge:)` only type-checks through the AnyTransition overload, so type it explicitly (`let t: AnyTransition = ...`).

**Regression risks:** If the completion never fires or is skipped, the catalog stays in memory until the next load (the original proposal's guard had exactly this hole for cross-kind switches; the corrected guard closes it). unload() clears loadToken (PlaylistContentStore.swift:184), so it must never run while a playlist of the same kind is selected - the corrected guard preserves that. For 0.3 s longer the removed dashboard still observes a loaded store, which is today's behaviour during the slide anyway. Does not touch the settings rows next to TipJarRow().

**How to verify:** Device with a 100k+ VOD playlist: Instruments (Hitches + Time Profiler) on 'Back to playlists', measure tap-to-first-frame and hitch time before/after; check Allocations that catalog memory is released after the slide. UI tests: (a) leave the dashboard and immediately open a second Xtream playlist - its catalog must load; (b) leave an Xtream dashboard and immediately open an M3U playlist - PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreams must be empty afterwards; (c) leave and re-enter the same playlist quickly - content still shown.

## transitions-motion-15 — Custom motion in the browse UI ignores Reduce Motion: the detail hero parallax and the playlist slide always run

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Playlist list, Dashboard
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:63-70`, `ContentView.swift:66-69`

**What the user perceives:** With Settings > Accessibility > Motion > Reduce Motion on, the backdrop still drifts at a different speed than the page while scrolling a detail, and the dashboard still slides in from the side. System transitions in the same app switch to cross-fades, so the custom ones stand out.

**Mechanism (finder):** accessibilityReduceMotion is read only by the player (Views/PlayerView.swift:309, :366, :5555 and Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:122). DetailHero applies `offset(y: min(0, minY * 0.18))` unconditionally inside visualEffect (DetailComponents.swift:63-70); ContentView uses .move(edge: .trailing) unconditionally (ContentView.swift:66-69).

**Proposed fix (finder):** DetailHero: `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion`, capture it outside the visualEffect closure and use `let parallax = reduceMotion ? 0 : min(0, minY * 0.18)`; keep the overscroll stretch, it follows the finger directly. ContentView: opacity transition when reduceMotion (see the playlist transition finding). The zoom navigation transition, if adopted, is handled by the system.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion (iOS 13.0); View.visualEffect(_:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Confirmed from code: outside the out-of-scope player, `accessibilityReduceMotion` is read only in Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:122 (grep), so no browse screen honours it. DetailHero applies `.offset(y: min(0, minY * 0.18))` unconditionally inside visualEffect (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:63-70): the backdrop moves 18% faster than the page while scrolling, up to about 68 pt over the 380 pt hero. ContentView always uses `.move(edge: .trailing)` (ContentView.swift:66-69). Neither has a comment or history marking the omission as deliberate (both date from d2489f9).

Correction to the claim: 'System transitions in the same app switch to cross-fades' is not what Reduce Motion alone does. Navigation pushes and sheets keep sliding with Reduce Motion on; they cross-fade only when the separate 'Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions' sub-setting is enabled (UIKit exposes it as UIAccessibilityPrefersCrossFadeTransitions, iOS 14). So the playlist slide does not 'stand out' against system transitions under plain Reduce Motion; it only does when the user has also asked for cross-fades. The parallax part stands as stated: decorative scroll-linked depth motion is exactly what Reduce Motion is meant to remove, and the effect is small, so severity stays low.

Fix check: adding `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` to DetailHero and capturing the Bool in a local before the `@Sendable` visualEffect closure compiles (Bool is Sendable; `h` is already captured the same way at DetailComponents.swift:50, 67). Keeping the overscroll stretch is right.

**Corrected claim:** The detail hero's scroll parallax ignores Reduce Motion (real, low impact). The playlist<->dashboard slide ignores the 'Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions' setting; with Reduce Motion alone the system's own pushes still slide, so the custom slide is only inconsistent for users who enabled cross-fades.

**Corrected fix:** DetailHero: add `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion`; in backdropLayer `let reduce = reduceMotion` next to `let h = heroHeight`, and inside visualEffect `let parallax = reduce ? 0 : min(0, minY * 0.18)`; keep the overscroll scale.
ContentView: mirror the system rule rather than Reduce Motion alone: `private var switchTransition: AnyTransition { (reduceMotion && UIAccessibility.prefersCrossFadeTransitions) ? .opacity : .move(edge: .trailing) }` used for both insertion and removal at ContentView.swift:66-69 (typed as AnyTransition so the ternary compiles). Using Reduce Motion alone to switch to a fade is also acceptable but goes further than the system does; that is the owner's call. No iOS 26 API involved.

**API check:** EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion: `public var accessibilityReduceMotion: Swift.Bool { get }` in `@available(iOS 13.0) extension EnvironmentValues` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:18334). View.visualEffect: `nonisolated public func visualEffect(_ effect: @escaping @Sendable (EmptyVisualEffect, GeometryProxy) -> some VisualEffect) -> some View`, @available(iOS 17.0) (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:16281-16286) - the closure is @Sendable, so the environment value must be copied to a local Bool first. UIKit: `UIKIT_EXTERN BOOL UIAccessibilityPrefersCrossFadeTransitions(void) API_AVAILABLE(ios(14.0))` (UIKit.framework/Headers/UIAccessibility.h:570), Swift name `UIAccessibility.prefersCrossFadeTransitions` (UIKit.apinotes:2992); change notification UIAccessibilityPrefersCrossFadeTransitionsStatusDidChangeNotification (header :571). SwiftUI has no environment value for it (grep of both swiftinterface files: none). View.transition(AnyTransition) overload present (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19751).

**Regression risks:** Minimal. With parallax off the backdrop scrolls exactly with the page; the gradient and overlay layers are unaffected. `UIAccessibility.prefersCrossFadeTransitions` is read when the body is evaluated and is not observed, so a change made while the app is open applies on the next ContentView re-render, which is acceptable for a root switch. Overlaps with transitions-motion-14's edits to the same lines in ContentView; apply together.

**How to verify:** Move the factor into a pure function `heroParallax(minY:reduceMotion:)` and unit-test it (0 when reduceMotion, min(0, minY*0.18) otherwise). Simulator with Reduce Motion on (Settings > Accessibility > Motion): scroll a movie detail and confirm the backdrop no longer drifts relative to the poster/title overlay; with 'Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions' also on, open a playlist and confirm a cross-fade while a normal in-app push cross-fades too; with only Reduce Motion on, confirm both still slide.

## transitions-motion-16 — Settings rows and sections appear without row animation when data lands or a toggle reveals options, and hiding a category by swipe snaps

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings, Category picker sheet
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:226-259, 263-345, 448-457`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:126-140`, `Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:122-134`

**What the user perceives:** Settings opens with a short form; when the account request returns, three rows and up to four sections appear at once and 'About' jumps several screen heights down. The statistics first show 0 and then the counts. Switching the TV guide toggle makes its extra rows appear or vanish instantly, where the system Settings app slides rows in and out. Swiping 'Hide' on a category makes the row vanish and reappear in the Hidden section with no movement.

**Mechanism (finder):** fetchAuthInfo assigns authResponse and isLoading with no transaction (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:454-457); the Form inserts the conditional rows (:238-258) and the sections behind `authResponse?.userInfo != nil` (:263-345) without animation. fetchLocalStats runs after fetchAuthInfo (:393-394), so the counts change after the section is visible. `Toggle(..., isOn: $epgEnabled)` (EPGSettingsSections.swift:126) drives `if epgEnabled { ... }` (:131-140) through a plain binding. hiddenStore.setHidden is called outside withAnimation (CategoryPickerSheet.swift:125).

**Proposed fix (finder):** - PlaylistSettingsView.swift:454-457: `withAnimation { self.authResponse = response; self.isLoading = false }` so the Form animates the insertions; run fetchLocalStats before or concurrently with fetchAuthInfo and add `.contentTransition(.numericText())` to the four count texts.
- EPGSettingsSections.swift:126: `isOn: $epgEnabled.animation()`.
- CategoryPickerSheet.swift:125: `withAnimation { hiddenStore.setHidden(!isHidden, ...) }` (a List diff, fine at a few thousand rows).
All edits are outside the tip-jar lines; TipJarRow() at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:355 is not touched.

**APIs:** Binding.animation(_:) (iOS 13.0); ContentTransition.numericText(countsDown:) (iOS 16.0); withAnimation(_:_:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** I re-read all three sites. The mechanisms are real, but the perception is overstated for Settings and one part of the fix does nothing as written.

1. Settings insertions (real, mostly off-screen on iPhone). Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:8-9 start with authResponse = nil and isLoading = true. fetchAuthInfo assigns both inside a plain MainActor.run (:454-457) with no transaction, so the three rows at :238-258 and the sections behind `authResponse?.userInfo != nil` (:263-345) are inserted unanimated. No withAnimation exists anywhere in this file, and `git log -S'withAnimation'` on the three files returns nothing, so this is an omission, not a deliberate choice. However, shots/iphone-light/T01-settings-1.png shows the first viewport ends inside Player Settings; Playlist Information only starts on the second screen (T02). On iPhone the user sees the pop-in only if they scroll down before the verify() request returns. 'About jumps several screen heights' is wrong: four sections are inserted above About, about one screen, and normally off-screen. The iPad variant has no Settings screenshot yet, so I could not check whether the section is in the first viewport there.

2. A snap the finding missed. fetchAuthInfo sets `isLoading = true` at :449 on every run. It runs from .task (:392-396), .refreshable (:397-401), the header refresh button (:175) and Try Again (:236). Because the branch order is `if isLoading {spinner} else if error else if userInfo` (:226-259), every refresh collapses the three subscription rows into one spinner row and expands them again, even when a valid authResponse is already held. Wrapping only the success assignment gives a snap-collapse followed by an animated expand, and the catch path (:467-470) stays unanimated.

3. Stats 0 then counts (real, tiny). The order at :393-394 is fetchAuthInfo then fetchLocalStats, and the counts start at 0 (:20-23). The window is one local COUNT read (:415-421), and the stats section sits below Playlist Information, so it is even further off-screen. Counts live in @State, so it happens only on first open.

4. The numericText part of the fix does not work as written. A content transition only runs inside an animated transaction, and the count assignments at :423-428 are unanimated. If fetchLocalStats is moved first, the counts are already set when the section appears, so the modifier never fires on load.

5. EPG toggle (confirmed). Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:126 uses the plain `$epgEnabled` binding and :131-140 gate two to four Form rows on it, so they appear and vanish instantly. `$epgEnabled.animation()` is the standard fix, and the onChange save at :127-129 is unaffected.

6. Category hide (mechanism confirmed, visual result not observed). Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:125 calls setHidden with no animation from a non-destructive swipe button. Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:27-38 is synchronous on the main actor and bumps the @Published `version` at :37, so wrapping the call in withAnimation carries the transaction into the sheet's List diff (:64-80). The row leaves one ForEach and enters another, so it is a remove plus insert, not a move. I could not run the simulator, so how this combines with the swipe-close animation is unverified.

**Corrected claim:** Three small unanimated list changes, all low severity.

(a) In the Xtream Settings form, the subscription rows and the Statistics / Server / TV Guide / Content Management sections are inserted without animation when verify() returns. On iPhone this is below the first viewport (T01 vs T02), so it is seen only by a user who scrolls before the request finishes, or possibly on iPad. In addition, every refresh (pull-to-refresh, header refresh button, each run of .task) collapses the three subscription rows into a spinner row and back, because `isLoading` takes precedence over an existing authResponse. The stats show 0 for the duration of one local COUNT read on first open only.

(b) The TV guide toggle reveals and hides its extra rows instantly, where system Settings animates them.

(c) Hiding or unhiding a category by swipe in CategoryPickerSheet re-partitions the List with no animation.

The M3U settings view has no such conditional auth block and is not affected.

**Corrected fix:** 1. Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:226 — show the spinner row only when nothing is held yet: `if isLoading && authResponse == nil { ... }`. A refresh then keeps the existing rows in place instead of collapsing them. Optionally swap the header arrow (:174-179) for a small ProgressView while isLoading, so the refresh button still gives feedback.

2. Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:454-457 and :467-470 — wrap both state assignments in `withAnimation { ... }` so the first-load insertion and the error row animate.

3. Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:392-401 — run the local work first in both .task and .refreshable: `await fetchLocalStats(); await refreshDownloadUsage(); await fetchAuthInfo()`. The counts are then set before the section exists.

4. Drop `.contentTransition(.numericText())` from the proposal. If the owner wants the history count to roll after 'Clear history', it also needs `withAnimation` around the assignments at :423-428; that is optional polish, not a fix.

5. Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:126 — `isOn: $epgEnabled.animation()`.

6. Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:125 — `withAnimation { hiddenStore.setHidden(!isHidden, playlistId: pid, type: t, categoryId: entry.id) }`. Check it on the simulator before keeping it (see how_to_verify).

No iOS 26-only API is involved, so no availability gate or fallback is needed. All edits are outside the tip-jar lines; TipJarRow() at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:355 is untouched.

**API check:** All found in SwiftUICore.swiftmodule/arm64-apple-ios-simulator.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk).

- `public func withAnimation<Result>(_ animation: SwiftUICore.Animation? = .default, _ body: () throws -> Result) rethrows -> Result` — line 17530, @available(iOS 13.0).
- `public func animation(_ animation: SwiftUICore.Animation? = .default) -> SwiftUICore.Binding<Value>` in `extension SwiftUICore.Binding` — line 11639, @available(iOS 13.0).
- `public static func numericText(countsDown: Swift.Bool = false) -> SwiftUICore.ContentTransition` — line 16087, on `ContentTransition`, @available(iOS 16.0).
- `nonisolated public func contentTransition(_ transition: SwiftUICore.ContentTransition) -> some SwiftUICore.View` — line 16098, @available(iOS 16.0).

All are below the iOS 18.0 deployment target. The numericText pair is available but not needed by the corrected fix.

**Regression risks:** - Hidden-category consumers: withAnimation around setHidden also reaches every other observer of HiddenCategoryStore. Live, Movies, Series and Search recompute asynchronously via `.task(id:)` (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:107, Views/VODView.swift:159, Views/SeriesView.swift:160, Views/SearchView.swift:247) and assign their results later, outside the transaction, so they are unaffected. Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:26-29 filters `visibleShelfGroups` synchronously in body, so the M3U shelf list behind the medium-detent sheet will animate the shelf's removal. That is probably fine but should be looked at.
- Swipe actions: animated List diffs triggered from inside a swipe action can combine oddly with the swipe-close animation, especially on full swipe (allowsFullSwipe is true at CategoryPickerSheet.swift:122).
- Spinner condition: after the change a refresh no longer shows the in-section spinner, so without the optional header ProgressView the refresh button gives no visible feedback.
- Reordering the task: fetchAuthInfo does not depend on the local stats and only writes playlist.serverTimezone (:460-465), so order is safe. Pull-to-refresh will run the two local reads before the network call; the difference is not visible.
- Performance: none of the earlier deliberate work (Equatable shelf rows, off-main filtering, pagination) is touched. The picker's single-pass partitionedEntries (CategoryPickerSheet.swift:37-51) is unchanged.
- Tip jar: only lines away from TipJarRow() at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:355 change, so the owner's uncommitted work stays intact.

**How to verify:** Simulator screen recordings, on iPhone and on iPad (the iPad may show Playlist Information in the first viewport):

1. Open Settings against a panel with 1-2 s of added latency, scroll to Playlist Information before the response lands, and check that the rows and sections slide in. Then pull to refresh and tap the header refresh button: the three subscription rows must stay in place.
2. Confirm the Statistics rows never show 0 on first open.
3. Switch to another tab and back to Settings while scrolled to Playlist Information: I expect .task to re-run on each appear, so confirm the rows no longer blink to a spinner.
4. Toggle the TV guide switch on and off: the refresh, last-updated and matched-channels rows should animate in and out.
5. In the category picker (Live, and an M3U playlist with a few thousand groups), hide and unhide by button tap and by full swipe. Check that the row animates out and into the Hidden section without a glitch against the swipe-close animation, and that the shelf list behind the half-height sheet does not hitch. If the full swipe glitches, drop edit 6 and keep the rest.

## scroll-perf-1 — Coming back from a movie or series detail re-runs the grid's recompute, which resets pagination to the first 90 cells and throws away the scroll position.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Recently Added (movies) grid, Series category detail, All Series, Recently Added (series) grid
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:653-668, 737-739`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:615-627, 678-680`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577, 629-631`

**What the user perceives:** Scroll a category or 'All Movies' past roughly 7 screens (item 75+ on iPhone), open a film, go back: the grid collapses to its first 90 posters and you land near item 80 instead of where you were. With a sort active on a big list the collapse arrives up to a second after you are back, under your finger, and it can happen up to three times in a row. Apple's TV / Photos return you to the exact cell.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODCategoryContent attaches three tasks that all call recompute(): .task(id: itemsToken), .task(id: sortOption), .task(id: fileTypeFilter) (VODView.swift:737-739). A SwiftUI task is started on appearance and cancelled on disappearance, so pushing MovieDetailView and popping back starts all three again with unchanged ids. recompute() ends with an unconditional `visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count)` (VODView.swift:666; pageSize = 90 at :626), so a grid that had grown to 180/270/... cells shrinks to 90 and UIScrollView clamps the offset to the new, shorter content. SeriesCategoryContent has the same shape (SeriesView.swift:625, 678-680) and additionally has no Task.isCancelled guard. Each recompute also re-sorts the whole list off-main first (name sort of 150k titles measured at 0.54 s on the host Mac), which is why the collapse is delayed. LiveCategoryContent has the same code (LiveStreamsView.swift:575, 629-631) but is not hit by a pop because channels open the overlay player instead of pushing; it still runs the work three times on first appearance. Not reproducible with the demo catalog (12 movies < 90), which is why the screenshot tour cannot show it. The one runtime assumption is the documented task lifetime (restart on re-appearance after a NavigationStack pop).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Collapse the three tasks into one keyed task and remember which inputs were last applied, so a re-appearance is a no-op and visibleCount is only reset when the inputs really changed. In VODCategoryContent (same for SeriesCategoryContent / LiveCategoryContent):

private struct RecomputeKey: Hashable { let items: Int; let sort: VODSortOption; let fileTypes: Set<String> }
@State private var appliedKey: RecomputeKey?
private var recomputeKey: RecomputeKey { .init(items: itemsToken, sort: sortOption, fileTypes: fileTypeFilter) }

.task(id: recomputeKey) { await recompute(for: recomputeKey) }

private func recompute(for key: RecomputeKey) async {
    guard key != appliedKey else { return }   // back from a detail: keep page and offset
    ... existing detached sort/filter ...
    guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
    displayItems = result; streamQueue = queue; fileTypes = types
    visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count)
    appliedKey = key
    prefetch(result)
}

Keeps the off-main sort, the O(1) itemsToken and the Equatable signature untouched. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:653-668 and 737-739: three separate .task(id:) modifiers (itemsToken, sortOption, fileTypeFilter) all call recompute(), which ends with an unconditional `visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count)` (pageSize = 90, :626). Views/SeriesView.swift:615-627 and 678-680 have the same shape and no Task.isCancelled guard. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577 and 629-631 are the same, also without the guard. The grid cells push MovieDetailView / SeriesDetailView with NavigationLink (VODView.swift:692-693, SeriesView.swift:650), so the grid disappears on push and re-appears on pop; .task is cancelled on disappearance and restarted on appearance with unchanged ids, so all three recomputes run again and each one resets visibleCount to 90. ForEach is driven by displayItems.prefix(visibleCount) (:691), so the content shrinks and the scroll offset is clamped. Nothing guards against it: no applied-key state, no comment, and `git log -S'visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize'` shows a single commit (654cefc, which introduced pagination) with no later fix. The live grid is not hit because channels open the in-window overlay (LiveStreamsView.swift:480-492) and the detail screens hide the tab bar (:497), so nothing makes it disappear. One scope correction: the two Recently Added grids receive at most 20 items (VODView.swift:189 `.prefix(20)`, SeriesView.swift:243), so they can never exceed one page and do not collapse. The only runtime assumption is the task restart on pop, which is standard NavigationStack behaviour; I could not run the simulator to watch it.

**Corrected claim:** In Movies category detail, All Movies, Series category detail and All Series, returning from a detail screen restarts the grid's three recompute tasks; each resets visibleCount to 90, so a grid scrolled past the first page collapses and loses its position (with a sort active, after the off-main re-sort finishes; up to three times). The Recently Added grids are not affected (at most 20 items). The live grid only pays the triple recompute on first appearance.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: one `.task(id: recomputeKey)` with a nested `RecomputeKey` (items token, sort option, filter) plus `@State appliedKey`, and `guard key != appliedKey else { return }` at the top of recompute; set appliedKey only after the results are assigned. .task(id:) needs Equatable only, so the Hashable key compiles; VODSortOption / SeriesSortOption / LiveSortOption are String-raw enums and LiveStreamFilter is an OptionSet (use its rawValue in the key). Add the missing `guard !Task.isCancelled` to the Series and Live variants. Leave the `.onChange(of: sortOption)` / `.onChange(of: fileTypeFilter)` scroll-to-top in VODView.swift:719-728 untouched.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166 `func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) -> some View where T : Equatable`, in an extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, ...). No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Low. The key keeps the existing O(1) itemsToken, so the Equatable signature compare and the off-main sort are untouched. A list whose content changes while count/first/last stay equal is already not recomputed today (same token), so nothing is lost. Hasher is per-process seeded, which is fine for an in-memory key. If a recompute is cancelled by a push before it finishes, appliedKey stays unset and the pop reruns it, which is the wanted behaviour.

**How to verify:** UI test with a scaled fixture (400+ movies in one category): scroll about 12 swipes, note a hittable poster, open it, go back (also with the interactive swipe), assert the same poster is still hittable. Repeat with sort = name and in All Series. Fails today once more than 90 cells were loaded.

## scroll-perf-2 — Live TV and M3U shelves change height after they are on screen: the EPG line is added to every card when the first EPG snapshot arrives, and the loading placeholder is a different height from the loaded row.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, M3U channels home, Live category grid, Favorites (live)
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:372-375, 382-400, 451-454`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363-382, 439-442`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:130-137`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:83-91, 159-167`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:41-69`

**What the user perceives:** On every launch of a playlist that has EPG, the Live TV shelves are laid out, the user starts scrolling, and one to a few seconds later every shelf grows by 32 pt at once: the row under the finger moves by 32 pt times the number of rows above it. A smaller jump happens earlier when the channel icons replace the loading placeholders.

**Mechanism (finder):** LiveStreamCard adds the EPG line only when the snapshot exists: `if let snapshot = epgSnapshot { EPGNowNextLine(..., reserveSpace: true) }` (LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454; same in M3UChannelCard, M3UChannelsView.swift:439-442). reserveSpace keeps the height constant once a snapshot exists, but not across nil -> non-nil. The snapshot is nil until DashboardView's task has finished the whole catalog load and only then binds the EPG store (DashboardView.swift:131-137: `await contentStore.loadPlaylist` then `epgStore.setActivePlaylist`), which sets snapshot = nil and reloads asynchronously (EPGStore.swift:83-91, 159-167). When it lands, every realized card grows by 22 pt + 10 pt VStack spacing, and the Live/M3U shelf has no fixed height (unlike Movies/Series, VODView.swift:467), so every row grows. Separately the loading placeholder is `Color.clear.frame(height: liveShelfIcon + 30)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:374) = 86 pt on iPhone while a loaded row is 56 + 10 + 16..32 pt (82-98 pt, 114-130 pt with EPG).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Decide whether live cards carry the EPG line from a value that is known synchronously, not from the presence of the snapshot. (1) EPGStore: persist a per-playlist 'guide configured' flag (UserDefaults key epg.configured.<playlistId>) where loadSourceStatus already computes `configured` (EPGStore.swift:102-112) and expose `static func isConfiguredCached(_ id: UUID) -> Bool`. (2) New environment value `epgLineReserved: Bool`, set in DashboardView / M3UDashboardView next to epgSnapshot: `.environment(\.epgLineReserved, EPGStore.isConfiguredCached(playlist.id) || epgStore.snapshot != nil)`. (3) Cards: `if epgLineReserved { EPGNowNextLine(nowNext: epgSnapshot?[key], width: width, reserveSpace: true) }`. (4) Give the Live and M3U shelf ScrollView an explicit height computed from the same parts (icon + 10 + two caption lines + (reserved ? 32 : 0)) and use that number for the loading placeholder, as Movies/Series already do. The once-per-minute snapshot publish and its O(1) Equatable stay as they are.

**Verifier reasons:** The card code is as described: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454 and Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:439-442 add EPGNowNextLine only inside `if let snapshot = epgSnapshot`, so reserveSpace (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:66-67) holds the height only once a snapshot exists. The snapshot is nil at launch: Views/DashboardView.swift:131-136 awaits the whole catalog load (PlaylistContentStore.swift:152 sets streamsLoaded, which is what makes the shelves render) and only then calls setActivePlaylist, which sets snapshot = nil and starts an async reload of three database reads (EPG/EPGStore.swift:83-99, 211-245; rebuildResolution reads every liveStream row). So cards are on screen first and gain 22 pt + 10 pt spacing afterwards. Live and M3U shelves have no explicit height (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397, M3UChannelsView.swift:363-377), unlike Movies/Series (VODView.swift:467). What I could not settle from code is what the user sees: either every shelf grows by 32 pt, or the lazy row keeps its first height and clips the line. The comment at EPGComponents.swift:48-50 ('shelves that were laid out before EPG arrived could clip the progress capsule') says the owner has already seen the clipping variant. Both are defects and the same fix covers both. The demo fixture has no EPG (iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows no EPG line), so the screenshots cannot show it. The placeholder sub-claim is narrower than stated: displayCategories is only assigned in recomputeFilter, keyed on streamsLoaded / query / hidden ids (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107), so on a cold start the restored tab never shows the 86 pt placeholder (LiveStreamsView.swift:374); it appears only when a tab is first opened while the streams are still loading, or for empty categories during a full reload. M3U has no loading placeholder at all.

**Corrected claim:** On every launch of a playlist with a configured guide, Live TV and M3U channel cards are rendered without the EPG line and gain it (32 pt per card) when the first snapshot arrives after the catalog load; shelves have no fixed height, so they either grow (rows shift) or clip the line. The placeholder/loaded height mismatch (86 pt vs 82-98 pt) exists but is only reachable when the Live tab is first opened during the stream load or during a full reload, not on a normal cold start.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the proposal's direction: decide synchronously whether live cards carry the EPG line. Persist a per-playlist 'guide configured' flag where EPGStore computes `configured` (EPGStore.swift:102-112 and :472), clear it when the guide is disabled or its source removed, and combine it with playlist.epgEnabled. Inject `epgLineReserved` next to epgSnapshot in DashboardView.swift:130 and M3UDashboardView.swift:84; cards render `EPGNowNextLine(nowNext: epgSnapshot?[key], width:, reserveSpace: true)` when it is true. Give the Live and M3U shelf ScrollView an explicit height (icon + 10 + two caption lines + 32 when reserved) and use the same number for the loading placeholder; this depends on the two-line title reservation from scroll-perf-4. Do not change the once-per-minute publish or the version-based Equatable.

**API check:** No new Apple API is needed; EnvironmentKey / EnvironmentValues are already used for epgSnapshot (EPGComponents.swift:5-18). If the height is derived from text style: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12151 `@propertyWrapper public struct ScaledMetric<Value>` @available(iOS 14.0), `init(wrappedValue:relativeTo:)` at :12152.

**Regression risks:** A stale flag would reserve 32 pt of blank space on every card for a playlist whose guide was removed, so the flag must be cleared on disable/removal. A fixed shelf height can clip at large Dynamic Type sizes if it is not derived from the text style (EPGNowNextLine's own 22 pt is fixed). The Equatable shelf rows are unaffected because cards read the environment directly.

**How to verify:** Needs a simulator run with an EPG-seeded fixture: record the minY of the third shelf header right after the shelves appear and again 5 s later, and screenshot a card to see whether the EPG line is fully visible or clipped. Before the fix expect a shift or a clipped line; after it, identical frames and a fully visible line.

## scroll-perf-3 — 'Recently added' and 'Continue watching' are inserted above the shelves after the first frame, pushing the whole Movies / Series home down.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, Live TV home, M3U channels home
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:65-80, 175-192`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:66-81, 229-246`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:21-28`, `Models/Requests.swift:406-428`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:380-392`

**What the user perceives:** On a cold start the category shelves appear, then 'Continue watching' pops in (about 170 pt), then once the catalog is in memory 'Recently added' pops in (about 226 pt on iPhone, about 420 pt on iPad). The first category the user was looking at jumps down twice.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODView assigns displayCategories and displayItemsByCategory synchronously, then awaits a detached pass over the whole catalog before assigning recentlyAddedVODs (VODView.swift:175-192; measured 100 ms for 150k movies on the host Mac, more on a phone). The shelf is conditional and sits above the LazyVStack (VODView.swift:78-80), so it is inserted after the shelves are already visible. SeriesView is identical (SeriesView.swift:229-246, 79-81). ContinueWatchingRow renders nothing while its @Query still has the default [] (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:28); the request uses GRDB's default asynchronous scheduling (Requests.swift:407-420), so the first value always arrives after the first render.

**Proposed fix (finder):** (1) Compute the recently-added candidates where the catalog is loaded, off the main thread, and publish them together with the streams: in PlaylistContentStore.fetchVODStreamsData / fetchSeriesData add one query in the same read (`ORDER BY CAST(added AS INTEGER) DESC LIMIT 60`, series: lastModified) and expose `recentlyAddedVOD` / `recentlyAddedSeries`. VODView.recomputeFilter then filters those 60 by hidden category synchronously and assigns all three states in the same turn; the per-appearance 150k sort disappears. (2) While `!contentStore.streamsLoaded`, render the recently-added slot as header + `Color.clear.frame(height: shelfRowTotalHeight)` like the category placeholders (VODView.swift:435-436) so the fill-in does not move anything. (3) Give the limit-10 history request an immediate first value: `ValueObservation.tracking{...}.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader, scheduling: .immediate)` for the ContinueWatchingRow variant only (10 rows from a small table; the reader is a DatabasePool, Persistence.swift:54, so it does not wait on writers).

**APIs:** GRDB ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with .immediate (GRDB checkout in SourcePackages (ValueObservation.swift:464-487); not an Apple SDK API)

**Verifier reasons:** Recently added: Views/VODView.swift:175-192 assigns displayCategories and displayItemsByCategory synchronously, then awaits a detached filter + sort over contentStore.vodStreams before assigning recentlyAddedVODs; the shelf is conditional and sits above the LazyVStack (:78-80), so it is inserted after the shelves are visible. Views/SeriesView.swift:229-246 and 79-81 are identical. `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` (:160) makes it a hard jump. The same pass runs three times per appearance (three tasks, :157-159) and again on every tab switch or pop, but the value is then unchanged, so the visible jump happens on the first open of each tab and after leaving the inline search (:194 clears it). Continue watching: Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:28 renders nothing while the query holds its default []; Models/Requests.swift:406-420 uses `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)` whose default scheduler is `.async(onQueue: .main)` (GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487), and the row only mounts together with the shelves (VODView.swift:62-76), so its first value always arrives after the first shelf frame. No comment or history marks either as deliberate. Three parts of the fix need correcting. (a) A SQL `LIMIT 60` taken before the hidden-category filter changes results: today the filter runs first and then takes 20 (VODView.swift:183-189), so a user who hides the most frequently updated categories could get fewer than 20 or none. (b) The `!streamsLoaded` placeholder targets the wrong state: on a cold start displayCategories is not populated until streamsLoaded flips (tasks at :157-159), so the shelves and that placeholder never coexist there, and a reserved slot would itself collapse for panels with no `added` values. (c) Live TV and M3U homes only have the Continue watching part.

**Corrected claim:** On the first open of the Movies and Series tabs (and after cancelling the inline search) the category shelves render first, then Continue watching is inserted a frame or two later, then Recently added is inserted once an off-main sort of the whole catalog finishes; the shelves jump down twice without animation. Live TV and M3U homes have only the Continue watching insertion. The catalog pass also reruns three times on every re-appearance, off the main thread.

**Corrected fix:** (1) Compute the recents once where the catalog is read, inside the existing off-main read closure in PlaylistContentStore.fetchVODStreamsData / fetchSeriesData (PlaylistContentStore.swift:380-406), in Swift with the same Int(added) / Int(lastModified) rule, keeping a larger top-K (for example 200) so the view can filter hidden categories synchronously and take 20; fall back to the current async pass only if fewer than 20 survive while K was exhausted. Publish it with the streams in loadPlaylist, reloadFromDatabase and reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only:), and clear it in clearLists. recomputeFilter then assigns all three states in one turn. (2) Drop the streamsLoaded placeholder. (3) Give ContinueWatchingRow's limit-10 request `scheduling: .immediate`, behind a flag on RecentWatchHistoryRequest so WatchHistoryListView's limit-500 use (WatchHistoryListView.swift:27) stays asynchronous.

**API check:** GRDB (third-party checkout, not Apple SDK): ValueObservation.swift:485-487 `public func publisher(in reader: any DatabaseReader, scheduling scheduler: some ValueObservationScheduler = .async(onQueue: .main))`; `.immediate` exists in ValueObservationScheduler.swift:107-126 and must be started from the main queue, otherwise it traps. GRDBQuery's own docs use it inside `publisher(in:)` (Documentation.docc/Extensions/Queryable.md:29). No Apple API involved.

**Regression risks:** `.immediate` performs the first fetch synchronously on the main thread; the reader is a DatabasePool (Database/Persistence.swift:54) with the default reader count, so if all readers are busy (three parallel catalog reads at launch, PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-142) the main thread waits for one. The query itself is small and walks index_watchHistory_lastWatchedAt (Database/AppDatabase.swift:173). A top-K computed before the hidden filter can under-fill the shelf unless the fallback is kept. The recents copy goes stale after applyVODMetadata exactly as today's state does. Must not undo the off-main filtering or the Equatable shelves.

**How to verify:** Unit test for the store's top-K (order by added, non-numeric excluded) and for the hidden-category filter with fallback. Simulator UI test with history and `added` values seeded: record the frame of the first category header when the Movies tab first appears and 3 s later; it must not move. Time the first main-thread fetch of the history row on a cold start with a large catalog.

## scroll-perf-4 — Poster and channel titles have no reserved two-line block: Movies/Series shelves cut every title to one line on iPhone, grid rows are vertically misaligned, and Live/M3U shelf rows vary in height.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, Live TV home, M3U channels home, All Movies / All Series / All Channels, Category grids, Favorites
- Code: `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:49-50`, `Views/VODView.swift:350, 467, 528-534, 635-637`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:327, 439, 500-506, 598-600`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397, 443-449, 597-599`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363-377, 431-437, 573-576`

**What the user perceives:** In the Movies and Series shelves a long title is truncated after one line ('Echoes of Tom...', 'Whispers in th...', 'Modern Family...') although the same card shows two lines in the grid. In 'All Movies' and 'All Channels' a poster with a two-line title sits about 8 pt higher than its neighbours in the same row, so rows look uneven while scrolling. In Live TV a shelf can change height when a channel with a longer name scrolls in.

**Mechanism (finder):** Cards use `.lineLimit(2)` without reserving the space (VODView.swift:528-534, SeriesView.swift:500-506, LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449, M3UChannelsView.swift:431-437), so card height depends on the title. Shelves: the row is pinned to `shelfRowTotalHeight = shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64)` (PosterMetrics.swift:50; VODView.swift:467). On iPhone layoutScale is 0.5, so the allowance is 32 pt, but poster 150 + VStack spacing 8 + two caption lines 32 = 190 > 182; the text does not scale with the poster, so the second line never fits (screenshots iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png, M02-movies-home-scrolled.png, L02-live-home-scrolled.png which actually shows the Series tab). On iPad (scale 1.0, 64 pt) it fits. Grids: LazyVGrid centres cells of unequal height inside a row (default GridItem alignment), visible in iphone-light/M04-movies-all.png ('Echoes of Tomorrow') and iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png ('Morning Update', 'Cinema Channel'). Live/M3U shelves have no explicit height (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397), so the LazyHStack takes the height of the cards it has realized so far.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make every card the same height regardless of title: `Text(stream.name) ... .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true)` in VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, LiveStreamCard, M3UChannelCard. Derive the shelf height from the text style instead of from the poster scale: in the shelf rows `@ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var captionLine: CGFloat = 16` and `rowHeight = posterMetrics.shelfPosterHeight + 8 + 2 * captionLine` (used for both the ScrollView frame and the loading placeholder); remove the scaled(64) allowance from PosterMetrics.shelfRowTotalHeight or keep it only as the iPad value. With equal-height cells the grid misalignment disappears; `GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:), spacing:, alignment: .top)` is the belt-and-braces variant. Constant row heights also make the lazy containers' size estimates exact (stable scroll indicator, accurate category jump).

**APIs:** View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16.0); ScaledMetric (iOS 14.0); GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The screenshots show both symptoms. iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png: the shelf title 'Whispers in th...' is cut to one line. iphone-light/M04-movies-all.png: 'Echoes of Tomorrow' wraps to two lines and its poster sits higher than its row neighbours. iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png: the same for 'Morning Update', 'Cinema Channel' and 'Discovery Stories'. Code: Views/PosterMetrics.swift:50 `shelfRowTotalHeight = shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64)`; layoutScale is clamped to 0.5 on iPhone (:13), so the row is 150 + 32 = 182 pt while poster 150 + default VStack spacing + two caption lines needs about 190, and the shelf frame (VODView.swift:350, 467; SeriesView.swift:327, 439) leaves room for one line. The comment at PosterMetrics.swift:49 says the intent is about two caption lines, so this is a bug, not a choice. Cards use `.lineLimit(2)` without reserving space (VODView.swift:528-534, SeriesView.swift:500-506, LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449, M3UChannelsView.swift:431-437) and the grids use default GridItem alignment (VODView.swift:635-637, SeriesView.swift:598-600, LiveStreamsView.swift:597-599), which centres unequal cells. Live/M3U shelves have no explicit height (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397), so their height follows the realized cards; whether a longer name scrolling in makes the row grow or clip is not visible in the screenshots, but the equal-height fix removes the question.

**Corrected claim:** As stated. Additional detail: on iPhone the live shelf label is 58 pt wide, so nearly every channel name already wraps to two lines (iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png); the varying-height case there is the occasional one-line name.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with three details. Set an explicit `VStack(spacing: 8)` in VODStreamCard and SeriesCard (they use the default today, VODView.swift:501, SeriesView.swift:473) so the height formula is exact. Put the @ScaledMetric caption line in the shelf row views (PosterMetrics is a plain struct) and use the same value for the ScrollView frame and the loading placeholder. In the grids, reserving two lines makes every row about 16 pt taller even when all titles are short (most live grid names are one line); `GridItem(..., alignment: .top)` alone fixes the misalignment without that cost, so which of the two to use in grids is a small design choice for the owner.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8855-8856 `@available(iOS 16.0, ...) func lineLimit(_ limit: Int, reservesSpace: Bool) -> some View`. SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12146-12152 `@available(iOS 14.0, ...) @propertyWrapper public struct ScaledMetric<Value>` with `init(wrappedValue: Value, relativeTo textStyle: Font.TextStyle)`. SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `@available(iOS 14.0, ...) public struct GridItem` with `init(_ size: GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment? = nil)` (:23539). All available on the iOS 18 target; no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** iPad shelves become about 24 pt shorter if scaled(64) is replaced outright (300 + 8 + 32 vs 364 today); keep the larger of the two if the current iPad spacing is wanted. Grid density drops slightly where two lines are reserved. Favorites and search reuse the same cards with an extra category line, so check those screens too. Adding a @ScaledMetric to the Equatable shelf rows does not weaken their custom ==.

**How to verify:** Re-take iphone-light/M01, M02, M04 and iphone-dark/L05: shelf titles wrap to two lines, and all posters in a grid row share one top edge. Repeat at the largest Dynamic Type size and on iPad to confirm nothing clips.

## scroll-perf-5 — Global search with a type filter puts every match into one List; with a real catalog a two-letter query renders tens of thousands of rows and re-diffs them on each keystroke.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search (filter Live TV / Movies / Series)
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:149-222, 246-248, 273-277`, `Models/DBModels.swift:29, 61, 86, 174-190`

**What the user perceives:** With 'Movies' selected and a short query (2-3 letters) on a 50k-150k catalog, typing stutters and switching the filter chip hitches: each debounced keystroke replaces a list of many thousands of rows.

**Mechanism (finder):** In 'All' mode each section shows 4 rows, but with a type filter `visible = allMoviesShown ? movieResults : Array(movieResults.prefix(4))` (SearchView.swift:154, 178, 203) hands the full result array to ForEach inside a List. A List needs every row id to build and diff its data source; the ids are `"\(streamId)_\(playlistId)"` (DBModels.swift:61, 177-189), an Int plus a UUID formatted into a heap String per row (measured 0.16 us per id on the host Mac: 5 ms per 30k rows before any List bookkeeping, and both the old and the new set are hashed on every update). The results are replaced wholesale on each query (SearchView.swift:275-277) and, on first appearance, three times because three tasks run the same search (SearchView.swift:246-248).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Page the filtered sections like the grids. `@State private var visibleLimit = 100`, reset in `.onChange(of: query)` / `.onChange(of: filter)`; render `ForEach(movieResults.prefix(allMoviesShown ? visibleLimit : 4), id: \.stream.streamId)` (ArraySlice, no copy; Int ids, unique per playlist) and append a footer row inside the List that loads the next page when it appears:

if allMoviesShown && movieResults.count > visibleLimit {
    ProgressView().frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
        .onAppear { visibleLimit += 100 }
}

The section header keeps showing the full count. Merge the three tasks into one keyed task (see the separate finding).

**Verifier reasons:** The code is as described: with a type filter the full result array goes into ForEach inside a List (Views/SearchView.swift:154-155, 178-179, 203-204), whereas the 'All' mode shows 4 rows per section. Row ids are heap Strings built per element (`"\(streamId)_\(playlistId)"`, Models/DBModels.swift:29, 61, 86, forwarded at :174-190). Results are replaced wholesale per debounced query (SearchView.swift:273-277), three tasks run the same search on every appearance (:246-248), and they rerun when the user pops back from a detail. The matcher is a plain substring test (:126-128), so a two-letter query on a 50k-150k catalog does return tens of thousands of rows; 'N more results' (:190) is the normal way into this state. What is not established is the size of the hitch: the finding measured only id construction on a Mac (about 5 ms per 30k), and the cost of a List diffing tens of thousands of ids was not measured. The screenshots (Q05-search-filter-movies.png, 12 movies) say nothing about it. The mechanism is credible and the fix is cheap, but the user-perceived stutter is inferred, not shown.

**Corrected claim:** With a type filter active, global search hands every match (tens of thousands of rows for a short query on a real catalog) to one List, recomputes it on each debounced keystroke, three times on each appearance, and again on return from a detail. This is expected to hitch on the main thread, but the magnitude is unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: page the filtered sections with `@State visibleLimit = 100`, reset on query or filter change, `ForEach(results.prefix(allShown ? visibleLimit : 4), id: \.stream.streamId)` (series: `\.series.seriesId`), and a footer row that raises the limit on appear; the section header keeps the full count and playLive keeps using the full liveResults for the queue (:283-305). Give the footer ProgressView a fresh `.id` per page, since a reused spinner row in a List can stop animating. Merge the three tasks into one keyed task so a re-appearance does not search three times.

**API check:** No new API. ForEach over an ArraySlice with an explicit id key path and onAppear on a List row are existing iOS 13+ SwiftUI; nothing iOS 26-specific.

**Regression risks:** Int ids are unique only within one playlist, which holds here because search is per playlist (SearchView.swift:4). The 'more results' count and section totals must keep using the full arrays. Scroll position in the results list resets when the limit is reset on a new query, which matches today's behaviour.

**How to verify:** On a device with a 50k+ catalog (or a scaled fixture): select Movies, type a two-letter query, and record main-thread hangs in Instruments (Hangs / SwiftUI template) per keystroke and when tapping the filter chip, before and after. In a UI test, XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric while scrolling the filtered results. A hang above about 50 ms per update before the fix would confirm the severity.

## scroll-perf-6 — Each shelf prefetches 32 posters when it appears and never cancels them, so a vertical fling queues thousands of downloads for shelves already gone and, on iPad, overflows the image cache.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, Live TV home
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:395-398, 468-487`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:372-374, 440-459`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:333-335, 398-416`, `Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift:7-41`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:26-29`

**What the user perceives:** After a fast scroll through the home shelves the posters of the shelf you stop at arrive late, and when you scroll back up posters you already saw show placeholders again.

**Mechanism (finder):** Every shelf row calls ListImagePrefetch.start for the first 32 items in `.onAppear` (VODView.swift:468-470, 476-487; same in Series and Live). start() never has a matching stop: ListImagePrefetch exposes no stop and Nuke's prefetcher keeps every request until it finishes (ImagePrefetcher.swift:105-143; stopPrefetching exists at :174-194 but is not called). A fling past 100 shelves queues about 3,200 requests behind 3 concurrent slots; with dead or slow icon hosts each can take up to the 10 s request timeout (CachedImage.swift:21). The prefetch is also along the wrong axis for the main gesture: it warms cards 5-32 of the shelf that is already visible, not the first cards of the shelves about to scroll in. Memory: a shelf poster decodes to 200x300 px (240 KB) on iPhone and 400x600 px (0.92 MB) on iPad; 32 per shelf is 7 MB / 29 MB, so the 150 MB / 1500-entry cache (CachedImage.swift:28-29) holds about 20 shelves of prefetch on iPhone and about 5 on iPad, after which LRU eviction drops posters that were on screen a moment ago.

**Proposed fix (finder):** (1) Add `ListImagePrefetch.stop(urls:width:height:contentMode:loadProfile:)` that builds the same requests and calls `prefetcher.stopPrefetching(with:)`; call it from the shelf's `.onDisappear`. (2) Size the batch to what a swipe can reach instead of a constant 32: `Int(ceil(UIScreen.main.bounds.width / (posterWidth + 14))) * 2`. (3) Prefetch ahead vertically: in the parent ForEach add `.onAppear { prefetchHead(ofRowsAfter: category.id) }` that warms the first screenful of the next two categories (index looked up in a [String: Int] built once in recomputeFilter). Request construction stays in CachedImage.request so cache keys keep matching.

**APIs:** Nuke ImagePrefetcher.stopPrefetching(with:) (Nuke 13 checkout (Prefetching/ImagePrefetcher.swift:174); not an Apple SDK API)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:395-398,468-487, Views/SeriesView.swift:372-374,440-459, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:333-335,398-416, Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift:1-42, Views/CachedImage.swift:19-37,75-80,125-130 and Nuke 13.0.1 (Prefetching/ImagePrefetcher.swift, Internal/TaskQueue.swift, Caching/ImageCache.swift:107-117, Pipeline/ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:166-178).

What holds:
- Every shelf row calls ListImagePrefetch.start for the first 32 items in .onAppear, and nothing in the app ever calls stopPrefetching (git log -S'stopPrefetching' is empty; ListImagePrefetch has only start). Nuke keeps each PrefetchTask until its request finishes (ImagePrefetcher.swift:123-143).
- The 32 is not a tuned value: git log -S'prefetchHeadCount' only shows the initial import and the monorepo move, and there is no comment defending it. The screenshot iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png shows about 3.4 posters per shelf, so about 10x the visible set is prefetched per shelf.
- Cache maths reproduced: shelf poster is scaled(200)x scaled(300) pt with layoutScale 0.5 on iPhone and 1.0 on iPad (PosterMetrics.swift), decode scale capped at 2 (CachedImage.swift:129), cost = bytesPerRow*height (ImageCache.swift:107-117): 200x300 px = 240 KB on iPhone, 400x600 px = 0.92 MB on iPad. 32 per shelf = 7.7 MB / 29 MB against a 150 MB limit (CachedImage.swift:28): about 19 shelves on iPhone, about 5 on iPad. No Nuke dataCache is configured (only URLCache), so an evicted poster needs a URLCache read plus a new decode, which shows the placeholder again.

What is overstated:
- "Posters of the shelf you stop at arrive late" behind 3,200 queued requests. Nuke's TaskQueue is priority-bucketed (TaskQueue.swift:10-11: highest priority dequeued first, FIFO within a priority), prefetch requests are forced to .low (ImagePrefetcher.swift:37,112-117) and LazyImage requests are .normal. Stale prefetches therefore never sit in front of visible posters. The real interference is bounded: at most 3 non-preemptible in-flight prefetches (maxConcurrentRequestCount 3) holding 3 of the 6 data-loading slots and up to 3 of the 4 per-host connections for up to the 10 s timeout, plus the single decode lane (imageDecodingQueue = 1).
- So the perceivable part is (a) on iPad, placeholders reappearing after scrolling back about 5 shelves, and (b) minutes of wasted download/decode work after a long fling (3,200 requests at 3 concurrent). On iPhone the eviction needs about 20 shelves.
- The M3U home shelf is a different scheme (6-item warmup plus 10-ahead per card, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:313-318,373-381), also never stopped but far smaller; the finding's file list does not cover it.

**Corrected claim:** Each Xtream home shelf (Movies, Series, Live) prefetches its first 32 images on appear and never cancels them. Visible posters are not queued behind those requests (prefetch is .low in a priority queue), but up to 3 in-flight stale prefetches share data-loading slots and per-host connections with them, a long fling leaves thousands of pointless downloads/decodes running, and on iPad (0.92 MB per shelf poster, 150 MB cache) five shelves of prefetch fill the memory cache so posters seen a moment ago are evicted and pop in again when scrolling back. On iPhone the same eviction needs about 20 shelves.

**Corrected fix:** Do (1) and (2); treat (3) as optional and only after (1).
(1) Add ListImagePrefetch.stop(urls:width:height:contentMode:loadProfile:) that builds the requests through CachedImage.request (same keys) and calls prefetcher.stopPrefetching(with:); call it from the same view that has the .onAppear (the horizontal ScrollView in the three shelf rows). Cancelling a prefetch only removes the prefetcher's subscription; a visible LazyImage on the same request keeps loading (Nuke coalesces).
(2) Cut the batch to what one swipe reaches: about 2 screenfuls, e.g. Int(ceil(UIScreen.main.bounds.width / (posterWidth + spacing))) * 2 (the code base already derives PosterMetrics from UIScreen.main.bounds, DashboardView.swift:38), which is about 8 on iPhone and 10-12 on iPad instead of 32. This alone removes the iPad cache overflow (5 shelves becomes about 15).
(3) Vertical look-ahead for the next two categories is a new feature, not a fix; if added it must live on the parent ForEach row (the Equatable shelf row has no access to neighbouring categories) and must be stopped in onDisappear too, otherwise it adds to the fling backlog.
Do not touch the cache limits or the .shelf no-cancel-on-disappear rule (CachedImage.swift:75-80), both deliberate.

**API check:** Nuke 13.0.1 checkout, Sources/Nuke/Prefetching/ImagePrefetcher.swift:174 `nonisolated public func stopPrefetching(with requests: [ImageRequest])` and :189 `nonisolated public func stopPrefetching()`; both exist and are callable from the main actor. :105 startPrefetching(with: [ImageRequest]) is what ListImagePrefetch already uses. Third-party, not an Apple SDK API; no new dependency. No SwiftUI API beyond onAppear/onDisappear is needed.

**Regression risks:** Two shelves that share a poster URL share one prefetch task key, so a disappearing shelf can cancel a prefetch a still-visible shelf also asked for; the visible cards still load through LazyImage, only the warm-up is lost. A smaller batch means the sixth to tenth card of a shelf is less often warm on first horizontal swipe. Request construction must stay in CachedImage.request or keys stop matching (comment at ListImagePrefetch.swift:17-21).

**How to verify:** Device or simulator with a real catalog, iPad first: scroll down 8 shelves slowly, scroll back to the top, count posters that show the placeholder again (before vs after). Debug counter: log the number of entries in ImagePrefetcher (or count ImagePipeline delegate task starts with priority .low) 2 s after a fling across 100 shelves; expect thousands before and about one screen's worth after.
