## scroll-perf-7 — The M3U group grid has neither the pagination nor the Equatable guard of the Xtream grids, and rebuilds an indexed copy of the whole group on every keystroke; the M3U shelf does the same copy each time a shelf scrolls in.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: M3U group detail, M3U channels home, M3U favorites
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:365, 373, 494-499, 514, 542-595`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:40-42`, `Views/VODView.swift:622-626`

**What the user perceives:** Opening a large M3U group (10k-50k entries are normal in the 300k-channel playlists this store is written for) is slow, typing in its search field stutters, and scrolling deep into it gets heavier. On the home screen a frame drops when the shelf of a very large group scrolls in.

**Mechanism (finder):** M3UGroupGridContent renders `ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id)` over the full group inside one LazyVGrid (M3UChannelsView.swift:579) with no visibleCount. The Xtream grids were paginated precisely because of this ('a 10k-item catalog ... froze on first load and when scrolling to the end', VODView.swift:622-623). The view is not Equatable and receives a fresh closure (M3UChannelsView.swift:494-499), and its parent holds `@State searchText` and observes M3UContentStore, so every keystroke and every store publish re-runs its body and rebuilds the tuple array: measured 3.7 ms for 50k channels on the host Mac (224-byte tuples, 11 MB), before SwiftUI re-walks the ForEach. M3UGroupShelfRow does the same per shelf materialization (M3UChannelsView.swift:365).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Mirror LiveCategoryContent (LiveStreamsView.swift:526-577): make M3UGroupGridContent `View, Equatable` with the count/first/last signature and wrap it in `.equatable()` at both call sites; add `@State visibleCount` with pageSize 90 and the existing end-of-page trigger; reset it through a single keyed task that skips unchanged input (see the pagination finding). Replace both `Array(items.enumerated())` with a zero-copy indexed view so the index for prefetchAhead stays available:

struct Indexed<Base: RandomAccessCollection>: RandomAccessCollection where Base.Index == Int {
    let base: Base
    var startIndex: Int { base.startIndex }
    var endIndex: Int { base.endIndex }
    subscript(i: Int) -> (offset: Int, element: Base.Element) { (i - base.startIndex, base[i]) }
}
ForEach(Indexed(base: items.prefix(visibleCount)), id: \.element.id) { index, channel in ... }

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:320-404,481-595 and Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:1-94.
- M3UGroupGridContent (M3UChannelsView.swift:542-595) is a plain View with a closure property, no Equatable, no visibleCount; line 579 is `ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id)` over the whole group in one LazyVGrid.
- Its parent M3UGroupDetailView reads searchText in body (.onChange(of: searchText), :504) and observes M3UContentStore (:490), so each keystroke and each store publish re-evaluates it and hands the grid a fresh closure (:494-499); SwiftUI cannot compare closures, so the grid body and the O(n) tuple copy run again.
- The Xtream grids were fixed for exactly this in 654cefc (git log -S'visibleCount'), with comments stating the cause: VODView.swift:596-599 (parent re-render forced SwiftUI to re-process a 10k view, froze for seconds) and :622-623 (one giant ForEach froze on first load). The M3U grid kept the old shape; `Array(items.enumerated())` dates from the monorepo import (git log -S), nothing marks it as deliberate.
- Size is realistic: M3UFavoritesView.swift:5 documents 310K+ channel catalogs, and a playlist without group-title lands entirely in the single ungrouped bucket (M3UContentStore.ungroupedLabel), so a 10k-50k group does not need an exotic playlist.
- Benchmark re-run on the host (scratchpad/agents/scrollperf/bench): Array(enumerated()) for 50k DBM3UChannel = 3.55 ms, 5k = 0.35 ms; matches the finding. The shelf copy (M3UChannelsView.swift:365) is inside an Equatable row, so it only runs when a shelf is materialised: negligible except for very large groups.
- The stale-closure concern with .equatable() does not bite: both closures read @State (displayItems / filtered) through self at call time, the same pattern LiveCategoryContent already relies on (LiveStreamsView.swift:531-539).
- The proposed Indexed wrapper compiles: typechecked a scratch file with the exact struct, `ForEach(Indexed(base: items.prefix(visibleCount)), id: \.element.n) { index, item in ... }` inside a LazyVGrid, and ran it on Array.prefix and on an ArraySlice with non-zero startIndex (offsets 0,1 as expected, Indices inferred as Range<Int>).

**Corrected claim:** As stated. The grid part is the real defect (no pagination, no Equatable guard, full indexed copy per keystroke and per store publish); the shelf part is a small per-materialisation copy that only matters for very large groups.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with one refinement: reset visibleCount with `.onChange(of: itemsToken)` (count + first id + last id hashed, as in LiveStreamsView.swift:555-561) instead of a `.task(id:)`, because a task also re-runs on every re-appearance and would shrink the grid back to one page. Make M3UGroupGridContent `View, Equatable` (count / first?.id / last?.id), add `.equatable()` at M3UChannelsView.swift:494 and M3UFavoritesView.swift:40, add `@State visibleCount` with pageSize 90 and the `index >= visibleCount - 15` trigger next to the existing prefetchAhead onAppear, show the trailing ProgressView while more pages exist, and iterate `Indexed(base: items.prefix(visibleCount))`. prefetchAhead keeps indexing into the full `items`, which is still correct. The shelf can use the same Indexed wrapper (M3UChannelsView.swift:365).

**API check:** No Apple API beyond what the file already uses. View.equatable(): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:16311-16312, `extension View where Self : Equatable { func equatable() -> EquatableView<Self> }`, iOS 13.0. ForEach(_:id:content:) with a RandomAccessCollection and a key path into a labelled tuple typechecks with the proposed Indexed struct (verified by compiling a scratch file against the SwiftUI SDK).

**Regression risks:** The count/first/last signature can miss a change that keeps all three (same weakness the Xtream grids accept). Environment-driven updates (EPG snapshot, poster metrics) still pass through an EquatableView, so the now/next line keeps updating. Pagination adds the 90-item indicator step the Xtream grids already have. The favorites grid shares the component and gets the same behaviour.

**How to verify:** Unit test for Indexed (Array, ArraySlice with non-zero startIndex). M3U fixture with 20k channels and no group-title: open the single group, type in its search field and scroll; compare hitches with XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric / Instruments SwiftUI template before and after. Check that the favorites grid still updates when a favorite is removed.

## scroll-perf-8 — Every browse screen attaches two or three tasks that call the same recompute, and all of them run again on each return to the screen; the Movies / Series home re-sorts the whole catalog three times per appearance.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Search results, Category detail and All grids
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:157-159, 175-192, 574-575, 833-835`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:158-160, 229-246, 546-547, 772-774`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, 508-509, 733-735`, `Views/SearchView.swift:246-248, 251-278`, `Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:18-21`

**What the user perceives:** Switching to the Movies or Series tab, or popping back to it, starts background work that competes with poster decoding for a few hundred milliseconds, so posters fill in later; the first search results arrive later than necessary and the list is replaced three times.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODView has `.task(id: debouncedQuery)`, `.task(id: streamsLoaded)` and `.task(id: hiddenIds)` all calling recomputeFilter() (VODView.swift:157-159). On every appearance (first display, tab switch, pop) all three start. With an empty query each one filters, maps and sorts the complete movie list to pick 20 recently added items (VODView.swift:180-191): measured 100 ms per run for 150k movies on the host Mac, and each run materializes a temporary array of (DBVODStream, Int) tuples, 320 bytes x 150k = 48 MB, so up to about 144 MB transient across the three. The detached tasks are not cancelled when the view's task is. SearchResultsView runs the full three-catalog search three times on first appearance and again after every pop from a detail (SearchView.swift:246-248). The hidden-category id is a Set rebuilt from UserDefaults on every body evaluation just to serve as a task id (HiddenCategoryStore.swift:18-21).

**Proposed fix (finder):** One task per view, keyed by a small Hashable value, plus a guard that skips the work when the key was already applied:

private struct FilterKey: Hashable { let query: String; let loaded: Bool; let hiddenVersion: Int; let playlist: UUID }
@State private var appliedKey: FilterKey?
.task(id: FilterKey(query: debouncedQuery, loaded: contentStore.streamsLoaded, hiddenVersion: hiddenStore.version, playlist: playlist.id)) { ... guard key != appliedKey ... }

`hiddenStore.version` (already published, HiddenCategoryStore.swift:10) replaces the per-body Set. Apply to LiveStreamsView, VODView, SeriesView, the three category detail / All views and SearchResultsView. Note for the Live home: also include a catalog revision in the key (see notes on pull-to-refresh), otherwise the accidental refresh-on-reappear that currently hides that bug disappears.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:157-215,558-589,737-739,817-855, Views/SeriesView.swift:158-160,222-246,546-547,772-774, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:22-39,105-107,278-315,508-509,733-735, Views/SearchView.swift:246-278, Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift, Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-318.

Confirmed:
- Three .task(id:) modifiers per screen call the same function, and .task restarts on every appearance (tab switch, pop), so each return runs it three times. Present since the first import (git log -S'.task(id: hiddenStore.hiddenIds' shows only the import and 654cefc); no comment marks it as intended.
- VOD/Series home with an empty query: each run does lazy filter + compactMap + sorted over the whole catalog in a Task.detached (VODView.swift:180-191, SeriesView same). Re-ran the finder's benchmark on the host: 95 ms for 150k, 27 ms for 50k; DBVODStream stride 312 bytes, so the (DBVODStream, Int) temp array is about 48 MB per run at 150k. Detached tasks do not inherit cancellation, so all three run to completion.
- SearchResultsView: three tasks, each starting three detached filter+sort jobs with localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare (SearchView.swift:246-271), again after every pop from a movie or series detail. Host timing of that comparator: 171 ms for 50k names, 525 ms for 150k, so a broad query is expensive, and the three result arrays are reassigned three times, which makes the List re-diff on the main thread.
- hiddenIds(...) as a task id reads UserDefaults and builds a Set on every body pass (HiddenCategoryStore.swift:18-21); real but tiny.
- Extra cost the finding did not mention: LiveStreamsView.recomputeFilter sets playbackModelMemo.model = nil on every run (LiveStreamsView.swift:292), so each return to the Live tab throws away the memo whose comment says it exists so that opening the player does not copy the whole catalog on the main thread (:22-25). The next channel tap pays that copy again.

Why not fully confirmed:
- The perceived effect is overstated for the home screens: the heavy work is off the main thread; on main it is three cheap body passes (shelf rows are Equatable and Array == short-circuits on identical buffers). "Posters fill in later" is plausible core contention, not a stall.
- The fix as written would regress. The re-run on reappear is currently the only thing that propagates several store changes that do not flip streamsLoaded: the scoped pull-to-refresh (PlaylistContentStore.swift:234-278 replaces categories and streams without touching streamsLoaded) and applyVODMetadata (:164-178). With `guard key != appliedKey` and a key of query/loaded/hiddenVersion/playlist, a pull-to-refresh on Movies or Series would never show its result until the query changes, and metadata fetched in a detail would never reach the shelves. The finding only asks for a catalog revision on the Live home; it is needed on every screen that gets the guard.

**Corrected claim:** Each browse screen attaches two or three tasks that call the same recompute and all re-run on every appearance. On Movies and Series home that is three concurrent full-catalog sorts (about 95 ms and 48 MB each at 150k on a Mac) per tab switch or pop; on Search it is the whole three-catalog search three times after every pop, followed by three main-thread list updates; on Live it also discards the playback-model memo so the next channel tap re-copies the catalog on the main thread. On the home screens the cost is background CPU and transient memory rather than dropped frames. The same re-run is, by accident, what currently refreshes the screens after a scoped pull-to-refresh or a metadata update.

**Corrected fix:** 1. Add a catalog revision to PlaylistContentStore (a plain Int bumped wherever the lists are replaced or patched: loadPlaylist phase 2, reloadFromDatabase, reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only:), applyVODMetadata, clearLists; it changes together with @Published properties, so it needs no publisher of its own).
2. One task per view keyed by a small Hashable: query, streamsLoaded, hiddenStore.version, playlist id, activePlaylistId, catalog revision. Keep reading the hidden Set inside the recompute, not in body.
3. Guard with `appliedKey`, and set appliedKey only after the result was assigned (the recompute returns early on Task.isCancelled, e.g. VODView.swift:212; setting it earlier would leave a cancelled run marked as done).
4. Apply to LiveStreamsView, VODView, SeriesView, the category detail and All views, and SearchResultsView. In LiveStreamsView clear playbackModelMemo only when the key really changed.
5. Optional: memoise the recently-added list separately so a metadata-only revision does not re-sort the catalog.
This also fixes the stale shelves after pull-to-refresh instead of merely keeping the accident alive.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5160-5166: `@available(iOS 15.0, ...) extension View { @inlinable nonisolated public func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) -> some View where T : Equatable }`. A Hashable struct key typechecks (compiled a scratch file with the proposed FilterKey). HiddenCategoryStore.version is `@Published private(set) var version: Int` (HiddenCategoryStore.swift:10) and is already used as a task id at SearchView.swift:247.

**Regression risks:** Any store mutation that is not reflected in the key becomes invisible on these screens: missing the revision bump in one of the five mutation sites reproduces the stale-after-refresh bug permanently instead of until the next tab switch. Seven views change. The inner grids (VODCategoryContent and siblings) have their own three-task pattern that also resets visibleCount on reappear; that belongs to the pagination finding and must be changed consistently.

**How to verify:** os_signpost or a debug counter around recomputeFilter / runSearch: one tab switch should log one run on first display and none on return; a pop from a detail none (one if metadata was just fetched). Then the regression checks: pull-to-refresh on Movies, Series and Live must update the shelves without leaving the tab; opening a movie whose metadata loads and popping back must still show updated data; hiding a category must still remove its shelf. Instruments Allocations for the transient peak on entering Movies with a 150k catalog.

## scroll-perf-9 — Shelves and paged grids still do O(n) main-thread work per shelf or per page: a full copy of the category for the play queue, an indexed copy of all loaded cells, and String ids built from a UUID.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home, Movies category detail, All Movies, All Series, All Channels
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:444-452, 626, 691, 707`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:590, 649, 660`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:551, 602, 611`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:11, 97, 230-234`, `Models/DBModels.swift:61`

**What the user perceives:** Mostly invisible with ordinary categories. With a very large category (20k+ titles) a frame drops when its shelf scrolls in, and deep in 'All Movies' each new page costs a little more than the last; the scroll indicator also jumps every 90 items.

**Mechanism (finder):** (a) VODCategoryShelfRow builds `let queue = items.map(\.stream)` in body (VODView.swift:447). The comment explains it replaced a per-cell copy, but it is still one full copy per shelf materialization: measured 0.65 ms per 5k and 6.2 ms per 50k on the host Mac (312-byte elements), only to be captured by NavigationLink destinations that are almost never opened. (b) The grids render `Array(displayItems.prefix(visibleCount).enumerated())` (VODView.swift:691, SeriesView.swift:649, LiveStreamsView.swift:602): a new 336-byte-per-element array on every body pass, 0.45 ms at 5k loaded cells and 4.5 ms at 50k, i.e. every page append and every watch-progress change. (c) The VOD grid keys cells by `\.element.stream.id`, a String interpolated from Int + UUID (DBModels.swift:61; 0.16 us each), while the Live and Series grids already use the Int id. Phone numbers will be roughly 1.5-3x the Mac figures.

**Proposed fix (finder):** (a) Let MovieDetailView take the queue lazily: `enum VODQueue { case streams([DBVODStream]); case items([VODWithCategory]); var streams: [DBVODStream] { ... map only here ... } }`, pass `.items(items)` from the shelf (shares the buffer, O(1)) and resolve `queue.streams` at MovieDetailView.swift:230-234 when Play is tapped. (b) Replace the enumerated copies with the zero-copy `Indexed(base: displayItems.prefix(visibleCount))` wrapper from the M3U finding; the `index >= visibleCount - 15` trigger stays as is. Optional native alternative that removes the per-cell onAppear: drive loadMore from the scroll view, `.onScrollGeometryChange(for: Bool.self) { $0.contentOffset.y + 2 * $0.containerSize.height > $0.contentSize.height } action: { _, near in if near { loadMore() } }`. (c) Use `id: \.element.stream.streamId` in the VOD grid. Once a page append is O(1), consider pageSize 240 (divisible by 2-6 columns, fewer indicator jumps); measure first, the pagination itself must stay.

**APIs:** View.onScrollGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 18.0 (equals the deployment target, no fallback needed)); ScrollGeometry (iOS 18.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:444-452,616-626,691-707, Views/SeriesView.swift:590,649,660, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:551,602,611, Views/MovieDetailView.swift:8-11,24-27,97,230-234, Models/DBModels.swift:61,180-184, Database/AppDatabase.swift:55-66.

The three facts are true and the numbers reproduce (re-ran scratchpad/agents/scrollperf/bench on the host): items.map(\.stream) 0.84 ms per 5k and 5.8 ms per 50k; Array(prefix(n).enumerated()) 0.50 ms per 5k and 3.9 ms per 50k; String ids 0.73 ms per 5k versus 0 for Int ids. DBVODStream.id is "\(streamId)_\(playlistId)" (DBModels.swift:61) and the VOD grid keys on it (VODView.swift:691) while Live and Series key on the Int (LiveStreamsView.swift:602, SeriesView.swift:649).

But the finding itself says the effect is mostly invisible, and I agree: (a) runs once per shelf materialisation because the row is Equatable, and the comment at VODView.swift:444-446 shows it is already the deliberate fix for a per-cell copy (commit 0ab5bcd); under 1 ms for categories up to 5k. (b) runs per body pass of an already paginated grid; with 90-item pages a user must load more than 50 pages before it exceeds 0.5 ms on a Mac. None of this is a dropped frame at ordinary sizes; it is cleanup, not a perceivable defect.

Two parts of the fix should be dropped:
- The optional onScrollGeometryChange(for: Bool.self) trigger fires only when the Bool changes. If one appended page does not push the content beyond two container heights (few columns left after a filter, short last pages, large iPad container), the value stays true and paging stops. The per-cell trigger it would replace is documented as deliberate (VODView.swift:705-706: triggered from inside the lazy grid so onAppear is reliable).
- pageSize 240 has no evidence behind it; the 90 came with the fix for the freeze (VODView.swift:622-623).

**Corrected claim:** Three small O(n) main-thread costs remain in the Movies shelves and the paged grids: a per-shelf copy of the category for the play queue, a per-body indexed copy of the loaded cells, and String ids built from Int + UUID in the VOD grid. Measured cost is below 1 ms up to about 5k items, so they are not perceivable at normal category sizes; they only matter for 20k+ categories or thousands of loaded cells.

**Corrected fix:** Keep it to the cheap, safe parts:
(c) VODView.swift:691: `id: \.element.stream.streamId`. One line; streamId is unique per playlist (primary key streamId + playlistId, AppDatabase.swift:65) and every list shown by VODCategoryContent is one playlist.
(b) If the Indexed wrapper is introduced for the M3U grid finding, use it at VODView.swift:691, SeriesView.swift:649 and LiveStreamsView.swift:602 too; the `index >= visibleCount - 15` trigger stays.
(a) Only if someone wants it: let MovieDetailView take the queue lazily (enum or closure) so the shelf passes `items` and the map happens when Play is tapped (MovieDetailView.swift:230-234; also forward it unchanged at :97 and keep the [DBVODStream] callers at VODView.swift:335 and :693 working). Low value; skip unless a profile shows it.
Do not adopt the onScrollGeometryChange trigger or change pageSize.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13688-13689: `@available(iOS 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 18.0, watchOS 11.0, visionOS 2.0, *) nonisolated public func onScrollGeometryChange<T>(for type: T.Type, of transform: @escaping (ScrollGeometry) -> T, action: @escaping (_ oldValue: T, _ newValue: T) -> Void) -> some View where T : Equatable`. SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:224-225: `@available(iOS 18.0, ...) public struct ScrollGeometry : Equatable, Sendable` with contentOffset, contentSize, contentInsets, containerSize, visibleRect, bounds. Both exist at the deployment target, but I recommend not using them here. The Indexed wrapper and ForEach over it typecheck (scratch compile).

**Regression risks:** (c) none found: ids stay unique and stable. (b) none beyond the wrapper's own correctness (unit-testable). (a) touches MovieDetailView's initialiser and four call sites; a mistake changes previous/next behaviour in the VOD player hand-off. The dropped parts would have risked paging that stops (Bool trigger) and undoing the tuned page size.

**How to verify:** Unit test Indexed. Instruments Time Profiler on device while paging All Movies past 5k cells and while a 20k category shelf scrolls in: look for Array.init/enumerated and String interpolation frames under the grid body before and after. Expect no visible difference at ordinary sizes.

## scroll-perf-10 — A home shelf contains its whole category (thousands of cards in one horizontal row) instead of a capped preview with a 'See all' end tile.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels home
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:448-466`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:420-438`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363-377`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should home shelves be capped (about 30 items plus a 'See all' tile) like Apple's TV / App Store, or keep the full category scrollable in place? This changes browsing behaviour, not just performance.

**What the user perceives:** A shelf scrolls sideways through 5,000 posters with no end in sight and no indicator; the natural gesture in Apple's TV and App Store is a short shelf that ends in 'See All', with the full list one tap away (the category header already leads there).

**Mechanism (finder):** `ForEach(items)` over the full category inside the LazyHStack (VODView.swift:450). This is also what makes the per-shelf costs scale with category size (queue copy, 32-item prefetch that can never cover the row, Equatable compare when buffers differ: 0.69 ms per 5k measured).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Render `items.prefix(30)` and append a trailing 'See all (N)' card that pushes the existing category detail view; keep the play queue for a card opened from the shelf as the full category (resolved lazily, see the O(n) finding) so previous/next behaviour does not change. Per-shelf work becomes O(30) regardless of catalog size.

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:444-470, Views/SeriesView.swift:420-441, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-401, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363-381 and looked at shots/iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png.

The code fact is right: every home shelf does ForEach over the whole category inside a LazyHStack, with no cap. It is lazy, so this is not a performance defect by itself; the per-shelf O(n) costs it feeds (queue copy, Equatable compare on differing buffers) are sub-millisecond up to about 5k (see scroll-perf-9, benchmark re-run: 0.59 ms per 5k for the compare). So this is a native-feel and product question, as the finding's decision_needed says, not a fluidity fix.

Corrections to the fix:
1. The home search filters the shelves in place: with a query, displayItemsByCategory holds only the matches (VODView.swift:197-214, same in Series, Live and M3U), while the shelf header opens the unfiltered category (VODCategoryDetailView(playlist:category:), VODView.swift:418-419). Capping at 30 in that mode would hide matches with no way to reach them. The cap may only apply when the query is empty.
2. Apple's TV, Music and App Store shelves put the full list behind the header (title with chevron / See All). That header link already exists on every shelf here (visible in the screenshot: "Action >"). A trailing tile is an extra, not the system pattern.
3. "See all (N)" needs a new format string in ten languages, in the files that hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys. A plain tile can reuse `category.see_all`, which already exists in all ten Localizable.strings and is currently unused in Swift, so the .strings files need not be touched.
4. Live TV and M3U shelves are used to pick a channel directly from the home screen; capping them changes how people zap far more than it does for posters. That part is clearly the owner's call.

**Corrected claim:** Home shelves render the entire category in one horizontal lazy row instead of a short preview. This is a browsing-pattern difference from Apple's shelf design (finite shelf, full list behind the header), with only minor performance relevance because the row is lazy; the header link to the full category already exists.

**Corrected fix:** Product decision first. If the owner wants capped shelves: render `items.prefix(N)` (N about 30) only while the home query is empty; keep full filtered results in search mode. Keep the play queue as the full category (VODView queue stays items.map(\.stream) or the lazy variant; Live already uses the screen-wide playback model). Rely on the existing header chevron for the full list; if a trailing tile is wanted, label it with the existing `category.see_all` key and push the same category detail view the header pushes. Consider applying it to Movies and Series only and leaving Live TV / M3U channel shelves uncapped. If the owner prefers the current behaviour: none.

**API check:** No new API: Collection.prefix and NavigationLink, both already used in these files. Localization key `category.see_all` is present once in each of the ten Localization/*.lproj/Localizable.strings (en: "See All") and has no Swift call site today.

**Regression risks:** Hidden search matches if the cap is applied while a query is active. Changed channel-browsing habit on Live TV and M3U home. The shelf prefetch (first 32 items) and the M3U per-card look-ahead would reach past the cap unless trimmed. A "See all (N)" label would add keys to the .strings files that carry the owner's uncommitted tip-jar keys; reusing category.see_all avoids that.

**How to verify:** Owner decision on the pattern. Then a UI test: shelf of a 100-item category ends after N cards (plus tile if chosen) with an empty query; with a home search that matches more than N items in one category every match is still reachable; the header and the tile open the same category grid; previous/next in the movie player still walks the full category.

## scroll-perf-11 — History cards load their images with the 'standard' profile inside scrolling containers, against the rule written in CachedImage, and search rows clip their thumbnail twice.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Watch history list, Continue watching row, Search results
- Code: `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77`, `Views/SearchView.swift:317-318`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:41-51, 80, 87-93`

**What the user perceives:** In the history grid (up to 500 items) thumbnails fade in one by one while scrolling and ones you scrolled past start loading again; small, but it reads as pop-in next to the other grids.

**Mechanism (finder):** CachedImage documents 'use grid or shelf while scrolling a list/grid' (CachedImage.swift:41) because `.standard` cancels the request on disappear (:80) and puts an easeIn animation on every transaction of the cell (:87-93). HistoryCardGridItem and HistoryCard omit loadProfile and so get `.standard` (WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169, ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77). ResultRow applies a second clipShape on top of the one CachedImage already applies (SearchView.swift:317-318).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Pass `loadProfile: .grid` in HistoryCardGridItem and `.shelf` in HistoryCard; in ResultRow pass `cornerRadius: 6` to CachedImage and drop the extra `.clipShape`.

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read all four files and Nuke's LazyImage/FetchImage.

What holds:
- Views/CachedImage.swift:41-51 documents the rule (use grid/shelf while scrolling a list/grid; standard = single/header, cancel on leaving view). :80 applies `.onDisappear(loadProfile == .standard ? .cancel : nil)`, :87-93 forces `.easeIn(duration: 0.12)` on every transaction through the image subtree for `.standard` and nil otherwise. The comment at :75-79 (added in 0ab5bcd) says no-cancel for grid/shelf is deliberate.
- Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169 (HistoryCardGridItem, inside the LazyVGrid at :66-75, query limit 500 at :27) and Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77 (HistoryCard) omit loadProfile and get `.standard`. Every other scrolling call site passes .grid/.shelf (DownloadsView:241, SearchView:317, EPGGuideRowViews:148, SeriesView:1399, the shelf/grid cards via imageLoadProfile). History shows no deliberate choice: neither 0ab5bcd nor later commits touched these two call sites' profile; they are simply leftovers from the original import (d2489f9).
- Views/SearchView.swift:317-318 does clip twice (CachedImage's own clip at CachedImage.swift:82 with default radius 8, then radius 6 outside).

What needs correcting:
1. 'Ones you scrolled past start loading again' is overstated. Nuke LazyImage.swift:173-181 -> FetchImage.cancel() (FetchImage.swift:229-236) only cancels an in-flight task and keeps a displayed image; on reappear load() (FetchImage.swift:103-129) does reset() plus a synchronous memory-cache hit in the same tick. Only cells whose request was still in flight when they left the viewport (fast fling, slow panel image host, 4 connections per host at CachedImage.swift:20) restart. Already loaded thumbnails do not reload.
2. The perception is described backwards. `.standard` gives a 0.12 s fade; the other grids hard-cut (animation nil). After the fix history thumbnails will hard-cut like every other grid: consistent, but not 'less pop-in'. The real gain is no cancel/restart churn on scroll-back plus consistency.
3. ContinueWatchingRow: the cards live in a non-lazy HStack (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:46-47, max 10 items at :22). In Live/Movies/Series the row is a direct eager child of the ScrollView, outside the LazyVStack (LiveStreamsView.swift:212-213, VODView.swift:64-65, SeriesView.swift:65-66), so onDisappear never fires while scrolling; cancellation only happens on push/tab switch. Only M3UChannelsView.swift:153-157 hosts it inside a LazyVStack. So for this surface the change is consistency only, with essentially no perceptible effect.
4. Search rows: the outer radius-6 clip is a visual no-op, because the inner radius-8 shape is contained in it; the effective radius today is 8. The proposed fix (cornerRadius: 6) therefore changes the look from 8 to 6 for square logos and placeholders. For portrait posters nothing changes: contentMode is .fit, the image is letterboxed inside 44x44 and shows square corners (visible in shots/iphone-light/Q03-search-results-mi.png). The cost of one redundant clip per lazy List row is not perceptible; this is code tidiness, not fluidity.

The cache key is identical for standard/shelf/grid (CachedImage.swift:125-130), so switching profile causes no re-download or re-decode and does not disturb ListImagePrefetch keys.

**Corrected claim:** HistoryCardGridItem (history grid, up to 500 items in a LazyVGrid) and HistoryCard (continue-watching row) use the default `.standard` image profile, against the rule documented in CachedImage. In the history grid this cancels in-flight thumbnail requests when a cell leaves the viewport, so on a fast scroll with a slow image host the cells you scroll back to must restart their download, and thumbnails fade in over 0.12 s while every other grid hard-cuts. Thumbnails that already loaded are not reloaded. In the continue-watching row (non-lazy, max 10 cards, eager on the Xtream tabs) the effect is practically nil outside the M3U home; it is a consistency fix. In search rows the extra `.clipShape(cornerRadius: 6)` is redundant and has no visual effect (effective radius is the inner 8); it is tidiness, not a perceptible performance issue.

**Corrected fix:** Add `loadProfile: .grid` to the CachedImage call in HistoryCardGridItem (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:162-169) and `loadProfile: .shelf` in HistoryCard (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-77). In ResultRow (Views/SearchView.swift:317-318) just delete the outer `.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6))`, which keeps today's rendering (radius 8). Passing `cornerRadius: 6` instead is an optional visual change (8 -> 6 on square logos and placeholders), not a performance fix. No availability gating needed; nothing here is iOS 26-only.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. In-repo: `CachedImage` memberwise init has `loadProfile: ImageLoadProfile = .standard` as its last parameter (Views/CachedImage.swift:54-60), and `ImageLoadProfile` has `.standard/.shelf/.grid/.high` (:42-51), so appending `loadProfile: .grid` / `.shelf` after `iconName:` compiles. Nuke (checked-out source): `LazyImage.onDisappear(_ behavior: DisappearBehavior?)` with default `.cancel` (Sources/NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:27, 124-126); `FetchImage.cancel()` keeps the displayed image (Sources/NukeUI/FetchImage.swift:228-236); `FetchImage.load` does a synchronous memory-cache lookup (:120-129).

**Regression risks:** History and continue-watching thumbnails lose the 0.12 s fade and appear with a hard cut, like every other shelf and grid. Without cancel-on-disappear, a fast fling through a long history keeps requests alive until the lazy cell is torn down (FetchImage.deinit cancels), which is the same deliberate behaviour as the other grids (comment at CachedImage.swift:75-79). Cache keys are unchanged, so no extra downloads. If `cornerRadius: 6` is chosen for search rows, square channel logos and placeholders get a slightly smaller radius. Does not touch the tip-jar work, the player files, or any earlier performance work.

**How to verify:** Device or simulator with a history of 200+ entries and a throttled network (Network Link Conditioner, e.g. 3G): fling to the bottom of the history grid, scroll back up, and compare before/after how many cells are still placeholders (before: cells cancelled mid-flight restart; after: they completed in the background). Optionally log ImageTask starts via `ImagePipeline.Configuration` delegate or Nuke's `onStart` to count restarted requests per URL. Search row: screenshot a live-channel result with a square logo before/after to confirm the radius is unchanged when only the outer clip is removed.

## movies-browse-detail-1 — Opening a film without cached metadata swaps the detail screen to a full-screen spinner after one frame of content, and a failed get_vod_info leaves the film unplayable.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:14, 73-82, 99-121, 143-146, 268-312`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:26-32, 46-73`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:87-93, 138-147`, `Database/MockFixture.swift:131`

**What the user perceives:** On first open of any film the hero slides in, then the whole screen is replaced by a centred spinner ('Loading movie info...') until the panel answers (often 0.5-5 s), then the content pops back with genre chips and plot. If the request fails or times out, the screen shows only a red error and 'Try again': no Play, no Download, although the stream URL is already known. When the backdrop URL arrives the hero flips to a grey box with a large film glyph, then the backdrop pops in without a fade.

**Mechanism (finder):** isLoading starts false (MovieDetailView.swift:14), so the first frame renders contentScroll from list data. The .task at :99-103 calls fetchMovieInfo, which sets isLoading = true (:269); the branch at :74 then shows ProgressView instead of content. On failure the branch at :77 shows errorView (:106-121) and nothing else, although playback needs only streamId and containerExtension (:143-146, :242-247). When metadata lands, backdropURL becomes non-nil, DetailHero changes the URL, drops blur and opacity at once (DetailComponents.swift:61-62) and CachedImage shows its placeholder (CachedImage.swift:138-147, glyph is 0.28 x 380 pt) until the image loads; the .high profile disables animation (CachedImage.swift:87-93). The demo fixture has metadataLoaded: true (MockFixture.swift:131), so the screenshots never hit this path.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Always render contentScroll; make metadata a progressive enhancement.
1) MovieDetailView.body: remove the spinner and error branches. Inside contentScroll, after the action bar and download button:
   if isLoading && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded { DetailPlotBlock(plot: placeholderText).redacted(reason: .placeholder) }
   else if let errorMessage, !currentMovie.metadataLoaded { HStack { Text(errorMessage).font(.footnote).foregroundStyle(.secondary); Button(L("common.try_again")) { Task { await fetchMovieInfo() } } } }
2) Move GenreChipRow (:130) below the action bar and download button so late metadata never moves the Play button; add .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: currentMovie.metadataLoaded) on the content VStack.
3) DetailHero.backdropLayer: keep the blurred poster as a permanent base layer and draw the real backdrop on top only once loaded (a LazyImage whose content is the image with .transition(.opacity) and no placeholder, or a new showsPlaceholder: Bool = true parameter on CachedImage), so the hero cross-fades.
No iOS 26 API involved; identical on iOS 18.

**APIs:** View.redacted(reason:) (iOS 14+ (present in SwiftUICore interface)); View.animation(_:value:) (iOS 13+)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/MovieDetailView.swift. isLoading starts false (:14), so the first body pass takes the else branch (:80) and renders contentScroll from list data. The .task (:99-103) then calls fetchMovieInfo, whose first statement sets isLoading = true (:269), and the branch at :74 replaces the whole screen with ProgressView(L("detail.loading_movie")). On any throw, :308-311 sets errorMessage and the branch at :77 renders errorView (:106-121), which has only a retry button. Play and Download need only streamId and containerExtension (:143-146, :242-247), both present in list data. The request timeout is 20 s (Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:28), so a slow or dead get_vod_info blocks Play for up to 20 s and then leaves the film unplayable until a retry succeeds.

Not deliberate: the comment at Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-163 calls the re-entry case a 'spinner flaşı' and applyVODMetadata was added to remove it. The first open still has it. metadataLoaded defaults to false (Models/DBModels.swift:54) and is set only at MovieDetailView.swift:281, so every film hits this path once. Database/MockFixture.swift:131 has metadataLoaded: true, so M07-movie-detail.png cannot show it.

Backdrop: DetailHero (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:26-32, 46-73) switches the CachedImage URL from poster to backdrop and drops blur and opacity at once (:61-62). CachedImage shows its grey placeholder with a glyph of min(w,h)*0.28, about 106 pt, until the image arrives (Views/CachedImage.swift:138-147), and the .high profile sets animation to nil (:87-93). Because the spinner branch tears contentScroll down, the user actually sees spinner, then a new hero with the grey placeholder, then the backdrop popping in.

Why partly: the 'one frame of content' detail is timing-dependent and not verified; what matters is the full-screen spinner and the blocking error. Fix step 3 as written does not work: CachedImage forces animation off for .high, and the comment at CachedImage.swift:65 says a custom LazyImage transaction was deliberately avoided. Fix step 2 (moving the genre chips) is a design choice, not a fix.

**Corrected claim:** On the first open of any film (metadataLoaded is false until get_vod_info has succeeded once), the detail screen is replaced by a full-screen spinner for the whole request, up to the 20 s timeout. If the request fails, the screen shows only an error and 'Try Again', with no Play or Download, although playback needs nothing from that response. When metadata lands, the hero shows a grey placeholder with a large film glyph and the backdrop then appears without a fade; genre chips appear above the Play button and push it down.

**Corrected fix:** 1) MovieDetailView.body: always render contentScroll; delete the spinner and error branches (:74-79) and errorView.
2) Inside contentScroll, after the DownloadButton: while isLoading && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded, show a redacted plot placeholder (a plain Text block with .redacted(reason: .placeholder), not DetailPlotBlock, which has measuring state). When errorMessage != nil && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded, show an inline footnote row with the message and a 'Try Again' button (L("common.try_again")). Play and Download stay active throughout.
3) Late genre chips must not move the Play button. Either move GenreChipRow (:130) below the action bar and download button, or keep it in place and reserve its height while loading. This is the owner's design decision.
4) Backdrop cross-fade in DetailHero.backdropLayer, without touching CachedImage's transaction: keep the blurred poster (blur 28, opacity 0.55) as a permanent base layer. On top, when config.backdropURL != nil, add a NukeUI LazyImage(request: CachedImage.request(url:width:height:contentMode:.fill, loadProfile:.high)) whose content returns the image only (no placeholder), with .onCompletion { if case .success = $0 { withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.25)) { backdropLoaded = true } } } and .opacity(backdropLoaded ? 1 : 0). Reset backdropLoaded when the URL changes. Apply the existing visualEffect parallax to the ZStack of both layers.
No iOS 26 API; identical on iOS 18. The same spinner and error structure sits at Views/SeriesView.swift:868-871, but seasons there are required content, so only the hero change carries over.

**API check:** All found in the iOS 26.0 simulator SDK.
- View.redacted(reason: RedactionReasons): SwiftUICore swiftinterface:6107, in an extension marked @available(iOS 14.0, ...).
- View.animation(_:value:): SwiftUICore:13425 (iOS 13+).
- NukeUI LazyImage.init(request:transaction:content:) and LazyImage.onCompletion(_:) exist in the Nuke 13 checkout (Sources/NukeUI/LazyImage.swift:78-86, 130-132). The proposed fix uses onCompletion, not the transaction parameter.
- CachedImage.request(url:width:height:contentMode:loadProfile:) is an existing static (Views/CachedImage.swift:102).

**Regression risks:** DetailHero is shared with SeriesDetailView (Views/SeriesView.swift:961), so the layered backdrop changes the series hero as well; it needs a visual check there, in dark mode, and with a film that has no poster (the LinearGradient fallback at DetailComponents.swift:74-83 must remain). The permanent blurred layer costs one extra blurred image per detail screen. Removing the spinner branch means hero metadata (year, runtime, rating) appears in place when it arrives and shifts the title up about 26 pt; animate it or accept it. Do not add a LazyImage transaction inside CachedImage (deliberately avoided, CachedImage.swift:65).

**How to verify:** UI test with a fixture film that has metadataLoaded = false and an unreachable host: assert 'Watch Now' exists within 1 s of the push, stays hittable during the request, and still exists after the request fails, with an inline 'Try Again' visible. Screen recording of the push on a throttled network (Network Link Conditioner, 3G): no full-screen spinner, Play button does not move when metadata arrives, backdrop fades in over the blurred poster with no grey placeholder frame. Repeat on a series detail to check the shared hero.

## movies-browse-detail-2 — Returning from a film to a category or All Movies grid resets pagination to the first 90 items, so the scroll position is lost.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Recently Added list
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:624-626, 653-668, 737-739`, `Views/VODView.swift:574-589, 833-854`

**What the user perceives:** In a category with more than 90 films: scroll to around the 300th poster, open it, go back. The grid is no longer where it was; it sits near item 80-90 with the bottom spinner, and the user has to scroll down again. Apple's apps return to the exact cell. I have not run this; the demo catalog has 12 films, so the tour cannot show it.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODCategoryContent drives recompute() from three .task(id:) modifiers (VODView.swift:737-739). A .task is cancelled when its view disappears and runs again when it reappears, and a NavigationStack root disappears under a push. So every pop runs recompute() three times, and each run ends with visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count) (:666) even though items, sort and filter are unchanged. The LazyVGrid shrinks to 90 cells (:691) and the offset is clamped. The same re-fire makes VODCategoryDetailView (:574-575) and AllVODView (:833-835) re-filter the catalog two or three times per appearance.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Run the work once per real input change and skip it on a plain re-appear.
In VODCategoryContent:
  private struct InputKey: Hashable { let items: Int; let sort: VODSortOption; let types: Set<String> }
  @State private var appliedKey: InputKey?
  private var inputKey: InputKey { .init(items: itemsToken, sort: sortOption, types: fileTypeFilter) }
  .task(id: inputKey) { await recompute(inputKey) }   // replaces the three tasks at :737-739
  private func recompute(_ key: InputKey) async {
      guard key != appliedKey else { return }   // re-appear after a pop: keep page and scroll
      ... existing detached sort/filter ...
      guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
      displayItems = result; streamQueue = queue; fileTypes = types
      visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count)
      appliedKey = key
  }
Apply the same single-keyed-task-plus-guard pattern to VODCategoryDetailView.recomputeItems and AllVODView.recompute (key: debouncedQuery, streamsLoaded, hidden ids). The off-main sort, the cheap signature and the pagination stay as they are. SeriesView.swift:625 and LiveStreamsView.swift:575 carry the same reset (sibling lenses).

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15+)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:592-740. VODCategoryContent has three task modifiers (:737-739), each calling recompute(), which unconditionally ends with visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count) (:666). SwiftUI's .task cancels on disappear and runs again on appear, and a NavigationStack screen covered by a push disappears and re-appears on pop. So after returning from MovieDetailView, recompute() runs three times with unchanged inputs and visibleCount drops back to 90 (pageSize, :626). The grid at :691 renders displayItems.prefix(visibleCount), so the content height shrinks and the scroll offset is clamped; the bottom ProgressView (:713-717) shows because visibleCount < count.

Nothing guards this: the only guard is !Task.isCancelled (:662). History (git log -S'visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize') shows pagination and the task(id:) trio arrived together in 654cefc, with no comment saying the reset on return is intended. The same unconditional reset exists at Views/SeriesView.swift:625 and Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:575. The three tasks also triple the detached sort on every appearance.

Not run on a simulator; the diagnosis rests on documented .task lifecycle semantics. The demo catalog (12 films) cannot show it.

Why partly: the guard in VODCategoryContent is right, but extending the same skip-on-reappear guard to VODCategoryDetailView.recomputeItems and AllVODView.recompute would introduce a regression. Their re-run on appear is what picks up a catalog reload that happened while the screen was covered (for example 'refresh' from the Settings tab). The scoped reload (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:234-262) does not toggle streamsLoaded, so a key of (query, streamsLoaded, hidden ids) would not change and the grid would stay stale.

**Corrected claim:** Returning from a film to a category, All Movies or Recently Added grid re-runs VODCategoryContent.recompute() (three times, once per .task), and each run resets visibleCount to 90. In any list longer than 90 films the scroll position is lost on every round trip. Code-derived, not yet observed on a simulator.

**Corrected fix:** Change VODCategoryContent only.
  private nonisolated struct InputKey: Hashable { let items: Int; let sort: VODSortOption; let types: Set<String> }
  @State private var appliedKey: InputKey?
  private var inputKey: InputKey { .init(items: itemsToken, sort: sortOption, types: fileTypeFilter) }
  .task(id: inputKey) { await recompute(inputKey) }   // replaces :737-739
In recompute(_ key:): guard key != appliedKey else { return } at the top; after the existing detached work and the Task.isCancelled guard, assign displayItems, streamQueue, fileTypes and visibleCount, then appliedKey = key. A cancelled run leaves appliedKey unchanged, so the next appearance recomputes.
Mark the key nonisolated because the target builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (VODSortOption is already declared nonisolated).
Leave VODCategoryDetailView.recomputeItems and AllVODView.recompute re-running on appear: they run off the main thread, and when the result has the same count/first/last the Equatable wrapper and itemsToken make the child ignore it. If the triple filter in the parents is worth removing, merge their tasks into one keyed task without a skip guard.
The off-main sort, the cheap signature and pagination stay as they are. The same change applies to SeriesCategoryContent and the live grid.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:) is at SwiftUI swiftinterface:5166, in an extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, ...), with the constraint T : Equatable and no Sendable requirement, so a Hashable key struct is accepted. No other API is needed.

**Regression risks:** With the guard, a re-appear no longer refreshes displayItems when the item contents changed but count, first and last id did not. That is already the behaviour while the screen stays visible. Do not add the skip guard to the parent views (stale grid after a scoped catalog reload). The scroll-to-top on sort or filter change (:719-728) is separate and stays. The combined key removes two of the three parallel detached sorts on first appearance, which is a gain, not a risk.

**How to verify:** UI test with a fixture category of about 300 films: scroll until cell 200 is visible, tap it, tap back, assert cell 200 is hittable without scrolling. Run it before the fix first: it should fail, which confirms the diagnosis. Repeat for All Movies and for a non-default sort. Also check that changing sort still scrolls to top and resets paging, and that a catalog refresh from Settings while the grid is covered is reflected on return.

## movies-browse-detail-3 — Every push of a category, All Movies or Recently Added screen first renders the 'No movies found.' empty state, then swaps to the grid.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Recently Added list
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:556-559, 578-582`, `Views/VODView.swift:616, 653-668, 677-686`, `Views/VODView.swift:815-818, 838-854`

**What the user perceives:** While the screen slides in, a film icon and 'No movies found.' appear in the middle, then the posters replace them. In a small category it is a few frames of flicker; on All Movies with 100k+ items the wrong message can stay for a noticeable fraction of a second, because a full off-main filter and sort must finish first.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODCategoryDetailView starts with displayItems = [] (VODView.swift:556) and fills it in a .task (:574, :578-582). VODCategoryContent has its own displayItems = [] (:616), filled only after a detached task returns (:657-663). Its body shows the empty state whenever displayItems.isEmpty (:677-686); there is no 'not computed yet' state. AllVODView adds a detached hidden-filter over the whole catalog before that (:846-851).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Seed synchronously where the data is already in memory: in VODCategoryDetailView.init set _displayItems = State(initialValue: PlaylistContentStore.shared.vodStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? []). This is an O(1) lookup of a shared array.
2) In VODCategoryContent distinguish 'not computed' from 'empty':
   @State private var hasComputed = false   // set to true at the end of recompute()
   private var shown: [VODWithCategory] { hasComputed ? displayItems : (sortOption == .defaultOrder && fileTypeFilter.isEmpty ? items : []) }
   Render the grid from shown; show the empty state only when hasComputed is true and shown is empty, otherwise Color.clear. With the default sort the first frame already shows posters; the off-main pass then only fills streamQueue and fileTypes.
3) AllVODView: pass an isLoading flag (included in ==) so the content shows nothing rather than the empty state until its first filter has returned.
4) Optional: when the list is empty because of a query, show ContentUnavailableView.search(text:), as SearchView.swift:241 already does.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) (iOS 17+)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift. VODCategoryDetailView starts with displayItems = [] (:556) and fills it in a .task (:574, :578-582). VODCategoryContent has its own displayItems = [] (:616), filled only after a detached task returns (:657-663). Its body shows the film icon and L("vod.empty.no_movie") ('No movies found.', en.lproj:244) whenever displayItems.isEmpty (:677-686); there is no 'not computed yet' state. AllVODView (:815, :838-853) adds a detached filter over the whole catalog before that. RecentlyAddedVODDetailView passes items synchronously (:365-376) but still goes through the child's empty first state.

Perception at realistic sizes: for a category of a few hundred films the wrong state lasts two or three frames at the start of the push, when the incoming screen's centre is still off-screen, so it is probably not visible. For All Movies with 100k+ items the child's pass maps the whole list to streamQueue and runs VODFileType.available over it (Models/VODSortOption.swift:80-86, a trim and lowercase per item), three times in parallel. With a persisted non-default sort (@AppStorage at :610) it also runs localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare over the whole list (Models/VODSortOption.swift:43-50). I estimate hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of 'No movies found.'; not measured.

One more case the finding missed: a shelf header is tappable while streams are still loading (the shelf shows Color.clear at :434-436), and the pushed category screen then shows 'No movies found.' until streamsLoaded flips.

No comment or history marks this as deliberate. Severity re-rated to medium: wrong message, but brief on typical categories.

**Corrected claim:** Every push of a category, All Movies or Recently Added screen renders the 'No movies found.' empty state until the first off-main pass returns. On typical categories this is a few frames and probably hidden by the push. On All Movies, on very large categories, with a non-default sort, or while the catalog is still loading streams, the wrong message is visible for a noticeable time.

**Corrected fix:** The proposed fix stands, with three additions.
1) VODCategoryDetailView.init: seed _displayItems from PlaylistContentStore.shared.vodStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? [] only when playlist.id == PlaylistContentStore.shared.activePlaylistId (same guard as :579).
2) VODCategoryContent: @State private var hasComputed = false, set true at the end of recompute(). Render from shown = hasComputed ? displayItems : (sortOption == .defaultOrder && fileTypeFilter.isEmpty ? items : []). Show the empty state only when hasComputed is true and shown is empty.
3) Addition: when nothing can be shown yet (not computed and a non-default sort, or the parent is still loading), show a centred ProgressView rather than a blank screen, since that wait can be long.
4) Addition: give VODCategoryContent an isLoading: Bool = false parameter, included in ==. AllVODView passes true until its first filter has returned; VODCategoryDetailView and AllVODView also pass !contentStore.streamsLoaded.
5) Optional: when the list is empty because of a query, show ContentUnavailableView.search(text:); this needs the query passed to the content view.
streamQueue is empty until the first pass, so a tap in that instant opens the film without a queue; MovieDetailView already handles an empty queue (:10-11).

**API check:** ContentUnavailableView.search(text: String) is at SwiftUI swiftinterface:17625, in an extension marked @available(iOS 17.0, ...). State(initialValue:) and ProgressView are long-standing. PlaylistContentStore is @MainActor (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:12-13) and the target uses default MainActor isolation, so reading the shared store in the view's init compiles.

**Regression risks:** NavigationLink destinations are built eagerly when a shelf row renders (see the comment at VODView.swift:444-446), so the init seed runs per visible shelf row; it is a dictionary lookup plus an array reference, which is cheap. Adding isLoading to == must not weaken the cheap signature compare (keep count/first/last). Rendering items directly before the first pass must keep prefix(visibleCount) so pagination is not bypassed. The same pattern exists in SeriesCategoryContent and the live grid; changing only Movies leaves the app inconsistent.

**How to verify:** Screen recording at 60 fps of the push into All Movies and into a large category with a large real playlist, stepped frame by frame, once with default sort and once with name sort: count the frames showing 'No movies found.' before and after. UI test: right after tapping a shelf header, assert the static text 'No movies found.' never exists while the first poster cell does. Also tap a shelf header while streams are still loading and check for a spinner rather than the empty message.

## movies-browse-detail-4 — Poster rows are vertically misaligned in grids when titles wrap, and shelf titles are cut to one line on iPhone although the code asks for two.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home shelves, Movies category detail, All Movies, Favorites (movies)
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:501, 528-534, 635-637`, `Views/VODView.swift:350, 467`, `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:49-50`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: One title line or two under posters, and centred (current) or leading-aligned as in TV, Music and the App Store. The fix above keeps centred two-line titles; a single line everywhere is the alternative.

**What the user perceives:** In All Movies the poster above 'Echoes of Tomorrow' sits about 8 pt higher than its neighbours, and the same happens in row four (iphone-light/M04-movies-all.png, iphone-dark/M04). On the home shelves 'Whispers in th...' is truncated to one line (M01-movies-home.png), while the same title gets two lines in the grid.

**Mechanism (finder):** The title is .lineLimit(2) without reserved space (VODView.swift:531), so card height depends on the text. LazyVGrid centres each cell vertically in its row (GridItem at :636 has no alignment), so a two-line card raises its poster. In shelves the row height is shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64) (PosterMetrics.swift:50). On iPhone layoutScale is 0.5, so the title budget is 32 pt, of which the VStack's default spacing takes 8; the remaining 24 pt fits one caption line. The comment at PosterMetrics.swift:49 says the budget is meant for two lines. The budget also ignores Dynamic Type.

**Proposed fix (finder):** VODStreamCard: Text(stream.name).lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true), and give the VStack an explicit spacing of 6.
Grid: GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: w), spacing: s, alignment: .top).
Shelves (VODCategoryShelfRow, RecentlyAddedVODShelf): replace the scaled constant with a text-relative one:
   @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var titleBlock: CGFloat = 40   // spacing + two caption lines
   .frame(height: posterMetrics.shelfPosterHeight + titleBlock)
Keep the fixed row height; only its formula changes. SeriesCard uses the same pattern (Series lens).

**APIs:** View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16+); GridItem(_:spacing:alignment:) (iOS 14+); @ScaledMetric(relativeTo:) (iOS 14+)

**Verifier reasons:** Screenshots: iphone-light/M04-movies-all.png shows the poster above 'Echoes of Tomorrow' (two-line title) sitting higher than its row neighbours, and the third poster in row four higher than the other two. iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png shows 'Whispers in th...' cut to one line on the shelf.

Code: VODStreamCard's title is .lineLimit(2) with no reserved space (Views/VODView.swift:528-534) inside a VStack with default spacing (:501), so card height depends on the text. The grid column is GridItem(.adaptive(...), spacing:) with no alignment (:635-637), so each cell is centred vertically in its row and a taller card pushes its poster up.

Shelves fix the row height at shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64) (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:50; used at VODView.swift:350, :436, :467). On iPhone layoutScale is 0.5 (PosterMetrics.swift:13), so the title budget is 32 pt; after the VStack's default spacing about 24 pt remain, which fits one caption line, although the comment at PosterMetrics.swift:49 says the budget is for about two lines. The budget does not follow Dynamic Type.

History: shelfRowTotalHeight dates from the monorepo import (d2489f9), with no later deliberate tuning. The 'Favorites (movies)' surface is code-only: M09-favorites-movies.png shows an empty list, but Views/FavoritesView.swift:32, :135-139 uses the same card and column definition.

**Corrected claim:** In movie grids a card with a two-line title is taller than its neighbours and, because grid cells are centred vertically, its poster sits higher than the rest of the row. On iPhone the shelf row height leaves room for only one caption line, so shelf titles truncate where the grid shows two lines.

**Corrected fix:** The proposed fix stands, with one addition.
- Grid: GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: w), spacing: s, alignment: .top). This alone fixes the misalignment.
- VODStreamCard: Text(stream.name).lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true) and an explicit VStack spacing of 6, so all cards have equal height.
- Shelves (VODCategoryShelfRow, RecentlyAddedVODShelf): @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var titleBlock: CGFloat = 40, and .frame(height: posterMetrics.shelfPosterHeight + titleBlock).
- Addition: the streams-loading placeholder at VODView.swift:436 must use the same height, otherwise shelves jump when streams arrive.
Keep the fixed row height. The same card change affects FavoritesView (movies); Series shelves use the same shelfRowTotalHeight and should follow.
Product decision for the owner: one title line or two under posters, and centred (current) or leading-aligned.

**API check:** All found in the iOS 26.0 simulator SDK.
- View.lineLimit(_ limit: Int, reservesSpace: Bool): SwiftUICore swiftinterface:8856, @available(iOS 16.0, ...).
- GridItem.init(_ size: GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment? = nil): SwiftUI swiftinterface:23539, struct @available(iOS 14.0, ...).
- ScaledMetric: the finding marked it unverified; it is present. @propertyWrapper public struct ScaledMetric<Value> with init(wrappedValue: Value, relativeTo textStyle: Font.TextStyle), SwiftUICore swiftinterface:12151-12152, @available(iOS 14.0, ...).

**Regression risks:** reservesSpace adds a blank line under every one-line title in grids and in Favorites, so rows look about 16 pt further apart. On iPad the shelf title budget drops from 64 pt to 40 pt, so shelves get about 24 pt shorter; two caption lines still fit. The Equatable shelf rows are unaffected: @ScaledMetric is a DynamicProperty and invalidates on its own. PosterMetrics.shelfRowTotalHeight is also used by SeriesView.swift:327, :412, :439; if the constant itself is changed rather than the two VOD call sites, Series shelves change too.

**How to verify:** Screenshot comparison of M04-movies-all (all poster tops in a row on one line) and M01-movies-home ('Whispers in the Dark' on two lines). One run at the largest Dynamic Type size to check that shelf titles are not clipped. Check a shelf while streams are loading for a height jump.

## movies-browse-detail-5 — Movie grids do not fill the width: fixed 100 pt posters float in 118 pt columns, leaving 25 pt side margins against a 16 pt title and search field.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Recently Added list, Favorites (movies)
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:635-637, 690-711, 787-800`, `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-20, 44-45`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Decoded poster size in grids grows from 200x300 px to about 236x354 px on iPhone, roughly 39% more memory per poster within the existing 150 MB cache limit. On iPad the minimum width decides the column count (200 pt gives 3 columns in portrait; about 160 pt would give 4-5).

**What the user perceives:** The first poster starts about 9 pt to the right of the large title and the search field, and the gaps between posters are about 26 pt (iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png, M04-movies-all.png). By the same arithmetic an 11-inch iPad in portrait would show three 200 pt posters with roughly 73 pt gaps; there is no iPad Movies grid screenshot to confirm it.

**Mechanism (finder):** Columns are .adaptive(minimum: categoryGridPosterWidth) with spacing 8 inside 16 pt padding (VODView.swift:636, :710). On a 402 pt screen that gives three columns of 118 pt, but the card draws a fixed 100 x 150 poster (:698-699) centred in the column. PosterMetrics derives one size from the screen's short side (PosterMetrics.swift:9-14) and never from the container width.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Compute the column count and cell width from the real container width, and feed that one size to the card and to the prefetch so the Nuke keys still match (CachedImage.swift:100-101 requires this).
PosterMetrics (pure, unit-testable):
   func gridLayout(containerWidth: CGFloat, inset: CGFloat = 16) -> (count: Int, cell: CGSize) {
       let avail = max(containerWidth - 2 * inset, categoryGridPosterWidth)
       let n = max(Int((avail + gridSpacing) / (categoryGridPosterWidth + gridSpacing)), 1)
       let w = floor((avail - CGFloat(n - 1) * gridSpacing) / CGFloat(n))
       return (n, CGSize(width: w, height: (w * 1.5).rounded()))
   }
VODCategoryContent: @State private var containerWidth = UIScreen.main.bounds.width, updated with .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.width } on the ScrollView. Columns become Array(repeating: GridItem(.fixed(cell.width), spacing: gridSpacing, alignment: .top), count: n). Pass cell.width and cell.height to VODStreamCard and to prefetch(_:). On iPhone 17 Pro this gives 3 x 118 pt with 8 pt gaps and 16 pt margins.

**APIs:** View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (back-deployed to iOS 16 (already used at DetailComponents.swift:376)); GridItem.Size.fixed (iOS 14+)

**Verifier reasons:** Arithmetic from the code: on a 402 pt iPhone, layoutScale = max(0.5, 402/834) = 0.5 (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-14), so categoryGridPosterWidth = 100 and gridSpacing = 8 (:19, :44). The grid is .adaptive(minimum: 100) with spacing 8 inside 16 pt padding (Views/VODView.swift:636, :710): 370 pt available gives three columns of 118 pt. The card draws a fixed 100 x 150 poster (:698-699) centred in the column, so the first poster starts at 16 + 9 = 25 pt and the gaps are 26 pt.

Screenshots agree: in iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png and M04-movies-all.png the first poster's left edge is at about 25 pt while the large title and search field start at 16 pt.

iPad 11-inch portrait by the same arithmetic: three 200 pt posters in 257 pt columns, about 73 pt gaps. There is no iPad Movies screenshot (ipad-light has only Live TV), so that part is unconfirmed visually. 'Favorites (movies)' is code-only (Views/FavoritesView.swift:32, :135-139); M09 shows an empty list.

Why partly: the problem is real, but the fix needs corrections.
1) PosterMetrics is computed once from UIScreen.main.bounds (Views/DashboardView.swift:38, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:17), so image request sizes are currently stable across rotation and iPad window resizing. Deriving the decode size from the live container width re-keys every poster request on each width change: the Nuke key includes the Resize size (Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift:16-20, Views/CachedImage.swift:100-101).
2) Seeding containerWidth from UIScreen.main.bounds.width is wrong on iPad with the sidebar or in Split View; the prefetch issued from recompute() would then use the wrong size and every poster would decode twice, which is exactly what the comment at ListImagePrefetch.swift:16-20 warns about.
3) The same column and card pattern is used in SeriesCategoryContent (Views/SeriesView.swift:599, :654, :734) and FavoritesView; changing Movies alone leaves the app inconsistent.

**Corrected claim:** Movie grids use adaptive columns but draw a fixed-size poster centred in each column. On iPhone 17 Pro the posters are 100 pt in 118 pt columns, so the grid starts 25 pt from the edge (title and search field start at 16 pt) with 26 pt gaps. By the same arithmetic an 11-inch iPad in portrait shows three 200 pt posters with about 73 pt gaps; not confirmed by a screenshot.

**Corrected fix:** Size the cell from the real container width, but keep image request sizes stable.
1) PosterMetrics: add the pure gridLayout(containerWidth:inset:) function as proposed (column count from categoryGridPosterWidth and gridSpacing, cell width = floor of the remaining width per column, height = width * 1.5).
2) VODCategoryContent: measure the width with .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.width } on the outer Group. Hold it as an optional and do not prefetch until it is measured; do not seed it from UIScreen.
3) Columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.fixed(cell.width), spacing: gridSpacing, alignment: .top), count: n). Pass cell.width and cell.height to VODStreamCard.
4) Decode size: derive it from a bucketed width (cell width rounded up to the next 20 pt, height = 1.5x) and use that same bucket for both CachedImage's request and ListImagePrefetch, so a few points of width change do not create a new cache key. This needs an optional decode-size parameter on CachedImage (default: the layout size), which leaves every other call site unchanged.
5) Apply the same to SeriesCategoryContent and the poster grids in FavoritesView in the same change.
Owner decisions: decoded poster size on iPhone grows from 200x300 px to about 240x360 px (roughly 44% more memory per poster, within the existing 150 MB cache cost limit), and the iPad minimum width decides the column count (200 pt gives 3 columns in portrait; about 160 pt would give 4).

**API check:** All found in the iOS 26.0 simulator SDK.
- View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:): SwiftUICore swiftinterface:6067, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient, in an extension marked @available(iOS 16.0, ...); already used at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:376.
- GridItem.Size.fixed(CGFloat): SwiftUI swiftinterface:23531, @available(iOS 14.0, ...).
- GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:): SwiftUI swiftinterface:23539.
No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Image request tuning is earlier deliberate work: prefetch and render requests must stay byte-identical (CachedImage.swift:100-101, ListImagePrefetch.swift:16-20), and decode size is capped at 2x to save memory (CachedImage.swift:128-130). A width-derived decode size without bucketing would re-decode every poster on rotation and during iPad window resizing, and fill the memory cache with several sizes of the same poster. Larger decoded posters lower how many fit under the 150 MB cost limit (CachedImage.swift:28-29). VODStreamCard is shared with shelves and FavoritesView; only the grid call sites should receive the computed size. @State for the measured width inside the Equatable VODCategoryContent is fine: internal state still invalidates.

**How to verify:** Unit test for gridLayout (402 pt gives 3 x 118; 834 pt and 1194 pt give the expected counts). Screenshot comparison of M03 and M04: first poster's left edge aligned with the title at 16 pt, 8 pt gaps. In Instruments, confirm prefetched posters are memory-cache hits on first scroll (request keys still match). Rotate the device and resize an iPad Split View while watching memory and decode counts. Capture an iPad Movies grid screenshot, which does not exist yet.
