## movies-browse-detail-6 — The watch-progress bar on poster cards is laid out at the top edge of the poster and 4 pt off to the left, not along the bottom.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Favorites (movies)
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:502-526`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:474-498, 1391-1414`

**What the user perceives:** A partly watched film should show a thin accent line across the very top of its poster, starting 4 pt outside the left edge, next to the rating badge. It reads as a rendering glitch, not as progress, and that card's poster sits 4 pt to the right of its title. I derived this from the layout code; no screenshot has watch history and I did not run it.

**Mechanism (finder):** The bar is a child of ZStack(alignment: .topTrailing) (VODView.swift:502), an alignment chosen for the rating badge. Its modifiers (.padding(.bottom, 2), .padding(.horizontal, 4) at :520-521) were written for a bottom-aligned stack: the episode row uses the same block inside ZStack(alignment: .bottom) (SeriesView.swift:1391-1412). With horizontal padding the bar is posterWidth + 8 wide, so it widens the ZStack and the trailing-aligned poster shifts by 4 pt.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Attach both decorations as overlays of the image so neither affects layout:
   CachedImage(...)
     .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) { PosterRatingBadge(rating: stream.rating).padding(6) }
     .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
        if let p = watchProgress, p > 0 {
           Capsule().fill(.black.opacity(0.35)).frame(height: 4)
             .overlay(alignment: .leading) { Capsule().fill(Color.accentColor).frame(width: max(4, (posterWidth - 12) * min(p, 1)), height: 4) }
             .padding(.horizontal, 6).padding(.bottom, 6)
        }
     }
SeriesCard (SeriesView.swift:474-498) has the same code and should get the same change.

**APIs:** View.overlay(alignment:content:) (iOS 15+)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:502-526. The bar is a direct child of ZStack(alignment: .topTrailing), so it is pinned to the top edge of the poster; nothing aligns it to the bottom. Its .padding(.bottom, 2) and .padding(.horizontal, 4) (:520-521) only make sense in a bottom-aligned stack, which is how the episode row uses the same block (Views/SeriesView.swift:1391-1412, ZStack(alignment: .bottom)). SeriesCard repeats the code (Views/SeriesView.swift:474-498).

The 4 pt shift also checks out. On iPhone 17 Pro (402 pt wide) Views/PosterMetrics.swift gives a 100 pt poster and 8 pt spacing, so the adaptive grid has 3 columns of 118 pt. The bar's frame(maxWidth: posterWidth) resolves to 100 and the padding makes it 108, so the ZStack is 108 wide. The trailing-aligned poster then sits at x 8-108 while the 100 pt title is centred at 4-104. The same arithmetic gives the shift on a 375 pt phone (109 pt columns) and on iPad.

Call sites that pass watchProgress: Views/VODView.swift:701, Views/SeriesView.swift:657, Views/FavoritesView.swift:142 and :168. Shelves do not pass it, so they are unaffected. git log -S shows the block only in the monorepo move (d2489f9); no comment marks the placement as deliberate. The newer comment at Models/Requests.swift:443-451 confirms the cards are meant to draw a progress bar. No screenshot has watch history, so this is derived from layout rules, but those rules are deterministic.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands. On grid cards (category detail, All Movies, All Series, Favorites) a partly watched title draws its 4 pt progress bar across the top edge of the poster, starting 4 pt left of the poster, and that card's poster is shifted 4 pt right of its title and of its neighbours. One addition: the episode row (Views/SeriesView.swift:1391-1412) is bottom-aligned, but the same horizontal padding should widen its ZStack by 8 pt when history exists, nudging that thumbnail 4 pt right. I derived this from the layout code and did not see it rendered.

**Corrected fix:** The original fix stands: attach the rating badge and the bar as overlays of CachedImage, .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) for the badge and .overlay(alignment: .bottom) for the bar, so neither takes part in layout. Apply it to VODStreamCard and SeriesCard. Two suggestions: put the bar in one small shared view (for example PosterProgressBar(progress:width:)) used by both cards, and use the same overlay form in the episode row so it loses the 8 pt widening. Keep the progress > 0 condition: Models/Requests.swift:449-451 relies on it.

**API check:** View.overlay(alignment:content:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3382, `func overlay<V>(alignment: Alignment = .center, @ViewBuilder content: () -> V)`, in an extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, ...). Capsule and frame need no availability check. No iOS 26 API is involved.

**Regression risks:** Low. The cards' outer size becomes posterWidth in every state, which is what the grid already assumes. VODCategoryContent's Equatable and pagination are untouched. If the bar is drawn with the proposed 6 pt insets, check that a 0.01 fraction still shows a sliver: the proposed max(4, ...) covers that.

**How to verify:** Seed one vod watch-history row (lastTimeMs at 40% of durationMs) and one series row in the mock fixture. Screenshot All Movies, a movie category, Favorites and All Series before and after. Before: the line is at the top of the poster and the poster is 4 pt right of its title. After: the bar is inside the bottom edge and the poster's left edge lines up with the cards above and below.

## movies-browse-detail-7 — The detail hero's blurred fallback backdrop bleeds past the hero's bottom edge, leaving a visible seam behind the Play button, and fades out along the top.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:35-44, 48-72, 86-99`

**What the user perceives:** For films without a backdrop (most of them until metadata loads) there is a hard horizontal line exactly at the hero's bottom, with a haze continuing below it behind 'Watch Now' and 'Download' (iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png and iphone-dark/M07-movie-detail.png, at 380 pt). The top of the hero fades to the page background under the status bar.

**Mechanism (finder):** .blur(radius: 28) is applied after the image is clipped to its own frame (DetailComponents.swift:60-61), and a non-opaque blur spreads beyond the bounds and feathers the edges. Nothing clips the hero, because the overscroll stretch has to grow upward. The gradient that hides the lower part (:86-99) covers only the hero frame, so the bleed below it is uncovered.

**Proposed fix (finder):** In backdropLayer:
   .blur(radius: backdropIsFallback ? 28 : 0, opaque: true)   // no feathered edges
and cut everything below the hero while leaving the stretch free, after the .visualEffect:
   .mask(alignment: .bottom) { Rectangle().frame(height: h * 3) }
If the 0.55 opacity is kept, put Color(.systemBackground) behind the image inside the same mask so the result does not depend on what is underneath.

**APIs:** View.blur(radius:opaque:) (iOS 13+); View.mask(alignment:_:) (iOS 15+)

**Verifier reasons:** The seam is visible in the screenshots. In iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png there is a hard horizontal line at about 379 pt, the hero's bottom (heroHeight 380), with a grey haze below it behind Watch Now that fades out over roughly 55 pt. The hero's top fades to the page colour under the status bar. iphone-dark/M07 shows the same seam more faintly.

The code matches. Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:60-62 applies .blur(radius: 28) with the default opaque: false after CachedImage has clipped itself (Views/CachedImage.swift:83), so the blur feathers the edges and spreads past the frame. Nothing clips the hero (:35-44). The gradient (:86-99) reaches full systemBackground exactly at the hero's bottom, which makes the uncovered bleed below read as a line. No comment or history marks this as intended (git log -S shows only d2489f9).

One part of the claim is wrong: 'most of them until metadata loads'. While metadata loads the screen shows a full-screen ProgressView (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:74-76), not the hero. The fallback appears after loading, for titles whose provider returns no backdrop. Series detail uses the same DetailHero (Views/SeriesView.swift:961).

**Corrected claim:** For movies and series whose provider supplies no backdrop, the detail hero shows the blurred poster as a fallback. Its non-opaque 28 pt blur bleeds about 55 pt below the hero, leaving a hard seam at the hero's bottom edge with haze behind the Play button, and it fades to the page background along the top under the status bar. The hero is not shown while metadata is loading, so it is not 'most films until metadata loads'.

**Corrected fix:** Start with the blur flag alone: .blur(radius: backdropIsFallback ? 28 : 0, opaque: backdropIsFallback). An opaque blur should keep hard edges with no feathering, which should remove both the bleed below and the top fade. The content is fully opaque (image or the systemGray6 placeholder), so the opaque renderer has no transparent areas to turn dark.

Take a screenshot before adding anything else. Add the proposed .mask(alignment: .bottom) { Rectangle().frame(height: h * 3) } only if a bleed remains. The mask sits outside the .visualEffect scale, and whether it clips the overscroll stretch (which grows upward and sideways) can only be seen on a pull-down. The extra Color(.systemBackground) layer is not needed: the page behind the hero is already systemBackground.

**API check:** View.blur(radius:opaque:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3786, `func blur(radius: CGFloat, opaque: Bool = false)`, extension @available(iOS 13.0, ...). View.mask(alignment:_:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4758, `func mask<Mask>(alignment: Alignment = .center, @ViewBuilder _ mask: () -> Mask)`, extension @available(iOS 15.0, ...). No iOS 26 API is involved.

**Regression risks:** With an opaque blur the top of the hero is full-strength blurred poster at 0.55 opacity instead of fading out; check the back and favorite buttons still read well on it in light and dark. If the mask is added, it could cut the overscroll stretch or its sideways growth on iPad. A poster with real transparency (rare) would show dark areas under an opaque blur.

**How to verify:** Re-take M07-movie-detail and S04-series-detail in light and dark: no line at 380 pt, no haze behind Watch Now, uniform top edge. Then pull down by hand on a fallback hero and on a film with a real backdrop to confirm the stretch still fills the gap, and scroll up to confirm the parallax is unchanged.

## movies-browse-detail-8 — The detail action bar uses hand-drawn buttons with no pressed state, a disclosure chevron on Play, and a trailer label hard-coded in Turkish.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:209-252, 255-271, 274-314`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:132-141`, `Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:365`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Visual identity: moving to system-styled buttons drops the custom gradient and glow. If a branded primary button is wanted, keep the look but implement it as a ButtonStyle with a pressed state.

**What the user perceives:** Tapping 'Watch Now' gives no visual response before the player appears. The button is a blue gradient slab with a coloured glow and a '>' chevron, which on iOS means 'navigates' rather than 'plays' (M07-movie-detail.png, light and dark). Restart and Trailer are grey material rectangles. In every language the trailer button reads 'Fragman'.

**Mechanism (finder):** primaryCTA is a Button with .buttonStyle(.plain) around a label that paints its own gradient, clip shape and shadow (DetailComponents.swift:241-251); plain style has nothing to dim on explicit colours. The chevron is at :226-228. Secondary buttons repeat this with ultraThinMaterial on an opaque page (:288-314). The trailer title is the literal "Fragman" (:265), although movie.trailer exists in all ten string files (en line 365).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use system button styles; they bring pressed states, Dynamic Type sizing and the current look on both iOS 18 and iOS 26 with no availability check.
   Button(action: onPrimary) {
       VStack(spacing: 6) {
           Label { VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) { Text(primaryTitle).font(.headline); if let sub = primarySubtitle { Text(sub).font(.caption2).opacity(0.85) } } } icon: { Image(systemName: "play.fill") }
           if let progress { ProgressView(value: progress).tint(.white) }
       }.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
   }
   .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large).buttonBorderShape(.capsule)
Secondary: Button / Link { Label(title, systemImage: icon).frame(maxWidth: .infinity) }.buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large).buttonBorderShape(.capsule).
Drop the chevron, the gradient and the glow. Replace "Fragman" with L("movie.trailer"); the key already exists, so no strings file is edited.

**APIs:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.borderedProminent / .bordered (iOS 15+); View.buttonBorderShape(_:) (iOS 15+); View.controlSize(.large) (iOS 15+); PrimitiveButtonStyle.glassProminent (optional, not needed) (iOS 26+)

**Verifier reasons:** Three parts are confirmed in code and screenshots.

1. The trailer label is the literal "Fragman" at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:265. The key movie.trailer exists in all ten string files (en:365, tr:365, the other eight at :397) and no Swift file uses it. History shows only the monorepo move, so this is a leftover, not a choice. It affects movie and series detail (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:140, Views/SeriesView.swift:967-976).

2. The disclosure chevron on the primary button is at DetailComponents.swift:226-228 and is visible in M07-movie-detail.png in both themes.

3. The primary button paints its own gradient, clip shape and coloured glow (:241-249). The secondary buttons use ultraThinMaterial on an opaque page (:305-312).

The 'no pressed state' part is not proven. All these buttons use .buttonStyle(.plain) (:251, :267, :284), and the SDK documents PlainButtonStyle as a style that may apply a visual effect for the pressed state. On iOS that effect acts on the foreground style, and here every colour is explicit (.white at :230, the gradient, Color.primary at :301), so it is likely nothing changes. That is an inference; I did not run it. The Dynamic Type argument is weak: the labels already use text styles.

**Corrected claim:** The detail action bar has one certain bug and two native-feel gaps. The trailer button reads 'Fragman' in every language although movie.trailer is translated in all ten. The primary Play button carries a navigation chevron and a custom gradient with a glow. It probably shows no pressed feedback, because plain style has only explicit colours to work on; that needs a press-and-hold on the simulator to confirm.

**Corrected fix:** Split it into a no-decision part and a decision part.

No decision needed:
- Replace "Fragman" with L("movie.trailer") at DetailComponents.swift:265. No strings file is edited.
- Remove the chevron and its Spacer (:225-228).

Pressed feedback, smallest change that keeps the current look: move the gradient, clip and shadow into a private ButtonStyle that reads configuration.isPressed (for example opacity 0.85 and scale 0.98), and give the secondary label the same treatment. Apply it to the Link as well.

Owner's decision: switching to .borderedProminent / .bordered with .controlSize(.large) and .buttonBorderShape(.capsule), as proposed. It compiles on iOS 18 with no availability check and gives the system look, but it drops the gradient and glow. If this is chosen, DownloadButton (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:101-123) must be restyled in the same pass, because it sits directly under the secondary row and currently copies its look.

**API check:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.borderedProminent: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:21631, extension @available(iOS 15.0, ...). PrimitiveButtonStyle.bordered: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17130, @available(iOS 15.0, ...). View.buttonBorderShape(_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:15050, @available(iOS 15.0, ...); ButtonBorderShape.capsule at :15059 carries only macOS 14 / tvOS 17 limits, so on iOS it follows the struct (iOS 15). View.controlSize(_:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6168, extension @available(iOS 15.0, ...); ControlSize.large (:6133) has only a macOS 11 limit. glassProminent: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:3447, @available(iOS 26.0, ...), not needed. Link is a struct at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:11533 (iOS 14); the interface does not show whether it adopts .bordered, so check that it renders as a bordered button. PlainButtonStyle: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8850 (iOS 13).

**Regression risks:** The L() change and chevron removal carry no risk beyond a different label. A custom ButtonStyle keeps the look and layout. System styles change the height, corner shape and colour of the buttons on both detail screens, and the progress bar inside the primary label needs a visual check on the prominent background. DetailActionBar is shared, so Series detail changes with it. MovieDetailView.swift:159-161 uses a -10 top padding to align DownloadButton with the secondary row; recheck that spacing after any restyle.

**How to verify:** Run the UI in English with a fixture film that has youtubeTrailer and assert the button reads 'Trailer'. Screenshot M07-movie-detail and S04-series-detail in light and dark. Press and hold Watch Now, Restart and Trailer on the simulator before the change, to settle whether the current build has any highlight, and after it.

## movies-browse-detail-9 — The Download button ignores taps while queued, downloading or completed; cancel and delete exist only behind an undiscoverable long-press.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail (episode rows)
- Code: `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:77-83, 145-174, 176-202`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:143-162`

**What the user perceives:** After starting a download the button shows a percentage, and tapping it does nothing. When it turns green ('Downloaded'), tapping still does nothing. Nothing hints that a long-press offers Cancel or Delete. In TV, Music and Podcasts a tap on the progress ring stops the download and a tap on the downloaded mark offers 'Remove Download'.

**Mechanism (finder):** primaryAction() returns without doing anything for .downloading, .queued and .completed (DownloadButton.swift:195-200). The only path to manager.cancel and manager.delete is the .contextMenu at :82 and :145-174.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the four derived states and the existing menu items; change only how they are reached.
   switch state {
   case .idle: Button(action: primaryAction) { labelContent }
   case .failed: Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent } primaryAction: { primaryAction() }   // tap retries, hold offers delete
   case .queued, .downloading, .completed: Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent }           // tap opens Cancel or Delete
   }
Apply .buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large) in the full-size variant so it matches the secondary buttons.

**APIs:** Menu(content:label:primaryAction:) (iOS 15+)

**Verifier reasons:** The behaviour is as described. primaryAction() does nothing for .downloading, .queued and .completed (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:195-200), and on this screen cancel and delete are reached only through .contextMenu (:82, :145-174). The two comments at :196 and :199 show this was a conscious choice ('cancel via context menu'), not an oversight, so changing it is a behaviour change for the owner to approve.

The word 'only' is wrong app-wide. The Downloads screen offers swipe actions for Cancel and Delete (Views/DownloadsView.swift:188-200).

The native-feel point holds: during a long film download the main control on the detail page is a dead tap with no visible way to stop it.

The proposed structure fits the code. The compact button in episode rows is a sibling of the tappable text area, not nested inside another button (Views/SeriesView.swift:1447-1471), so a Menu works there. Series detail has no full-size DownloadButton.

**Corrected claim:** On movie detail and in episode rows the Download button ignores taps while queued, downloading or completed. On those screens Cancel and Delete are reachable only by an unhinted long-press; they are also available by swipe on the Downloads screen. The current behaviour is deliberate per the code comments, so this is a native-feel change, not a bug fix.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the proposed switch, with three adjustments.

1. Keep .buttonStyle(.plain) on the Menu branches so the label looks the same as today, and leave the label views untouched.
2. Keep .contextMenu only on the idle Button, or drop it there; a Menu already opens on long-press.
3. Leave .buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large) out of this change. It belongs to the styling decision in movies-browse-detail-8 and should be done together with it.

Resulting shape: idle -> Button(action: primaryAction); failed -> Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent } primaryAction: { primaryAction() }; queued, downloading, completed -> Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent }.

**API check:** Menu.init(content:label:primaryAction:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7143, `init(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content, @ViewBuilder label: () -> Label, primaryAction: @escaping () -> Void)`, extension @available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 17.0, *). View.menuStyle(_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2894, @available(iOS 14.0, ...), if a style is needed. No iOS 26 API is involved.

**Regression risks:** DownloadButton re-renders on every progress tick because it observes DownloadManager. Check that an open menu stays open while the percentage updates, and that it behaves sensibly when the state changes under it (downloading to completed). A Menu label may be tinted or dimmed differently from the plain Button; the label sets explicit colours, so it should hold, but compare screenshots. Delete becomes two taps away with no confirmation, which matches Apple's apps but is easier to trigger than a long-press. The compact episode-row target is small; check it does not steal taps meant for the row.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test: tap Download, tap the button again and assert a Cancel item appears; with a completed fixture download, tap and assert Delete appears; with a failed one, tap and assert it retries, long-press and assert Delete appears. By hand: open the menu during an active download and watch for two or three progress updates to confirm it stays open. Repeat on an episode row.

## movies-browse-detail-10 — On Movies home the 'Recently Added' shelf is inserted above the category shelves after they are already on screen, pushing the whole list down.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:78-80, 157-159, 166-194`

**What the user perceives:** When the Movies tab appears after launch or a playlist switch, the category shelves show first and then jump down by one shelf height (about 220 pt on iPhone) when 'Recently Added' appears above them. The delay grows with catalog size.

**Mechanism (finder):** recomputeFilter assigns displayCategories and displayItemsByCategory synchronously (VODView.swift:176-177) and only then awaits a detached job that filters the whole catalog, builds a (DBVODStream, Int) tuple per film and fully sorts it to keep 20 (:180-191). The shelf is conditional on the result (:78-80) with no reserved space. The assignment after the await has no cancellation check, and the job is started by three separate .task(id:) modifiers on every appearance (:157-159).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Make the job cheap: sort small keys, not film structs.
   var keyed: [(ts: Int, idx: Int)] = []; keyed.reserveCapacity(allVODs.count)
   for (i, v) in allVODs.enumerated() where visibleCatIds.contains(v.stream.categoryId ?? "") { if let ts = v.stream.added.flatMap(Int.init) { keyed.append((ts, i)) } }
   keyed.sort { $0.ts > $1.ts }
   return keyed.prefix(20).map { allVODs[$0.idx].stream }
2) Remove the jump: await this result first, then assign displayCategories, displayItemsByCategory and recentlyAddedVODs together; while contentStore.streamsLoaded is false, reserve the shelf's slot with the same clear placeholder the category rows use (:435-436).
3) Add guard !Task.isCancelled before the assignment and merge the three tasks into one keyed on (debouncedQuery, streamsLoaded, hidden ids) so the work runs once per change. The work stays off the main thread.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15+)

**Verifier reasons:** The jump is real, and its main cause is bigger than the finding's mechanism says.

Primary cause: the catalog loads in two phases. Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:127-137 publishes categories first with isLoading = false (the comment says the UI shows categories immediately), and :140-152 publishes the streams later with streamsLoaded = true. In between, Movies home shows category headers with clear placeholders (Views/VODView.swift:434-436) and no Recently Added slot (:78-80). When the streams arrive the shelf is inserted above them. On iPhone that is about 226 pt (150 pt poster + 32 pt title area + header + padding). The gap is the database read of the whole catalog, so it grows with catalog size, and the dashboard restores the last tab (Views/DashboardView.swift:22), so a user who left on Movies sees this on every cold launch.

Secondary cause, the one the finding describes: recomputeFilter assigns the categories synchronously (:176-177), then awaits a detached job that copies every DBVODStream into a tuple and sorts them all to keep 20 (:180-191). DBVODStream has about twenty optional strings (Models/DBModels.swift:40-60), so at 100k films this takes several frames.

Also confirmed: no cancellation check before the assignment at :180, and three .task(id:) modifiers (:157-159) each start the full job on every appearance, including tab returns and pops. Views/SeriesView.swift:216-245 has the identical pattern.

Step 2 of the fix would cause a regression. While displayCategories is empty and the store is not loading, the body shows the 'no category' empty state (:52-60). Holding the category assignment until the sort finishes extends that wrong state from one frame to the job's duration, and it would also undo the deliberate categories-first paint in phase 1.

**Corrected claim:** On Movies home (and Series home, same code) the Recently Added shelf has no reserved space and is inserted above the category shelves after they are on screen, pushing the list down by one shelf (about 226 pt on iPhone). The main trigger is the two-phase catalog load: categories paint first and the shelf appears when the streams finish loading, seconds later on a large catalog. A second, shorter jump comes from the full-catalog sort that runs after the categories are assigned. The job also runs three times per appearance and assigns without a cancellation check.

**Corrected fix:** 1. Keep step 1 (sort small keys, not film structs), with a deterministic tie-break (timestamp descending, then index ascending).

2. Do not delay the category assignment. Reserve the slot instead: make the result three-state, for example recentlyAddedVODs: [DBVODStream]? where nil means not computed yet. While it is nil, or while contentStore.streamsLoaded is false, render a clear placeholder with the full shelf height, header included (the shelf's own VStack: header + shelfRowTotalHeight + vertical padding). When the result is an empty array, render nothing. Do not reset it to nil on re-appearance, so returning to the tab never shows the placeholder.

3. Keep guard !Task.isCancelled before the assignment, and merge the three tasks into one keyed on an Equatable value of (debouncedQuery, streamsLoaded, hidden ids). hiddenIds returns Set<String>, so the key is Equatable. The work stays off the main thread.

4. Apply the same change to Views/SeriesView.swift:216-245.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166, `func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) where T : Equatable`, extension @available(iOS 15.0, ...) at :5159. Nothing else beyond the standard library is used. No iOS 26 API is involved.

**Regression risks:** A catalog with no usable 'added' timestamps shows the placeholder and then collapses it once: a single upward jump instead of today's downward one. That is rare and happens once per load. The tie-break may change which films appear when many share a timestamp, so a test comparing against the old implementation must use distinct timestamps. Merging the tasks must keep all three triggers; a missed one would leave the shelves stale after hiding a category. Row Equatable conformances and off-main filtering are untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit test for the extracted top-N function on a shuffled fixture with distinct timestamps: same 20 ids as the current code. With a large playlist (50k+ films) and Movies as the restored tab, record a cold launch: the first category header must not move after first paint, neither when the streams arrive nor afterwards. Repeat on Series. Then switch tabs away and back and confirm the shelf does not blink to a placeholder.

## movies-browse-detail-11 — Shelf headers on Movies home render as small accent-blue links, unlike the 'Continue Watching' header on the same screen.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:314-329, 417-432`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44`

**What the user perceives:** 'Action >', 'Drama >' and 'Comedy >' are blue (iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png, iphone-dark/M01). 'Continue Watching' on the same screen is larger, bold, label-coloured and indented 20 pt instead of 16 pt. Only the text itself is tappable, a target about 22 pt tall. In TV and the App Store shelf headers are label-coloured bold titles with a grey chevron, and the whole row is tappable.

**Mechanism (finder):** The header NavigationLink has no button style (VODView.swift:315-326, :418-429). Inside a default-styled link, .foregroundStyle(.primary) resolves to the tint, so the text and the chevron come out blue. ContinueWatchingRow uses .buttonStyle(.plain), .title2.weight(.bold) and 20 pt padding (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:35, :43-44). The Spacer sits outside the link label (:327, :430), so the tap target is only the text.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Extract one ShelfHeader view and use it for both shelf types and for ContinueWatchingRow:
   NavigationLink { destination } label: {
       HStack(spacing: 6) {
           Text(title).font(.title3.weight(.bold)).foregroundStyle(.primary)
           Image(systemName: "chevron.right").font(.footnote.weight(.semibold)).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
           Spacer(minLength: 0)
       }
       .padding(.vertical, 6).contentShape(Rectangle())
   }
   .buttonStyle(.plain).padding(.horizontal, 16)
Keep the Equatable row wrappers unchanged.

**APIs:** View.buttonStyle(.plain) on NavigationLink (iOS 13+); View.contentShape(_:) (iOS 13+)

**Verifier reasons:** The claim holds. iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png shows 'Action >', 'Drama >' and 'Comedy >' in accent blue with a paler blue chevron. Views/VODView.swift:315-326 and :418-429 are NavigationLinks with no button style; the label carries .foregroundStyle(.primary) (:325, :428), so the author meant label colour and got the tint. The Spacer sits outside the link (:327, :430), so only the text is tappable. Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44 uses .buttonStyle(.plain), title2 bold, 20 pt padding and a Spacer inside the label, so two header styles share one screen. History shows nothing deliberate: every cited line dates from d2489f9, the monorepo move.

The scope is wrong. The same header block is copied into Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-369, Views/SeriesView.swift:292-305 and :394-407, and Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:337-349 (which has a trailing item count). Fixing only Movies would make Movies differ from Live TV and Series.

**Corrected claim:** Shelf headers on every home screen render as accent-blue links with a text-only tap target: Movies (VODView.swift:315-326, :418-429), Live TV (LiveStreamsView.swift:356-369), Series (SeriesView.swift:292-305, :394-407) and M3U (M3UChannelsView.swift:337-349). The code asks for .primary, so the blue is unintended. 'Continue Watching' on the same screens uses a different style: plain, title2 bold, 20 pt inset.

**Corrected fix:** Extract one ShelfHeader<Destination: View> with an optional trailing accessory for the M3U count, and use it at all six shelf sites plus ContinueWatchingRow.

The minimal native fix is three things: .buttonStyle(.plain) on the NavigationLink, the Spacer moved inside the label, and .contentShape(Rectangle()). Change the chevron from .tertiary to .secondary if wanted.

The font change from .headline to .title3.bold is a design choice, not part of the defect; pick one size for all shelves.

If ContinueWatchingRow adopts the 16 pt inset, change its card row padding too (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:55 uses 20), otherwise the header and cards misalign.

Leave the Equatable row wrappers and their == functions untouched.

**API check:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.plain: 'extension PrimitiveButtonStyle where Self == PlainButtonStyle { static var plain }', @available(iOS 13.0, *), SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8843-8845.

View.contentShape(_:eoFill:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13251, iOS 13+.

No iOS 26-only API is involved.

**Regression risks:** The plain style drops the tint highlight and dims the label on press instead, which is acceptable.

A full-row tap target sits directly above a horizontal ScrollView. It does not overlap the scroll area, so it should not steal scroll gestures.

Shelf rows are Equatable and the header only uses playlist and category, which are already in ==, so no invalidation change.

The M3U header needs the trailing count kept.

**How to verify:** Re-run the screenshot tour: M01, L01 and S01 in light and dark should show label-coloured headers with a grey chevron.

UI test: tap at the far right edge of a header row and assert the category screen is pushed.

Check that the Continue Watching header and its cards share one leading inset.

## movies-browse-detail-12 — Movie posters have no context menu: a long-press does nothing until release and then opens the detail.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies home shelves, Movies category detail, All Movies, Favorites (movies)
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-707`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:205-281`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-456`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:190-266, 315-332`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Which actions the menu offers. Play straight from the grid skips the detail screen; Download from the menu needs the same 'download while playing' warning path as the detail button.

**What the user perceives:** The screenshot taken after a long-press (iphone-light/M06-movie-card-long-press.png) shows the detail screen: no preview and no quick actions. Every poster in TV, Music and the App Store answers a long-press with a lifted preview and actions. The app's own M3U cards already have a context menu.

**Mechanism (finder):** The NavigationLink cells in VODView carry no .contextMenu (VODView.swift:334-345, :451-462, :692-707). The actions exist only inside MovieDetailView (presentMoviePlayer :190-266, toggleFavorite :315-332). M3UChannelsView.swift:446-456 and M3UDownloadMenuItems (DownloadButton.swift:205-281) show the pattern already used here: menu items as a small view whose @Query, per its own comment, only costs anything when the menu opens.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add a MovieCardMenuItems view (playlist, stream, queue) following the M3UDownloadMenuItems pattern, with its own @Query<IsFavoriteRequest>, and attach it to the three cell sites:
   .contextMenu { MovieCardMenuItems(playlist: playlist, stream: item.stream, queue: queue) } preview: {
       CachedImage(url: posterURL, width: 220, height: 330, cornerRadius: 12, contentMode: .fill, iconName: "film")
   }
Items: Play (L("movie.play")), Add to / Remove from Favorites (L("favorites.add") / L("favorites.remove")), Download (L("download.action")). All four keys exist, so no strings file is edited. Move the presentation code of MovieDetailView.presentMoviePlayer and the favourite write into a small shared helper so the menu and the detail screen use the same resume and local-file rules.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) (iOS 16+)

**Verifier reasons:** The gap is real. A grep for contextMenu under Views finds only M3UChannelsView.swift:446 and DownloadButton.swift:82. The three movie cell sites (VODView.swift:334-345, :451-462, :692-707) and FavoritesView.swift:134 have none. iphone-light/M06-movie-card-long-press.png is the detail screen, so the link simply fires on release. The shots README notes the same for Live cards, so this is app-wide, not Movies-only. All four string keys exist in en.lproj/Localizable.strings (:137, :138, :363, :424).

The fix needs four corrections:

1. **Custom preview causes pop-in.** CachedImage.request (Views/CachedImage.swift:102-123) puts a Resize(size:) processor in the cache key. A 220x330 preview is a different key from the shelf or grid poster, so it misses the memory cache and shows the grey placeholder inside the lifted preview.

2. **Stale first menu frame.** IsFavoriteRequest (Models/Requests.swift:269-290) uses ValueObservation.publisher(in:) with default scheduling. GRDB documents that default as asynchronous on the main queue (ValueObservation.swift:482-487). An @Query in the menu therefore first renders the default, false: an already-favourited film can show 'Add to Favorites', and with today's non-idempotent insert the tap would hit the primary-key conflict.

3. **'Play' is not a small shared helper.** MovieDetailView.presentMoviePlayer (:201-266) depends on view state: resumeMs from its @Query, pendingMovieDetail for onNavigateToDetail, and the playerOverlay EnvironmentObject.

4. **The menu closures are non-escaping**, so they run for every cell at body time. Anything placed directly in the closure costs per cell; the existing M3U code does a synchronous store read there.

**Corrected claim:** Movie posters (shelves, category and All Movies grids, Favorites) have no context menu; a long-press only opens the detail on release. Series and Live cards have the same gap. Only M3U cards have a menu.

**Corrected fix:** Attach .contextMenu { MovieCardMenuItems(...) } to the three NavigationLink cells in VODView and to FavoritesView.swift:134.

- **Preview:** use no custom preview. The already-rendered card lifts with no image reload. Add .contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)) for the platter shape. If a poster-only preview is wanted, build it with the same width, height and profile as the cell so the Nuke key matches.
- **Menu items view:** a small View whose init only stores values, with nothing computed in the closure. Give its favourite query immediate scheduling (a new request, or a flag on IsFavoriteRequest using scheduling: .immediate) so the label is right on the first menu frame. The cost is one primary-key read on main per menu open.
- **Favourite write:** write the target state idempotently: delete, or insert(db, onConflict: .ignore).
- **First version:** Favourite and Download only. The download item can follow M3UDownloadMenuItems.
- **'Play':** an owner decision. If wanted, pass a closure from the parent that owns playerOverlay and pendingMovieDetail. Do not use @EnvironmentObject inside the menu items.
- Apply the same pattern to Series cards for consistency.

**API check:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:): 'nonisolated public func contextMenu<M, P>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> M, @ViewBuilder preview: () -> P) -> some View', @available(iOS 16.0, *), SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9873-9876. Both closures are non-escaping.

View.contextMenu(menuItems:): iOS 13+, :9870.

ContentShapeKinds.contextMenuPreview: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4000; the struct is iOS 15+.

View.contentShape(_ kind:_ shape:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13336.

GRDB: PersistableRecord.insert(_ db:, onConflict:) at PersistableRecord+Insert.swift:34-36. ValueObservationScheduler .immediate exists (ValueObservationScheduler.swift:107-112).

**Regression risks:** Per-cell cost: the modifier and the menu view's init run for every cell in the paginated grid. Keep the init trivial so the earlier 'All Movies' scroll work is not undone.

I could not confirm that SwiftUI refreshes an open context menu when an async @Query value arrives. That is why immediate scheduling is advised. The existing M3UDownloadMenuItems has the same unverified behaviour.

An @EnvironmentObject inside the menu or preview content can crash if the environment is not propagated. Pass values and closures instead.

The long-press recogniser on cells inside horizontal shelves must not delay or steal horizontal scrolling. M3U shelves already behave acceptably with it.

**How to verify:** UI test: long-press a poster for one second and assert 'Add to Favorites' exists. Choose it, reopen the menu and assert 'Remove from Favorites' is shown on the first frame. Assert the film appears under Favorites > Movies.

Instruments (Time Profiler plus SwiftUI) on All Movies with a 50k catalog, before and after: no new per-cell body or query work while scrolling.

By hand: horizontal shelf scrolling still starts immediately when the finger lands on a poster.

## movies-browse-detail-13 — The detail toolbar reacts late and silently: the favourite star waits for the database round-trip, and the navigation title is an empty string that pops in.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:83-92, 180-186, 315-332`, `Models/Requests.swift:269-290`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:465-470`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the star gives no haptic and no symbol animation; the icon flips only after the write has come back through the observation. During a catalog refresh the star can stay unchanged for seconds. A quick double tap can end in the wrong state. While scrolling, the film title appears in the bar abruptly instead of fading. Until then the screen has no title, so VoiceOver and the back-button history menu have nothing to show.

**Mechanism (finder):** The star's appearance is bound to the @Query value isFavorite (MovieDetailView.swift:88-89). toggleFavorite queues a write and reads isFavorite inside the write closure on GRDB's writer queue (:318-326), so two quick taps can both see the old value; the second insert then violates the primary key (AppDatabase.swift:148-155) and the error is only printed. Writes are serial, and a refresh rewrites the catalog in one transaction (PlaylistContentStore.swift:465-470), so the favourite write waits behind it. The title is .navigationTitle(showNavTitle ? name : "") (:83); the withAnimation at :184 cannot animate a UIKit bar title.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Favourite:
   @State private var favoriteOverride: Bool?            // optimistic value until the query catches up
   private var shownFavorite: Bool { favoriteOverride ?? isFavorite }
   Button { let target = !shownFavorite; favoriteOverride = target; Task { await setFavorite(target) } } label: {
       Image(systemName: shownFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star").contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
   }
   .tint(shownFavorite ? .yellow : nil)
   .accessibilityLabel(L(shownFavorite ? "favorites.remove" : "favorites.add"))
   .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: shownFavorite)
   .onChange(of: isFavorite) { _, _ in favoriteOverride = nil }
setFavorite(_:) writes the target state idempotently (delete, or insert with onConflict: .ignore) and never reads view state inside the closure.
Title: always set .navigationTitle(currentMovie.name) and fade a principal item:
   ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Text(currentMovie.name).font(.headline).lineLimit(1).opacity(showNavTitle ? 1 : 0).accessibilityHidden(true) }
If iOS 26 draws a glass capsule behind the principal item, add .sharedBackgroundVisibility(.hidden) inside if #available(iOS 26, *); the iOS 18 path needs nothing.

**APIs:** ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:) (iOS 17+); View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) (iOS 17+); ToolbarItemPlacement.principal (iOS 14+); ToolbarContent.sharedBackgroundVisibility(_:) (iOS 26+)

**Verifier reasons:** The real parts:

- **Star is query-bound, with no feedback.** Its appearance comes only from the @Query value (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:88-89). There is no haptic, symbol transition or accessibility label.
- **Race in toggleFavorite.** It reads isFavorite inside the write closure (:319), which runs on GRDB's writer queue. The same file's comment at :275-277 calls exactly this a data race, and fetchMovieInfo was fixed for it. DBFavorite has no conflict policy (Models/DBModels.swift:164-171) and the table has a composite primary key (Database/AppDatabase.swift:147-156), so a second insert throws and is only printed (:329).
- **Title pops.** .navigationTitle(showNavTitle ? name : "") at :83; the withAnimation at :184 cannot animate a UIKit bar title.
- **Series has the same code.** Views/SeriesView.swift:877, :882-885, :1249-1252.

The overstated parts:

- 'Stays unchanged for seconds' needs a catalog rewrite to be in progress. Those are user-initiated only: pull-to-refresh (VODView.swift:97), settings sync (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:519) and first load. I did not measure the transaction length. Normally the write and observation round-trip is a few milliseconds.
- The double-tap window is equally small outside that case.
- M08-movie-detail-scrolled.png shows short detail pages never reach the 240 pt threshold, so the title pop only shows on longer pages.

One defect in the proposed fix: .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: shownFavorite) fires on screen open for every already-favourited film. IsFavoriteRequest delivers its first value asynchronously on main (GRDB ValueObservation.swift:482-487), so shownFavorite goes false to true right after the push. The symbol replace transition animates on open for the same reason.

**Corrected claim:** The favourite star has no optimistic state, haptic, symbol transition or accessibility label. toggleFavorite reads @Query state on the writer queue and is not idempotent, so a duplicate insert throws. The inline title is swapped between "" and the name and pops in. The lag is normally imperceptible; it becomes seconds only while a user-initiated catalog rewrite holds the writer. SeriesDetailView has the same code.

**Corrected fix:** **Favourite.** Keep the optimistic override:

- @State favoriteOverride: Bool? and shownFavorite = favoriteOverride ?? isFavorite.
- The button sets the override, increments an @State favoriteTapCount, and calls setFavorite(target).
- setFavorite captures target, streamId and playlistId as values, never view state. It deletes, or does DBFavorite(...).insert(db, onConflict: .ignore). In catch it resets favoriteOverride to nil on main.
- .onChange(of: isFavorite) { favoriteOverride = nil }.
- Haptic: .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: favoriteTapCount), attached to the screen's root view, not to the toolbar button and not keyed on shownFavorite.
- Add .accessibilityLabel(L(shownFavorite ? "favorites.remove" : "favorites.add")). Keep the existing yellow/primary colouring.
- .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)) on the Image is fine. To stop it animating on open, give IsFavoriteRequest immediate scheduling, or apply the transition only once favoriteTapCount > 0.

**Title.** Always set .navigationTitle(currentMovie.name), and add ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { Text(name).font(.headline).lineLimit(1).opacity(showNavTitle ? 1 : 0).accessibilityHidden(true) }. Keep the existing withAnimation; it now animates the opacity. Only if iOS 26 draws glass behind the principal item, wrap it in if #available(iOS 26, *) with .sharedBackgroundVisibility(.hidden). iOS 18 needs no fallback.

Apply the same to SeriesDetailView.

**API check:** ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:): 'public static func symbolEffect<T>(_ effect: T, options: SymbolEffectOptions = .default) -> ContentTransition where T: ContentTransitionSymbolEffect, T: SymbolEffect', iOS 17+, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4578-4580. ReplaceSymbolEffect conforms (Symbols.swiftinterface:579).

View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:): iOS 17+, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1981-1983.

ToolbarItemPlacement.principal: struct is iOS 14+, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:6097-6101.

ToolbarContent.sharedBackgroundVisibility(_ visibility: Visibility): @available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *), SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5789-5794.

GRDB insert(_:onConflict:): PersistableRecord+Insert.swift:34-36.

**Regression risks:** A failed write would leave the star showing the wrong state unless the override is reset in catch.

A principal item replaces the system inline title. Long names need lineLimit(1). Whether iOS 26 puts glass behind it is unverified.

Always setting navigationTitle changes the back-button title of a detail pushed on top (the next film via pendingMovieDetail) from 'Back' to the film name. That is the native behaviour, but it is a visible change.

Whether a symbol content transition animates inside a bar button item on iOS 18 and iOS 26 is unverified; worst case it has no effect.

**How to verify:** Unit test: call setFavorite(true) twice and expect one row and no throw; then setFavorite(false) twice and expect zero rows.

UI test: tap the star and assert its accessibility label flips at once.

Device: open the detail of an already-favourited film and confirm no haptic and no star animation on push; tap the star and confirm one haptic.

Scroll a long detail page and confirm the title fades. Check on iOS 26 that the principal item has no glass capsule.

## movies-browse-detail-14 — The detail screen has no size-class handling: the hero is a fixed 380 pt and the content column is unbounded.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail (iPad), Movie detail (iPhone landscape), Series detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:124-178`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:21, 35-44, 201-207, 402-403`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: On iPad, a capped single column (proposed, small) or a two-column layout with poster and actions beside the plot (larger redesign).

**What the user perceives:** By the layout arithmetic, on an iPad in landscape 'Watch Now' is a bar over 1300 pt wide and the plot runs in lines of about 200 characters under a short, heavily cropped backdrop strip. On an iPhone in landscape the hero takes almost the whole 402 pt of height, so the Play button is below the fold. There is no iPad or landscape detail screenshot; this is from code only.

**Mechanism (finder):** DetailHero is called with heroHeight: 380 (MovieDetailView.swift:126; default at DetailComponents.swift:21) whatever the size class. DetailActionBar, DetailPlotBlock and the info blocks stretch to the full width with 16 pt padding (DetailComponents.swift:206, :402-403, :426-427). The view reads neither horizontalSizeClass nor verticalSizeClass.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest change, in MovieDetailView (SeriesDetailView can follow):
   @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) private var hSize
   @Environment(\.verticalSizeClass) private var vSize
   private var heroHeight: CGFloat { vSize == .compact ? 220 : (hSize == .regular ? 460 : 380) }
   // everything below the hero:
   VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 20) { actionBar; download; plot; director; cast }
       .frame(maxWidth: hSize == .regular ? 680 : .infinity, alignment: .leading)
Use the same heroHeight in the title-fade threshold (:181) instead of the constant 240.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues.horizontalSizeClass / verticalSizeClass (iOS 13+)

**Verifier reasons:** Nothing in the detail screen adapts to size. heroHeight is the literal 380 at Views/MovieDetailView.swift:126 and Views/SeriesView.swift:961 (default at Components/DetailComponents.swift:21). Neither view reads a size class. DetailActionBar, DetailPlotBlock and DetailInfoTextBlock all stretch to full width with 16 pt padding (DetailComponents.swift:206, :402-403, :426-427).

The container imposes no width limit either: Views/DashboardView.swift:85 uses .sidebarAdaptable with one NavigationStack per tab. PosterMetrics (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-14) scales only poster sizes.

iPhone landscape is reachable: the project allows landscape on iPhone (project.pbxproj:567) and the AppDelegate lock defaults to .allButUpsideDown (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:5). With the ScrollView ignoring the top safe area (:187), a 380 pt hero fills almost all of a 402 pt-high landscape screen, so the action bar starts below the fold.

On a 1366 pt-wide iPad the Watch Now button is about 1334 pt wide and the hero is a 3.6:1 strip. That follows from the code; the exact characters per line was not measured.

No iPad or landscape movie screenshot exists; ipad-light has only Live TV. The evidence is arithmetic from code. History shows no deliberate choice (all lines from d2489f9).

**Corrected claim:** The movie and series detail screens ignore size class. The hero is a fixed 380 pt and every block below it stretches to the full window width. On iPad that gives a full-width CTA, very long plot lines and a heavily cropped backdrop. On iPhone landscape the hero fills the screen and the play button is off-screen.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed:

- Read horizontalSizeClass and verticalSizeClass.
- heroHeight = vSize == .compact ? 220 : (hSize == .regular ? 460 : 380).
- Derive the title-fade threshold from it (heroHeight - 140) instead of the literal 240 at :181.
- Cap the column below the hero with .frame(maxWidth: hSize == .regular ? 680 : .infinity, alignment: .leading).

One correction: a leading-aligned 680 pt column leaves the right half of an iPad empty and hard against the left edge. Either keep it leading so it lines up with the hero's poster and title (also at 16 pt), or centre both the column and the hero overlay. That alignment, and one column versus two, is the owner's decision.

Apply the same change to SeriesDetailView (SeriesView.swift:961) in the same pass, since it shares DetailHero and the blocks.

**API check:** EnvironmentValues.horizontalSizeClass: 'public var horizontalSizeClass: UserInterfaceSizeClass?', @available(iOS 13.0, *), SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:17116-17118.

EnvironmentValues.verticalSizeClass: iOS 13+, SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:17132-17134.

No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** The hero backdrop request size follows heroHeight (DetailComponents.swift:51-59), so a rotation changes the Nuke key and reloads the backdrop once. That is acceptable.

The series detail's season bar and EpisodesPanel need the same width treatment or they will look inconsistent beside a capped column.

A compact-height hero of 220 must still fit the poster overlay. It does: about 88 pt on phones.

**How to verify:** Screenshots of the movie and series detail on an iPad simulator in portrait and landscape, and on iPhone in landscape, before and after.

Expect the play button visible without scrolling in iPhone landscape, plot lines of readable length on iPad, and the title fade triggering as the hero leaves the screen.

## movies-browse-detail-15 — The full-screen poster viewer slides up as a plain cover, starts with a spinner on black, and places its close button with a hard-coded offset.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:93-95, 126-128`, `Views/Components/FullscreenImageViewer.swift:7-27`, `Views/Components/ZoomableImageView.swift:26-45, 52-56, 134-167`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:103-122`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the poster slides a black sheet up from the bottom with a spinner, although the poster is already on screen. In Photos and the App Store the image zooms out of its thumbnail and can be dragged back into it. Here a drag only moves the image down and the cover then slides away. The close button sits at a fixed distance below the status area regardless of device.

**Mechanism (finder):** Presentation is a plain .fullScreenCover (MovieDetailView.swift:93-95). ZoomableImageView starts a new full-size load and shows only an activity indicator until it finishes (ZoomableImageView.swift:26-45), never the cached thumbnail. Dismissal is a custom pan that applies a translation (:134-157). The close button uses .padding() plus .padding(.top, 40) (FullscreenImageViewer.swift:22-25).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Zoom transition (the deployment target is iOS 18, so no fallback is needed):
   @Namespace private var posterZoom
   // DetailHero poster (new optional namespace parameter): .matchedTransitionSource(id: "poster", in: posterZoom)
   .fullScreenCover(item: $enlargedImage) { FullscreenImageViewer(url: $0.url).navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID: "poster", in: posterZoom)) }
   Then remove the custom pan (ZoomableImageView.swift:52-56, :134-167) in favour of the system's interactive dismissal.
2) Seed the image view with the thumbnail before the full-size load: ImagePipeline.shared.cache.cachedImage(for: CachedImage.request(...)) (present in the Nuke checkout, ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:52).
3) Close button: on iOS 26 use Button(role: .close) { dismiss() } with .buttonStyle(.glass); on iOS 18 keep xmark.circle.fill but drop the fixed 40 pt.

**APIs:** View.navigationTransition(_:) with .zoom(sourceID:in:) (iOS 18+); View.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:) (iOS 18+); ButtonRole.close (iOS 26+); PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass (iOS 26+)

**Verifier reasons:** The claim holds from code:

- **Plain cover.** Presentation is .fullScreenCover at Views/MovieDetailView.swift:93-95.
- **Spinner on black.** ZoomableImageView.swift:26-45 adds a spinner and loads the bare URL. That key has no processors, while the hero poster's key includes a Resize processor (Views/CachedImage.swift:102-123), so the memory cache always misses. The pipeline has no Nuke data cache (CachedImage.swift:31-37), so the image is at best re-read from URLCache and re-decoded, at worst re-downloaded.
- **Custom dismiss.** The pan only translates the scroll view and then calls onDismiss (ZoomableImageView.swift:134-157).
- **Close button.** It has .padding() plus .padding(.top, 40) (FullscreenImageViewer.swift:22-25). This is cosmetic and barely perceivable.

History shows nothing deliberate (all from d2489f9). No screenshot of the viewer exists.

The fix is workable but needs four corrections:

1. cachedImage(for:) defaults to caches: [.all]; pass [.memory] to stay off disk on the main thread.
2. The seed must use the exact request of the hero poster (seriesDetailHeroWidth by seriesDetailHeroHeight, .fill, .standard), so the viewer needs that request handed in.
3. Removing the custom pan depends on unverified gesture behaviour and must not come first.
4. The zoom makes the whole black cover grow out of the poster frame, not just the image.

**Corrected claim:** The poster viewer is a plain fullScreenCover that always starts with a spinner on black, because it loads a differently-keyed full-size request and never shows the thumbnail already in memory. Its dismissal is a custom translate-only pan. The close button's extra 40 pt top offset is cosmetic.

**Corrected fix:** Do it in this order.

**1. Seed the thumbnail (S, low risk, most of the perceived gain).** Pass the hero poster's ImageRequest into FullscreenImageViewer and ZoomableImageView. In makeUIView set imageView.image = ImagePipeline.shared.cache.cachedImage(for: request, caches: [.memory])?.image. Show the spinner only when that is nil, and swap in the full image when the load completes. Layout still runs in updateUIView once bounds are known.

**2. Zoom transition.** Add @Namespace in the detail view. Put .matchedTransitionSource(id: "poster", in: ns) on the DetailHero poster through an optional Namespace.ID parameter so SeriesDetailView keeps compiling. Put .navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID: "poster", in: ns)) on FullscreenImageViewer inside the cover. Both are iOS 18, so no fallback is needed.

**3. Custom pan.** Keep it until a device run shows the system's interactive dismiss works with the UIScrollView at zoom scale 1 and does not fight pinch-zoom. Remove ZoomableImageView.swift:52-56 and :134-167 only then.

**4. Close button (optional).** On iOS 26, Button(role: .close) { dismiss() }.buttonStyle(.glass). On iOS 18 keep xmark.circle.fill and drop the extra .padding(.top, 40).

**API check:** View.navigationTransition(_ style: some NavigationTransition): iOS 18+, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8946-8947.

NavigationTransition.zoom(sourceID:in:): @available(iOS 18.0, *), macOS unavailable, :8971-8974.

View.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:): iOS 18+, :14899-14900.

ButtonRole.close: 'public static let close', @available(iOS 26.0, *), :9567-9568.

Label-less Button(role:action:): 'extension Button where Label == DefaultButtonLabel { init(role: ButtonRole, action:) }', iOS 26+, :23038-23040.

PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass: @available(iOS 26.0, *), :1315-1318.

Nuke: 'public func cachedImage(for request: ImageRequest, caches: Caches = [.all]) -> ImageContainer?' at ImagePipeline+Cache.swift:52; 'ImagePipeline.cache' at ImagePipeline.swift:43; static CachedImage.request(url:width:height:contentMode:loadProfile:) at Views/CachedImage.swift:102.

**Regression risks:** The system zoom-dismiss gestures (drag down, pinch in) may conflict with the scroll view's pinch and double-tap zoom, or fail to begin over a UIScrollView. Removing the custom pan first could leave no drag-to-dismiss at all.

DetailHero is shared with SeriesDetailView, so the new namespace parameter must be optional.

A seeded thumbnail of about 118x176 pt at 2x looks soft at full screen until the full image arrives. That is still better than a spinner.

A glass close button over a black background needs a contrast check.

**How to verify:** Simulator or device recording, with an image already shown in the hero: the viewer opens with the poster visible at once and no spinner, then sharpens.

After step 2: the cover zooms out of the poster and back into it. Pinch-zoom and double-tap still work. Drag-down at scale 1 dismisses interactively; drag while zoomed in pans the image and does not dismiss.

Repeat on the series detail.

## movies-browse-detail-16 — The sort and filter menu draws its own checkmarks, marks 'Clear filter' as destructive, closes after each file-type pick, and its icon is a circle inside the iOS 26 glass circle.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Recently Added list
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:742-777`, `Models/VODSortOption.swift:16`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: The sort choice is stored globally (VODSortOption.swift:16) and also applies to the 'Recently Added' list, which can then open sorted A-Z. Either hide the sort menu there or keep it global.

**What the user perceives:** The toolbar button shows a ring inside a ring (iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png, M04). Choosing a second file type means reopening the menu each time. 'Clear filter' is red like a delete action. Selected file types show the checkmark as a leading icon instead of the system selection mark.

**Mechanism (finder):** File types are plain Buttons whose label switches to Label(..., systemImage: "checkmark") (VODView.swift:753-761). The clear action is Button(role: .destructive) (:764). The label symbol is line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle(.fill) (:773) with a forced semibold weight (:774); on iOS 26 the bar already puts items in a glass circle. The sort Picker inside the Menu (:744-748) is correct.

**Proposed fix (finder):**    Section(L("filter.file_type")) {
       ForEach(fileTypes, id: \.self) { ext in
           Toggle(ext.uppercased(), isOn: Binding(get: { fileTypeFilter.contains(ext) }, set: { _ in toggleFileType(ext) }))
       }
       if !fileTypeFilter.isEmpty { Button(L("filter.clear")) { fileTypeFilter.removeAll() } }   // no destructive role
   }
   .menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled)   // multi-select stays open
Label: if #available(iOS 26, *) use Image(systemName: "line.3.horizontal.decrease") with .foregroundStyle(isFilterActive ? AnyShapeStyle(.tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.primary)); on iOS 18 keep the current .circle and .circle.fill pair. Drop the forced semibold weight.

**APIs:** View.menuActionDismissBehavior(_:) with .disabled (iOS 16.4+); Toggle inside Menu (iOS 14+)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:742-777. All four code facts hold: file types are plain Buttons whose label switches to Label(..., systemImage: "checkmark") (:753-761); the clear action is Button(role: .destructive) with xmark.circle (:764-768); the label is line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle(.fill) with .font(.body.weight(.semibold)) (:773-774); the sort Picker (:744-748) is the correct native construct. No menuActionDismissBehavior anywhere in the app (grep), so each file-type tap closes the menu. No comment explains any of this as deliberate; git blame puts the whole menu in 654cefc ("add catalog sort/filter, flat browse views..."), a feature commit, not performance work, so rule 5 is not in play.

Screenshots: iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png clearly shows the ringed glyph inside the iOS 26 glass circle (ring in ring) - confirmed. M05-movies-sort-menu.png shows only the sort Picker: the demo catalog has a single container extension, so the `fileTypes.count > 1` gate (:750) hides the file-type section. The checkmark, red 'Clear filter' and dismiss-per-pick parts are therefore code-only evidence, not code+screenshot. iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png (the identical Live construct) shows how it lays out on iOS 26: the Picker's checkmark sits in a dedicated leading selection column, while the Filter section's rows start at the icon column; a Button with Label(systemImage: "checkmark") would put its tick in the icon column, i.e. not aligned with the Picker's tick and not announced as selected to VoiceOver. So the 'own checkmark' claim is real but subtle.

Scope correction: the finding lists only Movies surfaces, but the same code is copy-pasted in Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:634-674 (catch-up / has-EPG buttons, destructive clear at :662, same icon at :670) and Views/SeriesView.swift:683-718 (genre buttons, destructive clear at :705, same icon at :714). Fixing only VODView would make the three tabs inconsistent with each other, which is worse than today.

Fix corrections: (1) keeping the menu open while state changes is not free here: each toggle mutates fileTypeFilter, which re-runs recompute() (:739), resets visibleCount, fires an animated scrollTo (:724-728), swaps the toolbar label symbol (isFilterActive, :773) and inserts/removes the 'Clear filter' row inside the open menu. Whether the open UIMenu survives the toolbar item being re-rendered underneath it cannot be decided from code. (2) foregroundStyle(.tint) on an Image used as a toolbar Menu label is not guaranteed to be honoured by the iOS 26 glass bar item (bar items are rendered monochrome by default); needs a look on the simulator. The app sets no global tint (grep in App/ContentView/DashboardView), so .tint is system blue. (3) Dropping the semibold weight is harmless.

The decision_needed note is accurate: RecentlyAddedVODDetailView (:357-391) wraps VODCategoryContent, which reads the global @AppStorage sort (:610, VODSortOption.swift:16), so 'Recently Added' can open sorted A-Z.

**Corrected claim:** In the three sort/filter menus (Movies VODView.swift:742-777, Live LiveStreamsView.swift:634-674, Series SeriesView.swift:683-718) the multi-select filter rows are plain Buttons that fake selection with a 'checkmark' icon in the icon column (not the system selection column the adjacent sort Picker uses, and not exposed as selected to accessibility), 'Clear filter' carries the destructive role although nothing is destroyed, the menu closes after every filter pick, and the toolbar glyph is a .circle variant that draws a ring inside the iOS 26 glass circle (visible in iphone-light/M03). All cosmetic/low; only the ring-in-ring is proven by a screenshot, the rest is from code because the demo catalog has one file type.

**Corrected fix:** Apply the same change to all three menus, not only Movies:
- Filter rows: Toggle(title, isOn: Binding(get: { set.contains(x) }, set: { on in if on { set.insert(x) } else { set.remove(x) } })) inside the existing Section (Live: one Toggle each for .catchup and .hasEPG). The sort Picker stays as is.
- 'Clear filter': keep the Button and its xmark.circle icon, drop role: .destructive.
- Stay-open: put .menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled) on the filter Section only (the sort Picker must keep dismissing). Treat this as conditional: check on the simulator that the menu really stays open while the grid recomputes and the toolbar label changes; if it closes or flickers, ship without this modifier rather than work around it.
- Icon: if #available(iOS 26, *) use Image(systemName: "line.3.horizontal.decrease") with no forced weight; fallback on iOS 18 is the current .circle / .circle.fill pair. For the active state on iOS 26, first try .tint on the Menu / foregroundStyle(.tint) on the image and look at the result; if the glass bar item ignores it, an acceptable fallback is keeping "line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle.fill" for the active state only.
- Owner decision (not a fix): the sort is global and also applies to 'Recently Added'; either hide the sort Picker there (needs a flag on VODCategoryContent) or leave it.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13737-13738: `@available(iOS 16.4, macOS 13.3, tvOS 16.4, watchOS 9.4, *) nonisolated public func menuActionDismissBehavior(_ behavior: MenuActionDismissBehavior) -> some View`; :13742-13748 `public struct MenuActionDismissBehavior` with `static let disabled` (tvOS 17, unavailable on macOS/watchOS; iOS follows the struct, 16.4) - fine for the iOS 18 target, no availability guard needed. SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5029 `public struct Toggle<Label>` (iOS 13) and :5054 `init<S>(_ title: S, isOn: Binding<Bool>) where S: StringProtocol` - compiles with ext.uppercased(). That a Toggle inside a Menu renders as a checkmarked menu item is runtime behaviour and cannot be read from the interface; it is long-standing documented behaviour but should be eyeballed once. SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:5542 `@frozen public struct AnyShapeStyle`, :19569 `static var tint: TintShapeStyle`, :19578 `struct TintShapeStyle` - exist. Button(_:action:) StringProtocol init at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22940. Section(_ title: S, content:) at :12843. Whether a toolbar bar item on iOS 26 honours foregroundStyle(.tint) on its label is not derivable from the SDK.

**Regression risks:** Menu staying open while the grid behind it recomputes, scrolls to top and the toolbar label re-renders could dismiss or flicker the menu; the 'Clear filter' row appearing/disappearing inside an open menu shifts rows under the finger. Changing only Movies would leave Live and Series with the old look. Removing the .circle glyph on iOS 26 loses the filled 'active' cue unless the tint really shows. No UI test references these menus (grep of the test targets), no performance work is touched (recompute stays off-main, pagination untouched), tip-jar files untouched.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 26 and iOS 18: use a fixture with at least two container extensions (the demo data has one, so the file-type section is hidden; alternatively check the Live menu, whose Filter section always shows). Open the menu in a category grid, tap two filter rows in a row and observe: (a) the menu stays open, (b) the tick appears in the same leading column as the sort Picker's tick, (c) 'Clear filter' is not red, (d) the grid behind updates without the menu closing or jumping. Screenshot the toolbar button inactive and active on iOS 26 to confirm a single glass circle and a visible active state; repeat in dark mode. VoiceOver: filter rows should announce selected state.
