## data-main-thread-1 — On every cold launch the selected tab shows the "No category found" empty state for the whole stream load, because the shelf state is only recomputed when streamsLoaded flips.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: App launch, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-152`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17, 65-88, 105-107, 278-294, 372-375`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:38-61, 157-159, 166-178`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:39-62, 158-160, 220-231`, `another-iptv-player/ContentView.swift:134-138, 145-149`, `another-iptv-player/Models/Requests.swift:9-24`

**What the user perceives:** Launch with a large playlist: a blank background frame, then a spinner ("Preparing channels..."), then a centred tv.slash icon with "No category found." for as long as the catalog decode takes (0.67 s for 150k movies on an M4 Pro Mac, so roughly 1-2 s on a phone, my estimate), then all shelves at once. The category headers with reserved shelf space that phase 1 was written for never appear. Opening Movies or Series for the first time later flashes the same empty state for a frame before the shelves.

**Mechanism (finder):** loadPlaylist publishes the categories and sets isLoading = false (PlaylistContentStore.swift:133-137) while streamsLoaded stays false until :152. The tab views copy store data into @State (LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17) only inside recomputeFilter, which is started by three .task(id:) keyed on debouncedQuery, streamsLoaded and hiddenIds (:105-107). None of those ids changes when phase 1 lands, so displayCategories stays [] and body falls through to the empty-state branch (:79-87: not loading, no error). Same in VODView.swift:38-61/157-159 and SeriesView.swift:39-62/158-160. The placeholder branch for isStreamsLoading (LiveStreamsView.swift:372-375) is therefore unreachable on a cold start. Before that, ContentView draws a bare Color until PlaylistRequest delivers on the default async scheduler (ContentView.swift:134-138, Requests.swift:11-17), and loadPlaylist makes two sequential database hops (needsNetworkBootstrap :115, categories :128) before any UI. On a first open of another tab the @State starts empty and the tasks run after the first render, hence the one-frame flash.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Store: add `@Published private(set) var catalogRevision = 0` and increment it wherever catalog fields are assigned (after :135, after :152, in each case of :237-274, at :317 and in clearLists).
2) Views (LiveStreamsView, VODView, SeriesView): stop copying the unfiltered catalog into @State; read the store in body and keep only search results in state:
```swift
@State private var searchResult: ShelfSearchResult?   // nil while the query is empty
private var shelfCategories: [DBCategory] {
    if let searchResult { return searchResult.categories }
    let hidden = hiddenStore.hiddenIds(playlistId: playlist.id, type: "live")
    return hidden.isEmpty ? contentStore.liveCategories
                          : contentStore.liveCategories.filter { !hidden.contains($0.id) }
}
private func shelfItems(_ id: String) -> [LiveStreamWithCategory] {
    (searchResult?.byCategory ?? contentStore.liveStreamsByCategoryId)[id] ?? []
}
.task(id: ShelfKey(query: debouncedQuery, revision: contentStore.catalogRevision,
                   hidden: hiddenStore.version)) { await recomputeSearch() }
```
The arrays handed to the Equatable shelf rows still share the store's buffers, so their == keeps the O(1) identity path. Reset playbackModelMemo in the same task.
3) PlaylistRequest: `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader, scheduling: .immediate)` so the dashboard is the launch frame; drop the three print calls (Requests.swift:10, 14, 20).
4) Fold needsNetworkBootstrap into the categories read (no categories means sync needed) to save one hop.
No iOS 26 API involved, so no fallback needed.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166)); ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with .immediate (GRDB 7.10.0 package, not an SDK API; verified in checkout GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485 and ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148. GRDBQuery 0.11.0 handles synchronous first values (Query.swift isUpdating guard))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read the code path. Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:132-137 publishes the categories and sets isLoading = false while streamsLoaded stays false until :152. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17 keeps displayCategories/displayItemsByCategory in @State that is only written by recomputeFilter (:278-315), and recomputeFilter is only started by the three .task(id:) at :105-107 (debouncedQuery, streamsLoaded, hiddenIds). None of those ids changes at phase 1 (streamsLoaded is assigned false again, same value). The view tasks and DashboardView's .task(id: playlist.id) (Views/DashboardView.swift:131-136) are all enqueued in the first layout pass, so they run before the phase-1 continuation, which needs two database hops (:115, :128); recomputeFilter therefore always sees an empty liveCategories first. After phase 1 body takes :65 (displayCategories.isEmpty) -> :66 false (not loading, active id matches) -> :75 no error -> :79-87 the tv.slash / live.empty.no_category state, until :152 flips streamsLoaded. Same structure in Views/VODView.swift:38-61,157-159 and Views/SeriesView.swift:39-62,158-160. The isStreamsLoading placeholder (LiveStreamsView.swift:372-375) is only reachable for a tab first opened inside the phase-2 window. Duration: I rebuilt and re-ran the author's benchmark (scratchpad/agents/mainthread-bench, build in agents/verify-dmt): 660-670 ms for 150k VOD rows on an M4 Pro, so the wrong empty state lasts roughly that long or more on a phone. History: displayCategories as @State dates from the monorepo import (d2489f9), two-phase load from 0ab5bcd; no comment marks the empty state as intended, and the 'UI kategorilerle hemen gosterilir' comment at :137 states the opposite intent. ContentView.swift:134-138 does draw a bare Color until the async PlaylistRequest delivers (Models/Requests.swift:17, default scheduler). Not verified: the 'one-frame flash' on a later first open of another tab; the .task fills the state in the next main-queue turn and may land in the same displayed frame.

**Corrected claim:** On every cold launch the initially selected tab (Live TV, Movies or Series) shows the 'No category found' empty state from the moment the categories are published until the full stream load finishes, because the shelf @State is only recomputed when streamsLoaded, the debounced query or the hidden set changes. The category-header placeholders written for phase 1 are not reachable for that tab. The claimed one-frame flash when another tab is first opened later is plausible but unproven.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the proposal with three adjustments. (1) Store: add @Published private(set) var catalogRevision and bump it after :134 (phase 1), after :151, once per case in the scoped reload :237-274, after :294 and :316, and in clearLists. (2) Views: read categories and per-category items from the store in body for the non-search path and keep only search results (and VOD's recentlyAdded) in @State, driven by ONE .task keyed on (debouncedQuery, catalogRevision, hiddenStore.version) instead of three tasks; compute the hidden set once per body (hiddenIds reads UserDefaults on each call, Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:18-21) and clear playbackModelMemo in that task. Arrays read from the store keep buffer identity, so LiveCategoryShelfRow's == (LiveStreamsView.swift:345-350) stays O(1). Side benefit: today the three tasks each rerun recomputeFilter on every re-appear, which in VODView runs the recently-added sort three times (about 170 ms each off-main for 150k in the benchmark). (3) PlaylistRequest with scheduling: .immediate: also gate the playlist-list branch in ContentView.swift:80 on hasAttemptedAutoLoad (or resolve the saved playlist before choosing the branch); otherwise the first body builds the playlist-list NavigationStack before .onAppear selects the saved playlist. Remove the three print calls. (4) Folding needsNetworkBootstrap into the category read saves about one millisecond; optional. Adjacent observation for whoever touches these lines: loadPlaylist :146-151 does not apply mergeUncategorized/appendingUncategorized while reloadFromDatabase :305-310 does, so orphan streams are only bucketed after a refresh.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166, inside an extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, *) (:5160). ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with default .async(onQueue: .main): GRDB 7.10.0 checkout GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485-487; static var immediate: ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148 and :177; doc comment states immediate requires starting on the main queue (fatal error otherwise). GRDBQuery 0.11.0 Query.swift:266-321: Tracker.update subscribes inside DynamicProperty.update on the main actor and has an isUpdating guard for values published on subscription, so the first body sees an immediate value. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Three large view files change how they source shelf data; the Equatable shelf rows, the detached search filter and the playback-model memo must be kept (stale memo if it is not reset on revision change). With .immediate on PlaylistRequest the first body can build the playlist list unless gated. An immediate fetch runs on the main thread and needs a free reader connection (pool of 5); harmless for PlaylistRequest at launch. Does not touch the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Unit test on the store with a seeded throwaway playlist: catalogRevision must change when categories are published while streamsLoaded is still false, and again when streams land. UI test with a large seeded catalog behind a launch argument: poll from launch until the first shelf exists and assert the live.empty.no_category text never appears. Manual: launch with a 50k+ playlist and record the screen; the tv.slash icon must not appear between the spinner and the shelves.

## data-main-thread-2 — Pull-to-refresh on Live TV, Movies and Series updates the store, but the home shelves keep showing the pre-refresh copy.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category detail grids
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:210-220, 234-278, 295, 317`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:45-53, 105-107, 242-249, 508-509`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:95-99, 157-159, 574-575`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:96-100, 158-160, 546-547`

**What the user perceives:** Pull to refresh: the spinner runs, the panel is downloaded and written, and the page does not change. New channels or movies and removed categories only show up after relaunching the app or typing in the search field. The category picker and the "All" grid already show the new data, so one tab disagrees with itself.

**Mechanism (finder):** refreshable calls refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only:) (LiveStreamsView.swift:247), which ends in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:). That assigns liveCategories, liveStreams and liveStreamsByCategoryId (PlaylistContentStore.swift:245-249) but leaves streamsLoaded at true. The three task ids (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107) are unchanged, so recomputeFilter never runs and the @State copies stay stale. pickerEntries (:45-53) and AllLiveView (:741) read the store directly, hence the disagreement. Same for Movies and Series and for the category detail screens. The scoped refresh came in with commit 1cce013; the full reload from Settings works only because it toggles streamsLoaded false then true (PlaylistContentStore.swift:295, 317). No test covers the store.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Same change as the launch finding: a catalogRevision counter in the store, used in the single task key or, better, direct store reads for the non-search path. The smallest possible patch, if the larger change is deferred, is to replace `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` with `.task(id: contentStore.catalogRevision)` in the nine places it appears (LiveStreamsView.swift:106, 509, 734; VODView.swift:158, 575, 834; SeriesView.swift:159, 547, 773) and in SearchView.swift:248.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166))

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:242-249 calls refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only: .live) (same in Views/VODView.swift:95-99 and Views/SeriesView.swift:96-100). Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:210-220 -> :234-278 assigns the categories, flat list and by-category dictionary for that type and never touches streamsLoaded. The home views copy store data into @State only in recomputeFilter, started by .task(id:) on debouncedQuery, streamsLoaded and hiddenIds (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107; VODView.swift:157-159; SeriesView.swift:158-160); none changes, so the shelves keep the pre-refresh copy while pickerEntries (LiveStreamsView.swift:45-53) reads the store. git show 1cce013 (2026-07-24) confirms the home views were switched from refreshFromNetwork(playlist:), which toggles streamsLoaded at :295/:317, to the scoped variant in that commit. No test references PlaylistContentStore. Two corrections. (a) 'Only after relaunching or typing in search' is overstated: .task(id:) is cancelled on disappear and runs again on appear, so switching tabs or pushing and popping a detail reruns recomputeFilter and heals the copy. That re-run on re-appear is also the only way the applyVODMetadata fix (PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-178) can reach these @State copies. I did not run the app to confirm it. (b) 'Category detail grids' are not affected in practice: .refreshable exists only on the three home views (grep), a detail screen covers the home while mounted, and the Settings refresh uses the full reload which toggles streamsLoaded.

**Corrected claim:** After pull-to-refresh on the Live TV, Movies or Series home, the store is updated but the visible shelves keep the pre-refresh copy until the view disappears and re-appears (tab switch, push/pop) or the search text changes; the category picker already shows the new data. Category detail and 'All' grids are not affected in practice.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: add a catalogRevision counter to PlaylistContentStore, bump it once at the end of each case in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) (:247-249, :259-261, :271-273) and wherever else catalog fields are assigned, and key the recompute tasks on it. If the larger change from data-main-thread-1 is deferred, replacing .task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded) with .task(id: contentStore.catalogRevision) at LiveStreamsView.swift:106, 509, 734; VODView.swift:158, 575, 834; SeriesView.swift:159, 547, 773 and SearchView.swift:248 is sufficient (line numbers verified by grep). SearchView.swift:225 keeps using streamsLoaded for its loading state.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166, extension @available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, *). No other API involved; no iOS 26 API.

**Regression risks:** Low. One extra recompute per catalog publish (phase 1 and phase 2 at launch, once per scoped reload). In VODView each recompute reruns the detached recently-added sort; keep it off-main as it is. If revision is also bumped in applyVODMetadata every film detail open would trigger that sort; the proposal does not bump there, keep it that way.

**How to verify:** Unit test: load a seeded throwaway playlist, insert one more liveStream row, call reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only: .live), assert liveStreamsByCategoryId contains the row and catalogRevision changed. Manual in the simulator with the network stubbed: add a row while the app runs, pull to refresh and confirm the shelf changes without leaving the tab. To settle correction (a): before the fix, pull to refresh, then switch tab and back and check whether the shelf updates.

## data-main-thread-3 — Panel JSON for the whole catalog is decoded on the main actor during first import, pull-to-refresh and "refresh all".

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Add playlist (Xtream), Pull-to-refresh on Live TV / Movies / Series, Settings refresh
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:34, 85-143, 165-205`, `another-iptv-player/Models/XtreamModels.swift:4-26, 187-222, 266-273`, `another-iptv-player.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:578, 619`, `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:447-461, 475-508`, `another-iptv-player/Models/XtreamImporter.swift:24-32`

**What the user perceives:** While a refresh is running, the refresh spinner, scrolling and the import progress view freeze in chunks: once per endpoint as its response arrives. For a 150k-movie panel the movie list alone blocks the main thread for 515-590 ms on an M4 Pro Mac (58 MB of JSON); expect well over a second on a phone, plus series and live.

**Mechanism (finder):** The app target builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:578, 619), so `class XtreamAPIClient` (XtreamAPIClient.swift:34) is main-actor isolated. In fetch (:85-143) the code resumes on the main actor after `await urlSession.data(from:)` and runs `JSONDecoder().decode(T.self, from: data)` there (:130-131), followed by `failable.compactMap { $0.base }` (:185-203). The models use lenient `try?` decoding per field (XtreamModels.swift:4-26, 210-221), which makes the decode slower. The code reads as async, which hides the stall.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Decode off the main actor, using the idiom the code base already uses:
```swift
private func fetch<T: Decodable & Sendable>(...) async throws -> T {
    ...
    let (data, response) = try await urlSession.data(from: url)
    ...
    return try await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
        try JSONDecoder().decode(T.self, from: data)
    }.value
}
```
Mark the DTOs (XtreamCategory, XtreamLiveStream, XtreamVODStream, XtreamSeries, the info types), FailableDecodable and the KeyedDecodingContainer extension `nonisolated`, as was done for EPGGuideProgrammeRecord and AdultContentFilter, so their Decodable conformances are not main-actor isolated. Move the `compactMap { $0.base }` into the detached task by decoding to `[FailableDecodable<X>]` and returning `[X]` from one helper. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** Task.detached(priority:operation:) (iOS 13.0+ (_Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014))

**Verifier reasons:** another-iptv-player.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:577-578 and :618-619 set SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES and SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor for the app target (SWIFT_VERSION 5.0). Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:34 'class XtreamAPIClient' has no isolation annotation (PanelURLSession just above it is explicitly nonisolated), so fetch (:85-143) is main-actor isolated: it resumes on the main actor after urlSession.data(from:) at :108 and runs JSONDecoder().decode at :127-128, then failable.compactMap at :162-205 on the main actor as well. Callers are main-actor too: PlaylistContentStore.swift:448-461 and :478-508, and Models/XtreamImporter.swift:7 (enum without nonisolated) :24-32. The DTOs use per-field try? decoding (Models/XtreamModels.swift:4-26, 210-221). I rebuilt and ran the author's jsonbench: 150,000 get_vod_streams items, 58.6-58.8 MB, decode 480-573 ms best of 3 on an M4 Pro. No comment or history marks main-actor decoding as deliberate; the code base moves comparable work off the main actor elsewhere (30 Task.detached uses, nonisolated EPG parser and records). The same fetch also decodes get_series_info and get_vod_info on the main actor when a detail screen opens, which the fix covers too.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands: every Xtream response, including the whole-catalog lists, is JSON-decoded on the main actor, blocking it for roughly half a second per 150k-item list on a fast Mac and longer on a phone, during first import, pull-to-refresh and refresh-all; detail responses are decoded there as well.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed. Decode inside Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) in fetch (T: Decodable & Sendable) and move the compactMap { $0.base } into the same detached task via one helper returning [X]. Mark the DTO structs in Models/XtreamModels.swift, FailableDecodable and the KeyedDecodingContainer extension (:4) nonisolated; the extension is required, because under default MainActor isolation its helper methods are main-actor isolated and could not be called from a nonisolated init(from:). Keep the DEBUG logging and the XtreamError.decodingError mapping around the detached call. A plain nonisolated async helper is not enough here: with SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY it would run on the caller's actor, so Task.detached (the code base idiom) or @concurrent is needed.

**API check:** Task.detached(name:priority:operation:): _Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014 (non-throwing) and :4133 (throwing), @available(macOS 10.15, iOS 13.0, watchOS 6.0, tvOS 13.0, *), @_alwaysEmitIntoClient. Precedent for nonisolated types in this target: Models/AdultContentFilter.swift:5, EPG/EPGStore.swift:20, Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:5. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Low. Task.detached does not inherit cancellation, so a cancelled refresh finishes its decode before the result is dropped (the refresh already runs in an unstructured Task for that reason, LiveStreamsView.swift:243-248). Making the DTOs nonisolated changes no behaviour; AdultContentFilter (nonisolated) already consumes them. Does not touch the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Unit test with a URLProtocol stub session (the initializer takes a URLSession): serve a synthetic 150k-item get_vod_streams body, run getVODStreams() while a main-actor heartbeat task records the longest gap between ticks; assert it stays under about 50 ms (it is several hundred ms today). The benchmark is scratchpad/agents/mainthread-bench/Sources/jsonbench.

## data-main-thread-4 — The in-memory catalog is decoded through synthesized Decodable, which makes launch-to-posters about five times slower than it needs to be.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: App launch, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-152, 366-406`, `another-iptv-player/Models/DBModels.swift:15-89, 143-162, 174-190`, `another-iptv-player/Models/M3UContentStore.swift:115-122`, `another-iptv-player/Database/AppDatabase.swift:248-253`

**What the user perceives:** Every launch, and every reload after a refresh, waits for the full catalog before the first poster can appear. Measured on an M4 Pro Mac for 150k movies: 671 ms to fetch and decode, against 134 ms with hand-written row decoding (74 ms of that is SQLite stepping). For an M3U list of 100k entries: 348 ms against 57 ms. Phones will be slower, and M3U lists of 300k entries are mentioned in the code comments.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODWithCategory, SeriesWithCategory and LiveStreamWithCategory are `FetchableRecord, Decodable` (DBModels.swift:174-190), so fetchAll (PlaylistContentStore.swift:376, 390, 404) goes through GRDB's row decoder: one keyed-container lookup per property, 21 for DBVODStream, with the nested `stream` decoded from the same row. M3UContentStore.fetchChannels (:115-122) does the same for DBM3UChannel and also sorts through a temporary B-tree, because the only index is (playlistId, groupTitle, sortIndex) (AppDatabase.swift:248-253); EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows "USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY". The reads already run off the main actor in parallel, so this is waiting time, not a stall.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add private bulk row types next to the fetch functions that decode by column index from an explicit column list, leaving the record types and all other call sites untouched:
```swift
private struct CatalogVODRow: FetchableRecord {
    let value: VODWithCategory
    static let columns = "vodStream.streamId, vodStream.name, vodStream.streamIcon, ..."
    init(row: Row) throws {
        value = VODWithCategory(
            stream: DBVODStream(streamId: row[0], name: row[1], streamIcon: row[2], ...),
            categoryName: row[21])
    }
}
```
Decoding by column name with the existing `SELECT *` is the lower-risk variant and measured 269 ms (2.5 times faster). For M3U add a migration `idx_m3uChannel_playlist_sort` on (playlistId, sortIndex), registered with `foreignKeyChecks: .immediate` so the upgrade launch does not run a whole-database foreign key check (measured 90 ms against 4 ms on a 323 MB database). No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** FetchableRecord.init(row:) (GRDB 7.10.0 package, not an SDK API; verified in checkout GRDB/Record/FetchableRecord.swift:122); Row subscript by column index (GRDB 7.10.0 package; verified in checkout GRDB/Core/Row.swift:386, 417); DatabaseMigrator.registerMigration(_:foreignKeyChecks:migrate:) (GRDB 7.10.0 package; verified in checkout GRDB/Migration/DatabaseMigrator.swift:215)

**Verifier reasons:** Models/DBModels.swift:174-190: LiveStreamWithCategory, VODWithCategory and SeriesWithCategory are FetchableRecord + Decodable with a nested record decoded from the same row; Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:376, 390, 404 fetch them with fetchAll inside reads that already run off the main actor in parallel (:140-142). Models/M3UContentStore.swift:115-122 does the same for DBM3UChannel ordered by sortIndex, and the only m3uChannel index is (playlistId, groupTitle, sortIndex) (Database/AppDatabase.swift:248-253). I rebuilt and ran the author's benchmark on the same class of machine (M4 Pro): 150k VOD rows 660-670 ms via synthesized Decodable, 249-272 ms with init(row:) by column name on the unchanged SELECT *, 122-133 ms by column index, 73.5 ms raw SQLite stepping; M3U 100k rows 345 ms today, 137 ms by index, 57 ms by index plus a (playlistId, sortIndex) index; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN prints 'USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY' for the M3U query. The numbers match the finding. This is waiting time before content, not a main-thread stall, and it is only user-visible as time-to-posters at launch and after a reload. GRDB Migration.swift:33-48 and :69-100 confirm that the default deferred mode runs db.checkForeignKeys() over the whole database and that .immediate skips it. I did not re-run the migration timing (90 ms vs 4 ms).

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands: catalog rows are decoded through GRDB's Decodable path, about five times slower than hand-written column-index decoding (2.5 times slower than by-name decoding), and the M3U fetch additionally sorts through a temporary B-tree. It lengthens launch-to-content and reloads; it does not block the main thread.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with implementation notes for this target. Put the bulk row types (or an init(row:) added in an extension, so the memberwise initializers used at PlaylistContentStore.swift:526, 544, 563 survive) next to the fetch functions, with an explicit column list for the by-index variant. Declare the row types nonisolated and preferably mark the DB record structs nonisolated too: under default MainActor isolation their initializers are main-actor isolated and today's off-main decoding only compiles because of Swift 5 leniency. If the column-order risk is not wanted, by-name init(row:) on the unchanged SELECT * already gives 2.5 times. For M3U add migration idx_m3uChannel_playlist_sort on (playlistId, sortIndex) with foreignKeyChecks: .immediate; safe because the migration only creates an index.

**API check:** All package APIs, GRDB 7.10.0 checkout (git describe v7.10.0): FetchableRecord.init(row:) and Row index/name subscripts are exercised by the benchmark I compiled and ran against this checkout; DatabaseMigrator.registerMigration(_:foreignKeyChecks:migrate:) at GRDB/Migration/DatabaseMigrator.swift:215 with enum ForeignKeyChecks { deferred, immediate } at :50-78. Database is a DatabasePool with default configuration (Database/Persistence.swift:54, 99-100). No SDK or iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Column-index decoding silently mis-assigns fields if the SELECT list and the initializer drift apart, and every future column needs both places updated; the equality test against the Decodable path is required, not optional. The new index adds a little write cost to M3U imports and a one-off index build on the upgrade launch. Other call sites keep using the Decodable path, so nothing else changes. Does not undo earlier performance work.

**How to verify:** Unit tests against AppDatabase.empty(): for rows with every optional column nil and set, the new row type must equal the existing Decodable result for all three catalog types and DBM3UChannel; a timing test with 100k synthetic rows with a generous bound. Re-run scratchpad/agents/mainthread-bench (bench target, third batch) for the numbers. On a device: os_signpost around PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-152 before and after with a 50k+ playlist.

## data-main-thread-5 — Every @Query delivers its first value after the first frame, so rows and buttons pop in and shift the layout on browse and detail screens.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Movie detail, Series detail, M3U channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/Requests.swift:197-207, 254-264, 276-289, 382-397, 406-428, 507-521`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:7, 21-28`, `another-iptv-player/Views/MovieDetailView.swift:20-35, 74-76, 99-103, 132-141`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:809-820, 1363, 1379, 1402-1437`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:28, 58, 285-297`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:217-222, 236-241, 254-262`, `another-iptv-player/Database/AppDatabase.swift:158-174`

**What the user perceives:** Opening a tab: the shelves render, then the Continue Watching row is inserted above them and pushes everything down. Opening a movie with history: the button says "Watch now", then during the push it turns into "Resume" with a time line and progress bar, a Restart row appears below it, and the download button and plot move down; the favourite star flips from outline to filled. In a season, episode rows with history grow by one line after they appear. Re-opening a movie whose details were already fetched can still flash the full-screen spinner and refetch.

**Mechanism (finder):** All requests use `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)`, whose default scheduler is .async(onQueue: .main), so the view's first body sees the default value (nil, false or []). ContinueWatchingRow renders nothing while historyItems is empty (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:28). MovieDetailView derives resumeMs from the async watchHistory (:37-42), which changes the action bar's height (DetailComponents.swift:217-222, 236-241, 254-262). MovieDetailView's .task (:99-103) checks currentMovie.metadataLoaded before movieRecord has arrived, so it reads the stale catalog copy and starts a network fetch. EpisodeDetailRow opens two observations per row (SeriesView.swift:1363 and DownloadButton.swift:28) and inserts a label when history arrives (:1423-1437). WatchHistoryRequest filters on streamId, playlistId and type, for which watchHistory has no index (AppDatabase.swift:158-174), so each row's observation is a table scan that reruns on every history write.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use the immediate scheduler for the small indexed requests that decide first-frame layout: PlaylistRequest, RecentWatchHistoryRequest (limit 10), VODByIDRequest, SeriesByIDRequest, SeasonsRequest, IsFavoriteRequest, WatchHistoryRequest, LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest and DownloadedItemByIDRequest:
```swift
ValueObservation.tracking { db in ... }
    .publisher(in: appDatabase.reader, scheduling: .immediate)
```
GRDBQuery already supports publishers that emit on subscription. Add a migration with an index on watchHistory(playlistId, type, streamId), registered with `foreignKeyChecks: .immediate`, so those lookups are index hits. For seasons, replace the per-row pair of observations with one map per season, as WatchProgressMapRequest already does for poster grids. Leave the catalog-wide requests on the async scheduler. Caveat: immediate fetches run on the main thread and need a free reader; the pool has 5 (GRDB Configuration.maximumReaderCount) and three are busy during the launch load, so keep the list short. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with .immediate (GRDB 7.10.0 package, not an SDK API; verified in checkout GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485 and ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed: all 17 requests in Models/Requests.swift use .publisher(in: appDatabase.reader), whose default scheduler is .async(onQueue: .main) (GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487), so the first body always sees defaultValue. Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:27-28 renders nothing while historyItems is empty; Views/MovieDetailView.swift:37-48 derives resumeMs/resumeProgress from the async watchHistory and feeds DetailActionBar (:132-141), whose subtitle, progress bar and restart row change its height (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:217-222, 236-241, 254-262); EpisodeDetailRow opens WatchHistoryRequest per row (Views/SeriesView.swift:1363, 1379) plus DownloadButton's @Query (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:28, 58) and inserts a label when history arrives (:1423-1437); watchHistory has only the id primary key and an index on lastWatchedAt (Database/AppDatabase.swift:158-174). What does not hold as stated: (1) Perception is unproven. The value normally arrives one main-queue turn after the first body, i.e. in the first or second frame. For a pushed detail that is while the screen is still at the start of the push, so 'turns into Resume during the push' is at most a one-to-two-frame change, probably not noticed. The Continue Watching insertion above already-visible shelves on launch and first tab open is the case most likely to be seen. (2) The refetch claim is narrow: the home and grid copies are refreshed when the view re-appears after applyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-178), so MovieDetailView.swift:99-103 sees a stale metadataLoaded mainly for films reached through a queue captured earlier (:96-97). (3) The missing index costs little: history tables are small and the re-fetches run on reader queues, deduplicated by removeDuplicates (Requests.swift:393-397). Risk the finding understates: an immediate observation performs its first fetch synchronously on the main thread through dbPool.read / walSnapshotTransaction (GRDB ValueConcurrentObserver.swift:284-295, 543-550), which waits when all 5 readers are busy; the launch load holds 3 for the whole decode.

**Corrected claim:** Every @Query delivers its first value one main-queue turn after the first body, so views start from the default value and re-layout once. The effect most likely to be visible is the Continue Watching row being inserted above shelves that are already on screen at launch and on a tab's first open; on movie and series detail the Resume/star/restart changes fall in the first frames of the push and need a frame capture to prove. The refetch-with-spinner case is limited to stale queue entries, and the missing watchHistory index is a minor cost.

**Corrected fix:** Scope it down. Use scheduling: .immediate only for RecentWatchHistoryRequest (Continue Watching), VODByIDRequest, SeriesByIDRequest, IsFavoriteRequest, LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest and the detail-screen WatchHistoryRequest; all are single-row or LIMIT 10 lookups. Leave SeasonsRequest, per-row episode requests and DownloadButton on the async scheduler unless the frame capture shows a problem; do not make per-row requests immediate, since that puts two synchronous reads per row on the main thread while scrolling. Before making WatchHistoryRequest immediate, give it an indexed path: either the proposed index on watchHistory(playlistId, type, streamId) via a migration with foreignKeyChecks: .immediate, or a primary-key lookup, since ids are written as "\(playlistId)_\(type)_\(streamId)" (Views/PlayerView.swift:3093-3094, read for the hand-off only). Because data-main-thread-1 will mount Continue Watching while three readers are busy, consider raising Configuration.maximumReaderCount in Database/Persistence.swift:99-100 or land data-main-thread-4 first. The one-observation-per-season refactor is optional follow-up. PlaylistRequest is covered by data-main-thread-1.

**API check:** ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) default .async(onQueue: .main): GRDB 7.10.0 checkout GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485-487; .immediate: ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148 and :177 (ImmediateValueObservationScheduler :109), must start on the main queue or it traps. GRDBQuery 0.11.0 Query.swift:266-321 and :327-335 subscribe from DynamicProperty.update on the main actor and tolerate values published on subscription. Configuration.maximumReaderCount default 5: GRDB/Core/Configuration.swift:360. registerMigration(_:foreignKeyChecks:migrate:): DatabaseMigrator.swift:215. No SDK or iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Immediate fetches run on the main thread: a main-thread stall appears if the reader pool is exhausted (launch load, long EPG reads) or if a non-indexed request is made immediate for many rows. Any future off-main subscription to an immediate publisher traps (today only @Query subscribes, on main). The deliberate removeDuplicates on the history requests must stay. Does not touch the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Decide by measurement first: record the simulator at 60 fps (or log os_signpost at first body and at value delivery) for (a) cold launch and first open of each tab with history present, (b) pushing a movie and a series that have history. Count the frames in which the default state is visible and whether the shelves move. After the change, a unit test per changed request: subscribe on the main actor against AppDatabase.empty() with a seeded row and assert the value is delivered before sink returns; a UI test that opens a movie with history and asserts the Resume label in the first snapshot; and a main-thread hang check during a cold launch with a large catalog to rule out reader-pool waits.

## data-main-thread-6 — Opening a movie's details copies the whole movie catalog on the main actor and invalidates every catalog observer.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Movies home, All Movies
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:26-32, 161-178`, `another-iptv-player/Views/MovieDetailView.swift:99-103, 268-306`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:596-605`

**What the user perceives:** A hitch during or just after the push into a movie the first time its details load: 19 ms on an M4 Pro Mac for 150k movies, so several dropped frames on a 120 Hz phone. The comment at VODView.swift:596-599 records that the resulting re-render once froze All Movies for seconds.

**Mechanism (finder):** applyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:164-178) runs when get_vod_info returns (MovieDetailView.swift:303-305). It scans the flat array with firstIndex(where:) and then writes `vodStreams[i] = ...` through a @Published property. @Published has only get and set, so the array is read (second reference), mutated (not uniquely referenced, so the whole buffer of 328-byte elements is copied) and written back. It then copies a bucket and reassigns the dictionary. Each assignment fires objectWillChange on a store that DashboardView, the three tab views, search and the open grids all observe. The patch does not reach the views' @State copies, so re-opening the same movie from a home shelf still sees metadataLoaded == false.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Once VODByIDRequest uses the immediate scheduler (previous finding), MovieDetailView reads the database row on its first frame and the .task check at :99-103 is correct without any catalog patch. Then delete applyVODMetadata and its call at MovieDetailView.swift:304. If the method is kept, make it O(1) and silent: build a `[Int: Int]` index from streamId to position off the main actor in fetchVODStreamsData, keep the arrays in plain private storage exposed through read-only accessors, and mutate in place without publishing. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with .immediate (GRDB 7.10.0 package, not an SDK API; verified in checkout GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485)

**Verifier reasons:** The copy is real. Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:164-178 scans the flat array and then writes `vodStreams[i] = ...` through `@Published private(set) var vodStreams` (:27). Combine's Published subscript in the iOS 26 SDK interface (Combine.swiftinterface:965-968) declares only `get` and `set`, so the write is read, copy-on-write of the whole buffer, write back. It then reassigns one bucket of the dictionary (:171-175). I rebuilt the path with a real ObservableObject (scratchpad/agents/verify-mainthread-b/main.swift): stride of VODWithCategory is 328 bytes; best of 5 on this Mac is 9.4 ms for 150k movies and 3.7 ms for 50k, with objectWillChange firing twice per call. The finding's 19 ms is a first-run figure; the order of magnitude holds. On a phone that is roughly 1 dropped frame at 50k and 2 to 5 at 150k, once per movie whose details were never loaded, landing when get_vod_info returns (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:303-305). Eleven views observe the store (DashboardView.swift:6, VODView.swift:7/552/810, SeriesView.swift:9/524/749, LiveStreamsView.swift:7/471/691, SearchView.swift:136).

The method is deliberate earlier work, not an accident: commit 0ab5bcd added it to stop a repeat network request and spinner flash on re-entry (comment at PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-163), and 654cefc then added the coarse Equatable on VODCategoryContent to contain its publish storm (comment at Views/VODView.swift:596-599). Any fix must keep the benefit 0ab5bcd was after.

One part of the claim is probably wrong. The finding says the patch does not reach a home shelf. VODView's three `.task(id:)` modifiers (VODView.swift:157-159) restart when the root reappears after a pop, and recomputeFilter reassigns `displayItemsByCategory = allByCategory` from the patched store (:176-177), so the home shelves should get the patched row. Where the patch cannot arrive is the paginated grids: VODCategoryContent's `==` compares only count and first/last id (:600-605), so the EquatableView keeps its old `items` and its @State `displayItems`; reopening the same movie from a category grid or All Movies still passes `metadataLoaded == false`, and MovieDetailView then shows stale content, a full-screen spinner (MovieDetailView.swift:74-76) and content again, plus a redundant request. I did not run this; it rests on NavigationStack calling disappear/appear on push/pop.

The proposed fix depends on a finding I was not given (VODByIDRequest with the immediate scheduler). No request in the app uses `.immediate` today (grep: none); Models/Requests.swift:254-264 uses the default async scheduler.

**Corrected claim:** The first time a movie's details load, applyVODMetadata copies the whole flat movie array on the main actor (about 49 MB at 150k; 9 ms on an M4 Pro, so 2 to 5 dropped frames on a phone; about 1 frame at 50k) and publishes twice to eleven observing views. The patch it exists for does reach the home shelves when they reappear, but never reaches the paginated grids (category detail, All Movies), whose coarse Equatable keeps the old rows; reopening a visited movie from a grid still flashes a spinner and repeats the network request.

**Corrected fix:** Make MovieDetailView decide from the database row instead of from the catalog copy, so no catalog patch is needed and every entry point is covered:
```swift
.task {
    let sid = movie.streamId, pid = playlist.id
    let row = try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in
        try DBVODStream.filter(Column("streamId") == sid && Column("playlistId") == pid).fetchOne(db)
    }
    if !(row?.metadataLoaded ?? movie.metadataLoaded) { await fetchMovieInfo() }
}
```
Then delete applyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-178) and its call (MovieDetailView.swift:304). This is one primary-key read off the main thread and does not depend on any other finding. Switching VODByIDRequest to `.immediate` is an optional extra for first-frame content; treat it separately because it performs a synchronous read on the main thread. Do not do the 'silent in-place storage' variant: it removes @Published from the catalog arrays and every screen relies on those publishes.

**API check:** Combine `Published` static subscript `_enclosingInstance`: `{ get set }` only, no modify accessor (Combine.swiftinterface:965-968 in the iOS 26 SDK), which is what forces the full copy. GRDB 7.10.0 checkout: `ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:)` at GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485-487 (default `.async(onQueue: .main)`), `.immediate` at ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148 and :177, documented to require starting on the main actor. GRDBQuery checkout is 0.11.0. `AppDatabase.read` async exists at Database/AppDatabase.swift:485-489. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Removing the patch must not bring back what 0ab5bcd fixed; the database check in `.task` covers that, including the grids the patch never reached. In-memory rows keep their list-level fields for the session (plot, genre and so on stay nil until the next catalog load); I found no reader of those fields outside MovieDetailView except the player subtitle built from queue rows (VODView.swift:896-897), which was already stale for the grids. If the `.immediate` scheduler is adopted instead, the initial fetch waits for a free reader on the main thread: the pool has 5 readers (GRDB Configuration.swift:360; DatabasePool at Database/Persistence.swift:54) and the catalog load holds 3 for its duration (PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-142).

**How to verify:** Unit test: load a synthetic 150k catalog, subscribe to objectWillChange, complete a detail fetch and assert zero store publishes. UI check on a real catalog: open a movie from a category grid, go back, open it again; expect no "detail.loading_movie" spinner and no second get_vod_info request (proxy log). Simulator check for the disputed part: after returning from a detail to Movies home, confirm recomputeFilter ran (log) to settle whether the home shelves were ever stale.

## data-main-thread-7 — Each browse screen runs its recompute two or three times on appear, and "Recently added" is found by sorting the whole catalog in memory each time.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, All Movies, All Series, All Channels, Category detail grids, Search
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:157-159, 175-192, 574-575, 619, 653-668, 737-739, 833-835, 838-854`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:158-160, 229-246, 546-547, 615-627, 678-680, 772-774`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, 508-509, 567-577, 629-631, 733-735`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:246-248`, `another-iptv-player/Database/AppDatabase.swift:305-321`

**What the user perceives:** First open of Movies or Series: the shelves appear, and a moment later the Recently added shelf pops in above them and pushes them down. Opening All Movies on a 150k catalog allocates roughly 290 MB transiently and resets the grid's page counter up to three times in the first few hundred milliseconds.

**Mechanism (finder):** Several .task(id:) modifiers call the same function, and all of them fire on appear: three in VODView (:157-159), three in VODCategoryContent (:737-739), three in AllVODView (:833-835), two in the category detail (:574-575), with the same pattern in the Series and Live files and in SearchResultsView (SearchView.swift:246-248). Each VODView run detaches a filter, compactMap and full sort of every movie to take 20 (:180-191): 170 ms on an M4 Pro Mac for 150k, three times concurrently, and the shelf appears only when it finishes. Each AllVODView run filters into a new 49 MB array (:847); each VODCategoryContent run maps a new 47 MB [DBVODStream] queue and scans all file types (:657-661, 53 ms) and then resets visibleCount (:666). The indexes created for this ordering, idx_vodStream_playlist_added and idx_series_playlist_lastModified (AppDatabase.swift:309-320), are not used by any query.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) One task per screen, keyed on a small Equatable struct of all inputs (query, catalogRevision, hiddenStore.version; for the grid content: itemsToken, sortOption, filter).
2) Recently added: fetch a short list once in the store's read closure using the existing index, and let the view only drop hidden categories and take 20:
```sql
SELECT * FROM vodStream WHERE playlistId = ? ORDER BY added DESC LIMIT 60
```
Measured 0.21 ms against 170 ms. `added` is a text column; ten-digit unix timestamps order correctly as text, and the Swift side keeps the existing `Int(added)` filter for junk values. The same applies to series.lastModified. The shelf is then available in the same frame as the others.
3) VODCategoryContent: build the play queue when the player is presented, not on every recompute (pass the items and map in presentMoviePlayer), and skip the copy in AllVODView when nothing is hidden and the query is empty. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166))

**Verifier reasons:** Confirmed from code: three `.task(id:)` modifiers call the same function and all start on appear in VODView (Views/VODView.swift:157-159), VODCategoryContent (:737-739), AllVODView (:833-835), two in VODCategoryDetailView (:574-575), and the same in SeriesView.swift:158-160, LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107 / 508-509 / 629-631 / 733-735 and SearchView.swift:246-248 (nine detached scans on first appearance). History shows the pattern came with the original code (d2489f9); no comment marks it as deliberate.

Recently added is a full in-memory sort per run (VODView.swift:180-191; SeriesView.swift:231-246). I measured 172 ms for 150k and 41 ms for 50k on this Mac (scratchpad/agents/verify-mainthread-b), matching the finding. The pop-in is real in code: displayCategories and displayItemsByCategory are assigned first (:176-177) and the shelf, which sits above the category stack (:78-80), is assigned after the await. The demo data has no such shelf (shots/iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png), so the screenshots cannot show it. The two indexes at Database/AppDatabase.swift:309-320 are used by no query (grep for added/lastModified ordering finds only the in-memory sort options).

Overstated: the 290 MB figure. VODCategoryContent's full-size recompute runs once on open, because the second and third AllVODView results compare equal under its coarse `==` (:600-605); the three early runs see an empty list. Peak is nearer 150 to 200 MB: three 49 MB filter results plus one 47 MB queue.

Problems in the fix:
1. `catalogRevision` does not exist anywhere in the code base; it must come from another finding.
2. `LIMIT 60` then dropping hidden categories changes results: if the newest 60 rows are in hidden categories the shelf shrinks or disappears, while today's code filters first (:183).
3. Text ordering puts any non-numeric `added` value above all digits, so junk can fill the limited window and the Swift-side Int filter then leaves nothing.
4. Part 3 undoes deliberate work: `streamQueue` is prebuilt off the main thread on purpose (comment at :617-619); mapping at presentation moves a 150k map (about 15 ms here, more on a phone) onto the tap and changes MovieDetailView's and VODPlayerShell's queue type, which is hand-off territory.
5. One task per screen still restarts on every reappear.

**Corrected claim:** Each browse screen starts its recompute two or three times on appear and again on every reappear. On Movies and Series home each run sorts the whole catalog to find 20 recent items (172 ms per run for 150k on an M4 Pro), and the shelf is assigned after the category shelves, so it pops in above them and pushes them down on first open. Opening All Movies makes three 49 MB filtered copies where one, or none, is needed.

**Corrected fix:** 1. One `.task(id:)` per screen keyed on an Equatable struct of the existing inputs (debouncedQuery, contentStore.streamsLoaded, the hidden-id set; for the grid content itemsToken, sortOption, the filter). Use a catalog revision only if another change introduces one.
2. Recently added, keeping today's semantics: have the store compute a candidate list once per catalog load inside the read closure that already runs off the main thread (fetchVODStreamsData / fetchSeriesData), by sorting only (index, timestamp) pairs and keeping the top 200. Sorting pairs measured 17 ms against 172 ms with the same result. The view then filters visible categories and takes 20 synchronously, in the same assignment as the shelves, so nothing pops in. If fewer than 20 survive and the candidate list was truncated, fall back to the current detached path. An index-ordered SQL cursor is an alternative, but it needs a numeric guard (`added GLOB '[0-9]*'`), an early exit after 20 visible rows instead of LIMIT 60, and accepts a different order among equal timestamps.
3. AllVODView / AllSeriesView / AllLiveView: when nothing is hidden and the query is empty, assign the store's array directly and skip the detached filter.
4. Leave streamQueue as it is.
5. Remember the last applied key in @State and return early when it is unchanged, so a reappear neither repeats the work nor touches visibleCount.

**API check:** `View.task(id:priority:_:)`: `@inlinable nonisolated public func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, @_inheritActorContext _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) -> some View where T : Equatable`, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166, iOS 15. `Task.detached(name:priority:operation:)`: _Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014, iOS 13. The id only needs Equatable, so a small struct holding a String, a Bool and a Set<String> compiles. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** A merged key that omits an input silently stops a refresh; each screen's key must list every input its current tasks use. The early-return guard must be keyed on the same struct or a real change is skipped. Storing a candidate list in the store adds a published property that must be set at all three load sites (PlaylistContentStore.swift:146-152, :259-261, :311-317) and cleared in clearLists (:37-48). Keeping streamQueue preserves the deliberate off-main queue; the Equatable shelf rows and pagination are untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit test: for a synthetic catalog including nil, non-numeric and duplicate `added` values and a hidden category holding the newest 300 rows, the new recents result equals the current filter + sort + first 20. Counter test: exactly one recompute per appear and zero on reappear with unchanged inputs. Simulator check that only a run can settle: on a real catalog scroll All Movies past the first page (more than 90 items), open a movie and go back; VODCategoryContent.recompute sets `visibleCount = min(pageSize, count)` (VODView.swift:666), so if the tasks restart on reappear the grid collapses to 90 items and the scroll position is lost. Record whether that happens before and after.

## data-main-thread-8 — Text filtering re-normalizes every title for every query, and the detached scans are never cancelled.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Search tab, Inline search on Live TV / Movies / Series, All Movies / All Series / All Channels search, Category detail search, Category picker
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:13-30, 40-83`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:197-210, 583-586, 846-851`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:296-309, 517-520, 744-749`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:250-263, 555-558, 783-788`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:126-128, 246-278`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:38-52`

**What the user perceives:** Typing in a search field on a large catalog: results trail the keyboard by a second or more and arrive late when typing continues. One inline query over 150k movies costs 657-1186 ms on an M4 Pro Mac; the Search tab's own matcher costs 111-365 ms per content type plus 180 ms to sort a broad result.

**Mechanism (finder):** CatalogTextSearch.matches normalizes the title on every call (fold, replace, split on non-alphanumerics, join: four allocations) and re-normalizes each query word per row (CatalogTextSearch.swift:13-30). The work runs in Task.detached(...).value (for example VODView.swift:197-210). A detached task is not cancelled when the surrounding .task(id:) is, so every debounced keystroke starts another full scan that runs to completion and competes with the newest one. SearchResultsView uses a different matcher (localizedCaseInsensitiveContains, SearchView.swift:126-128), runs three scans per query, and on first appearance does so three times because of its three tasks (:246-248).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Precompute the normalized key once per catalog load, off the main actor, and search the keys:
```swift
// store, built lazily on the first search and cached per catalogRevision
private(set) var vodSearchKeys: [Int: String]   // streamId -> CatalogTextSearch.normalize(name)
// CatalogTextSearch
static func matches(normalizedWords: [[UInt8]], key: String) -> Bool   // memmem over key.utf8
```
Measured on the same 150k catalog: 2-10 ms per query with memmem over UTF-8, 23-257 ms with String.contains, results identical to the current function. Building the keys costs about 790 ms once, off the main actor. Wrap the detached work so cancellation propagates and check Task.isCancelled every few thousand rows:
```swift
let task = Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) { ... }
return await withTaskCancellationHandler { await task.value } onCancel: { task.cancel() }
```
Let SearchResultsView use the same matcher and a single task. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** withTaskCancellationHandler(operation:onCancel:isolation:) (iOS 13.0+, back-deployed (_Concurrency.swiftinterface:2881)); Task.detached(priority:operation:) (iOS 13.0+ (_Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014)); memmem (Darwin libc, usr/include/_string.h:187 in the iOS 26 SDK)

**Verifier reasons:** Claim confirmed. Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:21-30 normalizes the title on every call and normalizes each query word again per row; normalize (:13-19) is fold, replace, split, join. Measured on this Mac over 150k titles: 620 to 1165 ms per query (215 to 390 ms at 50k), matching the finding. The scans run in `Task.detached(...).value` (Views/VODView.swift:197-210, 583-586, 846-851; LiveStreamsView.swift:296-309; SeriesView.swift:250-263), and cancelling the awaiting `.task(id:)` does not cancel a detached task, so every debounced query runs to completion and competes with the next. Stale results are not applied (`guard !Task.isCancelled`, e.g. VODView.swift:212), and the work is off the main thread, so typing itself stays smooth; what the user sees is late results.

The Search tab uses a different matcher (Views/SearchView.swift:126-128, `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains`), which I measured at 118 ms per 150k per content type, runs three scans per query (:260-271) and three times on first appearance (:246-248). It is also locale-sensitive, so it misses the Turkish I/ı case the comment at CatalogTextSearch.swift:9-12 says was fixed for inline search. History gives no reason for the difference (both date from d2489f9).

The fix works but is larger than needed. A per-catalog key dictionary needs a lazy build (about 0.8 s here, several seconds on a phone before the first result), invalidation at every catalog assignment, and `catalogRevision`, which does not exist. A much smaller change gets most of the gain: normalize the query once, and fold pure-ASCII titles byte by byte without Foundation, falling back to the current normalize for anything else. I measured that at 52 to 58 ms per query over 150k with about 6% non-ASCII titles, against 620 to 1165 ms, with identical results on the catalog and on a set of odd inputs (Turkish, full-width, ß, CJK, punctuation). For ASCII, the fold is exactly lowercase A-Z and keep a-z0-9, which is what the current fold and CharacterSet.alphanumerics do.

**Corrected claim:** Inline search on Live TV, Movies and Series and in the All and category screens re-normalizes every title and every query word per row (620 to 1165 ms per query for 150k movies on an M4 Pro), and the detached scans are never cancelled, so results arrive a second or more after typing stops on a large catalog. The Search tab uses a separate, faster but locale-sensitive matcher and runs its three scans three times on first appearance.

**Corrected fix:** Step 1 (small, no stored state):
- CatalogTextSearch: add a prepared query (words normalized once) and an ASCII fast path that lowercases and keeps [a-z0-9] over `text.utf8` into a reused buffer, then `memmem`; on any byte >= 0x80 fall back to the existing normalize. Keep `matches(search:text:)` as a wrapper so existing callers and CatalogTextSearchTests are unchanged. The sortXByRelevance comparators (:40-83) normalize inside the comparator; precompute equals/startsWith flags per item before sorting.
- Cancellation: `let task = Task.detached { ... }; return await withTaskCancellationHandler { await task.value } onCancel: { task.cancel() }`, and check `Task.isCancelled` every few thousand rows inside the loop.
- SearchResultsView: one task keyed on (query, hiddenStore.version, streamsLoaded), and use CatalogTextSearch. That changes what the Search tab matches (diacritic-insensitive, ignores spaces and punctuation, correct under a Turkish locale), which is a small behaviour change the owner should accept knowingly.
Step 2 (only if catalogs with mostly non-Latin titles are still slow): the per-catalog normalized key cache as proposed, built off the main actor after load.

**API check:** `withTaskCancellationHandler<T>(operation:onCancel:isolation:)`: _Concurrency.swiftinterface:2881, `@available(iOS 13.0)` with `@backDeployed(before: iOS 18.0)`. `Task.detached(name:priority:operation:)`: _Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014, iOS 13. `memmem`: usr/include/_string.h:187 in the iOS 26 simulator SDK. The project builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393, 415, 578, 619); CatalogTextSearch is already `nonisolated enum` (CatalogTextSearch.swift:5), so new static helpers there are callable from detached tasks. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** The matcher has a twin in the database configuration that must stay in sync (comment at Database/Persistence.swift:105-107); the fast path is semantically identical, but the equivalence test must pin it. A key cache, if added, can go stale unless invalidated at every catalog assignment. Changing the Search tab matcher alters result sets and should keep its alphabetical ordering unless the owner wants relevance ordering there too. Off-main filtering and sorting stay off-main.

**How to verify:** Extend CatalogTextSearchTests: for the existing vectors plus a synthetic 100k catalog with mixed ASCII, Turkish, Cyrillic and Arabic titles, the fast matcher returns exactly the indices of the current `matches`. Cancellation test: start a scan, cancel the parent task, assert it returns early. Timing on a device with a real catalog: time from last keystroke to results on Movies inline search, before and after; scratchpad/agents/verify-mainthread-b/main.swift reproduces the Mac numbers.

## data-main-thread-9 — With the adult-content filter on, an M3U playlist is filtered on the main actor at every load.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U channels (launch and reload)
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/M3UContentStore.swift:57-63, 83-87, 124-130, 139-146`, `another-iptv-player/Models/AdultContentFilter.swift:39-51`

**What the user perceives:** For M3U users who enabled the filter, the app is frozen right after launch and after each refresh: 433 ms per 100k channels on an M4 Pro Mac, so more than a second for the 310k lists the comments mention, and longer on a phone.

**Mechanism (finder):** loadPlaylist calls applyAdultFilter synchronously between two awaits (M3UContentStore.swift:60; again at :85). The function is `nonisolated` but not async, so it runs on the caller, the main actor. It calls isAdultCategoryName twice per channel; each call uppercases the string and splits it with a freshly inverted CharacterSet (AdultContentFilter.swift:40-44). The grouping right after it was moved off the main actor for this very reason (comment at :124).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Run the filter inside the same detached task as the grouping:
```swift
let (visible, grouped) = await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
    let visible = Self.applyAdultFilter(fetched, enabled: enabled)
    return (visible, Self.group(channels: visible, ungroupedLabel: label))
}.value
```
Make applyAdultFilter static, and hoist `CharacterSet.alphanumerics.inverted` into a static constant in AdultContentFilter. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** Task.detached(priority:operation:) (iOS 13.0+ (_Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014))

**Verifier reasons:** Models/M3UContentStore.swift:60 and :85 call `applyAdultFilter` synchronously inside @MainActor methods. The function is `nonisolated private func` and not async (:139-146), so it runs on the caller, the main actor. It calls `AdultContentFilter.isAdultCategoryName` for the name and the group of every channel; each call uppercases the string and splits it with a freshly inverted CharacterSet (Models/AdultContentFilter.swift:39-51). I measured 434 ms for 100k channels (200k calls) on this Mac, matching the finding's 433 ms. The grouping directly after it was moved to a detached task for the same reason (comment at M3UContentStore.swift:124, class comment at :7-8), so the filter staying on the main actor is an oversight, not a decision; history shows no separate rationale (d2489f9). It only applies when the playlist's adult filter is on, which defaults to off (Models/Playlist.swift:16), and only to M3U playlists. The fix compiles in this structure: DBM3UChannel is Sendable (Models/DBModels.swift:143), Grouping is Sendable (:132), and `group` is already `nonisolated private static` (:148).

**Corrected claim:** With the adult-content filter on, an M3U playlist is filtered on the main actor at every load and reload: 434 ms per 100k channels on an M4 Pro, so about a second or more on a phone for the 310k lists the code comments mention. The filter is off by default, so only users who enabled it are affected.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: make `applyAdultFilter` `nonisolated private static`, capture `enabled` and the label before the task, and run filter plus grouping in the one detached task in both loadPlaylist and reloadIfActive; keep the `loadToken` check after the await. Hoist `CharacterSet.alphanumerics.inverted` into a static constant in AdultContentFilter.

**API check:** `Task.detached(name:priority:operation:)`: _Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014, iOS 13. With SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393) the helper must be explicitly `nonisolated static`, as `group` already is; AdultContentFilter is already `nonisolated enum` (AdultContentFilter.swift:5). No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Low. Filter results are unchanged and covered by AdultContentFilterTests. reloadIfActive has no token check today (:80-91); moving the filter adds no new race beyond the existing await on grouping.

**How to verify:** Unit test: seed 100k M3U channels with filterAdultContent = true, run loadPlaylist while a main-actor heartbeat records its longest gap, assert it stays under about 50 ms. On a device: open a large M3U playlist with the filter on and confirm the dashboard transition no longer freezes.

## data-main-thread-10 — Opening the TV guide builds a row for every channel on the main actor.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: EPG guide
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:66-67, 138-150, 218-221, 249-275, 277-280`, `another-iptv-player/EPG/EPGStore.swift:54, 259-264`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the guide button stalls before the screen settles: 76 ms for 50k Xtream channels and 408 ms for 100k M3U entries on an M4 Pro Mac. On a phone with a large M3U list that is a freeze of a second or more.

**Mechanism (finder):** EPGGuideViewModel is @MainActor (:66-67) and load() calls buildRows() synchronously (:218-221). Per channel it normalizes two keys, resolves the stored key, builds a String id, trims the category and parses the icon URL (:253-262); for M3U it first parses and classifies every URL to drop non-live entries (:264, :277-280). rebuildSections then groups all rows (:138-150). The programme layouts are already computed off the main actor; the row model is not.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Snapshot the inputs on the main actor (the store's array, and the EPG alias map through a new read-only accessor on EPGStore for `resolution`), then build rows and sections in a detached task and assign them once:
```swift
let entries = PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreams
let aliases = EPGStore.shared.resolutionSnapshot
let built = await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
    Self.makeRows(xtream: entries, aliases: aliases)   // nonisolated static
}.value
guard generation == loadGeneration else { return }
rows = built.rows; orderedSections = built.sections; recomputeItems()
```
Show the existing loading state meanwhile. The now/next snapshot is untouched. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** Task.detached(priority:operation:) (iOS 13.0+ (_Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014))

**Verifier reasons:** Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:66-67 is @MainActor and `load()` calls `buildRows()` synchronously (:218-221). Per Xtream channel it normalizes two keys, resolves the stored key, builds the id string, trims the category and parses the icon URL (:253-262); for M3U it first parses and classifies every URL (:265, :280-283). `rebuildSections` then groups all rows (:138-150), and `rebuildLayouts` builds `Set(rows.map(\.channelKey))` on the main actor too (:288). EPGGuideView starts this from `.task` on push (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:54-57), so the stall lands at the start of the push transition. I compiled and ran the finding's benchmark: 84 ms for 50k Xtream channels and 413 ms for 100k M3U entries on this Mac, matching its 76 and 408 ms. The programme layouts are already computed off the main actor (:315-329), so moving the row model is consistent with the existing design, and nothing in comments or history marks the synchronous build as deliberate. The visible states do not change: the screen shows the loading state until layouts are ready (:331-332) either way.

One compile detail the sketch leaves out: the project defaults declarations to @MainActor (project.pbxproj:393; explained at EPG/EPGConstants.swift:6-8). EPGGuideRow has an explicit initializer (:19-29) and `category(id:name:)` is a plain private static (:193), so both are main-actor isolated today and cannot be called from a detached task as written.

**Corrected claim:** Opening the TV guide builds a row for every channel on the main actor at the start of the push: 84 ms for 50k Xtream channels and 413 ms for 100k M3U entries on an M4 Pro, several times that on a phone.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with the isolation annotations this project needs: mark `EPGGuideRow` `nonisolated` (and Sendable), make `category(id:name:)` and the new `makeRows` `nonisolated static`, and add a read-only snapshot of `resolution` to EPGStore, the same way refresh already copies it before a read (EPG/EPGStore.swift:141). Snapshot the store arrays and the alias map on the main actor, build rows and sections in a detached task, check `generation == loadGeneration` after the await, then assign rows and orderedSections and call recomputeItems once. Move the `Set(rows.map(\.channelKey))` at :288 into the same result. `EPGConstants`, `M3UParser`, `M3UStreamClassifier.classify` and `L()` are already nonisolated.

**API check:** `Task.detached(name:priority:operation:)`: _Concurrency.swiftinterface:4014, iOS 13. Callable off the main actor today: `nonisolated enum EPGConstants` (EPG/EPGConstants.swift:9), `nonisolated enum M3UParser` (Networking/M3UParser.swift:61), `nonisolated static func classify` (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:955), `nonisolated func L` (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:127). Not callable yet: EPGGuideRow's explicit init and `category(id:name:)`, which need `nonisolated`. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** load() is re-entered by the refresh buttons (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:92, :280) and cancelled on disappear (:58-62); the generation check after the new await must cover both or a stale row set can be assigned. The alias map must be the one in force when the rows are built; snapshot it in the same main-actor step as the channel array. The now/next snapshot and the layout precompute are not touched.

**How to verify:** Add to EPGGuidePerformanceTests: makeRows for 50k synthetic streams returns the same rows and section order as the current buildRows plus rebuildSections, and a main-actor heartbeat during load() shows no gap above about 50 ms. On a device with a large playlist: tap the guide button and confirm the push animation starts without a stall. Benchmark source: scratchpad/agents/mainthread-bench/Sources/guidebench.
