## data-main-thread-11 — Streams without a valid category are hidden after a normal launch and only appear under "Uncategorized" after a refresh; the merge that fixes it runs on the main actor.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category picker
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:144-152, 245-249, 302-317, 366-406, 410-440`

**What the user perceives:** Channels or movies whose category id is null, "0" or missing from the category list are not on any shelf after launch. After a pull-to-refresh or a Settings refresh an "Uncategorized" category appears with them; after the next launch it is gone again. On a reload the main thread also stalls while every bucket is copied: 22 ms best case and up to 208 ms on a first run for 150k movies on an M4 Pro Mac, per content type.

**Mechanism (finder):** Commit 0ab5bcd added mergeUncategorized and appendingUncategorized to reloadFromDatabase (:305-310) and later to the scoped reload (:246-247 and the other cases), but loadPlaylist still assigns the raw grouping (:146-151) and never appends the synthetic category. The LEFT JOIN fetch keeps the orphans (:366-406), but their bucket key is "" or an unknown id that no category row references. mergeUncategorized (:410-419) is a static function of a main-actor class called after the awaits, and it rebuilds every bucket with `result[key, default: []].append(contentsOf:)`, which copies each array instead of sharing it.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Do the merge inside the nonisolated fetch functions, which already run on the reader queue, and use the same result in all three load paths:
```swift
nonisolated private static func fetchVODStreamsData(playlistId: UUID, validIds: Set<String>, db: Database) throws -> VODStreamsData {
    let streams = try ...
    var by: [String: [VODWithCategory]] = [:]
    for s in streams {
        let id = s.stream.categoryId ?? ""
        by[(id.isEmpty || !validIds.contains(id)) ? uncategorizedCategoryId : id, default: []].append(s)
    }
    return VODStreamsData(streams: streams, byCategory: by)
}
```
loadPlaylist then calls appendingUncategorized exactly like reloadFromDatabase does. This removes the main-actor copy and makes launch and refresh agree. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Verifier reasons:** Read Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift. loadPlaylist assigns the raw grouping (:146-151) and the Phase-1 category list (:132-134); it never calls mergeUncategorized or appendingUncategorized. reloadFromDatabase (:305-310) and the scoped reload (:246-247, :258-259, :270-271) do. The fetch functions group by `categoryId ?? ""` (:377, :391, :405), so after a launch orphans sit under "" or an unknown id. The home shelves iterate the category list and index the dictionary by category id (Views/VODView.swift:83-87, same pattern in Live and Series), so those buckets are never shown. git log -S'mergeUncategorized' gives 0ab5bcd (commit message: "uncategorized streams surfaced instead of silently dropped") and 1cce013; nothing marks the launch path as deliberate, and the first-import path (:115-125) also goes through the unmerged assignment. So the correctness claim holds.

Three corrections. (1) Orphans are not fully hidden after launch: the flat arrays still carry them, so they appear in All Movies / All Series / All Channels (VODView.swift:841), Search (SearchView.swift:252-254) and the guide. They are missing from shelves, the category picker and the live zap queue. (2) After a pull-to-refresh the shelves do not pick up the new category straight away: the scoped reload never toggles streamsLoaded, and the home views recompute only on `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)`, the query and the hidden set (VODView.swift:157-159, LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, SeriesView.swift:158-160). The picker reads the store directly (VODView.swift:13-20), so it lists "Uncategorized" immediately while the shelf row appears only when the tab or screen re-appears; picking it meanwhile scrolls to a row that does not exist. (3) Main-actor cost: mergeUncategorized is a main-actor static (:410) and append(contentsOf:) copies every bucket. My own run (150k VOD, 300 buckets, M4-class Mac, release build) gave 23 ms best and 30 ms first run; the 208 ms figure did not reproduce. It is a one-off hitch as a refresh finishes, minor next to the correctness problem.

**Corrected claim:** After a normal launch, and after the first import, streams whose category id is null, empty or not in the category list are on no shelf, not in the category picker and not in the live zap queue; they remain reachable through the All screens, Search and the guide. A Settings refresh adds an "Uncategorized" category holding them; a pull-to-refresh adds it to the picker at once but to the shelves only when the screen re-appears, because the scoped reload does not trigger the shelf recompute. On the next launch it is gone again. The merge that produces it runs on the main actor and copies every bucket: about 23-30 ms for 150k movies on a Mac, once per reload.

**Corrected fix:** Build the buckets with the uncategorized remap inside the nonisolated fetch functions and use that result in all three load paths, as proposed, with two adjustments.

1. Take the valid ids from the same read instead of passing them in. The scoped reload fetches categories and streams concurrently (:239-245), so a `validIds` parameter is not available there. Either read them in the fetch function:
```swift
let validIds = try String.fetchSet(db, sql: "SELECT id FROM category WHERE playlistId = ? AND type = 'vod'", arguments: [playlistId])
```
or fetch categories and streams in one read closure. Both also give a consistent snapshot.

2. In loadPlaylist, after Phase 2, set the three category lists with appendingUncategorized exactly as reloadFromDatabase does (:308-310). mergeUncategorized can then be deleted.

Separately, and needed for this to be visible after a pull-to-refresh: make the scoped reload trigger the shelf recompute, for example a catalog revision counter bumped by every load path and used as the `.task(id:)` value in the three home views. Check whether another finding already covers that.

**API check:** No SDK API. GRDB 7.10.0 checkout: `public static func fetchSet(_ db: Database, sql: String, arguments: StatementArguments = StatementArguments(), adapter: (any RowAdapter)? = nil) throws -> Set<Self>` at GRDB/Core/DatabaseValueConvertible.swift:524, available to String. `uncategorizedCategoryId` is already `nonisolated static let` (:361), so the nonisolated fetch functions can use it.

**Regression risks:** Playlists with orphans gain an "Uncategorized" shelf at the end on every launch; that is the behaviour 0ab5bcd intended, and it appears after Phase 2 as it does today after a refresh. HiddenCategoryStore keys on the fixed id, so hiding it keeps working. applyVODMetadata already probes both the raw key and the synthetic key (:170). The Recently Added filter still excludes orphans, because it tests the raw categoryId against visible category ids (VODView.swift:183); unchanged, worth noting. The Equatable shelf rows and the off-main filtering are untouched.

**How to verify:** Make the fetch functions internal and unit-test them against AppDatabase.empty(): seed one category, one stream in it, one with categoryId nil, one with "0" and one with an unknown id; assert that the bucket keys are the category id and "__uncategorized__" and that the latter holds three streams. Do not drive this through loadPlaylist in a test: the store is bound to AppDatabase.shared and an empty category table triggers a network bootstrap. Manual check with the same data: launch, confirm the shelf and picker entry are present, pull to refresh, confirm they are still there and that the picker entry scrolls to the shelf.

## data-main-thread-12 — The catalog is held twice in memory, and the All Movies screen adds two more full copies.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort L · risk medium
- Screens: All screens of an Xtream playlist, All Movies, All Series, Search
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:26-32, 377, 391, 405`, `another-iptv-player/Models/DBModels.swift:34-64, 180-184`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:616-619, 657-664, 815, 847`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:140-142, 260-277`, `another-iptv-player/Models/M3UContentStore.swift:17-18`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Step 1 is a plain fix. Steps 2 and 3 change the store's shape and touch every browse view; the owner should decide whether the memory saving (about 64 MB for a catalog of 150k movies, 40k series and 30k channels) is worth that refactor now.

**What the user perceives:** Not a visible defect by itself, but it is the reason memory warnings arrive early on large playlists: the image cache is purged (posters reload while scrolling) and the app is a more likely eviction target in the background, so it cold-starts more often.

**Mechanism (finder):** MemoryLayout<VODWithCategory>.stride is 328 bytes: DBVODStream carries eleven optional detail fields that are nil for almost every list row (DBModels.swift:43-56). The store keeps a flat array and a per-category dictionary built with Dictionary(grouping:), which copies each element into separate arrays (PlaylistContentStore.swift:377, 391, 405). For 150k movies that is 49 MB twice, before string storage; series (264-byte DBSeries, plot text included) and live (128 bytes) add their own pairs. AllVODView filters into another 49 MB array (VODView.swift:847) and VODCategoryContent builds a 47 MB [DBVODStream] queue (:664). Broad search results are further full-size copies.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Step 1 (small, with the recompute finding): build the play queue when the player is presented, and share the store's buffer in the All screens when nothing is filtered. This removes about 96 MB on All Movies for a 150k catalog.
Step 2: keep one copy. Either keep only the per-category buckets and build the flat sortIndex-ordered list on demand, off the main actor, for the All screens, search and the guide; or keep the flat array and store per-category `[Int32]` index arrays behind a small RandomAccessCollection wrapper that the shelf rows iterate. The flat arrays are read in few places (LiveStreamsView.swift:125, VODView.swift:120, SeriesView.swift:121, EPGGuideViewModel.swift:253 and the recompute and search functions).
Step 3, optional: a slim list record (id, name, icon, categoryId, rating, extension, added, sortIndex, about 112 bytes) with details read per screen from the database.

**Verifier reasons:** The facts hold. Measured strides with the models copied verbatim: VODWithCategory 328, DBVODStream 312, SeriesWithCategory 280, DBSeries 264, LiveStreamWithCategory 128, DBLiveStream 112. The store publishes a flat array and a per-category dictionary for each type (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:26-32); Dictionary(grouping:) (:377, :391, :405) copies each element, sharing only string storage. AllVODView.recompute always filters into a new array, even with nothing hidden and no query (Views/VODView.swift:847). VODCategoryContent.recompute builds `sorted.map(\.stream)` for the whole list (:660, :664); with default order and no file-type filter `sorted` shares the caller's buffer (Models/VODSortOption.swift:40-42, :89), so All Movies adds two catalog-sized buffers, about 49 MB and 47 MB at 150k movies. Search results are filtered copies (Views/SearchView.swift:260-271). M3UContentStore holds channels and channelsByGroup the same way (:17-18).

What does not hold is the user-facing consequence. "Memory warnings arrive early, the image cache is purged, the app is evicted more often" is asserted from code alone. Roughly 130-200 MB of catalog is far below the foreground limit of current iPhones and iPads, and no measurement shows a memory warning. That part can only be settled on a device.

History: the owner already knows about the duplication and deferred it. The 0ab5bcd commit message says it fixed 95 of 96 findings and that "the remaining one is an optional catalog memory-layout optimization, deliberately deferred"; unload() exists to drop "flat + kategori sözlükleri" when leaving the dashboard (:180-182). The prebuilt queue is deliberate performance work: "Prebuilt play queue matching displayItems, so body passes don't re-map a large array on every render (critical for All Movies)" (VODView.swift:617-619).

**Corrected claim:** The Xtream catalog is stored twice (flat array plus per-category buckets: about 98 MB of element storage for 150k movies, 22 MB for 40k series, 8 MB for 30k channels, before string storage), and the All Movies screen adds two more catalog-sized buffers (about 96 MB at 150k). This is a memory-footprint cost with no demonstrated user-visible effect; whether it causes memory warnings or background eviction is unmeasured. The duplication was recorded as an optional optimisation and deliberately deferred in 0ab5bcd.

**Corrected fix:** Step 1 only, and only the half that is free: in AllVODView.recompute (and the Series and Live equivalents) assign the store's array directly when the hidden set and the query are both empty, so the buffer is shared; that removes about 49 MB at 150k with no behaviour change.

The play-queue half needs care. Replacing the prebuilt `streamQueue` with a map at play time costs 20-29 ms on a Mac for 150k items (measured), so it must run off the main actor in the detail screen's existing async play path, and the grid must pass the shared `[VODWithCategory]` buffer rather than re-mapping per render, or it undoes the work described at VODView.swift:617-619. The 47 MB then moves to the playback session instead of disappearing. Treat it as optional.

Steps 2 and 3 (single copy, slim list record): do not schedule on this evidence. They are the item the owner deferred, they touch every browse view, and nothing shows a user-visible gain. Reopen only if a device measurement shows memory warnings.

**API check:** No SDK API involved; nothing to verify. Standard-library Array and Dictionary only.

**Regression risks:** Play-queue change: re-mapping on the main actor at tap, or per render, brings back the freeze the prebuilt queue removed. The queue also crosses into VODPlayerShell, which is out of scope and takes `[DBVODStream]`. Steps 2-3: every shelf, grid, search and the EPG guide read these arrays; the Equatable shelf rows compare bucket arrays, and an index-wrapper collection changes their element type and equality. applyVODMetadata writes into both copies and would need rewriting.

**How to verify:** Device only. On an iPhone with a real 150k-movie playlist, read the memory gauge (or phys_footprint) at the Movies home, on All Movies, and after scrolling 2,000 posters; log UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification and Nuke cache purges; background the app for ten minutes with other apps in use and note whether it cold-starts. If there are no warnings and the footprint stays in the low hundreds of MB, only the free buffer-sharing change is justified. A unit test can pin the strides with MemoryLayout.

## data-main-thread-13 — Catalog imports write each row with save() and build M3U ids with String(format:) per byte, which makes refreshes about two to three times longer than needed.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Pull-to-refresh, Settings refresh, Add playlist
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:517-527, 535-546, 554-579`, `another-iptv-player/Models/XtreamImporter.swift:51-90`, `another-iptv-player/Models/M3UImporter.swift:30-60, 69-83`

**What the user perceives:** The "saving" phase of a refresh or first import lasts longer than it has to, and while it runs every other write waits behind it: a favourite toggle or a watch-progress save does not land until the import transaction commits.

**Mechanism (finder):** After `DELETE FROM ... WHERE playlistId = ?`, each row is written with save(db) (PlaylistContentStore.swift:522, 527, 540, 546, 559, 579; XtreamImporter.swift:56-89; M3UImporter.swift:59). GRDB's save tries an UPDATE first and inserts when no row changed, so every row costs two statements. Measured on an M4 Pro Mac: 150k movies take 3.42 s with save and 1.33 s with insert; 100k M3U rows take 2.40 s against 0.85 s. M3UImporter.stableChannelID formats the SHA-256 digest with `String(format: "%02x")` once per byte (:82): 1.83 s per 100k ids against 84 ms with a hex table, same output. All of it runs inside one write transaction.

**Proposed fix (finder):** In the replace functions, where the rows were just deleted, use `try row.insert(db, onConflict: .replace)`; this keeps the last-one-wins behaviour for duplicate ids in a panel response. In XtreamImporter the rows may already exist (edit flow), so use the same call or delete first as the refresh path does. Replace the hex formatting with a lookup table:
```swift
let hex = Array("0123456789abcdef".utf8)
var out = [UInt8](); out.reserveCapacity(64)
for b in digest { out.append(hex[Int(b >> 4)]); out.append(hex[Int(b & 0x0f)]) }
return String(decoding: out, as: UTF8.self)
```
No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** PersistableRecord.insert(_:onConflict:) (GRDB 7.10.0 package, not an SDK API; verified in checkout GRDB/Record/PersistableRecord+Insert.swift:34)

**Verifier reasons:** Every import row is written with save(db): Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:522, 527, 540, 546, 559, 579; Models/XtreamImporter.swift:56-89; Models/M3UImporter.swift:59. GRDB's save tries UPDATE first and inserts on recordNotFound (GRDB/Record/MutablePersistableRecord+Save.swift:375-402), so after the preceding DELETE each row costs a failed UPDATE plus an INSERT. I rebuilt the benchmark with the real foreign key to playlist and three secondary indexes: 150k VOD rows take 3.56 s with save and 1.77 s with insert(onConflict: .replace) on a Mac, a factor of 2.0 (the finding's 2.6 was measured without the foreign key). Duplicate ids keep last-one-wins: two rows with the same key leave one row holding the second value.

M3UImporter.stableChannelID formats each digest byte with String(format:) (:82). Measured 1.75 s per 100k ids against 85 ms with a hex table, with identical output for plain, empty, `#n` and non-ASCII inputs. It runs inside the write closure (:44), so it lengthens the transaction; M3UContentStore's own comment speaks of 310K+ channel lists, where this alone is about 5 s on a Mac.

The writer is a DatabasePool (Database/Persistence.swift:54): other writes queue behind the import transaction, reads do not. No comment or history marks save() as deliberate beyond "upsert avoids conflicts" (XtreamImporter.swift:50), which the replacement preserves.

Scope note: only the save phase shortens, by about half. The network fetch and JSON decoding are untouched, so the title's "refreshes two to three times longer" overstates the whole-refresh effect.

**Corrected claim:** Catalog imports write each row with save(), which costs a failed UPDATE plus an INSERT per row, and M3U ids are hex-encoded with String(format:) per byte. The database-save phase of a refresh or first import takes about twice as long as needed (3.6 s against 1.8 s for 150k movies on a Mac, more on a phone), and M3U imports spend a further 1.7 s per 100k channels on id formatting. Other writes (favourite toggles, watch progress) wait for that transaction. Network and decoding time are unaffected.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with one refinement for the add/edit importer.

- PlaylistContentStore.replace*Catalog and M3UImporter.replace (rows were just deleted): `try row.insert(db, onConflict: .replace)`.
- M3UImporter.stableChannelID: the hex lookup table as written in the finding.
- XtreamImporter.syncAndSave: rows can already exist when a playlist is edited (Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:129-130 reuses the id). INSERT OR REPLACE deletes and re-inserts an existing series row, and that delete cascades to its cached seasons and episodes (verified with sqlite3: the child row is gone after REPLACE and kept after UPDATE). Either accept that, since a refresh already does the same and save() resets seasonsLoaded to false anyway, or use `try row.upsert(db)`, which is a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and keeps today's semantics. upsert was not benchmarked here.

**API check:** GRDB 7.10.0 checkout, not an SDK API. `public func insert(_ db: Database, onConflict conflictResolution: Database.ConflictResolution? = nil) throws` at GRDB/Record/PersistableRecord+Insert.swift:34; `case replace = "REPLACE"` at GRDB/Core/Database.swift:2164. `public func upsert(_ db: Database) throws` at GRDB/Record/PersistableRecord+Upsert.swift:220, marked `@available(iOS 15, macOS 12, tvOS 15, watchOS 8, *)`, fine for the iOS 18 target. CryptoKit SHA256 and String(decoding:as:) are already in use or standard library.

**Regression risks:** stableChannelID output must stay byte-identical, or M3U favourites and watch history lose their channels; the lookup table produces the same lowercase hex. INSERT OR REPLACE in the edit flow drops cached seasons and episodes of existing series through the cascade; they are refetched on the next detail open, but a series opened offline after an edit would show no episodes. The atomic delete-then-insert transaction from 0ab5bcd is unchanged.

**How to verify:** Unit tests against AppDatabase.empty(): (1) stableChannelID equals a set of recorded current outputs, including an occurrence > 0 and the empty-URL fallback; (2) replaceVODCatalog with a duplicated stream_id leaves one row with the last values; (3) for the importer, seed a series with a season, run the import, and assert the chosen behaviour (season kept with upsert, removed with REPLACE). Timing: 100k-row import before and after on a device, reading the existing "DATABASE: Total Insertion completed" log line.

## data-main-thread-14 — Playing a movie from Continue Watching scans every category bucket on the main actor to find its queue.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home (Continue Watching), Movies history list, M3U channels (Continue Watching)
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:217-256`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:286-291`

**What the user perceives:** A short delay between the tap on a Continue Watching card and the player appearing: up to 20 ms on an M4 Pro Mac for 150k movies when the movie sits in a late bucket or is no longer in the catalog. It adds to the database round trip that precedes it.

**Mechanism (finder):** presentHistoryPlayer first awaits DownloadManager.localURL (VODView.swift:219-226) and then, on the main actor, loops over all values of vodStreamsByCategoryId calling first(where:) on each (:249-255). The M3U counterpart does a string-id first(where:) over the flat channel array (M3UChannelsView.swift:287).

**Proposed fix (finder):** The handler is already asynchronous, so resolve the category from the database in the same task (a primary-key lookup) and index the bucket directly:
```swift
let movie = try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in
    try DBVODStream.fetchOne(db, key: ["streamId": streamIdInt, "playlistId": playlist.id])
}
let key = movie?.categoryId ?? ""
let bucket = contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId[key]
    ?? contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId[PlaylistContentStore.uncategorizedCategoryId] ?? []
```
For M3U, build a `[String: Int]` id index in the detached grouping pass. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** FetchableRecord.fetchOne(_:key:) with a dictionary key (GRDB 7.10.0 package, not an SDK API; the checkout was not grepped for this exact overload. The filter-based fetch already used at VODView.swift:235 is an equivalent that is known to compile)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is as described. presentHistoryPlayer awaits DownloadManager.localURL, hops back to the main actor (Views/VODView.swift:219-226) and then loops over every bucket with first(where:) (:249-255). Measured worst case (stream not in the catalog, 150k movies, 300 buckets) on a Mac: 13.7 ms best, 19.4 ms first run; a hit costs about half on average. The bucket's queue map is negligible (0.07 ms for 500 items). The M3U counterpart is one first(where:) on a string id over the flat array (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:287), a few milliseconds even at 300k channels.

What I do not accept is that a user perceives it. It is a single block of one to three frames on a phone, before the player's presentation starts, not during an animation or a scroll. Nearby code shows the owner already tunes this kind of tap latency where it mattered (LiveStreamsView.swift:322-327 replaced an eager flatMap with a lazy scan for the same reason), so the cleanup is in keeping with the code base, but it is polish, not a visible defect.

The proposed fix compiles: the dictionary-key fetchOne exists and my benchmark fetched a row with `key: ["streamId": Int, "playlistId": UUID]`. It adds a database round trip to save an in-memory scan, and it must still confirm that the movie is in the chosen bucket, since the in-memory key can be the synthetic uncategorized id. The M3U id index would cost several MB of dictionary for a saving of a few milliseconds.

**Corrected claim:** Playing a movie from Continue Watching or the history list scans all category buckets on the main actor to find its queue: up to about 14-20 ms on a Mac for 150k movies, likely one to three frames on a phone, once per tap and before the player appears. It is real but below what a user would notice on its own. The M3U lookup is cheaper still.

**Corrected fix:** Optional, lowest priority. If done, keep it in memory and move it off the main actor rather than adding a database query: the handler is already asynchronous, so capture `contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId` (a reference copy), run the scan and the `map(\.stream)` in a detached task alongside the DownloadManager lookup, then present on the main actor. Behaviour, queue contents and the single-item fallback stay identical. Leave the M3U lookup as it is.

**API check:** GRDB 7.10.0 checkout, not an SDK API: `public static func fetchOne(_ db: Database, key: [String: (any DatabaseValueConvertible)?]?) throws -> Self?` at GRDB/Record/FetchableRecord+TableRecord.swift:474. It requires a unique key; (streamId, playlistId) is the vodStream primary key (Database/AppDatabase.swift:65). Compiled and returned the row in my benchmark. The corrected fix needs no new API.

**Regression risks:** Hand-off into the out-of-scope VODPlayerShell: the queue passed must stay the same bucket in the same order, or previous/next changes. With the database variant, a key that resolves to a bucket not containing the movie would open the player with a wrong queue unless membership is checked. With the detached variant, a second tap during the scan could present twice; reuse the existing guard on pending presentations.

**How to verify:** Extract a pure `queue(for:in:)` helper and unit-test it: same queue as the current loop for a hit in the first and last bucket, nil for a stream that is not in the catalog. To decide whether it is worth doing at all, time the loop with a signpost on a device with a 150k catalog; under about 30 ms, skip it.

## settings-ux-1 — Xtream Settings hides Statistics, TV Guide, the adult filter and Clear Watch History whenever the account request has not succeeded, and makes local numbers wait for that request

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream)
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:263-345`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:392-401`, `Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:26-30`

**What the user perceives:** Offline, or when the panel is down, Settings jumps from 'Playlist Information' straight to 'About': no content counts, no TV Guide section, no adult filter, no 'Clear Watch History' (iphone-light/T02-settings-2.png and T03-settings-3.png show exactly this with the demo playlist's HTTP 404). When the request does succeed, four sections pop in below the fold a moment after the screen appears and push About down. 'Storage used' reads 'Zero KB' and 'Delete all downloads' is missing until the network call returns or times out (20 s).

**Mechanism (finder):** PlaylistSettingsView.swift:263 wraps four sections in `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil`: Stats (264-292), Server (294-315), XtreamEPGSettingsSection (318) and Content Management (321-344). Only the Server section depends on that response; the others are local (SQLite counts, EPG flag, history delete). In addition `.task` at 392-396 awaits fetchAuthInfo() before fetchLocalStats() and refreshDownloadUsage(), so local values wait on PanelURLSession's 20 s request timeout (XtreamAPIClient.swift:28). The gate dates from the original import (git log -S: d2489f9), there is no comment giving a reason.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make the three local sections unconditional and keep only the Server section behind the response; load local data first and the account in parallel.

```swift
Section(L("settings.stats.title")) { /* counts */ }        // always
if hasServerInfo { Section(L("settings.server.title")) { ... } }
XtreamEPGSettingsSection(playlist: playlist)               // always
Section(L("settings.content_management.title")) { ... }   // always
...
.task {
    async let account: Void = fetchAuthInfo()
    await fetchLocalStats()
    await refreshDownloadUsage()
    await account
}
```
No new API, no iOS 26 dependency.

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift. Line 263 `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil {` wraps Stats (264-292), Server (294-315), XtreamEPGSettingsSection (318) and Content Management (321-344). Only the Server section reads authResponse; the counts come from SQLite (fetchLocalStats 412-432), the EPG section reads the playlist row and DBEPGSource (Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:113-166), clear-history is a local DELETE (434-446). verify() throws on HTTP errors and also when auth == 0 (Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:153-163), so the sections are missing offline, when the panel is down and for an expired account. Screenshots iphone-light/T02-settings-2.png and T03-settings-3.png show exactly this: 'Playlist Information' with the red 404 row, then 'About', nothing in between. `.task` (392-396) awaits fetchAuthInfo() before fetchLocalStats() and refreshDownloadUsage(), so 'Storage used' shows 'Zero KB' (T01-settings-1.png) and 'Delete all downloads' (115) is absent until the request returns; PanelURLSession's request timeout is 20 s (XtreamAPIClient.swift:28). History: `git log -S'if authResponse?.userInfo != nil'` returns only d2489f9 (monorepo import); no comment gives a reason, and nothing in the three local sections needs the response. No UI test references these rows. Severity lowered to medium: in the normal online case the pop-in happens below the fold on iPhone (T01 ends at Player Settings), and the 20 s wait only applies to an unresponsive panel (offline fails at once).

**Corrected claim:** Xtream Settings hides Content Statistics, TV Guide (EPG), the adult filter and Clear Watch History whenever the account request has not succeeded (offline, panel down, expired account: verify() throws for auth == 0), and they pop in late when it does succeed. Storage used and the Delete-all-downloads row wait for that request (up to 20 s on an unresponsive panel).

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: remove the outer gate at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:263, keep only the Server section conditional (its existing inner condition at 294-295 is already sufficient), and run the local loads first:

.task {
    async let account: Void = fetchAuthInfo()
    await fetchLocalStats()
    await refreshDownloadUsage()
    await account
}

Apply the same order in `.refreshable` (397-401). Leave TipJarRow() at line 355 untouched.

**API check:** No new API. `async let` with a Void-returning MainActor method compiles in Swift 5 mode with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393).

**Regression risks:** With the adult-filter toggle always reachable, the stale-flag bug of settings-ux-2 becomes reachable offline too (sync fails, syncError is shown in the top section). The section order on screen changes for nobody; nothing else reads the gate. Does not touch the tip-jar row.

**How to verify:** UI test with the demo fixture (verify returns 404): open Settings, scroll to the bottom, assert 'Content Statistics', 'TV Guide (EPG)', 'Filter Adult Content' and 'Clear Watch History' exist and that the counts are 13 / 12 / 8. Compare with iphone-light/T02 and T03.

## settings-ux-2 — Flipping 'Filter Adult Content' in Xtream Settings starts a full catalog re-download without asking, runs it with the previous flag value, and shows its progress in a different section

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Live TV, Movies, Series
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:322-332`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:496-536`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:56-85`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:447-470`, `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:141-146`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: How should the switch behave: confirm and re-download now (proposed), save now and apply on the next refresh, or filter locally at load time as the M3U store does (no network, but adult rows stay in SQLite)?

**What the user perceives:** A single tap on a switch near the bottom of Settings silently kicks off a download of the whole catalog (minutes on a 100k+ playlist). Nothing changes next to the switch: the spinner and the phase text appear in the first section, usually off-screen. When it finishes, adult content is still listed (or still hidden). Flipping the switch back while it runs starts a second full download in parallel.

**Mechanism (finder):** `.onChange(of: filterAdultContent)` (330-332) calls saveFilterSetting, which writes `updated` to the database (497-502) and then calls `syncContents()` (504). syncContents passes the view's immutable `playlist` (519), the copy ContentView captured when the playlist was opened, and syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal reads `playlist.filterAdultContent` from that argument (PlaylistContentStore.swift:463). The new value is therefore saved but not applied. The edit-playlist sheet does the same job correctly with the new struct (AddPlaylistView.swift:141-146). The toggle is not disabled while `isSyncing`, and syncContents has no re-entrancy guard (513), so two toggles mean two concurrent full syncs; the first to finish clears isSyncing. Progress and errors render only in the top section (62-85).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Fix the value: `syncContents(using: updated)` and pass that to syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal; add `guard !isSyncing` at the top. 2) Ask before starting, anchored to the row, reusing existing strings. 3) Disable the toggle and show a spinner in the same section while it runs.

```swift
@State private var pendingAdultFilter: Bool?
Toggle(isOn: Binding(get: { filterAdultContent },
                     set: { pendingAdultFilter = $0 })) { ... }
    .disabled(isSyncing)
    .confirmationDialog(L("settings.filter_adult.title"),
        isPresented: Binding(get: { pendingAdultFilter != nil },
                             set: { if !$0 { pendingAdultFilter = nil } }),
        titleVisibility: .visible) {
        Button(L("settings.refresh_all")) {
            guard let v = pendingAdultFilter else { return }
            filterAdultContent = v
            Task { await saveFilterSetting(newValue: v) }
        }
        Button(L("common.cancel"), role: .cancel) { }
    } message: { Text(L("settings.filter_adult.xtream_desc")) }
```
Remove the `.onChange`. No new strings are needed.

**APIs:** View.confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The core bug is real. PlaylistSettingsView.swift:330-332 calls saveFilterSetting, which saves `updated` (497-502) and then calls syncContents() (504); syncContents passes the view's immutable `playlist` (519) and Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:463 reads `playlist.filterAdultContent` from that argument. `playlist` is stale: ContentView.swift:161/167 set `selectedPlaylist` once, and onChange(of: playlists) only calls attemptAutoLoad, which returns after the first run (153). So the new flag is saved but the re-download runs with the old one. No test covers it (grep of another-iptv-playerTests for filterAdult / syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal: no hits). The toggle is not disabled while isSyncing and syncContents has no guard (512-514), so two flips run two full syncs; progress renders only in the first section (62-85). The code is from d2489f9, unchanged.

Corrections: (1) The automatic re-download is deliberate: comment at 503 ('Filtre değişince içerikleri otomatik yeniden indir') and the row's own subtitle 'Content must be re-downloaded after change' (en.lproj/Localizable.strings:184). Adding a confirmation is a product decision, not a defect fix. (2) The proposed `syncContents(using: updated)` fixes only the Settings path. Pull-to-refresh on the tabs passes the same stale dashboard copy (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:247, Views/VODView.swift:97, Views/SeriesView.swift:98 -> PlaylistContentStore.swift:480), so the next pull on Movies would re-sync VOD with the old flag and undo the filter. (3) The proposed Binding getter `{ filterAdultContent }` relies on SwiftUI snapping the switch back when the setter does not change the value; safer to show the pending value.

**Corrected claim:** Flipping 'Filter Adult Content' in Xtream Settings saves the new value but re-downloads the catalog with the previous one, so the filter does not take effect in the session; the same stale flag is used by pull-to-refresh on Live TV, Movies and Series. The switch stays enabled during the sync (a second flip starts a second full sync) and progress shows only in the first section. The automatic re-download itself is deliberate.

**Corrected fix:** 1) Read the flag from the row, in one place, so no caller's copy matters. In both syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal overloads (PlaylistContentStore.swift:463 and 480) resolve it inside the write closure:

let fallback = playlist.filterAdultContent
try await AppDatabase.shared.write { db in
    let filterAdult = try Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: pid)?.filterAdultContent ?? fallback
    ...
}

This fixes Settings and the three pull-to-refresh sites together.
2) In PlaylistSettingsView add `.disabled(isSyncing)` to the toggle and `guard !isSyncing else { return }` at the top of syncContents; show a ProgressView in the Content Management section while isSyncing (the existing phase text can stay in the first section).
3) Owner's decision: confirm before starting. If wanted, use the proposed confirmationDialog but with `get: { pendingAdultFilter ?? filterAdultContent }` so the switch shows the pending value and animates back on cancel; existing strings settings.filter_adult.title, settings.refresh_all, common.cancel, settings.filter_adult.xtream_desc are enough.

**API check:** View.confirmationDialog<S, A, M>(_ title: S, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, actions:, message:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17519, in an extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, ...). Playlist.fetchOne(db, key:) is already used in this code base (EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:267). Strings exist in en.lproj/Localizable.strings lines 3, 142, 183, 184.

**Regression risks:** Reading the row inside the write adds one primary-key lookup, negligible. The fallback keeps the bootstrap path working if the row is missing. With `guard !isSyncing` but without disabling the toggle, a second flip would be saved but not applied, so both must go in together. A confirmation dialog changes a flow the owner chose; ask first.

**How to verify:** Unit test on an in-memory AppDatabase with a stubbed URLSession: save the row with filterAdultContent = true, call syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal with a Playlist copy whose flag is false, assert no adult category or stream rows were written; repeat for the `only:` overload. UI: flip the switch, assert it is disabled and a spinner is visible in the same section.

## settings-ux-3 — Settings writes save a frozen copy of the whole Playlist row, so one setting silently reverts another and an M3U re-download resets the adult filter and the saved EPG URL

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U), EPG settings
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:460-465`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:496-502`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:321-370`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:393-400`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:94-101`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:158-162`, `Models/M3UImporter.swift:25-31`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:80-83`, `ContentView.swift:145-163`

**What the user perceives:** Xtream: turn 'Show TV guide' off, then change the adult filter: the guide is enabled again in the database while its switch still shows off. M3U: save a manual EPG URL, then flip the adult filter: the URL is gone after the next launch. M3U: turn the adult filter on, then tap 'Re-download from URL': adult channels are back while the switch still shows on. After 'Reload from File' the screen still shows the old source URL and the 'Re-download from URL' row.

**Mechanism (finder):** ContentView sets `selectedPlaylist` once (161, 167) and its onChange only calls attemptAutoLoad, which returns after the first run (153), so every dashboard view holds the value from when the playlist was opened. Each writer does `var updated = playlist; updated.x = …; try updated.save(db)`, and GRDB `save` writes all columns: saveFilterSetting (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:497-502, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:394-399), XtreamEPGSettingsSection.saveEnabled (EPGSettingsSections.swift:159-161), the timezone write in fetchAuthInfo (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:460-465) and M3UImporter.replace (M3UImporter.swift:25-31). M3UEPGSettingsSection keeps its own private @State copy (EPGSettingsSections.swift:57) that the parent never sees. refreshFromURL/refreshFromLocalFile then call `reloadIfActive(playlist: playlist)` with the frozen value, and the store copies its flag from it (M3UContentStore.swift:82).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make the database row the only source for mutable flags.

```swift
extension AppDatabase {
    /// Re-reads the row inside the write so a caller's copy cannot revert other columns.
    @discardableResult
    func updatePlaylist(id: UUID, _ change: @escaping @Sendable (inout Playlist) -> Void) async throws -> Playlist? {
        try await write { db in
            guard var p = try Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: id) else { return nil }
            change(&p); try p.update(db); return p
        }
    }
}
```
Use it at the five sites above (and EPG/PanelTimeZoneResolver.swift:55-60, same pattern). In both settings views keep `@State private var current: Playlist` (seeded from `playlist`), replace it with the returned row, and use `current` for display and for syncContents / M3UImporter.replace / reloadIfActive / the EPG sections (pass a Binding to M3UEPGSettingsSection instead of its private copy). M3UImporter.replace should fetch the row inside its transaction rather than save its argument.

**Verifier reasons:** All four user-visible scenarios check out from the code. The dashboard copy is frozen (ContentView.swift:153-167). Every writer does `var updated = playlist; ...; try updated.save(db)` and GRDB save writes every column: PlaylistSettingsView.swift:497-502 and 460-465, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:394-399, Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:96-99 and 159-161, Models/M3UImporter.swift:25-31, EPG/PanelTimeZoneResolver.swift:55-60. M3UEPGSettingsSection keeps a private @State copy (EPGSettingsSections.swift:57) that the parent's later save overwrites. refreshFromURL / refreshFromLocalFile pass the frozen value to reloadIfActive (M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:339, 365) and the store copies the flag from it (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:82). The source rows read `playlist.serverURL` (52, 169), so they stay after 'Reload from File'. The code base already documents this hazard: EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:273-281 writes only the timeshiftStyle column 'because saving the caller's snapshot would write its other, possibly stale columns back'.

Corrections: (1) Scope is wider than the five sites: pull-to-refresh on the M3U Channels tab does the same stale replace + reload (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:208, 214-219), and Xtream pull-to-refresh reads the stale adult flag (LiveStreamsView.swift:247, VODView.swift:97, SeriesView.swift:98). A settings-local `@State current` does not reach those. (2) M3UImporter.replace is also the create path (Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:297), where the row does not exist yet; 'fetch the row inside the transaction' needs an insert fallback. (3) The target uses SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393) and AppDatabase's accessors live in `nonisolated extension AppDatabase` (Database/AppDatabase.swift:467, 478); the helper must be declared the same way.

**Corrected claim:** Every settings write, the M3U importer and the timezone write save a frozen copy of the whole Playlist row, so one setting silently reverts another (EPG enabled, adult filter, EPG URL override, source URL, cached timezone / timeshift style). The frozen copy is also what the M3U Channels pull-to-refresh and the Xtream tab pull-to-refresh use, so the revert is not limited to the Settings screens.

**Corrected fix:** Three small parts.
1) Column-scoped writes, following CatchupURLResolver.persistStyle. Add in a `nonisolated extension AppDatabase`:

@discardableResult
func updatePlaylist(id: UUID, _ change: @escaping (inout Playlist) -> Void) async throws -> Playlist? {
    try await write { db in
        guard var p = try Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: id) else { return nil }
        change(&p); try p.update(db); return p
    }
}

Use it at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:462-464 and 497-502, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:394-399, EPGSettingsSections.swift:96-99 and 159-161, PanelTimeZoneResolver.swift:58-60. Pass the returned row on to reloadIfActive / forceRefresh / refreshIfStale.
2) M3UImporter.replace: inside its transaction use `var row = try Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: pid) ?? playlist`, apply m3uEpgURL / clearServerURL to `row`, then `try row.save(db)` (insert on the create path, fresh columns on refresh). Have M3UContentStore.reloadIfActive read the flag from the row instead of the argument.
3) Keep the dashboard's copy current instead of adding per-screen copies: in ContentView.swift:145-149 extend the existing onChange:

if let sel = selectedPlaylist, let fresh = newList.first(where: { $0.id == sel.id }), fresh != sel { selectedPlaylist = fresh }

(Playlist is Equatable; `.task(id: playlist.id)` does not re-run because the id is unchanged.) That refreshes the displayed source URL, the 'Re-download from URL' row and every pull-to-refresh caller. M3UEPGSettingsSection can then take `let playlist` and drop its private copy.

**API check:** GRDB only, no SwiftUI API. `Playlist.fetchOne(db, key:)` and `Playlist.filter(key:).updateAll(db, [Column(..).set(to:)])` are both already used in EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:267 and 279-281; `update(db)` is used at Views/MovieDetailView.swift:299. AppDatabase.write signature: `func write<T>(_ updates: @escaping (Database) throws -> T) async throws -> T` (Database/AppDatabase.swift:479).

**Regression risks:** Part 3 makes the whole dashboard receive a new `playlist` value after each row write (settings change, first timezone write, a catch-up probe persisting timeshiftStyle during playback): tab roots re-evaluate once; check that Equatable shelf rows do not compare the full Playlist and that the player overlay root, which is captured at presentation time, is not remounted. `update(db)` throws if the row was deleted, which is the wanted behaviour (no re-insert of a deleted playlist), but call sites that used `try?` must keep it. M3UImporter.replace must still insert for AddM3UPlaylistView.

**How to verify:** Unit tests on an in-memory AppDatabase: (a) two stale copies, set epgEnabled = false through one and filterAdultContent = true through the other, assert both persist; (b) set epgURLOverride and filterAdultContent, run M3UImporter.replace with a stale Playlist, assert both survive and m3uEpgURL is updated; (c) replace with a Playlist that is not in the table inserts it. UI: M3U playlist, 'Reload from File', assert the 'Re-download from URL' row is gone.

## settings-ux-4 — Subscription info is refetched every time Settings appears and swaps its rows for a spinner; failures show as red body text plus a second button row

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream)
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:170-181`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:226-259`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:392-401`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:448-472`

**What the user perceives:** Each return to the Settings tab, and each pop back from Downloads or App Language, replaces the three rows 'Time Remaining / Active / Max connections' with one centred 'Loading subscription info...' spinner and then puts them back, so everything below moves by two rows twice. On pull-to-refresh there are two spinners. A failure shows 'Could not fetch info: Server error: HTTP 404' in red at body size with a separate 'Try Again' row (T02-settings-2.png), and hides the last good values.

**Mechanism (finder):** `.task` (392-396) restarts on every appearance of the tab root (tab switch, pop). fetchAuthInfo always sets `isLoading = true` and clears the error (449-450); the row builder checks `isLoading` first, then `errorMessage`, then the data (226-259), so known values are thrown away while refreshing or after a failure. The header button (170-181), `.refreshable` (397-401) and 'Try Again' (235-237) are three ways to run the same request.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the rows stable and revalidate behind them.

```swift
private func fetchAuthInfo(force: Bool = false) async {
    if !force, let t = lastAccountFetch, Date().timeIntervalSince(t) < 300 { return }
    if authResponse == nil { isLoading = true }   // spinner only on the very first load
    ...
}
// rows always present; the value side changes, not the row count
LabeledContent(L("settings.playlist.subscription")) {
    if let info = authResponse?.userInfo { Text(calculateRemainingDays(expDate: info.expDate)) }
    else if isLoading { ProgressView() } else { Text("—") }
}
```
Move the error into the section footer in secondary style (`Section { … } footer: { if let errorMessage { Text(L("settings.playlist.info_error", errorMessage)) } }`); pull-to-refresh is the retry (`fetchAuthInfo(force: true)`). Remove the refresh button from the section header. In M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:285-288 `.refreshable` only re-reads two local counts; remove it there.

**APIs:** LabeledContent (iOS 16.0); View.refreshable(action:) (iOS 15.0 (already in use))

**Verifier reasons:** PlaylistSettingsView.swift:448-450: fetchAuthInfo always sets isLoading = true and clears errorMessage; the row builder tests isLoading first, then errorMessage, then the data (226-259), so three known rows are replaced by one spinner row on every run, and a later failure hides the last good values. `.task` (392-396) is attached to the tab root, so it re-runs on each tab selection and on each pop back from Downloads / App Language; each run also sends a request to the panel. The header button (170-181), `.refreshable` (397-401) and 'Try Again' (235-237) all run the same request. The error state in iphone-light/T02-settings-2.png is body-size red text plus a separate 'Try Again' row. No comment or history marks any of this as deliberate (file history: d2489f9, ff061f0, 0ab5bcd, 1cce013; none touches this logic with a stated reason).

Severity lowered to low: on iPhone the section is below the fold when Settings is at its top (T01-settings-1.png ends at Player Settings), so the row swap is seen only when the user is scrolled to it; no iPad settings screenshot exists to check the larger layout. One addition: when the user leaves the tab mid-request the task is cancelled and the catch branch stores the cancellation as errorMessage; with rows kept on screen this must be ignored.

**Corrected claim:** The account request is repeated on every appearance of Settings; while it runs the three subscription rows are replaced by one spinner row, and after a failure the last good values are hidden behind red body text plus a 'Try Again' row. On iPhone the swap is off-screen unless the user is scrolled to Playlist Information.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two adjustments.
- fetchAuthInfo(force:): skip when the last success is under 5 minutes old; set isLoading only when authResponse == nil; on failure keep authResponse; in the catch, return without setting errorMessage when Task.isCancelled.
- Keep the three rows always present and change only the value side (value, ProgressView on first load, or a dash). The file's existing HStack / Spacer / secondary Text pattern is enough; LabeledContent is optional.
- Show the error as the section footer in secondary style; pull-to-refresh calls fetchAuthInfo(force: true) and is the retry. Remove the refresh button from the section header (170-181) and the 'Try Again' row.
- Removing `.refreshable` from M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:285-288 is the owner's call: it is harmless, it only re-reads local counts and download usage.

**API check:** LabeledContent: `public struct LabeledContent<Label, Content>` @available(iOS 16.0) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4018-4019, with `init<S>(_ title: S, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where S : StringProtocol` at 4036. `refreshable(action:)` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9266 in an extension @available(iOS 15.0). Section with content/header/footer is already used in this code base (Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:67-87).

**Regression risks:** With a 5-minute TTL, 'Active connections' can be up to 5 minutes old on return to the tab; pull-to-refresh forces it. The timezone write at 460-465 runs less often, which is fine. Removing the header button removes the only tap target for refresh, so `.refreshable` must stay on the Xtream form.

**How to verify:** UI test: open Settings, scroll to Playlist Information, switch to Movies and back, assert the three subscription rows exist throughout and no 'Loading subscription info...' element appears. With the demo fixture (404) assert the error is a footer and no 'Try Again' row exists. Count requests to player_api.php with a stubbed session across three tab switches: one, not three.

## settings-ux-5 — Choosing a language rebuilds the whole app from the root: the user is thrown from Settings to the last content tab, a docked mini player is destroyed and the catalog is reloaded

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Settings › App Language, Dashboard, Mini player
- Code: `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:51-67`, `Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:30-61`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:8-23`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:131-137`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:11-14`, `ContentView.swift:134-163`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-152`

**What the user perceives:** Tap a language in Settings › App Language: the screen blanks for a frame and reopens on Live TV (or the last content tab), not in Settings. Anything playing in the mini player stops. All navigation stacks, scroll positions and the search text are gone, and on a large playlist the tabs reload their content. A running 'Re-download All Content' loses its progress row.

**Mechanism (finder):** AppRootView applies `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` to ContentView (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66). The new ContentView starts with `selectedPlaylist == nil` and `playlists == nil` (blank Color, ContentView.swift:134-137) until the async GRDB observation delivers and attemptAutoLoad re-selects the playlist (152-163). The new DashboardView takes its tab from restoreInitialTab(), which never returns Settings (DashboardView.swift:22, 200-215); M3U starts at 0. `@StateObject playerOverlay` (DashboardView.swift:8, M3UDashboardView.swift:11) is recreated, which unmounts the player. `.task(id: playlist.id)` runs loadPlaylist again, which re-reads all three catalogs from SQLite (PlaylistContentStore.swift:128-152). The root id was added on purpose in 0ab5bcd so every L() string updates (comment at 51-55); that goal has to be kept.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Scope the identity to the parts that only hold strings. Remove `.id` at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66 (keep `.locale` and `.layoutDirection`). In DashboardView and M3UDashboardView observe the manager and put the id on the TabView only:

```swift
@ObservedObject private var localization = LocalizationManager.shared
TabView(selection: tabBinding) { ... }
    .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)
    .id(localization.selectedLanguage)   // tabs are rebuilt; selectedTab, playerOverlay and .task(id:) survive
```
In ContentView observe the manager and put the same id on the playlist-list NavigationStack (line 80). Result: the user stays on the Settings tab (stack popped to its root, in the new language), playback continues, no catalog reload. In LanguagePickerListView add `.accessibilityAddTraits(manager.selectedLanguage == lang.code ? .isSelected : [])` to the rows. Optional alternative: the app ships ten .lproj folders, so iOS already offers a per-app Language row in the Settings app and the 'System Language' option follows it through Locale.preferredLanguages (LocalizationManager.swift:104-114); a row that opens UIApplication.openSettingsURLString would be the fully native route.

**APIs:** View.id(_:) (iOS 13.0); UIApplication.openSettingsURLString (iOS 8.0)

**Verifier reasons:** another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66 puts `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` on ContentView. A new ContentView starts with selectedPlaylist == nil, hasAttemptedAutoLoad == false and the @Query value nil (ContentView.swift:6, 17-18), shows the blank Color (134-137), then attemptAutoLoad re-selects the last playlist (152-163). The new DashboardView takes its tab from restoreInitialTab(), which clamps Settings and Search to a content tab (DashboardView.swift:22, 206-216); M3UDashboardView starts at 0 (M3UDashboardView.swift:14). `@StateObject playerOverlay` is recreated in both dashboards (DashboardView.swift:8, M3UDashboardView.swift:11), which unmounts the player. `.task(id: playlist.id)` re-runs loadPlaylist, which re-reads all three catalogs and flips streamsLoaded false then true (PlaylistContentStore.swift:128-152), restarting every `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` recompute in the tabs. The root id is deliberate (comment at 51-55, added in 0ab5bcd so every L() string updates), but that commit predates the in-window player overlay, so losing the mini player is a later side effect, not a choice. LanguagePickerSection is used only in the two settings views (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:128, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:123), so the language can only change while a dashboard is on screen. No UI test changes the language in-app.

Severity lowered to low: the default is the system language and this is a once-per-install action. Two amendments to the fix are needed (below).

**Corrected claim:** Choosing a language rebuilds the app from the root: the user lands on the last content tab instead of Settings, a docked mini player is torn down, all navigation and search state is lost and the catalog is re-read from SQLite. The rebuild is deliberate for the strings; the loss of the player and of the tab is not.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, scoped: remove `.id` at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66 (keep `.locale` and `.layoutDirection`), add `@ObservedObject private var localization = LocalizationManager.shared` to DashboardView and M3UDashboardView and put `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` on the TabView only (after `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)`). selectedTab, globalSearchText, playerOverlay and `.task(id:)` live outside that identity and survive, so the user stays on Settings (popped to its root) and playback continues.
Amendments:
- The id on the playlist-list NavigationStack in ContentView is not needed: the list is not in the hierarchy while a dashboard is open and is built fresh, in the new language, when the user goes back.
- Category names resolved at load time stay in the old language once the catalog is no longer reloaded: L("content.uncategorized") is baked in at PlaylistContentStore.swift:376, 390, 404, 433. Either accept it until the next reload, or add in DashboardView `.onChange(of: localization.selectedLanguage) { _, _ in Task { await contentStore.reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId: playlist.id) } }` (off-main read; the tabs are being rebuilt anyway).
- Add `.accessibilityAddTraits(manager.selectedLanguage == lang.code ? .isSelected : [])` to the language rows.
- Opening the system per-app language page instead is a product decision; note that iOS shows that row only when the device has more than one preferred language.

**API check:** `func id<ID>(_ id: ID) -> some View where ID : Hashable` at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:18608, @available(iOS 13.0). `AccessibilityTraits.isSelected` at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4934; `accessibilityAddTraits(_:)` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23208 in an extension @available(iOS 14.0). `UIApplicationOpenSettingsURLString` API_AVAILABLE(ios(8.0)) at UIKit.framework/Headers/UIApplication.h:613.

**Regression risks:** The player overlay is a sibling of the TabView and is no longer rebuilt: a docked or fullscreen player keeps old-language strings until its next re-render, and for Arabic it receives a live layoutDirection change during playback (out-of-scope files, check by hand). DashboardView's own alerts and sheet re-evaluate because it now observes the manager. All tab NavigationStacks and scroll positions are still reset, which is the intended cost. Only a simulator run can show whether replacing a sidebarAdaptable TabView by identity keeps the selection without a visible flash on iOS 18 and iOS 26.

**How to verify:** UI test: Settings > App Language > Deutsch, assert the selected tab is still Settings, its title and the tab labels are German. Repeat with a mini player docked and assert it is still present and playing. Choose Arabic and check the RTL flip of the tab content and the docked player. On a playlist with uncategorized streams, check the 'Uncategorized' shelf title after the switch. Run on both an iOS 18 and an iOS 26 simulator.

## settings-ux-6 — Settings is one four-screen form that opens with 'Back to Playlists' and 'Re-download All Content', with playlist data, preferences and maintenance actions interleaved

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U)
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44-372`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40-249`, `../another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:116-169`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Does the owner want the regrouping and a 'Playlist Information' sub-page, and should 'Back to Playlists' stay in Settings or move to a toolbar item on the tab roots?

**What the user perceives:** The first row of Settings leaves the screen, the second starts a long download (T01-settings-1.png). The Downloads section header is followed by a row with the same title. Which playlist is open only shows three screens down, between player switches and About. Order is Actions, Downloads, Language, Player, Playlist info, Statistics, Server, TV Guide, Content management, About; it reads as a list of features in the order they were built.

**Mechanism (finder):** Both forms are a flat sequence of ten sections with about 35 rows (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:45-371). Navigation ('Back to Playlists', 46-54), a network job (56-67), read-only account data (170-260), toggles (131-167, 322-332) and destructive actions (116-125, 334-343) share one level; only Downloads and Language push a sub-page.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Group like the Settings app: identity first, preferences in the middle, data management and About last.
1. Playlist: one row with the playlist name, host and remaining time as subtitle that pushes a 'Playlist Information' page (account rows, statistics, server info), followed by the 'Back to Playlists' button.
2. Content: Re-download All Content, TV Guide rows, Filter Adult Content.
3. Playback: the four switches.
4. Downloads: link, Wi-Fi only, storage used, delete all.
5. Language.
6. Clear Watch History.
7. About: Version, the tip row where it is now (between Version and GitHub), GitHub.

```swift
Section {
    NavigationLink { PlaylistInfoView(playlist: playlist) } label: {
        LabeledContent { } label: { Text(playlist.name); Text(host) }
    }
    Button(L("settings.back_to_list"), systemImage: "rectangle.stack") { onDismiss() }
}
```
Keep the labels the UI tests look up ('Back to Playlists', 'Re-download All Content', 'Player Settings', 'Playlist Information', 'Downloads') or update ScreensUITests.swift:116-169 in the same change. M3U uses the same skeleton without the account rows.

**APIs:** LabeledContent (iOS 16.0); Button(_:systemImage:action:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44-372 and Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40-249. The section order is as described for Xtream (actions 45-86, Downloads 88-126, Language 128, Player 131-167, Playlist info 170-260, Stats 264-292, Server 296-314, EPG 318, Content management 321-344, About 347-371). M3U has nine sections, not ten. T01-settings-1.png shows 'Back to Playlists' and 'Re-download All Content' as the first two rows and the Downloads header followed by a Downloads row; T02 shows Playlist Information on the second screen. 'Back to Playlists' is the only route back to the playlist list: DashboardNavigationModifier (Views/DashboardView.swift:222-245) receives onDismiss but never uses it, so the row cannot simply be dropped. git blame shows the layout dates from the first commits (fe55017, 2849d94) with no comment marking it as deliberate. What the finding missed: (1) Stats, Server, EPG and Content management are all inside `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil` (263-345), so when verify() fails they are hidden; T02-T04 show exactly that (only five sections, with a red error and Try Again). The regrouping has to decide what is gated. (2) fetchAuthInfo (448-472) also refreshes the cached serverTimezone used for timeshift, so it must keep running at the Settings root and not move into a sub-page. (3) The observation is information architecture, not a defect; nothing here costs frames or state.

**Corrected claim:** The Xtream settings form is a flat list of ten sections (nine on M3U) in build order: navigation and a network job first, the playlist identity on the second screen, statistics/EPG/content management only visible after a successful auth call. It works, but it does not follow the identity / preferences / data / about order of Apple's settings screens. This is a product decision for the owner, not a bug.

**Corrected fix:** If the owner wants it: regroup as proposed (playlist row first, then content, playback, downloads, language, history, about), with these corrections. Keep fetchAuthInfo and its timezone side effect in the root view's .task and pass authResponse into the new 'Playlist Information' page. Decide explicitly which rows stay behind the auth gate at 263; local-only rows (statistics counts, Clear Watch History, adult filter) do not need it, but un-gating is a behaviour change to confirm with the owner. Keep a visible 'Back to Playlists' control in Settings, since no toolbar route exists. A plain NavigationLink label with two Text views is enough; the empty-content LabeledContent wrapper is unnecessary. Keep the section header texts 'Player Settings' and 'Playlist Information' and the button labels 'Back to Playlists', 'Re-download All Content', 'Downloads', or update ScreensUITests.swift:116-169, 240, 419, 433 in the same change. Leave the TipJarRow() line between Version and GitHub.

**API check:** LabeledContent: `@available(iOS 16.0, ...) public struct LabeledContent<Label, Content>` with `init(@ViewBuilder content:, @ViewBuilder label:)` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4019-4026). Button(_:systemImage:action:) exists, contrary to the finding's 'not verified / iOS 17': `@available(iOS 14.0, ...) extension Button where Label == Label<Text, Image> { @_disfavoredOverload @_alwaysEmitIntoClient init<S>(_ title: S, systemImage: String, action:) where S : StringProtocol }` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22942-22955). Both are fine on the iOS 18 target with no availability check.

**Regression risks:** Hiding or moving the auth fetch would stop the serverTimezone refresh (448-465) and break timeshift start times. Four UI tests look up 'Back to Playlists' and one looks for 'Playlist Information' and 'Player Settings' after two swipes; a sub-page or renamed header fails them. The uncommitted TipJarRow() line sits in the About section of both files and must stay. Moving 'Re-download All Content' away from the adult-filter toggle's sync (496-510) makes the progress row appear off-screen unless they end up in the same section, as proposed.

**How to verify:** After the change, run the ScreensUITests settings tests (showsCoreSections, refreshAllButton_exists, downloadsRow_opensDownloadsScreen, backToList_opensPlaylistList). Capture the Settings screens with a playlist whose verify() succeeds and with the demo playlist (verify fails) and compare with T01-T04. Confirm the playlist's serverTimezone column still updates after opening Settings.

## settings-ux-7 — Settings rows are hand-built HStack { Text; Spacer; Text } with trailing icons instead of LabeledContent and Label, and values cannot be copied

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U), EPG settings, App Language row
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:49-53, 92-96, 108-113, 119-123, 182-201, 239-258, 265-291, 298-303, 337-341, 348-352`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:45-49, 68-72, 87-91, 103-108, 161-182, 188-199, 218-222, 228-231`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:33-44, 134-138`, `Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:12-17`

**What the user perceives:** A long server URL wraps inside the right-hand column and squeezes the label; at large text sizes label and value fight for one line. The Downloads row shows a custom glyph next to the system chevron (T01-settings-1.png). Icons sit on the trailing edge where iOS puts values and chevrons. Long-pressing the server URL or username does nothing, so the values cannot be copied.

**Mechanism (finder):** About 25 rows across the two forms repeat `HStack { Text(label); Spacer(); Text(value).foregroundColor(.secondary) }` (e.g. PlaylistSettingsView.swift:189-194 with no line limit). Action and link rows use `HStack { Text; Spacer; Image }` (49-53, 92-96, 119-123, 337-341). Toggle descriptions are manual `VStack` + `.font(.caption)` (100-105, 133-165, 323-328). No row has textSelection or a context menu.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use the system row types; the form then follows the platform's layout rules on iOS 18 and 26 without custom code.

```swift
LabeledContent(L("settings.playlist.server_url"), value: playlist.serverURL)
    .textSelection(.enabled)                       // long-press › Copy, system-localized
NavigationLink { DownloadsView(playlist: playlist) } label: {
    Label(L("download.title"), systemImage: "arrow.down.circle")
}
NavigationLink { LanguagePickerListView() } label: {
    LabeledContent(L("settings.language.title"), value: currentLanguageDisplayName)
}
Toggle(isOn: $pipEnabled) {                      // title + subtitle convention documented for Toggle
    Text(L("settings.player.pip.title"))
    Text(L("settings.player.pip.desc"))
}
Button(L("history.clear.button_entry"), systemImage: "trash", role: .destructive) { ... }
```
Apply to both forms and EPGSettingsSections. Leave the TipJarRow() line as it is.

**APIs:** LabeledContent(_:value:) (iOS 16.0); View.textSelection(_:) (iOS 15.0); Label (iOS 14.0); Toggle label with two Text views (title + subtitle) (documented in the SDK's SwiftUI doc comments for Toggle/Picker/LabeledContent; no separate symbol)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read all cited rows. The pattern is real: about 25 rows are `HStack { Text; Spacer; Text.foregroundColor(.secondary) }` (e.g. PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-201, 239-258, 265-291; M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:161-199; EPGSettingsSections.swift:33-44, 134-138; LanguagePickerSection.swift:12-17), action and link rows put an SF Symbol on the trailing edge (49-53, 92-96, 119-123, 337-341), and no settings row has textSelection or a context menu (grep found textSelection only in Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:95). T01 shows the Downloads row with a glyph next to the system chevron and the trailing icon on 'Back to Playlists'. However, at the default text size with short values the label/value rows are visually indistinguishable from system rows (T02: Name, Server URL, Username), so the visible defect is limited to the trailing icons; the long-URL and large-text claims are plausible but have no evidence (the demo URL is 19 characters) and the exact HStack wrapping was not shown. The M3U source URL is already a deliberate stacked layout with lineLimit(3) (M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:170-176). The fix as written also has two problems: a leading Label icon on one row of a section (Downloads) next to rows without icons (Wi-Fi only, Storage used) misaligns titles, and the system title+subtitle style will differ from TipJarRow's hand-built `.caption` subtitle and trailing heart (Views/Components/TipJarView.swift:12-23), which is the owner's uncommitted work and sits in the same form.

**Corrected claim:** Settings rows are hand-built stacks. At default size they look like system rows, but action and link rows carry trailing decorative icons where iOS puts values and chevrons, the rows do not get the system's layout for long values and large text, and server URL / username cannot be copied.

**Corrected fix:** Replace the label/value stacks with `LabeledContent(L(...), value: ...)` (or the content-closure form for `Text(last, style: .relative)` in EPGSettingsSections.swift:33-37) and the language row with `NavigationLink { ... } label: { LabeledContent(title, value: name) }`. Put `.textSelection(.enabled)` on the value Text of Server URL and Username only (use `LabeledContent(title) { Text(value).textSelection(.enabled) }`), not on whole rows. Remove the trailing glyphs from the Downloads link, 'Back to Playlists', 'Delete all downloads' and 'Clear Watch History' rather than moving them to a leading Label, unless every row in that section gets an icon. Keep the stacked M3U source URL row. Toggles can use the two-Text label form, but leave the About section's GitHub row in its current shape so it keeps matching TipJarRow, and do not edit TipJarView.swift; the owner can align both when the tip jar lands.

**API check:** `LabeledContent` iOS 16.0; `@_disfavoredOverload public init<S1, S2>(_ title: S1, value: S2) where S1 : StringProtocol, S2 : StringProtocol` and `init<S>(_ title: S, @ViewBuilder content:)` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4037-4045). `textSelection<S>(_ selectability: S) where S : TextSelectability`, `@available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, *)` (1821-1825). `Button.init<S>(_ title: S, systemImage: String, role: ButtonRole?, action:)` in an `@available(iOS 15.0, ...)` extension, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient (22997-23015). The title+subtitle convention for Toggle is in the SDK doc comments (SwiftUI .swiftdoc, Toggle section: 'use a view builder that creates multiple Text views where the first text represents the title and the second text represents the subtitle'); same text for Picker, DatePicker and LabeledContent. L() returns String, so the StringProtocol overloads are the ones selected.

**Regression risks:** Subtitle font changes from .caption to the system subtitle style, so toggle rows get slightly taller and no longer match TipJarRow and the GitHub row unless those are left alone. UI tests look up `app.buttons["Downloads"]`, `"Re-download All Content"`, `"Back to Playlists"`; labels stay the same if only the icon is removed. textSelection adds a long-press gesture on the value; keep it off rows that are buttons or links.

**How to verify:** Simulator run: screenshot Settings at default size and at the largest accessibility size, before and after, with a playlist whose server URL is 45+ characters; check that label and value do not collide and that long-press on Server URL shows Copy. Run the ScreensUITests settings tests.
