## settings-ux-8 — Destructive actions are confirmed with a centred alert titled like the action and a generic 'Yes, Delete' button

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U)
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:373-391`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:262-280`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:434-446`

**What the user perceives:** 'Clear Watch History' and 'Delete all downloads' open an alert in the middle of the screen that asks 'Are you sure?' / 'Continue?' with 'Yes, Delete'. iOS confirms an action the user just chose with an action sheet attached to the control, whose red button repeats the verb. After confirming there is no feedback, and in the Xtream form a failed history delete is only printed to the console.

**Mechanism (finder):** Both forms attach two `.alert` modifiers to the Form (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:373-391, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:262-280) with `common.confirm_delete_yes`. clearHistory in the Xtream form swallows errors with print (443-445) while the M3U form shows an alert (414-417).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Attach a confirmationDialog to the row itself so the system can anchor it there (popover on iPad), and reuse the row title as the destructive button; no new strings.

```swift
Button(L("history.clear.button_entry"), systemImage: "trash", role: .destructive) {
    showClearHistory = true
}
.disabled(historyCount == 0)
.confirmationDialog(L("history.clear.title"), isPresented: $showClearHistory, titleVisibility: .visible) {
    Button(L("history.clear.button_entry"), role: .destructive) { Task { await clearHistory() } }
    Button(L("common.cancel"), role: .cancel) { }
} message: { Text(L("history.clear.message.all")) }
.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: historyClearedCount)
```
Same for 'Delete all downloads'. Surface clearHistory failures in the Xtream form the way the M3U form does.

**APIs:** View.confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:) (iOS 15.0); View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Confirmed in code: both forms attach two `.alert` modifiers to the Form (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:373-391, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:262-280) with title 'Clear History' / 'Delete all downloads', messages ending 'Are you sure?' / 'Continue?' and the button 'Yes, Delete' (en.lproj/Localizable.strings:15, 123-126, 443-444). Xtream clearHistory only prints on failure (443-445) while M3U shows an alert (414-417). Two corrections. First, 'no feedback after confirming' is overstated: clearHistory calls fetchLocalStats, which sets historyCount to 0, so the 'Clear Watch History' button dims immediately (343) and the history count row updates; after deleting downloads, 'Storage used' drops to zero and the delete row disappears (115). Second, the same alert pattern is used for every destructive confirmation in the app (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:110-117 with the same title and 'Yes, Delete', ContentView.swift:117-128 for playlist delete), so changing only Settings leaves two confirmation styles for the same 'Clear History' action. Alerts for destructive confirmation are also used by Apple, so this is polish, not a defect.

**Corrected claim:** Destructive actions across the app (Settings clear-history and delete-all-downloads, the history list's trash button, playlist delete) are confirmed with a centred alert whose button says 'Yes, Delete' instead of an action sheet anchored to the control with a button that repeats the verb. In the Xtream settings form a failed history delete is only printed.

**Corrected fix:** Attach `.confirmationDialog(title, isPresented:, actions:, message:)` to the row button (after `.disabled`, so the dialog's buttons are not disabled with it) with a destructive button that reuses the row title and a Cancel button. Leave titleVisibility at its default so the title is not shown a second time above the message and the same-worded button. Apply the same change to WatchHistoryListView.swift:110-117 (attach to the toolbar trash button) so the two 'Clear History' confirmations match; playlist delete in ContentView can follow. Add an error state to PlaylistSettingsView and show the existing 'misc.history_delete_error' string as the M3U form does. A success haptic is optional; if added it needs a new counter state incremented after a successful delete, attached once to the Form.

**API check:** `@_disfavoredOverload func confirmationDialog<S, A, M>(_ title: S, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> A, @ViewBuilder message: () -> M) where S : StringProtocol` in an `@available(iOS 15.0, ...) extension View` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17519). `func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T) where T : Equatable`, `@available(iOS 17.0, ...)` (1981-1983); already used in Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:231. `Button.init<S>(_:systemImage:role:action:)` iOS 15 (23015). No availability check needed on iOS 18.

**Regression risks:** Any UI test that expects an alert for these actions would need updating (none found in ScreensUITests for these two). The 'Delete all downloads' row is conditional (115); the dialog is dismissed before the row disappears, so this is safe. If only Settings is converted, the history list keeps the old alert for the same action.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test: tap 'Clear Watch History' with history present, assert a sheet (not an alert) with 'Clear Watch History' and 'Cancel'; confirm and assert the row becomes disabled. Screenshot on iPhone iOS 26, iPhone iOS 18 and iPad to check where the dialog is anchored.

---

## settings-ux-9 — Long-running rows (re-download, reload from file, EPG refresh) add and remove rows while they run, end without any success signal and report errors three different ways

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U), EPG settings
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:56-85`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:512-536`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:52-80`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:257-261`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:21-51`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping 'Re-download All Content' inserts a caption row under it that pushes the Downloads section down and removes it again at the end; when it finishes the spinner just vanishes, no haptic, no 'updated' text. In the M3U form the spinner sits on the 'Re-download from URL' row even while a file is being reloaded. Errors are a red caption with a nested button (Xtream), a modal alert (M3U) or a red footnote row (EPG).

**Mechanism (finder):** Progress text is a conditional row (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:69-73, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:76-80) inserted without animation. Success only resets `isSyncing` (525-528). M3U has one `isSyncing` flag and renders the ProgressView only in the URL row (59). Error presentation: inline red VStack with a second Button in the same row (75-85), `.alert(L("common.error"))` (M3U 257-261), red Text row (EPGSettingsSections.swift:46-50). No haptics exist in any settings file.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One pattern for all three: the row keeps its trailing ProgressView, status and errors go to the section footer (secondary style, the row itself is the retry), completion gives a haptic.

```swift
Section {
    Button { Task { await syncContents(using: current) } } label: {
        LabeledContent { if isSyncing { ProgressView() } } label: {
            Label(L("settings.refresh_all"), systemImage: "arrow.triangle.2.circlepath")
        }
    }.disabled(isSyncing)
} footer: {
    if let progressMessage { Text(progressMessage) }
    else if let syncError { Text(syncError) }
}
.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: syncSuccessCount)
.sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: syncFailureCount)
```
M3U: track which action runs (`enum SyncSource { case url, file }`) so the spinner is on the tapped row, and use the same footer instead of the alert.

**APIs:** View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) (iOS 17.0); LabeledContent (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Confirmed in code: the progress text is a conditional row (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:69-73, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:76-80) toggled by plain state writes with no animation, so the first section grows and shrinks by a row; success only clears isSyncing/progressMessage (525-528; M3U defer at 324-327, 349-352); M3U has a single isSyncing flag and the only ProgressView is in the URL row (59), so a file reload spins the wrong row, and a file-only playlist shows no spinner at all; errors are shown as an inline red caption with a nested Try Again button (75-85), a modal alert (M3U 257-261) and a red footnote row (EPGSettingsSections.swift:46-50). The fix needs correcting. (1) A footer that is empty when idle and shows text while syncing still changes height, so the sections below still jump; the proposed row-count test would pass while the layout shift remains. (2) The inline sync error with its own Try Again was added on purpose in 0ab5bcd (see the comment at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:11-13: syncError was split from errorMessage because 'Try Again' triggered the wrong action); dropping the explicit retry is a change to that work. (3) `.sensoryFeedback` on a Section is applied per row; attach it once to the Form. (4) The snippet calls `syncContents(using: current)`, which does not exist (the function is `syncContents()` at 512). (5) EPGRefreshStatusView is a group of rows used inside sections that already have their own header and, on M3U, a footer (EPGSettingsSections.swift:83-87); it cannot set its parent's footer without restructuring both EPG sections. Severity is low: these are short, user-started operations and nothing stalls.

**Corrected claim:** While a re-download or reload runs, a caption row is inserted and removed without animation, shifting the rest of the form; completion has no signal beyond the spinner stopping; the M3U spinner is tied to the URL row whichever action runs; and the three long-running actions report errors in three different ways.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest change: wrap the state writes that add or remove the progress and error rows in `withAnimation { ... }` so the rows animate in and out, or show the phase text as the row's second label line so no separate row appears. In M3U track which action is running (an enum for URL versus file) and put the ProgressView on that row. Add one `.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: syncSuccessCount)` and one `.sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: syncFailureCount)` on the Form, incrementing the counters at the end of the sync functions. Keep the Xtream inline error with its Try Again; for M3U, either keep the alert or adopt the same inline row, the owner can choose. Leave the EPG error row as it is.

**API check:** `func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T) where T : Equatable`, `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, visionOS 26.0, *)` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1981-1983). `LabeledContent` iOS 16.0 (4018-4026), only needed if the row label is rebuilt; not required by the corrected fix. `withAnimation` is already used throughout the app.

**Regression risks:** Removing the inline Try Again would undo the 0ab5bcd separation of sync errors from account-info errors. The adult-filter toggle also calls syncContents (504), so any haptic fires for that path too. `app.buttons["Re-download All Content"]` is looked up by ScreensUITests; keep the label text unchanged.

**How to verify:** Simulator run with a playlist that takes a few seconds to sync: record the screen while tapping 'Re-download All Content' and check that the Downloads section moves with an animation or not at all, at start and at end. For M3U, start 'Reload from File' on a URL playlist and check which row shows the spinner. Haptics on a device only.

## settings-ux-10 — The Password row is taller than its neighbours, shows the exact password length, stays revealed after leaving Settings and cannot be copied

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream) › Playlist Information
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:203-224`

**What the user perceives:** In the Playlist Information group the Password row is visibly taller than Name, Server URL and Username (T02-settings-2.png: about 168 px against 118 px in the scaled screenshot). The dots count the real characters. After tapping the eye the password stays readable when switching tabs and in the app switcher snapshot.

**Mechanism (finder):** The eye Button label has `.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)` (219), which sets the row's content height above the system row height. The mask is `String(repeating: "•", count: playlist.password.count)` (210). `isPasswordRevealed` is view state that is never reset (15), and the value has no `.privacySensitive()` or text selection.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make the whole row the control, as the Wi-Fi password row in iOS Settings does, and drop the fixed-size frame.

```swift
Button { isPasswordRevealed.toggle() } label: {
    LabeledContent(L("settings.playlist.password")) {
        HStack(spacing: 8) {
            Text(isPasswordRevealed ? playlist.password : "••••••••")
                .privacySensitive()
            Image(systemName: isPasswordRevealed ? "eye.slash" : "eye").foregroundStyle(.tint)
        }
    }
}
.tint(.primary)
.accessibilityLabel(L("settings.playlist.password"))
.accessibilityHint(isPasswordRevealed ? L("settings.hide_password") : L("settings.show_password"))
.onDisappear { isPasswordRevealed = false }
```
When revealed, add `.textSelection(.enabled)` to the value for Copy.

**APIs:** View.privacySensitive(_:) (iOS 15.0); LabeledContent (iOS 16.0); View.textSelection(_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read PlaylistSettingsView.swift:203-224 and measured T02-settings-2.png: Name, Server URL and Username rows are about 118 px tall, the Password row about 168 px. The cause is `.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)` on the eye button label (219). git blame shows that line came from 0ab5bcd, whose message lists '44pt tap targets', so the frame is deliberate accessibility work; the fix must keep a 44pt target, which a whole-row button does. The mask repeats a bullet per real character (210). isPasswordRevealed is @State (15) and is never reset, and the Settings tab stays alive inside the TabView, so a revealed password stays visible across tab switches and in the app switcher. The value has no copy affordance. Three parts of the proposed fix do not work as described. (1) `.privacySensitive()` only redacts when the system applies the privacy redaction reason (widgets, Always-On); it does nothing for the app switcher snapshot. (2) `.tint(.primary)` on the button also changes what `.foregroundStyle(.tint)` resolves to on the eye icon, so the icon loses the accent colour. (3) `.textSelection(.enabled)` on a Text inside a Button label competes with the button's own gesture and is unlikely to give a Copy menu.

**Corrected claim:** The Password row is about 40 percent taller than its neighbours because of a deliberate 44pt minimum frame on the eye button; the mask shows the real password length; a revealed password stays revealed when leaving the tab or backgrounding the app; and the password cannot be copied.

**Corrected fix:** Make the whole row a Button that toggles isPasswordRevealed, with `LabeledContent(L("settings.playlist.password")) { HStack { Text(isPasswordRevealed ? playlist.password : "••••••••"); Image(systemName: ...).foregroundStyle(Color.accentColor) } }` as its label, the label Text given `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` instead of overriding tint, and no fixed frame (the row is already at least 44pt tall, so the tap target from 0ab5bcd is kept). Keep the accessibility label and add an accessibility value or hint for the masked/revealed state. Reset isPasswordRevealed in `.onDisappear` on the Form and in `.onChange(of: scenePhase)` when the phase leaves `.active`; drop `.privacySensitive()`. For copy, add `.contextMenu` on the row with a Copy action that writes to UIPasteboard (this needs one new localized string in the ten languages; the existing key 'player.stream_url.copy' says 'Copy stream URL'), or leave copy out.

**API check:** `func privacySensitive(_ sensitive: Bool = true)`, `@available(iOS 15.0, ...)` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:2864-2870): exists but does not address the app switcher. `tint<S>(_ tint: S?) where S : ShapeStyle` and the disfavored `tint(_ tint: Color?)` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19516, 19529): `.tint(.primary)` compiles but overrides the tint the icon uses. `LabeledContent.init<S>(_ title: S, @ViewBuilder content:)` iOS 16.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4037-4038). `contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems:)` present (9870). `textSelection` iOS 15.0 (1825). `scenePhase` is not yet used in the non-player views but is a standard environment value.

**Regression risks:** Removing the frame without making the whole row tappable would undo the 44pt tap target added in 0ab5bcd. VoiceOver currently reads 'Show password' / 'Hide password' on the eye button; the whole-row button must keep an equivalent label or hint. `.onDisappear` on a row inside a lazy Form also fires when the row scrolls off screen, so put the reset on the Form.

**How to verify:** Screenshot comparison with T02: all four rows in the group the same height. Simulator UI test: reveal the password, switch to another tab and back, assert the value is masked; reveal again, send the app to the background and reopen, assert masked. Check on a device that the app switcher card shows the masked value.

## settings-ux-11 — The M3U TV-guide URL editor inserts a newline on Return, has an always-enabled 'Save EPG URL' button with no result, and 'Last updated' counts seconds

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (M3U) › TV Guide, Settings (Xtream) › TV Guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:32-44`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:68-82`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:126-140`

**What the user perceives:** Typing or pasting a guide URL and pressing Return adds a line break instead of saving; the keyboard stays up. 'Save EPG URL' can be tapped at any time, including with nothing changed, and nothing confirms the save. 'Last updated' shows a running counter such as '3 min, 12 sec' that changes every second. In the Xtream form, turning 'Show TV guide' on or off makes two or three rows appear or vanish without animation.

**Mechanism (finder):** `TextField(…, axis: .vertical)` with `.lineLimit(1...3)` (68-72) has no `.onSubmit`; vertical text fields treat Return as a newline. The Button at 74-76 has no `.disabled`. `Text(last, style: .relative)` (36) is the self-updating two-unit timer style. `if epgEnabled { … }` (131-140) is driven by a plain binding, so the row insertion is not animated.

**Proposed fix (finder):** ```swift
TextField(L("epg.settings.url_placeholder"), text: $epgURLDraft)
    .keyboardType(.URL).textInputAutocapitalization(.never).autocorrectionDisabled()
    .submitLabel(.done)
    .onSubmit { Task { await saveURL() } }
Button(L("epg.settings.save_url")) { Task { await saveURL() } }
    .disabled(draftTrimmed == (playlist.epgURLOverride ?? playlist.m3uEpgURL ?? ""))

LabeledContent(L("epg.last_updated")) {
    Text(last, format: .relative(presentation: .named))   // "5 minutes ago", "yesterday"
}
Toggle(L("epg.settings.enable"), isOn: $epgEnabled.animation())
```
Show a save failure in the section footer in place of the red row at 80-82.

**APIs:** View.submitLabel(_:) (iOS 15.0); View.onSubmit(of:_:) (iOS 15.0); Text(_:format:) with Date.RelativeFormatStyle .relative(presentation: .named) (iOS 15.0); Binding.animation(_:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift. (1) :68-72 is `TextField(..., axis: .vertical)` + `.lineLimit(1...3)` with no `.onSubmit`, no `.submitLabel`, no focus handling: a vertical-axis field takes Return as a line break and nothing dismisses the keyboard. saveURL() (:95) trims only leading/trailing whitespace and newlines, so a newline typed or pasted inside the URL is saved as part of it. The field arrived with the EPG feature in 1cce013 (2026-07-24) with no comment; the vertical axis is evidently there to wrap long XMLTV URLs, not a guarded decision. Real. (2) :74-76 the Save button has no `.disabled`. True, but "nothing confirms the save" is overstated: a non-empty save calls EPGStore.forceRefresh (:102-104), which shows the spinner on the refresh row (:27) and then updates Last updated or prints the red failure (:46-50). Only saving an empty or unchanged value is silent. (3) :36 `Text(last, style: .relative)` is the self-ticking two-unit style ("3 min, 12 sec", no "ago"). Real. (4) :126-140 the toggle uses a plain `$epgEnabled`, so the `if epgEnabled` rows are inserted and removed without a transaction animation. Real. No screenshot covers this section (the demo Xtream playlist fails verify, so the gated TV Guide section is absent in T01-T04, and there is no M3U settings shot); the verdict is from code. Problems in the proposed fix: (a) `Text(last, format: .relative(presentation: .named))` is a static text. It is formatted against "now" only when resolved, and the Settings tab stays alive, so it can read "now" or "5 minutes ago" for hours. (b) The proposed disabled test `draft == (epgURLOverride ?? m3uEpgURL ?? "")` never becomes true after the user clears the field on a playlist that has an x-tvg-url header: saveURL stores override = nil, the draft stays "", the baseline is m3uEpgURL (Models/Playlist.swift:72-77 effectiveEPGURL), so Save stays enabled, the field shows empty and Refresh stays disabled (:78) although the header URL is in effect. (c) `.onSubmit { saveURL() }` without a changed-guard starts a full forceRefresh on every Return, even with nothing edited. (d) Dropping `axis: .vertical` means a long URL (xmltv.php?username=...&password=...) no longer wraps; that is the native single-line URL field behaviour but it is a visible trade-off. (e) `draftTrimmed` does not exist in the file and must be added.

**Corrected claim:** In the M3U TV-guide section, Return inserts a line break into the URL field and never dismisses the keyboard (an interior newline is saved into the URL); Save is enabled even when nothing changed and gives no feedback when the value is cleared or unchanged (a non-empty save does show the refresh spinner); "Last updated" is a ticking two-unit counter with no "ago"; in the Xtream section the rows under "Show TV guide" appear and disappear without animation.

**Corrected fix:** Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift only. (1) Make the field single-line: drop `axis: .vertical` and `.lineLimit`, add `.submitLabel(.done)` and `.onSubmit { if isDirty { Task { await saveURL() } } }`. Single-line gives Return = submit + keyboard dismissal and strips pasted newlines; the cost is that long URLs scroll instead of wrapping. (2) Add `private var draftTrimmed: String` and `private var isDirty: Bool { draftTrimmed != (playlist.epgURLOverride ?? playlist.m3uEpgURL ?? "") }`; `.disabled(!isDirty)` on Save; after a successful save set `epgURLDraft = updated.epgURLOverride ?? updated.m3uEpgURL ?? ""` so that clearing the override shows the header URL that is actually in effect and the button disables. (3) Last updated: keep it self-updating but coarse. Either the iOS 18 form `Text(.currentDate, format: .reference(to: last, allowedFields: [.day, .hour, .minute], maxFieldCount: 1))` (check the rendered wording once on the simulator), or `TimelineView(.everyMinute) { _ in Text(last.formatted(.relative(presentation: .named).locale(locale))) }` with `@Environment(\.locale)` so the in-app language is used. Do not use a bare static `Text(last, format:)`. (4) `Toggle(L("epg.settings.enable"), isOn: $epgEnabled.animation())`. Moving the save error into the footer is optional.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8932 `func submitLabel(_:)` iOS 15.0. :7739 `func onSubmit(of triggers: SubmitTriggers = .text, _ action:)` iOS 15.0. :5265 `TextField.init(_:text:axis:)` iOS 16.0 (the current call). SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:7494 `Text.init<F>(_ input: F.FormatInput, format: F) where F: FormatStyle, F.FormatInput: Equatable, F.FormatOutput == String` iOS 15.0 (static, not self-updating). Foundation.swiftinterface:1808 `Date.RelativeFormatStyle` iOS 15.0, :1880 `static func relative(presentation:unitsStyle:)`, :1836 `.named`. SwiftUICore:11639 `Binding.animation(_:)` in an iOS 13.0 extension. Self-updating alternatives: SwiftUICore:14199/14201 `Text.init<V, F>(_ source: TimeDataSource<V>, format: F) where F: DiscreteFormatStyle` iOS 18.0; :14187 `TimeDataSource.currentDate` iOS 18.0; :642 `FormatStyle.reference(to:allowedFields:maxFieldCount:thresholdField:)` -> `SystemFormatStyle.DateReference` iOS 18.0; SwiftUI:22830 `TimelineView` iOS 15.0; SwiftUICore:2128 `.everyMinute`. All are at or below the iOS 18.0 deployment target, no availability guard needed.

**Regression risks:** A single-line field no longer shows a long URL in full. Disabling Save when unchanged removes the "tap Save again to re-fetch" path; the Refresh row covers it. A static relative Text would go stale while the tab stays alive, hence the self-updating form. Relative formatting must follow the app's `\.locale` (set at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:64), not the device locale, or the value appears in a different language from its label. `.animation()` on the toggle binding also animates the later matched-channels row only if that state change falls in the same transaction; harmless.

**How to verify:** UI test on an M3U playlist: type a URL, press Return, assert the keyboard is gone, the field value contains no newline, Save is disabled and the refresh row shows a spinner. Clear the field on a playlist imported with an x-tvg-url header, save, and assert the field shows the header URL and Save is disabled. Leave the Settings tab open for 3 minutes after a refresh and check that Last updated advances by minutes, not seconds, in the in-app language (set the app language to one that differs from the device). On Xtream, flip Show TV guide and watch the rows animate.

## settings-ux-12 — On iPad the settings Form has no width cap, so labels and values sit at opposite edges of the screen

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Settings (Xtream) on iPad, Settings (M3U) on iPad, Downloads, App Language
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:70-75`, `Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:35`

**What the user perceives:** On an 11- or 13-inch iPad the Settings tab is a full-width grouped list: 'Server URL' on the far left, its value up to a thousand points away on the far right, switches at the screen edge. Apple's own settings either sit in a split-view column or in a form sheet about 540-700 pt wide.

**Mechanism (finder):** The Form is the root of a tab's NavigationStack (DashboardView.swift:70-75, M3UDashboardView.swift:37-43) with no frame, content margin or readable-width constraint; an inset-grouped list fills the container. No iPad screenshot of Settings exists yet (the ipad-light set has only the Live TV tab), so this is read from code.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Centre the form content in regular width with a shared modifier, used by both forms, DownloadsView and LanguagePickerListView.

```swift
struct ReadableFormWidth: ViewModifier {
    @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) private var hSize
    @State private var width: CGFloat = 0
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self) { $0.size.width } action: { width = $0 }
            .contentMargins(.horizontal,
                            hSize == .regular ? max(20, (width - 672) / 2) : nil,
                            for: .scrollContent)
    }
}
```
`nil` keeps the system margin on iPhone and in narrow multitasking widths. contentMargins on a List is already used in TipJarView.swift:100.

**APIs:** View.contentMargins(_:_:for:) (iOS 17.0); View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 16.0 (back-deployed))

**Verifier reasons:** Code: Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44 and Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40 are bare `Form {}` roots of a tab's NavigationStack (Views/DashboardView.swift:70-75, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:37-43) with no frame or margin; a search of the app sources finds no `horizontalSizeClass` or readable-width handling anywhere outside the player. Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:35 and Views/DownloadsView.swift:79 are plain Lists pushed on the same stack. There is still no iPad Settings screenshot (ipad-light holds only L01-L06 at the final listing), but ipad-light/L06-favorites.png shows the iPad layout: tab bar floating at the top, content edge to edge, large title at the leading edge. A Form in that container will span the full 834 pt (portrait) or about 1210 pt (landscape). So the claim is very likely true but not seen. The proposed modifier compiles against the SDK, yet it has two open points: (a) the settings screens use large titles (DashboardView.swift:229-230; M3UDashboardView.swift:39-40). Centring the rows in a 672 pt column leaves the large "Settings" title at the screen's leading edge, up to about 270 pt left of the content in landscape. (b) How an inset-grouped List applies a horizontal `.scrollContent` margin (replacing or adding to its own inset, behaviour during pull-to-refresh) is not shown anywhere in this code base: TipJarView.swift:100 uses `.top` only. The first layout pass also runs with width = 0, so the margin starts at 20 and then changes; whether that is visible has to be looked at.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad the two settings forms, Downloads and the language list fill the full window width, so each row's label and value sit far apart. Inferred from code and from the iPad Favorites screenshot; not yet seen on an iPad Settings screenshot.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the shared-modifier approach (content margins rather than a framed Form, so the whole width still scrolls and the grouped background stays full-bleed), but settle the title alignment on the simulator before applying it. If the centred column under a left-aligned large title looks wrong, use `.navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)` for these screens in regular width, or cap less aggressively. iPhone and compact widths keep the system margin (`nil`). Owner decision: a centred readable column versus leaving the full-width form as many SwiftUI apps do.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4238 `func contentMargins(_ edges: Edge.Set = .all, _ length: CGFloat?, for placement: ContentMarginPlacement = .automatic)` iOS 17.0; the optional length makes the `nil` branch valid. :10405 `ContentMarginPlacement.scrollContent`. SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6067 `func onGeometryChange<T>(for:of:action:)` with the single-value action is `@_alwaysEmitIntoClient` in an extension marked iOS 16.0 (the two-value variant at :6078 is iOS 18.0); already used at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:376. `horizontalSizeClass` environment is iOS 13. No availability guard needed on iOS 18.0.

**Regression risks:** Large title no longer lines up with the rows. Possible one-frame margin change on first appearance. Row swipe actions and the pull-to-refresh indicator in a margin-inset List need a look. DownloadsView switches between ContentUnavailableView and List (DownloadsView.swift:70-79), so the modifier must sit on the List, not the container. No interaction with the tip-jar sheet (it has its own List).

**How to verify:** iPad Pro 11-inch simulator, Settings tab, before and after, in portrait, landscape, Split View half width and Slide Over: measure the row width (target about 672 pt in regular width, unchanged in compact), check the large title against the row leading edge, pull to refresh, push Downloads and App Language, and watch the first frame after switching to the tab for a margin jump.

## settings-ux-13 — The Xtream and M3U settings forms have drifted: different section order and error handling, and three sections are copy-pasted between the two files

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U)
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:88-167`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:83-158`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:160-200`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:189-194`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:31`

**What the user perceives:** A user with one playlist of each kind sees TV Guide above Statistics in one and below it in the other, a source URL laid out in two different ways, and failures that are an alert in one form and inline text or nothing in the other.

**Mechanism (finder):** Section order after Playlist Information is Statistics, Server, TV Guide, Content (Xtream, 264-344) against TV Guide, Statistics, Content (M3U, 185-225). The URL row is a single HStack (Xtream 189-194) against a stacked footnote with lineLimit(3) (M3U 170-176). The Downloads section (Xtream 88-126, M3U 83-121) and the Player section (131-167, 125-158) are identical copies, as is About. M3U observes LocalizationManager (31) although the root rebuild makes that redundant; Xtream does not.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Extract the shared sections into one file, e.g. Views/Components/SettingsSections.swift, and use them from both forms in the same order:

```swift
struct DownloadSettingsSection: View { let playlist: Playlist; /* @AppStorage wifi-only, usedBytes, delete-all dialog */ }
struct PlaybackSettingsSection: View { /* the four @AppStorage toggles */ }
```
Leave the About section and its TipJarRow() line in each form untouched. Align the order (TV Guide before Statistics in both, or the order chosen in the regrouping finding) and use the URL layout from the row-grammar finding in both.

**Verifier reasons:** Facts check out. Order after Playlist Information: Xtream is Statistics (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:264), Server (:296), TV Guide (:318), Content (:321); M3U is TV Guide (Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:185), Statistics (:187), Content (:202). Downloads (:88-126 vs :83-121), Player (:131-167 vs :125-158) and About are the same code twice. Errors: Xtream shows inline text (:75-85, :232-237) and only prints a failed history clear (:444); M3U routes everything to one alert (:257-261). M3U observes LocalizationManager (:31), which the root rebuild at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66 (`.id(selectedLanguage)`) makes redundant but harmless. Corrections: (1) Little of this is something a user feels. The duplication is a maintenance matter, and almost nobody compares the two forms side by side. (2) The URL layout difference is justified by content: an M3U source is a long get.php URL with credentials (stacked footnote, :170-176), an Xtream server URL is a short host (:189-194). (3) The Xtream inline sync error is deliberate (comment at :11-13, commit 0ab5bcd, 2026-07-22) and must be kept. (4) The drift that does affect users is not in the finding: Xtream wraps Statistics, TV Guide and Content Management in `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil` (:263, from 2849d943; the EPG section was added inside the gate in 1cce013). None of the three needs the panel's auth response (local COUNT queries, the EPG toggle, the adult filter, Clear history). While verify() is in flight the sections are missing and then pop in above About; when verify fails they never appear. iphone-light/T03-settings-3.png shows exactly that: "Could not fetch info: HTTP 404" followed directly by About. M3U always shows them. (5) touches_user_wip should be true: both files carry the uncommitted TipJarRow() line (the working-tree diff is only that line, +1 and +2).

**Corrected claim:** The two settings forms duplicate the Downloads, Player and About sections and order TV Guide and Statistics differently; that is mostly a maintenance problem. The user-visible drift is that the Xtream form hides Statistics, TV Guide and Content Management until the panel auth call succeeds, so they pop in late or are missing when the server is unreachable, while the M3U form always shows them.

**Corrected fix:** 1) In PlaylistSettingsView move Statistics, XtreamEPGSettingsSection and Content Management out of the `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil` block (:263-345); keep only the Server section conditional. This removes the pop-in and keeps the TV-guide toggle, adult filter and Clear history reachable offline. 2) Use one section order in both forms (owner picks; TV Guide before Statistics matches M3U). 3) Optionally extract `DownloadSettingsSection(playlist:)` and `PlaybackSettingsSection()` into Views/Components; attach the delete-all confirmation to the delete button row rather than to the Section, and let the section load its own usage in `.task` (the parent's `.refreshable` then needs a refresh token or the usage stays owned by the parent). Leave About and the TipJarRow() line as they are, keep the two URL layouts, keep Xtream's inline sync error.

**API check:** No new API. The extraction uses @AppStorage, Section, NavigationLink and alert, all already used in these files.

**Regression risks:** Both files contain the owner's uncommitted TipJarRow() line; an extraction that moves or rewrites the About section would disturb it. Moving the download-usage state into a child section breaks the parent's pull-to-refresh and the post-delete refresh unless they are rewired. A modifier on a Section inside a Form can be applied per row, so an alert there may register more than once. ScreensUITests (another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:116-160) asserts the Downloads row, "Player Settings" and "Playlist Information" by label; keep those strings and the row order reachable by one swipe. Un-gating the Xtream sections changes what the demo-fixture screenshots show (more rows above About).

**How to verify:** Xtream playlist with the server unreachable (the demo fixture already returns 404): Statistics, TV Guide and Content Management must be present and usable. With a slow server, open Settings and check that no section appears late above About. Run the existing settings UI tests; compare screenshots of the Xtream and M3U forms for section order.

## settings-ux-14 — Subtitles of the link rows in About render in light tint blue instead of secondary grey

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings › About
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:357-370`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:234-247`

**What the user perceives:** 'Contribute to the project on GitHub' under 'Support on GitHub' is pale blue on white and hard to read (T03-settings-3.png; darker blue on dark grey in iphone-dark/T03-settings-3.png), while every other description in the form is grey.

**Mechanism (finder):** Inside a Link the foreground style is the tint; `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:363) is the hierarchical secondary level of that tint, not the label colour. The toggle descriptions use the same modifier outside a button and therefore come out grey.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use the concrete colour for the subtitle of the GitHub row in both forms: `.foregroundStyle(Color.secondary)` (lines 363 and 240), or switch the row to the two-Text label form from the row-grammar finding and set `.tint(.primary)` on the Link with the arrow glyph in `.tint`. The tip row above it has the same rendering; it is the owner's work in progress and is left alone here. Its position between Version and GitHub is the right place for it.

**APIs:** Color.secondary (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Screenshots confirm it: in iphone-light/T03-settings-3.png "Contribute to the project on GitHub" is pale blue on white, and in iphone-dark/T03-settings-3.png it is dim blue on dark grey; both are hard to read. The toggle descriptions on the same screen are grey (T02). Code: Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:361-363 and Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:238-240 use `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` inside a `Link` label. That is the hierarchical secondary level of the current foreground style, which inside a link is the tint. The same row proves the fix: the arrow glyph uses `.foregroundColor(.secondary)` (the concrete colour, :368 and :245) and renders grey in both screenshots. Scope correction: the tip row directly above has the identical defect (Views/Components/TipJarView.swift:15-17, visible in the same screenshots). Fixing only the GitHub row leaves a grey subtitle directly under a pale-blue one in the same section.

**Corrected claim:** The caption lines of both tappable rows in About (Tip the Developer and Support on GitHub) render as a faded tint blue with poor contrast in light and dark, because `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` inside a Button or Link label resolves against the tint.

**Corrected fix:** Change `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` to `.foregroundStyle(Color.secondary)` at Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:363 and Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:240, and make the same one-token change at Views/Components/TipJarView.swift:17 so the two adjacent rows match. That last edit is in the owner's uncommitted tip-jar file; it changes one colour token and leaves the work intact, but it is the owner's call. If the owner prefers not to touch TipJarView yet, apply all three together later rather than only two. Leave the `.tint(.primary)` variant out; it would also turn the row titles black, which is a design decision.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:7605 `public static let secondary: SwiftUICore.Color` in the `extension Color` block (iOS 13.0); the finding listed it as unverified, it is present. The hierarchical one the code currently resolves to is :6679 `ShapeStyle where Self == HierarchicalShapeStyle { static var secondary }`. `foregroundStyle(_:)` is already in use in these files.

**Regression risks:** None functional. If only the GitHub row is changed, About shows two differently coloured captions next to each other. The settings files and TipJarView.swift are part of the owner's uncommitted work: touch only the colour token, not the TipJarRow() call or the row structure.

**How to verify:** Re-take T03-settings-3 in light and dark: both captions in About should match the grey of the toggle descriptions in T02, and the row titles stay tint blue.

## onboarding-playlists-1 — The Xtream import runs behind a small HUD with one static, wrong status line; Cancel dismisses the sheet but the import keeps running, the form stays editable, and nothing keeps the screen awake for a multi-minute import.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Add Xtream playlist sheet, Add M3U sheet (Xtream auto-detect and M3U import), Playlist list
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:85-119, 122-212`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:104-143, 185-224, 228-317`, `Models/XtreamImporter.swift:23-41, 51-91`, `Views/Components/LoadingProcessView.swift:1-57`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should adding an Xtream playlist stay a blocking sheet with honest, cancellable progress, or verify credentials only and let the catalog download inside the dashboard?

**What the user perceives:** After Save a floating card shows a scaled spinner and 'Downloading categories...' for the whole download (which is really the movie and series lists), then 'Saving to database... Please wait.'. There is no bar, no counts and no hint how long it takes. Fields and the adult-filter toggle behind the card still respond. Tapping Cancel closes the sheet, yet the playlist appears in the list a minute later anyway; if it failed, nothing is ever shown. If the phone auto-locks during a long import, the import is likely to fail on return.

**Mechanism (finder):** The HUD is an .overlay card on the Form (AddPlaylistView.swift:97-111, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:121-134) with ProgressView().scaleEffect(1.5) and a 0.9-opacity systemBackground; the Form is never .disabled, so it stays interactive. Cancel is not tied to the work: Button { dismiss() } (AddPlaylistView.swift:86-88, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:105) while the import is an unstored Task (AddPlaylistView.swift:92, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:109), so nothing cancels it; only the swipe is blocked (interactiveDismissDisabled, :119 / :143). After a Cancel the importer still saves the playlist row and content (XtreamImporter.swift:36-38, 51-91) and the error alert state belongs to a dismissed view. Progress is two strings: progress(L("add_playlist.fetching_categories")) before all six parallel fetches (XtreamImporter.swift:23-32) and saving_db (:41); the keys add_playlist.fetching_live/movies/series exist in Localizable.strings but no Swift file uses them. loading.takes_time_hint is only used by LoadingProcessView, which nothing instantiates. No isIdleTimerDisabled or beginBackgroundTask exists outside the player (grep), so auto-lock suspends the default-session requests.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Plain fix, both forms: (1) keep the task: @State private var saveTask: Task<Void, Never>?; Save: saveTask = Task { await savePlaylist() }; Cancel: saveTask?.cancel(); dismiss(). async let children and URLSession.data(from:) honour cancellation; add try Task.checkCancellation() in XtreamImporter before the first write (line 36) and before M3UImporter.replace; in the catch blocks return silently when Task.isCancelled. (2) Form { ... }.disabled(isLoading) and replace the card with a first Section: HStack { ProgressView(); Text(progressMessage) }, ProgressView(value: Double(step), total: 7), footer Text(L("loading.takes_time_hint")). (3) Real progress: wrap each of the six fetches so completion bumps a MainActor counter and reports the existing fetching_live/movies/series strings, step 7 = saving. (4) UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true with defer reset, plus beginBackgroundTask(withName:) around the import. Larger option (decision): after verify() save only the playlist row, dismiss and enter the dashboard; PlaylistContentStore.loadPlaylist already bootstraps an empty playlist (PlaylistContentStore.swift:115-125) and the tabs already render loadingMessage (LiveStreamsView.swift:66-74), so the user waits inside the app instead of behind a modal.

**APIs:** ProgressView(value:total:) (iOS 14.0); View.interactiveDismissDisabled(_:) (iOS 15.0); UIApplication.isIdleTimerDisabled (iOS 2.0 (UIApplication.h:95)); UIApplication.beginBackgroundTask(withName:expirationHandler:) (iOS 7.0 (UIApplication.h:142))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/AddPlaylistView.swift, Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift, Models/XtreamImporter.swift, Views/Components/LoadingProcessView.swift. The core claims hold. (a) Cancel is a bare dismiss() (AddPlaylistView.swift:86-88, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:105) while the import is an unstored Task (AddPlaylistView.swift:92, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:109); nothing cancels it, so XtreamImporter still writes the playlist row and content (XtreamImporter.swift:36-38, 51-91) and M3UImporter.replace still runs; a failure after Cancel sets showError on a dismissed view and is never seen. The comment at AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:141-142 shows the owner already fixed exactly this for the swipe gesture (interactiveDismissDisabled, git 0ab5bcd) but the Cancel button was left with the same hole, so this is an oversight, not a decision. (b) The HUD is a small .overlay card (AddPlaylistView.swift:97-111, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:121-134); the Form is never disabled so fields and the toggle stay live. (c) Progress really is two strings: 'Downloading categories...' is set once before all six parallel fetches (XtreamImporter.swift:23-32), then saving_db (:41). grep confirms add_playlist.fetching_live/movies/series exist in en.lproj/Localizable.strings:50-52 with no Swift user, and LoadingProcessView is only referenced by its own preview. (d) isIdleTimerDisabled/beginBackgroundTask exist only in Networking/VideoPlayerController.swift:1547-1548, 2343 and PlayerCore/AirPlayRemux/CastController.swift:3001. Corrections: the auto-lock failure is plausible (PanelURLSession has a 20 s request timeout, XtreamAPIClient.swift:28) but is not provable from code; it needs a device. The 7-step bar is not 'real progress': the three category calls return in under a second and the bar then sits at 3/7 for the whole movie/series download. Cancellation inside XtreamAPIClient.fetch surfaces as XtreamError.networkError(URLError.cancelled) (XtreamAPIClient.swift:146-147) and in M3UService as M3UServiceError.networkError (M3UService.swift:44-45), and M3UParser.parseAsync / readLocalAsync use Task.detached (M3UParser.swift:135, M3UService.swift:69) which does not inherit cancellation, so the catch blocks must test Task.isCancelled rather than the error type, and a checkCancellation is needed after parse. Extra observation that affects the 'larger option': the app target builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393, 415) and XtreamAPIClient is an unannotated class (XtreamAPIClient.swift:34), so JSONDecoder.decode at :131 appears to run on the main actor; if so the form (and, for the dashboard-bootstrap option, every tab) is frozen during the decode of a large movie list. That should be measured before choosing the dashboard option. Severity lowered to medium: real bug, but a once-per-playlist flow outside the owner's main ask.

**Corrected claim:** While an Xtream or M3U import runs, the add sheet shows a small HUD whose only texts are 'Downloading categories...' (displayed during the whole six-endpoint download) and 'Saving to database...'. The form behind it stays editable. The Cancel button only dismisses the sheet: the import task is not cancelled, the playlist still appears later, and a later failure is never shown. Nothing keeps the screen awake; whether auto-lock actually breaks a long import must be checked on a device.

**Corrected fix:** Both forms: (1) store the task (@State private var saveTask: Task<Void, Never>?), Cancel = saveTask?.cancel(); dismiss(). Add try Task.checkCancellation() in XtreamImporter.syncAndSave right before the first write (line 36), and in AddM3UPlaylistView after fetchRemote and after parseAsync (the detached parse does not see cancellation). In every catch block return silently when Task.isCancelled (the error arrives wrapped as XtreamError.networkError / M3UServiceError.networkError, so do not match on CancellationError). (2) Block the form: Form { ... }.disabled(isLoading) applied directly on the Form, before .navigationTitle/.toolbar so Cancel stays enabled; set focusedField = nil on Save so the keyboard does not cover the status. Either keep the card but make it system-like (plain ProgressView() with .controlSize(.large), .regularMaterial background) or show a status Section at the top of the form inserted inside withAnimation. (3) Honest status instead of a 7-step bar: keep an indeterminate spinner and report what is still outstanding by wrapping the three large fetches so their completion updates the text using the existing add_playlist.fetching_live/movies/series strings (e.g. show the last one still running), then saving_db; add loading.takes_time_hint as secondary text. (4) UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true with a defer reset inside savePlaylist (safe: the add sheets are only presented from the playlist list, where no player exists, ContentView.swift:79-116), optionally beginBackgroundTask(withName:) with a matching endBackgroundTask in both the expiration handler and the defer; it only buys about 30 s. The 'download inside the dashboard' option is a product decision and should wait until main-thread JSON decoding in XtreamAPIClient.fetch is measured.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: ProgressView init<V>(value: V?, total: V = 1.0) at :3985, @available(iOS 14.0). View.interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) at :23593, iOS 15.0. View.disabled(_:) in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:190 (iOS 13). UIApplication.h:95 idleTimerDisabled (getter isIdleTimerDisabled); UIApplication.h:142 beginBackgroundTaskWithName:expirationHandler: API_AVAILABLE(ios(7.0)). Task.checkCancellation / Task.isCancelled are Swift stdlib. All available on iOS 18; no iOS 26-only API involved.

**Regression risks:** A cancel check placed between the two writes of XtreamImporter would leave a playlist row without content (it would then bootstrap on first open via PlaylistContentStore.swift:115-119), so check only before the first write. .disabled placed after .toolbar would also disable Cancel. Forgetting to reset isIdleTimerDisabled on an early return would keep the screen awake on the playlist list. Wrapping the async-let fetches must keep them parallel (deliberate, XtreamImporter.swift:20-21). The edit path uses the same code: cancelling an edit must leave the old row untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit test with a URLProtocol-stubbed URLSession (XtreamAPIClient.init takes urlSession, XtreamAPIClient.swift:38): start syncAndSave in a Task, cancel while the stub is holding the responses, assert no playlist row exists. UI test against a slow local stub: tap Save, assert the text fields are not enabled, tap Cancel, wait, assert the list has no new row. Device: 30 s auto-lock, slow panel, check whether the import survives with and without the idle-timer change. Instruments Time Profiler or a main-thread hang check during the import of a 100k-movie panel to see whether JSON decoding runs on the main thread.

## onboarding-playlists-2 — The Xtream Server URL field is pre-filled with "http://", so pasting a full address produces "http://http://...", the empty-URL check never fires, and a pasted get.php link is not understood.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Add Xtream playlist sheet
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:30, 47-53, 94`, `Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:57-83`, `Networking/XtreamLinkDetector.swift:19-42`

**What the user perceives:** Providers send the address as a complete link and most people paste it. Pasting into the field gives 'http://http://host:8080'; Save is enabled, the spinner runs until the request fails, then an alert says 'Network error: A server with the specified hostname could not be found.' Pasting the whole 'get.php?username=..&password=..' link fails with a decode error. Users with an https panel must first delete the prefix.

**Mechanism (finder):** _url = State(initialValue: editingPlaylist?.serverURL ?? "http://") (AddPlaylistView.swift:30); screenshot P03-add-xtream-form.png shows the pre-filled text. Save is disabled on url.isEmpty (line 94), which is never true with the prefix, and no field is trimmed, so whitespace-only values pass. getBaseURLComponents only checks hasPrefix("http://") and appends /player_api.php to the raw string (XtreamAPIClient.swift:60-70), so a doubled scheme resolves host "http", and a pasted get.php link ends up as '...get.php?...m3u_plus/player_api.php' with the query then overwritten (line 77). XtreamLinkDetector can already split such links but is only called from the M3U form (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:267-269). The client already prepends http:// when the scheme is missing (XtreamAPIClient.swift:60-62), so the prefill is not needed.

**Proposed fix (finder):** AddPlaylistView: start empty and show the scheme as a prompt: TextField(L("add_playlist.server_url"), text: $url, prompt: Text(verbatim: "http://example.com:8080")). Add .onChange(of: url) { _, new in if let c = XtreamLinkDetector.detect(urlString: new) { url = c.serverURL; username = c.username; password = c.password; if name.isEmpty { name = URLComponents(string: c.serverURL)?.host ?? "" } } }. Extend XtreamLinkDetector.detect to also accept a path ending in /player_api.php. Validate with a computed property: trim, prepend http:// when no scheme, require URLComponents.host to be non-empty; use it and trimmed username/password in the Save .disabled condition. This also keeps the rule that add-form defaults stay empty.

**APIs:** TextField(_:text:prompt:) (iOS 15.0); View.onChange(of:_:) two-parameter form (iOS 17.0 (already used at ContentView.swift:145))

**Verifier reasons:** AddPlaylistView.swift:30 pre-fills "http://" for a new playlist; iphone-light/P03-add-xtream-form.png shows the field containing the literal text http:// and no visible 'Server URL' label at all (the prefill hides the placeholder). The prefill dates from the first commit of the tree (git log -S'?? "http://"' gives only d2489f9, the monorepo move) and has no comment explaining it; it is also redundant because getBaseURLComponents prepends http:// itself (XtreamAPIClient.swift:60-62). I reproduced the URL building with a scratch Swift script that copies lines 58-80: 'http://http://host.example:8080' becomes http://http//host.example:8080/player_api.php with host 'http'; 'http://host:8080/get.php?username=a&password=b&type=m3u_plus&output=ts' becomes http://host:8080/get.php?username=<field>&password=<field> (the pasted query is thrown away, the path stays get.php), so verify() gets an M3U body or an HTTP error instead of JSON. The Save guard (AddPlaylistView.swift:94) uses untrimmed isEmpty checks, and url.isEmpty can never be true on the add path. XtreamLinkDetector.detect is only called from AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:268. So the mechanism is real. Corrections: Save is not enabled by the prefill alone (username and password are still required), and the doubled scheme is visible in the field, so the user can recover; I rate it medium, not high. The proposed validator ('host non-empty') would accept 'http://http://host' because its host parses as 'http', so the normaliser must collapse repeated schemes explicitly. Rewriting url/username/password from onChange on every keystroke can fire while a user is hand-typing a get.php link (it triggers on the first password character); it should also run at save time. Existing XtreamLinkDetectorTests have no case that pins player_api.php as a non-match, so extending detect is safe there, but it also changes the M3U form (a pasted player_api link would then be added as Xtream).

**Corrected claim:** The Xtream Server URL field starts with the literal text "http://". Pasting a full address after it yields "http://http://...", which the client resolves to host "http" and fails with a hostname error; a pasted get.php link is requested as get.php with the form's credentials and fails to decode. The prefill also hides the field's placeholder and makes the empty-URL check dead. The existing XtreamLinkDetector is not used by this form.

**Corrected fix:** AddPlaylistView: default the URL to "" on the add path and show the hint as a prompt: TextField(L("add_playlist.server_url"), text: $url, prompt: Text(verbatim: "http://example.com:8080")). Add one pure helper (unit-testable, e.g. in XtreamLinkDetector or next to it) that trims, collapses a repeated scheme ("http://http://", "http://https://"), prepends http:// when none is present and returns nil when URLComponents has no host. Use it both for the Save .disabled condition (with trimmed name/username/password) and in savePlaylist before building the Playlist. Apply XtreamLinkDetector.detect in onChange(of: url) for the paste case and again in savePlaylist as a safety net; fill username/password (and the name from the host only when empty). Extending detect to paths ending in /player_api.php is optional; if done, add tests and accept that the M3U form will then also treat such links as Xtream. Keep the edit path unchanged (it shows the stored URL).

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5320 '@_disfavoredOverload nonisolated public init<S>(_ title: S, text: Binding<String>, prompt: Text?) where S : StringProtocol', @available(iOS 15.0). SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827 'func onChange<V>(of value: V, initial: Bool = false, _ action: @escaping (_ oldValue: V, _ newValue: V) -> Void)', iOS 17.0, already used at ContentView.swift:145. Both fine for iOS 18; nothing iOS 26-only.

**Regression risks:** Stored playlists keep their URL, so the edit path is unaffected. No UI test types into this field (grep typeText in another-iptv-playerUITests shows only search fields). Auto-filling username/password from onChange overwrites whatever was typed there; acceptable for a paste, but guard it so it only runs when detect returns credentials. Changing XtreamLinkDetector.detect also changes AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:267-269 behaviour. Matches the owner's rule that add-form defaults stay empty.

**How to verify:** Unit tests for the normaliser: "host:8080", "https://host", "http://http://host:8080", "  ", and for detect with player_api.php if extended. UI test: paste a get.php link into Server URL, assert username and password are filled and Save is enabled; type only spaces, assert Save stays disabled.

## onboarding-playlists-3 — Adding a playlist takes two consecutive sheets: the type picker dismisses, a 0.2 s timer fires, then a second sheet rises.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list, Playlist type sheet, Add Xtream / Add M3U sheets
- Code: `Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:14-38`, `ContentView.swift:11-13, 89-116, 189-200`, `../another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:173-226`

**What the user perceives:** Tap +, a full-height sheet with two rows slides up (P02-playlist-type-sheet.png: about 80% empty). Tap a row: the sheet slides all the way down, the list is visible for a moment, then another sheet slides up. Roughly a second of sheet animation for one choice, where a native app would show a menu under the + button or push inside the same sheet.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each row calls dismiss() and then DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.2) { onSelectXtream() } (PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:15-18, 28-31). The parent drives three independent booleans and three .sheet modifiers plus a fourth for editing (ContentView.swift:98-116). The 0.2 s delay is shorter than the dismissal, so SwiftUI queues the second presentation until the first sheet is gone; the timing is a guess rather than a completion. The picker rows also use hand-drawn chevrons (lines 67-69) although nothing is pushed.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the picker sheet with a Menu on the toolbar button and one sheet driven by an enum. ContentView: private enum PlaylistSheet: Identifiable { case addXtream, addM3U, edit(Playlist) }; @State private var activeSheet: PlaylistSheet?; ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) { Menu { Button { activeSheet = .addXtream } label: { Label(L("playlist_type.xtream.title"), systemImage: "server.rack"); Text(L("playlist_type.xtream.subtitle")) }; Button { activeSheet = .addM3U } label: { Label(L("playlist_type.m3u.title"), systemImage: "list.bullet.rectangle.portrait"); Text(L("playlist_type.m3u.subtitle")) } } label: { Image(systemName: "plus") } }; .sheet(item: $activeSheet) { ... }. Use the same Menu as the empty-state action. Delete PlaylistTypeSelectionView and the asyncAfter. All strings already exist. Alternative if the explanatory rows should stay: keep one sheet and push the form with NavigationLink inside its NavigationStack. Update ScreensUITests.swift:173-186, which asserts the 'Add Playlist' navigation bar of the picker; the two following tests match buttons by label and keep working with menu items.

**APIs:** Menu (iOS 14.0); View.sheet(item:onDismiss:content:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:14-18 and 27-31 call dismiss() and then DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(.now() + 0.2) to flip a second boolean; ContentView.swift:98-116 carries three boolean sheets plus an item sheet. iphone-light/P02-playlist-type-sheet.png shows a full-height sheet whose only content is two rows with hand-drawn chevrons (PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:67-69), although nothing is pushed. History gives no rationale: the 0.2 s timer exists since the first commit (git log -S gives only d2489f9) and the file comment only says the sheet opens on '+'. So the two-sheet sequence with a guessed delay is real and not deliberate. A Menu on the + button with one item-driven sheet is the standard pattern and all four strings already exist (en.lproj/Localizable.strings:30-33). Severity lowered to low: it is a once-per-playlist interaction. The one thing code reading cannot settle is how the two-line menu item (Label plus a second Text as subtitle) renders on iOS 18 and 26; that needs one look in the simulator. The UI-test note is right: test_playlistList_addButton_opensTypeSelectionSheet (ScreensUITests.swift:173-186) asserts the picker's navigation bar and must change; the two following tests match buttons by label and menu items are buttons to XCUITest.

**Corrected claim:** Adding a playlist goes through two consecutive sheets: the type picker dismisses itself, a 0.2 s timer fires, then the form sheet is presented. The picker is a near-empty full-height sheet with fake disclosure chevrons.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: in ContentView replace the three booleans and playlistToEdit with one enum state (private enum PlaylistSheet: Identifiable { case addXtream, addM3U, edit(Playlist); var id: String }) and a single .sheet(item:). Make the + toolbar item a Menu with two Buttons (Label(title, systemImage:) followed by Text(subtitle)); check in the simulator that the subtitle renders, and drop it if it does not. For the empty state use the same Menu with the existing big-button label, or two plain buttons. Delete PlaylistTypeSelectionView and the asyncAfter. Update ScreensUITests.swift:173-186. If the owner prefers to keep the explanatory screen, keep one sheet and push the form inside its NavigationStack instead.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7118 'public struct Menu<Label, Content>' @available(iOS 14.0); init(content:label:) at :7132. SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7482 'func sheet<Item, Content>(item: Binding<Item?>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content:) where Item : Identifiable', iOS 13.0. Nothing iOS 26-only. Subtitle rendering of a second Text inside a Menu button is runtime behaviour and not verifiable from the interface file.

**Regression risks:** One UI test must be rewritten; ZZScreenTourUITests (temporary) also taps through the picker. The swipe-action edit path must set the new enum state. PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift must be removed from the Xcode target if the project lists files explicitly. No interaction with the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** UI test: tap +, tap the 'Xtream Code' menu item, assert the Credentials section appears with no intermediate 'Add Playlist' picker navigation bar; same for M3U. Visual check on iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 and 26) that the menu shows icon, title and subtitle.

## onboarding-playlists-4 — A finished import just closes the sheet: the user is left on the playlist list and has to tap the new row to get in.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Add Xtream playlist sheet, Add M3U sheet, Playlist list
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:199-203`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:208-212, 304-308`, `ContentView.swift:104-109, 165-170`, `Models/XtreamImporter.swift:35-38`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should a newly added playlist open automatically every time, or only when it is the first playlist?

**What the user perceives:** On first run the user waits through the import, the sheet drops, and the screen shows a list with one row. Nothing says it worked and there is no haptic; a second tap is needed to reach the content that was just downloaded. With Xtream the row already appears behind the sheet in the middle of the import.

**Mechanism (finder):** Success paths only reset state and call dismiss() (AddPlaylistView.swift:199-203; AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:208-212 and 304-308). The add views have no completion callback, so ContentView cannot react (ContentView.swift:104-109). The Xtream importer saves the playlist row before the content (XtreamImporter.swift:35-38), so the @Query list updates while the sheet is still busy.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give both add views an optional onAdded: ((Playlist) -> Void)? called just before dismiss() on the add path (not on edit; in the M3U view also from addAsXtream with the Xtream playlist it created). In ContentView keep @State private var justAdded: Playlist? and enter the dashboard from the sheet's onDismiss so the sheet is fully gone before the root switches: .sheet(item: $activeSheet, onDismiss: { if let p = justAdded { justAdded = nil; selectPlaylist(p) } }) { ... AddPlaylistView(onAdded: { justAdded = $0 }) }. Add .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: justAdded?.id) on the list.

**APIs:** View.sheet(item:onDismiss:content:) (iOS 13.0); View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The described behaviour is real: the success paths only reset state and dismiss (AddPlaylistView.swift:199-203; AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:208-212, 304-308), the add views have no completion callback (ContentView.swift:104-109), and the Xtream importer writes the playlist row before the content (XtreamImporter.swift:35-38, deliberate per the doc comment at :10-11), so the row can appear behind the busy sheet. But this is not a defect in the 'native' sense: Apple's own add-account flows (Mail, Calendar) also return to the list. It is a convenience change and a product decision, so I rate it low. The fix as written has two problems. (1) .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: justAdded?.id) fires on every change of the trigger, so it plays once when the id is set and again when justAdded is reset to nil in onDismiss. (2) Passing the form's own Playlist value to selectPlaylist is wrong for M3U: M3UImporter.replace copies the struct and sets m3uEpgURL (and may blank serverURL) on its private copy (M3UImporter.swift:25-27), so the form's newPlaylist (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-282, m3uEpgURL nil) is stale; M3UDashboardView hands that struct to EPGStore.setActivePlaylist (M3UDashboardView.swift:88) and EPGStore skips M3U playlists with no effectiveEPGURL (EPGStore.swift:440), so the guide would stay empty until the playlist is re-opened. The callback should carry the id and ContentView should resolve the saved row.

**Corrected claim:** After a successful add the sheet closes and the user lands on the playlist list and must tap the new row; there is no success feedback. Whether a new playlist should open automatically is a product decision, not a bug.

**Corrected fix:** If the owner wants auto-open: give both add views onAdded: ((UUID) -> Void)? called on the add path just before dismiss() (in the M3U view also from addAsXtream with the Xtream playlist's id). In ContentView keep @State private var justAddedID: UUID? and, in the sheet's onDismiss, resolve the saved row (playlists?.first { $0.id == id }, falling back to a DB fetch by id) and call selectPlaylist with it, never with the form's struct. For the haptic use the condition overload so it fires once: .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: justAddedID) { _, new in new != nil }, attached to the list NavigationStack. Recommended default: auto-open only when the list was empty before the add (first run); otherwise stay on the list.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7482 sheet(item:onDismiss:content:), iOS 13.0. SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1983 'func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T) where T : Equatable' and :1985 'func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (_ oldValue: T, _ newValue: T) -> Bool)', both @available(iOS 17.0). Nothing iOS 26-only.

**Regression risks:** Entering the dashboard starts RatingManager.registerSuccessfulSession and the 8 s review timer (ContentView.swift:70-77) and writes lastPlaylistId; acceptable. Selecting with a stale struct would break M3U EPG as described. The @Query list is updated asynchronously, so the lookup in onDismiss needs the DB fallback. Edit path must not trigger auto-open.

**How to verify:** UI test with a small local .m3u file or stubbed panel: add a playlist from an empty list, assert the dashboard tab bar appears without tapping a row; add a second one, assert behaviour matches the chosen rule. For M3U with an x-tvg-url header, assert the guide loads on that first automatic entry. Haptic on device only (once, not twice).
