## onboarding-playlists-5 — Editing an existing playlist does not replace its catalog (Xtream) and wipes the manual EPG URL (M3U).

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Edit Xtream playlist sheet, Edit M3U sheet
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:129-146, 193-197`, `Models/XtreamImporter.swift:51-91`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:465-470, 513-581`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-282`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:94-98`

**What the user perceives:** Turning on 'Filter Adult Content' in the edit sheet runs a full import and the adult categories are still there afterwards. Changing the server address or account leaves the old server's channels and movies mixed with the new ones. Editing the URL of an M3U playlist silently drops the EPG URL the user typed in Settings and switches EPG back on.

**Mechanism (finder):** The edit path calls XtreamImporter.syncAndSave (AddPlaylistView.swift:195), which only upserts with save() and skips filtered rows with continue; it never deletes (XtreamImporter.swift:51-91). The Settings refresh uses delete-then-insert per type in one transaction (PlaylistContentStore.swift:465-470, 517-518, 535-536, 554-555), so the two code paths behave differently; the importer also writes fewer series columns (XtreamImporter.swift:87 versus PlaylistContentStore.swift:563-578). In the M3U form the changed-source path builds a fresh Playlist with only id, name, serverURL and filterAdultContent (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-282), so epgURLOverride (written at EPGSettingsSections.swift:97), epgEnabled and createdAt fall back to defaults; the name-only path correctly copies the existing row (line 241). The Xtream form also rebuilds the struct (AddPlaylistView.swift:129-139) and resets createdAt.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Start from the existing row in both forms: var newPlaylist = editingPlaylist ?? Playlist(name: ..., serverURL: ..., type: ...), then assign only the edited fields. Make the three replace helpers (PlaylistContentStore.swift:513-581) nonisolated internal statics, or move them into XtreamImporter, and have XtreamImporter's write be one transaction: try playlist.save(db); try replaceLiveCatalog(...); try replaceVODCatalog(...); try replaceSeriesCatalog(...). PlaylistContentStore.syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal then calls the same helpers, so add, edit and refresh share one implementation and keep the atomic guarantee described at PlaylistContentStore.swift:445-446.

**Verifier reasons:** Xtream part confirmed. The edit path calls XtreamImporter.syncAndSave (AddPlaylistView.swift:195), which only upserts with save() and skips filtered rows with continue; there is no DELETE anywhere in XtreamImporter.swift:51-91. Primary keys are (id, playlistId, type) for category and (streamId, playlistId) / (seriesId, playlistId) for content (AppDatabase.swift:38, 51, 65, 81), so rows left out of the new payload simply stay. Nothing filters adult content at read time for Xtream: grep shows filterAdultContent is only read inside the two sync paths (PlaylistContentStore.swift:463, 480; XtreamImporter.swift:45), and the toggle exists only in the edit sheet (PlaylistSettingsView has none). So switching the filter on in the edit sheet runs a full import and removes nothing, and a changed server/account leaves the old catalog mixed in. The Settings refresh does delete-then-insert in one transaction (PlaylistContentStore.swift:465-470, 517-518, 535-536, 554-555) and writes more series columns (563-578 versus XtreamImporter.swift:87). M3U part confirmed for the override: the changed-source path builds a fresh Playlist (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-282) and M3UImporter.replace saves that whole row (M3UImporter.swift:25-31), so epgURLOverride written at EPGSettingsSections.swift:97 is lost; the name-only path correctly copies the row (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:241-242). Corrections: 'switches EPG back on' does not apply, because the M3U settings section has no enable toggle (epgEnabled is only toggled in XtreamEPGSettingsSection, EPGSettingsSections.swift:113-160) and the Xtream form already carries epgEnabled/serverTimezone/timeshiftStyle on purpose (AddPlaylistView.swift:127-139, commit 1cce013). The createdAt reset is invisible: nothing reads Playlist.createdAt and PlaylistRequest is unordered (Requests.swift:13). On the fix: do not mark the helpers nonisolated. The target uses SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393, 415) and the DB record structs are unannotated (DBModels.swift), so a nonisolated helper would call main-actor initialisers; just drop 'private' so the same closure pattern as PlaylistContentStore.swift:465-470 is reused. Merging the playlist save into the content transaction would undo the documented behaviour 'the playlist row is saved before content so it stays visible even if a later step fails' (XtreamImporter.swift:10-11, 35); keep the row-first write for the add path.

**Corrected claim:** Editing an Xtream playlist (filter toggle, server or account change) re-imports with upserts only, so rows that should disappear (adult categories, the old server's items) remain, unlike the Settings refresh which replaces the catalog atomically. Editing the source of an M3U playlist rebuilds the row from scratch and drops the manual EPG URL override set in Settings.

**Corrected fix:** M3U: start from the existing row: var newPlaylist = editingPlaylist ?? Playlist(name:..., serverURL:..., type: .m3u), then assign name and serverURL only. Xtream form: same pattern (var newPlaylist = editingPlaylist ?? Playlist(...)), assigning name, serverURL, username, password, filterAdultContent. Catalog: change the three helpers at PlaylistContentStore.swift:513-581 from private static to static (no isolation change) and have XtreamImporter keep its first write (playlist.save) and replace its second write with one transaction calling PlaylistContentStore.replaceLiveCatalog / replaceVODCatalog / replaceSeriesCatalog, so add, edit and refresh share one implementation and series get the full column set. Whether the playlist row and the content should become a single transaction on the edit path is the owner's call; the add path should keep the row-first behaviour.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. GRDB: PersistableRecord.save(db) and db.execute(sql:arguments:) are already used at the cited lines; AppDatabase.write takes a non-Sendable escaping closure (AppDatabase.swift:479), which is why the existing main-actor static helpers compile inside it.

**Regression risks:** Deleting series rows cascades to season and episode rows (AppDatabase.swift:93, 108), exactly as the Settings refresh already does; favorites and watch history reference only the playlist (AppDatabase.swift:151, 162) and survive. Making the playlist save part of the content transaction would change the deliberate 'row survives a content failure' behaviour. Adding nonisolated to the helpers would not compile cleanly under the project's default main-actor isolation. Starting the M3U edit from the existing row keeps filterAdultContent, epgEnabled and the override, which is the intent.

**How to verify:** Unit tests on an in-memory AppDatabase: write a catalog with the filter off, run the edit import with the same payload and the filter on, assert adult categories and their streams are gone; import payload A then payload B under one playlist id, assert no A-only stream ids remain and series rows carry cast/director; save an M3U playlist with epgURLOverride, run the changed-URL edit path, assert the override is still set.

## onboarding-playlists-6 — Swipe-to-delete goes through onDelete plus a generic alert that captures row offsets; the confirmed delete then gives no feedback until the cascade finishes, and Edit exists only as a hidden leading swipe.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list
- Code: `ContentView.swift:15-16, 117-128, 243-252, 257-284`, `Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:24-25`

**What the user perceives:** Swiping a row fully commits the system delete gesture before any question is asked, and the alert that follows says 'Delete Playlist / Are you sure you want to delete this playlist and all its content?' without naming which one. After confirming, the row stays for as long as the database needs to remove a large catalog, then disappears without the usual collapse animation. Nothing on screen hints that a row can be edited; long-press does nothing.

**Mechanism (finder):** .onDelete(perform: deletePlaylists) (ContentView.swift:252) only stores the IndexSet and raises the alert (257-260); the data is not removed, so the List's destructive swipe has nothing to animate to (the exact row behaviour before the alert needs a simulator check). The pending delete is kept as offsets and resolved against the current array at confirm time (265-266), so any change to the @Query result in between, for example a background import finishing, shifts the index to another playlist. The delete is one write with ON DELETE CASCADE over every content table (AppDatabase.swift:37-393) and the row is only removed when the @Query republishes; there is no animation or optimistic state, and errors are printed (line 280). Edit is only .swipeActions(edge: .leading) (243-250); there is no .contextMenu.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace onDelete with an explicit, non-destructive-role swipe button so the row stays put until confirmed, keep the playlist itself, and remove the row optimistically: @State private var pendingDelete: Playlist?; @State private var deletingIDs: Set<UUID> = []. Row: .swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: false) { Button { pendingDelete = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") }.tint(.red) } and .contextMenu { Button { playlistToEdit = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.edit"), systemImage: "pencil") }; Button(role: .destructive) { pendingDelete = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") } }. Alert: .alert(L("playlists.delete.title_named", p.name), isPresented: ..., presenting: pendingDelete) { p in Button(L("common.delete"), role: .destructive) { withAnimation { deletingIDs.insert(p.id) }; performDelete(id: p.id) }; Button(L("common.cancel"), role: .cancel) {} } message: { _ in Text(L("playlists.delete.message")) }. ForEach over playlists.filter { !deletingIDs.contains($0.id) }; on failure remove the id again and show the error. New key playlists.delete.title_named ("Delete “%@”?") in the ten Localizable.strings files, added next to the existing playlist keys.

**APIs:** View.swipeActions(edge:allowsFullSwipe:content:) (iOS 15.0); View.alert(_:isPresented:presenting:actions:message:) (iOS 15.0); View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read ContentView.swift. Confirmed from code: delete is `.onDelete(perform: deletePlaylists)` (ContentView.swift:252), which only stores an IndexSet and raises an alert (257-260); the alert title/message are generic (117-128; en strings 24-25 'Delete Playlist' / 'Are you sure you want to delete this playlist and all its content?'); the confirmed delete awaits `Playlist.deleteAll` (267-269) and the row only leaves when the @Query republishes, with no animation transaction and no optimistic state; errors are only printed (280); Edit exists only as a leading swipe (243-250) and there is no contextMenu on the row. Database/AppDatabase.swift has 14 `onDelete: .cascade` references, so a large catalog delete is a multi-table cascade and the row will linger. History: `offsetsToDelete` dates from the original import (d2489f9), no comment marks it deliberate. Corrections: (1) the 'index shifts to another playlist' race is theoretical. PlaylistRequest is `Playlist.fetchAll(db)` with no ORDER BY on a rowid table (Models/Requests.swift:13, AppDatabase.swift:20-27), so inserts append and edits are UPDATEs; the alert is also modal. Holding the Playlist instead of offsets is still the right shape, but this is not a live data-loss bug. (2) What the row does visually after the destructive swipe commits without a data change (slide out then pop back) is not provable from code; no screenshot covers it. (3) The fix sketch does not compile as written: `p` is used in the alert title outside the `presenting` closure. (4) With the optimistic filter, line 82 `playlists.isEmpty` must use the same filtered array or the last row's delete shows an empty List until the DB finishes. Severity lowered: deleting a playlist is rare and the screen is outside the browsing surfaces the owner named.

**Corrected claim:** On the playlist list, delete uses onDelete plus a generic, unnamed alert; after confirming, the row stays until the cascading delete finishes and then vanishes without animation, failures are silent, and Edit is discoverable only through a leading swipe (no context menu). The offsets-based pending delete is fragile in shape but has no realistic wrong-row path today. The exact row behaviour between swipe and alert needs a simulator look.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with three corrections. (a) `@State private var pendingDelete: Playlist?` and `@State private var deletingIDs: Set<UUID>`; compute `let visible = playlists.filter { !deletingIDs.contains($0.id) }` once and use it for both the `isEmpty` branch (line 82) and the ForEach. (b) Row: `.swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: false) { Button { pendingDelete = playlist } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") }.tint(.red) }` (no destructive role, so the row is not animated away before confirmation), keep the leading Edit swipe, add `.contextMenu { Edit; Button(role: .destructive) Delete }`. (c) Alert title must be built outside the closure: `.alert(L("playlists.delete.title_named", pendingDelete?.name ?? ""), isPresented: Binding(get: { pendingDelete != nil }, set: { if !$0 { pendingDelete = nil } }), presenting: pendingDelete) { p in ... }`. On confirm: `withAnimation { deletingIDs.insert(p.id) }`, then delete by id; on failure remove the id again and show the existing error alert pattern instead of print. One new key `playlists.delete.title_named` in the ten Localizable.strings files next to the playlists.* keys, leaving the tip keys untouched.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `extension View { func swipeActions<T>(edge: HorizontalEdge = .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: Bool = true, @ViewBuilder content: () -> T) }` under @available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, watchOS 8.0) (line 16388-16391). `func alert<S, A, M, T>(_ title: S, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, presenting data: T?, actions: (T) -> A, message: (T) -> M) where S: StringProtocol` in an extension @available(iOS 15.0) (10694-10711). `func contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems)` @available(iOS 13.0) (9867-9870). `L(_ key:, _ args: CVarArg...)` exists (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:135). All fine for iOS 18.

**Regression risks:** Touches Localizable.strings in ten languages, which also holds the uncommitted tip keys: add lines only. A row hidden optimistically must be restored on failure. The filtered array must drive the empty-state check. No existing UI test covers delete, so nothing else is expected to break; test_playlistList_* tests only use the plus button.

**How to verify:** Simulator: before the change, record a full swipe on a row to document what the row does while the alert is up. After: swipe shows a Delete button and the row stays; the alert title names the playlist; on confirm the row collapses immediately with animation even with a large imported catalog; long press shows Edit and Delete; deleting the last playlist goes straight to the empty state.

## onboarding-playlists-7 — The switch between playlist list and dashboard is a hand-made slide that frees the whole in-memory catalog on the main thread in the same tick the animation starts, ignores Reduce Motion and has no defined layering on the way back.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list, Dashboard (Settings > Back to Playlists), M3U dashboard
- Code: `ContentView.swift:42-69, 130-133, 165-170`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:37-48, 183-190`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:46-54`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Keep the playlist list as a separate root screen with a slide, or treat the switch as an account change (cross-fade, or a switcher sheet opened from Settings)?

**What the user perceives:** Entering looks like a push from the right, but the list underneath fades instead of staying put and there is no swipe-back. Leaving from Settings: with a large catalog the tap on 'Back to Playlists' hesitates before anything moves, then the dashboard slides right while the list fades in from nothing, so the two screens blend instead of one revealing the other. With Reduce Motion on, the full-screen slide still plays.

**Mechanism (finder):** The root is a ZStack if/else: dashboard .transition(.move(edge: .trailing)) (ContentView.swift:66-69), list .transition(.opacity) (130-133), both under withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) (48, 58, 166) with no zIndex, so the order of the leaving and entering view during removal is left to SwiftUI. Right after the animated state change the exit closures call PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload() / M3UContentStore.shared.unload() and EPGStore.setActivePlaylist(nil) synchronously (51-53, 61-62). unload() runs clearLists(), which assigns ten @Published properties (PlaylistContentStore.swift:37-48): the arrays and dictionaries holding the catalog are released on the main actor before the first animation frame, and every mounted tab root observing the store is invalidated while it slides out. The comment at ContentView.swift:51 shows the unload itself is deliberate; only its timing is the problem. No accessibilityReduceMotion check exists.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the unload, move it behind the animation and guard against a fast re-entry: withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .smooth(duration: 0.35)) { selectedPlaylist = nil } completion: { guard selectedPlaylist == nil else { return }; PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload(); EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil) } (same for the M3U branch). Add .zIndex(1) to the dashboard group and use .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .trailing)). To get a real push/pop look, keep the list NavigationStack mounted underneath whenever playlists != nil (with .accessibilityHidden(selectedPlaylist != nil)) and drop its opacity transition, so the dashboard slides over and off a fully drawn list. Move the UserDefaults write out of the withAnimation body in selectPlaylist (line 168).

**APIs:** withAnimation(_:completionCriteria:_:completion:) (iOS 17.0); EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion (iOS 13.0); Animation.smooth(duration:extraBounce:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts confirmed. ContentView.swift:42-139 is a ZStack if/else: dashboard `.transition(.move(edge: .trailing))` (66-69), list `.transition(.opacity)` (130-133), `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3))` (48, 58, 166), no zIndex, no reduce-motion check (the only accessibilityReduceMotion uses are in player files). The exit closures call `unload()` and `EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil)` synchronously right after the animated state change (51-53, 61-62); `unload()` runs `clearLists()` which assigns ten @Published properties (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:37-48, 183-190). The unload is deliberate (comments at ContentView.swift:51 and PlaylistContentStore.swift:180-182, commit 0ab5bcd); its timing is not argued anywhere. What does not stand as written: (1) The hitch is not proven. The catalog arrays are released on the main actor in the tap's run-loop turn, but my estimate is tens of milliseconds, not an obvious stall, and the fix only moves that work to after the animation. Only Instruments can size it. (2) 'Every mounted tab root is invalidated while it slides out' is true for LiveStreamsView/VODView/SeriesView/SearchView (all @ObservedObject contentStore), but the only exit path is the Settings tab row (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:46-54, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:46), and the settings form does not render catalog lists, so there is no visible content pop on the leaving screen. (3) Reduce Motion: system pushes keep sliding with Reduce Motion alone; they cross-fade only with the separate Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions option. Honouring reduceMotion on a hand-made full-screen slide is still reasonable, but 'the slide still plays' is not a deviation from system behaviour. (4) 'No swipe-back' is not a defect for a root switch. (5) The layering during removal is genuinely unspecified without zIndex, but which way it currently renders needs a recording. (6) Keeping the list NavigationStack permanently mounted under the dashboard is the risky part of the fix: a second UIKit navigation bar and scroll view stay in the window (status-bar scroll-to-top, focus, and UI tests that query app.navigationBars / app.textFields.firstMatch could be affected; SwiftUI accessibilityHidden over a UIKit-hosted bar is not guaranteed).

**Corrected claim:** The list/dashboard switch is a custom ZStack transition that mixes a slide (dashboard) with a fade (list), has no explicit z-order, ignores Reduce Motion, and releases the in-memory catalog on the main actor in the same turn the exit animation starts. The mixed transition is a visible but minor polish issue on a rarely used path; whether the catalog release costs perceptible frames at 100k+ items is unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** Minimal version only: (1) defer the unload to the animation's completion and guard re-entry: `withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) { selectedPlaylist = nil } completion: { guard selectedPlaylist == nil else { return }; PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload(); EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil) }` (same for the M3U branch with M3UContentStore). (2) Add `.zIndex(1)` to the dashboard Group so it always slides over/off the list. (3) `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)`: use `.transition(.opacity)` for the dashboard when it is on. Do not keep the list mounted underneath and do not change the curve unless a recording shows the fade is objectionable; that and any switcher-sheet redesign are the owner's product decision. Moving the UserDefaults write out of withAnimation (line 168) is cosmetic.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface line 10277-10282: `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *) public func withAnimation<Result>(_ animation: Animation? = .default, completionCriteria: AnimationCompletionCriteria = .logicallyComplete, _ body: () throws -> Result, completion: @escaping () -> Void) rethrows -> Result`. `EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion: Bool` present (line 18334, iOS 13 extension). `Animation.smooth(duration:extraBounce:)` present at 13314 as @_alwaysEmitIntoClient inside an extension marked iOS 13.0 (the finding says iOS 17; either way fine for an iOS 18 target). `View.zIndex(_:)` (8180) and `View.accessibilityHidden(_:)` (13252, iOS 14) present.

**Regression risks:** Deferring unload: a load still in flight can populate the store during the 0.3 s before it is cleared (harmless, cleared in completion); the re-entry guard is required or a fast re-open would be wiped after loadPlaylist started. If the completion were ever skipped the catalog would stay in memory, undoing the deliberate memory fix from 0ab5bcd, so keep the unload unconditional when selectedPlaylist is nil. test_settings_backToList_opensPlaylistList and navigateToPlaylistList (ScreensUITests.swift:160-169, 237-243) wait for navigationBars["Playlists"] and should stay green with the minimal fix; the keep-mounted variant could change what those queries and the dashboard's own navigationBars queries see.

**How to verify:** Screen-record enter and exit before/after and step frame by frame to see which view is on top and whether the list fades over the sliding dashboard. On a device with a 100k+ catalog, Instruments Hitches/Time Profiler around the 'Back to Playlists' tap: measure main-thread time between the tap and the first animation frame (array deallocation under PlaylistContentStore.clearLists) before and after. Run the existing back-to-list UI tests; add one that exits and immediately re-enters the same playlist and asserts content is shown.

## onboarding-playlists-8 — Every failure in the add forms is an alert titled "Error" with raw technical text, and the form shows no mark on the field that caused it.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Add Xtream playlist sheet, Add M3U sheet
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:112-116, 173-190, 204-210`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:135-139, 155-159, 309-316`, `Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:10-18, 144-148`, `Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:236-240, 408-411`

**What the user perceives:** A wrong address ends in 'Error – Network error: A server with the specified hostname could not be found.'; an address that is not an Xtream panel gives 'Error – Data decode error: The data couldn't be read because it isn't in the correct format.'; a blocked panel gives 'Server error: HTTP 403'. After OK the form looks exactly as before, with no focus and no hint which field to fix.

**Mechanism (finder):** Both forms funnel everything into errorMessage = error.localizedDescription and .alert(L("common.error"), ...) (AddPlaylistView.swift:112-116, 185; AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:135-139, 311). XtreamError wraps the Foundation description into net.error.network / misc.xtream.decode_error / misc.xtream.server_error (XtreamAPIClient.swift:10-18). Only the wrong-credentials case has a human message (misc.xtream.auth_error). The import path adds a second prefix, add_playlist.download_save_error (AddPlaylistView.swift:206).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the alert for failures after verification (download or database), and show verification failures inline. AddPlaylistView: private enum FormIssue { case server(String), credentials(String) }; @State private var issue: FormIssue?. Put the message in the footer of the matching Section (Text(msg).foregroundStyle(.red)), set focusedField to .url or .username, and clear issue in .onChange(of: url/username/password). Map errors once: XtreamError.unauthenticated -> .credentials(L("misc.xtream.auth_error")); URLError .cannotFindHost / .cannotConnectToHost / .timedOut / .notConnectedToInternet -> short localized sentences; decodingError -> 'This address did not answer like an Xtream server. Check the address and port.'; serverError keeps the HTTP code in one sentence. Same pattern for the M3U URL field. New keys go into the existing net.error.* block of the ten Localizable.strings files.

**APIs:** Section(content:header:footer:) (iOS 13.0); FocusState (iOS 15.0 (already used at AddPlaylistView.swift:13))

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed in code. Both forms assign `error.localizedDescription` to errorMessage and show `.alert(L("common.error"), ...)` (Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:112-116, 155-157, 183-189; Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:135-139, 157-159, 169-171, 309-315). XtreamError.errorDescription wraps the Foundation text: networkError -> net.error.network 'Network error: %@', decodingError -> misc.xtream.decode_error 'Data decode error: %@', serverError -> 'Server error: %@' (Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:10-18, 124-148); M3UServiceError does the same (Networking/M3UService.swift:10-16). The import path adds a second prefix, add_playlist.download_save_error 'Error downloading or saving content: %@' (AddPlaylistView.swift:206). After OK nothing is focused or marked. So the quoted alert texts are what a user gets. What I do not accept is the framing that an alert itself is un-native: Apple's own account and network forms report verification failures with alerts. The non-native parts are the generic 'Error' title and the raw wrapped text, plus no return to the offending field. Inline red footers are a legitimate design choice but a larger change than needed. Also note AddPlaylistView.swift:173-181's else branch is effectively dead, because verify() already throws .unauthenticated for auth == 0 or missing userInfo (XtreamAPIClient.swift:158-160).

**Corrected claim:** Every failure in the two add forms is shown as an alert titled 'Error' whose message is a wrapped Foundation description (sometimes double-prefixed), and after dismissal the form gives no focus or hint about which field to fix. Only wrong credentials has a human message.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest change: keep the alert, give it a specific title and a human message, and refocus the field. Add one mapping function (internal, unit-testable) from Error to (title, message, field): XtreamError.unauthenticated -> credentials message, focus .username; XtreamError.networkError(let e as URLError) / M3UServiceError.networkError with .cannotFindHost, .cannotConnectToHost, .timedOut, .notConnectedToInternet, .appTransportSecurityRequiresSecureConnection -> short localized sentences, focus .url; decodingError -> 'This address did not answer like an Xtream server. Check the address and port.', focus .url; serverError -> one sentence keeping the HTTP code, focus .url. Store the title in state and use it instead of L("common.error"); set `focusedField` in the alert's OK action. Drop the add_playlist.download_save_error wrapper when the inner error is already mapped. Showing the same message as a red Section footer instead of the alert is an optional design step for the owner, not required for a native feel. New keys go next to net.error.* in the ten Localizable.strings files, adding lines only.

**API check:** Nothing new is required for the alert variant: `View.alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:)` and `@FocusState` are already used in these files (AddPlaylistView.swift:13, 112). For the optional inline variant, `Section(content:header:footer:)` is already used at AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:61. URLError codes are Foundation, not checked in the SwiftUI interface.

**Regression risks:** Localizable.strings holds the uncommitted tip keys; append only. XtreamError/M3UServiceError descriptions are also used by settings refresh (misc.refresh_error, settings.playlist.info_error) and by PlaylistContentStore.loadError, so change the form-side mapping rather than errorDescription itself, or those messages change too. Setting focus from an alert action while the alert is dismissing can be dropped by SwiftUI; may need to set it on the next run loop.

**How to verify:** Unit test the mapping for each error case. Simulator: enter an unresolvable host, a reachable non-Xtream URL, and wrong credentials; check alert title/message are plain sentences in at least en and tr, and that after OK the keyboard is up on the URL or username field. Repeat the URL cases in the M3U form.

## onboarding-playlists-9 — The add forms open with no field focused, carry no persistent labels or content types, the keyboard's final key only hides the keyboard, and a name is mandatory although it can be derived.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Add Xtream playlist sheet, Add M3U sheet
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:39-80, 94`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:39-47, 52-70, 155-176`, `Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:46`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Is the playlist name allowed to be optional and default to the server host or file name?

**What the user perceives:** The sheet appears without a keyboard (P03-add-xtream-form.png, N01-add-m3u-form.png); the first tap is always 'tap a field'. Once text is typed the placeholders are gone and three of the four rows no longer say what they are. After the password the keyboard key says 'done' and only closes the keyboard; Save has to be found in the top corner. The password cannot be revealed although provider passwords are random strings. Save stays grey until a name is invented, also when a file called 'my-list.m3u' was just picked. The toggle text reads 'Hides XXX, 18+, adult categories and is_adult content', an API field name.

**Mechanism (finder):** No initial focus is set; FocusState is only advanced through onSubmit (AddPlaylistView.swift:43-68, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:56-58). Fields are bare TextField(placeholder, text:) rows with no LabeledContent. No .textContentType is set on URL, username or password. Password uses .submitLabel(.done) with onSubmit { focusedField = nil } (67-68); the M3U URL field has .submitLabel(.done) and no onSubmit (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:67). Save requires name on both forms (AddPlaylistView.swift:94, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:40); handleFileImport stores the file name (168) but does not offer it as the name. The description sits inside the Toggle label (AddPlaylistView.swift:72-79) instead of the section footer.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Both forms: .onAppear { if editingPlaylist == nil { focusedField = .url } } (or .defaultFocus($focusedField, .url)). Rows as LabeledContent(L("add_playlist.server_url")) { TextField("", text: $url, prompt: ...).multilineTextAlignment(.trailing) }, reusing the existing label strings. Add .textContentType(.URL), .textContentType(.username), .textContentType(.password). Password and M3U URL: .submitLabel(.go) and .onSubmit { if canSave { saveTask = Task { await savePlaylist() } } }. Add a reveal toggle next to the password (the settings screen already has one, PlaylistSettingsView.swift:15). Make the name optional: when empty at save time use the host (Xtream, M3U URL) or the picked file name without extension, and show that value as the name prompt. Move the adult-filter description into the Section footer and reword the string in the ten languages without 'is_adult'.

**APIs:** LabeledContent (iOS 16.0); View.textContentType(_:) with UITextContentType.URL / .username / .password (iOS 13.0 (types iOS 10.0 / 11.0)); View.submitLabel(.go) / View.onSubmit(of:_:) (iOS 15.0); View.defaultFocus(_:_:priority:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Each code fact checks out: no initial focus (focus only moves via onSubmit, AddPlaylistView.swift:43-68, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:56-58) and P03/N01 screenshots show the sheets without a keyboard; password uses `.submitLabel(.done)` with `onSubmit { focusedField = nil }` (67-68); the M3U URL field has `.submitLabel(.done)` and no onSubmit (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:67); Save requires a name (AddPlaylistView.swift:94, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:40); handleFileImport stores the file name (168) but never offers it as the name; the adult-filter description sits inside the Toggle label (72-79) and the English string is 'Hides XXX, 18+, adult categories and is_adult content' (en strings line 46, visible in P03). add_playlist.filter_adult.desc is used only here. But several sub-claims are taste, not native-feel defects: placeholder-only rows are what Apple's Contacts and Calendar forms use, so LabeledContent rows are optional and cost field width for long URLs and long labels in de/ru; a password reveal button is a feature (SecureField has none natively); textContentType(.username/.password) mainly switches on Password AutoFill and possibly a save-password prompt for a server that has no associated domain, with little benefit since keyboardType/autocapitalization are already set. Focusing `.url` on appear skips the name field that sits above it and only makes sense if the owner agrees to make the name optional. Also `saveTask` in the fix sketch does not exist; the code uses a bare `Task { await savePlaylist() }` (line 92), and the Xtream form has no `canSave` property. This is a bundle of small polish items on a form used once per playlist, so severity is low.

**Corrected claim:** The add forms open without a focused field, the last field's return key only hides the keyboard instead of submitting, a picked file's name is not offered as the playlist name, and the adult-filter explanation is inside the toggle label and exposes the API field name 'is_adult'. Missing persistent labels, content types and a password reveal are optional improvements, not deviations from system forms. Whether the name may be optional is a product decision.

**Corrected fix:** Core, no product decision needed: (1) on new forms focus the first field: `.onAppear { if editingPlaylist == nil { focusedField = .name } }` (or `.defaultFocus($focusedField, .name)`; check on the simulator which one reliably raises the keyboard inside the sheet). (2) Password field and M3U URL field: `.submitLabel(.go)` and `.onSubmit { guard canSave else { return }; Task { await savePlaylist() } }`, extracting the Xtream disable condition at line 94 into a `canSave` property shared with the Save button. (3) In handleFileImport, after a successful read, `if name.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty { name = url.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent }`. (4) Move the description to `Section(header:footer:)` footer with a plain `Toggle(L("add_playlist.filter_adult"), isOn:)` and reword add_playlist.filter_adult.desc in the ten languages without 'is_adult'. Optional, owner's call: optional name defaulting to host or file name; LabeledContent rows; a reveal toggle modelled on PlaylistSettingsView.swift:206-223; `.textContentType(.URL)` on the URL fields. Leave `.username/.password` content types out unless a device check shows no unwanted AutoFill or save-password prompts.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `func defaultFocus<V>(_ binding: FocusState<V>.Binding, _ value: V, priority: DefaultFocusEvaluationPriority = .automatic)` @available(iOS 17.0) (line 4382-4383). `public struct SubmitLabel` @available(iOS 15.0) with `static var go` (8900-8907); `func submitLabel(_:)` iOS 15 (8930-8932); `func onSubmit(of: SubmitTriggers = .text, _ action:)` iOS 15 (7737-7739). `public struct LabeledContent<Label, Content>` @available(iOS 16.0) (4018-4019) with `init<S>(_ title: S, content:) where Label == Text` (7138). `func textContentType(_ textContentType: UIKit.UITextContentType?)` @available(iOS 13.0) (19311-19314); UITextInputTraits.h: UITextContentTypeURL ios(10.0), UITextContentTypeUsername ios(11.0), UITextContentTypePassword ios(11.0). `TextField(_:text:prompt:)` StringProtocol overload iOS 15 (5319-5320).

**Regression risks:** Autofocus changes what the add sheets look like on open; test_playlistTypeSelection_xtream_opensXtreamForm and _m3u_opensM3UForm (ScreensUITests.swift:188-225) only check for the Credentials label and a text field, so they should hold, but the keyboard now covers the lower half of the form. Submitting from the keyboard must honour the same disabled condition as Save or an import could start with empty fields. Rewording add_playlist.filter_adult.desc touches the ten strings files that hold the uncommitted tip keys: edit that one line only. Prefilling the name from a file must not overwrite a name the user typed.

**How to verify:** Simulator, software keyboard on: open each add form and check the keyboard is up on the first field; walk the fields with the return key and confirm the last one starts verification when the form is valid and does nothing when it is not; pick a file named my-list.m3u with an empty name and confirm the name field fills; re-shoot P03 and compare the content-settings section. If content types are added, check on a real device with iCloud Keychain enabled that no save-password sheet appears after a successful add.

## onboarding-playlists-10 — A half-filled add or edit form can be swiped away or cancelled with no warning, losing a hand-typed address and password.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Add Xtream playlist sheet, Add M3U sheet, Edit sheets
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:85-89, 119`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:104-106, 143`

**What the user perceives:** After typing a long server address, user name and password, a downward drag that was meant to scroll or to hide the keyboard closes the sheet and everything is gone. Apple's own editing sheets hold the sheet and ask 'Discard Changes?'.

**Mechanism (finder):** interactiveDismissDisabled is bound only to isLoading (AddPlaylistView.swift:119, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:143) and Cancel calls dismiss() unconditionally (86-88, 105). There is no notion of a dirty form.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Both forms: private var isDirty: Bool comparing the fields with their initial values (editingPlaylist or empty, plus hasLocalFile in the M3U form); .interactiveDismissDisabled(isLoading || isDirty); Cancel: if isDirty { confirmDiscard = true } else { dismiss() }; .confirmationDialog(L("form.discard.title"), isPresented: $confirmDiscard, titleVisibility: .visible) { Button(L("form.discard.confirm"), role: .destructive) { dismiss() }; Button(L("form.discard.keep_editing"), role: .cancel) {} }. Three new keys in the ten Localizable.strings files.

**APIs:** View.interactiveDismissDisabled(_:) (iOS 15.0); View.confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** `.interactiveDismissDisabled(isLoading)` is the only dismissal guard on both forms (Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:119, Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:143) and Cancel calls `dismiss()` unconditionally (AddPlaylistView.swift:86-88, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:105). There is no dirty-state concept and no discard string in the English table. The comments next to interactiveDismissDisabled (118, 141-142) explain why loading blocks the swipe and say nothing against extending it, and history (0ab5bcd) shows it was added for that loading case only. Holding a dirty sheet and asking 'Discard Changes?' is what system editing sheets do. Two additions from reading the code: Cancel stays enabled while isLoading, so tapping it during an import dismisses the sheet and leaves the unstructured save Task running, which is exactly the situation the comment at AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:141-142 says the swipe guard was added to prevent; and SwiftUI has no dismiss-attempt callback (none found in the interface), so a blocked swipe will only rubber-band and the dialog can appear only from Cancel.

**Corrected claim:** A half-filled add or edit form can be swiped away or cancelled with no warning, losing a typed address and password. In addition, Cancel remains tappable during verification/import and dismisses the sheet while the save task keeps running.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: `private var isDirty: Bool` comparing fields with their initial values (new Xtream form: name "", url "http://", username "", password "", filter false; edit: editingPlaylist's values; M3U: also hasLocalFile); `.interactiveDismissDisabled(isLoading || isDirty)`; Cancel: `if isDirty { confirmDiscard = true } else { dismiss() }`; attach `.confirmationDialog(L("form.discard.title"), isPresented: $confirmDiscard, titleVisibility: .visible) { Button(L("form.discard.confirm"), role: .destructive) { dismiss() }; Button(L("form.discard.keep_editing"), role: .cancel) {} }` to the Cancel button itself so iPad and iOS 26 anchor it there. Also add `.disabled(isLoading)` to Cancel on both forms (or cancel the save task). Three new keys in the ten Localizable.strings files, appended without touching the tip keys.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true)` @available(iOS 15.0) (line 23591-23593). `func confirmationDialog<S, A>(_ title: S, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> A) where S: StringProtocol` in an extension @available(iOS 15.0) (17491-17502). No SwiftUI API for a dismiss-attempt callback was found (grep for DismissAttempt returned nothing); the UIKit equivalent is `presentationControllerDidAttemptToDismiss:` API_AVAILABLE(ios(13.0)) in UIPresentationController.h:60, which would need a UIKit bridge and is not worth it here.

**Regression risks:** A blocked swipe gives no explanation, only resistance; acceptable but different from Contacts, which shows the dialog on the swipe. The dirty comparison must use the same trimming as save or an untouched edit form could count as dirty. The existing isLoading guard and its comments must stay. Strings files carry the uncommitted tip keys: append only. Disabling Cancel during loading removes the only way out of a hung import apart from the 20 s request timeout (XtreamAPIClient.swift:28), so cancelling the task instead may be preferable.

**How to verify:** Simulator: untouched form dismisses by swipe and by Cancel immediately; after typing in any field the swipe is refused and Cancel shows the discard dialog anchored at the button (check iPhone and iPad); Discard closes, Keep Editing returns with text intact; in edit mode an unchanged form dismisses freely; during verification Cancel is disabled.

## onboarding-playlists-11 — The first-run empty state is hand-built: fixed 80 pt icon, a 10 pt-radius full-width button with 40 pt margins, and the title "No Playlists Found".

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list (empty, first launch)
- Code: `ContentView.swift:172-203`, `Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:20-22`

**What the user perceives:** The very first screen of the app does not look like the system's empty states: the icon does not scale with text size, the button is a flat rounded rectangle next to iOS 26's capsule controls and stretches across the whole width on iPad, and the headline reads like a failed search rather than a start.

**Mechanism (finder):** emptyState is a VStack with Image(...).resizable().frame(width: 80, height: 80) (ContentView.swift:174-178), a Button whose label is Text + .padding() + .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) + .background(Color.accentColor) + .cornerRadius(10) + .padding(.horizontal, 40) (189-200), white hard-coded text, no ScrollView. No screenshot exists because the demo fixture always seeds a playlist (MockFixture.swift:23-39).

**Proposed fix (finder):** ContentView.emptyState: ContentUnavailableView { Label(L("playlists.empty.title"), systemImage: "tv.badge.wifi") } description: { Text(L("playlists.empty.message")) } actions: { Menu { /* the two type buttons from the toolbar menu */ } label: { Text(L("playlists.empty.add_button")) }.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent) }. Optionally, inside if #available(iOS 26, *), use .buttonStyle(.glassProminent); the iOS 18 fallback is .borderedProminent. Change the value of playlists.empty.title to the neutral form ('No Playlists') in the ten languages.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0); ButtonStyle.borderedProminent (iOS 15.0); ButtonStyle.glassProminent (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts hold. ContentView.swift:172-203 is a hand-built VStack: fixed 80x80 icon (174-178), label with .padding() + .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) + .background(Color.accentColor) + .cornerRadius(10) + .padding(.horizontal, 40) (189-200), white text (194). On iPad the button stretches to window width minus 80 pt. Nothing marks it as deliberate: no comment, and history shows it arrived with the monorepo move (d2489f9). The rest of the app already uses ContentUnavailableView for empty states (Views/DownloadsView.swift:71, Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:53, Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:28, Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:81, Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:58), so this screen is the odd one out. No test references the empty state. No screenshot exists because the fixture always seeds a playlist, so the visual claim rests on code only.

Three corrections to the fix:
1. It says to reuse 'the two type buttons from the toolbar menu'. There is no toolbar menu: the toolbar is a plain Button that sets showingTypePicker (ContentView.swift:90-96) and opens PlaylistTypeSelectionView as a sheet (98-103). The Menu only exists if a sibling finding lands first.
2. 'Change the title in the ten languages' is overstated. Only en ('No Playlists Found'), de ('Keine Playlists gefunden'), ru ('Плейлисты не найдены'), tr ('Playlist Bulunamadı') and zh ('未找到播放列表') use the 'found' wording; ar, es, fr, hi and pt are already neutral (Localization/*.lproj/Localizable.strings:20).
3. The .glassProminent branch is unnecessary: .borderedProminent already gets the iOS 26 capsule look when built against the iOS 26 SDK.

Severity lowered: the screen is shown once per install, or again after deleting every playlist.

**Corrected claim:** The first-run empty state (ContentView.swift:172-203) is a custom VStack with a fixed 80 pt icon and a hand-drawn full-width rounded-rectangle button, while every other empty state in the app uses ContentUnavailableView. In five of ten languages (en, de, ru, tr, zh) the title reads like a failed search ('No Playlists Found'). It is seen only on first launch or after all playlists are deleted.

**Corrected fix:** Replace emptyState with ContentUnavailableView { Label(L("playlists.empty.title"), systemImage: "tv.badge.wifi") } description: { Text(L("playlists.empty.message")) } actions: { Button(L("playlists.empty.add_button")) { showingTypePicker = true }.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent) }. If the sibling finding that turns the '+' toolbar button into a Menu is adopted, use the same Menu here in place of the Button. No iOS 26 branch is needed. Change playlists.empty.title to the neutral form in en, de, ru, tr and zh only (line 20 of each file), leaving the uncommitted tip keys untouched. The copy change is a small product decision for the owner.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576: @available(iOS 17.0, ...) public struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions> with public init(@ViewBuilder label: () -> Label, @ViewBuilder description: () -> Description = { EmptyView() }, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions = { EmptyView() }). Line 21629-21631: @available(iOS 15.0, ...) static var borderedProminent: BorderedProminentButtonStyle. Line 3444-3447: @available(iOS 26.0, ...) static var glassProminent: GlassProminentButtonStyle (exists, but not needed).

**Regression risks:** The accent-coloured icon becomes the system's secondary-tinted one (the native look, but a visible change). The five edited Localizable.strings files carry the owner's uncommitted tip keys, so the edit must touch only line 20. No test references the empty state. No interaction with earlier performance work.

**How to verify:** Run the ContentView preview with the empty database (ContentView.swift:287-290), or a fresh install without -UITests, on iPhone and iPad in light and dark and at the largest accessibility text size. Check that the large 'Playlists' title and the '+' button are unchanged and that the action button opens the type picker.

## onboarding-playlists-12 — Playlist rows print the raw source URL, which for M3U links contains the user name and password, and draw their own chevron that does not flip in right-to-left languages.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list
- Code: `ContentView.swift:211-242`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-277`, `Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:43-54`

**What the user perceives:** An M3U playlist row shows something like 'http://host:8080/get.php?username=ali&pas…put=ts' under the name; on iPad the whole link fits, password included, so it ends up in screenshots and is readable over the shoulder. In Arabic the arrow at the row's edge points the wrong way. The arrow is also lighter and smaller than the system disclosure indicator used elsewhere in the app.

**Mechanism (finder):** The subtitle is Text(playlist.serverURL...) with middle truncation (ContentView.swift:228-232), and the M3U form stores the full link as serverURL (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:276). The API client already masks credentials in error text for exactly this reason (XtreamAPIClient.swift:43-54). The chevron is Image(systemName: "chevron.right").font(.caption).foregroundColor(.secondary) (235-237); 'chevron.right' is a fixed-direction symbol while the app sets layoutDirection for Arabic (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:61-65). Screenshot P01-playlist-list.png shows the row as rendered.

**Proposed fix (finder):** ContentView: derive the subtitle without query or user info: private func sourceLabel(_ p: Playlist) -> String { guard !p.serverURL.isEmpty else { return L("playlists.local_file") }; guard let c = URLComponents(string: p.serverURL), let host = c.host else { return String(p.serverURL.prefix { $0 != "?" }) }; return c.port.map { "\(host):\($0)" } ?? host }. Chevron: Image(systemName: "chevron.forward").font(.footnote.weight(.semibold)).foregroundStyle(.tertiary). Add .lineLimit(2) to the name so the badge keeps its place with long names.

**APIs:** View.foregroundStyle(_:) with HierarchicalShapeStyle.tertiary (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The credential part is real but narrower than stated, and the right-to-left chevron part is unproven and probably wrong.

Credentials: ContentView.swift:228-232 prints playlist.serverURL verbatim, and Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:276 stores the full typed link for M3U playlists. The owner already treats this as a leak elsewhere (Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:43-54 masks username and password, with a comment about alert screenshots). Scope corrections:
- Since bc3bb86 (2026-06-11), a new get.php link whose player_api verifies is saved as an Xtream playlist with only the base URL (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:267-271, Networking/XtreamLinkDetector.swift:33-41). The raw link survives only for panels where verify fails (199-202), playlists added before that commit, re-saves through the edit flow (detection is skipped when editingPlaylist != nil), and non-Xtream links with a token in the query or path.
- The finding missed Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:169-175, which prints the same URL with .lineLimit(3) and therefore shows the whole link, password included, on iPhone too. That is the worse exposure.

Fix defects:
- sourceLabel is a private func on the view, so the proposed unit test cannot reach it.
- The fallback String(serverURL.prefix { $0 != "?" }) still leaks credentials carried in the path of a scheme-less link.
- .lineLimit(2) on the name does not keep the badge in place; the badge needs .fixedSize().

Chevron: I could not confirm that 'chevron.right' stays unflipped in Arabic. The SF Symbols bundle in the installed iOS 18.1 runtime (SFSymbols.framework/CoreGlyphs.bundle/legacy_flippable.plist) lists 'chevron.right' among the symbols that are mirrored automatically. There is no Arabic screenshot. The weight and colour difference from the system disclosure indicator is visible in P01-playlist-list.png (thin .caption, secondary colour) and is cosmetic. The same hand-drawn chevron is at Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:67.

**Corrected claim:** M3U playlist rows (ContentView.swift:228-232) and the M3U settings info section (Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:169-175) print the stored source link verbatim. For M3U playlists not converted to Xtream on add (panel API not answering, added before June 2026, re-saved by editing, or token-style links) that link contains the user name and password or a token. In settings it is fully readable on iPhone; in the list it is fully readable on iPad. The row's hand-drawn chevron is thinner and darker than the system disclosure indicator. Whether it fails to mirror in Arabic is unverified and the symbol bundle suggests it does mirror.

**Corrected fix:** Add an internal computed property on Playlist (Models/Playlist.swift), e.g. var displaySource: String. Empty serverURL returns L("playlists.local_file"). If URLComponents(string:) yields a host, return host, or host:port. Otherwise strip any scheme and return the text up to the first '/' or '?'. Use it at ContentView.swift:228. At Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:172, either use the same property or a masked full link (query values for username/password/token replaced by '***', as XtreamAPIClient.redacted does); which one is the owner's call. That edit does not touch the TipJarRow() line. Chevron in ContentView.swift:235 and Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:67: Image(systemName: "chevron.forward").font(.footnote.weight(.semibold)).foregroundStyle(.tertiary); harmless whether or not the old name mirrors. For long names, put .lineLimit(2) on the name and .fixedSize() on the type badge.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:9293: @inlinable nonisolated public func foregroundStyle<S>(_ style: S) -> some View where S : ShapeStyle; line 6682: static var tertiary: HierarchicalShapeStyle (iOS 15). 'chevron.forward' is in the SF Symbols name_availability.plist as release 2020 = iOS 14.0. URLComponents is Foundation, no availability concern.

**Regression risks:** Two playlists on the same host become distinguishable only by name in the list. Users lose the scheme and path in the list subtitle; the edit sheet still shows the full link. Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift has uncommitted tip-jar work, so the edit must stay on line 172. If other lenses change the remaining eight 'chevron.right' uses (shelf headers), keep them consistent.

**How to verify:** Unit tests for Playlist.displaySource: get.php link with credentials, plain host, host with port, scheme-less host:port, scheme-less link with credentials in the path, IPv6 host, empty string. For the chevron: launch with the app language set to Arabic and screenshot the playlist list before the change; if the arrow already points left, the mirroring claim is false and only the weight/colour change remains.

## m3u-browse-1 — M3U group and favourites grids render every item through one un-paginated, non-Equatable ForEach, so large groups hitch on open, on scroll and on every search keystroke

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U group detail, M3U favourites, M3U Channels (search results inside a group)
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:481-540`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:542-595`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:526-632`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:40-43`

**What the user perceives:** Opening a big M3U group (a VOD dump with 5k-50k entries, or the single 'Other' group of an ungrouped playlist) stalls the push, the scroll indicator jumps while scrolling, and typing in the group's search field lags behind the keyboard. The same category on an Xtream playlist is smooth.

**Mechanism (finder):** M3UGroupGridContent (M3UChannelsView.swift:542-595) builds `ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id)` over the WHOLE group: an O(n) copy of ~200-byte DBM3UChannel structs (about a dozen string retains each) on every body pass, plus an id-keyed ForEach of n elements inside LazyVGrid. The view is not Equatable and takes a closure, so every M3UGroupDetailView body pass re-runs it; the parent body re-runs on each keystroke because `.onChange(of: searchText)` reads the state (M3UChannelsView.swift:504) and on every M3UContentStore publish (line 490). The Xtream grid got exactly this fixed in 654cefc: LiveCategoryContent is Equatable with a cheap signature (LiveStreamsView.swift:534-539), paginates 90 at a time (548-551, 579-582, 602-620) and is wrapped in `.equatable()` (494). None of that was ported to M3U.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give the M3U grid the same three properties. Smallest change, in M3UChannelsView.swift:

struct M3UGroupGridContent: View, Equatable {
  static func == (l: Self, r: Self) -> Bool {
    l.items.count == r.items.count && l.items.first?.id == r.items.first?.id && l.items.last?.id == r.items.last?.id
  }
  @State private var visibleCount = 90
  ...
  ForEach(Array(items.prefix(visibleCount).enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, channel in
    M3UChannelCard(...).onAppear { if index >= visibleCount - 15 { visibleCount = min(visibleCount + 90, items.count) }; prefetchAhead(from: index) }
  }
  if visibleCount < items.count { ProgressView().frame(maxWidth: .infinity).padding(.vertical, 24) }
}

and call it with `.equatable()` in M3UGroupDetailView (line 494) and M3UFavoritesView (line 40); reset visibleCount in a `.task(id: itemsToken)` like LiveStreamsView.swift:555-561/629. Better (stops the drift, see the sharing finding): make LiveCategoryContent generic over the item (`PagedChannelGrid<Item: Identifiable & Sendable, Card: View>`) and use it from both variants. No new API; nothing iOS 26-only.

**APIs:** View.equatable() (iOS 13.0); View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:481-595 and Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:40-43. The structure is as described: M3UGroupGridContent is not Equatable, takes a closure, and builds `ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id)` over the whole array (M3UChannelsView.swift:579) with no page limit. The parent body re-runs per keystroke (`.onChange(of: searchText)` at :504 reads the state) and on every M3UContentStore publish (:490), so the grid body re-runs each time. The Xtream counterpart was deliberately fixed in 654cefc (commit body: "category content views compare by cheap signatures ... grids paginate so 10k+ item lists no longer freeze navigation"); LiveStreamsView.swift:526-632 has the Equatable signature, pageSize 90 and `.equatable()` at :494. None of it exists on the M3U side, and no comment or history marks that as deliberate (M3UGroupGridContent dates from the monorepo move d2489f9). What does not hold: (a) the magnitude. I benchmarked the O(n) copy on the Mac host with a 14-field struct shaped like DBM3UChannel: 50k = about 4 ms, 5k = 0.3 ms, 300k = 28 ms. So the array copy alone is not a keystroke hitch below roughly 100k; the rest of the cost is SwiftUI's ForEach update over n ids, which cannot be read from code. (b) "the scroll indicator jumps while scrolling" is not caused by the missing pagination; pagination makes the indicator rescale every 90 items. (c) Scope: only groups in the 10k+ range (ungrouped playlists that land in the single "Diğer" group, or "ALL" groups); ordinary M3U groups of a few hundred entries are unaffected, and get.php links are now auto-added as Xtream on iOS, which makes giant M3U catalogs rarer. Severity medium, not high.

**Corrected claim:** The M3U group and favourites grids did not receive the large-list treatment the Xtream grid got in 654cefc: no Equatable signature, no pagination, and an O(n) `Array(items.enumerated())` on every parent body pass (each keystroke and each M3UContentStore publish). For groups of 10k+ entries this is the same pattern that froze navigation on the Xtream side; for groups up to a few thousand entries the cost is below a frame. The size of the hitch on real hardware is unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the small version of the proposed fix in Views/M3UChannelsView.swift: make M3UGroupGridContent `View, Equatable` with the cheap signature (count + first id + last id, closure ignored), add `@State visibleCount = 90`, render `items.prefix(visibleCount)`, load the next 90 when a card within the last 15 appears, show a trailing ProgressView while `visibleCount < items.count`, reset visibleCount in `.task(id: itemsToken)`, and call it with `.equatable()` from M3UChannelsView.swift:494 and M3UFavoritesView.swift:40. The closures stay correct when body is skipped because they read @State (`displayItems`, `filtered`) through the state box, the same as LiveCategoryDetailView. Do not do the generic `PagedChannelGrid` refactor as part of this: LiveCategoryContent also owns the sort/filter menu and toolbar, so merging the two is a larger change with regression surface on the Xtream grid.

**API check:** `extension View where Self: Equatable { nonisolated public func equatable() -> EquatableView<Self> }`, @available(iOS 13.0), SwiftUI.swiftinterface:16310-16312. `nonisolated public func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) -> some View where T: Equatable`, @available(iOS 15.0), SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166. Both are already used by LiveCategoryContent (LiveStreamsView.swift:494, 629), including the MainActor-isolated Equatable conformance, so the shape compiles in this project.

**Regression risks:** The cheap signature can keep a stale grid when the item set changes but count, first id and last id stay the same (the Xtream grid accepts the same risk). Pagination makes the scroll indicator rescale as pages load and breaks any future scroll-to-item beyond the loaded page. prefetchAhead must index into the paged prefix consistently. EPG now/next still updates because M3UChannelCard reads `\.epgSnapshot` from the environment itself.

**How to verify:** There is no M3U fixture in Database/MockFixture.swift today. Add one with a single 30k-channel group, then in a simulator UI test push the group and type four characters in its search field; record hitch time ratio with XCTOSSignpostMetric (navigationTransitionMetric for the push, scrollDecelerationMetric for a fling) before and after. Decide on device (Instruments > Hangs / SwiftUI template): count main-thread body time of M3UGroupGridContent per keystroke at 5k, 30k and 100k.

## m3u-browse-2 — A half-watched M3U film restarts from 0:00 when opened from its shelf, group grid or favourites; only the Continue Watching card resumes

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels, M3U group detail, M3U favourites
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:264-274`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:529-539`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:83-93`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:286-304`, `Views/VODView.swift:935-957`

**What the user perceives:** The user watches 40 minutes of a film from an M3U playlist, later finds it again in its group or in favourites, taps it, and it starts from the beginning. On an Xtream playlist the same tap resumes. There is also no progress indication on the M3U card.

**Mechanism (finder):** All three M3U entry points build `M3UPlayerShell(playlist:channel:queue:)` without `resumeTimeMs` (M3UChannelsView.swift:268-272, 533-537; M3UFavoritesView.swift:87-91). PlayerView only resumes when it is handed a value (`shouldStartFromResume = !isLiveStream && (resumeTimeMs ?? 0) > 5000`, PlayerView.swift:1598). The history row exists (it is what `presentHistoryItem` uses at M3UChannelsView.swift:301), it is just never looked up on these paths. Xtream looks it up (MovieDetailView.swift:22-41, VODView.swift:940-957).

**Proposed fix (finder):** One shared presenter used by the three call sites (also removes the triplicated present code), in M3UChannelsView.swift next to M3UStreamClassifier:

@MainActor enum M3UPlayback {
  static func present(_ channel: DBM3UChannel, queue: [DBM3UChannel], playlist: Playlist, overlay: PlayerOverlayController) {
    guard let url = M3UParser.sanitizedURL(from: channel.url) else { return }
    guard !M3UStreamClassifier.classify(url: url, groupTitle: channel.groupTitle).isLive else {
      overlay.present { M3UPlayerShell(playlist: playlist, channel: channel, queue: queue) }; return
    }
    Task {
      let pid = playlist.id, sid = channel.id
      let history = try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in
        try DBWatchHistory.filter(Column("streamId") == sid && Column("playlistId") == pid && Column("type") == "vod").fetchOne(db)
      }
      overlay.present { M3UPlayerShell(playlist: playlist, channel: channel, queue: queue, resumeTimeMs: history?.resumePositionMs(as: .film)) }
    }
  }
}

Same one-shot read and the same `.film` rule VODView.swift:940-957 already uses. M3UPlayerShell itself is not changed.

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read the three entry points: Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:264-274 and :529-539, Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:83-93. All build `M3UPlayerShell(playlist:channel:queue:)` with no resumeTimeMs; only presentHistoryItem (:286-304) passes one. The shell forwards its own state to PlayerView (:691), and PlayerView only resumes from the value it is handed (`shouldStartFromResume = !isLiveStream && (resumeTimeMs ?? 0) > 5000`, Views/PlayerView.swift:1598); its only DBWatchHistory use is the save at :3093, so there is no fallback lookup. Worse than stated: saveWatchHistory writes the same primary key `"\(playlistId)_\(type)_\(streamId)"` (PlayerView.swift:3093-3095), so the restart from 0:00 overwrites the stored 40-minute position and the Continue Watching card loses it too. No comment or history marks this as deliberate. One correction to the comparison: on Xtream a film tap opens MovieDetailView, which offers Resume (MovieDetailView.swift:22-41); it does not resume on tap. M3U has no detail screen, so resuming on tap is the equivalent behaviour. The async one-shot read before presenting follows the existing VODView.swift:940-957 pattern, and the database is a DatabasePool (Database/Persistence.swift:54), so the read does not wait behind an import write.

**Corrected claim:** A half-watched M3U film opened from its shelf, group grid or favourites starts at 0:00 because none of those paths looks up its watch-history row, and the fresh playback then overwrites the saved position. Only Continue Watching resumes.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two compile and behaviour notes. (1) Views/M3UChannelsView.swift imports only SwiftUI and the target sets SWIFT_UPCOMING_FEATURE_MEMBER_IMPORT_VISIBILITY = YES, so the shared presenter needs `import GRDB` in the file it lives in (or put the history read behind a small helper in a file that already imports GRDB). (2) Guard against a double tap during the read: keep a single in-flight Task (cancel the previous one) so two taps do not present twice. Keep the live branch synchronous, as proposed. The lookup can stay the three-column filter used at VODView.swift:941-948.

**API check:** No SwiftUI or UIKit API involved. GRDB: `AppDatabase.read` (Database/AppDatabase.swift:485) and `DBWatchHistory.filter(...).fetchOne(db)` are the calls VODView.swift:941-948 already makes; `resumePositionMs(as: .film)` is at Models/WatchResume.swift:44. `PlayerOverlayController.present(onDismiss:skipDownloadCheck:playlistId:content:)` at Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:29; M3UPlayerShell's init already accepts `resumeTimeMs:` (M3UChannelsView.swift:630-635).

**Regression risks:** Presentation moves one async hop later for VOD entries (a pool read, normally a few ms). A film finished to 98 percent or more starts over by the `.film` rule, which matches Xtream. Users who expect a grid tap to start over have no detail screen to choose from; whether a restart affordance is wanted is a small product decision. M3UPlayerShell and PlayerView are untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit: WatchResumeTests already covers the rule. UI test on the simulator with an M3U fixture holding one .mp4 entry and a seeded watchHistory row (type vod, lastTimeMs at 50 percent): tap the card in its shelf, in the group grid and in favourites; assert the elapsed-time label is not 0:00 and that the row's lastTimeMs is not reset after a few seconds.

## m3u-browse-3 — Refreshing an M3U playlist writes back the playlist row captured when the dashboard opened, silently undoing the EPG URL and adult-filter changes made since

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels (pull to refresh), M3U Settings (refresh from URL / file), Edit M3U playlist
- Code: `Models/M3UImporter.swift:19-31`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:205-224`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:321-370`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:393-405`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:94-108`, `ContentView.swift:17-54`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-282`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:80-91`

**What the user perceives:** The user enters an XMLTV URL in Settings and taps Save (guide loads), then pulls to refresh the channel list or taps 'Refresh from URL'. The guide keeps working until the next launch, then it is gone and the URL field is empty. Likewise: turn the adult filter on, refresh, and the hidden channels are back while the toggle still shows ON.

**Mechanism (finder):** ContentView keeps `selectedPlaylist` as a one-time snapshot (ContentView.swift:17, 165-169) and hands it to the dashboard for the whole session. Settings writes go to the database only: M3UEPGSettingsSection.saveURL saves `epgURLOverride` from its own @State copy (EPGSettingsSections.swift:94-101), saveFilterSetting saves a local `updated` (M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:393-400). Every refresh then calls `M3UImporter.replace(playlist: playlist, ...)` with the stale snapshot (M3UChannelsView.swift:214-218; M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:333-337, 358-363), and replace does `var updated = playlist; ...; try updated.save(db)` (M3UImporter.swift:25-31): a full-row UPDATE that puts epgURLOverride back to nil and filterAdultContent back to its old value. `reloadIfActive(playlist: playlist)` then re-applies the stale flag in memory (M3UContentStore.swift:82). The comment at Playlist.swift:70-71 shows the override was meant to survive re-imports. Editing the URL in AddM3UPlaylistView rebuilds a Playlist with defaults (273-282) and drops the override and epgEnabled the same way.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make the importer authoritative about which columns it owns. Models/M3UImporter.swift:

try await AppDatabase.shared.write { db in
  // The caller's struct is a snapshot; settings saved since live only in the row.
  var row = try Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: pid) ?? playlist
  row.name = playlist.name
  row.serverURL = clearServerURL ? "" : playlist.serverURL
  row.m3uEpgURL = epgURL
  try row.save(db)
  ... (channel replace unchanged)
}

and let the store read the flag from the row instead of trusting the argument, keeping the signature so the settings view needs no edit (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:80-91):

let (row, fetched) = try await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in
  (try Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: playlist.id), try DBM3UChannel.filter(Column("playlistId") == playlist.id).order(Column("sortIndex")).fetchAll(db))
}
filterAdultContent = row?.filterAdultContent ?? playlist.filterAdultContent

Follow-up (optional, M): ContentView resolves the selected playlist by id from its `@Query playlists` so both dashboards always see the live row.

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real and I confirmed every step. ContentView keeps `selectedPlaylist` as a one-time @State snapshot (ContentView.swift:17, 165-169) and passes it to M3UDashboardView, which hands the same `let playlist` to M3UChannelsView and M3UPlaylistSettingsView (Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:29, 39). M3UImporter.replace does `var updated = playlist; ...; try updated.save(db)` (Models/M3UImporter.swift:25-31), a full-row write, and all three refresh paths pass the snapshot (M3UChannelsView.swift:214-218; M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:333-337, 358-363). `reloadIfActive(playlist:)` then copies the snapshot's flag into memory (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:82). The code base already documents this exact hazard for another column: CatchupURLResolver.swift:274-283 writes only `timeshiftStyle` with the comment "Saving the caller's snapshot would write its other, possibly stale columns back". Why partly: the proposed fix covers only the importer and the store. The two settings writers clobber each other with no refresh involved. saveFilterSetting does `var updated = playlist` on the dashboard snapshot and saves the full row (M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:393-400), which resets an EPG URL override saved earlier in the session to nil. M3UEPGSettingsSection.saveURL saves its own @State copy (Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:94-101), whose filterAdultContent is the value from dashboard open, so saving an EPG URL after turning the adult filter on silently turns the filter off in the database. Both stay broken after the proposed fix.

**Corrected claim:** On an M3U playlist every writer of the playlist row saves a full snapshot taken when the dashboard opened: the importer (pull to refresh, refresh from URL or file, edit with a new URL), the adult-filter toggle and the EPG-URL save. Each one therefore reverts the columns the others changed since: a refresh or an adult-filter toggle wipes the saved EPG URL override, and a refresh or an EPG-URL save reverts the adult filter (in memory at once on refresh, in the database for the next launch).

**Corrected fix:** Three parts, all small. (1) Importer, as proposed (Models/M3UImporter.swift:25-31): inside the write, `var row = try Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: pid) ?? playlist`, set only name, serverURL and m3uEpgURL, then save; a new playlist still inserts through the `?? playlist` branch, and an edit with a new URL (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:273-282) keeps epgURLOverride, epgEnabled and createdAt. (2) Store, as proposed (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:80-91, and the same in loadPlaylist for the alert's Try Again path): read the row in the same read as the channels and take filterAdultContent from it, falling back to the argument. (3) Added: make the two settings writers column-scoped with the idiom already used at CatchupURLResolver.swift:280-281: `try Playlist.filter(key: id).updateAll(db, [Column("filterAdultContent").set(to: newValue)])` in M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:393-400 and `[Column("epgURLOverride").set(to: trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed)]` in EPGSettingsSections.swift:94-101. Part (3) edits M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift, which carries the owner's uncommitted tip-jar line (TipJarRow() at :233); the edit is confined to saveFilterSetting and leaves that work intact, but touches_user_wip is true for this finding. The Xtream settings writers use the same full-row pattern (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:464, 501; EPGSettingsSections.swift:161; PanelTimeZoneResolver.swift:60) and deserve the same treatment under their own finding. The optional ContentView follow-up is not needed once the writers are column-scoped.

**API check:** GRDB checkout: `public static func fetchOne(_ db: Database, key: some DatabaseValueConvertible) throws -> Self?` (GRDB/Record/FetchableRecord+TableRecord.swift:184); `public static func filter(key: some DatabaseValueConvertible) -> QueryInterfaceRequest<Self>` (GRDB/QueryInterface/TableRecord+QueryInterfaceRequest.swift:477); `updateAll(_:_:)` taking column assignments (GRDB/Record/TableRecord.swift:787-876 and on QueryInterfaceRequest); `ColumnExpression.set(to: (any SQLExpressible)?) -> ColumnAssignment` (GRDB/QueryInterface/Request/QueryInterfaceRequest.swift:1919). All three are already used on Playlist at EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:267 and :280-281. No SwiftUI API involved.

**Regression risks:** The importer keeps writing the caller's serverURL, so a URL refresh after a local-file refresh still restores the old URL (unchanged behaviour). With updateAll the settings writers no longer re-insert a playlist deleted meanwhile, which is the desired behaviour. After saveURL the section's own @State copy must still be updated so EPGStore.forceRefresh gets the new URL. Tip-jar code in the settings view must not be moved.

**How to verify:** Unit tests against an in-memory database (give M3UImporter.replace a `db: AppDatabase = .shared` parameter like CatchupURLResolver has): insert a playlist, set epgURLOverride and filterAdultContent on the row, call replace with the original struct, assert both survive; then run the two settings writes in both orders and assert neither reverts the other. Manual: Settings > EPG URL > Save, toggle the adult filter, pull to refresh, relaunch; the URL field and the toggle must both hold.
