## m3u-browse-4 — On an M3U playlist the TV guide cannot start playback: tapping a channel opens its schedule and the programme sheet has no play button

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: EPG guide (M3U), Programme detail sheet (M3U), Channel schedule (M3U)
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:398-409`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:205-206`, `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:78-90`, `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:123-131`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:263-273`

**What the user perceives:** Xtream: tap a channel in the guide and it plays; long-press shows the schedule; the programme sheet offers 'Play channel'. M3U: the same tap pushes the schedule, long-press does the same thing, and the programme sheet only has Close. The guide is read-only and the user has to go back and find the channel in its group.

**Mechanism (finder):** EPGGuideRow carries `liveStream: DBLiveStream?` as the only playable payload and the M3U rows are built with `liveStream: nil` (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:270). playChannel falls back to `detailChannel = row` with the comment 'M3U: no single-view live shell here' (EPGGuideView.swift:399-401), and the sheet gates its play button on `liveStream != nil` (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:81). The M3U shell exists and the row id is the channel id (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:268), so nothing is missing except the wiring.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Resolve the channel from the store by row id and present the M3U shell. EPGGuideView.swift:398:

guard let stream = row.liveStream else {
  if case .m3u(let playlist) = model.source, let channel = M3UContentStore.shared.channel(id: row.id) {
    playerOverlay.present { M3UPlayerShell(playlist: playlist, channel: channel, queue: M3UContentStore.shared.queue(for: channel)) }
  } else { detailChannel = row }
  return
}

Add to M3UContentStore: `func queue(for:)` (moves the canonical-key logic of M3UChannelsView.swift:279-283 into the store) and `func channel(id:)` (linear scan is ~6 ms at 310k; fine for a tap). In EPGProgrammeDetailSheet and ChannelEPGDetailView replace the `liveStream != nil` gate with an optional `onPlayLive: (() -> Void)?` that both variants fill; catch-up stays Xtream-only (M3U catch-up is deliberately deferred, DBModels.swift:155-156).

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:204-206 and :398-409: for a row without `liveStream` the tap handler sets `detailChannel = row`, the same thing the long-press does, with the comment "M3U: no single-view live shell here". M3U rows are built with `liveStream: nil` and `id: channel.id` (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:263-273). The sheet's Play button is gated on `liveStream != nil` (Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:81) and playLiveChannel is Xtream-only (:123-131); ChannelEPGDetailView passes the same nil through (:49). The comment came in with 1cce013 and reflects missing wiring, not a product decision: M3UPlayerShell is an internal struct with an init that takes playlist, channel and queue (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:602, 630-635), the guide has the overlay controller in its environment, and `model.source` is a readable `let` with case `.m3u(Playlist)` (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:67-81). Only catch-up is documented as deferred for M3U (Models/DBModels.swift:155-156). The linear id lookup costs about 19 ms at 300k channels on the Mac host (my benchmark), acceptable for a tap.

**Corrected claim:** On an M3U playlist the TV guide cannot start playback: a channel tap opens the schedule (same as long-press) and the programme sheet has only Close, because the guide's only playable payload is an Xtream DBLiveStream. The M3U shell and the channel id are both available; only the wiring is missing.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed. In EPGGuideView.playChannel, for `.m3u` resolve the channel by `row.id` from M3UContentStore and present M3UPlayerShell with the channel's group as queue; fall back to the schedule only when the channel cannot be resolved. Add `channel(id:)` and `queue(for:)` to M3UContentStore (the canonical-key rule from M3UChannelsView.swift:279-283). In EPGProgrammeDetailSheet and ChannelEPGDetailView add an optional `onPlayLive: (() -> Void)?` and show the Play button when either it or `liveStream` is present; leave the catch-up button gated on `liveStream`. The sheet is documented as self-contained (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:3-6), so keep its Xtream path as it is and only add the closure for M3U.

**API check:** No system API. In-project: `M3UPlayerShell.init(playlist:channel:queue:resumeTimeMs:)` (M3UChannelsView.swift:630), `PlayerOverlayController.present(...)` (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:29), `EPGGuideViewModel.source` and `Source.m3u(Playlist)` (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:67-81), `M3UContentStore.channels` / `channelsByGroup` (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:17-18).

**Regression risks:** The Xtream branch must stay byte-for-byte the same. The M3U queue is the channel's whole group and can contain VOD entries; the shell already handles mixed queues. If the store was reloaded with the adult filter since the rows were built, the lookup can miss; keep the schedule fallback. Long-press must keep opening the schedule.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test with an M3U fixture and a seeded EPG source: open the guide, tap the first channel cell and assert the player overlay appears; long-press and assert the schedule is pushed; open a programme and assert the Play channel button exists and starts playback. Re-run the existing Xtream guide tests unchanged.

## m3u-browse-5 — Three M3U-only passes over the whole catalog run on the main thread: the adult filter at load, the UTF-8 decode of a refreshed playlist, and live/VOD classification when the guide opens

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: M3U dashboard open, M3U Channels (pull to refresh), M3U Settings (adult filter toggle, refresh), EPG guide (M3U)
- Code: `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:57-63`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:83-87`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:137-146`, `Models/AdultContentFilter.swift:39-52`, `Networking/M3UService.swift:29-46`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:263-283`

**What the user perceives:** With the adult filter on, the dashboard freezes mid slide-in when a large M3U playlist opens, and again when the toggle is flipped. The pull-to-refresh spinner stops spinning for a moment when the download finishes. Opening the TV guide on a big M3U playlist hangs before the push completes.

**Mechanism (finder):** The module defaults to MainActor isolation (project.pbxproj: SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor), so a `nonisolated` synchronous helper runs on its caller's thread. (1) `applyAdultFilter` is called inline from the @MainActor load path (M3UContentStore.swift:60, 85) and runs `AdultContentFilter.isAdultCategoryName` twice per channel: uppercased() + components(separatedBy:) + five substring scans (AdultContentFilter.swift:39-52), a few microseconds each, with the group title re-checked for every channel of the group. At 310k channels that is on the order of a second; at 30k, 100-200 ms. The grouping right after it was deliberately moved off-main (comment at line 124) but the filter was not. (2) `M3UService.fetchRemote` is MainActor and calls `decode(data:)` after the await (M3UService.swift:36-40); String(data:encoding:.utf8) on a 50-100 MB body, plus up to three failed fallbacks, runs on main. readLocalAsync already documents and avoids this for files (61-71). (3) EPGGuideViewModel is @MainActor and `buildRows` filters the catalog with `M3UParser.sanitizedURL` + `M3UStreamClassifier.classify` per channel (264, 280-283): a URL parse plus path lowercasing for every entry.

**Proposed fix (finder):** (1) Fold the filter into the existing detached grouping task and memoise per group title. M3UContentStore.swift:

private func prepareOffMain(_ fetched: [DBM3UChannel], filterAdult: Bool) async -> (visible: [DBM3UChannel], grouping: Grouping) {
  let label = Self.ungroupedLabel
  return await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
    let visible = Self.applyAdultFilter(fetched, enabled: filterAdult)   // nonisolated static, [String: Bool] cache for group titles
    return (visible, Self.group(channels: visible, ungroupedLabel: label))
  }.value
}

(2) M3UService.swift:40: `let service = self; return try await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) { try service.decode(data: data) }.value` (same shape as readLocalAsync). (3) Classify once: compute `vodChannelIDs: Set<String>` in the same detached task and expose `func isLive(_:)` on the store; EPGGuideViewModel.swift:264, the context menu (M3UChannelsView.swift:460-461) and the panel builders then do a set lookup instead of re-parsing URLs.

**Verifier reasons:** Build settings confirm SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393, 415, 578, 619), so a synchronous `nonisolated` helper runs on its caller's thread. (1) `applyAdultFilter` is a nonisolated sync method called inline from the MainActor load paths (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:60, 85, 139-146) and calls AdultContentFilter.isAdultCategoryName twice per channel (Models/AdultContentFilter.swift:39-52). I benchmarked a copy of that code on the Mac host: 300k channels = 1.9 s, 30k = 180 ms; an iPhone will not be faster. The grouping next to it was deliberately moved off-main (comment at :124), the filter was not. It only runs when the adult filter is on (default off). (2) M3UService is a MainActor struct; fetchRemote calls the sync `decode(data:)` after the await (Networking/M3UService.swift:36-40), so it runs on main, while readLocalAsync documents and avoids exactly that (:61-71). Measured on a 68 MB body: 26 ms for valid UTF-8, 205 ms when it falls through to Windows-1254. This is the weakest of the three: one to two frames in the common case. (3) EPGGuideViewModel is @MainActor and buildRows filters the whole catalog through sanitizedURL + classify (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:264, 280-283): measured 1.4 s at 300k and 136 ms at 30k. Corrections to the description: the first item freezes the loading spinner and touch handling after the row fetch rather than the slide-in itself on large playlists, and the row mapping that follows in buildRows (two normalizeChannelKey calls plus storedKey per channel, :265-273) also runs on main for both playlist kinds, so the classification is only part of the guide-open cost.

**Corrected claim:** Three M3U-only whole-catalog passes run on the main thread: the adult filter at load and reload (about 0.2 s at 30k channels, about 2 s at 300k, only with the filter on), the text decode of a refreshed playlist (about 25 ms for 68 MB of UTF-8, about 200 ms for a Windows-1254 file), and live/VOD classification when the guide opens (about 0.14 s at 30k, about 1.4 s at 300k). Figures are Mac-host measurements of the same code; device times will be equal or higher.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed. (1) Fold the filter into the existing detached grouping task as a nonisolated static function with a per-group-title cache; AdultContentFilter is already a `nonisolated enum`. (2) Decode in a detached task the way readLocalAsync does (`let service = self; try await Task.detached { try service.decode(data: data) }.value`). (3) Compute the live/VOD split once in the same detached task and expose a set lookup on the store; keep the current rule that a channel whose URL cannot be parsed counts as live (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:281). Order by value: (1) and (3) first, (2) is minor.

**API check:** No system UI API. Swift concurrency only: `Task.detached(priority:)` is already used with the same captures at M3UContentStore.swift:127-129 and M3UService.swift:66-70; `decode(data:)` is already `nonisolated` (M3UService.swift:75); `Grouping` is already Sendable (M3UContentStore.swift:132).

**Regression risks:** The loadToken check must still run after the combined detached step so a stale load cannot overwrite a newer one. The filter output must equal the current one (name OR group title match). A cached VOD id set adds memory proportional to the catalog and must be cleared in unload() and clearLists(). The context menu and panel builders keep working if they still call the classifier directly; switching them to the set is optional.

**How to verify:** Unit test: push a 300k synthetic [DBM3UChannel] through the new off-main step and assert equality with the current filter + group output. Device, Instruments > Time Profiler with a large M3U playlist and the adult filter on: main-thread time inside AdultContentFilter.isAdultCategoryName, String(data:encoding:) and M3UStreamClassifier.classify during dashboard open, pull to refresh and guide open should drop to zero. Add an M3U case to EPGGuidePerformanceTests.

## m3u-browse-6 — Coming back to the M3U Channels screen during a search swaps the filtered shelves for the full catalog and back, because the screen mirrors the store into @State and re-seeds it on every appear

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:17-29`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:136-149`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:228-260`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:513-514`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:109-113`

**What the user perceives:** Search 'sport', open one of the matching groups, go back (or switch to Settings and back): the result list is replaced by every group of the playlist while the search field still says 'sport', the scroll position jumps, and a moment later the filtered list returns. On a large playlist the wrong list stays for as long as the filter takes. After a refresh that changed nothing there is also a short stall when the spinner ends.

**Mechanism (finder):** `displayGroups` / `displayChannelsByGroup` are @State copies of the store (M3UChannelsView.swift:18-19). `.onAppear { applyFull() }` (141) overwrites them with the unfiltered catalog on every appearance, including a pop and a tab switch, without looking at `debouncedQuery`; `.task(id: debouncedQuery)` (136) restarts on the same appearance and re-filters asynchronously in a detached task (242-255), so the full list is on screen in between. The Xtream screen has no such reset (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107). Second cost of the mirror: `.onChange(of: store.channels)` (137, 514) compares two [DBM3UChannel]. Unchanged arrays share a buffer and compare in O(1), but after any reload the buffers differ and an equal-content refresh compares all n elements field by field on the main thread (about a dozen string compares each), then triggers a recompute that produces the same result. The same mirror also means the screen passes through 'no results' between the store publishing and the copy being made.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Read the store directly when there is no query and keep @State only for search results:

// M3UContentStore
@Published private(set) var revision = 0          // += 1 in apply(channels:grouping:) and clearLists()

// M3UChannelsView
private var isSearching: Bool { !debouncedQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty }
private var groups: [String] { isSearching ? filteredGroups : store.groupNames }
private var itemsByGroup: [String: [DBM3UChannel]] { isSearching ? filteredByGroup : store.channelsByGroup }
...
.task(id: FilterKey(query: debouncedQuery, revision: store.revision)) { await recomputeFilter() }   // no-op when not searching or when the key equals the last applied one

Delete `applyFull()`, `.onAppear`, and both `.onChange(of: store.channels)` (M3UGroupDetailView keys its task on `store.revision` too; 654cefc replaced `.task(id: store.channels.count)` there because a count misses same-size changes, and a revision keeps that property at O(1)). The instant return to the full list on clearing the field (comment at line 115) is preserved for free: `groups` falls back to the store the moment `debouncedQuery` is emptied.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:12-29, 112-149, 228-260 and Models/M3UContentStore.swift:103-113. The mechanism is real: `.onAppear { applyFull() }` (141) unconditionally copies store.groupNames/channelsByGroup into the @State mirror (145-149) and never looks at debouncedQuery; `.task(id: debouncedQuery)` (136) also restarts on every re-appearance and only replaces the mirror after an awaited Task.detached (242-259), so at least one frame, and at realistic sizes many, show the unfiltered catalog while the search field still holds the query. CatalogTextSearch.matches normalizes every name (Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:21-29), so the interlude scales with the catalog, and the LazyVStack is rebuilt twice. The Xtream screen has no such reset (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93-107: only .task(id:) recomputes, state is never re-seeded). History: line 141 is from the original file (blame 2849d943, April), no comment marks it as deliberate; it is the first-frame seed, not performance work. The 'no results' interlude is also real by code: after store.apply publishes, body takes the `visibleShelfGroups.isEmpty` branch (50-59) until the Task spawned in onChange (137-140) copies the data. Corrections: (1) the equal-content O(n) compare and the redundant recompute are mutually exclusive (if arrays compare equal, onChange does not fire); I measured the compare with a struct of the same shape (stride 216 B): same buffer about 0.001 ms, distinct equal buffers about 0.6 ms at 5k, 12-16 ms at 100k, 40-60 ms at 310k on an M-series Mac (-O), so it is a one-off post-refresh hitch only on very large playlists. (2) The blame claim about 654cefc replacing `.task(id: store.channels.count)` at line 514 is correct (verified in git show 654cefc). (3) The proposed refactor has a gap: `isSearching` derived from debouncedQuery flips to true before the first filter result exists, so `filteredGroups` is empty or stale and the screen would show 'no results' (or the previous query's result) for the duration of the filter; it also drops the `playlist.id == store.activePlaylistId` guard that applyFull/recomputeFilter have today. Whether search stays active across a push/pop or tab switch (so the query is still there on return) is standard UISearchController behaviour but was not run here.

**Corrected claim:** Returning to the M3U Channels screen (pop from a group, the guide or favourites, or tab switch) while a search query is applied re-seeds the screen with the unfiltered catalog in onAppear and then re-filters asynchronously, so the full list is shown under an active query for the duration of the filter (frames on small lists, hundreds of ms on 100k+). Separately, because the screen mirrors the store into @State, it shows the 'no results' placeholder for a frame between the store publishing and the mirror being filled, and an equal-content refresh costs one O(n) array compare on the main thread (about 40-60 ms at 310k on a Mac, negligible below about 50k).

**Corrected fix:** Step 1 (smallest, fixes the visible swap): M3UChannelsView.swift:141 becomes `.onAppear { if debouncedQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty { applyFull() } }`. Step 2 (optional refactor, removes the placeholder frame and the O(n) compare): add `private(set) var revision = 0` to M3UContentStore, bumped in apply(channels:grouping:) and clearLists(); in the view read `store.groupNames` / `store.channelsByGroup` directly when no search result is applied, guarded by `playlist.id == store.activePlaylistId`; keep @State only for `filteredGroups`, `filteredByGroup` and an `appliedQuery: String` that is set together with the results and cleared synchronously where line 118/132 clear debouncedQuery. Derive 'is showing search results' from `appliedQuery`, not from debouncedQuery, so the full list (or the previous result) stays on screen until the new result arrives. Key the filter with `.task(id: FilterKey(query: debouncedQuery, revision: store.revision))`, and replace both `.onChange(of: store.channels)` (137, 514) with the revision; M3UGroupDetailView can read `store.channelsByGroup[group]` directly when its query is empty, which also removes its first-frame 'no channel' placeholder. queueForChannel and the CategoryPickerSheet entries must switch to the same derived source.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `@inlinable nonisolated public func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, @_inheritActorContext _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) -> some View where T : Equatable`, under `@available(iOS 15.0, ...)`. onChange(of:initial:_:) two-parameter form found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface (iOS 17). FilterKey only needs Equatable. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Step 1: none beyond the first-frame seed staying as it is. Step 2: the instant return to the full list on clearing the field (comment at 115) must be kept by clearing appliedQuery synchronously; M3UGroupShelfRow's Equatable compare stays O(1) only while rows receive the store's own arrays (same buffer), which the direct read preserves; M3UFavoritesView keys on store.channels.count and is untouched; the player shell reads the store independently (out of scope).

**How to verify:** UI test with an M3U fixture of 3+ groups: type a query matching one group, push that group via the header chevron, pop, and assert during the pop that a non-matching group header never exists (poll every frame for about 1 s); repeat with a Settings tab round-trip. For step 2 add a unit test that revision bumps on load and unload, and a UI assertion that the 'list.no_result' label never appears between the spinner and the first shelf on cold load. Measure the filter duration with a 50k+ fixture to size the interlude.

## m3u-browse-7 — A playlist without group-title (or with one giant group) is presented as a single horizontal shelf holding every channel, and each shelf body copies its whole group

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:151-183`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363-382`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:148-159`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: (a) Confirm that a single-group playlist should open as a grid. (b) Capping shelves is a product choice: Xtream shelves are uncapped today, so either cap both variants (recommended, with the header chevron and a trailing See All tile) or keep both uncapped and only remove the per-body copy.

**What the user perceives:** A plain M3U list with no groups opens as one row titled 'Other' with a count and hundreds or thousands of channels that can only be browsed by swiping sideways; the rest of the screen is empty. With a very large group, scrolling the shelf list stutters when that row comes on screen.

**Mechanism (finder):** M3UContentStore.group puts every channel without group-title under the single canonical key (M3UContentStore.swift:153-156) and M3UChannelsView always renders groups as shelves (151-183), so one group means one LazyHStack with n cards. Inside the row, `ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id)` (365) allocates an n-element tuple array on each row body; negligible for a 200-channel group, tens of milliseconds and tens of megabytes for a 100k+ group. The Xtream shelf iterates `ForEach(items)` with no copy (LiveStreamsView.swift:384).

**Proposed fix (finder):** (a) Layout: when exactly one group is visible and no search is active, render the paginated grid from the first finding as the tab's content instead of a shelf, with ContinueWatchingRow as a header above the grid and the same `.refreshable`. M3UGroupGridContent needs a `header` ViewBuilder slot for that, because it owns its ScrollView.
(b) Shelf: bound the preview so the copy is constant-size and the shelf reads like a system shelf:

let shown = items.prefix(M3UShelf.previewLimit)            // e.g. 40
ForEach(Array(shown.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, channel in ... }
if items.count > shown.count { NavigationLink { M3UGroupDetailView(playlist: playlist, group: group) } label: { SeeAllTile(count: items.count) } }

The per-card look-ahead prefetch (M3UChannelsView.swift:373, 389-403) keeps working unchanged on the bounded slice. Queue for prev/next still comes from the full group (queueForChannel).

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:151-183, 320-404 and Models/M3UContentStore.swift:148-159. Layout claim is correct: every channel without group-title goes under the single key `ungroupedLabel` (153-156) and the screen has only the shelf layout, so a plain ungrouped list renders as one horizontal row titled 'Other' with a count and nothing else. The grid is one tap away through the header chevron (337-339). The performance claim is overstated: `ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id)` (365) does allocate an n-element tuple array per row body, but the row is `.equatable()` (179, 326-330), so its body runs when the row is created or its items change, not on scroll frames. I measured the copy with a struct of the same shape (tuple stride 224 B): 0.4 ms at 5k, 7-12 ms and about 22 MB transient at 100k, 21-38 ms at 310k on an M-series Mac (-O). So it is invisible for normal groups and a single hitch only for a 100k+ group; 'stutters while scrolling the shelf list' holds only in that extreme. The comparison with Xtream is correct (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:384 `ForEach(items)`, uncapped, head-only prefetch at 406-416). History: the enumerated ForEach and the per-card look-ahead are from the original file (git log -S points at d2489f9 only), not from a later tuning pass. Fix problems: (a) depends on a paginated grid from another finding; today's M3UGroupGridContent (542-595) is not paginated and copies the whole array the same way (579), so using it as the tab root for an ungrouped 20k+ list without that work would move the cost, not remove it. Switching layout on 'no search active' would flip grid to shelves as soon as the user types, which is itself a layout jump. (b) There is no SeeAllTile view in the code base (the `category.see_all` string exists in Localizable.strings but no Swift file references it), and capping changes behaviour Xtream shelves do not have. No M3U screenshot exists to judge the visual.

**Corrected claim:** A playlist whose channels have no group-title (or that has a single group after hiding) opens as one horizontal shelf titled 'Other' holding every channel, with the rest of the screen empty; browsing needs sideways swiping or a tap on the header to reach the grid. Independently, each shelf row body copies its whole group into a tuple array; this is negligible for ordinary groups and costs one hitch of roughly 10-40 ms plus tens of MB only when a single group has 100k+ entries.

**Corrected fix:** Two separable parts. (1) No product decision, removes the copy and keeps the look-ahead prefetch: iterate lazily instead of materializing, e.g. `ForEach(items.indices.lazy.map { (index: $0, channel: items[$0]) }, id: \.channel.id) { pair in M3UChannelCard(...).onAppear { prefetchAhead(from: pair.index) } }` (LazyMapCollection over Range<Int> is a RandomAccessCollection, O(1) to build), in both M3UGroupShelfRow (365) and M3UGroupGridContent (579). (2) Product decision: when the playlist has exactly one visible group in the store (decide on `store.groupNames` minus hidden, not on the search state), use the grid as the tab's content with ContinueWatchingRow as a header and the same .refreshable, and let the search filter that grid; this should wait for the paginated/shared M3U grid, since the current grid builds one ForEach over everything. Capping shelves with a trailing See All tile is a separate product choice that should be made for Xtream and M3U together, not for M3U alone.

**API check:** No new SwiftUI API. ForEach(_:id:content:) with a RandomAccessCollection and a key-path id is long-standing (iOS 13); the lazy map over `items.indices` is Swift stdlib. DBM3UChannel is Identifiable (Models/DBModels.swift:143). The proposed `SeeAllTile` does not exist in the project and would be new code.

**Regression risks:** Part 1: keep the id as the channel id (not the index) so diffing on search results stays stable; prefetch sizes must stay liveShelfIcon/.shelf and liveGridIconSize/.grid so Nuke cache keys still match (Views/CachedImage.swift:100-123). Part 2: the grid owns its ScrollView, so the header slot, pull-to-refresh and the category-jump button (disabled or hidden for one group) must be re-homed; the M3UGroupShelfRow Equatable path is untouched. Capping shelves would change queue expectations only if the queue were taken from the capped slice; it must keep coming from the full group (queueForChannel, 279-283).

**How to verify:** Two M3U fixtures on the simulator: one ungrouped with about 500 channels (screenshot before/after; with part 2 expect a grid with Continue Watching above it, also while searching), one with a single 100k group (Time Profiler or signpost around the shelf row body: expect the 10-40 ms array copy to disappear with part 1; Allocations should no longer show the transient n x 224 B buffer).

## m3u-browse-8 — The favourite entry in the M3U card context menu shows the state from the last render: after 'Add to Favourites' the next long-press still says 'Add', and tapping it removes the favourite

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels, M3U group detail
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:170-180`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:326-330`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:205-212`

**What the user perceives:** Long-press a channel, choose 'Add to Favourites', long-press the same card again: the menu still offers 'Add to Favourites'. Choosing it now removes the favourite. The label only corrects itself after the card has been scrolled off screen and back.

**Mechanism (finder):** The comment at M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450 assumes the menu closure is rebuilt each time the menu opens. It is not: `contextMenu(menuItems:)` takes a non-escaping `() -> MenuItems` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `nonisolated public func contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems)`), so `let isFavorite = M3UFavoriteStore.shared.isFavorite(...)` (451) is evaluated when the card body runs. The card deliberately does not observe the favourite store, and its parent row is `.equatable()` on (playlist, group, items) (326-330), so nothing re-runs the card body after the toggle. The same eager evaluation runs `M3UParser.sanitizedURL` and `M3UStreamClassifier.classify` (460-461) for every card that scrolls into view, although they are only needed when a menu opens.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Move the menu content into its own view; a view's body inside a context menu is resolved when the menu is built, which is what M3UDownloadMenuItems already relies on (DownloadButton.swift:207-210).

.contextMenu { M3UChannelMenu(channel: channel) }

private struct M3UChannelMenu: View {
  let channel: DBM3UChannel
  var body: some View {
    // Read, not observed: resolved when the menu is built; cards keep zero store subscriptions.
    let isFavorite = M3UFavoriteStore.shared.isFavorite(channelId: channel.id)
    Button { Task { await M3UFavoriteStore.shared.toggle(channel: channel) } } label: {
      Label(isFavorite ? L("favorites.remove") : L("favorites.add"), systemImage: isFavorite ? "star.slash" : "star")
    }
    if let url = M3UParser.sanitizedURL(from: channel.url) { ...existing download branch... }
  }
}

No @ObservedObject in the wrapper, so the earlier fix against thousands of re-rendering cards stays intact whichever way SwiftUI schedules the body. If the simulator shows the body is still resolved with the card, fall back to a card-local `@State private var favoriteOverride: Bool?` set in the button action.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0 (menuItems is a non-escaping closure))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:408-477, 320-330, Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift and Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:205-281. The defect is certain from the code: `contextMenu(menuItems:)` takes a non-escaping builder, so the closure at 446-475 runs inside the card's body and `let isFavorite = M3UFavoriteStore.shared.isFavorite(...)` (451) plus the Label built from it are baked into the card's view value. The card has no dependency on the favourite store (deliberately, comment 447-450 from 0ab5bcd), and the parent row is equatable on (playlist, group, items), so a toggle does not re-run the card body. `toggle(channel:)` is a real toggle against the DB (M3UFavoriteStore.swift:42-66), so pressing the stale 'Add' removes the favourite. The comment's assumption ('menu is rebuilt on every open') is wrong for the inline closure. One nuance the finding misses: the card reads `@Environment(\.epgSnapshot)` (415), which EPGStore republishes about once a minute when a guide is configured (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:10-13), so with EPG the label heals within a minute; without EPG it stays stale until the card is recreated. Also stale in the other direction: a favourite toggled from the player (M3UChannelsView.swift:714-717) or removed in M3UFavoritesView is not reflected either. The secondary point (sanitizedURL + classify at 460-461 run for every card body) is true but cheap. Fix: the wrapper view is the right direction and matches what M3UDownloadMenuItems already assumes (its comment at DownloadButton.swift:207-210 claims evaluation only when the menu opens, while holding @ObservedObject + @Query), but the proposed version reads the store without observing it. That is only correct if SwiftUI re-resolves the wrapper's body on every presentation; if the menu content's attributes stay in the graph after the first open, the body is cached (its input, `channel`, has not changed) and the label is stale again from the second open. This cannot be settled from the SDK interface. The proposed fallback (`favoriteOverride` set in the button action) misses toggles made elsewhere and is wrong if the DB write fails.

**Corrected claim:** The favourite item in the M3U card context menu is built when the card body runs, not when the menu opens, because contextMenu's builder is non-escaping and the card intentionally does not observe the favourite store. After adding or removing a favourite (from the menu, the player or the favourites screen) the next long-press shows the old label and icon, and since the action is a toggle, choosing the stale 'Add to Favourites' removes the favourite. The label only refreshes when the card body re-runs (EPG snapshot tick about once a minute if a guide is configured, or the card being recreated).

**Corrected fix:** Move the menu content into `private struct M3UChannelMenu: View { let channel: DBM3UChannel; @ObservedObject private var favorites = M3UFavoriteStore.shared; var body ... }` and use `.contextMenu { M3UChannelMenu(channel: channel) }`. Observing inside the wrapper (the same shape as M3UDownloadMenuItems) makes the label correct regardless of whether SwiftUI rebuilds or caches menu content between presentations, and keeps the card itself free of store dependencies; the URL sanitizing and classification move into the wrapper body with it. Update the comment at 447-450. Then verify on the simulator that wrapper bodies are not evaluated for cards whose menu was never opened (counter or signpost in the wrapper body while toggling a favourite with a few hundred cards alive). If they are evaluated eagerly, replace the observation with card-local `@State private var isFavorite` fed by `.onReceive(M3UFavoriteStore.shared.$favoriteIds.map { $0.contains(channel.id) }.removeDuplicates())`, which re-renders only the card whose state changed.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `@available(iOS 13.0, macOS 10.15, tvOS 14.0, *) extension View { nonisolated public func contextMenu<MenuItems>(@ViewBuilder menuItems: () -> MenuItems) -> some View where MenuItems : View }` - the builder is non-escaping, confirming eager evaluation. Fallback API: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface `@available(iOS 13.0, ...) @inlinable nonisolated public func onReceive<P>(_ publisher: P, perform action: @escaping (P.Output) -> Void) -> some View where P : Publisher, P.Failure == Never`. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** The earlier fix (0ab5bcd) removed store observation from the card because one toggle re-rendered thousands of cards; the wrapper keeps that as long as SwiftUI instantiates menu content lazily, which is why the body-count check is part of the fix. M3UDownloadMenuItems (owner's download code, not the tip-jar WIP) stays nested unchanged. M3UChannelCard is shared by the shelf, the group grid and M3UFavoritesView, so all three get the change at once.

**How to verify:** UI test with an M3U fixture: long-press the first card, tap 'Add to Favourites', long-press the same card again and assert 'Remove from Favourites' exists; repeat twice more to cover the second and third presentation, and once after toggling the favourite from the player. Add a temporary counter in the wrapper body and confirm that toggling one favourite with a full screen of cards evaluates only the wrapper(s) whose menu has been opened.

## m3u-browse-9 — M3U has no sort or filter menu and no flat 'All Channels' view; Xtream Live got both

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels, M3U group detail
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:64-94`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:493-515`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:118-127`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:634-674`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:688-753`, `Models/LiveSortOption.swift:14-70`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should M3U get the same sort/filter menu and an All Channels grid as Xtream Live? Recommended yes; the work is small once the grid is shared.

**What the user perceives:** In an Xtream category the toolbar has a sort/filter menu (Default, Name A-Z, Name Z-A, Has EPG; iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png) and the Live tab has an All Channels grid (iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png). In an M3U group the toolbar is empty and the order is whatever the file had; there is no way to see all channels in one grid.

**Mechanism (finder):** 654cefc added LiveSortOption / LiveStreamFilter and AllLiveView and wired them into LiveCategoryContent only (LiveStreamsView.swift:543-545, 624-628, 634-674, 688-753). LiveSortOption.apply and LiveStreamFilter.apply are typed to [LiveStreamWithCategory] (LiveSortOption.swift:41-70), so M3UGroupGridContent could not reuse them, and the M3U toolbar (M3UChannelsView.swift:64-94) has guide, favourites and category jump but no All button.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Comes almost for free once the grid is shared (first finding). Make the sort generic and add the M3U pieces:

// LiveSortOption.swift
func apply<T>(to items: [T], name: KeyPath<T, String>) -> [T]

- M3U grid: same Menu + Picker as LiveStreamsView.swift:634-674 with Default / Name A-Z / Name Z-A and one filter 'Has EPG' (`!(channel.tvgId ?? "").isEmpty`). Leave catch-up out: M3U catch-up playback is deferred (DBModels.swift:155-156). Sorting stays off-main like LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577.
- `M3UAllChannelsView`: the same grid over `store.channels` minus hidden groups, reached from a `square.grid.2x2` toolbar item like LiveStreamsView.swift:118-127, reusing the existing `browse.all_live` string.
The sort choice can share `LiveSortOption.storageKey` so both variants remember one preference.

**APIs:** Menu (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Facts check out. The M3U toolbar (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:64-94) has guide, favourites and category jump only; M3UGroupDetailView (481-515) has no toolbar item and M3UGroupGridContent (542-595) shows file order. Xtream Live has the All Channels entry (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:118-127), the sort/filter menu (634-674, visible in shots/iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png: Default, Name A-Z, Name Z-A, Catch-up available, Has EPG) and AllLiveView (688-753). LiveSortOption.apply and LiveStreamFilter.apply are typed to [LiveStreamWithCategory] (Models/LiveSortOption.swift:40-69). 654cefc touched M3UChannelsView only for the onChange line and nonisolated annotations (git show), and no comment says M3U was left out on purpose, so this is an omission rather than a decision. `browse.all_live` is 'All Channels' / 'Tüm Kanallar' / 'Alle Sender', so it fits M3U. DBModels.swift:155-156 confirms M3U catch-up playback is deferred. Caveats that do not change the verdict: this is feature parity, not a fluidity defect, and it is the owner's call; the 'almost free' estimate depends on the shared paginated grid from another finding, because today's M3U grid is unpaginated (579) and an All Channels grid over 100k+ entries must not be built on it; an M3U 'all' list also contains films and episodes; the proposed 'Has EPG' test on tvgId mirrors the Xtream filter (epgChannelId only) although EPGChannelKey.forM3U also falls back to tvgName/name (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:32-34), so name-matched channels would be filtered out in both variants.

**Corrected claim:** M3U group screens have no sort or filter menu and the M3U tab has no flat All Channels grid, while Xtream Live has both since 654cefc; the sort and filter helpers are typed to the Xtream model, so the M3U grid could not reuse them. This is a parity gap and a product decision, not a performance defect.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with three conditions. (1) Do it after the M3U grid is paginated/shared; AllLiveView works because LiveCategoryContent pages at 90 items (LiveStreamsView.swift:548-551, 602-611). (2) Keep the existing `apply(to: [LiveStreamWithCategory])` as a thin wrapper over a generic `apply<T>(to items: [T], name: (T) -> String) -> [T]` (or a key path written literally inside the detached closure) so the Xtream call site at 572 is unchanged; run it off-main as at 567-577. (3) M3U menu: Default / Name A-Z / Name Z-A and 'Has EPG' only, no catch-up item. All Channels: `store.channels` minus hidden groups, behind a `square.grid.2x2` toolbar item with accessibility label `browse.all_live`, disabled while the store is empty. Sharing LiveSortOption.storageKey between variants is acceptable but should be stated to the owner.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `@available(iOS 14.0, macOS 11.0, tvOS 17.0, *) public struct Menu<Label, Content> : View`. Picker inside a Menu and @AppStorage with a RawRepresentable enum are already used at LiveStreamsView.swift:543 and 634-641. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Changing LiveSortOption.apply's signature would break LiveCategoryContent.recompute (572) unless the old overload is kept. localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare over 100k+ names takes on the order of a second, so it must stay in Task.detached and the grid must show the previous order until the result arrives. A fourth trailing toolbar item on the M3U root crowds a compact navigation bar (guide, favourites, jump already there). A shared storage key means changing the sort in one playlist type changes the other.

**How to verify:** Unit test: generic sort on [DBM3UChannel] for the three options and the tvgId filter. UI test on an M3U fixture: open a group, open the menu, pick Name (A-Z), assert the first card's label; open All Channels and assert hidden groups are excluded. With a 50k+ fixture confirm no main-thread stall when changing the sort (Time Profiler).

## m3u-browse-10 — Films and episodes in an M3U playlist are shown as live-channel tiles in a tab called Channels: square logo tile, TV placeholder, reserved EPG line, no progress

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort L · risk medium
- Screens: M3U dashboard, M3U Channels, M3U group detail, M3U favourites
- Code: `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:3-3`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:26-44`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:408-445`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:939-968`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:53-60`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: How far should M3U go towards the Xtream structure: (1) leave as is, (2) one Channels tab but poster-style cards and progress for VOD groups (recommended), or (3) separate Live / Movies / Series tabs derived from URL classification?

**What the user perceives:** An M3U export of a panel (m3u_plus) carries tens of thousands of films and episodes. They appear between the live groups as small square tiles with the poster letterboxed inside, a TV glyph when the poster is missing, and an empty line under the title where live channels show the current programme. The Xtream version of the same content has Movies and Series tabs, 2:3 posters and progress bars.

**Mechanism (finder):** M3UDashboardView has one content tab by design ('Canlı/Film/Dizi ayrımı yok', line 3). M3UChannelCard renders every entry the same way: `CachedImage(width: iconSize, height: iconSize, iconName: "tv")` with the default `.fit` content mode (M3UChannelsView.swift:422-429; CachedImage.swift:58-59) and `EPGNowNextLine(reserveSpace: true)` whenever a snapshot exists (439-442). The app already knows which entries are VOD (M3UStreamClassifier, 939-968) and uses that for the player and for the download menu, but not for browsing.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest step that makes VOD look like VOD without new tabs: classify once per group in the store's detached grouping pass (see the main-thread finding) and expose `vodGroups: Set<String>` (a group counts as VOD when all sampled entries classify as non-live). M3UChannelCard gets `style: .channel | .poster`; `.poster` uses `CachedImage(url:, width: posterMetrics.shelfPosterWidth, height: posterMetrics.shelfPosterHeight, contentMode: .fill, iconName: "film")`, left-aligned title, no EPG line, and a progress bar from one `WatchProgressMapRequest(playlistId:type: "vod")` held by the screen (the pattern FavoritesView.swift:15-16 uses). Shelf and grid pick the style per group; prefetch sizes follow the style so the Nuke cache key still matches (ListImagePrefetch.swift:16-21).
Larger alternative: split the M3U dashboard into Live / Movies / Series tabs from the same classification; series would need episode-name parsing and is a separate project.

**Verifier reasons:** The description of the rendering is accurate: M3UDashboardView has a single content tab by design (Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:3, 26-44); M3UChannelCard draws every entry with a square CachedImage, `iconName: "tv"` and the default `.fit` mode (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:422-429; Views/CachedImage.swift:58-59) and reserves the EPG line whenever a snapshot exists (439-442; reserved height 22 pt in Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:52); cards carry no progress. The classifier exists and is used only for playback and the download menu (460-461, 667-668, 939-968). The fix ingredients exist: PosterMetrics.shelfPosterWidth/Height (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:16-17), CachedImage's contentMode parameter, WatchProgressMapRequest(playlistId:type:) (Models/Requests.swift:438-441) used as described in Views/FavoritesView.swift:15-16 and 24, and M3U VOD history is written with type 'vod' and streamId = channel.id (M3UChannelsView.swift:689-690). What needs correcting: (1) Frequency. The headline scenario, an m3u_plus export of a panel, is mostly intercepted on iOS: get.php links are detected and added as an Xtream playlist when the panel answers the API (Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:263-269, Networking/XtreamLinkDetector.swift), so the user gets the Movies and Series tabs. The M3U path with large VOD sets remains for panels that block player_api, local files, non-panel lists and playlists added before auto-detection. (2) The single Channels tab is a stated design choice, so this is a product decision, not a defect. (3) Fix gaps: M3UFavoritesView and search results have no single group to pick a style from (favourites mixes live and VOD in one adaptive grid sized for square tiles); the shelf row's Equatable (326-330) must include the style and must not take the progress map as a compared input, or every progress save re-renders all rows (Xtream reads the map inside the grid content, Views/VODView.swift:608, 632, 701, not in the equatable shelf rows); classifying 'all sampled entries' needs a defined sample and a rule for mixed groups; tvg-logo on non-panel lists is often not 2:3 art, so `.fill` will crop. No M3U screenshot exists (shots/README.txt: demo data is Xtream only), so the visual was not checked.

**Corrected claim:** In playlists that stay on the M3U path (panel blocks the Xtream API, local file, non-panel list), films and episodes are browsed as live-channel tiles inside the single Channels tab: square letterboxed artwork, TV placeholder, an empty reserved EPG line when a guide is loaded, and no watch progress on the cards. This follows from the deliberate one-tab M3U design; panel get.php links are already converted to Xtream playlists on add, which limits how many users see it.

**Corrected fix:** Owner decision first. If option 2 is chosen: compute `vodGroups: Set<String>` in the store's existing detached grouping pass from a bounded sample per group (for example first, middle and last 8 entries all non-live), publish it with the grouping; give M3UChannelCard a `style` (.channel / .poster) and add it to M3UGroupShelfRow's `==`; poster style uses CachedImage with posterMetrics.shelfPosterWidth/Height (grid: categoryGridPosterWidth/Height), `.fill`, `iconName: "film"`, no EPG line, and prefetch with the same size and content mode so cache keys match. Scope progress to the group grid only at first (one `@Query<WatchProgressMapRequest>` inside the grid content, as VODCategoryContent does), not to shelf rows. Decide the style per card (classifier on the single channel) in M3UFavoritesView and split that screen into two sections or keep square tiles there. A cheap interim step that needs no decision: skip the reserved EPG line and use a film placeholder for entries the classifier marks as VOD only if that is computed off the body path (for example from vodGroups), not per card body.

**API check:** No SwiftUI API beyond what the project already uses. Project API checked in source: CachedImage(url:width:height:cornerRadius:contentMode:iconName:loadProfile:) (Views/CachedImage.swift:53-60), PosterMetrics.shelfPosterWidth/shelfPosterHeight (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:16-17), WatchProgressMapRequest(playlistId:type:) (Models/Requests.swift:438-441), M3UStreamClassifier.classify(url:groupTitle:) nonisolated (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:955).

**Regression risks:** Mixed row heights and a new compared field in the Equatable shelf rows; passing a progress map into rows would undo the shelf-row equatable work; URL parsing for classification must stay off the main thread and bounded (310k entries would add about a second to the grouping pass if every entry were classified); prefetch requests must change size and content mode together with the card or the Nuke cache misses; non-poster logos get cropped by `.fill`; the player shell derives live/VOD per channel on its own and must stay consistent with the group-level style.

**How to verify:** Simulator screenshots with an M3U fixture that has one live group, one group of .mp4 entries with 2:3 art, one mixed group and one VOD group with square logos; check shelf, group grid, search results and favourites. Confirm that an add-by-URL of a get.php link still lands on the Xtream dashboard. Scroll a 20k-entry VOD group with Time Profiler to confirm no per-card classification on the main thread.

## m3u-browse-11 — M3U has no Search tab: the only search is the inline filter that returns results as one horizontal shelf per matching group

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: M3U dashboard, M3U Channels
- Code: `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:26-45`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:77-83`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:112-136`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:242-255`, `Views/SearchView.swift:144-166`, `Models/M3UContentStore.swift:95-99`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Add a Search tab to M3U playlists (recommended, matches Xtream), or keep search inline and switch its results to a flat list while a query is active?

**What the user perceives:** On an Xtream playlist the tab bar ends in the system search button and results come as a flat list with artwork, name and category (iphone-dark/Q03-search-results-mi.png). On an M3U playlist the tab bar has two items and no search button; searching 'bbc' in Channels gives a dozen group shelves with one to three cards each, so the user scans headers and swipes sideways per group to see the matches.

**Mechanism (finder):** M3UDashboardView declares two tabs (27-43); DashboardView adds `Tab(..., role: .search)` (77-83). The M3U inline search keeps the shelf structure by filtering each group's array (M3UChannelsView.swift:242-255). A flat search already exists in the store, `M3UContentStore.search(_:)` (95-99), but nothing calls it and it would scan on the main actor.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add the search tab to M3UDashboardView so both playlist kinds have the same tab-bar shape:

Tab(L("dashboard.search"), systemImage: "magnifyingglass", value: 2, role: .search) {
  NavigationStack { M3USearchView(playlist: playlist, searchText: $globalSearchText).navigationTitle(L("dashboard.search")) }
}

M3USearchView: `.searchable`, 250 ms debounce, a detached filter over `store.channels` minus hidden groups, relevance order (exact, prefix, then name; same rule as CatalogTextSearch.sortLiveByRelevance), and a plain `List` of rows (logo 44 pt, name, group as subtitle). Make `ResultRow` in SearchView.swift:310-325 internal and reuse it. Tap presents through the shared M3U presenter with the result list as queue. Empty state: `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` as SearchView.swift:241 does. Remove the unused main-actor `search(_:)` from the store. No iOS 26-only API: on iOS 18 the role renders as a regular trailing tab, on iOS 26 as the separate search button, exactly like the Xtream dashboard.

**APIs:** Tab(_:systemImage:value:role:content:) (iOS 18.0); TabRole.search (iOS 18.0); ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Verified in code: M3UDashboardView declares exactly two tabs (Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:27-43) while DashboardView adds Tab(..., role: .search) (Views/DashboardView.swift:77-83). The inline M3U filter keeps the shelf structure by filtering each group (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:242-255, rendered by M3UGroupShelfRow at 170-181). M3UContentStore.search(_:) (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:95-99) has no caller anywhere (grep) and would scan on the main actor. So the facts stand. Corrections: (a) The 'results as one shelf per group' shape is not an M3U lag: Xtream Live TV inline search does exactly the same (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:296-309), and the file header says the M3U screen deliberately mirrors that pattern (M3UChannelsView.swift:3). The only real parity gap is the missing flat global search. (b) For a single-catalog playlist an inline .searchable on the one content tab is itself a native pattern, so adding a tab is a product decision, not a defect fix. (c) Evidence is code-only for the M3U side: there is no M3U dashboard screenshot in any variant (only N01-add-m3u-form.png); Q03-search-results-mi.png shows the Xtream search only. (d) Fix details that do not match the code base: there is no 'shared M3U presenter' - present() is a private method duplicated in M3UChannelsView:264, M3UGroupDetailView:529 and M3UFavoritesView:83; ResultRow is `private struct` (Views/SearchView.swift:309) and needs to be moved/renamed, not just un-privated in place; CatalogTextSearch.sortLiveByRelevance (Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:41-54) is typed to LiveStreamWithCategory and re-normalises both names up to four times per comparison, so reusing that rule over tens of thousands of M3U hits would cost seconds even off-main; Xtream SearchView does not use relevance ordering at all (it sorts alphabetically, SearchView.swift:261-262). (e) At 310k channels (the size the store comments cite, M3UContentStore.swift:7) a two-character query can return tens of thousands of rows; the proposal has no cap, and M3UPlayerShell.init does queue.firstIndex on the main thread (M3UChannelsView.swift:641).

**Corrected claim:** M3U playlists have no flat search: the only search is the inline filter on Channels, which (like Xtream Live TV's inline search) returns one horizontal shelf per matching group. Xtream additionally has a Search tab with a flat result list; M3U has no equivalent. Whether M3U gets a Search tab or a flat inline result list is a product decision.

**Corrected fix:** Owner decision between two options. Option A (tab parity): add `Tab(L("dashboard.search"), systemImage: "magnifyingglass", value: 2, role: .search) { NavigationStack { M3USearchView(playlist:searchText:) } }` to M3UDashboardView plus `@State globalSearchText`. Option B (smaller): keep inline search and render a flat list while debouncedQuery is non-empty. Either way: filter off-main with CatalogTextSearch.matches over store.channels minus hidden groups (hiddenStore.hiddenIds(playlistId:type: M3UChannelsView.hiddenCategoryType)); compute the relevance rank once per hit (precomputed normalised key: exact / prefix / other, then name) instead of calling sortLiveByRelevance's comparator; cap the rendered rows (e.g. first 200 with a 'more results' row as SearchView does with prefix(4)); rows = logo 44 pt + name + group via a shared row view extracted from SearchView's private ResultRow into Views/Components; tap calls `playerOverlay.present { M3UPlayerShell(playlist:channel:queue:) }` directly (no shared presenter exists) with the capped result list as queue; empty state ContentUnavailableView.search(text:). Delete the unused M3UContentStore.search(_:). iOS 18 fallback: none needed, role .search renders as a normal trailing tab on iOS 18 and as the separate search button on iOS 26, same as the Xtream dashboard.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `@available(iOS 18.0, macOS 15.0, tvOS 18.0, watchOS 11.0, visionOS 2.0, *) public struct Tab<Value, Content, Label>` (line 14326); `nonisolated public init<S>(_ title: S, systemImage: Swift.String, value: Value, role: SwiftUI.TabRole?, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where Label == DefaultTabLabel, S : StringProtocol` (line 14370, already used at DashboardView.swift:77); `@available(iOS 18.0, ...) public struct TabRole { public static var search: TabRole }` (line 13693-13694); `@available(iOS 17.0, ...) extension ContentUnavailableView where Label == SearchUnavailableContent.Label ... { public static func search(text: Swift.String) -> ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions> }` (line 17620-17625). All present, no iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** A third tab changes the M3U tab bar shape and adds a second search entry point next to the inline one (the same redundancy Xtream has). Unbounded result lists or comparator-side normalisation would reintroduce main-thread or multi-second work the earlier off-main filtering avoided. Moving ResultRow must not change the Xtream search rows. Passing a very large queue to M3UPlayerShell runs firstIndex on the main thread at tap time.

**How to verify:** UI test on an M3U fixture: open search, type two characters, assert a flat result row exists and tapping it presents the player. On a 300k-channel fixture measure with Instruments (Time Profiler + Hangs) that typing produces no main-thread hang and that the detached filter+rank completes in an acceptable time; screenshot the M3U tab bar on iOS 18 and iOS 26 next to the Xtream one.

## m3u-browse-12 — M3U error and empty states lag behind Xtream: a failed load leaves 'No channels' with no retry, 'Try Again' after a failed pull-to-refresh only re-reads the database, and favourites flash 'No favourites' before they appear

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels, M3U favourites, M3U dashboard alert
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:32-63`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:205-224`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:285-292`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:91-108`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:25-39`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:66-81`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:65-88`, `Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:1-34`

**What the user perceives:** (1) Pull to refresh with the network down: an alert titled 'Loading error' offers Try Again; tapping it closes the alert and nothing was retried. (2) If the catalog fails to load, dismissing the alert leaves a tv.slash 'No channels' screen that cannot be pulled or retried. (3) On a large playlist, opening Favourites shows the 'No favourites yet' placeholder for a few frames, then the grid. (4) Hiding every group shows a magnifying glass and 'No results'. (5) A Continue Watching card whose channel disappeared in a refresh does nothing when tapped.

**Mechanism (finder):** (1) refreshCatalog reports through `store.loadError` (M3UChannelsView.swift:220-223) and the dashboard alert's Try Again calls `store.loadPlaylist(playlist)` (M3UDashboardView.swift:102-105), which is the database read, not the download. (2) The body never consults `loadError` and the empty branches are plain VStacks outside a ScrollView (33-59); Xtream shows CatalogLoadErrorView with a retry (LiveStreamsView.swift:75-78), added because users were stranded exactly this way (CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:3-6). (3) `favoriteChannels` starts empty and is filled by a detached scan of the full catalog (M3UFavoritesView.swift:66-81), so the first branch (27-32) renders until the scan returns. (4) `visibleShelfGroups.isEmpty` is used both for 'no search hits' and 'everything hidden' (50-59). (5) presentHistoryItem returns silently (287-291) although its doc comment promises an alert (285).

**Proposed fix (finder):** - Give the store a refresh entry point (see the sharing finding) that keeps `refreshError` separate from `loadError`; the alert's Try Again repeats whichever operation failed.
- M3UChannelsView body: `if store.activePlaylistId != playlist.id || (store.isLoading && store.channels.isEmpty) { loading } else if let e = store.loadError, store.channels.isEmpty { CatalogLoadErrorView(message: e) { Task { await store.loadPlaylist(playlist) } } } else if store.channels.isEmpty { empty } else if isSearching && groups.isEmpty { ContentUnavailableView.search(text: debouncedQuery) } else if groups.isEmpty { all-hidden message with a button that opens the category picker } else { shelvesList }`.
- M3UFavoritesView: `@State private var hasLoaded = false`, set at the end of recompute(); render `Color.clear` until then.
- presentHistoryItem: when the channel is gone, show a short alert and delete the stale history row so the card disappears.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) (iOS 17.0); ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Sub-claim by sub-claim, from the code. (1) Confirmed mechanism: refreshCatalog writes store.loadError (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:220-223); the dashboard alert's Try Again calls store.loadPlaylist (Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:102-105), which only reads the database (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:57-58, 115-121). But this is not M3U lagging behind Xtream: Xtream has the identical defect - refreshFromNetwork(only:) sets loadError (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:210-219) and its alert also calls loadPlaylist (Views/DashboardView.swift:149-152), which skips the network when data exists (PlaylistContentStore.swift:115-116). (2) Mostly wrong as stated: an M3U 'catalog load' is a local GRDB read, not a download, so loadError with empty channels is practically unreachable; CatalogLoadErrorView exists for Xtream's network bootstrap (Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:3-6). What is real next to it: M3UChannelsView has no `activePlaylistId != playlist.id` guard (lines 33/41), so the first frame, rendered before the dashboard .task sets isLoading (M3UDashboardView.swift:85-87), shows the tv.slash 'No channel found' state during the slide-in; LiveStreamsView guards this at line 66. And a genuinely empty playlist cannot be pulled because the empty branches are plain VStacks (41-49) - same on Xtream (LiveStreamsView.swift:80-87). (3) Confirmed by code: favoriteChannels starts [] and is filled only after .task(id:) plus a detached scan (Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:17, 27-32, 59, 66-81), so the 'No favourites' ContentUnavailableView is always the first frame; how visible it is needs a device. (4) Confirmed: visibleShelfGroups.isEmpty serves both 'no hits' and 'all hidden' (26-29, 50-59); the picker button stays enabled (91), so it is recoverable. (5) Confirmed that the tap is dead and that the doc comment (285) contradicts the body; the inline comment (288-289) shows the silence is deliberate, but its premise is false: M3UImporter.replace never touches watchHistory (Models/M3UImporter.swift:31-33), so the dead card never goes away. The proposed auto-delete is unsafe: store.channels is the adult-filtered set (M3UContentStore.swift:60), so a card whose channel is merely filtered (or temporarily missing from the provider) would have its history destroyed on tap. The new alert/all-hidden texts also need new keys in ten Localizable.strings files, which carry the owner's uncommitted tip keys (additive only, but touches_user_wip is not 'false').

**Corrected claim:** M3U error/empty states have five small gaps: (1) Try Again after a failed pull-to-refresh only re-reads the database (same defect exists on Xtream); (2) the first frame of M3U Channels shows 'No channel found' before the loading state because the view lacks the activePlaylistId guard Xtream has, and an empty playlist cannot be pulled to refresh (a failed catalog load itself is a local DB read and practically unreachable); (3) M3U Favourites always renders 'No favourites yet' for the first frame(s) before the detached scan returns; (4) 'everything hidden' shows the search 'No results' state; (5) a Continue Watching card whose channel is gone or adult-filtered does nothing when tapped and never disappears.

**Corrected fix:** (1) Keep the refresh failure out of store.loadError: hold `@State refreshError` in M3UChannelsView (or a store-level refreshError once a shared store.refreshFromSource exists) and show an alert whose Try Again calls refreshCatalog() again; apply the same correction to Xtream separately. (2) First branch becomes `if store.activePlaylistId != playlist.id || (store.isLoading && store.channels.isEmpty) { loading }`; CatalogLoadErrorView for `loadError != nil && channels.isEmpty` is harmless parity but low value; optionally wrap the empty state in a ScrollView so .refreshable works. (3) `@State private var hasLoaded = false`, set at the end of recompute(); render Color.clear until then (or show the empty state immediately only when favorites.favoriteIds.isEmpty). (4) Split the branch: `!debouncedQuery.isEmpty && groups.isEmpty` -> ContentUnavailableView.search(text: debouncedQuery); otherwise an all-hidden ContentUnavailableView with an action that sets showingCategoryPicker = true. (5) Show a short alert ('no longer in this playlist') and fix the comment; do NOT delete the history row automatically - at most offer a destructive 'Remove' button in the alert (owner decision). New strings go into all ten Localizable.strings files additively, leaving the tip keys untouched.

**API check:** `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *) public struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions> : View` with `public init(@ViewBuilder label: () -> Label, @ViewBuilder description: () -> Description = { EmptyView() }, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions = { EmptyView() })` (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576) and `public static func search(text: Swift.String)` (17625, iOS 17.0). CatalogLoadErrorView(message:onRetry:) is the app's own view (Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:7-9). No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Changing the loading condition must keep shelves visible during reloadIfActive (channels non-empty). Gating the favourites body on hasLoaded must not blank the grid on later recomputes (set once, never reset). Separating refreshError must not suppress the existing alert for reloadIfActive DB errors. Auto-deleting history rows would lose user data for adult-filtered or temporarily missing channels. New string keys touch Localizable.strings that contain the owner's uncommitted tip keys.

**How to verify:** UI test with an M3U fixture whose URL is unreachable (stub URLProtocol): pull to refresh, tap Try Again, assert a second request. Screen-record the playlist-list -> M3U dashboard transition at 120 fps and step frames to confirm the tv.slash frame is gone. For the favourites flash, push Favourites on a device with a >=100k-channel playlist and at least one favourite, record and step frames. Screenshot the all-hidden and no-result states. Tap a Continue Watching card after removing its channel from the fixture and re-importing.

## m3u-browse-13 — The M3U screens are forks of the Xtream ones and have already drifted; four small extractions would stop it

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: M3U dashboard, M3U Channels, M3U group detail, M3U favourites, M3U Settings
- Code: `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:52-82`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:92-123`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:408-445`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:205-224`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:321-344`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:284-302`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:83-158`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:88-167`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:61-63`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:57-59`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Which side wins where the two differ today: shelf count badge, Favourites title style and tab-bar visibility, Continue Watching during search, refresh error presentation?

**What the user perceives:** Small inconsistencies between the two playlist kinds that add up to 'this is a different app': M3U shelf headers show a count and Xtream ones do not; M3U Favourites has an inline title and hides the tab bar while Xtream Favourites has a large title and keeps it; Continue Watching disappears during an M3U search but stays during an Xtream one; a failed refresh is an alert in M3U Settings and an inline red row in Xtream Settings; long-press gives a menu on M3U cards and starts playback on Xtream cards (shots/README.txt: 'there is no context menu').

**Mechanism (finder):** Copy-paste pairs that are edited one at a time. (a) The overlay host block is verbatim in both dashboards, including the identity-sensitive modifiers (M3UDashboardView.swift:52-82 vs DashboardView.swift:92-123). (b) The card label of LiveStreamCard and M3UChannelCard is identical apart from the model type (LiveStreamsView.swift:433-457 vs M3UChannelsView.swift:421-445); the shelf row and grid differ only where one side received a fix (pagination, Equatable, sort on Xtream; context menu on M3U). (c) The M3U download > parse > replace > reload pipeline exists three times (M3UChannelsView.swift:205-224, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:321-344, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:284-302), which is also why a pull to refresh and the Settings refresh can run concurrently. (d) The Downloads and Player sections of the two settings forms are the same ~75 lines (M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:83-158 vs PlaylistSettingsView.swift:88-167).

**Proposed fix (finder):** In order of value per line changed:
1. `ChannelTile(name:logoURL:epgKey:width:iconSize:profile:)` in Views/Components, used as the label of both cards; then `PagedChannelGrid<Item, Card>` generalised from LiveCategoryContent (first finding). The M3U context menu moves with the tile and Xtream gains it.
2. `M3UContentStore.refreshFromSource(playlist:progress:)` owning the pipeline plus an `isRefreshing` flag that de-duplicates concurrent callers; the three call sites become one line each.
3. `PlayerOverlayHost<Content: View>` (or a `.playerOverlayHost(_:)` modifier) wrapping the TabView with the existing ZStack, environment keys, keyboard rule and animation unchanged; both dashboards use it, so the next overlay fix lands once. Keep the unconditional structure the comments require.
4. `SettingsDownloadsSection(playlist:)` and `SettingsPlayerSection()` views used by both forms. Leave the About section, and with it the `TipJarRow()` line, exactly where it is in both files.

**Verifier reasons:** All listed drifts are real in the code: count badge only on M3U shelves (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:350-353 vs Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:368-369); M3U Favourites inline title + hidden tab bar (Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:62-63) vs Xtream large title, tab bar kept (Views/FavoritesView.swift:56-58); Continue Watching hidden while searching in M3U (M3UChannelsView.swift:156) but unconditional in Xtream (LiveStreamsView.swift:213); refresh error as alert in M3U Settings (Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:257-261, 340-343) vs inline red row with retry in Xtream (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:75-85); context menu only on M3UChannelCard (M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475), none on LiveStreamCard (LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457; shots/README.txt confirms long press plays). The duplications are also real: overlay host block (M3UDashboardView.swift:52-82 vs DashboardView.swift:92-123), card label (421-443 vs 433-455), Downloads/Player settings sections (M3U 83-158 vs Xtream 88-167), and three download>parse>replace call sites (M3UChannelsView.swift:211-219, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:328-339, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:284-302). What does not stand is the fix as a response to this request. By its own verification plan steps 1, 3 and 4 are pixel-identical, i.e. they change nothing the owner would feel; it is L effort / medium risk for maintainability, against rule 6 (smallest change). Step 3 restructures the player hand-off host that was reworked last week (commit 2ec2c18 touched M3UDashboardView.swift; the comments at 65-67 and 74-77 warn that structural changes remount PlayerView) for zero visible gain. Step 4 rewrites both settings files that carry uncommitted owner work. Step 1 is inaccurate: the context menu is attached to the Button outside the label and its contents are M3U-specific (M3UFavoriteStore, M3UDownloadMenuItems), so it cannot 'move with the tile'; Xtream gaining a live-card context menu is a new feature that needs the Xtream favourites path, not a by-product. The three pipelines are not identical either (Add builds a new Playlist, passes clearServerURL and drives progress messages; Settings drives syncMessage; pull-to-refresh has none). The concurrency remark is true (isSyncing is view-local @State, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:14) but M3UImporter.replace is one write transaction, so the cost is duplicate work, not corruption.

**Corrected claim:** The M3U and Xtream screens differ in five user-visible ways (shelf count badge, Favourites title style and tab-bar visibility, Continue Watching during search, refresh error presentation, live-card context menu) because they are copy-paste forks. The inconsistencies are the user-facing issue; the duplication is a maintainability concern that does not affect native feel by itself.

**Corrected fix:** Treat the five differences as individual owner decisions and align each with a small direct edit (each S): pick count badge on/off for both; pick one Favourites chrome; keep or hide Continue Watching during search on both; use the inline error row with retry in M3U Settings; add a context menu to LiveStreamCard as a separate feature if wanted. Of the extractions keep only (2) `M3UContentStore.refreshFromSource(playlist:progress:)` with an isRefreshing guard, used by pull-to-refresh and Settings (the Add flow can call it too but keeps its own playlist construction), because it also fixes the Try Again defect in m3u-browse-12. A shared ChannelTile label is optional and safe. Do not do (3) PlayerOverlayHost and (4) shared settings sections as part of this work; defer them until the player rework and the tip-jar work have landed.

**API check:** No SDK API involved; nothing to verify. All referenced types are the app's own.

**Regression risks:** Original step 3: any change to the structural position of item.root or its modifiers remounts PlayerView and tears down playback/AirPlay (comments at M3UDashboardView.swift:65-67, 74-77), touching work finished last week. Original step 4: edits around the uncommitted TipJarRow() lines in both settings forms. Generalising grids/cards risks losing the deliberate Equatable shelf rows and pagination on the Xtream side. The corrected fix only risks the usual per-screen regressions and, for refreshFromSource, changing progress messaging in Settings.

**How to verify:** After each alignment edit: existing unit suite and UI tests green; screenshots of Live home, M3U Channels, both Favourites screens and both Settings forms side by side to confirm the chosen behaviour matches. For refreshFromSource: start a pull-to-refresh and the Settings refresh at the same time against a stubbed URLProtocol and assert a single download.
