## m3u-browse-14 — M3UDashboardView subscribes to the favourite store it never reads, so every favourite toggle re-evaluates the dashboard and the mounted player

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U dashboard, Mini player alongside M3U Channels
- Code: `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:8-11`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:52-64`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:85-90`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457`

**What the user perceives:** Nothing visible on its own; it is avoidable work on the main thread at the moment the user adds or removes a favourite while a stream is playing in the mini card, in an app whose player was just tuned for smoothness.

**Mechanism (finder):** `@ObservedObject private var favorites = M3UFavoriteStore.shared` (M3UDashboardView.swift:9) is used only for `favorites.track(playlistId:)` inside `.task` (86), but the wrapper subscribes the view to `favoriteIds`. Each change re-runs the dashboard body, which re-creates the closures passed through `.environment(\.playerOverlayDismiss / Minimize / Expand)` (58-64). Closures cannot be compared, so every reader of those keys, PlayerView first, is invalidated. The card-level comment (M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450) shows the team already removed this subscription from the cards for the same reason.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Delete line 9 and call the singleton directly:

.task(id: playlist.id) {
  M3UFavoriteStore.shared.track(playlistId: playlist.id)
  await store.loadPlaylist(playlist)
  ...
}

M3UPlayerShell and M3UFavoritesView keep their own subscriptions, which they need.

**Verifier reasons:** The subscription is real and unused in body: `@ObservedObject private var favorites = M3UFavoriteStore.shared` (Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:9) is referenced only at line 86 inside .task; M3UFavoriteStore publishes favoriteIds (Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:11), so each toggle re-runs the dashboard body and re-creates the three environment closures (58-64), which PlayerViewImpl reads (Views/PlayerView.swift:218-222, hand-off only). The fix is safe: the store is a @MainActor singleton, .task inherits the main actor, and nothing else in the dashboard needs the wrapper. What does not stand is the claimed benefit. When a player is mounted, M3UPlayerShell observes the same store (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:626) and rebuilds PlayerView with fresh closures on every change (697-717: onPreviousChannel, onSelectChannelPanelItem, onToggleFavorite ...); PlayerView is not Equatable (PlayerView.swift:58), so the player body is re-evaluated in the same transaction regardless of the dashboard. When no player is mounted there is no reader of those keys. The dashboard's children do not re-run either: M3UChannelsView(playlist:) and M3UPlaylistSettingsView(playlist:onDismiss:) receive unchanged inputs (Playlist is Equatable, onDismiss is the same stored closure). So removing line 9 saves one evaluation of M3UDashboardView.body and the TabView diff per favourite toggle (a single user-initiated event) - not measurable, as the finding itself concedes ('nothing visible').

**Corrected claim:** M3UDashboardView holds an unnecessary @ObservedObject on M3UFavoriteStore; each favourite toggle re-evaluates the dashboard body once. The mounted player is re-evaluated on a toggle in any case because M3UPlayerShell observes the same store, so removing the dashboard subscription is a harmless cleanup with no perceptible effect.

**Corrected fix:** Optional cleanup, as proposed: delete Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:9 and call `M3UFavoriteStore.shared.track(playlistId: playlist.id)` inside the existing `.task(id: playlist.id)`. Do not expect a fluidity gain; do not touch M3UPlayerShell's or M3UFavoritesView's subscriptions.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. `.task(id:)` is already used at the same place; M3UFavoriteStore.track(playlistId:) is the app's own @MainActor method (Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:18).

**Regression risks:** None of substance: track() is still called at the same moment, the singleton keeps its own GRDB observation alive, and favourites still update through M3UPlayerShell and M3UFavoritesView. Does not touch the overlay host structure.

**How to verify:** Temporarily add `let _ = Self._printChanges()` to M3UDashboardView.body and to M3UPlayerShell.body; toggle a favourite from a card context menu with the mini player showing. Before: both print. After: the dashboard no longer prints, M3UPlayerShell still does (confirming the player-side re-evaluation is unchanged). Confirm the star in the player and the favourites grid still update.

## states-loading-empty-error-1 — On launch the selected tab shows the empty state "No category found." between the spinner and the shelves, for as long as the stream rows take to load

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:65-88, 105-107`, `Views/VODView.swift:38-61, 157-159`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:39-62, 158-160`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:127-152`

**What the user perceives:** Cold start into a playlist: a spinner with "Preparing channels..." for a few milliseconds, then an icon with "No category found." as if the playlist were empty, then every shelf pops in at once. With the demo catalog the middle state is about one frame. With 100k+ rows it lasts as long as phase 2 of the load; I estimate a second or more, but this is not measured.

**Mechanism (finder):** The shelves are drawn from @State copies (displayCategories / displayItemsByCategory) that are refreshed only by `.task(id: debouncedQuery)`, `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` and `.task(id: hiddenIds)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107). All three run once on appear, before any category exists. loadPlaylist then publishes the categories and sets `streamsLoaded = false; isLoading = false` (PlaylistContentStore.swift:132-137). streamsLoaded was already false, so no task id changes and recomputeFilter does not run. The body then sees displayCategories empty, isLoading false, the playlist active and no loadError, and falls into the final else branch (LiveStreamsView.swift:79-87; VODView.swift:52-60; SeriesView.swift:53-61), which is the real empty state. Recompute runs only when streamsLoaded flips to true at PlaylistContentStore.swift:152. The same code was already present before 0ab5bcd (old LiveStreamsView lines 86-88). Side effect: the `isStreamsLoading` spacer branch in the shelf rows (LiveStreamsView.swift:373-374) is never reached on the launch tab. It is only reached when another tab is opened for the first time during phase 2.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give the store one change signal and key the recomputes on it instead of on streamsLoaded.

```swift
// PlaylistContentStore
@Published private(set) var catalogRevision = 0
// bump with `catalogRevision &+= 1` after: line 137 (phase 1), line 152 (phase 2), both phases of reloadFromDatabase (294, 317),
// each case of reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only:), and clearLists().
// Do NOT bump in applyVODMetadata: that would bring back the re-render storm the Equatable rows avoid.

// LiveStreamsView:106, VODView:158, SeriesView:159 (and :509/:734, :575/:834, :547/:773, SearchView:248)
.task(id: contentStore.catalogRevision) { await recomputeFilter() }

// state switch: the real empty state only once the catalog is fully loaded
if contentStore.isLoading || playlist.id != contentStore.activePlaylistId
    || (!contentStore.streamsLoaded && contentStore.loadError == nil) { loadingView }
```
After this, phase 1 shows the shelf headers at once (with the skeleton from the skeleton finding) and phase 2 fills them. No iOS-version dependency.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read the code; the mechanism is exactly as described. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107 recompute only on debouncedQuery, contentStore.streamsLoaded and hiddenIds (same at Views/VODView.swift:157-159, Views/SeriesView.swift:157-159). Views/DashboardView.swift:131-132 starts loadPlaylist at the same appear, so the three tasks run once while liveCategories is still empty. Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:132-137 then publishes the categories, sets streamsLoaded = false (it already was false, so no task id changes) and isLoading = false. The body (LiveStreamsView.swift:65-88) now has displayCategories empty, isLoading false, the playlist active and loadError nil, so it falls into the final else: the tv.slash icon with live.empty.no_category. Nothing recomputes until streamsLoaded flips at PlaylistContentStore.swift:152. Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift reads UserDefaults synchronously, so the third task key cannot rescue it. This contradicts the owner's own intent: the comment at PlaylistContentStore.swift:137 says the UI should show the categories immediately, and the isStreamsLoading spacer at LiveStreamsView.swift:373-374 exists for that phase but is unreachable on the launch tab. The flash is certain from code (at least one frame). Its length equals phase 2 (three full-table reads plus Dictionary(grouping:), lines 140-144); with 100k+ rows that is plausibly several hundred ms to over a second, but this is not measured. Adjacent, not part of this finding: loadPlaylist (lines 146-151) never applies mergeUncategorized/appendingUncategorized, while both reload paths do, so orphan streams are missing on launch and appear after a refresh.

**Corrected claim:** On every cold entry into an Xtream playlist, the launch tab shows the real empty state ("No category found.") between the spinner and the shelves for the whole of phase 2 of loadPlaylist, because nothing re-runs recomputeFilter when the categories arrive. With the demo data this is about one frame; with real catalogs it lasts as long as the three stream reads (not measured, likely 0.3 s to more than 1 s). The phase-1 'headers first' state the store was designed for is never reached on the launch tab.

**Corrected fix:** The proposed fix stands. Add `@Published private(set) var catalogRevision = 0` to PlaylistContentStore (same pattern as HiddenCategoryStore.version) and bump it after phase 1 (line 137), after phase 2 (line 152), in both phases of reloadFromDatabase (295, 317), at the end of each case in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only:), and in clearLists(). Do not bump it in applyVODMetadata. Replace `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` with `.task(id: contentStore.catalogRevision)` at LiveStreamsView.swift:106/509/734, VODView.swift:158/575/834, SeriesView.swift:159/547/773 and SearchView.swift:248. Also add `|| (!contentStore.streamsLoaded && contentStore.loadError == nil)` to the spinner condition in the three roots: it covers the one frame between the phase-1 publish and the recompute. If only this finding were fixed (not finding 2), that one extra condition per root is already enough to remove the false empty state.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:) found at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166 inside the `@available(iOS 15.0, ...) extension View` block; the id needs only Equatable, so an Int works. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Each bump re-runs recomputeFilter. In VODView that includes the detached recently-added sort over the whole VOD list, so the number of bump sites must stay small (two per load, as today). When the arrays are replaced, the Equatable shelf rows compare `items == items` element by element once (LiveStreamsView.swift:347); this already happens on the Settings refresh path. A bump in applyVODMetadata would bring back the re-render storm described at VODView.swift:596-599. During phase 2 the shelves render as headers over Color.clear spacers, which looks bare until a skeleton exists.

**How to verify:** Add a DEBUG-only delay before phase 2 (PlaylistContentStore.swift:139), launch into a playlist and assert in a UI test that the static text for live.empty.no_category never exists and that shelf headers exist before the cards. On a device with a 100k+ catalog, record the screen at launch and measure how long the false empty state shows before the fix, and the time from first frame to headers and to cards after it.

## states-loading-empty-error-2 — Pull-to-refresh on the three tab roots downloads and stores the new catalog but the shelves keep showing the old one

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Search results
- Code: `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:207-220, 234-278`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:106, 242-249`, `Views/VODView.swift:95-99, 158`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:96-100, 159`, `Views/SearchView.swift:248`

**What the user perceives:** The user pulls, the spinner runs for the whole sync and ends, and nothing on screen changes. New channels or movies appear only after switching tabs and back, pushing and popping a screen, or typing a search. The category picker already lists the new categories, but tapping a new one scrolls nowhere because the shelf list does not contain it.

**Mechanism (finder):** The scoped refresh introduced in 1cce013 ends in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) (PlaylistContentStore.swift:234-278). It replaces liveCategories / liveStreams / liveStreamsByCategoryId but never touches `streamsLoaded`. The tab roots copy the catalog into @State and recompute only on `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:106; VODView.swift:158; SeriesView.swift:159), so their copies stay stale until the view re-appears and the tasks re-run. Before 1cce013 the pull called the full refreshFromNetwork(playlist:), whose reloadFromDatabase toggles streamsLoaded false then true (lines 295, 317); that hid the problem. pickerEntries reads the store directly (LiveStreamsView.swift:45-53), which is why the picker is fresh while the shelves are not. SearchResultsView has the same key (SearchView.swift:248).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use the `catalogRevision` signal from the previous finding and bump it at the end of each case in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:). Do not toggle streamsLoaded there: that would blank the shelves through the isStreamsLoading branch. With the revision key the shelves diff in place when the refresh spinner ends.

**APIs:** View.refreshable(action:) (iOS 15.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9264-9266))

**Verifier reasons:** The pull-to-refresh at Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:242-249, Views/VODView.swift:95-99 and Views/SeriesView.swift:96-100 calls refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only:), which ends in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:234-278). That function replaces the categories, the flat list and the by-category dictionary for one type and touches nothing else: streamsLoaded is not changed. The roots render from @State copies (displayCategories, displayItemsByCategory, recentlyAddedVODs) that are refreshed only by the three `.task(id:)` keys at LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, none of which changes, so the copies stay stale. pickerEntries reads the store directly (LiveStreamsView.swift:45-53), so the picker is fresh while the shelf list is not. SearchResultsView has the same key at Views/SearchView.swift:248. History: `git log -S` shows the scoped call arrived in 1cce013; the unscoped refreshFromNetwork(playlist:) (whose reloadFromDatabase toggles streamsLoaded at 295/317) no longer has any caller, and Settings uses reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:) (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:524), which is why only the pull is broken. No comment marks this as deliberate. A user only sees it when the panel content actually changed, which is the reason they pull.

**Corrected claim:** After a pull-to-refresh on Live TV, Movies or Series the new catalog is stored and loaded into the store, but the shelves, the recently-added row and open search results keep showing the old copy until the view's tasks run again (re-appear, a search, or hiding a category). The category picker and the 'All' button already see the new data.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: bump the catalogRevision from finding 1 at the end of each case in reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) and key the recompute tasks on it. Do not toggle streamsLoaded there. The unscoped refreshFromNetwork(playlist:) is dead code and can stay or go; it is not part of the fix.

**API check:** View.refreshable(action:) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9266 inside the `@available(iOS 15.0, ...)` extension at 9264-9265. View.task(id:priority:_:) at 5166, iOS 15.0. Nothing iOS 26-only.

**Regression risks:** When the refresh ends, every shelf row gets a new array and the Equatable rows do one full element comparison each; the VOD root re-sorts for the recently-added row off-main. Both are one-off costs at the end of a user-initiated refresh. The existing comment at LiveStreamsView.swift:243-246 (detached Task so the refreshable cancellation does not reach URLSession) must stay as it is.

**How to verify:** With a local mock panel or an editable fixture: load the playlist, add a category and a stream on the server side, pull on Live TV and assert that the new shelf header exists without leaving the tab. Repeat on Movies and check that the recently-added row changes. A store-level test after the store accepts an injected database: reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only: .live) must increase catalogRevision.

## states-loading-empty-error-3 — Movie and series detail pages hide everything behind a full-screen spinner until the metadata request returns, and a failed request replaces the whole page with red error text

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:73-82, 99-121, 143-146`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:866-876, 892-896, 941-956, 1006-1013, 1223`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-178`, `Models/Requests.swift:191-208`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a poster pushes a blank page with a centred "Loading movie info..." spinner. Title, poster and the play button appear only after get_vod_info / get_series_info answers, which on a slow panel can take up to the 20 s timeout. If the request fails, the page is only "Error" with red text such as "Server error: HTTP 404" and a Try Again button. Screenshot iphone-light/S03-series-detail-loading.png (identical to S04) shows this: no title, no poster, and a movie cannot be played even though its stream URL needs no metadata. In the TV app the artwork and title are there as the page slides in.

**Mechanism (finder):** `if isLoading && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded { ProgressView } else if let error { errorView } else { contentScroll }` (MovieDetailView.swift:74-81; SeriesView.swift:868-875). The passed-in row already has what the hero needs: name, poster and rating, and for series also plot and genre (PlaylistContentStore.swift:563-578). DetailHero has a fixed height and falls back to the blurred poster (DetailComponents.swift:26-32, 42-43). Playback needs only streamId and containerExtension (MovieDetailView.swift:143-146). The series page has a second problem: fetchSeriesInfo writes seasonsLoaded only to the database (SeriesView.swift:1223) and the in-memory catalog copy is never updated. Every revisit therefore starts with series.seasonsLoaded == false, and the `.task` at :892-896 races the asynchronous @Query (Requests.swift:204). The owner's own comment at PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-163 describes this exact symptom for movies (needless request plus spinner flash), where applyVODMetadata fixed it. Series has no equivalent. The existing `series.loading_seasons` text at SeriesView.swift:1009 cannot be reached while loading.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Always render contentScroll and move the three states into the part that depends on the request.

```swift
// SeriesDetailView.body
contentScroll   // hero, chips, plot from the list row, immediately

// seasonsSection, when seasons.isEmpty
if let error = errorMessage {
    ContentUnavailableView {
        Label(L("catalog.load_failed.title"), systemImage: "wifi.exclamationmark")
    } description: { Text(error) } actions: {
        Button(L("common.try_again")) { Task { await fetchSeriesInfo() } }
    }
} else if !currentSeries.seasonsLoaded {
    ProgressView(L("series.loading_seasons")).frame(maxWidth: .infinity).padding()
} else { Text(L("series.no_seasons_info")) }
// primary button: .disabled(seasons.isEmpty)
```
Movie: always show contentScroll. While `isLoading && !metadataLoaded`, reserve the genre-chip row and plot block with `.redacted(reason: .placeholder)` so the Watch button does not move when the metadata lands. On error keep the page usable and show at most a secondary-colour footnote row with a retry.

Series revisit: make SeriesByIDRequest deliver its first value synchronously (see the @Query finding), or add an applySeriesMetadata(_:) to the store that mirrors applyVODMetadata.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576)); View.redacted(reason:) with RedactionReasons.placeholder (iOS 14.0 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6086-6107))

**Verifier reasons:** The core claim holds. Views/MovieDetailView.swift:73-81 and Views/SeriesView.swift:867-875 replace the whole page with a spinner while the info request runs and with errorView (red text, lines 106-121 and 941-956) when it fails. Screenshot iphone-light/S03-series-detail-loading.png shows exactly that: no title, no poster, only 'Error / Server error: HTTP 404 / Try Again'; M07-movie-detail.png shows what the page looks like when it does render. The list row already carries what the hero needs (name, poster, rating; for series also plot and genre, Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:563-578), and movie playback needs only streamId and containerExtension (MovieDetailView.swift:143-146). Two things the finding missed or got wrong. (1) isLoading starts false and is set to true inside the `.task` (MovieDetailView.swift:99-103, 269), so the first frame of the push renders contentScroll, then the spinner replaces it, then the content returns: content, spinner, content. (2) The revisit problem is not limited to series. applyVODMetadata updates the store's arrays, but the screens pass rows from their own @State copies (VODView.swift:30, 556, 616), which are only refreshed by a recompute, so a movie reopened from the same screen still arrives with metadataLoaded == false. For both types the `.task` then races the @Query, whose publisher uses GRDB's default `.async(onQueue: .main)` scheduling (Models/Requests.swift:191-208, GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-488). If the task wins, the request is repeated, and a failure (for example offline) sets errorMessage, which replaces a page whose data is already in the database. Which side wins the race cannot be told from the code. The existing series.loading_seasons text at SeriesView.swift:1009 is indeed unreachable while loading.

**Corrected claim:** Movie and series detail pages show a full-screen spinner for the whole get_vod_info / get_series_info request and a full-screen red error when it fails, although title, poster, rating and (for movies) playback are available from the list row. The push shows content for one frame, then the spinner, then content again. On a revisit from the same screen both movies and series can repeat the request because the passed-in row is stale and the @Query value arrives asynchronously; when that repeated request fails, the error page hides data that is already cached.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the main proposal: always render contentScroll in both views. Series: put the three states inside seasonsSection when seasons is empty (error: ContentUnavailableView with a retry action; loading: ProgressView(L("series.loading_seasons")); otherwise series.no_seasons_info), keyed on isLoading and errorMessage. Add an `isPrimaryDisabled` parameter to DetailActionBar and pass `seasons.isEmpty && !hasResume`, rather than `.disabled` on the whole bar, which would also disable the trailer button. Movie: while loading, reserve the genre row and plot with `.redacted(reason: .placeholder)`; on error show a secondary footnote row with a retry and keep Watch and Download usable. For the revisit, replace both `.task` checks with a database read before deciding to fetch, the way Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:66-71 already does: `let fresh = try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in try DBSeries.filter(...).fetchOne(db) }; if fresh?.seasonsLoaded != true { await fetchSeriesInfo() }` (same for DBVODStream.metadataLoaded). This removes the race for movies and series without an applySeriesMetadata mirror (an O(n) search on the main thread plus a store publish) and without switching the @Query to `.immediate` scheduling.

**API check:** ContentUnavailableView: `@available(iOS 17.0, ...) public struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` with `init(@ViewBuilder label:description:actions:)` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576. View.redacted(reason:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6107, in an extension marked iOS 14.0 (6103). View.task(priority:_:) iOS 15.0 at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5160-5162. GRDB (not SDK): `publisher(in:scheduling:)` defaults to `.async(onQueue: .main)` at GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservation.swift:485-488. All fine for the iOS 18 target; no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** When the metadata lands, the genre row, year/runtime and the real backdrop appear, so the Watch button can move by one chip row unless the row height is reserved; if the movie has no genre the reserved row collapses instead. The hero switches from the blurred poster to the backdrop image. `.immediate` scheduling on the @Query would run a database read on the main thread during the push; AppDatabase holds `any DatabaseWriter` (Database/AppDatabase.swift:8), and with a DatabaseQueue that read would wait behind a running sync transaction, so avoid it. Do not bump a catalog revision from the detail fetch (see VODView.swift:596-599).

**How to verify:** UI test with the demo fixture, where series info returns 404 as in S03: open a series and assert the title and an inline retry exist together. Open a movie with metadataLoaded = false behind a throttled or failing endpoint and assert Watch Now exists before the request ends and stays after it fails. Revisit: open a series, go back, turn the network off, open it again from the same shelf; the seasons must still be shown. Log whether fetchSeriesInfo / fetchMovieInfo is called on that second open to settle which side wins the race today.

## states-loading-empty-error-4 — A catalog load error is reported twice, dismissing the alert removes the inline retry, and "Try Again" after a failed pull-to-refresh does not retry the refresh

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels, Dashboard alerts
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:138-155`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:91-108`, `Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:3-6`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:75-78`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-116, 195-220`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:41-49, 205-224`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: For a failed pull-to-refresh, keep a modal alert (the current pattern, acceptable for a user-initiated action) or use a non-modal note. This is the owner's call; the fix above keeps the alert.

**What the user perceives:** (a) First load fails: a modal "Loading error" alert sits on top of an inline "Content could not be loaded" view with the same message and the same retry. Tapping OK makes the inline view disappear too; what remains is "No category found." with no way to retry. (b) Pull-to-refresh fails while offline: an alert with OK and Try Again appears, and Try Again visibly does nothing. (c) M3U has no inline error view at all: after OK it shows "No channel found.".

**Mechanism (finder):** One field, contentStore.loadError, drives both surfaces. The alert is bound to it and both its OK button and its dismiss setter set it to nil (DashboardView.swift:144-148). The inline CatalogLoadErrorView is shown only `if let loadError = contentStore.loadError` (LiveStreamsView.swift:75; VODView.swift:48; SeriesView.swift:49). OK therefore removes it, which recreates the dead end the view's header comment says it was added to remove (CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:3-6). The refresh paths write the same field (PlaylistContentStore.swift:202, 217; M3UChannelsView.swift:222), but the alert's retry calls loadPlaylist (DashboardView.swift:151). When categories already exist that is only a local database reload (needsNetworkBootstrap, :115-116, :280-285), not the failed network sync. Separately, refreshFromNetwork writes loadError and loadingMessage without checking activePlaylistId or loadToken (:195-220), so a refresh that fails after a playlist switch alerts on the wrong playlist.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Split the two meanings.

```swift
// PlaylistContentStore
struct RefreshFailure: Equatable { let message: String; let scope: CatalogContentType? }
@Published var refreshError: RefreshFailure?   // set in the two refreshFromNetwork catch blocks, guarded by activePlaylistId
// loadError stays for loadPlaylist / reloadFromDatabase only

// DashboardView: bind the alert to refreshError only
Button(L("common.try_again")) {
    let scope = contentStore.refreshError?.scope; contentStore.refreshError = nil
    Task { if let scope { await contentStore.refreshFromNetwork(playlist: playlist, only: scope) }
           else { await contentStore.refreshFromNetwork(playlist: playlist) } }
}
```
Drop the alert for loadError: the inline CatalogLoadErrorView already owns that state, and the screen then keeps its retry. M3U: add a branch `else if store.channels.isEmpty, let e = store.loadError { CatalogLoadErrorView(message: e) { Task { await store.loadPlaylist(playlist) } } }` and move the refresh failure at M3UChannelsView.swift:222 to its own field whose retry calls refreshCatalog().

**APIs:** View.alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) (iOS 15.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10666))

**Verifier reasons:** All three symptoms follow from the code. (a) Views/DashboardView.swift:138-155 binds the alert to contentStore.loadError and both OK and the dismiss setter clear it; the inline CatalogLoadErrorView is shown only while that same field is set (LiveStreamsView.swift:75, VODView.swift:48, SeriesView.swift:49). So a failed first load shows the alert over the inline view, and OK removes the inline retry and leaves 'No category found.' with no scroll view to pull. That is the dead end the header comment at Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:3-6 says the view was added to remove. (b) Both refreshFromNetwork catch blocks write loadError (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:202, 217); the alert's Try Again calls loadPlaylist (DashboardView.swift:151), which with existing categories skips the network (needsNetworkBootstrap, 115-116, 280-285) and only reloads from the database. (c) Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:33-49 has no error branch, and the refresh failure at line 222 goes to the same alert, whose retry at Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:104 is a database reload. The missing activePlaylistId guard in refreshFromNetwork (195-220) is real but only matters when the playlist is switched during a refresh. The fix needs a correction: removing the alert for loadError entirely leaves some load failures with no surface at all.

**Corrected claim:** One field drives both the modal alert and the inline error view, so a failed first load is reported twice and tapping OK removes the inline retry. A failed pull-to-refresh uses the same field and alert, and its Try Again reloads from the local database instead of retrying the network sync. M3U has no inline error state. A refresh that fails after a playlist switch can alert on the wrong playlist (edge case).

**Corrected fix:** Split the two meanings as proposed: `refreshError` for failed refreshes (set in the refreshFromNetwork catch blocks behind `guard activePlaylistId == playlist.id`), loadError for loadPlaylist and the reload paths. Stop clearing loadError from the alert so the inline view keeps its retry. Correction: do not drop the loadError alert completely. The inline view exists only on the three content tabs and only while displayCategories is empty, so a phase-2 or reload failure with categories already shown, or a failure while Settings or Search is selected, would become silent. Keep an alert for loadError only when the store already has categories, or widen the inline condition to `loadError != nil && !streamsLoaded`. For the refresh alert, either retry the same scope as proposed (the retry runs outside .refreshable, so there is no progress indicator while it works), or offer OK only and let the user pull again; this is the owner's choice. M3U: add `else if store.channels.isEmpty, let e = store.loadError { CatalogLoadErrorView(message: e) { Task { await store.loadPlaylist(playlist) } } }` before the plain empty branch at M3UChannelsView.swift:41, and give the failure at line 222 its own field whose retry calls refreshCatalog().

**API check:** View.alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) with a String title at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10666, in the `@available(iOS 15.0, ...)` extension at 10655-10656. `struct RefreshFailure: Equatable { let message: String; let scope: CatalogContentType? }` compiles: CatalogContentType (PlaylistContentStore.swift:7-9) is a payload-free enum, so Equatable is synthesized. No new SwiftUI API.

**Regression risks:** Dropping the loadError alert without the correction above hides load failures on the Settings and Search tabs and after categories are on screen. PlaylistSettingsView.swift:524 calls reloadFromDatabaseIfActive, whose failure also lands in loadError; check that path still reports. The settings views contain the owner's tip-jar row; this fix does not need to touch them. loadingMessage = nil at lines 204 and 219 is also unguarded and can clear the message of a newer load after a playlist switch.

**How to verify:** (1) New playlist with an unreachable host: expect exactly one error surface, and the retry still present after any alert is dismissed. (2) Loaded playlist, network off, pull on Live TV: the alert's retry (if kept) must issue the network requests again, visible in the DEBUG log or a proxy. (3) M3U playlist with a failing URL: pull, and check the retry downloads again. (4) Fail a load while the Settings tab is selected and confirm the error is still shown somewhere.

## states-loading-empty-error-5 — Category, "All" and M3U grids start in their empty state: "No movies found." is the first thing drawn on every push and stays while a sort or the stream load is still running

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live category detail, All Channels, Movies category detail, All Movies, Series category detail, All Series, M3U group detail, M3U channels, M3U favorites
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:469, 512-523, 547, 567-577, 586-595`, `Views/VODView.swift:556, 578-589, 616, 653-668, 677-686`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:528, 550-561, 584, 615-627, 636-645`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:50-59, 137-141, 488, 562-571`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:17-18, 27-32, 66-81`

**What the user perceives:** The pushed screen slides in showing an icon and "No movies found." and then swaps to the grid without a transition. In a small category with the default sort this is two or three frames at the start of the push and barely visible. In "All Movies" with a large catalog, or with a saved non-default sort, the wrong message is readable for hundreds of milliseconds or longer. If a category is opened while the catalog is still loading, it says "No channel found." until the load finishes. M3U: "No search results." flashes when the channel list arrives, and a user with favourites sees "No favorites yet" first.

**Mechanism (finder):** There are two layers of asynchronously filled @State, both starting as []. The wrapper (for example VODCategoryDetailView.displayItems, VODView.swift:556) is filled by a `.task` after appear (:574-575). The content view's own displayItems (:616) is filled by a detached recompute keyed on itemsToken (:653-668, :737), and the body treats an empty array as the empty state (:677-686). Nothing distinguishes "not computed yet" from "computed, empty", or "catalog still loading" (contentStore.streamsLoaded false) from "category empty". The sort is persisted in @AppStorage (:610), so a saved A-Z sort runs localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare over the whole list while the empty state is on screen. M3U root: displayGroups is filled one runloop turn after store.channels through `.onChange` plus a Task (M3UChannelsView.swift:137-140). In between the body reaches the `visibleShelfGroups.isEmpty` branch (:50-59); the same branch shows "No search results." when the user has hidden every group. M3UFavoritesView: favoriteChannels is [] until the detached filter returns (:66-81).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Model the third state and seed the common case synchronously.

```swift
// wrappers (Live/VOD/SeriesCategoryDetailView): O(1) dictionary lookup, the array is copy-on-write
init(playlist: Playlist, category: DBCategory) {
    self.playlist = playlist; self.category = category
    _displayItems = State(initialValue: PlaylistContentStore.shared.vodStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? [])
}

// content views (LiveCategoryContent, VODCategoryContent, SeriesCategoryContent, M3UGroupGridContent)
var isSourceLoading = false              // parent: !contentStore.streamsLoaded, or its first recompute not finished
@State private var hasComputed = false   // set at the end of recompute()
// seed displayItems = items in init when the stored sort is .defaultOrder (identity, VODSortOption.swift:38-41)
if displayItems.isEmpty {
    if isSourceLoading || !hasComputed { ProgressView().frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity) }
    else { emptyState }
}
// add isSourceLoading to the hand-written == so the Equatable short-circuit still holds
```
M3U root: assign displayGroups synchronously inside the `.onChange(of: store.channels)` closure when the query is empty (this is what applyFull() does), and show a "categories hidden" message with a button to the picker instead of "No search results." when the query is empty. M3UFavoritesView: make favoriteChannels optional and show the empty state only when it is non-nil and empty.

**APIs:** ProgressView (iOS 14.0 (already used throughout))

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real. The wrapper's @State starts empty and is filled by a `.task` after appear (Views/VODView.swift:556, 574-582; Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:469, 508-516; Views/SeriesView.swift:528, 546-554). The content view has a second empty @State filled by a detached recompute (VODView.swift:616, 653-668, 737) and treats empty as the empty state (677-686; LiveStreamsView.swift:586-595; SeriesView.swift:636-645). The sort is persisted in @AppStorage (VODView.swift:610) and the name sorts use localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare over the whole list (Models/VODSortOption.swift:42-49). Nothing separates 'not computed yet' or 'catalog still loading' from 'empty'. Two corrections. Scope: for an ordinary category with the default sort the wrong state lasts two or three frames at the very start of the push, when the incoming screen has barely moved, so it is practically invisible; it becomes readable in the 'All' screens with large catalogs (two detached passes over the full list, AllVODView at VODView.swift:838-853), with a saved non-default sort, or when a category is opened during phase 2 of the catalog load. The M3U root case is at most one frame (onChange plus Task, M3UChannelsView.swift:137-140) and I could not show it is ever drawn; M3UFavoritesView (17, 27-32, 66-81) is a few frames. Fix: the proposed `hasComputed` flag is wrong as written. The content view's first recompute runs with the still-empty input and sets the flag; when the parent then delivers the real list and clears isSourceLoading, the content view's own list is still empty while its second recompute (the slow sort) runs, so the empty state is shown again in exactly the slow case.

**Corrected claim:** Category, 'All' and M3U grids cannot tell 'not computed yet' or 'catalog still loading' from 'empty', so they start in their empty state. This is invisible for small categories with the default sort, and shows as a readable wrong message ('No movies found.') in the 'All' screens on large catalogs, with a saved name/rating sort, and when a category is opened while the catalog is still loading. M3U favorites show 'No favorites yet' for a few frames; the M3U root flash is at most one frame and unproven.

**Corrected fix:** Smaller change, without @State seeding in init. (1) Wrappers: when the query is empty, pass the store's array straight through, e.g. `VODCategoryContent(playlist: playlist, items: debouncedQuery.isEmpty ? (contentStore.vodStreamsByCategoryId[category.id] ?? []) : displayItems, isSourceLoading: !contentStore.streamsLoaded)`: an O(1) dictionary lookup, the array is copy-on-write. 'All' wrappers keep their off-main filter and pass `isSourceLoading: !contentStore.streamsLoaded || !didCompute`. (2) Content views: when the sort is .defaultOrder and no filter is set, render `items` directly instead of displayItems (the result is identical, VODSortOption.swift:38-41), so the grid is there on the first frame. (3) Replace hasComputed with a token: `@State private var computedToken: Int?`, set to the itemsToken captured at the start of recompute once it finishes. Show the empty state only when `!isSourceLoading && computedToken == itemsToken` (or the identity case with items empty); otherwise show a ProgressView or nothing. (4) Add isSourceLoading to the hand-written `==`. M3UFavoritesView: make favoriteChannels optional and show the empty state only when it is non-nil and empty. M3U root: assign displayGroups synchronously in the onChange closure when the query is empty. The 'all groups hidden' message is a product decision, not a fix.

**API check:** ProgressView and View.task(id:priority:_:) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166, iOS 15.0) are already used in these files. View is `@preconcurrency @MainActor public protocol View` (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13881), so reading PlaylistContentStore.shared from a view body or init is actor-correct. No new or iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Do not seed the play queue with `items.map(\.stream)` in an init: the init runs on every parent body pass (NavigationLink destinations are built eagerly), which would bring back the O(n) main-thread work that the Equatable content views and the prebuilt streamQueue (VODView.swift:617-619) removed. In the identity case streamQueue is still filled asynchronously, so for a few milliseconds a tapped movie would open with an empty prev/next queue. The hand-written `==` must include the new flag or the loading-to-loaded change is swallowed by `.equatable()`. Keep pagination (visibleCount) and the off-main sort untouched.

**How to verify:** UI test: push a category and 'All Movies' and poll during the transition; the empty-state text must never exist. Repeat with vod.sortOption set to nameAsc in UserDefaults and a seeded large fixture (50k+ movies). Open a category while a DEBUG delay holds phase 2 of the load and check for a spinner instead of 'No channel found.'. On a device with a real catalog, a frame-by-frame recording of the 'All Movies' push settles how long the wrong state is visible today.

## states-loading-empty-error-6 — Every GRDBQuery-backed screen renders its default value first, so empty states flash, Continue Watching pops in and pushes the shelves down, and the detail button flips from "Watch Now" to "Resume"

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Favorites, Watch history, Downloads, Channel EPG, Movie detail, Series detail, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Playlist list
- Code: `Models/Requests.swift:17, 204, 224, 261, 286, 313, 340, 367, 389, 420, 494, 515`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:21-28`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:101-104, 126-129, 152-155`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:52-57`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:70-75`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:20-22, 132-141`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:39-40`, `ContentView.swift:134-138`

**What the user perceives:** Favourites pushes in showing "No favorite movies yet." for a frame or two before the grid replaces it; History and Downloads do the same with "No history" and "No downloads". The first time each tab's shelves appear, the Continue Watching row is inserted after the first frame and moves every shelf down by roughly 200 pt. On a half-watched film the blue button is drawn as "Watch Now" and then grows into "Resume, 42:10" with a progress bar and a Restart row, and the favourite star fills a frame late.

**Mechanism (finder):** All custom Queryable types build their publisher with `ValueObservation.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)`. In GRDB 7.10.0 that defaults to `scheduling: .async(onQueue: .main)` (GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487), so @Query returns `Request.defaultValue` (GRDBQuery Query.swift:28) until the first asynchronous delivery. The views map the default straight to a visible state: [] becomes an empty state (FavoritesView.swift:103-104; WatchHistoryListView.swift:52; DownloadsView.swift:70; ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:39), [] makes the row absent (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:28), nil history gives "Watch Now" (MovieDetailView.swift:133), false gives the outline star. GRDBQuery's own ValueObservationQueryable uses `.immediate` for this reason (GRDBQuery ValueObservationQueryable.swift:62). ContentView already works around it with a nil default and a blank screen (ContentView.swift:134-138).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Fetch the first value synchronously for the small requests:

```swift
.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader, scheduling: .immediate)
```
Apply to PlaylistRequest, SeriesByIDRequest, SeasonsRequest, VODByIDRequest, IsFavoriteRequest, the three Favorite*Request types, WatchHistoryRequest, RecentWatchHistoryRequest, WatchProgressMapRequest, LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest (Models/Requests.swift), AllDownloadsRequest (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:299) and ChannelEPGRequest (EPG/EPGRequests.swift:16). Leave LiveStreamsRequest, VODStreamsRequest and SeriesRequest asynchronous: they fetch the whole catalog. GRDBQuery's tracker already handles a value delivered during `update()` (Query.swift:295-322, the `isUpdating` flag). `.immediate` must be subscribed from the main thread; GRDBQuery does that in DynamicProperty.update. SeasonEpisodesObserver (SeriesView.swift:1276-1287) keeps its own receive(on:) and needs no change.

**APIs:** GRDB ValueObservation.publisher(in:scheduling:) with the .immediate scheduler (Third-party, not in the iOS SDK. Verified in the package checkout: GRDB 7.10.0, ValueObservation.swift:465-487 and ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148, 177)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed. Every custom Queryable calls `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader)` with no scheduler (Models/Requests.swift:17, 204, 224, 261, 286, 313, 340, 367, 389, 420, 494, 515; Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:293, 310; EPG/EPGRequests.swift:25). GRDB 7.10.0 defaults to `.async(onQueue: .main)` (GRDB ValueObservation.swift, `publisher(in:scheduling:)` signature), and GRDBQuery 0.11.0 returns `tracker.value ?? Request.defaultValue` (Query.swift:27-29). The views map the default straight to a visible state: FavoritesView.swift:103, 127, 153 (empty state), WatchHistoryListView.swift:52, DownloadsView.swift:70, ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:39-40, ContinueWatchingRow.swift:28 (row absent, and it sits above the shelves in the same ScrollView at LiveStreamsView.swift:213 and VODView.swift:65, so its arrival pushes them down), MovieDetailView.swift:133-139 (Watch Now, then Resume plus a Restart row). No history shows the async scheduling was a deliberate choice (`git log -S'scheduling:'` returns nothing). The flash is one or two frames at the start of a push, which I could not observe without a simulator run.

The fix is where this needs correcting. On a DatabasePool every observation, immediate or async, takes its initial value inside a WAL snapshot transaction that keeps its reader connection until the writer queue is free (GRDB ValueConcurrentObserver.swift:284-336 and 423-464; DatabasePool.swift:689-701; SQLITE_ENABLE_SNAPSHOT is defined in GRDB Package.swift:17). The pool has 5 readers (Configuration.swift:360; Database/Persistence.swift sets no override). This app has multi-second single write transactions: the EPG staging swap (EPG/EPGRefreshCoordinator.swift:241-269, runs automatically in the background) and the catalog replace on pull-to-refresh (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:489-507). During such a write, the sixth observation start waits for a reader. Today that wait is on a background queue. With `.immediate` it is `readerPool.get()` on the main thread, so the app freezes until the write ends. FavoritesView alone starts 5 observations (FavoritesView.swift:12-16); a series detail starts 4 plus one WatchHistoryRequest and one DownloadButton query per visible episode row (SeriesView.swift:809-812, 1363, 1454). The finder flagged this hazard only for the in-memory DatabaseQueue fallback.

Also wrong: WatchHistoryRequestTests subscribes to no publisher (it tests only the pure helpers), so nothing there traps.

**Corrected claim:** Every GRDBQuery-backed screen renders its default value for one or two frames because the observations use GRDB's default async scheduler. Empty states flash on Favorites, History, Downloads and Channel EPG; Continue Watching is inserted after the first frame and pushes the shelves down; the movie detail button flips from Watch Now to Resume. Switching everything to `.immediate` would remove the flashes but can freeze the main thread for the length of a long write transaction (EPG swap, catalog refresh), because each observation pins one of the 5 pool readers until the writer is free.

**Corrected fix:** Split by what the screen needs.

1) List screens (the three Favorite*Request types, AllDownloadsRequest, ChannelEPGRequest, RecentWatchHistoryRequest as used by WatchHistoryListView): keep async scheduling and make "not delivered yet" distinguishable, as PlaylistRequest already does (optional value, nil default, or a wrapper request). The view draws only its background until the first value and shows the empty state only for a delivered empty array. No main-thread I/O.

2) Where the value decides layout on the first frame (ContinueWatchingRow's RecentWatchHistoryRequest, and on the detail screens WatchHistoryRequest, LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest, IsFavoriteRequest, VODByIDRequest, SeriesByIDRequest, SeasonsRequest): use `.publisher(in: appDatabase.reader, scheduling: .immediate)`, with three guards:
- Add a flag on WatchHistoryRequest (for example `var immediate = false`, part of Equatable) so EpisodeDetailRow (SeriesView.swift:1379) stays async. Per-row immediate starts are what exhaust the pool.
- Raise `config.maximumReaderCount` in Persistence.databaseConfiguration() (for example to 12) so one screen cannot use up the pool.
- Leave PlaylistRequest (ContentView already handles nil), the three catalog requests, the per-card DownloadedItemByIDRequest and WatchProgressMapRequest async.

The residual freeze risk during the EPG swap or catalog replace remains for part 2. Whether to accept it, or chunk those writes first, is the owner's decision.

**API check:** Third-party, not in the iOS SDK; verified in the package checkout. GRDB v7.10.0 ValueObservation.swift: `public func publisher(in reader: any DatabaseReader, scheduling scheduler: some ValueObservationScheduler = .async(onQueue: .main)) -> DatabasePublishers.Value<Reducer.Value>`. ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148 and 177: `public static var immediate: ImmediateValueObservationScheduler`, documented "requires that the observation is started from the main actor. A fatal error is raised otherwise". GRDBQuery 0.11.0 Query.swift:295-325 handles a value delivered during `update()` through the `isUpdating` flag, and `Query.update()` runs under `MainActor.assumeIsolated` (Query.swift:333-340). GRDBQuery's own ValueObservationQueryable.swift:62 uses `scheduling: .immediate`. `Configuration.maximumReaderCount: Int = 5` at GRDB Configuration.swift:360.

**Regression risks:** `.immediate` runs a synchronous read on the main thread during the view update. If all pool readers are pinned or busy, the UI freezes: 3 readers are busy for seconds during catalog phase 2 (PlaylistContentStore.swift:140-142), and every observation started during a long write pins one. Per-row immediate queries in episode lists add main-thread work while scrolling. Changing a request's Value to optional touches each consumer. `L("content.uncategorized")` inside the favorites tracking closures would run on main for the first fetch, which is harmless. No earlier deliberate work is undone; the `.removeDuplicates()` calls stay.

**How to verify:** 1) Simulator UI test: seed one favourite, one history row and one download; push Favorites, History and Downloads and assert the empty-state texts never exist. 2) Screen-record the first frames of a half-watched movie detail and of each tab home with history present: the button must not relabel and the shelves must not shift. 3) Freeze test, which decides part 2: in a DEBUG build hold a write transaction for 5 s (`AppDatabase.shared.write { _ in Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 5) }`), then push Favorites, then a movie detail, then a series detail. Measure main-thread hangs with the Instruments Hangs template, before and after raising maximumReaderCount. 4) Time Profiler on the series detail mount, to confirm rows did not become synchronous.

## states-loading-empty-error-7 — Settings hides the EPG, content-management and statistics sections until the panel's auth request succeeds, and swaps the subscription rows for a spinner on every appearance

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream)
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:9, 226-237, 263-345, 392-401, 448-472`

**What the user perceives:** Offline, or with a panel that is down, Settings ends after "Playlist Information" with a red line "Could not fetch info: Server error: HTTP 404" (screenshot iphone-light/T02-settings-2.png). The TV-guide switch, the adult filter, Clear watch history and the content counts are missing, although all of them are local. Online, each time the Settings tab or screen appears (also when coming back from Downloads) the three subscription rows collapse into one spinner row and expand again, so everything below shifts twice, including while the user is scrolled further down.

**Mechanism (finder):** `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil { stats, server, XtreamEPGSettingsSection, content management }` (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:263-345) gates local sections on a network response. No comment explains the gate and it dates from the initial import (d2489f9). fetchAuthInfo runs from `.task` on every appearance (:392-396) and sets `isLoading = true` first (:449). The row switch `if isLoading {...} else if let error {...} else if let userInfo {...}` (:226-259) then replaces rows that already have valid data. The error row prints the raw error string in red (:233-234).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Move the statistics, EPG and content-management sections out of the `authResponse?.userInfo != nil` condition; keep only the server section and the subscription rows dependent on it. 2) Show the spinner row only when there is nothing to show (`isLoading && authResponse == nil`). While re-fetching, keep the old rows and put a small ProgressView where the header's refresh button is (:173-180). 3) Error row in secondary colour with the existing retry button; keep the last known subscription rows visible on a failed re-fetch. The TipJarRow() line at :355 is not touched.

**APIs:** ProgressView (iOS 14.0 (already used at PlaylistSettingsView.swift:63, 229))

**Verifier reasons:** Confirmed in code and screenshot. Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:263-345 wraps statistics, server info, `XtreamEPGSettingsSection(playlist:)` and Content Management in `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil`. XtreamEPGSettingsSection (Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:113-156) needs only the playlist and the local database; the adult filter and Clear history are local too. No comment explains the gate, and `git log -S` traces it to the initial import (fe55017 / d2489f9) with the EPG section later added inside it. iphone-light/T02-settings-2.png shows Playlist Information ending in a red "Could not fetch info: Server error: HTTP 404" plus Try Again, followed directly by About.

The row swap is real: `fetchAuthInfo()` sets `isLoading = true` first (:449), and the chain at :226-259 then replaces the three subscription rows with one spinner row although `authResponse` still holds valid data. `.task` (:392-396) re-runs on each appearance of the tab root. I am inferring from SwiftUI's lifecycle that this includes tab switches and popping back from Downloads; I did not run it.

One gap in the fix: `.task` awaits `fetchAuthInfo()` before `fetchLocalStats()` (:393-394). Once the sections are ungated, the counts read 0 and Clear history is disabled (`.disabled(historyCount == 0)`, :343) for as long as the network call takes, which offline means until the request times out. The gate hides that today.

**Corrected claim:** As stated. In addition, the local statistics load only after the auth request returns, so simply ungating the sections would show zero counts and a disabled Clear history button while the network call is pending or timing out.

**Corrected fix:** 1) Move the statistics section, XtreamEPGSettingsSection and Content Management out of `if authResponse?.userInfo != nil`. Keep only the server section (:294-315) and the subscription rows dependent on the response.
2) Reorder `.task` and `.refreshable` so local work is first: `await fetchLocalStats(); await refreshDownloadUsage(); await fetchAuthInfo()`.
3) Show the spinner row only when `isLoading && authResponse == nil`. While re-fetching with data present, keep the three rows and replace the header's refresh button (:173-180) with a small `ProgressView()`.
4) Restructure the chain: subscription rows whenever `authResponse?.userInfo` exists; the error as an extra row in secondary colour with the existing Try Again button, so a failed re-fetch keeps the last known rows.
5) Optional: skip the automatic re-fetch when the last success is under a minute old.
The `TipJarRow()` line at :355 and the tip files are not touched. The file has uncommitted edits, so apply this as a small diff around :170-345 and :392-401.

**API check:** `ProgressView`: `@available(iOS 14.0, ...) public struct ProgressView<Label, CurrentValueLabel>` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:3960-3961. Already used in this file. No other API involved.

**Regression risks:** UI tests that scroll Settings by position will see three more sections on the demo fixture (auth returns 404): ScreensUITests and the tip-jar row lookup need a re-run. With the gate gone, the EPG toggle and adult filter are usable when the panel is unreachable; both write only to the local database, so that is the intended result. Leaving the server section gated keeps it from rendering empty. The tip-jar work is not restructured.

**How to verify:** Simulator with the demo fixture: the TV Guide, Content Management and Statistics sections exist, the counts are non-zero as soon as the screen appears, and Clear history is enabled when history exists. Compare against T02 to T04. With a reachable panel: switch away from Settings and back, and pop back from Downloads; assert the three subscription rows never leave the hierarchy and the rows below do not move. This also settles whether `.task` re-runs on a tab switch.

## states-loading-empty-error-8 — Global search shows "No Results" before the first search has finished, and draws it as a card inside a list row instead of a full-screen state

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:48-65, 140-142, 149, 224-249, 251-278`

**What the user perceives:** After the second typed character "No Results for 'mi'" appears for a moment and is then replaced by results. On a large catalog the three filters and sorts take long enough to read it. The same happens again whenever the query goes below two characters and back up. A genuine no-result state is a white rounded card at the top of a grey grouped list (screenshot iphone-light/R01-search-no-results.png). System apps centre this state in the available area, as DownloadsView in this app does (T05-downloads.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** SearchResultsView's three result arrays start empty (SearchView.swift:140-142) and are filled only after the detached filter and sort return (:251-278). The empty check at :224-243 can tell "catalog still loading" apart, but not "this query has not been searched yet", so it shows `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` straight away. The view is created only when `debouncedQuery.count >= 2` (:48-65), so its state is lost each time the query drops below two characters. The ContentUnavailableView is a row of the `.insetGrouped` List (:149, :241), hence the card.

**Proposed fix (finder):** ```swift
@State private var resolvedQuery: String?          // the query the three arrays belong to
// end of runSearch(): resolvedQuery = q

var body: some View {
    let isEmpty = liveResults.isEmpty && movieResults.isEmpty && seriesResults.isEmpty
    Group {
        if isEmpty {
            if !contentStore.streamsLoaded || resolvedQuery != query {
                ProgressView().frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            } else {
                ContentUnavailableView.search(text: query)    // outside the List: centred, no card
            }
        } else { List { /* sections unchanged */ }.listStyle(.insetGrouped) }
    }
    .task(id: query) { await runSearch() } // tasks stay on the Group
}
```
Keep the comment and behaviour at :225-228 (no false no-result while the catalog loads). The idle state (:48-57, hand-built magnifier, screenshot Q01) can become a ContentUnavailableView in the same change. Note that `.search(text:)` is localised by the system, not through L(); see the empty-state finding.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) (iOS 17.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17620-17625))

**Verifier reasons:** Claim confirmed. `SearchResultsView` is created only when `debouncedQuery.count >= 2` (Views/SearchView.swift:48-65) with three empty @State arrays (:140-142). `runSearch()` fills them only after three detached filter-and-sort passes return (:251-278). The check at :224-243 distinguishes "catalog still loading" but not "this query has not been searched yet", so `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` renders on the first pass. With 150k movies the filter plus `localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare` sort takes long enough to read it. Dropping below two characters destroys the view and its state, so the flash repeats. The view is a row of the `.insetGrouped` List (:149, :241, :245); iphone-light/R01-search-no-results.png shows it as a white rounded card at the top of a grey list, unlike the centred state in T05-downloads.png.

Two problems the fix leaves or adds:
- The emptiness test ignores the filter. With filter Movies and a query that matches only channels, no section renders and the test at :224 is false, so the list is blank. The proposed `isEmpty` keeps this.
- The `Group { if ... ProgressView ... else List }` shape flashes a centred spinner for a frame or two on every first search of a small catalog, and flips the background between plain and grouped as the List is torn down and rebuilt.

Also noted: the three `.task(id:)` modifiers at :246-248 all fire on mount, so the first search runs three times in parallel.

**Corrected claim:** As stated, plus: with a type filter selected and results only in other types, the results list is blank with no message at all, because the emptiness check at SearchView.swift:224 looks at all three arrays regardless of the filter.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the List mounted and put the states in an overlay, the documented pattern for this view:

```swift
@State private var resolvedQuery: String?   // set at the end of runSearch(): resolvedQuery = q

private var visibleIsEmpty: Bool {
    switch filter {
    case .all:    liveResults.isEmpty && movieResults.isEmpty && seriesResults.isEmpty
    case .live:   liveResults.isEmpty
    case .movies: movieResults.isEmpty
    case .series: seriesResults.isEmpty
    }
}

List { /* three sections unchanged; delete the block at :224-243 */ }
    .listStyle(.insetGrouped)
    .overlay {
        if visibleIsEmpty {
            if !contentStore.streamsLoaded {
                ProgressView(L("common.loading"))
            } else if resolvedQuery == query {
                ContentUnavailableView.search(text: query)
            }   // pending search: show nothing
        }
    }
```

The comment and behaviour at :225-228 stay (no false no-result while the catalog loads). The three tasks stay on the List; folding them into one `.task(id:)` keyed on a small Hashable of query, hiddenStore.version and streamsLoaded removes the triple first search. The idle state at :48-57 can become a ContentUnavailableView in the same change. If the owner prefers in-app language over system language (see finding 10), replace `.search(text:)` with `ContentUnavailableView(L("favorites.empty.no_result.title"), systemImage: "magnifyingglass", description: Text(L("category_picker.not_found.message")))`.

**API check:** `ContentUnavailableView`: `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *)` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17575. `public static func search(text: Swift.String) -> ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` and `static var search` at :17620-17625 in an iOS 17.0 extension. `init<S>(_ title: S, systemImage name: String, description: Text? = nil) where S : StringProtocol` at :17616, iOS 17.0. `ProgressView` iOS 14.0. All below the iOS 18 deployment target; no availability check needed.

**Regression risks:** An overlay over an empty insetGrouped List keeps the grouped background, which matches the results state. The overlay is centred in the List's safe area; check it stays above the keyboard on iPhone and in the iPad sidebar layout. Merging the three tasks must keep the re-search on `hiddenStore.version` and `streamsLoaded` changes. The off-main filtering stays as it is.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test: type "mi" and assert no element containing "No Results" exists at any point before the first result row appears. Type "zzzzqq" and compare with R01: the message is centred with no card. Select the Movies chip and search a term that matches only channels: the no-result state must show instead of a blank list. With a 100k-item fixture, confirm there is no spinner flash and no early no-result message.

## states-loading-empty-error-9 — While categories are loaded but streams are not, shelves are blank gaps under their titles; on Live the gap is shorter than the real row, so the list jumps when the cards arrive

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:66-74, 372-374, 433-455`, `Views/VODView.swift:39-47, 160, 434-436`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:40-48, 161, 410-412`, `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:26-27, 50`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:138-147`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether the very first state (centred spinner with "Preparing channels...") should also become skeleton shelves. With a local database that state lasts a few milliseconds, so a skeleton avoids one layout flip. For the rare network-bootstrap case the spinner with its progress text is more informative. Recommendation: skeleton for the local load, keep the spinner only while loadingMessage is non-nil.

**What the user perceives:** When a tab is first opened while the catalog is still loading (and, after the first finding is fixed, on every cold start), the page is a column of category titles with empty space between them and disabled toolbar buttons. Then every card appears in one frame, with no transition. On Live TV the shelves also get taller at that moment, so everything below the first shelf shifts down.

**Mechanism (finder):** The loading branch of the shelf rows is `Color.clear.frame(height:)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:373-374; VODView.swift:435-436; SeriesView.swift:411-412). On Live the reserved height is `liveShelfIcon + 30`, but a real card is icon + 10 + a two-line caption + 10 + the reserved EPG now/next line (:433-455), so each shelf grows when the items arrive. VOD and Series reserve the exact shelfRowTotalHeight, so they do not jump but are still blank. `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` on the VOD and Series roots (VODView.swift:160; SeriesView.swift:161) makes the swap a hard cut. The state before that is a centred `ProgressView().scaleEffect(1.2)` with text (LiveStreamsView.swift:67-74), a third different layout within the first second.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the clear spacer with a skeleton made of the same primitives as the real card, so the layout is identical before and after.

```swift
// LiveCategoryShelfRow, isStreamsLoading branch
HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
    ForEach(0..<6, id: \.self) { _ in
        VStack(spacing: 10) {
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12).fill(Color(.systemGray6))      // same fill as CachedImage.placeholder
                .frame(width: posterMetrics.liveShelfIcon, height: posterMetrics.liveShelfIcon)
            Text("Channel name").font(.caption).fontWeight(.medium)
                .frame(width: posterMetrics.liveShelfLabelWidth)
                .redacted(reason: .placeholder)
            // plus the same EPGNowNextLine(reserveSpace: true) the real card adds when a snapshot exists
        }
    }
}
.padding(.horizontal, 16).accessibilityHidden(true).allowsHitTesting(false)
```
Same for VOD and Series with shelfPosterWidth x shelfPosterHeight inside the existing `.frame(height: shelfRowTotalHeight)`. Keep `isStreamsLoading` in the hand-written == (it already is). Because CachedImage shows the same grey rectangle while a poster downloads, skeleton to card to image becomes one continuous change. If the hard cut still shows, add `.animation(.default, value: isStreamsLoading)` on the row only; the root-level `.transaction` stays as it is.

**APIs:** View.redacted(reason:) with RedactionReasons.placeholder (iOS 14.0 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6086-6107))

**Verifier reasons:** The blank phase is real and deliberate. PlaylistContentStore.swift:127-152 publishes categories first (comment: UI is shown immediately with categories), then runs three parallel reads and sets `streamsLoaded` only when all three finish. The Live tab therefore shows empty shelves for as long as the largest read (movies) takes, which is seconds on a real catalog. The loading branches are `Color.clear.frame(height:)` at LiveStreamsView.swift:372-374, VODView.swift:434-436 and SeriesView.swift:410-412. VOD and Series reserve the exact `shelfRowTotalHeight` (PosterMetrics.swift:50), so they do not jump.

Three corrections:
- Live does not simply grow. A real card is icon + 10 + a caption with `.lineLimit(2)` that does not reserve space (LiveStreamsView.swift:443-446) + an optional 10 + 22 pt EPG line when a snapshot exists (:451-454; EPGComponents.swift:51). Against the reserved icon + 30 that is roughly 4 pt shorter for one-line names, 12 pt taller for two-line names and about 32 pt more with EPG. A skeleton cannot be "identical before and after" unless the caption reserves two lines.
- Missed glitch on all three tabs: the row gets `isStreamsLoading: !contentStore.streamsLoaded` (LiveStreamsView.swift:235, VODView.swift:88), but `displayItemsByCategory` is filled later by `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:106, 289-292; VODView.swift:158, 175-177). For one update pass the row has loading false and no items, so every shelf collapses to the caption "No channel in this category." and then expands to cards. A skeleton keyed on the same flag would not remove this. Whether that pass reaches the screen needs a recording.
- The proposed snippet's 6-card HStack is wider than an iPhone screen. Inside `VStack(alignment: .leading)` that widens the whole row, and the LazyVStack centres it, pushing the title off the left edge.

The root `.transaction { $0.animation = nil }` (VODView.swift:160) dates from the initial import with no comment; the fix leaves it alone.

**Corrected claim:** While categories are loaded but streams are not, shelves are blank gaps under their titles for the duration of the full catalog read. On Live the reserved height does not match the real row (shorter or taller depending on caption lines and whether EPG data exists), so shelves shift when cards arrive. On all three tabs there is also a one-pass window after loading finishes in which each shelf shows its "nothing in this category" caption and collapses, before the cards replace it.

**Corrected fix:** 1) Close the collapse window first; it is the cheapest and largest win. Drive the row's flag from view state set together with the items: add `@State private var displayReady = false`, set it in `recomputeFilter()` when `contentStore.streamsLoaded` is true at the point the items are assigned, and pass `isStreamsLoading: !displayReady` in LiveStreamsView, VODView and SeriesView. The hand-written `==` already compares the flag.
2) Make the Live card height deterministic: `.lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true)` on the caption in LiveStreamCard (:443-446). This adds about 16 pt to shelves whose names all fit on one line, a small visual change the owner should accept.
3) Replace the clear spacer with a skeleton built from the same primitives, laid out so it cannot widen the row:

```swift
ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false) {
    HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
        ForEach(0..<8, id: \.self) { _ in
            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12).fill(Color(.systemGray6))
                    .frame(width: posterMetrics.liveShelfIcon, height: posterMetrics.liveShelfIcon)
                Text("Placeholder\nname").font(.caption).fontWeight(.medium)
                    .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true)
                    .frame(width: posterMetrics.liveShelfLabelWidth)
                    .redacted(reason: .placeholder)
                // plus EPGNowNextLine(nowNext: nil, width:, reserveSpace: true) when the epgSnapshot environment value is non-nil
            }
        }
    }
    .padding(.horizontal, 16)
}
.scrollDisabled(true).allowsHitTesting(false).accessibilityHidden(true)
```

VOD and Series use the same shape with shelfPosterWidth x shelfPosterHeight inside the existing `.frame(height: posterMetrics.shelfRowTotalHeight)`. Keep the root `.transaction`. If the cut still reads as abrupt, add `.animation(.default, value: isStreamsLoading)` on the row only.

**API check:** `View.redacted(reason:)`: `nonisolated public func redacted(reason: SwiftUICore.RedactionReasons) -> some View` in an `@available(iOS 14.0, ...)` extension, SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6102-6107; `RedactionReasons.placeholder` at :6089, iOS 14.0. `lineLimit(_ limit: Int, reservesSpace: Bool)`: `@available(iOS 16.0, ...)`, SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8855-8856. `View.scrollDisabled(_:)`: `@available(iOS 16.0, ...)`, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:12478-12479. All below the iOS 18 target.

**Regression risks:** The Equatable shelf rows stay; the skeleton lives inside the existing loading branch and `isStreamsLoading` is already in `==`. The skeleton must not add @State or observe a store. Reading the epgSnapshot environment value in the Live row is safe, since environment changes bypass the custom `==`. Reserving two caption lines changes Live shelf heights in the home list and wherever LiveStreamCard is reused (the Favorites live grid, FavoritesView.swift:107-116). A row-level `.animation` must not animate horizontal scroll content; keep it scoped to the flag.

**How to verify:** Add a DEBUG delay before `streamsLoaded = true` (PlaylistContentStore.swift:152). Screen-record the cold start at 60 fps on each tab and step frame by frame: (a) no frame shows the "No ... in this category" captions; (b) shelf titles and card frames coincide between the loading frame and the loaded frame, including with EPG enabled on Live; (c) the shelf title stays at x = 16 on an iPhone SE-width device, which catches the wide-HStack mistake. Repeat on iPad. Item (a) is the part only a recording can settle.
