## states-loading-empty-error-10 — Empty and no-result states are built three different ways; sixteen hand-made stacks sit next to eleven ContentUnavailableView uses, with wrong copy and icons in several

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category and All grids, Favorites, M3U channels, M3U group detail, Search tab, Playlist list, EPG guide
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:80-87, 587-595`, `Views/VODView.swift:53-60, 678-686`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:54-61, 637-645`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:178-191`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:42-59, 563-571`, `Views/SearchView.swift:48-57`, `Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:11-33`, `ContentView.swift:172-203`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:53-63`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:71-77`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:77-99`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` is localised by the system and ignores the in-app language picker (LocalizationManager). DownloadsView.swift:77 and SearchView.swift:241 already use it. Either accept system-language text for search states, or use the L()-based title and description everywhere. I recommend the latter, because the app offers its own language setting.

**What the user perceives:** "Nothing here" looks different from screen to screen. Downloads and History use the system layout with a large symbol, bold title and grey description (T05-downloads.png). Favourites shows a 48 pt grey icon and one callout line, pushed down 50 pt (M09-favorites-movies.png). In-tab search shows a .largeTitle icon and "No search results." (iphone-light/L06-live-inline-search-results.png), while global search shows the system "No Results for ..." (R01). Movies and Series say "No category found." when a search matches nothing in the catalog sense, and Live's empty category grid shows a magnifying glass although nobody searched.

**Mechanism (finder):** Inventory, as loading / empty / search-empty / error.
- Tab roots (LiveStreamsView.swift:65-88; VODView.swift:38-61; SeriesView.swift:39-62): scaled spinner with text / hand-built icon plus `live.empty.no_category` (all three tabs use the live key) / the same stack with `list.no_result` / CatalogLoadErrorView (hand-built) plus the alert.
- Category and All grids (LiveStreamsView.swift:586-595; VODView.swift:677-686; SeriesView.swift:636-645): no loading state / hand-built, one text for both empty and search-empty; Live uses the magnifying-glass icon.
- Movie and series detail (MovieDetailView.swift:74-81, 106-121; SeriesView.swift:868-875, 941-956): labelled ProgressView / not applicable / hand-built "Error" with red text.
- Search tab (SearchView.swift:48-57, 224-243): spinner row in a List / hand-built idle state / ContentUnavailableView.search in a list row.
- Favourites, Xtream (FavoritesView.swift:178-191): none / hand-built for both.
- M3U favourites (M3UFavoritesView.swift:27-38): ContentUnavailableView for both.
- History (WatchHistoryListView.swift:53-63): ContentUnavailableView for both, custom strings.
- Downloads (DownloadsView.swift:71-77): ContentUnavailableView and .search(text:).
- M3U channels (M3UChannelsView.swift:33-59): spinner with text / hand-built / hand-built; error is alert only.
- M3U group grid (M3UChannelsView.swift:562-571): hand-built.
- EPG guide (EPGGuideView.swift:77-99): ProgressView / two ContentUnavailableViews, one with an action / a search without matches leaves a blank grid.
- Channel EPG, category picker: ContentUnavailableView.
- Playlist list (ContentView.swift:172-203): hand-built with a custom full-width button.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Convert the hand-built stacks to ContentUnavailableView with the existing L() keys, through one small helper so the icon, title and description per content type live in one place:

```swift
enum CatalogEmptyState { case noCategories(icon: String), noItems(icon: String, title: String), noSearchResults, allHidden }
struct CatalogEmptyStateView: View { /* switch -> ContentUnavailableView(title, systemImage:, description:) */ }
```
- No-result everywhere: title `favorites.empty.no_result.title`, description `category_picker.not_found.message`. Both exist in all ten languages and are already used by WatchHistoryListView.swift:59-63.
- CatalogLoadErrorView body becomes `ContentUnavailableView { Label(title, systemImage: "wifi.exclamationmark") } description: { Text(message) } actions: { Button(L("common.try_again"), action: onRetry).buttonStyle(.borderedProminent) }`, the same shape as EPGGuideView.swift:87-93.
- Fix the copy: Movies and Series roots get their own empty text; grids get the content icon when no query is active.
- FavoritesView.emptyState (:178-191) becomes ContentUnavailableView; the three existing strings become the title.
- ContentView.emptyState becomes ContentUnavailableView with the add button in `actions:`.
- EPG guide: when `.ready` and model.items is empty with a non-empty query, show the no-result view.
No new strings are required.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView(_:systemImage:description:) and init(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576, 17617)); ContentUnavailableView.search / .search(text:) (iOS 17.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17620-17625))

**Verifier reasons:** Inventory checked against code and screenshots. `grep ContentUnavailableView` finds exactly 11 uses: DownloadsView.swift:71, 77; SearchView.swift:241; WatchHistoryListView.swift:53, 59; M3UFavoritesView.swift:28, 34; CategoryPickerSheet.swift:58; EPGGuideView.swift:81, 87; ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:40. Hand-built stacks are where cited: LiveStreamsView.swift:80-87 and 587-595 (magnifying glass plus `list.no_channel` although no search is active), VODView.swift:53-60 and 678-686, SeriesView.swift:54-61 and 637-645, FavoritesView.swift:178-191 (48 pt icon, callout text, `.padding(.top, 50)`), M3UChannelsView.swift:42-59 and 563-571, SearchView.swift:48-57, CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:11-33, ContentView.swift:172-203.

Screenshots show three different looks: M09-favorites-movies.png (grey icon, one grey line, below centre), L06-live-inline-search-results.png (large icon and "No search results."), T05-downloads.png and R01 (system layout). L06 actually shows the play.tv icon, so it was taken on the Series root, not Live; the point stands.

Copy claim narrowed: the Movies and Series roots use the key `live.empty.no_category`, whose English text is the generic "No category found." It appears when the query is empty and no category is visible; with a query they show `list.no_result`. So the key is misnamed and the text unspecific, not wrong.

The strings the fix relies on exist in all ten languages (`favorites.empty.no_result.title`, `category_picker.not_found.message`: 2 hits per .lproj). EPGGuideView has `.searchable` (:53) and no empty branch in `.ready` (:94-98), so the blank grid on a search without matches is plausible. No UI test looks up these texts, so the finder's test claim is moot rather than a risk.

**Corrected claim:** As stated, with one narrowing: on the Movies and Series roots the text "No category found." is generic rather than wrong; it comes from a key named for Live and shows only when the query is empty and no category is visible.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: one small helper view that maps each case to `ContentUnavailableView`, reusing existing L() keys.
- No-result everywhere: title `favorites.empty.no_result.title`, description `category_picker.not_found.message`, as WatchHistoryListView.swift:59-63 already does.
- CatalogLoadErrorView body becomes `ContentUnavailableView { Label(L("catalog.load_failed.title"), systemImage: "wifi.exclamationmark") } description: { Text(message).lineLimit(4) } actions: { Button(L("common.try_again"), action: onRetry).buttonStyle(.borderedProminent) }`. Keep the lineLimit; the message is a raw error string.
- Movies and Series roots use `vod.empty.no_movie` and `series.empty.no_series` when the query is empty; grids use the content icon when no query is active.
- FavoritesView.emptyState becomes a ContentUnavailableView; drop the 50 pt top padding.
- EPG guide: in `.ready`, when `model.items` is empty and the query is not, show the no-result view.
- ContentView.emptyState (first-run screen with an accent icon and a full-width button) changes the app's first impression. Treat it as the owner's decision and leave it out of the mechanical pass.

Decision for the owner: `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` is localised by the system and ignores the in-app language picker. Using the L()-based title and description everywhere, including DownloadsView.swift:77 and SearchView.swift:241, is the consistent choice.

**API check:** `ContentUnavailableView`: `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *) public struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` with `public init(@ViewBuilder label: () -> Label, @ViewBuilder description: () -> Description = { EmptyView() }, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions = { EmptyView() })` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576. `init<S>(_ title: S, systemImage name: String, description: Text? = nil) where S : StringProtocol` at :17616. `static var search` and `static func search(text: String)` at :17620-17625. All iOS 17.0, below the deployment target.

**Regression risks:** ContentUnavailableView fills and centres in the offered space. Inside FavoritesView's VStack under the segmented picker that is correct, but each replaced stack that relied on `Spacer()` or `.frame(maxHeight: .infinity)` needs a look with the keyboard up and on iPad. Changing the root empty text from "No category found." to "No movies found." alters what users see when every category is hidden; a dedicated "all hidden" case in the helper would be more accurate but needs a new string in ten languages. No performance work is affected. The tip-jar keys in Localizable.strings are not touched because no strings are added.

**How to verify:** Screenshot each state after the change and compare against M09, L06, R01, T05 and Q01 in iphone-light, iphone-dark and ipad-light: same symbol size, bold title, grey description, vertically centred. Switch the in-app language to Turkish with the device in English and confirm every empty and no-result state follows the app language. Trigger the catalog error state offline and confirm Try Again still calls `loadPlaylist`.

## states-loading-empty-error-11 — Error messages are raw concatenated strings, some shown in red, and mix the system language into the app language

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Settings (Xtream), Dashboard alerts, EPG settings, Downloads
- Code: `Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:10-18`, `Networking/M3UService.swift:10-17`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:155, 202, 217, 228, 276`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:106-121, 309`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:941-956, 1243`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:75-85, 233-234`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:46-50, 80-82`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:314-318`

**What the user perceives:** Offline, the user reads "Network error: The Internet connection appears to be offline.". A panel hiccup gives "Data decode error: The data couldn't be read because it isn't in the correct format.". Detail pages print this in red under a bare "Error" headline (S03-series-detail-loading.png); Settings prints "Could not fetch info: Server error: HTTP 404" in red inside a form row (T02-settings-2.png). With the app language set to Turkish on an English phone, the sentence is half Turkish ("Ağ hatası:") and half English, because the second half comes from the system. Apple's apps state what happened in plain words in secondary colour and offer one action.

**Mechanism (finder):** XtreamError and M3UServiceError wrap `error.localizedDescription` into an L() format string (XtreamAPIClient.swift:13-16; M3UService.swift:13-15). Views and stores then store `error.localizedDescription` as a String (PlaylistContentStore.swift:155, 202, 217; MovieDetailView.swift:309; SeriesView.swift:1243) and print it with `.foregroundColor(.red)` (MovieDetailView.swift:110-111; SeriesView.swift:945-946; PlaylistSettingsView.swift:77-79, 233-234; EPGSettingsSections.swift:47-49, 81; DownloadsView.swift:315-317). URLError's description follows the system locale, while L() follows the in-app override (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:29-58). Because the error is flattened to a String, no layer can tell offline from timeout from a wrong server.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add one mapper and use it wherever an error reaches the screen:

```swift
struct UserFacingError: Equatable { let title: String; let message: String; let symbol: String }
extension UserFacingError {
    init(_ error: Error) {
        let underlying: Error = { if case XtreamError.networkError(let e) = error { return e }; return error }()
        switch (underlying as? URLError)?.code {
        case .notConnectedToInternet, .networkConnectionLost, .dataNotAllowed:
            self.init(title: L("error.offline.title"), message: L("error.offline.message"), symbol: "wifi.slash")
        case .timedOut, .cannotFindHost, .cannotConnectToHost, .dnsLookupFailed:
            self.init(title: L("error.unreachable.title"), message: L("error.unreachable.message"), symbol: "exclamationmark.icloud")
        default: /* .unauthenticated, .serverError(status), .decodingError -> one short sentence each */
        }
    }
}
```
Render with ContentUnavailableView (full-screen cases) or a `.secondary` footnote row (form rows). Keep red for destructive actions only. Keep the technical text for the log (UIUtils/Log.swift). About six new keys in the ten Localizable.strings files; added as new lines, the uncommitted tip keys are not moved or changed.

**APIs:** URLError.Code (.notConnectedToInternet, .timedOut, .cannotFindHost, ...) (Foundation, all iOS versions (Foundation.swiftinterface:21454; NSURLError.h:113)); ContentUnavailableView (iOS 17.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574))

**Verifier reasons:** Claim verified from code and screenshots. Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:13,15 and Networking/M3UService.swift:13,15 format `error.localizedDescription` into an L() string (en: "Network error: %@", "Data decode error: %@"; tr: "Ağ hatası: %@"). L() follows the in-app override stored in UserDefaults (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:75-92); the app never sets AppleLanguages (grep: no hits), so the URLError/DecodingError half follows the system language. The mix is real for anyone using the in-app language picker. The flattened String is then stored (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:155,202,217,228,276; Views/MovieDetailView.swift:309; Views/SeriesView.swift:1243; Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:468,507,531) and drawn in red (MovieDetailView.swift:106-121, SeriesView.swift:941-956, PlaylistSettingsView.swift:77-79 and 233-234, EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:47-49 and 81, DownloadsView.swift:315-317). Screenshots confirm: iphone-light/S03-series-detail-loading.png shows a bare "Error" headline with red "Server error: HTTP 404"; iphone-light/T02-settings-2.png shows red "Could not fetch info: Server error: HTTP 404" in a form row. No comment or history marks this as deliberate; the only deliberate error view is Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift (commit 0ab5bcd), which already uses secondary colour, and ContentUnavailableView is already used in 8 other places, so the two detail errorViews are the outliers. Why only partly: (1) the mapper as sketched unwraps only XtreamError.networkError; the same wrapping exists in M3UServiceError.networkError (M3UService.swift:13), EPGError.network (EPG/EPGError.swift:18) and EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:97, and URLError.cancelled / CancellationError are not handled. (2) "Keep the technical text for the log" would hide HTTP status codes that this project uses for support (e.g. a panel answering HTTP 884 means get.php is blocked); the code must stay visible in the sentence. (3) A much smaller change reaches every call site: do the URLError-code mapping inside the four `errorDescription` implementations, so the ~25 `error.localizedDescription` call sites need no edits and no store type changes. (4) Red caption for a failed download row (DownloadsView.swift:315-317) is a status colour, not a defect; leave it.

**Corrected claim:** User-facing error text is built by formatting system `localizedDescription` strings into app-localized prefixes in four error enums (XtreamError, M3UServiceError, EPGError, CatchupURLResolver's error). The result is technical wording ("Network error: ...", "Data decode error: ...") and, for users of the in-app language picker, a sentence in two languages. Movie and series detail replace the page with a hand-rolled view that prints it in red under a bare "Error" title; the Xtream settings form and EPG settings print it in red rows. The failed-download caption in red is acceptable and not part of the problem.

**Corrected fix:** 1) Add one small helper (e.g. `enum NetworkErrorText { static func describe(_ error: Error) -> String }`) that switches on `(error as? URLError)?.code`: notConnectedToInternet / networkConnectionLost / dataNotAllowed -> L("error.offline"); timedOut / cannotFindHost / cannotConnectToHost / dnsLookupFailed -> L("error.unreachable"); cancelled -> existing cancelled text; default -> one generic localized sentence. Call it from the `.networkError` / `.network` cases of XtreamError, M3UServiceError, EPGError and the CatchupURLResolver error, and give `.decodingError` a fixed localized sentence ("The server sent an unexpected response"). Keep the HTTP status code in the server-error sentence. Log the raw error through Log (UIUtils/Log.swift). Call sites stay unchanged. 2) Replace the two detail errorViews (MovieDetailView.swift:106-121, SeriesView.swift:941-956) with `ContentUnavailableView { Label(title, systemImage:) } description: { Text(message) } actions: { Button(L("common.try_again")) {...} }`, and optionally CatalogLoadErrorView for consistency. 3) In PlaylistSettingsView.swift:77-79 and 233-234 and EPGSettingsSections.swift:47-49, 81 use `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)` with footnote size. Leave DownloadsView and Models/TipStore.swift:96 alone. About four new keys added as new lines in the ten Localizable.strings files; the tip keys are not moved. A structured UserFacingError with title and symbol is optional and only needed if the full-screen cases should show different icons per cause.

**API check:** ContentUnavailableView: `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, *) public struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17575; no gate needed on iOS 18. URLError.Code static members found in Foundation.swiftinterface: cancelled :21424, cannotFindHost :21436, networkConnectionLost :21442, dnsLookupFailed :21445, notConnectedToInternet :21454, dataNotAllowed :21555 (all iOS versions). Log helper exists at UIUtils/Log.swift.

**Regression risks:** Dropping the HTTP status code or the server detail from the visible text would make user bug reports useless; keep the code. DownloadManager persists `errorMessage` into the database at failure time (Models/DownloadManager.swift:179,221,845), so rows written before the change keep the old wording. The dashboard alert (Views/DashboardView.swift:138-155) and add-playlist alerts show the same strings and change wording too; check they still read well with their prefixes ("Error refreshing content: %@", "Could not fetch info: %@"). Localizable.strings files hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys: add lines only. No tests reference these strings (grep of the test targets found none).

**How to verify:** Unit tests: XtreamError.networkError(URLError(.notConnectedToInternet)).localizedDescription equals L("error.offline") and contains no system text; XtreamError.serverError("HTTP 404") still contains "404"; same for M3UServiceError and EPGError. A test that every new key exists in all ten .lproj files. Then re-shoot S03 (series detail with the demo server answering 404) and T02 and compare: no red text, system empty-state layout. Manual: set app language to Turkish on an English simulator, turn networking off, open a movie detail; the whole sentence must be Turkish.

## states-loading-empty-error-12 — During the first import the add-playlist sheet shows a floating card that says "Downloading categories..." for the whole download, the form stays editable, and Cancel closes the sheet while the import keeps running

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Add Xtream playlist, Add M3U playlist
- Code: `Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:85-111, 119, 122-126, 193-211`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:104-134, 143, 185-224`, `Models/XtreamImporter.swift:23-41`, `Views/Components/LoadingProcessView.swift:3-53`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Cancel during import: abort and discard (proposed), or simply disable Cancel while importing, which is the smallest change. Also whether the app should open the new playlist directly after a successful import instead of returning to the list; that belongs to the add-playlist lens.

**What the user perceives:** After Save, a white card with a 1.5x spinner floats over the form. For a large panel it reads "Downloading categories..." for tens of seconds, although movies and series are what is being downloaded, and then "Saving to database... Please wait.". The text fields behind the card can still be tapped and edited. Tapping Cancel dismisses the sheet, and some time later a playlist appears in the list anyway. If the import failed after Cancel, its error alert has nowhere to show.

**Mechanism (finder):** The loading UI is an `.overlay` card as large as its content (AddPlaylistView.swift:97-111), so the Form under and around it stays interactive. Only the Save button is disabled (:94). Cancel calls dismiss() unconditionally (:86-88), and the import runs in an unstructured `Task { await savePlaylist() }` (:92) that nothing holds or cancels; interactiveDismissDisabled (:119) blocks only the swipe. XtreamImporter reports one message before the six parallel requests (XtreamImporter.swift:23) and one before the write (:41). The strings add_playlist.fetching_live / _movies / _series still exist in Localizable.strings but are no longer referenced. LoadingProcessView is dead code: its only reference is its own #Preview (LoadingProcessView.swift:56).

**Proposed fix (finder):** ```swift
@State private var saveTask: Task<Void, Never>?

Form { ... }.disabled(isLoading)
.toolbar {
    ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) {
        Button(L("common.cancel")) { saveTask?.cancel(); dismiss() }
    }
    ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) {
        if isLoading { ProgressView() }
        else { Button(L("common.save")) { saveTask = Task { await savePlaylist() } }.disabled(!canSave) }
    }
}
.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) {       // replaces the floating card
    if isLoading, let progressMessage { Label(progressMessage, systemImage: "arrow.down.circle").font(.footnote).padding() }
}
```
In XtreamImporter.syncAndSave add `try Task.checkCancellation()` before the playlist row is saved (line 36), so a cancelled import leaves nothing behind, and return silently from the catch blocks when `Task.isCancelled`. Replace the single message with a count of finished endpoints ("Downloading... 4 of 6") or a determinate `ProgressView(value:total:)`. Delete LoadingProcessView or use it; the same applies to the unused phase strings. Same changes in AddM3UPlaylistView.

**APIs:** View.interactiveDismissDisabled(_:) (iOS 15.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23591-23593)); View.safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 15.0 (SwiftUI; standard modifier, signature not grepped in this run))

**Verifier reasons:** Claim verified. Views/AddPlaylistView.swift:97-111 and Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:121-134 draw the loading state as an `.overlay` VStack that is only as large as its content, so the Form stays hit-testable; only Save is disabled (AddPlaylistView.swift:94, AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:39-40,111). Cancel calls dismiss() with no isLoading check (AddPlaylistView.swift:86-88; AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:105) while the import runs in an unstructured `Task { await savePlaylist() }` (:92 / :109) that nobody holds, so it continues after dismissal, writes the playlist (Models/XtreamImporter.swift:36-38, 51-91) and sets alert state on a view that is gone (AddPlaylistView.swift:205-210). History supports this being an oversight, not a choice: commit 0ab5bcd added `.interactiveDismissDisabled(isLoading)` with the comment at AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:141-142 that a swipe "left the Task invisibly in the background" - the Cancel button has the same effect and was missed. The single message is real: XtreamImporter.swift:23 reports "Downloading categories..." once before six parallel requests (parallelism is deliberate, comment at :20-21) and :41 reports "Saving to database... Please wait."; add_playlist.fetching_live/_movies/_series have no code references. PanelURLSession allows up to 300 s per resource (Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:28-29), so the wait can be long. LoadingProcessView has no reference besides its own #Preview (grep). Why only partly: the fix's promise that a cancelled import "leaves nothing behind" does not hold as written. XtreamImporter writes in two transactions (playlist row at :36-38, content at :51-91) and GRDB 7 async writes honour task cancellation (GRDB/Core/SerializedDatabase.swift:256-264, Database.swift:370-372 throw CancellationError and roll back). A Cancel that lands during the content write rolls back the content but leaves the already committed playlist row: an empty playlist appears in the list (in edit mode: new credentials are saved although the user cancelled). `Task.checkCancellation()` before line 36 does not close that window. Also touches_user_wip is true, not false: a counter string or removing unused keys edits the ten Localizable.strings files that carry the uncommitted tip keys.

**Corrected claim:** As stated, with one addition: the progress text is also wrong in the Settings refresh and first-load paths, which use the same single "Downloading categories..." phase (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:452, 482).

**Corrected fix:** Keep the proposed UI: `@State private var saveTask: Task<Void, Never>?`; `Form { ... }.disabled(isLoading)`; set `focusedField = nil` on Save; replace Save with a ProgressView in `.confirmationAction` while loading; show the phase text in a `.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)` footnote (or a Form section footer) instead of the floating card. Cancellation, corrected: Cancel does `saveTask?.cancel(); dismiss()` only while the network phase runs. Make the database phase uninterruptible so no half state can exist: in XtreamImporter.syncAndSave call `try Task.checkCancellation()` after the six fetches, then run both writes inside `try await Task { ... }.value` (the same shield pattern as Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:243-248), and report the saving phase so the views can disable Cancel while it runs. M3UImporter.replace is a single transaction (Models/M3UImporter.swift:30-32) and needs only the cancellation check before it. In the catch blocks return without setting alert state when `Task.isCancelled`; in AddM3UPlaylistView add `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` after `addAsXtream` returns false (:267-271), otherwise a cancelled verify falls through to the plain M3U download. Progress text: count finished endpoints on the main actor and show "Downloading... n of 6" (one new key in ten languages, added as new lines) or reuse a neutral existing string; keep the six requests parallel. Delete Views/Components/LoadingProcessView.swift and the unused keys only if the owner wants the cleanup. Smallest alternative (product decision): disable Cancel while isLoading; that fixes the ghost import but leaves the user without an exit for up to five minutes on a dead panel.

**API check:** View.interactiveDismissDisabled(_:): `@available(iOS 15.0, ...)` at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23591-23593. View.safeAreaInset(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment:spacing:content:): `@available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, *)` at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19075-19082 (the finding had not grepped it; it exists). ProgressView.init(value:total:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:3985. Task.checkCancellation / Task.isCancelled: Swift concurrency standard library. GRDB (7.x, Package.resolved pins master 36e30a6) throws CancellationError from async `write` in a cancelled task: GRDB/Core/SerializedDatabase.swift:256-264.

**Regression risks:** Cancellation propagates into the six `async let` requests as URLError.cancelled wrapped in XtreamError.networkError; without the `Task.isCancelled` guard this would surface as an error alert. Without the shield around the writes, a cancel during the content transaction leaves an empty playlist row (new) or half-applied credentials (edit). The comment at XtreamImporter.swift:10-11 and :35 says the playlist row is saved first on purpose so it stays visible if content insertion fails; keep that order. `.disabled(isLoading)` on the Form also applies during the local-file read in AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:162-175, which is fine. The M3U Xtream auto-detect fallback (verify fails -> plain M3U) must not be triggered by a cancelled verify. String edits touch files with uncommitted tip keys: add or remove other lines only.

**How to verify:** Unit test with a stub URLSession that delays responses: start XtreamImporter.syncAndSave in a Task, cancel it during the fetch, assert no playlist row and no category rows exist for that id. Second test: cancel after the saving phase was reported and assert the playlist and its content are both present. UI check on a simulator with a slow mock panel: after Save the fields are disabled and the Save button shows a spinner; Cancel during download closes the sheet and no playlist appears within 30 s; Cancel is disabled while "Saving" is shown. Screenshot of the progress state on iPhone and iPad.

## states-loading-empty-error-13 — A long catalog refresh shows only the pull spinner, the progress text is published but never drawn, and nothing tells the user how old the catalog is or refreshes it automatically

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Settings (Xtream)
- Code: `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-125, 195-220, 280-285, 447-470`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:66-74, 242-249`, `Views/VODView.swift:39-47`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:32-44`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should the catalog refresh by itself when it is older than some threshold (for example 24 hours, in the background after launch, as the EPG does)? It costs a full panel download per refresh and some panels rate-limit, so this is a product decision. Also whether a permanent "Updated ..." subtitle is wanted or only the in-progress text.

**What the user perceives:** Pulling to refresh Movies on a 150k-title panel leaves the small system spinner at the top for the whole download and database write, possibly a minute, with no text. Otherwise the catalog is exactly as old as the last manual refresh: offline launch correctly shows the stored catalog, but so does every online launch, and the app never says "updated 3 weeks ago". The TV guide does both: it refreshes when stale and shows its last update time.

**Mechanism (finder):** refreshFromNetwork forwards the phase text to `loadingMessage` (PlaylistContentStore.swift:197-199, 212-214), but the only readers are inside the `displayCategories.isEmpty` branch (LiveStreamsView.swift:70; VODView.swift:43; SeriesView.swift:44), which cannot be reached while content is on screen. loadPlaylist goes to the network only when the playlist has zero categories (PlaylistContentStore.swift:115-116, 280-285). No sync timestamp is stored for the catalog; the EPG side has one (EPGSettingsSections.swift:32-44).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Store a per-playlist, per-type `catalogSyncedAt` date. UserDefaults keyed like HiddenCategoryStore is enough, with no migration; write it after each successful replace*Catalog. 2) Show status where iOS 26 puts it:

```swift
if #available(iOS 26, *) {
    content.navigationSubtitle(Text(contentStore.loadingMessage ?? lastUpdatedText))   // tab roots, via dashboardNavigation
} else { content }   // iOS 18: no subtitle; the pull spinner stays the only indicator
```
3) In Settings add a "Last updated" row under "Refresh all" using `Text(date, style: .relative)`, as the EPG section does; this works on iOS 18 too. Place it in the first section, away from the TipJarRow() line.

**APIs:** View.navigationSubtitle(_:) (iOS 26.0 on iOS (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:18677-18691); needs an #available gate, the iOS 18 fallback is no subtitle); Text(_:style:) with .relative (iOS 14.0 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:7530))

**Verifier reasons:** The facts hold. Both refreshFromNetwork variants publish the phase text (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:197-199, 212-214) but the only readers of `loadingMessage` are inside the `displayCategories.isEmpty` branches (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:65-70, Views/VODView.swift:43, Views/SeriesView.swift:33-44); during a pull-to-refresh content is on screen, so the text is never drawn. The pull spinner stays up for the whole job because of `await work.value` (LiveStreamsView.swift:242-249). loadPlaylist goes to the network only when the playlist has zero categories (PlaylistContentStore.swift:115-116, 280-285), and no catalog sync time exists anywhere: Models/Playlist.swift has only createdAt, and the only lastSuccess fields are EPG ones (EPG/EPGStore.swift:51, EPGSettingsSections.swift:32-44). Why only partly: (1) a spinner without text during pull-to-refresh is the system behaviour, so the first part is a refinement, not a defect; the real gap is the missing "last updated" information and the fact that the catalog never refreshes by itself, and the latter is a product decision as the finding says. (2) The fix as written has gaps: the timestamp is written only after replace*Catalog, but the first import goes through XtreamImporter.syncAndSave (Models/XtreamImporter.swift:51-91), which does not call those helpers, so a fresh playlist would show no date until its first manual refresh; replace*Catalog run inside the database transaction, so the write must happen after `AppDatabase.shared.write` returns, not inside them. (3) DashboardNavigationModifier (Views/DashboardView.swift:220-245) does not observe the store; it needs `@ObservedObject` for the subtitle to update. (4) `loadingMessage` is one global value with the misleading text "Downloading categories..." (PlaylistContentStore.swift:452, 482); shown as a subtitle it would appear under every tab, including Settings, during a Movies refresh.

**Corrected claim:** The app keeps no record of when a playlist's catalog was last synced and never refreshes it on its own; the user has to know to pull down or use Settings > Refresh all. The EPG side already has both a stale check and a "last updated" row. While a manual refresh runs, the only indicator is the system pull spinner; the phase text the store publishes is not drawn anywhere while content is visible. Low severity; automatic refresh and a permanent "Updated ..." subtitle are product decisions.

**Corrected fix:** 1) Store `catalogSyncedAt` per playlist and content type in UserDefaults (same keying as Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:19,36), written after the write call returns successfully in both syncFromNetworkReplacingLocal variants (PlaylistContentStore.swift:465-470, 489-507) and at the end of XtreamImporter.syncAndSave; remove the keys when the playlist is deleted. Existing installs have no value: show no row rather than "Never". 2) Settings: add a "Last updated" row directly under "Refresh all" in the first section of Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift (after :73), built like EPGSettingsSections.swift:32-37 with `Text(date, style: .relative)`; this is far from the TipJarRow() line at :355. This part works on iOS 18 and is the piece worth doing first. 3) Optional, iOS 26 only: in DashboardNavigationModifier add `@ObservedObject private var contentStore = PlaylistContentStore.shared` and, when `type != nil`, `if #available(iOS 26, *) { content.navigationSubtitle(Text(subtitle)) } else { content }` where subtitle is a neutral "Updating..." string while a refresh for that tab's type is running and otherwise empty (or the relative date, if the owner wants a permanent subtitle). iOS 18 fallback: no subtitle, the pull spinner remains the only indicator. Do not show the raw "Downloading categories..." text. 4) Automatic refresh when stale is left to the owner.

**API check:** View.navigationSubtitle: `@available(iOS 26.0, macCatalyst 14.0, macOS 11.0, *)` extension at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:18677-18691 with overloads `(_ subtitle: Text)`, `(_ subtitleKey: LocalizedStringKey)` and `<S: StringProtocol>(_ subtitle: S)`; needs `if #available(iOS 26, *)`. `Text.init(_ date: Date, style: Text.DateStyle)` at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:7530 inside an `@available(iOS 14.0, ...)` block; already used at Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:36.

**Regression risks:** Adding @ObservedObject to DashboardNavigationModifier makes the four tab roots' modifier bodies re-run on every store publish; the root views already observe the same store, so the cost is small, but keep the modifier body cheap. How a subtitle sits under the large title together with .searchable on iOS 26 needs a visual check. An automatic refresh would add a full panel download per launch and some panels rate-limit; do not add it without the owner's decision. Settings views contain the uncommitted TipJarRow() line and Localizable.strings the tip keys: add one row and one key, change nothing else there. `Text(date, style: .relative)` ticks every second, as the EPG row already does.

**How to verify:** Unit test for the timestamp store: set after a simulated successful sync, unchanged after a thrown sync, removed on playlist delete, present right after XtreamImporter.syncAndSave. Simulator, iOS 26: pull to refresh on Movies with a slow mock panel and screenshot the navigation bar (subtitle visible, large title not clipped, search field in place), then check Live TV shows no subtitle. iOS 18 simulator: screens unchanged. Settings screenshot showing the new row under "Refresh all".

## search-ux-1 — Global Search uses a locale-dependent matcher: on a Turkish-locale device "film", "bein" and "history" do not find FILM / BEIN / HISTORY, and no query matches across accents or punctuation.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:126-128, 260-271`, `Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:9-30`, `another-iptv-playerTests/CatalogTextSearchTests.swift:23-38`

**What the user perceives:** A user whose iPhone is set to Turkish types "bein" or "film" in the Search tab and gets "No Results", although the same text typed into the Live TV or Movies field finds the channel. On any device "sehir" does not find "Şehir", "amelie" does not find "Amélie", "spiderman" does not find "Spider-Man". Search looks broken or the catalog looks incomplete.

**Mechanism (finder):** SearchView.swift:126-128 matches with `text.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains(token)`, which compares under Locale.current and does no diacritic folding. A probe compiled against Foundation and run with `-AppleLocale tr_TR` returned false for "FILM 4K"/"film", "BEIN SPORTS 1"/"bein" and "HISTORY HD"/"history"; under en_US it returned false for "Şehir"/"sehir", "İSTANBUL"/"istanbul" and "Spider-Man"/"spiderman". Every other search site uses CatalogTextSearch, whose comment (CatalogTextSearch.swift:9-12) and tests (CatalogTextSearchTests.swift:23-38) record the fix for exactly this. The Search tab's matcher was never migrated: git log shows it unchanged since d2489f9 (654cefc only added `nonisolated`).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Delete the private `search(_:in:)` and filter through CatalogTextSearch with the query prepared once:

```swift
// CatalogTextSearch.swift
static func matcher(for search: String) -> (String) -> Bool {
    let words = search.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace)
        .map { normalize(String($0)) }.filter { !$0.isEmpty }
    return { text in let t = normalize(text); return words.allSatisfy(t.contains) }
}
// SearchView.runSearch
let matches = CatalogTextSearch.matcher(for: q)
live.filter { !hiddenLive.contains($0.stream.categoryId ?? "") && matches($0.stream.name) }
```

Cost: the CatalogTextSearch scan measured 612 ms per 150k names against 123 ms for the current matcher (dev Mac, -O, synthetic catalog). Land it together with the faster scalar fold from the Arabic finding (150 ms per 150k) or the pre-folded index (3 ms). No availability fork.

**APIs:** String.folding(options:locale:) (Foundation, already in use) (iOS 2.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The claim is fully confirmed; only the proposed code needs a one-line guard.

- **Code:** Views/SearchView.swift:126-128 matches with `text.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains($0)`; it is used at 261, 265 and 269. Every other search site goes through `CatalogTextSearch.matches` (grep: VODView, LiveStreamsView, SeriesView, M3U*, Favorites, Downloads, WatchHistory, CategoryPickerSheet).
- **History:** blame shows line 127 dates from fe550171 (the original app); 654cefc only added `nonisolated`. Commit 0ab5bcd ("Search: locale-invariant normalization") fixed Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:6-19 and Database/Persistence.swift:105-113 but never touched the Search tab matcher. No comment marks it as deliberate.
- **Reproduced:** I compiled my own probe (scratchpad/agents/verify-search/v.swift) and ran it with `-AppleLocale tr_TR -AppleLanguages (tr)`. FILM 4K/film, BEIN SPORTS/bein, Titanic/TITANIC and TITANIC/titanic all returned false; under en_US all returned true. The app ships tr.lproj, so a Turkish-language iPhone gets `Locale.current` = tr.
- **Scope is wider than stated:** any i/I case mismatch fails, so by the same mechanism a lowercase query misses any title with a capital I ("inception" vs "Inception"), not only ALL-CAPS names.
- **Accents and punctuation:** the auditor's probe returned false for Şehir/sehir under every locale I ran, and their bench probes returned false for Amélie/amelie and Spider-Man/spiderman.
- **Defect in the proposed `matcher(for:)`:** it drops words that normalize to empty, so a punctuation-only query ("--", "!!") leaves `words` empty and `allSatisfy` returns true for the whole catalog. I compiled it: `matcher(for: "--")("FOX TV")` is true. The existing `matches` returns false there, because Foundation's `"abc".contains("")` is false.
- **Cost:** re-running the auditor's bench gave 116-152 ms per 150k names for the current matcher, 551-663 ms for `CatalogTextSearch.matches`, and 400-425 ms for a matcher with the query normalized once.

**Corrected claim:** The Search tab (Views/SearchView.swift:126-128) still uses `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains`, which the rest of the app replaced in 0ab5bcd. On a device whose language is Turkish, any query whose i/I case differs from the title finds nothing ("film" vs FILM, "bein" vs BEIN, "titanic" vs TITANIC, "inception" vs Inception). On every device it does no diacritic or punctuation folding (sehir/Şehir, amelie/Amélie, spiderman/Spider-Man). The same text typed into the Live TV, Movies or Series field does match, so the two searches disagree.

**Corrected fix:** Delete the private `search(_:in:)` and route the three scans in `runSearch` through CatalogTextSearch with the query prepared once, plus an empty-words guard:

```swift
static func matcher(for search: String) -> @Sendable (String) -> Bool {
    let words = search.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace)
        .map { normalize(String($0)) }.filter { !$0.isEmpty }
    guard !words.isEmpty else { return { _ in false } }   // "--" must not match the whole catalog
    return { text in let t = normalize(text); return words.allSatisfy { t.contains($0) } }
}
```

- Mark the closure `@Sendable`; it is captured by `Task.detached`.
- Best landed as part of search-ux-3's single-pass `rankedFilter`, so the Search tab gets matching and ranking in one normalize per name.
- Land search-ux-5 with it: the scan gets about 3-4x slower, which lengthens the false "No Results" flash.
- No availability fork.

**API check:** - `String.folding(options:locale:)`: found in Foundation.swiftmodule/arm64-apple-ios-simulator.swiftinterface:22567, `public func folding(options: Swift.String.CompareOptions = [], locale: Foundation.Locale?) -> Swift.String`. Already used at Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:14.
- No SwiftUI or UIKit API involved.
- The proposed matcher and the empty-words behaviour compiled and ran with `swiftc -O -swift-version 5`.

**Regression risks:** - Without the guard, a punctuation-only query returns every item.
- The scan costs about 400 ms per 150k names instead of about 120 ms (dev Mac, off-main), so results arrive later until search-ux-3 or the index lands.
- Matching becomes more permissive: the collapsed key lets "eta" match "The Tale" across a word boundary. That is already the behaviour of every inline field, so it is consistent.
- Database/Persistence.swift:105 says the SQL `normalize` must stay in sync with `CatalogTextSearch.normalize`. If the fold itself is changed (the "scalar fold" mentioned in the finding), change both.
- UserFlowsUITests and ScreensUITests search tests only assert that a mock result exists, so they are unaffected.

**How to verify:** - Unit tests in CatalogTextSearchTests for `matcher(for:)`: FILM 4K/film, BEIN SPORTS 1/bein, Şehir/sehir, Spider-Man/spiderman, and "--" matching nothing.
- UI test launched with `-AppleLanguages (tr) -AppleLocale tr_TR`: type a lowercase query containing "i" against a mock title with a capital I in the Search tab and assert the row exists.
- Independent probe source: scratchpad/agents/verify-search/v.swift.

## search-ux-2 — Global Search orders hits alphabetically and shows four per section, so the best match is usually not on screen.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:154, 178, 203, 262, 266, 270`, `Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:40-83`

**What the user perceives:** Q03-search-results-mi.png: typing "mi" lists "Family Ties" above "Midnight Horizon". Typing "bat" on a real catalog shows the four alphabetically first titles that contain "bat" anywhere (the probe ordered a sample as Abattoir, Acrobat, Alita: Battle Angel, Batman Begins, Combat Zone, EN - Batman). "Batman" only appears after tapping "N more results" and scrolling past every earlier title. The same query in All Movies puts "Batman Begins" first, so the two searches disagree.

**Mechanism (finder):** runSearch sorts each result set with `localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare` (SearchView.swift:262, 266, 270) and the All scope renders `prefix(4)` (lines 154, 178, 203). The per-category and All-* screens use CatalogTextSearch.sortXByRelevance (exact, then name prefix, then alphabetical; CatalogTextSearch.swift:40-83). Neither path has a word-start tier, so catalogs that prefix names ("EN - Batman", "TR: ...") fall through to plain alphabetical order in both.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use one ranking for every search site, with the tier computed once per hit in the filter pass:
- 0: exact
- 1: name starts with the query
- 2: a word starts with the query (fold the name a second time keeping single spaces and test `spaced.hasPrefix(q) || spaced.contains(" " + q)`)
- 3: substring
Tie-break alphabetically.

In SearchView replace the three `.sorted { localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare }` calls with it. For the All scope only the best four per section are needed, so select the top four instead of sorting everything. Keep the existing collapsed-key matching ("foxtv" finds "FOX TV"); the spaced key is for ranking only.

**Verifier reasons:** The alphabetical order and the four-row cap are real; the fix has one part that cannot work as written and the severity is overstated.

- **Code:** Views/SearchView.swift:262, 266, 270 sort each result set with `localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare`; lines 154, 178, 203 show `prefix(4)` in the All scope. No comment or commit marks alphabetical order as a choice; the lines date from fe550171.
- **Inline fields rank differently:** Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:40-83 orders exact, then prefix, then alphabetical, and Models/VODSortOption.swift:40-42 keeps that order under the default sort ("preserve caller's ordering (sortIndex or search relevance)"). So the two searches do disagree.
- **Screenshot:** iphone-light/Q03-search-results-mi.png shows "Family Ties" above "Midnight Horizon" for "mi".
- **Probe:** the auditor's probe output for "bat" is Abattoir, Acrobat, Alita: Battle Angel, Batman Begins, Combat Zone, EN - Batman.
- **"Select the top four instead of sorting everything" does not fit the code.** The same `liveResults` / `movieResults` / `seriesResults` arrays feed the per-type scopes (lines 154, 178, 203 when the filter is not All; "N more results" only flips the filter) and the player queue (line 299, `queue: liveResults.map(\.stream)`). The full arrays must stay fully ordered.
- **The word-start tier is a ranking change, not parity.** No existing path has it, and the SQL ordering in Models/Requests.swift:76-80 would stay three-tier.
- **Severity:** hits are not lost and a full-word query narrows quickly. The bad case is short queries and short exact titles ("ted", "up", "bat"). I rate it medium.

**Corrected claim:** The Search tab orders each section alphabetically (Views/SearchView.swift:262, 266, 270) and shows four rows per section in the All scope. For short queries the exact or prefix match is often below the fold, and the order differs from the exact / prefix / alphabetical ranking that the category and All-* screens use.

**Corrected fix:** 1. **Parity (the fix):** use the same exact / prefix / alphabetical ranking in the Search tab, through search-ux-3's single-pass `rankedFilter`. Do not call the current `sortXByRelevance`; it is the slow path. Keep the full sorted arrays, because the per-type scopes and the live player queue read them. `prefix(4)` then shows the top-ranked four.
2. **Word-start tier (optional, owner's decision):** add it inside `rankedFilter` so every in-memory site gets it. Compute one "spaced" fold per name and derive the collapsed key from it, so there is no second fold per hit. Tiers 0 and 1 stay on the collapsed key so "foxtv" still ranks "FOX TV" first. Leave Requests.swift alone or update it knowingly.

**API check:** No SDK API involved; only Swift standard library and Foundation string calls already used in Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift.

**Regression risks:** - A top-four selection would break the per-type scopes and the live queue order (SearchView.swift:154, 299).
- A word-start tier changes the order on the category and All-* screens too. The existing tests `sortLivePrioritizesExactMatch` and `sortLivePrioritizesPrefixOverInfix` still pass with it (checked by reasoning: "Sports Tonight" is tier 1, "Today Sports" tier 2).
- A second fold per hit would add about 400 ms per 150k hits for broad queries.

**How to verify:** - Unit test: ["Acrobat", "EN - Batman", "Combat Zone", "Batman Begins"] with "bat" puts "Batman Begins" first (and "EN - Batman" second if the word-start tier is adopted).
- Existing CatalogTextSearchTests sort tests stay green.
- Re-shoot Q03 and expect "Midnight Horizon" above "Family Ties".
- In the Search tab, tap "N more results" and check the per-type list is the same order extended, and that channel next/previous follows it.

## search-ux-3 — The relevance sort re-normalizes both strings eight times per comparison, so a broad query in All Movies, All Series, All Channels or a large category leaves stale results on screen for seconds.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All Movies, All Series, All Channels, Movie category grid, Series category grid, Live category grid
- Code: `Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:13-19, 32-38, 45-52, 60-67, 75-82`, `Views/VODView.swift:583-588, 846-853`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:517-522, 744-751`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:555-560, 783-790`

**What the user perceives:** In All Movies on a 100k+ catalog the user types "t", "th", "the": the grid keeps showing the previous content for several seconds with no progress indication, the phone warms up, and results for an intermediate query can land late. Narrow queries are fine, which makes the lag look random.

**Mechanism (finder):** The comparator calls `equals` twice and `startsWith` twice (CatalogTextSearch.swift:45-52). Each of those normalizes the text and the query again (lines 32-38), and `normalize` is folding + replacingOccurrences + components + joined (13-19). That is 8 normalizations per comparison, times n log n comparisons. Measured with a copy of the code (swiftc -O, dev Mac, 150k synthetic names): filter 612 ms; sort 2,314 ms for 7,533 hits; 5,361 ms for 20,000 hits; 9,078 ms for 27,471 hits. The inline fields have no minimum length (VODView.swift:842-851), so one- and two-letter queries hit the worst case. The work runs in `Task.detached` and awaiting its value does not propagate cancellation, so every superseded query finishes its sort anyway.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest change, in CatalogTextSearch only: normalize once per item during the filter, keep the tier, sort on the tier.

```swift
static func rankedFilter<T>(_ items: [T], search: String, name: (T) -> String) -> [T] {
    let words = search.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace).map { normalize(String($0)) }
    let whole = normalize(search)
    var hits: [(tier: UInt8, item: T)] = []
    for item in items {
        let k = normalize(name(item))
        guard words.allSatisfy(k.contains) else { continue }
        hits.append((k == whole ? 0 : k.hasPrefix(whole) ? 1 : 2, item))
    }
    hits.sort { $0.tier != $1.tier ? $0.tier < $1.tier
        : name($0.item).localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare(name($1.item)) == .orderedAscending }
    return hits.map(\.item)
}
```

Measured on the same data: 434 ms + 122 ms instead of 612 ms + 9,078 ms. Replace the filter + sortXByRelevance pairs at the six call sites listed in files; work stays off the main thread.

Add cancellation at those sites: `let work = Task.detached { ... }; let r = await withTaskCancellationHandler { await work.value } onCancel: { work.cancel() }`, with a `Task.isCancelled` check every few thousand items.

**APIs:** withTaskCancellationHandler(operation:onCancel:) (Swift concurrency) (iOS 13.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism, the measurements and the fix all hold.

- **Code:** Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:45-52 (and 60-67, 75-82) calls `equals` twice and `startsWith` twice per comparison. Each normalizes both the text and the query (lines 32-38), and `normalize` is folding + replacingOccurrences + components + joined (13-19). That is 8 normalizations per comparison.
- **Call sites checked:** Views/VODView.swift:583-586 and 848-851, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:517-520 and 746-749, Views/SeriesView.swift:555-558 and 785-788. All use `Task.detached { filter; sortXByRelevance }.value`.
- **No minimum length:** the inline fields push any non-empty text after 280 ms (VODView.swift:565-572).
- **Cancellation:** awaiting `.value` of a detached task does not cancel it, so a superseded query runs its full sort.
- **Benchmark re-run** (scratchpad/agents/search/bench, 150k synthetic names, dev Mac, -O):
  - filter: 551-663 ms
  - sort, 7,414 hits: 2,261 ms
  - sort, 20,000 hits: 5,126 ms
  - sort, 27,498 hits: 8,822 ms
  - single pass (bench2): 400-425 ms filter + 114 ms sort for 27k hits, 628 ms for 131k hits
- **Fix compiles:** I compiled the proposed `rankedFilter` verbatim (scratchpad/agents/verify-search/v.swift, Swift 5 mode). It returned Sports, Sports News, sports plus, Sports Tonight, Today Sports for "sports", which is the existing order, and [] for "--", which is the existing behaviour.
- **Not deliberate:** the comments only require the work to be off-main; nothing defends the comparator's shape. `VODSortOption.apply` (Models/VODSortOption.swift:40-42) relies on the caller's relevance order, so the order must be kept, and the fix keeps it.
- **One inaccuracy:** stale results cannot land late. Each site has `guard !Task.isCancelled` after the await and `.task(id:)` cancels the old task. The real effect is the stale grid staying up while orphaned sorts hold cores.
- **Perception:** the UI does not hang, but with 100k+ movies a query like "the" or "a" leaves the old grid on screen for many seconds.

**Corrected claim:** The relevance sort normalizes text and query 8 times per comparison (Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:45-52). A broad query in All Movies, All Series, All Channels or a large category keeps the previous grid on screen for seconds (about 9 s for 27k hits on a dev Mac) with no progress indication. Superseded queries are never cancelled, so their sorts keep running and slow the current one. Results for a superseded query are dropped, not shown late.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with small adjustments:

- Add `rankedFilter` to CatalogTextSearch: normalize once per item, keep the tier, sort on (tier, `localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare`).
- Write the predicate as a closure, `words.allSatisfy { k.contains($0) }`.
- Add a `Task.isCancelled` check every few thousand items.
- Keep `sortLiveByRelevance` / `sortVODByRelevance` / `sortSeriesByRelevance` as thin wrappers, or reimplement them with a precomputed tier, so the existing tests and the unused store helpers (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:53-96) still compile.
- Replace the filter + sort pairs at the six call sites; the hidden-category filter stays in front, in the same detached task.
- Wrap the await: `let work = Task.detached { ... }; let r = await withTaskCancellationHandler { await work.value } onCancel: { work.cancel() }`.

**API check:** - `withTaskCancellationHandler(operation:onCancel:isolation:)`: found in usr/lib/swift/_Concurrency.swiftmodule/arm64-apple-ios-simulator.swiftinterface:2879-2881, `@available(iOS 13.0, *)`, `@backDeployed(before: iOS 18.0)`, `public func withTaskCancellationHandler<T>(operation: () async throws -> T, onCancel handler: @Sendable () -> Void, isolation: isolated (any Actor)? = #isolation) async rethrows -> T`. Usable on the iOS 18.0 target with no fork.
- `Task.detached`, `Task.isCancelled` and `Task.cancel()` are already used in these files.
- No SwiftUI API involved.

**Regression risks:** - The order must stay exact, then prefix, then alphabetical. Grids under the default sort depend on it (VODSortOption.swift:40-42), and CatalogTextSearchTests asserts it.
- `VODCategoryContent`'s Equatable check and `itemsToken` (count + first id + last id, VODView.swift:600-605, 641-647) are untouched.
- The off-main structure must be kept. Under `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor` (project.pbxproj:392-393) the helper has to stay inside the `nonisolated enum`, or it would run on the main actor.
- Cancelling mid-scan returns a partial array. The existing `guard !Task.isCancelled` after the await already discards it; keep that guard.

**How to verify:** - Existing CatalogTextSearchTests sort tests pass unchanged.
- Add a performance test: 150k synthetic names, queries "a" and "the", assert filter + rank under about 1.5 s on the simulator host.
- Device, real 100k+ catalog: in All Movies type "t", "th", "the" slowly and measure time from the debounce firing to the grid updating. Check in Instruments that no orphaned `CatalogTextSearch` sort keeps running after the next keystroke.

## search-ux-4 — Every search site re-folds the whole catalog per query, the Search tab runs its first query three times over and no scan is ever cancelled; a pre-folded index would make search fast enough to drop the 250 ms debounce and the two-character minimum.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort L · risk medium
- Screens: Search tab, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category and All grids, M3U channels
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:70-79, 140-142, 246-278`, `Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:21-30`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:37-48, 140-152, 366-406`, `Models/DBModels.swift:29, 61, 86`, `Views/VODView.swift:146-153, 565-572`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:113-127`

**What the user perceives:** In the Search tab nothing happens on the first character. Results come 250 ms plus the scan time after the last keystroke, and the first query of a session is the slowest. Deleting back to one character replaces the list with the placeholder at once. A one-character Chinese query can never be searched although the app ships a zh localization. In 14 of the 17 fields, tapping the clear button leaves the filtered content on screen for 250-280 ms.

**Mechanism (finder):** - Three `.task(id:)` modifiers (SearchView.swift:246-248) all fire on appear, each calling runSearch, which starts three `Task.detached` scans plus sorts (260-271): nine full passes for the first query.
- `async let x = Task.detached{}.value` is unstructured, so the `.task(id:)` cancellation never reaches the scans.
- Measured per type per 150k names (dev Mac, -O): 123 ms filter plus up to 744 ms alphabetical sort when most items hit.
- CatalogTextSearch.matches normalizes the name and every query word again for each item (lines 22, 27-29): 612 ms per 150k.
- Result arrays are unbounded (140-142) and each element id is a freshly interpolated String (DBModels.swift:29, 61, 86), which List diffing reads for every element when one scope shows all hits.
- The debounce block is copy-pasted 17 times with 250 or 280 ms; only M3UChannelsView:115-121, WatchHistoryListView:86-90 and M3UFavoritesView:48-52 skip the wait on empty text.
- The two-character minimum is at SearchView.swift:73.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. New Models/CatalogSearchIndex.swift: one flat `[UInt8]` of folded names plus `[UInt32]` offsets per content type, built in the existing off-main fetch helpers (PlaylistContentStore.swift:366-406 return it next to streams and byCategory; M3UContentStore.groupOffMain likewise). Positions equal array positions. Rebuild wherever the arrays are reassigned (146-151, 248, 260, 272, 311-316) and clear in clearLists. applyVODMetadata replaces in place, so positions stay valid. Measured: build 365 ms once per 150k (150 ms with the scalar fold from the Arabic finding), 4.2 MB, scan plus tier 2-3 ms per query, rank sort under 2 ms.
2. `index.search(query, limit: 200) -> (hits: [Int32], total: Int)`, used by SearchView, the three tab roots (group hits by category) and the category/All screens (filter hits by category id).
3. Cancellation: keep Task.detached wrapped in withTaskCancellationHandler. The project builds with SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES and default MainActor isolation (project.pbxproj:392-393), so a plain nonisolated async function would not leave the main actor.
4. One `.task(id: SearchKey(query, hiddenVersion, streamsLoaded))` in SearchResultsView instead of three.
5. Then lower the debounce to 0-100 ms, allow one character, and move the debounce into one shared helper that applies empty text immediately.

Equatable rows, paginated grids and off-main filtering stay as they are.

**APIs:** withTaskCancellationHandler(operation:onCancel:) (Swift concurrency) (iOS 13.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The individual mechanisms are real. The headline remedy (a pre-folded index, then dropping the debounce and the minimum everywhere) is an optimization and product choice, not a defect fix.

**Confirmed in code**
- Views/SearchView.swift:246-248 has three `.task(id:)` modifiers. All run on appear, each calls `runSearch`, which starts three detached scans and sorts (260-271). That is nine passes on mount.
- `SearchResultsView` is unmounted whenever the text drops below two characters (48, 73), so the triple run repeats on every re-entry, not only once per session.
- `async let x = Task.detached {}.value` does not propagate cancellation.
- `CatalogTextSearch.matches` re-normalizes the name and every query word per item (Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:22, 27-29).
- There are 17 copy-pasted debounce blocks at 250 or 280 ms (grep, excluding the two zap debounces).
- project.pbxproj:392-393 does set `SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES` and `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`, so the note about plain nonisolated async functions is right.
- `M3UContentStore.groupOffMain` exists (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:125).
- Benchmark re-run: 357-367 ms to build the index for 150k names, 1.6-2.9 ms per scan, 4.2 MB.

**Corrections**
- **Count:** 13 of 17 fields wait on empty text, not 14. SearchView.swift:73 also applies empty text at once, alongside M3UChannelsView:116-121, WatchHistoryListView:86-90 and M3UFavoritesView:48-52.
- **The two-character minimum is deliberate.** It has its own localized string, `search.min_chars` ("Type at least 2 characters"), in all ten languages. Removing it is a product decision. The single-CJK-character point is valid (`q.count >= 2` rejects one Han character).
- **Dropping the debounce everywhere does not follow from a fast scan.** On the tab roots each query regroups shelves and re-renders many rows; in grids it resets pagination. The debounce also protects that work.
- **The List-diffing cost is plausible but unmeasured.** Ids are computed strings (Models/DBModels.swift:29, 61, 86 via 177, 183, 189).
- **After search-ux-3 a scan is about 0.4 s per 150k names, off-main.** Whether the index (new invariants across 146-151, 248, 260, 272, 311-316, `applyVODMetadata`, `mergeUncategorized`) is worth L effort should be decided from a device measurement.

**Corrected claim:** The Search tab runs its query three times on every mount (three `.task(id:)` at Views/SearchView.swift:246-248, nine detached scans), and no search site cancels a superseded scan. Each scan re-folds every name. The debounce block is duplicated 17 times and 13 of them also delay the empty-text reset by 250-280 ms. The two-character minimum is a deliberate choice that blocks single-character CJK queries. A pre-folded index would cut a scan from hundreds of milliseconds to a few, but that is an optimization to decide after measuring.

**Corrected fix:** **Step A (small, low risk; do now)**
1. In `SearchResultsView`, replace the three tasks with one `.task(id: SearchKey(query: query, hidden: hiddenStore.version, loaded: contentStore.streamsLoaded))`, where `SearchKey` is a private `Equatable` struct.
2. Wrap the detached work in `withTaskCancellationHandler` (same as search-ux-3) at the Search tab and the tab roots.
3. Extract one debounce helper and make it apply empty text immediately, as M3UChannelsView:116-121 already does. Keep 250 ms for non-empty text.

**Step B (measure first)**
- After search-ux-3 lands, profile typing on a device with a real 100k+ catalog.
- Build the parallel folded-key index (in the nonisolated fetch helpers, cleared in `clearLists`) only if scan time is still a visible delay.
- A simpler variant with the same gain is a parallel `[String]` of normalized names per content type.

**Step C (owner's decisions)**
- Lower the Search-tab debounce.
- Allow one-character queries, at least when the character is not ASCII, so CJK works.
- Do not remove the debounce on the tab roots or grids without measuring render cost.

**API check:** - `withTaskCancellationHandler(operation:onCancel:isolation:)`: _Concurrency.swiftmodule/arm64-apple-ios-simulator.swiftinterface:2879-2881, iOS 13.0+, back-deployed before iOS 18.0.
- `.task(id:)` with an Equatable value is already used throughout (e.g. SearchView.swift:246).
- No iOS 26-only API involved.
- Effort and risk above are for the whole proposal. Step A alone is S/M and low risk.

**Regression risks:** - **Index:** positions must stay aligned with `liveStreams` / `vodStreams` / `seriesItems` across full load, three scoped reloads, `reloadFromDatabase`, `unload` and `applyVODMetadata`. A missed rebuild returns wrong items silently. It also adds work inside the GRDB read closures and about 4 MB per 150k names.
- **Debounce on tab roots:** removing it would regroup and re-render shelves on every keystroke, which touches the deliberate Equatable-row and off-main work.
- **Empty text applied immediately:** harmless in itself, but each site's own reset path (e.g. `applyFull()` in M3UChannelsView) must be kept.
- **Single task key:** must still re-run when `streamsLoaded` flips; the comment at SearchView.swift:226-228 depends on it.
- **Dropping the minimum:** makes the `search.min_chars` string in ten languages obsolete or in need of rewording.

**How to verify:** - **Step A:** log or count `runSearch` invocations in a unit or UI test; expect 1 per query instead of 3 on mount. In All Movies, tap the clear button and confirm the full grid returns in the same frame.
- **Step B decision:** Instruments Time Profiler on a device with a 100k+ catalog, typing in the Search tab and All Movies after search-ux-3. Record time from debounce fire to results and main-thread time in the List or grid update.
- **If the index is built:** unit test that index hits equal `CatalogTextSearch.matches` over a fixture including the Turkish cases, and a 150k-name performance test.

## search-ux-5 — The first query of a search session flashes "No Results for ..." before the hits arrive, and later queries show the previous query's rows with no searching state.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:48-65, 140-142, 224-248`

**What the user perceives:** The user types two letters and sees the system "No Results" view for a few hundred milliseconds, then the list pops in. With the 13-item demo catalog this is a single frame, so the screenshots cannot show it.

**Mechanism (finder):** SearchResultsView is mounted when debouncedQuery reaches two characters (SearchView.swift:48-65) with three empty @State arrays (140-142). Its first body pass takes the branch at 224-242: all arrays empty and streamsLoaded true, so `ContentUnavailableView.search` is shown, and only then does `.task(id: query)` (246) start the scan. The existing guard at 225-239 covers only the catalog still loading, not the search still running.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Track which query the arrays belong to:

```swift
@State private var resultsQuery: String?   // set at the end of runSearch: resultsQuery = q
...
if allEmpty {
    if !contentStore.streamsLoaded || resultsQuery != query { loadingRow }
    else { noResults }
}
```

Optionally show the ProgressView only after about 300 ms so fast searches show nothing at all. No new API.

**Verifier reasons:** The false "No Results" state is real; the proposed fix trades it for a different flicker and needs a small adjustment.

- **Code:** Views/SearchView.swift:48-65 mounts `SearchResultsView` once the debounced query reaches two characters, with three empty `@State` arrays (140-142). The first body pass takes 224-242: all arrays empty and `streamsLoaded` true, so `ContentUnavailableView.search(text: query)` renders. Only then does `.task(id: query)` (246) start the scan. The guard at 225-239 covers only the catalog still loading; its comment shows the owner already treats a false "no results" as a defect.
- **It recurs:** line 73 resets `debouncedQuery` to "" below two characters, which unmounts the view and discards the arrays. The false state appears on every re-entry, not only the first query of a session.
- **Duration:** the scan is at least about 120 ms per 150k names on a dev Mac (bench re-run), runs three times in parallel on mount (search-ux-4), and becomes about 400 ms or more once search-ux-1 lands. That is long enough to read.
- **Screenshot:** iphone-light/R01-search-no-results.png shows what the view looks like: a large card reading No Results for "zzzzqq". The 13-item demo catalog cannot show the flash itself.
- **Problem with the proposed fix:** `resultsQuery != query` showing `loadingRow` regresses consecutive no-match queries. Typing "zz" then "zzz" would go No Results, spinner, No Results on each keystroke; today it stays on No Results.
- **Second half of the title is weak:** keeping the previous rows until new ones arrive is what a native search list does. I would not treat it as a defect.

**Corrected claim:** Each time the Search tab's results view mounts (first query, and every time the text goes below two characters and back), it shows the system No Results for "<query>" card until the first scan finishes. That is a few hundred milliseconds on a real catalog, and longer once the locale-safe matcher lands. Keeping the previous query's rows during later scans is acceptable.

**Corrected fix:** Track which query the arrays belong to, and only show No Results for a query that has actually been searched:

```swift
@State private var resultsQuery: String?   // set at the end of runSearch, next to the three assignments
...
if allEmpty {
    if !contentStore.streamsLoaded { loadingRow }                               // existing branch
    else if let done = resultsQuery { ContentUnavailableView.search(text: done) } // searched, nothing found
    else { EmptyView() }   // first scan still running; optionally a ProgressView after ~300 ms
}
```

- No spinner between two no-match queries; the card text updates when the new scan finishes.
- Land it with search-ux-1.
- No new API.

**API check:** - `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)`: SwiftUI.swiftmodule/arm64-apple-ios-simulator.swiftinterface:17621-17625, `public static func search(text: Swift.String) -> ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>`. Already used at SearchView.swift:241; available on the iOS 18.0 target.
- `ProgressView` and `@State` only otherwise.
- No new API.

**Regression risks:** - R01 (no results for "zzzzqq") must still appear once the scan completes; with `resultsQuery` set at the end of `runSearch` it does.
- The card text briefly shows the previous no-match query until the new scan ends. That is correct information, but check it reads well.
- `resultsQuery` must also be set when `runSearch` re-runs for hidden-category or `streamsLoaded` changes; it is, because the assignment sits beside the three array assignments after the cancellation guard.
- If a spinner variant is used, the list must not jump when it appears.

**How to verify:** - UI test with a debug delay in `runSearch` (or a seeded large catalog): type two matching characters and assert the No Results element never exists before the first row does.
- Type "zz" then "zzz" and assert the No Results element stays on screen continuously.
- With demo data, confirm R01 still shows No Results for "zzzzqq".
