## search-ux-6 — Selecting the Search tab lands on a blank page that says "Type at least 2 characters": the field is not focused, there are no recent searches and nothing to tap.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:48-57, 69`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:48, 77-85`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Choose A, B or both. With A alone, cancelling search returns the user to the tab they came from (system behaviour). With B alone, keep activation automatic, as Apple does when the page has content. B stores query strings on the device.

**What the user perceives:** Q01-search-idle.png: after tapping the magnifier, the user sees a large title, four chips, a grey glyph and an instruction, and has to tap again at the bottom to get the keyboard (Q02). Apple's TV, Music and App Store search tabs show recents or browse content there; search screens with nothing to browse open with the keyboard up.

**Mechanism (finder):** - The idle branch is a hand-made placeholder (SearchView.swift:48-57). There is no recent-search store and no `.searchSuggestions` anywhere in the target.
- The TabView sets no search activation (DashboardView.swift:48-85), so the default `TabSearchActivation.automatic` applies. UISearchTab.h:17-20 documents the default as NO; when YES, selecting the tab activates the field and cancelling returns to the previously selected tab.
- On iOS 26 the system hosts the field of a `Tab(role: .search)` in the tab bar (Q01, Q02), whatever placement `.searchable` asks for. On iOS 18 the same code gives a trailing magnifier tab and a drawer field under the large title, also unfocused.
- `searchToolbarBehavior` and `DefaultToolbarItem(kind: .search)` only affect toolbar-hosted fields, not this tab.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Option A (smallest): activate on selection.

```swift
// DashboardView.swift, after .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)
.modifier(SearchTabActivation())
struct SearchTabActivation: ViewModifier {
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if #available(iOS 26, *) { content.tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection) }
        else { content }
    }
}
```

iOS 18 fallback: keep today's behaviour, or add `@FocusState` plus `.searchFocused($focused)` in SearchView and set it in onAppear.

Option B: give the idle page content. A small RecentSearchStore (UserDefaults, per playlist, 10 entries, local only), written from `.onSubmit(of: .search)` and when a result is opened, cleared with the playlist. The idle state becomes a List section "Recent" with a Clear button whose rows set searchText. This needs two new strings appended to the ten Localizable.strings files, which hold the uncommitted tip keys; append only, hence touches_user_wip.

**APIs:** View.tabViewSearchActivation(_:) (iOS 26.0); TabSearchActivation.searchTabSelection (iOS 26.0); UISearchTab.automaticallyActivatesSearch (iOS 26.0); View.searchFocused(_:) (iOS 18.0); View.onSubmit(of:_:) with SubmitTriggers.search (iOS 15.0); View.searchSuggestions(_:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/SearchView.swift:48-57: the idle branch is a hand-built Spacer/Image/Text placeholder ("search.min_chars"); no recents, no .searchSuggestions and no .searchFocused anywhere in the target (grep over all .swift). Views/DashboardView.swift:48-85: the TabView has Tab(role: .search) at :77 and .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable) at :85 with no tabViewSearchActivation, so the default (.automatic / UISearchTab.automaticallyActivatesSearch = NO, UISearchTab.h:17-21) applies. Q01-search-idle.png shows exactly that: large title, chips, grey glyph, unfocused field hosted in the tab bar although the code asks for navigationBarDrawer(.always) (SearchView.swift:69); Q02 shows the keyboard only after a second tap. History (git log --follow on SearchView.swift; -S'role: .search') shows this came with the initial native app (6e8bd95/fe55017) with no comment giving a reason, so it is not deliberate. One correction to the fix: the second iOS 18 fallback ("@FocusState + .searchFocused set in onAppear") is wrong for this view, because SearchView is the root of a NavigationStack that pushes MovieDetailView/SeriesDetailView (SearchView.swift:180-181, 205-206); onAppear fires again on every pop, so the keyboard would come back over the results each time the user returns from a detail. Existing tests (ScreensUITests.swift:29-44, UserFlowsUITests.swift:292-316) tap the tab, then the field, then type; they stay valid with an already-focused field.

**Corrected claim:** Selecting the Search tab lands on a hand-made idle page (SearchView.swift:48-57) with an unfocused field; the user must tap a second time to get the keyboard, and the page offers no recent searches. On iOS 26 the field is hosted in the tab bar regardless of the requested placement (Q01/Q02). The iOS 18 rendering described in the finding (trailing magnifier tab, drawer field) is plausible but was not checked on an iOS 18 runtime.

**Corrected fix:** Option A as proposed: a small ViewModifier on the TabView in DashboardView (after .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable), line 85) that applies .tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection) under `if #available(iOS 26, *)` and returns content unchanged otherwise. iOS 18 fallback: keep today's behaviour. Do NOT set a search FocusState in SearchView.onAppear (it re-fires on pop from a detail); if iOS 18 auto-focus is wanted, drive it from the tab-selection change in DashboardView (onChange of selectedTab == .search) instead. Option B (per-playlist recent-search list, UserDefaults, append-only strings) stays an owner decision; if done, append the two new keys at the end of the ten Localizable.strings files without touching the uncommitted tip keys.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:11397-11401 `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *) nonisolated public func tabViewSearchActivation(_ activation: SwiftUI.TabSearchActivation) -> some View` (unavailable tvOS/watchOS/visionOS). :11405-11415 `public struct TabSearchActivation` iOS 26.0 with `static var automatic` and `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *) static var searchTabSelection`. UISearchTab.h:21 `automaticallyActivatesSearch API_AVAILABLE(ios(26.0))`, doc comment: default NO; when YES the field activates on tab selection and cancelling restores the previously selected tab. :5926-5929 `searchFocused(_ binding: FocusState<Bool>.Binding)` iOS 18.0. :7737-7739 `onSubmit(of: SubmitTriggers = .text, _:)` iOS 15.0, `SubmitTriggers.search` at :10041. :10813-10814 `searchSuggestions(_:)` iOS 16.0. `if #available` inside ViewModifier.body is valid (implicit ViewBuilder).

**Regression risks:** (1) With .searchTabSelection, cancelling search (the X in Q02) jumps to the previously selected tab instead of staying on Search; it goes through tabBinding (DashboardView.swift:26-34), which is fine, but it is a behaviour change. (2) PlayerOverlayController.present resigns first responder (PlayerOverlayController.swift:39-41) when a live result is opened; it must be checked that this resign is not treated as a search cancel that switches tabs behind the player (deliberate earlier hand-off work, covered by UserFlowsUITests.swift:292-310). (3) A docked mini player stays above the keyboard (DashboardView.swift:118), so with auto-activation the card sits near the lifted search field every time the tab is selected, not only after a manual tap. (4) Option B stores query strings on device; must be cleared with the playlist.

**How to verify:** iOS 26 simulator: tap Search tab, assert the keyboard exists without a second tap; tap X and note which tab is selected; open a live result and after minimizing the player assert the Search tab and its results are still shown; repeat with a mini player docked and check the card does not cover the field. Run ScreensUITests test_searchTab_* and UserFlowsUITests test_search_* unchanged. On an iOS 18 runtime confirm nothing changed.

## search-ux-7 — The All / Live TV / Movies / Series filter is a hand-made capsule row above the list instead of the system search scope bar.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:24-46, 69`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:37-44`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: If the system scope bar looks wrong with the iOS 26 tab-bar search field, decide between the segmented fallback and keeping the chips restyled.

**What the user perceives:** Q01 to Q02: the chip row jumps up by about 105 pt when the field is focused, because the navigation bar hides and the row is ordinary content. It is an opaque white band with a hairline, so the grey grouped list cannot scroll under it (Q03). It is shown on the idle page where there is nothing to filter. VoiceOver reads four plain buttons with no selected state. Favorites uses a segmented control for the same Live / Movies / Series choice (M09), so the two screens differ.

**Mechanism (finder):** SearchView.swift:25-44 builds the chips from Buttons with Color(.systemGray5) or accentColor backgrounds and cornerRadius(20), followed by a Divider (46), inside a VStack above the results. There is no `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected)`. The selection is view-local @State (line 8), which is fine and survives tab switches.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Attach the scopes to the search field and delete lines 25-46:

```swift
.searchable(text: $searchText, placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always), prompt: L("search.placeholder"))
.searchScopes($selectedFilter, activation: .onSearchPresentation) {
    ForEach(SearchFilter.allCases, id: \.self) { Text($0.displayName).tag($0) }
}
```

This is iOS 16.4 API, so one code path covers iOS 18 and 26. Where the scope bar renders next to the tab-bar-hosted field on iOS 26 has to be checked on the simulator. If it does not suit, keep one control but make it a segmented Picker in `.safeAreaInset(edge: .top)` (or `.safeAreaBar(edge: .top)` on iOS 26, so the list scrolls under it), matching Favorites.

**APIs:** View.searchScopes(_:activation:_:) (iOS 16.4); SearchScopeActivation.onSearchPresentation (iOS 16.4); View.safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Facts confirmed: Views/SearchView.swift:25-44 builds the four filters from Buttons with accentColor / Color(.systemGray5) backgrounds and cornerRadius(20), followed by Divider (:46), in a VStack above the content; there is no .accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected) (a real VoiceOver defect); the row is shown in the idle branch too (Q01). Views/FavoritesView.swift:37-44 uses a segmented Picker for the same Live/Movies/Series choice (M09), so the two screens do differ. Q03 confirms the white band over the grey inset-grouped list. Corrections: (a) the ~105 pt jump between Q01 and Q02 (measured: chip row y 444 -> 201 px in the 920-px render, about 106 pt) is the system hiding the large-title navigation bar when search activates; any content, including the result list or a replacement picker, moves by the same amount, so it is not caused by the chips being hand-made. (b) The primary fix cannot be confirmed: where SwiftUI renders .searchScopes for a field hosted in the tab bar by Tab(role: .search) on iOS 26, with the navigation bar hidden while search is active (Q02), is not derivable from the SDK interface; the finding itself says it must be checked. The fallback (one segmented Picker pinned with safeAreaInset / safeAreaBar) is deterministic on both OS versions and matches Favorites. No history or comment marks the chips as deliberate (they came with the initial app commit).

**Corrected claim:** The Search filter is a hand-made capsule row (SearchView.swift:25-46) that differs from the segmented control Favorites uses for the same choice, sits on an opaque band the list cannot scroll under, and exposes no selected state to VoiceOver. The position jump on focus is system search-activation behaviour, not a chip defect.

**Corrected fix:** Make the deterministic variant the default and treat the system scope bar as an experiment: replace lines 25-46 with `Picker(L("favorites.type") or a search-specific label, selection: $selectedFilter) { ForEach(SearchFilter.allCases, id: \.self) { Text($0.displayName).tag($0) } }.pickerStyle(.segmented)` hosted in `.safeAreaBar(edge: .top)` under `if #available(iOS 26, *)` and in `.safeAreaInset(edge: .top)` with a `.bar` background on iOS 18. This keeps the existing onSelectFilter path (SearchView.swift:63) working and gives the selected trait for free. Only switch to `.searchScopes($selectedFilter, activation: .onSearchPresentation) { ... }` if a simulator run on iOS 26 and iOS 18 shows the scope bar in a sensible place next to the tab-bar-hosted field. If the owner prefers to keep chips, the minimum fix is `.accessibilityAddTraits(selectedFilter == filter ? .isSelected : [])` on each chip.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2493-2495 `@available(iOS 16.4, macOS 13.3, tvOS 16.4, *) func searchScopes<V, S>(_ scope: Binding<V>, activation: SearchScopeActivation, @ViewBuilder _ scopes: () -> S)` (V: Hashable; SearchFilter is a String enum, so it compiles). :2475-2485 `struct SearchScopeActivation` iOS 16.4 with `automatic`, `onTextEntry`, `onSearchPresentation` (the last unavailable on tvOS only). :17361-17362 `@available(iOS 26.0, ...) func safeAreaBar(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment:, spacing:, content:)`. safeAreaInset(edge:) is in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19082 (iOS 15). Nothing in the interface says how scopes render for a Tab(role: .search) field.

**Regression risks:** Scope bar placement with the iOS 26 tab-bar search field is unknown and could end up hidden or duplicated. A segmented control with four localized titles must be checked in the longest languages (de, ru, hi) at large Dynamic Type; the chips scroll horizontally today, a segmented control truncates. The orchestrator's tour (ScreensUITests.swift:402) looks up a button named "Movies"; the committed tests (ScreensUITests.swift:29-44, UserFlowsUITests.swift:292-316) do not touch the filter.

**How to verify:** Simulator on iOS 26 and an iOS 18 runtime: compare against Q02/Q05, check the control in idle, focused and results states, in dark mode and in German/Russian at the largest text size. Accessibility Inspector must report the selected segment. If testing .searchScopes: record where the bar appears with the field in the tab bar and whether it survives keyboard dismissal.

## search-ux-8 — Search results draw posters letterboxed into 44-pt squares in an inset-grouped list, with an icon-and-count header and a blue "N more results" text row.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:154-170, 178-195, 203-220, 245, 309-335`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:58, 81-82`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Row list (as now, restyled) or a poster grid for movie and series hits: design choice.

**What the user perceives:** Q03 and Q04: each movie poster is a thin, sharp-cornered image about 29 x 44 pt floating in a square slot. The second line carries only the category. The header reads "Movies (2)" with a film glyph spaced far from the text. More hits sit behind a small blue footnote row. The page background flips from white (idle, Q01) to grouped grey (results). Elsewhere the app shows the same content as large rounded posters.

**Mechanism (finder):** - ResultRow asks CachedImage for 44 x 44 with the default `.fit` content mode (SearchView.swift:317, CachedImage.swift:58), so a 2:3 poster is letterboxed. The rounded clip is applied to the square frame (line 318, CachedImage.swift:81-82) and never touches the image.
- SectionLabel is a Label with a count (328-335).
- The more-results buttons are footnote text rows (164-169, 189-194, 214-219).
- `.listStyle(.insetGrouped)` (245) is used over an idle state built on the plain background (48-57).

**Proposed fix (finder):** - Give ResultRow an artwork kind: movies and series use `CachedImage(url:, width: 48, height: 72, cornerRadius: 6, contentMode: .fill, loadProfile: .grid)`; channels keep 48 x 48 with `.fit`. Drop the outer clipShape.
- Second line: category plus rating when present (DBVODStream.rating, DBSeries.rating).
- Header: `HStack { Text(title).font(.headline); Spacer(); Button(L("category.see_all")) { onSelectFilter(.movies) } }` when more than four hits. That key already exists (en line 368), so no new strings. Remove the footnote rows.
- `.listStyle(.plain)` so idle and results share one background.

**Verifier reasons:** Views/SearchView.swift:317 calls `CachedImage(url:, width: 44, height: 44, iconName:, loadProfile: .grid)`; CachedImage defaults contentMode to .fit (Views/CachedImage.swift:58) and applies frame + clipShape to the 44x44 box (CachedImage.swift:81-82), and line 318 clips the same square again, so a 2:3 poster renders about 29x44 pt with square corners. Q03 and Q05 show exactly that. SectionLabel is `Label("\(title) (\(count))", systemImage:)` (SearchView.swift:328-335), rendered in Q03 with a wide gap between glyph and text. The more-results rows are footnote accent text (164-169, 189-194, 214-219). The idle branch sits on the plain background (48-57, Q01 white) while results use .insetGrouped (245, Q03 grey), so the background flips. git log on SearchView.swift shows no commit that chose these sizes on purpose (0ab5bcd only added the loading row and the O(N) grouping; 654cefc did not touch the row). The fix compiles against this code base: CachedImage's memberwise init has cornerRadius and contentMode before iconName/loadProfile (CachedImage.swift:54-60); DBVODStream.rating (Models/DBModels.swift:39) and DBSeries.rating (:75) exist; RatingLabel(rating:) exists (Views/RatingLabel.swift:30-52); "category.see_all" exists in all ten Localizable.strings (en line 368). No performance work is undone: the search itself stays off-main (SearchView.swift:260-271) and List stays lazy.

**Corrected claim:** As stated. Addition: the row is shared between square channel logos and 2:3 posters, which is why posters were forced into a square; the fix must keep .fit for channels.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with three details: (1) keep passing `iconName: typeIcon` so the placeholder glyph survives; (2) keep channel logos at a square size with .fit and use `contentMode: .fill` only for movie/series rows, removing the outer .clipShape at line 318 (CachedImage already clips); (3) pick the poster size with the keyboard up in mind: at 48x72 only about four rows fit between the filter row and the lifted search field (about 357 pt in Q03), so the 'All' scope shows a single section; 40x60 keeps two sections partly visible. The header 'See All' button replacing the footnote rows and `.listStyle(.plain)` are sound; leave the now-unused "search.more_results_format" key in place. Row list versus poster grid remains an owner design choice.

**API check:** No new SwiftUI API. In-repo: `struct CachedImage { url, width, height, cornerRadius = 8, contentMode = .fit, iconName = "photo", loadProfile = .standard }` (Views/CachedImage.swift:54-60); `ImageLoadProfile.grid` decodes at min(scale, 2) x and does not cancel on disappear (CachedImage.swift:42-51, 126-130), which suits a List.

**Regression risks:** New 48x72 (or 40x60) requests produce their own resized cache entries, same as the current 44x44 ones, so no extra network load. Taller rows show fewer hits above the keyboard. Plain list style makes section headers sticky and changes the background behind the filter row. The header button must keep calling onSelectFilter so the scope control updates. UI tests look up result rows by static text ("Midnight Horizon", "World News 24"), which is unaffected.

**How to verify:** Screenshots against Q03/Q04/Q05 in light and dark, at the largest Dynamic Type size, and in Arabic (RTL). Check a channel hit (logo still fitted, not cropped), a movie without artwork (placeholder glyph), and a query with more than four movie hits (See All switches the scope). Run test_searchTab_typingQueryShowsResults and the two UserFlows search tests.

## search-ux-9 — There are three ways to search on each tab (root field, Search tab, a field in every pushed grid), and nine pushed lists pin the field permanently, including lists that are empty or hold 20 items.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category grids, All Movies / Series / Channels, Recently Added, Favorites, Downloads
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93, 498, 723`, `Views/VODView.swift:145, 200-208, 381, 564, 823`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:146, 358, 536, 762`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:503`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:58`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:122`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:77-83`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether the tab-root fields go away on Xtream playlists, and whether pushed lists keep a pinned field, a collapsing one or the iOS 26 bottom placement.

**What the user perceives:** iphone-light/L01-live-home.png (a Series-tab capture): a search field under the title and a search button in the tab bar on the same screen, and they return different things. The root field filters the shelves in place, unranked, and a category-name hit returns the whole category. M03 and M04: the field stays pinned above every grid and takes about 52 pt. M09 and T05: Favorites and Downloads show a search field above an empty list.

**Mechanism (finder):** - Root fields at LiveStreamsView.swift:93, VODView.swift:145 and SeriesView.swift:146 feed recomputeFilter, which keeps the shelf layout (VODView.swift:200-208).
- Pushed lists use `.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always)` at the nine sites listed. git log -S shows that came in with the views (d2489f9, 654cefc), with no comment giving a reason.
- The two Recently Added lists are capped at 20 items (VODView.swift:189) and still get a pinned field (381; SeriesView.swift:358).
- Favorites and Downloads attach `.searchable` unconditionally.
- Apple's tabbed media apps keep one Search tab and no root field; fields inside long lists scroll away; iOS 26 system apps put a pushed screen's field in the bottom toolbar.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Pick per screen type:
1. Xtream dashboard roots: remove the three root `.searchable` blocks and their debounce state, since the Search tab with scopes covers them. The M3U dashboard keeps its root field because it has no Search tab (M3UDashboardView.swift:26-44).
2. Pushed grids: switch to `.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic)` so the field collapses while scrolling. Check on an iOS 18 runtime that it is still visible right after the push (a possible reason `.always` was chosen). On iOS 26, optionally `if #available(iOS 26, *) { .toolbar { DefaultToolbarItem(kind: .search, placement: .bottomBar) } }`; these screens already hide the tab bar. Check that against the docked mini player first. Fallback: the drawer.
3. Drop the field from the two 20-item lists and attach it conditionally (only when the list has content) in Favorites, Downloads and History.

**APIs:** SearchFieldPlacement.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode:) (iOS 15.0); DefaultToolbarItem(kind: .search, placement:) (iOS 26.0); View.searchToolbarBehavior(_:) / SearchToolbarBehavior.minimize (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Facts confirmed in code: root fields at Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93, Views/VODView.swift:145, Views/SeriesView.swift:146 (default placement, isPresented binding) coexist with the Search tab (DashboardView.swift:77-83); iphone-light/L01 shows both on one screen. They do return different things: the root filter keeps the shelf layout and a category-name hit returns the whole category (VODView.swift:200-208), the Search tab returns flat name-sorted lists. Nine pushed lists use .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always): LiveStreamsView.swift:498, 723; VODView.swift:381, 564, 823; SeriesView.swift:358, 536, 762; M3UChannelsView.swift:503 (M03 shows the pinned field). Recently Added is capped with .prefix(20) (VODView.swift:189) and still gets a field (VODView.swift:381, SeriesView.swift:358). Favorites (FavoritesView.swift:58), Downloads (DownloadsView.swift:122) and History (WatchHistoryListView.swift:83) attach .searchable unconditionally (M09, T05). git log -S'navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always)' gives only d2489f9 and 654cefc, no comment explains the choice. The M3U dashboard indeed has no Search tab (M3UDashboardView.swift:26-44). What does not stand as a defect: (1) removing the three root fields is a feature removal (in-place shelf filtering plus category-name matching, which the Search tab does not offer), not a fix; (2) switching to .automatic can leave the field collapsed or hidden right after the push, which is the usual reason .always is chosen, and these content views swap between a non-scrolling empty VStack and a ScrollView once the async recompute lands (VODView.swift:677-690, SeriesView.swift:634-647, LiveStreamsView.swift:594-605), which can make the bar change height after the push; only a simulator run settles that; (3) Apple's own apps (Notes, Files, Mail) keep the search field on empty lists, so a field above an empty Favorites/Downloads list is not un-native, and attaching .searchable conditionally makes the field pop in when the first item arrives; (4) the iOS 26 bottom-bar search item would share the bottom edge with the docked mini player, which reserves only a tab-bar allowance there (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:475-478, 534).

**Corrected claim:** The app has redundant search entry points on Xtream playlists (root drawer field plus Search tab on the same screen) and pins a search drawer on all nine pushed grids, including the two Recently Added lists that never hold more than 20 items. This is a consistency and space issue and mostly a product decision, not a defect; the empty-list fields in Favorites/Downloads/History match system apps and are not a problem.

**Corrected fix:** Split by certainty. Safe and small: drop .searchable and its debounce state from RecentlyAddedVODDetailView (VODView.swift:356-392) and RecentlyAddedSeriesDetailView (SeriesView.swift:333-365); 20 items need no filter. Needs a simulator check before adopting: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic) on the seven remaining pushed grids; adopt only if the field is visible right after the push on iOS 18 and iOS 26 and the bar does not jump when the grid replaces the empty placeholder. Do not use DefaultToolbarItem(kind: .search, placement: .bottomBar) unless it is verified against the docked mini player. Owner decision, not a fix: removing the three Xtream root fields; if chosen, keep recomputeFilter's empty-query path (hidden categories, Recently Added) and the off-main filtering untouched, and keep the M3U root field. Leave Favorites, Downloads and History as they are.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9342-9346 `@available(iOS 15.0, *) static func navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: SearchFieldPlacement.NavigationBarDrawerDisplayMode) -> SearchFieldPlacement`. :6275-6277 `@available(iOS 26.0, ...) struct DefaultToolbarItem : ToolbarContent { init(kind: ToolbarDefaultItemKind, placement: ToolbarItemPlacement = .automatic) }`; :17114-17123 `ToolbarDefaultItemKind.search` is `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0, *)`; `ToolbarItemPlacement.bottomBar` at :6191. :19963-19983 `struct SearchToolbarBehavior` iOS 26.0 with `minimize` (iOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0) and `func searchToolbarBehavior(_:)` iOS 26.0. All exist as stated; none of them documents the initial visibility of an .automatic drawer on a pushed large-title screen.

**Regression risks:** Removing root fields deletes a way to find a category by name and the in-place shelf filter, and UI flows that type into a root field (the orchestrator's tour does at ScreensUITests.swift:333). An .automatic drawer may hide the only filter on a 50k-item 'All Movies' grid until the user pulls down. A bottom-bar search field can collide with the mini player card. Conditional .searchable changes view identity and resets the grid's local state (sort/filter, visibleCount).

**How to verify:** Simulator on iOS 18 and iOS 26 runtimes: push a category grid and All Movies with .automatic, record whether the field is visible before any scroll, whether it collapses on scroll, and whether the title/bar height changes when the grid appears after the first async recompute. With a mini player docked, check nothing overlaps. Compare with L01, M03, M04.

## search-ux-10 — "No Results" is drawn as a card inside the results list in the Search tab and looks different in every other search field (six variants).

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Search tab, Live / Movies / Series home, Category and All grids, Favorites, Watch history, Downloads, Category picker
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:224-245`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:54-61, 636-646`, `Views/VODView.swift:53-60, 677-686`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:80-87, 586-595`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:50-59, 562-571`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:178-191`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:58-63`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:76-77`, `Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:48-66`

**What the user perceives:** R01: the system no-results view sits in a white rounded card at the top of the list instead of centred in the free area. iphone-light/L06: the Series field shows a TV glyph and "No search results.". A category grid that filters to nothing says "No movies found." or "No channel found.", which is the empty-category message. Favorites, History, Downloads and the category picker each look different again.

**Mechanism (finder):** - SearchView places `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` as a row of an inset-grouped List (lines 241, 245).
- The other sites use hand-made VStacks or custom ContentUnavailableViews (lines in files).
- `ContentUnavailableView.search` is localized by the OS, while the app switches language through its own bundle lookup (LocalizationManager.swift:48-66). With an in-app language different from the device language, the Search tab and Downloads empty states appear in the device language.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One `SearchNoResultsView` in Views/Components:

```swift
ContentUnavailableView {
    Label(L("favorites.empty.no_result.title"), systemImage: "magnifyingglass")
} description: { Text(L("category_picker.not_found.message")) }
```

Both keys already exist (en lines 135 and 102). Use it as an `.overlay` on the List in SearchView rather than as a row, and in place of the VStacks elsewhere. The category content views need an `isFiltered` flag to choose between the empty-category and no-results messages; include it in their Equatable `==`.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/SearchView.swift:241 places ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) as a row of the List styled .insetGrouped (:245); R01 shows it as a white rounded card at the top instead of centred. The other sites really differ: root screens use a tab glyph plus L("list.no_result") (LiveStreamsView.swift:80-87, VODView.swift:53-60, SeriesView.swift:54-61; iphone-light/L06 shows the play.tv glyph with "No search results."); category grids always show the empty-category text even when a search filtered them to nothing (VODView.swift:677-686 "vod.empty.no_movie", SeriesView.swift:636-646 "series.empty.no_series", LiveStreamsView.swift:594-603 and M3UChannelsView.swift:562-571 "list.no_channel"); Favorites uses its own VStack with the type glyph (FavoritesView.swift:106, 178-191); History uses a custom ContentUnavailableView with the two keys the fix reuses (WatchHistoryListView.swift:58-63); Downloads uses ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) full-screen (DownloadsView.swift:76-77); the category picker has its own title (CategoryPickerSheet.swift:58-62). Both proposed keys exist in all ten languages. Overlaying the view on the List is Apple's documented pattern for ContentUnavailableView. One sub-claim is not proven: the app also sets .environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: code)) at the root (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:64), and SwiftUI-rendered system text may follow that, so 'appears in the device language' needs a run; the fix is right either way because it moves the text to the app's own L() lookup.

**Corrected claim:** As stated for the visual inconsistency (at least seven distinct no-results presentations, and a card-in-list in the Search tab). The statement that the two ContentUnavailableView.search sites show the device language instead of the in-app language is unverified, because the root view injects \.locale.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: one SearchNoResultsView in Views/Components built from ContentUnavailableView { Label(L("favorites.empty.no_result.title"), systemImage: "magnifyingglass") } description: { Text(L("category_picker.not_found.message")) }. In SearchResultsView apply it as `.overlay` on the List when all three result arrays are empty AND contentStore.streamsLoaded is true, and keep the existing loading row for the not-yet-loaded case (SearchView.swift:225-239 is deliberate, see its comment). In the category content views add an `isFiltered` input, include it in the Equatable ==, and choose between the existing empty-category text and the shared view; when the grid's own file-type or sort filter empties the list, keep the current text. WatchHistoryListView already matches and only needs to switch to the shared view.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17574-17576 `@available(iOS 17.0, ...) struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` with `init(@ViewBuilder label:, @ViewBuilder description: = { EmptyView() }, @ViewBuilder actions: = { EmptyView() })`; :17620-17625 `static var search` and `static func search(text: String)` (iOS 17.0), the two system-localized variants in use today.

**Regression risks:** The Equatable shelf/grid content views are deliberate performance work: isFiltered must be added to == (otherwise the message would not update) without widening the comparison beyond that one Bool. The loading row in SearchResultsView must not be replaced by the overlay, or a still-loading catalog would show 'no results'. An overlay on an empty inset-grouped List keeps the grey background; if search-ux-8 switches to .plain the two changes should land together.

**How to verify:** Screenshots against R01 and iphone-light/L06 after typing "zzzzqq" in each field (Search tab, three roots, a category grid, All Movies, Favorites, History, Downloads, category picker): same glyph, title and message, centred. Set the in-app language to one that differs from the simulator language and compare the text before and after the change to settle the localization sub-claim. Kill the network during catalog load and confirm the Search tab still shows the loading row, not the no-results view.

## search-ux-11 — The TV Guide declares a search field that is not visible when the guide opens, has no localized prompt and uses a fourth matcher.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51-53, 105, 134, 168, 259-280`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:28, 93-98, 155-160`

**What the user perceives:** iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows no search field or search button on the guide, so channel search there is undiscoverable. When the field does appear, its placeholder is the system "Search" in the device language, and "sehir" does not find "Şehir TV".

**Mechanism (finder):** - `.searchable(text: $model.searchQuery)` (EPGGuideView.swift:53) uses the default placement on an inline-title screen whose first scroll views are horizontal (105, 134) and whose body is a two-axis scroller (168). The drawer is collapsed on open. Whether pulling down reveals it could not be confirmed without a simulator run.
- No `prompt:` is passed.
- Matching is `searchName.contains(q)` over `displayName.lowercased()` (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:28, 155-160), which does no diacritic or Turkish folding.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Present search from the toolbar instead of relying on a pull-down:

```swift
@State private var searchPresented = false
...
.searchable(text: $model.searchQuery, isPresented: $searchPresented, prompt: L("live.search_placeholder"))
// in toolbarContent
ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarTrailing) {
    Button { searchPresented = true } label: { Image(systemName: "magnifyingglass") }
        .accessibilityLabel(L("common.search"))
}
```

This works the same on iOS 18 and 26 and costs no vertical space. Build `searchName` with CatalogTextSearch's fold (make `normalize` internal) and fold the query the same way. The precomputed key and the EPG snapshot stay.

**APIs:** View.searchable(text:isPresented:placement:prompt:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** All three sub-claims hold in the code; the fix needs three corrections.

- **Field not visible:** Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:53 is `.searchable(text: $model.searchQuery)` with no placement, no `isPresented` and no prompt. It is the only one of the app's 20 `.searchable` call sites without a prompt. iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows back, title and three toolbar items, and no search field. Live TV home (LiveStreamsView.swift:93, also default placement) does show its field on open in iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png, so the guide is the odd one out.
- **Why it differs:** the guide has an inline title (line 50) and its content is a VStack of a horizontal ScrollView (105), another horizontal one (134) and a two-axis ScrollView (168). Whether a pull-down reveals the field is not decidable from code.
- **Prompt:** the system default prompt follows the device language, while the app has its own language override (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:30-45), so the two can disagree.
- **Matcher:** EPGGuideViewModel.swift:28 stores `displayName.lowercased()`, and 155-160 does `searchName.contains(q)`. In a scratch run this matcher returned false for "sehir" in "Şehir TV", "istanbul" in "İSTANBUL HABER", "isik" and "ışık" in "IŞIK TV", "fox tv" in "FOX-TV" and "sports tv" in "Sports HD TV". CatalogTextSearch matches all six.
- **Not deliberate:** the search came in with 1cce013 and `searchName` with 654cefc. The comment at EPGGuideViewModel.swift:15-16 only argues for precomputing the key, not for skipping the fold.

Corrections to the fix:
1. "Fold the query the same way" is wrong if the whole query is folded. `normalize` strips spaces, so "sports tv" becomes "sportstv" and misses "sportshdtv". The query must be split into words and each word folded, as `CatalogTextSearch.matches` does (Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:21-30).
2. `buildRows()` runs on the main actor (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-278). Folding 50k Turkish channel names took 121 ms with the current `normalize`, 58 ms with the search-ux-12 version and 30 ms with `lowercased()`, measured on a Mac; a phone is slower. The fix adds main-thread time to guide open.
3. A fourth trailing item is tight. In L06 the three-item group spans about x=515-883 of 920 and the title ends near x=330. English fits; "Телепрограмма", "TV-Programm" or a narrower iPhone will probably truncate the title.

**Corrected claim:** The TV Guide's channel search is not visible when the guide opens (inline title, default placement, no vertical scroller at the top of the content); whether a pull-down reveals it is unverified. It has no localized prompt, so the placeholder follows the device language rather than the in-app language. Its matcher is a plain `lowercased().contains`, which misses diacritics, Turkish İ/ı, punctuation and multi-word queries that every other inline field handles. A Turkish user typing "istanbul" or "sehir" gets no rows.

**Corrected fix:** 1. Keep the toolbar presentation as proposed: `@State private var searchPresented = false`, `.searchable(text: $model.searchQuery, isPresented: $searchPresented, prompt: L("live.search_placeholder"))`, and a magnifier `ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarTrailing)` with `.accessibilityLabel(L("common.search"))`. This is the same overload LiveStreamsView.swift:93 and DownloadsView.swift:122 already use. If four items truncate the title on narrow iPhones or long locales, fold Refresh into the existing categories Menu; that is a product decision.
2. Matching: expose the fold from CatalogTextSearch, for example `static func key(_ text: String) -> String` and `static func matches(search: String, key: String) -> Bool`, the latter splitting the query on whitespace and folding each word. Build `EPGGuideRow.searchName` with `key(displayName)` and filter with `matches(search:key:)` in `recomputeItems`. Do not fold the whole query as one string.
3. Land the faster fold from search-ux-12 first, or build the keys lazily on the first non-empty query, so guide open does not gain a main-thread stall on large playlists.

The precomputed key, the EPG snapshot and the row Equatable stay as they are.

**API check:** - `searchable<S>(text: Binding<String>, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, placement: SearchFieldPlacement = .automatic, prompt: S) where S: StringProtocol`: found at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5786, `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, *)`, unavailable on tvOS and watchOS. It needs no availability guard on an iOS 18 target and takes the String that `L()` returns. The Text? and LocalizedStringKey overloads are at 5763 and 5769.
- `ToolbarItemPlacement.topBarTrailing`: already used in this file (EPGGuideView.swift:261).
- iOS 26 alternative, not required: `DefaultToolbarItem(kind:placement:)` at 6276, `ToolbarDefaultItemKind.search` at 17123 and `searchToolbarBehavior(_:)` at 19983 with `.minimize` at 19972 all exist and are iOS 26.0 only.
- `L("live.search_placeholder")` and `L("common.search")` exist (en.lproj/Localizable.strings:81 and :10).

**Regression risks:** - Four trailing items can truncate the inline title on narrow iPhones and long locales.
- Folding the key in `EPGGuideRow.init` adds main-actor work to `buildRows()`, roughly 60-120 ms per 50k channels on a Mac depending on which `normalize` is in place.
- Folding the whole query instead of per word would break multi-word queries.
- `searchName` takes part in the synthesized Equatable/Hashable of `EPGGuideRow`. It is still derived from `displayName`, so equality semantics do not change.
- When search is dismissed, `searchQuery` should be cleared so collapsed categories return; check the Cancel path.
- Nothing in the player hand-off or the EPG snapshot is touched.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iPhone, iOS 26 and iOS 18:
1. Open Live TV, then TV Guide. Before any change, drag down on the grid at the top and record whether a search field appears. If it does not, the feature is unreachable today and severity is medium.
2. After the change, tap the magnifier and assert `app.searchFields.firstMatch` exists with the keyboard up and the localized placeholder. Type "sehir" against a "Şehir TV" row and "sports tv" against "Sports HD TV" and assert the rows remain. Cancel and assert the full list and collapse state return.
3. Screenshot the nav bar in German and Russian on the smallest supported iPhone to check title truncation.
4. Unit tests: `CatalogTextSearch.matches(search:key:)` for "istanbul"/"İSTANBUL HABER", "isik"/"IŞIK TV", "fox tv"/"FOX-TV".
5. Time `buildRows()` with 50k synthetic rows before and after.

## search-ux-12 — Search folding does not cover Arabic or full-width text: "احمد" does not find "أحمد", and vowel marks or tatweel break matches.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Every search field
- Code: `Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:13-19`, `Database/Persistence.swift:105-113`, `another-iptv-playerTests/CatalogTextSearchTests.swift:16-38`

**What the user perceives:** An Arabic-speaking user (the app ships an ar localization) types a name without hamza or vowel marks, as people normally type, and titles stored with them are not found. Full-width Latin titles in CJK catalogs do not match ASCII queries.

**Mechanism (finder):** `normalize` folds with [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive] only (CatalogTextSearch.swift:14). Measured with a copy of the function:
- normalize("مُحَمَّد") differs from normalize("محمد")
- matches("احمد", "أحمد") is false
- ta marbuta, alef maqsura and tatweel variants are false
- "abc" against full-width "ＡＢＣ" is false
Hindi, Cyrillic (ё/е) and ß/ss already work.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the body of `normalize` with one fold plus one scalar pass:

```swift
let folded = s.folding(options: [.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive, .widthInsensitive], locale: foldLocale)
var out = String.UnicodeScalarView()
for u in folded.unicodeScalars {
    switch u.value {
    case 0x0131: out.append("i")
    case 0x064B...0x065F, 0x0670, 0x0640: continue
    case 0x0622, 0x0623, 0x0625, 0x0671: out.append("\u{0627}")
    case 0x0649, 0x06CC: out.append("\u{064A}")
    case 0x0629: out.append("\u{0647}")
    case 0x06A9: out.append("\u{0643}")
    default: if alphanumericSet.contains(u) { out.append(u) }
    }
}
return String(out)
```

Tested in a scratch build: all existing expectations (history, ışık, isik, çılgın, İSTANBUL, fox tv, Hindi) still hold, and it is 2.6 times faster (150 ms against 393 ms per 150k names). Make `normalize` internal and call it from the SQL function in Persistence.swift:108-113 so the two cannot drift.

**APIs:** String.CompareOptions.widthInsensitive (Foundation) (iOS 2.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The folding gap and the fix are both correct; the stated scope is not.

- **Code:** Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:13-19 folds with `[.caseInsensitive, .diacriticInsensitive]`, maps "ı" to "i" and strips non-alphanumerics. Database/Persistence.swift:108-113 holds a hand-kept duplicate with a "must stay in sync" comment.
- **Reproduced:** I recompiled both versions in a scratch file. The current fold leaves U+0623 intact, keeps harakat (64f, 64e, 651), tatweel (640), ta marbuta (629), alef maqsura (649) and full-width letters (ff41...). So "احمد"/"أحمد", "محمد"/"مُحَمَّد", "مدرسه"/"مدرسة", "علي"/"على", "اخر"/"آخر", "abc"/"ＡＢＣ" and "4k"/"４Ｋ" are all false today and all true with the proposed body.
- **No regression on existing expectations:** history, ışık, isik, çılgın, istanbul, sehir, video, fox.tv, world news, Hindi, ё/е and ß/ss give identical output. On a 17-name mixed corpus the only difference was half-width katakana folding to full-width, which is an improvement.
- **Speed:** 379 ms against 148 ms per 150k Latin names, and 121 ms against 58 ms per 50k Turkish names. The 2.6 times claim holds.
- **No persisted state depends on the fold:** `normalize` is private, no normalized key is stored, and no index uses `localized_*`; the only SQL users are Models/Requests.swift:73-175.

Scope correction: "Every search field" is wrong. The Search tab uses its own matcher, `text.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains` (Views/SearchView.swift:126-127, used at 261-269). The TV Guide uses `lowercased().contains` (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:28, 160). Neither calls `normalize`, so this fix leaves both unchanged. It covers the inline fields on Live, Movies, Series, All and category views, favorites, history, downloads, the category picker and M3U.

The proposed fold still misses Hebrew niqqud and hamza on yeh or waw (ئ, ؤ). That is acceptable but should not be described as complete Arabic folding.

**Corrected claim:** The shared fold in `CatalogTextSearch.normalize`, and its duplicate in the SQL functions, does not cover Arabic orthographic variants (hamza or madda on alef, harakat, tatweel, ta marbuta, alef maqsura, Farsi yeh and keheh) or full-width forms. In the inline search fields that use it, "احمد" does not find "أحمد" and "abc" does not find "ＡＢＣ". The Search tab (SearchView.swift:127) and the TV Guide (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:28, 160) use other matchers and are affected only once they are moved onto this fold.

**Corrected fix:** Apply the proposed `normalize` body as written: one `folding` call with `.widthInsensitive` added, then a single scalar pass with the Arabic and Persian mappings. Make `normalize` internal and call `CatalogTextSearch.normalize` from Persistence.swift:108-113, including as the closure passed to `NormalizedQueryCache.words(for:normalize:)`, and delete the duplicate there.

The Search tab and the TV Guide get the benefit only if their matchers are pointed at CatalogTextSearch; that belongs to the matcher-unification findings, such as search-ux-11 for the guide. Add the Arabic, full-width and half-width-katakana cases to CatalogTextSearchTests.

**API check:** - `.widthInsensitive`: `NSWidthInsensitiveSearch API_AVAILABLE(macos(10.5), ios(2.0), watchos(2.0), tvos(9.0)) = 256` at Foundation.framework/Headers/NSString.h:56, imported into Swift as `String.CompareOptions.widthInsensitive`. The finder had marked this unverified; it is present.
- `StringProtocol.folding(options:locale:)`: already used at CatalogTextSearch.swift:14.
- `String.UnicodeScalarView()`, `append(_:)`, `String(_:)` and `CharacterSet.contains(Unicode.Scalar)`: compiled and ran in a scratch build with swiftc -O.
- Isolation: the target sets `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`, but `CatalogTextSearch` is declared `nonisolated enum` (line 5), so the call from the `@Sendable` closure inside GRDB's `prepareDatabase` compiles.

**Regression risks:** - Ta marbuta to heh, alef maqsura to yeh and keheh to kaf slightly widen matches. This is the standard Arabic and Persian search normalization and gives only extra hits, no lost ones.
- Half-width katakana now folds to full-width, so those names match more queries.
- Output for Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Hindi, CJK and Hangul was byte-identical on the sample, so the relevance sort (`equals`/`startsWith`) and the existing tests are unaffected.
- The SQL functions are registered `pure: true`. No expression index or stored column uses them, so changing the fold cannot leave stale index contents.
- The off-main filtering, the query cache and the debounce are untouched, and the fold gets faster.

**How to verify:** 1. Unit tests in another-iptv-playerTests/CatalogTextSearchTests.swift: add "احمد"/"أحمد", "محمد"/"مُحَمَّد", "مدرسه"/"مدرسة", "علي"/"على", "محمد"/"مـحـمد", "abc"/"ＡＢＣ", "4k"/"４Ｋ". All existing tests must stay green.
2. One GRDB test that `localized_contains('أحمد', 'احمد')` returns 1, to prove the SQL path shares the fold.
3. Scratch reproduction: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ogulcanozcan-repositories-another-iptv-player/001e9d37-eba7-4a79-997e-bc1be1bce855/scratchpad/agents/verify-search-b/v.swift, which prints old and new results and timings.
4. Simulator: in the Movies inline field, with an Arabic-titled item in the catalog, type the un-hamzated form and confirm the row appears. Then confirm the Search tab still misses it until its matcher is unified.

## search-ux-13 — Search prompts end in three full stops in all ten languages ("Search movie...", "Search...").

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab, Every inline search field
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:81, 87, 89, 100, 108, 122, 136, 258, 431`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Wording of the Search tab prompt, if it changes.

**What the user perceives:** Every field reads like a loading label (L01 "Search series...", M04 "Search movie...", Q01 "Search..."). Apple's own placeholders are plain noun phrases without an ellipsis ("Search", "Shows, Movies, and More").

**Mechanism (finder):** The nine `*.search_placeholder` and `search.placeholder` values carry a literal "..." in en, tr, de, ar, zh and the other five files.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Remove the trailing "..." from the nine keys in each of the ten Localizable.strings files. Optionally make the Search tab prompt say what is searchable, for example "Channels, Movies, Series". Those files contain the uncommitted tip keys: edit the nine existing lines only.

**Verifier reasons:** - **Strings:** I grepped all ten Localization/*.lproj/Localizable.strings files. Each has the same nine keys (live, vod, series, category_picker, m3u, history, favorites, download `.search_placeholder`, and `search.placeholder`), and all 90 values end in three ASCII full stops. The cited line numbers are right for en and tr (81, 87, 89, 100, 108, 122, 136, 258, 431); in the other eight files the last two keys sit at 256 and 409.
- **Screenshots:** iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows "Search channel...", M04-movies-all.png shows "Search movie...", and Q01-search-idle.png shows "Search..." in the bottom search field.
- **Native reference:** Apple's prompts are plain phrases with no ellipsis, such as "Search" or "Shows, Movies, and More".
- **Not deliberate:** the strings predate the monorepo move (`git log -S` reaches only d2489f9) and no comment explains the ellipsis.
- **Tests:** UI tests find fields with `app.searchFields.firstMatch` (ScreensUITests.swift:31, 37, 333, 397, 409; UserFlowsUITests.swift:296, 316), never by placeholder text, so nothing breaks.
- **Tip-jar work:** the uncommitted tip keys are separate added hunks (en: after lines 188 and 191). Editing the nine existing lines does not touch them.

**Corrected claim:** The nine search prompt strings end in a literal "..." in all ten languages (90 values). Apple's search placeholders carry no ellipsis, so every search field in the app reads slightly non-native. Line numbers for `download.search_placeholder` and `search.placeholder` are 431 and 258 in en and tr, and 256 and 409 in the other eight files.

**Corrected fix:** Remove the trailing "..." from the nine keys in each of the ten Localizable.strings files, editing only those lines so the uncommitted tip keys stay as they are.

Optional, and the owner's call: make `search.placeholder` say what is searchable (for example "Channels, Movies, Series"), and align the Turkish capitalisation ("Kanal Ara" against "Kategori ara").

**API check:** No API involved; this is a strings-only change. The prompts reach SwiftUI through the existing `searchable(..., prompt: L(...))` call sites, for example SearchView.swift:69 and LiveStreamsView.swift:93, which stay unchanged.

**Regression risks:** - No test asserts placeholder text, and any key-parity check is unaffected because no key is added or removed.
- The Localizable.strings files hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys; a careless whole-file rewrite or re-sort would disturb them, so the edit must be line-level.
- If the Search tab prompt wording changes, it needs translating into all ten languages.

**How to verify:** 1. `grep -n 'search_placeholder"\|"search.placeholder"' Localization/*.lproj/Localizable.strings | grep '\.\.\."'` returns nothing.
2. `git diff` on the ten files shows exactly nine changed lines each, plus the pre-existing tip-key hunks unchanged.
3. Re-capture Q01, L01 and M04 and compare.
4. Run the existing UI tests that type into search fields.

## secondary-screens-1 — A favourite cannot be removed from the Favorites screen: the grid has no context menu, swipe or edit mode, and a live channel can only be un-starred from inside the player

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Favorites (Xtream)
- Code: `Views/FavoritesView.swift:106-121, 131-147, 157-173`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457`

**What the user perceives:** Long-pressing a card in Favorites does nothing useful: a movie or series card just opens its detail, a channel card starts playback (shots/README.txt: "long press = playback starts, there is no context menu"; iphone-dark/L08-live-card-long-press.png, iphone-light/M06-movie-card-long-press.png). To drop a favourite the user has to open the detail screen and tap the star, or for a channel start the stream and find the star in the player chrome. When the row finally changes, the card vanishes without any reflow animation.

**Mechanism (finder):** FavoritesView renders LiveStreamCard / NavigationLink{VODStreamCard} / NavigationLink{SeriesCard} with no .contextMenu (Views/FavoritesView.swift:108-119, 133-145, 159-171). The only Xtream favourite toggles live in MovieDetailView.swift:87, SeriesView.swift:882 and the live player shell (LiveStreamsView.swift:1159). The M3U side already has the native pattern (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457) and the strings exist (favorites.remove / favorites.add). The three @Query lists update outside any animation transaction, so the LazyVGrid re-lays out instantly.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add a context menu to the three ForEach cells in FavoritesView only (not to the shared card structs, so the big browse grids are untouched). Every item on this screen is a favourite, so no per-card state query is needed:

.contextMenu {
    Button { removeFavorite(streamId: item.stream.streamId, type: "vod") } label: {
        Label(L("favorites.remove"), systemImage: "star.slash")
    }
}

private func removeFavorite(streamId: Int, type: String) {
    let pid = playlist.id
    Task { try? await appDatabase.write { db in
        _ = try DBFavorite.filter(Column("streamId") == streamId && Column("playlistId") == pid && Column("type") == type).deleteAll(db)
    } }
}

(add `import GRDB` and `@Environment(\.appDatabase)`; same delete as MovieDetailView.swift:319-322). Animate the reflow with `.animation(.snappy, value: favoriteVODs.map(\.stream.streamId))` on each grid (lists are small). Same label and icon as the M3U menu so both playlist kinds match. No new strings.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0); View.animation(_:value:) (iOS 13.0 (found in SwiftUICore interface))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/FavoritesView.swift:106-121, 131-147, 157-173: the three ForEach cells are a bare LiveStreamCard, NavigationLink{VODStreamCard} and NavigationLink{SeriesCard}; there is no .contextMenu, swipe or edit mode anywhere in the file. A repo-wide grep for contextMenu finds only Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446 and Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:82, so no Xtream card has one. DBFavorite is written in exactly three places: MovieDetailView.swift:315-331, SeriesView.swift:1249-1264 and the live player shell (LiveStreamsView.swift:1159-1181). LiveStreamCard (LiveStreamsView.swift:418-459) is a plain Button, so a favourite channel can only be un-starred after starting playback. shots/README.txt confirms long press just starts playback. The Favorite*Request observations (Models/Requests.swift:292-371) deliver outside any animation transaction, so the grid reflows instantly. No comment or history marks the absence as deliberate (the file was last touched by 0ab5bcd / 2ec2c18, neither discusses it). The fix compiles here: \.appDatabase exists (Database/Environment.swift:8, already used the same way at WatchHistoryListView.swift:20), AppDatabase.write is async throws with an escaping closure (Database/AppDatabase.swift:479), the strings favorites.remove / favorites.add exist (en Localizable.strings:137-138), and the icon/label match the M3U menu at M3UChannelsView.swift:452-456. Because the menu is attached at the FavoritesView call sites, the shared card structs and the big browse grids are untouched. Severity lowered to medium: movies and series can still be removed through their detail screen; only live channels have no out-of-player path.

**Corrected claim:** On the Xtream Favorites screen a card has no context menu, swipe or edit mode. A movie or series can only be removed by opening its detail and tapping the star; a live channel can only be removed by starting the stream and using the star in the player chrome. When a favourite is removed the grid re-lays out without animation.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: in FavoritesView only, add `.contextMenu { Button { removeFavorite(streamId:type:) } label: { Label(L("favorites.remove"), systemImage: "star.slash") } }` to the three ForEach cells (on the LiveStreamCard and on the two NavigationLinks), add `import GRDB` and `@Environment(\.appDatabase)`, and delete with the same filter as MovieDetailView.swift:319-322 (capture playlist.id in a local before the write closure). Mark the button `role: .destructive` only if the owner wants it red; the M3U menu does not. Animate the reflow with `.animation(.snappy, value: favoriteVODs.map(\.stream.streamId))` on each LazyVGrid (keyed on the unfiltered query result so typing in search is not animated). Optional polish: `.contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))` on the cell so the lifted preview has card-shaped corners.

**API check:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9870 under @available(iOS 13.0, ...). View.animation(_:value:) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13425 (iOS 13.0). Animation.snappy found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13317 (@_alwaysEmitIntoClient; iOS 17 API, fine for the iOS 18 target). ContentShapeKinds.contextMenuPreview found at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4000 and contentShape(_:_:eoFill:) at :13336, both iOS 15.0. No iOS 26-only API involved.

**Regression risks:** Low. The context menu sits on a plain Button (live) and on NavigationLinks (movie, series); tap must still play / navigate, which is standard behaviour but should be tapped through once. The default lifted preview includes the title text under the poster; acceptable, or constrain with the contextMenuPreview content shape. The animation modifier must stay keyed on ids of the unfiltered list, otherwise progress-map or metadata refreshes would animate. Removing the last item swaps the ScrollView for the empty state without a transition (unchanged from today). No tip-jar file touched.

**How to verify:** UI test with one seeded favourite per type: open Favorites, long-press the card, tap "Remove from Favorites", assert the cell disappears and the empty state shows; assert a plain tap still opens the detail (movie/series) or the player (live). Manually with 6+ favourites: the remaining cards slide into place, and typing in the search field does not animate.

## secondary-screens-2 — The Favorites type picker is a fixed material slab above three separate scroll views, so a third of the phone screen is static header with a hard two-tone seam

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Favorites (Xtream)
- Code: `Views/FavoritesView.swift:35-59, 101-176`

**What the user perceives:** On iPhone the header (large title + search + picker) ends at y=665 of 2000 in iphone-light/M09-favorites-movies.png: one third of the screen never scrolls. The band behind it is a flat grey block that stops with a hard edge against the white (light) or pure black (iphone-dark/M09-favorites-movies.png) content, unlike every other screen where content scrolls under a soft iOS 26 edge effect. In light mode the search field's capsule is invisible against that grey (compare iphone-light/T05-downloads.png where the same field has a visible pill). ipad-light/L06-favorites.png shows the same slab.

**Mechanism (finder):** body is `VStack { Picker.padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial); Group { liveGrid | vodGrid | seriesGrid } }` (Views/FavoritesView.swift:36-55). `.background(.ultraThinMaterial)` ignores the top safe area by default, so the material fills from the top of the screen to the bottom of the picker and nothing ever scrolls beneath it (there is nothing to blur). Because the root is a VStack and each type owns its own ScrollView (:106, :131, :157), the navigation bar has no scroll view adjacent to it: the iOS 26 scroll-edge effect cannot form and the large title most likely never collapses (to confirm in the simulator).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make one ScrollView the root and hang the picker on its top safe area so content scrolls under it:

ScrollView {
    switch selectedType { case "live": liveGridContent; case "vod": vodGridContent; default: seriesGridContent }   // LazyVGrid only
}
.overlay { if currentListIsEmpty { emptyState } }
.modifier(TopBar { typePicker.padding(.horizontal).padding(.vertical, 8) })

struct TopBar<Bar: View>: ViewModifier {
    @ViewBuilder var bar: () -> Bar
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if #available(iOS 26, *) { content.safeAreaBar(edge: .top) { bar() } }
        else { content.safeAreaInset(edge: .top, spacing: 0) { bar().background(.bar) } }
    }
}

iOS 26: safeAreaBar extends the system scroll-edge effect over the picker (no opaque slab). iOS 18 fallback: safeAreaInset with the standard `.bar` material, which now has real content scrolling beneath it. Keep the three @Query properties as they are (type switching stays instant).

**APIs:** View.safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 26.0); View.safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 15.0 (found in SwiftUICore interface))

**Verifier reasons:** Views/FavoritesView.swift:36-55 is `VStack(spacing: 0) { Picker.pickerStyle(.segmented).padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial); Group { liveGrid | vodGrid | seriesGrid } }`, and each grid owns its own ScrollView (:106, :131, :157). `background(_:)` with a ShapeStyle ignores safe-area edges by default, so the material runs from the top of the screen to the bottom of the picker and nothing ever scrolls behind it. Screenshots confirm the result: iphone-light/M09-favorites-movies.png and iphone-light/L04-favorites-live.png show a flat grey band ending in a hard edge at y~665 of 2000, with the search field's capsule invisible against it (compare iphone-light/T05-downloads.png where the same field has a visible pill); iphone-dark/M09 shows the same band against pure black; ipad-light/L06-favorites.png shows the slab on iPad. So the visual claim stands. Two parts are not proven: (1) all available screenshots show the empty state, so nothing demonstrates what a populated grid looks like at the seam; (2) the statement that the large title never collapses is the finder's own guess and needs a simulator run. The fix also needs correcting: one shared ScrollView for the three types keeps the scroll offset when the user switches type (today each type gets a fresh scroll view at the top), and it is a larger restructure than needed.

**Corrected claim:** The Favorites type picker sits in a VStack above the content with a full-bleed .ultraThinMaterial background, producing a static grey header block (about a third of an iPhone screen together with the large title and search field) with a hard seam against the content and an invisible search pill in light mode. Because the scroll views are not the root content, the iOS 26 scroll-edge effect cannot form under the bar; whether the large title collapses is unverified.

**Corrected fix:** Smaller variant that keeps the three grids and their scroll views: delete the VStack and the `.background(.ultraThinMaterial)`, keep `Group { if selectedType == "live" { liveGrid } else if ... }` as the root, and hang the picker on the top safe area of that Group with the proposed modifier: iOS 26 `content.safeAreaBar(edge: .top) { picker.padding(.horizontal).padding(.vertical, 8) }`, iOS 18 fallback `content.safeAreaInset(edge: .top, spacing: 0) { picker....background(.bar) }`. The safe-area inset propagates into whichever ScrollView (or empty state) is showing, so content scrolls under the picker, each type still starts at the top when selected, and the three @Query properties are untouched. Do not merge the grids into one ScrollView unless the scroll offset is also reset on type change.

**API check:** safeAreaBar(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment:, spacing:, content:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17362 under @available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0, *): must be behind `if #available(iOS 26, *)`. safeAreaInset(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment:, spacing:, content:) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19082 (iOS 15.0). ShapeStyle.bar (Material) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6340. The proposed ViewModifier with a `@ViewBuilder var bar: () -> Bar` stored closure compiles against both signatures (both take a non-escaping builder).

**Regression risks:** Interaction of a top safe-area bar with the large title plus the navigation-bar search field (.searchable at FavoritesView.swift:58) cannot be judged from code: the picker may be placed between the search field and the content as intended, or the large-title collapse may behave differently on iOS 18 vs 26. The empty state (FavoritesView.swift:178-191) is not a scroll view; it will simply be inset, which changes its vertical centring slightly. On iOS 18 the .bar material is visible only when content is under it; with few favourites it looks like a plain bar. No effect on other screens; no tip-jar file touched.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 26 and iOS 18, iPhone and iPad, light and dark, with 30+ favourites of one type: (a) no grey slab or hard seam, search pill visible in light mode; (b) scroll: the large title collapses, the picker stays pinned and content is visible/blurred beneath it; (c) switch type while scrolled: the new type starts at the top; (d) empty state still centred. Re-shoot M09 (light/dark) and ipad L06 for comparison.

## secondary-screens-3 — The detail-screen download button ignores taps while downloading and once downloaded, and the compact variant changes width as the percentage changes, re-wrapping the episode row

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail (episode rows)
- Code: `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:77-83, 101-143, 176-202`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1446-1473`

**What the user perceives:** After tapping Download the button turns into a spinner with a percentage and stops responding: tapping it again does nothing, and tapping the green "Downloaded" state does nothing either. Cancelling or deleting only works through an undiscoverable long-press. In an episode list the icon-only button grows into "spinner + 7%", then "12%", then "100%", and each width change shrinks the text column next to it, so the episode title and plot re-wrap while the user is reading.

**Mechanism (finder):** primaryAction() is a no-op for .downloading/.queued/.completed (DownloadButton.swift:195-200); the actions exist only in `.contextMenu` (:82, :146-173). Compact idle is an icon with 8pt padding (:102-114) while compact downloading is ProgressView + Text("%d%%") (:126-134); the neighbouring text VStack is `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` (SeriesView.swift:1446), so it absorbs every width change. The progress indicator is `ProgressView(value:).progressViewStyle(.circular).controlSize(.mini)` (:127-129); check in the simulator whether it reflects the value at all (the circular style has had no determinate rendering on iOS).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Make the non-idle states a real menu on tap, keep the plain button for idle/failed:

switch state {
case .idle, .failed: Button(action: primaryAction) { labelContent }.buttonStyle(.plain).contextMenu { contextMenuItems }
default: Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent }.buttonStyle(.plain)
}

(contextMenuItems already holds Cancel / Delete with existing strings.)
2) Compact downloading label: a fixed-size determinate ring with the same footprint as the idle icon, no text:

ZStack {
    Circle().stroke(.quaternary, lineWidth: 2)
    Circle().trim(from: 0, to: progress).stroke(Color.accentColor, style: .init(lineWidth: 2, lineCap: .round)).rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))
    Image(systemName: "stop.fill").font(.system(size: 7))
}
.frame(width: 18, height: 18)
.animation(.linear(duration: 0.3), value: progress)

plus `.accessibilityValue("\(Int(progress*100))%")`. The full-width variant keeps its text; give the percentage a fixed minimum width so 9% -> 10% does not shift the label.

**APIs:** Menu(content:label:) (iOS 14.0); Shape.trim(from:to:) / View.animation(_:value:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:176-202: primaryAction() does nothing for .downloading/.queued/.completed; Cancel and Delete exist only in the .contextMenu (:82, :146-173). The Turkish comments at :196 and :199 show this was written on purpose ("tap ignored while downloading; use the context menu to cancel"), so it is a deliberate choice, but it is the opposite of the system pattern (App Store / TV / Music: tap the progress ring to stop, tap the downloaded badge for a Remove menu), and a button that visibly does nothing on tap is what the owner asked to eliminate. Width: compact idle/queued/completed/failed is a lone footnote icon with 8 pt padding (:101-114); compact downloading is ProgressView + Text(L("download.downloading_format")) with the same padding (:125-134); the string is "%d%%" (en Localizable.strings:425). The neighbouring text column in the episode row is `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` (Views/SeriesView.swift:1446) with a 5-line plot (:1438-1443), so it absorbs every width change. Correction of detail: the text is .monospacedDigit(), so the width changes at state transitions (idle -> downloading -> completed) and at 10 % and 100 %, not at every percent. DownloadManager only publishes when the integer percent changes (Models/DownloadManager.swift:56-59, 566-571), so the proposed 0.3 s linear ring animation fits the update rate. The circular ProgressView with a value (:127-129) is documented to possibly render as an indeterminate spinner off macOS; replacing it with a drawn ring removes that doubt. The full-width variant in MovieDetailView.swift:147 uses maxWidth .infinity, so only its centred label shifts by a few points.

**Corrected claim:** The download button ignores taps while queued, downloading and once downloaded; cancel and delete are reachable only by long-press (deliberate per the code comments, but not the system pattern). In episode rows the compact button grows from an icon to spinner-plus-percentage and back, changing width at each state change and at 10 % and 100 %, which re-wraps the episode title and plot beside it.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two refinements. (1) Non-idle states respond to tap: keep `Button(action: primaryAction)` + contextMenu for .idle/.failed; for .queued/.downloading/.completed use `Menu { contextMenuItems } label: { labelContent }.buttonStyle(.plain)` (existing strings). Owner decision: for .queued/.downloading a direct tap-to-cancel on the stop ring is the App Store behaviour and one step shorter; the Menu is the safer variant because cancel deletes the partial file and resume data (Models/DownloadManager.swift:230-247). (2) Compact downloading label: a determinate ring (Circle().trim(from: 0, to: progress) over a track, stop.fill glyph) with no text. To guarantee the same footprint at every Dynamic Type size, size it from the idle glyph instead of a hard-coded 18 pt: `Image(systemName: "arrow.down.circle").font(.footnote.weight(.semibold)).hidden().overlay { ring }`, inside the same padding/background as the other compact states. Add .accessibilityLabel/.accessibilityValue with the percentage. The full-width variant keeps its text; the fixed minimum width for the percentage is optional.

**API check:** Menu<Label, Content> found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7118 (@available iOS 14.0). Shape.trim(from:to:) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:5716 (iOS 13.0). View.animation(_:value:) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13425 (iOS 13.0). accessibilityValue(_:) StringProtocol overloads found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:65 (ModifiedContent extension annotated iOS 16.0; the View extension is older). CircularProgressViewStyle found at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5012 (iOS 14.0); nothing in the interface promises determinate rendering on iOS. No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Changes behaviour the author chose on purpose (tap ignored), so it should be accepted by the owner. The Menu label re-renders once per percent while the menu may be open; label-only updates do not dismiss a menu on iOS 16+, but check it. Button and Menu swap identity when the state flips to/from idle (no animation between them unless added). The episode row's text column has its own onTapGesture (SeriesView.swift:1447-1450); the button is a sibling, so hit areas do not overlap. M3UDownloadMenuItems (same file, :211-281) is untouched.

**How to verify:** Simulator with a throttled or large download: in a series detail start an episode download and compare the frame of the episode title/plot Text before, during (9 % -> 10 % -> 100 %) and after: it must not change. Tap the ring: Cancel is offered (or the download stops, per the decision). Tap the green Downloaded state: Delete is offered. Check at the largest Dynamic Type size that the ring and the idle icon have the same footprint, and that VoiceOver reads the percentage.
