## secondary-screens-14 — Favorites and the catalog error view hand-build their empty/error states while History, Downloads and the EPG guide use ContentUnavailableView

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Favorites (Xtream), Live TV / Movies / Series load error
- Code: `Views/FavoritesView.swift:103-104, 128-129, 154-155, 178-191`, `Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:11-33`, `Views/Components/LoadingProcessView.swift:3-53`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Optional: add a one-line hint to the Favorites empty state explaining how to add one (new string in ten languages).

**What the user perceives:** The Favorites empty state is a 48pt grey icon and one callout line, visibly different from the bold-title-plus-description layout of "No downloads" (iphone-light/M09-favorites-movies.png vs iphone-light/T05-downloads.png), and its no-results case uses a different sentence than the system search empty state used in Downloads. It offers no next step.

**Mechanism (finder):** FavoritesView.emptyState is a custom VStack with `.padding(.top, 50)` (FavoritesView.swift:178-191) and uses `list.no_result` for searches (:104, :129, :155), while WatchHistoryListView.swift:53-63, DownloadsView.swift:71-77 and EPGGuideView.swift:81-93 use ContentUnavailableView (the guide even with an action). CatalogLoadErrorView re-creates the same layout by hand (CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:12-32). LoadingProcessView is referenced only by its own #Preview.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Favorites: `ContentUnavailableView(L("favorites.empty.movie"), systemImage: "film")` per type (existing strings), and `ContentUnavailableView.search(text: searchText)` when the query has no match. CatalogLoadErrorView body:

ContentUnavailableView {
    Label(L("catalog.load_failed.title"), systemImage: "wifi.exclamationmark")
} description: { Text(message) } actions: {
    Button { onRetry() } label: { Label(L("common.try_again"), systemImage: "arrow.clockwise") }.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
}

Delete LoadingProcessView.swift if the owner confirms it is unused.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0); ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/FavoritesView.swift:178-191 is a hand-built VStack (48pt grey icon, callout text, .padding(.top, 50)); iphone-light/M09-favorites-movies.png shows it and it clearly differs from the ContentUnavailableView in iphone-light/T05-downloads.png (bold title plus description). Search no-match uses `list.no_result` ('No search results.') at :104, :129, :155. Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:12-32 is a hand-built icon/headline/message/button stack used at Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:76, Views/VODView.swift:49, Views/SeriesView.swift:50; it sits directly in a Group (not a ScrollView), so a ContentUnavailableView would centre correctly. LoadingProcessView has no reference outside its own file (grep over sources, tests and project file). All confirmed. Correction to the fix: `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` renders system-provided strings, but the app switches language at runtime through its own bundle (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:47-60, L() at :127), so with an in-app language different from the device language the system text would appear in the wrong language. Downloads already has this flaw (Views/DownloadsView.swift:77); History avoids it with app strings (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:59-63). Also the existing `favorites.empty.*` strings end with a period ('No favorite movies yet.'), which looks odd as a bold title. The catalog error view is already close to the system look, so that part is marginal.

**Corrected claim:** The Xtream Favorites empty and no-result states are hand-built and visibly lighter than the ContentUnavailableView used by History, Downloads and the EPG guide. CatalogLoadErrorView re-creates the same layout by hand (minor). LoadingProcessView is dead code.

**Corrected fix:** Favorites empty: `ContentUnavailableView(L("favorites.empty.movie"), systemImage: "film")` per type (existing strings; whether to strip the trailing period in ten languages is the owner's call). Favorites no-match: use the app-localized pattern already in WatchHistoryListView.swift:59-63, `ContentUnavailableView(L("favorites.empty.no_result.title"), systemImage: "magnifyingglass", description: Text(L("category_picker.not_found.message")))`, NOT `.search(text:)`; consider switching DownloadsView.swift:77 to the same for language consistency. CatalogLoadErrorView: the proposed label/description/actions body is fine; keep `.lineLimit(4)` on the description Text because loadError can be a long raw error. Delete LoadingProcessView.swift only with the owner's confirmation.

**API check:** SwiftUI interface line 17575: `ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` @available iOS 17.0, with `init(label:description:actions:)` and the `init<S: StringProtocol>(_ title: S, systemImage:description:)` overload that L() strings use. `static func search(text: String)` iOS 17.0 (line 17625): exists, but not recommended here because its text is system-localized.

**Regression risks:** Removing `.padding(.top, 50)` moves the empty state to true centre under the segmented picker (intended). ContentUnavailableView drops the 4-line cap on the error message unless re-added. Deleting LoadingProcessView has no runtime effect.

**How to verify:** Screenshot Favorites empty for the three types and a no-match search, light and dark, next to T05-downloads.png; repeat with the in-app language set to a language different from the device language and confirm all text follows the in-app language. Force a catalog load failure (airplane mode on first load) and compare the error state before/after.

## secondary-screens-15 — The history grid draws fixed 160pt cards inside flexible columns, leaving uneven margins that grow with screen width

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Watch history list
- Code: `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:65-77, 160-200`

**What the user perceives:** On a 402pt iPhone the two cards sit about 24pt from the edges with a 33pt gap, on a 440pt phone 34pt and 52pt, instead of the 16pt margins and gutters used elsewhere; thumbnails stay 160x95 on every device, including iPad.

**Mechanism (finder):** Columns are `GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 160), spacing: 16)` in 16pt padding (WatchHistoryListView.swift:66-69, 76), so each column is wider than 160 (177pt on a 402pt screen), while the card and its image are hard-coded to width 160 (:164-165, :183, :199) and centred in the column.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Derive the card width once from the container and pass it down: read the grid width with `.onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self, of: { $0.size.width })` on the ScrollView, compute `cols = max(2, Int((w - 32 + 16) / 176))`, `cardW = floor((w - 32 - 16 * CGFloat(cols - 1)) / CGFloat(cols))`, use `Array(repeating: GridItem(.fixed(cardW), spacing: 16), count: cols)` and give HistoryCardGridItem `width: cardW, height: cardW * 9 / 16` (CachedImage needs concrete sizes for its request). The progress bar width uses the same value.

**APIs:** View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 16.0 (back-deployed; already used at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:376))

**Verifier reasons:** Arithmetic is right: Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:66-69 uses GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 160), spacing: 16) with 16pt padding (:76), cards are fixed 160 wide (:164-165, :183, :199) and centred in the column. On 402pt: 2 columns of 177, so about 24.5pt outer margin and 33pt gap; on 440pt: 34 and 52. But the comparison 'instead of the 16pt margins and gutters used elsewhere' is false. Every grid in the app uses the same adaptive-minimum column with a fixed-size card centred in it: Views/VODView.swift:636, Views/SeriesView.swift:599, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:598, Views/FavoritesView.swift:30-32, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:574. Measured on iphone-light/M04-movies-all.png the poster grid has about 25pt outer margins and 26pt gaps (title at 16pt). So History's margin on a 402pt phone is the same as the main grids; only the gap is somewhat wider (33 vs 26). Fixing History alone to exact 16pt margins would make it the odd screen out. Real but smaller than stated: the cards do not use PosterMetrics, so they stay 160x95 on iPad while every other grid scales. The proposed code also has a first-pass bug: before onGeometryChange fires w is 0, giving cardW = floor((0-32-16)/2) = -24 and a negative frame. No screenshot of this screen exists.

**Corrected claim:** The history grid follows the app-wide pattern of fixed-size cards centred in adaptive columns, so its outer margins (about 24pt on a 402pt phone) match the poster grids; its gap is a little wider (33pt vs 26pt), and its 160x95 cards ignore PosterMetrics and do not scale on iPad. It is not an outlier against a 16pt standard.

**Corrected fix:** Either leave it (consistent with the other grids), or handle it inside one shared grid-metrics change for all grids rather than in this file alone. If only History is touched, the minimal tweak is to scale the card through the existing `@Environment(\.posterMetrics)` like the other grids. If the container-width approach is taken app-wide, guard the first pass (`if width > 0`) so no negative frame is produced, and keep passing concrete width/height to CachedImage.

**API check:** SwiftUICore interface line 6067: `onGeometryChange<T>(for:of:action: (_ newValue: T) -> Void)` @available iOS 16.0, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient (back-deployed); the two-parameter (oldValue, newValue) overload at line 6078 is iOS 18.0. `GridItem(.fixed)` iOS 14.

**Regression risks:** A History-only exact-fit grid would look different from Movies/Series/Favorites grids. Changing card size changes the CachedImage request size (width/height feed the downsample target, Views/CachedImage.swift:104-134), so thumbnails are re-decoded at the new size; negative frame warnings on first layout if width 0 is not guarded.

**How to verify:** Seed watch history and screenshot the history list on iPhone 17 Pro, a Pro Max and an iPad next to the Movies 'All' grid; compare outer margins and gaps between the two screens rather than against 16pt.

## native-reference-1 — Returning from a movie or series detail to a paginated grid re-runs the sort and resets the rendered window to the first 90 items, so the user loses their scroll position

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All Movies, Movie category detail, Recently Added (movies/series), All Series, Series category detail, All Channels / Live category detail (tab switch on iPad)
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:653-668, 737-739`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:615-627, 678-680`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577, 629-631`

**What the user perceives:** In All Movies the user scrolls a few hundred posters down, opens a film, goes back: the grid first shows where they were, then snaps to somewhere around item 80-90 with the paging spinner under it. Photos, TV and App Store always return to the exact cell that was tapped. Not run here; derived from code.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODCategoryContent drives its data from three lifecycle tasks: `.task(id: itemsToken)`, `.task(id: sortOption)`, `.task(id: fileTypeFilter)` (Views/VODView.swift:737-739). A `.task` is cancelled when a pushed screen covers the view and starts again when the view re-appears (the code base already guards against exactly that in Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:54-57 `guard model.state == .loading`). Each restart calls `recompute()`, which unconditionally ends with `visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count)` (Views/VODView.swift:666, pageSize 90 at :626). The ForEach is `displayItems.prefix(visibleCount)` (:691), so the grid shrinks to 90 cells and UIScrollView clamps the offset. Same code in SeriesCategoryContent (Views/SeriesView.swift:625, 678-680) and LiveCategoryContent (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:575, 629-631; Live is only hit on tab switches because channels open the overlay instead of pushing). Side effect of the same structure: on first appearance all three tasks fire, so a 150k catalog is filtered and sorted three times in parallel and `displayItems` is assigned three times.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep pagination and off-main sorting, but key one task on a combined value and skip the work when nothing changed. Sketch for VODCategoryContent (same shape for Series and Live):

private struct InputKey: Equatable { let items: Int; let sort: VODSortOption; let types: Set<String> }
private var inputKey: InputKey { .init(items: itemsToken, sort: sortOption, types: fileTypeFilter) }
@State private var appliedKey: InputKey?
...
.task(id: inputKey) {
    guard appliedKey != inputKey else { return }   // re-appear after a pop: keep window and offset
    await recompute()
    guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
    appliedKey = inputKey
}

Move `visibleCount = min(pageSize, count)` behind the same guard, and add the missing `guard !Task.isCancelled` after the detached sort in SeriesView.swift:622 and LiveStreamsView.swift:573. No new API.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0 (already used))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/VODView.swift:592-740, Views/SeriesView.swift:564-681, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:526-632. The core mechanism is real: VODCategoryContent has three independent lifecycle tasks (VODView.swift:737-739), each calls recompute(), and recompute() ends unconditionally with `visibleCount = min(Self.pageSize, result.count)` (VODView.swift:666, pageSize 90 at :626); the ForEach is `displayItems.prefix(visibleCount)` (:691). `.task` is tied to appear/disappear, and a NavigationStack push makes the covered grid disappear and re-appear on pop, so all three tasks restart with unchanged ids. The code base already defends against exactly this in Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:54-57 (`guard model.state == .loading`). Nothing guards it here: no comment, no applied-key check; git log -S for the reset line shows it arrived with 654cefc (sort/filter + pagination) and was never revisited. The `.equatable()` wrapper (VODView.swift:596-605) only stops parent-driven body passes, it does not stop the view's own tasks. Same structure in SeriesCategoryContent (SeriesView.swift:615-627, 678-680) which additionally lacks `guard !Task.isCancelled` (:622-623), and in LiveCategoryContent (LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577, 629-631, also no cancel guard). The triple recompute on first appearance (three detached filter+sort passes and three displayItems assignments) is also real. Scope corrections: (a) Live is NOT reachable today. Channels open the in-window overlay (LiveStreamCard is a Button, LiveStreamsView.swift:430; DashboardView.swift:92-113 is a ZStack sibling, no disappear), and the tab bar is hidden on these screens on iPad as well (shots/ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png shows no top tab bar), so the 'tab switch on iPad' path does not exist in the current build. It becomes reachable for all three grids the moment native-reference-4 removes the hidden tab bar. (b) Lists with 90 items or fewer (most Recently Added shelves, small categories) are unaffected because the window never grew. (c) The exact visual (snap to ~item 80-90 vs. a blank gap before the clamp) was not run; only the loss of position is certain from code.

**Corrected claim:** In the Movies and Series paginated grids (All Movies, movie category detail, All Series, series category detail, and Recently Added when it has more than 90 items), popping back from a detail restarts the three `.task(id:)` modifiers, re-runs the off-main filter/sort three times and resets `visibleCount` to 90, so a user who had scrolled past roughly item 75 loses their position. On first appearance the same structure sorts the catalog three times in parallel. The Live grids share the code but are not affected in the current build (no push, tab bar hidden on iPhone and iPad); they become affected on tab switches if the tab bar is made visible on those screens.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, for all three content views: one `.task(id: inputKey)` keyed on (itemsToken, sortOption, filter) plus an `@State appliedKey` that short-circuits when nothing changed; set `appliedKey` only after a non-cancelled recompute; add `guard !Task.isCancelled` after the detached work in SeriesView.swift:622 and LiveStreamsView.swift:573. `visibleCount` reset and `prefetch` stay inside recompute, so they only run when the key really changed. Keep the two `onChange` scroll-to-top handlers in VODView.swift:719-728 as they are. Do Live too even though it is unreachable today, because native-reference-4 depends on it. This fix must land before or together with native-reference-4.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166 (`@inlinable nonisolated public func task<T>(id value: T, priority: ..., _ action: ...) -> some View where T : Equatable`), available since iOS 15 and already used here. The key struct only needs Equatable: VODSortOption / SeriesSortOption / LiveSortOption are String-raw enums (Models/VODSortOption.swift:5, SeriesSortOption.swift:5, LiveSortOption.swift:14), Set<String> and Int are Equatable. No new API.

**Regression risks:** Low. The applied-key guard inherits the deliberately weak items signature (count + first + last id) that `==` and itemsToken already use, so it adds no new staleness case. Must not replace itemsToken with full array equality (that was removed on purpose, comment at VODView.swift:639-640). If the key is set before the cancelled check, a cancelled first run would leave the grid empty forever, so order matters. Prefetch no longer re-runs on re-appear, which is harmless (Nuke cache).

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test with a fixture of more than 300 movies: open All Movies, scroll until a cell with index above 200 is on screen, tap it, tap Back, assert the same cell is still hittable without scrolling. Repeat in a series category. Add a log or signpost in recompute() and assert it fires once on first appearance and zero times on pop. Unit-test the key/skip decision as a pure function.

## native-reference-2 — Movie and series detail replace content they already have (poster, title, rating) with a full-screen spinner, and with a full-screen error when the info request fails

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:14, 72-82, 99-103, 106-121, 268-270`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:801, 866-876, 892-896, 941-956, 1006-1013, 1176-1178`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping a poster for the first time pushes a screen whose hero appears for a frame, is swapped for a centred 'Loading...' spinner while get_vod_info / get_series_info runs, and then pops back in. If the panel answers with an error the whole page becomes 'Error / Server error: HTTP 404 / Try Again' with no title or artwork (shots/iphone-dark/S03-series-detail-loading.png, S04-series-detail-settled.png). Apple TV and App Store draw the product page immediately from what the list already knows and fill the rest in place.

**Mechanism (finder):** `@State private var isLoading = false` (MovieDetailView.swift:14) means the first body pass renders `contentScroll`; `.task` then calls `fetchMovieInfo()` which sets `isLoading = true` (:269), and `if isLoading && !currentMovie.metadataLoaded { ProgressView(...) }` (:74-76) replaces the entire scroll view until the DB write flips `metadataLoaded`. `errorView` (:77-78, 106-121) likewise replaces everything. SeriesDetailView is identical (SeriesView.swift:868-872, 1177) even though it already has an in-place state for the missing part: `Text(currentSeries.seasonsLoaded ? ... : L("series.loading_seasons"))` at :1009, which the full-screen spinner hides. HIG Loading: 'Show something as soon as possible ... consider showing placeholder text, graphics, or animations as content loads'.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Always render `contentScroll`; make loading and error local to the part that is missing.
- Movie: drop the `isLoading &&` branch; while `!currentMovie.metadataLoaded && isLoading` show a redacted plot block: `DetailPlotBlock(plot: placeholderText).redacted(reason: .placeholder)`; on error show an inline row under the action bar (message + 'Try Again' using the existing `common.try_again`) instead of `errorView`.
- Series: drop the branch, keep hero/actions, let `seasonsSection` show a small `ProgressView` row while seasons load and the inline retry row on error.
No new strings are required. This is also the precondition for a zoom transition (separate finding): zooming a poster into a spinner looks worse than today.

**APIs:** View.redacted(reason:) (iOS 14.0); ContentUnavailableView (iOS 17.0 (optional, for the inline error))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/MovieDetailView.swift:14, 72-82, 99-121, 268-313 and Views/SeriesView.swift:801, 866-896, 941-956, 1006-1013, 1176-1247. `isLoading` starts false, so the first body pass renders `contentScroll` with the hero built from list data (title, poster, rating: heroConfig at MovieDetailView.swift:58-70); `.task` then calls fetchMovieInfo(), which sets `isLoading = true` (:269) and the branch at :74-76 swaps the whole scroll view for a centred ProgressView until the DB write flips metadataLoaded. So the push animation shows hero, then spinner, then hero again. On failure `errorView` (:77-78, 106-121) replaces everything. SeriesDetailView is identical (SeriesView.swift:868-872, 1177) and already has an in-place state for the missing part (:1009) that the spinner hides. shots/iphone-dark/S03-series-detail-loading.png and S04 show the result: a black page with 'Error / Server error: HTTP 404 / Try Again' and no title or artwork, while M07-movie-detail.png shows how much the list already knows. No comment marks this as deliberate; git log -S shows the branch dates from the initial import (d2489f9). At real catalog sizes almost no film has metadataLoaded, so nearly every first open takes this path, and panel latency is typically hundreds of ms to seconds. Additional consequence the finding did not state: on error the movie page hides Watch Now and Download although the playback URL only needs streamId + containerExtension (MovieDetailView.swift:143-146), so a failing get_vod_info blocks playback entirely.

**Corrected claim:** As stated. Add: on a failed info request the movie detail also removes the Watch Now and Download actions, although playback does not depend on that request.

**Corrected fix:** Always render `contentScroll`; make loading and error local. Movie: derive the loading state from `!currentMovie.metadataLoaded && errorMessage == nil` (not from `isLoading`, which is false on the first frame and would make the placeholder pop in one frame late); show a redacted DetailPlotBlock while loading; on error show an inline message + 'Try Again' row under the action bar using the existing common.try_again string. Keep Watch Now and Download usable in both states. Series: drop the full-screen branch; in `seasonsSection` show a small ProgressView row while `!seasonsLoaded && errorMessage == nil` and the inline retry row on error (otherwise the existing text at SeriesView.swift:1009 would say 'loading seasons' forever after a failure). One addition the proposal missed: the series primary button calls playFirstEpisode(), which silently returns when `seasons` is empty (SeriesView.swift:1084-1086), so while seasons are missing the primary CTA must be disabled or hidden; DetailActionBar has no disabled state today (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:189-210), so add an `isPrimaryEnabled` parameter defaulting to true rather than disabling the whole bar (the trailer button should stay live).

**API check:** View.redacted(reason:) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6107, extension available iOS 14.0. ContentUnavailableView found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17575, iOS 17.0 (already used in Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:53). Both are below the iOS 18 deployment target; no availability guard needed.

**Regression risks:** Content now arrives in place, so genre chips, plot, backdrop and director/cast still shift the layout when metadata lands; the redacted plot only partly reserves that space. The series Watch button becomes visible before seasons exist and must be disabled (see fix). DetailActionBar is shared by both detail screens, so the new parameter needs a default. `showNavTitle` scroll tracking keeps working because the ScrollView is no longer swapped out. Does not touch the player hand-off.

**How to verify:** Screenshot comparison of S03/S04: hero, title and action bar must be visible with an inline error row. Simulator UI test with the info endpoint stubbed slow: push a movie with metadataLoaded == false and assert the title and the Watch Now button exist during loading; stub a 404 and assert Watch Now is still hittable and the retry row exists. For series assert the primary button is disabled until seasons arrive.

## native-reference-3 — No Xtream card has a context menu: long-pressing a channel, poster, history card or search row does nothing (or just plays)

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home and grids, Movies home and grids, Series home and grids, Continue Watching, Watch history, Favorites, Search results
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459`, `Views/VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-704`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:311-322, 423-434, 650-660`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:70-74`, `Views/SearchView.swift:155-188, 204-213`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:207-281`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Which actions each menu carries (favorite, download, guide, remove from history) is a product choice; the mechanism is a plain addition.

**What the user perceives:** In TV, Music, App Store and Photos every lockup lifts on long press and offers the obvious actions. Here a long press on a channel starts playback and on a poster does nothing (screenshots README: 'long press = playback starts, there is no context menu'; shots/iphone-dark/M06-movie-card-long-press.png is just the detail). Favoriting a film needs: open detail, tap star, go back. A single item cannot be removed from Continue Watching at all, only 'clear all' (WatchHistoryListView.swift:101-107).

**Mechanism (finder):** `contextMenu` exists only on the M3U channel card (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446) and on DownloadButton (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:82). LiveStreamCard, VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, HistoryCard and the search rows have none. The app's own copy already promises the gesture: `favorites.empty.message` = 'Long press a channel ... to add' (Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:134).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add `.contextMenu` at the call sites (outside the card structs so the Equatable shelf rows keep their signature), reusing the existing lazy pattern so no per-card @Query is opened while scrolling (comment at VODView.swift:497, precedent `M3UDownloadMenuItems`):

struct CatalogFavoriteMenuButton: View {          // body runs only when the menu is built
    @Query<IsFavoriteRequest> private var isFavorite: Bool
    let streamId: Int; let playlistId: UUID; let type: String
    var body: some View { Button { toggle() } label: { Label(isFavorite ? L("favorites.remove") : L("favorites.add"), systemImage: isFavorite ? "star.slash" : "star") } }
}

NavigationLink { MovieDetailView(...) } label: { VODStreamCard(...) }
    .buttonStyle(.plain)
    .contextMenu {
        CatalogFavoriteMenuButton(streamId: item.stream.streamId, playlistId: playlist.id, type: "vod")
        M3UDownloadMenuItems(...)        // generalise its hard-coded type: "vod"
    }

Live cards: favorite + 'TV Guide' (push ChannelEPGDetailView). Series: favorite. History cards: 'Remove' (one new string, 10 languages) deleting the DBWatchHistory row. Keep menus to 2-3 items (HIG: small number, same actions available elsewhere, destructive last). `favorites.add` / `favorites.remove` already exist in all ten languages.

**APIs:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) (iOS 13.0); View.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) (iOS 16.0 (optional preview))

**Verifier reasons:** The core fact is verified: `grep contextMenu` over the sources finds only Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446 and Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:82. LiveStreamCard (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459), VODStreamCard (Views/VODView.swift:490-545), SeriesCard, HistoryCard (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53, a plain onTapGesture), HistoryCardGridItem (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:154-203) and the search rows (Views/SearchView.swift:155-213) have none. Single history entries can only be removed by clear-all (WatchHistoryListView.swift:101-107, 129-149; the only other deletes are the settings wipes). Two parts of the claim do not hold. (1) The supporting evidence 'the app's own copy already promises the gesture' is wrong for Xtream: `favorites.empty.message` is used only in Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:31, the M3U screen where the context menu does exist; the Xtream FavoritesView uses favorites.empty.live/movie/series (Views/FavoritesView.swift:104, 129, 155). (2) This is a missing feature, not a defect: nothing is broken, favoriting works from the detail screen. Fix corrections are needed as well, see corrected_fix.

**Corrected claim:** Xtream lockups (channel, movie, series, history cards, search rows) have no context menu, unlike the M3U channel card and unlike Apple's TV, Music and App Store lockups. Favoriting a film or series requires opening the detail, and a single item cannot be removed from watch history. This is a native-feel addition and a product decision, not a bug; no existing copy promises the gesture on Xtream screens.

**Corrected fix:** Add `.contextMenu` at the call sites as proposed, with these corrections. (a) Put the whole menu in ONE small view struct per content type that takes only (playlist, stream) and does all work in `body` (favorite @Query, PlaybackURLBuilder, download item). The `menuItems` closure is non-escaping and runs eagerly on every cell body pass, so building URLs or several sub-views inline there would add per-cell work while scrolling; a single struct init is the cheap equivalent of the M3UDownloadMenuItems precedent (DownloadButton.swift:207-211). (b) IsFavoriteRequest (Models/Requests.swift:269-290) and DownloadedItemByIDRequest publish asynchronously, so the menu can be built with the default value (false) and show 'Add to Favorites' for an item that is already a favorite. Either give the menu its own request with GRDB's `.immediate` scheduling (exists at GRDB/ValueObservation/ValueObservationScheduler.swift:148) or make the action a true toggle inside the write transaction so a stale label cannot insert a duplicate. (c) Add `.contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: ...))` so the lifted preview is the poster shape and not a rectangle around poster + title. (d) First pass: favorite toggle on movie, series and channel cards (grids, shelves, Favorites, search rows), download on movies, and 'Remove' on history cards (one new string in ten languages). Leave 'TV Guide' out of the live menu for now: it needs a navigation push from inside Equatable shelf rows, which means threading a callback or path through them. (e) M3UDownloadMenuItems hard-codes type "vod" (DownloadButton.swift:268), which is already right for Xtream movies; no generalisation is needed unless episodes are added.

**API check:** View.contextMenu(menuItems:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9870, iOS 13.0. View.contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) found at :9876, iOS 16.0. ContentShapeKinds.contextMenuPreview found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4000 (struct available iOS 15.0). All below the iOS 18 target, no availability guard needed. favorites.add / favorites.remove exist (Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:137-138).

**Regression risks:** Per-cell cost while scrolling if the menu closure does real work (see fix a). Wrong favorite label from the async first value (fix b). Long press on a live card currently ends in playback on release; with a menu it lifts instead, which is the intended change but alters a habit. The Equatable shelf rows keep their signature as long as the modifier is added inside the row body and takes no new stored inputs. The new 'Remove' string edits the ten Localizable.strings files that also hold the owner's uncommitted tip keys: append only, leave those keys untouched.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test: long-press a movie card on the Movies home, assert 'Add to Favorites' exists, tap it, open Favorites and assert the movie is listed; long-press the same card again and assert the label is now 'Remove from Favorites' (this catches the async-default problem). Instruments on a large catalog: scrolling a shelf and a grid must not start IsFavoriteRequest observations and must show no extra main-thread time in cell bodies.

## native-reference-4 — The tab bar is hidden on twelve pushed browse screens but not on the detail screens behind them, so it leaves and returns as the user drills in; the iOS 26 minimise-on-scroll behaviour is not adopted

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Live/Movies/Series category detail, All Channels / All Movies / All Series, Recently Added, Watch history, TV Guide, M3U group detail and favorites, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722`, `Views/VODView.swift:380, 563, 822`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:502`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:63`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:82`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:85`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:45`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: On iOS 18 the grids lose about 49 pt of height when the bar stays. Owner chooses between Apple's always-visible bar (recommended) and keeping the extra height; if hiding is kept it must at least be consistent across the pushed chain.

**What the user perceives:** Movies (bar) -> Action (bar slides away, shots/iphone-dark/M03, M04) -> a film (bar comes back, M07) -> Back (bar leaves) -> Back (bar returns). The chrome moves on every step and the user cannot switch tabs from a category. In Apple's TV, Music and App Store the tab bar stays through every push; on iOS 26 it shrinks while scrolling down instead of disappearing.

**Mechanism (finder):** `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` is applied on the twelve screens listed; MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView and FavoritesView carry no such modifier, so the default (visible) applies when they are pushed from a hidden-bar screen. HIG Tab bars: 'Make sure the tab bar is visible when people navigate to different sections of your app. If you hide the tab bar, people can forget which area of the app they're in.' Neither TabView (DashboardView.swift:48-85, M3UDashboardView.swift:26-45) sets a minimise behaviour.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Remove the twelve `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` lines and give both TabViews the iOS 26 behaviour:

extension View {
    @ViewBuilder func tabBarMinimizesOnScroll() -> some View {
        if #available(iOS 26, *) { self.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown) } else { self }
    }
}
// DashboardView.swift:85 / M3UDashboardView.swift:45
.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)
.tabBarMinimizesOnScroll()

iOS 18 fallback: the standard bar simply stays visible (content already scrolls under it). The mini player's fixed bottom allowance (PlayerView.swift:1954, MiniPlayerMetrics.tabBarAllowance = 49) then matches reality on every screen instead of only on root screens; with the minimised iOS 26 bar it should be re-checked by the mini-player owner.

**APIs:** View.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:) (iOS 26.0); TabBarMinimizeBehavior.onScrollDown (iOS 26.0 (iOS only)); View.toolbar(_:for:) with .tabBar (iOS 16.0 (being removed))

**Verifier reasons:** `grep 'for: .tabBar'` returns exactly the twelve lines cited (LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722; VODView.swift:380, 563, 822; SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761; M3UChannelsView.swift:502; M3UFavoritesView.swift:63; WatchHistoryListView.swift:82; EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51). MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView and FavoritesView have no such modifier, so the bar returns when they are pushed from a hidden-bar screen. Screenshots confirm the sequence: iphone-dark/M01 (bar), M03 and M04 (no bar), M07 (bar back). The iPad top tab bar is hidden too (ipad-light/L03), so on those screens the user cannot switch tabs on either device. Neither TabView sets a minimise behaviour (Views/DashboardView.swift:48-85). No comment explains the hiding; git log -S shows it came with the initial import (d2489f9) and was copied onto newer screens (1cce013, 654cefc), so it is a default carried forward rather than a recorded decision. Supporting point from the hand-off code: the docked mini player always reserves a tab-bar allowance on compact widths (PlayerView.swift:1954, MiniPlayerSupport.swift:475-478), so on the twelve hidden-bar screens it floats 49 pt above nothing; a visible bar makes that allowance true everywhere. The HIG wording quoted in the finding could not be checked offline; the verdict rests on the code and screenshots, not on the quote.

**Corrected claim:** As stated. Note that the bar is hidden on iPad as well, and that the EPG guide (a full-screen 2D timetable) is the one screen where hiding the bar is a defensible choice.

**Corrected fix:** Remove the `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` lines so the bar stays through every push, with two conditions. (1) Land native-reference-1 first or together: once the bar is visible on the grids, switching tabs makes the grid disappear and re-appear, which today restarts the three `.task(id:)` modifiers and resets the paginated window, for Live as well as Movies and Series. (2) Treat `tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)` behind `if #available(iOS 26, *)` as a separate, optional step for the owner to accept after a device check with the docked mini player, since the 49 pt allowance was sized for the full bar (the earlier review already left 'is 49 pt still right for the iOS 26 bar, including minimised' open at ios-player-airplay-review.md:3132). iOS 18 fallback: the standard bar stays visible. Owner decisions: whether the EPG guide keeps its hidden bar, and whether to prefer always-visible (Apple's pattern) over the extra grid height.

**API check:** View.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8977-8978, `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0, *)`. TabBarMinimizeBehavior struct at :8981-8982 (iOS 26.0) with `static let onScrollDown`, `@available(iOS 26.0, *)` and unavailable on macOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS; `automatic` and `onScrollUp` also present. Must sit behind `if #available(iOS 26, *)`; the proposed @ViewBuilder wrapper compiles in this structure. View.toolbar(_:for:) with .tabBar is the existing call being removed.

**Regression risks:** Tab switching from pushed grids becomes possible, which exposes the pagination reset of native-reference-1 on all three tabs unless that fix is in. Grids lose the bar's height on iOS 18. On iOS 26 with minimise-on-scroll the mini card keeps its fixed allowance and may sit with a visible gap above the collapsed bar, or near the separate search button; this is in the mini-player owner's area and needs a device look. The EPG guide loses vertical space if its line is removed too. No interaction with the tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Screenshot comparison of M03/M04/L05 (bar present). Simulator UI test: push category, then detail, then back twice and assert the 'Movies' tab button exists at every step; switch tab from a scrolled grid and back and assert the scroll position is kept (depends on native-reference-1). On an iOS 26 device: scroll a grid with the mini player docked bottom-trailing and check the bar minimises and the card neither overlaps it nor floats with an odd gap; repeat on an iOS 18 simulator to confirm the plain fallback.

## native-reference-5 — Grid cells are centre-aligned, so posters and channel icons in one row sit at different heights whenever one title wraps to two lines

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All Movies, Movie/Series category detail, All Channels, Live category detail, Favorites, M3U group detail, Watch history
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:528-534, 635-637`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:500-506, 598-600`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449, 597-599`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:28-33`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:431-437, 573-576`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:66-69`

**What the user perceives:** In shots/iphone-dark/M04-movies-all.png the middle poster of row 1 ('Echoes of Tomorrow') starts about 9 pt above its neighbours and the bottom-right poster of row 4 as well; in L05-live-all-channels.png 'Morning Update', 'Cinema Channel' and 'Discovery Stories' are shifted the same way. The grid looks ragged; Apple's lockup grids are top-aligned with a fixed title area.

**Mechanism (finder):** `GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:), spacing:)` is built without an alignment (VODView.swift:636, SeriesView.swift:599, LiveStreamsView.swift:598, FavoritesView.swift:30/32, M3UChannelsView.swift:574), so LazyVGrid centres each cell in its row. The card title is `.lineLimit(2)` without reserved space (VODView.swift:531, SeriesView.swift:503, LiveStreamsView.swift:446), so a two-line title makes that cell one line taller and every one-line neighbour is centred half a line lower.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Two one-line changes that reinforce each other:
1. `GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: w), spacing: s, alignment: .top)` in the six column definitions.
2. In VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, LiveStreamCard and M3UChannelCard: `.lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true)` so every cell has the same height (this also makes the shelf height constant `shelfRowTotalHeight` exact instead of approximate).

**APIs:** GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:) (iOS 14.0); View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The problem and its mechanism are confirmed. All grid column definitions omit the alignment: VODView.swift:636, SeriesView.swift:599, LiveStreamsView.swift:598, FavoritesView.swift:30 and 32, M3UChannelsView.swift:574, WatchHistoryListView.swift:67, so LazyVGrid centres each cell in its row, and the titles are `.lineLimit(2)` with no reserved space (VODView.swift:531, SeriesView.swift:503, LiveStreamsView.swift:446, M3UChannelsView.swift:434, WatchHistoryListView.swift:189). Measured in shots/iphone-dark/M04-movies-all.png: the 'Echoes of Tomorrow' poster starts about 8 pt above its row neighbours, and the bottom-right poster of row 4 likewise; in L05-live-all-channels.png 'Morning Update', 'Cinema Channel' and 'Discovery Stories' are shifted the same way. Part 1 of the fix (alignment: .top) is correct and sufficient. Part 2 is not safe as written, and its justification is wrong: the card structs are shared with the horizontal shelves, whose height is `shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64)` (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:50). On iPhone layoutScale is 0.5, so the title area is 32 pt, which after the VStack spacing holds only one caption line. M01-movies-home.png shows this: 'Whispers in th...' is truncated to one line on a shelf despite lineLimit(2). So `reservesSpace: true` would not make shelfRowTotalHeight 'exact'; it would make every shelf card taller than its fixed-height row, with clipping or a vertical shift as the possible result. The fix list also says six column definitions but there are seven (WatchHistoryListView.swift:67 is in the files list but not counted).

**Corrected claim:** Grid cells are centre-aligned in seven column definitions, so posters and channel icons in one row sit at different heights whenever one title wraps to two lines. Shelves are not affected (LazyHStack(alignment: .top), and on iPhone shelf titles are limited to one line by the fixed row height).

**Corrected fix:** 1. Add `alignment: .top` to the GridItem in all seven places (VODView.swift:636, SeriesView.swift:599, LiveStreamsView.swift:598, FavoritesView.swift:30 and :32, M3UChannelsView.swift:574, WatchHistoryListView.swift:67). This alone lines up the artwork. 2. Optional, grids only: for a uniform row pitch add a parameter such as `reservesTitleSpace: Bool = false` to VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, LiveStreamCard and M3UChannelCard, apply `.lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: reservesTitleSpace)`, and pass true only from the grid call sites. Do not turn it on for the shelf call sites and do not change shelfRowTotalHeight as part of this.

**API check:** GridItem.init(_ size: GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment? = nil) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23539, struct available iOS 14.0. View.lineLimit(_ limit: Int, reservesSpace: Bool) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8855-8856, iOS 16.0. Both below the iOS 18 target.

**Regression risks:** Part 1: none found; it only changes vertical placement inside a grid row. Part 2 applied unconditionally to the shared card structs would make shelf cards exceed the fixed shelf height on iPhone (clipped second line area or shifted posters on every home screen), which is why it must be opt-in per call site. With reserved space, rows whose titles are all one line get a little taller, costing roughly one caption line of density per row.

**How to verify:** Screenshot comparison of M04 and L05: all artwork tops of a row on one line. Re-capture M01, S01 and L01 and confirm the home shelves are pixel-identical to before. If part 2 is taken, check a grid at the largest Dynamic Type size.

## native-reference-6 — The Search tab uses hand-made filter chips, an empty 'type 2 characters' idle screen, no suggestions or recent searches, and a different matcher and sort order than every in-tab search

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:24-57, 67-69, 126-128, 246-248, 260-271`, `Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift:13-31, 41-55`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:77-85`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether to store recent searches at all (privacy on a shared device); the matcher/sort unification in step 1 is a plain fix.

**What the user perceives:** Opening Search shows four custom pills and a grey magnifier (shots/iphone-dark/Q01-search-idle.png); nothing can be tapped until two letters are typed, and yesterday's query has to be typed again. Typing 'isik' finds 'IŞIK TV' in the Live TV tab's own search but not here, and results are ordered A-Z instead of exact and prefix matches first. Music and App Store show recent searches and suggestions before typing and use the system scope bar.

**Mechanism (finder):** Scope is a ScrollView of Buttons with manual colours (SearchView.swift:25-44) with no selected trait; idle state is a hand-built VStack (:48-57). There is no `searchSuggestions`/`searchCompletion` and no stored history. Matching uses a private `search()` built on `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains` (:126-128) and `localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare` sorting (:262, 266, 270), while Live/Movies/Series/History/Favorites use `CatalogTextSearch.matches` (diacritic-insensitive fold) and `sort*ByRelevance`. Three lifecycle tasks (:246-248) all fire on appearance, so every new result view scans the three catalogs three times. HIG Searching: 'Clearly display the current scope of a search', 'display a person's recent searches before they start typing'.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. Matcher: replace `search(q, in:)` with `CatalogTextSearch.matches(search:text:)` and the three sorts with `CatalogTextSearch.sortLiveByRelevance / sortVODByRelevance / sortSeriesByRelevance`; collapse the three tasks into one keyed on (query, hiddenStore.version, streamsLoaded).
2. Scope: `.searchScopes($selectedFilter, activation: .onSearchPresentation) { ForEach(SearchFilter.allCases, id: \.self) { Text($0.displayName).tag($0) } }` and delete the chip row.
3. Recents: keep the last ~8 submitted queries per playlist in UserDefaults and offer them while the field is empty: `.searchSuggestions { ForEach(recents, id: \.self) { Label($0, systemImage: "clock").searchCompletion($0) } }` plus a 'Clear' row (HIG: provide a way to clear search history). Needs 2 new strings in 10 languages.
4. Optional when no recents exist: on iOS 26 focus the field on tab selection with `.tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection)` on the TabView; no fallback needed on iOS 18 where the field is always visible in the bar.
All of 1-3 are iOS 16 API; no availability check.

**APIs:** View.searchScopes(_:activation:_:) (iOS 16.4); View.searchSuggestions(_:) (iOS 16.0); View.searchCompletion(_:) (iOS 15.0); View.tabViewSearchActivation(_:) / TabSearchActivation.searchTabSelection (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/SearchView.swift, Models/CatalogTextSearch.swift, Views/DashboardView.swift:77-85, Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:50-96 and shots iphone-dark/Q01, Q03, Q05.

Stands:
- Matcher mismatch is real. SearchView.swift:126-128 uses localizedCaseInsensitiveContains (case-insensitive only) while every other search uses CatalogTextSearch.matches (LiveStreamsView.swift:300-302/518/747, VODView.swift:201-203/584/849, SeriesView.swift:254-256/556/786, FavoritesView.swift:67-77, WatchHistoryListView.swift:35, DownloadsView.swift:31, PlaylistContentStore.swift:57-95). I ran both matchers in a scratch program: 'isik' vs 'IŞIK TV' gives old=false, new=true. git log -S shows the private matcher has been there since the initial import (d2489f9) and CatalogTextSearch too, so it is an oversight, not a decision.
- Sort is plain A-Z (SearchView.swift:262/266/270). This matters more than the finding says: the All scope shows only prefix(4) per section (:154, :178, :203), so an exact-name hit can be pushed out of the visible four by alphabetically earlier partial hits.
- Three .task modifiers (:246-248) all fire when SearchResultsView appears, so each fresh result view runs 3 x 3 detached scans. Scope correction: only on first appearance (each time the query goes from <2 to >=2 characters); later query changes re-run only the query task. Task.detached is also not cancelled when the parent task is cancelled, so stale scans run to completion.
- Chips are hand-built Buttons with no selected trait (:25-44); the idle state is a hand-built VStack (:48-57); no suggestions or recents exist (no searchSuggestions/searchCompletion anywhere in the target).

Needs correcting:
- The proposed sort swap is a performance regression. sort*ByRelevance (CatalogTextSearch.swift:40-83) calls normalize up to 8 times per comparison. My scratch benchmark on a synthetic 150k-name catalog (macOS, -O): query 'th' (22.6k hits) current sort 0.08 s, sortByRelevance 6.3 s; 'night' (31.9k hits) 0.21 s vs 12.4 s. A rank computed once per item gives the same ordering in 0.15-0.24 s. The matches filter itself is about 4-5x slower than the current one (0.65 s vs 0.15 s per 150k), which is acceptable off-main.
- Chips versus a scope bar is a style choice, not a defect; Apple's own search results also use pill filters in places. Where a SwiftUI scope bar and suggestions render with the iOS 26 bottom search field of a role-.search tab (Q01/Q03 show the field at the bottom and the nav bar hidden while searching) cannot be settled from code.
- Recents: search here is live-as-you-type with no onSubmit, so 'last submitted queries' would rarely record anything.

**Corrected claim:** The Search tab matches and orders differently from every in-tab search: it is not diacritic/Turkish-ı insensitive ('isik' does not find 'IŞIK TV') and sorts A-Z instead of exact/prefix first, which matters because the All scope shows only the first four hits per section. On first appearance the result view runs the whole three-catalog scan three times. Separately, as optional polish: the scope chips are hand-built without a selected trait, the idle screen is hand-built, and there are no recent searches.

**Corrected fix:** Must-do (plain fix, no decision needed):
1. Filter with CatalogTextSearch.matches(search:text:). Do NOT call sortLiveByRelevance/sortVODByRelevance/sortSeriesByRelevance on the global result sets. Add a single-pass helper to CatalogTextSearch (normalize the query once, normalize each matched name once, rank 0 = equal, 1 = prefix, 2 = other, then sort by rank and localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare) and use it in runSearch. The same helper could later back sort*ByRelevance, which has the same cost in the in-tab 'All' searches (PlaylistContentStore.swift:77-96), but that is a separate change.
2. Replace the three .task modifiers with one .task(id:) keyed on an Equatable struct of (query, hiddenStore.version, contentStore.streamsLoaded); a tuple is not Equatable. Keep the off-main filtering.
3. Add .accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected) to the selected chip if the chips stay.

Optional, after a simulator run on iOS 26 and iOS 18:
4. .searchScopes($selectedFilter, activation: .onSearchPresentation) in place of the chip row, only if the segmented control renders sensibly with the bottom search field and stays visible while results scroll. Otherwise keep the chips.

Owner decision:
5. Recent searches via .searchSuggestions + .searchCompletion while the field is empty. Record a query when a result is opened (or on .onSubmit(of: .search)), not only on submit. Needs a Clear row and 2 new strings in 10 languages.
6. .tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection) behind if #available(iOS 26, *): auto-raises the keyboard on every Search tab selection; leave off unless the owner wants it.

Keep the 2-character minimum.

**API check:** All found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk):
- searchScopes<V, S>(_ scope: Binding<V>, activation: SearchScopeActivation, _ scopes: () -> S): iOS 16.4. SearchScopeActivation.onSearchPresentation exists (iOS 16.4, unavailable on tvOS).
- searchSuggestions<S>(_ suggestions: () -> S): iOS 16.0.
- searchCompletion(_ completion: String): iOS 15.0.
- tabViewSearchActivation(_ activation: TabSearchActivation): iOS 26.0; static var searchTabSelection: iOS 26.0.
No availability guard needed for the first three at an iOS 18 target; the last needs if #available(iOS 26, *).

**Regression risks:** Using sort*ByRelevance as originally proposed would delay broad two- or three-letter queries by seconds on real catalogs, with uncancelled detached tasks piling up per keystroke. Switching matcher changes result sets slightly (punctuation is stripped, diacritics folded): intended, but worth a unit test. A scope bar with activation .onSearchPresentation hides the scope in the idle state and may sit differently on iOS 26 versus iOS 18. searchSuggestions overlays the results while non-empty, so they must be offered only when the field is empty. Playing a live result builds its queue from liveResults (SearchView.swift:283-306), so order changes also change channel up/down order in the player: acceptable, but note it.

**How to verify:** Unit tests on pure functions: 'isik' matches 'IŞIK TV'; the ranked helper puts an exact name first, then prefix hits, then A-Z, and returns the same order as sortVODByRelevance on a small fixture. Time the helper on a 150k-name fixture (target well under 0.5 s). Log or count runSearch invocations when the result view first appears: expect 1, currently 3. Simulator on iOS 26 and iOS 18 for the scope bar and suggestions placement, compared with Q01-Q05.

## native-reference-7 — Shelf headers render in the accent colour and differ from the Continue Watching header in size, colour and left edge

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:355-370`, `Views/VODView.swift:314-329, 417-432`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:291-306, 393-408`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:336-355`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44, 55`

**What the user perceives:** Every category title on the home screens is blue with a pale blue chevron (shots/iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png, M01-movies-home.png, ipad-light/L01-live-home.png) while 'Continue Watching' above them is white, larger and starts 4 pt further right. Apple's shelves use one header style: primary-colour title, grey chevron, shared leading margin.

**Mechanism (finder):** The header label sets `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` and `.tertiary` inside a NavigationLink that keeps the default button style (VODView.swift:418-428). Inside a tinted button label the hierarchical styles resolve against the tint, so `.primary` is the accent colour; the author's intent was the label colour. ContinueWatchingRow adds `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:43) and therefore renders primary, but uses `.title2.weight(.bold)` and `.padding(.horizontal, 20)` (:35, :44, :55) against `.headline` and 16 in the category rows (VODView.swift:423, 432, 465).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Extract one `ShelfHeader(title:destination:)` view used by all seven call sites: NavigationLink + `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, title `.font(.title3.weight(.semibold))` in `Color.primary`, chevron `.foregroundStyle(.secondary)`, 16 pt leading; align ContinueWatchingRow's 20 pt paddings to 16. The Equatable `==` of the shelf rows is untouched because the header takes only values already compared.

**APIs:** View.buttonStyle(.plain) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Screenshots iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png, iphone-dark/M01-movies-home.png and ipad-light/L01-live-home.png all show category headers in accent blue with a pale blue chevron. Code: the six category/recently-added headers are NavigationLinks with the default button style whose label sets .foregroundStyle(.primary) and .tertiary on the chevron (LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367, VODView.swift:315-326 and 418-429, SeriesView.swift:292-303 and 394-405, M3UChannelsView.swift:337-348). The written intent is clearly the label colour; the hierarchical style resolves against the button tint, which the screenshots prove. ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44 is the only header with .buttonStyle(.plain), and it uses .title2.weight(.bold) and 20 pt horizontal padding (:35, :44, :55) against .headline and 16 pt elsewhere. The large title and the category headers sit on the same 16 pt edge in M01, so 20 pt would be the odd one out. git log -S shows this code unchanged since the initial import; no comment marks the blue as deliberate. grep for chevron.right finds exactly these seven shelf headers. No screenshot contains a Continue Watching row (the demo data has no history), so the size and edge mismatch is from code only.

**Corrected claim:** Shelf headers render in the accent colour because their NavigationLink keeps the default button style, and they differ from the Continue Watching header in font (.headline vs .title2 bold), colour and leading edge (16 vs 20 pt).

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: one shared ShelfHeader used by all seven sites, NavigationLink + .buttonStyle(.plain), title in Color.primary, grey chevron, 16 pt leading; change ContinueWatchingRow's two 20 pt paddings to 16. Details: the M3U header also has a trailing item count (M3UChannelsView.swift:349-353), so the shared view needs a trailing slot or the caller keeps its outer HStack. The header font (.title3 semibold versus the current .headline) is a small style choice; the minimal variant is just adding .buttonStyle(.plain) to the six links and aligning Continue Watching's font and padding.

**API check:** buttonStyle(.plain) / PlainButtonStyle: iOS 13, already used throughout the target (for example ContinueWatchingRow.swift:43, VODView.swift:345). No new API.

**Regression risks:** Low. The Equatable == of the shelf rows is untouched. A larger header font raises each shelf row by a few points; rows are not fixed-height. Losing the blue removes the only colour cue that the header is tappable, but the chevron remains, as in Apple's shelves.

**How to verify:** Screenshots of L01/M01/S01 and the M3U channels screen in light and dark: headers in label colour with a grey chevron. With one item in watch history, check that Continue Watching, category headers, large title and first card share one leading edge.

## native-reference-8 — Horizontal shelves scroll freely and stop mid-poster; they do not snap to an item edge the way Apple's shelves do

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels, Continue Watching
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397`, `Views/VODView.swift:331-350, 448-467`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:308-327, 420-439`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363-377`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:46-57`

**What the user perceives:** After a flick a shelf comes to rest with a poster cut by the screen edge at an arbitrary point. In TV, App Store and Music a shelf always settles with a poster aligned to the leading margin, which makes the rows feel deliberate and keeps titles readable.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each shelf is `ScrollView(.horizontal) { LazyHStack { ... }.padding(.horizontal, 16) }` with no scroll target behaviour (e.g. VODView.swift:448-466). The margin is content padding, so the system has no alignment line to snap to.

**Proposed fix (finder):** On each shelf:

ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false) {
    LazyHStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 14) { ... }
        .scrollTargetLayout()
}
.contentMargins(.horizontal, 16, for: .scrollContent)
.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned(limitBehavior: .never))

`.never` keeps full momentum (no one-card-per-swipe paging) and only aligns the resting position. Remove the inner `.padding(.horizontal, 16)`. All iOS 17 API, no availability check. Roll out on one shelf type first: shelves hold whole categories (thousands of cells in a LazyHStack), so the alignment pass must be profiled before it goes everywhere.

**APIs:** View.scrollTargetBehavior(_:) (iOS 17.0); ViewAlignedScrollTargetBehavior.LimitBehavior.never / .viewAligned(limitBehavior:) (iOS 17.0); View.scrollTargetLayout(isEnabled:) (iOS 17.0); View.contentMargins(_:_:for:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code confirms the mechanism: every shelf is ScrollView(.horizontal) { LazyHStack { ... }.padding(.horizontal, 16) } with no scroll target behaviour (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397, VODView.swift:331-349 and 448-466, SeriesView.swift:308-326 and 420-438, M3UChannelsView.swift:363-377; ContinueWatchingRow.swift:46-57 uses a plain HStack). No use of scrollTargetBehavior in the target or in history. Apple's shelves in TV, Music and App Store do settle on an item edge, so the reference claim is fair, but free scrolling is not perceived as broken; this is a refinement.

The fix is API-correct, but its safety is not established from code. Shelves really do hold whole categories: VODView.swift:200-206 passes allByCategory[cat.id] unfiltered, so a LazyHStack can have thousands of children. View-aligned targeting on a lazy stack has to estimate positions for cells that are not yet realised when a hard flick lands far away; whether that produces mis-snaps or hitches at this size can only be measured on a device. The finder already says to roll out on one shelf first; I agree and would tighten the order.

**Corrected claim:** Horizontal shelves scroll freely and rest at arbitrary offsets; Apple's shelves rest on an item edge. This is a polish gap, not a defect.

**Corrected fix:** Same modifiers, staged:
1. Start with ContinueWatchingRow (non-lazy HStack, at most 10 items, no performance question): .scrollTargetLayout() on the HStack, move its horizontal padding to .contentMargins(.horizontal, 16, for: .scrollContent) (16 to match the header fix), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned(limitBehavior: .never)). Keep the .padding(.bottom, 8).
2. Then one poster shelf type (VODCategoryShelfRow), measured on a device with a category of more than 2,000 items before touching the others. If hitch rate or resting accuracy is worse, stop there and leave the lazy shelves free-scrolling.
3. Only then Series, Live and M3U shelves.
No availability guard: all iOS 17 API.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: scrollTargetBehavior(_:) iOS 17.0; scrollTargetLayout(isEnabled:) iOS 17.0; contentMargins(_ edges:, _ length: CGFloat?, for:) iOS 17.0; ViewAlignedScrollTargetBehavior iOS 17.0 with LimitBehavior.automatic/.always/.never at iOS 17.0 (alwaysByFew/alwaysByOne are iOS 18.0); static func viewAligned(limitBehavior:) iOS 17.0.

**Regression risks:** Scroll hitches or wrong resting positions on very long lazy shelves; changed deceleration feel on every home screen. Replacing the inner padding with content margins must keep the first card on the 16 pt edge and must not clip card shadows or context-menu previews. Shelf rows are Equatable and sit in a vertical lazy stack; the modifiers do not affect == but should be checked for scroll-position resets when rows are recycled.

**How to verify:** Device only. Flick a shelf of a category with more than 2,000 items hard and gently, in both directions: the resting card must align to the leading margin with no visible correction jump. Compare Animation Hitches in Instruments before and after on that shelf and on vertical scrolling of the home screen.

## native-reference-9 — Posters push their detail screen with the plain slide; the iOS 18 zoom transition that keeps the artwork on screen is not used

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies shelves and grids, Series shelves and grids, Favorites, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-704`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:311-322, 423-434, 650-660`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:134-144, 160-170`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Zoom changes the feel of every poster tap (and adds drag-down-to-dismiss on detail pages). Apple uses it in Photos but TV and Music keep the plain push, so this is a style choice for the owner.

**What the user perceives:** A tapped poster disappears to the left and a new page arrives from the right; the artwork the user touched and the hero poster on the detail page are not connected. In Photos, and anywhere Apple opens a large cell, the cell grows into the destination and can be dragged back down into its place.

**Mechanism (finder):** All poster links are `NavigationLink { MovieDetailView(...) } label: { VODStreamCard(...) }` with no transition source; `matchedTransitionSource` and `navigationTransition` do not occur in the target. WWDC24 'Enhance your UI animations and transitions': 'In parts of your app where you transition from a large cell, the zoom transition can increase the sense of continuity'.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Per shelf row / grid, one namespace captured by the destination closure (no navigation refactor needed):

@Namespace private var posterZoom
...
NavigationLink {
    MovieDetailView(playlist: playlist, movie: item.stream, queue: queue)
        .navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID: item.stream.id, in: posterZoom))
} label: {
    VODStreamCard(...)
}
.matchedTransitionSource(id: item.stream.id, in: posterZoom) { $0.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)) }

iOS 18.0 API, so no availability check. Do it only after the detail page renders immediately (finding on the full-screen spinner). Live cards open the overlay player and are not affected. Keep small search-row thumbnails on the default push.

**APIs:** View.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:configuration:) (iOS 18.0); View.navigationTransition(_:) (iOS 18.0); NavigationTransition.zoom(sourceID:in:) (iOS 18.0); MatchedTransitionSourceConfiguration.clipShape(RoundedRectangle) (iOS 18.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The factual part is true: all poster links are plain NavigationLinks with no transition source (VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-704; SeriesView.swift:311-322, 423-434, 650-660; FavoritesView.swift:134-144, 160-170) and neither matchedTransitionSource nor navigationTransition occurs in the target or its history.

It is not a gap against the native reference, though. The plain push is the system default and is what Apple's TV, Music and App Store use when opening a title from a shelf; the finding's own decision note says so. The benefit is also smaller here than described: the zoom morphs the cell into the whole destination page, not into the hero poster. MovieDetailView's top is a blurred backdrop with a small poster thumbnail at the lower left (shots/iphone-dark/M07-movie-detail.png, MovieDetailView.swift:123-128), so the tapped artwork does not land on matching artwork. When metadata is not cached the destination is a full-screen spinner (MovieDetailView.swift:74-76; S03-series-detail-loading.png), so the poster would zoom into a spinner. The detail is a ScrollView that ignores the top safe area (MovieDetailView.swift:187) and gains a drag-down dismiss gesture that competes with its scrolling. Sources live in lazy stacks and paginated grids, where a recycled source cell falls back to the default transition.

**Corrected claim:** Poster taps use the standard push. That matches Apple's media apps; a zoom transition is an optional stylistic enhancement whose benefit is limited by the current detail layout (blurred backdrop, small poster, loading spinner), not a native-feel defect.

**Corrected fix:** none as part of this pass. If the owner wants it: first make the detail render immediately from the data the card already has (no full-screen spinner), then prototype on one paginated grid only (VODCategoryContent) with a per-view @Namespace, attaching matchedTransitionSource to the poster image inside the card rather than to the whole card with its title, and decide on a device. Leave shelves, Favorites and search rows on the default push until that prototype is judged.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: matchedTransitionSource(id:in:) and matchedTransitionSource(id:in:configuration:) iOS 18.0; navigationTransition(_:) iOS 18.0; NavigationTransition.zoom(sourceID:in:) iOS 18.0 (ZoomNavigationTransition, unavailable on macOS); MatchedTransitionSourceConfiguration.clipShape(_ shape: RoundedRectangle) iOS 18.0 (the generic Shape overload is marked unavailable). The proposed code would compile at an iOS 18 target without a guard.

**Regression risks:** Changes the feel of every poster tap and adds drag-down and pinch dismissal on detail pages that scroll vertically under a hidden top safe area. Interrupted or cancelled zooms change when the destination's .task runs (MovieDetailView.swift:99-103 fetches metadata). Source cells recycled by LazyHStack or by grid pagination fall back to a different animation, giving inconsistent transitions. Must be checked alongside the docked mini player overlay and on iPad.

**How to verify:** Device, only if the owner opts in: open and drag-dismiss a detail from a grid cell loaded on a later page and from a shelf cell scrolled far to the right; confirm the poster returns to its cell, the nav bar and tab bar do not flicker, the metadata fetch is not repeated on an interrupted push, and vertical scrolling of the detail page does not trigger dismissal mid-scroll.

## native-reference-10 — Several tap targets are bare tap gestures: Continue Watching cards have no pressed state, and an episode's thumbnail is not tappable at all

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Continue Watching, Series detail episodes, Channel schedule list
- Code: `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1390-1451`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:60-63`

**What the user perceives:** Touching a Continue Watching card gives no visual response until the player appears, unlike every other card on the same screen. In a season list, tapping the episode picture does nothing; only the text to its right starts playback. In TV the artwork is the primary target. VoiceOver does not announce these as buttons.

**Mechanism (finder):** `HistoryCard(item:).onTapGesture { onPlay(item) }` (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52) is not a Button, so there is no highlight, no button trait and no pointer hover. In EpisodeDetailRow the `.contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture` is attached to the text VStack only (SeriesView.swift:1416-1451); the thumbnail ZStack (:1391-1414) has no gesture. ChannelEPGDetailView rows use `.onTapGesture` inside a List (:62-63), so the row never shows the system selection highlight.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use Buttons so the system supplies pressed state, traits and hover:
- ContinueWatchingRow: `Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item) }.buttonStyle(.plain)` (the same pattern WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201 already uses).
- EpisodeDetailRow: wrap thumbnail + text column in one `Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } label: { HStack { thumbnail; textColumn } }.buttonStyle(.plain)` and leave DownloadButton outside as a sibling.
- ChannelEPGDetailView: `Button { selected = programme } label: { row(programme) }` with `.foregroundStyle(.primary)`.

**APIs:** Button + PlainButtonStyle (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** All three mechanisms are as described.
- ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52: HistoryCard(item:).onTapGesture, not a Button. Every other card on the home screens is a plain-style Button or NavigationLink (LiveStreamCard at LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457; poster links at VODView.swift:451-462), so this card alone has no pressed state and no button trait. No accessibility modifiers in the file.
- SeriesView.swift:1390-1451: the thumbnail ZStack (:1391-1414) has no gesture; .contentShape + .onTapGesture is attached only to the text VStack (:1447-1451). Tapping the episode image does nothing. This is the most user-visible item and a functional defect.
- ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:59-63: List rows use .contentShape + .onTapGesture, so there is no system row highlight before the sheet opens.
git log shows all three unchanged since they were introduced, with no comment marking them as deliberate.

The fix needs two corrections:
1. EpisodeDetailRow: Button labels centre multi-line text by default. The plot text wraps up to 5 lines (SeriesView.swift:1439-1444), so the label needs .multilineTextAlignment(.leading); the code base already does exactly this in WatchHistoryListView.swift:186-190.
2. ChannelEPGDetailView: by the mechanism established in native-reference-7 (and shown in the screenshots), hierarchical .foregroundStyle(.primary) inside a default-style button resolves to the tint, so the proposed modifier risks blue programme titles. Use the concrete Color.primary on the label. Do not use .tint(.primary): the row's NOW capsule and progress bar use Color.accentColor (:106, :113, :125). The .id(rowID(programme)) used by scrollTo (:61, :79) must move onto the Button.

**Corrected claim:** Continue Watching cards and channel-schedule rows are bare tap gestures with no pressed or highlight state and no button trait, and in a season list the episode thumbnail is not tappable at all; only the text column starts playback.

**Corrected fix:** - ContinueWatchingRow: Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item) }.buttonStyle(.plain), as proposed.
- EpisodeDetailRow: one Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } wrapping HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { thumbnail; text column } with .buttonStyle(.plain), .multilineTextAlignment(.leading) on the label and .contentShape(Rectangle()); DownloadButton stays outside as a sibling in the outer HStack.
- ChannelEPGDetailView: Button { selected = programme } label: { row(programme).foregroundStyle(Color.primary) } with .id(rowID(programme)) on the Button; keep the default button style so the List supplies the row highlight; drop the contentShape/onTapGesture pair.

**API check:** Button and PlainButtonStyle: iOS 13, used throughout the target. multilineTextAlignment(_:) iOS 13. No new API and no availability guard.

**Regression risks:** Episode row: centred plot text if the alignment modifier is forgotten; the plain style's pressed dimming now covers the thumbnail and the progress bar. Schedule list: blue titles if a hierarchical style is used instead of Color.primary; scroll-to-now breaks if the .id is lost; the dimmed past-programme opacity (:129) must stay on the row. Continue Watching: none expected; titles are single-line.

**How to verify:** UI test: in a series detail, tap the centre of the first episode thumbnail and assert the player overlay appears. Manual or screenshot: press and hold a Continue Watching card and an episode row to see the pressed state; tap a schedule row and see the row highlight before the sheet; check the plot text is still leading-aligned and programme titles are still label-coloured in light and dark. VoiceOver or performAccessibilityAudit: the three targets are announced as buttons, and the jump-to-now toolbar button still scrolls to the current programme.
