## native-reference-11 — The three home tabs each carry their own search field next to the Search tab; on iPad the bar shows two magnifier buttons side by side

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Search tab, iPad top bar
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93-107`, `Views/VODView.swift:145-159`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:146-160`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:77-83`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Removing shelf filtering from the home screens changes a feature people may use (category-name match keeps whole shelves). Owner decides between a single search location and keeping both.

**What the user perceives:** On iPad the floating bar reads 'Live TV, Movies, Series, Settings, magnifier | star, more | magnifier' (shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png): two search buttons with different results. On iPhone each home screen has a field under the title that filters shelves, plus the Search tab that lists rows; the same query gives different result sets and layouts depending on which one was used.

**Mechanism (finder):** `.searchable(text:isPresented:prompt:)` is attached to LiveStreamsView (:93), VODView (:145) and SeriesView (:146) while DashboardView also declares `Tab(..., role: .search)` (:77). On regular width iOS 26 collapses the per-screen field into a toolbar button next to the search tab's own button. HIG Searching: 'Aim to make your app's content searchable through a single location.'

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest native option: remove the three home-level `.searchable` modifiers (and their debounce state) and let the Search tab open pre-scoped to the tab the user came from (store the last content tab in DashboardView and set `selectedFilter` when the search tab is selected). Category and All screens keep their own field: that is in-list filtering of the list on screen, which Apple apps also offer. If the shelf filter on the home screens is to stay, mark it secondary on iOS 26 with `.searchToolbarBehavior(.minimize)` behind `if #available(iOS 26, *)` (iOS 18 fallback: unchanged drawer field) so it never competes with the tab.

**APIs:** View.searchToolbarBehavior(_:) / SearchToolbarBehavior.minimize (iOS 26.0); Tab(_:systemImage:value:role:) with .search (iOS 18.0 (already used))

**Verifier reasons:** The problem is real. `.searchable(text:isPresented:prompt:)` with automatic placement sits on the three Xtream home screens (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93, Views/VODView.swift:145, Views/SeriesView.swift:146) and DashboardView also declares `Tab(..., role: .search)` (Views/DashboardView.swift:77). shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png shows the result: the search-tab magnifier inside the tab pill, then star and overflow, then a second standalone magnifier. shots/iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows a field under the large title plus the Search tab button.

The two paths also return different results. The home filter uses CatalogTextSearch.matches (diacritic and punctuation folding, and a category-name match keeps the whole shelf; LiveStreamsView.swift:296-309). The Search tab uses `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains` with a 2-character minimum and a flat list (Views/SearchView.swift:126-128, 48). History (d2489f9, 654cefc) and the surrounding comments show nothing that marks the duplication as deliberate.

The fix needs correcting in two places:
- `.searchToolbarBehavior(.minimize)` turns a search field into a toolbar button. On iPad the home search already is a button, so nothing changes. On iPhone it could create the same second magnifier, next to four existing toolbar buttons. It works against the stated problem.
- Pre-scoping the Search tab from the previous tab is not what Apple's Search tabs do (TV, Music and App Store open global). It would also overwrite a scope the user chose earlier. It is a design idea, not a native reference.

A smaller fix exists and the finding missed it. shots/ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png shows that `placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always)`, already used at LiveStreamsView.swift:498, renders a labelled field under the title on iPad iOS 26, not a magnifier button.

I could not check the HIG quote offline. M3UDashboardView has no search tab (Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:27, 37), so M3UChannelsView:112 must keep its field.

**Corrected claim:** On the Xtream dashboard the three home screens each attach an automatically placed `.searchable` shelf filter while the TabView also has a `.search`-role tab. On iPad (regular width, iOS 26) the home filter collapses into a second magnifier button beside the search tab's magnifier. On iPhone each home screen shows a field under the title in addition to the Search tab. The two paths use different matchers (CatalogTextSearch versus localizedCaseInsensitiveContains with a 2-character minimum) and different layouts, so the same query gives different results. The M3U dashboard has no search tab and is not affected.

**Corrected fix:** Two options; the owner picks.

A. Single search location (product decision). Remove the home-level `.searchable` from LiveStreamsView:93, VODView:145 and SeriesView:146, together with searchText, debounceTask, isSearchActive and the query branch of recomputeFilter. Keep the empty-query path, because it also applies hidden categories. Category and All screens keep their drawer fields, and the Search tab stays global. Do not pre-scope the Search tab unless the owner wants it. The orchestrator's temporary tour at ScreensUITests.swift:333 expects the inline field.

B. Keep the shelf filter, smallest change. Pass `placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic)` to the three home `.searchable` calls so iPad shows a labelled field under the title, as the category screens do, with a single magnifier left in the bar. Also switch SearchView's `search()` to CatalogTextSearch.matches so both paths match the same way.

Drop `.searchToolbarBehavior(.minimize)` from the proposal.

**API check:** - `searchToolbarBehavior(_:)`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:19983, `@available(iOS 26.0, ...)`. `SearchToolbarBehavior.minimize`: :19968-19974, iOS 26.0 / visionOS 26.0. Both exist, but are not recommended here.
- `TabRole.search`: :13692-13694, iOS 18.0, already used.
- `searchable(text:isPresented:placement:prompt:)`: :5763, placement defaults to `.automatic`; iOS 17 per the finding and my recollection, the attribute line was not read.
- `SearchFieldPlacement.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode:)`: :9346, iOS-only; iOS 15 by recollection, and already used in this target with `.always`.
- `tabViewSearchActivation(_:)`: :11401, iOS 26. Present but not needed.

**Regression risks:** Option A removes shelf filtering by category name; CategoryPickerSheet's own search still covers jumping to a category. The empty states at LiveStreamsView:75-88 read debouncedQuery and need simplifying. `isSearchActive` exists only for this field. Do not touch the off-main filtering in recomputeFilter or the Equatable shelf rows.

Option B: `.automatic` drawer mode hides the field until pull-down on iPhone, which matches today's look. The iPad rendering with `.automatic` rather than `.always` is unverified. M3UChannelsView must stay as it is.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iPad Pro 11 portrait and landscape: capture Live, Movies and Series home and count magnifier buttons in the top bar; expect one. iPhone: capture L01 and confirm either no field (A) or an unchanged field (B). For B, type 'sinema' and 'cinéma' in both the home field and the Search tab and compare result sets after the matcher is unified.

## native-reference-12 — Adding a playlist opens a full-height sheet with two rows and then a second sheet after a fixed 0.2 s delay, where a pull-down menu on the + button is the system pattern

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list, Add playlist
- Code: `ContentView.swift:89-109, 189-193`, `Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:13-36`

**What the user perceives:** Tap +, a large sheet slides up with two options (shots/iphone-dark/P02-playlist-type-sheet.png), tap one, the sheet slides down, a pause, another sheet slides up. Two modal animations for a two-way choice; Files, Reminders and Mail put such a choice in a menu that opens from the button itself.

**Mechanism (finder):** The + toolbar button sets `showingTypePicker` (ContentView.swift:91-92) which presents PlaylistTypeSelectionView; its rows call `dismiss()` and then `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.2) { onSelectXtream() }` (PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:15-18, 26-29) to present the real form. The hand-off depends on a timer instead of on the dismissal finishing.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the button with a Menu and present the form sheet directly; PlaylistTypeSelectionView and the timer go away (the empty-state button at ContentView.swift:189-193 can use the same Menu):

ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) {
    Menu {
        Button { showingAddXtreamPlaylist = true } label: { Label(L("playlist_type.xtream.title"), systemImage: "server.rack") }
        Button { showingAddM3UPlaylist = true } label: { Label(L("playlist_type.m3u.title"), systemImage: "list.bullet.rectangle.portrait") }
    } label: { Image(systemName: "plus") }
}

Existing strings are reused.

**APIs:** Menu (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The code matches the claim. The + button and the empty-state button set `showingTypePicker` (ContentView.swift:91-92, 189-190), which presents PlaylistTypeSelectionView as a full-height sheet (:98-103). Its two rows call `dismiss()` and then `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.2)` to raise the real form sheet (Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:14-18, 27-30).

shots/iphone-dark/P02-playlist-type-sheet.png shows a large sheet holding two rows. PlaylistTypeSelectionView is used only from ContentView. History (d2489f9, 2849d94) and the single Turkish comment ("opens when + is pressed") give no reason for the timer.

A pull-down menu on an Add button is the HIG pattern for a short choice. The perceived cost is two modal transitions and a timer-based hand-off for a two-way choice; that is low severity.

One addition: the sheet rows carry explanatory subtitles (`playlist_type.xtream.subtitle`, `playlist_type.m3u.subtitle`). The proposed Menu drops them, and a first-time user benefits from them. A menu button can keep them as a second Text.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands as stated. Adding a playlist presents a full-height sheet with two rows, then a second sheet after a fixed 0.2 s `asyncAfter`. A pull-down Menu on the + button is the system pattern for this choice.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, keeping the subtitles:

Menu {
    Button { showingAddXtreamPlaylist = true } label: {
        Label(L("playlist_type.xtream.title"), systemImage: "server.rack")
        Text(L("playlist_type.xtream.subtitle"))
    }
    Button { showingAddM3UPlaylist = true } label: {
        Label(L("playlist_type.m3u.title"), systemImage: "list.bullet.rectangle.portrait")
        Text(L("playlist_type.m3u.subtitle"))
    }
} label: { Image(systemName: "plus") }

Give the Menu label `.accessibilityLabel` so VoiceOver does not read "plus". Use the same Menu content with the existing styled label for the empty-state button (ContentView.swift:189-200). Remove `showingTypePicker`, its `.sheet`, and Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift. The project uses file-system-synchronized groups, so the user's modified project.pbxproj needs no edit. Leave `playlist_type.title` and `playlist_type.section` in the .strings files.

**API check:** - `Menu<Label, Content>`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7116-7118, `@available(iOS 14.0, macOS 11.0, tvOS 17.0, *)`.
- A second Text in a menu Button's label renders as a subtitle; this is from memory (iOS 15+), not checked in the interface.

**Regression risks:** Two UI tests need rewriting: the one asserting `staticText("Playlist Type")` (ScreensUITests.swift:183) and the one tapping the Xtream row (:188-198), since menu items are found as buttons after tapping `navigationBars.buttons["plus"]`. The orchestrator's temporary tour (:423) also taps that row.

The empty-state Menu label must keep its full-width button look. Presenting a sheet from a Menu action is standard, and no timer is needed.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test: tap +, assert menu items 'Xtream Code' and 'M3U / M3U8' exist, tap each, and assert the matching form appears with a single sheet animation. Repeat from the empty state with zero playlists. Screenshot the open menu to confirm the subtitles render.

## native-reference-13 — Browsing gives no haptic or symbol feedback: favorite toggles, scope and season chips and download actions change state silently

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Search scopes, Season picker, Download button, Category picker hide swipe
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:86-91, 315-332`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:880-887`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:443-447`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:176-194`, `Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:231-233`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the star swaps the glyph instantly with no tap in the hand; choosing a season or starting a download feels the same as tapping empty space. The reworked player already ticks on scrubbing, so the browsing side feels flatter than the player.

**Mechanism (finder):** `sensoryFeedback` is used only in Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:231-233 and UINotificationFeedbackGenerator only in PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:211/222; nothing outside the player emits feedback. The favorite buttons switch `star`/`star.fill` without a content transition (MovieDetailView.swift:88, SeriesView.swift:884). HIG Playing haptics: selection feedback 'while the values of a UI element are changing', notification success when a task completes, used consistently and sparingly.

**Proposed fix (finder):** A small, consistent set (all iOS 17 API):
- Favorite toolbar buttons: `Image(systemName: isFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star").contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))` and `.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: isFavorite) { old, new in new && !old }` on the button.
- DetailSeasonTabBar and the search scope control: `.sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: selectedId)`.
- DownloadButton: `.sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: item?.downloadStatus == .queued)` when a download is enqueued.
Toggles, pickers, pull-to-refresh and swipe actions already get system haptics; add nothing to scrolling or to plain navigation taps.

**APIs:** View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) / sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:condition:) (iOS 17.0); SensoryFeedback.selection / .success (iOS 17.0); ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:) with ReplaceSymbolEffect (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The factual claim holds. Outside the player, nothing emits feedback: `sensoryFeedback` appears only in Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:231-233, and UIKit feedback generators only in PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:211/222 and PlayerView. The favorite buttons swap `star`/`star.fill` with no transition (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:86-91, Views/SeriesView.swift:880-887). This is a polish gap, not a defect.

Three parts of the fix are wrong:
- Favorite trigger. `isFavorite` is a GRDBQuery `@Query<IsFavoriteRequest>` whose default is false (Models/Requests.swift:269-288) and whose real value arrives asynchronously. `.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: isFavorite) { old, new in new && !old }` would therefore fire a success haptic every time the detail of an already-favorited title opens.
- Download trigger. `item?.downloadStatus == .queued` with no condition fires on entering and on leaving queued. DownloadManager.enqueue always writes `.queued` first and the pump promotes it at once (Models/DownloadManager.swift:179-201). That gives a double tick on tap, and spontaneous ticks later when queued episodes visible in an episode list start on their own.
- Selection haptics on the season chips and search-scope chips are not a native reference. System segmented controls and scope bars do not tick, and the TV app's season picker is a menu.

Whether the symbol-replace transition animates inside a bar button on iOS 26 needs a run; it is harmless if it does not.

**Corrected claim:** Outside the player, no user action produces haptic or symbol-transition feedback. The favorite toggle on the movie and series detail screens and the start of a download change state silently. This is a low-severity polish gap. Segmented and scope selection giving no haptic is consistent with system controls and is not a gap.

**Corrected fix:** Drive feedback from the user's tap, not from database-derived state.

- Favorites: add `@State private var favoriteFeedback = 0` to the movie and series detail views. Increment it in toggleFavorite only when adding. Attach `.sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: favoriteFeedback)` to the screen's root Group, not inside the ToolbarItem. Add `.contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))` to the star Image.
- DownloadButton: add `@State private var enqueueFeedback = 0`, increment it in the `.idle, .failed` branch of primaryAction (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:178), and attach `.sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: enqueueFeedback)`.
- Drop the `.selection` feedback on DetailSeasonTabBar and the search scope chips, or leave it as the owner's taste decision.
- Add nothing to scrolling or navigation taps.

**API check:** - `sensoryFeedback<T>(_:trigger:)` and `sensoryFeedback<T>(_:trigger:condition:)`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1981-1985, `@available(iOS 17.0, macOS 14.0, tvOS 17.0, watchOS 10.0, visionOS 26.0, *)`, `T : Equatable`.
- `SensoryFeedback.success` (:842), `.selection` (:845), `.impact(weight:intensity:)` (:855).
- `ContentTransition.symbolEffect(_:options:)`: :4578-4580, iOS 17.0.
- The `.replace` symbol effect lives in the Symbols module; I did not locate it there, but `.symbolEffect(.pulse)` already compiles in LoadingProcessView.swift:36.

**Regression risks:** With the original state-derived triggers: phantom haptics when opening favorited titles and when queued downloads advance. With the corrected tap-driven counters: none beyond an extra @State per view. DownloadButton is instantiated once per episode row, so keep the modifier cheap (one Int state) and leave its @Query structure alone.

**How to verify:** Device only, since the simulator has no Taptic Engine. Check four things:
1. Open the detail of an already-favorited movie: no haptic.
2. Tap the star to add: one success haptic. Tap to remove: none.
3. Tap Download: exactly one light impact, and none when a queued item later starts.
4. Watch the star in the navigation bar for the replace animation on iOS 18 and iOS 26.

## native-reference-14 — Filter entries in the sort/filter menus are Buttons with a hand-placed checkmark, and the menu closes after every toggle

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live category / All Channels, Movie category / All Movies, Series category / All Series
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:642-667`, `Views/VODView.swift:750-770, 779-785`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:691-711, 720-726`

**What the user perceives:** Picking three genres means opening the menu three times. Selected filters are not announced as selected by VoiceOver, and their titles shift sideways when the checkmark image appears because unselected rows have no icon slot.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each filter is `Button { toggle } label: { if selected { Label(title, systemImage: "checkmark") } else { Text(title) } }` (e.g. SeriesView.swift:694-702). The sort part of the same menu is already a `Picker` and gets the system checkmark column (shots/iphone-dark/M05-movies-sort-menu.png).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use `Toggle` rows, which a Menu renders with the system checkmark and selected trait, and keep the menu open for multi-select:

Section(L("filter.genre")) {
    ForEach(genres, id: \.self) { genre in
        Toggle(genre, isOn: Binding(get: { genreFilter.contains(genre) }, set: { on in if on { genreFilter.insert(genre) } else { genreFilter.remove(genre) } }))
    }
}
.menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled)

Same for the file-type and catch-up/EPG filters; the 'Clear' button stays a normal dismissing Button outside the section.

**APIs:** Toggle inside Menu (iOS 14.0); View.menuActionDismissBehavior(_:) (iOS 16.4)

**Verifier reasons:** The code matches. The filter rows are `Button { toggle } label: { if selected { Label(title, systemImage: "checkmark") } else { Text(title) } }` at Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:643-660, Views/VODView.swift:753-761 and Views/SeriesView.swift:694-702. The sort part of the same menu is a Picker (LiveStreamsView:636, VODView:744, SeriesView:685).

shots/iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png shows the Picker rows with the system checkmark column plus an icon column. The filter rows are plain text starting at the icon column, so a selected row's hand-placed checkmark would land in the icon slot and push its title right. No screenshot shows a selected filter; that shift is inferred from the layout.

A menu Button dismisses on tap, so choosing three genres takes three openings. A plain Button exposes no selected trait. History (654cefc, which added sort/filter) has no comment explaining Button over Toggle.

One caveat. Toggle rows are clearly the native construct. Keeping the menu open is a usability gain, but I cannot confirm Apple's own filter menus stay open, so treat that part as optional. It also needs a run: the grid re-filters and scrolls to top behind the open menu (VODView.swift:719-728), the toolbar icon flips to `.fill`, and the conditional 'Clear' row appears, all while the menu is presented.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands as stated. Filter entries in the three sort/filter menus are Buttons with a manually placed checkmark Label: they have no system checkmark column or selected trait, the title position shifts on iOS 26, and the menu closes after every toggle.

**Corrected fix:** Replace each filter Button with a Toggle bound to set membership, for example `Toggle(genre, isOn: Binding(get: { genreFilter.contains(genre) }, set: { on in if on { genreFilter.insert(genre) } else { genreFilter.remove(genre) } }))`. For live, bind to `filter.contains(.catchup)` and `.hasEPG` with insert/remove.

Optionally apply `.menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled)` to the Toggles only, so the Picker and the 'Clear' button keep dismissing. If the open menu resizes or dismisses when the conditional 'Clear' row appears, keep 'Clear' always present with `.disabled(filter.isEmpty)`, or drop the dismiss-behavior modifier and keep only the Toggle change.

**API check:** - `menuActionDismissBehavior(_:)`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13737-13738, `@available(iOS 16.4, macOS 13.3, tvOS 16.4, watchOS 9.4, *)`.
- `MenuActionDismissBehavior.disabled`: :13741-13748, available on iOS; unavailable on macOS and watchOS.
- `Toggle.init<S: StringProtocol>(_ title: S, isOn: Binding<Bool>)`: :5054.
- `Menu`: :7116-7118, iOS 14.0.

**Regression risks:** State changes while the menu is open: `.task(id:)` recompute, the scroll-to-top in VODView.swift:719-728, the label icon change and the appearing 'Clear' row. Confirm the menu updates in place and does not dismiss or flicker on iOS 18 and iOS 26.

A UI test that taps a filter by button label needs to look for a switch or button with a selected value. Off-main sort and filter and the paginated grid are untouched.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 18 and iOS 26: in All Series open the menu and tap two genres. Assert the menu stays open, both rows show the system checkmark, and the grid count changes. Tap Clear: the menu closes and the filters reset. Compare screenshots of a selected row before and after for title alignment. With VoiceOver, a selected row should announce 'selected'.

## native-reference-15 — Settings value rows are hand-built HStacks: values cannot be copied and do not reflow at large text sizes

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings (Xtream), Settings (M3U)
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:108-113, 182-201, 239-258, 265-291, 298-303, 348-353`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:103-108, 161-182, 188-199, 228-232`, `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:33-43, 134-138`

**What the user perceives:** In Apple's Settings a long press on a value such as a version or an address offers Copy, and at large accessibility text sizes label and value stack instead of squeezing. Here the server URL, username and M3U source cannot be copied (useful when moving a playlist to another device), and label/value pairs share one line whatever the text size.

**Mechanism (finder):** Every info row is `HStack { Text(label); Spacer(); Text(value).foregroundColor(.secondary) }` (e.g. PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-187); `LabeledContent` does not occur in the target and `textSelection` only in the player's track sheet.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the pairs with `LabeledContent(L("settings.playlist.server_url"), value: playlist.serverURL)` and add `.textSelection(.enabled)` to the copy-worthy ones (name, server URL, username, M3U source URL, version). Leave the password row and the TipJarRow() line exactly as they are. Mechanical change, no new strings.

**APIs:** LabeledContent (iOS 16.0); View.textSelection(_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The code matches. Every info row is `HStack { Text(label); Spacer(); Text(value).foregroundColor(.secondary) }`: Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:108-113, 182-201, 239-258, 265-291, 298-303, 348-353; Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift (storage, name, type, source, stats, version); Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:33-43, 134-138. `LabeledContent` does not occur in the target, and `textSelection` only at Views/Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:95.

shots/iphone-light/T03-settings-3.png shows the Name, Server URL, Username and Version rows as plain label/value pairs. Nothing in the comments or history marks the HStack form as deliberate.

The user's uncommitted change to both settings files is only the `TipJarRow()` line (git diff: +2 and +1 lines), so the swap leaves it intact. The Version row is directly above it and can be edited without touching it.

Three notes:
- The M3U source-URL row is already a stacked VStack and only needs `.textSelection`.
- The EPG 'last updated' row uses `Text(last, style: .relative)` and needs the content-closure form.
- I could not confirm from the SDK that LabeledContent stacks label and value at accessibility sizes; that needs a screenshot. The copy benefit does not depend on it.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands as stated. Settings info rows are hand-built HStacks: values such as server URL, username, M3U source and version cannot be copied, and the rows do not use the system labelled-row layout.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed. Use `LabeledContent(L("..."), value: string)` for plain pairs, and `LabeledContent(L("...")) { Text(value).textSelection(.enabled) }` for name, server URL, username and version. Add `.textSelection(.enabled)` to the existing M3U source-URL Text. Use the content-closure form for the relative-date EPG row. Leave the password row and the `TipJarRow()` lines untouched. No new strings.

If the AX-size screenshot shows no reflow, the minimal fix is `.textSelection(.enabled)` on the existing value Texts.

**API check:** - `LabeledContent<Label, Content>`: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4018-4019, `@available(iOS 16.0, ...)`.
- `init<S1, S2>(_ title: S1, value: S2)` where both are StringProtocol: :4045.
- `init<S>(_ title: S, content:)`: :4036.
- `textSelection(_:)`: :1821-1825, `@available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, *)`; unavailable on tvOS and watchOS.

**Regression risks:** Touches the two settings files that carry the user's tip-jar work; the edits sit next to the `TipJarRow()` lines but do not change them. Default-size appearance should be the same (label primary, value secondary and trailing); check that long server URLs still wrap acceptably. A long-press on a row with text selection shows the Copy callout; no row here has a competing gesture.

**How to verify:** Screenshot T02/T03 at default size before and after and expect no visible change. Take another at an accessibility Dynamic Type size to see whether rows stack. Manually long-press Server URL and Username and check that Copy appears and the pasteboard holds the value. Confirm the Tip row is unchanged.

## native-reference-16 — No keyboard shortcuts or menu commands on iPad: the iPadOS 26 menu bar and the hold-Command overlay show only system defaults

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: iPad, all dashboard tabs
- Code: `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:44-48`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:26-34, 48-85`

**What the user perceives:** With a Magic Keyboard, Command-F does not open search, Command-1...4 do not switch tabs, Command-R does not refresh and Command-comma does not open Settings; the iPadOS 26 menu bar has no app-specific items. Apple's media apps answer all of these.

**Mechanism (finder):** `keyboardShortcut` and `.commands` do not occur in the target (grep count 0); the scene is a bare `WindowGroup { AppRootView() }` (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:44-48). HIG Settings: 'when a physical keyboard is connected, people often use the standard Command-Comma'.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Publish the dashboard's tab binding as a focused scene value and add scene commands:

WindowGroup { AppRootView() }
    .commands {
        CommandGroup(after: .toolbar) {
            Button(L("dashboard.live")) { tab?.wrappedValue = .live }.keyboardShortcut("1")
            Button(L("dashboard.movies")) { tab?.wrappedValue = .movies }.keyboardShortcut("2")
            Button(L("dashboard.series")) { tab?.wrappedValue = .series }.keyboardShortcut("3")
            Button(L("dashboard.search")) { tab?.wrappedValue = .search }.keyboardShortcut("f")
        }
        CommandGroup(replacing: .appSettings) { Button(L("dashboard.settings")) { tab?.wrappedValue = .settings }.keyboardShortcut(",") }
    }

with `.focusedSceneValue(\.dashboardTab, tabBinding)` on the TabView (DashboardTab must become internal). Existing strings only.

**APIs:** Scene.commands(content:) (iOS 14.0); View.keyboardShortcut(_:modifiers:) (iOS 14.0); View.focusedSceneValue(_:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** What stands: the app defines no keyboard shortcuts or menu commands for browsing. A grep for keyboardShortcut, .commands, focusedSceneValue, FocusedValue, UIKeyCommand and buildMenu over the app target returns nothing; the only hardware-key code is the player's onKeyPress (Views/PlayerView.swift:1049-1085, :1263), which is out of scope and explicitly leaves Command/Control/Option combinations to the system (:1051-1054). The scene is a bare WindowGroup { AppRootView() } (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:44-48). The app is universal (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = "1,2" in project.pbxproj) and uses TabView with .sidebarAdaptable (Views/DashboardView.swift:48-85). History shows no earlier removal: git log -S'keyboardShortcut' and -S'.commands' on apps/ios return no commits, so this is an omission, not a decision.

What does not stand as written:
1. The claims about what currently happens are untested. Nothing in the code or the UIKit headers tells me whether iPadOS already answers Command-F for a .searchable field, Command-comma via the default Settings item (UIMenuPreferences exists, UIMenu.h:143), or tab switching for a UITabBarController. Only a simulator run with a hardware keyboard settles that. "Apple's media apps answer all of these" is asserted without evidence, and the Command-R complaint is not addressed by the proposed fix at all.
2. The snippet does not compile as shown: `tab` is never declared. It needs a Commands struct with @FocusedValue(\.dashboardTab) (or @FocusedBinding) and a FocusedValues key.
3. The fix covers only DashboardView. Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:14,26-37 uses an Int selection with two tabs, so M3U playlists would get nothing, or dead menu items.
4. The player is an in-window overlay above the TabView (Views/DashboardView.swift:92-122). With the binding published unconditionally, Command-1/2/3 would switch tabs invisibly behind a fullscreen player. The code already has isPlayerCoveringContent (:42-44) to gate on.
5. Menu titles would go stale after an in-app language change. L() is a plain function (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:127-129) and the language rebuild is done by .id(localization.selectedLanguage) inside AppRootView (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:56-67); scene-level commands sit outside that rebuild.
6. Command-F as proposed only selects the Search tab. SearchView's .searchable has no focus or isPresented binding (Views/SearchView.swift:69), so the user would still have to tap the field, which is not what Command-F does in a native app.
7. Command-F may collide with the system Edit > Find item (UIMenuFind, UIMenu.h:186); this needs a check on the simulator.
8. With no dashboard open (playlist list in ContentView.swift:42-59) the items must be disabled, and replacing .appSettings removes the system Settings item even then.

No iPad screenshot is relevant: ipad-light holds only Live TV screens (L01-L06) and the claim is not visual.

**Corrected claim:** The app declares no keyboard shortcuts or menu commands for browsing (only the out-of-scope player handles hardware keys), so on an iPad with a hardware keyboard the iPadOS 26 menu bar and the hold-Command overlay carry no app-specific items for switching tabs, opening search or opening the in-app Settings tab. Whether the system already supplies Command-F for the search field or Command-comma (to the system Settings page) has not been checked and needs a simulator run. This is a low-priority gap for keyboard users, not a browsing-fluidity defect, and the comparison with Apple's media apps is unverified.

**Corrected fix:** Optional, low priority; whether to do it at all is the owner's call. If done:

1. Make DashboardTab internal and add a focused-value key holding Binding<DashboardTab> (FocusedValueKey, or @Entry in an extension FocusedValues).
2. In DashboardView, publish with the optional overload: .focusedSceneValue(\.dashboardTab, isPlayerCoveringContent ? nil : tabBinding), so shortcuts are inert while the fullscreen player covers the catalog. Do not touch the player subtree.
3. Add `struct DashboardCommands: Commands` in another_iptv_playerApp.swift with @FocusedValue(\.dashboardTab) private var tab and @ObservedObject private var localization = LocalizationManager.shared, so titles follow an in-app language change. Body: CommandGroup(after: .toolbar) with Buttons for Live / Movies / Series on Command-1/2/3 and Search on Command-F, each .disabled(tab == nil). Attach with WindowGroup { AppRootView() }.commands { DashboardCommands() }.
4. Command-comma to the in-app Settings tab via CommandGroup(replacing: .appSettings) is a product decision: it replaces the system Settings item. If chosen, disable it when tab == nil.
5. For Command-F to feel native, also focus the field: add a @FocusState in SearchView with .searchFocused($focused) and set it when the shortcut fires (for example a second focused value or a counter passed down from DashboardView). If Command-F collides with the system Edit > Find item on the simulator, move the item or drop the shortcut.
6. Either give M3UDashboardView the same treatment (its Int tabs need their own focused key, or a shared enum), or accept that M3U playlists show the items disabled.
7. Do not add Command-R: refresh is pull-to-refresh per screen, and a global refresh command would need new plumbing into the independent refresh tasks.

Existing strings only (dashboard.live, dashboard.movies, dashboard.series, dashboard.search, dashboard.settings). No iOS 26-only API, so no availability gate or fallback is needed.

**API check:** All from the iOS 26.0 simulator SDK SwiftUI.swiftinterface unless noted.
- Scene.commands: `nonisolated public func commands<Content>(@CommandsBuilder content: () -> Content) -> some Scene where Content : Commands`, iOS 14.0 (line 13500).
- CommandGroup: init(before:addition:), init(after:addition:), init(replacing:addition:), iOS 14.0 (21325-21330).
- CommandGroupPlacement: static let appSettings, toolbar, sidebar, textEditing, iOS 14.0 (21346-21361).
- View.keyboardShortcut: `keyboardShortcut(_ key: KeyEquivalent, modifiers: EventModifiers = .command)`, iOS 14.0 (20953). KeyEquivalent is ExpressibleByExtendedGraphemeClusterLiteral (21043), so "1", "f" and "," compile.
- View.focusedSceneValue: `(_ keyPath: WritableKeyPath<FocusedValues, T?>, _ value: T)` iOS 15.0 (20318); optional overload `(_:_ value: T?)` iOS 16.0 (20323), which is the one needed to publish nil under the fullscreen player.
- @FocusedValue (20234) and @FocusedBinding (20265), iOS 14.0; FocusedValueKey protocol iOS 14.0 (20328).
- @Entry macro present in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3014.
- View.searchFocused(_: FocusState<Bool>.Binding), iOS 18.0 (5929), for focusing the search field.
- XCUIElement typeKey:modifierFlags: is declared without an availability restriction in the iOS XCUIAutomation XCUIElement.h:127, so the proposed UI test compiles.
- UIKit: UIMenuFind, UIMenuPreferences, UIMenuView, UIMenuToolbar iOS 13.0 and UIMenuSidebar iOS 15.0 exist in UIMenu.h; the headers do not say which default items the system menu bar shows for this app.

**Regression risks:** - Tab switching behind the fullscreen player overlay unless the focused value is nil while isPlayerCoveringContent is true.
- Stale menu titles after an in-app language change unless the Commands struct observes LocalizationManager.
- Command-F may conflict with the system Edit > Find item; SwiftUI or UIKit may drop one of the two.
- CommandGroup(replacing: .appSettings) removes the system Settings menu item, including on the playlist list where the in-app Settings tab does not exist.
- A Binding is not Equatable, so each DashboardView body pass (it observes contentStore and epgStore) republishes the focused value and re-evaluates the commands. This is cheap but should be confirmed not to cause visible work during catalog load.
- Changing the tab from a command goes through tabBinding, so the saved-tab persistence (DashboardView.swift:26-34) keeps working; assigning selectedTab directly would bypass it.
- No interaction with the tip-jar work in progress, the player key handling (it ignores Command combinations) or the earlier performance work.

**How to verify:** On the iPad simulator with Connect Hardware Keyboard on, before any change: hold Command and note the overlay contents; open the iPadOS 26 menu bar and note the View and app menus; press Command-F on Live TV and on the Search tab; press Command-comma; press Command-1..5. That records what the system already supplies and whether the claim holds in full.

After the change:
- Command-1/2/3 switch tabs and the saved tab survives a relaunch.
- Command-F selects Search and the field has the caret.
- With the fullscreen player up, Command-2 does nothing and space / arrows still drive the player; with the mini player docked, the shortcuts work.
- Change the app language in Settings and confirm the menu titles change.
- On the playlist list the items are disabled.
- Open an M3U playlist and check the items behave as decided.
- UI test: app.typeKey("2", modifierFlags: .command), then assert the Movies navigation title.

## ipad-adaptivity-1 — Poster, shelf and grid sizes are computed once from UIScreen.main, so iPad Split View, Slide Over and resized iOS 26 windows keep full-screen iPad sizes (a single 200 pt poster column at 320-375 pt)

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category grids, All Movies / All Series / All Channels, Favorites, M3U channels, Movie and series detail
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:36-38, 86`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:15-17, 46`, `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-14, 53-68, 75-79`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:125-136`

**What the user perceives:** On an 11-inch iPad in 1/3 Split View or Slide Over (320-375 pt wide) the movie grid is one column of 200x300 posters, a shelf shows 1.4 posters and the live grid shows one 180 pt tile per row. An iPhone at the same width shows three columns. Dragging the iOS 26 window handle or changing the split never changes card sizes.

**Mechanism (finder):** DashboardView.swift:38 and M3UDashboardView.swift:17 store `PosterMetrics(windowSize: UIScreen.main.bounds.size)` in a `let`. PosterMetrics.swift:11-13 derives `layoutScale = clamp(min(w,h)/834, 0.5, 1)` from the screen, not the window, so every iPad window is ~1.0 regardless of its width. Computed with the code's own formula (LazyVGrid padding 16, `.adaptive(minimum:)`): 320 pt iPad window -> 1 column (200x300 poster, 180 live tile); 375 -> 1 column; 507 (13-inch half split) -> 2 columns. Full-screen for reference: iPhone 390 -> 3 columns of 100x150 (scale 0.5); iPad mini 744 -> 3 columns of 178x268; 1024 -> 4 columns of 200x300; 1366 -> 6 columns. The value was moved to UIScreen in commit 1cce013 because the earlier `GeometryReader` in `.background` measured the safe-area size: with the keyboard up, or the status bar toggled by the player, the height shrank, `min(w,h)` flipped to the height and all posters resized (the comment at DashboardView.swift:36-37). `UIScreen.main` is also formally deprecated in the iOS 26 SDK (UIScreen.h:57).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Measure the full window, not the safe area, and quantise the result. In DashboardView and M3UDashboardView replace the `let` with state seeded by today's value (so the first frame is unchanged) and a reader that ignores every safe-area region, keyboard included:

@State private var posterMetrics = PosterMetrics(windowSize: UIScreen.main.bounds.size) // seed only
...
.background {
    Color.clear
        .onGeometryChange(for: PosterMetrics.self, of: { PosterMetrics(windowSize: $0.size) }) { posterMetrics = $0 }
        .ignoresSafeArea()   // .all regions: container and keyboard
}

Keep `min(width, height)` in PosterMetrics.init so rotation and the player's forced landscape still do not change the scale. Quantise it: `layoutScale = (min(1, max(0.5, raw)) * 8).rounded() / 8`. `PosterMetrics` is already `Equatable, Sendable`, so the action fires only when a step is crossed and a live window resize costs at most four relayouts and four image re-keys. Move `.environment(\.posterMetrics, ...)` from the TabView (line 86) to the root ZStack so the Downloads sheet (line 173) stops falling back to `PosterMetricsKey.defaultValue`. Optional follow-up: pass `@Environment(\.displayScale)` instead of `UIScreen.main.scale` at CachedImage.swift:129/133 and PosterMetrics.swift:54/63. Prefetch and render keep matching because both read the same metrics. No iOS 26-only API is involved.

**APIs:** View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 16.0+ (back-deployed, SwiftUICore interface line 6061-6067); already used at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:376); View.ignoresSafeArea(_:edges:) (iOS 14.0+ (default regions .all, which includes .keyboard)); UIScreen.main (deprecated ios(2.0, 26.0) in UIScreen.h:57; no warning at deployment target 18); EnvironmentValues.displayScale (iOS 13.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** Claim confirmed from code. Views/DashboardView.swift:38 and Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:17 hold `private let posterMetrics = PosterMetrics(windowSize: UIScreen.main.bounds.size)`; Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-14 clamps min(w,h)/834 to 0.5...1; Views/PosterMetrics.swift:75-79 uses the same screen value as the environment default. UIScreen.main.bounds is the display, not the window, so every iPad window gets scale 1.0. All grids are `.adaptive(minimum:)` on these metrics (LiveStreamsView.swift:598, VODView.swift:636, SeriesView.swift:599, FavoritesView.swift:30-32, M3UChannelsView.swift:574), so a 320-375 pt iPad window gets one 200 pt column while a phone of the same width gets three. History matches the finding: commit 1cce013 replaced a `.background(GeometryReader)` + `@State windowSize` with the `let`, and the comment at DashboardView.swift:36-37 names the keyboard/status-bar/player shrink as the reason. That old reader measured the safe-area size, so measuring with all safe-area regions ignored does not undo the deliberate fix.

Three things in the proposed fix are wrong:
1. It does not compile here. The app target builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor and SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES (project.pbxproj:577-578, 618-619), and Swift.xcspec:854-858 maps the latter to InferIsolatedConformances. I typechecked the exact snippet with swiftc against the iOS 26 SDK using those flags: `error: main actor-isolated conformance of 'PosterMetrics' to 'Equatable' cannot satisfy conformance requirement for a 'Sendable' type parameter` on `onGeometryChange(for: PosterMetrics.self, ...)`. Measuring a CGSize and building the metrics in the action typechecks cleanly (scratch: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ogulcanozcan-repositories-another-iptv-player/001e9d37-eba7-4a79-997e-bc1be1bce855/scratchpad/agents/verify-ipad/t2.swift).
2. The Downloads-sheet rationale is moot: DownloadsView does not read posterMetrics (readers are DashboardView, FavoritesView, MovieDetailView, LiveStreamsView, VODView, M3UChannelsView, DetailComponents, M3UDashboardView, SeriesView). And putting `.environment` on the root ZStack before `.sheet` (DashboardView.swift:173) would not reach the sheet anyway; the file already re-injects playerOverlay inside the sheet at line 182 for that reason.
3. 'First frame unchanged' is not exact: 1/8 quantisation moves today's scale on some full-screen devices (iPad mini 744 pt: 0.892 -> 0.875, poster 178 -> 175; 430/440 pt phones: 0.516/0.528 -> 0.5, poster 103/106 -> 100; 810/820 pt iPads: 0.97/0.98 -> 1.0). I recomputed the column counts for those widths and they are unchanged, so this is cosmetic.

Severity re-rated to medium: full-screen iPad and all iPhones are unaffected; only Split View, Slide Over and resized iPadOS 26 windows are.

**Corrected claim:** Poster, shelf and grid sizes come from UIScreen.main.bounds captured once in a `let`, so an iPad window narrower than the screen (Split View, Slide Over, a resized iPadOS 26 window) keeps full-screen iPad sizes: one 200x300 poster column and one 180 pt live tile per row at 320-375 pt, two columns at about 507 pt. Full-screen iPad and iPhone layouts are correct today.

**Corrected fix:** In DashboardView and M3UDashboardView:

@State private var posterMetrics = PosterMetrics(windowSize: UIScreen.main.bounds.size) // seed
...
.background {
    Color.clear
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self, of: { $0.size }) { size in
            let next = PosterMetrics(windowSize: size)
            if next != posterMetrics { posterMetrics = next }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()   // all regions, keyboard included
}

Measure CGSize, not PosterMetrics (the isolated-conformance error above). Keep min(width, height) and add the 1/8 quantisation in PosterMetrics.init so a live resize crosses at most four steps. Leave `.environment(\.posterMetrics, ...)` on the TabView; moving it is unnecessary. Optional: seed from the key window's bounds instead of the screen so a launch straight into Split View does not relayout once after the first frame. Leave the UIScreen.main.scale calls in CachedImage.swift:129/133 and PosterMetrics.swift:54/63 alone; they are correct for the built-in display and changing them risks the prefetch/render key match. No iOS 26-only API.

**API check:** View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:): SwiftUICore interface 6055-6067, iOS 16.0+, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient @preconcurrency, requires T: Equatable & Sendable; fails for PosterMetrics under this project's flags, passes for CGSize (swiftc -typecheck). View.ignoresSafeArea(_:edges:): SwiftUICore 16817, defaults .all/.all. EnvironmentValues.displayScale: SwiftUICore 17074. UIScreen.mainScreen: UIScreen.h:57, API_DEPRECATED ios(2.0, 26.0).

**Regression risks:** The original bug (posters resizing when the keyboard appears or the player toggles the status bar or forces landscape) returns if the reader does not ignore the keyboard region or if min(w,h) is dropped. Each quantisation step re-keys every poster request (Resize size is part of the Nuke cache key), so a resize triggers re-decodes and, with no data cache configured, possibly re-downloads. A launch directly into Split View relayouts once after the first frame. Sizes shift by up to 3% on iPad mini and 430/440 pt phones.

**How to verify:** Unit test PosterMetrics: (834x1194)->1.0, (1366x1024)->1.0, (375x1024)->0.5, (507x1024)->0.625, (874x402)->0.5, (744x1133)->0.875. iPad 11-inch simulator: Movies > All in full screen, 1/2 split and 1/3 split; compare column counts. Regression on iPad landscape and iPhone: focus a category search field (keyboard up), start, minimise and close the player; poster size must not change in any of those.

## ipad-adaptivity-2 — Multi-window is enabled by the generated scene manifest, but catalog, EPG and orientation state are process singletons, so a second iPad window breaks the first

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Playlist list, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Search, Movie detail
- Code: `another-iptv-player.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:563, 604`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:44-48`, `ContentView.swift:43-63, 152-163`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:14-16, 100-108, 183-185`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:65-73`, `Views/SearchView.swift:251-306`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:268-301`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:8, 131-137`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Single-window app (recommended, S) or real multi-window support with per-scene catalog stores and a shared playback policy (L).

**What the user perceives:** On iPad a second window can be opened (app shelf '+', Dock, iOS 26 menu bar). If window B goes back to the playlist list or opens another playlist, window A's Live TV, Movies and Series tabs fall back to the 'preparing' spinner and never recover. Window A's Search then lists the other playlist's titles; tapping one plays the wrong stream or opens a detail that fetches and stores metadata from the wrong server. Two windows can also play at once, which exceeds the usual one-connection Xtream limit.

**Mechanism (finder):** `INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation = YES` (project.pbxproj:563, 604) is documented in Xcode's CoreBuildSystem.xcspec as producing 'an entry suitable for a multi-window application'; the built Info.plist contains `UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes => true`. Each `WindowGroup` window (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:45) has its own `ContentView.selectedPlaylist` and `PlayerOverlayController` (DashboardView.swift:8), but they share `PlaylistContentStore.shared`, `EPGStore.shared` and `AppDelegate.orientationLock`. Leaving a dashboard calls `PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload()` (ContentView.swift:61), which clears `activePlaylistId` (PlaylistContentStore.swift:183-185); the other window then sits in `playlist.id != contentStore.activePlaylistId` (LiveStreamsView.swift:66) and its `.task(id: playlist.id)` (DashboardView.swift:131) does not rerun. SearchResultsView does not check `activePlaylistId` (SearchView.swift:251-278): it searches whatever catalog is loaded and builds `LivePlayerShell(playlist: A, ...)` / `MovieDetailView(playlist: A, movie: <row of B>)`; MovieDetailView.swift:273-300 then calls A's panel with B's stream id and `update`s B's row.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest fix: make the app single-window, as Apple's TV and Music apps are. Set `INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation = NO` in both build configurations (a SwiftUI `App` needs no scene manifest), or add an explicit `UIApplicationSceneManifest` with `UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes = false` to App-Info.plist. The single window stays resizable under iPadOS 26 windowing, Split View and Stage Manager. The alternative, real multi-window support, means per-scene stores keyed by playlist id and one shared player/connection policy; that is L effort and touches the data layer.

**APIs:** INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation (build setting) (Xcode 26.0.1, CoreBuildSystem.xcspec:4432-4439); UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes (Info.plist) (iOS 13.0+; present as true in the built product's Info.plist)

**Verifier reasons:** Every link in the mechanism checks out. project.pbxproj:563 and 604 set INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation = YES; CoreBuildSystem.xcspec:4432-4439 describes it as 'an entry suitable for a multi-window application'; `plutil -p` on the built product (scratchpad/build/DD/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/another-iptv-player.app/Info.plist) shows UIApplicationSceneManifest => { UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes => true }. App-Info.plist has no manifest of its own and UIRequiresFullScreen is not set. another_iptv_playerApp.swift:45 is a plain WindowGroup. Per-window state: ContentView.swift:17 selectedPlaylist, DashboardView.swift:8 PlayerOverlayController. Process-wide state: PlaylistContentStore.shared (PlaylistContentStore.swift:14), EPGStore.shared, AppDelegate.orientationLock (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:5).

Leaving a dashboard runs PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload() and EPGStore.shared.setActivePlaylist(nil) (ContentView.swift:61-62; M3U at 52-53); unload() clears activePlaylistId and the lists (PlaylistContentStore.swift:183-190). The other window then stays in the spinner branch (`playlist.id != contentStore.activePlaylistId`: LiveStreamsView.swift:66, VODView.swift:39, SeriesView.swift:40), and its `.task(id: playlist.id)` (DashboardView.swift:131) does not rerun because the id did not change. SearchResultsView.runSearch (SearchView.swift:251-278) reads contentStore lists with no activePlaylistId guard, and MovieDetailView.fetchMovieInfo (MovieDetailView.swift:268-301) calls the window's playlist API with the row's streamId and `update`s that row. A second window auto-opens the same last playlist (ContentView.swift:152-163), so the usual symptom is the stuck spinner after 'Back to list' in one window; the cross-playlist search and metadata write need two different Xtream playlists.

Nothing in the app uses multi-window (no openWindow, requestSceneSessionActivation or scene configuration code) and history shows no deliberate choice; it is the Xcode template default. The defect is deterministic from code but I did not run it. Severity re-rated to medium: iPad only, and only after the user deliberately opens a second window.

**Corrected claim:** The generated scene manifest sets UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes = true, so iPad can open a second window, while the catalog, EPG and orientation state are process singletons. When one window returns to the playlist list or opens another playlist, the other window's Live TV, Movies and Series tabs fall to the 'preparing' spinner and do not recover; with two different Xtream playlists, Search and movie detail in the first window operate on the other playlist's rows.

**Corrected fix:** Make the app single-window, and do it with an explicit manifest rather than by removing the manifest. Add to App-Info.plist:

UIApplicationSceneManifest = { UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes = false; UISceneConfigurations = {}; }

and set INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation = NO in both app configurations (project.pbxproj:563, 604) so the generated entry cannot override it. Setting Generation = NO alone, with no manifest at all, is not verified: it is unclear whether the app keeps the scene lifecycle that the iOS 26 SDK expects, so I would not ship that variant without a run. The single window stays resizable under iPadOS 26 windowing, Split View and Stage Manager. Real multi-window support (per-scene stores, one playback policy) stays the L-effort alternative and is the owner's call.

**API check:** INFOPLIST_KEY_UIApplicationSceneManifest_Generation: CoreBuildSystem.xcspec:4432-4439 (Xcode 26.0.1), Boolean. UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes: present as true in the built Info.plist; Info.plist key since iOS 13. Whether an explicit key in App-Info.plist wins over the generated one when both exist is not verified; hence set both.

**Regression risks:** project.pbxproj carries the owner's uncommitted Tips.storekit reference (two added lines); editing the two build-setting lines leaves it intact, but the file must be edited by hand, not regenerated. AirPlay and external-display playback must be rechecked on a device (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:697-699 mentions an extra scene being connected; those are system-role scenes and should not depend on this key, unverified). iPads that already have two saved windows of the app will have one discarded on update.

**How to verify:** After the change, `plutil -p` on the built app's Info.plist must show UIApplicationSupportsMultipleScenes => false. iPad simulator: launch works (no black screen), the app shelf and the iPadOS 26 menu bar offer no new window, the window still resizes and enters Split View. Device: AirPlay and external display playback. Repro of today's defect (needs a simulator run): open two windows, in the second go Settings > back to list, look at the first.

## ipad-adaptivity-3 — Pushed screens hide the tab bar on iPad too, where it sits in the navigation bar row: tab switching disappears on some screens and stays on others

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live category detail, All Channels, Movie category detail, All Movies, Recently added, Series category detail, All Series, Watch history, TV Guide, M3U group detail, M3U favorites
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722`, `Views/VODView.swift:380, 563, 822`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:502`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:63`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:82`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:56-58`

**What the user perceives:** On iPad, opening a category makes the top tab pill animate away (shots/ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png) and popping brings it back. Favorites, pushed from the same bar, keeps it (ipad-light/L06-favorites.png). From a category grid the user cannot jump to Movies or Search without going back first. Apple's TV and Music apps keep the top bar on every pushed screen.

**Mechanism (finder):** Twelve pushed screens apply `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` unconditionally (e.g. LiveStreamsView.swift:497). On iPad with `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)` (DashboardView.swift:85) the tab bar is the pill in the navigation bar row, so hiding it frees no content height: ipad-light/L03 shows the back and filter buttons still occupying that row. FavoritesView and the detail screens carry no such modifier, hence the inconsistency. Whether the modifier also hides the sidebar when the user has switched to sidebar mode could not be checked without the simulator.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One shared modifier that hides the bar only where it is a bottom bar, and replace the twelve call sites:

private struct HidesBottomTabBar: ViewModifier {
    @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) private var hSize
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.toolbarVisibility(hSize == .compact ? .hidden : .automatic, for: .tabBar)
    }
}

Compact width (iPhone, Slide Over, narrow split) keeps today's behaviour; regular width keeps the top bar or sidebar. Whether iPhone should hide the bar at all belongs to the navigation lens.

**APIs:** View.toolbarVisibility(_:for:) (iOS 18.0+ (the current `toolbar(_:for:)` is iOS 16.0+, soft-deprecated in its favour)); EnvironmentValues.horizontalSizeClass (iOS 13.0+); EnvironmentValues.tabBarPlacement (iOS 18.0+ (.topBar / .sidebar / .bottomBar); a possible more precise signal, not required)

**Verifier reasons:** The problem is real and visible. Twelve pushed screens apply `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` unconditionally (LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722; VODView.swift:380, 563, 822; SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761; M3UChannelsView.swift:502; M3UFavoritesView.swift:63; WatchHistoryListView.swift:82; EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51). shots/ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png shows the tab pill gone while the bar row still holds the back and sort buttons, so no height is gained. shots/ipad-light/L06-favorites.png (FavoritesView has no such modifier) keeps the pill. The modifier dates from the first native iOS commit (6e8bd95) and is uncommented; nothing marks hiding the iPad top bar as intended.

The proposed condition is wrong. Keying on `horizontalSizeClass == .compact` changes iPhone behaviour: Plus and Pro Max phones are regular width in landscape but still have a bottom tab bar, so the bar would reappear on pushed screens in landscape and toggle on rotation. The correct signal is where the bar actually is, `EnvironmentValues.tabBarPlacement` (iOS 18.0+, equal to the deployment target), which the finder listed as optional.

Two interactions the finding missed: (a) once the pill stays visible, the pushed screens that use automatic search placement (WatchHistoryListView.swift:83, M3UFavoritesView.swift:45, EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:53) will show the same duplicate magnifier as finding 4; (b) L06 shows the large title sitting about 55 pt lower when pill, back button and a trailing item share the bar, so the grids may shift the same way.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad, where `.sidebarAdaptable` puts the tabs in the navigation bar row, twelve pushed screens hide them and gain no space, while Favorites and the detail screens keep them; the user cannot switch tab from a category grid, All Movies, the guide or watch history without going back first.

**Corrected fix:** One shared modifier keyed on the bar's real placement, replacing the twelve call sites:

struct HidesBottomTabBar: ViewModifier {
    @Environment(\.tabBarPlacement) private var placement
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let keepsBar = placement == .topBar || placement == .sidebar
        content.toolbarVisibility(keepsBar ? .automatic : .hidden, for: .tabBar)
    }
}

A nil or .bottomBar placement keeps today's hiding, so every iPhone, in both orientations, and compact-width iPad windows are unchanged. This typechecks with the project's compiler flags. If the simulator shows tabBarPlacement is not populated inside tab content, fall back to `UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .pad && horizontalSizeClass == .regular`. Apply together with the search-placement change of ipad-adaptivity-4 on the three pushed screens named above. No iOS 26-only API.

**API check:** View.toolbarVisibility(_:for:): SwiftUI interface 10071-10072, iOS 18.0+; the current toolbar(_:for:) at 10065-10069 is iOS 16.0+, soft-deprecated (deprecated: 100000.0) in its favour. EnvironmentValues.tabBarPlacement: SwiftUI 5500-5510, iOS 18.0+, Optional. TabBarPlacement: SwiftUI 5520-5526, iOS 18.0+, static lets topBar, sidebar, bottomBar, ornament, pageIndicator. The modifier typechecks under -default-isolation MainActor with the project's upcoming features. What tabBarPlacement reports inside a tab's NavigationStack on iPad was not checked at run time.

**Regression risks:** iPhone must be pixel-identical (bar hidden on the twelve screens in both orientations). On iPad the mini player docks relative to the bars, so check its position on a pushed grid with the pill visible. Possible lower large title as in L06. Sidebar mode on iPad needs a look: whether the sidebar stays and whether the toggle remains reachable.

**How to verify:** iPad simulator screenshots: Live TV > category, All Movies, TV Guide and Watch history must show the tab pill like ipad-light/L06; repeat with the sidebar open and in a compact-width window (bar must hide). iPhone 17 Pro and a Pro Max in portrait and landscape: the same screens must match the current shots (no bottom bar). Log tabBarPlacement once on iPad to confirm it is .topBar or .sidebar.

## ipad-adaptivity-4 — On iPad the top bar shows two identical magnifiers (Search tab and in-tab filter) and the three browse actions collapse into an untitled overflow menu

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels, Favorites
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93, 108-138`, `Views/VODView.swift:112-133, 145`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:113-134, 146`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:64-93, 112`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:58`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:77-83, 231-241`

**What the user perceives:** On an 11-inch iPad in portrait the bar reads: sidebar toggle, Live TV, Movies, Series, Settings, magnifier, star, '...', magnifier (shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png). The first magnifier opens global search; the second filters the current tab. TV Guide, All Channels and Jump to category are behind '...', so the guide is two taps away and has no visible entry point.

**Mechanism (finder):** The Search tab (DashboardView.swift:77, `role: .search`) renders as a magnifier at the end of the tab pill. Each home screen also attaches `.searchable(text:isPresented:prompt:)` with automatic placement (LiveStreamsView.swift:93, VODView.swift:145, SeriesView.swift:146, M3UChannelsView.swift:112, FavoritesView.swift:58), which iPadOS resolves to a trailing toolbar search button; on iPhone the same code gives a field under the title (iphone-light/L01-live-home.png). The centred tab pill leaves room for only two trailing items, so the star stays and the three inner items overflow. Their labels are bare `Image(systemName:)` with only an `accessibilityLabel` (LiveStreamsView.swift:113-116, 122-126, 131-136), and two of them are `NavigationLink`s; whether the overflow rows show a title and navigate was not verified.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) Give the in-tab filter the same shape on iPad as on iPhone and on the pushed grids (ipad-light/L03 shows that field): `.searchable(text: $searchText, isPresented: $isSearchActive, placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic), prompt: ...)` at the five sites. That removes the second magnifier and frees toolbar width. 2) Give toolbar items real titles so the overflow menu is readable: `Label(L("epg.guide.title"), systemImage: "calendar.day.timeline.left")` instead of `Image` + `accessibilityLabel` (the bar still shows the icon only). 3) If the overflow rows turn out not to navigate, replace the two toolbar `NavigationLink`s with `Button` + `navigationDestination(isPresented:)`. No iOS 26-only API.

**APIs:** SearchFieldPlacement.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode:) (iOS 15.0+); View.searchable(text:isPresented:placement:prompt:) (iOS 17.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The claim is confirmed by shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png: the bar reads sidebar toggle, Live TV, Movies, Series, Settings, magnifier (Search tab), then star and '...', then a second magnifier. Code agrees: the Search tab has role .search (DashboardView.swift:77); each home attaches `.searchable` with automatic placement (LiveStreamsView.swift:93, VODView.swift:145, SeriesView.swift:146, M3UChannelsView.swift:112, FavoritesView.swift:58), which iPadOS resolves to a trailing toolbar button, while the pushed grids use `.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always)` and get a field under the title (ipad-light/L03). The three inner Live TV items (LiveStreamsView.swift:108-138) are Image-only with an accessibilityLabel, and the dashboard star (DashboardView.swift:234-238) has no label at all. On iPhone the same code already renders a field under the title (iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png), so explicit drawer placement leaves iPhone unchanged.

Why only partly:
1. The fix does not remove the overflow on an 11-inch iPad in portrait. Measured from L01: the pill ends at about 651 pt of 834, star + '...' take about 105 pt (about 52 pt per item) and the magnifier about 44 pt. Dropping the magnifier leaves about 160 pt, room for three items; Live TV needs four (star, guide, all, jump). Movies and Series (three items) probably fit; Live TV and M3U still overflow in portrait. How to arrange those four is a product decision the finding does not name.
2. Whether the overflow rows show a title and whether the two NavigationLink items navigate from the menu cannot be told from code or the existing shots (no screenshot of the open '...' menu).
3. A full-width field under the title is consistent with the app's pushed grids but is not Apple's iPad pattern on iOS 26, where search sits in the trailing toolbar; the duplication exists because the app has both a Search tab and per-tab filters. Which one keeps the magnifier on iPad is the owner's choice.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad the navigation bar row shows two identical magnifiers (the Search tab at the end of the tab pill and the per-tab filter resolved to a toolbar button), and on an 11-inch iPad in portrait three of the four Live TV actions collapse into an untitled '...' overflow. Removing the second magnifier fixes the duplication but frees room for only about three trailing items in portrait.

**Corrected fix:** 1) At LiveStreamsView.swift:93, VODView.swift:145, SeriesView.swift:146 and M3UChannelsView.swift:112 use `.searchable(text:isPresented:placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic), prompt:)`; at FavoritesView.swift:58 the same placement without isPresented. If ipad-adaptivity-3 is applied, do the same at WatchHistoryListView.swift:83, M3UFavoritesView.swift:45 and EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:53, otherwise they gain the duplicate magnifier.
2) Give every toolbar item a real title: `Label(L("epg.guide.title"), systemImage: ...)` instead of Image + accessibilityLabel, including the star at DashboardView.swift:234-238 (key favorites.title exists, used at M3UChannelsView.swift:82).
3) Product decision for 11-inch portrait, where four items do not fit: order the items so the guide stays visible, or merge 'All' and 'Jump to category' into one titled Menu on regular width.
4) Only if a simulator run shows the overflow rows do not navigate: replace the toolbar NavigationLinks with Button + navigationDestination(isPresented:).
All of 1 and 2 typecheck with the project's flags. No iOS 26-only API.

**API check:** SearchFieldPlacement.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode:): SwiftUI interface 9342-9346, iOS 15.0+. View.searchable(text:isPresented:placement:prompt:) with StringProtocol prompt: SwiftUI 5783-5786, iOS 17.0+, placement defaults to .automatic. Label in a ToolbarItem inside a NavigationLink label typechecks. iOS 26 alternatives exist (searchToolbarBehavior at SwiftUI 19982-19983, DefaultToolbarItem at 6275-6276) but are not needed.

**Regression risks:** `isPresented: $isSearchActive` drives the reset of searchText and debouncedQuery (LiveStreamsView.swift:102 and the equivalents); confirm cancel still clears the filter with drawer placement. With displayMode .automatic the field scrolls away with the large title; iPhone must look exactly like today. On iPad the shelves move down by the height of the field.

**How to verify:** iPad 11-inch simulator, portrait and landscape: one magnifier in the bar, the filter field under the title, count the trailing items that stay visible on Live TV, Movies, Series and M3U. Open '...' and check that each row has icon and title and that TV Guide and All Channels push. iPhone screenshots must match shots/iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png.

## ipad-adaptivity-5 — The detail hero is a fixed 380 pt and the content below it has no maximum width: it fills an iPhone screen in landscape and stretches the Play button and plot across a 13-inch iPad

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:19-44, 46-72, 189-252, 346-405`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:123-188`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:958-1004`

**What the user perceives:** iPhone landscape (402 pt tall on a 17 Pro): the hero takes 380 pt, so the detail opens showing only artwork and a title; Play, Download and the plot need a scroll. iPad 13-inch landscape: the backdrop is a 1366x380 strip (3.6:1), which shows the middle half of a 16:9 image; Watch Now is 1334 pt wide and the plot runs in lines of about 200 characters.

**Mechanism (finder):** Both detail screens pass `heroHeight: 380` (MovieDetailView.swift:126, SeriesView.swift:961) and `DetailHero` pins every layer to it (DetailComponents.swift:43, 60, 72, 97). The scroll view ignores the top safe area (MovieDetailView.swift:187), so in compact height the hero covers the screen. Below it, `DetailActionBar` (DetailComponents.swift:202-207), `DownloadButton` (MovieDetailView.swift:147-158), `DetailPlotBlock` (402) and `DetailInfoTextBlock` (426) all use `maxWidth: .infinity` with 16 pt padding. The nav-title threshold `contentOffset.y > 240` (MovieDetailView.swift:181, SeriesView.swift:997) is tied to the same constant.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Compute the hero height from size classes inside `DetailHero` (it already owns the layout) and cap the text and actions:

@Environment(\.verticalSizeClass) private var vSize
@Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) private var hSize
private var height: CGFloat { vSize == .compact ? 200 : (hSize == .regular ? 480 : heroHeight) }

Use `height` everywhere `heroHeight` is used and expose it so the callers' title threshold becomes `height - 140`. In the two `contentScroll` builders constrain the blocks under the hero: `DetailActionBar` and `DownloadButton` `.frame(maxWidth: 420, alignment: .leading)`, plot and info blocks `.frame(maxWidth: 700, alignment: .leading)`; the hero stays full-bleed and the season/episode list stays full width. Phone portrait is unchanged because the caps exceed its width. The iPad hero height (480 or a ratio of the width) is a design choice to settle on a device.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues.verticalSizeClass (iOS 13.0+); EnvironmentValues.horizontalSizeClass (iOS 13.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is as described. Both callers pass `heroHeight: 380` (MovieDetailView.swift:126, SeriesView.swift:961); DetailHero pins the stack, backdrop, fallback gradient and scrim to it (Components/DetailComponents.swift:43, 71, 82, 97); both scroll views ignore the top safe area (MovieDetailView.swift:187, SeriesView.swift:1003). The app rotates outside the player (AppDelegate.orientationLock = .allButUpsideDown, another_iptv_playerApp.swift:5; iPhone landscape is in the supported orientations), so on a 402 pt tall phone in landscape the hero fills the screen. That state is easy to reach: closing the player while holding the phone sideways leaves the UI in landscape on the detail screen. Below the hero nothing has a width cap: DetailActionBar (DetailComponents.swift:202-207), DownloadButton (MovieDetailView.swift:147-158), DetailPlotBlock (:402) and DetailInfoTextBlock (:426) fill the width with 16 pt padding. The nav-title threshold 240 (MovieDetailView.swift:181, SeriesView.swift:997) is the same constant minus 140. There is no iPad or landscape screenshot of the detail screen (ipad-light has only L01-L06), so the visual magnitude rests on arithmetic; shots/iphone-dark/M07-movie-detail.png confirms the portrait baseline.

Corrections to the fix:
1. The 420 pt cap is narrower than a 430 pt (Plus) or 440 pt (Pro Max) phone in portrait, so 'phone portrait is unchanged' is false for those: Watch Now and Download would end 10-20 pt short of the right margin. The caps must apply only in regular width.
2. DetailHero already takes heroHeight as a parameter. Computing the height inside the hero and then 'exposing' it to the callers for the title threshold is more machinery than needed; compute it once in the callers.
3. In compact height the overlay (poster 88 pt at phone scale, title of up to three lines, 20 pt bottom padding) must clear the navigation bar because the scroll view ignores the top safe area; 200 pt is tight and has to be checked on a simulator.

**Corrected claim:** The detail hero is a fixed 380 pt and the blocks under it have no maximum width: on an iPhone in landscape (about 400 pt tall, reachable by closing the player while holding the phone sideways) the screen opens showing only artwork and title, and on a 13-inch iPad the backdrop is a 1366x380 strip with a Play button about 1334 pt wide and plot lines spanning the whole width.

**Corrected fix:** Add one shared helper, e.g. `enum DetailLayout { static func heroHeight(h: UserInterfaceSizeClass?, v: UserInterfaceSizeClass?) -> CGFloat }` returning about 220 for compact height, a taller value for regular width (480 or a fraction of the width; design choice) and 380 otherwise. MovieDetailView and SeriesDetailView read the two size classes, pass the result as the existing `heroHeight:` argument and use `heroHeight - 140` in onScrollGeometryChange; DetailHero itself does not change. Width caps only in regular width: `.frame(maxWidth: hSize == .regular ? 420 : .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on DetailActionBar and on DownloadButton (after its own horizontal padding so both line up), `maxWidth: hSize == .regular ? 700 : .infinity` on the plot and info blocks; hero and season/episode list stay full width. The exact numbers are a design decision to settle on a device. No iOS 26-only API.

**API check:** EnvironmentValues.horizontalSizeClass: SwiftUICore interface 17116-17118, iOS 13.0+. EnvironmentValues.verticalSizeClass: SwiftUICore 17132-17134, iOS 13.0+. A conditional `frame(maxWidth:alignment:)` on size class typechecks under the project's flags. onScrollGeometryChange is already in use at both sites.

**Regression risks:** The backdrop request is keyed by width and height with the .high profile (DetailComponents.swift:50-59), so a rotation that changes the hero height refetches or re-decodes the backdrop once. The parallax and overscroll maths use the same height and follow automatically. Caps without the regular-width gate would misalign buttons on 430/440 pt phones. The inline-title threshold must track the new height or the title appears too early or late.

**How to verify:** Simulator screenshots: iPhone 17 Pro landscape movie and series detail (Play visible without scrolling, title not under the back button); iPhone Pro Max portrait (buttons reach both margins); iPad 13-inch landscape and portrait (button width, plot line length, backdrop crop); iPhone portrait must match shots/iphone-dark/M07-movie-detail.png. Scroll each to confirm the inline title appears as the hero leaves.
