## ipad-adaptivity-6 — An 11-inch iPad shows no more posters per screen than an iPhone, and the fixed-size cards float inside wider adaptive columns

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movie category grid, All Movies, Series category grid, All Series, Favorites, Watch history, Continue watching shelf
- Code: `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-20, 44-45`, `Views/VODView.swift:490-545, 635-637, 690-710`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:462-490, 598-600, 648-663`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:28-33`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:66-68, 160-199`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:70-107`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Target poster density on iPad: keep the current 200 pt posters (3-6 per row) or go to about 150-160 pt (5-8 per row), closer to Apple's TV app.

**What the user perceives:** iPad 11-inch portrait: three 200x300 posters per row with about 73 pt of empty space between them, roughly nine titles per screen, which is what an iPhone shows (three columns of 100x150). In a 50k-150k title catalog the larger screen gives no browsing advantage. The Continue Watching cards stay at the phone size (160x90) next to posters twice as large.

**Mechanism (finder):** `referenceShortSide = 834` makes every iPad use scale ~1.0, i.e. 200x300 posters (PosterMetrics.swift:10-19). Columns come from `GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: categoryGridPosterWidth), spacing: gridSpacing)` (VODView.swift:636, SeriesView.swift:599), but the card is a fixed `posterWidth` frame (VODView.swift:505-506, 533), so the leftover of each column becomes extra gap. Computed: 744 pt -> 3 columns 228 pt wide holding a 178 pt poster (50 pt slack); 834 -> 3 columns, 256.7 wide, 56.7 slack; 1024 -> 4 columns, 36 slack; 1194 -> 5, 19.6 slack; 1366 -> 6, 9 slack; iPhone 390 -> 3 columns, 14 slack. With the sidebar open at 834 (514 pt left) the grid drops to 2 columns. WatchHistoryListView.swift:67 and ContinueWatchingRow.swift:72-73 hard-code 160 pt and bypass PosterMetrics.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Decide a target poster width for regular-width windows (150-160 pt gives 4-5 columns at 834, 6 at 1024, 8 at 1366) and let PosterMetrics return the column count and the exact cell width for a given content width, so the card fills its column and the gaps equal `gridSpacing`:

func grid(for width: CGFloat) -> (columns: Int, cell: CGFloat) {
    let n = max(2, Int((width - 32 + gridSpacing) / (targetPoster + gridSpacing)))
    return (n, floor((width - 32 - CGFloat(n - 1) * gridSpacing) / CGFloat(n)))
}

Use `Array(repeating: GridItem(.fixed(cell), spacing: gridSpacing), count: n)`. To leave the image tuning intact, keep the decode size separate from the layout size: add an optional `decodeSize` to `CachedImage` and `ListImagePrefetch.start`, fed by the nominal metric, so prefetch and render keys still match and do not change on rotation. Route the two history cards through PosterMetrics. Pagination (`pageSize = 90`) and the Equatable wrappers are untouched.

**APIs:** GridItem(.fixed(_:), spacing:) (iOS 14.0+); View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 16.0+ (to read the grid's content width))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-derived the numbers from the code and they hold. Views/PosterMetrics.swift:10-13 clamps layoutScale to 1.0 on every iPad (short side >= 834), so categoryGridPosterWidth is 200 and gridSpacing 16 (lines 19, 44). Views/VODView.swift:636 and Views/SeriesView.swift:599 use GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 200), spacing: 16) inside .padding() (VODView.swift:710), while the card is a fixed frame (VODView.swift:505-506, 533; CachedImage.swift:81). At 834 pt: content 802, 3 columns of 256.7, 56.7 slack per column, 72.7 pt between posters. At 744: 3 columns of 228 holding 178. At 1194: 5 columns, 19.6 slack. iPhone 390: 3 columns of 114 holding 100. shots/iphone-light/M04-movies-all.png shows 3 columns and about 3.5 rows on the phone; an 11-inch iPad in portrait fits about 2.6 rows of 3, so the iPad shows no more titles than the phone. No iPad Movies screenshot exists yet (ipad-light has only L01-L06). What needs correcting: (1) the 200x300 size is deliberate, not an oversight: PosterMetrics.swift:4 names the 11-inch iPad as the design reference, and the file is unchanged since the initial commit (git log --follow). So the density is a product decision; only the uneven gaps are a side effect of adaptive columns with fixed cards. (2) The fix as written has three defects, listed in corrected_fix. Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:67, 164-165, 199 and Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:72-73, 93, 107 do hard-code 160 pt, but they are 16:9 thumbnails rather than posters, so routing them through PosterMetrics is optional polish.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad the category, All, Favorites and Recently Added poster grids show 3 columns in 11-inch portrait (5 in landscape) of fixed 200x300 posters, with up to 57 pt of slack per adaptive column (73 pt gaps instead of the intended 16). That is no more titles per screen than an iPhone. The poster size is a deliberate design reference (PosterMetrics.swift:4), so the density is an owner decision; the uneven gaps are the only unintended part. Live TV grids are barely affected (180 pt tiles, 8.5 pt slack at 834; see shots/ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png).

**Corrected fix:** Owner decides the iPad target poster width first (about 150-160 pt gives 4-5 columns at 834, 7 at 1194). Then make the grid cell fill its column. Two workable shapes: (A) the proposed computed columns with GridItem(.fixed(cell)), or (B) keep GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: target)) and give the grid cards a flexible variant (image with aspectRatio(2/3) and maxWidth .infinity, title with maxWidth .infinity, progress bar as a full-width bar scaled on x). B needs no width state and no extra layout pass, so I would prefer it. Corrections needed for A: (1) the width state starts at 0, and max(2, ...) with floor((0 - 32 - spacing) / 2) gives a negative cell width; fall back to the nominal metric until the width is known, or the first frame is wrong and the grid jumps. (2) A decode size 'fed by the nominal metric' is too small: the cell is always at least the target and up to (n+1)/n times wider, so posters would be upscaled 15-25% and look soft. Decode at a fixed upper bound instead, for example ceil(target * 1.25), used identically by CachedImage.request and ListImagePrefetch.start so the keys still match (ListImagePrefetch.swift:17-21) and do not change on rotation. (3) On iPhone the posters grow from 100 pt to about 114-118 pt once they fill the column, and the gaps shrink to 8 pt; three columns stay but rows per screen drop slightly, so the owner should see it before it ships. Keep the fixed-size card path for the shelves. Apply the same columns in FavoritesView.swift:28-33 and the Recently Added screens (they reuse VODCategoryContent and SeriesCategoryContent). Leave pageSize, the Equatable wrappers and the off-main recompute alone. The history cards are optional.

**API check:** GridItem(.fixed/.adaptive, spacing:) is already used in the repo (iOS 14). View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) is in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6061-6067 as @available(iOS 16.0), @_alwaysEmitIntoClient, and is already used at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:376. View.containerRelativeFrame(_:count:span:spacing:alignment:) is iOS 17.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1536) if wanted. No iOS 26-only API is involved.

**Regression risks:** Changes the Nuke cache key (Resize size) for every grid poster; if prefetch and render do not use the same decode size, each poster decodes twice (the documented pitfall in ListImagePrefetch.swift:17-21). Reading a view width goes against the note at Views/DashboardView.swift:36-37 (metrics deliberately tied to the display because transient layout shrinks); width is not affected by the keyboard, but sidebar toggles and iPadOS 26 window resizing will re-lay the grid. iPhone grid appearance changes slightly. VODStreamCard and SeriesCard are shared with shelves and Favorites, so a card change must not alter shelf sizing.

**How to verify:** Unit-test the column function at 0, 320, 390, 402, 744, 834, 1024, 1194 and 1366 (no negative or zero cell; iPhone stays at 3). iPad 11-inch simulator, All Movies in portrait and landscape, and with the sidebar open: gaps equal gridSpacing and there is no jump on first appearance or rotation. Compare iPhone M04 before and after. With the image server, confirm one decode per poster (prefetch hit) and that posters are not soft at 2x.

## ipad-adaptivity-7 — Settings forms, result lists and a few controls stretch edge to edge on iPad instead of keeping a readable width

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings, M3U settings, Language picker, Search results, Downloads, Favorites, Playlist list
- Code: `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40`, `Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:34`, `Views/SearchView.swift:149, 245`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:79, 117`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:37-44`, `ContentView.swift:189-200, 207-255`

**What the user perceives:** On a 13-inch iPad in landscape a settings row has its label at the far left and its switch or value about 1300 pt away. Search results are 44 pt thumbnails in rows as wide as the screen. The Favorites segmented control is 1334 pt wide (834 pt in shots/ipad-light/L06-favorites.png) and the empty playlist screen shows a 1286 pt wide Add button. Apple's apps either cap such content at a readable width or present it in a form sheet.

**Mechanism (finder):** `Form` and inset-grouped `List` fill the navigation stack's width; nothing constrains them (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40, SearchView.swift:149-245, DownloadsView.swift:79-117, ContentView.swift:208). FavoritesView.swift:37-44 pads a segmented `Picker` to the full width. ContentView.swift:196-199 gives the empty-state button `maxWidth: .infinity` with 40 pt padding.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One modifier that centres scroll content at a readable width while the scroll view and its grouped background stay full-bleed, so scrolling from the margins still works:

struct ReadableContentWidth: ViewModifier {
    var maxWidth: CGFloat = 700
    @State private var width: CGFloat = 0
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .contentMargins(.horizontal, width > maxWidth + 40 ? (width - maxWidth) / 2 : nil, for: .scrollContent)
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self, of: { $0.size.width }) { width = $0 }
    }
}

Apply it to the two settings forms, the language list, DownloadsView's list, the search results list and the playlist list. `contentMargins` on a `List` is already used in this repo (Views/Components/TipJarView.swift:100). Cap the segmented picker with `.frame(maxWidth: 420)` and the empty-state button with `.frame(maxWidth: 360)`. Phones are unaffected because the margin stays nil below the threshold. The settings change is one added modifier on the `Form`; the `TipJarRow()` lines are not touched.

**APIs:** View.contentMargins(_:_:for:) (iOS 17.0+); View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 16.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The code matches the claim: Form at Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:44 and Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:40, List at Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:34, Views/SearchView.swift:149-245 (ResultRow is a 44 pt thumbnail, line 317), Views/DownloadsView.swift:79-117 and ContentView.swift:208 have no width constraint. Views/FavoritesView.swift:37-44 pads a segmented Picker to full width, and ContentView.swift:196-199 gives the empty-state button maxWidth .infinity with 40 pt padding. shots/ipad-light/L06-favorites.png confirms the segmented control spans the screen; measured it is about 802 pt (834 minus 2 x 16), not 834, so the 13-inch landscape figure is about 1334. No iPad screenshots of Settings, Search or Downloads exist yet. Corrections: (1) severity is overstated. Apple's own Settings app does not cap its detail column either; full-width inset-grouped rows are standard iPad behaviour, so this is polish, with the 800-1334 pt segmented control and the 1286 pt button the clearest outliers. (2) The fix compiles, but its key behaviour is unverified here: horizontal contentMargins on a Form or inset-grouped List (the repo precedent at Views/Components/TipJarView.swift:100 is .top only), and the width state starting at 0 means the first layout may be full width before the margins apply. (3) In FavoritesView the cap must go before .padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial) or the material band shrinks with the control.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad the settings forms, language list, Downloads, search results and playlist list run the full width of the window (standard for a list, but sparse at 1024-1366 pt), the Favorites segmented control is about 802 pt wide at 11-inch portrait and about 1334 pt at 13-inch landscape, and the empty-playlist Add button is up to about 1286 pt wide. This is cosmetic and iPad-only.

**Corrected fix:** Do the two certain items first: in FavoritesView use Picker(...).pickerStyle(.segmented).frame(maxWidth: 420).frame(maxWidth: .infinity).padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial), and cap the empty-state label at ContentView.swift:196 with .frame(maxWidth: 360). The ReadableContentWidth modifier (contentMargins(.horizontal, _, for: .scrollContent) plus onGeometryChange) is acceptable for the two settings forms, the language list, the Downloads list, the search results List and the playlist List, but only after a simulator check that horizontal margins take effect on Form and insetGrouped List on iOS 18 and 26 and that there is no visible full-width first frame. If there is one, read the width synchronously with a GeometryReader around the list instead of the state. Add the modifier to the Form itself and leave the TipJarRow() lines and section order untouched. Whether settings should be capped at all is the owner's call.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4233-4242: contentMargins(_ edges: Edge.Set = .all, _ length: CGFloat?, for: ContentMarginPlacement = .automatic), @available(iOS 17.0); the optional length overload exists, so passing nil compiles. ContentMarginPlacement.scrollContent is at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10405. onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) is iOS 16.0 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6061-6067). No iOS 26-only API.

**Regression risks:** Edits the two settings views that carry the uncommitted tip-jar row; one added modifier on the Form leaves it intact. Swipe actions (playlist list, Downloads rows) and section headers move with the margins. A one-frame margin jump on iPad when a screen first appears is possible. iPhone is unaffected while the threshold is not reached.

**How to verify:** iPad 13-inch landscape and 11-inch portrait: Settings, language list, Downloads, search results and playlist list show rows about 700 pt wide and centred, scrolling works from the side margins, swipe actions still work, and no frame shows full-width rows on first appearance (record at 60 fps or step frames). Favorites: control about 420 pt, material band still full width. iPhone T01-T05, Q03 and P01 unchanged. The tip-jar row still opens its sheet.

## ipad-adaptivity-8 — No browse card, chip or custom button reacts to the pointer; the only two hoverEffect sites are in the player

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Category grids, Favorites, Watch history, Movie and series detail, Search, TV Guide
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457`, `Views/VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 490-545, 692-704`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:462-490`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:418-445`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-52, 64-110`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:158-202`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:209-252, 274-314, 443-466`, `Views/SearchView.swift:28-39`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:109-118`

**What the user perceives:** With a trackpad or mouse on iPad, moving over posters, channel tiles, shelf headers, the Watch Now button, season chips or search filter chips gives no highlight or lift; only system bar buttons and list rows respond. Posters in Apple's TV app and App Store highlight under the pointer.

**Mechanism (finder):** Every card is a `Button` or `NavigationLink` with `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:457, VODView.swift:345/462/704, DetailComponents.swift:251/284/465), and plain style has no pointer effect. A grep for `hoverEffect` finds only Views/Components/GlassSystemIconButton.swift:43-48 and Views/PlayerView.swift:3971-3972. `UIApplicationSupportsIndirectInputEvents` is already YES (project.pbxproj:564), so only the effects are missing.

**Proposed fix (finder):** A shared modifier applied to the artwork of each card and to the custom buttons, with the shape matching the visible corner radius:

extension View {
    func cardHover(cornerRadius: CGFloat = 8) -> some View {
        contentShape(.hoverEffect, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
            .hoverEffect(.highlight)
    }
}

Put it on the `CachedImage` in LiveStreamCard (radius 12), VODStreamCard and SeriesCard (8), M3UChannelCard, HistoryCard and HistoryCardGridItem, and on the labels of DetailActionBar's primary button (16), DetailSecondaryLabel (12), season chips, search filter chips and EPG day chips (`Capsule()`). Prefer `.highlight` to `.lift`: lift scales the view and would be clipped by the shelf scroll views. It has no effect on touch. Because it is added to cells of very long lazy grids, re-run the existing scroll-performance measurement on iPad afterwards.

**APIs:** View.hoverEffect(_:) with HoverEffect.highlight (iOS 13.4+ (CustomHoverEffect overload iOS 18.0+)); View.contentShape(.hoverEffect, _:) (iOS 15.0+ (ContentShapeKinds.hoverEffect))

**Verifier reasons:** The grep is right: hoverEffect appears only at Views/Components/GlassSystemIconButton.swift:43-48 and Views/PlayerView.swift:3971-3972, and UIApplicationSupportsIndirectInputEvents is YES (project.pbxproj:564, 605). Cards using .buttonStyle(.plain) and so having no pointer effect: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:457, Views/VODView.swift:345, 462, 704, Views/SeriesView.swift:322, 434, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:445, Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:201, Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:251, 267, 284, 465, Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:118. But 'every card and chip' is wrong. Several sites use the default button style, which should already get the system pointer effect: shelf headers (VODView.swift:315-326, 418-429; LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367), the Series category grid links (SeriesView.swift:650, no plain style), the Favorites movie and series grids (FavoritesView.swift:134, 160), and the search filter chips (SearchView.swift:28-39). So the real state is inconsistent rather than absent. HistoryCard (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52) is an onTapGesture and not a button at all. The fix's choice of .highlight for artwork is doubtful: per its SwiftUI documentation, highlight morphs the pointer into a platter behind the view, which an opaque poster hides, leaving only the pointer disappearing and a slight parallax; .lift is the effect meant for artwork-sized elements. The existing use in GlassSystemIconButton is on a translucent disc, where highlight is right. I could not observe pointer behaviour (no simulator access), and iPadOS 26 changed the pointer, so the effect choice needs a device or simulator check. Last week's player audit rated the equivalent player item low (ios-player-airplay-fix-report.md:270); the same rating fits here.

**Corrected claim:** Pointer feedback while browsing on iPad is inconsistent. Cards and chips built with .buttonStyle(.plain) (live tiles, movie and series shelf cards, the movie grid, M3U tiles, history grid cards, detail action buttons, season chips, EPG day chips) and the tap-gesture Continue Watching cards have none. Default-style links and buttons (shelf headers, the Series grid, Favorites grids, search filter chips) should already get the system effect; this was not observed.

**Corrected fix:** Add one shared modifier, but choose the effect per element. For artwork (the CachedImage in LiveStreamCard, VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, M3UChannelCard, HistoryCard, HistoryCardGridItem) use contentShape(.hoverEffect, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: r, style: .continuous)) with .hoverEffect(.lift), or .hoverEffect() for automatic, after trying both in the simulator; if lift is clipped in the shelves, add .scrollClipDisabled() to the horizontal shelf ScrollViews. For text chips and buttons (DetailActionBar primary and secondary, season chips, EPG day chips) use .hoverEffect(.highlight) with a matching Capsule or RoundedRectangle content shape. Leave the search filter chips alone unless the simulator shows they have no effect. Apply the same modifier to the Series grid and Favorites grid cards so every poster behaves alike, or give those links .buttonStyle(.plain) plus the modifier. A custom scale effect is not possible on iOS (see api_check). All of this is iOS 18-safe; no fallback needed.

**API check:** hoverEffect(_ effect: HoverEffect = .automatic): @available(iOS 13.4) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9444-9451); the isEnabled overload is iOS 17.0 (9454-9458). HoverEffect has .automatic, .highlight and .lift (9483-9494). ContentShapeKinds.hoverEffect: struct is iOS 15.0, member not restricted on iOS (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3985-4004). The closure form hoverEffect(in:isEnabled:body:) on View is @available(iOS, unavailable), visionOS 2.0 only (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9470-9479). scrollClipDisabled(_:) is iOS 17.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:12495-12496).

**Regression risks:** A lift effect scales the artwork and can be clipped by the shelf scroll views or overlap the title; scrollClipDisabled changes shelf clipping and needs a visual check. An extra modifier on every lazy cell is a small cost; re-measure scrolling on All Movies. A hover content shape must not replace the interaction content shape (use the .hoverEffect kind only). No effect on touch.

**How to verify:** iPad simulator with Capture Pointer, on iOS 18 and iOS 26. First, on the current build, hover a Series category grid card (default style) and a Movies grid card (plain) to see what exists today. After the change, hover a poster, a channel tile, Watch Now, a season chip and an EPG day chip: the effect follows the rounded shape, is visible on opaque artwork, and is not clipped in shelves. Scroll-performance run on All Movies before and after.

## ipad-adaptivity-9 — There are no keyboard shortcuts while browsing: no Cmd-F, Cmd-R or Cmd-1...5, although the player already handles hardware keys

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Dashboard tabs, Search, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:46-86`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:26-46`, `Views/SearchView.swift:67-69`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:44-48`

**What the user perceives:** With a Magic Keyboard, holding Command shows an empty shortcut list. The user cannot switch tabs, jump to search or refresh from the keyboard, which Apple's TV, Music and App Store apps allow. On iPadOS 26 the app's menu bar has no app-specific commands either.

**Mechanism (finder):** A grep for `keyboardShortcut`, `onKeyPress` and `.commands` in the non-player sources returns nothing; the only key handling is PlayerView.swift:1052-1085, which deliberately leaves Command combinations to the system (line 1055). `TabView` does not add Cmd-number shortcuts by itself.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add zero-size buttons behind the TabView in DashboardView (and the two-tab equivalent in M3UDashboardView); their titles appear in the Command-hold overlay:

.background {
    Group {
        Button(L("dashboard.live"))   { tabBinding.wrappedValue = .live }.keyboardShortcut("1")
        Button(L("dashboard.movies")) { tabBinding.wrappedValue = .movies }.keyboardShortcut("2")
        Button(L("dashboard.series")) { tabBinding.wrappedValue = .series }.keyboardShortcut("3")
        Button(L("dashboard.settings")) { tabBinding.wrappedValue = .settings }.keyboardShortcut("4")
        Button(L("dashboard.search")) { tabBinding.wrappedValue = .search; searchFocusRequest += 1 }.keyboardShortcut("f")
        Button(L("settings.refresh_all")) { Task { await contentStore.refreshFromNetwork(playlist: playlist) } }.keyboardShortcut("r")
    }
    .frame(width: 0, height: 0).opacity(0).accessibilityHidden(true)
    .disabled(isPlayerCoveringContent)
}

In SearchView add `@FocusState var fieldFocused: Bool`, `.searchFocused($fieldFocused)` and set it when `searchFocusRequest` changes. The `disabled` line keeps the shortcuts from switching tabs behind the fullscreen player. A `CommandMenu` on the `WindowGroup` can come later for the iPadOS 26 menu bar.

**APIs:** View.keyboardShortcut(_:modifiers:) (iOS 14.0+); View.searchFocused(_:) (iOS 18.0+); Scene.commands(content:) / CommandMenu (iOS 14.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** A grep for keyboardShortcut, onKeyPress, .commands, UIKeyCommand and pressesBegan outside PlayerCore finds only Views/PlayerView.swift:1263 (onKeyPress), which leaves Command combinations to the system (PlayerView.swift:1053-1056). Views/DashboardView.swift:46-86, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:26-46 and another_iptv_playerApp.swift:45-47 (a plain WindowGroup with no commands) have no shortcuts. So the absence is real. Not verified: the statement that TabView adds no Cmd-number shortcuts by itself, and whether the system already offers a search or sidebar shortcut on iPadOS 18 or 26; that needs one look at the Command-hold overlay or menu bar. The fix needs three corrections. (1) Cmd-R as written calls PlaylistContentStore.refreshFromNetwork(playlist:) (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:195), the full six-endpoint re-download that replaces local data, whereas pull-to-refresh on each tab deliberately uses the scoped variant (LiveStreamsView.swift:247, VODView.swift:97, SeriesView.swift:98; PlaylistContentStore.swift:210). There is also no re-entry guard, so repeated presses would start parallel syncs. (2) searchFocusRequest does not exist; SearchView takes only playlist and searchText (SearchView.swift:3-5). If the Search tab has not been mounted yet, an onChange on the counter never fires for the first request, and focus set before the field exists is dropped. (3) Hidden background buttons do not populate the iPadOS 26 menu bar; Scene.commands is the native place there. The player audit rated the equivalent player item low (ios-player-airplay-fix-report.md:270).

**Corrected claim:** The app defines no keyboard shortcuts or menu commands outside the player: no tab switching, no jump to search, no refresh. Whether the system TabView or search field supplies any on iPadOS 18 or 26 was not checked.

**Corrected fix:** First hold Command (iOS 18) and open the menu bar (iOS 26) in the iPad simulator to see what the system already provides. Then add the hidden-button block behind the TabView for Cmd-1 to Cmd-4 and Cmd-F in DashboardView (Cmd-1 and Cmd-2 in M3UDashboardView), disabled while isPlayerCoveringContent, using the existing L() keys. For Cmd-F add @State searchFocusRequest in DashboardView, pass it to SearchView, and in SearchView use @FocusState with .searchFocused($focused) driven by .task(id: searchFocusRequest) with a guard for values above 0, so a first request that mounts the tab is still honoured. For Cmd-R either leave it out or make it the scoped refresh of the selected content tab (refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only:)), ignored on Settings and Search and while a refresh is already running; do not bind the full re-download. Follow-up, an owner decision: move the same actions into .commands { CommandMenu(...) } on the WindowGroup, fed through focusedSceneValue, so they appear in the iPadOS 26 menu bar.

**API check:** keyboardShortcut(_ key: KeyEquivalent, modifiers: EventModifiers = .command): @available(iOS 14.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:20949-20953). searchFocused(_ binding: FocusState<Bool>.Binding): @available(iOS 18.0) (5926-5929), so no fallback is needed at the iOS 18 target. Scene.commands(content:): iOS 14.0 (13496-13500); CommandMenu: iOS 14.0 (16664-16667); focusedSceneValue(_:_:) is present (20318). The localization keys dashboard.live, movies, series, settings, search and settings.refresh_all exist (en.lproj/Localizable.strings:73-78, 142).

**Regression risks:** Shortcuts must not fire behind the fullscreen player (the disabled line covers it) or collide with the player's own key handling (it ignores Command combinations, so no clash). A Cmd-R bound to the full sync could start a multi-minute re-download by accident and run concurrently with pull-to-refresh. Adding a parameter to SearchView changes its only call site (DashboardView.swift:79). If the system already supplies tab or search shortcuts, duplicates would appear in the overlay.

**How to verify:** iPad simulator with a hardware keyboard: hold Command before and after and compare the list. UI test: typeKey("2", modifierFlags: .command) selects Movies; Cmd-F selects Search with the field focused, both when the Search tab was never opened and when it was; with the player fullscreen Cmd-2 does nothing; with the mini player docked it switches tabs and playback continues. If Cmd-R ships: pressing it twice starts one refresh.

## ipad-adaptivity-10 — The sidebar offered by .sidebarAdaptable only repeats the five tabs (two for M3U) while Favorites, History, Downloads and the playlist switch stay behind toolbar buttons and Settings

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Dashboard (iPad), M3U dashboard (iPad)
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:48-85, 231-241`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:26-45`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:45-54, 88-97`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Enrich the sidebar with a Library section (Favorites, History, Downloads, playlist switch), or drop the sidebar with .tabBarOnly. Either is defensible; the current state is the weakest of the three.

**What the user perceives:** The sidebar button at the start of the iPad tab pill (shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png) opens a column listing Live TV, Movies, Series, Settings and Search and nothing else. It takes about 320 pt, which drops the poster grid from three columns to two at 834 pt. In the M3U dashboard it lists two rows. In Apple's TV and Music apps the sidebar is where library sections live.

**Mechanism (finder):** DashboardView.swift:48-85 declares five flat `Tab`s and no `TabSection`, sidebar header or customisation; M3UDashboardView.swift:26-45 declares two. Favorites is a toolbar star (DashboardView.swift:233-239), watch history is reachable only from the Continue Watching header, Downloads and 'Back to list' are rows in Settings (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:45-54, 88-97).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Recommended shape, not a plain fix: keep the five tabs and add one sidebar-only section for existing destinations, plus the playlist name as header:

TabSection(L("sidebar.library")) {
    Tab(L("favorites.title"), systemImage: "star", value: DashboardTab.favorites) { NavigationStack { FavoritesView(playlist: playlist) } }
    Tab(L("history.title"), systemImage: "clock.arrow.circlepath", value: DashboardTab.history) { ... }
    Tab(L("download.title"), systemImage: "arrow.down.circle", value: DashboardTab.downloads) { ... }
}
.defaultVisibility(.hidden, for: .tabBar)
...
.tabViewSidebarHeader { Text(playlist.name).font(.headline) }
.tabViewSidebarBottomBar { Button(L("settings.back_to_list"), action: onDismiss) }

The new cases stay non-persisted like Settings and Search (`isPersisted`). Do not model provider categories as sidebar tabs: a panel has hundreds per type and each `Tab` would need its own stack. The cheaper alternative is `.tabViewStyle(.tabBarOnly)`, at least for the two-tab M3U dashboard, which removes a sidebar that adds nothing. All of this is iOS 18 API, so no fallback is needed.

**APIs:** TabSection (iOS 18.0+); TabContent.defaultVisibility(_:for:) (iOS 18.0+ (AdaptableTabBarPlacement .tabBar / .sidebar)); View.tabViewSidebarHeader(content:) / tabViewSidebarBottomBar(content:) (iOS 18.0+); View.tabViewCustomization(_:) / TabContent.customizationID(_:) (iOS 18.0+ (not needed for a fixed set of tabs)); TabViewStyle.tabBarOnly (iOS 18.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The claim matches the code. Views/DashboardView.swift:48-85 declares five flat Tab values with .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable) and no TabSection, header or customization; Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:26-45 declares two. Favorites is a toolbar star per tab (DashboardView.swift:233-239), history is reached only from the Continue Watching header (LiveStreamsView.swift:217, VODView.swift:69, SeriesView.swift:70), and Downloads and 'Back to list' are settings rows (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:46-54, 88-97). shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png shows the sidebar toggle at the start of the tab pill; no screenshot shows the sidebar open. The style has been there since the first commit with no comment, so it is not a recorded decision. Not verified: that the open sidebar pushes content (rather than overlaying it) in portrait and so drops the grid to two columns. The proposed sidebar section is incomplete in three places. (1) A History tab cannot simply reuse WatchHistoryListView: it needs an onPlay closure (WatchHistoryListView.swift:22), and the play logic for live, movies and series lives privately inside each tab's view, so an all-types handler has to be written. (2) WatchHistoryListView hides the tab bar (.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar), line 82); as a tab root that would remove the tab bar on that tab. (3) 'sidebar.library' is a new string needed in all ten Localizable.strings files, which carry the uncommitted tip keys, so touches_user_wip is true for that option (adding keys leaves the tip work intact).

**Corrected claim:** On iPad the sidebar offered by .sidebarAdaptable lists only the same five tabs (two for M3U); Favorites, watch history, Downloads and the playlist switch are not in it. This is a product-shape question, not a defect.

**Corrected fix:** Owner decision between two options. Option A, smallest: switch to .tabViewStyle(.tabBarOnly), at least in M3UDashboardView where the sidebar holds two rows, and optionally in DashboardView; the top tab pill and the iPhone tab bar stay as they are. Option B, enrich: add a sidebar-only TabSection with .defaultVisibility(.hidden, for: .tabBar) for Favorites and Downloads (both already take only a playlist), plus .tabViewSidebarHeader with the playlist name and .tabViewSidebarBottomBar with the 'Back to Playlists' button. Add History only after extracting a shared all-types play handler and making the tab-bar hiding in WatchHistoryListView conditional. Give the new DashboardTab cases raw values above 4 so isPersisted stays false, keep the migration in restoreInitialTab untouched, and add the new section title to all ten languages. Do not model provider categories as tabs.

**API check:** TabSection: @available(iOS 18.0), with init(_ title: S, content:) for a String title (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:16071-16096). TabContent.defaultVisibility(_:for: AdaptableTabBarPlacement...): iOS 18.0 (21747-21751); AdaptableTabBarPlacement has .automatic, .tabBar and .sidebar on iOS (24438-24444). tabViewSidebarHeader, tabViewSidebarFooter and tabViewSidebarBottomBar: iOS 18.0 (14475-14483). TabViewStyle.tabBarOnly and .sidebarAdaptable: iOS 18.0 (13047-13050, 7639-7642). tabViewCustomization and customizationID exist (22750, 4938) and are not needed. Everything is iOS 18, so no fallback.

**Regression risks:** Option B adds three more NavigationStack roots and new selection values. A selected sidebar-only tab has to behave sensibly when the window turns compact (iPhone, Slide Over), where it is hidden from the tab bar. FavoritesView and DownloadsView as tab roots need their titles and the environment from the TabView (they get playerOverlay and posterMetrics there). The tab-bar hiding in WatchHistoryListView would strand the user if reused unchanged. Option A removes the sidebar for anyone who uses it today. The tab persistence logic (DashboardView.swift:190-216) must keep clamping to content tabs.

**How to verify:** iPad simulator, portrait and landscape. Option A: the tab pill has no sidebar toggle and tab state is kept. Option B: the open sidebar shows the Library section, the playlist header and the bottom button; the tab pill and the iPhone tab bar still show five tabs; selecting Favorites and returning to Movies keeps the Movies stack and scroll position; resizing to compact width with Favorites selected leaves a usable tab bar; relaunching restores a content tab, never a sidebar-only one. Also note whether the open sidebar pushes or overlays the grid in portrait.

## ipad-adaptivity-11 — The category jump picker opens as a centred modal sheet on iPad; its medium detent only applies in compact width

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels
- Code: `Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:53-99`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:128-149`, `Views/VODView.swift:123-144`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:124-145`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:84-111`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Popover on iPad (native for a jump list) or keep the modal sheet.

**What the user perceives:** On iPhone the picker is a half-height sheet that leaves the shelves visible. On iPad the same tap dims the whole screen and puts a form sheet in the middle for what is a quick jump list. Apple's iPad apps use a popover from the bar button for this kind of picker.

**Mechanism (finder):** All four screens present `CategoryPickerSheet` with `.sheet(isPresented:)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:139). The sheet asks for `.presentationDetents([.medium, .large])` (CategoryPickerSheet.swift:97); detents apply to edge-attached sheets, and in regular width the sheet is centred, so they have no effect there.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Present it as a popover that adapts to today's sheet in compact width:

Button { showingCategoryPicker = true } label: { ... }
    .popover(isPresented: $showingCategoryPicker) {
        CategoryPickerSheet(...)
            .frame(minWidth: 360, idealWidth: 400, minHeight: 420, idealHeight: 600)
            .presentationCompactAdaptation(.sheet)
    }

The detents inside CategoryPickerSheet keep working when it adapts to a sheet. The popover needs a visible anchor, so do this after the toolbar no longer collapses the button into '...' on iPad (see the two-magnifier finding); if the button stays in the overflow, keep the sheet and add `.presentationSizing(.form)` instead.

**APIs:** View.popover(isPresented:attachmentAnchor:arrowEdge:content:) (iOS 13.0+); View.presentationCompactAdaptation(_:) (iOS 16.4+); View.presentationSizing(_:) with .form (iOS 18.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts check out: all four screens present the picker with `.sheet(isPresented:)` at view level (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:139, Views/VODView.swift:134, Views/SeriesView.swift:135, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:95) and the sheet asks for `.presentationDetents([.medium, .large])` plus a drag indicator (Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:97-98). iPhone rendering matches shots/iphone-dark/L07-live-category-picker.png. No comment or history marks the sheet as a deliberate iPad choice.

What does not stand as written:
1. There is no iPad screenshot of the picker (ipad-light has only L01-L06), so the iPad look is inferred from platform behaviour, not observed. The sub-claim that detents "have no effect" in regular width is not supported by the SDK: UISheetPresentationController.h:60 says a custom detent of 200 gives "200 + safeAreaInsets.bottom when edge-attached, and just 200 when floating", so detents can size a floating sheet. The core point (a centred, dimming modal rather than a bottom half-sheet) is still very likely true.
2. On iPad the jump button is not visible: shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png shows the trailing bar as star, "...", magnifier, so the three other items (guide, all, category list from Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:109-137) sit in the overflow menu. A popover attached to that Button has no anchor there. The finding admits this dependency, so the primary fix is not applicable today.
3. The proposed `.frame(minWidth: 360, ..., minHeight: 420, ...)` is applied outside CategoryPickerSheet and therefore also when the popover adapts to a sheet. A 420 pt minimum exceeds the medium detent on small phones and the whole sheet height in iPhone landscape (iPhone landscape is allowed: project.pbxproj:567), so the NavigationStack would overflow the sheet and push the Close bar out of view.
4. A centred form sheet for a searchable list with swipe-to-hide management is itself a normal iPad pattern; popover versus sheet is a preference, which the finding correctly flags as an owner decision.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad in regular width the category jump picker is presented as a centred modal sheet (reached through the '...' overflow, because the list button is collapsed there), not as the half-height bottom sheet seen on iPhone. This is inferred from code and platform behaviour; no iPad screenshot of the picker exists, and the statement that detents have no effect when floating is unverified. Whether a popover would be better is a product choice, not a defect.

**Corrected fix:** Step 1 (safe, no decision needed): in Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift add `.presentationSizing(.form)` next to `.presentationDetents` (line 97). One line covers all four screens, changes nothing in compact width, and keeps the iPad sheet at the compact form size instead of the larger page size.

Step 2 (owner decision, and only after the list button is a visible bar item on iPad): move the presentation to `.popover(isPresented: $showingCategoryPicker)` on the toolbar Button, with `.frame(idealWidth: 400, idealHeight: 600)` only (no minWidth/minHeight, or apply the frame only when horizontalSizeClass == .regular) and `.presentationCompactAdaptation(.sheet)` inside the popover content. Keep the detents inside CategoryPickerSheet for the adapted iPhone sheet. Leave the onSelect closures unchanged.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `popover<Content>(isPresented:attachmentAnchor:arrowEdge:content:)` at line 12276, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient, unavailable on tvOS/watchOS, usable on iOS 18 (the arrowEdge-optional form forwards to internal overloads marked iOS 18.0). `presentationCompactAdaptation(_:)` line 22150 in an extension marked iOS 16.4; `PresentationAdaptation.sheet` line 22196. `presentationSizing(_:)` line 11033, iOS 18.0; `PresentationSizing.form` line 11007, iOS 18.0. `presentationDetents(_:)` line 22139, iOS 16.0. All usable at the iOS 18.0 deployment target without availability guards.

**Regression risks:** Step 1: none in compact width; on iPad the sheet may become narrower than today. Step 2: with the min frame as originally proposed, the adapted sheet overflows on small or landscape iPhones; a popover attached to a toolbar item that is collapsed into the overflow menu will not present on iPad; the Close button and drag indicator become redundant inside a popover; the popover is dismissed if the toolbar item is rebuilt while it is open. Category hide/unhide swipe actions and the scroll-to-category hand-off must keep working on all four screens.

**How to verify:** iPad simulator, Live TV: open '...' > category list and screenshot before and after Step 1 (sheet width/height, dimming, whether a medium detent is visible). If Step 2 is taken: iPad shows a popover anchored to the list button and dismisses on outside tap; iPhone portrait still matches shots/iphone-dark/L07-live-category-picker.png; iPhone landscape and a small phone show the full Close bar; selecting a category still scrolls the home list on Live, Movies, Series and M3U.

## ipad-adaptivity-12 — The TV guide always uses its compact metrics, so iPad gets the 104 pt channel column that truncates names; the regular variant in the code is never selected

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:35, 131-137, 204-207`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:197-212`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309-310`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:143-157`

**What the user perceives:** On a 1366 pt wide iPad the guide's channel column still leaves about 48 pt for the name, so names break mid-word as they do on the phone ('Busi-ness...', 'Morn-ing U...' in shots/iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png), with more than 1200 pt of timeline beside it.

**Mechanism (finder):** `private let metrics = EPGGuideMetrics(compact: true)` (EPGGuideView.swift:35) and the same literal in the view model (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309). `EPGGuideMetrics.init` defines a regular variant, 172 pt column and 180 pt per hour (EPGComponents.swift:206-212), that no call site uses. The column cell spends 32 pt on the icon, 8 on spacing and 16 on padding (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:144-156).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Widen only the channel column in regular width; it is view-only, so the view model's precomputed cell frames (which depend on `hourWidth` alone) stay valid and the scroll sync is untouched:

@Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) private var hSize
private var metrics: EPGGuideMetrics {
    var m = EPGGuideMetrics(compact: true)
    if hSize == .regular { m.channelColumnWidth = 172 }
    return m
}

`EPGChannelColumnCell` and `EPGChannelRowView` compare `metrics` in their `==`, so they re-render once when the size class changes and not during scroll.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues.horizontalSizeClass (iOS 13.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** `private let metrics = EPGGuideMetrics(compact: true)` (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:35) and the same literal in the view model (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309) are the only two call sites in the app; the regular variant in `EPGGuideMetrics.init` (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:206-212, 172 pt column, 180 pt/hour) is never selected. No view outside the player reads horizontalSizeClass. The literal has been there since the file was created (commit 1cce013) and no comment marks it as deliberate.

The arithmetic holds: the column cell uses a 32 pt icon, 8 pt spacing and 2 x 8 pt padding inside 104 pt (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:144-156), leaving 48 pt for a two-line caption. shots/iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows the result: "Busi-ness...", "Morn-ing U...", "Foot-ball L...", "Cine-ma C...". The same code runs on iPad, so the same truncation appears beside a very wide timeline.

The fix is sound. The view model uses only `hourWidth` and `dayWidth` (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:310-312, 324), so widening the column in the view does not invalidate precomputed cell frames. Scroll sync stays consistent at any column width: body content is column + dayWidth (EPGGuideView.swift:229) in the full viewport, the axis is dayWidth in viewport minus column (EPGGuideView.swift:133-136), so both have the same maximum offset. Both now-lines derive from the same x after the column (EPGGuideView.swift:151-156, 219-223). The Equatable cells include `metrics` in `==` (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:12-16, 139-141), so they re-render only when the size class changes, not during scroll.

**Corrected claim:** The TV guide always uses its compact metrics, so iPad (and any regular-width window) gets the 104 pt channel column with about 48 pt for the name, which hyphenates and truncates channel names as on the phone; the regular variant defined in EPGGuideMetrics is never selected.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: in Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift replace the stored `metrics` with a computed property that starts from `EPGGuideMetrics(compact: true)` and sets `channelColumnWidth = 172` when `@Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass)` is `.regular`. Keep `hourWidth` at the compact value in both the view and the view model (add a one-line English comment saying they must stay in sync), and do not switch to `compact: false` unless the view model is passed the same metrics.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface line 17118: `EnvironmentValues.horizontalSizeClass: UserInterfaceSizeClass?`, @available(iOS 13.0, ...). `EPGGuideMetrics.channelColumnWidth` is a `var` (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:200), so the mutation compiles. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** Low. The column also widens on Max-size iPhones in landscape (regular width), which is acceptable. Crossing the compact/regular boundary while resizing an iPad window re-renders the visible rows once. The earlier performance work (Equatable row and column cells, off-main layout precompute, single two-axis scroller, one-directional scroll sync) is untouched as long as hourWidth is not changed in the view alone.

**How to verify:** iPad simulator, TV Guide in portrait and landscape: channel names fit on one or two lines without mid-word breaks; after scrolling horizontally, the axis now-line and the row now-lines sit on the same x and the hour labels line up with the programme cells; scrolling to the far right ends at the same point in axis and body. Resize the window to compact width and confirm the column returns to 104 pt. iPhone portrait unchanged against shots/iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png.

## ipad-adaptivity-13 — In iPhone landscape the horizontal shelves are probably clipped at the safe-area edges instead of running to the screen edges

- Verdict: **undecidable** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels, Continue watching shelf
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397`, `Views/VODView.swift:331-350, 448-467`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:308, 420`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:46-57`

**What the user perceives:** Holding an iPhone sideways, shelf cards should be cut off about 62 pt before each screen edge, level with the Dynamic Island inset, leaving blank bands left and right; in Apple's TV app and App Store the cards slide under those bands to the physical edge. This is derived from the code; there is no landscape screenshot.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each shelf is a `ScrollView(.horizontal)` nested in the tab's vertical `ScrollView` (LiveStreamsView.swift:212, 382). The vertical scroll view lays its content out inside the horizontal safe area, so the nested scroller's frame, and with it its clip rectangle, ends at the safe-area inset. No shelf uses `scrollClipDisabled` or ignores the horizontal safe area. The rest of the landscape layout is fine: the scale stays 0.5 (short side), a movie shelf is 182 pt tall and the grids give 6 poster or 7 channel columns.

**Proposed fix (finder):** First confirm with a landscape screenshot. If confirmed, add `.scrollClipDisabled()` to the shelf scroll views (the outer vertical scroll view still clips at the screen edge). Watch for one side effect of lazy stacks: a card may be removed as soon as it leaves the inner scroll view's bounds, which would show as a pop-out inside the band; if that happens, extend the shelf into the safe area instead with `.padding(.horizontal, -safeInset)` plus matching content padding, taking the insets from an `onGeometryChange` on the outer scroll view.

**APIs:** View.scrollClipDisabled(_:) (iOS 17.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** The structure is as described: each shelf is a `ScrollView(.horizontal)` with a LazyHStack padded 16 pt, nested in the tab's vertical ScrollView (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:212, 382-397; Views/VODView.swift:331-350, 448-467; Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:46-57; Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:363). No shelf uses scrollClipDisabled, contentMargins, safeAreaPadding or a horizontal ignoresSafeArea (grep over Views found only top-edge and keyboard uses). iPhone landscape is reachable outside the player: project.pbxproj:567 lists both landscape orientations for iPhone and `AppDelegate.orientationLock` defaults to `.allButUpsideDown` (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:5). The side numbers also check out (PosterMetrics scale clamps to 0.5 on the short side, shelf height 150 + 32 = 182).

Whether the cards are actually cut at the safe-area edge depends on how SwiftUI lays out the vertical ScrollView's content on the cross axis and whether the nested scroller's frame stops at the inset. That is likely, but it cannot be read from this code, and there is no landscape screenshot in any variant. The finding itself says "probably" and "needs-simulator-run". The reference to Apple's TV app and App Store is weak evidence: to my knowledge those do not rotate their browsing UI on iPhone.

The primary fix is doubtful. `.scrollClipDisabled()` only stops clipping; the inner scroll view's frame, and with it its hit-testing area, still ends at the safe-area inset, so cards drawn in the bands would be visible but not tappable or draggable. The shelves use LazyHStack, which may drop cards once they leave the scroll view's bounds, giving pop-out in the band (the finding concedes this).

**Corrected claim:** On iPhone in landscape the horizontal shelves may be clipped at the horizontal safe-area insets (about 62 pt on each side on iPhone 17 Pro), leaving empty bands instead of cards scrolling to the screen edge. Unverified; needs a landscape screenshot.

**Corrected fix:** Confirm with a landscape screenshot first. If confirmed, extend the shelf scroller's frame rather than only disabling its clip:
A. Try `.ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .horizontal)` on each shelf ScrollView; if it takes effect inside the vertical scroll content, the horizontal scroller should inset its own content by the safe area, so the first card stays aligned with the shelf title and cards scroll to the physical edge.
B. If A has no effect: read the horizontal safe-area insets once on the outer vertical ScrollView with `onGeometryChange`, pass them to the shelves through an environment value (as posterMetrics is, so the `.equatable()` shelf rows keep working without changing their `==`), and apply `.padding(.horizontal, -inset)` to the shelf ScrollView plus `.contentMargins(.horizontal, inset, for: .scrollContent)`.
Do not ship `.scrollClipDisabled()` alone.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface line 12496: `scrollClipDisabled(_ disabled: Bool = true)`, iOS 17.0. Line 4238: `contentMargins(_ edges: Edge.Set = .all, _ length: CGFloat?, for placement: ContentMarginPlacement = .automatic)`, iOS 17.0. SwiftUICore.swiftinterface line 16817: `ignoresSafeArea(_ regions: SafeAreaRegions = .all, edges: Edge.Set = .all)`, iOS 14.0. Line 6067: `onGeometryChange(for:of:action:)`, extension marked iOS 16.0 (back-deployed, T must be Equatable and Sendable). Line 19159: `safeAreaPadding(_:_:)`, iOS 17.0. All usable at iOS 18.0 without guards.

**Regression risks:** scrollClipDisabled alone: dead touch zone over visible cards in the bands, lazy pop-out, and titles can paint over neighbouring shelves because vertical clipping is also off. Option B: passing the inset as a stored property would defeat the Equatable shelf rows unless it goes through the environment; negative padding must be zero in portrait and on iPad so the current layout (shots/iphone-dark/M01-movies-home.png, shots/ipad-light/L01-live-home.png) is unchanged. Touches five shelf implementations, so the continue-watching row and M3U shelves must be changed consistently.

**How to verify:** iPhone 17 Pro simulator, landscape, Movies home with a shelf of 10+ items scrolled halfway: measure the x of the leftmost and rightmost visible poster pixels. If they stop at about 62 pt and screen width minus 62 pt with empty bands, the claim holds. After the fix: posters reach the physical edges, the first card at rest lines up with the shelf title, a card in the band can be tapped and dragged, no card appears or vanishes abruptly inside the band during a slow scroll, and portrait plus iPad layouts are pixel-identical to before. Repeat on Live TV, Series, M3U channels and the continue-watching row.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-1 — Stepping to the next episode from the series detail re-runs present(), so a docked mini card jumps to fullscreen, the keyboard is dismissed and the download warning is asked again (twice in a row on the first episode).

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail, Any screen browsed with the mini card docked, Search (keyboard up), Download-warning alert
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:899-939, 1121-1165`, `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:29-57`, `Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:144-186 (contrast: in-place switch)`

**What the user perceives:** An episode started from the series detail is minimised and the user browses or types a search. When the episode ends (5 s auto-advance) or Next is pressed on the lock screen, the card takes over the whole screen and the keyboard drops. The same episode chain started from Continue Watching stays docked. While a download is running, tapping an episode shows the 'download in progress' alert, and right after 'Continue' the same alert appears again over the playing player; every following episode asks again.

**Mechanism (finder):** SeriesDetailView has no shell: it changes the episode by calling playerOverlay.present() again (SeriesView.swift:916, reached from selectAdjacentEpisode at 1147-1165 and from loadEpisodeNeighbors at 1138-1143, which re-presents the same episode only to refresh the prev/next flags). present() is written for a user tap: it resigns the first responder (PlayerOverlayController.swift:39-41), re-evaluates hasActiveDownload and parks the item in pendingPresentation (43-49), and forces mode = .fullscreen (54). The player's auto-advance and remote commands call onNextEpisode with no mini check (PlayerView.swift:1528-1534, reference only). Double alert: confirmPending mounts the player, its .task(id: ep.id) (SeriesView.swift:935-937) finds neighbours, neighborsChanged is true, present() runs again and shouldWarn is still true. 'Cancel' on that second alert leaves the first presentation, which was built with canGoToNextEpisode == false (929-930), so Next and auto-advance are dead. LivePlayerShell (LiveStreamsView.swift:1123-1144), VODPlayerShell (VODView.swift:935-958) and HistorySeriesPlayerShell switch in place and do not have this problem. The re-present pattern predates the mini player (git log -S'neighborsChanged': d2489f9; mini mode arrived in 1cce013).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Overlay boundary plus the browse call site, no player change. Add a continuation entry point to PlayerOverlayController:

@MainActor func replaceContent<Content: View>(onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) {
    guard presentation != nil else { return }   // player was closed meanwhile: do not reopen
    presentation = PlayerOverlayPresentation(root: AnyView(content()), onDismiss: onDismiss)
    // mode, first responder and the download prompt are left alone
}

In SeriesDetailView give presentEpisodeOverlay(ep:history:localOverrideURL:) an isContinuation flag; selectAdjacentEpisode (1162) and the neighbour refresh (1142) pass true and call replaceContent, the user taps (1062, 1078, 1095) keep present(). Same root type, so PlayerView identity and AirPlay continuity are unchanged.

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read the code. SeriesDetailView has no shell: every episode change goes through playerOverlay.present() at Views/SeriesView.swift:916, reached from selectAdjacentEpisode (1147-1165) and from loadEpisodeNeighbors (1138-1143), which re-presents the SAME episode only to refresh the prev/next flags captured at 929-930. present() (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:29-57) unconditionally resigns first responder (39-41), re-evaluates DownloadManager.hasActiveDownload (43-47), parks the item in pendingPresentation when it warns (49) and otherwise forces mode = .fullscreen (54). The player calls onNextEpisode with no mini check: auto-advance fires on player.state == .ended (Views/PlayerView.swift:1412-1418, 1528-1534) and the remote command is wired at 1546-1554. Auto-advance is ON by default (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:39, PlaylistSettingsView.swift:31), so this is the normal path, not an edge case. Double alert traced: first tap -> pending -> confirmPending (59-64) mounts the player -> .task(id: ep.id) (SeriesView.swift:935-937) -> neighborsChanged true (nav state starts nil, 807-808) -> presentEpisodeOverlay -> present() -> hasActiveDownload still true -> second alert over the playing player; Cancel there keeps the first package built with canGoToNextEpisode == false. HistorySeriesPlayerShell.jumpTo (Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:144-186) mutates @State session in place and never touches the controller, so the same chain from Continue Watching stays docked and never re-asks: the inconsistency is real. Not deliberate for this path: the comment at PlayerOverlayController.swift:51 ('A new stream always opens fullscreen') is about a user pick; the re-present pattern predates mini mode (git log -S'neighborsChanged' -> d2489f9; PlayerOverlayMode arrives in 1cce013). The earlier audit (ios-player-airplay-review.md:1815-1819) only decided where the resign goes for user taps. I also checked that the fix does not re-steal focus in mini: PlayerView's onChange(of: overlayPresentationID) (1308-1332) calls claimHardwareKeyboardFocus, which is guarded by acceptsHardwareKeys = !isMiniCommitted && ... (1036-1047), so a docked card leaves the search field alone.

**Corrected claim:** Stands as stated: stepping episodes from the series detail (auto-advance, in-player Next/Previous, lock-screen Next) re-runs PlayerOverlayController.present(), so a docked mini card jumps to fullscreen, the keyboard is dismissed, and while a download is active the warning is asked again on every step and twice in a row on the first episode (when the episode has neighbours). Auto-advance is on by default, so this hits the ordinary binge flow.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two small hardenings. Add to PlayerOverlayController: @MainActor func replaceContent<Content: View>(onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) { guard presentation != nil else { return }; presentation = PlayerOverlayPresentation(root: AnyView(content()), onDismiss: onDismiss) } - no resign, no download check, mode untouched. In SeriesDetailView add an isContinuation flag to presentEpisodeOverlay; selectAdjacentEpisode (1162) and the neighbour refresh (1142) pass true, user taps (1062, 1078, 1095) keep present(). Hardenings: (a) the two continuation paths hop through async work (DB read at 1152, localURL at 901), so capture playerOverlay.presentation?.id before the hop and skip replaceContent if it changed (otherwise a late completion can overwrite an item the user picked in between; the same race exists today with present()); (b) keep the new presentation id on replace (as proposed) - PlayerView relies on the id change to adopt the new item (PlayerView.swift:1308-1318).

**API check:** No SDK API involved; only app types (PlayerOverlayController, PlayerOverlayPresentation). The fix compiles against the existing structure: same root type (PlayerView + .task(id:)) inside AnyView, so PlayerView identity and its StateObject are preserved exactly as with present() today.

**Regression risks:** 1) Next/auto-advance no longer shows the download warning; if the first episode was a local file (skipDownloadCheck) and the next one streams remotely while a download runs, the connection-limit warning is skipped - this matches what HistorySeriesPlayerShell already does, but say so to the owner. 2) Must not change present() itself: the unconditional resign and fullscreen reset there are deliberate (PlayerOverlayController.swift:35-38, 51-54). 3) Do not touch PlayerView.

**How to verify:** Unit test on PlayerOverlayController: present -> minimize -> replaceContent keeps mode == .mini, pendingPresentation == nil and changes presentation.id; replaceContent with presentation == nil is a no-op. Simulator: series detail -> play episode -> minimise -> focus Search field -> seek near the end with auto-advance on: card stays docked, keyboard stays up, next episode plays. With an active download on the playlist: tap an episode -> exactly one alert; after Continue the Next button is enabled within a moment and stepping asks nothing.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-2 — No scroll view reserves space for the docked mini card, so the end of every grid and list sits under it and taps there expand the player.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home and category grids, All Channels / All Movies / All Series, Favorites, History, Search results, Downloads, M3U channels, Movie and series detail
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:47-123`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:25-82`, `Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:471-541 (geometry, read only)`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:212, 600`, `Views/VODView.swift:64, 689`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:65, 647, 959`, `Views/SearchView.swift:149`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:106, 131, 157`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:65`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:153, 577`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:79`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: The controller does not know which corner the card is docked in, so the clearance (about 120 pt of extra scroll room at the end) would also apply while the card is docked at a top corner. Accept that, or have the player report its docked edge to the controller.

**What the user perceives:** With the card docked (default bottom-trailing, 193 x 109 pt on iPhone 17 Pro) the last row of a grid can only be scrolled to just above the tab bar, exactly where the card is: the right-hand items of the last row stay hidden, and a tap on them expands the player instead of opening the item. In Search with the keyboard up the card covers the trailing half of the last two visible result rows. The only way out is to drag the card to another corner.

**Mechanism (finder):** The overlay is a ZStack sibling of the TabView (DashboardView.swift:92-122) and nothing on the browse side knows about it: grep over the browse views finds no safeAreaInset, safeAreaPadding or contentMargins (the only hit is the tip jar). The card rests 49 + 12 pt above the container bottom (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:473-478, 534; PlayerView.swift:1954 reference), i.e. y 670-779 pt on a 874 pt screen, while list content ends at the tab bar top (about 792 pt, measured in iphone-light/L01-live-home.png) or at the home indicator on pushed screens that hide the tab bar (iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png).

**Proposed fix (finder):** One browse-side modifier in Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift, applied to the vertical ScrollView / List of each screen listed above:

struct MiniPlayerScrollClearance: ViewModifier {
    @EnvironmentObject private var overlay: PlayerOverlayController
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let docked = overlay.presentation != nil && overlay.mode == .mini
        content.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom, spacing: 0) {
            Color.clear.frame(height: docked ? Self.clearance : 0).allowsHitTesting(false)
        }
    }
    static var clearance: CGFloat { MiniPlayerMetrics.cardWidth(container: UIScreen.main.bounds.size) * 9 / 16 + MiniPlayerMetrics.margin }
}

The inset view is always present (height 0 when not docked) so the scroll view keeps its identity and offset. Applied to the vertical scroller only, the horizontal shelves inside are untouched and the Equatable rows are not invalidated. The Downloads sheet already receives the environment object (DashboardView.swift:182). tabViewBottomAccessory (iOS 26) is the system slot for a now-playing bar but cannot host this card, which is the player view itself; not proposed.

**APIs:** View.safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 15 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19082, no newer availability attribute)); View.tabViewBottomAccessory(content:) (iOS 26 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13709); checked, not proposed)

**Verifier reasons:** The geometry is real: grep over the browse views finds no safeAreaInset / safeAreaPadding / contentMargins except Views/Components/TipJarView.swift:100, and the overlay is a ZStack sibling above the TabView (Views/DashboardView.swift:47-123). The card rests tabBarAllowance(49) + margin(12) above the container bottom on compact widths regardless of whether the tab bar is showing (Views/PlayerView.swift:1948-1967, Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:471-478, 520-541). But two things in the finding do not hold up. (1) 'Native' framing: the card is explicitly modelled on system PiP ('hugs the picture like system PiP', MiniPlayerSupport.swift:466-468) and is draggable to any of four corners (MiniPlayerCorner, PlayerView.swift:2099-2110). System PiP also covers content and no Apple app insets its scroll views for it; moving the window is the native answer. So this is a product decision, not a defect, and lower severity. (2) The proposed clearance is wrong on exactly the screens it names. clearance = cardWidth*9/16 + 12 = ~121 pt only clears the card on tab-root screens where the tab bar already contributes ~49 pt of bottom safe area. All Channels, category grids, All Movies/Series, M3U group grids, EPG and M3U favorites hide the tab bar (.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar): LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722; VODView.swift:380, 563, 822; SeriesView.swift:357, 535; M3UChannelsView.swift:502; M3UFavoritesView.swift:63; confirmed by shots/iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png), while the card still floats 61 pt above the bottom, so the last row would remain ~49 pt under the card. The card height is also not 16:9: it follows the video aspect clamped to 0.62-2.4 and maxHeight (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:509-518), so a 4:3 or portrait stream needs more clearance, and the height changes on every zap. The effort is also not S: about 15 scroll hosts plus Settings and the EPG guide, which the list omits.

**Corrected claim:** While the mini card is docked at a bottom corner, the trailing (or leading) items of the last row of any grid/list end up under it and a tap there expands the player; the user has to drag the card to another corner, exactly as with system PiP. Real but minor, and a product decision rather than a native-feel defect. On pushed screens that hide the tab bar the card additionally floats 61 pt above the bottom edge.

**Corrected fix:** Owner decision first: keep PiP semantics (do nothing) or reserve end-of-scroll room. If reserving: the browse side cannot compute the clearance from MiniPlayerMetrics alone (unknown video aspect, corner, and tab-bar visibility). Have the overlay boundary publish the docked card's frame (global space, nil when not docked or docked at a top corner) - e.g. a CGRect? on PlayerOverlayController written by the player, one additive line in the out-of-scope player file - and let the shared modifier compute clearance per scroll view as max(0, scrollViewSafeAreaBottomGlobalY - card.minY + margin) using onGeometryChange (iOS 16+ back-deployed) and apply it with safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom, spacing: 0) { Color.clear.frame(height: clearance) } on the vertical scroller only. Without the player reporting its frame, the fallback is a constant that adds MiniPlayerMetrics.tabBarAllowance on screens that hide the tab bar and accepts being wrong for non-16:9 streams. Do not use contentMargins(.bottom, for: .scrollContent): it propagates to the nested horizontal shelves.

**API check:** View.safeAreaInset(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment:spacing:content:) found at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19082, @inlinable, no iOS availability newer than the extension (iOS 15). View.safeAreaPadding(_:_:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19159, iOS 17. View.contentMargins(_:_:for:) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4238, iOS 17 (not recommended here). View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6067/6078 (back-deployed, usable on iOS 18). View.tabViewBottomAccessory(content:) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13709, iOS 26 only - correctly not proposed. View.safeAreaBar(edge:...) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17362 is iOS 26 only and not needed.

**Regression risks:** A bottom safe-area change on dock/undock re-lays out every lazy grid once and, when the user is scrolled to the end, shifts content under the finger; it also moves anything centred in the safe area (empty states, ProgressViews) if the modifier is applied to a container instead of the scroller. Observing PlayerOverlayController in a modifier on every screen re-runs that modifier body on every presentation/mode change (cheap, content is opaque, Equatable rows untouched). With the constant from the finding the fix silently under-clears on tab-bar-hidden screens. Must not edit PlayerView beyond a single additive line, and only with the owner's agreement.

**How to verify:** Simulator, card docked bottom-trailing: (a) Live TV home, (b) All Channels (tab bar hidden), (c) Search results with keyboard up; scroll to the end and compare the last cell's frame with the miniPlayer.expand element's frame - they must not intersect in all three. Repeat with a 4:3 stream. With no player open, screenshots must be pixel-identical to today. Check that docking/undocking while scrolled to the end does not jump.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-3 — Episode rows and Continue Watching cards start playback through onTapGesture: the episode thumbnail is not tappable at all and neither shows a pressed state.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail (episode list), Continue Watching shelf on Live TV, Movies, Series and M3U home
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:1390-1451`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201 (the same card done right, as a Button)`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping an episode's thumbnail, the most obvious play target, does nothing; only the text column next to it starts playback. Where the tap does land there is no highlight, and the overlay appears one async hop later (local-file lookup), so the tap reads as dead for a moment. Continue Watching cards behave the same way, while the identical card in the full history grid dims on press.

**Mechanism (finder):** EpisodeDetailRow attaches .contentShape + .onTapGesture to the text VStack only (SeriesView.swift:1447-1451); the thumbnail ZStack (1391-1414) carries no gesture. ContinueWatchingRow wraps HistoryCard in .onTapGesture (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52). A tap gesture has no pressed state and no button trait. The hand-off after the tap is async: presentEpisodeOverlay awaits DownloadManager.localURL (SeriesView.swift:899-908), so nothing visible happens in the frame of the tap.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make both real buttons with the plain style, as WatchHistoryListView.swift:159 already does.

// EpisodeDetailRow
HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
    Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } label: {
        HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { thumbnail; textColumn }.contentShape(Rectangle())
    }
    .buttonStyle(.plain)
    if let remoteURL { DownloadButton(...) }   // stays outside the row button
}

// ContinueWatchingRow
Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item) }.buttonStyle(.plain)

**APIs:** PlainButtonStyle / .buttonStyle(.plain) (iOS 13 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8850))

**Verifier reasons:** EpisodeDetailRow (Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1474): the thumbnail ZStack (1391-1414) has no gesture; .contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture sits on the text VStack only (1447-1451); nothing in EpisodesPanel (1318-1333) wraps the row in a button. So a tap on the episode thumbnail does nothing. History shows this is an accidental regression, not a choice: before d2489f9 the whole row was 'Button(action: { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) }) { HStack ... }.contentShape(Rectangle())'; d2489f9 added DownloadButton to the row and replaced the Button by a tap gesture on the text column (diff saved at scratchpad/agents/series_d2489f9.diff, lines 416-438), dropping the thumbnail from the hit area. ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-52 uses HistoryCard(item:).onTapGesture - no pressed state, no button trait, and no contentShape so the 8 pt gap between image and title is dead; the same card in the full history grid is a plain-style Button (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201). ContinueWatchingRow is used on Live, Movies, Series and M3U home (LiveStreamsView.swift:213, VODView.swift:65, SeriesView.swift:66, M3UChannelsView.swift:157). No UI test references these rows (grep of another-iptv-playerUITests). The 'async hop' remark (SeriesView.swift:899-908) is true but is a single actor hop and not perceptible by itself; the missing pressed state is what makes the tap feel dead.

**Corrected claim:** Stands: the episode thumbnail is not tappable (regression from d2489f9, where the row Button was replaced by a tap gesture on the text column when the download button was added), and neither episode rows nor Continue Watching cards show a pressed state or expose a button trait.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed. EpisodeDetailRow: outer HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } label: { HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { thumbnail; textColumn }.contentShape(Rectangle()) }.buttonStyle(.plain); if let remoteURL { DownloadButton(...) } } - keep the existing .padding on the outer HStack and keep .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading) on the text column so the download button stays pinned right. ContinueWatchingRow: Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item).contentShape(Rectangle()) }.buttonStyle(.plain).

**API check:** PlainButtonStyle / .buttonStyle(.plain): iOS 13, already used in this code base (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:43, WatchHistoryListView.swift:200). No new API.

**Regression risks:** The DownloadButton must stay a sibling of the row button, not inside its label, or its taps are swallowed. The row becomes one accessibility element (title + meta combined); fine, but any future UI test must query buttons, not staticTexts. Plain style keeps foreground styles, so the green 'Watched' and accent 'remaining' labels are unchanged. No interaction with the Equatable shelf rows (ContinueWatchingRow is its own @Query view).

**How to verify:** Simulator: series detail -> tap the centre of an episode thumbnail -> player opens; press and hold a row -> it dims; tap the download button -> download starts and the player does not open. Continue Watching card on each of the four home screens dims on press and plays on tap; horizontal scrolling that starts on a card still scrolls. XCUITest: episode row and card are .button elements.
