## player-handoff-miniplayer-4 — The catalog is laid out again in landscape underneath the fullscreen player, so a deep-scrolled channel grid can come back at a different position after watching in landscape.

- Verdict: **undecidable** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live category grid, All Channels, Favorites (Live), M3U group grid, M3U favorites
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:36-38, 47-123`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:597-613`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:573-591`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:28-33, 106-122`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:5-10`, `Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:714-732 (orientation lock, read only)`

**What the user perceives:** The user scrolls far down a channel grid, taps a channel, watches in landscape (rotating the phone or using the player's rotate button) and comes back: the grid is no longer where it was left, typically somewhere around the middle of the loaded rows. A system full-screen presentation would not do this, because the presenting screen is not laid out while it is covered.

**Mechanism (finder):** The player is an in-window overlay, so the TabView stays mounted and visible to layout (DashboardView.swift:48-122). Any rotation, including the process-wide forced landscape (AppDelegate.orientationLock, MiniPlayerSupport.swift:714-720), resizes the selected tab. Live grids use GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:)) with poster metrics fixed to the portrait screen (DashboardView.swift:38), so the column count roughly doubles in landscape, the content height halves, and an offset beyond the shorter content has to be clamped; rotating back does not restore it. Movie and series grids are not affected (the player opens from a pushed detail, the grid below is not in the hierarchy), shelves are not affected (row heights do not depend on width). The double relayout is certain from the code; the clamped offset has to be confirmed in the simulator before fixing. The demo catalog (13 channels) is too small to show it.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Browse side, one shared modifier on the grid scroll views (LiveCategoryContent, M3UGroupGridContent, the live grid in FavoritesView): remember offset and width while the catalog is uncovered, restore when the player uncovers it and the width is back.

struct KeepsOffsetAcrossPlayer: ViewModifier {
    @EnvironmentObject private var overlay: PlayerOverlayController
    @State private var position = ScrollPosition()
    @State private var box = OffsetBox()          // final class, never observed
    private var covered: Bool { overlay.presentation != nil && overlay.mode == .fullscreen }
    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.scrollPosition($position)
            .onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGPoint.self, of: { CGPoint(x: $0.containerSize.width, y: $0.contentOffset.y) }) { _, v in
                if covered { return }
                if let y = box.restoreY { if v.x == box.width { box.restoreY = nil; position.scrollTo(y: y) } }
                else { box.width = v.x; box.y = v.y }
            }
            .onChange(of: covered) { _, c in if c { box.restoreY = box.y } }
    }
}

The modifier's body does not re-evaluate the grid (content is opaque), and the per-frame callback only writes a reference box. Alternative, larger: freeze the TabView's frame while the fullscreen player covers it; rejected for now because the forced landscape is released 0.45 s after minimise (PlayerView.swift:1448-1452), which would show a portrait-sized catalog in a landscape window.

**APIs:** ScrollPosition, View.scrollPosition(_:anchor:), ScrollPosition.scrollTo(y:) (iOS 18 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:682-688; SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22734); already used in Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift); View.onScrollGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 18 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13689))

**Verifier reasons:** What the code proves: the player is an in-window overlay, the TabView stays mounted and laid out (Views/DashboardView.swift:47-123), the catalog is allowed to rotate (PlayerOrientationLock.defaultMask = .allButUpsideDown, Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:714-732), and live grids use GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: posterMetrics.liveGridIconSize)) with display-fixed metrics (LiveStreamsView.swift:597-613, M3UChannelsView.swift:573-576, FavoritesView.swift:28-33; PosterMetrics.swift uses the short side, so the metric is orientation-independent by design, DashboardView.swift:36-38). On iPhone 17 Pro that is scale 0.5 -> 90 pt cells + 8 pt spacing: 3 columns in portrait (matches shots/iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png) and about 7 in landscape, so content height drops to roughly 43 % and any offset deeper than that cannot be kept. What the code does not prove: that SwiftUI's ScrollView + LazyVGrid clamps the offset under the covered player and then keeps the clamped offset when the width returns. That is framework behaviour I cannot derive from source; the finding itself marks it needs-simulator-run and the 13-channel demo fixture cannot show it. Separately, the proposed modifier has a logic flaw: restore only happens inside onScrollGeometryChange, which fires only when width or offset changes. In the most common flow (rotate back to portrait first, then minimise/close) the width is already back while covered (callbacks ignored), nothing changes on uncover, restoreY stays armed, and the first later scroll tick calls position.scrollTo(y:) and yanks the grid mid-gesture. In the no-rotation case restoreY is also left armed and fires a programmatic scrollTo on the user's next drag.

**Corrected claim:** The live/M3U channel grids are re-laid out in landscape (3 -> ~7 columns on an iPhone) underneath the fullscreen player. Whether that loses a deep scroll position on return is plausible (content shrinks to ~43 %) but unproven; it needs a simulator run with a large category before any fix is written.

**Corrected fix:** none until measured. If the loss is reproduced, use the modifier with these corrections: track width even while covered (box.currentWidth updated in every callback); in onChange(of: covered) handle BOTH edges - on cover: box.savedY = box.y, box.savedWidth = box.width; on uncover: if box.currentWidth == box.savedWidth { if current y != savedY { position.scrollTo(y: savedY) }; clear savedY } else keep savedY armed and restore from the geometry callback when width == savedWidth (covers the forced-landscape release 0.45 s after minimise, PlayerView.swift:1448-1452); always clear savedY once restored or once the user scrolls with the width unchanged, so a programmatic scrollTo never fires during a drag. Apply only to LiveCategoryContent, M3UGroupGridContent and the live grid in FavoritesView.

**API check:** public struct ScrollPosition at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:688 (iOS 18); mutating func scrollTo(y: CGFloat) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:734 (iOS 18); View.scrollPosition(_ position: Binding<ScrollPosition>, anchor: UnitPoint? = nil) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22734 (iOS 18); View.onScrollGeometryChange(for:of:action:) at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13689 (iOS 18). All available at the deployment target, no gate needed. The code base already binds scroll positions in Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:138, 180; the three target grids use neither scrollPosition nor ScrollViewReader, so there is no conflict.

**Regression risks:** A scrollPosition binding on the paginated grids adds a state write per user scroll gesture (modifier body only, grid content opaque) - acceptable, but the armed-restore bug above would produce a visible jump on the first scroll after every playback if shipped as written. scrollTo(y:) on a lazy grid depends on visibleCount still covering that offset (it is @State and survives, LiveStreamsView.swift:602-609). In landscape under the player the grid's onAppear pagination can load extra pages; harmless. Must not change PosterMetrics or the adaptive columns (deliberate).

**How to verify:** Simulator, fixture with >= 300 channels in one category, iPhone portrait: open the category grid, scroll to ~80 %, record the label of the first hittable cell and the scroll view's contentOffset.y; tap a channel; (A) rotate device to landscape and back, then minimise; (B) use the player's rotate button, then minimise (forced landscape released 0.45 s later); (C) no rotation. After each, record the first hittable cell and offset again. The claim holds if A or B differ from the recorded cell while C does not. Also record whether the offset is clamped while covered (debug print from onScrollGeometryChange). Repeat on an iPad (smaller column ratio).

## player-handoff-miniplayer-5 — Nothing in the catalog marks the channel or title that is currently playing in the docked card.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV shelves and grids, EPG guide channel column, Search results, M3U channels, Favorites
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:408-446`, `Views/SearchView.swift:309-326`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:48-123`, `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:17-23`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: New visible element: does the owner want a now-playing badge on tiles, and is one additive .preference line in PlayerView acceptable, or should the less exact watch-history derivation be used to keep the player file untouched?

**What the user perceives:** With a channel playing in the mini card, the channel's own tile looks like every other tile. The user cannot see where 'what is on' sits in the list they are scrolling, and re-tapping it is a guess. Music and Podcasts mark the playing row; a TV grid with a live picture in the corner invites the same expectation.

**Mechanism (finder):** PlayerOverlayPresentation carries only an AnyView and a UUID (PlayerOverlayController.swift:5-9); the identity of the playing item lives inside the shells and changes there on zap, so the browse side has nothing to compare against. LiveStreamCard, M3UChannelCard and ResultRow take no playing state.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Boundary value plus card badge. Define NowPlayingKey { type, streamId } and a PreferenceKey in PlayerOverlayController.swift. DashboardView / M3UDashboardView read it from the overlay content and hand it to the tabs as an environment value:

item.root.onPreferenceChange(NowPlayingPreference.self) { nowPlaying = $0 }
TabView { ... }.environment(\.nowPlaying, playerOverlay.presentation == nil ? nil : nowPlaying)

Cards read the environment key (only views that read it re-evaluate, and only when the playing item changes; the Equatable shelf rows stay skipped):

@Environment(\.nowPlaying) private var nowPlaying
let isPlaying = nowPlaying == NowPlayingKey(type: "live", streamId: String(stream.streamId))
CachedImage(...).overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {
    if isPlaying { Image(systemName: "waveform").symbolEffect(.variableColor.iterative).padding(6).background(.thinMaterial, in: Circle()) }
}
.accessibilityAddTraits(isPlaying ? .isSelected : [])

The value has to be published where the playing item is known: one additive line on PlayerView's root, .preference(key: NowPlayingPreference.self, value: suppressWatchHistory ? nil : NowPlayingKey(type: type, streamId: streamId)). That file is otherwise out of scope, hence the decision below. Alternative with zero player edits: derive the key in DashboardView from the newest DBWatchHistory row while a presentation exists (live rows are written when the channel first plays, PlayerView.swift:1687-1694); less exact for films (up to 10 s late) and it needs a mapped request so the 10 s progress writes do not re-publish.

**APIs:** View.preference(key:value:) / onPreferenceChange(_:perform:) (iOS 13 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:9972, 14677)); View.symbolEffect(_:options:isActive:) with .variableColor (iOS 17 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4476; Symbols.swiftinterface:84)); View.accessibilityAddTraits(_:) with .isSelected (iOS 14 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23208))

**Verifier reasons:** The observation is factually correct: PlayerOverlayPresentation carries only id, an AnyView and onDismiss (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:5-9), the playing item lives inside the shells / PlayerView, and no card on the browse side takes or reads a playing state (grep for nowPlaying|isPlaying in LiveStreamsView.swift, M3UChannelsView.swift, SearchView.swift returns nothing). But it is a new feature, not a native-feel defect: Apple's TV app does not mark the playing title in its grids, and system PiP gives no such marker either; only Music/Podcasts mark list rows. The finding already flags it as an owner decision. The technical route is sound: a PreferenceKey set on PlayerView propagates up through AnyView, .frame, .environment and .transition to item.root in DashboardView.swift:94; PlayerView has streamId/type/suppressWatchHistory (Views/PlayerView.swift:76, 160); a custom environment value set on the TabView reaches pushed destinations and is re-read only by views that declare it, so the Equatable shelf rows keep being skipped while the visible cards update. It does, however, require one line in Views/PlayerView.swift, which is out of scope for this audit, and wiring in every card type on both dashboards (LiveStreamCard, M3UChannelCard, search ResultRow, EPG channel column, favorites), so it is M, not a quick win. The watch-history alternative is not worth it (late, and it couples a UI marker to 10 s progress writes).

**Corrected claim:** Nothing in the catalog marks the item playing in the docked card. This is a missing enhancement (Music-style now-playing marker), not a deviation from how Apple's video apps behave; severity low.

**Corrected fix:** Owner decision. If wanted: NowPlayingKey { type, streamId } + PreferenceKey (reduce: take the non-nil next value) in PlayerOverlayController.swift; one additive .preference(key:value:) on PlayerView's root (needs the owner's OK because the file is out of scope); DashboardView and M3UDashboardView store it in @State via onPreferenceChange on item.root and pass .environment(\.nowPlaying, playerOverlay.presentation == nil ? nil : nowPlaying) on the TabView; cards read @Environment(\.nowPlaying) and overlay a small 'waveform' symbol with .symbolEffect(.variableColor.iterative) plus .accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected). Start with the live cards only (Live TV grid/shelves, M3U channels), where zapping makes the marker most useful; skip the watch-history derivation.

**API check:** View.preference(key:value:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:9972 (iOS 13, @inlinable). View.onPreferenceChange(_:perform:) at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:14677, signature 'perform action: @escaping (K.Value) -> Void where K.Value: Equatable' - NowPlayingKey? must be Equatable. View.symbolEffect(_:options:isActive:) for IndefiniteSymbolEffect at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:4476 (iOS 17, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient); .variableColor.iterative is in the Symbols framework (iOS 17) per the finding - I did not re-open Symbols.swiftinterface. accessibilityAddTraits is long-standing (iOS 14 form). All within the iOS 18 target, no gate needed.

**Regression risks:** Touches PlayerView.swift (one additive line) - out of scope without the owner's consent. A constantly animating symbol on a tile adds a small render cost while that tile is visible; keep it off when Reduce Motion is on. The environment value must be set on the TabView, not on DashboardView's ZStack, or the overlay itself re-reads it. Cards must read the environment themselves; passing an isPlaying parameter through the Equatable shelf rows would break the deliberate row skipping.

**How to verify:** Simulator: play a channel, minimise; the tapped tile shows the marker in the shelf, the category grid and All Channels, and no other tile does; zap next in the player, minimise, the marker moves; close the card, the marker disappears. Instruments (SwiftUI template) while zapping with a shelf screen visible: only the two affected cards re-evaluate, shelf row bodies do not.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-6 — Expanding the docked card while a search field is being edited does not end editing, so the player grows to fullscreen underneath the software keyboard.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab, Inline search on Live TV, Movies, Series, M3U, Any searchable list with the mini card docked
- Code: `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:35-41, 94-99`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:114-118`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:74-78`

**What the user perceives:** The user is typing in search with the card docked above the keyboard and taps the card. The player expands, but the keyboard stays over its lower third for the length of the expand animation, and only then (if at all) goes away.

**Mechanism (finder):** present() resigns the first responder before anything else (PlayerOverlayController.swift:39-41, added after the last review), but expand() only flips mode (94-99). The keyboard lives in its own window above the in-window overlay, and on expand the host switches to ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard) (DashboardView.swift:118), so the player is laid out behind it. The player claims hardware-keyboard focus 0.44 s after the expand starts (PlayerView.swift:1480-1491, reference), which is the earliest moment the search field can lose focus.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Move the resign into a private helper of the controller and call it from expand() as well:

private func endEditing() {
    UIApplication.shared.sendAction(#selector(UIResponder.resignFirstResponder), to: nil, from: nil, for: nil)
}
@MainActor func expand() { guard presentation != nil else { return }; endEditing(); mode = .fullscreen }

**APIs:** UIApplication.sendAction(_:to:from:for:) (iOS 2 (UIKit/UIApplication.h:111); already used at PlayerOverlayController.swift:39)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:28-57 and 94-99: present() sends resignFirstResponder first (39-41, comment 35-38 explains the overlay sits below the software keyboard), expand() only sets mode = .fullscreen. The host switches to ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard, edges: .all) as soon as mode leaves .mini (Views/DashboardView.swift:114-118, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:74-78), so the fullscreen player is laid out behind a keyboard nothing has dismissed. The card is reachable while typing: in mini mode the overlay respects the keyboard safe area on purpose (comment DashboardView.swift:116). The only thing that can move focus afterwards is claimHardwareKeyboardFocus() in the 0.44 s completion of the expand (PlayerView.swift:1479-1490, 1044-1047, reference only); whether a SwiftUI FocusState change takes first responder away from the UIKit search field is not provable from code, but the keyboard is over the player for at least those 0.44 s either way. The second caller of expand, the PiP return (PlayerView.swift:3645-3650), also wants the keyboard gone. History: ios-player-airplay-fix-report.md:253 (presentation-transitions-2 'Player opens underneath the keyboard') fixed present() only; expand() is the uncovered remainder, not a deliberate choice. grep shows no other resignFirstResponder / endEditing in the app. Screenshot iphone-light/Q02-search-focused.png shows the iOS 26 search field directly above the keyboard, i.e. the keyboard takes roughly the lower 40% of the screen.

**Corrected claim:** Expanding the docked card (tap, or automatic expand when PiP returns) while a search field is first responder does not end editing: the player grows to fullscreen behind the software keyboard for at least the 0.44 s expand, and possibly until the user dismisses it. Applies to every searchable screen in both dashboards.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: private endEditing() helper in PlayerOverlayController, called from present() (replacing lines 39-41) and from expand() before mode = .fullscreen. Host side only, no PlayerView change. Search text and the active search state are kept (resign only ends editing), same as present() today.

**API check:** UIApplication.sendAction(_:to:from:for:): UIKit/UIApplication.h:111 '- (BOOL)sendAction:(SEL)action to:(nullable id)target from:(nullable id)sender forEvent:(nullable UIEvent *)event;' (iOS 2). Already compiled at PlayerOverlayController.swift:39; expand() is @MainActor (line 95), so the call is legal there.

**Regression risks:** Minimal. In mini mode the player has given up hardware-keyboard focus (PlayerView.swift:1445), so the resign can only hit a catalog text field. On iOS 26 the Search tab's bottom field collapses back to the tab bar when it loses focus, same as on present(). The container already jumps from keyboard-reduced to full height on the mode flip today; the fix does not add to that.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 18 and iOS 26: Search tab, type two letters, play a result, minimise, tap the search field (keyboard up), tap the card. Before: keyboard over the lower part of the growing player. After: keyboard animates out as the expand starts, search text still there after minimising again. UI test: after tapping the card's expand, app.keyboards.count == 0. Repeat on an inline search (Live TV home) and on the M3U dashboard.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-7 — The player's title tap ('go to detail') closes the player and pushes the detail in the tab that started playback; after a minimise plus tab switch or pop, playback just stops and no detail appears.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movies home (Continue Watching), Series home (Continue Watching), Movie detail, Downloads
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:231-243`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:181-193`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:206-228`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:399-429`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:26-34, 48-84`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should a title tap keep playback running in the mini card while the detail is shown, instead of closing the player? That part is the player's own performPlayerDismiss call and is out of scope here.

**What the user perceives:** A film is playing in the mini card, the user has moved to the Live TV tab, expands the card and taps the title to open the film's page. The player closes, playback is gone and the screen still shows Live TV; the film page was pushed in the Movies tab, out of sight.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each call site builds its own onNavigateToDetail closure that captures the originating view: playerOverlay.dismiss() followed by pendingMovieDetail / pendingSeriesDetail = ... on that view's own NavigationStack (VODView.swift:237-240, SeriesView.swift:187-190, DownloadsView.swift:408-411). MovieDetailView's closure only dismisses when the id matches (MovieDetailView.swift:211-214), which assumes the detail is still on top. These closures were written when the player could only be closed, not minimised and carried across tabs. The player calls the closure and then closes itself (PlayerView.swift:3158-3164, reference).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Route through the dashboard instead of the originating view. PlayerOverlayController gets @Published var detailRequest: PlayerDetailRequest? (movie(DBVODStream) / series(DBSeries)) and one helper requestDetail(type:id:playlistId:) that does the database lookup the four closures duplicate today. DashboardView observes it and sets selectedTab to .movies / .series; the tab roots, which already own navigationDestination(item:) (VODView.swift:161, SeriesView.swift:162), take the request in .onChange(of: playerOverlay.detailRequest) and set their pending item. The four closures collapse to { type, id in playerOverlay.requestDetail(...) }.

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real. Title tap runs onNavigate(type,id) then performPlayerDismiss() (PlayerView.swift:3158-3164, reference). The closures set @State of the view that started playback: VODView.swift:231-243 (pendingMovieDetail on the Movies root, destination at 161), SeriesView.swift:181-193 (destination at 162), DownloadsView.swift:400-429, MovieDetailView.swift:206-228. TabView keeps the non-selected tab alive, so after minimise + tab switch the detail is pushed in the hidden origin tab while the player closes over the current tab. After a pop, MovieDetailView's same-id branch (211-214) only dismisses and its state is gone, so nothing appears. Additional case the finding missed: playback started from the Downloads sheet closes that sheet (DashboardView.swift:125-129), so DownloadsView's pendingMovieDetail/pendingSeriesDetail is set on a dismissed view and the title tap never shows a detail, even without minimising. The fix as written needs correcting: (1) MovieDetailView's same-id short-circuit is the common path (detail -> play -> title tap -> player closes onto the detail still underneath, also when that detail lives in the Search or Favorites stack). Collapsing it into requestDetail would jump to the Movies tab and push a duplicate detail: a regression. (2) A tab that was never opened has no mounted root, so .onChange(of: detailRequest) never fires there; the request has to be consumed on appear as well. (3) The tab roots use NavigationStack without a path; activating the root's navigationDestination(item:) while other screens are pushed above it is not something the code can prove behaves well. (4) Title tap closing playback at all was already recorded as an open product decision (ios-player-airplay-review.md:1986-1995, fix report line 260); this finding should be decided together with it. Severity low stands: it needs minimise + tab switch/pop + expand + a tap on a title that has no visible affordance.

**Corrected claim:** The title tap's 'go to detail' closure writes navigation state of the view that started playback. If that view is no longer the visible context (other tab selected after minimising, origin detail popped, or the Downloads sheet that auto-closes on playback start), the player closes and no detail appears where the user is; in the tab case the detail is pushed unseen in the origin tab.

**Corrected fix:** Route only when the origin cannot show the detail itself. PlayerOverlayController gets @Published var detailRequest: PlayerDetailRequest? (enum movie(DBVODStream) / series(DBSeries), Equatable) plus requestDetail(type:id:playlistId:) with the shared DB lookup. DashboardView selects .movies / .series through tabBinding in .onChange(of: playerOverlay.detailRequest). VODView and SeriesView roots consume it with .onChange(of: playerOverlay.detailRequest, initial: true) (so a tab mounted by the switch still gets it), set their pending item and clear the request. VODView, SeriesView and DownloadsView closures become requestDetail calls. MovieDetailView keeps its same-id branch (just dismiss) while it is still on screen, tracked by a small reference box flipped in onAppear/onDisappear and captured by the closure; otherwise it calls requestDetail. Check in the simulator what the root's navigationDestination(item:) does when the Movies stack already has pushed screens; if it misbehaves, give the Movies/Series tabs a NavigationPath and append instead. Decide together with the open question from the last review whether the title tap should minimise instead of close.

**API check:** navigationDestination(item:destination:): already used at VODView.swift:161, SeriesView.swift:162 (iOS 17). onChange(of:initial:_:): SwiftUI, iOS 17, two-parameter closure form already used across the app (e.g. DashboardView.swift:125). No new API beyond these.

**Regression risks:** Collapsing MovieDetailView's closure would break the common 'title tap returns to the detail under the player' path and pull Search/Favorites users into the Movies tab. Cross-tab programmatic selection must go through tabBinding or the saved tab goes out of sync (DashboardView.swift:26-34). Root-level navigationDestination(item:) with a deeper stack is unverified. M3U dashboard has no detail screens and must simply ignore the request.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI tests: (a) Movies -> Continue Watching -> minimise -> Live TV tab -> expand -> tap title: Movies tab selected, detail title visible. (b) Search -> movie detail -> play -> tap title: still on Search tab, same detail, no second push. (c) Movie detail -> play -> minimise -> back -> expand -> tap title: detail shown. (d) Downloads sheet -> play a downloaded film -> tap title: detail shown. (e) Movies tab with a category pushed, then (a): note the resulting stack. Unit test for requestDetail type/id mapping.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-8 — The dock positions of the mini card are computed from constants inside the player, not from the browse chrome: on Plus / Pro Max phones in landscape the card sits on the tab bar, and the top corners cover the back button, the toolbar buttons and a focused search field.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All tabs with the mini card docked, iPhone Plus / Pro Max landscape, Pushed screens with a back button, iPad top tab bar
- Code: `Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:471-541`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:92-122`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:52-81`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: The values are supplied at the overlay boundary, but two lines of the card geometry in PlayerView would read them, and that file was reworked last week. Also a design call: should the top dock sit below the navigation bar, or is covering it acceptable for a card the user placed there (system PiP covers bars too)?

**What the user perceives:** Default corner, iPhone portrait: fine (see healthy). On a Pro Max held sideways the card rests 12 pt above the home-indicator area, on top of the trailing end of the tab bar, so the last tab (Search on iOS 26) cannot be tapped. Dragged to a top corner, the card covers the back button (leading) or the sort / favourites buttons and the search field's cancel button (trailing); on iPad it covers the ends of the top tab bar.

**Mechanism (finder):** The bottom allowance is 'compact width ? 49 : 0' (PlayerView.swift:1954 with isCompactWidth at 3977, reference). Plus / Pro Max phones report a regular width in landscape but still show the bottom tab bar, so they get 0. The top rest position is safeArea.top + 12 (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:531), and the overlay's safe area is the window's, not the navigation bar's: 74 pt on iPhone 17 Pro, while the bar buttons occupy 62-106 pt (iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png, iphone-dark/S02-series-category-detail.png; iPad: ipad-light/L02-live-home-scrolled.png, bar at 33-75 pt, card top at 36 pt).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Let the host state the obstruction instead of the player guessing it. In PlayerOverlayController.swift add an environment value playerOverlayDockInsets (top, bottom); DashboardView and M3UDashboardView set it on item.root:

let phone = UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .phone
.environment(\.playerOverlayDockInsets, .init(top: 44, bottom: (phone || horizontalSizeClass == .compact) ? MiniPlayerMetrics.tabBarAllowance : 0))

The two constants in the card-rect computation (bottom allowance, top rest offset) read it. No iOS 26-only API.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues custom key + View.environment(_:_:) (iOS 13; same pattern as PlayerOverlayController.swift:102-154)

**Verifier reasons:** Two different things are bundled. (a) Bottom, real defect: PlayerView.swift:1954 reserves the tab bar only when horizontalSizeClass == .compact (isCompactWidth at 3977); the comment at MiniPlayerSupport.swift:475-478 shows the 0 was meant for iPad ('iPad .sidebarAdaptable has no bottom bar'). iPhone supports landscape (project.pbxproj:567/608), Plus / Pro Max phones are regular width in landscape and iPhone always keeps the bottom tab bar, so the card rests at safe-area bottom + 12 pt (cardOrigin, MiniPlayerSupport.swift:534), inside the tab bar's band at the default corner (.bottomTrailing, PlayerView.swift:401). The path is ordinary: watch with the phone turned sideways, pull down to minimise. Not provable from code is how much of the last tab is actually blocked; no screenshot covers landscape or a docked card (checked all three folders twice). (b) Top: topY = window safeArea.top + 12 (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:531). Screenshots confirm the geometry: iphone-dark/L05 shows bar buttons at about 62-106 pt, so a card at 74 pt covers their lower part; ipad-light/L02 shows the top bar at about 31-76 pt with sidebar toggle and toolbar buttons inside the 240 pt card span. But the top corners are only reached when the user drags the card there, system PiP covers bars the same way, and the proposed top: 44 just moves the obstruction onto the large title and the always-visible search drawer (L05: search field at about 170-212 pt), which the finding itself lists as something to keep clear. That part is a design choice, not a defect. Scope: both geometry lines live in PlayerView.swift / MiniPlayerSupport.swift, which the audit marks as out of scope and reworked last week (2ec2c18); the finding says so in decision_needed. The environment-value plumbing across three files is more than the bottom fix needs.

**Corrected claim:** On iPhones that report regular width in landscape (Plus / Pro Max) the docked card reserves no space for the bottom tab bar and overlaps its trailing end at the default corner. Separately, a card the user drags to a top corner overlaps the navigation bar buttons (iPhone) or the ends of the top bar (iPad); that is user-placed and comparable to system PiP.

**Corrected fix:** Bottom only, smallest change: PlayerView.swift:1954 becomes 'let bottomInset = (isCompactWidth || UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom == .phone) ? MiniPlayerMetrics.tabBarAllowance : 0' (the same idiom test is already used at PlayerView.swift:1937) and the comment at MiniPlayerSupport.swift:475-478 is updated. It is a one-line edit in a file that is out of scope for this audit, so it needs the owner's go-ahead. Top corners: no change unless the owner wants the card kept below the bar; if so, that is a design decision and a fixed 44 pt is not enough (large titles, search drawers, iPad top bar).

**API check:** No new API. UIDevice.current.userInterfaceIdiom is UIKit (iOS 3.2) and already used in PlayerView.swift:1937 and 1010. The proposed custom EnvironmentKey pattern exists at PlayerOverlayController.swift:102-154 but is not needed for the corrected fix.

**Regression risks:** bottomInset also feeds the card's max height (PlayerView.swift:1957-1961); in a Pro Max landscape container (about 420 pt high) the 0.42 factor still wins, so card size is unchanged. iPad regular width stays at 0, iPad compact width stays at 49. Adding a top offset would change every top-docked rest position and the drag snap targets, and would cover search fields instead of bar buttons.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iPhone 17 Pro Max landscape, iOS 26 and iOS 18: start playback, pull down to minimise, screenshot the card against the tab bar and tap the last tab (UI test: tab button isHittable). Before: card overlaps the bar. After: card clears it by about 12 pt. Re-check iPhone 17 Pro portrait and landscape and iPad regular / Slide Over for unchanged positions.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-9 — While a download is running, every play tap from the catalog is interrupted by the same three-button warning; the answer is never remembered.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series, Search, EPG guide, Favorites, History
- Code: `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:24-68`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:156-172`, `Models/DownloadManager.swift:380-388`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: The prompt protects against the panel's connection limit. Is 'ask once per download session' acceptable, or must every new stream be confirmed?

**What the user perceives:** A film download takes a long time. For its whole duration each channel tap from a list shows 'download in progress' with Cancel / Go to downloads / Continue, although the user already chose Continue a minute ago. Zapping inside the player is not asked, so the rule also feels arbitrary.

**Mechanism (finder):** present() asks DownloadManager.hasActiveDownload(playlistId:) on every call and parks the presentation in pendingPresentation whenever it is true (PlayerOverlayController.swift:43-49); confirmPending() (59-64) keeps no record. hasActiveDownload is true for as long as any task of that playlist is active (DownloadManager.swift:381-388).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Remember the confirmation until that playlist has no active download left. Keep the playlist id on the pending presentation and add to the controller:

private var acknowledged: Set<UUID> = []
// in present():
let active = DownloadManager.shared.hasActiveDownload(playlistId: playlistId)
if !active { acknowledged.remove(playlistId) }
let shouldWarn = active && !acknowledged.contains(playlistId)
// in confirmPending(): acknowledged.insert(pendingPlaylistId)

The continuation entry point of the first finding already removes the repeated prompt on episode steps.

**Verifier reasons:** Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:43-49: every present() without skipDownloadCheck and with a playlistId asks DownloadManager.hasActiveDownload and parks the presentation; confirmPending() (59-64) records nothing. Models/DownloadManager.swift:381-388: true while any task of the playlist is active (maxConcurrentPerPlaylist = 1 at line 32, queued items start one after another, so this can last for a whole queue). 15 of the 19 present call sites take this path (Live, VOD, Series, Search, Favorites, EPG guide, programme sheet, catch-up); in-player zapping swaps inside the shells and never calls present(), so it is not asked. A stream already running in the mini card does not suppress the prompt either. The alert is DashboardView.swift:156-172, text en.lproj/Localizable.strings:445-448 ('the download may pause due to the server's connection limit'). History (git log -S hasActiveDownload, -S player_warning) shows only the original feature and localisation commits; no comment says repetition is intended, but the prompt itself is deliberate protection, so changing its frequency is the owner's call, as the finding states. M3U playback passes no playlistId (M3UChannelsView.swift:267) and is unaffected.

**Corrected claim:** While a download of the same Xtream playlist is active, every new playback started from the catalog shows the same three-button warning again, including right after the user chose Continue and while another stream is already playing; channel changes inside the player are not asked. This is a product rule to relax, not a bug.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two details: store the pending playlist id next to pendingPresentation (clear it in cancelPending too), and make the 'has active download' check an injectable closure defaulting to DownloadManager.shared.hasActiveDownload so it can be unit-tested. Note the acknowledgment is only cleared at the next present() that finds no active download, so a queue of consecutive downloads counts as one session; that is acceptable and arguably wanted, but say so in the comment. Owner decides whether once per download session is enough.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. DownloadManager is @MainActor (DownloadManager.swift:24-25) and present() is @MainActor, so the synchronous call compiles as today; confirmPending() is not @MainActor-annotated but only touches the controller's own set.

**Regression risks:** Fewer warnings means a user can start a stream that pauses a download without being reminded; that is the trade the owner has to accept. The controller is a @StateObject of the dashboard, so the acknowledgment is dropped when the playlist is left. 'Go to Downloads' and Cancel must not record an acknowledgment.

**How to verify:** Unit test with the injected closure: first present parks, confirmPending presents, second present goes straight through, cancelPending does not acknowledge, after one present with the closure returning false the prompt is back. Simulator: start a long download, play a channel (prompt), Continue, close, play another channel (no prompt). Also check the alert requested while the EPG programme sheet is dismissing (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:82-85) still appears.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-10 — VoiceOver reaches the docked card only after the whole screen and the tab bar, and nothing moves focus or announces a change when the player minimises, expands or closes.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All dashboard tabs with the mini card docked, M3U dashboard
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:85-123`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:45-82`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Order choice: card first on every screen while docked (proposed), or leave it last and only fix the focus hand-over.

**What the user perceives:** After the escape gesture or the minimise button, VoiceOver focus is left on a control that no longer exists and lands wherever the system picks. To pause or close the docked player, a VoiceOver user has to swipe through the navigation bar, the visible catalog and all tab-bar items first.

**Mechanism (finder):** The overlay ZStack is declared after the TabView (DashboardView.swift:92), so its elements follow everything inside the TabView in the accessibility order. The host flips accessibilityHidden on the catalog when the mode changes (line 90) but posts no notification; the only accessibility posts in the app are player announcements (PlayerView.swift:1405, 3743, 3930, 4731, 5472, reference).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Both dashboards, host side only, no new strings:

ZStack { /* overlay */ }
    .accessibilitySortPriority(playerOverlay.mode == .mini ? 1 : 0)   // card is read first while docked
...
.onChange(of: playerOverlay.mode) { _, _ in AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged().post() }
.onChange(of: playerOverlay.presentation == nil) { _, _ in AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged().post() }

The modifiers are unconditional (value changes only), so PlayerView is not remounted.

**APIs:** View.accessibilitySortPriority(_:) (iOS 14 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:6932)); AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged().post() (iOS 17 (Accessibility.swiftinterface:242, 260))

**Verifier reasons:** What code proves: the host posts nothing when the overlay changes. DashboardView.swift:85-123 and M3UDashboardView.swift:45-82 only flip accessibilityHidden on the TabView (line 90 / 50) and offer the escape action (108 / 68). grep over the app finds only .announcement posts in the player (PlayerView.swift:1405, 3743, 3930, 4731) and no screenChanged / layoutChanged / AccessibilityFocusState anywhere, so a full-screen swap between player and catalog happens with no focus hand-over. Where VoiceOver focus actually lands, and the claimed reading order (card after catalog and tab bar because the overlay ZStack is declared after the TabView at line 92), cannot be settled from code: the TabView is UIKit-hosted and the player subtree is deep; only a device shows the order. The fix needs correcting: (1) accessibilitySortPriority on the overlay ZStack is applied to a view that is not an accessibility element; whether it reorders against the UIKit tab controller is unproven. (2) If it does work, 'card first' means every screen change inside the tabs (push, pop, tab switch) lands VoiceOver focus on the card's buttons instead of the back button or title, which is worse than today; Apple Music keeps its mini player in geometric order, not first. (3) AccessibilityNotification lives in the Accessibility module, which SwiftUI imports but does not re-export (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:5 'import Accessibility', no @_exported), so the snippet needs 'import Accessibility' or the UIKit form the code base already uses. (4) Posting at the moment mode flips fires before the morph settles: on expand the fullscreen chrome stays hidden for 0.44 s (PlayerView.swift:1459-1490), so focus would land on nothing useful. (5) Closing the docked card is a layout change, not a new screen.

**Corrected claim:** The dashboards never tell VoiceOver that the player covered, uncovered or left the screen, so focus is left to the system after minimise, expand and close. The docked card is probably reached only after the catalog and tab bar; that order is unverified.

**Corrected fix:** Host side, both dashboards, focus hand-over only: in .onChange(of: playerOverlay.mode) and .onChange(of: playerOverlay.presentation == nil), wait for the transition (about 0.5 s, cancellable Task) and then call UIAccessibility.post(notification: .screenChanged, argument: nil) when a fullscreen player appears, expands, minimises or closes from fullscreen, and .layoutChanged when a docked card closes. Guard with UIAccessibility.isVoiceOverRunning. Leave the reading order alone until a device run shows it; if the card really is last, try .accessibilityElement(children: .contain) on the overlay ZStack before any sort priority, and do not make it first.

**API check:** View.accessibilitySortPriority(_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:6930-6932, '@available(iOS 14.0, ...) nonisolated public func accessibilitySortPriority(_ sortPriority: Swift.Double)'. AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged: Accessibility.swiftinterface, enum at '@available(iOS 17.0, ...) public enum AccessibilityNotification', 'public struct ScreenChanged' with 'public init(_ element: Any? = nil)', post() from the protocol extension; needs 'import Accessibility' (not re-exported by SwiftUI). UIAccessibilityScreenChangedNotification / UIAccessibilityLayoutChangedNotification: UIKit/UIAccessibilityConstants.h:129 and 136; UIAccessibility.post is already used at PlayerView.swift:1405.

**Regression risks:** Sort priority 'card first' would steal initial focus on every catalog screen change while a card is docked. An immediate ScreenChanged during the morph can focus a control that is about to unmount and plays the screen-change sound twice together with UIKit's own navigation posts. Modifiers on the overlay ZStack must stay unconditional so PlayerView is not remounted (comment DashboardView.swift:105-107).

**How to verify:** Device with VoiceOver (the simulator cannot settle this): 1. minimise with the chevron and with the two-finger scrub, note which element is focused; 2. expand from the card, note focus after the chrome appears; 3. close from fullscreen and from the card; 4. from the top of a tab swipe right and count swipes until the card's buttons are reached, and note whether they come before or after the tab bar. Repeat after the change; also push a category screen with a card docked and confirm focus goes to the back button or title, not the card.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-11 — In All Channels every channel tap copies and compares the whole catalog on the main thread, and the first tap also builds the channel-panel model for all of it before the player appears.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: All Channels, Live category detail
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:474, 480-491, 699, 705-717, 1253-1300`

**What the user perceives:** On a 40k-channel playlist the first channel tap in All Channels shows the player two to four frames late; later taps cost about one frame. Not a dead tap, but it is the one entry point where the earlier tap-latency work does not apply.

**Mechanism (finder):** AllLiveView.currentStreams is a computed displayItems.map(\.stream) evaluated per tap (LiveStreamsView.swift:699, 706), and the queue is passed as one section with id "all" (711). LiveChannelPanelSectionCache.resolve then (a) cannot use its O(1) shared-buffer equality, because the array is a fresh buffer each tap (comment at 1247-1248), and (b) on the first tap treats the whole catalog as 'the current category' and builds it inline (1284-1290), bypassing the 1500-channel inline limit (1256). Measured on an M-series Mac, -O, 40,000 synthetic channels: map 2-3 ms, equality on distinct buffers 2-3 ms, panel build (one URL(string:) per channel) 15-23 ms. LiveCategoryDetailView evaluates the same computed map twice per tap (474, 486).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Browse side only. Build the stream array once, off the main thread, where displayItems is produced, and keep it in @State so every tap passes the same buffer:

// AllLiveView.recompute(), inside the detached task
return (result, result.map(\.stream))
...
displayItems = result.0; streams = result.1
Task { _ = await LiveChannelPanelSectionCache.shared.resolveAll(
    [LiveChannelCategorySection(id: "all", title: L("browse.all_live"), streams: streams)], playlistId: playlist.id) }

resolveAll (1303-1327) already builds missing sections on a detached task, so the first tap finds the section cached and resolve() is O(1). Same @State array in LiveCategoryDetailView.

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read the code; the mechanism is exact. Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:699 `currentStreams` is a computed `displayItems.map(\.stream)`, evaluated once per tap at :706 and passed as one section with id "all" (:711). LivePlayerShell.init (:825) calls LiveChannelPanelSectionCache.resolve synchronously on the tap. In resolve (:1264-1300) a cold cache gives missing=[0]; 40k > inlineBuildLimit 1500 (:1256, :1277), so it takes the 'current category' branch (:1284-1290) and buildAndStore maps the whole catalog inline, one URL(string:) per channel (:1349-1360). On later taps cachedSection (:1335-1339) compares `entry.streams == section.streams` on two distinct buffers, so the O(1) shared-buffer shortcut described at :1247-1248 never applies. LiveCategoryDetailView does evaluate the computed map twice per tap (:485 and :486; the finding cites :474/:486).

I reproduced the numbers with a -O benchmark on this Mac (40,000 synthetic DBLiveStream values with the real field layout from Models/DBModels.swift:15-32): map 1.3-2.2 ms, equality on distinct buffers 1.9 ms, panel build 12-14 ms. So first tap is roughly 16-18 ms here (more on older phones), later taps 3-4 ms. That is at the edge of perception and is dwarfed by stream start-up, so 'low' is right.

Corrections:
1. 'The one entry point where the earlier tap-latency work does not apply' is overstated. The EPG guide and programme sheet (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:405, Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:126) call LiveChannelCategorySection.xtreamLiveQueue() (Views/PlayerView.swift:20-39), which copies the whole catalog into fresh arrays on every tap and therefore also pays the element-wise compare for every category. Search (Views/SearchView.swift:280-304) and Favorites (Views/FavoritesView.swift:81-99) do the same at their own sizes. What is unique to All Channels is the first-tap whole-catalog inline build.
2. The fix as sketched has two gaps. AllLiveView has three `.task(id:)` modifiers (:733-735) that all fire recompute() on first appear, so the sketch would produce three arrays and three prewarm builds; resolveAll stores whichever finishes last (:1319-1324), which need not be the buffer left in @State, so later taps can still fall back to the O(n) compare. The prewarm Task is also unstructured and runs for every search result set.
3. The detached closure has two return paths (:746 and :748); both must return the tuple.

Concurrency is fine: the app target builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (apps/ios/another-iptv-player.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:393, 415, 578, 619), so the cache and resolveAll are main-actor isolated and only makePanelSection runs detached (:1313, :1348). History: the cache came in with 2ec2c18 (last week's player work); the fix does not modify it, it only calls resolveAll from the browse side. No screenshot is relevant (tiny demo catalog).

**Corrected claim:** In All Channels, every channel tap maps the whole catalog into a fresh [DBLiveStream] on the main thread (LiveStreamsView.swift:699, 706) and LiveChannelPanelSectionCache then compares it element-wise with the cached copy (:1338); the first tap also builds the channel-panel model for the whole catalog inline because the single "all" section counts as the current category (:1284-1290), bypassing the 1500-channel inline limit. Measured at 40k channels on an M-series Mac: about 2 ms map, 2 ms compare, 12-14 ms build. That is about one to three 120 Hz frames once per visit, then well under a frame. It is not the only entry point with a per-tap whole-catalog copy and compare: the EPG guide and programme sheet do it through xtreamLiveQueue() (PlayerView.swift:20-39). Only the first-tap whole-catalog build is unique to All Channels. LiveCategoryDetailView maps its category twice per tap (:485-486), which is negligible at category sizes.

**Corrected fix:** Browse side only, no change to LiveChannelPanelSectionCache or LivePlayerShell.

AllLiveView:
- Add `@State private var streams: [DBLiveStream] = []`.
- Produce it in the existing detached task in recompute(); both return paths return `(items, items.map(\.stream))`.
- After the `guard !Task.isCancelled` assign `displayItems` and `streams` together; the tap handler passes `streams` for both `queue` and the "all" section, and the computed `currentStreams` goes away.
- Prewarm from inside recompute(), after the assignment, with exactly the array just stored: `_ = await LiveChannelPanelSectionCache.shared.resolveAll([LiveChannelCategorySection(id: "all", title: L("browse.all_live"), streams: newStreams)], playlistId: playlist.id)`. Running it inside the `.task` (not a free `Task {}`) ties it to the view's lifetime.
- Collapse the three `.task(id:)` at :733-735 into one task keyed on a combined value (query, streamsLoaded, hidden ids) so first appear does one recompute and one prewarm instead of three. Without this the cached entry can end up holding a different buffer than @State and taps fall back to the 2 ms compare.
- Optional: skip the prewarm when the result is at most 1500 items, since resolve builds those inline anyway.

LiveCategoryDetailView: hoist `let streams = currentStreams` once inside the tap closure (one map instead of two). A @State array is not worth it at category sizes.

Out of scope here but same pattern: xtreamLiveQueue() for the EPG entry points could reuse a memo in the same way.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. Project-internal: LiveChannelPanelSectionCache.resolveAll(_:playlistId:) async -> [ChannelPanelSection] at Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:1303-1327 exists, is internal (callable from AllLiveView in the same file and module), builds missing sections in Task.detached and stores Entry(streams: source.streams) with the caller's buffer, so a later resolve() with the same array hits Array =='s shared-buffer fast path. The class is main-actor isolated through SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393/415/578/619), so calling it from a View task is race-free.

**Regression risks:** Small. (1) A 40k-item panel model (about 13 ms of background CPU, a few MB) is now built whenever All Channels opens, even if nothing is tapped; today it is built only on the first tap. (2) If the prewarm has not finished when the user taps, resolve() builds inline exactly as today and the late resolveAll overwrites the entry with equal content; harmless. (3) Collapsing the three .task modifiers must keep all three triggers (debounced query, streamsLoaded, hidden category ids), otherwise hiding a category would stop refreshing the grid. (4) Must not touch LiveCategoryContent's Equatable/itemsToken work (:534-561); the fix does not. (5) The title passed to the prewarm must be the same L("browse.all_live") string as at tap time or cachedSection misses (:1337).

**How to verify:** Unit test: call resolveAll with a 2,000-item section id "all", then resolve() with the same array instance and assert isComplete == true and that the returned section is the stored one; repeat with a copied array to cover the fallback path. On a device with a 40k-channel playlist, put os_signpost intervals around the onStreamSelected closure in AllLiveView (through playerOverlay.present returning) before and after: expect roughly 16-35 ms then 3-7 ms before, and under 1 ms for both after. Log how many times recompute() runs on first appear to confirm one run after collapsing the tasks.

## player-handoff-miniplayer-12 — Playing an item of another kind while a card is docked swaps the player with a hard cut; the 0.14 s fade only covers first appearance. (A spatial link to the tapped card is not realistic for this overlay.)

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Any play tap while a mini card of a different kind is docked (live card docked, film or episode started, and the reverse)
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:92-122`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:52-81`, `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:5-9, 42-56`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Accept the plain fade as the entry transition (recommended), or invest in a hero from the tapped card, which means frame tracking in every cell and coordination with the player's launch-flash constraint (effort L, already rated that way in ios-player-airplay-review.md).

**What the user perceives:** With a live channel in the mini card, tapping Play on a film makes the card vanish and a full black player appear in the same frame, with no transition. Every other way into the player fades.

**Mechanism (finder):** The host animates only on presentation != nil (DashboardView.swift:121). Replacing a LivePlayerShell root with a VODPlayerShell, HistorySeriesPlayerShell, CatchupPlayerShell or bare PlayerView changes the type inside the AnyView (PlayerOverlayController.swift:42), which is an identity change without an insertion, so neither the transition nor the animation applies. Same-kind replacements keep identity on purpose and morph from the card. On the entry itself: the opacity-only insertion is deliberate (comment at DashboardView.swift:109-111, moving the video subtree produced a launch flash), and a fade to black is also what Apple's TV app does when playback starts. matchedTransitionSource / navigationTransition(.zoom) need a NavigationStack push or a sheet / fullScreenCover, which would give up the docked card and the preserved player identity; tracking card frames for a custom hero costs geometry work in every lazy cell. Neither is recommended.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give the presentation a kind and key identity and animation on it, with an immediate removal so two engines never overlap (panels often allow a single connection):

struct PlayerOverlayPresentation { let id = UUID(); let kind: String; ... }   // kind = String(reflecting: Content.self), set in present()

item.root
    ...
    .id(item.kind)
    .transition(.asymmetric(insertion: .opacity, removal: .identity))
...
.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.14), value: playerOverlay.presentation?.kind)

Same-kind presentations keep the same id, so the behaviour that protects AirPlay continuity is unchanged; a different kind is already a new identity today. Note that removal becomes immediate for a plain close as well; the player has finished its own exit animation before it calls dismiss, and the browse-side dismiss() calls are followed by a push.

**APIs:** AnyTransition.asymmetric(insertion:removal:), AnyTransition.identity (iOS 13 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4572, 15402)); View.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:) / navigationTransition(_:) (iOS 18 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:14900, 8947); checked, not applicable to an in-window overlay)

**Verifier reasons:** The hard cut is real by code reading. Views/DashboardView.swift:92-121 and Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:52-80 keep one `if let item` branch with `.transition(.opacity)` and animate only on `presentation != nil`. present() (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:42-55) sets mode = .fullscreen and swaps the AnyView; when the wrapped type differs (LivePlayerShell vs VODPlayerShell, HistorySeriesPlayerShell, CatchupPlayerShell or bare PlayerView) the subtree is replaced in a transaction that carries no animation, so the docked card disappears and the new fullscreen player appears with no fade. The finder's reading that the opacity-only entry is deliberate (comment at DashboardView.swift:109-111, :119-120) and that a zoom/hero is not realistic is also right. I could not observe it: no screenshot shows the mini player, and how noticeable a cut versus a 0.14 s fade is can only be judged from a recording.

The proposed fix does not stand as written:
1. Its key safety note is wrong. 'The player has finished its own exit animation before it calls dismiss, and the browse-side dismiss() calls are followed by a push' holds only for the player's own exits (Views/PlayerView.swift:940-970, 2026-2032, 2140-2147). The title tap at PlayerView.swift:3158-3164 calls onNavigateToDetail first and performPlayerDismiss second, and the browse-side closures call playerOverlay.dismiss() straight away: synchronously and with no push at Views/MovieDetailView.swift:208 and :212, and a few milliseconds later (after one DB read, well inside the 0.25 s exit) at MovieDetailView.swift:221/225, Views/VODView.swift:238, Views/SeriesView.swift:188, Views/DownloadsView.swift:409/425. On those paths the host's 0.14 s opacity removal is the only exit animation the fullscreen player gets. With `removal: .identity` they become a hard cut from fullscreen player to catalog, which is a worse and far more common regression than the case being fixed. PlayerOverlayController.swift:72-74 also documents that the exit transition is relied on.
2. Whether an `.identity` removal under an animated transaction tears the old PlayerView and its engine down in the same update (the 'two engines never overlap' premise on single-connection panels) is not something the SDK interface can show; it needs a run.
3. The cited SDK line for AnyTransition.identity is wrong: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:15402 is EmptyModifier.identity. The real declaration is at :16242.
4. Keying on String(reflecting: Content.self) is fine for today's call sites (each present() closure builds exactly one concrete type), but the change sits in the host lines that last week's commit 2ec2c18 deliberately guarded ('must not animate the entire player subtree').

**Corrected claim:** When a player of one kind is docked as the mini card and the user starts an item whose root view type differs (live shell vs VOD shell, series-history shell, catch-up shell or bare PlayerView), the overlay swaps the whole player subtree in a transaction without animation: the card vanishes and a fullscreen player appears with no fade, because the host animates only on presentation != nil (DashboardView.swift:121, M3UDashboardView.swift:80). Same-type presentations keep identity on purpose and expand from the card. This is a minor polish gap on an uncommon path; it has not been observed on screen, only derived from the code.

**Corrected fix:** Do not change the removal transition or the existing `.animation(value: presentation != nil)` line. Either leave it as is (my recommendation unless the owner sees it as a problem on a recording), or add an insertion-only fade that leaves teardown exactly as today:

- PlayerOverlayPresentation gets `let kind: String` (String(reflecting: Content.self), set in present()).
- PlayerOverlayController gets `@Published private(set) var swapOpacity: Double = 1`. In present() and confirmPending(), when a presentation of a different kind is being replaced, set swapOpacity = 0 in the same update as the new presentation, then on the next main-queue turn `withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.14)) { swapOpacity = 1 }`.
- Both hosts add `.opacity(playerOverlay.swapOpacity)` on item.root, outside the AnyView. No `.id`, no new transition, so the old engine is torn down in the same update as now, the close paths keep their 0.14 s fade, and same-kind switches are untouched.

This needs a simulator check that the two state changes are not coalesced into one update (if they are, there is no fade and nothing else changes). The hero/zoom alternative stays not recommended, as the finder says.

**API check:** AnyTransition.asymmetric(insertion:removal:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4572, `public static func asymmetric(insertion: AnyTransition, removal: AnyTransition) -> AnyTransition`, iOS 13.0 (extension header :4566-4571). AnyTransition.identity: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:16242, `public static var identity: AnyTransition { get }`, iOS 13.0 (:16236); the finder's line 15402 is EmptyModifier.identity. AnyTransition.opacity: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4315. View.navigationTransition(_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8947, iOS 18.0. View.matchedTransitionSource(id:in:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:14900, iOS 18.0; both need a NavigationStack push or sheet/fullScreenCover and do not apply to this in-window overlay. The corrected fix uses only View.opacity, withAnimation and @Published, all iOS 13.

**Regression risks:** Original fix: (a) title tap to detail from the fullscreen player (MovieDetailView.swift:208/212/221/225, VODView.swift:238, SeriesView.swift:188, DownloadsView.swift:409/425) loses its only fade and becomes a hard cut; (b) adding `.id` and a kind-keyed animation to the host touches the identity and animation rules that protect AirPlay continuity and the launch-flash fix from 2ec2c18; (c) if `.identity` removal does not tear down immediately, two engines hold connections for 0.14 s on single-connection panels. Corrected fix: the new player is invisible for the first update, so the catalog shows for up to 0.14 s where the card was; if the opacity reset and the animated restore coalesce there is simply no fade; an opacity below 1 on the UIKit-backed video surface during attach should be checked against the launch-flash issue (the existing insertion transition already does the same thing on first appearance).

**How to verify:** Simulator or device screen recording at 120 fps, stepped frame by frame: dock a live channel, start a film from its detail page (before and after). Regression checks: (1) with a fullscreen movie playing, tap the title; the player must still fade out over the detail page; (2) zap between live channels from the catalog with the card docked; the card must still expand to fullscreen with identity kept, and an AirPlay session must survive; (3) on a single-connection panel, start a film while a live card is docked and confirm the new stream connects on the first attempt; (4) close the mini card with its X and by drag; the exit must look as before.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-1 — Movie and series shelf titles are cut to one line on iPhone at the default text size (and clipped at accessibility sizes) because the fixed shelf height reserves only 32 pt for the caption

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, Recently Added shelves (Movies, Series)
- Code: `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:49-50`, `Views/VODView.swift:350, 436, 467, 501, 528-534`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:327, 412, 439, 473, 500-506`

**What the user perceives:** On the Movies and Series home screens every longer title ends in an ellipsis after one line ("Whispers in th...", "Echoes of Tom...") although the same title gets two lines in the category grid and channel names get two lines on Live TV. With larger text the single line no longer fits either: from AX1 upwards its lower part is cut off by the shelf.

**Mechanism (finder):** shelfRowTotalHeight = shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64) (PosterMetrics.swift:50). On phones layoutScale is 0.5, so the shelf is 150 + 32 = 182 pt and is applied as .frame(height:) on the horizontal ScrollView (VODView.swift:350/467, SeriesView.swift:327/439). The card is a VStack with default spacing (about 8 pt) of a 150 pt poster and Text(.caption).lineLimit(2) (VODView.swift:501, 528-531), so the text is offered 182 - 150 - 8 = 24 pt: one 16 pt caption line fits, the second does not. The caption allowance is scaled with the poster (64 x 0.5) although text does not shrink with the poster, and it has no relation to Dynamic Type. Screenshots: iphone-dark/M01-movies-home.png ("Whispers in th..."), iphone-dark/M02 and iphone-light/M02-movies-home-scrolled.png ("Echoes of Tom..."); the unconstrained grid in M03 and the Live shelf in L01 show two lines. git log -S shelfRowTotalHeight shows it only in the monorepo-move commit, so this is original sizing, not later tuning.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep a deterministic fixed height (it keeps LazyVStack rows from jumping) but derive the text part from text metrics instead of from the poster scale. PosterMetrics: func shelfRowHeight(captionBlock: CGFloat) -> CGFloat { shelfPosterHeight + captionBlock }. In VODCategoryShelfRow, RecentlyAddedVODShelf, SeriesCategoryShelfRow, RecentlyAddedSeriesShelf: @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var captionBlock: CGFloat = 42 (8 spacing + 2 x 16 line + 2 slack) and .frame(height: posterMetrics.shelfRowHeight(captionBlock: captionBlock)); use the same value for the Color.clear loading placeholder (VODView.swift:436, SeriesView.swift:412). Make the card spacing explicit, VStack(spacing: 8), in VODStreamCard and SeriesCard so the constant is not an implicit default. The rows already read an @Environment value, so one more DynamicProperty does not change the .equatable() behaviour. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** ScaledMetric(wrappedValue:relativeTo:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism is real, the numbers are slightly off. Views/PosterMetrics.swift:13 clamps layoutScale to 0.5 on phones, so shelfRowTotalHeight (PosterMetrics.swift:50) = 150 + 32 = 182 and is applied as .frame(height:) on the horizontal ScrollView at Views/VODView.swift:350, 467 and Views/SeriesView.swift:327, 439 (placeholders at VODView.swift:436, SeriesView.swift:412). The card (VODView.swift:500-534, SeriesView.swift:472-506) is a default-spacing VStack of a 150 pt poster and Text(.caption).lineLimit(2). The comment at PosterMetrics.swift:49 says the allowance is meant for 'about 2 lines of caption', so one line on iPhone is unintended; on iPad (scale 1.0, 64 pt) two lines fit. git log -S shelfRowTotalHeight shows only the monorepo-move commit d2489f9, so no later tuning is being undone. Screenshots confirm: iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png shows 'Whispers in th...', iphone-light/M02 shows 'Echoes of Tom...', while the unconstrained grid in iphone-light/M04-movies-all.png wraps 'Echoes of / Tomorrow' on the same 100 pt width. Correction: I measured the screenshots at 3x (M01 poster bottom y=1243 px, cap top y=1264 px; M04 the same 21 px). That puts the text frame about 4 pt under the poster, not 8 (SwiftUI reduces the default gap next to Text). So the title is offered about 28 pt, not 24; two caption lines need about 31. The conclusion is unchanged, but bottom clipping would start around AX2-AX3 rather than AX1. Nobody ran an accessibility text size, so that part is derived from the code only. No other consumer of shelfRowTotalHeight exists (grep). Live shelves have no fixed height and are unaffected.

**Corrected claim:** On iPhone, Movies and Series home shelves (including Recently Added) show every title on one line with an ellipsis at the default text size, because the fixed shelf height (182 pt) leaves about 28 pt under the 150 pt poster while two caption lines need about 31 pt. The 64 pt caption allowance is multiplied by the phone layout scale of 0.5 although text does not shrink with the poster, and it does not follow Dynamic Type. At accessibility sizes even the single line exceeds the space and its lower edge is clipped by the shelf scroll view (threshold roughly AX2-AX3, not checked in a simulator). iPad is unaffected at the default size.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the fixed shelf height but derive the caption part from text metrics. In PosterMetrics add func shelfRowHeight(captionBlock: CGFloat) -> CGFloat { shelfPosterHeight + captionBlock }. In VODCategoryShelfRow, the Recently Added VOD shelf, SeriesCategoryShelfRow and the Recently Added series shelf add @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var captionBlock: CGFloat, and use it for both the ScrollView frame and the Color.clear loading placeholder. Make the card spacing explicit in VODStreamCard and SeriesCard, but use VStack(spacing: 4), which matches what is rendered today. The proposed spacing of 8 would push every title about 4 pt further from its poster in shelves, grids and Favorites. With spacing 4 the base value is about 38 (4 + two lines of about 31 + 3 slack); 42 only if the owner wants the 8 pt gap. The shelf grows by 6-10 pt per row at the default size. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** ScaledMetric: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12151-12152, '@propertyWrapper public struct ScaledMetric<Value> : DynamicProperty where Value : BinaryFloatingPoint' with 'public init(wrappedValue: Value, relativeTo textStyle: Font.TextStyle)', @available(iOS 14.0). Nothing else is needed. Not used anywhere in the app yet (grep), so this is the first use.

**Regression risks:** Equatable shelf rows are not undone: VODCategoryShelfRow already carries an @Environment property (VODView.swift:413) and ScaledMetric is another DynamicProperty, so the custom == and .equatable() keep working. Each shelf gets slightly taller, so slightly fewer shelves per screen. Explicit card spacing also affects the category grids and Favorites that reuse VODStreamCard and SeriesCard (VODView.swift:695, SeriesView.swift:651, FavoritesView.swift:135, 161), which is why it should match the current 4 pt. ScaledMetric uses UIFontMetrics, which only approximates the font-size ratio; keep a few points of slack and check one accessibility size.

**How to verify:** Rerun the screenshot tour: 'Whispers in the ...' (Movies home, Drama) and 'Echoes of Tomorrow' (Sci-Fi) wrap to two lines, and one-line titles still sit directly under the poster. Repeat with launch argument -UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName UICTContentSizeCategoryAccessibilityL and check that no caption is cut at the shelf's bottom edge. Compare the poster-to-title gap before and after in M04-movies-all (21 px at 3x today).
