## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-2 — Text under posters and on the rating badge is set in fixed 9-10 pt fonts that ignore Dynamic Type, the badge loses contrast on bright posters, and the Director/Cast labels use the tertiary label colour

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home and grids, Series home and grids, Favorites, Continue Watching, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/RatingLabel.swift:75-84`, `Views/VODView.swift:536-542`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:508-514`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:100-105`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:416-419`

**What the user perceives:** The rating on every poster, the category line in Favorites and the series name under a Continue Watching card stay tiny whatever text size the user has chosen (they are below the 11 pt minimum Apple uses). On a bright poster the white rating is hard to read ("8.7" over the calendar poster). On the detail screens the DIRECTOR / CAST labels are faint grey on the background.

**Mechanism (finder):** PosterRatingBadge uses .font(.system(size: 9/10)) and a 55 percent black capsule (RatingLabel.swift:77-84); over a white poster that scrim composites to mid-grey, see iphone-light/M02-movies-home-scrolled.png and iphone-dark/M02 (first Documentary poster). VODStreamCard/SeriesCard category line and HistoryCard subtitle use .font(.system(size: 10)) (VODView.swift:538, SeriesView.swift:510, ContinueWatchingRow.swift:102). Fixed sizes do not scale with the content size category. DetailInfoTextBlock draws an 11 pt label with .foregroundStyle(.tertiary) (DetailComponents.swift:416-419); tertiaryLabel is roughly 2:1 against the system background in both appearances, far below what body text needs.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the four fixed sizes with text styles: .caption2 (11 pt at the default size, scales) for the category line and the history subtitle; .caption2.weight(.semibold) for the badge text and star. Cap only the badge so it cannot cover the poster: .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.accessibility1) on PosterRatingBadge. Raise the scrim to about Color.black.opacity(0.72) (a plain colour, no per-cell material blur, so scroll cost is unchanged). DetailInfoTextBlock label: .foregroundStyle(.secondary). The other fixed-size sites (FavoritesView.swift:182, SearchView.swift:51, CachedImage.swift:143) are decorative glyphs and can stay.

**APIs:** View.dynamicTypeSize(_: range) (iOS 15.0); Font.caption2 (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Fixed sizes are real: Views/RatingLabel.swift:77, 79 (.system(size: 9/10)), Views/VODView.swift:538, Views/SeriesView.swift:510, Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:102 (.system(size: 10)). The grep for '.system(size:' outside the player finds only these plus decorative glyphs and the tip-jar file. They do not scale with Dynamic Type and sit below the 11 pt floor of caption2. The equivalent grid card already uses .caption2 for the same subtitle (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:194), so the 10 pt in HistoryCard is an inconsistency, not a decision. History shows only the monorepo-move commit. DetailInfoTextBlock label uses .foregroundStyle(.tertiary) at Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:416-419: confirmed in code. The demo data has no director or cast, so no screenshot shows it; the contrast figure of roughly 1.7-2:1 is computed from the system tertiary label colour. The badge contrast claim does not hold. I enlarged the badge over the calendar poster from iphone-light/M02-movies-home-scrolled.png: the 55 percent black capsule over white composites to roughly #737373, white text on it is about 4.7:1 and reads clearly. Raising the scrim is optional polish, not a defect. Category line sites: categoryName is only passed in Favorites (FavoritesView.swift:138, 164), an unconstrained grid, so the larger font cannot be clipped by the fixed shelf height.

**Corrected claim:** The poster rating badge (9/10 pt), the category line under Favorites cards (10 pt) and the subtitle under Continue Watching cards (10 pt) use fixed font sizes below the 11 pt system minimum and ignore the user's text size. The DIRECTOR / CAST labels on detail screens use the tertiary label colour, about 2:1 against the background. The rating badge itself is legible on bright posters at the current 55 percent scrim.

**Corrected fix:** VODView.swift:538, SeriesView.swift:510, ContinueWatchingRow.swift:102: .font(.caption2). PosterRatingBadge: .font(.caption2.weight(.semibold)) for star and text, capped with .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge) rather than accessibility1. On a 100 pt phone poster an accessibility1 badge (19 pt text) would be over 60 pt wide and cover most of the poster top. DetailInfoTextBlock label: .foregroundStyle(.secondary). Leave the scrim at 0.55; a darker value up to about 0.7 is an optional look decision for the owner. Leave the decorative glyph sites (FavoritesView.swift:182, SearchView.swift:51, CachedImage.swift:143) and TipJarView.swift:130 alone.

**API check:** Font.caption2: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12287-12288, @available(iOS 14.0) 'public static let caption2: Font'. View.dynamicTypeSize<T>(_ range: T) where T: RangeExpression, T.Bound == DynamicTypeSize: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:11912, extension @available(iOS 15.0). DynamicTypeSize cases xxxLarge and accessibility1 are present in the enum (iOS 15.0). The range form is already used in the code base at Views/PlayerView.swift:2827.

**Regression risks:** The badge grows from 10 to 11 pt at the default size on every poster. If finding 1's captionBlock is sized for exactly two title lines, check that nothing else in the shelf card grows: the category line is not shown in shelves, so it is safe. HistoryCard subtitle sits in a row without fixed height (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:46-57), so growth cannot clip. Does not touch the tip-jar files.

**How to verify:** Screenshot Movies home and Favorites at the default size (badge 1 pt larger, nothing else moves), then with -UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName UICTContentSizeCategoryXXXL: badge, Favorites category line and Continue Watching subtitle grow, and the badge stops growing at xxxLarge. Open a title that has director/cast metadata (not in the demo data) in light and dark and compare the label colour.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-3 — Card text columns are as narrow as 58 pt (channels) and 100 pt (posters) on iPhone and never widen with the text size; the EPG now-line under a channel has a fixed 22 pt height

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home and grids, M3U channels, Movies and Series shelves and grids, Favorites
- Code: `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:9-14, 16-28`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:36-38`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:15-17`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:431-437`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:48-51, 55-67`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Part (b) changes density: at large text sizes should grids drop to fewer, larger cards (as App Store and TV do) or keep three columns and accept truncation? Part (a) needs no decision.

**What the user perceives:** With the text size slider at its upper end (not even an accessibility size) a channel name has room for about five characters per line, so most names become "World Ne...". At accessibility sizes poster titles show three or four letters. The thin programme progress bar under a channel name disappears from xxLarge upwards.

**Mechanism (finder):** PosterMetrics is built once from the screen size (DashboardView.swift:38) and clamps layoutScale to 0.5 on phones: liveShelfLabelWidth = 58, shelf and grid posters = 100, live grid = 90 (PosterMetrics.swift:16-28). The titles are .caption with lineLimit(2) inside .frame(width:) (LiveStreamsView.swift:443-448, VODView.swift:528-533), so only the font grows. iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png already hyphenates "Motor-sport HD" at the default size. EPGNowNextLine pins itself to height 22 (EPGComponents.swift:51, 63): caption2 line + 3 spacing + 3 bar is 19 pt at the default size but 24 pt at xxLarge and 26 pt at xxxLarge, so the bar is pushed outside the frame and clipped by the shelf scroll view. The comment at EPGComponents.swift:48-50 records that the 22 was hand-tuned for the default size.

**Proposed fix (finder):** (a) Plain fix: @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption2) private var reservedHeight: CGFloat = 22 in EPGNowNextLine (placeholder and populated state keep the same, now scaled, height). (b) Layout: give PosterMetrics a text factor. DashboardView and M3UDashboardView read @Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize) and build PosterMetrics(windowSize: UIScreen.main.bounds.size, textScale: s) with s = 1.0 up to xxLarge, 1.25 at xxxLarge, 1.5 when typeSize.isAccessibilitySize; init: layoutScale = min(1, max(0.5, raw) * textScale). On iPhone this gives 87 pt channel labels and 150 pt posters (2 columns instead of 3) at accessibility sizes; iPad is unchanged by the min(1, ...). Raise lineLimit to 3 when isAccessibilitySize. Prefetch and render both read the same posterMetrics (CachedImage.request), so image cache keys stay matched. The comment at DashboardView.swift:36-37 asks for metrics tied to the display rather than to transient layout; the text size is not transient, so that intent is kept.

**APIs:** ScaledMetric (iOS 14.0); EnvironmentValues.dynamicTypeSize (iOS 15.0); DynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Widths are real: PosterMetrics.swift:13 clamps to 0.5 on phones, giving liveShelfLabelWidth 58, shelf and grid posters 100, live grid 90 (PosterMetrics.swift:16-28). It is built once from the screen at Views/DashboardView.swift:38 and Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:17. Titles are .caption, lineLimit(2), inside .frame(width:) (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:431-437). iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png shows 'Motor-/sport HD' at the default size; the fixture name is 'Motorsport HD' (Database/MockFixture.swift:71), so the 58 pt column already forces hyphenation without any larger text. Part (a): Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:51 pins reservedHeight to 22 and line 63 applies it as a fixed frame. caption2 line + 3 + 3 is about 19 pt at the default size, 22 at xLarge, 24 at xxLarge, 26 at xxxLarge, so the progress capsule overflows the frame. Live shelves have no fixed height (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397), so the overflow is clipped by the scroll view only on the tallest card of a shelf: about 2 of 3 pt lost at xxLarge, fully outside from xxxLarge. In grids it is not clipped but overlaps the row gap. The 22 came in with 1cce013 specifically to keep placeholder and populated heights equal; a scaled value keeps that invariant. EPGNowNextLine is used only by the two channel cards (LiveStreamsView.swift:452, M3UChannelsView.swift:440), not by the player. Part (b) as written is wrong in scope: layoutScale also drives seriesDetailHeroWidth/Height (Components/DetailComponents.swift:105-106), episodeThumbWidth/Height (SeriesView.swift:1394), season strip, search row icon and grid spacings. Multiplying it by 1.5 at accessibility sizes makes the detail hero poster and episode thumbnails 50 percent larger inside HStacks, taking width away from the text beside them exactly when text is largest. No larger-text run exists; the truncation estimate is arithmetic.

**Corrected claim:** On iPhone the channel label column is 58 pt and poster title columns are 100 pt regardless of text size; 58 pt already hyphenates 'Motorsport HD' at the default size, and at the largest non-accessibility sizes a channel name gets roughly five to six characters per line. Separately, the EPG now-line under a channel card has a fixed 22 pt height: from xxLarge the progress capsule is pushed out of that frame, and on the tallest card of a shelf it is partly (xxLarge) or fully (xxxLarge and up) clipped.

**Corrected fix:** (a) Do now: in EPGNowNextLine replace the computed constant with @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption2) private var reservedHeight: CGFloat = 22; both the populated frame (line 63) and the placeholder (line 67) keep using it. (b) Owner decision, and not via the global layoutScale. If wanted, add a separate text factor that only feeds the card-facing metrics (shelfPosterWidth/Height, categoryGridPosterWidth/Height, liveShelfIcon, liveShelfLabelWidth, liveGridIconSize, searchGrid/searchCard sizes and the matching prefetch sizes) and leave detail hero, episode thumbnail, season strip and spacings on the display scale. DashboardView and M3UDashboardView would read @Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize) and pass the factor (1.0 up to xxLarge, about 1.25 at xxxLarge, about 1.5 for isAccessibilitySize, capped so iPad stays at 1.0). A cheaper first step that needs no decision: widen only liveShelfLabelWidth relative to the icon on phones (for example icon 56, label about 72) so ordinary channel names stop hyphenating at the default size.

**API check:** ScaledMetric: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12151-12152, @available(iOS 14.0), init(wrappedValue:relativeTo:). EnvironmentValues.dynamicTypeSize: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:11899, extension @available(iOS 15.0). DynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:11878, on enum DynamicTypeSize @available(iOS 15.0). All below the iOS 18.0 target, no availability guard needed.

**Regression risks:** (a) is safe: placeholder and populated state still share one height, so the jump the 22 was introduced to prevent (commit 1cce013) does not return; cards get taller only above the default size. (b) changes image request sizes with the text size, so prefetch and render must read the same PosterMetrics from the environment (PosterMetricsKey.defaultValue at PosterMetrics.swift:75-79 has no text factor and would mismatch wherever the environment is not injected). Grid column counts change (three to two on phones at accessibility sizes), and a text-size change mid-session relays out every shelf and re-decodes posters. Applying the factor to the global layoutScale, as proposed, would enlarge detail hero and episode thumbnails and reduce text width there.

**How to verify:** (a) Live TV home with EPG data and -UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName UICTContentSizeCategoryXXXL: the progress capsule is fully visible under a one-line and a two-line channel name, and shelves do not change height when EPG data arrives. (b) If adopted: unit test the card metrics for a 402x874 window at factor 1.0 and 1.5 and assert the detail hero and episode thumbnail metrics are unchanged; screenshot Live TV, Movies and a category grid at XXXL and AccessibilityL.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-4 — VoiceOver reads movie and series cards as star glyph, rating, then title, never mentions watch progress, and reads the detail meta row as five separate fragments

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Movies home and grids, Series home and grids, Favorites, Movie detail, Series detail, Episode rows
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:500-545`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:472-517, 1495-1510`, `Views/RatingLabel.swift:39-52, 73-86`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:144-185`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:64-65`

**What the user perceives:** Swiping through a shelf, a VoiceOver user hears the star symbol's system description and a bare number before each title (for example "favorite, 8.1, Midnight Horizon, button"), with no hint that the number is a rating and nothing about a half-watched film. On a detail screen the line under the title is five stops: star, 8.1, 2024, clock, runtime.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODStreamCard and SeriesCard are plain VStacks inside a NavigationLink; the link label is composed from the children in view order: the PosterRatingBadge (Image(systemName: "star.fill") plus Text) sits in the poster ZStack before the title (VODView.swift:502-534). The progress bar is a Rectangle with no accessibility value (VODView.swift:512-522). RatingLabel and PosterRatingBadge expose the star image and the number separately (RatingLabel.swift:41-48, 75-80), and DetailHeroMetaRow is not grouped (DetailComponents.swift:151-183). The live channel card already does this correctly: EPGNowNextLine collapses itself into one labelled element inside the card button (EPGComponents.swift:64-65).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) RatingLabel.swift, both views: .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore).accessibilityLabel("\(L("movie.rating")) \(text)") (key exists in all languages). 2) VODStreamCard and SeriesCard, on the outer VStack: .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore).accessibilityLabel(label) where label joins stream.name, the rating phrase, the category name when present and, when watchProgress is set, a percent phrase built with existing keys (detail.watched). 3) DetailHeroMetaRow: .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore).accessibilityLabel([rating phrase, year, runtime].compactMap{$0}.joined(separator: ", ")). The label string is built only for realised cells of the lazy containers and does not touch the Equatable shelf rows. Existing UI tests locate the card through its inner static text and must switch to the button: UserFlowsUITests.swift:581 and ScreensUITests.swift:43, 100 use app.staticTexts["Midnight Horizon"]; replace with app.buttons.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label BEGINSWITH %@", ...)).

**APIs:** View.accessibilityElement(children:) (iOS 13.0); View.accessibilityLabel(_:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code structure matches. VODStreamCard and SeriesCard (Views/VODView.swift:500-545, Views/SeriesView.swift:472-517) are plain VStacks used as NavigationLink labels. The PosterRatingBadge (Image(systemName: "star.fill") + Text, Views/RatingLabel.swift:75-80) sits in the poster ZStack before the title Text. The progress bar is a bare Rectangle (VODView.swift:512-522) with no accessibility value. DetailHeroMetaRow (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:150-183) has no grouping, and its star and clock images are unlabeled SF Symbols. FlowMetaRow (SeriesView.swift:1495-1510) is the same pattern. The live card does group its EPG line (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:64-65). Supporting evidence for a merged label: the orchestrator's tour finds the poster with app.buttons.matching(label CONTAINS 'Midnight Horizon') (ScreensUITests.swift:353), i.e. the button label is more than the title. What I could not establish from code: the exact spoken order and the wording for the star ('favorite'). That is SwiftUI's default child merge and symbol description, and needs Accessibility Inspector or a device. Corrections to the fix: (1) the test impact is larger than the three lines cited. staticTexts lookups of card titles exist at UserFlowsUITests.swift:43, 51, 67, 173, 242, 247, 581, ScreensUITests.swift:100, 357 and ScreenshotsUITests.swift:34 (lines 43 and 321 are search results, which do not use these cards). (2) 'detail.watched' is 'Watched' and is used for episodes that are 95 percent or more complete (SeriesView.swift:1425-1426); gluing a percentage onto it is not a sound phrase in ten languages. (3) Severity: cards stay reachable and activatable; this is announcement quality.

**Corrected claim:** Movie and series cards expose the rating badge (star symbol plus bare number) ahead of the title in the card button's accessibility label, never expose watch progress, and the detail meta row is several separate unlabeled fragments (star, rating, year, clock, runtime). The exact spoken order and symbol wording need confirmation in Accessibility Inspector.

**Corrected fix:** 1) RatingLabel and PosterRatingBadge: .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore).accessibilityLabel("\(L("movie.rating")) \(text)"). 2) VODStreamCard and SeriesCard, on the outer VStack: .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore), .accessibilityLabel joining title, rating phrase and category when present, and progress as .accessibilityValue(Text(progress, format: .percent)) instead of a phrase built from 'detail.watched' (system-localized, no new string). 3) DetailHeroMetaRow: .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore).accessibilityLabel of the rating phrase, year and runtime joined by ', '. 4) Update all card-title staticTexts lookups listed in the reasons to a button query (label BEGINSWITH title), or add .accessibilityIdentifier to the card and query by that.

**API check:** View.accessibilityElement(children: AccessibilityChildBehavior = .ignore): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23737, extension @available(iOS 13.0). View.accessibilityLabel(_: Text): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:822, extension @available(iOS 14.0); the StringProtocol overload accessibilityLabel<S>(_ label: S) is declared in the same iOS 14.0 extension (line 828). accessibilityValue<S>(_ value: S) StringProtocol overload: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:65; I did not print its enclosing extension's availability. Localization keys 'movie.rating' ('Rating') and 'detail.watched' exist in all ten Localizable.strings.

**Regression risks:** UI tests that find cards by inner static text break (ten call sites listed above) until updated. The label string is built per realised cell only; the Equatable shelf rows and their == are untouched. Grouping RatingLabel also changes how the episode row meta line is read (FlowMetaRow uses it). If the card VStack is made a single element, any future child control inside the card would become unreachable.

**How to verify:** Before the change, dump app.debugDescription on Movies home or use Accessibility Inspector on a card to record the current button label (settles the order and 'favorite' question). After: one element per card with label 'Midnight Horizon, Rating 8.1', a percent value on a half-watched film, and one element for the detail meta row. Run UserFlowsUITests, ScreensUITests and ScreenshotsUITests. VoiceOver read-through on a device for wording in at least English and Turkish.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-5 — Six tappable surfaces are built with tap gestures instead of buttons, so VoiceOver does not announce them as actionable and Voice Control, Switch Control and Full Keyboard Access cannot target them

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Continue Watching row (all tabs), Series detail episode list, TV Guide grid, Channel schedule, Movie and Series detail hero
- Code: `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1390-1451`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:20-27, 143-170`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:59-64`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:103-122`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201`

**What the user perceives:** A VoiceOver user lands on the title of a Continue Watching card or an episode and hears only text, no "button"; title, duration, rating, watched state and plot of one episode are five separate stops. With Voice Control, "Show names" puts no label on these items and "Tap <episode name>" does nothing. Switch Control and an external keyboard skip them entirely. In the TV guide every programme and channel is plain text.

**Mechanism (finder):** HistoryCard is activated by .onTapGesture (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52). EpisodeDetailRow puts .onTapGesture on the text column only (SeriesView.swift:1447-1451). Guide programme cells use .onTapGesture (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:24-26) and the channel column uses LongPressGesture.exclusively(before: TapGesture()) (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169). Schedule rows use .onTapGesture inside a List (ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:62-63). The hero poster uses .onTapGesture (DetailComponents.swift:116-121). A gesture gives no button trait and no grouping; assistive technologies that enumerate actionable elements do not see these views. The full history grid already uses a real Button (WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201).

**Proposed fix (finder):** ContinueWatchingRow: Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item) }.buttonStyle(.plain), mirroring HistoryCardGridItem. EpisodeDetailRow: wrap thumbnail and text column together in one Button(.plain) and keep DownloadButton as a sibling (also makes the thumbnail tappable). ChannelEPGDetailView: Button { selected = programme } label: { row(programme) }.buttonStyle(.plain). Guide cells: keep the gestures (rows are Equatable and cheap) and add .accessibilityElement(children: .combine).accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton) to cells that have a programme; channel cell: the same two modifiers plus .accessibilityAction(named: L("epg.guide.title")) { onLongPress() } so the schedule is reachable without a long press. Hero poster: either a Button with a label or leave it decorative (see the CachedImage finding). No new strings are required.

**APIs:** View.accessibilityAddTraits(_:) with AccessibilityTraits.isButton (iOS 14.0 (trait iOS 13.0)); View.accessibilityElement(children: .combine) (iOS 13.0); View.accessibilityAction(named:_:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** All cited sites exist and are the only non-player tap gestures in Views/ (grep): Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52 (HistoryCard + .onTapGesture), Views/SeriesView.swift:1447-1451 (text column only, so the episode thumbnail at 1391-1414 is not tappable at all), Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:24-26 (programme cells) and 159-169 (LongPressGesture.exclusively(before: TapGesture()) on the channel cell), Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:62-63 (List rows), Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:116-121 (hero poster). The same card is already a real Button in the full history grid (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201), so the gesture in the row is an inconsistency. git log -S shows these date from the monorepo-move commit (the channel-cell gesture from 654cefc), with no comment marking them deliberate. Episode rows live in a LazyVStack (SeriesView.swift:1318), not a List, so two sibling buttons are safe. What code establishes: none of these carry the button trait, and their texts are separate VoiceOver stops; there is no pressed-state feedback either. What code does not establish: that Voice Control, Switch Control and Full Keyboard Access 'cannot target them'. SwiftUI may expose a tap gesture as a default accessibility action, so that part needs a device. Fix correction: L("epg.guide.title") is 'TV Guide', the title of the screen the user is already on; as the name of the action that opens one channel's schedule (EPGGuideView.swift:204-206: tap plays, long press sets detailChannel) it is misleading. No existing key fits, so 'no new strings are required' does not hold for that item.

**Corrected claim:** Five tappable surfaces outside the player are built with gestures instead of buttons (Continue Watching cards, episode rows, TV-guide programme cells, the TV-guide channel cell, channel-schedule rows) plus the detail hero poster. They have no button trait, no pressed feedback, and their texts are read as separate elements; the episode thumbnail is not tappable at all. Whether Voice Control, Switch Control and Full Keyboard Access skip them entirely is not established from code.

**Corrected fix:** ContinueWatchingRow: Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item) }.buttonStyle(.plain), as in HistoryCardGridItem. EpisodeDetailRow: one Button(.plain) around thumbnail + text column with .contentShape(Rectangle()) on the label, DownloadButton stays a sibling. ChannelEPGDetailView: Button { selected = programme } label: { row(programme) } with .id(rowID(programme)) kept on the button; try the default list button style with .tint(.primary) first so the row gets the system highlight, fall back to .plain. Guide programme cells: keep the gesture, and after it add .accessibilityElement(children: .combine).accessibilityAddTraits(cell.programme != nil ? .isButton : []). Guide channel cell: the same two modifiers plus .accessibilityAction(named:) for the schedule, with a new string (for example 'epg.a11y.show_schedule') added to all ten Localizable.strings without touching the tip keys. Hero poster: leave as is or make it a Button with a label; lowest priority.

**API check:** View.accessibilityAddTraits(_: AccessibilityTraits): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23208, extension @available(iOS 14.0). AccessibilityTraits.isButton: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4932, struct @available(iOS 13.0), a SetAlgebra so [] is valid for the no-programme case. View.accessibilityElement(children:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23737, iOS 13.0; AccessibilityChildBehavior.combine not printed separately. View.accessibilityAction(named: Text, _:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:24773, extension @available(iOS 13.0); the StringProtocol overload accessibilityAction<S>(named: S, _:) is at line 24797 in an iOS 14.0 extension, so passing L(...) compiles.

**Regression risks:** EPG guide rows stay Equatable (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:12-16, 139-141); accessibility modifiers add no state, and the action closure is captured exactly like the existing gesture closure. Wrapping the episode row in a Button changes the hit area (thumbnail becomes tappable) and must keep the DownloadButton outside the label. A Button in the schedule List changes row highlight and, with the default style, tints the title unless .tint(.primary) is set. A Button around HistoryCard inside the horizontal ScrollView adds a pressed state; .plain keeps the look. A new string must be added in ten languages. UI tests that tap Continue Watching or episode titles via staticTexts keep working, because Button children remain static texts.

**How to verify:** UI test: app.buttons containing the first Continue Watching title and an episode title exist (today only staticTexts do), and tapping an episode thumbnail starts playback. Accessibility Inspector on Series detail, the TV Guide and a channel schedule: each row or cell is one element with the button trait; the channel cell lists the schedule action. On a device, before and after: Voice Control 'Show names', Switch Control scanning and Full Keyboard Access Tab navigation on the Continue Watching row and an episode list, to settle whether those were unreachable.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-6 — Seven icon-only buttons have no label of their own: the Favorites link and the favourite toggles rely on the star symbol's system description, with no on/off state and not in the in-app language

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series navigation bar, Movie detail, Series detail, Playlist list, TV Guide, Settings, Poster viewer, Episode download button
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:234-238`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:87-90`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:881-886`, `ContentView.swift:91-95`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:279-284`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:174-178`, `Views/Components/FullscreenImageViewer.swift:16-24`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:86-110`, `../another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:51-52, 176, 190, 212`

**What the user perceives:** The star in the navigation bar that opens the Favorites list and the star that marks a film as favourite are both announced through the generic description of the star symbol, the toggle sounds identical whether the film is a favourite or not, and the wording follows the device language instead of the language chosen in the app. Voice Control users have to guess the name. The compact download button on an episode row is an icon whose meaning (download, queued, downloaded, failed) is never spoken.

**Mechanism (finder):** These buttons contain only Image(systemName:) and no .accessibilityLabel: DashboardView.swift:234-238 (the M3U twin has one at M3UChannelsView.swift:82), MovieDetailView.swift:87-90, SeriesView.swift:881-886, ContentView.swift:91-95, EPGGuideView.swift:279-284, PlaylistSettingsView.swift:174-178, FullscreenImageViewer.swift:16-24. The UI test says so itself: "Toolbar star button has no localized label - locate by symbol-derived identifier" (ScreensUITests.swift:51-52). DownloadButton drops its Text when compact (DownloadButton.swift:105-109), leaving only the state icon. The neighbouring toolbar buttons are labelled correctly (LiveStreamsView.swift:116, 126, 136).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add labels from keys that already exist: DashboardView star link .accessibilityLabel(L("favorites.title")); detail toggles .accessibilityLabel(L(isFavorite ? "favorites.remove" : "favorites.add")); playlist plus .accessibilityLabel(L("playlists.empty.add_button")); guide refresh .accessibilityLabel(L("epg.refresh")); viewer close .accessibilityLabel(L("common.close")); DownloadButton.button(icon:title:): .accessibilityLabel(title) on the HStack so the compact variant speaks its state. The settings refresh icon needs a label too (no exact key exists; it is one modifier next to, not inside, the tip-jar work). Give the star and plus buttons explicit .accessibilityIdentifier values and point ScreensUITests.swift:52, 176, 190, 212 at them, so the tests no longer depend on the symbol name.

**APIs:** View.accessibilityLabel(_:) (iOS 14.0); View.accessibilityIdentifier(_:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read every cited site. All seven buttons have a bare Image(systemName:) label and no .accessibilityLabel: Views/DashboardView.swift:234-238 (star NavigationLink), Views/MovieDetailView.swift:87-90 and Views/SeriesView.swift:881-886 (star / star.fill toggle), ContentView.swift:91-95 (plus), Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:279-284 (refresh), Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:174-178 (refresh in a section header), Views/Components/FullscreenImageViewer.swift:16-24 (xmark). The M3U twin is labelled (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:82), as are the neighbouring toolbar buttons (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:116,126,136), so this is an omission, not a decision. The UI test confirms it (another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:51-52 looks the button up as "star.fill"; 176, 190, 212 use "plus"). The in-app language point holds: L() reads a per-language bundle (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:48-64) and the app only sets \.locale and \.layoutDirection (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:64-65), so system-supplied symbol descriptions stay in the device language. DownloadButton drops its Text when compact (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:105-109) and the compact variant is used on every episode row (Views/SeriesView.swift:1470). Two corrections. (1) These buttons are not silent: SwiftUI gives a symbol image a system description, so plus, xmark and arrow.clockwise are most likely already announced sensibly in the device language. The real gaps are the favourite toggle (same announcement for star and star.fill, so no on/off state), the wrong language, and the compact download states. "Never spoken" for the download icon is not provable from code. (2) The proposed .accessibilityLabel(title) on the HStack inside the button label is the wrong attachment point: that HStack is not an accessibility element.

**Corrected claim:** Seven icon-only buttons rely on the system description of their SF Symbol instead of an app label. The favourite toggles on movie and series detail therefore announce the same thing whether the item is a favourite or not, the wording follows the device language rather than the in-app language, and the compact episode download button exposes its state (download, queued, downloaded, retry) only through whatever description the system has for the icon. The plus, close and refresh buttons most likely already get a usable system label; for them the gain is language consistency and stable UI-test lookups.

**Corrected fix:** Use the existing keys. DashboardView.swift:238: .accessibilityLabel(L("favorites.title")) on the NavigationLink. MovieDetailView.swift:90 and SeriesView.swift:886: .accessibilityLabel(L(isFavorite ? "favorites.remove" : "favorites.add")) on the Button. ContentView.swift:95: .accessibilityLabel(L("playlists.empty.add_button")). EPGGuideView.swift:283: .accessibilityLabel(L("epg.refresh")). FullscreenImageViewer.swift:23: .accessibilityLabel(L("common.close")). DownloadButton: attach the label to the Button, not the inner HStack: compute the state title once and add .accessibilityLabel(stateTitle) after .buttonStyle(.plain) at DownloadButton.swift:81 (for .downloading keep the percent text). Leave the settings refresh icon (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:177) alone: no fitting key exists, a new one would have to be added to the ten Localizable.strings files that carry the uncommitted tip keys, and arrow.clockwise most likely already has a usable system label. Give the star link and the plus button explicit .accessibilityIdentifier values and point ScreensUITests.swift:52, 176, 190, 212 at them in the same change, because the "star.fill" / "plus" lookups may stop matching once a label is set.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: View.accessibilityLabel<S: StringProtocol>(_:) in an extension marked @available(iOS 14.0, ...) (line 819-828). View.accessibilityIdentifier(_ identifier: String) @available(iOS 14.0, ...) (line 17319-17321). Keys favorites.title, favorites.add, favorites.remove, playlists.empty.add_button, epg.refresh, common.close exist in Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings (lines 132, 137, 138, 22, 524, 6).

**Regression risks:** ScreensUITests looks buttons up by "star.fill" and "plus"; these may fail after labels are added unless the identifiers and the test lines change together. ScreensUITests.swift is already modified in the working tree (the orchestrator's ZZScreenTourUITests), so edit only the four cited lines. With the settings icon left out, no tip-jar file is touched. No effect on layout or scrolling.

**How to verify:** Accessibility Inspector on the simulator: the Movies navigation-bar star reads "Favorites"; the movie detail star reads "Add to Favorites" and, after a tap, "Remove from Favorites"; an episode row's compact download button reads "Download" / "Downloaded". Switch the in-app language to Turkish with the device in English and confirm the labels follow the app. Run ScreensUITests after the identifier change.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-7 — The selected search filter, season and guide day are shown by colour only, and the sort menus draw their own checkmarks, so the current selection is never announced

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search, Series detail, TV Guide, Live, Movies, Series category grids (sort and filter menu)
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:27-40`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:441-466`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:107-119`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:642-673`, `Views/VODView.swift:750-776`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:691-717`, `Views/Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:273`

**What the user perceives:** VoiceOver reads "All, button; Live TV, button; Movies, button" without saying which filter is active; the same for Season 1 / Season 2 and Yesterday / Today / Tomorrow. In the sort menu an active filter is read as the word for the checkmark symbol followed by the title instead of as a selected item. The filter button itself gives no sign that a filter is active (only the icon is filled).

**Mechanism (finder):** The chips are Buttons whose selection is expressed through background and foreground colour only (SearchView.swift:33-38, DetailComponents.swift:450-463, EPGGuideView.swift:113-116); no .isSelected trait is added. The filter rows in the three sort menus are Buttons that swap Text for Label(..., systemImage: "checkmark") (LiveStreamsView.swift:643-660, VODView.swift:753-761, SeriesView.swift:694-702). The menu button label is a constant L("sort.title") (LiveStreamsView.swift:673). The player sheet already uses the right pattern (PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:273).

**Proposed fix (finder):** .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : []) on the three chip buttons. In the menus replace each Button/checkmark pair by a Toggle, which Menu renders with the system checkmark and a spoken state: Toggle(L("filter.catchup"), isOn: Binding(get: { filter.contains(.catchup) }, set: { _ in filter.formSymmetricDifference(.catchup) })); same for hasEPG, file types and genres. On the menu label add .accessibilityValue(isFilterActive ? L("filter.title") : ""). The Picker for the sort order is already native and stays.

**APIs:** AccessibilityTraits.isSelected (iOS 13.0); Toggle (inside Menu) (iOS 13.0 (Menu iOS 14.0)); View.accessibilityValue(_:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Chips: Views/SearchView.swift:27-40 (selection through background, foreground and font weight only), Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:441-466 (season capsule fill only), Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:107-119 (day capsule colour and weight only). None adds .isSelected; a grep shows the only isSelected trait outside the player is Views/Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:273. Screenshot iphone-light/Q05-search-filter-movies.png confirms the selected chip differs only by fill colour. Menus: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:642-660, Views/VODView.swift:750-761, Views/SeriesView.swift:691-702 swap Text for Label(..., systemImage: "checkmark") inside a Button, so the selected state is an icon, not a menu-item state. Screenshot iphone-dark/L04-live-category-sort-menu.png shows the consequence on iOS 26: the Picker rows above use the system checkmark column plus an icon column, while the filter rows sit in a different column, so a hand-drawn checkmark would not line up with the Picker's. History: these rows came in with 654cefc ("add catalog sort/filter ..."); no comment marks the Button form as deliberate. Corrections: how VoiceOver reads the checkmark Label inside a menu item ("checkmark, title" versus title only) cannot be established from code; either way no selected state is exposed. The proposed .accessibilityValue(isFilterActive ? L("filter.title") : "") would read "Sort, Filter", which does not say that a filter is active.

**Corrected claim:** The selected search scope chip, season chip and guide day chip expose their selection only visually (no selected trait), and the filter rows of the three sort menus are plain Buttons that draw a checkmark icon instead of carrying a menu-item on/off state. Assistive technologies get no selected state, and on iOS 26 the filter rows do not use the same checkmark column as the system Picker above them.

**Corrected fix:** Chips: .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : []) on the Button at SearchView.swift:40, DetailComponents.swift:465 and EPGGuideView.swift:118. Menus: replace each Button/checkmark pair with a Toggle, e.g. Toggle(L("filter.catchup"), isOn: Binding(get: { filter.contains(.catchup) }, set: { _ in filter.formSymmetricDifference(.catchup) })), likewise hasEPG, and Toggle(ext.uppercased(), isOn: Binding(get: { fileTypeFilter.contains(ext) }, set: { _ in toggleFileType(ext) })) and the genre equivalent with toggleGenre(genre). Keep the Picker and the destructive "Clear filter" button. Drop the accessibilityValue on the menu button, or add a dedicated "filter active" string in all ten languages if the owner wants the active state spoken; that is optional and a small product decision.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface: struct AccessibilityTraits @available(iOS 13.0, ...) with static let isSelected (line 4926-4934). SwiftUI.swiftinterface: View.accessibilityAddTraits(_:) @available(iOS 14.0, ...) (line 23206-23208); Toggle where Label == Text, init<S: StringProtocol>(_ title: S, isOn: Binding<Bool>) in an extension @available(iOS 13.0, ...) (line 5047-5054); View.accessibilityValue<S: StringProtocol>(_:) @available(iOS 14.0, ...) (line 56-65). No iOS 26-only API involved.

**Regression risks:** The Toggle setters must keep calling the existing mutation paths (formSymmetricDifference, toggleFileType, toggleGenre) so the .task(id:) recompute triggers (LiveStreamsView.swift:629-631 and the twins) still fire; off-main filtering is untouched. The checkmark moves from the icon position to the system checkmark column, a small visible change that should be checked in a screenshot on iOS 18 and iOS 26. The menu still closes after a selection, as it does today.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test: after tapping the Movies chip in Search, app.buttons["Movies"].isSelected is true and app.buttons["All"].isSelected is false; same for a season chip and a guide day chip. Screenshot the Live category sort menu with "Has EPG" active and confirm its checkmark lines up with the Picker's. Confirm the grid still re-filters after toggling.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-8 — Shelf titles and detail section titles are not marked as headings, so VoiceOver users cannot jump between categories and must swipe through every card of a shelf

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels, Continue Watching, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367`, `Views/VODView.swift:315-326, 418-429`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:292-303, 394-405, 877, 1017-1018`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:337-348`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:125-129, 360-362`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:83`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:124-126`

**What the user perceives:** With a real catalog (hundreds of categories, each a horizontal shelf of hundreds of items) the Headings rotor is empty on the three home screens: the only way from one category to the next is to swipe past every card in between. On a detail screen the navigation title is empty until the user scrolls, and neither the film title nor "Plot" or "Seasons" is a heading, so nothing announces what screen this is.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each shelf header is a NavigationLink whose label is Text(.headline) plus a chevron image, with no header trait (LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367 and the six equivalent sites). The detail screens set navigationTitle to an empty string until 240 pt of scroll (MovieDetailView.swift:83, SeriesView.swift:877) and the hero title, "Plot" and "Seasons" are plain Text (DetailComponents.swift:125-129, 360-362; SeriesView.swift:1017). The TV guide's category header already does it (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:124-126).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) to the seven header NavigationLinks (the element stays a button and gains the heading trait) and .accessibilityHidden(true) to the chevron image inside them. Add .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) to the hero title, the Plot title and the Seasons title. All of this is static metadata; it does not affect the Equatable shelf rows or scrolling.

**APIs:** AccessibilityTraits.isHeader (iOS 13.0); View.accessibilityHidden(_:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** All cited shelf headers are a NavigationLink whose label is HStack { Text(.headline); Image(systemName: "chevron.right") } with no header trait: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367, Views/VODView.swift:315-326 and 418-429, Views/SeriesView.swift:292-303 and 394-405, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:337-348, Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44. Detail screens: navigationTitle is "" until showNavTitle (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:83, Views/SeriesView.swift:877); the hero title (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:125-129), the Plot title (360-362) and the Seasons title (Views/SeriesView.swift:1017-1018) are plain Text. A grep finds .isHeader in browse code only at Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:126, so the app already uses the pattern once. No comment or commit marks the omission as deliberate. Two points in the description are overstated and lower the severity: the large navigation title of each tab is a heading by default, so the rotor is not literally empty, and each home screen already has a labelled "Jump to category" toolbar button (LiveStreamsView.swift:136, VODView.swift:131, SeriesView.swift:132), so swiping through every card is not the only route. The claim itself (shelf and section titles are not headings) and the fix stand.

**Corrected claim:** Shelf titles on the Live TV, Movies, Series and M3U home screens, the Continue Watching title, and the hero / Plot / Seasons titles on detail screens are not marked as headings, so the VoiceOver Headings rotor cannot step from shelf to shelf or announce the detail screen's sections. Users can still reach a category through the "Jump to category" button, so this is a missing convenience that Apple's own shelf UIs provide, not a blocker.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) on the seven header NavigationLinks (they stay buttons and gain the heading trait) and .accessibilityHidden(true) on the chevron image inside each; .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) on the hero title (DetailComponents.swift:125), the Plot title (DetailComponents.swift:360) and the Seasons title (SeriesView.swift:1017).

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface: AccessibilityTraits.isHeader, struct @available(iOS 13.0, ...) (line 4926-4933). SwiftUI.swiftinterface: View.accessibilityAddTraits(_:) @available(iOS 14.0, ...) (line 23206-23208); View.accessibilityHidden(_ hidden: Bool) @available(iOS 14.0, ...) (line 13250-13252).

**Regression risks:** None for performance: the modifiers are static and sit inside the Equatable shelf rows without changing their inputs. Rows live in lazy stacks, so the rotor only reaches shelves that are currently realized; that is the standard behaviour for lazy content.

**How to verify:** Accessibility Inspector on the simulator: each shelf title shows traits Button + Header and the chevron is no longer part of its label; the movie title, "Plot" and "Seasons" show Header. On a device: VoiceOver rotor set to Headings steps News -> Sports -> Entertainment on Live TV.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-9 — Opening and closing the in-window player posts no screen-change to VoiceOver, so focus is left on a card that has just been hidden and is not brought back afterwards

- Verdict: **undecidable** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Hand-off into the player from every tab, Return from the player to the catalog
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:42-44, 90, 92-113`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:20-22, 50, 52-73`, `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:51-56, 70-77, 89-99`

**What the user perceives:** A VoiceOver user double-taps a channel: playback starts, but there is no screen-change sound and the cursor stays where the card was, on an element that no longer exists for VoiceOver; they have to touch the screen to find the player. After closing or minimizing the player the cursor does not return to the catalog. A system full-screen cover does both automatically.

**Mechanism (finder):** The player is a sibling view in the dashboard ZStack, not a presentation (DashboardView.swift:92-113). The catalog is hidden with .accessibilityHidden(isPlayerCoveringContent) (DashboardView.swift:90), which removes the focused element, and nothing tells VoiceOver that the screen changed: the only UIAccessibility.post calls in the app are announcements inside PlayerView, and there is no AccessibilityFocusState anywhere. PlayerOverlayController.present/dismiss/minimize/expand only flip published state (PlayerOverlayController.swift:54-55, 75, 91, 98).

**Proposed fix (finder):** In DashboardView and M3UDashboardView add .onChange(of: isPlayerCoveringContent) { _, _ in UIAccessibility.post(notification: .screenChanged, argument: nil) }. VoiceOver then plays the screen-change cue and moves to the first element of whatever is now on top (the player when it opens or expands, the catalog when it closes or minimizes). This stays outside the player's own code. Restoring focus to the exact originating card would need a per-card AccessibilityFocusState and is not worth its cost in the large grids.

**APIs:** UIAccessibility.post(notification: .screenChanged, argument:) (iOS 3.0 (UIAccessibilityScreenChangedNotification))

**Verifier reasons:** What the code establishes: the player is a sibling in the dashboard ZStack, not a presentation (Views/DashboardView.swift:92-113); the catalog is removed from accessibility with .accessibilityHidden(isPlayerCoveringContent) (DashboardView.swift:90, mirrored in Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:50); PlayerOverlayController only flips published state (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:54-55, 75, 91, 98); a grep finds no .screenChanged or .layoutChanged post and no AccessibilityFocusState anywhere, and every UIAccessibility.post in the app is an .announcement inside PlayerView. So no screen-change notification is sent; that is certain. What it does not establish: where the VoiceOver cursor ends up. When the focused element leaves the tree VoiceOver normally re-homes the cursor by itself, so "focus is left on a card that no longer exists" and "they have to touch the screen" are assumptions, and the finding itself rates its evidence as needs-device. The accessibilityHidden line and the escape action arrived last week in 2ec2c18, so this area was considered deliberately and stopped short of posting a notification. The proposed fix also has a timing flaw: onChange(of: isPlayerCoveringContent) runs in the same update that inserts the overlay (which then fades in over 0.14 s, DashboardView.swift:121), so a notification posted there can be processed before the accessibility tree contains the player.

**Corrected claim:** Opening, expanding, minimizing and closing the in-window player sends no screen-change notification to VoiceOver. Whether the cursor is stranded, or simply re-homes without the screen-change cue, has to be observed on a device with VoiceOver.

**Corrected fix:** Only if the device check shows a stranded or badly placed cursor: in DashboardView and M3UDashboardView add .onChange(of: isPlayerCoveringContent) and post UIAccessibility.post(notification: .screenChanged, argument: nil) after the overlay has been inserted (a short deferred Task, roughly 0.2-0.3 s, tuned on the device), guarded by UIAccessibility.isVoiceOverRunning. Keep it in the dashboards, outside the player files. Returning focus to the originating card is not worth a per-card focus state.

**API check:** UIKit Headers/UIAccessibilityConstants.h:129 UIAccessibilityScreenChangedNotification ("posted when a new view appears that encompasses a major portion of the screen"; optional argument is the element to move to); UIAccessibility.h:521 UIAccessibilityPostNotification. The Swift spelling UIAccessibility.post(notification:argument:) is already used and compiles in this code base (Views/PlayerView.swift:1405, 3743, 4731).

**Regression risks:** A screen-change post makes VoiceOver move to the first element of the window, which could pull focus away from where the player wants it (for example its surface element, PlayerView.swift:4611-4618) or interrupt the player's own announcements. Posting too early lands the cursor on the outgoing screen. Do not wrap item.root in a condition: the comments at DashboardView.swift:105-107 and 116-117 say that remounts PlayerView and tears playback down.

**How to verify:** Device with VoiceOver on (the simulator has none). 1) Focus a channel card on Live TV and double-tap: note whether a screen-change cue plays and which element is focused once playback starts, and whether a right swipe moves inside the player. 2) Two-finger scrub to minimize: note where the cursor lands (catalog, mini card or nothing). 3) Close the player from fullscreen: same. 4) Expand from the mini card: same. If the cursor is on a sensible element in all four cases, close the finding; otherwise apply the deferred post and repeat.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-10 — Actions that exist only behind a long press (favourite an M3U channel, cancel or delete a download, open a channel's schedule) have no accessibility action

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U channels and groups, Movie detail download button, Episode rows, TV Guide channel column
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:78-83, 145-202`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:188-203`

**What the user perceives:** For a VoiceOver or Switch Control user a finished download reads "Downloaded, button" and activating it does nothing; nothing says that deleting or cancelling exists. Adding an M3U channel to favourites is impossible to discover (the empty Favorites screen says "Long press a channel"). The Actions rotor is empty on all of these.

**Mechanism (finder):** M3UChannelCard offers favourite and download only in .contextMenu (M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475). DownloadButton ignores taps while downloading, queued or completed and puts cancel/delete in .contextMenu (DownloadButton.swift:82, 195-200). The guide's channel cell opens the schedule on a 0.5 s LongPressGesture (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169). Context menus and custom gestures are not published as accessibility custom actions. By contrast the list rows that use .swipeActions (DownloadsView.swift:188-203, CategoryPickerSheet.swift:122-135, ContentView.swift:243-252) get their actions for free.

**Proposed fix (finder):** DownloadButton (its state is already observed through @Query): .accessibilityAction(named: L("download.cancel")) { manager.cancel(id: id) } while downloading or queued, and .accessibilityAction(named: L("download.delete")) { Task { await manager.delete(id: id) } } when completed or failed. M3UChannelCard: .accessibilityAction(named: L(isFav ? "favorites.remove" : "favorites.add")) { Task { await M3UFavoriteStore.shared.toggle(channel: channel) } } with isFav read once in body exactly like the menu does (M3UChannelsView.swift:451), which keeps the deliberate decision not to observe the store per card; announce the result with UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, ...) because the action name can be stale until the card re-renders. Guide channel cell: .accessibilityAction(named: L("epg.guide.title")) { onLongPress() }. All keys exist.

**APIs:** View.accessibilityAction(named:_:) (iOS 13.0); UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, argument:) (iOS 4.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts check out. M3UChannelCard offers favourite and download only in .contextMenu (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-475). DownloadButton's primaryAction does nothing while downloading, queued or completed and puts cancel / delete in .contextMenu (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:82, 195-200; the Turkish comments say context menu is the intended route). The guide's channel cell opens the schedule on a 0.5 s LongPressGesture (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:159-169, wired at Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:204-206). A grep finds no accessibilityAction outside the player and the dashboards' escape action. Corrections. (1) "Activating it does nothing" and "impossible to discover" are overstated: VoiceOver can perform a long press on the focused element (double-tap and hold), which opens a context menu and triggers the long-press gesture, and Switch Control offers tap-and-hold. The gap is that nothing announces these actions and the Actions rotor is empty. M3U favourites can also be toggled from the player (M3UChannelsView.swift:715-717). (2) The guide channel cell is an HStack with a gesture and no accessibility element, button trait or label of its own (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:146-169), so a named action has nothing dependable to attach to without combining the cell first. (3) L("epg.guide.title") ("TV Guide") is a misleading action name inside the TV Guide. (4) .contextMenu's builder runs when the card's body runs, so reading isFavorite in body costs the same as today; the action name can go stale exactly as the existing menu label can.

**Corrected claim:** Cancel / delete on the download button, favourite on an M3U channel card and "open this channel's schedule" in the TV guide are reachable only through a long press. Assistive technologies can perform that long press, but nothing announces that it exists and none of these is offered as an accessibility action; the guide's channel cell is not even exposed as a single button.

**Corrected fix:** DownloadButton (state already comes from its @Query): on the Button add .accessibilityAction(named: L("download.cancel")) { manager.cancel(id: id) } while downloading or queued, and .accessibilityAction(named: L("download.delete")) { Task { await manager.delete(id: id) } } when completed or failed (apply through a small switch on state so only the valid action is present). M3UChannelCard: read isFavorite once in body as the menu does (M3UChannelsView.swift:451) and add .accessibilityAction(named: L(isFavorite ? "favorites.remove" : "favorites.add")) { Task { await M3UFavoriteStore.shared.toggle(channel: channel) } }; keep the store unobserved per card as the comment at 447-450 requires, and announce the outcome with UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, ...) since the name can be stale. Guide channel cell: .accessibilityElement(children: .combine), .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton), .accessibilityAction { onTap() } and .accessibilityAction(named: <schedule label>) { onLongPress() }; use a dedicated string for the action name (a new key in all ten languages) rather than "TV Guide", or accept "TV Guide" as a stopgap; that wording is the owner's call. Download for M3U VOD items stays context-menu only: exposing it would need a per-card @Query, which the comment at DownloadButton.swift:207-210 deliberately avoids.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: View.accessibilityAction<S: StringProtocol>(named: S, _ handler:) in an extension @available(iOS 14.0, ...) (line 24790-24797); the Text-named variant and accessibilityAction(_ actionKind: = .default, _:) @available(iOS 13.0, ...) (line 24770-24773); View.accessibilityElement(children:) @available(iOS 13.0, ...) (line 23735-23737); AccessibilityTraits.isButton (SwiftUICore line 4932, iOS 13.0). UIKit Headers/UIAccessibilityConstants.h:143 UIAccessibilityAnnouncementNotification API_AVAILABLE(ios(4.0)). manager.cancel(id:), manager.delete(id:) and M3UFavoriteStore.shared.toggle(channel:) exist (DownloadButton.swift:154, 160; Models/M3UFavoriteStore.swift:42). Keys download.cancel, download.delete, favorites.add, favorites.remove exist.

**Regression risks:** M3UChannelCard: do not add @ObservedObject on the favourite store (the comment at M3UChannelsView.swift:447-450 records that it re-rendered thousands of cards). EPGChannelColumnCell is Equatable on row and metrics so the sticky column can move without rebuilding (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:130-141); the accessibility modifiers must not add inputs to that comparison, and combining children must be checked not to disturb the tap / long-press gesture or guide scrolling. A new string key touches the Localizable.strings files that hold the uncommitted tip keys; add lines only.

**How to verify:** Accessibility Inspector on the simulator: a finished DownloadButton lists Delete, a downloading one lists Cancel, an M3U card lists Add to Favorites, a guide channel cell is one Button element with a schedule action; performing each from the inspector changes the state or opens the schedule. On a device: VoiceOver Actions rotor shows the same, and scrolling the guide with VoiceOver off is as smooth as before.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-11 — Arabic chosen inside the app is applied only through the SwiftUI layoutDirection, and three strings plus one glyph ignore language and direction

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Whole app when the in-app language differs from the device language, Movie and Series detail, TV Guide
- Code: `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:56-67`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:157, 265, 499-511`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:103-106`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:183-193`, `../another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:497-504`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: If verification shows UIKit chrome stays left-to-right: is a fully mirrored UI for in-app Arabic on a non-Arabic device required, or is in-app Arabic documented as text-only and the system per-app language setting recommended instead?

**What the user perceives:** Certain: the trailer button says "Fragman" and series runtimes read "45 dk" / "1s 30dk" in every language including Arabic and English; the collapsed-category chevron in the TV guide points right in Arabic too. To be confirmed on a simulator: a user whose phone is in English or Turkish and who picks Arabic in Settings may get mirrored content under navigation bars, back swipe, tab order, search field and swipe actions that still run left to right.

**Mechanism (finder):** AppRootView sets .environment(\.layoutDirection, ...) and .environment(\.locale, ...) from the in-app choice (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:60-66) and nothing at UIKit level (no semanticContentAttribute anywhere). UIKit-backed chrome takes its direction from the process language, which follows the device. The only right-to-left test relaunches with -AppleLanguages (ar) (UserFlowsUITests.swift:497-504), i.e. the case where UIKit is already right-to-left; the in-app switch on a left-to-right device is untested and there is no Arabic screenshot variant. Hard-coded Turkish: "Fragman" (DetailComponents.swift:265) although movie.trailer exists in all ten languages; "dk"/"s" (DetailComponents.swift:502-508). String(format: "%.1f") (DetailComponents.swift:157) and date.formatted (EPGComponents.swift:185-186) use the device locale, not the app locale. EPGCategoryHeader rotates chevron.down by -90 degrees (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:103-106); a rotation is not mirrored.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) L("movie.trailer") at DetailComponents.swift:265; build the runtime with Duration/Measurement formatting or the existing epg.detail.minutes_format key. 2) Mirror the rotation: .rotationEffect(.degrees(collapsed ? (layoutDirection == .rightToLeft ? 90 : -90) : 0)). 3) First verify with device language English and in-app Arabic. If the chrome is not mirrored, set the UIKit side where the language is applied: UIView.appearance().semanticContentAttribute = selected == "system" ? .unspecified : (isRTL ? .forceRightToLeft : .forceLeftToRight) before the .id(selectedLanguage) rebuild, and re-run the player tests because the player pins several subtrees to left-to-right on purpose. The hand-written chevron.right and arrow.up.right symbols need no change (see healthy).

**APIs:** UIView.semanticContentAttribute (via UIView.appearance()) (iOS 9.0); EnvironmentValues.layoutDirection (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read another_iptv_playerApp.swift:56-67, Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:157, 265, 499-511, Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:100-127, Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:183-193, Localization/LocalizationManager.swift, ../another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:389-504.

CONFIRMED parts: (a) DetailComponents.swift:265 passes the literal "Fragman"; the key movie.trailer exists in all ten Localizable.strings and is referenced by no Swift file (grep), so it is an orphaned key, not a deliberate choice. (b) DetailFormatting.seriesRuntime (DetailComponents.swift:502-508) builds "\(h)s \(m)dk" / "\(minutes) dk"; used at Views/SeriesView.swift:833, so every series detail shows Turkish units in every language.

REFUTED part: the TV-guide chevron. SwiftUI mirrors rotationEffect under right-to-left by itself. In the iOS 26.0 simulator runtime's SwiftUICore binary, `_RotationEffect.Data.init(_:size:layoutDirection:)` (0x21ac6c) selects `-angle` and `width - anchor.x*width` when layoutDirection != .leftToRight (fcsel on the layoutDirection byte). So `.rotationEffect(.degrees(collapsed ? -90 : 0))` at EPGGuideRowViews.swift:106 already points the other way in Arabic, and the proposed manual negation would double-flip it and create the bug it claims to fix.

WRONG detail: `String(format: "%.1f")` (DetailComponents.swift:157) is locale-independent (no locale argument), not device-locale; L() also formats with locale nil (LocalizationManager.swift:137), so numbers are consistently Latin/dot app-wide. EPGTimeFormat.time uses the device locale and its comment says so (EPGComponents.swift:184); keeping the device's 12/24-hour preference is defensible, not a defect.

UNDECIDABLE part (headline): it is true that the app sets nothing at UIKit level (no semanticContentAttribute anywhere) and that the only RTL tests launch with -AppleLanguages (ar) (UserFlowsUITests.swift:497-504). But whether the bars stay left-to-right is not established: the SwiftUI binary itself references setSemanticContentAttribute:, setLayoutDirection:, UIViewController/UIPresentationController traitOverrides and a LayoutDirection <-> UITraitEnvironmentLayoutDirection bridge, so SwiftUI may already carry the environment value into its own navigation, tab and list hosts. Only a run settles it. What is certain regardless of direction: system-supplied strings (Back, Search placeholder, Cancel, Delete swipe, Edit/Done) follow the device language, not the in-app choice.

**Corrected claim:** Two hard-coded Turkish strings ignore the app language: the trailer button ("Fragman") and the series runtime units ("dk" / "s"). The guide chevron is not a defect (SwiftUI mirrors rotationEffect in right-to-left). Whether in-app Arabic on a non-Arabic device leaves navigation bars, tab order, back swipe, search field and swipe actions left-to-right is unverified and needs a simulator run; system-supplied strings will stay in the device language either way.

**Corrected fix:** 1) DetailComponents.swift:265: title: L("movie.trailer"). 2) seriesRuntime: format with the app language, e.g. Duration.seconds(minutes * 60).formatted(.units(allowed: [.hours, .minutes], width: .narrow).locale(Locale(identifier: <effective app language code>))); it needs a small nonisolated accessor for the effective language code (the existing systemLanguageCode() is private). Do not reuse epg.detail.minutes_format alone: there is no hours key. Keep the pass-through for server strings that already contain "m"/"h" (line 501). 3) Leave the chevron rotation as is. 4) Do NOT pre-approve UIView.appearance().semanticContentAttribute: first run English device + in-app Arabic. If chrome is not mirrored, this is a product decision (drop the in-app picker in favour of the system per-app language setting, which iOS offers automatically because the bundle ships ten localizations and which also translates system strings; or accept text-only Arabic). The appearance-proxy route is a last resort: it is global (reaches the player's UIKit views, AVKit route picker, StoreKit sheets from the tip jar), does not update views already in the window, and the player deliberately pins subtrees to left-to-right.

**API check:** Duration.UnitsFormatStyle: Foundation swiftinterface line 4209, iOS 16.0; `.locale(_:)` line 4314; `static func units(allowed:width:...)` line 4337. EnvironmentValues.layoutDirection: SwiftUICore line 57, iOS 13.0. UIView.semanticContentAttribute: UIView.h:173, API_AVAILABLE(ios(9.0)) (exists, but not recommended here). rotationEffect RTL mirroring: verified by disassembly of SwiftUICore `_RotationEffect.Data.init(_:size:layoutDirection:)` in the iOS 26.0 simulator runtime, not by a run.

**Regression risks:** String fixes: none beyond a changed runtime label ("1h 30m" instead of "1s 30dk"); Turkish output becomes "1 sa 30 dk". Negating the chevron angle as originally proposed would break Arabic. UIView.appearance() would leak into player/AirPlay UIKit views and StoreKit UI used by the owner's tip-jar work.

**How to verify:** Unit test seriesRuntime("45") and ("90") with app language en, tr, ar. Simulator: launch with -AppleLanguages (en) and UserDefaults app.selected_language = ar; screenshot Live TV, a category grid, a movie detail, Search, Settings and the TV Guide with one category collapsed. Check: back button side, large-title alignment, tab order, search field alignment, swipe-action edge, edge-swipe-back side, sheet content direction, collapsed chevron pointing left. Repeat the mirror case (device Arabic, in-app English).
