## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-12 — The TV guide, the channel schedule and several list rows use fixed frames and one-line limits that do not reflow at large text sizes

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide, Channel schedule, Search results, Category picker, Settings value rows
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:197-212`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:40-51, 77-82, 107-119, 148-156`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309-312`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:96-110`, `Views/SearchView.swift:319-322`, `Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:106-109`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-201, 239-258, 265-291`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:161-199`

**What the user perceives:** In the guide the channel names are already truncated at the default size ("World New...", "Busi-ness...") and at larger sizes two lines of caption no longer fit the 56 pt row. In the schedule a 12-hour time such as "10:00 AM" does not fit the 52 pt time column. In Search and the category picker a long title is cut after one line however large the text is, where Apple's lists wrap. Settings rows squeeze label and value side by side (server URL, source URL).

**Mechanism (finder):** EPGGuideMetrics hard-codes rowHeight 56, axisHeight 28, headerHeight 34, channelColumnWidth 104 (EPGComponents.swift:206-212) while the cells use .caption/.caption2/.subheadline text (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:41-47, 78, 108, 149-151); iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows the truncation at the default size. The schedule's time column is .frame(width: 52) (ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:96-99). ResultRow, the picker row and the schedule title use lineLimit(1) (SearchView.swift:320-321, CategoryPickerSheet.swift:109, ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:102, 110). Settings value rows are hand-built HStack { Text; Spacer; Text } (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-201 and about twenty more).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Guide: keep hourWidth (it is baked into the off-main layout, EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309-312) and scale only the vertical metrics and the channel column: EPGGuideView gets @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) var textScale: CGFloat = 1 and EPGGuideMetrics(compact:textScale:) multiplies rowHeight, axisHeight, headerHeight and channelColumnWidth by min(textScale, 1.5); add .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.accessibility1) on the grid so text cannot outgrow the scaled rows. Schedule: @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .subheadline) var timeColumn: CGFloat = 64. Rows: .lineLimit(dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? 3 : 1) in ResultRow, the picker row and the schedule title. Settings: replace the HStack value rows by LabeledContent(L("...")) { Text(value) } (one spoken element, system value styling; check in the simulator that it stacks at accessibility sizes, otherwise wrap in ViewThatFits { HStack...; VStack... }). The TipJarRow() lines stay untouched.

**APIs:** ScaledMetric (iOS 14.0); View.dynamicTypeSize(_: range) (iOS 15.0); LabeledContent (iOS 16.0); ViewThatFits (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:197-218, Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift, Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:35, 127-254, Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309-324, Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:91-130, Views/SearchView.swift:309-325, Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:101-119, Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:182-291; screenshots iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png, iphone-light/T03-settings-3.png, Q03-search-results-mi.png.

Real: EPGGuideMetrics hard-codes rowHeight 56, channelColumnWidth 104, axisHeight 28, headerHeight 34 while all text is .caption/.caption2/.subheadline with no Dynamic Type cap in Views/EPG. L06 shows names cut at the default size ("World New...", "Busi-ness..."): the column leaves 104 - 16 padding - 32 logo - 8 spacing = 48 pt for the name. That is a default-size layout problem first, and scaling by Dynamic Type alone does not fix it. The schedule's time column is a fixed 52 pt (ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:99) with .subheadline and no lineLimit, so 12-hour times and any time at large sizes wrap inside the column (wrap, not truncate; iOS joins time and AM/PM with a non-breaking narrow space, so the break is mid-string). lineLimit(1) at SearchView.swift:320-321, CategoryPickerSheet.swift:109, ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:102, 110 is as described.

Corrections: (1) `private let metrics = EPGGuideMetrics(compact: true)` (EPGGuideView.swift:35) is a stored constant; a @ScaledMetric cannot feed it, it has to become a computed property. (2) A @ScaledMetric with base 1 used as a factor is fragile; scale the real base values. (3) "Apple's lists wrap" is overstated: Apple's media lists (TV, Music search) keep one-line titles at standard sizes; more lines only at accessibility sizes is the right scope, which is what the fix does. (4) Settings rows look native at the default size (T03); the gain from LabeledContent is one VoiceOver element per row and system stacking at accessibility sizes, not a visible defect today. The password row (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:203-223) contains a button and must stay hand-built. No settings UI test queries these rows (grep), no LabeledContent exists in the app yet.

**Corrected claim:** The TV guide and channel schedule use fixed metrics that do not follow Dynamic Type, and the guide's 104 pt channel column already truncates most names at the default size. Search results, the category picker and the schedule title keep one line even at accessibility sizes. Settings value rows are visually fine at default size but are two separate VoiceOver elements and do not stack at accessibility sizes.

**Corrected fix:** Guide: give EPGGuideMetrics an init with default arguments (compact:, rowHeight: 56, channelColumnWidth: 104, axisHeight: 28, headerHeight: 34) so EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309 stays unchanged and hourWidth stays untouched; in EPGGuideView declare @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) for those four base values, clamp each to 1.5x, and turn `metrics` into a computed property; add .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.accessibility1) on `grid` (same precedent as Views/PlayerView.swift:2827). Separately widen the compact channel column (about 120-128 pt) or drop the logo to 28 pt so two-line names fit at the default size; that is a small design decision. Schedule: size the time column from the text instead of a constant, e.g. a hidden Text(EPGTimeFormat.time(<a 22:00 sample date>)) with the real time in an overlay, or @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .subheadline) with a base wide enough for 12-hour (64 pt is borderline for "10:00 AM"; measure) plus .lineLimit(1).minimumScaleFactor(0.8). Rows: .lineLimit(dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? 3 : 1) in ResultRow, the picker row and the schedule title. Settings: LabeledContent(L("..."), value: ...) for plain label/value rows only; leave the password row and the TipJarRow() lines untouched; treat as optional polish.

**API check:** ScaledMetric: SwiftUICore swiftinterface line 12151, iOS 14.0. View.dynamicTypeSize<T: RangeExpression>(_:): line 11912, iOS 15.0. DynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize: line 11878, iOS 15.0. EnvironmentValues.dynamicTypeSize: line 11899, iOS 15.0. LabeledContent: SwiftUI swiftinterface line 4019, iOS 16.0, with init<S1, S2>(_ title: S1, value: S2) (line 4045) and init<S>(_ title: S, content:) for String titles. ViewThatFits: SwiftUICore line 11374, iOS 16.0. No iOS 26 gate needed.

**Regression risks:** EPGChannelRowView and EPGChannelColumnCell are Equatable on metrics (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:12-16, 139-141): metrics must stay a stable value per text size or every row re-renders during scroll; a computed property returning equal values is fine. hourWidth must not be scaled: it is baked into the off-main cell layout (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:309-324) and scroll offsets (EPGGuideView.swift:351-356). Taller guide rows mean fewer channels per screen. Settings files carry the owner's uncommitted TipJarRow() line; edits must leave it in place. LabeledContent merges label and value into one accessibility element, which would break any future UI test that looks up the value text separately.

**How to verify:** Launch with -UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName UICTContentSizeCategoryXXXL and UICTContentSizeCategoryAccessibilityL; screenshot TV Guide, a channel schedule (also with -AppleLocale en_US for 12-hour times), Search results, the category picker and Settings. Unit test: the new EPGGuideMetrics init keeps hourWidth and dayWidth identical to EPGGuideMetrics(compact: true). Scroll the guide with a large playlist after the change and confirm no extra row re-renders (Instruments SwiftUI template or a body counter).

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-13 — Posters and logos loaded through CachedImage are exposed to VoiceOver as unlabeled images and are inverted by Smart Invert

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie and Series detail hero, Episode rows, TV Guide channel column, Programme sheet, All poster grids under Smart Invert
- Code: `Views/CachedImage.swift:62-94, 138-147`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:48-71, 103-122`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1391-1400`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:148`, `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:36`

**What the user perceives:** On a detail screen VoiceOver stops on two nameless images (backdrop and poster) before it reaches the title; every episode row and every guide row starts with a nameless image. With Smart Invert on, posters and channel logos turn into colour negatives, which Apple's own apps avoid.

**Mechanism (finder):** CachedImage renders NukeUI's state.image, which is Image(uiImage:) (Nuke/Sources/NukeUI/LazyImageState.swift:44), with no accessibility modifier (CachedImage.swift:66-82); the SF Symbol placeholder is likewise an image (CachedImage.swift:142-144). Wherever the image is not inside a Button it becomes its own element without a label. There is no accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors anywhere in the app. Every call site pairs the image with a text title, so the image is decorative.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One place, CachedImage.body: add .accessibilityHidden(true) and .accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors() on the outer Group (after .transaction). Inside buttons this changes nothing; standalone posters stop being VoiceOver stops. If the tap-to-enlarge poster in the hero should stay reachable, make it a Button with a label at DetailComponents.swift:103-122; otherwise it is simply decorative. No effect on the image request, cache keys or prefetch.

**APIs:** View.accessibilityHidden(_:) (iOS 14.0); View.accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors(_:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/CachedImage.swift:53-148, Nuke/Sources/NukeUI/LazyImageState.swift:40-46 (`imageContainer.map { Image(uiImage: $0.image) }`), all 16 CachedImage call sites (grep), Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:46-123, Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1474, Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:143-170, Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:35-38, Views/PlayerView.swift:4823-4836.

The mechanism is real in code: CachedImage attaches no accessibility modifier, Image(uiImage:) carries no label, the placeholder is Image(systemName:) (which gets a symbol-derived label such as "Photo" or "TV"), and there is no accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors anywhere in the app. Standalone sites (detail backdrop and poster, episode thumbnail, guide logo, programme sheet logo, downloads row) are not inside a Button, so they are separate image elements. The player rework already treated this per site: Views/PlayerView.swift:4835 adds .accessibilityHidden(true) to its CachedImage, which supports the view that the image is decorative.

Why not fully confirmed: (1) no Accessibility Inspector or Smart Invert run backs it; the VoiceOver part follows standard SwiftUI behaviour, the Smart Invert part is plausible but unverified for SwiftUI-rendered images. (2) Fix placement: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors on the outer Group also exempts the placeholder tile (systemGray6 + symbol), which would then stay light on an inverted screen; it belongs on the loaded image branch only. (3) Scope: the change also reaches three player call sites (Views/PlayerView.swift:4823, 5417, 5602); harmless there (one is already hidden, one is inside a Button, one sits beside its title) but the finding did not mention it. (4) The hero poster has an onTapGesture (DetailComponents.swift:117); hiding it removes the enlarge action for VoiceOver, which is acceptable for a poster but is a choice.

**Corrected claim:** Images rendered by CachedImage carry no accessibility treatment: where they are not inside a button (detail hero backdrop and poster, episode thumbnails, guide and programme-sheet logos, download rows) VoiceOver gets an extra unnamed image stop, or a symbol name such as "Photo" when the placeholder shows. Posters and logos are probably inverted by Smart Invert; that part needs a run.

**Corrected fix:** In CachedImage.body: add .accessibilityHidden(true) on the outer Group (after .transaction), and add .accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors() only on the loaded branch (after .aspectRatio(contentMode:) on `image`), not on the placeholder. If the tap-to-enlarge poster should stay reachable for VoiceOver, wrap it in a Button with a label at DetailComponents.swift:103-122; otherwise leave it hidden. The existing .accessibilityHidden(true) at Views/PlayerView.swift:4835 becomes redundant and can stay. No change to requests, cache keys or prefetch.

**API check:** View.accessibilityHidden(_ hidden: Bool): SwiftUI swiftinterface line 13252, iOS 14.0. View.accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors(_ active: Bool = true): SwiftUICore swiftinterface line 16762, iOS 14.0. Both exist; no iOS 26 gate needed.

**Regression risks:** Touches three out-of-scope player call sites through the shared view (no behaviour change expected). Any UI test that locates a poster through an image element would stop finding it (none found by grep). VoiceOver users lose the poster-enlarge tap on detail screens unless it is made a labelled Button. One extra modifier per image: no effect on the Equatable shelf rows or scroll cost.

**How to verify:** Accessibility Inspector on a movie detail, a series episode list and the TV Guide before and after: count image elements ahead of the title and per row. Smart Invert (simulator Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size) on Movies home in light appearance before the change to confirm posters really invert, then after to confirm they keep their colours while placeholders still invert.

## accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-14 — Reduce Motion is honoured in the player but not in browsing: the detail hero keeps its parallax and zoom and the playlist-to-dashboard switch keeps its slide

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Playlist list to dashboard, Category jump on the home screens
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:63-70, 443-446, 472-475`, `ContentView.swift:48, 58, 66-69, 166`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:250-254`, `Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:122`

**What the user perceives:** A user who turned on Reduce Motion still gets the backdrop that drifts and scales while scrolling a detail screen and a full-width slide when entering or leaving a playlist; the system's own transitions around them have already switched to cross-fades.

**Mechanism (finder):** DetailHero applies scaleEffect and a parallax offset in .visualEffect unconditionally (DetailComponents.swift:63-70). ContentView animates selectedPlaylist with easeInOut and a .move(edge: .trailing) transition (ContentView.swift:48, 58, 66-69, 166). The category jump and season chip scroll are animated (LiveStreamsView.swift:252, DetailComponents.swift:444, 474). None of these read accessibilityReduceMotion; the player code does (PlayerTimeline.swift:122).

**Proposed fix (finder):** @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion in DetailHero and ContentView. Hero: capture let still = reduceMotion and return content unchanged inside visualEffect when still (keep the overscroll stretch only if wanted). ContentView: transition reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .trailing). Scroll jumps: perform proxy.scrollTo without withAnimation when reduceMotion is true.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Read Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:46-84, 433-478, ContentView.swift:41-170, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:250-257; grep shows accessibilityReduceMotion is read only in Views/Components/PlayerTimeline.swift:122 and Views/PlayerView.swift:309, 366, 5555.

Real: DetailHero's visualEffect applies a 0.18 parallax offset and an overscroll scale unconditionally (DetailComponents.swift:63-70), and ContentView slides the whole dashboard in and out with .move(edge: .trailing) over 0.3 s (ContentView.swift:48, 58, 66-69, 166). Neither reads Reduce Motion.

Corrections: (1) "the system's own transitions around them have already switched to cross-fades" is wrong. With Reduce Motion alone, navigation pushes still slide; they cross-fade only when the user also enables Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions. The native-equivalent gate for the dashboard slide is that setting, not Reduce Motion alone. (2) Returning the hero content unchanged under Reduce Motion removes the overscroll stretch too, which leaves a blank band above the backdrop when the user pulls down. Only the parallax offset should go; the stretch is direct manipulation and should stay. (3) Animated scrollTo for the category jump and the season chips is not a Reduce Motion violation (the system keeps animated programmatic scrolls); that part should be dropped. (4) If another finding replaces ContentView's custom ZStack switch with standard navigation, the transition part becomes moot.

**Corrected claim:** Two browse animations ignore the motion accessibility settings: the detail hero's backdrop parallax, and the full-screen slide between the playlist list and the dashboard. Impact is small: the parallax is 18% and finger-driven, and the system itself still slides pushes under Reduce Motion unless Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions is on.

**Corrected fix:** DetailHero: add @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion, capture `let still = reduceMotion` next to `let h = heroHeight`, and inside visualEffect use `.offset(y: still ? 0 : parallax)` while keeping the scaleEffect. ContentView: choose the dashboard transition when the state changes: `(reduceMotion && UIAccessibility.prefersCrossFadeTransitions) ? .opacity : .move(edge: .trailing)`; using Reduce Motion alone is also acceptable if the owner prefers the simpler rule. Leave the scrollTo animations as they are.

**API check:** EnvironmentValues.accessibilityReduceMotion: SwiftUICore swiftinterface line 18334, iOS 13.0. UIAccessibilityPrefersCrossFadeTransitions(): UIAccessibility.h:570, API_AVAILABLE(ios(14.0)), main-actor; Swift spelling UIAccessibility.prefersCrossFadeTransitions. No SwiftUI environment value for it exists in the interface (grep found none), so it is read from UIKit. View.visualEffect: SwiftUICore line 16286, iOS 17.0 (already in use); its closure is @Sendable, a captured Bool is fine.

**Regression risks:** Minimal. The hero keeps its look for users without Reduce Motion. An .opacity transition on the dashboard must stay paired with the existing .opacity transition of the playlist list (ContentView.swift:130-133) so the two do not show through each other mid-fade. Reading the UIKit flag in body does not update live if the setting changes while the screen is open; it is re-read on the next state change, which is enough here.

**How to verify:** Simulator with Reduce Motion on: record a scroll of a movie detail and confirm the backdrop moves 1:1 with the content while pull-down still stretches it with no gap. With Reduce Motion + Prefer Cross-Fade Transitions on: open and leave a playlist and confirm a cross-fade; with only Reduce Motion on, compare against a system push in the same recording. A screen recording is needed; screenshots cannot show it.

## ios26-design-1 — The floating tab bar is hidden on category, All and history grids but comes back on detail screens, so it slides in and out at every level of a drill-down.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV category / All Channels, Movies category / All Movies / Recently Added, Series category / All Series / Recently Added, Watch history, M3U group detail, M3U favorites, TV Guide, iPad top tab bar
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:380, 563, 822`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761`, `another-iptv-player/Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:82`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:502`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:63`, `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:48-85`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:26-45`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Keep the tab bar visible on every browse level (recommended) or keep hiding it below the tab root. If hiding stays, apply it to detail, Favorites and Downloads as well, and not on iPad.

**What the user perceives:** On iPhone the glass tab bar and the Search button slide away when a category or All grid is pushed (iphone-dark/L03, L05, M03, M04; iphone-light/S02). They return on the movie or series detail pushed from that grid (M07) and on Favorites (M09), then vanish again on the way back. One drill-down makes the bar appear and disappear two or three times. On iPad the hidden bar is the top tab pill, so no space is gained and the tabs simply disappear (ipad-light/L03 against L06).

**Mechanism (finder):** `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` sits on 12 pushed destinations (lines above). MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView, FavoritesView and DownloadsView do not hide the bar, so visibility flips per level. The modifier predates the iOS 26 design (present since d2489f9, extended in 654cefc and 1cce013) and no comment explains it. On iOS 26 the system way to gain room while browsing is the minimizing tab bar.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Delete the modifier from the browse grids, history and M3U favorites. Keeping it on EPGGuideView.swift:51 is defensible because the guide is a dense two-axis grid. Add a gated helper and apply it to both TabViews after `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)`:

extension View {
  @ViewBuilder func tabBarMinimizesOnScroll() -> some View {
    if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown) } else { self }
  }
}

iOS 18 fallback: the classic tab bar simply stays visible on pushed screens. Interplay to check: the mini card reserves a fixed 49 pt above the bottom (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:478), so a gap appears under the card while the bar is minimized.

**APIs:** View.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:) (iOS 26.0); TabBarMinimizeBehavior.onScrollDown (iOS 26.0 (iOS only))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read every site. `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` is on exactly 12 pushed destinations: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:497 (LiveCategoryDetailView), :722 (AllLiveView); Views/VODView.swift:380, :563, :822 (Recently Added, category, All); Views/SeriesView.swift:357, :535, :761; Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:502; Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:63; Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:82; Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:51. MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView (SeriesView.swift:795+), FavoritesView (Views/FavoritesView.swift:56-58) and DownloadsView have no such modifier, so the bar returns one level deeper. No comment at any site; history (git log -S) shows only d2489f9 (monorepo move), 1cce013, 654cefc, none with a rationale. Screenshots agree: iphone-dark/L03 has no tab bar, iphone-dark/M07 and iphone-light/M07 have it; ipad-light/L03 loses the top tab pill with no space gained while ipad-light/L06 (Favorites) keeps it. Supporting point the finding missed: the mini card always reserves the tab bar height on compact width (Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:478, used at Views/PlayerView.swift:1954) regardless of whether the bar is hidden, so on today's hidden-bar grids the card already floats 49 pt above nothing. Caveat on evidence: the grid -> detail -> back flip itself was not captured (the tour opened M07 from the home shelf, ScreensUITests.swift:357); it follows from code and SwiftUI's per-destination toolbar visibility. Why only partly: removing the hides is the fix; bundling `tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown)` into the same S-sized change is a separate product choice with its own risks (UI tests that tap `app.tabBars.buttons[label]` after scrolling, ScreensUITests.swift:231 and UserFlowsUITests.swift:757; gap under the mini card while minimized).

**Corrected claim:** The tab bar is hidden on 11 browse/history/favorites destinations plus the TV Guide, but not on movie/series detail, Favorites or Downloads, so its visibility flips at each level of a drill-down (and Search / tab switching is unreachable from a category grid). On iPad the hidden bar is the top tab pill, so nothing is gained. The hide is undocumented and predates the floating iOS 26 bar. The mini card does not follow the hidden bar, so it already leaves a 49 pt gap on those screens.

**Corrected fix:** Step A (the fix, S): delete `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` at LiveStreamsView.swift:497, 722; VODView.swift:380, 563, 822; SeriesView.swift:357, 535, 761; M3UChannelsView.swift:502; M3UFavoritesView.swift:63; WatchHistoryListView.swift:82. Keep EPGGuideView.swift:51 (dense two-axis grid) or decide separately. Works unchanged on iOS 18 (classic bar stays visible). Step B (optional, separate decision, iPhone only): the gated helper `if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown) } else { self }` on both TabViews after `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)`; do it only after checking the mini card position and the UI-test tab helpers with a minimized bar. Do not touch MiniPlayerSupport/PlayerView for this.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8977-8978 `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0, *) nonisolated public func tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_ behavior: SwiftUI.TabBarMinimizeBehavior) -> some View`. :8981-9001 `public struct TabBarMinimizeBehavior` with `automatic`, and `onScrollDown`, `onScrollUp`, `never` each `@available(iOS 26.0, *)` and unavailable on macOS/tvOS/watchOS/visionOS. `.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)` is existing code. Step A needs no new API.

**Regression risks:** Step A: grids lose roughly the tab bar height of visible rows on iOS 18 (opaque bar); on iOS 26 content scrolls under the floating bar. Bottom-of-list pagination sentinels are unaffected. Step B: tests that locate other tabs via app.tabBars.buttons after a scroll may not find them while the bar is minimized; a fixed 49 pt allowance leaves a gap under the mini card while minimized (same gap exists today on hidden-bar screens). Step A risk low, step B medium.

**How to verify:** UI test on iPhone: Movies -> category header -> poster -> back -> back, asserting app.tabBars.firstMatch.exists at every level; same for Live TV category, All, Recently Added, watch history, M3U group. Re-shoot iphone L03/M03/M04/S02 and ipad L03. With the mini card docked, open a category grid and confirm the card sits directly above the bar. Run the existing ScreensUITests/UserFlowsUITests.

## ios26-design-2 — Three or four icon-only toolbar buttons are fused into one glass group with forced semibold weight and an accent-tinted star, and on iPad they collapse into an overflow whose items have no titles.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels, iPad Live TV
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:231-241`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:108-138`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:112-133`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:113-134`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:64-94`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Only for the optional step: whether TV Guide, All and Jump to Category may move behind one menu, which puts the guide two taps away.

**What the user perceives:** The top-right capsule holds star, guide, grid and list icons with no separation (iphone-dark/L01; iphone-light/M01). The star is blue and all icons are heavier than the back chevron and the TV Guide toolbar (iphone-dark/L06), so weights differ between screens. After scrolling, the collapsed title sits at the leading edge on Live, Movies and Series (iphone-light/L02, M02) but is centred in Settings (T02). On iPad the group is cut to star plus an overflow button (ipad-light/L01).

**Mechanism (finder):** Every item is `Image(systemName:)` with `.font(.body.weight(.semibold))` (e.g. LiveStreamsView.swift:113-114, 122-123, 132-133). The Favorites link adds `.foregroundStyle(Color.accentColor)` and has no accessibility label (DashboardView.swift:235-237). Adjacent items of one placement share one glass background on iOS 26. Image-only labels give the system overflow no title to show. The leading-aligned title is consistent with the centred title not fitting beside the wide trailing group; that part is a hypothesis to confirm.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Minimal step (S): use `Label(L("…"), systemImage:)` for every item and drop the font and tint overrides; the bar still shows only the icon, overflow menus and VoiceOver get the title. Separate the cross-tab Favorites link from the tab's own actions on iOS 26:

ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarTrailing) { NavigationLink { FavoritesView(…) } label: { Label(L("favorites.title"), systemImage: "star") } }
if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { ToolbarSpacer(.fixed, placement: .topBarTrailing) }

iOS 18 fallback: no spacer, plain bar buttons as today. Optional larger step (M): keep Favorites plus one Menu holding All, Jump to Category and TV Guide, driven by `navigationDestination(isPresented:)`.

**APIs:** ToolbarSpacer(_:placement:) (iOS 26.0); SpacerSizing.fixed (iOS 26.0); ToolbarContentBuilder.buildLimitedAvailability (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts hold: every home toolbar item is `Image(systemName:)` with `.font(.body.weight(.semibold))` (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:113-114, 122-123, 132-133; VODView.swift:118, 128; SeriesView.swift:119, 129; M3UChannelsView.swift:69-70, 78-80, 88-89); the Favorites link adds `.foregroundStyle(Color.accentColor)` and has no accessibility label (Views/DashboardView.swift:233-238), and a real test documents that: ScreensUITests.swift:51-52 'Toolbar star button has no localized label - locate by symbol-derived identifier' (`buttons["star.fill"]`). Screenshots: iphone-dark/L01 shows one capsule with blue star + three heavier icons; iphone-dark/L06 (TV Guide) icons are regular weight; ipad-light/L01 shows star + an ellipsis overflow. iphone-light/M02 shows the collapsed 'Movies' title at the leading edge next to a 3-icon group starting at about x=217 pt, while T02 (no trailing items) is centred, consistent with the title simply not fitting centred. Not established: that overflow rows have no titles (the overflow was never opened; the three tab items do carry accessibilityLabel, which may or may not be used as the menu title). Fix corrections: (1) the proposed ToolbarSpacer makes the trailing cluster wider (two capsules instead of one), which works against the crowding/leading-title symptom the finding cites and may push items into overflow on 375 pt phones; (2) switching the star to a Label changes its identifier and breaks ScreensUITests.swift:52 unless updated; (3) the stated availability of buildLimitedAvailability is wrong (17.5, not 14.0), harmless at target 18.0.

**Corrected claim:** The home toolbars override the system bar-button look (semibold weight on every icon, accent-filled star), the Favorites link has no app-localized label, and three to four icon-only items share one glass capsule that is wide enough to push the collapsed inline title to the leading edge on iPhone and to collapse into an overflow on iPad portrait. Whether the iPad overflow rows are untitled is unverified.

**Corrected fix:** Step A (S, safe): replace each `Image(...)` label with `Label(L(key), systemImage:)` using the existing keys (epg.guide.title, browse.all_live / browse.all_movies / browse.all_series, list.jump_to_category, favorites.title), remove `.font(.body.weight(.semibold))` and the accent tint; keep the existing `.disabled(...)`. Update ScreensUITests.swift:52 to `buttons["Favorites"]`. Whether the star stays filled/tinted is a small design call. Step B (decision, M): reduce the cluster to Favorites + one Menu (All, Jump to Category, TV Guide) so the title can centre and nothing overflows; this is the change that actually addresses crowding. Do not add `ToolbarSpacer(.fixed, ...)` by default; only consider it if a simulator run at 375 pt and on iPad shows no overflow, gated with `if #available(iOS 26.0, *)` (iOS 18: no spacer).

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22876-22881 `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *)` (tvOS/watchOS/visionOS unavailable) `public struct ToolbarSpacer : ToolbarContent, CustomizableToolbarContent { public init(_ sizing: SpacerSizing = .flexible, placement: ToolbarItemPlacement = .automatic) }`. :280-286 `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *) public struct SpacerSizing` with `static let flexible`, `static let fixed`. ToolbarContentBuilder.buildLimitedAvailability: the type-erasing overload at :9648-9649 is `@available(iOS 17.5, ...)`; the generic iOS 14 overload at :9657-9661 is `obsoleted: 17.5`. So the finding's 'iOS 14.0' is wrong, but with deployment target 18.0 `if #available(iOS 26, *)` inside `.toolbar {}` compiles. `Label` in a navigation bar item renders icon-only by default (existing SwiftUI behaviour, no new API).

**Regression risks:** ScreensUITests.swift:52 (and the tour) look up `buttons["star.fill"]`; a titled Label changes that identifier. A fixed spacer widens the trailing group and can force overflow or a more truncated inline title on narrow iPhones. Moving TV Guide into a menu puts it two taps away (owner decision). No effect on Equatable shelf rows or data paths.

**How to verify:** Re-shoot L01/M01/S01 at rest and scrolled on a 402 pt and a 375 pt iPhone; check the inline title position. On iPad portrait open the ellipsis overflow before and after and confirm each row shows a title. VoiceOver: the Favorites button reads the localized title in a non-English app language. Run test_moviesTab_starToolbarButton_opensFavoritesScreen after updating the query.

## ios26-design-3 — Shelf headers render in the accent colour although the code asks for `.primary`, because the header NavigationLink keeps the default tinted button style.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:315-326, 418-429`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:292-303, 394-405`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:337-348`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Confirm the blue was not deliberate; the code's `.primary` and the Continue Watching header both suggest it was not.

**What the user perceives:** Every category title is bright blue with a pale blue chevron (iphone-light/M01, L01; iphone-dark/L01; ipad-light/L01), so the home screens read as a list of links. The Continue Watching header on the same screen is label-coloured, larger and inset differently.

**Mechanism (finder):** The label uses `.foregroundStyle(.primary)` and `.tertiary` inside a NavigationLink with no button style. Inside a tinted button the hierarchical styles resolve against the tint, so they produce accent blue and faded blue. ContinueWatchingRow.swift:43 adds `.buttonStyle(.plain)` and gets the intended look. Card titles avoid it by using `Color.primary` (VODView.swift:534). Font and inset also differ: `.headline` with 16 pt here, `.title2.bold` with 20 pt in ContinueWatchingRow.swift:35, 44.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add `.buttonStyle(.plain)` to the six header NavigationLinks so `.primary` and `.tertiary` resolve to label colours. While there, align font and inset with the Continue Watching header (for example `.title3.weight(.bold)` and one inset value). The change is inside the Equatable shelf rows and does not affect their `==`. No availability gate is needed.

**APIs:** View.buttonStyle(.plain) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Six shelf-header NavigationLinks have no button style and a label that uses hierarchical styles: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:356-367, VODView.swift:315-326 and 418-429, SeriesView.swift:292-303 and 394-405, M3UChannelsView.swift:337-348 (`.foregroundStyle(.primary)` on the HStack, `.tertiary` on the chevron). The Continue Watching header uses the same label but adds `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44). Screenshots show the result: iphone-dark/L01, iphone-light/M01, M02 and ipad-light/L01 all render the category titles in accent blue with a paler blue chevron, i.e. hierarchical levels of the link's tint rather than label colours. The code's explicit `.primary` and the sibling header's `.plain` both indicate the blue is accidental; history gives no contrary intent (all in d2489f9, squashed monorepo move). Small corrections: the poster cards are not blue mainly because their links already carry `.buttonStyle(.plain)` (VODView.swift:345, 462; SeriesView.swift:322, 434; LiveStreamsView.swift:457), not only because of `.foregroundColor(.primary)` at VODView.swift:534; and the inset difference is real (16 pt at the shelves, 20 pt at ContinueWatchingRow.swift:44, 55) but the value to converge on is 16, which matches the large title and the cards.

**Corrected claim:** Shelf headers render in the accent colour although the code asks for `.primary`/`.tertiary`, because the six header NavigationLinks keep the default tinted button style; Continue Watching, which adds `.buttonStyle(.plain)`, gets label colours. Header font (.headline vs .title2 bold) and inset (16 vs 20 pt) also differ between the two header kinds.

**Corrected fix:** Add `.buttonStyle(.plain)` to the six header NavigationLinks (after the label closure). No availability gate. Optional, as a design decision: unify the header style across shelves and Continue Watching, converging the inset on 16 pt (change ContinueWatchingRow.swift:44 and :55, not the shelves) and choosing one font (e.g. `.title3.weight(.bold)`). Leave the rows' Equatable `==` untouched.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8843-8850 `@available(iOS 13.0, ...) extension PrimitiveButtonStyle where Self == PlainButtonStyle { static var plain }` and `public struct PlainButtonStyle : PrimitiveButtonStyle`. Already used on NavigationLinks throughout these files.

**Regression risks:** Plain style changes the pressed feedback of the header from tint-dim to a plain dim; hit area stays the label. Elements remain buttons named after the category, so the UI tour's `app.buttons["News"]` / `["Action"]` keep working. Changing header font would change shelf row heights (affects only layout, not the `==` or scrollTo ids). If the owner actually likes the blue link look, this is a revert-by-preference.

**How to verify:** Re-shoot L01/M01/S01 (iPhone light and dark, iPad) and confirm titles are label-coloured with a tertiary grey chevron; tap a header and confirm it still pushes the category grid; run ScreensUITests.

## ios26-design-4 — After scrolling, the collapsed title and status bar sit on blurred but still readable poster captions and rows, and the only custom bar styling is a forced `.toolbarBackground(.visible)`.

- Verdict: **undecidable** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Settings, M3U channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:242-243`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:32-33`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:212`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:64`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:65`

**What the user perceives:** On Movies in light mode the inline title turns white on a grey veil and overlaps the caption of the poster underneath, with a second caption readable inside the button group (iphone-light/M02). In Settings the title sits on a still-readable row label (T02, T03, both variants). Text collides with text in the bar zone.

**Mechanism (finder):** `DashboardNavigationModifier` forces `.toolbarBackground(.visible, for: .navigationBar)`; it has been there since d2489f9 with no comment, and this overload is now soft-deprecated in favour of `toolbarBackgroundVisibility`. I could not establish from the screenshots whether this forced background or the default soft scroll edge effect causes the weak separation, because no scrolled screen without the modifier was captured. On iOS 18 the modifier certainly paints the bar material behind the large title at rest, which Apple's apps do not do.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Step 1: delete `.toolbarBackground(.visible, for: .navigationBar)` at DashboardView.swift:243 and M3UDashboardView.swift:33, then compare scrolled screenshots. On iOS 18 this gives the standard transparent large-title bar that gains its material on scroll. Step 2, only if captions still read through the title on iOS 26: give the shelf scroll views a firmer edge:

if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { content.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard, for: .top) } else { content }

iOS 18 fallback for step 2: none needed.

**APIs:** View.toolbarBackground(_:for:) (Visibility overload) (iOS 16.0, soft-deprecated, renamed toolbarBackgroundVisibility(_:for:) (iOS 18.0)); View.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(_:for:) (iOS 26.0); ScrollEdgeEffectStyle.hard / .soft (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The modifier exists as cited: Views/DashboardView.swift:242-243 (`.toolbar(.visible, for: .navigationBar)` + `.toolbarBackground(.visible, for: .navigationBar)`) and Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:32-33; it has no comment and dates from the original native app (fe55017, 2026-04-08), i.e. before the iOS 26 design. No UINavigationBarAppearance or toolbarColorScheme override exists anywhere in the app. The visual symptom is real in iphone-light/M02 (white 'Movies' title over the blurred caption 'The Quiet Path', glass group over 'Whispers in th...') and iphone-light/T02 (centred black 'Settings' over a legible blurred row). But static evidence cannot attribute it to the modifier: at rest (iphone-light/M01, iphone-dark/L01) no bar material is visible at all, and what M02/T02 show (progressive blur plus a dim veil, title/status-bar colour flipping to white over dark posters while the glass group stays light) looks like the stock iOS 26 soft scroll edge effect with content-adaptive bar foreground, which Apple's own apps also show. The finding itself rates this 'needs-simulator-run'. Step 2 (`scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard, for: .top)`) is a real API but is a deviation from the system default look rather than a move toward it, so it should be an owner decision, not a default fix.

**Corrected claim:** The dashboard forces the navigation bar background visible with a soft-deprecated overload and no stated reason. On iOS 18 this paints bar material and a hairline behind the large title at rest, which system apps do not do. On iOS 26 it is unknown whether it changes anything; the text-over-blurred-text seen when scrolled is at least mostly the standard soft scroll edge effect.

**Corrected fix:** Step 1: remove `.toolbarBackground(.visible, for: .navigationBar)` at DashboardView.swift:243 and M3UDashboardView.swift:33 only after an A/B confirms (a) no regression on iOS 26 and (b) on an iOS 18 runtime the bar still gains its material when shelves scroll under it (the first child of the vertical ScrollView is a horizontal ScrollView in ContinueWatchingRow, so scroll-edge tracking must be checked). Keep `.toolbar(.visible, for: .navigationBar)`. Step 2 (`if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { content.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard, for: .top) } else { content }`) only as an explicit owner decision if legibility over posters is still judged insufficient; iOS 18 needs no fallback.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10051-10055 `@available(iOS, introduced: 16.0, deprecated: 100000.0, renamed: "toolbarBackgroundVisibility(_:for:)") func toolbarBackground(_ visibility: Visibility, for bars: ToolbarPlacement...)`; :10057-10058 `@available(iOS 18.0, ...) func toolbarBackgroundVisibility(_:for:)`. :12394-12402 `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0, *) public struct ScrollEdgeEffectStyle` with `automatic`, `hard`, `soft`. :12413-12415 `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, *) @available(visionOS, unavailable) func scrollEdgeEffectStyle(_ style: ScrollEdgeEffectStyle?, for edges: Edge.Set)`; :12420 `scrollEdgeEffectHidden(_:for:)` same availability.

**Regression risks:** On iOS 18, removal changes the at-rest look of every dashboard tab (large title without bar material) and could expose a transparent bar over scrolled shelves if scroll-edge tracking misbehaves with the nested horizontal scroll views or on the non-scrolling loading/empty states. A hard edge style on iOS 26 would make the shelves look unlike other system apps and unlike the rest of this app's screens.

**How to verify:** Simulator A/B, same scroll offset: iOS 26 iphone-light and dark M02, L02 (with enough content to scroll) and T02, with and without line 243; compare title colour, veil density and caption legibility pixel-wise. iOS 18.x runtime: Live/Movies/Series/Settings at rest (is there a material band and hairline under the large title with the modifier, none without?) and scrolled (does the bar get its material without the modifier?), plus the loading and empty states. Only if the iOS 26 pair is identical is the modifier inert there and step 1 purely an iOS 18 clean-up.

## ios26-design-5 — The detail hero shows a hard seam with a blurred colour band below it whenever the backdrop falls back to the blurred poster.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, iPad detail
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:46-99`, `another-iptv-player/Views/MovieDetailView.swift:124-128, 187`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:959-963, 1003`

**What the user perceives:** Above the Watch Now button there is a straight horizontal edge and under it a grey-brown band that fades out (iphone-light/M07 and iphone-dark/M07). The top of the hero looks washed out under the status bar. It reads as two misaligned layers.

**Mechanism (finder):** With no `backdropPath` the poster is used with `.blur(radius: 28)` and 0.55 opacity (DetailComponents.swift:61-62). A non-opaque blur spreads about 28 pt beyond the 380 pt hero frame and nothing clips it. The gradient layer is exactly hero height and ends in opaque `systemBackground` (86-97), so the fade ends at the frame edge and the blur bleed shows below it. The same soft edge thins the image at the top.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make the fallback blur edge-clamped: `.blur(radius: backdropIsFallback ? 28 : 0, opaque: backdropIsFallback)`. Do not add `.clipped()` on the hero, because that would cut the overscroll stretch from the `visualEffect` at lines 63-70. Optional iOS 26 step for iPad: add `backgroundExtensionEffect()` to the backdrop layer behind `if #available(iOS 26.0, *)` so the artwork continues under the floating sidebar; iOS 18 fallback is the current layout. That step needs an iPad run to confirm it triggers with the `.sidebarAdaptable` sidebar.

**APIs:** View.blur(radius:opaque:) (iOS 13.0); View.backgroundExtensionEffect() (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism for the seam is real. Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:51-62: CachedImage is framed and clipped inside itself (Views/CachedImage.swift:81-82), then `.blur(radius: backdropIsFallback ? 28 : 0)` and `.opacity(0.55)` are applied outside that clip, so the non-opaque blur spreads past the 380 pt frame; nothing clips the hero ZStack (lines 35-43). The gradient layer is exactly hero-height and ends in opaque systemBackground (86-97), so the fade finishes at the frame edge and the bleed shows in the 20 pt VStack gap below (MovieDetailView.swift:124-128; same structure at SeriesView.swift:958-963). Screenshots match: iphone-light/M07 and iphone-dark/M07 show a straight edge at about y=380 pt and a grey/brown band of roughly 15-20 pt fading out under it. `backdropIsFallback` is true whenever backdropURL is nil (line 30-32), which is also the state before movie info loads, so most users see it at least briefly. History: unchanged since the original app (fe55017 / d2489f9), no comment claiming intent. Corrections: (1) the washed-out top is not explained by a 28 pt blur edge alone; the faded zone in M07 is about 110 pt tall and sits exactly under the status/navigation bar of a scroll view that ignores the top safe area (MovieDetailView.swift:187), so it is at least largely the iOS 26 scroll edge effect and will mostly remain after the fix; (2) the optional `backgroundExtensionEffect()` step is unsupported by any evidence: no iPad detail screenshot exists, and it is not established that the effect engages with a `.sidebarAdaptable` TabView sidebar.

**Corrected claim:** When the detail backdrop falls back to the blurred poster, the non-opaque 28 pt blur bleeds about 15-20 pt below the 380 pt hero while the systemBackground gradient ends exactly at the hero edge, producing a hard seam with a faded colour band beneath it (movie and series detail, light and dark). The pale top of the hero is mostly the system scroll edge effect, not this bug.

**Corrected fix:** DetailComponents.swift:61: `.blur(radius: backdropIsFallback ? 28 : 0, opaque: backdropIsFallback)`. Keep the hero unclipped so the `visualEffect` overscroll stretch (63-70) still works. No availability gate. Drop the optional backgroundExtensionEffect step unless an iPad run with the sidebar open shows a concrete benefit.

**API check:** SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3780-3786 `@available(iOS 13.0, ...) extension View { @inlinable nonisolated public func blur(radius: CGFloat, opaque: Bool = false) -> some View }`. SwiftUI.swiftinterface:12337-12341 `@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0, *) @MainActor @preconcurrency public func backgroundExtensionEffect()` and `backgroundExtensionEffect(isEnabled: Bool)` (exists, but not recommended here).

**Regression risks:** An opaque blur renders transparent source pixels as black, so a poster with an alpha channel (transparent PNG artwork) would get dark areas in the fallback backdrop; aspect-fill posters and the opaque systemGray6 placeholder (CachedImage.swift:138-147) are unaffected. The fallback will look slightly denser at its edges because they no longer fade. Real backdrops are untouched (radius 0, opaque false). Image request tuning (loadProfile .high) is not changed.

**How to verify:** Re-shoot M07 and a series detail in light and dark with an item that has no backdrop: the band under the hero edge must be gone and the gradient must end flush with the background. Pull down to confirm the overscroll stretch still scales the backdrop. Open a title that has a real backdrop and confirm no change. If available, test one poster with transparency.

## ios26-design-6 — The detail call-to-action and secondary buttons are hand-drawn (gradient, coloured glow, trailing chevron, material boxes with hairline strokes) instead of system button styles.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Episode rows, Playlist list empty state
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:209-252, 274-314`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:77-143`, `another-iptv-player/ContentView.swift:189-201`, `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:89, 112`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Confirm that the gradient and glow call-to-action may be replaced by the system prominent button.

**What the user perceives:** Watch Now is a 16 pt rounded rectangle with a blue gradient, a blue glow and a chevron that suggests navigation although it starts playback (iphone-light/M07, iphone-dark/M07). Download is a flat grey box with a hairline border. Neither matches the capsule buttons the system draws elsewhere in the app on iOS 26, such as Try Again in S04.

**Mechanism (finder):** Both are `.buttonStyle(.plain)` with custom backgrounds: a LinearGradient plus accent shadow (DetailComponents.swift:241-251), and `.ultraThinMaterial` on a plain background plus a stroke (303-312; DownloadButton.swift:115-122, 139-142). `.ultraThinMaterial` over a flat page colour is just a grey fill. The app already uses `.borderedProminent` and `.bordered` in EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:89, 112 and CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:29, so there are two button languages.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use system styles, which pick up the iOS 26 shapes and press behaviour and work unchanged on iOS 18:

Button(action: onPrimary) { VStack(spacing: 6) { Label(primaryTitle, systemImage: primaryIcon).frame(maxWidth: .infinity); if let progress { ProgressView(value: progress).tint(.white) } } }
  .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large).buttonBorderShape(.capsule)

Secondary and Download: `.buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large)` (`.small` for the compact episode variant), with `.tint(.green/.orange)` for the completed and failed states. Drop the chevron. Glass styles (`.glass`, `.glassProminent`) are only appropriate if the buttons are moved onto the hero artwork; on the plain page background the bordered styles are the right ones.

**APIs:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.borderedProminent / .bordered (iOS 15.0); ButtonBorderShape.capsule (iOS 15.0); PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass / .glassProminent (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:209-252: primaryCTA is a `.buttonStyle(.plain)` Button whose label paints a LinearGradient (241-247), clips to a 16 pt rounded rect (248), adds an accent-coloured shadow (249) and a trailing `chevron.right` (226-228). DetailSecondaryLabel (288-314) and DownloadButton.button()/downloadingLabel() (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:101-143) fill `.ultraThinMaterial` plus a hairline stroke; ContentView.swift:189-201 is a hand-filled accent rectangle with cornerRadius 10. System styles are already used at Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:89/112, Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:29, Views/MovieDetailView.swift:117, Views/SeriesView.swift:952, so two button languages do coexist. Screenshots iphone-light/M07 and iphone-dark/M07 show the gradient+glow+chevron CTA and the flat Download box; iphone-light/S04 shows the system capsule Try Again. History: `git log -S'chevron.right'` on DetailComponents.swift only returns d2489f9 (monorepo move), no comment explains the look as deliberate. So the observation is true. What does not stand: (1) the proposed replacement code drops `primarySubtitle` (DetailComponents.swift:218-223), which carries the resume position (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:134 `resumeMs.map { DetailFormatting.formatMs($0) }`, Views/SeriesView.swift:969 `resumeSubtitle`) - that is a functional regression, not a style change; (2) this is a brand/visual decision rather than a defect: nothing is broken, stalls or jumps, and the CTA is a consistent, polished element in both themes, so medium is too high; (3) the compact episode DownloadButton (Views/SeriesView.swift:1454-1471) is icon-only, so `.bordered` there needs a circle/small shape, not just `.controlSize(.small)`.

**Corrected claim:** The detail CTA, the secondary/Download buttons and the playlist empty-state button are custom-painted `.plain` buttons (gradient + accent glow + navigation-style chevron; material box + hairline) while the rest of the app uses `.borderedProminent`/`.bordered`. It is a visual-consistency / native-look issue and a product decision, not a functional defect. Low severity.

**Corrected fix:** Owner decision first. If accepted: keep the two-line label and the resume progress, only swap the chrome. Button(action: onPrimary) { VStack(spacing: 6) { HStack(spacing: 10) { Image(systemName: primaryIcon); VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) { Text(primaryTitle).font(.subheadline.weight(.bold)); if let sub = primarySubtitle, !sub.isEmpty { Text(sub).font(.caption2).opacity(0.82).lineLimit(1) } } }.frame(maxWidth: .infinity); if let progress { ProgressView(value: min(max(progress,0),1)).tint(.white) } } }.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large).buttonBorderShape(.capsule). Secondary/trailer Link and full-width DownloadButton: `.buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large)`, with `.tint(.green/.orange)` for completed/failed. Compact episode variant: `.buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.small).buttonBorderShape(.circle)` (icon-only). ContentView.swift:189-201: `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large)`. No availability gate needed. Minimal alternative if the owner wants to keep the brand CTA: only remove the `chevron.right` (it signals navigation on a button that starts playback) and leave the rest.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface: `extension PrimitiveButtonStyle where Self == BorderedProminentButtonStyle { static var borderedProminent }` @available(iOS 15.0) (line 21629-21631); `... BorderedButtonStyle { static var bordered }` @available(iOS 15.0) (17128-17130); `struct ButtonBorderShape` @available(iOS 15.0) with `static let capsule` (only macOS 14/tvOS 17 restricted, so iOS 15) and `static let circle` @available(iOS 17.0) (15055-15064); `func buttonBorderShape(_:)` iOS 15.0 (15048-15050). SwiftUICore: `enum ControlSize { case large }` available on iOS (only macOS 11 gate), `func controlSize(_:)`. `.glass` (1315-1318) and `.glassProminent` (3444-3447) exist, @available(iOS 26.0), visionOS unavailable - not needed for this fix.

**Regression risks:** Dropping primarySubtitle as in the original proposal would remove the resume timestamp / episode hint from the CTA. Label height changes shift the detail layout slightly (plot block moves). UI tests locate the CTA by label ("Watch Now" / BEGINSWITH "Resume": another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:552-575, ScreensUITests.swift:104, ScreenshotsUITests.swift:41); a subtitle inside the same Button becomes part of the accessibility label, as it already is today, so keep the title first. DownloadButton keeps `.contextMenu`; bordered style adds press feedback to states where the tap is a no-op (downloading/queued/completed, DownloadButton.swift:195-200), which looks more tappable than before. App Store screenshots (ScreenshotsUITests) change appearance. Does not touch tip-jar files.

**How to verify:** After the change, capture M07 (light/dark), a movie with saved progress (subtitle + progress bar visible), a series detail with resume, and the four download states in full-width and compact (episode row) variants on iOS 26 and iOS 18 simulators; check the largest Dynamic Type size for truncation; run UserFlowsUITests and ScreensUITests that tap Watch Now/Resume.

## ios26-design-7 — The Favorites type picker sits on a hand-made material band that paints a hard two-tone block over the navigation area.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Favorites (iPhone and iPad)
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/FavoritesView.swift:36-58`

**What the user perceives:** The top third of Favorites is a flat grey slab (dark grey in dark mode) from the status bar down to the segmented control, ending in a hard edge above the content (iphone-light/M09, iphone-dark/M09, ipad-light/L06). It does not look like the bar on any other screen. Title, search field and picker stack so that content starts about a third of the way down.

**Mechanism (finder):** The Picker is the first child of a VStack with `.padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial)` (FavoritesView.swift:37-44). `background(_:)` ignores safe-area edges by default, so the material extends under the navigation bar and search field. On iOS 26 that opaque band replaces the system scroll edge effect behind the glass buttons.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Remove the material and attach the picker as a bar accessory of the content:

extension View {
  @ViewBuilder func topAccessoryBar<V: View>(@ViewBuilder _ bar: () -> V) -> some View {
    if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { safeAreaBar(edge: .top, content: bar) }
    else { safeAreaInset(edge: .top, spacing: 0) { bar().background(.bar) } }
  }
}

Apply it to the Group holding the three grids. On iOS 26 the content scrolls under the picker with the system edge effect; on iOS 18 it keeps a standard bar material. Alternative: an inline title with the segmented Picker in `ToolbarItem(placement: .principal)`, which removes one row.

**APIs:** View.safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 26.0); View.safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/FavoritesView.swift:36-44: the segmented Picker is the first child of a VStack and has `.padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial)`. `background(_:ignoresSafeAreaEdges:)` with a ShapeStyle defaults to ignoring all safe-area edges, and the picker touches the top safe-area edge (it sits directly under the bar + search drawer), so the material is extended up to the top of the screen. Screenshots agree exactly: iphone-light/M09 shows a flat light-grey slab from the status bar to just below the picker with a hard edge against white content; iphone-dark/M09 shows a dark-grey slab against a black page; ipad-light/L06 shows the same slab behind the floating tab bar and title. No other screen has this (e.g. iphone-light/M07, ipad-light/L03 are plain). `git log -S'.background(.ultraThinMaterial)' -- Views/FavoritesView.swift` only returns d2489f9 (monorepo move) and there is no comment, so it is not documented deliberate work. Grep shows FavoritesView.swift:44 is the only such band outside the EPG guide; M3UFavoritesView.swift has no picker and is unaffected. Fix APIs exist and the helper compiles as written (non-escaping @ViewBuilder closure forwarded to safeAreaBar; `@ViewBuilder` func with `if #available`).

**Corrected claim:** The Favorites type picker's `.background(.ultraThinMaterial)` bleeds through the top safe area and paints a hard-edged grey band behind the navigation bar, title, search field and picker on iPhone and iPad (light and dark), unlike every other screen.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: delete FavoritesView.swift:44 and move the Picker out of the VStack into a top bar accessory on the Group at lines 46-54: `if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { content.safeAreaBar(edge: .top) { picker } } else { content.safeAreaInset(edge: .top, spacing: 0) { picker.background(.bar) } }` (picker keeps `.padding(.horizontal)` + small vertical padding). Two corrections: (a) on iOS 18 `.background(.bar)` also ignores the safe area and will tint the large-title/search area in dark mode; if that band is unwanted there, use `.background(Color(.systemBackground))` for the fallback so the picker simply sits on the page colour while content still scrolls under it; (b) do not use the suggested alternative `ToolbarItem(placement: .principal)`: on iPad the `.sidebarAdaptable` tab bar already occupies the centre of the top bar (ipad-light/L06), so a principal picker would collide with it. The absolute minimum, if no simulator time is available, is deleting line 44 alone: it removes the slab on both OS versions (content is then clipped at the picker's lower edge instead of scrolling under it).

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface 17361-17362: `nonisolated public func safeAreaBar(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> some View) -> some View` @available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0). `safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:)` is iOS 15.0. `.bar` ShapeStyle (BarMaterial) is iOS 15.

**Regression risks:** The Group contains either a ScrollView or the Spacer-based emptyState (FavoritesView.swift:178-191); the inset must be applied to the Group/container, not inside each grid, so the picker stays in place when switching type. How safeAreaBar stacks under a large title plus the search drawer on iOS 26.0 and whether the large title still collapses needs one simulator look. Picker identity must stay stable so `selectedType` animation is unaffected. No interaction with tip-jar files or earlier performance work.

**How to verify:** Screenshot M09 (light/dark) and ipad L06 after the change with enough favourites to scroll: no grey band, content passes under the picker with the system edge effect on iOS 26; on an iOS 18 simulator confirm the fallback has no dark band behind the large title and that content does not show through the picker.

## ios26-design-8 — Global search filters are hand-made chips on an opaque strip with a Divider instead of system search scopes.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:24-46, 67-69`

**What the user perceives:** When the field is focused the navigation bar collapses and a white strip of four pills with a hairline under it sits against the status bar, while the grouped results below are grey (iphone-light/Q02, Q03, Q05, R01). Results do not scroll under it with the system edge treatment. The pills do not look like any system control.

**Mechanism (finder):** The chips are Buttons with `Color.accentColor` or `systemGray5` backgrounds and `.cornerRadius(20)` inside a horizontal ScrollView, followed by `Divider()`, all in a VStack above the List (SearchView.swift:25-46). They are ordinary content, not part of the search UI, so they take no part in the bar or scroll edge behaviour.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the chip row and Divider with search scopes on the existing `.searchable`:

.searchScopes($selectedFilter, activation: .onSearchPresentation) {
  ForEach(SearchFilter.allCases, id: \.self) { Text($0.displayName).tag($0) }
}

No availability gate is needed (iOS 16.4). `onSelectFilter` keeps writing `selectedFilter`. Scopes show only while search is presented. If the scope bar does not render well together with the tab-role search field on iOS 26.0, keep the chips but host them with `safeAreaBar(edge: .top)` on iOS 26 and `safeAreaInset` plus `.background(.bar)` on iOS 18, and drop the Divider.

**APIs:** View.searchScopes(_:activation:_:) (iOS 16.4); SearchScopeActivation.onSearchPresentation (iOS 16.4); View.safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/SearchView.swift:24-46: the filters are four Buttons with `Color.accentColor`/`Color(.systemGray5)` fills and `.cornerRadius(20)` in a horizontal ScrollView followed by `Divider()`, stacked in a VStack above either the placeholder or the `.insetGrouped` List (245). The VStack has the default systemBackground while the List has the grouped background, which is exactly the white strip over grey results in iphone-light/Q03 and Q05; the chips are also shown in the idle state before any query (iphone-light/Q01). In dark mode (iphone-dark/Q03) both backgrounds are black, so only the hairline Divider remains: the two-tone strip is a light-mode-only artefact. History: only d2489f9, no comment. So the visual problem is real but smaller than described, and capsule filter pills as such are a common pattern, including in first-party media apps; the non-native part is the opaque strip + Divider + the chips living outside the scroll/bar system. The primary fix is unproven: `.searchScopes(_:activation:_:)` exists (iOS 16.4), but on iOS 26 this field is hosted by the `Tab(role: .search)` bottom bar (DashboardView.swift:77, Q02), and whether a scope bar is rendered at all, and where, in that configuration cannot be determined from the SDK interface; the finder acknowledges this by supplying a fallback. A four-segment segmented scope bar is also tighter than scrollable chips for the ten localisations. UI tests/tour tap `app.buttons["Movies"]` (ScreensUITests.swift:402) which would resolve differently with a scope bar.

**Corrected claim:** The search filter chips are laid out as plain content in a VStack with a Divider, so in light mode they sit on a white strip against the grey grouped results, they are visible before any query, and results cannot scroll under them with the system edge treatment. Dark mode shows only the divider. The chips themselves are an acceptable pattern; their hosting is what is off.

**Corrected fix:** Make the low-risk variant the primary fix: keep the chips, delete the Divider and the outer strip, show them only with results, and host them on the results List: in SearchView replace the VStack with the idle placeholder / `SearchResultsView(...)` branch and apply to the results branch `if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { .safeAreaBar(edge: .top) { chipRow } } else { .safeAreaInset(edge: .top, spacing: 0) { chipRow.background(.bar) } }`, so the strip shares the List's grouped background and gets the scroll-edge effect. Replace the idle Spacer/Image/Text with `ContentUnavailableView` if desired. Treat `.searchScopes($selectedFilter, activation: .onSearchPresentation) { ForEach(SearchFilter.allCases, id: \.self) { Text($0.displayName).tag($0) } }` as an optional upgrade only after a simulator run proves the scope bar renders with the tab-role search field on iPhone and iPad iOS 26.0 and on iOS 18, and fits all ten languages.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface 2493-2495: `func searchScopes<V, S>(_ scope: Binding<V>, activation: SearchScopeActivation, @ViewBuilder _ scopes: () -> S) -> some View where V: Hashable, S: View` @available(iOS 16.4, macOS 13.3, tvOS 16.4), watchOS unavailable. 2475-2487: `struct SearchScopeActivation` @available(iOS 16.4) with `automatic`, `onTextEntry`, `onSearchPresentation` (the latter two tvOS-unavailable). 17361-17362: `safeAreaBar(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment:spacing:content:)` @available(iOS 26.0). `SearchFilter` is `String, CaseIterable` hence Hashable, so the binding type-checks.

**Regression risks:** searchScopes: scope bar may not appear, or appear detached at the top while the field is at the bottom, with tab-role search on iOS 26; filters disappear whenever search is not presented; segmented titles may truncate in longer languages; `onSelectFilter` (SearchView.swift:63) keeps working either way. Chips-in-safe-area variant: none on behaviour; the `task(id:)` search pipeline and off-main filtering (SearchView.swift:246-278) are untouched. UI tour line 402 taps a button labelled Movies and must still find it.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 26.0 iPhone + iPad and iOS 18 iPhone: capture Q01/Q02/Q03/Q05 in light and dark; confirm no white strip, no divider, results scroll under the chips. If trying searchScopes: confirm the scope control is visible while the bottom search field is focused and after the keyboard is dismissed with a query present, in German/Russian/Arabic; UI test selecting Movies leaves only the Movies section.

## ios26-design-9 — Selecting the Search tab shows an empty placeholder page and needs a second tap on the morphed field before typing.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk medium
- Screens: Search tab (iPhone)
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:77-85`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:48-57`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Accept that the keyboard appears every time the Search tab is selected.

**What the user perceives:** Tapping the magnifier morphs the tab bar into a search field, but the page only shows a large Search title and a 'Type at least 2 characters' hint (iphone-light/Q01). The user must tap the field again to get the keyboard (Q02).

**Mechanism (finder):** The search tab uses the default activation, which presents the search page with the field unfocused. That default suits apps whose search page offers browse content; SearchView has only the placeholder branch at lines 48-57.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Activate search with the tab selection, gated, on the TabView in DashboardView:

if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { tabView.tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection) } else { tabView }

iOS 18 fallback: unchanged, the field is in the navigation drawer. Check that returning to the tab with an existing query (`globalSearchText`) keeps the results visible.

**APIs:** View.tabViewSearchActivation(_:) (iOS 26.0); TabSearchActivation.searchTabSelection (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** DashboardView.swift:77-83 declares `Tab(..., role: .search)` with no `tabViewSearchActivation`, so the default applies. The tour (another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:394-399) taps the Search tab, snaps Q01, then taps the field and snaps Q02: iphone-light/Q01 shows the tab bar morphed into an unfocused bottom field with only the title, chips and 'Type at least 2 characters'; Q02 shows the keyboard only after the second tap. SearchView.swift:48-57 indeed offers nothing to browse in the idle state. So the observation is correct. It is, however, the documented iOS 26 default and the same two-step behaviour Apple's own tabbed apps have, so it is a product choice rather than a defect, and severity is low. The fix API exists. What the finding omits: the UIKit counterpart documents a second effect. UIKit/UISearchTab.h:17-21 (`automaticallyActivatesSearch`, iOS 26.0): 'the search field will be activated when the tab is selected. Moreover, when search is cancelled, the previously selected tab in the tab bar will be restored and selected.' If SwiftUI's `.searchTabSelection` maps to this (likely, not provable from the interface), tapping the X leaves the Search tab altogether. That changes what the owner is deciding, and it interacts with `globalSearchText` kept in DashboardView.swift:14 and with pushed detail screens from results.

**Corrected claim:** On iOS 26 the Search tab opens with the bottom field unfocused and an empty placeholder page, so typing needs a second tap. This is the system default; because the search page has no browse content, activating search on tab selection is a reasonable product choice. Low severity.

**Corrected fix:** Optional, owner decision: wrap the TabView in a small modifier applied after `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)` in DashboardView: `struct SearchTabActivation: ViewModifier { func body(content: Content) -> some View { if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { content.tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection) } else { content } } }`. The branch is static per OS, so it does not remount the TabView or the player overlay. iOS 18 fallback: unchanged (field in the navigation drawer, `.always`). The decision to put to the owner is two-part: the keyboard comes up on every selection of the Search tab, and cancelling search (X) is expected to return to the previously selected tab instead of leaving an idle Search page. Verify both in the simulator before shipping; if the return-to-previous-tab behaviour drops the query or misbehaves after pushing a detail from results, keep the default.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface 11396-11401: `nonisolated public func tabViewSearchActivation(_ activation: TabSearchActivation) -> some View` @available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0), tvOS/watchOS/visionOS unavailable. 11404-11415: `public struct TabSearchActivation: Hashable, Sendable` @available(iOS 26.0) with `static var automatic` and `static var searchTabSelection` (@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0)). UIKit/UISearchTab.h:21 `@property BOOL automaticallyActivatesSearch API_AVAILABLE(ios(26.0))` with the cancel-restores-previous-tab documentation quoted above.

**Regression risks:** Cancel likely switches tabs: `tabBinding` (DashboardView.swift:26-34) will receive the restored tab, which is fine, but the user can no longer rest on an idle Search page. The keyboard appears on every Search-tab selection, including when returning to existing results; with the mini player docked it is deliberately kept above the keyboard (DashboardView.swift:114-118), so the card will jump up each time. Existing UI tests tap the tab and then `field.tap()` (ScreensUITests.swift:29-45, UserFlowsUITests.swift:293-322); they should still pass but need a run. iPad top-tab-bar behaviour is unverified.

**How to verify:** iOS 26 simulator, iPhone and iPad: tap Search and assert the keyboard is up and `app.searchFields.firstMatch` has focus; type a query, push a movie detail, go back (results still shown); tap X and record which tab becomes selected and whether the query is cleared; switch away and back with a query present; repeat with the mini player docked. iOS 18 simulator: behaviour unchanged.
