## ios26-design-10 — On iPad the top bar shows two magnifying-glass buttons side by side: the Search tab and the current tab's own filter field.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: iPad Live TV home, iPad Movies home, iPad Series home
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:145`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:146`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:77`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether the per-tab filter fields should exist at all next to the global Search tab is a product question for the search lens; the placement fix does not depend on it.

**What the user perceives:** ipad-light/L01 shows a magnifier inside the tab pill and a second one at the far right of the same row. They do different things (global search, filter this tab) and nothing tells them apart.

**Mechanism (finder):** The home views call `.searchable(text:isPresented:prompt:)` with automatic placement. On iPadOS 26 that resolves to a trailing toolbar item that is minimized to a button when space is tight. It lands next to the `Tab(role: .search)` item of the top tab bar. On iPhone the same call resolves to the drawer under the large title (iphone-dark/L01).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give the three home views an explicit `placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic)`. iPhone is unchanged. iPad shows the filter as a field under the title, like the pushed grids already do (ipad-light/L03), instead of a second magnifier. No availability gate is needed.

**APIs:** SearchFieldPlacement.navigationBarDrawer(displayMode:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** ipad-light/L01 shows the top bar with a magnifier inside the tab pill (the `Tab(role: .search)` item, DashboardView.swift:77) and a second, identical magnifier button at the far right. The three home views call `.searchable(text:isPresented:prompt:)` with automatic placement (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:93, Views/VODView.swift:145, Views/SeriesView.swift:146); on iPhone the same call lands in the drawer under the large title (iphone-dark/L01). So the duplication and its cause are real. Two corrections. Scope: the same duplication is visible on the pushed Favorites screen on iPad (ipad-light/L06: magnifier in the tab pill plus a trailing magnifier) because Views/FavoritesView.swift:58 also uses automatic placement and does not hide the tab bar; the finding lists only the three home tabs. Evidence for the fix: the finder cites ipad-light/L03 as proof of how the drawer looks on iPad, but that screen hides the tab bar (`.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)`, LiveStreamsView.swift:497), so it does not show the drawer together with the floating top tab bar; the result on the home tabs is plausible but not demonstrated. The fix also changes iPadOS 18 (automatic there is an inline trailing field in the bar), which the finding does not mention. M3UDashboardView has no search tab (only two Tabs at lines 27/37), so M3UChannelsView.swift:112 is not affected.

**Corrected claim:** On iPad with the top tab bar, every screen that keeps the tab bar visible and uses `.searchable` with automatic placement shows a second magnifier next to the Search tab: the Live TV, Movies and Series homes and the Favorites screen. They do different things (global search vs. filter this screen) and look identical.

**Corrected fix:** Add `placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .automatic)` to LiveStreamsView.swift:93, VODView.swift:145, SeriesView.swift:146 (the `searchable(text:isPresented:placement:prompt:)` overload) and to FavoritesView.swift:58. iPhone is unchanged on iOS 18 and 26 (automatic already resolves to the drawer there). No availability gate. Note for the owner: on iPad running iOS 18 the inline trailing search field also moves into a drawer row under the title. Confirm in the iPad simulator that the drawer field renders correctly under the floating tab bar before applying; whether the per-tab filter fields should exist next to global search remains a separate product question.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface 9342-9346: `public static func navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: SearchFieldPlacement.NavigationBarDrawerDisplayMode) -> SearchFieldPlacement` @available(iOS 15.0), macOS/tvOS/watchOS unavailable; 9354-9357: `struct NavigationBarDrawerDisplayMode { static let automatic; static let always }`. 5783-5786: `func searchable<S>(text: Binding<String>, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, placement: SearchFieldPlacement = .automatic, prompt: S) -> some View where S: StringProtocol` @available(iOS 17.0), so the existing `isPresented:` call accepts a placement.

**Regression risks:** iPad home tabs gain a full-width field row under the large title (one more row above the shelves) on both iPadOS 26 and 18. The `isSearchActive` binding and the reset in `.onChange(of: isSearchActive)` (LiveStreamsView.swift:102, VODView.swift:154, SeriesView.swift:155) keep working because only placement changes. With `.automatic` display mode the field may start collapsed on iPad until the user pulls down; if so use `.always` on iPad only. Does not touch shelf Equatable rows, filtering or pagination.

**How to verify:** iPad simulator (iOS 26.0 and iOS 18), portrait and landscape, tab bar and sidebar modes: screenshot Live TV, Movies, Series homes and Favorites; exactly one magnifier in the top bar and a filter field under the title that is visible at rest. iPhone L01/M01/S01/M09 pixel-identical to the current shots.

## ios26-design-11 — Season selector and TV Guide day selector are hand-drawn capsules with different metrics instead of a system toggle-button style.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail, TV Guide
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:433-478`, `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:104-123`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:318-342`

**What the user perceives:** The day chips in the guide (iphone-dark/L06) and the season chips look similar but not the same: different padding, one has an outline when unselected and the other a fill. They do not take the system's pressed look.

**Mechanism (finder):** Each is a `.buttonStyle(.plain)` Button with its own Capsule background: accent or `secondarySystemFill` with 12/6 padding (EPGGuideView.swift:112-118); accent or clear with a 1 pt stroke and 14/9 padding (DetailComponents.swift:448-465). Genre chips are a fourth variant on `.ultraThinMaterial` (326-335).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use one system control for selectable chips:

Toggle(isOn: Binding(get: { selectedId == season.id }, set: { if $0 { selectedId = season.id } })) { Text(title) }
  .toggleStyle(.button).buttonStyle(.bordered).buttonBorderShape(.capsule).controlSize(.small)

The on state gets the tinted system fill; the same code picks up the iOS 26 look. No gate is needed. Genre chips are labels, not controls, and can stay as plain capsule text with a `.quaternary` fill.

**APIs:** ToggleStyle.button (iOS 15.0); View.buttonBorderShape(_:) with .capsule (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:104-123 (day chips: caption font, 12/6 padding, accent or secondarySystemFill capsule, .buttonStyle(.plain)) and Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:433-478 (season chips: subheadline semibold, 14/9 padding, accent or clear capsule with a 1 pt stroke, .buttonStyle(.plain)). The metrics in the finding are accurate, and iphone-dark/L06 shows the day chips as described. Genre chips (DetailComponents.swift:318-342) are non-interactive labels, so they are not a 'fourth variant' of the same control. The finding missed a third selectable chip row: the search scope chips at Views/SearchView.swift:25-43 (systemGray5 fill, 14/7 padding, cornerRadius(20)), visible in iphone-light/Q03. No comment or history marks the differences as deliberate (git log -S'DetailSeasonTabBar' only returns the monorepo move d2489f9). Two parts of the claim are weaker than stated: the two rows are never on screen together, so the mismatch is a consistency nit a user will barely notice, and .plain buttons on iOS still dim when pressed, so 'no pressed look' is overstated. A real gap the finding did not mention: none of the chip rows expose the selected state to VoiceOver (no .isSelected trait anywhere in these blocks). There is no screenshot of season chips: iphone-*/S03 and S04 show an HTTP 404 error screen for the demo series. The proposed Toggle fix compiles, but how ButtonToggleStyle renders on/off under .bordered + capsule on iOS 26 and iOS 18 cannot be read from the SDK, and .controlSize(.small) would shrink the season chips' tap height (currently about 36 pt) to about 28 pt.

**Corrected claim:** Three selectable chip rows (TV Guide day picker, season picker, search scope chips) are hand-drawn with three different sets of padding, font and unselected fill, and none exposes its selected state to accessibility. It is a low-severity consistency and accessibility issue, not a visible defect on any single screen. Genre chips are labels and are not part of it.

**Corrected fix:** Unify the selectable chips behind one component and add the selected trait. Preferred, if a simulator screenshot on iOS 26 and iOS 18 confirms the look: Toggle(isOn: Binding(get: { isSelected }, set: { if $0 { select() } })) { Text(title) }.toggleStyle(.button).buttonStyle(.bordered).buttonBorderShape(.capsule), with default control size for the season row (do not use .small there). Keep the existing behaviour inside the setter: withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.85)) for seasons and Task { await model.selectDay(day) } for days; keep .id(season.id) and the onChange scrollTo. If the Toggle look is off (for example accent-coloured text in the off state), fall back to one shared private ButtonStyle (capsule, accent fill when selected, secondarySystemFill otherwise, opacity change on configuration.isPressed) plus .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : []), used at EPGGuideView.swift:109-118, DetailComponents.swift:443-466 and SearchView.swift:28-39. No availability gate needed either way. Leave GenreChipRow as is.

**API check:** ToggleStyle.button: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1144-1147, '@available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, watchOS 9.0, *) extension ToggleStyle where Self == ButtonToggleStyle { static var button }'. ButtonToggleStyle struct at :1151-1153, iOS 15.0. View.buttonBorderShape(_:) at :15048-15050, iOS 15.0; ButtonBorderShape.capsule at :15059 (iOS 15.0; the extra @available only restricts macOS 14 / tvOS 17). View.controlSize(_:) present in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6168. AccessibilityTraits.isSelected at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:4934; accessibilityAddTraits at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23208. How a button-style Toggle looks under .bordered is runtime behaviour and is not verifiable from the interface.

**Regression risks:** Season selection drives the episode reload and the centre-scroll (DetailComponents.swift:472-475, SeriesView.swift:1030-1042); the Toggle setter must keep the spring animation and ignore the 'off' tap on the selected chip. Day selection must stay async (model.selectDay). .controlSize(.small) would reduce tap targets. The Toggle look differs between iOS 18 and iOS 26, so both need a screenshot. UI tests that tap chips by label should keep working since the label text is unchanged, but a Toggle reports as a switch/toggle button element rather than a plain button, so check any app.buttons[...] lookups for 'Today', 'Movies' and so on.

**How to verify:** Simulator screenshots on iOS 26 and iOS 18, light and dark: TV Guide with the day row, a series with at least three seasons (the demo series returns 404, so use a playlist with real series info), and search results with the scope chips. Check selected and unselected contrast and chip height (at least about 34 pt for seasons). VoiceOver: the selected chip is announced as selected. Functional: tapping a season reloads episodes and centres the chip; tapping a day reloads the grid.

## ios26-design-12 — The sort/filter toolbar button uses a circle-outlined symbol, which draws a ring inside the round glass button on iOS 26.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV category / All Channels, Movies category / All Movies, Series category / All Series
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:669-673`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:772-776`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:713-717`

**What the user perceives:** The top-right button on grids is a circle inside a circle (iphone-dark/L03, M03; iphone-light/S02; ipad-light/L03). With an active filter it becomes a filled disc inside the glass disc.

**Mechanism (finder):** The label is `line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle` or `.circle.fill` with a forced semibold font. Before iOS 26 the circle variant supplied the button shape; now the glass capsule supplies it.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Pick the symbol by OS and show the active state with tint:

if #available(iOS 26.0, *) {
  Label(L("sort.title"), systemImage: "line.3.horizontal.decrease").foregroundStyle(isFilterActive ? Color.accentColor : Color.primary)
} else {
  Label(L("sort.title"), systemImage: isFilterActive ? "line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle.fill" : "line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle")
}

Drop the font override. iOS 18 keeps the circle pair.

**APIs:** SF Symbol line.3.horizontal.decrease (iOS 13.0 (SF Symbols 1))

**Verifier reasons:** Code is as cited: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:670-671, Views/VODView.swift:773-774 and Views/SeriesView.swift:714-715 all use Image(systemName: isFilterActive ? "line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle.fill" : "line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle").font(.body.weight(.semibold)) as the Menu label in a navigationBarTrailing ToolbarItem. Screenshots iphone-dark/L03, iphone-dark/M03 and iphone-light/S02 clearly show the circled glyph inside the round glass button, a ring within a ring. The symbols were introduced in 654cefc (catalog sort/filter) with no comment saying the circle is intentional; it is the pre-iOS 26 convention. No other circle-variant symbol sits in a browse toolbar (grep of Views for '.circle' symbols: the rest are in rows or sheets). So the claim stands. Two corrections to the fix: (1) the stated availability is wrong: in the system symbol catalog (CoreGlyphs name_availability.plist, both macOS and the iOS 26.0 simulator runtime) line.3.horizontal.decrease is release 2021 = iOS 15.0; the iOS 13 name was line.horizontal.3.decrease. Harmless for an iOS 18 target. (2) Showing the active state through .foregroundStyle on a Menu label inside a toolbar is not guaranteed to be honoured by the bar; if it is ignored, the active indication is lost on iOS 26. .tint on the Menu is the safer route and needs one screenshot to confirm.

**Corrected claim:** On iOS 26 the sort/filter toolbar button on the three category/All grids draws a circle-outlined (or circle-filled when active) symbol inside the system's round glass button. The claim stands as written.

**Corrected fix:** In the three sortFilterMenu labels pick the symbol by OS: on iOS 26 use Label(L("sort.title"), systemImage: "line.3.horizontal.decrease") and mark the active state with .tint(isFilterActive ? Color.accentColor : Color.primary) applied to the Menu (verify on the simulator that the glyph takes the tint; if not, try .foregroundStyle on the Label). On iOS 18 keep the existing circle / circle.fill pair. Drop the .font(.body.weight(.semibold)) override so the glyph matches the other toolbar icons. Because colour alone then carries the state on iOS 26, keep an accessibility signal as well (the Menu's Picker already shows the checked sort option; optionally add .accessibilityValue for the active state). A small shared helper view for the label avoids repeating the #available block three times.

**API check:** SF Symbol line.3.horizontal.decrease: present in CoreGlyphs name_availability.plist with release '2021' (iOS 15.0), not iOS 13.0 as the finding states; the .circle and .circle.fill variants are also 2021. Symbols are not in the SDK interface files. View.tint(_ tint: Color?) is declared in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19529 (iOS 15+). Menu: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7116-7118, iOS 14.0. Label and #available are standard.

**Regression risks:** If the tint or foregroundStyle is not honoured in the glass toolbar, the active-filter indication disappears on iOS 26; confirm with a screenshot before shipping. The UI tests find the button as app.buttons["Sort"] (ScreensUITests.swift:317, 350); a Label titled L("sort.title") keeps that label, so keep either the Label title or the existing .accessibilityLabel. No effect on the off-main sort/filter pipeline.

**How to verify:** Simulator screenshots of a Live, Movies and Series category grid on iOS 26 and iOS 18, each with default sort and with a non-default sort or an active filter: iOS 26 shows a plain three-line glyph that turns accent-coloured when active; iOS 18 is unchanged. Run the existing UI tests that tap app.buttons["Sort"].

## ios26-design-13 — The two-option playlist type picker opens as a full-height sheet, and the category picker's opaque list background covers the system glass at medium height.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Playlist list, Add playlist, Category picker sheet
- Code: `another-iptv-player/ContentView.swift:90-109, 189-201`, `another-iptv-player/Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:11-49`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:64-81, 97-98`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether the type choice may lose its explanatory full-row layout in favour of a menu.

**What the user perceives:** Tapping + covers the whole screen with a sheet holding two rows (iphone-light/P02), which then closes and a second sheet opens. The category picker at half height is a flat grey panel (iphone-light/L03, iphone-dark/L07) rather than the translucent glass that partial-height system sheets show on iOS 26.

**Mechanism (finder):** PlaylistTypeSelectionView is a NavigationStack with a List and no detents, and it chains `dismiss()` with a 0.2 s `asyncAfter` before presenting the form (lines 15-18, 28-31). CategoryPickerSheet uses detents correctly, but its `.insetGrouped` List paints `systemGroupedBackground` over the sheet. No sheet in the browse code sets `presentationBackground`, so there is nothing custom to drop.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Type picker: replace the sheet with a Menu on the + button, which morphs out of the glass button on iOS 26 and is a normal menu on iOS 18:

Menu {
  Button { showingAddXtreamPlaylist = true } label: { Text(L("playlist_type.xtream.title")); Text(L("playlist_type.xtream.subtitle")) }
  Button { showingAddM3UPlaylist = true } label: { Text(L("playlist_type.m3u.title")); Text(L("playlist_type.m3u.subtitle")) }
} label: { Label(L("playlist_type.title"), systemImage: "plus") }

Use the same Menu content for the empty-state button. Category picker (optional, iOS 26 only): `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` behind `if #available(iOS 26.0, *)`; check the `.large` detent, where rows could lose contrast in light mode. iOS 18 keeps the grouped background.

**APIs:** Menu (iOS 14.0); View.scrollContentBackground(_:) (iOS 16.0); View.presentationDetents(_:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Part (a), the type picker, is confirmed. ContentView.swift:90-109 presents PlaylistTypeSelectionView as a plain .sheet with no detents; Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:11-49 is a NavigationStack + List with two rows, and each row calls dismiss() then DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(0.2) before flipping the flag for the second sheet (lines 14-18, 27-31). iphone-light/P02 shows a full-height sheet with two rows and an empty remainder. The same flag is used by the empty-state button (ContentView.swift:189-200). No comment explains the design; history only shows the monorepo move. A user sees sheet up, sheet down, second sheet up. It is a rarely used flow (adding a playlist), so severity stays low. The finding missed that committed UI tests depend on the sheet: another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:173-186 asserts a navigation bar titled 'Add Playlist' or the static text 'Playlist Type' after tapping the plus button, and :188-225 tap rows by label; the first test breaks with a Menu, and the plus-button lookup (navigationBars.buttons["plus"]) may break if the label becomes a titled Label. Part (b), the category picker, is not established as a defect. Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:64-98 is a standard insetGrouped List in a NavigationStack with [.medium, .large] detents; iphone-light/L03 and iphone-dark/L07 show it opaque. The statement that no browse sheet sets presentationBackground is correct (grep: only presentationBackgroundInteraction in the player's track sheet). Whether hiding the list background gives a good glass sheet, and whether rows keep contrast at the large detent in light mode, cannot be decided from code; the same grouped look is used by the other detent sheets (EPGGuideView.swift:67-72, ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:50, the owner's TipJarView.swift:56), so changing one sheet would make them inconsistent.

**Corrected claim:** The add-playlist type choice (two options) is shown as a full-height sheet that then closes and, after a hard-coded 0.2 s delay, opens a second sheet with the form. That is heavier than the system pattern for a two-way choice. The category picker's opaque grouped background is the standard List look and is not shown to be a problem.

**Corrected fix:** Type picker: replace the first sheet with a Menu on the plus toolbar button in ContentView.swift:90-96, with two buttons that set showingAddXtreamPlaylist / showingAddM3UPlaylist directly (title Text plus subtitle Text, optionally an icon, so the explanation is kept). Keep Image(systemName: "plus") as the Menu label, or add .accessibilityIdentifier("plus"), so existing lookups still work. Use the same Menu content around the empty-state button label (ContentView.swift:189-200). Remove showingTypePicker, its .sheet and PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift (and the now unused playlist_type.section key, without touching the uncommitted tip keys in the same files; simplest is to leave the key in place). Update test_playlistList_addButton_opensTypeSelectionSheet to assert the two menu items instead of the sheet header. No availability gate. This is a product decision the owner should approve, because the explanatory rows become menu items. Category picker: do nothing now; if the owner wants glass sheets, treat it as a separate experiment across all detent sheets after a simulator check.

**API check:** Menu: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7116-7118, '@available(iOS 14.0, macOS 11.0, tvOS 17.0, *) public struct Menu<Label, Content>'. View.scrollContentBackground(_:): :10930-10933, iOS 16.0. View.presentationDetents(_:): :22137-22139, iOS 16.0. Menu items showing a second Text as a subtitle is runtime behaviour (iOS 15+) and is not visible in the interface. No presentationBackground call exists in the browse code (grep confirmed).

**Regression risks:** Three committed UI tests cover this flow (ScreensUITests.swift:173-225): the sheet-header assertion fails with a Menu and must be rewritten; the label-contains lookups for 'Xtream Code' and 'M3U' should still match menu items, but confirm, because a menu item's accessibility label combines title and subtitle. The empty-state button's custom full-width label must render correctly as a Menu label. If part (b) were applied anyway: white rows on a white sheet at the large detent in light mode, and inconsistency with the EPG and tip-jar sheets.

**How to verify:** Simulator: tap plus on the playlist list, confirm a menu with two items (title and subtitle) appears and that choosing Xtream or M3U opens the form directly with a single sheet animation; repeat from the empty state and on iPad. Run the three add-playlist UI tests after updating the first one. For part (b), only a simulator run can settle it: screenshot the category picker with .scrollContentBackground(.hidden) at medium and large detents, light and dark, on iOS 26, and compare row contrast.

## ios26-design-14 — Category and All grids never show how many items they hold; iOS 26 has a system subtitle slot for that.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV category / All Channels, Movies category / All Movies, Series category / All Series, Watch history
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:584-632`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:675-740`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:634-681`

**What the user perceives:** With tens of thousands of items, a category or a filtered or sorted result gives no sense of size (iphone-dark/M03, M04, L05). The only counts in the app are in the category picker and search section headers.

**Mechanism (finder):** The grid views hold the filtered result in `displayItems` but never surface the count. On iOS 26 the navigation bar can show a subtitle under the title.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add a gated helper and call it inside the three `*CategoryContent` bodies, next to their `.toolbar`:

extension View {
  @ViewBuilder func navigationSubtitleIfAvailable(_ text: String) -> some View {
    if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { navigationSubtitle(text) } else { self }
  }
}
.navigationSubtitleIfAvailable(L("browse.count.movies_format", displayItems.count))

iOS 18 fallback: no subtitle. It needs three new count keys in the ten Localizable.strings files; add them without touching the uncommitted tip keys.

**APIs:** View.navigationSubtitle(_:) (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The API is real: navigationSubtitle is available on iOS 26.0 only. The three grid bodies (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:584-632, Views/VODView.swift:675-740, Views/SeriesView.swift:634-681) hold displayItems and attach their own .toolbar, so a subtitle set there would reach the parent's large-title bar (titles are set by the parents with .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.large), e.g. LiveStreamsView.swift:495-498, VODView.swift:561-564, SeriesView.swift:533-536). L(key, args...) with a format exists (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:135-138). So the proposal compiles. But this is an added feature, not a defect: nothing is broken, and whether to show counts is the owner's call. Three problems with the fix as written: (1) displayItems is filled asynchronously by recompute() in a .task (LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577, VODView.swift:653-668, SeriesView.swift:615-627), so the subtitle would first read '0 ...' or be absent and then appear, which is exactly the pop-in and layout jump the owner wants removed; with a large title, adding a subtitle after the first frame can change the bar height. (2) Count strings in this project use plural rules in Localization/*.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict (keys such as settings.stats.history_items_format and detail.episode_count_plural, present in all ten languages); adding plain '%d movies' keys only to Localizable.strings gives wrong plurals in Russian and Arabic. (3) The M3U group grid (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:500-503) would be left without it. 'Watch history' is listed as a surface but no code for it is cited. Evidence is code only; there is no screenshot of a subtitle under this app's large title with the search drawer.

**Corrected claim:** The category and All grids show no item count. iOS 26 offers a navigation-bar subtitle that could carry one. This is an optional enhancement and a product decision, not a native-feel defect.

**Corrected fix:** If the owner wants it: add the gated helper (if #available(iOS 26.0, *) { navigationSubtitle(text) } else { self }) and call it in the three *CategoryContent bodies next to .toolbar, plus the M3U group grid for parity. Avoid pop-in: derive the count from data available on the first frame (items.count when no filter is active, displayItems.count once a filter is active) and pass an empty string while the count is 0. Use a plural-aware string: either reuse the existing settings.stats.history_items_format key (already in Localizable.strings and Localizable.stringsdict for all ten languages, which avoids touching the files that hold the uncommitted tip keys) or add one new generic key to both the .strings and .stringsdict files without disturbing the tip keys. iOS 18 fallback: no subtitle. Check on the simulator that the subtitle does not shift the grid when it appears.

**API check:** View.navigationSubtitle: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:18677-18691, '@available(iOS 26.0, macCatalyst 14.0, macOS 11.0, *)', unavailable on tvOS, watchOS and visionOS; overloads for Text, LocalizedStringKey, LocalizedStringResource and a disfavoured generic StringProtocol. Passing a Swift String from L(...) resolves to the StringProtocol overload. Must be gated behind #available(iOS 26.0, *).

**Regression risks:** A subtitle that appears after the async recompute can cause a visible jump under the large title during the push transition. Wrong plural forms if the string is not added to the stringsdict. Editing Localizable.strings touches files with the owner's uncommitted tip keys; reuse of an existing key avoids that. The count changes on every keystroke of the in-screen search, which is acceptable but should be checked for flicker. No effect on the paginated grid or the off-main sort/filter if the count is read from existing state.

**How to verify:** Simulator, iOS 26: open a category and All Movies/Series/Channels on a large catalog; record the push transition and confirm the subtitle is present from the first frame and the grid does not shift; toggle a filter and type in search to see the count update; scroll to check the collapsed inline bar. Repeat in Russian and Arabic for plural forms. iOS 18: confirm nothing changes.

## ios26-design-15 — Artwork corner radii are an unrelated set of values and look tight next to the iOS 26 bar and list shapes; search result thumbnails end up square.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Shelves and grids, Search results, Continue Watching, Detail hero
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/CachedImage.swift:57, 82`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:438`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:74`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:107, 248, 306`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:317-318`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Choose the poster radius; this is a look decision.

**What the user perceives:** Posters have small 8 pt corners while channel icons use 12, the hero poster 14 and the system rows around them are much rounder (iphone-light/M01 against Q03). In search results the movie thumbnails have square corners inside very round rows (Q03, Q05).

**Mechanism (finder):** `CachedImage` defaults to radius 8; callers override it with 12, 14, 8 or 6 ad hoc. In ResultRow the image is loaded with the default `.fit` mode into a 44x44 box, so a portrait poster is narrower than the box and the rounded clip never touches its corners.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Define two radii in one place (for example 12 for posters and channel icons, 8 for thumbnails under 60 pt) and use them at the listed sites. Give search thumbnails `contentMode: .fill` so the clip applies. `ConcentricRectangle` is not appropriate for posters, which are not nested inside a rounded container; keep fixed continuous radii. No availability gate is needed.

**APIs:** RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:style:) with .continuous default (iOS 13.0); ConcentricRectangle (iOS 26.0 (not recommended here))

**Verifier reasons:** The search thumbnail defect is confirmed. Views/SearchView.swift:317-318 loads CachedImage at 44x44 with the default contentMode .fit (Views/CachedImage.swift:58), and the clip is applied to the 44x44 frame (CachedImage.swift:81-82, then again at SearchView.swift:318), so a portrait poster is narrower than the box and its corners are never clipped. iphone-light/Q03 shows exactly this: square-cornered portrait thumbnails in rounded rows. The same pattern exists at Views/DownloadsView.swift:237-243 (56x56, .fit, outer clip 8), which the finding missed. The radius list is accurate (default 8 at CachedImage.swift:57; 12 at LiveStreamsView.swift:438, M3UChannelsView.swift:426 and ContinueWatchingRow.swift:74; 14 at DetailComponents.swift:107; 10 at WatchHistoryListView.swift:166; 6 in the EPG rows), but that the 8 pt posters 'look tight' is a matter of taste: in iphone-light/M01 and iphone-dark/M03 the posters look coherent, and different radii for different artwork sizes is normal. Two corrections to the fix: ResultRow is shared by live channels, movies and series (SearchView.swift:157-211); switching it wholesale to .fill would crop wide channel logos, which the app deliberately shows with .fit everywhere (LiveStreamsView.swift:434-441). And contentMode is part of the image request (CachedImage.swift:110-117), so the statement that requests are unaffected only holds for the radius; search has no prefetch (grep ListImagePrefetch), so the changed key is harmless there.

**Corrected claim:** Movie and series thumbnails in search results (and in the Downloads list) are shown with aspect-fit inside a square box, so the rounded clip never reaches the poster and the corners stay square. Separately, artwork radii vary by call site (6, 8, 10, 12, 14); consolidating them is optional polish and a look decision, not a defect.

**Corrected fix:** Search: give ResultRow a content-mode (or a 'poster' flag) parameter; pass .fill for the movie and series rows (SearchView.swift:183-186, 208-211) and keep .fit for live channel rows (157-160). Remove the redundant outer .clipShape at SearchView.swift:318 and pass cornerRadius to CachedImage instead. Optionally use a poster-shaped thumbnail (for example 40x60) for movies and series, as system media lists do, instead of a square crop; that changes row height and is the owner's call. Apply the same .fill change to the Downloads row (DownloadsView.swift:237-243), where every item is a movie or episode. Radius consolidation: only if the owner wants it, define two constants next to PosterMetrics and use them at the listed call sites; no availability gate; do not use ConcentricRectangle for free-standing posters.

**API check:** RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:style:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:10347-10354, style defaults to .continuous, so CachedImage's clip is already continuous. ConcentricRectangle: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface, '@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, visionOS 26.0, *) public struct ConcentricRectangle : Shape, Animatable' (correctly not proposed). CachedImage's contentMode maps into Nuke's ImageProcessors.Resize contentMode (Views/CachedImage.swift:110-117), so it is part of the request and cache key; cornerRadius is not.

**Regression risks:** Using .fill for all search rows would crop wide or transparent channel logos; keep .fit for live. Changing contentMode changes the Nuke request key, so render and any prefetch must use the same mode; search and downloads have no prefetch, but do not change contentMode on shelf or grid cards without updating ListImagePrefetch calls (LiveStreamsView.swift:410, 680; VODView.swift:480, 793; SeriesView.swift:452, 732), which is deliberate earlier work. A poster-shaped thumbnail increases search row height. Changing radii app-wide alters every shelf and grid and should be reviewed in screenshots first.

**How to verify:** Simulator screenshots of search results for a query that returns live channels, movies and series (Q03, Q05) and of the Downloads list, light and dark: movie and series thumbnails have rounded corners, channel logos are not cropped. If radii are consolidated, compare M01, L01, the Continue Watching row and the detail hero before and after.

## ios26-design-16 — `tabViewBottomAccessory` is the system home for a mini player on iOS 26, but it cannot replace the app's floating video card; keeping the card is an owner decision.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Dashboard with docked mini player
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:47-123`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:25-82`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Keep the floating video card (recommended) or additionally build a controls-only bottom accessory for iOS 26.

**What the user perceives:** Today a floating video card docks in a screen corner above the tab bar and can be dragged between corners. In Music and Podcasts on iOS 26 the mini player is a glass capsule attached to the tab bar that shrinks next to the minimized bar.

**Mechanism (finder):** The player is an in-window overlay above the TabView; minimizing keeps PlayerView mounted and transforms it into the card (DashboardView.swift:92-122). The system accessory is a fixed-height strip owned by the TabView. In this SDK the only overload is `tabViewBottomAccessory(content:)`, with no enable flag, so showing it conditionally means applying the modifier conditionally on the TabView.

**Proposed fix (finder):** No change proposed. For the accessory: the system places it, it follows `tabBarMinimizeBehavior`, it needs no hard-coded tab bar allowance, and it matches Music. Against it: the strip cannot show live video at a useful size, where the card is a picture-in-picture style video surface; it is iOS 26 only, so the card must stay for iOS 18 and there would be two implementations; conditional application risks rebuilding the TabView and its navigation state; and the video must stay in the overlay to keep playback and AirPlay continuity. If adopted later, it would be a second, controls-only surface for audio-style playback, not a replacement.

**APIs:** View.tabViewBottomAccessory(content:) (iOS 26.0 (only overload in the 26.0 SDK)); EnvironmentValues.tabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** I tried to refute this three ways and none held.

(1) The architecture is as described. The player is a sibling ZStack above the TabView with zIndex 10_000 (Views/DashboardView.swift:47-123, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:25-82). Minimizing only flips PlayerOverlayController.mode to .mini (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:88-92); item.root stays mounted. The comments at DashboardView.swift:105-107 and 116-121 say the modifiers are kept unconditional precisely so PlayerView is never remounted, and PlayerOverlayController.swift:52-53 ties that identity to AirPlay continuity. The card is a live video surface that docks to four corners (Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:458-464, PlayerView.swift:401), follows the video aspect "like system PiP" (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:466-470) and reserves a hard-coded 49 pt for the tab bar on compact widths (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:475-478, PlayerView.swift:1954).

(2) The SDK claim is exact. In the 26.0 SDK the only declaration is tabViewBottomAccessory(content:), iOS 26.0 only, with no isEnabled parameter, so showing it conditionally from SwiftUI means an if/else around the TabView. That changes the TabView's structural identity and would reset all five NavigationStacks.

(3) Deliberate earlier work argues against a swap. The mini card was reworked in 2ec2c18 last week and the files are out of scope. No source file uses tabViewBottomAccessory, tabBarMinimizeBehavior or any iOS 26 availability check today, so adoption would create a second mini-player implementation next to the iOS 18 card.

The product argument also holds: Music and Podcasts use the accessory for audio, while a video app's native analogue is a PiP-style floating surface, which is what the card is. No screenshot shows the docked mini player, so nothing visual contradicts the finding. "No change, owner decision" is the right outcome.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands as stated, with two additions.

- **UIKit has a removable accessory, but the app cannot reach it.** UITabBarController.bottomAccessory is nullable and has setBottomAccessory(_:animated:) on iOS 26.0, so UIKit can show and hide it without an identity change. The app uses a SwiftUI TabView and has no supported handle on the underlying controller, so this does not change the conclusion.
- **Whether an empty accessory collapses is unverified.** The interface file cannot tell whether an always-applied accessory with empty content collapses or leaves an empty glass capsule on iOS 26.0. That is one more reason not to adopt it on this SDK.

**Corrected fix:** none. Keep the floating video card. If the owner later wants the Music-style capsule, treat it as a separate product decision: an additional controls-only surface on iOS 26 (title, play/pause, expand), applied unconditionally to the TabView, with the video and the PlayerView staying in the existing overlay, and the card kept for iOS 18. Do not build it against the 26.0 SDK, where the only way to hide it from SwiftUI is conditional application.

**API check:** All in the iPhoneSimulator26.0 SDK (Xcode 26.0.1, build 17A400).

- **View.tabViewBottomAccessory**: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13703-13709, `@available(iOS 26.0, *)`, unavailable on macOS, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS: `nonisolated public func tabViewBottomAccessory<Content>(@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) -> some View where Content : View`. It is the only overload; there is no isEnabled variant.
- **EnvironmentValues.tabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement**: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5512-5515, iOS 26.0, type `TabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement?`, get-only.
- **TabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement**: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5536-5539, iOS 26.0, cases `.inline` and `.expanded`.
- **View.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(_:)**: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8977-8978, iOS 26.0. `TabBarMinimizeBehavior` (8981 onward) has `.automatic`, `.onScrollDown` and `.onScrollUp`.
- **UIKit**: `UITabAccessory` with `initWithContentView:` (UITabAccessory.h:16-25, iOS 26.0); `UITabBarController.bottomAccessory`, nullable, and `setBottomAccessory:animated:` (UITabBarController.h:128-131, iOS 26.0).

None of these are used anywhere in the app sources.

**Regression risks:** Doing nothing carries no regression risk. If the accessory were adopted anyway:

- **Navigation state loss.** Conditional application on the TabView resets every tab's NavigationStack and scroll position each time playback starts or stops.
- **Playback and AirPlay teardown.** Moving the video into the accessory would remount PlayerView, which the comments at DashboardView.swift:105-121 and PlayerOverlayController.swift:52-53 exist to prevent.
- **Two implementations.** The corner-docking card, its drag-to-dismiss gestures and the 49 pt allowance from commit 2ec2c18 would have to be kept for iOS 18 and maintained alongside the new surface.
- **Overlap.** With the tab bar minimized, the card's rest position and the accessory would compete for the same bottom region.

**How to verify:** Nothing to verify for the recommended no-change outcome.

If the owner chooses to prototype the controls-only accessory, test on an iOS 26 device, not only the simulator:

1. Start playback, minimize, switch through all five tabs and push a detail screen. Confirm navigation paths and scroll offsets survive the accessory appearing and disappearing.
2. Confirm audio, video and an active AirPlay session continue across minimize and expand.
3. With no playback, check whether an empty glass capsule is left above the tab bar.
4. Check the iPad sidebarAdaptable layout, in both tab bar and sidebar modes.

## design-system-consistency-1 — Grid rows are jagged: posters and channel tiles in the same row sit at different heights whenever one title wraps to two lines

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live category detail, All Channels, Movies category detail, All Movies, Series category detail, All Series, Favorites, M3U group detail, M3U favorites, Live TV home shelves
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397, 443-448, 597-613`, `Views/VODView.swift:528-533, 635-637, 690-709`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:500-505, 598-600, 648-662`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:431-436, 573-589`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:28-33`

**What the user perceives:** In every grid the artwork does not form a straight line: a card with a one-line title is pushed about half a text line lower than a neighbour with a two-line title, so rows look uneven while scrolling. Visible in iphone-dark/M04-movies-all.png ("Echoes of Tomorrow" poster starts ~8 pt above its neighbours), iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png (rows 1, 3 and 4) and iphone-dark/L03-live-category-detail.png. With real catalogs (long channel and movie names) almost every row is affected. On Live TV home the shelf height itself depends on which titles are currently realized.

**Mechanism (finder):** All grids build columns as GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:), spacing:) with no alignment (LiveStreamsView.swift:597-599, VODView.swift:635-637, SeriesView.swift:598-600, M3UChannelsView.swift:573-576, FavoritesView.swift:28-33), so LazyVGrid centres each cell vertically in its row. The cards have a variable intrinsic height because the title is .lineLimit(2) without reserved space (LiveStreamsView.swift:443-448, VODView.swift:528-533, SeriesView.swift:500-505, M3UChannelsView.swift:431-436). Shorter cards are therefore centred lower. The Live and M3U shelves have no fixed height either (LiveStreamsView.swift:382-397, M3UChannelsView.swift:363-377): the LazyHStack takes the height of the realized cards, so a shelf grows by one caption line when a long name scrolls in.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Two small changes that belong together. (1) Give every grid column a top alignment: GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: w), spacing: s, alignment: .top) in the five places above. (2) Make card height deterministic: replace .lineLimit(2) with .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true) in the four card titles (and .lineLimit(1, reservesSpace: true) is not needed for the optional category line, it is only used in Favorites where every card has it). After (2) the Live shelf placeholder at LiveStreamsView.swift:374 (liveShelfIcon + 30) should use the same height as a real card. For the Movies/Series shelves this must land together with the shelf-height finding, otherwise the reserved second line does not fit the fixed frame. No iOS 26 API involved.

**APIs:** GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:) (iOS 14.0); View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read every cited site. All six content grids build a single adaptive GridItem with no alignment: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:597-599, Views/VODView.swift:635-637, Views/SeriesView.swift:598-600, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:573-576, Views/FavoritesView.swift:28-33. GridItem.alignment is Optional and nil means centre, so a shorter cell is centred inside the row. The four cards have a variable height: title is .lineLimit(2) with no reserved space (LiveStreamsView.swift:443-448, VODView.swift:528-533, SeriesView.swift:500-505, M3UChannelsView.swift:431-436). Screenshots show exactly this: iphone-dark/M04-movies-all.png (the 'Echoes of Tomorrow' poster starts about 8 pt above its two neighbours), iphone-dark/L05-live-all-channels.png (rows 1, 3, 4) and iphone-dark/L03-live-category-detail.png ('Morning Update'). No comment or history marks this as deliberate (git log -S'alignment: .top' only hits the LazyHStack shelves, which are already top-aligned). With real IPTV names in 90 pt wide live tiles (liveGridIconSize = scaled(180) = 90 on iPhone, Views/PosterMetrics.swift:27) most rows will mix one- and two-line titles. One sub-claim is weaker than stated: that a Live/M3U shelf 'grows by one caption line when a long name scrolls in' is not provable from code. The comment at Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:46-48 ('shelves that were laid out before EPG arrived could clip the progress capsule') suggests the lazy shelf keeps its first measured height and clips later, taller cards rather than growing. Either outcome is a defect and the same fix removes it. The existing Live placeholder (LiveStreamsView.swift:374, icon + 30) already disagrees with a real card (icon + 10 + 16/32, plus 10 + 22 when the EPG line is shown).

**Corrected claim:** Grid rows are jagged on every poster and channel grid because cells are centre-aligned and card height depends on whether the title wraps. On the un-pinned Live and M3U shelves the shelf height depends on the first realised cards; a later two-line title either grows the shelf or gets its EPG line clipped (which of the two is not settled by reading the code).

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two adjustments. (1) GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: w), spacing: s, alignment: .top) in the five files; this alone straightens the artwork. (2) .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true) on the four card titles makes card height deterministic, which is what the shelves need; in grids it adds one empty caption line under rows where no title wraps, an accepted trade-off. VODStreamCard and SeriesCard are shared with the fixed-height Movies/Series shelves, so (2) must ship together with finding 3, otherwise the reserved second line overflows the 32 pt caption allowance. For the Live placeholder use icon + 10 + two caption lines, but do not add @Environment(\.epgSnapshot) to LiveCategoryShelfRow to account for the EPG line: that would re-evaluate every Equatable shelf row on each snapshot tick. Accept the EPG line difference or pass a plain Bool.

**API check:** GridItem: 'public init(_ size: GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment? = nil)', struct available iOS 14.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23529-23539). 'nonisolated public func lineLimit(_ limit: Int, reservesSpace: Bool) -> some View', @available(iOS 16.0) (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8855-8856). Both below the iOS 18 deployment target, no gate needed.

**Regression risks:** reservesSpace on the shared VODStreamCard/SeriesCard breaks the Movies/Series shelves unless finding 3 lands in the same change. Grids get up to one caption line of extra vertical space per row. Favorites cards with the extra category line stay consistent because categoryName is non-optional (Models/DBModels.swift:176-188). No effect on pagination, Equatable rows or image requests.

**How to verify:** Re-run the screenshot tour and compare M04-movies-all, L05-live-all-channels and L03-live-category-detail: artwork tops on one line in every row. UI test: in All Channels assert the first three cells' image frames share minY. To settle the shelf sub-claim, use a category whose first visible names are short and a later one is long with EPG enabled, scroll the shelf and watch whether the shelf height changes or the EPG capsule is clipped.

## design-system-consistency-2 — Shelf titles render accent blue by accident and the same role (shelf header) exists in three different typographies and two insets

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels, Continue Watching, Series detail
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:355-370`, `Views/VODView.swift:314-329, 417-432`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:291-306, 393-408, 1016-1028`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:336-355`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:29-45`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: The code asks for .primary but ships blue. Confirm that shelf headers should be label-coloured (Apple TV / App Store pattern) and pick one size (.title3 bold recommended, Continue Watching would shrink from .title2).

**What the user perceives:** Every category title on the three home tabs is a blue link ("Drama >", "Action >") in 17 pt semibold, while the "Continue Watching" title directly above it is black 22 pt bold and starts 4 pt further right. Apple's TV, Music and App Store shelves use one label-coloured bold header with a grey chevron. See iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png, iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png, ipad-light/L01-live-home.png.

**Mechanism (finder):** Header table (role: shelf / section title). A) Category and Recently Added shelves, six copies (LiveStreamsView.swift:355-370, VODView.swift:314-329 and 417-432, SeriesView.swift:291-306 and 393-408, M3UChannelsView.swift:336-355): NavigationLink with the default button style, Text .headline, chevron.right .caption.semibold .tertiary, .foregroundStyle(.primary), inset 16, header-to-content spacing 10, row padding 6. Inside a default-style button the hierarchical .primary/.tertiary resolve against the tint, so the title is accent blue and the chevron pale blue although the code asks for primary. B) ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-44: .buttonStyle(.plain), .title2.bold, label colour, inset 20, spacing 16, vertical padding 12. C) Series detail "Seasons" (SeriesView.swift:1016-1028): .title3.bold, no chevron, count in .caption.semibold. D) M3U adds a bare trailing count (M3UChannelsView.swift:350-353). Other section headers: Plot .headline (DetailComponents.swift:360), Director/Cast uppercased caption2.bold tertiary (DetailComponents.swift:416-419), search results Label with icon and "(n)" (SearchView.swift:328-335), EPG guide subheadline.semibold with capsule count (EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:100-122). All six shelf headers also use chevron.right, which does not mirror in the shipped Arabic localisation.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add Views/DesignSystem/ShelfHeader.swift and use it in the seven places listed (the Seasons header uses the non-link initialiser):
struct ShelfHeader<Destination: View, Trailing: View>: View {
  init(_ title: String, @ViewBuilder destination: @escaping () -> Destination, @ViewBuilder trailing: @escaping () -> Trailing)
}
Body: HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline) { NavigationLink(destination: destination) { HStack(spacing: 4) { Text(title).font(.title3.weight(.bold)).foregroundStyle(Color.primary); Image(systemName: "chevron.forward").font(.footnote.weight(.bold)).foregroundStyle(Color.secondary) } }.buttonStyle(.plain); Spacer(minLength: 8); trailing() }.padding(.horizontal, metrics.pageMargin).accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader). Color.primary / Color.secondary (not the hierarchical styles) keep the colour independent of the tint. The rows stay Equatable; only their header subtree is replaced. chevron.forward is in SF Symbols since the 2020 set (iOS 14) and mirrors in RTL.

**APIs:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.plain (iOS 13.0); View.foregroundStyle(_:) (iOS 15.0); View.accessibilityAddTraits(_:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The visible problem is real. Six shelf headers are NavigationLinks with the default button style whose label asks for .foregroundStyle(.primary) and a .tertiary chevron (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:355-370, Views/VODView.swift:314-329 and 417-432, Views/SeriesView.swift:291-306 and 393-408, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:336-355). Screenshots show them accent blue with a pale blue chevron (iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png, iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png, ipad-light/L01-live-home.png), consistent with hierarchical styles resolving against the button tint. Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:29-45 is the odd one out: .buttonStyle(.plain), .title2 bold, inset 20, spacing 16. The Seasons header is .title3 bold (Views/SeriesView.swift:1016-1028). The other table rows check out (DetailComponents.swift:360 and 416-419, SearchView.swift:328-335). RTL is real too: the app forces layoutDirection for Arabic (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:63-65) and there are 10 chevron.right and 0 chevron.forward outside the player. Corrections: (a) the fix uses metrics.pageMargin, which does not exist (grep finds no pageMargin; Views/PosterMetrics.swift has no such property). (b) On iPad the 16 pt shelf inset sits 4 pt left of the large title (ipad-light/L01: headers at about 16 pt, title at about 20 pt), while on iPhone 16 matches the title and Continue Watching's 20 is the one that is off, so a single constant cannot align both. (c) The blue is long-standing rather than new: the lines date from the monorepo import (d2489f9) and this is established SwiftUI behaviour, so the owner has always shipped blue headers. It is a product decision, as the finding itself says. (d) Severity high is overstated for a colour and type-size inconsistency. The Continue Watching comparison comes from code only; the demo screenshots contain no Continue Watching row.

**Corrected claim:** Shelf headers ship accent-coloured because hierarchical .primary/.tertiary inside a default-style NavigationLink resolve against the tint; the code's intent (and the one .plain sibling, Continue Watching) is label colour. The same role exists in three sizes (.headline, .title2 bold, .title3 bold) and two insets (16 and 20), neither of which matches the large title on both iPhone and iPad. chevron.right does not mirror in the Arabic layout the app forces.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest fix: add .buttonStyle(.plain) to the six NavigationLinks and change chevron.right to chevron.forward; that alone gives the label-coloured header the code asks for. For consistency, extract ShelfHeader as proposed, with these corrections: there is no metrics.pageMargin, so either keep the literal 16 or first add a page-margin token (16 compact, 20 regular width, e.g. 'var pageMargin: CGFloat' on PosterMetrics or from horizontalSizeClass) and apply it to header and shelf content together. Put .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) on the NavigationLink, not on the outer HStack, so the M3U trailing count does not get the header trait. Keep the title Text as the link's label so app.buttons["Action"], ["Drama"], ["News"] in ScreensUITests still match. The project uses file-system-synchronised groups, so a new file needs no project.pbxproj edit (that file carries tip-jar WIP). Colour and size remain the owner's call.

**API check:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.plain: 'public static var plain: PlainButtonStyle', extension @available(iOS 13.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:8843-8845). 'accessibilityAddTraits(_ traits: AccessibilityTraits)', @available(iOS 14.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23206-23208). foregroundStyle(_:) is iOS 15. 'metrics.pageMargin' is not an SDK API and is not defined in the code base. SF Symbol names cannot be checked in the swiftinterface; chevron.forward ships since SF Symbols 2 (iOS 14).

**Regression risks:** Header colour changes from blue to label colour on every home tab; the owner may prefer the current blue, so confirm first. Shrinking Continue Watching from .title2 to .title3 is a visible change. If a page margin of 20 is introduced on iPad, shelf content padding must move with the header or the header and first card stop lining up. The rows stay Equatable; the header has no state, so the earlier performance work is not touched.

**How to verify:** Screenshots of L01, M01, S01 (light and dark) and ipad-light/L01: headers label-coloured, one size, leading edge on the large title's edge. Switch the app language to Arabic and check the chevron points left. Run ScreensUITests: the category links must still be found by their titles.

## design-system-consistency-3 — Movie and series shelf titles are cut to one line on iPhone because the caption area is scaled with the poster instead of with the text

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies home, Series home, Recently Added shelves
- Code: `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:49-50`, `Views/VODView.swift:350, 436, 467, 528-533`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:327, 412, 439, 500-505`

**What the user perceives:** On the Movies and Series home the title under a poster is truncated after one line ("Whispers in th...", "Echoes of Tom..." in iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png and M02-movies-home-scrolled.png) although the very same card shows the full title on two lines in the grid (iphone-dark/M04-movies-all.png). On iPad the same shelves leave 24-40 pt of empty space under the titles. With larger text sizes the caption has even less room.

**Mechanism (finder):** PosterMetrics.shelfRowTotalHeight = shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64) (PosterMetrics.swift:50). scaled() multiplies by layoutScale, which is 0.5 on a 402 pt wide iPhone, so the caption allowance is 32 pt; the card needs poster + ~8 pt VStack spacing + two 16 pt caption lines = 40 pt. The shelves pin the ScrollView to that height (VODView.swift:350 and 467, SeriesView.swift:327 and 439), the LazyHStack proposes it to the card and the Text falls back to one line. The text size follows Dynamic Type, the allowance follows screen width, so the two never agree: 32 pt on iPhone, 64 pt on iPad.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the fixed shelf height (it keeps lazy rows stable) but derive the caption part from the font. In the four shelf row structs add @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var captionBlock: CGFloat = 44 (8 spacing + 2 x 16 line + 4 slack) and use posterMetrics.shelfPosterHeight + captionBlock in the six places; drop the scaled(64) from PosterMetrics.swift:50 (or turn shelfRowTotalHeight into func shelfRowHeight(captionBlock:)). Combine with .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true) on the card title so every card has the same height. @ScaledMetric is a DynamicProperty and still updates inside the .equatable() rows, like @Environment(\.posterMetrics) does today.

**APIs:** ScaledMetric (iOS 14.0); View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/PosterMetrics.swift:50 is 'shelfRowTotalHeight = shelfPosterHeight + scaled(64)', and its comment says the allowance is meant for about two caption lines. layoutScale is clamp(short side / 834, 0.5...1) (PosterMetrics.swift:10-13), so on a 402 pt iPhone the allowance is 32 pt. The shelves pin the horizontal ScrollView to that height (Views/VODView.swift:350 and 467, Views/SeriesView.swift:327 and 439; placeholders at VODView.swift:436 and SeriesView.swift:412). The card is a default-spacing VStack of poster plus .caption title with .lineLimit(2) (VODView.swift:528-533, SeriesView.swift:500-505): poster + about 8 + 2 x 16 = poster + 40 > poster + 32, so the title gets about 24 pt and falls back to one line. Screenshot iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png shows 'Whispers in th...' in the Drama shelf, while the same card shows two lines in the grid (iphone-dark/M04-movies-all.png, 'Echoes of Tomorrow'). The allowance scales with screen width while the text scales with Dynamic Type, so the comment's intent is not met on any iPhone (430 pt wide gives 33 pt). The line dates from the monorepo import (d2489f9) and nothing marks one-line truncation as deliberate. The 24-40 pt of slack on iPad follows from the arithmetic (64 pt allowance at scale 1.0) but there is no iPad Movies screenshot yet. All six usages are in the four named structs; no test references shelfRowTotalHeight.

**Corrected claim:** As stated: on iPhone the Movies and Series shelf caption area is 32 pt, less than the roughly 40 pt two caption lines need, so shelf titles truncate to one line although the same card shows two lines in grids; the allowance scales with screen width instead of with the caption font.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: keep the fixed shelf height and derive the caption part from the font. In RecentlyAddedVODShelf, VODCategoryShelfRow, RecentlyAddedSeriesShelf and SeriesCategoryShelfRow add '@ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var captionBlock: CGFloat = 44' and use posterMetrics.shelfPosterHeight + captionBlock in the six places (or 'func shelfRowHeight(captionBlock:)' on PosterMetrics). Land it together with .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true) from finding 1 so every card in a shelf has the same height. Optionally give the card VStack an explicit spacing: 8 so the 44 pt budget does not rely on the default stack spacing.

**API check:** '@propertyWrapper public struct ScaledMetric<Value> : DynamicProperty where Value : BinaryFloatingPoint' with 'public init(wrappedValue: Value, relativeTo textStyle: Font.TextStyle)', @available(iOS 14.0) (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12146-12153). lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) is @available(iOS 16.0) (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8855-8856). No gate needed.

**Regression risks:** Each Movies/Series shelf becomes about 12 pt taller on iPhone and about 20 pt shorter on iPad, so fewer or more shelves fit per screen. The rows have hand-written ==, so adding a property wrapper does not disturb Equatable conformance, and @ScaledMetric updates through the environment just as the existing @Environment(\.posterMetrics) does. At accessibility text sizes the block scales with the caption, which is the intended behaviour. Image request sizes and prefetch keys are unchanged.

**How to verify:** Screenshots M01, M02, S01 on iPhone: two-line titles inside shelves ('Whispers in the ...' fully shown or wrapped). Unit test for the height helper at scale 0.5 and 1.0. Check in the simulator at the largest non-accessibility text size that the second line is not clipped, and on iPad that the gap under titles is gone.

## design-system-consistency-4 — Detail hero: the blurred fallback backdrop bleeds below the hero and leaves a hard seam above the Watch button

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:46-72, 86-99`

**What the user perceives:** When a title has no backdrop (most Xtream movies), a horizontal edge cuts across the screen right under the hero: above it the image has faded to the background colour, below it a grey band starts abruptly and fades out behind the Watch Now button. Clearly visible in iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png at the bottom of the hero, fainter in iphone-dark/M07-movie-detail.png.

**Mechanism (finder):** The fallback backdrop is the poster with .blur(radius: 28) and .opacity(0.55) (DetailComponents.swift:60-62). A non-opaque blur draws a soft halo outside the view's frame and nothing clips it: the GeometryReader and the hero ZStack only set a frame. Inside the hero the gradient layer (DetailComponents.swift:86-99) fades the image to systemBackground, but the halo that extends ~50 pt below the hero frame is outside that gradient, so it shows at full strength exactly where the gradient ends.

**Proposed fix (finder):** In backdropLayer change the two modifiers to .blur(radius: backdropIsFallback ? 28 : 0, opaque: backdropIsFallback).clipped() before .opacity and before .visualEffect. Clipping before the visualEffect keeps the overscroll stretch (the scale is applied to the already clipped layer); the opaque blur also removes the washed-out edge at the top of the hero. No availability gate needed.

**APIs:** View.blur(radius:opaque:) (iOS 13.0); View.clipped(antialiased:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The seam is real and the mechanism holds. Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:50-71: the fallback backdrop is CachedImage.frame(...).blur(radius: 28).opacity(0.55).visualEffect{...} with no clip after the blur. CachedImage clips itself before the blur (Views/CachedImage.swift:81-82), so the non-opaque blur spreads a soft halo outside the 380 pt frame. The gradient layer (DetailComponents.swift:86-99) only covers the hero frame. In iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png the hard edge sits at about y = 868 of 2000 px, about 380 pt, exactly the hero bottom (the ScrollView ignores the top safe area, Views/MovieDetailView.swift:187; Views/SeriesView.swift:1003): pure background above, a grey band fading over about 18 pt below, behind the Watch Now button. It is fainter but present in iphone-dark/M07-movie-detail.png. The blur line dates from the monorepo import with no comment marking the bleed as intended. Correction to the fix: .clipped() alone removes the bleed. Adding opaque: true is a separate look change: it removes the soft fade at the top of the hero under the status bar and nav buttons, and while the image loads or fails the blur would be applied to the systemGray6 placeholder with a .quaternary icon (CachedImage.swift:138-147), where opaque rendering of semi-transparent content is not something code reading can vouch for. The claim 'most Xtream movies have no backdrop' is plausible but not something I verified.

**Corrected claim:** When the hero falls back to the blurred poster, the non-opaque blur halo extends below the hero frame, outside the gradient that fades the image out, leaving a hard seam with a grey band under the hero on movie and series detail.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest fix: add .clipped() directly after .blur(radius: backdropIsFallback ? 28 : 0) and before .opacity and .visualEffect in backdropLayer (DetailComponents.swift:60). Clipping before the visualEffect keeps the overscroll stretch and parallax, because the scale and offset apply to the already clipped layer. Treat 'opaque: backdropIsFallback' as an optional second step, adopted only after checking in the simulator how the top of the hero and the placeholder/loading state look in light and dark.

**API check:** '@inlinable nonisolated public func blur(radius: CGFloat, opaque: Bool = false) -> some View', extension @available(iOS 13.0) (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:3780-3786). '@inlinable nonisolated public func clipped(antialiased: Bool = false) -> some View', iOS 13.0 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:17594). No gate needed.

**Regression risks:** .clipped() alone: none expected; real backdrops (radius 0) are already frame-fit. With opaque: true: the hero top becomes fully saturated under the status bar and the glass nav buttons instead of fading out, and the placeholder state may render differently. The parallax offset and bottom-anchored scale are unaffected by a clip applied before visualEffect.

**How to verify:** Screenshot M07-movie-detail in light and dark: no band between the hero and Watch Now. In the simulator pull the detail screen down to confirm the stretch still works and scroll up to confirm parallax. If opaque is adopted, also check a title whose poster URL fails to load.

## design-system-consistency-5 — Favorites puts the segmented control on a material slab that spills under the navigation bar

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Favorites (Xtream)
- Code: `Views/FavoritesView.swift:35-59`

**What the user perceives:** The whole top of the Favorites screen (status bar, large title, search field, picker) is a flat grey block with a hard edge against the content, and the search field has no visible shape on it. No other screen in the app looks like this. See iphone-light/L04-favorites-live.png, iphone-dark/M09-favorites-movies.png, ipad-light/L06-favorites.png (the picker also starts 4 pt left of the title on iPad).

**Mechanism (finder):** FavoritesView.swift:37-44 places the Picker in a VStack above the grids with .padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial). background(_:ignoresSafeAreaEdges:) defaults to .all, and the picker is the first view under the bar, so the material extends up through the navigation bar and status bar. Because the content below is three separate ScrollViews inside a Group, the bar never gets a scroll-edge appearance either.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Smallest change: remove .background(.ultraThinMaterial) and replace .padding() with .padding(.horizontal, metrics.pageMargin).padding(.vertical, 8). Native placement: move the picker out of the VStack and attach it to the Group as a bar: if #available(iOS 26, *) { content.safeAreaBar(edge: .top) { picker } } else { content.safeAreaInset(edge: .top) { picker.background(.bar) } }. With safeAreaBar the system applies the iOS 26 scroll-edge effect under the picker; the iOS 18 fallback gives the classic bar material limited to the picker strip.

**APIs:** View.safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 26.0); View.safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) (iOS 15.0); View.background(_:ignoresSafeAreaEdges:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The defect is real. Views/FavoritesView.swift:37-44 puts the segmented Picker first in a VStack with .padding().background(.ultraThinMaterial). background(_:ignoresSafeAreaEdges:) defaults to .all, and the picker is the first view under the bar, so the material runs up through the navigation bar and status bar. Screenshots confirm it: iphone-light/L04-favorites-live.png shows one flat grey block from the status bar to under the picker with a hard edge against the content and an almost shapeless search field; ipad-light/L06-favorites.png shows the same slab, with the picker at about 16 pt and the large title at about 20 pt. M3UFavoritesView has no picker, so the scope is the Xtream Favorites screen only. The line dates from the monorepo import and carries no comment. Two corrections to the fix: (1) 'metrics.pageMargin' does not exist; the local property is posterMetrics and it has no page-margin value. (2) The iOS 18 fallback 'picker.background(.bar)' uses the same default ignoresSafeAreaEdges: .all, so inside a top safeAreaInset it extends under the transparent large-title navigation bar again and reproduces the slab; it needs ignoresSafeAreaEdges: [] to stay limited to the picker strip as the finding describes. The remark that the bar never gets a scroll-edge appearance because of the three ScrollViews in a Group was not verified and is not needed for the finding.

**Corrected claim:** On Xtream Favorites the segmented picker's material background ignores the safe area and floods the whole top of the screen (status bar, large title, search field, picker) as one grey slab with a hard lower edge; on iPad the picker also starts 4 pt left of the large title.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest change (recommended first): remove .background(.ultraThinMaterial) and replace .padding() with .padding(.horizontal, 16).padding(.vertical, 8); 16 matches the grids' .padding() below it. Aligning with the iPad large title needs a page-margin token that does not exist yet. Native placement (optional): take the picker out of the VStack and attach it to the Group: if #available(iOS 26, *) { content.safeAreaBar(edge: .top) { picker } } else { content.safeAreaInset(edge: .top) { picker.background(.bar, ignoresSafeAreaEdges: []) } }. The explicit empty edge set is required in the fallback so the material stays on the picker strip.

**API check:** 'nonisolated public func safeAreaBar(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> some View) -> some View', @available(iOS 26.0) (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17361-17362): must be gated. 'safeAreaInset<V>(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment:spacing:content:)' present in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19082 (iOS 15). 'background<S>(_ style: S, ignoresSafeAreaEdges edges: Edge.Set = .all) where S : ShapeStyle' (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:15747) confirms the default that causes the bug and that would re-cause it in the fallback. 'public static var bar: Material' exists (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6339-6340).

**Regression risks:** Smallest change: the picker sits on the plain background and grid content is cut off at the picker's lower edge while scrolling (same as today, minus the material). safeAreaBar/safeAreaInset variant: content scrolls under the picker, so on iOS 18 the bar background is required or cards show through; large-title collapse and the searchable field must be re-checked with the pinned picker, and the empty state (a plain VStack, FavoritesView.swift:179-192) must still centre below it. No effect on queries or the player hand-off.

**How to verify:** Screenshots of Favorites in light and dark on iPhone and iPad: top area matches the other screens, search field has its normal shape, no hard-edged slab. In the simulator on iOS 18 and iOS 26: scroll a populated favorites grid and check the large title collapses, the picker stays reachable and nothing shows through it.
