## design-system-consistency-6 — Watch progress on poster cards is drawn across the top edge of the poster and five different progress bars exist

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category detail, All Movies, Series category detail, All Series, Favorites, Continue Watching, History, Series detail episodes
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:501-526`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:473-498, 1402-1413`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:79-91`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:171-181`

**What the user perceives:** A partly watched movie or series shows its accent progress line at the top of the poster, running under the rating badge and sticking out past the poster's rounded corner, while Continue Watching, History and the episode list show progress at the bottom of the artwork.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODStreamCard and SeriesCard overlay the bar inside ZStack(alignment: .topTrailing) (VODView.swift:502, SeriesView.swift:474); the alignment was chosen for the rating badge and also positions the bar, whose own .padding(.bottom, 2) shows it was meant for the bottom edge. The bar adds .padding(.horizontal, 4) around a track that is already posterWidth wide (VODView.swift:513-521), so in a grid column wider than the poster the ZStack becomes 8 pt wider than the image and the track overhangs the leading edge. The other three implementations use ZStack(alignment: .bottom) with different track colours (black 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.55) and heights (4 / 3 pt).

**Proposed fix (finder):** One shared view in Views/DesignSystem/MediaCards.swift:
struct CardProgressBar: View { let fraction: Double }  // 3 pt, Capsule track .black.opacity(0.45), fill .tint, GeometryReader-free: Capsule().fill(.tint).frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading).scaleEffect(x: clamped, anchor: .leading)
Use it as .overlay(alignment: .bottom) { CardProgressBar(fraction: p).padding(.horizontal, 6).padding(.bottom, 6) } on the CachedImage in VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, EpisodeDetailRow, HistoryCard and HistoryCardGridItem, and keep the rating badge as .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing). The overlay never changes the card's size, so grid alignment stays stable.

**APIs:** View.overlay(alignment:content:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read the code. Views/VODView.swift:502 and Views/SeriesView.swift:474 use ZStack(alignment: .topTrailing); the progress Rectangle (VODView.swift:512-522, SeriesView.swift:484-494) is a plain ZStack child, so it is placed at the top edge although it carries .padding(.bottom, 2). Layout reasoning for a grid cell: iPhone 17 Pro (402 pt) gives posterWidth 100, gridSpacing 8, three adaptive columns of 118 pt. The bar is frame(maxWidth: posterWidth) = 100 plus .padding(.horizontal, 4) = 108, so the ZStack grows from 100 to 108; with trailing alignment the poster sits at x 8-108 and the track at x 4-104. The track therefore overhangs the poster's leading rounded corner by 4 pt and stops 4 pt short on the trailing side, and because the enclosing VStack is centre-aligned the poster of a watched item shifts 4 pt right relative to its title and to unwatched posters. Same widening in EpisodeDetailRow (SeriesView.swift:1391-1413, ZStack .bottom, bar 8 pt wider than the thumb), which pushes the text column 8 pt for watched episodes. Data really reaches the cards: VODView.swift:701, SeriesView.swift:657, FavoritesView.swift:142/168 pass progressMap values from WatchProgressMapRequest (Models/Requests.swift:438-482), so every partly watched title in a category grid, All Movies/Series and Favorites shows it. Five implementations confirmed: VODStreamCard (4 pt, black 0.3), SeriesCard (4 pt, 0.3), EpisodeDetailRow (3 pt, 0.3), HistoryCard (Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:79-91, 3 pt, 0.5), HistoryCardGridItem (WatchHistoryListView.swift:171-181, 3 pt, 0.55). No comment marks the top placement as intended; git log -S only reaches d2489f9 (monorepo restructure), so history neither supports nor contradicts it. Not visible in the screenshots (demo data has no watch history), so the verdict rests on code and layout rules only.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Additions: the track does not run 'under the rating badge' in the sense of overlapping it (bar y 0-4, badge starts at y 6); it sits above it on the top edge. Besides the wrong edge, the bar widens the poster ZStack by 8 pt, so a watched poster is shifted 4 pt sideways against its title and its neighbours in grids, and a watched episode row's text column is shifted 8 pt.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with two details. (1) Build the bar so it cannot influence layout: Capsule().fill(.black.opacity(0.45)).frame(height: 3).overlay(alignment: .leading) { Rectangle().fill(.tint).scaleEffect(x: clamped, y: 1, anchor: .leading) }.clipShape(Capsule()); scaling a Rectangle and clipping avoids the squashed capsule ends of the proposed scaled Capsule, and the explicit height is required (the proposal has none). (2) Attach it with .overlay(alignment: .bottom) on CachedImage and move PosterRatingBadge to .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing), removing the ZStack in VODStreamCard and SeriesCard; do the same in EpisodeDetailRow, HistoryCard and HistoryCardGridItem. Views/DesignSystem does not exist yet; the app target is a PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup, so a new file needs no project.pbxproj edit (that file is modified in the owner's WIP). Inset capsule versus the current flush full-width bar in the two history cards is a small look change the owner should see.

**API check:** View.overlay(alignment:content:): SwiftUICore interface line 3382, extension @available(iOS 15.0). View.scaleEffect(x:y:anchor:): SwiftUICore line 19001, iOS 13. TintShapeStyle (.tint): SwiftUICore line 19578, @available(iOS 15.0). All below the iOS 18 target, no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** Card size no longer changes with watch state, which is the intent; shelfRowTotalHeight and the Equatable shelf rows are untouched. WatchProgressMapRequest's 0.01 rounding (deliberate, Requests.swift:443-451) keeps working because the bar only reads the fraction. HistoryCard/HistoryCardGridItem lose the edge-to-edge bar look. Fixed image decode sizes are unchanged, so prefetch keys still match.

**How to verify:** Simulator: play a demo movie and a series episode for a minute, then open the category grid, All Movies, Favorites and the series' episode list. Check the bar is inside the poster at the bottom, the poster's x position equals that of an unwatched neighbour, and the episode text column does not move when history appears.

## design-system-consistency-7 — Detail components ship hard-coded Turkish text: the trailer button always says "Fragman" and series runtimes end in "s" / "dk"

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:263-268, 499-511`

**What the user perceives:** In any of the nine non-Turkish languages the secondary button under Watch Now is labelled "Fragman", and a series runtime reads "1s 30dk" or "45 dk".

**Mechanism (finder):** DetailComponents.swift:265 passes the literal title "Fragman" to DetailSecondaryLabel although the key movie.trailer exists in all ten Localizable.strings files and is referenced nowhere in the Swift sources. DetailFormatting.seriesRuntime builds "\(h)s \(m)dk" and "\(minutes) dk" by hand (DetailComponents.swift:506, 508).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Line 265: title: L("movie.trailer"). Runtime: format with Foundation instead of new string keys, so the Localizable.strings files in the working tree are not touched: Duration.seconds(minutes * 60).formatted(.units(allowed: [.hours, .minutes], width: .narrow).locale(appLocale)), where appLocale is a small static added to LocalizationManager that wraps the already resolved language code (the app has its own language override, so Locale.current is not enough).

**APIs:** Duration.UnitsFormatStyle (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:265 passes the literal "Fragman" to DetailSecondaryLabel. "movie.trailer" exists in all ten Localization/*.lproj/Localizable.strings files (en:365 "Trailer", tr:365 "Fragman", the others at line 397) and grep finds no Swift reference to the key. The button is reachable in both detail screens (trailerURL from youtubeTrailer: Views/MovieDetailView.swift:50-55/140, Views/SeriesView.swift:841-846/975). DetailFormatting.seriesRuntime (DetailComponents.swift:499-511) returns "\(h)s \(m)dk", "\(h)s" and "\(minutes) dk"; its only caller is SeriesView.swift:833. Movie runtime is the provider string passed through (MovieDetailView.swift:64), so only series are affected. git log -S'"Fragman"' reaches only d2489f9 (restructure); dbe929c later localised the remaining strings and missed these two, so nothing suggests intent. LocalizationManager (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:75-116) resolves the app's own language override and has no Locale accessor yet; systemLanguageCode() is private, so a small nonisolated static is needed as the finding says.

**Corrected claim:** Stands. Scope note: the runtime defect affects the series detail hero only, and only when the provider sends episode_run_time as a bare number of minutes (strings containing 'm' or 'h' pass through unchanged at line 501).

**Corrected fix:** Line 265: title: L("movie.trailer"). Runtime: Duration.seconds(minutes * 60).formatted(.units(allowed: [.hours, .minutes], width: .narrow).locale(LocalizationManager.effectiveLocale)), with nonisolated static var effectiveLocale: Locale added to LocalizationManager that repeats the stored-or-system resolution used in resolveLocalizedString (lines 77-78) and returns Locale(identifier: code). No Localizable.strings edits, so the owner's tip-jar keys are untouched. Expected output: en '1h 30m' / '45m', tr '1 sa 30 dk' / '45 dk'. One thing to look at: Locale(identifier: "ar") formats with Arabic-Indic digits while the year and rating next to it may use Latin digits; if that reads badly, build the locale as "ar@numbers=latn" or accept it.

**API check:** Foundation interface: Duration.UnitsFormatStyle at line 4209 under @available(macOS 13.0, iOS 16.0, ...); static func units(allowed:width:maximumUnitCount:zeroValueUnits:valueLength:fractionalPart:) at line 4334; func locale(_:) -> Duration.UnitsFormatStyle at line 4314; Duration.formatted<S>(_:) at line 4087, iOS 16.0. UnitWidth.narrow at line 4220.

**Regression risks:** None for the trailer label. Runtime text changes shape in Turkish too ('1s 30dk' becomes '1 sa 30 dk'), which is the system's own abbreviation. No unit test references seriesRuntime today, so nothing breaks; nothing in the tip-jar WIP is touched.

**How to verify:** Unit test: seriesRuntime("90") and ("45") with app.selected_language set to en, tr, de, ar. Simulator: series detail with a numeric episode run time and a youtube trailer, app language English, check the hero line and the secondary button.

## design-system-consistency-8 — Tapping a card feels different on every screen: four different press behaviours for the same kind of card

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series, Favorites, Continue Watching, Series detail episodes
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457`, `Views/VODView.swift:334-345, 451-462, 692-704`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:311-322, 423-434, 650-660, 1447-1451`, `Views/FavoritesView.swift:134-144, 160-170`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:48-53`

**What the user perceives:** A movie poster dims slightly when pressed, a series poster in a category grid or in Favorites flashes much more strongly, a Continue Watching card and an episode row show no reaction at all until the player opens. Apple's media grids give one consistent pressed state.

**Mechanism (finder):** Card press table. Button + .buttonStyle(.plain): LiveStreamCard (LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457), M3UChannelCard, HistoryCardGridItem. NavigationLink + .plain: VOD shelves and VOD grid (VODView.swift:345, 462, 704), series shelves (SeriesView.swift:322, 434). NavigationLink with the default borderless style, no .plain: series grid (SeriesView.swift:650-660) and both Favorites grids (FavoritesView.swift:134, 160). Bare .onTapGesture with no pressed state and no button trait: HistoryCard in Continue Watching (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52) and the episode row, where only the text column is tappable (SeriesView.swift:1447-1451).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add Views/DesignSystem/PressableCardStyle.swift and apply it to every card link/button; convert the two onTapGesture cards to Button:
struct PressableCardStyle: ButtonStyle {
  func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
    configuration.label
      .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed ? 0.97 : 1)
      .opacity(configuration.isPressed ? 0.85 : 1)
      .animation(.snappy(duration: 0.18), value: configuration.isPressed)
  }
}
extension ButtonStyle where Self == PressableCardStyle { static var pressableCard: PressableCardStyle { .init() } }
NavigationLink accepts a ButtonStyle, so call sites only change .buttonStyle(.plain) to .buttonStyle(.pressableCard) (and add it at SeriesView.swift:660, FavoritesView.swift:144 and 170). Animating only scale and opacity of the label keeps the Equatable rows untouched.

**APIs:** ButtonStyle / ButtonStyleConfiguration.isPressed (iOS 13.0); Animation.snappy(duration:extraBounce:) (iOS 17.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism table is accurate against the code: Button + .plain in LiveStreamCard (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:430-457), M3UChannelCard (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:418-445) and HistoryCardGridItem (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:159-201); NavigationLink + .plain at VODView.swift:345/462/704 and SeriesView.swift:322/434; NavigationLink with no style at SeriesView.swift:650-660 and FavoritesView.swift:134 and 160; bare .onTapGesture on HistoryCard (Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:49-52) and on the episode row's text column only (SeriesView.swift:1447-1451). The last one is more than feel: the thumbnail ZStack at SeriesView.swift:1391-1414 has no gesture, so tapping an episode's artwork does nothing, and neither tap-gesture surface has a pressed state or a button trait for VoiceOver. What I could not establish from code: how different .plain and the default borderless style look when pressed on iOS 26 ('dims slightly' versus 'flashes much more strongly'); that needs a device. Also Button + .plain and NavigationLink + .plain are the same style, so there are three behaviours (plain, default, none), not four. No comment or history marks the missing .buttonStyle(.plain) or the tap gestures as deliberate. No UI test references the Continue Watching cards or episode rows.

**Corrected claim:** Card taps use three different mechanisms: .plain button style (most cards), the default NavigationLink style (series category grid and both Favorites poster grids), and a bare tap gesture with no pressed feedback and no button semantics (Continue Watching cards, episode rows). In the episode row only the text column reacts; tapping the thumbnail does nothing. The size of the visual difference between the first two is unmeasured.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest fix: (a) add .buttonStyle(.plain) at SeriesView.swift:660 and FavoritesView.swift:144 and 170; (b) wrap HistoryCard in Button { onPlay(item) } label: { HistoryCard(item: item) } with .buttonStyle(.plain); (c) in EpisodeDetailRow wrap thumbnail and text column together in one Button and keep DownloadButton as a sibling in the HStack (no nested buttons), keeping .contentShape(Rectangle()) on the label. That alone gives one behaviour everywhere and fixes the dead thumbnail. The shared PressableCardStyle (scale 0.97, opacity 0.85) is optional polish on top and a look decision for the owner; if adopted, apply it at all the listed call sites including the three Button cards.

**API check:** ButtonStyle protocol: SwiftUI interface line 10436, @available(iOS 13.0); ButtonStyleConfiguration.isPressed: line 10450, iOS 13.0. Animation.snappy(duration:extraBounce:): SwiftUICore line 13320, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient inside an iOS 13.0 extension (documented as iOS 17), fine for the iOS 18 target. scaleEffect, opacity: iOS 13.

**Regression risks:** Episode row: the Button must not swallow the DownloadButton's taps or its contextMenu (Components/DownloadButton.swift:82), hence sibling placement. M3UChannelCard has a .contextMenu after the button style; with a scaling style the lift preview starts from the scaled state, check it looks right. A scale effect on press must not fire while a shelf is dragged horizontally. Equatable shelf rows and paginated grids are unaffected because only the label's style changes. Converting tap gestures to Buttons changes the accessibility element type from other to button, which no existing UI test depends on.

**How to verify:** Device or simulator, after the change: press and hold a card on Live, Movies, Series, Favorites, Continue Watching and an episode row and compare the feedback; tap an episode thumbnail and confirm playback starts; drag each shelf and confirm no pressed flash. To settle the unmeasured part of the claim beforehand, record a press on a movie grid card and a series grid card in the current build and compare frames.

## design-system-consistency-9 — Card captions are centred, 12 pt medium on every device, with fixed 9-10 pt sublabels; the channel tile mixes centred name and leading guide line

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series, M3U channels, Favorites, Continue Watching
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:433-455`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:421-443`, `Views/VODView.swift:528-543`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:500-515`, `Views/RatingLabel.swift:73-86`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:100-105`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:54-63`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Leading-aligned captions under posters (Apple pattern, recommended) change the look of every shelf. Channel tiles with square logos can stay centred if the owner prefers; the guide line then has to be centred as well.

**What the user perceives:** Titles float centred under posters and channel logos instead of lining up with the artwork's leading edge as in the TV app, App Store and Music. On iPad a 12 pt caption sits under a 200 pt poster (ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png). The category line in Favorites, the subtitle in Continue Watching and the rating badge do not grow with the user's text size. On a channel tile the name is centred while the programme title right below it is left aligned.

**Mechanism (finder):** Poster and tile titles: .font(.caption).fontWeight(.medium), .multilineTextAlignment(.center), .frame(width:) (VODView.swift:528-534, SeriesView.swift:500-506, LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449, M3UChannelsView.swift:431-437); the VStack is alignment .center (LiveStreamsView.swift:433). The guide line under it is built with .frame(width:, alignment: .leading) (EPGComponents.swift:55-63). Fixed sizes: category line .font(.system(size: 10)) (VODView.swift:538, SeriesView.swift:510), history subtitle size 10 (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:102), rating badge sizes 9 and 10 (RatingLabel.swift:77-79). The text style never changes with PosterMetrics.layoutScale, so the caption is the same 12 pt under a 100 pt and a 200 pt poster.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Define the caption once in the shared cards (see the kit finding): title .footnote, Color.primary, leading aligned, .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true); subtitle .caption with .foregroundStyle(.secondary), one line; rating badge .caption2.weight(.semibold). For channel tiles either keep the centred name and centre the guide line too, or leading-align both; the tile must use one alignment. The caption block height used by the shelves then comes from @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .footnote).

**APIs:** View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16.0); ScaledMetric (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts hold: titles are .caption + .medium, centred, fixed width (VODView.swift:528-534, SeriesView.swift:500-506, LiveStreamsView.swift:443-449, M3UChannelsView.swift:431-437); fixed point sizes at VODView.swift:538, SeriesView.swift:510, Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:102 (size 10) and RatingLabel.swift:77-79 (9 and 10), which ignore Dynamic Type; the channel tile centres the name (LiveStreamsView.swift:433) while EPGNowNextLine is leading-aligned (EPG/EPGComponents.swift:55-63). Screenshots confirm centred 12 pt captions on iPhone and under 180 pt tiles on iPad (ipad-light/L03-live-category-detail.png; the finding says 200 pt poster, the shot is a 180 pt channel tile). The demo build shows no EPG lines, so the mixed alignment is code-only. Centred versus leading captions is a look decision, not a defect, as the finding itself flags. Two concrete defects the finding did not list but which its fix addresses: (1) iphone-dark/L03-live-category-detail.png shows the tile with a two-line name sitting about 8 pt higher than its one-line neighbours, because the grid's GridItem has no alignment and cards differ in height; the same applies to movie and series grids. (2) iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png shows 'Whispers in th…' cut to one line in a shelf although lineLimit is 2: PosterMetrics.shelfRowTotalHeight (PosterMetrics.swift:50) is poster + scaled(64) = 32 pt on phones, which after the VStack spacing leaves room for one caption line only.

**Corrected claim:** Objective problems: four fixed 9-10 pt labels do not follow the user's text size; cards with one-line and two-line titles are vertically misaligned in every grid (visible in iphone-dark/L03); shelf titles on iPhone are silently cut to one line because the shelf height reserves too little caption space; on a channel tile with guide data the name is centred and the programme line leading-aligned. Subjective: centred captions and a 12 pt caption on iPad differ from Apple's leading-aligned media captions; that is the owner's call.

**Corrected fix:** Do the objective part without waiting for a shared card kit: (1) .font(.system(size: 10)) becomes .font(.caption2) at the three sublabel sites; PosterRatingBadge uses .caption2.weight(.semibold) for star and text. (2) Title gets .lineLimit(2, reservesSpace: true) in VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, LiveStreamCard and M3UChannelCard, and grid GridItems get alignment: .top, so all cards in a row have equal height. (3) Replace the fixed caption allowance in shelfRowTotalHeight with a value from @ScaledMetric(relativeTo:) declared in the shelf views (PosterMetrics is a plain struct and cannot hold a ScaledMetric), used for both the ScrollView frame and the loading placeholder at VODView.swift:436 and SeriesView.swift:412 so nothing jumps when streams arrive. (4) Channel tile: pick one alignment for name and guide line. Leading-aligned poster captions and a .footnote title are then a separate owner decision.

**API check:** View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:): SwiftUICore interface line 8856, @available(iOS 16.0). ScaledMetric: SwiftUICore line 12151, @available(iOS 14.0), init(wrappedValue:relativeTo:) present. GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:): SwiftUI line 23539, iOS 14. Text styles .caption2/.footnote: iOS 13/14.

**Regression risks:** Reserving two lines makes every shelf and grid row taller (one caption line, about 16 pt) and changes the look of all browse screens. The shelf rows are Equatable views (deliberate); adding @ScaledMetric is safe because dynamic properties still invalidate them, but the height used by the row and by its loading placeholder must stay identical or shelves jump on load. EPGNowNextLine's fixed 22 pt reservedHeight (deliberate, EPGComponents.swift:48-51) does not scale and should be left as is or scaled together. A rating badge that scales can cover small posters at accessibility sizes; cap it if needed.

**How to verify:** Screenshots before/after of L01, L03, M01, M03, S01, S02 on iPhone and iPad: image tops in a grid row on one line, two-line titles fully visible in shelves, no shelf height change when streams finish loading. One run at the largest non-accessibility text size and one at AX1 to see sublabels and badge scale. Live TV with an EPG source configured to check name and programme line alignment.

## design-system-consistency-10 — Horizontal margins come from three sources, so shelves, grids and titles do not share a leading edge

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series, Favorites, Continue Watching, iPad layouts
- Code: `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:44, 55`, `Views/VODView.swift:329, 348, 432, 465, 635-637, 710`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:306, 325, 408, 437, 598-600, 663`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:370, 396, 597-599, 614`, `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:5-14`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Step 2 (posters fill the column, about 18 percent larger on iPhone, three per row unchanged) is a visual choice and changes the decode size of grid images; step 1 is a plain fix.

**What the user perceives:** On iPhone the first poster of a category grid starts 25 pt from the edge while the title and search field above start at 16 pt (iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png, S02-series-category-detail.png). Continue Watching starts 4 pt further right than the shelves under it. On iPad the system title sits at 20 pt and every shelf at 16 pt (ipad-light/L01-live-home.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** Outside the player there are 27 hard-coded .padding(.horizontal, 16), two .padding(.horizontal, 20) (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:44, 55) and 14 bare .padding() calls. The system large-title margin is 16 pt on narrow iPhones and 20 pt on Max-size iPhones and iPad, so the fixed 16 cannot match everywhere. Grids use GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: posterWidth)) with fixed-size cards (VODView.swift:635-637, 698-699): the columns stretch to about 118 pt on a 402 pt screen, the 100 pt poster is centred in its column, which adds ~9 pt to the outer inset and leaves 26 pt gaps between posters.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Token first, layout second. (1) Add a stored let pageMargin: CGFloat to PosterMetrics, set in init as min(windowSize.width, windowSize.height) >= 414 ? 20 : 16, and replace the shelf/grid/ContinueWatching insets with posterMetrics.pageMargin; for horizontal shelves the inset can move to .contentMargins(.horizontal, pageMargin, for: .scrollContent) so cards scroll edge to edge. (2) Optional: let cards fill their grid column. Measure the grid width once with onGeometryChange, compute columnCount = max(2, floor((width - 2 * margin + spacing) / (minWidth + spacing))) and itemWidth, use Array(repeating: GridItem(.fixed(itemWidth), spacing: spacing, alignment: .top), count: columnCount) and pass itemWidth and itemWidth * 1.5 to the card and to ListImagePrefetch so render and prefetch keys still match.

**APIs:** View.contentMargins(_:_:for:) (iOS 17.0); View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 16.0 (back-deployed)); GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Counts reproduce: 27 .padding(.horizontal, 16) outside the player, two .padding(.horizontal, 20) (Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:44, 55), 14 bare .padding() outside the player. Measured in the screenshots: iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png has the large title and search field at about 16 pt and the first poster at about 25 pt, with about 26 pt between posters; that matches the arithmetic for GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 100), spacing: 8) in a 370 pt grid (three 118 pt columns, 100 pt poster centred; VODView.swift:635-637, 698-699, 710). ipad-light/L01-live-home.png has the large title at about 20 pt and shelf headers at about 16 pt; the channel icon sits at about 18 pt because the card is 116 wide around a 112 icon (PosterMetrics.swift:26-27). On iPad the category grid happens to line up (L03: about 20 pt). Continue Watching at 20 versus shelves at 16 is in the code; no screenshot contains that row. Corrections to the fix: (1) step 1 does not touch the headline symptom. On a 402 pt iPhone the token is 16, same as today; the 25 pt grid inset comes from adaptive columns stretching and only step 2 removes it, so step 2 is not optional if that symptom is to go. (2) Horizontal shelves already put the inset inside the scroll content (.padding on the LazyHStack inside the ScrollView), so cards already scroll edge to edge; moving it to contentMargins gains nothing. (3) PosterMetrics is built once from UIScreen.main.bounds (DashboardView.swift:38, M3UDashboardView.swift:17), not from the window, so a token stored there will not follow iPad Split View or resizable windows. (4) The 414 pt threshold for the 20 pt system margin is not backed by any screenshot; only 402 pt = 16 and iPad = 20 are observed.

**Corrected claim:** Three real misalignments: phone category/All/Favorites grids start about 9 pt inside the title and search field and have 26 pt gutters; on iPad (and presumably Max phones) shelf headers and cards sit 4 pt left of the system large title; Continue Watching is inset 4 pt more than the shelves below it. The cause of the first is the adaptive grid with fixed-size cards, not the padding constant.

**Corrected fix:** (a) Plain fix: ContinueWatchingRow.swift:44 and 55 use the same inset as the shelves. (b) Token: a pageMargin of 16 or 20 applied to shelf headers, shelf content and grids; confirm the threshold on a Max-size simulator before fixing the number, and prefer deriving it from the current window width over the one-time UIScreen value. Keep the shelf inset as padding on the LazyHStack. (c) Grid edge: measure the grid width with onGeometryChange, seed the state from posterMetrics so the first frame is not empty, compute a column count and use that many GridItem(.fixed(itemWidth), spacing:, alignment: .top). Either keep the poster size and widen the gutters (no image changes) or let posters fill the column (about 118 pt on iPhone) and pass the same itemWidth and itemWidth * 1.5 to CachedImage and ListImagePrefetch so decode size and prefetch keys still match. The second option is the better look and is the owner's decision because it changes grid image decode size.

**API check:** View.contentMargins(_:_:for:): SwiftUI interface lines 4234-4242, @available(iOS 17.0) (verified but not needed). View.onGeometryChange(for:of:action:) single-value form: SwiftUICore line 6067, @_alwaysEmitIntoClient in an @available(iOS 16.0) extension; the old/new-value form at line 6078 is iOS 18.0. GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:): SwiftUI line 23539, iOS 14. UIViewController.systemMinimumLayoutMargins exists (UIViewController.h:561, iOS 11) if the real system value is wanted instead of a guessed threshold.

**Regression risks:** Option with larger posters changes the decode size of the .grid image profile and must change ListImagePrefetch in step, otherwise prefetched images miss the cache and posters pop in (deliberate image tuning). A measured width arrives after the first layout pass; without a seeded initial value the grid jumps once on open. The paginated grids (pageSize 90, onAppear load-more) and the Equatable content views keep working as long as column computation stays out of the Equatable comparison. Changing the inset on iPad shifts every shelf by 4 pt, including the M3U screens that share the cards.

**How to verify:** Screenshots on iPhone 17 Pro, a Max-size iPhone and iPad, portrait: large title, search field, shelf header, first shelf card and first grid poster share one leading x; trailing poster edge mirrors it. On the Max simulator read the large title's leading x first to settle 16 versus 20. With larger posters: scroll a category grid on a cold cache and check that prefetched posters appear without a placeholder flash.

## design-system-consistency-11 — Continue Watching and History use two near-identical landscape cards that differ in every detail and ignore PosterMetrics

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Continue Watching, History
- Code: `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:64-110`, `Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:66-77, 154-203`

**What the user perceives:** The same item looks slightly different after tapping "Continue Watching >": the thumbnail is 5 pt taller, the corners are tighter, the title weight changes and suddenly wraps to two lines, the subtitle changes size. On iPad both stay 160 pt wide next to 200 pt posters.

**Mechanism (finder):** HistoryCard (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:64-110): 160x90, radius 12, spacing 8, title .caption.bold one line, subtitle .system(size: 10), progress track black 0.5 with cornerRadius 1.5, tapped through onTapGesture. HistoryCardGridItem (WatchHistoryListView.swift:154-203): 160x95, radius 10, spacing 6, title .caption.semibold two lines, subtitle .caption2, track black 0.55, Button with .plain. The grid uses literal GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 160), spacing: 16), spacing 20 and padding 16 (WatchHistoryListView.swift:66-76) instead of the scaled metrics every other grid uses. The comment at WatchHistoryListView.swift:152 calls it the grid twin of HistoryCard, so the drift is unintended.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One card in Views/DesignSystem/MediaCards.swift used by both screens:
struct LandscapeCard: View { let imageURL: URL?; let title: String; var subtitle: String? = nil; var progress: Double? = nil; var placeholderSymbol: String = "film"; var width: CGFloat = 160 }
16:9 artwork (height = width * 9 / 16), radius from the shared token, title/subtitle from the shared caption style, CardProgressBar at the bottom. Add var landscapeCardWidth: CGFloat { scaled(240) } clamped to at least 160 in PosterMetrics so the card grows on iPad, and use it for the row and as the adaptive minimum of the history grid (with alignment: .top). HistoryCard and HistoryCardGridItem become one-line adapters wrapped in Button + .pressableCard.

**APIs:** GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read both cards. Every cited difference is real: HistoryCard (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:64-110) is 160x90, radius 12, VStack spacing 8, title .caption.bold lineLimit 1, subtitle .system(size: 10) (does not scale with Dynamic Type), track black 0.5 + cornerRadius 1.5, and is tapped via .onTapGesture at :50 (no press feedback, no button trait for VoiceOver). HistoryCardGridItem (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:154-203) is 160x95, radius 10, spacing 6, title .caption.semibold lineLimit 2, subtitle .caption2, track 0.55, Button + .plain. The grid uses literals GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: 160), spacing: 16), spacing 20, padding 16 (WatchHistoryListView.swift:66-76) while every other grid uses posterMetrics (FavoritesView.swift:30-32, VODView.swift:636, SeriesView.swift:599, LiveStreamsView.swift:598, M3UChannelsView.swift:574). PosterMetrics scales posters 100 pt (iPhone, scale 0.5) to 200 pt (iPad) (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:13-17), so the fixed 160 pt landscape card is larger than a poster on iPhone and smaller on iPad. One inference in the finding is wrong: the comment at WatchHistoryListView.swift:152-153 says 'grid eş değeri — biraz daha büyük kart' (grid equivalent, a slightly larger card), so the 95 pt height was intended as 'bigger'; it is only 5 pt taller and the same width, so the intent was not achieved, but it is not pure drift. git history (0ab5bcd, d2489f9) gives no other rationale. Two things the finding missed that strengthen it: (a) the two sizes produce different Nuke processed-image cache keys (CachedImage.request uses width/height, Views/CachedImage.swift:102-123), so opening History re-decodes the same artwork the row already showed and shows the placeholder briefly; (b) the grid's GridItem has no alignment, so in a row mixing 1-line and 2-line titles the shorter card is centred vertically and its thumbnail sits lower than its neighbour's. No history exists in the demo screenshots, so the visual claim is from code only. The fix names helpers that do not exist in the code base (.pressableCard, CardProgressBar, Views/DesignSystem/) - they come from sibling findings and must be defined or dropped.

**Corrected claim:** Continue Watching (HistoryCard) and History (HistoryCardGridItem) render the same item with two hand-built landscape cards that differ in height (90 vs 95), radius (12 vs 10), spacing, title weight and line count, subtitle font (fixed 10 pt vs .caption2), progress track and tap handling (onTapGesture vs Button). The 5 pt height difference was meant as 'a slightly larger card' per the comment but is imperceptible as such; the rest is unexplained drift. Both ignore PosterMetrics (fixed 160 pt on iPhone and iPad), the two sizes defeat the processed-image cache between the row and the grid, the row card has no press feedback or button trait, and the grid has no top alignment so thumbnails in one row can sit at different heights.

**Corrected fix:** One shared card view (any file; a new Views/Components/LandscapeHistoryCard.swift is enough, no DesignSystem folder required): struct taking item: DBWatchHistory and width: CGFloat, artwork width x round(width*9/16) with contentMode .fill, one radius (12, matching channel tiles), title .caption.weight(.semibold), subtitle .caption2 (drops the fixed 10 pt font), progress bar clipped by the artwork clip. Add to PosterMetrics: var landscapeCardWidth: CGFloat { max(160, scaled(240)) } (160 on iPhone, 240 on iPad). ContinueWatchingRow: read @Environment(\.posterMetrics), wrap each card in Button { onPlay(item) } label: { card }.buttonStyle(.plain) instead of .onTapGesture, title lineLimit 1. WatchHistoryListView: columns [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: metrics.landscapeCardWidth), spacing: metrics.gridSpacing-or-16, alignment: .top)], same card with the same width so the Nuke cache key is shared, title lineLimit 2 with reservesSpace if equal heights are wanted. Do not reference .pressableCard / CardProgressBar unless the sibling finding that defines them is implemented first.

**API check:** GridItem: '@available(iOS 14.0, ...) public struct GridItem' with 'public init(_ size: SwiftUI.GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CoreFoundation.CGFloat? = nil, alignment: SwiftUICore.Alignment? = nil)' (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23528-23539). RoundedRectangle 'init(cornerRadius: CGFloat, style: RoundedCornerStyle = .continuous)' (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:10354). posterMetrics environment is injected at Views/DashboardView.swift:86 and Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:46 and has a UIScreen-based default (PosterMetrics.swift:75-79), so both screens can read it. .pressableCard and CardProgressBar: not found anywhere in the code base (grep).

**Regression risks:** On iPad the History grid goes from 4 columns of 160 pt to 3 columns of 240 pt in portrait (fewer items per screen). Continue Watching row gets taller on iPad (135 vs 90 pt artwork), shifting the shelves below it. New artwork size changes the Nuke request key once (one re-decode per image; no prefetch is involved for history). Button inside the horizontal ScrollView replaces onTapGesture: verify the NavigationLink header and scroll gestures still behave. ContinueWatchingRow is used on four screens (LiveStreamsView.swift:213, VODView.swift:65, SeriesView.swift:66, M3UChannelsView.swift:157), so check all four.

**How to verify:** Simulator with seeded watch history (movie with progress, episode with secondary title, live channel): screenshot the Continue Watching row and the History grid on iPhone and iPad, light and dark. Check: same card geometry and fonts in both; grid rows top-aligned when titles wrap; opening History shows artwork without a placeholder flash for items already in the row; press highlight and VoiceOver 'button' trait on row cards; largest Dynamic Type size scales the subtitle.

## design-system-consistency-12 — Four hand-built chip styles and three count-badge styles for the same two roles

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Search, TV Guide, Series detail, Movie detail, Category picker, M3U channels, Playlist list
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:25-46`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:104-123`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:318-342, 433-478`, `Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:111-118`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:111-115`, `ContentView.swift:220-226`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: For the Search tab the system alternative to a custom chip row is .searchScopes on the searchable modifier; whether to switch is a call for the search lens and the owner. The shared chip is the smaller step.

**What the user perceives:** The pill used to pick a search filter, a guide day, a season or a genre looks different each time: different height, text size, unselected fill and outline. Small number pills next to category names differ the same way.

**Mechanism (finder):** Selectable chips: Search filter (SearchView.swift:28-39) .subheadline, padding 14x7, Color.accentColor / Color(.systemGray5), .cornerRadius(20), default button style; guide day (EPGGuideView.swift:109-118) .caption, padding 12x6, accent / Color(.secondarySystemFill), Capsule; season (DetailComponents.swift:443-465) .subheadline.semibold, padding 14x9, accent / clear with a 1 pt primary 0.14 stroke; genre (DetailComponents.swift:326-335, not selectable) .caption.semibold, padding 12x6, .ultraThinMaterial plus 0.5 pt stroke. All use hard-coded .white on the accent fill. Count badges: CategoryPickerSheet.swift:111-118 caption.semibold on Color.secondary.opacity(0.15) with cornerRadius 8; EPGGuideRowViews.swift:111-115 caption2.medium on tertiarySystemFill Capsule; M3UChannelsView.swift:350-353 bare text; playlist type tag ContentView.swift:220-226 accent 0.15 with cornerRadius 4.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Views/DesignSystem/Chips.swift:
struct FilterChip: View { let title: String; let isSelected: Bool; let action: () -> Void }
struct CountBadge: View { let count: Int }
FilterChip: Button with .font(.subheadline.weight(isSelected ? .semibold : .regular)), padding 14x7, .background(isSelected ? AnyShapeStyle(.tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.fill.tertiary), in: Capsule()), selected text Color.white, .buttonStyle(.plain), .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : []). On iOS 26 the unselected state can become glass: if #available(iOS 26, *) { label.glassEffect(.regular, in: Capsule()) } else the fill above. CountBadge: .caption2.weight(.medium).monospacedDigit() on .fill.tertiary Capsule. Replace the three selectable chips and the three count pills; GenreChipRow reuses the unselected look.

**APIs:** ShapeStyle.fill (FillShapeStyle) (iOS 17.0); View.glassEffect(_:in:) (iOS 26.0); View.searchScopes(_:scopes:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** All cited styles verified in code. Selectable chips: Search filter (Views/SearchView.swift:27-39) .subheadline, padding 14x7, Color.accentColor / Color(.systemGray5), .cornerRadius(20), no buttonStyle; guide day (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:108-118) .caption, 12x6, accent / Color(.secondarySystemFill), Capsule, .plain; season (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:443-465) .subheadline.semibold, 14x9, accent / clear with 1 pt primary 0.14 stroke; genre (DetailComponents.swift:324-336, not interactive) .caption.semibold, 12x6, ultraThinMaterial + 0.5 pt stroke. Count pills: CategoryPickerSheet.swift:110-118 (secondary 0.15, cornerRadius 8), EPGGuideRowViews.swift:111-115 (tertiarySystemFill Capsule), M3UChannelsView.swift:350-353 (bare text); playlist tag ContentView.swift:220-226 (accent 0.15, radius 4) is a type tag, not a count. Screenshots iphone-light/Q03, iphone-dark/L06 and L07 match. No chip exposes .isSelected to accessibility (grep for a selected trait: none), which is a real gap the shared component would close. No git history or comment marks the differences as deliberate. However: the chips never appear side by side (each is on a different screen) and each looks acceptable alone in the screenshots, so user-perceived impact is small - this is code hygiene plus a minor consistency gain, not a medium native-feel defect. Three parts of the fix need correcting: (1) the iOS 26 glassEffect option puts Liquid Glass on content-layer elements inside scroll content (season bar in the detail ScrollView, genre row); each glassEffect is a separate backdrop effect, Apple reserves glass for the control/navigation layer, and it adds an OS-specific look for no functional gain - drop it. (2) 'GenreChipRow reuses the unselected look' would make non-interactive genre labels look identical to tappable unselected season chips directly below them on the series detail; today they are visually distinct. (3) For the category picker, which is a List row, the system idiom is View.badge(_:) rather than a custom capsule. Also FilterChip as specified has one size (.subheadline 14x7), which enlarges the dense EPG day row.

**Corrected claim:** Three selectable chip rows (search filter, EPG day, season) and one static chip row (genre) are each hand-built with different font, padding, unselected fill and outline, all with hard-coded white on the accent fill and none exposing a selected trait to VoiceOver; three count indicators (category picker, EPG category header, M3U group header) are styled three ways. The inconsistency is real but spans separate screens; its visible cost is low. The stronger practical gain of a shared chip is one place for the selected trait, hit target and fill tokens.

**Corrected fix:** Add one FilterChip (Views/Components is fine): Button(action:) { Text(title).font(compact ? .caption : .subheadline).fontWeight(isSelected ? .semibold : .regular).padding(.horizontal, compact ? 12 : 14).padding(.vertical, compact ? 6 : 7).foregroundStyle(isSelected ? Color.white : Color.primary).background(isSelected ? AnyShapeStyle(.tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.fill.tertiary), in: Capsule()) }.buttonStyle(.plain).accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : []). Use it for the search filter row, the EPG day picker (compact: true, keeps today's density) and DetailSeasonTabBar (the caller keeps its withAnimation spring, .id(season.id) and ScrollViewReader). No glassEffect variant. Leave GenreChipRow visually distinct from the selectable chip (keep it as is, or render genres as plain secondary text) because it is not tappable. Counts: in CategoryPickerSheet replace the custom pill with the List-row system badge (.badge(entry.count) on the row); keep the EPG header pill and give the M3U header the same small view only if a CountBadge is wanted - optional. Whether Search should use .searchScopes instead of a chip row stays a decision for the search lens and the owner.

**API check:** ShapeStyle.fill: '@available(iOS 17.0, ...) extension ShapeStyle where Self == SwiftUI.FillShapeStyle { static var fill }' (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1998-2005); ShapeStyle.tertiary instance property '@_alwaysEmitIntoClient public var tertiary: some ShapeStyle' (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6734, iOS 17 hierarchy levels on any style). ShapeStyle.tint: 'static var tint: TintShapeStyle' (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19568-19569, iOS 15). background(_:in:fillStyle:) found (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:15757). View.glassEffect: '@available(iOS 26.0, ...) nonisolated public func glassEffect(_ glass: Glass = .regular, in shape: some Shape = DefaultGlassEffectShape())' (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:2590-2593) - exists, but I recommend not using it here. View.searchScopes(_:scopes:) iOS 16.0 and searchScopes(_:activation:_:) iOS 16.4 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2470-2495). View.badge(_ count: Int) '@available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, *)' (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:20869-20873). All fine for an iOS 18 target without availability checks except glassEffect.

**Regression risks:** Season bar: selection animation and proxy.scrollTo must be kept by the caller; unselected season chips change from outline to tertiary fill over the hero fade (check contrast in light and dark). Search filter row height unchanged; EPG day row unchanged only if the compact variant is used (the guide header height feeds the fixed grid layout below it, so do not change its height casually). .badge on a List row whose content is a Button with swipeActions should be checked once in the simulator (badge is drawn by the list row; hidden rows have opacity 0.55). If glass were used anyway: many glass effects in scroll content cost GPU and look different from every other content element.

**How to verify:** Screenshot comparison before/after of Q01/Q03 (search chips), iphone-dark L06 (guide day chips), series detail season bar with a working series, L07 (category picker counts), light and dark. VoiceOver: each chip announces 'selected' for the active one. Check the season bar still centres the selected chip on change and the EPG grid header height is unchanged.

## design-system-consistency-13 — Colour and symbol use is not semantic: the star means three things in three colours, one toolbar icon is tinted, and filter icons are a circle inside the glass circle

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series, M3U channels, Movie detail, Series detail, Category grids
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:233-239`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:74-83`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:86-91`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:880-887`, `Views/RatingLabel.swift:42-44, 76-81`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:154-156, 301`, `Views/VODView.swift:772-775`, `Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset/Contents.json:1-11`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should a favourited item show a yellow star (today) or the app tint? And does the app want its own accent colour instead of default blue (AccentColor.colorset is empty)? Both are brand decisions; the fixes above work with either answer.

**What the user perceives:** In the top-right glass group one icon is blue and the others are black (iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png, iphone-dark/L01-live-home.png). On a detail screen a yellow star in the hero is the rating and a star in the toolbar is the favourite, which also turns yellow; yellow on the light glass button is hard to see. The sort button shows a ringed icon inside the round glass button (iphone-light/M03-movies-category-detail.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** Favorites entry: Image("star.fill").foregroundStyle(Color.accentColor) with .font(.body.weight(.semibold)) (DashboardView.swift:235-237, M3UChannelsView.swift:78-80); the neighbouring toolbar icons also force .body.semibold (LiveStreamsView.swift:113-134, VODView.swift:117-128, SeriesView.swift:118-129) while the detail and history toolbars set no font. Favourite toggle: .foregroundColor(isFavorite ? .yellow : .primary) (MovieDetailView.swift:89, SeriesView.swift:885). Rating: .yellow.opacity(0.95) (RatingLabel.swift:44), .yellow (DetailComponents.swift:156), white in the poster badge (RatingLabel.swift:81). Sort menu label line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle(.fill) (VODView.swift:773, SeriesView.swift:714, LiveStreamsView.swift:670) is drawn inside the iOS 26 circular glass button. Outside the player 113 foregroundColor calls (soft-deprecated in the SDK in favour of foregroundStyle) sit next to 86 foregroundStyle calls, with raw .red / .green / .orange for status. AccentColor.colorset has no colour, so the tint is default system blue.

**Proposed fix (finder):** (1) Toolbar: remove the foregroundStyle and the .font overrides from toolbar images and let the system style them. (2) Favourite state: Image(systemName: isFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star") with no explicit colour, or .tint for the filled state; keep yellow for ratings only and route all three rating stars through RatingLabel. (3) Sort label: if #available(iOS 26, *) use "line.3.horizontal.decrease" (SF Symbols 2021 set) and mark the active state with .foregroundStyle(.tint); keep the .circle / .circle.fill pair on iOS 18 where bar buttons have no background. (4) New code and the shared kit use foregroundStyle with .primary / .secondary / .tint and a small enum BrowseStatus { static let error = Color.red; warning = Color.orange; success = Color.green } so status colours have one home; no mass rewrite of the 113 call sites.

**APIs:** View.foregroundStyle(_:) (iOS 15.0); View.foregroundColor(_:) (iOS 13.0, deprecated: 100000.0, renamed foregroundStyle(_:)); View.tint(_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Code and screenshots confirm the core. Favorites entry is the only tinted toolbar icon: Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.body.weight(.semibold)).foregroundStyle(Color.accentColor) at Views/DashboardView.swift:235-237 and Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:78-80; iphone-light/M01 and iphone-dark/L07 show a blue star next to monochrome icons in the same glass group. Root toolbars force .body.semibold on 14 images (LiveStreamsView.swift:114,123,133,671; VODView.swift:118,128,774; SeriesView.swift:119,129,715; M3UChannelsView.swift:70,79,89; DashboardView.swift:236) while detail and history toolbars set none (MovieDetailView.swift:86-91, SeriesView.swift:880-887, WatchHistoryListView.swift:101-106), so icon weight differs between root and pushed screens. Favourite toggle: .foregroundColor(isFavorite ? .yellow : .primary) (MovieDetailView.swift:89, SeriesView.swift:885). Sort menu label uses line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle(.fill) at exactly three sites (VODView.swift:773, SeriesView.swift:714, LiveStreamsView.swift:670); iphone-light/M03 shows the ring inside the round glass button. AccentColor.colorset has no colour values. foregroundColor is soft-deprecated in the SDK; my count outside the player is 116 foregroundColor vs 89 foregroundStyle (finding said 113/86 - same order). git log -S shows all of this dates from the initial import (d2489f9) or 654cefc with no comment marking it deliberate. Corrections: (1) 'route all three rating stars through RatingLabel' is not a fix: PosterRatingBadge (Views/RatingLabel.swift:69-87) is deliberately white on a black 0.55 capsule for legibility over arbitrary poster art and already shares ContentRating.displayText; the hero pill (DetailComponents.swift:152-163) takes a Double and differs from RatingLabel only by yellow vs yellow 0.95, which nobody can see. The rating star is consistently yellow where it is coloured; the claim 'three colours' for ratings is overstated. PosterRatingBadge also sits inside the Equatable shelf cards, so it should not be touched for no gain. (2) The foregroundColor/foregroundStyle mix and a BrowseStatus enum have no user-visible effect; fine as a convention for new code, not part of the defect. (3) 'yellow on the light glass button is hard to see' is plausible (systemYellow on a light surface is low contrast) but no screenshot shows a favourited item; treat it as likely, not proven.

**Corrected claim:** Three real inconsistencies in toolbar symbol treatment: (a) the Favorites entry star is force-tinted with the accent colour while its neighbours in the same iOS 26 glass group are monochrome; (b) root-screen toolbar icons are forced to .body.semibold while pushed screens use the system default weight; (c) the sort/filter button uses a .circle / .circle.fill symbol that draws a ring inside the round glass button on iOS 26. Separately, the favourite toggle turns yellow (same colour as the rating star shown in the hero of the same screen), which is a brand choice with a probable contrast problem on light glass. Rating stars themselves are consistent (yellow in text contexts, white on the dark poster badge by design).

**Corrected fix:** (1) Delete .foregroundStyle(Color.accentColor) and the .font(.body.weight(.semibold)) overrides from toolbar images (the 14 sites listed) so the system styles them; on iOS 18 all bar icons then take the tint, on iOS 26 all are monochrome. While there, add .accessibilityLabel(L("favorites.title")) to the Xtream favourites link (DashboardView.swift:234), which the M3U one already has. (2) Sort label: one small helper used by the three sites - if #available(iOS 26, *) { Image(systemName: "line.3.horizontal.decrease").foregroundStyle(isFilterActive ? AnyShapeStyle(.tint) : AnyShapeStyle(.primary)) } else { the existing .circle / .circle.fill pair }. iOS 18 fallback: unchanged symbols, bar buttons have no background there. (3) Favourite toggle: owner decision between yellow and tint; if changed, Image(systemName: isFavorite ? "star.fill" : "star") with no colour (or .foregroundStyle(.tint) when filled). (4) Leave PosterRatingBadge, RatingLabel and the hero rating pill alone. Use foregroundStyle in new code; no mass rewrite and no BrowseStatus enum needed.

**API check:** View.foregroundStyle(_:) iOS 15 (present, used across the code base). View.foregroundColor(_:): '@available(iOS, introduced: 13.0, deprecated: 100000.0, renamed: "foregroundStyle(_:)")' style attributes at SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:1918-1923 (soft deprecation, no warning). ShapeStyle.tint 'static var tint: TintShapeStyle' (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:19568-19569). SF Symbols: line.3.horizontal.decrease, .circle and .circle.fill are all release 2021 in /System/Library/CoreServices/CoreGlyphs.bundle/Contents/Resources/name_availability.plist (iOS 15), so safe on iOS 18. The #available(iOS 26, *) branch is needed only to choose the symbol; no iOS 26-only API is called.

**Regression risks:** iOS 18: toolbar icons lose the semibold weight and the star is tinted like its neighbours (all blue) - intended. iOS 26: the star entry becomes monochrome, so it no longer stands out; that is the system look. Active-filter state on iOS 26 is signalled only by tint on a plain glyph: check it is noticeable in light and dark; if not, the owner may prefer keeping .circle.fill for the active state only. Changing the favourite colour is a brand change (decision needed). No interaction with the tip-jar WIP and no performance-sensitive code touched if the rating badges are left alone.

**How to verify:** Screenshots before/after: L01/M01/S01 (toolbar group all one colour and weight), M03/S02/live category (sort button without ring, active filter state tinted), M07 with a favourited movie in light and dark (star legibility on glass). One run on an iOS 18 simulator to confirm bar icons are uniformly tinted and the .circle sort symbol is still used there.

## design-system-consistency-14 — Detail action buttons are custom drawn (gradient, glow, chevron, 16 / 12 pt radii) instead of system button styles

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:209-252, 274-314`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:101-143`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:147-162`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: The gradient CTA is a deliberate look; replacing it with the system prominent button is a product decision. If the owner keeps it, at least drop the trailing chevron and build the secondary shape once.

**What the user perceives:** "Watch Now" is a blue gradient bar with a glow and a trailing chevron, which reads as a navigation row rather than a play button; "Download" and "Restart" are grey material rectangles with a hairline border. On iOS 26 they sit next to capsule-shaped system glass controls (iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** primaryCTA builds its own background (LinearGradient of Color.accentColor, RoundedRectangle 16, accent shadow radius 12) with .buttonStyle(.plain), hard-coded .white text and a chevron.right (DetailComponents.swift:209-252). DetailSecondaryLabel (DetailComponents.swift:288-313) and DownloadButton.button (DownloadButton.swift:101-123) draw the same material + stroke shape twice with slightly different strokes (primary 0.08 / 0.5 pt versus secondary 0.15 / 1 pt), and the two are aligned with a negative top padding (MovieDetailView.swift:159-161).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the layout, swap the chrome for system styles in one place (a DetailButtonStyles.swift next to the components): primary: Button(action:) { label }.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large).buttonBorderShape(.capsule) on iOS 18, and if #available(iOS 26, *) .buttonStyle(.glassProminent); the resume progress stays inside the label, the chevron goes. Secondary (Restart, Trailer, Download): .buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large).buttonBorderShape(.capsule), and .buttonStyle(.glass) on iOS 26. DownloadButton keeps its state machine and context menu and only replaces its private button(icon:title:accent:) background.

**APIs:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.glassProminent (iOS 26.0); PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass (iOS 26.0); PrimitiveButtonStyle.borderedProminent (iOS 15.0); View.buttonBorderShape(_:) / ButtonBorderShape.capsule (iOS 15.0); View.controlSize(_:) (iOS 13.0 (large: iOS 15))

**Verifier reasons:** Code verified: primaryCTA (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:209-252) is a .plain Button with its own LinearGradient of Color.accentColor, RoundedRectangle 16, accent shadow radius 12, hard-coded white text and a trailing chevron.right (:226-228). DetailSecondaryLabel (:288-313) draws ultraThinMaterial + 0.5 pt strokeBorder primary 0.08 at radius 12; DownloadButton.button (Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:101-123) draws the same shape again with a 1 pt stroke secondary 0.15, and downloadingLabel (:125-143) a third time with no stroke; the Download button is aligned with .padding(.top, -10) (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:157-161, comment says it neutralises the VStack spacing). iphone-light/M07 and iphone-dark/M07 show the gradient bar with chevron above a bordered grey rectangle, next to capsule glass bar buttons. The trailing chevron on a play action is the one clearly non-native element (it reads as a disclosure/navigation row). The rest is a deliberate custom look (introduced with the detail redesign, no comment against system styles) and replacing it is a product decision, as the finding itself says. Fix corrections: (1) .buttonStyle(.bordered) on iOS 18 tints its label with the accent colour, so 'Download' / 'Restart' turn blue unless the label keeps an explicit foregroundStyle - DownloadButton relies on per-state colours (.green completed, .orange failed, DownloadButton.swift:95-97), which must stay explicit. (2) DownloadButton has a compact icon-only variant used in episode rows (SeriesView.swift:1470) and a separate downloadingLabel; the fix must cover all three shapes, not only button(icon:title:accent:). (3) The primary label is multi-line when resuming (title + subtitle + linear ProgressView, DetailComponents.swift:215-239); in a capsule border shape that content sits close to the curved ends - a rounded-rectangle border shape is the safer fit. (4) A separate .glassProminent/.glass branch is not needed for a native result: on iOS 26 .borderedProminent/.bordered already adopt the new system appearance, so a single code path avoids an availability fork; glass buttons in plain scroll content over systemBackground have nothing to refract anyway. Side note found while reading: the trailer label is a hard-coded Turkish string "Fragman" (DetailComponents.swift:265), not localized.

**Corrected claim:** The detail action buttons are custom-drawn: the primary CTA is a gradient + glow bar with a trailing chevron that reads as a navigation row, and the secondary shape is implemented three times (DetailSecondaryLabel, DownloadButton.button, DownloadButton.downloadingLabel) with different strokes and stitched together with a negative top padding. The chevron and the duplicated secondary chrome are defects; the gradient look itself is a deliberate style whose replacement is the owner's call.

**Corrected fix:** Minimum (no product decision): remove the trailing chevron.right from primaryCTA; extract one secondary background (single ViewModifier or ButtonStyle used by DetailSecondaryLabel, DownloadButton.button and downloadingLabel, including the compact variant) so stroke and radius are identical; localize "Fragman". If the owner wants system chrome: primary Button { label }.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent).controlSize(.large).buttonBorderShape(.roundedRectangle(radius: 16)) (or .capsule only if the resume layout is reduced to one line), label keeps .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) and the resume progress; secondary and Download: .buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.large) with the label's explicit .foregroundStyle kept (primary / green / orange) so it is not tinted blue; compact episode-row variant uses .controlSize(.small). Same code on iOS 18 and iOS 26; the optional iOS 26 branch (.glassProminent / .glass behind if #available(iOS 26, *), fallback = the bordered styles above) only if the owner specifically wants glass. DownloadButton keeps its state machine, .contextMenu and Query untouched.

**API check:** PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass: '@available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, tvOS 26.0, watchOS 26.0, *) extension PrimitiveButtonStyle where Self == GlassButtonStyle { static var glass; static func glass(_ glass: Glass) }' (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:1315-1322). glassProminent: same availability, 'where Self == GlassProminentButtonStyle { static var glassProminent }' (:3444-3450). borderedProminent: '@available(iOS 15.0, ...) where Self == BorderedProminentButtonStyle' (:21629-21631); bordered: iOS 15.0 (:17128-17130). buttonBorderShape(_:) iOS 15.0 (:15048-15050); ButtonBorderShape.capsule, .roundedRectangle and roundedRectangle(radius:) present with no iOS restriction beyond the struct's iOS 15 (:15055-15062). controlSize(_:) iOS 15.0 with ControlSize.large (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:6130-6168).

**Regression risks:** Visual change to a deliberate branded CTA (owner decision). System bordered styles tint labels: state colours of DownloadButton must be kept explicit. The compact download button in episode rows (SeriesView.swift:1470) must keep its small footprint or episode rows grow. The negative top padding in MovieDetailView.swift:161 depends on current heights; re-check spacing after the change. Link (trailer) takes button styles, but verify it renders like its neighbour. Series detail shares DetailActionBar, so check both screens and the resume state with progress.

**How to verify:** Screenshots of movie detail and series detail in light and dark on iOS 26 and on an iOS 18 simulator, in four states: fresh (Watch Now), resume with progress + Restart, download in progress, download completed/failed; plus an episode row with the compact download button. Confirm no blue-tinted secondary labels, equal stroke/radius on Restart and Download, and no chevron on the primary button.

## design-system-consistency-15 — Nine corner radii with no scale, and list thumbnails letterbox posters in a square with two stacked clips

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search results, Downloads, Live TV, Movies, Series, History, Detail
- Code: `Views/CachedImage.swift:57, 82`, `Views/SearchView.swift:316-318`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:237-243`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:434-441`, `Views/VODView.swift:503-510`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:103-110, 248, 306`

**What the user perceives:** A 56 pt channel logo has rounder corners than a 100 pt poster next to it; in search results movie and series posters appear as narrow square-cornered slivers inside an invisible 44 pt box (iphone-light/Q03-search-results-mi.png).

**Mechanism (finder):** Radii found outside the player: 4 (playlist tag), 6 (search row clip, guide cells), 8 (CachedImage default, so every poster, episode thumb, downloads thumb), 10 (history grid card, empty-state button), 12 (channel tiles, Continue Watching card, secondary buttons, HUD), 14 (hero poster), 16 (primary CTA), 20 (search chips), Capsule. Posters use the default 8 (VODView.swift:503-510, SeriesView.swift:475-482) while the smaller channel tile passes 12 (LiveStreamsView.swift:438). ResultRow renders CachedImage 44x44 with the default .fit and radius 8 and then clips again with radius 6 (SearchView.swift:317-318); the clip applies to the 44 pt frame, not to the letterboxed poster, so poster corners stay square. DownloadsView does the same with 56x56 and 8 + 8 (DownloadsView.swift:237-243).

**Proposed fix (finder):** enum BrowseRadius in Views/DesignSystem/BrowseTokens.swift: thumb 6, poster 10, tile 12, control 12, heroPoster 14; pass them explicitly to CachedImage (keep its default at 8 so untouched call sites do not change). ResultRow and the downloads row take a kind: live rows keep a square 44 pt logo with .fit; movie and series rows use a 2:3 thumbnail (36x54) with contentMode .fill and cornerRadius BrowseRadius.thumb, and the extra .clipShape lines are removed. Prefetch is not used for these rows, so no request-key change matters.

**APIs:** RoundedRectangle.init(cornerRadius:style:) (default .continuous) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Radii verified by grep outside the player: 4 (ContentView.swift:226), 6 (x4, incl. SearchView.swift:318), 8 (CachedImage default at Views/CachedImage.swift:57, DownloadsView.swift:243), 10, 12 (x7, incl. LiveStreamsView.swift:438), 14 (DetailComponents.swift:107,113), 16 (:248), 20 (SearchView.swift:39) plus Capsule - nine values, no token. Posters use the CachedImage default 8 (VODView.swift:503-510, SeriesView.swift:475-482) while channel tiles pass 12. The search-row defect is real and visible: ResultRow (Views/SearchView.swift:316-318) builds CachedImage 44x44 with the default contentMode .fit and radius 8, then clips again with radius 6; CachedImage clips the 44 pt frame (CachedImage.swift:81-82), not the letterboxed image, so a 2:3 poster renders as a ~29x44 square-cornered sliver - exactly what iphone-light/Q03-search-results-mi.png shows for Family Ties, Midnight Horizon and Modern Family Days. DownloadsView.swift:237-243 has the same pattern (56x56, .fit, 8 + 8). Neither screen uses ListImagePrefetch (grep: no hits), so changing the request size has no prefetch-key consequence, as the finding says. No comment or history marks any of this as deliberate (d2489f9 import). Corrections: (1) the 'nine radii' part is code hygiene; the example given (56 pt logo rounder than a 100 pt poster 'next to it') does not occur on screen - tiles and posters live on different tabs - so only the thumbnail defect is user-perceivable. (2) A 36x54 poster next to 44 pt live logos in the same List ('All' filter) shifts the title column by 8 pt between sections and misaligns separators; the thumbnail needs a fixed-width leading slot. (3) Downloads episodes use episode.cover ?? seriesCover (SeriesView.swift:1461): the episode cover is usually a 16:9 still, so forcing 2:3 .fill would crop it badly; the downloads row needs a different rule than search. (4) Raising poster radius 8 -> 10 across shelves and grids is a visible change on the most-used screens for no clear gain; keep it out of the minimal fix.

**Corrected claim:** Search result rows and download rows show movie/series artwork letterboxed (.fit) inside a square frame, and the rounded clip (applied twice with different radii) hits the empty frame instead of the image, so posters appear as narrow square-cornered slivers (visible in Q03). Separately, corner radii outside the player are nine ad-hoc literals with no shared scale; this is a maintainability issue with little visible effect.

**Corrected fix:** Search: give ResultRow a kind. Live rows keep CachedImage 44x44, .fit, cornerRadius 6. Movie and series rows use CachedImage(width: 44, height: 66, cornerRadius: 6, contentMode: .fill, loadProfile: .grid) (2:3, same 44 pt leading width so titles and separators stay aligned across sections), and the extra .clipShape line is removed. If 66 pt rows are judged too tall, use 36x54 inside .frame(width: 44). Downloads: movies 2:3 as above at the existing 56 pt width slot; episodes keep a 16:9-friendly shape (e.g. 80x45 or the square 56x56) with contentMode .fill and a single radius; remove the second clipShape. Radius tokens: optional small enum (thumb 6, poster 8, tile 12, hero 14) adopted when files are touched; do not change the CachedImage default or the poster radius in shelves/grids as part of this fix.

**API check:** RoundedRectangle: '@inlinable public init(cornerRadius: CoreFoundation.CGFloat, style: SwiftUICore.RoundedCornerStyle = .continuous)' (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:10354), iOS 13. No other system API is involved; CachedImage already accepts cornerRadius and contentMode parameters (Views/CachedImage.swift:53-60) and builds the Nuke request from width/height/contentMode (:102-123).

**Regression risks:** Search rows get taller (66 pt artwork vs 44), so fewer results per screen and a different row height between Live and Movies/Series sections. The new size changes the Nuke processed-image key for these rows (one re-decode; no prefetch affected). .fill center-crops artwork whose aspect is not 2:3 (some panels return landscape or square movie art). Episode downloads with 16:9 stills must not be forced into 2:3. If the poster radius were changed globally it would alter every shelf and grid card; the cards are Equatable rows, and a constant radius does not affect their equality, but the look change is app-wide.

**How to verify:** Screenshots of Q03/Q04/Q05 (search results, All and Movies filter) in light and dark: posters fill their thumbnail with rounded corners and titles align between the Live, Movies and Series sections. T05 downloads with one downloaded movie and one episode (episode with a landscape still and one falling back to the series cover). Scroll a long result list on a real catalog to confirm no scrolling regression (loadProfile .grid unchanged).
