## design-system-consistency-16 — Shelf, card and grid code exists in four copies; a small shared kit would enforce the above without a redesign

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort L · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV, Movies, Series, M3U channels, Favorites, History, Search
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:337-459, 584-623`, `Views/VODView.swift:302-354, 400-545, 675-731`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:279-331, 376-517, 634-672`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:320-477, 560-594`, `Views/PosterMetrics.swift:16-50`

**What the user perceives:** Each tab drifts a little from the others (spacing 12 versus 14 versus 16, radius 8 versus 12, press feedback, header style), because every fix has to be made four times. The user feels it as an app assembled from similar but not identical screens.

**Mechanism (finder):** Card table (size source / radius / title / alignment / lines / badge / spacing / placeholder / tap). LiveStreamCard (LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459): PosterMetrics liveShelfIcon 112s or liveGridIconSize 180s / 12 / caption medium / centre / 2 / guide line / 10 / tv / Button plain. M3UChannelCard (M3UChannelsView.swift:408-477): identical body plus contextMenu. VODStreamCard (VODView.swift:490-545): 200x300 scaled / 8 / caption medium / centre / 2 (1 in iPhone shelves) / rating capsule 9-10 pt, progress at top / default 8 / film / NavigationLink. SeriesCard (SeriesView.swift:462-517): line-for-line copy of VODStreamCard with play.tv. HistoryCard (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:64-110): fixed 160x90 / 12 / caption bold / leading / 1 / progress bottom / 8 / tv or film / onTapGesture. HistoryCardGridItem (WatchHistoryListView.swift:154-203): fixed 160x95 / 10 / caption semibold / leading / 2 / progress bottom / 6 / Button plain. ResultRow (SearchView.swift:309-326): 44x44 / 8 then 6 / body / leading / 1. Shelf rows: LiveCategoryShelfRow, VODCategoryShelfRow, SeriesCategoryShelfRow, M3UGroupShelfRow plus two Recently Added shelves repeat the same VStack(spacing: 10) + header + horizontal LazyHStack with spacing 12 (live, M3U) or 14 (posters). The paginated grid body (ForEach over prefix(visibleCount).enumerated(), loadMore at visibleCount - 15, trailing ProgressView) is copied in LiveStreamsView.swift:600-621, VODView.swift:689-718 and SeriesView.swift:647-670; M3UGroupGridContent (M3UChannelsView.swift:577-591) is the unpaginated fourth copy. PosterMetrics also carries eight tokens nothing uses (searchGridMinWidth, searchCardWidth/Height, searchLiveRowIcon/LeadingInset, seasonStripWidth/Height, searchGridSpacing, searchSectionRowSpacing).

**Proposed fix (finder):** New folder Views/DesignSystem/ (the target uses file-system-synchronized groups, so project.pbxproj is not edited):
1. BrowseTokens.swift: enum BrowseRadius, enum BrowseSpacing { shelfItem = 12; headerToContent = 10; shelfVertical = 6 }, PosterMetrics.pageMargin, removal of the unused tokens.
2. PressableCardStyle.swift: struct PressableCardStyle: ButtonStyle.
3. ShelfHeader.swift: struct ShelfHeader<Destination: View, Trailing: View>: View.
4. MediaCards.swift: struct CardProgressBar: View { let fraction: Double }; struct PosterCard: View { let imageURL: URL?; let title: String; var subtitle: String? = nil; var rating: String? = nil; var progress: Double? = nil; var placeholderSymbol = "film"; let posterWidth: CGFloat; let posterHeight: CGFloat; var imageLoadProfile: ImageLoadProfile = .standard }; struct ChannelTile: View { let iconURL: URL?; let name: String; let nowNext: EPGNowNext?; let showsGuideLine: Bool; let width: CGFloat; let iconSize: CGFloat; var imageLoadProfile: ImageLoadProfile = .standard }; struct LandscapeCard: View (see the history finding).
5. ShelfSection.swift: struct ShelfSection<Header: View, Content: View>: View and struct ShelfScroller<Content: View>: View { var height: CGFloat? = nil; var spacing: CGFloat = BrowseSpacing.shelfItem; @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content }.
6. PagedCardGrid.swift: struct PagedCardGrid<Item, ID: Hashable, Cell: View>: View { let items: [Item]; let id: KeyPath<Item, ID>; let minimumCellWidth: CGFloat; @Binding var visibleCount: Int; var pageSize = 90; @ViewBuilder let cell: (Item) -> Cell }.
7. Chips.swift: FilterChip, CountBadge.
Safe to share: everything above, because it is leaf or container layout. Keep as they are: the four Equatable row structs and the three Equatable *CategoryContent structs with their ==, itemsToken, off-main recompute and prefetch calls; VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, LiveStreamCard, M3UChannelCard and HistoryCard stay as thin adapters over PosterCard / ChannelTile / LandscapeCard so call sites, the .equatable() contract and the UI-test lookups do not change. Do not merge the rows into one generic CategoryShelfRow<Item> with closures: the cheap == depends on concrete array equality and each row has its own destination and prefetch size. Order: tokens, header, progress bar and button style first (each S), then cards, then scroller and grid.

**APIs:** ButtonStyle (iOS 13.0); GridItem.init(_:spacing:alignment:) (iOS 14.0); View.lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:) (iOS 16.0); ScaledMetric (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** I re-read every cited block. The duplication and the drift are real; the description is slightly off in places and the fix is over-scoped in its last two steps.

DUPLICATION CONFIRMED
- Shelf rows: LiveCategoryShelfRow (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:337-417), VODCategoryShelfRow (Views/VODView.swift:400-488), SeriesCategoryShelfRow (Views/SeriesView.swift:376-460), M3UGroupShelfRow (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:320-404) and the two Recently Added shelves (VODView.swift:302-354, SeriesView.swift:279-331) all repeat VStack(spacing: 10) + NavigationLink header (headline + chevron, 16 pt inset) + horizontal LazyHStack + .padding(.vertical, 6). Item spacing is 12 for live and M3U (LiveStreamsView.swift:383, M3UChannelsView.swift:364) and 14 for posters (VODView.swift:332,449; SeriesView.swift:309,421).
- Cards: LiveStreamCard (LiveStreamsView.swift:419-459) and M3UChannelCard (M3UChannelsView.swift:408-477) have identical bodies apart from the context menu. VODStreamCard (VODView.swift:490-545) and SeriesCard (SeriesView.swift:462-517) are line-for-line copies apart from the placeholder symbol and image field.
- History cards: HistoryCard (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:64-110) is 160x90, radius 12, caption bold, 1 line, onTapGesture. HistoryCardGridItem (Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:154-203) is 160x95, radius 10, caption semibold, 2 lines, Button plain.
- Paginated grid: the block (ForEach over prefix(visibleCount).enumerated(), loadMore at visibleCount - 15, trailing ProgressView) is copied at LiveStreamsView.swift:600-621, VODView.swift:689-718 and SeriesView.swift:647-670. M3UGroupGridContent (M3UChannelsView.swift:577-591) is the unpaginated fourth copy. FavoritesView.swift:106-175 holds three more unpaginated grids the finding did not list.
- Synchronized groups: project.pbxproj:55-66 uses PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup for another-iptv-player, so a new Views/DesignSystem folder needs no project edit.

DRIFT A USER CAN PERCEIVE
- Press feedback: the series grid NavigationLink (SeriesView.swift:650-660) and both favourites grids (FavoritesView.swift:134,160) lack the .buttonStyle(.plain) that the movies grid has (VODView.swift:704). HistoryCard uses onTapGesture, so it has no press feedback and no button trait.
- Continue Watching header is title2 bold with 20 pt insets and 16 pt item spacing (ContinueWatchingRow.swift:35,44,47,55), sitting in the same scroll view as headline headers at 16 pt and 12/14 pt spacing.
- Poster progress bar sits at the top (ZStack alignment .topTrailing, VODView.swift:502-522) while history cards put it at the bottom.
- Search rows clip twice, radius 8 then 6 (Views/SearchView.swift:317-318).
- "1 line in iPhone shelves" is correct but it is not a lineLimit: the code says lineLimit(2) (VODView.swift:531). At layoutScale 0.5 shelfRowTotalHeight is 150 + 32 = 182 (Views/PosterMetrics.swift:50), less than poster 150 + spacing 8 + two caption lines, so the title is squeezed to one line. Screenshot iphone-light/M01-movies-home.png shows "Whispers in th...".

CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIM
- Nine unused tokens are listed, not eight. All nine have zero references outside PosterMetrics.swift, none in tests, and they date from the initial import (git log -S points only to d2489f9 / fe55017). Removal is safe.
- "Four copies" overstates it for cards: they are two identical pairs plus two history variants. Live and M3U match each other, as do Movies and Series.
- The live/home screenshots (iphone-dark/L01, iphone-light/M01) look coherent. The 12 vs 14 spacing and 8 vs 12 radius sit between different tile shapes and are not visible as inconsistency. Forcing shelfItem = 12 onto poster shelves is a visual change, not a bug fix.
- No history or comment marks the duplication as deliberate. The deliberate parts are the Equatable ==, itemsToken, pagination and prefetch, which the fix already keeps.

PROBLEMS WITH THE FIX AS WRITTEN
- PagedCardGrid's cell: (Item) -> Cell drops the index. M3UGroupGridContent needs it for prefetchAhead(from: index) (M3UChannelsView.swift:587).
- If PagedCardGrid owns the ScrollView, VODCategoryContent loses its ScrollViewReader / .id(gridTopID) scroll-to-top on sort and filter change (VODView.swift:688-728).
- Moving the M3U grid onto pagination is a behaviour change, not a refactor.
- UI tests find cards by app.staticTexts["Midnight Horizon"] and similar (another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:43,67,89,303,321). Shared cards must not add accessibilityElement(children: .combine) or a custom label unless the tests are updated.

Severity: the user-visible gain comes from the small steps; the generic scroller and grid are maintainability only. I rate it low as a standalone finding, since its value is as the delivery vehicle for the other consistency findings.

**Corrected claim:** Shelf, card and grid code is duplicated across Live, Movies, Series and M3U. Card bodies form two identical pairs (LiveStreamCard and M3UChannelCard; VODStreamCard and SeriesCard) plus two divergent history cards. The shelf scaffold is repeated six times, and the paginated grid body three times with an unpaginated M3U copy and three unpaginated favourites grids. The drift a user can actually perceive is narrow: press feedback (series grid and favourites grids lack .buttonStyle(.plain); HistoryCard uses onTapGesture), the Continue Watching header (title2 bold, 20 pt inset) against category headers (headline, 16 pt), history cards 160x90 radius 12 versus 160x95 radius 10, progress bar at the top on posters and at the bottom on history cards, and poster titles squeezed to one line in iPhone shelves because shelfRowTotalHeight is too short. The 12 vs 14 spacing and 8 vs 12 radius between channel tiles and posters is not perceptible as inconsistency. PosterMetrics carries nine unused tokens, not eight. The underlying issue is maintainability; the refactor is not itself a user-visible fix.

**Corrected fix:** Split the proposal into two tiers and do only the first now.

Tier 1 (S to M, low risk, visible gain), in new files under Views/DesignSystem/:
1. Tokens: delete the nine unused PosterMetrics tokens. Add pageMargin = 16 and shelf spacing tokens that keep today's values (12 for channel tiles, 14 for posters). Unifying them is a product decision for the owner.
2. ShelfHeader: one header view used by the six shelf rows and ContinueWatchingRow, so header font and inset match.
3. CardProgressBar: one view, bottom-aligned, used by VODStreamCard, SeriesCard and both history cards.
4. PressableCardStyle: ButtonStyle: apply at every card call site, including SeriesView.swift:650 and FavoritesView.swift:134,160, which have no style today. Turn HistoryCard's onTapGesture into a Button.
5. PosterCard, ChannelTile, LandscapeCard as leaf views. Keep VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, LiveStreamCard, M3UChannelCard, HistoryCard and HistoryCardGridItem as thin adapters; the context menu stays on M3UChannelCard and the epgSnapshot environment read stays in the adapters. Keep the title as a plain Text child with no accessibility combine, so the staticTexts lookups in the UI tests still resolve.

Tier 2 (optional, maintainability only; defer or do last): ShelfScroller and PagedCardGrid. If done, correct the signature:
- PagedCardGrid renders only the LazyVGrid and the trailing ProgressView. The ScrollView and ScrollViewReader stay in each *CategoryContent, so VOD keeps its .id(gridTopID) scroll-to-top.
- The cell closure receives (index, item), so the M3U per-cell prefetch still works.
- visibleCount stays @State in the owner and is passed as a Binding.
- Do not move M3UGroupGridContent or the favourites grids onto pagination as part of this refactor; that is a separate, measured change.

Keep untouched: the four Equatable shelf rows and two Equatable Recently Added shelves, the three Equatable *CategoryContent structs with their ==, itemsToken, off-main recompute and prefetch calls. No generic CategoryShelfRow<Item>. No iOS 26-only API is involved, so no availability gate or fallback is needed.

**API check:** Checked in the iPhoneSimulator26.0 SDK interface files.
- ButtonStyle: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:10435-10436, @available(iOS 13.0, ...) @MainActor public protocol ButtonStyle. ButtonStyleConfiguration with public let isPressed: Bool at 10442 and 10450.
- GridItem: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:23528-23529, @available(iOS 14.0, ...) public struct GridItem. Initialiser at 23539: public init(_ size: GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment? = nil).
- lineLimit(_:reservesSpace:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:8855-8856, @available(iOS 16.0, ...) nonisolated public func lineLimit(_ limit: Int, reservesSpace: Bool) -> some View.
- ScaledMetric: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:12146-12151, @available(iOS 14.0, ...) @propertyWrapper public struct ScaledMetric<Value>.
- EquatableView and View.equatable(): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:16297-16312, iOS 13.0. The existing contract is unaffected.
- Project type EPGNowNext exists (EPG/EPGModels.swift:124, Equatable, Sendable), and EPGNowNextLine takes nowNext: EPGNowNext? (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:41-45), so the proposed ChannelTile signature compiles.
- Name collisions: no existing symbols named PosterCard, ChannelTile, LandscapeCard, ShelfHeader, PressableCardStyle, PagedCardGrid, FilterChip, CountBadge, BrowseSpacing or BrowseRadius.
All APIs are available at the iOS 18.0 deployment target.

**Regression risks:** - Paginated grids: a generic PagedCardGrid that owns the ScrollView breaks VOD's scroll-to-top on sort or filter change (VODView.swift:688-728). A cell closure without the index breaks M3U prefetchAhead (M3UChannelsView.swift:587).
- Equatable rows: if ==, itemsToken or the .equatable() call sites change (LiveStreamsView.swift:237,494,719; VODView.swift:90,377,560,819; SeriesView.swift:91,354,532,758; M3UChannelsView.swift:179), the re-render storms on large catalogs that earlier work fixed come back.
- UI tests: cards are found by app.staticTexts[<title>] (UserFlowsUITests.swift:43,51,67,89,303,321,581). Accessibility grouping on the shared cards, or wrapping HistoryCard in a Button with a combined label, would break those lookups.
- Image cache keys: ListImagePrefetch and CachedImage must keep identical width, height, contentMode and profile (CachedImage.swift:100-123). If a shared card changes poster size or contentMode, prefetch stops matching render and posters pop in.
- Layout: changing shelf spacing 14 to 12, radius, or shelfRowTotalHeight shifts every shelf. EPGNowNextLine's reserved height (EPGComponents.swift:51-54) must stay in ChannelTile.
- Press style: a custom ButtonStyle on NavigationLink changes highlight behaviour while scrolling; check it does not flash on scroll touch-down.
- Tip-jar WIP is not touched.

**How to verify:** After each Tier 1 step:
1. Build, then run the existing unit suite and the UI suites (UserFlowsUITests, ScreensUITests); the staticTexts card lookups must still pass.
2. Re-run the screenshot tour and diff against the current shots for iphone-light, iphone-dark and ipad-light. Only the intended deltas should appear (Continue Watching header and inset, progress bar position, history card size).
3. On a large real playlist (50k+ movies), scroll All Movies and All Channels to the third page and back, and change sort. Confirm pagination still loads at visibleCount - 15, VOD still scrolls to top on sort change, and returning from a detail view does not stall (Instruments SwiftUI template: no extra *CategoryContent or shelf row body evaluations compared with a baseline trace).
4. Press-and-hold then drag on movie, series, favourites and history cards to compare press feedback across tabs.
5. Confirm posters in shelves and grids still arrive from the prefetch cache with no placeholder flash on a warm cache.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-1 — Episode next / previous / auto-play-next in the series detail flow run on @State of SeriesDetailView, so they stall or go stale once the detail is popped while the player is minimised

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Series detail, Mini player while browsing Series, Lock screen / Control Center next-track
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:806-808, 899-939, 1121-1165`, `Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:10-12, 44-58, 144-186 (reference only)`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:348-374 (precedent for the fix)`, `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:5-9, 70-77`

**What the user perceives:** Start an episode from a series page, pull the player down to the mini card and go back to keep browsing (or re-tap the Series tab, which pops to root). Predicted from code, not yet run: the first Next still works, the second Next does nothing except throw the mini card back to fullscreen; Previous is disabled or jumps to the wrong episode; at the end of the episode the 'next episode' countdown runs and then nothing loads. Binge-watching only works while the series page stays on the stack. (b) Only switching tabs: works, the detail stays mounted. (c) Opening another series from another tab: works for the same reason; opening it in the same stack means popping first, i.e. the broken case.

**Mechanism (finder):** The neighbours live in the detail: episodeNavPrevious / episodeNavNext / selectedEpisode are @State of SeriesDetailView (SeriesView.swift:806-808). The overlay content is built once per present() as a value: canGoToPreviousEpisode / canGoToNextEpisode are snapshot Bools and the closures call selectAdjacentEpisode on the captured view value (929-932). The .task(id: ep.id) that loads the neighbours is attached to the overlay content (935-937), so the overlay owns the task but its body writes into the detail's @State (1131-1143) and re-runs present() from there. After the detail leaves the NavigationStack its state storage is removed; the closures only keep orphaned State boxes alive. No view observes them, and SwiftUI does not document what a write to such a box does (my understanding of the implementation is that a location whose graph host is gone ignores set() while get() keeps returning the last value). Trace with dropped writes: Next reads the frozen episodeNavNext (E2) and presents E2; the task re-keys to E2 and loads (E1, E3) but cannot store them, and neighborsChanged compares frozen with frozen (1136-1137), so nothing is re-presented. The next Next reads E2 again: present() of the same streamId+url is absorbed by the player's identity guard (PlayerView.swift:852-854, 1568-1569, read only) but still sets mode = .fullscreen (PlayerOverlayController.swift:54). Auto-advance calls the same closure. If the boxes do accept writes, stepping keeps working only by accident, on state no view owns. Second part of the question: onDismiss: { selectedEpisode = nil } (916) is the only onDismiss passed to present() in the whole app (grep), it writes to the same removed view, and selectedEpisode is never rendered: it exists only so loadEpisodeNeighbors can re-present. It is not needed for correctness once the state moves into the overlay. HistorySeriesPlayerShell already keeps session and neighbours as its own @State inside the overlay (HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:10-12, 44-46) and steps in place without present() (144-186).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Yes, moving the detail flow onto HistorySeriesPlayerShell is the smallest fix, and it needs no change to the shell, PlayerView or PlayerCore: DownloadsView already feeds the shell a synthesised DBWatchHistory for an episode (DownloadsView.swift:348-374). In SeriesDetailView.presentEpisodeOverlay(ep:history:localOverrideURL:) build the seed and present the shell:

let sid = ep.episodeId ?? ep.id
var seed = history ?? DBWatchHistory(id: "\(playlist.id)_series_\(sid)", playlistId: playlist.id, streamId: sid, type: "series", lastTimeMs: 0, durationMs: 0, lastWatchedAt: Date(), seriesId: nil, title: episodeTitle(ep), secondaryTitle: currentSeries.name, imageURL: ep.cover ?? currentSeries.cover, containerExtension: ep.containerExtension)
seed.seriesId = String(currentSeries.seriesId)
seed.containerExtension = ep.containerExtension
playerOverlay.present(skipDownloadCheck: localOverrideURL != nil, playlistId: playlist.id) {
    HistorySeriesPlayerShell(playlist: playlist, history: seed, url: url, onNavigateToDetail: { _, _ in })
}

Episode rows keep passing resumableHistory(history) (nil when finished, so lastTimeMs 0); the Resume button keeps the raw history as today (1167-1170). Then delete selectedEpisode, episodeNavPrevious, episodeNavNext, loadEpisodeNeighbors, selectAdjacentEpisode and the onDismiss argument. By-products: stepping no longer re-runs present() (the sibling finding about mode resetting to fullscreen disappears for this flow), the overlay no longer retains the whole detail view with its four @Query observations, the episode title format becomes the shell's 'N. title' on every entry path, and detail -> Continue Watching hand-overs keep the same root type. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Verifier reasons:** Code facts are as described: selectedEpisode / episodeNavPrevious / episodeNavNext are @State of SeriesDetailView (Views/SeriesView.swift:806-808); the overlay content is a value built per present() with snapshot Bools and closures that call selectAdjacentEpisode on the captured view (929-932); the .task(id: ep.id) on the overlay content writes into the detail's @State and re-presents (935-937, 1131-1143); onDismiss at 916 is the only onDismiss passed to present() in the app (grep) and selectedEpisode is never rendered (grep: 806, 916, 1061, 1077, 1094, 1139, 1161). HistorySeriesPlayerShell owns its session and steps in place (Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:10-12, 144-186).

The predicted user-visible break, however, rests on one assumption: that a State box whose graph host is gone ignores set(). I checked that assumption in the framework binaries of both installed simulator runtimes (iOS 26.0 23A343 and iOS 18.1 22B81, SwiftUICore, arm64). StoredLocationBase.set(_:transaction:) calls isUpdating, then isValid (StoredLocation.isValid = weak host loaded and its graph non-nil). When isValid is false it runs 'closure #1 (inout Data) -> ()', which does assignWithCopy of the new value into Data.currentValue and then savedValue.removeAll(); only the graph commit is skipped. StoredLocationBase.get() copies Data.currentValue. So on both runtimes a write to an orphaned box is stored and the next read returns it. With accepted writes the trace is: Next reads episodeNavNext (E2), presents E2; the task re-keys, loadEpisodeNeighbors stores (E1, E3), neighborsChanged is true, selectedEpisode matches, re-present with fresh Bools; the next Next goes to E3. Stepping and auto-advance therefore keep working after the detail is popped. The captured view copy is the body-time copy (closures originate in EpisodesPanel's callback inside body and in Tasks started from it), so its State locations, the EnvironmentObject store and the GRDBQuery tracker (Query.swift:27-28, tracker.value ?? defaultValue) stay readable.

What remains real: (1) the playback session lives in boxes no view owns and depends on undocumented behaviour; (2) every step in this flow, auto-advance included (PlayerView.swift:1528-1534 calls onNextEpisode with no mode check), re-runs PlayerOverlayController.present(), which sends resignFirstResponder (PlayerOverlayController.swift:39-41) and sets mode = .fullscreen (54), and loadEpisodeNeighbors re-presents once more after each step (SeriesView.swift:1138-1143). So with the mini card docked, an auto-advance or a Control Center next-track throws the player back to fullscreen and drops the keyboard if the user is typing in Search. Playback started from Continue Watching does not do this because the shell never calls present() when stepping. That inconsistency is the user-visible reason to do the refactor, and it does not depend on popping the detail.

**Corrected claim:** Episode next / previous / auto-advance started from the series page keep working after the page is popped: on iOS 18.1 and 26.0 an orphaned @State box still stores writes (verified in SwiftUICore's StoredLocationBase.set/get). The defect is structural plus one visible side effect: the stepping state is owned by a view that may be gone and relies on undocumented behaviour, and each step or auto-advance re-runs present(), which expands a minimised player to fullscreen and resigns the keyboard, unlike playback started from Continue Watching or Downloads.

**Corrected fix:** The proposed fix stands as the smallest change: present HistorySeriesPlayerShell from SeriesDetailView.presentEpisodeOverlay(ep:history:localOverrideURL:) with a seed DBWatchHistory, exactly as DownloadsView.swift:348-374 does, and delete selectedEpisode, episodeNavPrevious, episodeNavNext, loadEpisodeNeighbors, selectAdjacentEpisode and the onDismiss argument. Corrections to the sketch: (a) episodeTitle(ep) does not exist in SeriesDetailView (the helper is private to EpisodeDetailRow, SeriesView.swift:1478-1483); add a small helper or build the 'N. title' string inline. (b) For a finished episode picked from the list, keep today's start-over behaviour by passing the synthesised seed (lastTimeMs 0), or copy DownloadsView's line 'if history.resumePositionMs(as: .episode) == nil { history.lastTimeMs = 0 }'; the Resume button keeps the raw history. (c) Always set seed.seriesId = String(currentSeries.seriesId) and seed.containerExtension = ep.containerExtension, and prefer ep.cover ?? currentSeries.cover for imageURL. No change to the shell, PlayerView or PlayerCore. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** No new API. DBWatchHistory memberwise init with the labels used (id, playlistId, streamId, type, lastTimeMs, durationMs, lastWatchedAt, seriesId, title, secondaryTitle, imageURL, containerExtension) matches Models/DBModels.swift:230-247 and the call at Views/DownloadsView.swift:348-361. HistorySeriesPlayerShell.init(playlist:history:url:onNavigateToDetail:) at Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:17. Framework check (binary, not interface): SwiftUI.StoredLocationBase.set(_:transaction:) and .get() in SwiftUICore for iOS 26.0 and iOS 18.1 simulator runtimes; invalid-host path still assigns Data.currentValue.

**Regression risks:** The overlay root type for this flow changes from PlayerView+task to HistorySeriesPlayerShell: a hand-over from another root type rebuilds the PlayerView (same as today between detail and Continue Watching), while detail <-> Continue Watching hand-overs now keep identity, which is what the AirPlay continuity comment in PlayerOverlayController.swift:51-53 wants. Player title becomes the shell's 'N. title' and, when a history row exists, the title stored in that row. Tapping another episode in the still-mounted detail relies on the shell's onChange(of: overlayPresentationID) reset (HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:47-58); it handles this already for Downloads. The shell's refreshNeighbors may call get_series_info when seasonsLoaded is false in the database; harmless here because the detail has just loaded it. Must not touch the shell itself (out of scope, reworked last week).

**How to verify:** Simulator, with one demo series seeded with one season and at least 3 episodes in Database/MockFixture.swift. Before any change: play episode 1 from the series page, minimise, pop to the Series home, expand, tap Next twice: the title should reach episode 3 (my prediction from the binary; if it stays on episode 2 the original claim is right and severity returns to high). Then, still before the change: minimise, let auto-advance fire or press next-track in Control Center: predicted the mini card jumps to fullscreen; repeat with the Search field focused: the keyboard drops. After the change: both steps keep the mini card docked, and a UI test in ScreensUITests asserts the title reaches episode 3 after pop.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-2 — The series page's primary Watch button does nothing when the first declared season has no episodes, and Resume does nothing when the episode row is missing

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:967-976, 1070-1099, 1106-1119`, `Models/XtreamModels.swift:298-313`, `Models/Requests.swift:216-223`, `Models/SeriesPlaybackOrdering.swift:13-27`

**What the user perceives:** On many real series the big Watch button is a dead tap: it highlights and nothing happens, no message. The page also opens on an empty season tab. Resume can fail the same silent way.

**Mechanism (finder):** playFirstEpisode takes seasons.first and fetches its first episode; both failure branches return without feedback (SeriesView.swift:1086 guard, 1087-1098 'if let first' with no else). seasons is ordered by seasonNumber (Requests.swift:221) and every season the panel declares is persisted even when it has no episode bucket (XtreamModels.swift:298-313; SeriesView.swift:1186-1202). Panels routinely declare TMDB seasons they do not carry: 'Specials' (season 0), or seasons 1-8 with only 3-5 uploaded. Then seasons.first has zero episodes and the CTA is dead although later seasons are playable. With no seasons at all the button is still shown and still dead (1008-1013 shows only a text). resumeLatestEpisode swallows a missing row the same way (1073-1080), and its lookup is not scoped to the playlist: Column("episodeId") == history.streamId || Column("id") == history.streamId (1074, also 1113). With two playlists whose numeric episode ids collide, fetchOne can return the other playlist's row, so the player gets that row's title, cover and containerExtension, and resolveInitialSeasonId falls back to the first season because the foreign seasonId does not match.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) First episode by play order, not by first season: let first = try SeriesPlaybackOrdering.orderedEpisodes(seriesId: currentSeries.seriesId, playlistId: playlist.id, db: db).first (it already walks seasons in order and skips empty ones). 2) Scope the Resume lookup to the playlist: DBEpisode.filter(Column("id") == DBEpisode.scopedId(playlistId: playlist.id, panelEpisodeId: history.streamId)); when the row is gone fall back to playFirstEpisode() instead of returning. 3) No episodes at all: disable the primary action (DetailActionBar(...).disabled(seasons.isEmpty && currentSeries.seasonsLoaded)); the existing 'series.no_seasons_info' text already explains why, so no new strings. 4) Same scoped lookup in resolveInitialSeasonId (1111-1114). SeriesView.swift only.

**APIs:** View.disabled(_:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** playFirstEpisode (Views/SeriesView.swift:1084-1099) returns silently when seasons is empty (1086) and has no else when the first season has no episode row (1087-1097). seasons is ordered by seasonNumber (Models/Requests.swift:216-223). Declared seasons are persisted even with no episode bucket (Models/XtreamModels.swift:298-313; SeriesView.swift:1186-1202, eps may be []). The code base's own regression test documents the shape: another-iptv-playerTests/XtreamSeriesInfoTests.swift:64-77 ('the panel declares season 1, but keys its episodes under 2') resolves to seasons [1, 2] with season 1 empty; with that payload seasons.first is season 1, the Watch button is a dead tap, and resolveInitialSeasonId (1106-1119) opens the page on the empty tab. With no seasons and seasonsLoaded true the button is shown above the 'series.no_seasons_info' text (1008-1013) and does nothing. resumeLatestEpisode swallows a missing row the same way (1073-1080). The lookups at 1074 and 1113 match on episodeId (the raw panel id) without playlist scope; DBEpisode has no playlistId column and only its id is scoped (Models/DBModels.swift:128-132), so a second playlist's row with the same panel id can be returned. That part is narrow (two playlists with colliding ids both loaded; same-panel duplicates return identical content) and I rate it low on its own. No comment or history marks any of this as deliberate (git log -S on the guard line shows only the initial import commits).

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands. Precision: the empty-first-season case is real and is the exact payload shape of the PR #107 test fixture; the cross-playlist lookup collision is a low-severity side issue; 'many real series' is plausible (season 0 'Specials', TMDB seasons not uploaded) but unquantified.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with four corrections. 1) First episode: SeriesPlaybackOrdering.orderedEpisodes(seriesId: currentSeries.seriesId, playlistId: playlist.id, db: db).first inside the existing AppDatabase.shared.read. 2) Scoped lookup: all rows have scoped ids since migration 'scopeSeasonEpisodeIdsByPlaylist' (Database/AppDatabase.swift:323-331), so filter on Column("id") == DBEpisode.scopedId(playlistId: playlist.id, panelEpisodeId: history.streamId) || Column("id") == history.streamId; the second term keeps episodes whose panel id was nil (their history streamId is the scoped id itself, since streamId = ep.episodeId ?? ep.id). Same in resolveInitialSeasonId. 3) Do not put .disabled on the whole DetailActionBar: it also disables the trailer Link in secondaryRow (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:254-264). Add a 'var primaryDisabled: Bool = false' to DetailActionBar and apply .disabled(primaryDisabled).opacity(primaryDisabled ? 0.5 : 1) to primaryCTA only (the label has explicit white foreground on a gradient, so .plain alone will not look disabled); MovieDetailView keeps the default. Disable when currentSeries.seasonsLoaded and no episode exists (seasons empty, or all seasons empty: derive from a small one-off read, not only seasons.isEmpty). 4) Also fix the empty opening tab, which the proposal names but does not fix: in resolveInitialSeasonId fall back to the seasonId of the first ordered episode before seasons.first. Resume with a missing row: falling back to playFirstEpisode is a product choice; the alternative that matches Continue Watching is to play straight from the history row through HistorySeriesPlayerShell, which needs no episode row.

**API check:** View.disabled(_:) found in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface line 190, in an extension available from iOS 13.0; already used throughout the app. SeriesPlaybackOrdering.orderedEpisodes(seriesId:playlistId:db:) exists at Models/SeriesPlaybackOrdering.swift:13-27. DBEpisode.scopedId(playlistId:panelEpisodeId:) exists at Models/DBModels.swift:130.

**Regression risks:** orderedEpisodes loads every episode row of the series to take the first; fine off the main thread for one tap, but do not call it from body. Adding a parameter to DetailActionBar touches a component shared with MovieDetailView; a defaulted parameter keeps that call site unchanged. Changing the initial season choice alters which tab opens for series whose first season is empty; that is the intended effect.

**How to verify:** Unit test on an in-memory AppDatabase with the PR #107 shape (season 1 declared, episodes only under season 2): assert the first-episode helper returns the season 2 episode and the initial season resolves to season 2; add a second playlist with an episode of the same panel id and assert the scoped lookup returns the row of the right playlist. Simulator: seed that shape in MockFixture, open the series, tap Watch: playback starts; a series with seasonsLoaded and no episodes shows a dimmed Watch button while the trailer button still works.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-3 — Episode rows start playback only from the text column: the thumbnail and the row margins are dead, and there is no pressed state

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail (episode list)
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1476 (gesture at 1447-1451, thumbnail at 1391-1414)`

**What the user perceives:** Tapping an episode's picture, the most obvious target and the one drawn with a play glyph placeholder, does nothing. Tapping the title works but the row never highlights, so with the short wait before the player appears it is unclear whether the tap registered. VoiceOver does not announce the row as a button.

**Mechanism (finder):** EpisodeDetailRow is an HStack of thumbnail, text column and DownloadButton. .contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture is attached to the text VStack only (1447-1451); the thumbnail ZStack (1391-1414) and the row padding (1474-1475) have no gesture. onTapGesture gives no highlight and no button trait.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Make thumbnail + text one Button and leave the download control outside it:

HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) {
    Button { onStreamSelected(episode, watchHistory) } label: {
        HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 12) { thumbnail; textColumn }
            .contentShape(Rectangle())
    }
    .buttonStyle(.plain)
    if let remoteURL { DownloadButton(...) }
}

.plain dims the label while pressed and adds the button trait. One file, no iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** PlainButtonStyle (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** EpisodeDetailRow.body (Views/SeriesView.swift:1389-1476) is an HStack of thumbnail ZStack (1391-1414), text VStack and DownloadButton; .contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture sits on the text VStack only (1447-1451). The thumbnail and the row padding (1474-1475) have no gesture, and onTapGesture gives neither a pressed state nor a button trait. History shows this is a regression, not a decision: before commit d2489f9 the whole row was Button { onStreamSelected(...) } label: { HStack { thumbnail; text }.padding.contentShape(Rectangle()) }.buttonStyle(.plain) (git show d2489f99^:native/ios/another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift, lines 1021-1089). The tap moved to the text column when the DownloadButton was added to the row, presumably to avoid a button inside a button; no comment explains it. The demo fixture has no episodes (S04 screenshot shows the 404 error page), so the screenshots cannot show the row.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands; additionally it is a regression from the earlier full-row Button, introduced when the download control was added.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: one Button wrapping thumbnail + text with .buttonStyle(.plain), DownloadButton as a sibling outside it. One refinement so the margins are live too: move the row padding into the button label (leading 16, vertical 12) and give the DownloadButton its own trailing/vertical padding, keeping .contentShape(Rectangle()) on the label; the Divider inset from posterMetrics.episodeRowDividerLeading stays as is. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** PlainButtonStyle: 'public struct PlainButtonStyle' in SwiftUI.swiftinterface around line 8850 (iOS 13.0); View.buttonStyle(_:) at 8488/10460. Both already used in this file's history and in DetailComponents.swift:251.

**Regression risks:** The DownloadButton must stay outside the Button or its taps are swallowed. A Button label merges its children into one accessibility element; check that the VoiceOver label is still the episode title first. Lazy rows keep their @Query per row; nothing in the earlier performance work is touched. Inside a ScrollView the highlight appears after the system touch delay, which is the native behaviour.

**How to verify:** Simulator with a seeded series: tap the centre of an episode thumbnail and the left margin of the row: the player appears; press and hold: the row dims; tap the download control: download starts and the player does not. UI test asserting the player appears after tapping the thumbnail.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-4 — A series opened earlier in the session is refetched on every re-open, and its cached page is replaced by an error when that refetch fails; the write-back also updates the row from the stale navigation value

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:823-825, 866-896, 1176-1247 (write-back 1222-1237)`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-179`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:275-305`, `Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:66-72, 135-140`

**What the user perceives:** Re-opening a series you already visited flashes a full-screen spinner over the page and hits the network again. Offline in the same session the page turns into 'Error ... Try Again' although seasons and episodes, including downloaded ones, are in the database.

**Mechanism (finder):** Answer to the second question: no, the in-memory catalog never learns seasonsLoaded. Only films have a write-back (applyVODMetadata, PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-179, whose comment describes exactly this symptom: needless request and spinner flash on every re-entry); grep finds no series equivalent. The cards pass the catalog's DBSeries, so series.seasonsLoaded stays false until the next full load. currentSeries is seriesRecord ?? series (823-825) and the @Query value arrives asynchronously (Requests.swift:197-206, default scheduling), so .task usually sees the stale prop and calls fetchSeriesInfo (892-896). That sets isLoading, which shows the spinner until the query delivers (868-870); on failure errorMessage wins over the content branch (871-875). Answer to the first question: the write-back builds updatedSeries from the navigation prop and update()s every column (1222-1237). Favourites are a separate table and are not affected. What can be overwritten: name, cover, categoryId, sortIndex and list metadata revert to the values from when the list was loaded if a catalog refresh ran in between; when the panel returns no info block, cast / director / backdrop / trailer from an earlier fetch are wiped by the prop's nils; and if a refresh removed the row, update() throws and rolls back the season and episode writes of the same transaction. MovieDetailView already does it the safe way (275-305).

**Proposed fix (finder):** SeriesView.swift only, three small changes. 1) Decide from the database, as HistorySeriesPlayerShell does (66-72):
.task {
    let loaded = (try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in
        try DBSeries.filter(Column("seriesId") == series.seriesId && Column("playlistId") == playlist.id).fetchOne(db)?.seasonsLoaded
    }) ?? false
    if !loaded { await fetchSeriesInfo() }
}
This avoids mutating the @Published catalog arrays (no invalidation storm on a 40k-series catalog). 2) Write back onto the current row inside the transaction (same shape as HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:135-140): guard var row = try DBSeries.filter(...).fetchOne(db) else { return }; row.seasonsLoaded = true; apply info fields; try row.update(db). 3) Let cached content win over a failed refresh: show errorView only when !currentSeries.seasonsLoaded. Optional, if the first frame should already be complete: add applySeriesMetadata to PlaylistContentStore mirroring applyVODMetadata.

**Verifier reasons:** The in-memory catalog never learns seasonsLoaded: PlaylistContentStore has applyVODMetadata only (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:161-179), and its comment describes this exact symptom for films ('needless network request and spinner flash on every re-entry'); grep for seasonsLoaded finds no series write-back outside SeriesView and HistorySeriesPlayerShell. SeriesDetailView.task (Views/SeriesView.swift:892-896) reads currentSeries = seriesRecord ?? series (823-825); the @Query value is tracker.value ?? defaultValue (GRDBQuery Query.swift:27-28) and SeriesByIDRequest uses the default ValueObservation publisher (Models/Requests.swift:190-206), which delivers the first value asynchronously, so the task normally sees the stale prop and calls fetchSeriesInfo. That sets isLoading, and body shows the full-screen ProgressView until the query delivers (868-870): content, spinner, content inside the push transition. On failure errorMessage wins over contentScroll (871-875), so a visited series turns into the error page offline although its rows are in the database; the screenshot S04-series-detail-settled.png shows how that page replaces everything. The refetch also rewrites every season and episode row (1186-1218), which re-fires the observations behind the episode list. The write-back builds from the navigation prop and update()s all columns (1222-1237); MovieDetailView reads the @Query-backed row on the main actor first (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:275-279) and HistorySeriesPlayerShell re-fetches the row inside the transaction (135-140). The overwrite consequences are minor in practice because a catalog refresh deletes and reinserts the series rows (PlaylistContentStore.swift:555), but the pattern is still wrong and trivially fixed.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands. Scope note: it affects series first opened in the current session (after a relaunch the catalog is loaded from the database with seasonsLoaded true). The stale write-back is a low-severity side issue; the refetch, spinner flash and error-over-cached-content are the user-visible parts.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, SeriesView.swift only: 1) in .task read seasonsLoaded from the database (DBSeries.filter(seriesId, playlistId).fetchOne(db)?.seasonsLoaded) and fetch only when false; 2) inside the write transaction re-fetch the row, set seasonsLoaded and the info fields on it, then update; 3) show errorView only when !currentSeries.seasonsLoaded. Either the database check or a PlaylistContentStore.applySeriesMetadata mirroring applyVODMetadata is acceptable; the database check avoids republishing the series arrays and is the smaller change. If the first frame should already show backdrop, cast and runtime instead of popping in when the query delivers, add applySeriesMetadata as well.

**API check:** No SwiftUI API involved. GRDB calls used (filter, fetchOne, update) are already used at SeriesView.swift:1074, 1237 and HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:68-70, 135-139.

**Regression risks:** After a catalog refresh the series rows are recreated with seasonsLoaded false and seasons cascade-deleted, so the database check correctly triggers a refetch. With fix 3 a failed fetch on a loaded series is silent; acceptable because fix 1 removes that fetch. If applySeriesMetadata is added, it mutates @Published arrays of a catalog that can hold 40k series: keep it to a single element replace as applyVODMetadata does, and do not touch the Equatable shelf rows.

**How to verify:** Simulator with a real playlist: open a series, go back, re-open: no spinner frame, and the network log shows one get_series_info per series per session. Enable airplane mode and re-open: seasons and episodes are shown, no error page. Unit test: extract the write-back into a static function (info, seriesId, playlistId, db); change the row's name and categoryId after 'loading the list', run it, assert both survive and seasonsLoaded is true.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-5 — M3U Continue Watching and history cards whose channel left the playlist are dead taps, and nothing ever removes them

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels (Continue Watching), M3U watch history list
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:285-304`, `Models/M3UImporter.swift:31-33, 69-84`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:140-154, 324-330 (pattern to copy)`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Alert with 'Remove from History' only, or also prune orphaned history automatically on every re-import?

**What the user perceives:** A card sits in Continue Watching with artwork and progress; tapping it does nothing, every time, with no explanation. With providers that rotate stream URLs this is every card after each playlist refresh.

**Mechanism (finder):** presentHistoryItem returns silently when the channel id is not in the store (M3UChannelsView.swift:287-291). The doc comment one line above promises an alert, and the inline comment says the row 'will be updated on the next refresh', but no code prunes history: the only deletes of watchHistory are the explicit clear actions (WatchHistoryListView.swift:129-149, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:411). A re-import deletes and rewrites m3uChannel (M3UImporter.swift:33); the id is SHA256(playlistId:url) (69-84), so a removed channel or a changed or tokenised URL orphans its history row for good.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Follow the app's own rule from DownloadsView.swift:326-328 (do not swallow; alert plus a way out). In M3UChannelsView add @State private var unavailableHistoryItem: DBWatchHistory?, set it in the guard's else branch, and attach
.alert(L("history.unavailable.title"), isPresented: <binding>, presenting: unavailableHistoryItem) { item in
    Button(L("history.remove"), role: .destructive) { Task { try? await AppDatabase.shared.write { db in _ = try item.delete(db) } } }
    Button(L("common.cancel"), role: .cancel) {}
} message: { _ in Text(L("history.unavailable.message")) }
The card disappears through the existing @Query. Three new keys in the ten Localizable.strings files, appended only; the tip keys stay untouched. Optional: prune orphaned rows inside M3UImporter.replace's transaction, excluding ids that still have a completed download.

**APIs:** View.alert(_:isPresented:presenting:actions:message:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The defect is real. presentHistoryItem returns silently when the channel id is not in the store (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:286-291); its doc comment promises an alert (285) and the inline comment says the row will be updated on the next refresh, but nothing prunes history: the only deletes of watchHistory are the clear actions (Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:411, Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:438, Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:136-141), and there is no per-item removal anywhere. A re-import deletes and rewrites m3uChannel (Models/M3UImporter.swift:33) and the id is SHA256(playlistId:url) (69-84), so a removed channel or a changed URL orphans its history row permanently. Both entry points share the handler: the Continue Watching card and the pushed WatchHistoryListView (M3UChannelsView.swift:157-166). The second guard at 292 (unsanitisable URL) is a second silent return the finding does not mention.

The fix needs one correction. The proposed .alert is attached to M3UChannelsView, but one of the two callers is WatchHistoryListView pushed on top of it by a NavigationLink (Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:30-31). An alert whose state flips on a view covered by a pushed destination is not guaranteed to present from there; I could not settle this without a simulator run, so the fix must not depend on it.

**Corrected claim:** The claim stands for both surfaces. Frequency depends on the provider: every card after each refresh when stream URLs carry rotating tokens, otherwise only for channels that were removed or re-addressed.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the approach (state + alert, modelled on DownloadsView.swift:140-154 and 324-330), with these corrections. 1) Make the alert reachable from both callers: put state and alert in a small ViewModifier and apply it to M3UChannelsView's content and to the WatchHistoryListView built in the destination closure, or hoist both to the view that owns the NavigationStack; then confirm on the simulator that exactly one alert shows from each path. 2) Set the same state in the second guard (unsanitisable URL, line 292). 3) Fewer new strings: reuse the existing 'common.delete' and 'common.cancel' and add only a title and a message key, appended to the ten Localizable.strings files without touching the tip keys. 4) Fix the misleading comment at 288-289. The optional prune inside M3UImporter.replace is a product decision for the owner (it silently discards resume positions when a provider merely re-addresses a channel); do not bundle it.

**API check:** View.alert(_:isPresented:presenting:actions:message:) with a StringProtocol title: declared in SwiftUI.swiftinterface line 10711 inside the extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, ...); the same overload is already used at Views/DownloadsView.swift:140-154. DBWatchHistory is a PersistableRecord (Models/DBModels.swift:230), so item.delete(db) exists.

**Regression risks:** Touches the owner's uncommitted Localizable.strings files in ten languages: append only, leave the tip.* keys and their order alone. Two alert modifiers bound to the same state must not both present; verify. Removing a history row also removes its resume position, which is why the action must be an explicit user choice.

**How to verify:** Simulator: import a local M3U, play a channel for a few seconds, re-import the file with that entry's URL changed. Tap the Continue Watching card: the alert appears, Delete removes the card through the existing @Query. Open the full history list from the row header and tap the same kind of item there: the alert must appear on top of the list as well (this is the case to check, since the handler lives in the covered view). Cancel leaves the row.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-6 — Playback started from the TV guide or a programme sheet gets the whole live catalog as its queue, including categories the user hid

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide, Programme detail sheet, Channel up/down and channel panel after starting from the guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:398-410`, `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:123-131`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-264`, `Views/PlayerView.swift:20-39 (read only)`, `Views/SearchView.swift:256-262`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:284-286`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Does 'Hide' mean hidden everywhere (guide and player queue included, as Search and the M3U player already treat it) or only on the shelves?

**What the user perceives:** Hide a category on Live TV (for example adult or a foreign-language pack), open the guide, start any channel: channel up/down walks into the hidden category and the in-player channel list shows it. The guide itself lists it too (shots/iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows every category as a header).

**Mechanism (finder):** xtreamLiveQueue() iterates PlaylistContentStore.liveCategories without consulting HiddenCategoryStore (PlayerView.swift:28-37) and is the queue for both guide entry points (EPGGuideView.swift:405-409, EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:126-130). The guide rows come from contentStore.liveStreams unfiltered (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:253); grep finds no reference to hidden categories under Views/EPG or EPG. Every other entry point respects the setting: Live home filters before building its queue (LiveStreamsView.swift:284-286), Search filters results and therefore the queue (SearchView.swift:256-262), the M3U player panel filters hidden groups (M3UChannelsView.swift:796-805). The other queues are consistent with their screens: Search = all hidden-filtered live results sorted by name, grouped by category for the panel (280-305), so channel up/down steps through the result list, including results beyond the four shown under 'All'; Favorites = the favourites as displayed, search filter included (FavoritesView.swift:83-98, M3UFavoritesView.swift:86-92); Continue Watching (live) = the home queue, with up/down disabled when the channel is not in it (LiveStreamsView.swift:172-188, 919-923); VOD history = the film's category in catalog order (VODView.swift:245-255). The adult filter is applied at import (XtreamImporter.swift:44-48), so every queue inherits it.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Stay out of PlayerView.swift: filter at the two call sites through one helper in the EPG folder.
@MainActor func visibleXtreamLiveQueue(playlistId: UUID) -> (queue: [DBLiveStream], sections: [LiveChannelCategorySection]) {
    let all = LiveChannelCategorySection.xtreamLiveQueue()
    let hidden = HiddenCategoryStore.shared.hiddenIds(playlistId: playlistId, type: "live")
    guard !hidden.isEmpty else { return all }
    let sections = all.sections.filter { !hidden.contains($0.id) }
    return (sections.flatMap(\.streams), sections)
}
Filter the guide rows the same way in EPGGuideViewModel.buildRows (drop entries whose stream.categoryId is hidden) and rebuild when HiddenCategoryStore.version changes; otherwise a channel from a hidden category could still be started from the guide and would have no position in its own queue.

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real. Views/PlayerView.swift:20-39 builds the queue from every entry of PlaylistContentStore.liveCategories with no hidden filter, and its only two callers are Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:405 and Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:126. Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:253 builds the guide rows from the unfiltered PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreams, and a grep for HiddenCategoryStore / hiddenIds finds no hit under Views/EPG or EPG. Every other live surface filters: Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:284-285 (home shelves, and through livePlaybackModel at 27-38 the queue), 740-744 (All channels), Views/SearchView.swift:256-262, and the M3U player panel at Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:796-805. No comment or commit marks the guide's behaviour as deliberate: the guide came in 1cce013 and collapsible categories in 654cefc, neither mentions hidden categories. The guide's own collapse state (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:87-89) is a separate feature. The screenshot shots/iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows the category headers but the demo data has nothing hidden, so it proves nothing on this point. The fix needs three corrections. (1) The M3U guide has the same gap: EPGGuideViewModel.swift:265 ignores the hidden groups stored under type "m3u". (2) Filtering rows on stream.categoryId misses the synthetic uncategorized category: orphans are regrouped under "__uncategorized__" (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:361, 415) while their own categoryId is nil, "0" or an unknown id. (3) Rebuilding on HiddenCategoryStore.version is unnecessary: the guide is a pushed screen with the tab bar hidden (EPGGuideView.swift:51), the view model is created per push and buildRows runs in load(), and the category picker is only reachable from the Live home. ChannelEPGSheet (Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:159) has no callers, so the programme sheet is reached only through the guide; once the rows are filtered, a hidden channel cannot be the initial stream.

**Corrected claim:** The TV guide (Xtream and M3U) ignores hidden categories: it lists their channels, and on Xtream playback started from a guide channel cell or a programme sheet gets the whole live catalog as its queue and channel panel, hidden categories included. Every other live surface (home shelves, All channels, Search, the M3U player panel) applies the hidden set. Nothing in comments or history marks this as intended.

**Corrected fix:** Leave PlayerView.swift untouched and filter in the EPG folder. (1) In EPGGuideViewModel.buildRows read the hidden set once. For Xtream use HiddenCategoryStore.shared.hiddenIds(playlistId:type:"live"), build a Set of the stream ids in PlaylistContentStore.shared.liveStreamsByCategoryId[hiddenId] for each hidden id, and drop those entries; this also covers the synthetic "__uncategorized__" category. For M3U use type M3UChannelsView.hiddenCategoryType and drop channels whose canonical group key (trimmed groupTitle, or M3UContentStore.ungroupedLabel when empty) is hidden. No version observation is needed. (2) Add one @MainActor helper in the EPG folder that calls LiveChannelCategorySection.xtreamLiveQueue(), removes the sections whose id is hidden, and returns (sections.flatMap(\.streams), sections). Give it an including: DBLiveStream parameter so the section of the stream being started is never removed. Use it at EPGGuideView.swift:405 and EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:126. Whether Hide applies to the guide at all is the owner's decision; the rest of the app already treats it as hidden everywhere.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. Project API checked: HiddenCategoryStore.hiddenIds(playlistId:type:) is @MainActor (Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:6, 18); EPGGuideViewModel.buildRows and both call sites already run on the main actor. LiveChannelCategorySection.id is the category id (Views/PlayerView.swift:36), the same id the picker persists (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:48-52).

**Regression risks:** A user who hid most categories and relied on the guide to still reach them loses that path. If every category is hidden the guide shows the existing 'no EPG data' empty state (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:222-229), which would be misleading. The extra filter on tap is O(sections) on top of the existing O(N) walk, so no perceptible cost. PlayerView.swift and the Live home's memoised queue stay untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit-test the helper with one hidden category and with the including: stream inside a hidden category. Simulator: hide 'Sports' in the Live category picker, open the guide (the Sports header and its 4 rows must be gone), start a News channel, open the channel panel and step down past the end of News: Sports must not appear. Repeat on an M3U playlist with a hidden group.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-7 — M3U playback always streams the remote URL even when the item has a completed download

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels, M3U group grid, M3U Favorites, M3U Continue Watching
- Code: `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:264-274, 286-304, 458-473, 529-539, 667`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:83-93`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:190-199, 229-251 (Xtream behaviour)`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:322-394`

**What the user perceives:** A film downloaded from an M3U playlist plays from the file only when started from Settings > Downloads. Tapping the same card in the channel grid, Favorites or Continue Watching streams it again: mobile data and a server connection are used, and offline it fails although the file is on the device. On Xtream the same tap plays the local file.

**Mechanism (finder):** M3U supports downloads for VOD-classified items (context menu, M3UChannelsView.swift:458-473, id from DownloadManager.idFor(m3uChannel:)). None of the four M3U play paths asks DownloadManager.localURL; M3UPlayerShell derives its URL from channel.url only (667). The Xtream paths resolve the local file first (MovieDetailView.swift:192-194, SeriesView.swift:901-903, VODView.swift:220-222).

**Proposed fix (finder):** One private helper used by the four call sites, without touching M3UPlayerShell: live items keep today's synchronous path; for VOD-classified items resolve the download first and play the file the way DownloadsView does.
func play(_ channel: DBM3UChannel, queue: [DBM3UChannel], resumeTimeMs: Int?) {
    guard let remote = M3UParser.sanitizedURL(from: channel.url) else { return }
    let cls = M3UStreamClassifier.classify(url: remote, groupTitle: channel.groupTitle)
    guard !cls.isLive else { presentShell(channel, queue, resumeTimeMs); return }
    Task {
        let local = await DownloadManager.shared.localURL(forId: DownloadManager.idFor(m3uChannel: playlist.id, channelId: channel.id))
        if let local {
            playerOverlay.present(skipDownloadCheck: true) { PlayerView(url: local, title: channel.name, subtitle: channel.groupTitle, artworkURL: channel.tvgLogo.flatMap { URL(string: $0) }, isLiveStream: false, playlistId: playlist.id, streamId: channel.id, type: "vod", resumeTimeMs: resumeTimeMs, containerExtension: cls.containerExtension) }
        } else { presentShell(channel, queue, resumeTimeMs) }
    }
}
streamId and type match what the shell writes, so the history row and resume position are shared. Same trade-off Xtream already accepts: a downloaded item plays without the prev/next queue (MovieDetailView.swift:229-230). When the grid has no history item at hand, read the resume position as DownloadsView.swift:334-342 does.

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is confirmed. M3U VOD-classified items are downloadable from the card context menu (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:458-473, id from DownloadManager.idFor(m3uChannel:), Models/DownloadManager.swift:369). The four M3U play paths (M3UChannelsView.swift:264-274, 286-304, 529-539; Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:83-93) hand the channel straight to M3UPlayerShell, whose URL comes only from channel.url (M3UChannelsView.swift:667). None calls DownloadManager.localURL(forId:) (Models/DownloadManager.swift:289). The Xtream paths do resolve the file first (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:190-199; SeriesView and VODView pass skipDownloadCheck: localOverrideURL != nil at SeriesView.swift:195-199, 916 and VODView.swift:274). The local file is only played from DownloadsView (Views/DownloadsView.swift:322-394), reachable for M3U at Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:85. History keys line up: the download stores streamId = channel.id, DownloadsView plays it as type "vod" (DownloadsView.swift:386-387), and the shell uses streamId = channel.id with playbackType "vod" for non-live items (M3UChannelsView.swift:689-690, 955-960). The fix needs corrections. The three call sites live in three structs across two files, so one private helper cannot serve them. Bypassing M3UPlayerShell with a bare PlayerView also drops the in-player favourite toggle the shell provides (M3UChannelsView.swift:714-717), in addition to the prev/next queue. The population is narrow: M3U playlists with VOD-classified entries that the user downloaded (get.php links are imported as Xtream).

**Corrected claim:** On M3U playlists a completed download is only used when playback starts from Settings > Downloads. Tapping the same item in the shelves, the group grid, Favorites or Continue Watching streams the remote URL again and fails offline. Xtream resolves the local file first at every entry point.

**Corrected fix:** Add one internal @MainActor helper, for example an extension on PlayerOverlayController in M3UChannelsView.swift or a small new file: presentM3U(playlist:channel:queue:resumeTimeMs:). Live-classified items keep today's synchronous present { M3UPlayerShell(...) }. For VOD-classified items, await DownloadManager.shared.localURL(forId: DownloadManager.idFor(m3uChannel: playlist.id, channelId: channel.id)) in a Task, as MovieDetailView.swift:190-199 does. If a file exists, call present(skipDownloadCheck: true) with PlayerView(url: local, title:, subtitle:, artworkURL:, isLiveStream: false, playlistId:, streamId: channel.id, type: "vod", resumeTimeMs:, containerExtension:); otherwise present the shell as today. Call it from the four sites. To keep the favourite button on local playback, also pass isFavorite / onToggleFavorite as the shell does. M3UPlayerShell stays untouched. Grid and favourites taps pass no resume position today, so reading history for the local path is optional and would be a behaviour change beyond parity.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. Project API checked: DownloadManager.localURL(forId:) async -> URL? returns nil unless the row is completed and the file exists (Models/DownloadManager.swift:289-300). PlayerOverlayController.present(onDismiss:skipDownloadCheck:playlistId:content:) is @MainActor (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:28-34). The PlayerView parameters used are the ones DownloadsView.swift:378-392 already passes.

**Regression risks:** VOD-classified taps gain one async DB read before the player appears, the same hop Xtream has; live channels must stay on the synchronous path. A downloaded item plays without the prev/next queue, and without the favourite toggle unless it is passed explicitly. A classifier false positive (a live stream under a /movie/ path) only costs the DB read, because no download row exists. The player-shell files are not modified.

**How to verify:** Simulator: M3U playlist with one .mp4 entry, download it from the context menu, cut the network, then tap the card in the shelf, the group grid, Favorites and Continue Watching: each must play the file, and Continue Watching must resume. Check that the history row is shared with playback from Settings > Downloads, and that a live channel still opens without delay.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-8 — In the M3U guide a channel tap opens the schedule instead of playing, and the programme sheet offers no way to play at all

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide (M3U playlists), Programme detail sheet (M3U)
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:202-207, 398-402`, `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:78-90`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:265-275`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:602-652`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Confirm that tap = play is wanted in the M3U guide as on Xtream (the current behaviour is documented in a comment as a deliberate fallback).

**What the user perceives:** On an Xtream playlist tapping a channel in the guide starts it and long-press shows the schedule. On an M3U playlist the same tap pushes the schedule, long-press does the same, and the sheet for the programme that is on right now has only Close. To watch what the guide shows the user has to leave it and find the channel in the shelves.

**Mechanism (finder):** playChannel falls back to detailChannel = row when row.liveStream is nil, with the comment 'M3U: no single-view live shell here' (EPGGuideView.swift:399-401). The sheet shows its play button only when liveStream != nil (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:81). A shell does exist: M3UPlayerShell(playlist:channel:queue:) is internal (M3UChannelsView.swift:602-652), and the M3U guide row already carries the channel id as row.id (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:270).

**Proposed fix (finder):** In EPGGuideView.playChannel, for an M3U row look the channel up and present the M3U shell with its group as queue (same rule as M3UChannelsView.queueForChannel, 279-283):
if let ch = M3UContentStore.shared.channels.first(where: { $0.id == row.id }), M3UParser.sanitizedURL(from: ch.url) != nil {
    let key = ch.groupTitle?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).nonEmpty ?? M3UContentStore.ungroupedLabel
    playerOverlay.present { M3UPlayerShell(playlist: model.playlist, channel: ch, queue: M3UContentStore.shared.channelsByGroup[key] ?? [ch]) }
} else { detailChannel = row }
Give EPGProgrammeDetailSheet an optional onPlayChannel: (() -> Void)? so M3U callers can show the existing 'epg.detail.play_channel' button. No new strings.

**Verifier reasons:** The behaviour is confirmed. Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:399-401 sends an M3U row (liveStream == nil) to detailChannel, which is exactly what the long-press does (line 206), so tap and long-press are identical on M3U. Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:81 shows 'Play channel' only when liveStream != nil, so an M3U sheet has only Close. The comment's reason ('no single-view live shell here') does not hold: M3UPlayerShell(playlist:channel:queue:resumeTimeMs:) is an internal struct with an internal init (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:602-652), and the M3U guide rows carry the channel id as row.id (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:270). History shows the fallback arriving with the guide itself in 1cce013 with no product rationale, so it is a workaround and not a decision. The M3U guide is reachable from Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:67. The proposed code needs corrections. String has no .nonEmpty; the only similar helper, nonEmptyOrNil, is a private extension in M3UChannelsView.swift:307-309 and is not visible from the EPG files. The sheet is also presented from the pushed schedule (Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:47-51), so the play hook has to be threaded through ChannelEPGDetailView as well; the finding only mentions the guide's own sheet. No M3U guide screenshot exists in shots/, so this is code evidence only.

**Corrected claim:** In the M3U guide a channel tap does the same as a long-press (opens the schedule) and the programme sheet has no play action, although an M3U player shell exists and is reachable from the EPG code. On Xtream the same tap plays the channel.

**Corrected fix:** Carry the channel in the row: add let m3uChannel: DBM3UChannel? to EPGGuideRow (DBM3UChannel is already Equatable and Hashable, Models/DBModels.swift:143) and set it at EPGGuideViewModel.swift:270; this avoids a linear scan of the catalog on tap. In EPGGuideView.playChannel, when row.m3uChannel is set and M3UParser.sanitizedURL(from:) is non-nil, compute the canonical group key inline (trimmed groupTitle, or M3UContentStore.ungroupedLabel when empty) and call playerOverlay.present { M3UPlayerShell(playlist: model.playlist, channel: ch, queue: M3UContentStore.shared.channelsByGroup[key] ?? [ch]) }, with no playlistId, as every other M3U entry point; otherwise keep detailChannel = row. Give EPGProgrammeDetailSheet and ChannelEPGDetailView an optional m3uChannel (or an onPlayChannel closure) and show the existing 'epg.detail.play_channel' button when it is set. No new strings. The owner should confirm tap = play for M3U.

**API check:** No SDK API involved. Project API checked: M3UPlayerShell init is internal (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:630-635); M3UContentStore.channelsByGroup and ungroupedLabel are accessible (Models/M3UContentStore.swift:18, 26); EPGGuideRow is Hashable (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:5), as navigationDestination(item:) at EPGGuideView.swift:63 requires.

**Regression risks:** Users used to tap = schedule on M3U now need the long-press, the same as Xtream. The queue taken from channelsByGroup contains the group's VOD-classified items as well, the same as the shelf queue (M3UChannelsView.swift:279-283). EPGGuideRow grows by one optional field per M3U row, and EPGChannelColumnCell equality (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:139-141) compares it; that is cheap. If finding 6 is applied, hidden M3U groups disappear from the guide first.

**How to verify:** Simulator with an M3U playlist that has an EPG URL: tap a channel cell in the guide, the player opens and channel up/down stays inside the group; long-press still pushes the schedule; the sheet of the current programme shows Play channel from both the guide and the pushed schedule; an Xtream playlist behaves as before.
