## gap-playback-inherited-state-9 — The download-in-progress warning is requested while the programme sheet is still on screen or dismissing, so 'Play channel' and catch-up may end as a dead tap with a pending alert left behind

- Verdict: **undecidable** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Programme detail sheet, Channel schedule
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:82-85, 93-102, 123-131`, `Views/EPG/CatchupPlayerShell.swift:58-82`, `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:43-50`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:125-129, 156-172`

**What the user perceives:** Unconfirmed, needs a run: with a download active on the playlist, 'Play channel' in a programme sheet closes the sheet and nothing plays; the warning may not appear at all, or may appear later out of context.

**Mechanism (finder):** With an active download present() does not present; it stores pendingPresentation and expects the dashboard's alert (PlayerOverlayController.swift:43-50; DashboardView.swift:156-172). The sheet's button calls dismiss() and present() in the same tick (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:83-84), and the catch-up path calls overlay.present while the sheet is fully up and dismisses afterwards (97-101; CatchupPlayerShell.swift:76). The alert therefore has to be presented from the dashboard while a sheet presented below it is on screen or mid-dismissal; UIKit refuses to present from a controller that is already presenting. The only sheet the dashboard handles for playback is its own Downloads sheet (125-129). I could not determine from code whether SwiftUI retries the alert after the sheet is gone.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Only if the run confirms it. Start playback after the sheet has gone, which is also the native order: the sheet stores the action and dismisses, the presenter runs it in onDismiss. In EPGGuideView.swift:67 and ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:47:
.sheet(item: $selected, onDismiss: { pendingPlay?(); pendingPlay = nil }) { ... EPGProgrammeDetailSheet(..., onPlay: { action in pendingPlay = action }) }
For catch-up keep the resolve and the inline error in the sheet and hand over only the final present.

**APIs:** View.sheet(item:onDismiss:content:) (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The code path is as described. With an active download, present() stores pendingPresentation instead of presenting (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:43-50), and the only consumer is the alert on the dashboard root (Views/DashboardView.swift:156-172). 'Play channel' calls dismiss() and then playLiveChannel() in the same button action (Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:82-85), so the sheet's dismissal and the alert request land in one update. The catch-up path calls overlay.present while the sheet is up (Views/EPG/CatchupPlayerShell.swift:76) and dismisses right after the await returns (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:97-101). Whether SwiftUI defers the alert until the sheet's dismissal transition has finished, presents it over the sheet, or drops it with a UIKit 'already presenting' warning cannot be read from this code base or from the swiftinterface. If it is dropped, the binding stays true and the alert may appear at the next re-evaluation of DashboardView, out of context. The precondition is narrow: an active download on the same playlist while starting playback from a programme sheet. The proposed fix has a cost the finding does not mention: running playback from the sheet's onDismiss delays the player by the whole dismissal animation on every start, including the common case with no download.

**Corrected claim:** Unchanged, and still unproven: with an active download on the playlist, the download warning is requested in the same update in which the programme sheet is dismissed (Play channel) or while it is still up (catch-up). Whether the alert appears reliably can only be settled by a run.

**Corrected fix:** None until a run confirms it. If confirmed, defer only the warning case so the normal path keeps its immediate start: in the sheet, check DownloadManager.shared.hasActiveDownload(playlistId: playlist.id) first. When it is false, keep today's dismiss() plus present. When it is true, hand the play action to the presenter, dismiss, and run it from .sheet(item:onDismiss:) in EPGGuideView.swift:67 and ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:47, so the dashboard alert is requested after the sheet is gone. For catch-up keep the resolve and the inline error in the sheet and hand over only the final present.

**API check:** View.sheet(item:onDismiss:content:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface line 7482 under @available(iOS 13.0, ...): func sheet<Item, Content>(item: Binding<Item?>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping (Item) -> Content). DownloadManager.hasActiveDownload(playlistId:) exists at Models/DownloadManager.swift:386.

**Regression risks:** The fix as originally proposed delays every playback start from a programme sheet until the dismissal animation ends. A pending action held in the presenter must be cleared when the sheet is closed by swipe or Close, or a stale action could run on a later dismissal. The catch-up path must keep the sheet open on a resolve error (EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:98-101).

**How to verify:** Simulator, Xtream playlist: start a film download so hasActiveDownload is true, then Live TV > guide > tap a programme > Play channel. Record whether the warning alert with Cancel / Go to Downloads / Continue appears, when it appears relative to the sheet's dismissal, and whether the console logs 'Attempt to present ... which is already presenting' or '... whose view is not in the window hierarchy'. Repeat with a catch-up programme and from the pushed channel schedule, on iOS 18 and iOS 26. If the alert shows every time, drop the finding.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-10 — M3U never shows the download-in-progress warning; this is deliberate in code and needs the owner's confirmation rather than a fix

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U Channels, M3U Favorites
- Code: `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:24-27, 43-47`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:267, 294, 532`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:86`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:83-108`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Should M3U playlists warn before playback while a download from the same playlist is running, as Xtream does?

**What the user perceives:** On an M3U playlist served by a connection-limited panel, starting a channel while a film downloads can stall or fail the download without the warning Xtream users get.

**Mechanism (finder):** All four M3U presentations omit playlistId, and present() documents that as intended: 'playlistId verilmezse uyarı gösterilmez (M3U / playlist-bağımsız oynatım için)' (PlayerOverlayController.swift:27). History gives no further rationale: the line predates the monorepo move (git log -S finds only d2489f9). It is consistent with the host: M3UDashboardView has no alert for pendingPresentation at all (83-108), so passing playlistId today would turn every tap during a download into a dead tap. The download side is already keyed per playlist for M3U (DownloadManager.swift:369, 386-388). Since get.php links are converted to Xtream on import, the remaining M3U playlists are mostly lists without a connection limit, which supports the current behaviour.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Leave as is unless the owner wants parity. If yes: copy the alert from DashboardView.swift:156-172 into M3UDashboardView (the existing 'download.player_warning.*' strings; 'Go to Downloads' selects the Settings tab, where Downloads is pushed at M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:85) and pass playlistId: playlist.id at the four call sites, both in the same change.

**APIs:** View.alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The claim describes the code accurately and correctly asks for no change by default. All four M3U presentations omit playlistId (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:267, 294, 532; Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:86). present() documents that as intended for M3U (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:27, shouldWarn at 43-47); git log -S finds the line only in d2489f9, the monorepo move. Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:83-109 has no alert bound to pendingPresentation, so passing playlistId without adding one would turn every tap during a download into a dead tap. The download side is keyed per playlist for M3U (Models/DownloadManager.swift:369, 386-388). One argument in the finding is weaker than stated: the only downloadable M3U items are VOD-classified ones, detected by /movie/, /series/, /vod/ paths or file extensions (M3UChannelsView.swift:939-954), and those typically come from Xtream-style panels that do have a connection limit. So this is a real owner decision, not a settled non-issue. The optional parity fix is also incomplete: selecting the Settings tab does not open Downloads; DashboardView uses a Downloads sheet plus an onChange that closes it when playback starts (Views/DashboardView.swift:125-129, 163-166, 173-183).

**Corrected claim:** M3U playlists never show the download-in-progress warning. This is documented as intended in PlayerOverlayController and consistent with M3UDashboardView having no pending-presentation alert. It is an owner decision and not a defect; the downloadable M3U items are the ones most likely to come from connection-limited panels, so the decision is not obvious.

**Corrected fix:** None unless the owner wants parity. If yes, do all of this in one change: copy the alert, the Downloads sheet and the onChange that closes it from DashboardView.swift:125-129 and 156-183 into M3UDashboardView (existing 'download.player_warning.*' strings; DownloadsView(playlist:) already works for M3U, see M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:85), and pass playlistId: playlist.id at the four M3U call sites. If finding 7 is applied, its local-file path must keep skipDownloadCheck: true.

**API check:** View.alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface in an extension marked @available(iOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, *); the StringProtocol overload used with L(...) is at line 10666: alert<S, A, M>(_ title: S, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, actions: () -> A, message: () -> M). It is the same call DashboardView.swift:156 already compiles.

**Regression risks:** With parity enabled, every M3U tap during a download gets an extra confirmation, live channels included. Passing playlistId without the alert in M3UDashboardView would create dead taps. A Downloads sheet over the M3U dashboard needs the same close-on-playback handling, or playback would start behind it.

**How to verify:** Only if enabled: simulator, M3U playlist with a downloadable film, start the download from the context menu, tap a channel: the alert appears; Continue plays, Cancel does not, Go to Downloads opens the list, and starting a completed download from there closes the sheet and plays.

## gap-playback-inherited-state-11 — The remaining play paths that return without feedback share no way to tell the user anything

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series, Movies, Live TV, M3U Channels, M3U Favorites, Downloads
- Code: `Views/SeriesView.swift:180, 914`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:242-249`, `Views/VODView.swift:272-273`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:166, 901`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:265, 292, 530, 667`, `Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:84`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:159, 208-212`

**What the user perceives:** In rare data conditions a card or button highlights and nothing follows.

**Mechanism (finder):** Complete list of silent returns on play paths, beyond the ones reported separately (series Watch / Resume, episode thumbnail, M3U history). Xtream URL guards: SeriesView.swift:180 and :914, MovieDetailView.swift:249, VODView.swift:273, LiveStreamsView.swift:166. They fire only when PlaybackURLBuilder returns nil, i.e. URL(string:) rejects the server address (PlaybackURLBuilder.swift:48-70); for a playlist that loaded its catalog this is practically unreachable. M3U guards: M3UChannelsView.swift:265, :292, :530 and M3UFavoritesView.swift:84 fire when sanitizedURL is nil, which is an entry with an empty or unencodable URL line (M3UParser.swift:149-160); rare but present in hand-edited lists. Two shells render nothing in the same condition while the overlay stays presented and the catalog stays hidden from VoiceOver: LiveStreamsView.swift:901 and M3UChannelsView.swift:667, the latter reachable by stepping onto such an entry with channel-down. Downloads: retry returns silently when the stored remote URL does not parse (159, 212), and rows in downloading / queued state are plain-style buttons with an empty action (208-209). Search, Favorites (Xtream), the guide's catch-up and a missing download file have no silent path (SearchView.swift:280-306; FavoritesView.swift:80-99; EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:62-64; DownloadsView.swift:324-330).

**Proposed fix (finder):** One small shared notice instead of per-screen plumbing: a PlaybackNoticeCenter: ObservableObject with @Published var message: String?, injected next to playerOverlay by both dashboards, each with one .alert(L("common.error"), ...) and .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: message). Replace the listed 'else { return }' with notices.report(L("playback.error.invalid_address")). One new key in the ten Localizable.strings files, appended only. Additionally drop entries without a usable URL from the queues handed to M3UPlayerShell at the call sites (queue.filter { M3UParser.sanitizedURL(from: $0.url) != nil }), so a step can never land on one, and make downloading / queued rows non-buttons.

**APIs:** View.sensoryFeedback(_:trigger:) (iOS 17.0); SensoryFeedback.error (iOS 17.0); View.alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read every cited site. The inventory of silent returns is accurate, but the reachability story and parts of the fix need correcting.

1) Xtream guards (Views/SeriesView.swift:180, :914; Views/MovieDetailView.swift:249; Views/VODView.swift:273; Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:166; and LivePlayerShell's `if let url = session.url` at LiveStreamsView.swift:901) fire only when URL(string:) rejects the string built in Networking/PlaybackURLBuilder.swift:48-70. A scratch run against current Foundation showed that happens only for authority-level garbage ("http://host:abc", "http://[x"); spaces, unicode hosts and odd characters are all accepted. A playlist with such a server address would not have loaded a catalog to tap on. The finding says the same: practically unreachable.

2) M3U guards (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:265, :292, :530; Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:84): the stated trigger, "an entry with an empty URL line", is wrong. Networking/M3UParser.swift skips blank lines (:188-189) and appends a channel only when the EXTINF carries a non-empty embedded URL or a following non-# line arrives (processLine, `.extinf` and `.uri` cases, about :228-292). An #EXTINF with no URL is overwritten by the next one (`lostPendingChannels`) and never becomes a channel, so the finding's repro recipe reproduces nothing. sanitizedURL (M3UParser.swift:149-160) returns nil only for a non-empty line URL(string:) rejects even after percent-encoding. Scratch run: nil for "http://h.com:8080 /live/u/p/1.ts" (space after the port), "http://host:abc/x.ts", "http://[::1/x", "{http://x}"; accepted for "not a url", "http://exa mple.com/a.ts", "http://a.com/a b|c.ts", "C:\\video\\a.mp4". So the guards are reachable only through authority-level typos in hand-edited lists: real, but rarer than described.

3) Blank shell (M3UChannelsView.swift:667, no else branch): real. Call sites pass unfiltered queues (queueForChannel :266/:293, displayItems :536, filtered :90 in M3UFavoritesView), and jump()/commitPendingZap() (:815-838) step onto index +/-1 with no URL check, so stepping onto such an entry leaves the overlay presented with nothing in it. Panel-driven queue changes are already safe: both panel builders skip unparseable entries (:882, :920) and selectPanelItem filters its new queue by those items (:868-870). Both shells are in the OUT-of-scope *PlayerShell structs, so only a fix outside them is admissible.

4) Downloads: the two retry guards (Views/DownloadsView.swift:159, :212) are unreachable, since remoteURL is always written from URL.absoluteString (Models/DownloadManager.swift:176, :196, :218). Downloading/queued rows are plain-style Buttons whose action is `break` (:185-190, :208-209): real but minor (pressed dimming with no result; VoiceOver announces a button that does nothing). The comment at :181-182 shows the tap/swipe pattern was applied to all statuses deliberately, without a primary action for these two.

5) History: all these guards date from the monorepo move (d2489f9) and carry no rationale comment. The only deliberate silent swallow is the missing-channel case at M3UChannelsView.swift:285-289, which is reported separately. DownloadsView.swift:327-328 shows the owner already treats a silent swallow as a defect, which supports the principle.

6) Fix problems. (a) `.sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: message)` on a String? also fires when the alert is dismissed and message returns to nil. (b) Filtering the queue at the call site runs on the main thread inside the tap: 43 ms per 100k entries in a release build on this Mac, more on a phone, and an ungrouped M3U group can be that large. That works against the off-main work documented at Models/M3UContentStore.swift:7 and M3UChannelsView.swift:866-868. (c) DownloadsView is also shown in a sheet (Views/DashboardView.swift:173-183) where playerOverlay is re-injected explicitly; a new environment object needs the same line, and an alert attached to the dashboard root cannot present over that sheet. (d) Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift matches the OUT-of-scope Views/Player*.swift pattern, so a separate object is the right shape if a notice is added at all.

Screenshots are not relevant: the claim is behavioural and no error state is captured.

**Corrected claim:** A handful of play paths return without feedback, but nearly all are unreachable in practice: the Xtream URL guards (SeriesView.swift:180/:914, MovieDetailView.swift:249, VODView.swift:273, LiveStreamsView.swift:166/:901) need a server address URL(string:) rejects, and the Downloads retry guards (DownloadsView.swift:159/:212) need a stored absoluteString that fails to parse. The reachable cases are: (1) M3U entries whose URL line is non-empty but malformed at the authority level (space after the port, non-numeric port, unbalanced IPv6 bracket), not empty URL lines, which the parser never turns into channels. Tapping one does nothing (M3UChannelsView.swift:265/:292/:530, M3UFavoritesView.swift:84), and stepping onto one with previous/next leaves the player overlay blank (M3UChannelsView.swift:667). (2) Downloading/queued rows in Downloads are buttons with an empty action (DownloadsView.swift:185-190, :208-209). Both are rare or minor.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest change that removes the reachable cases, without a notice centre:

1) M3U: stop unparseable entries from becoming channels, in the parser, which already runs off the main thread. In M3UParser.processLine, check `sanitizedURL(from:) != nil` before `state.channels.append` in the `.uri` case and the embedded-URL case. On failure skip that line, keep the pending EXTINF so a valid URL on the next line can still attach, and count it in diagnostics. This matches how the parser already drops EXTINF entries with no URL. It makes the four M3U tap guards and the blank M3UPlayerShell state unreachable for anything imported or refreshed afterwards, with no main-thread filtering at tap time and no shell edits. Keep the existing guards as defence for rows already in the database.

2) Downloads: in actionableRow, render `row(item)` without the Button for .downloading/.queued and keep the same .swipeActions; or keep the Button and remove the button trait for those states.

3) Optional, owner's decision: a shared notice for the remaining unreachable guards. If built, keep it separate from PlayerOverlayController, inject it at DashboardView.swift:124 and :182 and M3UDashboardView.swift:83, and use `.sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: message) { _, new in new != nil }` so dismissal does not vibrate. Append one new key to the ten Localizable.strings files without touching the tip keys. I would not build this for paths that cannot be hit.

Do not add `queue.filter { sanitizedURL... }` at the call sites.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk):
- :1981-1985, @available(iOS 17.0, ...): `func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T) -> some View where T: Equatable`, and the variant needed here, `func sensoryFeedback<T>(_ feedback: SensoryFeedback, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (_ oldValue: T, _ newValue: T) -> Bool)`.
- :844: `public static let error: SwiftUI.SensoryFeedback`.
- :10666, in an iOS 15.0 extension: `func alert<S, A, M>(_ title: S, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, actions: () -> A, message: () -> M) where S: StringProtocol`. The same form is already used at Views/DashboardView.swift:138 and :156.

All are below the iOS 18 deployment target, so no availability gate is needed. "common.error" exists (Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:7); "playback.error.invalid_address" does not and would be new. The corrected fix (parser check, Downloads row) uses no new API.

**Regression risks:** Parser change: an entry with an unparseable URL disappears from the list instead of being shown and inert, and channel counts and diagnostics shift slightly. Existing M3UParser unit tests that assert counts for malformed input may need updating. If the pending EXTINF is reset instead of kept on a rejected line, the next valid URL becomes an orphan and a real channel is lost. Rows already stored keep the old behaviour until the playlist is refreshed.

Downloads row: switching between Button and plain row when the status flips to completed changes the row's inner identity; check that the progress-to-completed transition does not flicker and that swipe actions still attach.

Optional notice centre: a new @EnvironmentObject must also be injected into the Downloads sheet (DashboardView.swift:182) to avoid a missing-object crash. Every view holding it re-evaluates when message changes, which is harmless because it is error-only. Localizable.strings holds the owner's uncommitted tip keys, so append only.

**How to verify:** Unit test, no simulator needed: parse "#EXTM3U\n#EXTINF:-1,Good\nhttp://h.com/1.ts\n#EXTINF:-1,Bad\nhttp://h.com:8080 /2.ts\n#EXTINF:-1,Good2\nhttp://h.com/3.ts". Today it yields 3 channels, the second with sanitizedURL == nil; after the fix it yields 2, both playable.

Simulator, current build: import that file, tap "Bad" and nothing happens; play "Good" and press next, and the overlay goes blank. After the fix "Bad" is absent and next goes from Good to Good2.

Do not use an empty URL line as the repro: the parser never creates a channel for it.

Downloads: start a download, tap the downloading row and confirm no pressed dimming, that VoiceOver no longer announces it as a button, and that the trailing swipe still offers Cancel.

## gap-session-state-retention-1 — Pull-to-refresh on Live TV, Movies and Series updates the store but the shelves keep showing the pre-refresh catalog until the tab is re-entered

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity high · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:210-220, 234-278, 287-318`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17, 105-107, 242-249, 278-294`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:29-31, 95-99, 157-159, 166-193`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:30-32, 96-100, 158-160, 220-247`

**What the user perceives:** The user pulls down, the spinner runs for the whole network sync and ends, and nothing on screen changes: new channels, new films and the Recently Added shelf stay as they were. The new content appears only after switching tab and back or after pushing and popping a screen. Meanwhile a category opened from the stale shelf, and the category picker, already show the new data, so root and detail disagree.

**Mechanism (finder):** The roots render @State copies (displayCategories / displayItemsByCategory / recentlyAddedVODs) that are written only by recomputeFilter(), which runs from three tasks keyed on debouncedQuery, contentStore.streamsLoaded and the hidden-id set (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, VODView.swift:157-159, SeriesView.swift:158-160). The pull-to-refresh path is the scoped refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only:) (PlaylistContentStore.swift:210-220) -> reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) (234-278), which replaces liveCategories / liveStreams / liveStreamsByCategoryId (or the vod / series equivalents) but never touches streamsLoaded. None of the three task ids change, so recomputeFilter() is not called. The full reload used by Settings (287-318) flips streamsLoaded false -> true and therefore does trigger it; the scoped variant was added in 1cce013 (2026-07-24) without an equivalent signal. The view only catches up because .task re-runs on the next onAppear. Side effect for this lens: in case (d) of the shelf-offset question the offsets survive only because nothing is recomputed.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give the store an explicit change signal and key the recompute on it. PlaylistContentStore: add `@Published private(set) var liveRevision = 0` (plus vodRevision, seriesRevision) and bump the matching counter at the end of every in-memory replacement: loadPlaylist phase 2 (line 152), reloadFromDatabase (317) and each case of reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(only:) (249, 261, 273). Roots: replace `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` with `.task(id: CatalogKey(loaded: contentStore.streamsLoaded, revision: contentStore.vodRevision))` (a two-field Equatable struct) in LiveStreamsView.swift:106, VODView.swift:158, SeriesView.swift:159; the same key belongs on the category / All* screens (LiveStreamsView.swift:509, 734; VODView.swift:575, 834; SeriesView.swift:547, 773) and SearchView.swift:248. Per-type counters keep a Live refresh from recomputing a Movies grid that sits on another tab's stack. After the fix the refresh replaces the arrays by value: unchanged categories compare equal in the Equatable shelf rows and are not re-rendered, changed ones keep their ForEach identity (category id), so shelf offsets and the root's vertical position survive the refresh by identity.

**APIs:** View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read from code. The three Xtream roots render @State copies (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:16-17, Views/VODView.swift:29-31, Views/SeriesView.swift recomputeFilter at 220-247) that are written only by recomputeFilter(), and recomputeFilter() is called only from three .task(id:) modifiers keyed on debouncedQuery, contentStore.streamsLoaded and the hidden-id set (LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, VODView.swift:157-159, SeriesView.swift:158-160). Pull-to-refresh calls refreshFromNetwork(playlist:only:) (LiveStreamsView.swift:247, VODView.swift:97, SeriesView.swift:98) -> Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:210-220 -> reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) at 234-278, which replaces the categories/streams/byCategory for one type and never touches streamsLoaded. None of the three ids change, so the roots keep the old arrays until .task re-runs on the next appear. The full reload (PlaylistContentStore.swift:287-318, used by Settings at Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:524) flips streamsLoaded false->true and does trigger a recompute. History confirms a regression rather than a deliberate choice: git show 1cce013 on VODView.swift changes `refreshFromNetwork(playlist: playlist)` (full path, flips streamsLoaded) to `refreshFromNetwork(playlist: playlist, only: .vod)`; no comment near either site explains the missing signal. The 'root and detail disagree' part also holds: pickerEntries reads contentStore directly (LiveStreamsView.swift:45-53, VODView.swift:13-21) and a pushed category reads contentStore.*ByCategoryId in its own recompute (LiveStreamsView.swift:512-516). Scope note: M3U is not affected (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift recomputes in .onChange(of: store.channels)). The pushed screens named in the fix are keyed on streamsLoaded only (LiveStreamsView.swift:509, 734; VODView.swift:575, 834; SeriesView.swift:547, 773; SearchView.swift:248), so a refresh that finishes while one of them is on screen leaves it stale as well.

**Corrected claim:** Pull-to-refresh on the Xtream Live TV, Movies and Series roots rewrites the database and the store's arrays but the roots' @State display copies are not recomputed, because the scoped reload (added in 1cce013) changes none of the three .task ids. The shelves and Recently Added stay at the pre-refresh catalog until the root re-appears (tab switch or pop). The category picker and pushed category screens read the store directly and already show the new data. M3U is not affected.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: add per-type @Published private(set) revision counters to PlaylistContentStore (liveRevision, vodRevision, seriesRevision), bump the matching one at the end of each case of reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only:) (after lines 249, 261, 273) and all three at the end of reloadFromDatabase (317) and loadPlaylist phase 2 (152), and replace `.task(id: contentStore.streamsLoaded)` with a two-field Equatable key (loaded + that type's revision) in the three roots and in the category / All* screens; SearchView needs all three revisions in its key. Two additions: (1) do NOT bump a revision in applyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:164-178), otherwise every movie-detail open would re-run the root recompute including the 150k-item Recently Added sort; (2) set the revision in the same synchronous block as the array assignments so the view sees one update. If the Search fix from finding 4 lands, fold the revisions into its single SearchKey instead of adding a fourth task.

**API check:** View.task(id:priority:_:) found in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166 as `@inlinable nonisolated public func task<T>(id value: T, priority: TaskPriority = .userInitiated, @_inheritActorContext _ action: @escaping @Sendable () async -> Void) -> some View where T : Equatable` (extension is iOS 15.0). A two-field Equatable struct is a valid id. @Published is Combine, already used by the store. No iOS 26 API involved, no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** After a refresh the by-category arrays have new buffers, so the Equatable shelf rows fall off the shared-buffer fast path once and do a full element compare for the instantiated rows (one time, acceptable). Rows whose rows really changed re-evaluate body but keep ForEach identity (category id), so shelf offsets survive. VOD/Series roots re-run the detached Recently Added sort once per refresh (already happens on every appear). Bumping in loadPlaylist together with the streamsLoaded flip must stay in one synchronous run or the roots recompute twice. The grids' cheap Equatable signature (count/first/last, LiveStreamsView.swift:534-539) is deliberate and stays as is; a refresh that changes only middle items of an open grid will still not redraw it.

**How to verify:** Unit test in another-iptv-playerTests: seed the DB for a playlist, loadPlaylist, insert a vod category + stream directly in the DB, call reloadFromDatabaseIfActive(playlistId:only: .vod), assert vodRevision increased, liveRevision and seriesRevision did not, and vodCategories contains the new row. Simulator (orchestrator): with a real or stub panel, add a category server-side, pull to refresh on Movies and assert the new shelf header exists without leaving the tab; repeat for Live and Series; scroll one shelf horizontally before the pull and assert its leading card is unchanged afterwards.

## gap-session-state-retention-2 — The TV guide jumps back to 'now' every time the user returns from a channel schedule, discarding the time he had scrolled to

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide (Xtream and M3U)
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:58-66, 193-198, 323-329, 358-396, 398-402`, `another-iptv-player/Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:16, 141-146`

**What the user perceives:** The user scrolls the timeline to tonight's 21:00, opens a channel's schedule (long-press on Xtream, a plain tap on M3U because playChannel falls back to the schedule at EPGGuideView.swift:399-402), goes back, and 50 ms later the grid snaps to the current time (or to 08:00 on another day). On M3U playlists this happens after every channel tap. The day and the vertical position are kept, which makes the horizontal jump look like a glitch.

**Mechanism (finder):** The initial positioning is attached as `.task(id: model.selectedDay) { await focusSelectedTimeAfterLayout() }` on the grid (EPGGuideView.swift:196-198). A SwiftUI task is cancelled on disappear and started again on appear, and a NavigationStack root disappears while the destination from navigationDestination(item: $detailChannel) (63-66) covers it. So the task re-runs on every pop and calls applyProgrammaticOffset(defaultTimeOffset) (358-362), overwriting both ScrollPosition values. Returning from the player or from the programme sheet does not re-run it (overlay and sheet do not make the guide disappear), so only the schedule push is affected. ChannelEPGDetailView already guards its own jump with hasScrolledToNow (ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:16, 141-146); the guide has no such guard.

**Proposed fix (finder):** EPGGuideView.swift: remember which day the automatic jump already ran for.

@State private var focusedDay: Date?
.task(id: model.selectedDay) {
    guard focusedDay != model.selectedDay else { return }   // re-appear after a pop: keep the user's offset
    await focusSelectedTimeAfterLayout()
    if !Task.isCancelled { focusedDay = model.selectedDay }
}

One companion change is required: onDisappear cancels targetReleaseTask (line 60). Today the re-run re-arms it; with the guard a push within 150 ms of a programmatic jump would leave programmaticTargetX set forever and propagate() would return at line 325, breaking axis/body sync. Add `programmaticTargetX = nil` next to the cancel in onDisappear. The clock toolbar button keeps working: on today it calls applyProgrammaticOffset directly, on another day it changes selectedDay, which differs from focusedDay.

**APIs:** ScrollPosition (iOS 18.0); View.scrollPosition(_:anchor:) (iOS 18.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift. The grid carries `.task(id: model.selectedDay) { await focusSelectedTimeAfterLayout() }` (196-198) with no run-once guard; focusSelectedTimeAfterLayout sleeps 50 ms and calls applyProgrammaticOffset(defaultTimeOffset) (358-362), which overwrites both ScrollPosition values and bodyOffsetX (373-387). The schedule is pushed with navigationDestination(item: $detailChannel) (63-66), set by long-press (206) and, when row.liveStream is nil, by a plain tap (398-402); M3U rows are built with liveStream: nil (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:272). A task modifier is cancelled when its view disappears and started again on appear, and a NavigationStack screen disappears while a pushed destination covers it. The file itself shows the authors rely on that: the load task at 54-57 has `guard model.state == .loading else { return }` precisely so it does not reload on re-appear, and onDisappear at 58-62 cancels work; the grid task has no such guard. ChannelEPGDetailView guards its own jump with hasScrolledToNow (Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:14, 141-146; the finding cites line 16, it is 14). The player overlay is an in-window ZStack layer (Views/DashboardView.swift:92-123) and the programme detail is a sheet (EPGGuideView.swift:67-72), so neither makes the guide disappear. Nothing in comments or history (654cefc, 1cce013) marks the re-jump as intended; the comment at 193-195 only talks about first layout. The companion change is needed and correct: onDisappear cancels targetReleaseTask (60) without clearing programmaticTargetX, and propagate() returns early while it is set (325).

**Corrected claim:** The guide re-runs its 'jump to default time' task every time it re-appears after the channel schedule was pushed over it, so the horizontal position the user had scrolled to is replaced by now (or 08:00 on other days) about 50 ms after the pop; day and vertical position are kept. On M3U playlists this follows every channel tap, on Xtream only the long-press path. On iPad it also follows a tab switch away and back if the sidebar/top tab bar is reachable.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, plus one guard for grid re-creation. EPGGuideView.swift: `@State private var focusedDay: Date?`; in the grid task: `guard focusedDay != model.selectedDay else { return }; await focusSelectedTimeAfterLayout(); if !Task.isCancelled { focusedDay = model.selectedDay }`. In onDisappear, next to targetReleaseTask?.cancel(), add `programmaticTargetX = nil`. Addition: `grid` only exists in state .ready (94-98) and is rebuilt with fresh scroll views if the state leaves and re-enters .ready (e.g. .ready -> .empty -> .ready after a refresh); reset the memo then: `.onChange(of: model.state) { _, s in if s != .ready { focusedDay = nil } }` (GuideState is Equatable, EPGGuideViewModel.swift:79).

**API check:** ScrollPosition: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:688 `public struct ScrollPosition : Sendable`, @available(iOS 18.0). scrollTo(x:) at line 732, iOS 18.0. View.scrollPosition(_:anchor:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22734 `nonisolated public func scrollPosition(_ position: Binding<ScrollPosition>, anchor: UnitPoint? = nil) -> some View`, iOS 18.0. View.task(id:) iOS 15.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166). The fix adds no new API; it only adds a @State Date? and an onChange.

**Regression risks:** If focusedDay is not reset when the grid is rebuilt, a rebuilt grid would stay at offset 0 (midnight) instead of jumping to now. A push inside the first 250 ms leaves focusedDay unset, so the jump re-runs on return (correct: the user has not scrolled yet). Clearing programmaticTargetX on disappear must not be skipped or axis/body sync can stay disabled after a quick push. The 'now' toolbar button is unaffected (same day: direct applyProgrammaticOffset at 348; other day: selectedDay changes and differs from focusedDay). The earlier hang fix (activeScroller latch, 304-319) is untouched.

**How to verify:** Simulator UI test (orchestrator): open the guide, wait for the grid, swipe the timeline left twice, record the first visible hour label on the axis, long-press a channel cell (Xtream) or tap it (M3U), tap Back, wait 500 ms, assert the same hour label is visible. Repeat after selecting Tomorrow. Then drag the body horizontally and assert the axis label moves with it (sync still alive). Also push within 100 ms of opening the guide and confirm the grid still lands on now after the pop.

## gap-session-state-retention-3 — No shelf owns its horizontal offset: typing in a tab's search field rebuilds the shelves and Cancel returns them at the first card; survival across a long vertical scroll is left to LazyVStack

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, M3U channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:25, 65-91, 226-240, 289-314, 337-349, 382-397, 1221-1228`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:38-62, 78-93, 175-214, 400-411, 448-467`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:39-63, 79-94, 229-267, 376-387, 420-439`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:50-62, 151-183, 320-330, 363-377`

**What the user perceives:** The user scrolls the 'Action' shelf to the 30th poster, searches for something in the same tab, cancels, and every shelf is back at its first card. If the query had no match the whole list was replaced by the empty state (shots/iphone-light/L06-live-inline-search-results.png) and is rebuilt from scratch on Cancel. Scrolling 40 shelves down and back may also reset the shelf. In TV, Music and the App Store a shelf stays where it was left for the whole session.

**Mechanism (finder):** grep finds scrollPosition only in the EPG guide; shelf offsets live solely in each row's UIScrollView, so they exist only while that row view exists. Per case: (b) tab switch and (c) push/pop: survive. The roots stay mounted, the re-run of recomputeFilter() on re-appear assigns the same arrays, ForEach ids are the category ids (LiveStreamsView.swift:227-238) and the Equatable rows compare equal (Array == short-circuits on a shared buffer), so nothing is re-rendered. (d) pull to refresh: survive, today only because the refresh never reaches the shelves (see the stale-shelves finding); after that fix they still survive by identity. (e) search: lost, deterministically. recomputeFilter() replaces displayCategories / displayItemsByCategory with the filtered set (LiveStreamsView.swift:296-314, VODView.swift:197-214, SeriesView.swift:250-267, M3UChannelsView.swift:242-259): rows of non-matching categories are removed and come back as new views at offset 0, matching rows keep an offset clamped to the filtered content, Recently Added is removed (VODView.swift:194, SeriesView.swift:248), and a zero-result query flips the `if displayCategories.isEmpty` branch (LiveStreamsView.swift:65, VODView.swift:38, SeriesView.swift:39, M3UChannelsView.swift:50) which destroys the root ScrollView. (a) 40 shelves down and back: not decidable from code. The rows are children of a LazyVStack; SwiftUI documents lazy creation and gives no guarantee that an off-screen row (and its nested scroll view) is retained. Needs a simulator run with a large catalog; the demo data has too few categories. The root's vertical position is not affected in practice: the search field sits at the top of the content, so the user is at the top when he starts and ends a search.

**Proposed fix (finder):** A per-tab memo of offsets kept outside observation, the same reference-in-@State pattern as LivePlaybackModelMemo (LiveStreamsView.swift:25, 1221-1228), read when a row is created and written when a scroll settles.

final class ShelfOffsetMemo {            // not ObservableObject: a write must not invalidate any view
    private var x: [String: CGFloat] = [:]
    subscript(id: String) -> CGFloat { get { x[id] ?? 0 } set { x[id] = newValue > 1 ? newValue : nil } }
}
// root: @State private var shelfOffsets = ShelfOffsetMemo()
// row gets `offsets: ShelfOffsetMemo` (excluded from ==) and `isFiltering: Bool` (included in ==)
@State private var position: ScrollPosition
init(...) { _position = State(initialValue: ScrollPosition(x: isFiltering ? 0 : offsets[category.id])) }
ScrollView(.horizontal) { ... }
    .scrollPosition($position)
    .onScrollPhaseChange { _, phase, context in
        if phase == .idle, !isFiltering { offsets[category.id] = context.geometry.contentOffset.x }
    }
    .onChange(of: isFiltering) { _, filtering in
        if !filtering { position.scrollTo(x: offsets[category.id]) }   // rows that survived the search
    }

Writing on the idle phase gives one dictionary write per gesture; onScrollGeometryChange(for: CGFloat.self, of: { $0.contentOffset.x }) is the per-frame alternative and is equally available. Keys: category id (Xtream), group title (M3U), a constant for Recently Added. Search-time offsets are never written, so Cancel restores the browse offsets for recreated rows (init) and surviving rows (onChange). Everything is iOS 18.0, no fallback needed. Watch one cost: the binding is written when the user starts dragging, which re-evaluates that row's body once per gesture; VODCategoryShelfRow maps the whole category there (`let queue = items.map(\.stream)`, VODView.swift:447), so measure with a 5k-item category.

**APIs:** ScrollPosition (init(x:), scrollTo(x:)) (iOS 18.0); View.scrollPosition(_:anchor:) (iOS 18.0); View.onScrollPhaseChange(_:) with ScrollPhaseChangeContext.geometry (iOS 18.0); View.onScrollGeometryChange(for:of:action:) (iOS 18.0)

**Verifier reasons:** What holds: grep finds scrollPosition only in Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift, so shelf offsets live only in each row's scroll view. In-tab search replaces the display arrays with the filtered set (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:296-314, Views/VODView.swift:197-214, SeriesView recomputeFilter, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift recomputeFilter), so non-matching rows are removed from the ForEach and return as new views at offset 0, matching rows get narrower content and their offset is clamped, Recently Added is emptied (VODView.swift:194), and a zero-result query flips the `displayCategories.isEmpty` branch (LiveStreamsView.swift:65, VODView.swift:38; M3U: visibleShelfGroups.isEmpty) which removes the root ScrollView (shots/iphone-light/L06-live-inline-search-results.png shows that empty state). So case (e) is real and deterministic. Cases (b)/(c) surviving is consistent with the code (same dictionary buffers are reassigned, Equatable rows at LiveStreamsView.swift:344-349 / VODView.swift:406-411). What needs correcting: (1) Severity. This only shows after an in-tab search that the user cancels, having previously scrolled a shelf sideways; because search here is an in-place filter of the shelves, a reset afterwards is a small annoyance, not a defect a user meets often. Low, not medium. (2) Case (a) (LazyVStack dropping an off-screen row's nested scroll view) is not decidable from code and the demo catalog has too few categories. (3) The fix as written has an ordering bug: on Cancel, debouncedQuery is cleared synchronously (LiveStreamsView.swift:102-104) but the unfiltered arrays are only restored later by the .task(id: debouncedQuery) run. If isFiltering is derived from the query, onChange(of: isFiltering) fires while the row still holds the filtered items, scrollTo(x:) is clamped to the short content, and the offset is lost anyway. (4) Whether an initial ScrollPosition(x:) is honoured on first layout by a ScrollView whose content is a LazyHStack (estimated content width) is unverified; the EPG guide needed a 50 ms delay plus a verify-and-retry for a fixed-width content (EPGGuideView.swift:193-195, 358-371), which is evidence that this is not reliable out of the box. (5) API spelling: there is no `init(x:)`; the declaration is `init(idType:x:)` with a defaulted first parameter, so `ScrollPosition(x: v)` does compile.

**Corrected claim:** Shelf rows do not own their horizontal offset. After an in-tab search is cancelled, the shelves on Live TV, Movies, Series and M3U Channels come back at (or near) their first card, and after a zero-result query the whole root list is rebuilt at the top. Tab switches, push/pop and (after finding 1 is fixed) pull-to-refresh keep the offsets by view identity. Whether a shelf also resets after a long vertical scroll away and back is unknown and needs a run with 60+ categories.

**Corrected fix:** Measure case (a) first; the result picks the fix. If off-screen rows keep their offset (a survives): do not add per-row state. Keep the browse list mounted during search and show the filtered result as a separate layer: hold the filtered arrays in their own @State pair, render `contentList` from the unfiltered pair always, and while the query is non-empty put the results list (or the no-result view) on top with the browse list set to .opacity(0), .allowsHitTesting(false) and .accessibilityHidden(true). Offsets, the vertical position and Recently Added then survive by identity, including the zero-result case, with no new API. If (a) loses offsets: use the proposed ShelfOffsetMemo + per-row ScrollPosition, with two corrections: drive `isFiltering` from a flag that recomputeFilter() sets in the same assignment as the display arrays (not from debouncedQuery), and verify on device that `ScrollPosition(x:)` given as the State initial value places a LazyHStack shelf on its first frame; if it does not, restore in a short post-layout task as the EPG guide does. Either way this is a low-priority polish item, and whether to do it at all is the owner's call.

**API check:** ScrollPosition: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:688, @available(iOS 18.0). Initialiser is `public init(idType: (some Hashable & Sendable).Type = Never.self, x: CGFloat)` (iOS 18.0); there is no bare init(x:), but `ScrollPosition(x:)` resolves to it. `public mutating func scrollTo(x: CGFloat)` line 732, iOS 18.0. `ScrollPosition.x` / `.y` getters are iOS 26.0 only (do not use; `point` is iOS 18.0). View.scrollPosition(_:anchor:) SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22734, iOS 18.0. onScrollPhaseChange three-argument form: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13686 `(_ oldPhase: ScrollPhase, _ newPhase: ScrollPhase, _ context: ScrollPhaseChangeContext) -> Void`, iOS 18.0; ScrollPhaseChangeContext.geometry: ScrollGeometry at 13670-13673. onScrollGeometryChange(for:of:action:) at 13689, iOS 18.0. All iOS 18.0, no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** Memo variant: a @State ScrollPosition in each Equatable shelf row is written when a drag starts, which re-evaluates that row's body once per gesture (VODCategoryShelfRow rebuilds `items.map(\.stream)` there, VODView.swift:447); a restore that runs before the unfiltered items land is clamped; a visible slide from 0 on first frame if the initial position is not honoured. Mounted-browse variant: the hidden list keeps its instantiated rows and image views alive during search (memory, not CPU; the Equatable rows do not re-render), and VoiceOver/keyboard focus must be kept off the hidden layer. Neither variant may drop .equatable() on the rows or move filtering back to the main thread.

**How to verify:** Case (e), UI test on demo data: Movies, swipe the first shelf left three times, record its leading poster label, type a query matching another category, tap Cancel, assert the leading poster is unchanged; repeat with a zero-result query and also assert the vertical position. Case (a), fixture with 60+ categories on iOS 18.x and iOS 26: swipe shelf 1 left, scroll down past shelf 45, scroll back, compare the leading poster. If the memo variant is built: record the screen and check a restored shelf is at its offset on its first frame, and take an Instruments Hitches trace while dragging a 5k-item shelf.

## gap-session-state-retention-4 — Deleting one character below the two-character minimum destroys the Search tab's results view; retyping shows 'No Results' until the new search returns

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search tab
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/SearchView.swift:8, 48-65, 70-79, 140-142, 224-243, 246-248, 251-278`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:14, 77-83`

**What the user perceives:** The user has results for 'mi', scrolls down, deletes the 'i' to fix a typo and types it again. The list is replaced by the 'type at least 2 characters' placeholder at once, then comes back scrolled to the top, and on a large catalog it first shows the system 'No Results for mi' screen for as long as the scan takes. App Store, Music and TV keep the previous results on screen until new ones arrive and never show an empty state for a search still in flight.

**Mechanism (finder):** SearchView switches structurally between the placeholder and SearchResultsView on debouncedQuery.count < 2 (SearchView.swift:48-65), and onChange sets debouncedQuery = "" synchronously as soon as the trimmed text is shorter than two characters (72-73). That removes SearchResultsView, so its @State arrays liveResults / movieResults / seriesResults (140-142) and the List's scroll position are destroyed. When the query is valid again a new SearchResultsView starts with three empty arrays; because contentStore.streamsLoaded is already true the branch at 224-243 renders ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) until runSearch() (three detached full-catalog filters plus sorts, 260-271) returns. The same false empty state appears on the very first query. What survives: the text (lifted to DashboardView.swift:14) and the scope chip (SearchView.swift:8), also across tab switches, and the tab's pushed detail. Related cost: the three .task modifiers at 246-248 all re-run on every re-appear (tab return, pop from a detail), so the whole catalog is scanned three times per return.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep one SearchResultsView mounted and gate only what it shows.

// SearchView body: no if/else around the results
SearchResultsView(playlist: playlist, query: debouncedQuery, filter: selectedFilter, onSelectFilter: { selectedFilter = $0 })
    .overlay { if debouncedQuery.count < 2 { minCharsHint.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity).background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground)) } }

// SearchResultsView
@State private var resultsQuery: String?          // the query the three arrays belong to
.task(id: SearchKey(query: query, hidden: hiddenStore.version, loaded: contentStore.streamsLoaded)) { await runSearch() }   // one task instead of three
// runSearch(): guard query.count >= 2 else { return }; after assigning the arrays: resultsQuery = query
// empty branch: show ContentUnavailableView.search only when resultsQuery == query, otherwise a ProgressView row or the previous rows

The previous rows stay under the hint while the query is too short and are replaced in place when the new search lands, so the List keeps its identity and scroll position.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) (iOS 17.0); View.task(id:priority:_:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/SearchView.swift. The body switches structurally on `debouncedQuery.count < 2` between the hint and SearchResultsView (48-65), and onChange sets `debouncedQuery = ""` synchronously when the trimmed text is shorter than two characters (70-73). SearchResultsView's result arrays are @State (140-142), so dropping below two characters destroys them and the List. A newly created SearchResultsView starts with three empty arrays; with contentStore.streamsLoaded already true the branch at 224-243 renders ContentUnavailableView.search(text: query) until runSearch() returns. runSearch (251-278) filters the full live/vod/series arrays with localizedCaseInsensitiveContains and then sorts every match with localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare; on a 150k-movie catalog a two-character query matches tens of thousands of rows, so the false 'No Results' is on screen for a clearly visible time. The same happens on the first query of a session. The comment at 226-228 shows the authors already guard against a false empty state while the catalog loads, but not while a search is in flight. The triple work is also real: three separate .task modifiers (246-248) each call runSearch on every appear, so first display and every return from a detail or another tab scans the catalog three times and assigns the arrays three times. Text and scope chip surviving is correct (Views/DashboardView.swift:14, SearchView.swift:8). No history entry or comment marks any of this as intended (654cefc, 0ab5bcd).

**Corrected claim:** On the Search tab, a new results view shows the system 'No Results' screen while its first search is still running (first query of a session, and again after the text drops below two characters), and dropping below two characters destroys the results list and its scroll position. Separately, every appear of the results view runs the full-catalog search three times.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, with three additions. (1) Keep one SearchResultsView mounted and show the min-chars hint as an opaque overlay; add `.accessibilityHidden(debouncedQuery.count < 2)` to the results view so VoiceOver and keyboard focus cannot reach the covered rows. (2) Replace the three tasks with one `.task(id: SearchKey(query:, hidden: hiddenStore.version, loaded: contentStore.streamsLoaded))` (add the store revisions from finding 1 if that lands); store the key the current arrays were computed for (`@State private var resultsKey: SearchKey?`) and return early from runSearch when it equals the current key, so a re-appear after a pop or tab switch does no scan at all. (3) Show ContentUnavailableView.search only when resultsKey matches the current key and all three arrays are empty; otherwise keep the previous rows, or a ProgressView row when there are none. The smallest possible version, if the owner wants only the false empty state gone, is item (3) alone inside the existing structure. Keeping the two-character minimum is a product decision already made for performance; this fix does not change it.

**API check:** ContentUnavailableView.search(text:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17625 `public static func search(text: String) -> ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` (ContentUnavailableView is iOS 17.0). View.task(id:priority:_:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5166, iOS 15.0; a three-field Equatable struct is a valid id. View.overlay and accessibilityHidden are long-standing API. HiddenCategoryStore.version exists (Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:10). No iOS 26 API, no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** With the results view always mounted, stale rows sit under the hint: they must be hidden from accessibility and must not receive touches (the opaque overlay blocks touches; accessibility needs the explicit modifier). After the user clears the field and types an unrelated query, the old rows are visible until the new search lands; if that looks wrong, clear the arrays when the text becomes empty (not when it is one character). The single task must still react to streamsLoaded so the 'catalog still loading' path at 225-239 keeps working. playLive (280-306) reads liveResults and is unaffected. Off-main filtering must stay in Task.detached.

**How to verify:** UI test on demo data: type 'mi', assert a result row exists, delete one character, type 'i' again, poll every 50 ms and assert the 'No Results' label never exists between the two states and a row exists afterwards. With a real large catalog (or a 150k-row fixture): screen-record the first two-character query and check no empty-state frame appears; add a counter or signpost in runSearch and assert exactly one run per query change and zero runs when returning from a movie detail.

## gap-session-state-retention-5 — Tapping the selected tab and tapping the status bar are left entirely to the system: the app has no reselect handling and its NavigationStacks have no path

- Verdict: **undecidable** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Dashboard tab bar, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Settings, M3U dashboard
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:26-34, 48-85`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:14, 26-45`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:63-109`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:211-259`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:64-110`

**What the user perceives:** In Apple's apps a tap on the current tab pops to the tab's root and a second tap scrolls the root to the top; a status-bar tap scrolls to the top as well. Here either gesture may do nothing, depending on the OS version. A movie or series detail pushed from a shelf keeps the tab bar visible (shots/iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png), so the re-tap is reachable from two levels deep.

**Mechanism (finder):** What the code contains: the selection binding only stores the tab and persists it (DashboardView.swift:26-34); every stack is `NavigationStack { ... }` without a path (50, 57, 64, 71, 78; M3UDashboardView.swift:28, 38), so the app can neither pop a stack nor tell whether it is at its root; the roots have a ScrollViewReader used only for jump-to-category. What the framework guarantees: nothing. Neither the SwiftUI interface nor UITabBarController.h documents pop-to-root or scroll-to-top on reselect (no reselect API exists in the iOS 26 SwiftUI interface; the only hook is the selection binding or UITabBarControllerDelegate.didSelectTab). For the status bar, UIScrollView.h:264-265 states the gesture scrolls the scroll view under the touch whose scrollsToTop is YES, and 'on iPhone ... only if there's one on-screen scroll view with scrollsToTop == YES. If more than one is found, none will be scrolled'. Every shelf is a nested horizontal ScrollView and SwiftUI exposes no scrollsToTop control, so whether the roots qualify depends on how SwiftUI configures horizontal scroll views. Observed behaviour only, to be checked: pop-to-root on reselect, scroll-to-top on a second reselect, whether the binding setter is called with the unchanged value, and the status-bar tap.

**Proposed fix (finder):** First run the checks below on iOS 18.x and iOS 26, iPhone and iPad. Implement only what the system does not already do, otherwise the gesture is handled twice.

Reselect, if needed. DashboardView.swift, in tabBinding.set: `if newTab == selectedTab { reselectTick[newTab, default: 0] &+= 1 }`, and pass each tab its tick through a custom EnvironmentKey. In each root add a zero-height marker with a fixed id as the first child of the ScrollView and:

.onChange(of: reselectTick) { _, _ in
    guard rootIsVisible.value else { return }      // a pushed screen is on top: leave this tap to the pop
    withAnimation { proxy.scrollTo(Self.topID, anchor: .top) }
}

rootIsVisible is a reference box set in the root's onAppear / onDisappear, so it does not invalidate the view. If the large title stays collapsed after ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo, use a ScrollPosition bound to the root and `position.scrollTo(edge: .top)`. If the system does not pop to root either, the stacks need NavigationStack(path:) (the change the existing restoration finding already asks for) and the handler becomes `if !path.isEmpty { path = NavigationPath() } else { scroll to top }`. M3UDashboardView gets the same binding wrapper.

Status bar: if the tap is dead on the roots there is no SwiftUI fix; report it instead of adding UIKit introspection.

**APIs:** TabView(selection:) with Tab(_:systemImage:value:role:content:) (iOS 18.0); TabViewStyle.sidebarAdaptable (iOS 18.0); ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo(_:anchor:) (iOS 14.0); ScrollPosition.scrollTo(edge:) (iOS 18.0); NavigationStack(path:root:) with NavigationPath (iOS 16.0); UIScrollView.scrollsToTop (documented rule in UIScrollView.h:264-267) (iOS 2.0); UITabBarControllerDelegate.tabBarController(_:didSelectTab:previousTab:) (iOS 18.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The code facts are accurate: the tab selection binding only stores and persists the value (Views/DashboardView.swift:26-34), every tab is `NavigationStack { ... }` without a path (50, 57, 64, 71, 78; Views/M3UDashboardView.swift, both tabs, which binds `$selectedTab` directly), and a repository search finds no reselect, pop-to-root, NavigationPath or scrollsToTop handling. The SDK check also matches: the SwiftUI interface contains no reselect API (grep for 'reselect' in both interface files returns nothing), and UIScrollView.h:264-267 states the status-bar rule quoted in the finding. But none of this shows a defect. Whether a re-tap pops the stack, whether a second re-tap scrolls to top, whether the status-bar tap works with nested horizontal shelves, and whether the selection binding's setter is even called for an unchanged value are all runtime behaviour of TabView/NavigationStack on iOS 18 and iOS 26 that cannot be read from source or from the still screenshots. The finding itself marks its evidence as needs-simulator-run and makes the fix conditional. Scope from code: on iPhone most pushed browse screens hide the tab bar (.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar) in category, All*, Recently Added, history and guide screens), so reselect from depth is reachable only from MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView, FavoritesView and Settings sub-screens (shots/iphone-light/M07-movie-detail.png shows the tab bar on a movie detail); on iPad with .sidebarAdaptable the tab control is always reachable.

**Corrected claim:** The app adds nothing of its own for tab re-tap or status-bar tap; whether the system already provides pop-to-root, scroll-to-top on re-tap and status-bar scroll-to-top on these screens is unknown until measured. It is a gap only for the behaviours the measurement shows missing.

**Corrected fix:** None until measured. Run the checks in how_to_verify on iPhone and iPad, iOS 18.x and iOS 26. Then implement only what is missing: for scroll-to-top on re-tap, the proposed reselect tick from a wrapped selection binding plus a top marker and ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo in each root, but only if check (5) shows the setter fires on an unchanged value (M3UDashboardView needs the same wrapper around its `$selectedTab`); for pop-to-root, NavigationStack(path:) per tab. If the status-bar tap is dead on the shelf roots there is no SwiftUI-level fix; report it rather than adding UIKit introspection. If everything already works, the correct fix is none.

**API check:** TabView(selection:) with Tab(_:systemImage:value:role:content:) and .sidebarAdaptable are already in use and compile against this SDK (iOS 18.0). No reselect API exists in SwiftUI.swiftinterface or SwiftUICore.swiftinterface (grep 'reselect' is empty). UITabBarControllerDelegate `tabBarController(_:didSelectTab:previousTab:)`: UITabBarController.h:162, API_AVAILABLE(ios(18.0)). UIScrollView.scrollsToTop and its rule: UIScrollView.h:264-267. ScrollPosition.scrollTo(edge:): SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:726, iOS 18.0. ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo(_:anchor:) is already used in the roots (LiveStreamsView.swift:253). NavigationStack(path:) / NavigationPath are iOS 16.0 (not re-grepped here; standard and below the deployment target).

**Regression risks:** Handling a re-tap that the system already handles produces a double action (pop plus scroll, or two competing scroll animations). Moving the stacks to NavigationStack(path:) touches every NavigationLink-based push and the navigationDestination(item:) sites (VODView.swift:161, EPGGuideView.swift:63) and can change the player hand-off that dismisses the overlay and pushes a detail (VODView.swift:231-243). A reselect tick passed through the environment invalidates every reader; keep it per tab. A custom binding must keep the existing persistence rule (Settings/Search are not persisted, DashboardView.swift:25-34).

**How to verify:** Simulator, iPhone and iPad, iOS 18.x and iOS 26, record per OS/device: (1) Movies, push a movie detail from a shelf, tap the Movies tab item again: does the stack pop to root, and is the root's scroll position unchanged? (2) At the Movies root scrolled five shelves down, tap Movies again: does it animate to the top with the large title expanded? (3) Same position, tap the status bar: does it scroll to top? (4) Repeat 1-3 on Live TV (shelves plus EPG lines), Series, Settings, Favorites pushed from the star, and the M3U Channels tab. (5) Temporary log in tabBinding.set: does it fire on a re-tap with the unchanged value? Only the behaviours that fail in this matrix are findings.

## gap-session-state-retention-6 — Changing the sort or a filter in the Series and Live TV grids leaves the user in the middle of the re-sorted list; only the Movies grid returns to the top

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series category grid, All Series, Live category grid, All Channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:615-627, 647-670, 678-680`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577, 600-621, 629-631`, `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:688-728`

**What the user perceives:** The user scrolls a few hundred series down, picks 'Name (A-Z)' and sees titles from somewhere in the middle of the alphabet with a spinner below, instead of the list starting at A. The same action in a Movies grid scrolls to the top first. Music and Files return to the top when the sort order changes.

**Mechanism (finder):** VODCategoryContent wraps its grid in a ScrollViewReader and scrolls to gridTopID on sortOption and fileTypeFilter changes (VODView.swift:688-728). SeriesCategoryContent (SeriesView.swift:647-670) and LiveCategoryContent (LiveStreamsView.swift:600-621) have no equivalent. Their recompute() replaces displayItems and resets visibleCount to one page (SeriesView.swift:623-625, LiveStreamsView.swift:574-575); the scroll view keeps its offset, clamps it to the now 90-item content, the last cells' onAppear call loadMore(), and the user ends up at an arbitrary place in the new order.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Give both grids the reader VODCategoryContent already has, and scroll when the new order lands rather than before it:

ScrollViewReader { proxy in
    ScrollView { LazyVGrid(...) { ... }.padding().id(Self.gridTopID) ... }
        .onChange(of: sortOption) { _, _ in pendingScrollToTop = true }
        .onChange(of: genreFilter) { _, _ in pendingScrollToTop = true }          // `filter.rawValue` in the Live grid
        .onChange(of: displayItems.first?.series.seriesId) { _, _ in consumeScrollToTop(proxy) }
}

Simplest variant: copy VODView.swift:719-728 verbatim, which scrolls on the option change itself. pendingScrollToTop can be a plain reference box so it does not invalidate the grid. No ScrollPosition binding here: a binding on the grid's ScrollView would re-evaluate a body that builds `Array(displayItems.prefix(visibleCount).enumerated())` on every drag start.

**APIs:** ScrollViewReader / ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo(_:anchor:) (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read all three grids. VODCategoryContent wraps its grid in ScrollViewReader, tags the LazyVGrid with .id(Self.gridTopID) and scrolls on sortOption / fileTypeFilter changes (Views/VODView.swift:627, 688-728). SeriesCategoryContent (Views/SeriesView.swift:647-670) and LiveCategoryContent (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:600-621) are plain ScrollViews with no reader; their recompute() swaps displayItems and resets visibleCount to one page (SeriesView.swift:623-625, LiveStreamsView.swift:574-575). Nothing resets the offset, so the scroll view keeps or clamps it. History: all three were written in the same commit 654cefc; the Series diff of that commit contains no scroll handling and no comment explaining an omission, so this is an oversight, not a decision. The grids are reused by SeriesCategoryDetailView, AllSeriesView, RecentlyAddedSeriesDetailView, LiveCategoryDetailView and AllLiveView, so the scope in the finding is right. Small correction to the perception text: after the clamp the user sits near the end of the first page (items ~75-95 of the new order, one extra page loaded by the onAppear at index >= visibleCount-15), or at the same pixel offset if he had not scrolled past page one; it is 'not at the top', not literally 'the middle of the alphabet'. The statement about Music/Files is not checkable from code. Additional adjacent defect found while reading: VOD's recompute has `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` (VODView.swift:662) but the Series and Live versions do not (SeriesView.swift:615-627, LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577), so a cancelled, slower sort can land after the newer one and leave the grid in an order that does not match the checked menu item.

**Corrected claim:** Changing the sort or a filter in the Series and Live TV grids (category grids, All Series, All Channels, Recently Added series) does not return to the top: the scroll offset is kept or clamped to the end of the first 90-item page, so the user sees items from some way into the new order. Only the Movies grid scrolls to the top. The same two grids also lack the cancellation guard the Movies grid has, so a superseded sort can overwrite a newer one.

**Corrected fix:** Use the finding's 'simplest variant', not the pendingScrollToTop variant: copy VODView.swift:688-689, 711 and 719-728 into both grids (ScrollViewReader around the ScrollView, `.id(Self.gridTopID)` on the padded LazyVGrid, `.onChange(of: sortOption)` and `.onChange(of: genreFilter)` / `.onChange(of: filter.rawValue)` calling `proxy.scrollTo(Self.gridTopID, anchor: .top)` in the same 0.25 s easeOut). The pendingScrollToTop variant keyed on `displayItems.first?.series.seriesId` must not be used: the first item often does not change (toggling a genre that the first item matches, default -> recently added on an already date-ordered list), so the scroll would silently not fire. While there, add `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` after the detached await in both recompute() functions, as in VODView.swift:662. No ScrollPosition binding (agreed with the finding: it would re-evaluate the grid body).

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:19346-19347 `@available(iOS 14.0, ...) @frozen public struct ScrollViewReader<Content>`; :19361-19364 `@available(iOS 14.0, ...) public struct ScrollViewProxy { public func scrollTo<ID>(_ id: ID, anchor: SwiftUICore.UnitPoint? = nil) where ID : Swift.Hashable }`. Both fine for the iOS 18 target; already used in VODView.swift.

**Regression risks:** Low. The Equatable signatures, off-main sorting and pagination are untouched. The scroll fires before the new order lands, so on a very large list the old order animates to the top and is then replaced (same as Movies today). If the grid is in the empty-state branch the reader is not mounted and the onChange is a no-op. Adding the cancellation guard means a recompute cancelled by the view disappearing leaves displayItems unchanged, which is what VOD already does.

**How to verify:** UI test with a fixture category of 300+ series: scroll several pages down, pick Name (A-Z), assert the first cell of the sorted order is hittable; repeat in a Live category with Name (Z-A) and with the catch-up filter. For the guard: on a 20k+ list switch Name (A-Z) -> Default quickly and assert the first cell matches Default order.
