## gap-session-state-retention-7 — The series detail keeps the season that was selected before playback even after next-episode or autoplay has moved into another season

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:803, 806, 916, 1030-1040, 1053-1063, 1106-1119, 1147-1165`, `another-iptv-player/Models/Requests.swift:501-522`, `another-iptv-player/Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:350, 472-475`

**What the user perceives:** The user starts S1E9, autoplay continues into S2E1 and S2E2, he closes the player: the page still shows Season 1 while the Resume button names a Season 2 episode. He has to find and tap Season 2 to see where he is. Popping and reopening the series does select Season 2. The TV app shows the season of the episode that is up next.

**Mechanism (finder):** What is kept, correctly: the detail stays mounted under the in-window overlay, so selectedSeasonId (SeriesView.swift:803), the page scroll offset and the plot's expanded flag (DetailComponents.swift:350) all survive playing and closing. What is missing: selectedSeasonId is written only by the season chips and by the one-time resolveInitialSeasonId (1030-1040). selectAdjacentEpisode (1147-1165) and the dismiss callback (`onDismiss: { selectedEpisode = nil }`, 916) never update it, although the episode they handle carries seasonId. On reopen, resolveInitialSeasonId (1106-1119) picks the season of the latest history entry and falls back to the first season: the right rule. It reads the @Query value `watchHistory`, whose ValueObservation publishes asynchronously (Requests.swift:507-520, default scheduling), from a Task started in the season bar's onAppear; if the seasons query lands first the screen opens on season 1 and nothing corrects it afterwards, because both call sites are gated on selectedSeasonId == nil. That window is small but real.

**Proposed fix (finder):** SeriesView.swift only. (1) Follow playback: in selectAdjacentEpisode's MainActor.run block (1159-1163) add `if seasons.contains(where: { $0.id == ep.seasonId }) { selectedSeasonId = ep.seasonId }`. In fullscreen the change is invisible; with the mini player the list follows what is playing. DetailSeasonTabBar already scrolls the chip into view on change (DetailComponents.swift:472-475) and EpisodesPanel reloads in place (SeriesView.swift:1348-1350). (2) Remove the race: let resolveInitialSeasonId read the latest history row inside its own AppDatabase.shared.read (same filter and order as LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest) instead of using the @Query property. Do not auto-scroll the page to the resumed episode on open: it would push the hero off screen during the push transition.

**Verifier reasons:** Claim verified. selectedSeasonId (Views/SeriesView.swift:803) is written only at 1033 and 1038 (both gated on == nil) and by the chips in DetailSeasonTabBar; grep shows no other writer. selectAdjacentEpisode (1147-1165) and the dismiss callback at 916 do not touch it, while the Resume label follows the live @Query watchHistory (812, 860-864), so after autoplay crosses a season the page shows the old season under a Resume button naming the new one. The supporting pieces exist: DBEpisode.seasonId is a non-optional String (Models/DBModels.swift:124), the tab bar scrolls the selected chip into view on change (Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:472-475), EpisodesPanel reloads on seasonId change (SeriesView.swift:1348-1350). The race is real: SeasonsRequest and LatestSeriesWatchHistoryRequest both use `.publisher(in:)` with GRDB's default `scheduling: .async(onQueue: .main)` (Models/Requests.swift:216-227, 507-520; GRDB ValueObservation.swift:485-487), so delivery order is not defined, and resolveInitialSeasonId reads the @Query value `watchHistory` (1107) from a Task started when the season bar appears; if seasons land first it returns seasons.first and nothing corrects it. The window is narrow (both observations start together and the Task adds a hop) so this part is rare. The proposed fix (1) needs correcting: setting selectedSeasonId unconditionally on every next/previous/auto-advance would yank the list back to the playing season whenever the user, with the mini player docked, is browsing another season of the same series (e.g. looking at Season 3 while S1E3 auto-advances to S1E4).

**Corrected claim:** The series detail does not follow playback across a season boundary: after next-episode or autoplay moves into another season the page still shows the season selected before playback while the Resume button names an episode of the new season. Separately, on open the initial season can (rarely) fall back to season 1 despite existing history, because it is resolved from an asynchronously delivered @Query value.

**Corrected fix:** SeriesView.swift only. (1) In selectAdjacentEpisode's MainActor.run block, follow only when the list was showing the season that was playing: `if let playing = selectedEpisode?.0, playing.seasonId == selectedSeasonId, ep.seasonId != playing.seasonId, seasons.contains(where: { $0.id == ep.seasonId }) { selectedSeasonId = ep.seasonId }` placed before `selectedEpisode = (ep, resumable)`. A user who deliberately switched to another season while the mini player runs is left alone. (2) As proposed: resolveInitialSeasonId fetches the latest history row itself inside its AppDatabase.shared.read (filter seriesId == String(series.seriesId) && playlistId == playlist.id, order lastWatchedAt desc, fetchOne) and then the episode, instead of reading the @Query property. No auto-scroll of the page (agreed).

**API check:** No new SDK API. Uses existing @State, GRDB `AppDatabase.shared.read`, and the existing onChange handlers in DetailSeasonTabBar and EpisodesPanel.

**Regression risks:** With the unconditional version from the finding: the episode list jumps away from a season the user is browsing next to the mini player; avoided by the guard above. With the guarded version: a season change while fullscreen reloads EpisodesPanel under the overlay (one DB read, invisible). The closures captured by PlayerView hold a copy of the view struct; writes go to the live @State storage while the detail is still mounted and are no-ops after it is popped. Player files are not touched.

**How to verify:** UI test with the demo series: play the last episode of season 1 from the Season 1 list, press next, close the player, assert the Season 2 chip is selected. Second test: start an episode, minimize, select Season 3 by hand, press next on the mini player, assert Season 3 stays selected. Race: unit-test the extracted resolver against a seeded DB (history in season 3 returns the season 3 id).

## gap-session-state-retention-8 — M3U channels: returning to the list while a search is active first repaints the full unfiltered list, then filters again

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: M3U channels
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:112-149, 228-260`

**What the user perceives:** The user searches 'sport', opens a group or plays into a pushed screen, comes back: for a moment every group of the playlist is on screen under a search field that still says 'sport', then the list collapses back to the matches. With a few thousand groups the swap is clearly visible and the shelves the user was looking at are recreated.

**Mechanism (finder):** `.onAppear { applyFull() }` (M3UChannelsView.swift:141) runs on every appear, not only the first, and applyFull() (145-149) unconditionally assigns the full groupNames / channelsByGroup. On the same appear `.task(id: debouncedQuery)` (136) restarts recomputeFilter(), which re-applies the query in a detached task (242-259) and assigns the filtered result some milliseconds to hundreds of milliseconds later. searchText and debouncedQuery are @State and still hold the query. The Xtream roots do not have this path: they have no onAppear reset.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One line: `.onAppear { if debouncedQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty { applyFull() } }`. The first appear (empty query) is unchanged, a return with an active query leaves the filtered arrays alone, and the task re-run produces an equal result that the Equatable rows ignore.

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Views/M3UChannelsView.swift. `.onAppear { applyFull() }` (141) is unconditional and applyFull (145-149) assigns the full store.groupNames / channelsByGroup. onAppear of a NavigationStack root fires again on every pop back to it and on every re-selection of its tab; `.task(id: debouncedQuery)` (136) is restarted on the same appear and, for a non-empty query, only assigns the filtered result after `await Task.detached(...)` (242-259). searchText / debouncedQuery are @State and still hold the query, so at least one frame (up to tens or hundreds of ms on a large M3U) renders every group under a search field that still shows the query; non-matching rows are inserted and removed again around the rows the user was on. A push is possible while searching: the shelf header is a NavigationLink to M3UGroupDetailView (337-339). Playing a channel does NOT trigger it (the player is an in-window overlay, 267-273), so the 'plays into a pushed screen' wording is wrong; the Channels -> Settings -> Channels tab switch is a second real trigger the finding does not mention. History: the line dates from 2849d94 and has no comment; its only function is filling the first frame synchronously so the 'no result' placeholder (50-59) does not flash before the task runs. The Xtream roots have no such onAppear (LiveStreamsView.swift:93-107, VODView.swift:145-159, SeriesView.swift:146-160), as stated. One assumption cannot be settled from code: that the search stays presented across the push (UISearchController normally does; if it were dismissed, 128-135 would clear the query and there would be no flash, and the fix would be a harmless no-op). The swap starts at the beginning of the pop transition, so part of it is hidden under the departing screen; visible on an interactive swipe-back and on tab re-selection.

**Corrected claim:** M3U channels: coming back to the list (pop from a group, or switching back from the Settings tab) while a search query is active first re-assigns the full unfiltered group list and then filters again, because onAppear unconditionally calls applyFull().

**Corrected fix:** As proposed, one line at M3UChannelsView.swift:141: `.onAppear { if debouncedQuery.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty { applyFull() } }`. First appear (empty query) still fills the first frame synchronously; with an active query the filtered arrays are left alone and the restarted task produces an equal result.

**API check:** No SDK API involved.

**Regression risks:** Minimal. If the store's channels changed while the screen was away, `.onChange(of: store.channels)` (137-140) and the restarted `.task(id: debouncedQuery)` still re-apply the current query, so nothing goes stale. The first-frame fill that the line exists for is kept.

**How to verify:** Simulator, M3U fixture with several groups: search a term matching one group, open that group from the shelf header, go back with a slow interactive swipe, and assert no non-matching group header exists during the pop and the 500 ms after it. Repeat with Channels -> Settings -> Channels. In the same run confirm isSearchActive stays true across the push; if it does not, the query is being cleared at 128-135 and that is the behaviour to fix instead.

## gap-session-state-retention-9 — Choosing a language rebuilds the whole app and drops the user from Settings onto the last content tab, closing any running or minimized player

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings > Language, Dashboard
- Code: `another-iptv-player/another_iptv_playerApp.swift:47-67`, `another-iptv-player/Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:37-39`, `another-iptv-player/Views/DashboardView.swift:8, 16-23, 200-216`, `another-iptv-player/Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:11, 14`, `another-iptv-player/ContentView.swift:17-18, 152-163`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Is landing on the Settings root enough, or should the language list itself stay on screen? The second needs a path-bound Settings stack.

**What the user perceives:** The user taps a language in Settings > Language and finds himself on Live TV (or whichever content tab was last used) in the new language, with every tab's stack, search text and scroll position reset and the mini player gone. Apps with an in-app language switch stay on the language screen.

**Mechanism (finder):** AppRootView applies `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66). The comment above it (47-51) says this is deliberate so every L() string re-resolves. The new identity recreates ContentView (selectedPlaylist and hasAttemptedAutoLoad start over, ContentView.swift:17-18, 152-163) and DashboardView, whose initial tab comes from restoreInitialTab(), which by design never returns Settings (DashboardView.swift:200-216), and whose @StateObject PlayerOverlayController (line 8) is recreated, which removes the player. M3UDashboardView always starts on tab 0 (line 14).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep the rebuild, restore the place. Add a one-shot hint that the dashboards consume in init: in LanguagePickerSection.swift:38 set a static `DashboardLaunchHint.pendingSettings = true` before assigning manager.selectedLanguage (only when the code actually changes); in DashboardView.init use `.settings` as the initial selectedTab when the hint is set and clear it, without touching savedTab; in M3UDashboardView initialise selectedTab to 1 the same way. The user then lands on Settings in the new language. The Settings views themselves are not edited. Keeping playback alive across the switch would mean hoisting PlayerOverlayController above the `.id`, which belongs to the player hand-off work.

**Verifier reasons:** Claim verified. AppRootView applies `.id(localization.selectedLanguage)` to ContentView (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:56-67) and the comment at 51-55 says the rebuild is deliberate. LanguagePickerListView sets manager.selectedLanguage on tap (Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:37-39). The new identity resets ContentView's selectedPlaylist / hasAttemptedAutoLoad (ContentView.swift:17-18), attemptAutoLoad re-selects the last playlist (152-163), DashboardView.init takes DashboardTab.restoreInitialTab(), which never returns Settings (Views/DashboardView.swift:16-23, 200-216), and the @StateObject PlayerOverlayController is recreated (DashboardView.swift:8, M3UDashboardView.swift:11), which removes any running or mini player. M3UDashboardView starts on tab 0 (M3UDashboardView.swift:14). The picker is only reachable from the two dashboard settings screens (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:128, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:123), so a hint set there cannot be raised from the playlist list. Two corrections. (a) The 'native' comparison is weak: the system per-app language switch (Settings app) terminates and relaunches the app, so losing place is what Apple's own mechanism does; the gap is against other apps with an in-app switch, and it is a rare action. (b) The proposed mechanism has a flaw: consuming and clearing a static flag inside View.init is a side effect in an initializer that SwiftUI may call more than once per identity, and a flag set when the tapped language is already selected (no id change) or when auto-load does not reach a dashboard stays armed and would send the next dashboard open to Settings.

**Corrected claim:** Choosing a language in Settings > Language rebuilds the whole hierarchy (deliberately) and lands the user on the last content tab (Xtream) or Channels (M3U) instead of Settings; all tab stacks, search text and scroll positions are reset and a running or minimized player is closed. Low frequency; the system's own per-app language switch also restarts the app.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the `.id` rebuild. Make the hint side-effect free and self-expiring: a small internal type, e.g. `enum DashboardLaunchHint { static var settingsRequestedAt: Date?; static var wantsSettings: Bool { settingsRequestedAt.map { Date().timeIntervalSince($0) < 2 } ?? false } }`. In LanguagePickerSection.swift:38 set `DashboardLaunchHint.settingsRequestedAt = Date()` only when `lang.code != manager.selectedLanguage`, before the assignment. DashboardView.init: `_selectedTab = State(initialValue: DashboardLaunchHint.wantsSettings ? .settings : DashboardTab.restoreInitialTab())` (savedTab untouched, so the next launch still opens the last content tab). M3UDashboardView: `@State private var selectedTab: Int = DashboardLaunchHint.wantsSettings ? 1 : 0`. No clearing in init; the 2 s expiry covers repeated inits and stale flags. Settings views and the tip-jar row are not edited. Keeping playback alive across the switch (hoisting PlayerOverlayController above the `.id`) is a separate, larger change that belongs to the player hand-off and is not recommended here.

**API check:** No new SDK API: State(initialValue:), a static property and Date. Nothing iOS 26-only.

**Regression risks:** With the finding's version: an armed flag that is never consumed opens the next dashboard on Settings, and a read-and-clear in init can be consumed by a throwaway init. With the time-bound version: a second dashboard opened within 2 s of a language change would also start on Settings, which cannot happen through the UI. The deliberate synchronous tab restore (DashboardView.swift:19-22) and the 'M3U always starts on Channels' rule (M3UDashboardView.swift:13) stay in force for normal launches. The player is still closed by the rebuild; that is unchanged, not fixed.

**How to verify:** UI test: Settings > Language > Deutsch, assert the Settings tab is selected and its title reads 'Einstellungen'; terminate and relaunch, assert the app opens on the last content tab. Repeat on an M3U playlist. Tap the already-selected language, leave to the playlist list, reopen the playlist after more than 2 s and assert it opens on the content tab.

## gap-session-state-retention-10 — One sort choice per content type applies to every category, to All Movies / All Series / All Channels, to Recently Added and to every playlist

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies category grid, Series category grid, Live category grid, All Movies / All Series / All Channels, Recently Added
- Code: `another-iptv-player/Views/VODView.swift:357-377, 610-613`, `another-iptv-player/Views/SeriesView.swift:334-354, 580-582`, `another-iptv-player/Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:543-545`, `another-iptv-player/Models/VODSortOption.swift:6-17`, `another-iptv-player/Models/SeriesSortOption.swift:6-16`, `another-iptv-player/Models/LiveSortOption.swift:15-21`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Sort scope: (A) keep one sort per content type for the whole app (current behaviour, matches Music's library lists; recommended, with Recently Added exempted), (B) remember it per category and playlist (matches Files folders and Music playlists, more keys to manage), or (C) per playlist. Also: should genre / file-type / catch-up filters survive leaving the grid? Today they do not, which is what Apple's apps do.

**What the user perceives:** The user sorts 'Kids' by Name (A-Z); from then on every movie category, All Movies and every other playlist open sorted by name, and the 'Recently Added' screen lists its 20 newest titles alphabetically, which contradicts its title. An inline search in a grid is also ordered by the stored sort instead of relevance. Filters reset when the grid is popped.

**Mechanism (finder):** sortOption is `@AppStorage` under one key per content type: 'vod.sortOption', 'series.sortOption', 'live.sortOption' (VODView.swift:610, SeriesView.swift:580, LiveStreamsView.swift:543). This is deliberate: git log -S on the keys leads to 654cefc ('Sort menus ... with per-screen filters'), and the neighbouring comments mark the filters as screen-local on purpose (VODView.swift:611-613, SeriesView.swift:581-582, LiveStreamsView.swift:544-545). RecentlyAddedVODDetailView and RecentlyAddedSeriesDetailView reuse the same content views (VODView.swift:376, SeriesView.swift:353) and inherit the stored sort. Lifetime of the @State filters and of a pushed grid's search text: kept across a detail push and return and across tab switches (the grid stays on the stack), lost on pop. Apple reference: Music keeps one sort per library list, persisted, and a separate sort per playlist; Files keeps it per folder; filters are session-scoped in both.

**Proposed fix (finder):** The scope is the owner's call. Independent of it, one small fix: Recently Added should not apply the stored sort. Add `var allowsSorting = true` to VODCategoryContent and SeriesCategoryContent, pass false from the two Recently Added screens, and when false use `.defaultOrder` and hide the Picker in the menu (the file-type or genre filter can stay). If the owner wants per-category sort, build the key from the context, e.g. `AppStorage(wrappedValue: .defaultOrder, "vod.sortOption.\(playlist.id.uuidString).\(categoryId)")` created in the view's init, with the global key as the default and removal of the keys on playlist delete next to ContentView.swift:270-278.

**APIs:** AppStorage(wrappedValue:_:store:) for RawRepresentable String values (iOS 14.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The facts are right. sortOption is @AppStorage under one global key per content type: 'vod.sortOption' (Models/VODSortOption.swift:17, Views/VODView.swift:610), 'series.sortOption' (Models/SeriesSortOption.swift:16, Views/SeriesView.swift:580), 'live.sortOption' (Models/LiveSortOption.swift, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:543), with no playlist or category in the key, so it applies to every category, to the All-* screens and to every playlist. git log -S on the keys leads to 654cefc, whose message says 'Sort menus ... with per-screen filters', and the comments at VODView.swift:611-613, SeriesView.swift:581-582, LiveStreamsView.swift:544-545 mark the filters as screen-local on purpose. So the scope is a deliberate design, not a defect, and most of this finding is a product decision rather than a fix. Ordering an inline search by the stored sort is also by design: `.defaultOrder` is documented as 'preserve caller's ordering (sortIndex or search relevance)' (VODSortOption.swift:7-9). The one concrete inconsistency stands: RecentlyAddedVODDetailView / RecentlyAddedSeriesDetailView pass their 20 newest items (VODView.swift:180-190 builds them newest-first with prefix(20)) into the same content views (VODView.swift:376, SeriesView.swift:353), which apply the stored sort, so with Name (A-Z) stored the 'Recently Added' screen is alphabetical. The Apple comparisons (Music, Files) are not verifiable from code. iphone-light/M05-movies-sort-menu.png confirms the menu content (Default / Name / Rating / Recently Added).

**Corrected claim:** Sort is stored once per content type for the whole app by design (654cefc); filters are screen-local by design. The only behaviour that reads as a bug is that the 'Recently Added' full-list screens (Movies and Series, 20 items) inherit that stored sort and can therefore show their items in an order that contradicts the title. Whether sort should be remembered per category or per playlist is an owner decision, not a fix.

**Corrected fix:** Fix only the Recently Added exemption: add `var allowsSorting = true` to VODCategoryContent and SeriesCategoryContent (memberwise default, existing call sites unchanged; the custom == needs no change because the value is constant per call site), pass `allowsSorting: false` from the two Recently Added screens, and inside the content view use `let sort = allowsSorting ? sortOption : .defaultOrder` in recompute() and in isFilterActive, and omit the sort Picker from the menu when false (keep the file-type / genre filter section; if no filter options exist, hide the toolbar item so no empty menu is shown). Leave the global sort scope as it is unless the owner chooses otherwise; do not build per-category keys speculatively (the content views do not receive a category id today, and per-key cleanup on playlist delete would be new surface).

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:7512-7513 `@available(iOS 14.0, ...) @frozen @propertyWrapper public struct AppStorage<Value>`; :7556 `public init(wrappedValue: Value, _ key: Swift.String, store: Foundation.UserDefaults? = nil) where Value : Swift.RawRepresentable, Value.RawValue == Swift.String` (the finding listed this as not verified; it is present, iOS 14.0). Only needed if the owner picks per-category / per-playlist scope; the Recently Added exemption needs no API.

**Regression risks:** Exemption: users lose the ability to re-sort the 20-item Recently Added screen (e.g. by rating); acceptable for a list whose title is its order, but it is a small product choice. `.task(id: sortOption)` still fires there and recomputes to the same result (harmless). Per-category keys, if chosen later: many UserDefaults keys, a new init parameter on the Equatable content views, and All-* / search contexts need their own key rule; this would change behaviour users may already rely on.

**How to verify:** UI test: set Name (A-Z) in a movie category, go back, open Recently Added from the Movies home, assert the first card is the newest title of the fixture and the menu shows no sort section; same for Series. Then confirm a normal category still opens with Name (A-Z) applied.

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-1 — After returning to the app, Live TV keeps the pre-background now/next lines for up to 60 s, and a guide older than its 6 h TTL is never refreshed without a relaunch

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Live category grids, All Channels, Favorites (live), M3U Channels
- Code: `EPG/EPGStore.swift:73-78, 116-133, 137-168, 431-442`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:130-137`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:84-90`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:72-79`, `EPG/EPGModels.swift:84-87`

**What the user perceives:** The user opens the app the next morning (process still in memory). Every channel card still shows last night's programme title with the progress bar frozen where it was; cards scrolled in show the old title with an empty bar. This lasts until the next wall-clock minute boundary (1-60 s, about 30 s on average), then all cards flip at once. If the app stays in memory for days, the guide itself is never downloaded again: Settings shows 'Last updated 2 days ago' and, once the provider feed's horizon is passed, the now-lines turn into blank reserved space and the guide shows empty rows.

**Mechanism (finder):** (a) didBecomeActive only calls startTimerIfActive (EPGStore.swift:76-78). The timer loop sleeps first and ticks second (118-126): delay = max(1, nextBoundary - now) (121-123), so the first tick after resume is 1-60 s away. Until then `snapshot` is the one published before backgrounding. The card derives its bar from `programme.progress(at: Date())` at body time (EPGComponents.swift:73), which returns nil once now >= stop (EPGModels.swift:85) -> fraction 0; cards that are not re-evaluated keep the old bar. (b) refreshIfStale has three callers: the dashboards' `.task(id: playlist.id)` (DashboardView.swift:131-137, M3UDashboardView.swift:85-90), which runs once per dashboard mount and not on foreground, and the settings toggle (EPGSettingsSections.swift:163). Nothing checks the 6 h TTL (EPGConstants.swift:11) on resume. (c) The retry cooldown only applies when there has never been a success (EPGStore.swift:436-437: `src.lastSuccessAt == nil`), so once refreshIfStale is called on every foreground a dead panel would be re-tried each time. grep confirms no scenePhase use anywhere in the app.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1) EPGStore: tick immediately when the timer is restarted after a background stay. In the didBecomeActive handler: `Task { @MainActor in guard let self, self.activePlaylistId != nil else { return }; if self.tickTask == nil { await self.tick() }; self.startTimerIfActive() }`. The `tickTask == nil` test keeps Control Center / notification-banner activations (inactive -> active, timer never stopped) from publishing an extra snapshot and re-rendering every card.
2) Check the TTL on foreground, driven by scenePhase, shared by both dashboards:
```swift
@Environment(\.scenePhase) private var scenePhase
.onChange(of: scenePhase) { _, phase in
    guard phase == .active else { return }
    Task { await epgStore.refreshIfStale(playlistId: playlist.id) }
}
```
Add `refreshIfStale(playlistId:)` to EPGStore that reads the Playlist row fresh from the database (`Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: id)`) and forwards to the existing function, because the dashboard's `playlist` value is a frozen copy (swiftui-invalidation-7) and its epgEnabled / EPG URL may be out of date. refreshIfStale is one small read when the guide is fresh.
3) Make the cooldown cover failures after a success: `if let attempt = src.fetchedAt, attempt > (src.lastSuccessAt ?? .distantPast), Date().timeIntervalSince(attempt) < EPGConstants.retryCooldown { return }` (recordAttempt already writes fetchedAt up front, EPGRefreshCoordinator.swift:36).
No iOS 26 API; identical on iOS 18. Leave stopTimer on didEnterBackground and the once-a-minute publish as they are.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues.scenePhase / ScenePhase (iOS 14.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5553, 5569)); View.onChange(of:initial:_:) with (oldValue, newValue) (iOS 17.0+ (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827)); UIApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification (iOS 4.0+ (UIApplication.h:554), already used)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed by reading. EPG/EPGStore.swift:73-78: didEnterBackground stops the timer, didBecomeActive only calls startTimerIfActive. EPGStore.swift:118-126: the loop sleeps to the next minute boundary (max 1 s) before its first tick, so after a background stay the published snapshot is the pre-background one for 1-60 s. Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:73 + EPG/EPGModels.swift:84-87: a programme that ended while backgrounded yields progress nil -> empty bar under the old title. TTL: refreshIfStale has exactly three callers (Views/DashboardView.swift:136, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:89, Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:163); the two dashboard ones sit in .task(id: playlist.id) and do not re-run on foreground. grep finds no scenePhase / willEnterForeground use outside PlayerView. Cooldown: EPGStore.swift:436-437 requires lastSuccessAt == nil, and EPGRefreshCoordinator.swift:280-286 writes fetchedAt before the download while recordSuccess (289-305) writes fetchedAt then lastSuccessAt, so the proposed `attempt > lastSuccessAt` test is sound. No comment or history marks any of this as deliberate (the minute publish and stop-in-background are deliberate and the fix keeps them). Corrections: (1) severity is over-rated: short background stays leave the title unchanged and the bar is recomputed from Date() at body time; the stale line only shows when a programme boundary was crossed and heals itself within 60 s. The multi-day in-memory case needs the process to survive, which is uncommon for an app that holds a 100k-row catalog in memory. (2) The scenePhase hook in the dashboards has a real hazard: the dashboards deliberately call refreshIfStale only after the catalog load ('Runs after the catalog load so the wanted-channel set is populated', DashboardView.swift:133-134). A scenePhase-driven refresh during the first catalog download (user leaves and returns while 'Preparing...' is up) runs gatherWanted (EPGRefreshCoordinator.swift:146-167) against an empty liveStream table, which ends either in emptyGuide or in a 'successful' empty guide that the 6 h TTL then protects. (3) The proposed handler ticks before restarting the timer; a didEnterBackground arriving during that await leaves a timer running in background.

**Corrected claim:** After a background stay that crossed a programme boundary, Live TV / M3U channel cards keep the pre-background now-line (old title, empty bar) until the next wall-clock minute (1-60 s), because the resume handler restarts a timer that sleeps before its first tick. Separately, the 6 h guide TTL is only checked when a dashboard mounts, so a process that stays alive for more than 6 h never refreshes the guide until relaunch, and the retry cooldown does not cover a failure that follows an earlier success.

**Corrected fix:** Do all of it inside EPGStore, no scenePhase in the dashboards. In the didBecomeActive handler: `Task { @MainActor [weak self] in guard let self, let pid = self.activePlaylistId else { return }; let wasStopped = self.tickTask == nil; self.startTimerIfActive(); guard wasStopped else { return }; await self.tick(); await self.refreshIfStale(playlistId: pid) }`. activePlaylistId is only set after the catalog load (DashboardView.swift:135, M3UDashboardView.swift:88), so this keeps the 'after catalog load' ordering, and `wasStopped` keeps Control Center / banner activations from publishing an extra snapshot. Add `refreshIfStale(playlistId:)` that reads the Playlist row fresh (`Playlist.fetchOne(db, key: id)`, same call shape as DBEPGSource.fetchOne(db, key:) at EPGStore.swift:104) and forwards to the existing function. Change the cooldown test at EPGStore.swift:436 to `if let attempt = src.fetchedAt, attempt > (src.lastSuccessAt ?? .distantPast), Date().timeIntervalSince(attempt) < EPGConstants.retryCooldown { return }`. Leave stopTimer on background and the once-a-minute publish as they are. Same on iOS 18 and 26.

**API check:** No new SwiftUI API needed in the corrected fix. UIApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification already used at EPG/EPGStore.swift:76. For the original proposal: `public var scenePhase: SwiftUI.ScenePhase` SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5569 (@available iOS 14.0), `enum ScenePhase` :5553 (iOS 14.0); `View.onChange<V>(of:initial:_:)` with (oldValue, newValue) SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827 (iOS 17.0). All present.

**Regression risks:** A guide refresh (download + XMLTV parse + batched writes) can now start on foreground while a stream is playing or in PiP; the same already happens at launch and the work is off-main (EPGRefreshCoordinator is nonisolated), but watch playback smoothness during the parse on a large feed. The immediate tick publishes one extra snapshot per real foreground, re-rendering visible cards once. The wider cooldown also makes the Settings toggle's refreshIfStale a no-op for 15 min after a failed attempt (the Refresh button uses forceRefresh and is unaffected).

**How to verify:** Unit (in-memory AppDatabase): seed an epgSource row with lastSuccessAt 7 h ago and fetchedAt 1 min ago, assert refreshIfStale returns without calling runRefresh; with fetchedAt 20 min ago assert it proceeds. Assert the resume path bumps snapshot.version without waiting for the timer. Simulator: seed a programme that ends in 1 minute, background the app for 2 minutes, reopen and check the card shows the new title in the first second (before the fix: up to 60 s). Set epgSource.lastSuccessAt to 7 h ago while backgrounded, reopen, expect refreshState to go .refreshing without relaunch. Also background and return during the first catalog download of a new playlist and confirm no guide refresh starts before the catalog is stored.

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-2 — A downloaded film or episode cannot be started offline from its own detail page once the catalog has been refreshed, because a refresh discards every cached film detail and every series' seasons and episodes

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Downloads
- Code: `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:531-548, 550-581`, `Database/AppDatabase.swift:85-109`, `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:74-81, 99-103, 190-199, 268-312`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:823-825, 868-875, 892-896, 1176-1247`, `Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:25-31`, `Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:66-76`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Change B for series: keep fetched seasons and episodes for every series across a refresh (then the detail page should re-fetch in the background when online so new episodes still appear, since a refresh is today the only thing that invalidates them), or only for series that have downloaded episodes (smaller, covers the offline case, leaves today's 'refresh re-fetches episodes' behaviour for everything else)? Recommended: only series with downloads, plus all films.

**What the user perceives:** Airplane-mode journey, traced in code. Cold launch into the last playlist: works, the catalog loads from SQLite only (PlaylistContentStore.swift:114-116, 280-285). Shelves: text and cached posters appear, uncached posters stay placeholders (requests fail at once, CachedImage.swift:23). Film with cached metadata: page opens, a downloaded film plays from the local file. Film without cached metadata: one frame of content, then a full-screen red 'Network error' page with only 'Try Again' (shots S03-series-detail-loading.png shows the same page for series); no Play and no Download button, even when the film is fully downloaded. Series: the same page; after a refresh the episode rows no longer exist locally, so downloaded episodes cannot be reached from the series at all. On a connected-but-dead network the same pages show a full-screen spinner for up to 20 s first. The only working route is Settings > Downloads (or a Continue Watching card). Settings itself opens with an error row and without Statistics / TV Guide / Content sections (settings-ux-1); a live channel tap opens the player, which fails there.

**Mechanism (finder):** 1) 'Cached' is rarer than it looks. replaceVODCatalog deletes every vodStream row and re-inserts list fields only (PlaylistContentStore.swift:536, 544-546), so metadataLoaded returns to its default false (DBModels.swift:54) for every film. replaceSeriesCatalog deletes every series row (555); season rows cascade from series and episode rows from season (AppDatabase.swift:93, 107-108; GRDB foreignKeysEnabled defaults to true), and seasonsLoaded resets to false. This runs on every pull-to-refresh (VODView.swift:95, SeriesView.swift:96), on Settings > Refresh all and automatically when the adult filter is toggled (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:504). The owner's comment at HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:66 records the cascade. 2) With the flag false, `.task` calls the panel (MovieDetailView.swift:99-103; SeriesView.swift:892-896); offline the request throws immediately, errorMessage is set and the body shows errorView instead of contentScroll (MovieDetailView.swift:77-78; SeriesView.swift:871-872), although playback needs only streamId and containerExtension and presentMoviePlayer already resolves the local file (190-199). 3) The series race is real in principle and I could not decide its outcome by reading: fetchSeriesInfo writes seasonsLoaded only to the database (1222-1237) and there is no series counterpart of applyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:164), so for every series opened since the catalog was loaded the passed-in `series` still says false. `currentSeries` is `seriesRecord ?? series` (823-825) and SeriesByIDRequest delivers its first value through GRDB's default `.async(onQueue: .main)` scheduling (Requests.swift:204; ValueObservation.swift:487). The `.task` body and that delivery are both main-queue jobs; whichever is enqueued first wins. If the task wins while offline, the error page replaces a series whose seasons and episodes are all in the database. Because the process can live for days, this affects exactly the 'still in memory next morning' case. Existing findings states-loading-empty-error-3, movies-browse-detail-1 and series-browse-detail-1 already propose always rendering the content; this finding adds the refresh wipe and the offline consequence.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Prerequisite: the 'always render contentScroll, show the error only inside the seasons block and only when no cached seasons exist' change from states-loading-empty-error-3 / series-browse-detail-1. With it a downloaded film is playable offline with no further work.
A) Decide the refetch from the database row, not from the catalog copy (removes the race):
```swift
.task {
    let loaded = (try? await AppDatabase.shared.read { db in
        try Bool.fetchOne(db, sql: "SELECT seasonsLoaded FROM series WHERE seriesId = ? AND playlistId = ?",
                          arguments: [series.seriesId, playlist.id]) }) ?? false
    if loaded != true { await fetchSeriesInfo() }
}
```
B) Keep fetched detail across a refresh, inside the existing single write transaction. Films: before the DELETE read `DBVODStream.filter(playlistId == pid && metadataLoaded == true).fetchAll(db)` (only titles the user has opened), and after the inserts write the eleven metadata columns plus metadataLoaded back with a column-scoped `updateAll` per kept row that still exists. Series: before the DELETE fetch the DBSeason and DBEpisode rows of the series to keep, re-insert them after the series rows for ids that still exist and set seasonsLoaded = 1 plus the detail columns.
C) Safety net in SeriesDetailView for the offline case: when `seasons.isEmpty && errorMessage != nil`, list this series' completed downloads from `downloadedItem` (seriesId, seasonNumber, episodeNumber, title are stored, DBModels.swift:218-220) as a 'Downloaded' section whose rows play the local file through the existing presentEpisodeOverlay path.
The replace* helpers are private static; make them internal for tests as was done for fetchNowIndex. No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView (for the inline error state from the prerequisite finding) (iOS 17.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17575))

**Verifier reasons:** Refresh wipe confirmed. Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:536 deletes every vodStream row and 544-546 re-inserts list fields only, so metadataLoaded falls back to false (Models/DBModels.swift:54). :555 deletes every series row; season cascades from series and episode from season (Database/AppDatabase.swift:93, 107-108); Database/Persistence.swift:99-100 uses a default GRDB Configuration and GRDB's Configuration.swift:28 has foreignKeysEnabled = true. The owner's own comment at Views/HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:66 records the cascade. Triggers: pull-to-refresh (Views/VODView.swift:95-99, Views/SeriesView.swift:96-100) and the adult-filter toggle (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:504). Offline consequence confirmed: Views/MovieDetailView.swift:99-103 fetches when metadataLoaded is false, the catch at 307-311 sets errorMessage and the body at 74-81 then shows errorView instead of contentScroll, although presentMoviePlayer (190-199) resolves the local file and needs no metadata. Series is identical (Views/SeriesView.swift:868-875, 892-896, 1241-1246), and after a refresh the episode rows are gone, so the downloaded episodes cannot be listed. Screenshot iphone-dark/S03-series-detail-loading.png shows exactly this full-screen error page with only Try Again (there with the fixture's HTTP 404). Timeout 20 s confirmed at Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:28. DownloadsView is reachable from Settings (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:90) so a working route exists. The series race is real in principle and not decidable by reading: `series` comes from the in-memory catalog, there is no series counterpart of applyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:164), and SeriesByIDRequest (Models/Requests.swift:197-206) delivers asynchronously. Corrections: severity is medium, not high (needs downloads + a user-initiated refresh after downloading + offline + entering through the catalog rather than Downloads). Fix B as written for series sets seasonsLoaded = 1 on preserved rows, which freezes the episode list of exactly the shows a user follows: nothing would re-fetch them again.

**Corrected claim:** A catalog refresh (pull-to-refresh on Movies or Series, Refresh all, adult-filter toggle) discards every cached film detail flag and every series' season and episode rows. Offline, the film and series detail pages then replace their whole content with a full-screen error, so a downloaded film has no Play button on its own page and downloaded episodes are not listed under their series; Settings > Downloads still plays them. Within one session a re-opened series may also re-fetch (and fail offline) even though its seasons are stored; whether it does depends on a main-queue ordering that only a run can settle.

**Corrected fix:** Prerequisite from the other findings: always render contentScroll; show the fetch error inline, and for series only when no cached seasons exist. That alone makes a downloaded film playable offline. A) as proposed: decide the refetch from the database row (`Bool.fetchOne(db, sql: "SELECT seasonsLoaded FROM series WHERE seriesId = ? AND playlistId = ?", ...)`, or the DBSeries filter already used at HistorySeriesPlayerShell.swift:67-72). B) films: before the DELETE read the rows with metadataLoaded = true into a [streamId: DBVODStream] dictionary and copy the eleven metadata fields plus the flag into dbVOD inside the existing insert loop (no second write pass). B) series: inside the same transaction read DBSeason / DBEpisode rows before the DELETE and re-insert them after the series rows for ids that still exist, but leave seasonsLoaded = false. The detail page then shows the cached seasons at once, re-fetches in the background when online (new episodes still arrive, as today) and offline keeps the cached list with at most an inline notice. Scope of what to keep (all opened series, or only series with downloads) is the owner's call; with seasonsLoaded left false either choice is safe. C) the extra 'Downloaded' section is new UI and optional once B is in; it only helps users whose rows were already wiped. Make the replace* helpers internal for tests. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** `public struct ContentUnavailableView<Label, Description, Actions>` SwiftUI.swiftinterface:17575, @available iOS 17.0; already used in the app (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:81). GRDB `Bool.fetchOne(db, sql:arguments:)` and `Record.fetchOne(db, key:)` are already used in this code base (EPG/EPGStore.swift:104). No other platform API involved.

**Regression risks:** replaceVODCatalog / replaceSeriesCatalog run for 50k-150k rows in one write transaction; the extra read must stay limited to opened titles (metadataLoaded = true) and to season/episode rows, otherwise refresh time grows. Preserved film metadata is never invalidated again (today a refresh forces a re-fetch); acceptable for static film data, but say so. Re-inserted episode rows that the panel has since removed stay until the next successful detail fetch, because fetchSeriesInfo upserts and never deletes (SeriesView.swift:1202, 1217). The prerequisite change touches the detail pages' loading states, which other findings also rework: do them together. fetchSeriesInfo writes back the stale passed-in `series` copy (SeriesView.swift:1222), so preserved detail columns can be overwritten by that copy; keep that in mind when testing.

**How to verify:** Unit (in-memory AppDatabase): insert a film with metadataLoaded = true and a series with seasons and episodes, run replaceVODCatalog / replaceSeriesCatalog with the same ids, assert metadata, seasons and episodes survive, seasonsLoaded is false, and rows whose id disappeared are gone. Simulator: UI test with a playlist on an unroutable host: open a film with metadataLoaded = false and a completed download fixture, expect Play present and the local file to start; open a series with preserved seasons, expect the episode list and no full-screen error. For the race: open a series online, cut the network, re-open it 20 times and count error pages before and after change A (this is the part only a run can settle). Device: real airplane mode after a pull-to-refresh on Movies and Series.

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-3 — Turning 'Show TV guide' off hides nothing: the now/next lines, the Guide button and the minute timer all stay, and only the background refresh stops

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings, Live TV home, Live category grids, TV Guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:126-129, 158-165`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:83-112, 116-128, 137-168`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:108-116, 451-454, 1065`, `ContentView.swift:17, 145-163`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: What 'off' means beyond hiding: keep the stored guide so re-enabling is instant (recommended) or delete epgProgramme / epgChannel rows for the playlist to free space; and hide the Guide toolbar button (recommended, smallest) or keep it and show a 'TV guide is turned off' state with a button that opens Settings.

**What the user perceives:** The user switches 'Show TV guide' off and goes back to Live TV: every card still shows its programme line and progress bar, the Guide button is still in the toolbar and the guide opens with data. After a relaunch it is the same, except that the guide now silently ages: nothing refreshes it any more, so some days later the lines turn into empty reserved space under every channel while the switch still says off.

**Mechanism (finder):** saveEnabled only writes the row and, when enabling, calls refreshIfStale (EPGSettingsSections.swift:158-165); EPGStore is never told. tick() does not read epgEnabled (EPGStore.swift:137-168) and keeps publishing a snapshot every minute; the cards draw the line whenever the environment snapshot is non-nil (LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454); the Guide NavigationLink is unconditional (108-116). On the next launch setActivePlaylist -> reload -> tick publishes from the rows already stored, again without a gate, while refreshIfStale returns at its first line (432). `configured` is true as long as an epgSource row exists (110), so when the stored programmes run out the store publishes an empty, non-nil snapshot and the cards keep their 22 pt reserved band (EPGComponents.swift:66-68). The only reader of the flag in the browse UI, the short-EPG fallback at LiveStreamsView.swift:1065, reads the dashboard's frozen Playlist copy (ContentView.swift:17, 161), so within a session it keeps asking the panel after the switch is off (swiftui-invalidation-7 / settings-ux-3 cover the frozen copy and the whole-row save).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Gate once, in the store, because every consumer already treats a nil snapshot as 'no guide':
```swift
// EPGStore
@Published private(set) var isGuideEnabled = true
func setActivePlaylist(_ playlist: Playlist?) { ...; isGuideEnabled = playlist?.epgEnabled ?? true; ... }
func setGuideEnabled(_ enabled: Bool, playlist: Playlist) async {
    guard playlist.id == activePlaylistId else { return }
    isGuideEnabled = enabled
    if enabled { await reload(playlist: playlist); await refreshIfStale(playlist: playlist) }
    else { stopTimer(); snapshot = nil }
}
func tick() async { guard let pid = activePlaylistId, isGuideEnabled else { snapshot = nil; return } ... }
// startTimerIfActive: add `isGuideEnabled` to its guard
```
XtreamEPGSettingsSection.saveEnabled calls `await EPGStore.shared.setGuideEnabled(enabled, playlist: updated)` instead of refreshIfStale. For the toolbar button add an environment value next to the existing one (DashboardView.swift:130): `.environment(\.epgGuideEnabled, epgStore.isGuideEnabled)` and wrap the ToolbarItem at LiveStreamsView.swift:108-116 in `if epgGuideEnabled`. Replace the `playlist.epgEnabled` read at LiveStreamsView.swift:1065 with the same environment value (the LivePlayerShell is hand-off code; this is a one-token change). M3U playlists have no such switch and keep the default true. No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** EnvironmentKey / EnvironmentValues custom key (same pattern as epgSnapshot) (iOS 13.0+, already used at Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:5-18)

**Verifier reasons:** Read every reader of the flag: `epgEnabled` is consulted only at EPG/EPGStore.swift:432 (refreshIfStale) and Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:1065 (short-EPG fallback, on the dashboard's frozen Playlist copy from ContentView.swift:17). saveEnabled (Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:158-165) writes the row and never tells the store. tick() (EPGStore.swift:137-168) has no enabled gate and keeps publishing; cards draw whenever the environment snapshot is non-nil (LiveStreamsView.swift:451-454, Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:439); the Guide NavigationLink is unconditional (LiveStreamsView.swift:108-117). On relaunch setActivePlaylist -> reload -> tick publishes from stored rows while refreshIfStale returns at its first line, so the guide ages silently; `configured` stays true while an epgSource row exists (EPGStore.swift:110), giving an empty non-nil snapshot and the 22 pt reserved band (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:66-68). The label is 'Show TV guide' / 'TV rehberini goster' (Localizable.strings:525), so hiding is the stated meaning; git log -S'epgEnabled' shows it arrived in 1cce013 with no comment that marks the current behaviour as intended. The fix compiles in this structure: `if` inside a toolbar builder is already used at Views/DashboardView.swift:232, and the custom EnvironmentKey pattern exists at EPGComponents.swift:5-18. One addition is needed (below).

**Corrected claim:** Turning 'Show TV guide' off only stops future guide downloads. The now-lines on channel cards, the Guide toolbar button, the guide itself and the minute timer all keep working from the stored data, in the same session and after relaunch, and the stored guide then ages until the lines become empty reserved space.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed (gate once in EPGStore with a published isGuideEnabled, set in setActivePlaylist and through a new setGuideEnabled called from saveEnabled; nil snapshot and stopped timer while off; environment value for the Guide toolbar button and for the read at LiveStreamsView.swift:1065), plus one guard: tick() awaits a database read, so re-check the flag after the await (`guard pid == activePlaylistId, isGuideEnabled, sequence > publishedTickSequence`), otherwise a tick in flight when the switch goes off republishes the snapshot. Note for the owner: the player's programme strip reads the same snapshot (Views/PlayerView.swift:225-230), so 'off' also removes the programme line in the player; that is consistent with the switch but is a visible change in the out-of-scope player. Keeping the stored rows (instant re-enable) versus deleting them, and hiding the Guide button versus showing a 'turned off' state, remain owner decisions.

**API check:** Custom EnvironmentKey / EnvironmentValues extension: already used at Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:5-18 (iOS 13.0). ToolbarContentBuilder.buildIf: SwiftUI.swiftinterface:9634, already relied on at Views/DashboardView.swift:232. No iOS 26 API.

**Regression risks:** A nil snapshot removes the reserved 22 pt line under every channel card, so shelves and grids get shorter when the switch goes off (the same state that exists today before the first guide load). The player loses its programme strip while the guide is off. ensureShortEPG ends with tick(); with the gate it must stay a no-op while off (it is, since the call site is gated by the same flag). M3U playlists have no switch and must keep the default true. setActivePlaylist returns early for an unchanged id (EPGStore.swift:84), so set the flag before that guard or it will not be picked up when the same playlist is re-bound.

**How to verify:** Unit: bind a playlist with guide rows, call setGuideEnabled(false), assert snapshot == nil and that tick() leaves it nil, including a tick started before the call; enable again and assert a snapshot is published. Simulator UI test: seeded guide, switch off in Settings, go to Live TV, assert no element with the 'now playing' accessibility label and no Guide button; relaunch and assert the same; switch back on and assert the lines return without a download.

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-4 — A TV Guide left open overnight keeps showing yesterday under a 'Today' chip, then flips the selected chip to 'Yesterday' and drops the now line; an open guide also never reloads after a refresh it did not start

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:117-130, 218-239`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:9, 54-57, 104-123, 277-285, 290-295, 342-349`

**What the user perceives:** The guide was open when the phone was put down. Next morning it shows the same grid with 'Today' highlighted and the red line at last night's time. Within a minute the chip row shifts by one day, 'Yesterday' becomes the highlighted chip, the red line disappears and the grid still shows yesterday's programmes at last night's scroll position. The user has to find the clock button to get back to now. Separately, when the guide finishes refreshing in the background (launch-time refresh, or the resume refresh proposed in the first finding), the open grid keeps the old layouts.

**Mechanism (finder):** selectedDay is fixed at view-model init to the start of the current day (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:119) and only changes through selectDay (235-239). The chips (availableDays, 127-130), their labels (EPGGuideView.swift:426-432), isToday and nowLineX (290-295) are recomputed from Date() on each body evaluation, but nothing evaluates the body on resume: the view reads no scenePhase and its only time-driven invalidation is the store's minute tick through `@ObservedObject epgStore` (9), which arrives 1-60 s after activation. After that evaluation the labels are relative to the new day while selectedDay and `layouts` are still yesterday's, hence 'Yesterday' selected and nowLineX == nil. load() runs only while state == .loading (54-57) and after the view's own refresh button (277-285), so a refresh that completes elsewhere does not rebuild the layouts.

**Proposed fix (finder):** View model: remember whether the user is on 'today' and roll forward when the calendar day changed.
```swift
private(set) var followsToday = true          // set in selectDay: followsToday = calendar.isDateInToday(day)
func rollToTodayIfNeeded() async {
    guard followsToday, !calendar.isDateInToday(selectedDay) else { return }
    await selectDay(Date())                    // existing path; the grid's .task(id: selectedDay) re-centres on now
}
```
View:
```swift
@Environment(\.scenePhase) private var scenePhase
.onChange(of: scenePhase) { _, phase in if phase == .active { Task { await model.rollToTodayIfNeeded() } } }
.onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .NSCalendarDayChanged)) { _ in Task { await model.rollToTodayIfNeeded() } }   // midnight while in the foreground
.onChange(of: epgStore.lastSuccess[model.playlist.id]) { _, _ in Task { await model.load() } }
```
Reading scenePhase also re-evaluates the body on activation, so the now line is correct in the first frame instead of after the next tick. With the lastSuccess observer the explicit `await model.load()` after forceRefresh at 280 and 92 becomes redundant (the generation counter makes a double call harmless). A user who deliberately selected another day keeps it. No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** EnvironmentValues.scenePhase (iOS 14.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5569)); View.onReceive(_:perform:) (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2856)); NSNotification.Name.NSCalendarDayChanged (iOS 8.0+ (Foundation NSCalendar.h:401))

**Verifier reasons:** Both mechanisms confirmed. Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:119 fixes selectedDay at init; it only changes through selectDay (235-239). availableDays (127-130), the chip labels (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:426-432), isToday and nowLineX (290-295) are derived from Date() at body time, and the only time-driven invalidation is the store's minute publish through @ObservedObject (EPGGuideView.swift:9). After a day change the next body pass therefore labels the still-selected day 'Yesterday', nowLineX becomes nil, and `layouts` remain the old day's. This also happens to a guide that sits behind the player across midnight, which is a more common case than the overnight one. load() runs only from .task while state == .loading (54-57) and after the view's own refresh buttons (92, 280), so a refresh started by the dashboard (DashboardView.swift:136) that finishes while the guide is open does not rebuild rows or layouts; on a new playlist that leaves an empty grid until the user leaves and re-enters. Screenshot iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows the chip row and now line as described. Two corrections to the fix: (1) EPGStore.performRefresh sets lastSuccess before `await rebuildResolution` (EPG/EPGStore.swift:469-475), and load() -> buildRows() reads `epg.storedKey` (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:258, 269). An observer on lastSuccess can therefore rebuild rows against the old alias map, leaving display-name-matched channels empty; today's `await forceRefresh; await model.load()` does not have that problem because it runs after the whole refresh. (2) NSCalendarDayChanged carries no thread guarantee; hop to the main queue before touching the view model.

**Corrected claim:** An open TV Guide never follows the calendar: after a day change (left open overnight, or sitting behind the player across midnight) the selected chip is relabelled 'Yesterday', the now line disappears and the grid keeps the old day until the user taps the clock button; until the next minute tick after resume it even shows the old day under 'Today'. An open guide also does not reload when a refresh it did not start finishes, so on a first run the grid stays empty.

**Corrected fix:** View model as proposed: `followsToday` set in selectDay, `rollToTodayIfNeeded()` that calls the existing selectDay(Date()) when the user was on today and the day changed. View: scenePhase observer calling it on .active; `.onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .NSCalendarDayChanged).receive(on: DispatchQueue.main))` for midnight in the foreground or behind the player. For the reload, do not observe lastSuccess as it is published today: in EPGStore.performRefresh move `lastSuccess[playlist.id] = Date()` to after `await rebuildResolution(playlist:)` (keep it unconditional for a non-active playlist), then `.onChange(of: epgStore.lastSuccess[model.playlist.id]) { _, _ in Task { await model.load() } }` is safe. The explicit `await model.load()` after forceRefresh can stay; the generation counter makes the double call harmless. A day the user picked deliberately is kept. No iOS 26 API; identical on iOS 18.

**API check:** `public var scenePhase: SwiftUI.ScenePhase` SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5569 (iOS 14.0). `View.onReceive<P>(_:perform:)` SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2856 (iOS 13.0). `View.onChange<V>(of:initial:_:)` two-parameter form SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:13827 (iOS 17.0). `NSCalendarDayChangedNotification` Foundation NSCalendar.h:401, API_AVAILABLE(ios(8.0)). All present.

**Regression risks:** Rolling to today changes selectedDay, which re-runs the grid's .task(id: model.selectedDay) and jumps the horizontal scroll to now; at midnight with the guide in view that is a visible jump (the alternative is today's silent relabel). A reload replaces rows and layouts under the user's finger; row ids are stable so the vertical position should hold, but check it on a large playlist. A 304 'not modified' refresh also changes lastSuccess and causes one cheap reload. Moving the lastSuccess assignment delays the 'Last updated' row in Settings by the few milliseconds of the resolution rebuild.

**How to verify:** Unit: give the view model an injectable `now`, select today, advance a day, call rollToTodayIfNeeded and assert selectedDay moved; select tomorrow explicitly and assert it does not move. Unit: assert lastSuccess is published after the resolution map is rebuilt. Simulator: open the guide, background, move the host date forward one day, reopen: expect 'Today' selected, red line present, grid centred on now in the first frame. New playlist: open the guide while the first guide download is still running and expect the grid to fill when it finishes without leaving the screen.

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-5 — The App Store review prompt is requested 8 s after the dashboard appears on the fourth launch, with no check for a playing video, an open sheet, the keyboard or a catalog that is still downloading, and its task is never cancelled

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Search, Player hand-off, Playlist list
- Code: `ContentView.swift:70-78`, `Models/RatingManager.swift:37-43, 47-70`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:92-113, 125-129`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Which moment counts as the natural pause: after closing a playback session of at least N minutes (recommended, N = 5), after a download completes, or keep the launch-time trigger and only add the guards. Also whether a session should count only once the catalog has loaded.

**What the user perceives:** On the fourth launch the system rating dialog appears eight seconds after the home screen. For an IPTV app that is typically just after the user tapped a channel: the dialog lands on top of a stream that has just started (the player is an in-window overlay, so the scene is still foregroundActive), possibly in forced landscape. If the user was typing in a search field the keyboard is dismissed; if they went back to the playlist list or opened the add-playlist sheet in those eight seconds, it appears there. On a newly added large playlist it can appear over the 'Preparing...' spinner before any content was seen.

**Mechanism (finder):** The dashboard Group's onAppear starts an unstructured `Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(8)); RatingManager.shared.requestReviewIfAppropriate() }` (ContentView.swift:70-78). It is not stored or cancelled, so it fires even after selectedPlaylist was set back to nil. requestReviewIfAppropriate checks the session count, the version, the 90-day gap and that some scene is foregroundActive (RatingManager.swift:50-64); nothing about the player overlay (DashboardView.swift:92-113), presented sheets or alerts, the keyboard, or contentStore.isLoading. registerSuccessfulSession counts on appearance, before the catalog load has succeeded (37-43). Second request in one launch: onAppear does fire again (re-entering a playlist; a language change rebuilds the root through `.id`, another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66), but the first call stores lastPromptVersion (68) and the guard at 55 then blocks every later call, so there is no double prompt. That same line also means the one request per version is spent at this bad moment.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Ask at a natural pause: when the user closes the player after having watched for a while. Remove the Task at ContentView.swift:73-77 (keep registerSuccessfulSession at 72). In DashboardView and M3UDashboardView extend the existing presentation observer:
```swift
@State private var playbackStartedAt: Date?
.onChange(of: playerOverlay.presentation?.id) { old, id in
    if old == nil, id != nil { playbackStartedAt = Date() }
    if id == nil, let start = playbackStartedAt {
        playbackStartedAt = nil
        RatingManager.shared.playbackEnded(watched: Date().timeIntervalSince(start)) {
            playerOverlay.presentation != nil || playerOverlay.pendingPresentation != nil
        }
    }
    ... existing downloads-sheet line ...
}
```
RatingManager:
```swift
private var pending: Task<Void, Never>?
func playbackEnded(watched: TimeInterval, isBlocked: @escaping @MainActor () -> Bool) {
    pending?.cancel()
    guard watched >= 300 else { return }
    pending = Task { @MainActor in
        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2))          // let the dismiss animation finish
        guard !Task.isCancelled, !isBlocked() else { return }
        requestReviewIfAppropriate()
    }
}
```
and inside requestReviewIfAppropriate, after resolving the scene: `guard scene.keyWindow?.rootViewController?.presentedViewController == nil, !isKeyboardVisible else { return }` (covers sheets, alerts and full-screen covers), with isKeyboardVisible kept from UIResponder.keyboardDidShowNotification / keyboardDidHideNotification. The existing count / version / 90-day gates stay. AppStore.requestReview(in:) stays; no iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** AppStore.requestReview(in:) (iOS 16.0+ (StoreKit.swiftinterface:1863-1867), already used); UIWindowScene.keyWindow (iOS 15.0+ (UIWindowScene.h:44)); UIViewController.presentedViewController (iOS 5.0+ (UIViewController.h:220)); UIResponder.keyboardDidShowNotification / keyboardDidHideNotification (iOS 2.0+ (UIWindow.h:133, 135))

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed: ContentView.swift:70-78 starts an unstructured Task in the dashboard's onAppear that sleeps 8 s and calls RatingManager.requestReviewIfAppropriate; it is neither stored nor cancelled, so it also fires after selectedPlaylist went back to nil. Models/RatingManager.swift:47-70 checks session count, version, the 90-day gap and a foregroundActive scene only; the player is an in-window overlay (Views/DashboardView.swift:92-113), so nothing stops the request while a stream is on screen, a sheet is up or the keyboard is open. registerSuccessfulSession counts on appearance, before the catalog load finished (RatingManager.swift:37-43). The single-prompt guard at :55 / :68 is as described. Corrections: (1) the launch-time trigger with a delay is deliberate, not an oversight: the comment at ContentView.swift:74 ('short delay so the user is not interrupted at the welcome moment') and the doc comment at RatingManager.swift:46 say so; only the guards are missing. (2) Severity is low: the request is made at most once per app version and 90 days, and the system shows it at most three times a year. (3) The proposed new moment (2 s after closing a playback of 5+ minutes) is a product change with its own downside for an IPTV app: wall-clock time since presentation does not tell a good session from one that ended because the stream died, so the prompt can land right after a failure. (4) M3UDashboardView has no presentation observer to 'extend'; it would need a new one.

**Corrected claim:** On the fourth launch the App Store review request is made 8 s after the dashboard appears with no check for a presented player, a sheet or alert, an open keyboard or a catalog that is still downloading, and the task is not cancelled when the user leaves the dashboard. It can therefore land on a stream that has just started. The launch-time trigger itself is intended; the missing guards are the defect.

**Corrected fix:** Smallest fix, no change of moment: move the delayed request out of ContentView into the two dashboards, which own the state needed for the guards, as a structured task that SwiftUI cancels when the dashboard goes away: `.task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(8)); guard !Task.isCancelled, playerOverlay.presentation == nil, playerOverlay.pendingPresentation == nil, !contentStore.isLoading, contentStore.loadError == nil else { return }; RatingManager.shared.requestReviewIfAppropriate() }` (M3U: `store` instead of `contentStore`). Keep registerSuccessfulSession at ContentView.swift:72. In requestReviewIfAppropriate, after resolving the scene, add `guard scene.keyWindow?.rootViewController?.presentedViewController == nil, !isKeyboardVisible else { return }` with isKeyboardVisible tracked from UIResponder.keyboardDidShowNotification / keyboardDidHideNotification. Because lastPromptVersion is only written after the request, a blocked attempt is simply retried on the next launch. Moving the prompt to 'after a good playback session' is an owner decision; if chosen, gate it on the playback having ended normally, not on elapsed time alone.

**API check:** `@MainActor public static func requestReview(in scene: UIKit.UIWindowScene)` on StoreKit.AppStore, StoreKit.swiftinterface:1863-1867, @available iOS 16.0; already used at Models/RatingManager.swift:66. `UIWindowScene.keyWindow` UIWindowScene.h:44, API_AVAILABLE(ios(15.0)). `UIViewController.presentedViewController` UIViewController.h:220, ios(5.0). `UIKeyboardDidShowNotification` / `UIKeyboardDidHideNotification` UIWindow.h:133, 135. All present.

**Regression risks:** With the guards the request can be skipped on a launch where the user starts playback within 8 s every time; it is then retried on later launches, so the prompt may come later than today but is not lost. RatingManager returns early under MockFixture (RatingManager.swift:38, 48), so UI tests are unaffected. A SwiftUI .task on the dashboard re-runs if the dashboard is rebuilt (language change rebuilds the root); the didCountThisLaunch and version guards already make a second call harmless. Do not touch the tip-jar files; none are involved.

**How to verify:** Unit: RatingManager with a stubbed requester and injected blocked/keyboard state: no request while a view controller is presented or the keyboard is visible, and lastPromptVersion is not written in that case. Simulator, debug build with sessionCount forced to 4: start a channel within 8 s of launch and confirm no dialog appears over the player; relaunch, stay on the tab root for 8 s and confirm the dialog appears there; go back to the playlist list within 8 s and confirm nothing appears.
