## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-6 — When the connection returns nothing outside the download queue recovers by itself: detail error pages, the Settings account block, a failed guide refresh and a failed first catalog load all wait for a manual retry

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movie detail, Series detail, Settings, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home
- Code: `Views/MovieDetailView.swift:106-121, 307-312`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:941-956, 1241-1246`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:226-237, 392-401`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:478-481`, `Views/Components/CatalogLoadErrorView.swift:7-33`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:19-24`, `Models/DownloadManager.swift:72-79, 724-743`

**What the user perceives:** The user walks out of a lift or leaves airplane mode while a detail page shows its error text. Nothing happens; they must tap 'Try Again' (or pop and push). Posters that failed stay grey until they are scrolled away and back. Settings keeps its red 'Could not fetch info' row (iphone-dark/T03-settings-3.png) until 'Try Again' or a tab switch. A guide refresh that failed at launch is not retried until the next launch. Apple's apps reload the visible screen when connectivity returns.

**Mechanism (finder):** There is no reachability source in the app (grep: no NWPathMonitor, no scenePhase). Each failure is terminal until user action: MovieDetailView and SeriesDetailView store errorMessage and offer only a button (MovieDetailView.swift:114-116; SeriesView.swift:949-951); PlaylistSettingsView re-runs fetchAuthInfo only from its button, pull-to-refresh or the tab's next appearance (232-237, 392-401); EPGStore records .failed (478-481) and refreshIfStale is only called at dashboard mount; a failed first catalog load shows the alert and CatalogLoadErrorView with a retry button; failed images are covered by image-pipeline-12, which already asks for 'a single shared NWPathMonitor'. What does recover alone: downloads, because the background URLSession waits for connectivity itself and failures are re-queued up to three times with resume data (DownloadManager.swift:74-78, 724-743), and every GRDB-observed list, which never depended on the network.

**Proposed fix (finder):** A small NWPathMonitor wrapper is justified because five independent places need the same trigger. About 25 lines, system framework, no dependency:
```swift
import Network
@MainActor final class NetworkStatus: ObservableObject {
    static let shared = NetworkStatus()
    @Published private(set) var isOnline = true
    @Published private(set) var reconnectCount = 0     // bumped on unsatisfied -> satisfied
    private let monitor = NWPathMonitor()
    private init() {
        monitor.pathUpdateHandler = { [weak self] path in
            Task { @MainActor in
                guard let self else { return }
                let online = path.status == .satisfied
                if online, !self.isOnline { self.reconnectCount += 1 }
                if online != self.isOnline { self.isOnline = online }
            }
        }
        monitor.start(queue: DispatchQueue(label: "network.path"))
    }
}
```
What it triggers, and nothing else: (1) detail pages: `.onChange(of: reconnectCount) { if errorMessage != nil { Task { await fetchMovieInfo() } } }` (same for series); (2) PlaylistSettingsView: refetch when errorMessage != nil; (3) EPGStore: refreshIfStale for the active playlist; (4) tab roots: `contentStore.loadPlaylist(playlist)` when loadError != nil and the catalog is empty; (5) the visible-image retry of image-pipeline-12. Views should receive `reconnectCount` as an environment value or observe only in the screens that are in an error state, so a path change does not re-evaluate the dashboard. Use it only as a retry trigger and to choose the error copy; never refuse a user action because isOnline is false (the path can be wrong behind captive portals, and a LAN panel works without internet). No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** NWPathMonitor (pathUpdateHandler, start(queue:), cancel()) (iOS 12.0+ (Network.swiftinterface:942-958)); NWPath.status / NWPath.Status.satisfied (iOS 12.0+ (Network.swiftinterface:875-885)); NWPathMonitor: AsyncSequence (alternative to the handler) (iOS 17.0+ (Network.swiftinterface:978-979))

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism is real. No reachability source exists: grep for NWPathMonitor / scenePhase / waitsForConnectivity over the app sources returns only EPG/EPGStore.swift:73-78 (background/active timer stop/start) and Views/CachedImage.swift:23 (waitsForConnectivity = false). Views/MovieDetailView.swift:74-78 replaces the whole page with errorView when errorMessage is set and 114-116 is the only retry; Views/SeriesView.swift:941-956 and 1241-1246 are the same; Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:232-237 shows the red row plus button and 392-401 refetches only from .task / .refreshable; EPG/EPGStore.swift:478-481 records .failed and refreshIfStale is called only from Views/DashboardView.swift:136, Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:89 and Views/EPG/EPGSettingsSections.swift:163. Downloads do recover alone (Models/DownloadManager.swift:74-78, 724-743). Corrections: (1) The EPG trigger as proposed is often a no-op: EPG/EPGRefreshCoordinator.swift:35-36 stamps fetchedAt before every attempt and EPGStore.swift:436-437 returns for 15 minutes (EPGConstants.retryCooldown, a deliberate guard) when the source has never succeeded, so a reconnect shortly after a failed first refresh does nothing; it only works when an older success exists. (2) The cited screenshot iphone-dark/T03-settings-3.png shows 'Server error: HTTP 404' from the demo host, a server error a reconnect would not cure; it proves the terminal error row, not the offline case. (3) 'Wait for a manual retry' is overstated for Settings and the detail pages: their .task re-runs on every re-appearance (tab switch, pop back), so they also recover that way. (4) The catalog trigger covers a rare case: PlaylistContentStore.loadPlaylist only needs the network when the playlist has zero categories (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:115-125, 280-285), i.e. the connection dropped between adding the playlist and its first sync. (5) 'Apple's apps reload the visible screen when connectivity returns' is not uniformly true (App Store shows a Retry button); this is polish, not parity. (6) A path turning satisfied precedes a usable connection (DHCP, DNS, captive portal), so a single immediate retry can fail again and leave the error on screen.

**Corrected claim:** After a connectivity loss, the movie and series detail error pages and the Settings account block stay in their error state until the user taps Try Again or leaves and re-enters the screen; a guide refresh that failed is not retried until the dashboard is mounted again; a failed first catalog sync waits for a tap. Nothing in the app listens for the network coming back. It is a low-severity polish gap: one tap recovers every case, and the Settings and detail screens also refetch on re-appearance.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the small NWPathMonitor wrapper, but narrow and harden it. (a) NetworkStatus as proposed (file needs 'import Network' because SWIFT_UPCOMING_FEATURE_MEMBER_IMPORT_VISIBILITY is on); publish only reconnectCount. (b) Consume it with .onReceive(NetworkStatus.shared.$reconnectCount.dropFirst()) in MovieDetailView, SeriesDetailView and PlaylistSettingsView, guarded by errorMessage != nil, so no view body depends on the object and nothing re-renders on a path change. (c) Wait about one second after the transition before retrying, and retry once more after a few seconds if the first retry fails, because 'satisfied' arrives before the link is usable. (d) EPG: call refreshIfStale for the active playlist from the store itself on reconnect, and accept that the 15-minute cooldown applies; do not bypass the cooldown. Optionally call the same from the existing didBecomeActive observer (EPGStore.swift:76-78) so a long-lived process also honours the 6-hour TTL. (e) Catalog: retry loadPlaylist only when loadError != nil and liveCategories is empty; optional, rare. (f) Images stay with image-pipeline-12. Never gate a user action on isOnline. No iOS 26 API, no fallback needed.

**API check:** Network.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk): 'final public class NWPathMonitor' @available(iOS 12.0) at line 942-943; '@preconcurrency final public var pathUpdateHandler: (@Sendable (_ newPath: NWPath) -> Void)?' line 953; 'final public func start(queue: DispatchQueue)' line 958; 'final public func cancel()' line 959; 'public struct NWPath : Equatable, CustomDebugStringConvertible, Sendable' iOS 12.0 line 870-871 with 'enum Status { case satisfied, unsatisfied, requiresConnection }' lines 875-878 and 'public let status' line 885; 'extension NWPathMonitor : Sendable, CustomDebugStringConvertible, AsyncSequence' line 979. View.onReceive(_:perform:) iOS 13.0 at SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2854-2856. The sketch compiles in this target (Swift 5 mode, SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor): all stored properties have defaults, the handler is @Sendable and hops to the main actor, NWPath is Sendable.

**Regression risks:** A retry storm if several screens observe at once (bounded: only screens currently in an error state fire, one request each). Auto-running loadPlaylist clears loadError and therefore dismisses the dashboard's error alert (DashboardView.swift:138-155) under the user; acceptable but visible. An EPG refresh on reconnect downloads a large XMLTV file, possibly on cellular; the existing TTL and cooldown must stay in force. Do not turn isOnline into a gate: LAN panels work without internet.

**How to verify:** Unit: expose apply(online:) and assert reconnectCount increments only on false -> true and not on the initial true. Simulator (follows the Mac's network): turn the Mac's Wi-Fi off, open a film whose metadataLoaded is false so the error page shows, turn Wi-Fi on, expect the page to load without a tap within a few seconds; repeat for Settings and series detail. EPG: with a source that succeeded more than 6 hours ago, confirm refreshState goes to .refreshing after reconnect; with a never-successful source confirm nothing happens inside 15 minutes (expected).

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-7 — A download that finished while the app was not running can be discarded and restarted from zero, and an interrupted queue does not resume after a relaunch until some download UI is opened

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Downloads, Movie detail, Series detail, Settings
- Code: `Models/DownloadManager.swift:72-80, 87-142, 601-611, 656-671`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:14-24, 31-42`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:27-28`, `Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:43-47`

**What the user perceives:** The user queues films, the system later terminates the suspended app, and the downloads finish in the background. On the next open a film that should be ready shows 'Downloading 0 %' and downloads its gigabytes again. In the other direction: after a force-quit or a reboot the queued items sit at 'Queued' / 'Downloading' and nothing moves until the user happens to open a detail page, the Downloads screen or the player.

**Mechanism (finder):** 1) DownloadManager.shared is created lazily; the app initializer does not touch it (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:31-42). The only first touches are DownloadButton / DownloadsView, PlayerOverlayController.present (46) and the background-events callback (22). restoreOutstandingTasks and pumpQueue run only from its init (DownloadManager.swift:79), so after a normal relaunch the queue is not restored. 2) When the background session is re-created, URLSession delivers the events that accumulated while the app was not running. The id maps are filled later by restoreOutstandingTasks, which first awaits a database read and then session.allTasks (88-112). The owner's comment at 661-665 states that events do arrive before that ('a delegate event delivered right after a relaunch ... before restoreOutstandingTasks could match anything') and handles the failure case by adopting the resume data. The success case has no such path: didFinishDownloadingTo returns when taskToId has no entry (607-611), the temporary file is deleted by the system when the delegate returns, the row stays 'downloading', restoreOutstandingTasks then finds no matching task, re-queues it and zeroes the byte counters (118-139). I could not run this; the ordering is taken from the code comment and needs a device to confirm.

**Proposed fix (finder):** a) Create the manager at launch so the session is re-attached and the queue pumps: add `_ = DownloadManager.shared` after `_ = AppDatabase.shared` in the App init (line 33), next to and without touching the TipStore line.
b) Resolve an unmapped success event synchronously from the database instead of dropping the file:
```swift
let mapped = MainActor.assumeIsolated { (self.taskToId[taskId], self.taskToRelativePath[taskId]) }
var id = mapped.0, relPath = mapped.1
if id == nil, let url = downloadTask.originalRequest?.url?.absoluteString,
   let row = try? AppDatabase.shared.reader.read({ db in
       try DBDownloadedItem.filter(Column("remoteURL") == url)
           .filter(["downloading", "queued"].contains(Column("status"))).fetchOne(db) }) {
    id = row.id; relPath = row.localPath
}
```
A pool read does not wait for the writer, so this is safe on the delegate (main) queue; the move must stay synchronous as the existing comment at 606 says.
c) In restoreOutstandingTasks, before re-queuing an orphan, check the destination: if the file exists and is non-empty (and equals totalBytes when that is known) call markCompleted instead of resetting the row. This also heals a kill between the file move and the database write.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** URLSessionDownloadDelegate.urlSession(_:downloadTask:didFinishDownloadingTo:) (iOS 7.0+, already implemented); GRDB DatabaseReader.read (synchronous) (GRDB checkout, DatabaseReader.swift:189)

**Verifier reasons:** Part 1 is confirmed from code. DownloadManager.shared is lazy and the App initializer does not touch it (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:31-42). restoreOutstandingTasks and the first pumpQueue run only from init (Models/DownloadManager.swift:72-80, 141). First touches are DownloadButton / DownloadsView (@ObservedObject, DownloadButton.swift:27, DownloadsView.swift:10), localURL(forId:) from the play buttons, PlayerOverlayController.present (Views/PlayerOverlayController.swift:46) and the background-events callback (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:22). The class comment (DownloadManager.swift:18-20) states the intent that unfinished downloads resume when the app is reopened, so lazy creation contradicts the documented behaviour. A consequence the finding missed: on the first playback after a relaunch, present() creates the manager and asks hasActiveDownload while the id maps are still empty, so the connection-limit warning is skipped even though a background task from before the termination may still be running, and the queue then starts beside the stream. The perception wording is off: the user cannot watch items 'sit at Queued', because any download UI creates the manager; what they notice is that nothing was downloaded during a browsing session. Part 2 is plausible but rests on event ordering that only a device can settle. didFinishDownloadingTo returns when taskToId has no entry (607-611) and the temporary file is then lost; didCompleteWithError adopts only resume data for unmapped tasks (660-671); the maps are filled after two suspensions (database read at 88-92, session.allTasks at 96). The owner's comment at 661-665 (added in 2ec2c18) says such unmapped events do arrive after a relaunch. If the success events are delivered before the maps are filled, the row is re-queued and zeroed at 118-139 exactly as claimed. The proposed fix has three gaps: (i) creating the session in App.init makes it possible for urlSessionDidFinishEvents (752-758) to run before the AppDelegate's Task stores the handler (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:21-23), in which case the system handler is never called; today the session is created inside that Task, so the handler is always stored first on a cold background launch. (ii) Even with the unmapped lookup, restoreOutstandingTasks can have read the row as 'downloading' before markCompleted's write lands, and its orphan write (120-134) sets 'queued' without re-checking the status, so step (c) is required for correctness, not an optional extra. (iii) If the events arrive after the orphan was already re-queued and restarted, the old file is adopted while a second task for the same id keeps downloading.

**Corrected claim:** After a relaunch the download manager does not exist until a download control, the Downloads screen or the first playback creates it, so the queue is not resumed during a browsing session and the first playback skips the active-download warning. Separately, a download that completes while the app is not running is probably thrown away and restarted from zero, because the completion event has no in-memory mapping at that moment and only the failure case has a fallback; the ordering needs a device run to confirm.

**Corrected fix:** (a) Create the manager at launch: '_ = DownloadManager.shared' after '_ = AppDatabase.shared' in the App init, leaving the TipStore line untouched. Together with it, make the completion handler order-independent: store the handler synchronously in the AppDelegate (it is already main-actor isolated; drop the Task hop), and in DownloadManager remember 'finish events seen' so that a handler stored after urlSessionDidFinishEvents is still called. (b) Identify tasks without the maps: set task.taskDescription = id + separator + relPath in startTask (the system keeps it with the background task), and in didFinishDownloadingTo fall back first to taskDescription and then, for tasks started by an older build, to the synchronous lookup by originalRequest ?? currentRequest URL that the finding proposes. Keep the move synchronous. If an in-memory task already exists for that id (the orphan was restarted), cancel it and clear its map entries before marking the row completed. (c) Make the orphan pass safe: inside the write at 120-134 re-queue only rows that are still 'downloading', and before re-queuing check the destination file: when it exists and is non-empty (and matches totalBytes when known) call markCompleted instead. The destination is written only by the completed move, so its presence means a finished download whose database write was lost. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** URLSessionTask.taskDescription: '@property (nullable, copy) NSString *taskDescription' at Foundation NSURLSession.h:369 (iOS 7+). GRDB synchronous read: 'func read<T>(_ value: (Database) throws -> T) throws -> T' at GRDB/Core/DatabaseReader.swift:189, reachable through AppDatabase.reader (Database/AppDatabase.swift:468, nonisolated). The production writer is a DatabasePool (Database/Persistence.swift:54), so a read does not wait for the writer; the ephemeral fallback is a DatabaseQueue (Persistence.swift:82, 95) where a synchronous main-thread read would wait for a running write. URLSessionDownloadDelegate and urlSessionDidFinishEvents are already implemented. DownloadManager.swift already imports GRDB, so Column compiles there.

**Regression risks:** Eager creation resumes the queue at every launch, so the first playback now shows the existing active-download warning more often (this is the designed behaviour, but the owner should expect it). The background session is created during App.init on the main thread, a small launch cost. The handler-ordering hazard described above if (a) is done without the hardening. URL matching can pick the wrong row if two rows share one remote URL; taskDescription avoids that. The synchronous read blocks the main thread when the database is the in-memory fallback queue and a long write is running. The file-exists shortcut must not fire for rows a user re-queued after deleting the file (it cannot: delete and cancel remove the file).

**How to verify:** Device, release-like build. Ordering test: start a large download, stop the process from Xcode (not a swipe-up quit, which cancels the tasks), wait until the transfer finishes, relaunch and read the 'Downloads' log category: before the fix a 'restore orphan' line followed by 'start id=' and a row at 0 %; after the fix the row is Completed and plays offline. Measure specifically whether didFinishDownloadingTo is logged before restoreOutstandingTasks finishes; add a temporary log line at both points. Eager creation: queue two items, stop the app, relaunch, stay on Live TV, expect a 'start id=' line without opening any download UI, and expect the active-download alert on the first channel tap. Unit: factor the unmapped lookup and the orphan decision into nonisolated static helpers and test them against an in-memory AppDatabase.

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-8 — On return from a background download the list and every button are correct, but the system completion handler is called before the completion is saved and before the next queued item is started, and Settings keeps the old storage figure

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Downloads, Series detail, Movie detail, Settings
- Code: `Models/DownloadManager.swift:642-644, 744-748, 752-758, 801-839`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:14-24`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:10-11`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:27-28, 63-75`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:108-125, 392-410`

**What the user perceives:** Answer to the direct question first: after the app was suspended and a download finished, the Downloads list and each DownloadButton show the right state on return without a relaunch, at worst one frame late. What can go wrong is behind it: with a season queued overnight (one download per playlist at a time) the next episode may not start until the app is opened again, and if the suspended app is killed right after a file was moved, that file is downloaded again. In Settings, 'Storage used' and the 'Delete all downloads' row do not change when a download finishes while the tab is showing.

**Mechanism (finder):** Both screens are database-driven: DownloadsView uses @Query AllDownloadsRequest (DownloadsView.swift:11) and DownloadButton @Query DownloadedItemByIDRequest (DownloadButton.swift:28, state derived at 63-75); markCompleted writes the row and clears `progress` (DownloadManager.swift:826-838), so they update whenever that write lands. In a background wake the delegate order is didFinishDownloadingTo (moves the file, then `Task { await markCompleted }`, 642-644), didCompleteWithError (`Task { await pumpQueue() }`, 747) and urlSessionDidFinishEvents, which calls the stored completion handler immediately (752-758). Both tasks still need database hops when the handler tells iOS the app is finished, so the process can be suspended with the row still 'downloading' and the next item not started; they complete on the next resume. A kill in that window leaves a moved file with a 'downloading' row, which restoreOutstandingTasks re-queues from zero. This is a race I could not observe without a device. Settings: downloadUsedBytes is computed only in `.task` and `.refreshable` (PlaylistSettingsView.swift:392-410); the manager's dbVersion counter, published for exactly this purpose (DownloadManager.swift:40-41), has no reader.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Hold the completion handler until the work started by this batch of events has finished:
```swift
private var eventWork: [Task<Void, Never>] = []     // append the markCompleted / markFailed / requeue / pumpQueue tasks created in the delegate methods
nonisolated func urlSessionDidFinishEvents(forBackgroundURLSession session: URLSession) {
    MainActor.assumeIsolated {
        let work = self.eventWork; self.eventWork = []
        Task { @MainActor in
            for task in work { await task.value }
            let handler = self.backgroundCompletionHandler
            self.backgroundCompletionHandler = nil
            handler?()
        }
    }
}
```
The work is a few database statements, far inside the background time iOS grants for this callback. Settings: `.onReceive(DownloadManager.shared.$dbVersion.dropFirst()) { _ in Task { await refreshDownloadUsage() } }` on the Form in both settings views (does not touch the TipJarRow line or the tip strings). No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** UIApplicationDelegate.application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:completionHandler:) (iOS 7.0+, already implemented); URLSessionDelegate.urlSessionDidFinishEvents(forBackgroundURLSession:) (iOS 7.0+, already implemented); View.onReceive(_:perform:) (iOS 13.0+ (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2856))

**Verifier reasons:** The code order is as described. didFinishDownloadingTo moves the file and only then starts 'Task { await markCompleted }' (Models/DownloadManager.swift:642-644); didCompleteWithError starts 'Task { await pumpQueue() }' (747); urlSessionDidFinishEvents calls the stored handler at once (752-758). markCompleted needs a pool read and a write (803-835) and pumpQueue a read, a write and startTask (405-451), so both are still pending when the system is told the app is done. Nothing in the comments or history (backgroundCompletionHandler dates from d2489f9 / 0ab5bcd) says the early call is deliberate. Whether iOS actually suspends the process inside that window cannot be read from code; with one download per playlist (maxConcurrentPerPlaylist = 1, line 32) a single lost race stalls the rest of a queued season until the app is opened, so the consequence is large relative to the cost of the fix. The UI statements check out: DownloadsView and DownloadButton are @Query-driven (DownloadButton.swift:28, 63-75). Settings: downloadUsedBytes is set only from .task / .refreshable / after delete-all (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:384-401, Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:275-287) and no code reads dbVersion (grep finds no use outside DownloadManager.swift), though the two @ObservedObject views are invalidated by it. The stale figure only occurs when a download finishes while Settings stays on screen, because .task re-runs on every re-appearance; that half is cosmetic. The proposed code needs one correction: urlSessionDidFinishEvents is only called for background wakes, so an eventWork array appended from every delegate callback is never drained during foreground use and grows for the life of the process. It also does not cover the restore task started in init on a cold background launch.

**Corrected claim:** The system completion handler for background transfer events is called before the completion is written to the database and before the next queued item is started. If the process is suspended in that gap the next download of the queue does not start until the app is opened, and a kill in the gap causes a re-download. The window is short and needs a device to observe. Separately, the Settings storage figure does not update when a download finishes while the Settings tab is on screen; it is correct on every re-appearance.

**Corrected fix:** Track the work started by delegate events in a self-pruning collection and wait for it before calling the handler: keep 'private var eventWork: [UUID: Task<Void, Never>]', start every markCompleted / markFailed / requeue / pumpQueue task through one helper that stores the task under a fresh key and removes the key when the task ends, also register the restoreOutstandingTasks task from init, and in urlSessionDidFinishEvents take the current values, await them all on the main actor, run one final pumpQueue, then call and clear the handler. Store the handler synchronously in the AppDelegate instead of through a Task hop. Settings: add '.onReceive(DownloadManager.shared.$dbVersion.dropFirst()) { _ in Task { await refreshDownloadUsage() } }' to the Form in both settings views; this is optional polish and leaves the TipJarRow line and the tip strings untouched. No iOS 26 API.

**API check:** UIApplicationDelegate application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:completionHandler:) and URLSessionDelegate urlSessionDidFinishEvents(forBackgroundURLSession:) are already implemented (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:14-24, DownloadManager.swift:752-758). View.onReceive(_:perform:): '@inlinable nonisolated public func onReceive<P>(_ publisher: P, perform action: @escaping (P.Output) -> Void) -> some View where P : Publisher, P.Failure == Never', iOS 13.0, SwiftUI.swiftinterface:2854-2856. '$dbVersion' is reachable from the views: the property is '@Published private(set) var' (DownloadManager.swift:41), so only the setter is private.

**Regression risks:** If any awaited task never finishes, the handler is never called; the awaited work is bounded database statements, but keep network waits out of it. Holding the handler for a long catalog write in progress could exceed the background allowance, so the final wait should not include unrelated work. The Settings hook creates the download manager when Settings is first shown and walks the download directory on every dbVersion bump (enqueue, start, finish, delete); it runs detached at utility priority, so it is cheap. Both settings files carry the owner's uncommitted tip-jar line; edit around it.

**How to verify:** Device only for the queue: queue three episodes on a real panel, lock the phone, and afterwards read the 'Downloads' log category: each completion should be followed by a 'start id=' line for the next episode while the app was never opened. To measure the window itself, log timestamps at the handler call, at the end of markCompleted and at startTask, and compare before and after. Simulator for Settings: keep the Settings tab visible while a small fixture download finishes and check that the storage value changes without leaving the tab.

## gap-lifecycle-connectivity-9 — The app has no memory-warning handling of its own; the image cache and SQLite already purge themselves, but the catalog copies and the live channel-panel cache are never released, so a large playlist is an expensive app to keep suspended

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Search, TV Guide
- Code: `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:23-32, 144-152, 183-190`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:26-29`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:1236-1259, 1327-1331`, `Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift:9-13`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:90, 329-332`, `ContentView.swift:56-63, 152-163`

**What the user perceives:** With a 150k-film playlist the app is one of the largest suspended processes on the phone, so iOS is more likely to terminate it in the background. The user then comes back to a cold start: the last playlist and the last content tab are restored, everything else (navigation depth, scroll position, search text, the open guide, the mini player) is gone, as described in navigation-architecture-9.

**Mechanism (finder):** What the process holds: PlaylistContentStore keeps each content type twice, as a flat array and as a by-category dictionary built with Dictionary(grouping:) (23-32, 377, 391, 405), and some screens add further copies (data-main-thread-12). The EPG snapshot is one dictionary of on-air programmes plus the alias map, small by comparison (EPGStore.swift:49, 54); the guide's `layouts` for every channel of a day exist only while the guide is open (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:90). LiveChannelPanelSectionCache keeps a panel model of the whole live catalog after the first playback and is cleared only when another playlist adopts it (LiveStreamsView.swift:1327-1331), not when the player closes and not by the unload path in ContentView.swift:61-62. Self-managing parts, verified in the checkouts: Nuke's memory cache (limited to 150 MB / 1500 images, CachedImage.swift:28-29) empties itself on memory-pressure warning and critical events (Nuke/Caching/Cache.swift:47-52) and trims to 10 % on didEnterBackground (66-70, 149-159); GRDB's DatabasePool releases memory on the memory-warning and background notifications (GRDB/Core/DatabasePool.swift:218-256, Configuration.automaticMemoryManagement default true, Configuration.swift:409). Nothing in the app observes UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Keep it small; do not unload the catalog on a warning (reloading costs seconds and would blank the screen).
1) One observer, e.g. in the App init or a tiny MemoryPressure helper:
```swift
NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(forName: UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification, object: nil, queue: .main) { _ in
    MainActor.assumeIsolated {
        ListImagePrefetch.cancelAll()                 // prefetcher.stopPrefetching()
        LiveChannelPanelSectionCache.shared.purgeIfIdle()   // only when no player is presented
    }
}
```
`purgeIfIdle` needs a flag the dashboards set from `playerOverlay.presentation != nil`; the cache rebuilds lazily on the next playback (it already handles a cold cache, 1253-1256). Also clear that cache from the two onDismiss closures in ContentView.swift:51-53 and 61-62, next to the existing unload calls.
2) The real reduction of the suspended footprint is the single-representation change in data-main-thread-12 (derive the flat arrays or the dictionaries, not both); this finding only adds the reason to prioritise it: it decides how often 'resume' is in fact a relaunch.
No iOS 26 API.

**APIs:** UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification (iOS 2.0+ (UIApplication.h:556)); Nuke ImagePrefetcher.stopPrefetching() (Nuke checkout, Prefetching/ImagePrefetcher.swift)

**Verifier reasons:** Facts that hold: the app has no memory-warning observer (grep for MemoryWarning over the sources is empty). Nuke's cache empties itself on memory-pressure warning and critical events and trims to 10 % on didEnterBackground (Nuke/Sources/Nuke/Caching/Cache.swift:49-53, 66-70, 149-159; the app's ImageCache with 150 MB / 1500 entries is at Views/CachedImage.swift:27-29). GRDB's DatabasePool releases memory on the memory-warning and background notifications (GRDB/Core/DatabasePool.swift:218-256, Configuration.swift:409). PlaylistContentStore keeps flat arrays and by-category dictionaries (Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:23-32). LiveChannelPanelSectionCache keeps, per category, the source [DBLiveStream] plus the panel section and is cleared only when another playlist adopts it (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:1258-1259, 1329-1333); ContentView's return to the playlist list unloads the stores (ContentView.swift:51-53, 61-62) but not this cache, which works against the stated purpose of unload() (PlaylistContentStore.swift:180-183: do not keep catalog copies in a singleton). What does not hold: the proposed memory-warning observer does not address the title's concern. A suspended process cannot run a handler, so nothing done on didReceiveMemoryWarning changes the suspended footprint; the hook that matters for that is didEnterBackground. The gain is also small: a panel item is an id, a name and an optional URL (Views/PlayerView.swift:45-49), roughly tens of megabytes at most for a 50k-channel list and far less than the film and series arrays; stopping the prefetcher frees almost nothing (at most 48 requests, 3 concurrent, Views/ListImagePrefetch.swift:7-13). The 'purgeIfIdle' flag is unnecessary: LivePlayerShell copies the resolved sections into its own state at init (LiveStreamsView.swift:825-829, 802-805, 1025-1030), so clearing the cache while a player is open is safe and only costs a rebuild on the next open, which the cache already handles for a cold start (1253-1256, 1284-1299). The link between footprint and how often the app is terminated in the background is reasonable but unmeasured here.

**Corrected claim:** The app adds no memory handling of its own; Nuke and GRDB already purge themselves. The live channel-panel cache survives both entering the background and returning to the playlist list, so it keeps a second model of the live catalog alive after the catalog itself was unloaded. This is a small part of the footprint; the dominant part is the duplicated catalog representation covered by data-main-thread-12. A memory-warning observer would not reduce the suspended footprint.

**Corrected fix:** Two small changes, both without a player-state flag. (1) Add 'func purge() { entries.removeAll() }' to LiveChannelPanelSectionCache and call it next to PlaylistContentStore.shared.unload() in ContentView.swift:61-62 (the M3U closure does not use this cache). (2) Call the same purge from a UIApplication.didEnterBackgroundNotification observer, which is the moment that decides the suspended footprint; the existing observer in EPGStore.swift:73-75 shows the pattern. A didReceiveMemoryWarning observer may call the same purge but is optional. Skip ListImagePrefetch.cancelAll. Do not unload the catalog on either event. Treat the real reduction as data-main-thread-12 and measure before investing more here.

**API check:** UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification: UIApplication.h in the iOS 26 SDK UIKit headers (cited line 556; iOS 2.0+). UIApplication.didEnterBackgroundNotification is already used at EPG/EPGStore.swift:73. Nuke ImagePrefetcher: 'nonisolated public func stopPrefetching()' at Nuke/Sources/Nuke/Prefetching/ImagePrefetcher.swift:189 exists, but the corrected fix does not need it. No iOS 26 API.

**Regression risks:** After a purge the next live playback on a large catalog builds only the current category inline and the rest off the main thread (inlineBuildLimit 1500), so the full channel list appears a moment later than with a warm cache; this is the existing cold-start path. The cache is main-actor state under the project's default isolation, so the notification closure must hop to the main actor as EPGStore does. Purging while resolveAll is in flight is safe: it stores only when the playlist id still matches and merely repopulates the entries.

**How to verify:** Simulator: load a large synthetic catalog, play one live channel, close the player, send the app to the background and compare a memory graph or the Xcode memory gauge before and after the change; then play again and confirm the channel panel still lists every category. Return to the playlist list and confirm no ChannelPanelSection or DBLiveStream arrays remain in the memory graph. The effect on background terminations needs a device: note the footprint shown in Xcode's memory report after pressing Home, before and after, together with the catalog de-duplication.

## gap-localization-runtime-1 — L(_:_:) formats stringsdict plurals with locale nil, so Russian and Arabic counts only ever use the one/other forms ('5 серии', '21 серии', '3 حلقة') on every device, including Russian and Arabic ones.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail (season episode count), Search results (N more results), Settings (time remaining, watch-history count), M3U settings
- Code: `Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:131-138`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:1023`, `Views/SearchView.swift:166,191,216`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:289,491`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:198`, `Localization/ru.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict:1-90`, `Localization/ar.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict:1-110`

**What the user perceives:** A Russian user sees '10 серии' next to the season tabs (correct: '10 серий'), 'Ещё 21 результата' in search (correct: 'Ещё 21 результат'), '365 дня' for the subscription. An Arabic user sees '2 حلقة' / '5 حلقة' instead of 'حلقتان' / '5 حلقات'. Reads like machine output, on the default configuration.

**Mechanism (finder):** The plural tables are complete (ru: one/few/many/other; ar: zero/one/two/few/many/other; tr, zh: other; the rest one/other) and the string returned by bundle.localizedString is an __NSLocalizedString that keeps its plural config through the Swift String round trip (verified; re-encoding the string loses it). But LocalizationManager.swift:137 calls NSString(format:locale:nil,arguments:). Host script scratchpad/agents/l10n/plural.swift, loading ru.lproj / ar.lproj by path exactly like the app, run with -AppleLanguages en-US, ru-RU and ar-SA: with locale nil the category is 'one' for n==1 and 'other' for everything else regardless of the device language (ru: 1 серия, 2 серии, 5 серии, 21 серии; ar: 2 -> '2 حلقة', 5 -> '5 حلقة'). Because ru 'other' holds the 'few' form, 0, 5-20, 25-30, 100 ... are all wrong. With locale: Locale(identifier:"ru") the output is 1 серия / 2 серии / 5 серий / 21 серия; with "ar" it is حلقة واحدة / حلقتان / 5 حلقات / 21 حلقة. String.localizedStringWithFormat, which the comment at lines 132-134 claims is used, would not be right either: it uses Locale.current, so device-ru + app-en gives '21 Episode' and device ar_SA switches the digits. Correction to the brief: settings.stats.history_items_format and search.more_results_format are in the stringsdict of all ten languages (it shadows the .strings entry; en gives '1 item', '1 more result'). The only live count string outside the stringsdict is epg.detail.minutes_format (Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:120, ar '5 دقيقة'); series.episode_count_format is not referenced anywhere.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Pass the app locale (language of the selection, see the formatter finding for AppLocale.current) instead of nil:

nonisolated func L(_ key: String, _ args: CVarArg...) -> String {
    let format = LocalizationManager.resolveLocalizedString(for: key)
    return withVaList(args) { NSString(format: format, locale: AppLocale.current, arguments: $0) as String }
}

Side effect to handle: with a locale, %d gains grouping separators and the locale's digits ('1,234 more results'). That is wanted for counts but not for Networking/M3UParser.swift:576 (misc.channel_fallback_name is persisted as the channel name) and the HTTP status keys; give those a non-localizing variant (or format the number to a String and use %@). Fix the stale comment. No iOS 18 fallback needed.

**APIs:** NSString.init(format:locale:arguments:) (iOS 2.0 (NSString.h:381))

**Verifier reasons:** Re-read Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:135-138: L(_:_:) calls NSString(format:locale:nil,arguments:). The comment at 131-134 claims String.localizedStringWithFormat is used; it is not. History: commit 0ab5bcd replaced String(format:arguments:) with the locale-nil call together with the stringsdict files, with the stated intent of making plurals work, so locale nil is an oversight, not a deliberate choice (git show 0ab5bcd). ru.lproj/Localizable.stringsdict has one/few/many/other with 'other' holding the few form; ar has all six categories. I rebuilt the check myself (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n/plural.swift, loading the real .lproj by path like the app) and ran it under en-US, ru-RU and ar-SA: with locale nil the output is identical in all three processes: ru 1 серия, 2 серии, 5 серии, 11 серии, 21 серии, 100 серии; ar 2 -> '2 حلقة', 5 -> '5 حلقة', 11 -> '11 حلقة'. With Locale('ru') it is 5 серий / 21 серия / 100 серий; with Locale('ar') حلقتان / 5 حلقات. Passing Locale.current is also wrong in a mismatched process (en device + ru strings gives 21 серии; ru device + ar strings gives 21 -> 'حلقة واحدة'), so the app-language locale is the right argument. Live call sites: Views/SeriesView.swift:1023, Views/SearchView.swift:166/191/216, Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:289 and 491, Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:198. No unit test covers these keys (grep in another-iptv-playerTests found none). Host is macOS Foundation, but the plural selection lives in shared CoreFoundation formatting code, so I treat it as settled. Severity lowered from high: it is a grammar defect for two of ten languages, not a functional or fluidity problem.

**Corrected claim:** L(_:_:) formats stringsdict plurals with locale nil, so the plural category is 'one' for 1 and 'other' for everything else on every device. Russian shows the few-form for 0, 5-20, 25-30, 100... ('5 серии', '21 серии', '365 дня') and Arabic never uses the two/few/many forms ('2 حلقة', '5 حلقة'). Other eight languages are unaffected.

**Corrected fix:** Pass a locale whose language is the app language: NSString(format: format, locale: <app locale>, arguments: $0). AppLocale does not exist yet and there is no L() cache in the current code (resolveLocalizedString reads UserDefaults and builds Bundle(path:) on every call), so either land it with the AppLocale helper from finding 2/5 or, as a standalone minimal fix, use Locale(identifier: effectiveCode). Building the merged locale costs about 0.6 µs per call on the host, so caching is optional. Handle the side effect: with a locale, %d gets grouping separators and, on a merged ar_SA locale, Arabic-Indic digits. Keep a non-localizing path (format the Int to String and use %@, or a second helper with locale nil) for Networking/M3UParser.swift:576 (persisted channel name) and the HTTP status keys (Networking/M3UService.swift:14, Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:16, EPG/EPGError.swift:19). The change also reaches player strings through the shared helper (PlayerCore/KSPlayerEngine.swift:1150-1222, Views/PlayerView.swift:2739/3530/3548); values there are small integers so only the digit set can change. Fix the stale comment.

**API check:** NSString -initWithFormat:locale:arguments: is declared at Foundation.framework/Headers/NSString.h:381 (nullable id locale, no availability restriction, i.e. iOS 2.0). Swift call NSString(format:locale:arguments:) with a Foundation.Locale argument compiles and runs (verified in my host script). String.localizedStringWithFormat exists at Foundation.swiftinterface:22347 but is not suitable (uses Locale.current).

**Regression risks:** Counts of 1000 and above gain a grouping separator ('1 234 записи', '1,234 more results'); wanted for counts, not for the persisted M3U fallback channel name or HTTP codes. With a region-carrying Arabic locale the digits in every L(%d) string switch to Arabic-Indic, including player strings that are out of scope. No performance risk.

**How to verify:** Unit test in another-iptv-playerTests: set UserDefaults app.selected_language to ru and assert L("detail.episode_count_plural", n) for 1, 2, 5, 21, 100 equals '1 серия', '2 серии', '5 серий', '21 серия', '100 серий'; ar: 2 == 'حلقتان', 5 contains 'حلقات'. Assert M3UParser fallback names and 'HTTP 404' keep plain digits. Reference output: scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n/plural.swift.

## gap-localization-runtime-2 — The guide's day chips and times, download sizes and poster ratings are formatted with the device locale, so they stay in the device language when the in-app language differs ('Dün  Bugün  Yarın  Sun 4  Mon 5', '10:00 AM', 'Zero KB').

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide, Channel schedule, Programme detail sheet, Live player programme strip (shared helper), Downloads, Settings (storage used), Movie and series posters
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:426-432`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:183-193`, `Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:149-155`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:45,77`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:111`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:106`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:300,311`, `Views/RatingLabel.swift:4-12`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:60-66`

**What the user perceives:** With the app in Turkish on an English iPhone the guide header reads 'Dün  Bugün  Yarın  Sun 4  Mon 5', the time axis '10:00 AM', section headers 'Sunday, October 4', and Settings shows 'Kullanılan depolama   Zero KB'. In reverse (English app, Turkish phone) 'Today  Tomorrow  4 Paz'. Screenshot iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png shows the strings in question.

**Mechanism (finder):** Date.formatted(...) without .locale uses Locale.autoupdatingCurrent (EPGGuideView.swift:431, EPGComponents.swift:186, ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:154). ByteCountFormatter has no locale property at all (NSByteCountFormatter.h lists only units/style/flags): digits follow Locale.current and the unit words follow the main bundle's preferred localization. NumberFormatter in RatingLabel.swift:6 is pinned to .current inside a static let. The root only sets the SwiftUI environment locale (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:64), which none of these read. Answer to 'which can be fixed by passing the locale': all three Date sites and the rating formatter yes; byte counts only by switching API to ByteCountFormatStyle. Host run (scratchpad/agents/l10n/fmt.swift, device en_US): tr -> '6 Sal', 'ÖS 7:30', '0 kB' / '2.34 GB'; ar -> 'ثلاثاء، 6', '7:30 م', 'صفر كيلوبايت'.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add one nonisolated source of truth and use it everywhere, including the root environment:

enum AppLocale {
    static var current: Locale {            // cached with the L() cache, cleared on language change
        guard let code = selectedCode else { return .current }   // 'system' -> untouched device locale
        var c = Locale.Components(locale: .current)
        c.languageComponents.languageCode = Locale.LanguageCode(code)
        c.languageComponents.script = nil
        return Locale(components: c)       // tr_US, ar_SA, en_DE: what iOS itself builds for a per-app language
    }
}

Then: day.formatted(.dateTime.weekday(.abbreviated).day().locale(AppLocale.current)); EPGTimeFormat.time with .locale(...); EPGTimeFormat.range via (start..<stop).formatted(.interval.hour().minute().locale(...)) which also collapses the day period ('7:30 – 8:00 PM'); bytes.formatted(.byteCount(style: .file).locale(...)) at the four ByteCountFormatter sites; RatingLabel's formatter takes the same locale (rebuild it when the cache is cleared). Cost check on the host: Date.formatted with a locale is 0.72 µs, same as today; the byte-count style is 9 µs vs 1.5 µs but only runs in Settings and Downloads rows. The merged locale keeps the device region, so Turkish on a US-region phone shows 12-hour 'ÖS 7:30' exactly as iOS does for a per-app language; the user's 24-Hour Time toggle should carry through Locale.Components(locale:) and must be confirmed on a device. The two settings views contain the uncommitted TipJarRow() line: only the single ByteCountFormatter line changes in each, TipJarRow() and the tip keys stay untouched.

**APIs:** Date.FormatStyle.locale(_:) (iOS 15.0); Date.IntervalFormatStyle.locale(_:) (iOS 15.0); ByteCountFormatStyle.locale(_:) / .byteCount(style:) (iOS 15.0); Locale.Components(locale:) / Locale(components:) (iOS 16.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The mechanism is real. Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:431, Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:186 and Views/EPG/ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:154 call Date.formatted without a locale, so they use the device locale, while the neighbouring Today/Tomorrow/Yesterday labels come from L(). ByteCountFormatter.string at Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:111, Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:106 and Views/DownloadsView.swift:300/311 has no locale input; Views/RatingLabel.swift:6 pins .current in a static let. Host run (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n/fmt.swift, process en_US): default chip 'Tue 6', time '7:30 PM', 'Zero KB'; with a tr locale '6 Sal', 'ÖS 7:30', '0 kB'. It only affects users whose in-app language differs from the device language; 'System' users are consistent. The screenshots are all English app on an English device, so they show which strings exist, not the mix. Two parts of the proposed fix are wrong. (1) Replacing EPGTimeFormat.range with (start..<stop).formatted(.interval.hour().minute()) regresses programmes that cross midnight: the host prints '10/2/2026, 11:30 PM – 10/3/2026, 12:30 AM' (en_US) and '2.10.2026 23:30 – 3.10.2026 00:30' (tr_TR) (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n/iv.swift), and start..<stop traps if a panel sends stop earlier than start. The helper also feeds Views/PlayerView.swift:5617 and Views/EPG/CatchupPlayerShell.swift:26, which are out of scope. (2) .byteCount(style:.file) with the default spellsOutZero prints 'Zero kB' for en and also for a pt_US merged locale, so the English word can still leak. Also: a static let formatter cannot be 'rebuilt', and the merged locale with script = nil resolves zh on a TW-region device to Traditional weekday names ('週二') while zh.lproj is Simplified ('删除').

**Corrected claim:** When the in-app language is set explicitly and differs from the device language, the guide's weekday chips, the schedule's day headers, EPG times (AM/PM marker) and byte counts stay in the device language ('Dün Bugün Yarın Sun 4 Mon 5', 'Zero KB'), because those formatters use the device locale and ignore the SwiftUI environment locale. Users on 'System' are not affected.

**Corrected fix:** Add one nonisolated AppLocale.current (app language + device region and preferences via Locale.Components(locale: .current) / Locale(components:); for zh pin script to Hans; return Locale.current when its language already equals the effective app language). Then: day.formatted(.dateTime.weekday(.abbreviated).day().locale(AppLocale.current)) at EPGGuideView.swift:431; the same .locale(...) at ChannelEPGDetailView.swift:154 and in EPGTimeFormat.time (EPGComponents.swift:186). Keep EPGTimeFormat.range as the existing two-time string; do not switch to the interval style. Byte counts: bytes.formatted(.byteCount(style: .file, spellsOutZero: false).locale(AppLocale.current)) at the four ByteCountFormatter sites (one line each; the TipJarRow() lines in the two settings views stay untouched). RatingLabel: leave it out of this change; its output does not depend on language, only on region and digits, which belongs to finding 5. Caching the locale is optional: building it per call measured 0.6 µs, Date.formatted 0.85 µs with or without the locale.

**API check:** Foundation.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0 SDK): Date.FormatStyle.locale(_:) present (iOS 15); Date.IntervalFormatStyle with locale(_:), hour(_:), minute() at lines 1755-1792 (iOS 15), exists but should not be used here; ByteCountFormatStyle at 3969 with locale(_:) and FormatStyle.byteCount(style:allowedUnits:spellsOutZero:includesActualByteCount:) at 4082 (iOS 15); Locale.Components at 12318 with init(locale:) at 4551 and Locale.init(components:) at 12073 (iOS 16). All below the iOS 18 target, no fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** Interval style would break midnight-crossing programmes and can trap on inverted ranges (dropped in the corrected fix). ByteCountFormatStyle prints 'kB' where ByteCountFormatter prints 'KB'. A merged locale such as tr_US shows 12-hour 'ÖS 7:30' on a US-region phone; that matches iOS per-app language behaviour but is a visible change. Whether the user's 24-Hour Time switch survives Locale.Components(locale:) could not be settled on the host (-AppleICUForce24HourTime had no effect there). EPGTimeFormat is shared with the live player's programme strip.

**How to verify:** Unit tests for AppLocale and EPGTimeFormat with an injected language code ('6 Sal' for tr; a 23:30-00:30 programme must still render as two plain times). Simulator: launch with '-AppleLanguages (en) -AppleLocale en_US -app.selected_language tr', open the guide, a channel schedule and Settings; chips, day headers and the storage row must be Turkish. Device: toggle 24-Hour Time with region US and the app in Turkish; guide axis must follow the toggle.

## gap-localization-runtime-3 — The in-app language picker duplicates iOS's per-app Language setting and is the root cause of the mixed-language cases and of the root .id rebuild; whether to replace it, bridge it to AppleLanguages or keep it is an owner decision.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk medium
- Screens: Settings (Language), Whole app
- Code: `Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift:4-62`, `Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:26-57,75-114`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:56-68`, `../App-Info.plist:5-17`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Replace the in-app picker with the system per-app Language setting (A), keep the picker but also write AppleLanguages so the system follows after a relaunch (B), or keep the current mechanism and patch call sites (C).

**What the user perceives:** Today a language picked in the app changes the app's own strings instantly but throws the user back to the first tab (rebuild), while every system-owned piece (search empty state, swipe Delete, document picker, review prompt, VoiceOver voice, date and size formats, UIKit bar direction for Arabic) stays in the device language until fixed one by one, and some never can be.

**Mechanism (finder):** L() loads <code>.lproj by path (LocalizationManager.swift:75-100) and the root overrides \.locale / \.layoutDirection and re-creates the tree with .id (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:60-66). Bundle.main.preferredLocalizations, Locale.current and UIKit's layout direction are fixed at launch from the AppleLanguages default, which is exactly what the system per-app Language row writes. App-Info.plist already declares the ten CFBundleLocalizations and the .lproj folders are real localizations, so that row already exists for this app and already works whenever the picker is on 'System' (systemLanguageCode() reads Locale.preferredLanguages, lines 104-114); with an explicit in-app choice the two mechanisms disagree.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Three options.
A. Native only: LanguagePickerSection becomes one row showing the current language that opens the app's Settings page: UIApplication.shared.open(URL(string: UIApplication.openSettingsURLString)!). L() resolves from Bundle.main; the \.locale / \.layoutDirection overrides and .id go away (iOS relaunches the app when the language changes). This removes every mixed-language case, makes localizedStringWithFormat-style plurals and all formatters correct by default, fixes VoiceOver voice and RTL chrome, and removes the rebuild. Lost: switching inside the app; the Language row is, as far as I know, only shown by iOS when the device has at least two preferred languages (it then lists all ten app languages) - confirm on a device; existing explicit choices need a one-time migration (if app.selected_language != 'system', write UserDefaults 'AppleLanguages' = [code] + current preferred languages, effective from the next launch, then drop the key).
B. Bridge (middle path): keep the picker UI but have it write 'AppleLanguages' (remove the key for 'System') in addition to the live L() switch, with a footnote that system texts follow after the next launch. From the next launch everything, including UIKit direction and Locale.current, matches. Keep a single source of truth (derive the shown selection from Bundle.main.preferredLocalizations at launch), otherwise iOS Settings and the picker can disagree because both write the same key.
C. Keep as is and apply the individual fixes in the other findings; the non-fixable list in the system-strings finding remains.
My recommendation: B as the smallest change that keeps the feature, A for the most native result. Either needs one or two new strings appended to the ten Localizable.strings; the uncommitted tip keys stay as they are and the change is confined to LanguagePickerSection.swift, so the TipJarRow() lines in the settings views are not touched.

**APIs:** UIApplication.openSettingsURLString (iOS 8.0 (UIApplication.h:613)); UserDefaults key 'AppleLanguages' (defaults key, not an SDK symbol; the same key the UI tests pass at another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:17) (all iOS versions)

**Verifier reasons:** The structural facts hold. L() loads <code>.lproj by path (Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:75-100), the root overrides \.locale and \.layoutDirection and rebuilds with .id(localization.selectedLanguage) (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:60-66), and App-Info.plist:5-17 declares the ten CFBundleLocalizations, so the system per-app Language row can exist alongside the picker. The rebuild cost is real: ContentView's @State selectedPlaylist and DashboardView's @StateObject PlayerOverlayController are recreated, and DashboardTab.restoreInitialTab (Views/DashboardView.swift:200-216) only restores content tabs, so after picking a language the user lands on the last content tab rather than Settings, and a docked mini player is torn down. But the premise that system text stays in the device language 'until fixed one by one' is overstated. I rendered ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) on the host (macOS 26.3 SwiftUI, process language en-US) with .environment(\.locale, tr): it shows '“zzzzqq” için sonuç yok / Yazım denetimi yapın veya yeni bir arama deneyin.' (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n/cuv-tr.png), and Arabic with ar. The iOS 26 simulator runtime's SwiftUI.framework/tr.lproj/Localizable.strings contains ContentUnavailableView_Search_Text, Delete, Back, Cancel, Done, Close, so SwiftUI-owned strings are resolved through the environment locale the root already sets. What really cannot follow the picker is UIKit- and system-owned text: UISearchBar's default placeholder and iOS 18 Cancel title, edit menus, the document picker, the StoreKit review and purchase sheets, the permission prompt, VoiceOver's voice, and UIKit bar direction. That is a smaller list than claimed, which weakens the case for replacing the picker. Options A and B are technically sound as described, but this is a product decision, not a defect.

**Corrected claim:** The in-app picker overlaps iOS's per-app Language setting. With an explicit in-app choice, the app's own strings and SwiftUI-owned system strings follow the picker (via the root environment locale), while UIKit- and system-owned text (document picker, StoreKit sheets, edit menus, default search placeholder, VoiceOver voice, UIKit bar direction) and every formatter that reads Locale.current follow the device. Changing the language rebuilds the whole tree: the user leaves Settings for the last content tab and a docked mini player is dropped.

**Corrected fix:** Owner decision. Recommended default: keep the picker (option C) and apply findings 1, 2 and 5; the remaining mismatch is limited to UIKit/system-owned text. If the owner wants those to match too, option B (also write the AppleLanguages default so the next launch agrees; derive the shown selection from one source of truth) is the smallest step; option A (replace the picker with a row that opens the app's page in Settings) is the most native but removes in-app switching and depends on the system Language row, which iOS shows only when the device has more than one preferred language (to be confirmed on a device). Independent of the option: make the language change not lose the user's place, for example by restoring the Settings tab after the .id rebuild.

**API check:** UIApplication.openSettingsURLString: UIKit.framework/Headers/UIApplication.h (iOS 8.0), present. 'AppleLanguages' is a defaults key, not an SDK symbol; the UI tests already pass it as a launch argument (another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:17, 500). EnvironmentValues.locale / layoutDirection: SwiftUICore, iOS 13.

**Regression risks:** A and B change behaviour existing users rely on (instant in-app switch; A needs a one-time migration of app.selected_language). B writes a key that iOS Settings also writes, so the picker and Settings can disagree unless the selection is derived from Bundle.main.preferredLocalizations. A removes the reason for the root .id, .locale and .layoutDirection overrides added in 0ab5bcd; removing them must not be done under B or C. Edits stay inside Localization/LanguagePickerSection.swift and LocalizationManager.swift; the tip-jar lines are not touched.

**How to verify:** Simulator with '-AppleLanguages (en) -app.selected_language tr': note which texts are English (expected: default search placeholder, document picker, edit menu, review prompt) and which are Turkish (expected: search empty state, swipe Delete). Device with two preferred languages: check that Settings > Apps > the app shows a Language row listing the ten languages, and what happens when it and the in-app picker disagree. For B: pick Arabic in the app, relaunch, confirm navigation bars, back-swipe edge and the document picker are Arabic and right-to-left.

## gap-localization-runtime-4 — System-provided text stays in the device language at four replaceable call sites (search empty state twice, the guide's default search prompt, swipe-to-delete on the playlist list); the rest of the system text cannot be changed inside the process.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search, Downloads, TV Guide, Playlist list, Add playlist forms, Review prompt
- Code: `Views/SearchView.swift:241`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:77`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:53`, `ContentView.swift:243-252`, `Views/Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:156`, `Models/RatingManager.swift:66`, `Views/AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:114`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:250`

**What the user perceives:** App in Turkish on an English phone: a search with no hits shows 'No Results for "zzzzqq" / Check the spelling or try a new search.' (iphone-light/R01-search-no-results.png) under Turkish filter chips; the guide's search field says 'Search'; swiping a playlist shows the app's own 'Düzenle' on the leading side and the system's 'Delete' on the trailing side.

**Mechanism (finder):** Replaceable: ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) ships its own strings (SearchView.swift:241, DownloadsView.swift:77); .searchable(text:) without prompt uses the system placeholder (EPGGuideView.swift:53; every other .searchable passes L()); .onDelete supplies the system 'Delete' title (ContentView.swift:252, also PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:156). Not changeable in-process, all follow the main bundle's launch-time localization: the search field's Cancel title on iOS 18 (on iOS 26 it is an xmark glyph, see iphone-light/Q02-search-focused.png, as is the keyboard's search key); text edit menus (Paste, AutoFill, Look Up) on the form and search fields; the document picker chrome behind .fileImporter (AddM3UPlaylistView.swift:114, M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:250); the StoreKit review prompt (RatingManager.swift:66) and the purchase sheet; the local-network permission text (InfoPlist.strings); the back button's VoiceOver label and its iOS 18 'Back' fallback (back-menu entries are app titles and are fine); VoiceOver's trait and hint speech and the voice it picks for L() strings. The keyboard's return-key word follows the keyboard language in every app and is not a defect. Not present: EditButton, default alert buttons (every .alert passes L() buttons), pull-to-refresh text.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the four sites with app strings using keys that already exist, the way Views/WatchHistoryListView.swift:59-62 and Views/M3UFavoritesView.swift:34-37 already do:

ContentUnavailableView {
    Label(L("favorites.empty.no_result.title"), systemImage: "magnifyingglass")
} description: { Text(L("category_picker.not_found.message")) }

EPGGuideView.swift:53 -> .searchable(text: $model.searchQuery, prompt: L("live.search_placeholder")). ContentView.swift:252 -> drop .onDelete and add .swipeActions(edge: .trailing) { Button(role: .destructive) { offsetsToDelete = IndexSet(integer: index); showingDeleteAlert = true } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") } }. Keeping the query echo ('No Results for …') would need one new format key in the ten Localizable.strings (append only, tip keys untouched); the minimal fix needs no new key. The non-changeable group is only solved by the language-mechanism decision (options A or B).

**APIs:** ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:) (iOS 17.0); View.searchable(text:placement:prompt:) (iOS 15.0); View.swipeActions(edge:allowsFullSwipe:content:) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The headline case is refuted. ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) at Views/SearchView.swift:241 and Views/DownloadsView.swift:77 does not stay in the device language: it is a SwiftUI-owned string resolved through the environment locale, which the root already sets to the app language (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:64). Host render (macOS 26.3 SwiftUI, process en-US, .environment(\.locale, tr) and merged tr_US / ar_US): '“zzzzqq” için sonuç yok / Yazım denetimi yapın veya yeni bir arama deneyin.' and the Arabic equivalent (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n/cuv-tr.png, m-tr.png, m-ar.png). The iOS 26 simulator runtime ships the same keys in SwiftUI.framework/tr.lproj/Localizable.strings ('ContentUnavailableView_Search_Text %@' => '“%@” için sonuç yok'). The cited screenshot iphone-light/R01-search-no-results.png is an English app on an English device and proves nothing about a mix. Replacing these two sites would also lose the native query echo. The .onDelete title (ContentView.swift:252) is probably the same case: SwiftUI's own table has 'Delete' => 'Sil', so it should follow the environment too; not confirmed without a simulator. The proposed replacement there does not compile as written (there is no 'index' in ForEach(playlists) { playlist in ... }) and Button(role: .destructive) in front of a confirmation alert makes the row animate away and snap back on Cancel. Views/Components/PlaybackTrackSettingsSheet.swift:156 is the player's track sheet and out of scope. What remains: .searchable(text:) without a prompt at Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:53. SwiftUI's string table has no 'Search' entry, so the placeholder comes from UIKit and follows the process language; every other .searchable in the app passes L(...). The 'cannot be changed in-process' list is correct for UIKit and system-owned text.

**Corrected claim:** One call site shows a system-language string under an explicit in-app language: the guide's search field has no prompt (Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:53) and falls back to UIKit's 'Search'. The search empty states already follow the in-app language through the environment locale; the playlist list's swipe 'Delete' most likely does as well. UIKit- and system-owned text (document picker, StoreKit sheets, edit menus, iOS 18 search Cancel) cannot be changed from inside the process.

**Corrected fix:** EPGGuideView.swift:53 -> .searchable(text: $model.searchQuery, prompt: L("live.search_placeholder")) (the query filters channels, EPGGuideViewModel.swift:155; the key exists in all checked languages). Leave both ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) sites as they are. Leave .onDelete in ContentView.swift:252 unless a simulator run shows 'Delete' in the device language; if it does, use .swipeActions(edge: .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: false) { Button { offsetsToDelete = IndexSet(integer: i); showingDeleteAlert = true } label: { Label(L("common.delete"), systemImage: "trash") }.tint(.red) } with i taken from playlists.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == playlist.id }), without role: .destructive because a confirmation alert follows.

**API check:** View.searchable(text:placement:prompt:) with a String prompt: SwiftUI.swiftinterface, iOS 15. View.swipeActions(edge:allowsFullSwipe:content:): iOS 15. ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) and ContentUnavailableView(label:description:actions:): iOS 17. All present; no iOS 18 fallback needed.

**Regression risks:** Applying the original fix would replace the system search empty state with a generic one and drop the query echo, and would introduce a destructive-role swipe that glitches on Cancel. The corrected one-line prompt change has no risk beyond the guide showing 'Search channel...' instead of 'Search'.

**How to verify:** Simulator, '-AppleLanguages (en) -AppleLocale en_US -app.selected_language tr': (1) search 'zzzzqq' in the Search tab and in Downloads, expect the Turkish empty state; (2) swipe a playlist row on the playlist list, read the trailing button title; (3) open the guide and read the search placeholder before and after the change.
