## gap-localization-runtime-5 — The root environment locale is a bare language code (Locale(identifier: "ar")), so on Arabic-region devices one screen mixes Arabic-Indic and Latin digits, and 'System' users lose their region's number formats in SwiftUI-formatted text.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: TV Guide, Settings statistics, Search section headers, Posters and detail hero, Downloads
- Code: `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:60-66`, `Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:268-289`, `Views/SearchView.swift:333`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:111`, `Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:111`, `Views/RatingLabel.swift:6`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:157`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: For Arabic: follow the device region's digits (Arabic-Indic in SA/EG, the system behaviour) or force Latin digits everywhere.

**What the user perceives:** On a Saudi or Egyptian iPhone with the app in Arabic (the default 'System' setting): guide chips and times are '٢٥ ،ثلاثاء' and '٧:٣٠ م', poster ratings '٧٫٥', download sizes '٢٫٣٤ GB', while channel counts are '12,345', '5 حلقات' and the detail-page rating is '7.5'. With Arabic chosen in the app on an English device all digits are Latin and consistent, but dates are English.

**Mechanism (finder):** effectiveLanguageCode strips the region even for 'system' and the root passes Locale(identifier: code). Host run (scratchpad/agents/l10n/fmt.swift): Locale(identifier:"ar").numberingSystem is latn while Locale.current on ar_SA / ar_EG is arab. Three families then disagree: (1) Text("\(n)") and Label("\(title) (\(count))") are LocalizedStringKey interpolations formatted with the environment locale -> Latin digits with grouping; (2) Date.formatted, NumberFormatter(.current) and ByteCountFormatter use the device locale -> Arabic-Indic; (3) String(format:) and L(%d) with locale nil -> plain Latin, no grouping (so Settings shows '45,123' above '12345 items'). For non-Arabic 'System' users the same stripping replaces de_CH / es_MX / en_GB by generic de / es / en for everything SwiftUI formats.

**Proposed fix (finder):** In AppRootView, do not override anything when the selection is 'system' (pass Locale.current and leave layoutDirection alone); for an explicit choice use AppLocale.current from the formatter finding (language from the app, region and preferences from the device) for \.locale, every formatter and the L(_:_:) locale. All three families then share one numbering system: ar_SA device -> Arabic-Indic everywhere, Arabic on a US-region device -> Latin everywhere. Route DetailComponents.swift:157 through the same rating formatter. If Latin digits are preferred for Arabic regardless of region, set c.numberingSystem = "latn" in AppLocale. another_iptv_playerApp.swift carries an uncommitted tip line (TipStore.shared.startObservingTransactions() at line 41); only AppRootView (lines 60-66) changes.

**APIs:** Locale.Components.numberingSystem / Locale(components:) (iOS 16.0); EnvironmentValues.locale (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Mechanism confirmed. another_iptv_playerApp.swift:60-64 passes Locale(identifier: code) where code is a bare language even for 'system' (LocalizationManager.swift:104-114 strips the region). Host: Locale(identifier:'ar').numberingSystem is latn while Locale.current on ar_SA is arab. I rendered the three families in one SwiftUI view in an ar_SA process with the bare 'ar' environment (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n/sa/bare-ar.png): Text("\(12345)") shows '12,345' (environment locale, Latin, grouped) and Date.formatted shows 'اثنين، ٢٤' (device locale, Arabic-Indic); L(%d) with locale nil gives plain '12345'. So on a device with Arabic-Indic digits, Settings statistics (Views/PlaylistSettingsView.swift:268-289), guide counts (Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:111), category counts (Views/Components/CategoryPickerSheet.swift:111) and search headers (Views/SearchView.swift:333) use Latin digits next to Arabic-Indic dates, times, ratings (Views/RatingLabel.swift:6) and sizes. The same render with a tr environment shows '12.345', confirming that Text interpolation is locale-formatted. A second, wider inconsistency the finding only touches: Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:157 uses String(format: "%.1f") ('7.5') while posters use NumberFormatter(.current) ('7,5' on any comma-decimal region such as TR, DE, FR, RU). The proposed fix needs one correction: 'pass Locale.current when the selection is system' is only right when the device language is one the app resolves to itself. For a zh-Hant device the app loads zh.lproj (Simplified) but Locale.current would not be zh; in that case the locale must still be derived from the effective code. Dropping the layoutDirection override for 'system' is unnecessary; computing it from the effective code is equal in the normal case and safer in the mismatch case. Severity lowered: it is a digit-set consistency issue for Arabic-Indic regions plus a decimal-separator mismatch, not a fluidity problem.

**Corrected claim:** The root environment locale is a bare language code, so SwiftUI-formatted numbers (Text interpolation, Label counts) use that language's default digits and grouping, while Date.formatted, NumberFormatter(.current) and ByteCountFormatter use the device locale and L(%d) uses none. On Arabic-Indic-digit devices one screen mixes '12,345' with '٧:٣٠ م' and '٧٫٥'; for all 'System' users the region's number format is replaced by the generic one in SwiftUI-formatted text; and the detail page rating ('7.5') disagrees with the poster rating ('7,5') on comma-decimal regions.

**Corrected fix:** Use the single AppLocale.current from finding 2 for \.locale at the root, for the formatters and for the L(_:_:) locale. Definition: if Locale.current's language code equals the effective app language, return Locale.current unchanged (covers 'system' in the normal case and keeps region, digits, calendar, hour cycle); otherwise build Locale(components:) from Locale.Components(locale: .current) with the app language (script Hans for zh). Keep the layoutDirection line as it is. Route DetailComponents.swift:157 through ContentRating's formatter and give that formatter AppLocale (a small cache keyed by locale identifier instead of the static let; displayText runs per poster cell). Only AppRootView changes in another_iptv_playerApp.swift; the TipStore line at 41 stays. Owner decision: for Arabic, follow the device's digits or force Latin (numberingSystem = latn in AppLocale).

**API check:** Foundation.swiftinterface: Locale.Components (12318) with numberingSystem (12323), hourCycle (12325), languageComponents (12319); Locale.Components.init(locale:) (4551); Locale.init(components:) (12073); Locale.numberingSystem (12230); all iOS 16. EnvironmentValues.locale: SwiftUICore, iOS 13. No iOS 26 API involved.

**Regression risks:** With a region-carrying locale in the environment, SwiftUI-formatted counts on Arabic-Indic devices switch to Arabic-Indic digits and Text(date, style:) picks up the device calendar (the host render shows a Hijri date for ar_SA); both are system behaviour but visible changes. SwiftUI-owned system strings still resolve with a merged locale (tr_US and ar_US rendered Turkish and Arabic on the host). When the environment locale equals Locale.current SwiftUI used the process localization in my host test, which in the app is the same language. RatingLabel sits on the poster scroll path: keep the formatter cached.

**How to verify:** Simulator, '-AppleLanguages (ar) -AppleLocale ar_SA': screenshot Settings statistics, the guide, a movie grid and a movie detail before and after; every number must use one digit set. Second run with '-AppleLanguages (tr) -AppleLocale tr_TR': poster badge and detail hero must both show '7,5'. Unit test: AppLocale for ('system', ar_SA) equals Locale.current; for ('ar', en_US) has latn digits; for ('zh', zh_TW) formats weekdays in Simplified.

## gap-localization-runtime-6 — The same rating is rendered with two decimal separators: '7,5' on posters (NumberFormatter with the device locale) and '7.5' on the detail hero (String(format:)).

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Movies shelves and grids, Series shelves and grids, Movie detail, Series detail
- Code: `Views/RatingLabel.swift:4-27,70-86`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:152-166`

**What the user perceives:** On any comma-decimal region (Turkey, Germany, Russia, France...) the poster badge says '7,5'; tapping it opens a hero that says '7.5'. No in-app language choice is needed to see it.

**Mechanism (finder):** PosterRatingBadge and RatingLabel go through ContentRating.displayText -> NumberFormatter with locale .current (RatingLabel.swift:5-11). DetailHeroMetaRow formats the numeric rating with String(format: "%.1f", rating10) (DetailComponents.swift:157), which never localizes, and only falls back to RatingLabel for non-numeric text. Host run: device tr_TR -> NumberFormatter '7,5', String(format:) '7.5'; device ar_SA -> '٧٫٥' vs '7.5'.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add ContentRating.displayText(_ value: Double) that uses the same formatter (with AppLocale.current once that exists) and call it at DetailComponents.swift:157. Keep the half-up rounding and the 'hide zero' rule in RatingLabel.swift:14-27.

**APIs:** NumberFormatter.locale (iOS 2.0)

**Verifier reasons:** Views/RatingLabel.swift:4-12 builds a static NumberFormatter with locale .current; RatingLabel (line 40) and PosterRatingBadge (line 74) both go through ContentRating.displayText. Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:152-157 renders the hero rating with String(format: "%.1f", rating10), and only falls back to RatingLabel at 164-165 when rating10 is nil or 0. Both detail screens pass a numeric value (Views/MovieDetailView.swift:65, Views/SeriesView.swift:834: rating5Based * 2), so the unlocalized branch is the normal path. My host probe (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n-c/units2.swift) gives NumberFormatter 7,5 for tr/de/es/fr/pt/ru and '٧٫٥' for ar_SA, against 7.5 from String(format:). git log -S shows both lines date from the initial monorepo commit d2489f9 with no comment, so this is not deliberate. The demo screenshots are en_US and cannot show it. One addition: the poster uses the device locale, not the in-app language, so an English in-app choice on a Turkish-region device shows '7,5' on posters inside an English UI.

**Corrected claim:** The same rating is rendered with two decimal separators on comma-decimal devices: posters and cards use NumberFormatter with the device locale ('7,5'), the detail hero uses String(format: "%.1f") ('7.5'). The poster format follows the device region, not the language chosen in the app.

**Corrected fix:** Add ContentRating.displayText(_ value: Double) -> String? that returns nil for values <= 0 and otherwise roundedFormatter.string(from: NSNumber(value: value)); call it at DetailComponents.swift:157. AppLocale does not exist in the tree (grep finds nothing), so until it does, keep the formatter's existing locale; that alone makes hero and poster agree. If the formatter is later tied to the in-app language, it can no longer be a static let that captures the locale once: rebuild it when LocalizationManager.selectedLanguage changes. Keep the half-up rounding and the hide-zero rule.

**API check:** NumberFormatter.locale and NumberFormatter.string(from: NSNumber) are Foundation, available since iOS 2.0. No SwiftUI API involved. AppLocale.current is not an existing symbol in this code base.

**Regression risks:** Minimal. On ar_SA devices the hero would switch to Arabic-Indic digits like the posters already do, while the year next to it stays in Western digits; that mix exists on posters today. The hero and poster can still show different numbers because they read different fields (rating5Based * 2 versus the rating string); this fix does not change that.

**How to verify:** Unit test with an injectable locale: displayText("7.46") and displayText(7.46) both return '7,5' for tr_TR and '7.5' for en_US; displayText(0.0) returns nil. Then one screenshot of a movie card and its detail on a simulator with region Turkey.

## gap-localization-runtime-7 — Ten chevron.right glyphs and the guide's collapsed-category chevron do not mirror in Arabic; the guide grid itself mirrors coherently in a host probe but has never been run right-to-left on iOS.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Live TV shelves, Movies shelves, Series shelves, M3U shelves, Continue Watching, Movie and series detail (primary button), Playlist list, Playlist type sheet, TV Guide
- Code: `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:113,362`, `Views/VODView.swift:321,424`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:298,400`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:69,343`, `Views/Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:37`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:226`, `Views/PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:67`, `ContentView.swift:235`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:23,82,103-106`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:155,208,222,247`

**What the user perceives:** In Arabic the shelf titles sit on the right but their disclosure chevrons still point right, away from the direction the screen will push; a collapsed guide category shows a chevron pointing right instead of left.

**Mechanism (finder):** chevron.right is a fixed-direction symbol; chevron.forward is the mirroring one. EPGGuideRowViews.swift:103-106 rotates chevron.down by -90 degrees when collapsed, which points right in both directions. calendar.day.timeline.left (LiveStreamsView.swift:113, M3UChannelsView.swift:69) has a .leading variant. Guide geometry: host probes scratchpad/agents/l10n/rtl/rtl.swift and scroll.swift (macOS SwiftUI, same SwiftUICore layout) show that under layoutDirection .rightToLeft a positive .offset(x:) moves toward the trailing side (a cell offset of +200 lands 200 pt left of the leading edge; the pinned column with +30 moves from x 500 to 470) and that ScrollGeometry.contentOffset.x and ScrollPosition.scrollTo(x:) are leading-relative (0 at rest, 500 after scrollTo(x: 500)). So the pinned column .offset(x: bodyOffsetX) (EPGGuideView.swift:208, 247), cell offsets (EPGGuideRowViews.swift:23, 82) and now-lines (EPGGuideView.swift:155, 222) should mirror together: channel column pinned on the right, time running right to left, which is the normal RTL convention. That is AppKit-backed evidence; the UIScrollView-backed iOS path is unverified.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Replace the ten sites with Image(systemName: "chevron.forward"); use calendar.day.timeline.leading; in EPGCategoryHeader read @Environment(\.layoutDirection) and rotate by +90 in RTL (or switch the symbol between chevron.down and chevron.forward). Needs a simulator run in Arabic before anything else in the guide is changed: (a) channel column stays pinned at the right edge while scrolling, jump-to-now lands on the now line, axis and body stay in sync; (b) with an English device and Arabic chosen in the app: navigation-bar back button side, swipe-back edge, tab-bar order, sheets and menus, because UIKit chrome follows the app-level direction and may not follow the SwiftUI environment override. If (a) fails on iOS, the conservative fix is .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight) on the grid at EPGGuideView.swift:127.

**APIs:** SF Symbol chevron.forward (iOS 14 (SF Symbols 2020)); SF Symbol calendar.day.timeline.leading (iOS 15 (SF Symbols 2021)); EnvironmentValues.layoutDirection (iOS 13.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The app does apply right-to-left from the in-app choice (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:60-66 sets \.locale and \.layoutDirection), so the question is real. I confirmed the ten chevron.right sites by grep: LiveStreamsView.swift:362, VODView.swift:321 and 424, SeriesView.swift:298 and 400, M3UChannelsView.swift:343, Components/ContinueWatchingRow.swift:37, Components/DetailComponents.swift:226, PlaylistTypeSelectionView.swift:67, ContentView.swift:235. Host probe scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n-c/chev.swift (macOS SwiftUI, ImageRenderer, pixel analysis of which side the tip is on): chevron.right points right under both layout directions; chevron.forward points right in LTR and left under .environment(\.layoutDirection, .rightToLeft). So that part stands, and the symbol follows the SwiftUI environment override. The guide-header part is wrong: the same probe shows chevron.down with rotationEffect(-90) points RIGHT in LTR and LEFT in RTL, because SwiftUI mirrors the rotation along with the rest of the geometry (consistent with the finder's own observation that .offset(x:) mirrors). EPGGuideRowViews.swift:103-106 is therefore already correct in Arabic, and the proposed '+90 in RTL' would make it point right, which is the bug it claims to fix. calendar.day.timeline.left vs .leading: the probe confirms .left is fixed and .leading mirrors; it is a toolbar icon for the guide, so this is cosmetic. The guide grid claim (EPGGuideView.swift:127-250, EPGGuideRowViews.swift:23, 82) rests on AppKit-backed probes only and there is no Arabic screenshot in shots/, so it stays undecided until a simulator run.

**Corrected claim:** Ten disclosure chevrons use the fixed-direction symbol chevron.right and keep pointing right in Arabic, where the shelf titles and the push direction are mirrored. The guide's collapsed-category chevron is not affected: its rotationEffect is mirrored by SwiftUI and already points left in right-to-left. Whether the guide grid (pinned channel column, time axis, now-line, jump-to-now) behaves correctly right-to-left on iOS is unverified.

**Corrected fix:** Replace the ten Image(systemName: "chevron.right") with "chevron.forward". Optionally switch calendar.day.timeline.left to calendar.day.timeline.leading at LiveStreamsView.swift:113 and M3UChannelsView.swift:69. Do not touch EPGCategoryHeader. Before changing anything in the guide, run it once in Arabic on the simulator; only if the pinned column or scroll sync fails, force .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight) on the grid at EPGGuideView.swift:127, which is the same approach the player scrub bar already takes (Views/PlayerScrubBar.swift:240).

**API check:** SF Symbols checked in /System/Library/CoreServices/CoreGlyphs.bundle name_availability.plist: chevron.forward = 2020 release (iOS 14.0), calendar.day.timeline.leading = 2021 release (iOS 15.0); both below the iOS 18 target. EnvironmentValues.layoutDirection is iOS 13. chevron.right appears in legacy_flippable.plist, but the probe built against the current SDK shows it does not flip, so that list applies only to old binaries.

**Regression risks:** chevron.forward is pixel-identical to chevron.right in left-to-right languages, so nine of ten languages are unchanged. The primary play button chevron (DetailComponents.swift:226) will also flip in Arabic, which is the intended reading. Following the original proposal for the guide header would introduce a wrong-direction chevron in Arabic. Forcing the guide to left-to-right without a simulator run could be a regression if it already mirrors correctly.

**How to verify:** Screenshot tour with the app language set to Arabic: shelf headers, Continue Watching, playlist list, movie detail and a collapsed guide category. In the guide, check that the channel column stays pinned to the right edge while scrolling horizontally, that jump-to-now lands on the now-line, and that the axis and body stay aligned. Separately, with an English device and Arabic chosen in the app, note which side the back button, swipe-back edge and tab order use.

## gap-localization-runtime-8 — Every L() call re-reads UserDefaults, rebuilds the supported-language Set and resolves the .lproj bundle by path: 7-9 µs per string where a cached lookup takes 0.05 µs.

- Verdict: **confirmed** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Settings, M3U settings, Live TV cards with EPG, M3U channel cards, TV Guide, Downloads
- Code: `Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:75-114,127-138`, `Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:65`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideRowViews.swift:54,125`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:634-674`, `Views/M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift:39-280`

**What the user perceives:** Not visible on its own; it is a fixed tax on every text. During a fast fling in All Channels it is a few percent of the frame budget; in Settings each body pass spends about half a millisecond (more on a phone) only on string lookups, repeated for every progress message during a re-download.

**Mechanism (finder):** resolveLocalizedString (lines 75-92) does UserDefaults.string, for 'system' builds Set(supportedLanguages.map...) and a Locale per preferred language (104-114), then Bundle.main.path(forResource:ofType:) + Bundle(path:) (94-100), and a second bundle on a miss. Host benchmark scratchpad/agents/l10n/bench/bench.swift (Apple silicon Mac, -O, same code): 6.8 µs with an explicit language, 9.0 µs with 'system' (the default), 12.7 µs for a missing key; cached bundle 0.37 µs; cached bundle plus per-key table 0.05 µs. For comparison Date.formatted is 0.72 µs. Calls per body: LiveStreamCard 0 direct, 1 through EPGNowNextLine's accessibility label when a programme is on (EPGComponents.swift:65); VODStreamCard, SeriesCard, HistoryCard 0; M3UChannelCard 1 in the context-menu closure, which is built with the body (M3UChannelsView.swift:455), plus the EPG one; guide programme cell 0, gap cell 1, category header 1; LiveCategoryContent 8-10 per body for its sort menu, re-run on every page append; Downloads row 1-3; settings Form 50-57. Estimate for a fling: at most ~12 live cards or ~10 guide rows materialise per frame -> about 0.1 ms on the Mac, 0.2-0.4 ms on an A13-class phone, 2-5% of an 8.3 ms frame. It also takes the UserDefaults path from detached tasks (M3UContentStore.displayName, error descriptions).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Cache per language behind a lock, readable from nonisolated callers, cleared on change:

nonisolated enum L10nCache {
    private struct State: @unchecked Sendable { var code: String; var locale: Locale; var bundle: Bundle?; var english: Bundle?; var table: [String: String] = [:] }
    private static let state = OSAllocatedUnfairLock<State?>(initialState: nil)
    static func invalidate() { state.withLock { $0 = nil } }
    static func string(_ key: String) -> String {
        state.withLock { s in
            if s == nil { s = load() }               // UserDefaults + systemLanguageCode(), once
            if let hit = s!.table[key] { return hit }
            let value = lookup(key, in: s!)          // selected bundle, then en, then key
            s!.table[key] = value
            return value
        }
    }
    static var locale: Locale { state.withLock { s in if s == nil { s = load() }; return s!.locale } }
}

Call invalidate() in selectedLanguage.didSet after the UserDefaults write (line 32; @Published emits in willSet, so the cache is clean before SwiftUI re-renders) and on NSLocale.currentLocaleDidChangeNotification for the 'system' case. The table stores the bridged __NSLocalizedString unchanged, which keeps the plural config (host-verified; a re-encoded copy loses it, so do not normalise the value). L() stays nonisolated with the same signature.

**APIs:** OSAllocatedUnfairLock (iOS 16.0 (os.swiftinterface:2449)); NSLocale.currentLocaleDidChangeNotification (iOS 2.0 (NSLocale.h:133))

**Verifier reasons:** Localization/LocalizationManager.swift:75-114 does, on every call, a UserDefaults read, for 'system' a Set build plus a Locale per preferred language, then Bundle.main.path(forResource:ofType:) and Bundle(path:), and a second bundle on a miss. I re-ran the finder's benchmark binary (scratchpad/agents/l10n/bench, a verbatim copy of those lines): 7.26 µs per call with an explicit language, 9.13 µs with 'system', 12.69 µs for a missing key, 0.39 µs with a cached bundle, 0.04-0.06 µs with a per-key table. The call sites are as described: EPGNowNextLine's accessibility label (Views/EPG/EPGComponents.swift:65), the M3U card context menu whose builder closure is non-escaping and so runs with the body (Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-457), the sort menu (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:634-674), and 57 and 64 L() calls in M3UPlaylistSettingsView.swift and PlaylistSettingsView.swift. The finding states itself that this is not perceptible alone, and I agree: about 0.5 ms per settings body and a few percent of a frame during a fling. It is a cheap, safe saving, not a visible defect. The project builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj), so the 'nonisolated enum' in the proposal is required, not decoration.

**Corrected claim:** Every L() call repeats a UserDefaults read, the system-language resolution and an .lproj bundle lookup: 7-9 µs per string on an Apple silicon Mac against 0.05 µs with a cache. This is a fixed tax, not a perceptible stall; it matters most in Settings (57-64 lookups per body pass) and on scrolling cards that call L() in their body.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed: a nonisolated, lock-protected cache holding the resolved language code, the selected and English bundles and a per-key table, invalidated in selectedLanguage.didSet after the UserDefaults write (LocalizationManager.swift:32). Store the String returned by localizedString(forKey:) as it is, which is what the current code already passes to NSString(format:), so plural handling is unchanged. The NSLocale.currentLocaleDidChangeNotification hook is optional: iOS relaunches the app when the system or per-app language changes. Add 'import os'. A cached bundle alone already removes 95% of the cost if the per-key table is judged unnecessary.

**API check:** os.swiftinterface:2449-2450: @available(macOS 13.0, iOS 16.0, ...) @frozen public struct OSAllocatedUnfairLock<State> : @unchecked Sendable; line 2492: withLock<R>(_ body: @Sendable (inout State) throws -> R) rethrows -> R where R : Sendable. Foundation NSLocale.h:133: NSCurrentLocaleDidChangeNotification, iOS 2.0. Type-level 'nonisolated' needs Swift 6.1 or later; Xcode 26.0.1 provides it.

**Regression risks:** A stale cache if anything writes app.selected_language to UserDefaults without going through LocalizationManager; today the only writer is LocalizationManager.swift:32, and launch-argument overrides are read on first load. Unit tests that flip the default directly would need to call invalidate(). Language switching already rebuilds the tree through .id(selectedLanguage) at another_iptv_playerApp.swift:66, after didSet has run.

**How to verify:** Unit tests: changing selectedLanguage changes the string returned for the same key; a stringsdict key (for example detail.episode_count_plural) still inflects for 1 and 5 after a cached hit; eight concurrent detached callers get consistent values. An XCTest measure block over 100k L() calls before and after.

## gap-localization-runtime-9 — The Search tab label and the Search screen title use different keys whose Arabic, Spanish and Portuguese values differ, and a dozen other same-English key pairs have drifted apart in translation.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Search, Settings, Add playlist, Player panel vs browse, Movie detail vs filter menu
- Code: `Views/DashboardView.swift:77-81`, `Views/SearchView.swift:67-68`, `Localization/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:10,78,256`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:265`

**What the user perceives:** In Spanish the tab says 'Buscar' and the large title of the screen it opens says 'Búsqueda'; Arabic 'بحث' vs 'البحث'; Portuguese 'Buscar' vs 'Busca'. Elsewhere the same thing has two names: German 'Alle Kanäle' in the player panel and 'Alle Sender' in browse; Portuguese 'Gênero' on the detail page and 'Género' in the filter menu.

**Mechanism (finder):** The tab item uses dashboard.search (DashboardView.swift:77); the visible large title comes from search.title (SearchView.swift:67-68). The outer .navigationTitle(L("dashboard.search")) and .inline at DashboardView.swift:80-81 lose to the inner modifiers (iphone-light/Q01-search-idle.png shows a large title), so those two lines are dead. Script scratchpad/agents/l10n/keys.py over the ten files (502 keys each, identical key sets, no duplicate keys) lists keys with the same English value and different translations. Real drift: player.all_channels vs browse.all_live (de); movie.genre vs filter.genre (pt mixes Brazilian and European spelling); settings.player.pip.title vs player.a11y.pip (tr, fr keep English in Settings, translate in the player); history.clear.title vs history.clear.label (tr 'Sil' vs 'Temizle'); add_playlist.fetching_* vs phase.fetch_* (ar, hi, ru, zh: the same progress step worded differently on first import and on refresh); add_m3u.saving_db / settings.m3u.saving vs phase.save_db (eight languages); net.error.network vs epg.error.network (ru, zh punctuation); add_playlist.username vs settings.playlist.username (ru); add_m3u.section.source vs settings.m3u.source (es); stream.live vs player.live_badge vs epg.detail.live_badge (fr, ru); download.play vs movie.play (hi spelling). Legitimately different (verb vs noun, singular vs plural): common.search, dashboard.series vs stream.series, common.cancel vs download.cancel, the 'Off' / 'Default' gender variants.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Delete DashboardView.swift:80-81 and use one key for both the tab and the title (dashboard.search, matching the App Store's 'Buscar' for both). Align the drifted values listed above in the affected languages. Remove or use the dead keys: series.episode_count_format, series.episode_format, common.search, common.back, common.yes are unreferenced, and movie.trailer exists while DetailComponents.swift:265 hard-codes 'Fragman'. The edits change existing values and remove unused lines in the ten Localizable.strings; the uncommitted tip.* and settings.about.tip.* keys are left exactly as they are.

**Verifier reasons:** The wiring is as described: the tab uses dashboard.search (Views/DashboardView.swift:77) and the screen sets search.title with a large display mode (Views/SearchView.swift:67-68); the outer navigationTitle and .inline at DashboardView.swift:80-81 lose, since iphone-light/Q01-search-idle.png shows a large title. Values differ in ar (بحث / البحث), es (Buscar / Búsqueda) and pt (Buscar / Busca); the other seven languages match. I re-ran scratchpad/agents/l10n/keys.py: 502 keys in each of the ten files, no duplicates, identical key sets, and the listed drifts are all present (player.all_channels vs browse.all_live in de, movie.genre vs filter.genre in pt, the PiP titles in tr and fr, history.clear.* in tr, the fetching_* and saving keys, net/epg network error in ru and zh). grep confirms common.search, common.back, common.yes, series.episode_format, series.episode_count_format and movie.trailer have no Swift reference, and DetailComponents.swift:265 hard-codes 'Fragman'. The scope needs correcting: the same screenshot shows that on iPhone with iOS 26 the search tab is an icon-only button that expands into a field, so the tab label is not on screen there. The mismatch is visible on iOS 18 iPhones, in the iPad sidebar and to VoiceOver. Several of the listed pairs are also defensible short-versus-long variants (saving, Playlist Info) and not errors.

**Corrected claim:** The Search tab label and the Search screen title come from two keys whose Arabic, Spanish and Portuguese values differ. It is visible on iOS 18 iPhones, in the iPad sidebar and to VoiceOver; on iPhone with iOS 26 the search tab has no visible label. About a dozen other same-English key pairs have drifted in single languages, six keys are unused, and the trailer button text is hard-coded in Turkish while a movie.trailer key exists.

**Corrected fix:** Delete DashboardView.swift:80-81 and use one key for both the tab and the title. Replace the hard-coded 'Fragman' at DetailComponents.swift:265 with L("movie.trailer"); this is the only item every non-Turkish user sees and should come first. Align the clear drifts (pt Gênero/Género, de Alle Kanäle/Alle Sender, tr PiP and Clear History, ru and zh network error). Treat the fetching/saving wording and the unused-key removal as optional tidying. Leave the uncommitted tip.* and settings.about.tip.* lines untouched.

**API check:** No API involved; string-table values and one L() call.

**Regression risks:** The ten Localizable.strings files carry the owner's uncommitted tip-jar keys (git diff --stat: 130 added lines), so edits must change other lines only. Removing unused keys is safe for the six named, since the only dynamic lookups (option.titleKey, tier.titleKey, VideoPlayerController.swift:2247) do not produce them. Which Spanish and Portuguese word to keep for Search is a wording choice for the owner.

**How to verify:** A unit test that loads the ten files and asserts identical key sets plus equal values for an explicit list of alias pairs. A screenshot of the movie detail in English showing 'Trailer', and of the Search tab in Spanish on an iOS 18 simulator.

## gap-localization-runtime-10 — Programme length, series runtime and download percentage are built from raw integers instead of locale formatters, giving '5 دقيقة', '1s 45dk' in every language and '45%' where the language writes it differently.

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Programme detail sheet, Series detail hero, Downloads, Download button
- Code: `Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:118-121`, `Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:499-511`, `Views/DownloadsView.swift:295`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:130`

**What the user perceives:** An English user sees a series runtime of '1s 45dk'; an Arabic user sees '5 دقيقة' where the language needs the plural 'دقائق'; French and Russian show '45%' where the system writes '45 %'.

**Mechanism (finder):** epg.detail.minutes_format is the one live count key that is not in the stringsdict, so its noun never inflects. DetailFormatting.seriesRuntime concatenates Turkish unit letters (DetailComponents.swift:506-508; the hard-coded text may already be listed by the accessibility lens, the formatter is the fix). download.downloading_format is a hand-written percent pattern per language (tr '%%%d' is right, fr/ru/de are not).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Use the system unit and percent styles with AppLocale.current: Duration.seconds(minutes * 60).formatted(.units(allowed: [.hours, .minutes], width: .narrow).locale(loc)) for runtimes, width .abbreviated for the programme length, and fraction.formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0)).locale(loc)) for progress. Host output (scratchpad/agents/l10n/units.swift): en '1h 45m', '45 min', '45%'; tr '1sa 45d', '45 dk.', '%45'; ru '1 ч 45 мин', '45 мин', '45 %'; ar_SA '١س ٤٥د', '٤٥ د', '٤٥٪'. The three format keys then become unused.

**APIs:** Duration.UnitsFormatStyle (.units(allowed:width:)) and .locale(_:) (iOS 16.0); FloatingPointFormatStyle.Percent (.percent) (iOS 15.0)

**Verifier reasons:** All three sites are real. Views/Components/DetailComponents.swift:499-511 returns Turkish unit letters ('\(h)s \(m)dk', '\(minutes) dk') in every language and feeds the series hero (Views/SeriesView.swift:833); git log -S shows it dates from the initial monorepo commit with no explaining comment. Views/EPG/EPGProgrammeDetailSheet.swift:118-121 uses epg.detail.minutes_format, which is in Localizable.strings only, not in the stringsdict, so Arabic gets '%d دقيقة' for every count. Views/DownloadsView.swift:295 and Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:130 use download.downloading_format, which is '%d%%' in nine languages and '%%%d' in Turkish. My host probe (scratchpad/agents/verify-l10n-c/units2.swift) reproduces the proposed output: en '1h 45m', '45 min', '45%'; tr '1sa 45d', '45 dk.', '%45'; ru '1 ч 45 мин', '45 %'; de, es, fr '45 %'. Three corrections. First, only two keys become unused, not three: seriesRuntime has no key. Second, .percent.precision(.fractionLength(0)) rounds, while the current Int(fraction * 100) truncates: the probe shows 0.455 becomes 46%, so 99.5% would read 100% while the download is still running. Third, AppLocale.current does not exist; with the locale the app root already uses (Locale(identifier: code), another_iptv_playerApp.swift:64) bare 'ar' yields Western digits ('1س 45د'), which matches every other number L() produces; ar_SA would yield Arabic-Indic digits and mix the two systems on one screen. The hard-coded Turkish runtime is the part users in nine languages see; the percent spacing and the Arabic minute plural are refinements.

**Corrected claim:** The series runtime is built from hard-coded Turkish unit letters and shows as '1s 45dk' in every language. The programme length uses a non-plural format key, and the download percentage a hand-written pattern, so neither follows the language's own conventions (Arabic plural, '45 %' in French, German, Spanish and Russian).

**Corrected fix:** Runtime: Duration.seconds(minutes * 60).formatted(.units(allowed: [.hours, .minutes], width: .narrow).locale(loc)) in DetailFormatting.seriesRuntime, keeping the existing pass-through for raw values that already contain letters. Programme length: the same with allowed [.minutes] and width .abbreviated. Percent: floor first to keep today's truncation, (floor(fraction * 100) / 100).formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0)).locale(loc)). For loc use the same language-only Locale the app root sets (Locale(identifier: effectiveLanguageCode)), so digits stay consistent with the rest of the UI. Two keys (epg.detail.minutes_format, download.downloading_format) then become unused.

**API check:** Foundation.swiftinterface: Swift.Duration.UnitsFormatStyle at line 4209, @available(macOS 13.0, iOS 16.0, ...); static func units(allowed:width:maximumUnitCount:zeroValueUnits:valueLength:fractionalPart:) at 4334; func locale(_:) -> Duration.UnitsFormatStyle at 4314. FloatingPointFormatStyle.Percent at 3175, @available(iOS 15.0); its locale(_:) at 3240; the .percent static at 3292. All below the iOS 18 target, no availability guard needed.

**Regression risks:** Rounding instead of truncating would show 100% before a download completes unless the fraction is floored. Using a region-qualified Arabic locale would introduce Arabic-Indic digits next to Western ones. The narrow Arabic and Hindi unit forms ('45 د', '45 मि॰') are terser than the current full words; the owner may prefer .abbreviated or .wide for the programme sheet. effectiveLanguageCode is MainActor-isolated, which is fine for these view-side helpers under the project's default MainActor isolation.

**How to verify:** Unit tests on DetailFormatting.seriesRuntime ("105", "45", "120", "45 min", "0") and on the programme time line with injected locales en, tr, ar, ru, checked against the strings above; a test that a 0.999 fraction renders 99% and never 100%.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-1 — MockFixture seeds only categories, 13 channels, 12 films and 8 series, so ten audited surfaces have no screenshot and no UI test

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort L · risk low
- Screens: Series detail (seasons, episodes), Live TV now/next line, TV Guide grid, programme sheet, channel schedule, M3U dashboard (all screens), Continue Watching, Watch history, progress bars, Resume, Favorites, Downloads, Recently Added, Movie detail first open, Settings with account loaded
- Code: `Database/MockFixture.swift:23-39, 52-91, 93-137, 139-177`, `another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:78-94`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:892-896, 1176-1247`, `Views/VODView.swift:180-191`, `Models/DownloadManager.swift:87-141, 289-298, 394-455`, `Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:25-41`
- Owner decision flagged by the audit: Whether the App Store screenshots should later move to the rich profile (guide lines, Continue Watching). The plan keeps them on the current data.

**What the user perceives:** Nothing the user sees directly. The effect is on the audit: every finding about seasons, episodes, the guide, history, favourites, downloads and M3U rests on code only. The screenshots show an error page for the series detail (iphone-dark/S04-series-detail-settled.png: 'Server error: HTTP 404'), a guide with empty rows (iphone-dark/L06-live-tv-guide.png), 'Could not fetch info: Server error: HTTP 404' in Settings (iphone-dark/T02-settings-2.png) and an empty Downloads screen (T05).

**Mechanism (finder):** MockFixture.swift:52-177 inserts categories, liveStream, vodStream and series rows only. Series are seeded with seasonsLoaded false (:172), so SeriesDetailView's task (Views/SeriesView.swift:892-896) calls get_series_info on https://example.com and the detail turns into the error page; ScreensUITests.swift:86-93 says so and only asserts the back button. Channels have epgChannelId nil (:84) and no epgProgramme, epgChannel or epgSource rows exist. No watchHistory, favorite, downloadedItem, season, episode or m3uChannel row is written. Films carry no 'added' value, so the Recently Added shelf (Views/VODView.swift:184-186 drops rows without a numeric 'added') never appears. All films have metadataLoaded true (:131), so the first-open path of the movie detail is never taken. All logos are opaque square photos (:83) and all names are short ASCII.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add a second profile 'rich' (launch argument -UITestsFixture rich, see the scale finding for the switch); the default profile stays byte-for-byte what it is, so ScreenshotsUITests keeps capturing the same six screens. Additions and the finding ids each one makes verifiable:
1. Seasons and episodes: two series with seasonsLoaded true; one with season 0 'Specials' plus two seasons of 30 episodes, one with a single season of 4; 16:9 episode covers, durations, plots. Ids from DBSeason.scopedId / DBEpisode.scopedId (Models/DBModels.swift:108-110, 130-132). -> series-browse-detail-2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 13; transitions-motion-8; haptics-touch-feedback-3; player-handoff-miniplayer-1, 3; swiftui-invalidation-2, 8; ios26-design-11; accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-5.
2. Guide data: epgChannelId on 10 of 13 channels, epgChannel rows, epgProgramme rows generated relative to Date() at seed time (local midnight -12 h to +36 h; 15, 30 and 120 minute programmes, one 24 h placeholder under real programmes, three channels without data, one channel with tvArchive 1), plus an epgSource row with lastSuccessAt = now so EPGStore.refreshIfStale returns (EPG/EPGStore.swift:431-436). -> live-tv-browse-2, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13; scroll-perf-2; swiftui-invalidation-4, 5; states-loading-empty-error-9; secondary-screens-11, 12; haptics-touch-feedback-10; search-ux-11; ipad-adaptivity-12; accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-3, 12.

Watch history: films at 40 % and 99 %, one episode row (type series, seriesId set), one live row, one M3U row. -> movies-browse-detail-6; series-browse-detail-5, 11; design-system-consistency-6, 11; secondary-screens-4, 8, 9, 15; scroll-perf-3, 11; transitions-motion-4, 5; states-loading-empty-error-6; data-main-thread-5; haptics-touch-feedback-5; m3u-browse-2.

**APIs:** URLSessionConfiguration.protocolClasses (iOS 7.0 (Foundation NSURLSession.h:849)); URLProtocol (iOS 2.0 (Foundation NSURLProtocol.h:163))

**Verifier reasons:** Fixture content verified in Database/MockFixture.swift:52-177: only category, liveStream, vodStream and series rows; epgChannelId nil (:84), metadataLoaded true (:131), seasonsLoaded false (:172), no 'added'. Consequences verified: Views/SeriesView.swift:892-896 fetches when seasonsLoaded is false; Views/VODView.swift:184-186 drops films without a numeric 'added'; Models/DownloadManager.swift:87-141 re-queues every 'downloading' row and pumpQueue (:394-455) starts a real task; localURL checks fileExists (:289-298). Screenshots match: iphone-dark/S04 shows 'Server error: HTTP 404', L06 a guide with empty rows, T02 'Could not fetch info: Server error: HTTP 404'. Helper references are right: DBSeason.scopedId / DBEpisode.scopedId at Models/DBModels.swift:108-110 and 130-132, M3UImporter.stableChannelID at Models/M3UImporter.swift:69, EPGStore.fetchNowIndex at EPG/EPGStore.swift:175, refreshIfStale at :431-441. PanelURLSession (Networking/XtreamAPIClient.swift:25-31) is also the default session of M3UService (Networking/M3UService.swift:25) and EPGDownloader (EPG/EPGDownloader.swift:9), so one stub covers panel, M3U and XMLTV.

Corrections: (1) 'no UI test' is overstated. Favorites and Downloads have smoke tests on the empty state (ScreensUITests.swift:49, 146) and series detail has a push test (:78); what is missing is any test or screenshot with data. (2) MockFixture.demoPlaybackURL (:189-194) only answers for demoPlaylistId and seedIfNeeded writes only the demo id to lastPlaylistId (:38); a rich profile with its own playlist id needs both extended, or the app opens the wrong playlist and hand-off tests try to play from the fixture host. (3) The seeders call AppDatabase.shared.writeSync directly; the proposed unit test against AppDatabase.empty() (Database/Persistence.swift:94) needs them to take a Database and a playlist id. (4) The project builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (project.pbxproj:393); the URLProtocol subclass must be declared nonisolated because its methods are called off the main thread. (5) EPG/CatchupURLResolver.swift:113 has its own session and is not covered by the stub. (6) The lists of other finding ids each addition 'makes verifiable' could not be checked from here.

**Corrected claim:** MockFixture seeds only categories, 13 channels, 12 films and 8 series with no guide, history, favourite, download, season, episode or M3U rows. Series detail, the guide, Continue Watching, populated Favorites and Downloads, Recently Added, the first-open movie detail path, the M3U dashboard and Settings with an account loaded therefore have no screenshot and no UI test with data; three of them have only empty-state smoke tests.

**Corrected fix:** Add the rich profile as proposed, with these changes: give it its own playlist id, write that id to lastPlaylistId, and make demoPlaybackURL answer for it; pass Database and playlistId into the seed functions so they can run against AppDatabase.empty(); declare the fixture URLProtocol nonisolated and prepend it to config.protocolClasses in PanelURLSession only in fixture mode, compiled under #if DEBUG; keep the DownloadManager in-progress seam behind the same condition. Split delivery: seasons and episodes, guide rows plus epgSource stamp, history and favourites first (pure data, small); M3U playlist, downloads seam and the panel stub second. Demo profile unchanged.

**API check:** URLSessionConfiguration.protocolClasses: NSURLSession.h:849 '@property (nullable, copy) NSArray<Class> *protocolClasses' (found). URLProtocol: Foundation, long-standing. No SwiftUI API involved.

**Regression risks:** Test-only code in shipping sources: PanelURLSession and DownloadManager gain fixture branches, which must be compiled out of Release. The scheme's Run action uses the Release configuration (xcscheme LaunchAction), so a DEBUG-gated profile is not reachable from Xcode Run, only from the test and snapshot actions. App Store screenshots stay unchanged only if the demo profile is truly untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit test: seed the rich profile into AppDatabase.empty(), assert row counts per table and that EPGStore.fetchNowIndex returns a programme for a seeded channel at Date(). UI: tour shows seasons in series detail, cells in the guide, a Continue Watching shelf, populated Favorites and Downloads, the M3U dashboard; a movie started from the rich playlist plays the demo stream.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-2 — No scale fixture exists in the repository; with today's per-row inserts a 240k-row catalog plus a 5k-channel guide takes 5.2 s optimised and 14.6 s unoptimised to seed, and seedIfNeeded would delete and rebuild it on every launch

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, All Movies / All Series / All Channels, Search, TV Guide, Playlist list
- Code: `Database/MockFixture.swift:9-16, 23-39`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:31-42`, `Database/AppDatabase.swift:358-403, 470-475`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:131-137, 206-216`, `another-iptv-player.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:483-484`, `fastlane/Snapfile:1-35`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. Without it, every estimate about scrolling, tab switches, search and the guide on catalogs of 50k to 150k items stays unchecked; the orchestrator's 120k baseline lives only in a scratch copy.

**Mechanism (finder):** seedIfNeeded (MockFixture.swift:23-39) runs synchronously in App.init (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:34), deletes the demo playlist (:28, which cascades to every child table) and re-inserts row by row through PersistableRecord.insert. Measured on the dev Mac with the app's schema and records (scratchpad/agents/fixture-bench, the simulator runs on the same CPU): 300 categories x 3, 50,000 channels, 150,000 films, 40,000 series = 1.7 s with -O, 5.6 s with -Onone; a guide of 5,000 channels x 96 programmes (480,000 rows) = 3.3-3.5 s with -O, 9.0 s with -Onone. One prepared statement per table brings the whole seed to 2.0 s (-O) / 4.4 s (-Onone). Deleting it again costs about 0.75 s. The database file is 61.9 MB with the catalog and 134.9 MB with the guide.
Gate today: isActive (MockFixture.swift:9-16) is true when argv contains -UITests or the environment has FASTLANE_SNAPSHOT=YES. It is not compiled out, so a Release build seeds the demo playlist and takes over lastPlaylistId (:38) for anyone who can pass launch arguments (Xcode scheme, devicectl, simctl); it cannot be reached from the Home Screen.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Generate once and keep; do not ship a prebuilt SQLite file. Reasons: 62-135 MB of binary in the repo, the app under test cannot read the UI-test runner's bundle on a device, programme times must be relative to the day of the run, and the file would have to be rebuilt after every migration. A kept catalog costs one 4 ms COUNT/name check per launch.

MockFixture.swift (demo path unchanged):
```swift
enum Profile: String { case demo, rich, scale }
static let profile: Profile = {
    #if DEBUG || PERF_FIXTURE
    if isActive, let raw = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: "UITestsFixture"),
       let value = Profile(rawValue: raw) { return value }
    #endif
    return .demo
}()

#if DEBUG || PERF_FIXTURE
static let scalePlaylistId = UUID(uuidString: "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555557")!
private static let scaleSignature = "Scale v1 50000/150000/40000/300"

private static func seedScaleIfMissing() throws {
    try AppDatabase.shared.writeSync { db in
        let name = try String.fetchOne(db, sql: "SELECT name FROM playlist WHERE id = ?", arguments: [scalePlaylistId])
        if name != scaleSignature {
            try db.execute(sql: "DELETE FROM playlist WHERE id = ?", arguments: [scalePlaylistId])
            try Playlist(id: scalePlaylistId, name: scaleSignature, serverURL: "https://panel.fixture.invalid",
                         username: "demo", password: "demo").insert(db)
            try insertScaleCatalog(db)      // db.makeStatement once per table, execute per row
        }
        try refreshScaleGuide(db)           // new rows only when the stored day differs; else re-stamp lastSuccessAt
    }
}
#endif
```
- Own playlist id per profile: the demo seeder's DELETE (:28) then never drops the scale catalog, and Cmd+U runs between perf runs cost nothing.
- Shape: 300 categories per type; 10 % of the categories hold 45 % of the rows (shelves of 2k-7k items), one empty category, 200 rows without a valid category; 'added' on every film; mixed Latin, Turkish, Arabic and Cyrillic names; 20 % two-line titles; metadataLoaded false on 5 % (meaningful with the panel stub only); 8 history rows; 24 favourites per type.
- Guide: epgChannelId on the first 5,000 channels, 96 half-hour programmes each around local midnight; the day is stored in epgSource.url; on a later day only the guide is regenerated (1.5 s with -O). lastSuccessAt is re-stamped on every launch (5 ms), otherwise EPGStore.refreshIfStale (EPG/EPGStore.swift:431-441) starts a network refresh after six hours.
- The first launch seeds inside App.init. That is fine on the simulator; on a phone expect several times the Mac figure, so make the first launch an unmeasured setup launch (the orchestrator's test_a00_seed does this) and run it from Xcode if the launch watchdog bites.
- Release: '#if DEBUG || PERF_FIXTURE' keeps the generator out of archives. Test and snapshot builds use Debug (xcscheme TestAction, fastlane/Snapfile configuration Debug; DEBUG is defined at project.pbxproj:483). Instruments builds use the Profile action, which is Release, so pass SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS='$(inherited) PERF_FIXTURE' there, or keep building Debug with -O as scratchpad/perf/build.sh does.
- Tests pin the tab with '-dashboard_selected_tab N -dashboard_removed_home_tab_migration_v1 YES'; without the second key restoreInitialTab (Views/DashboardView.swift:206-216) shifts the index down by one on a fresh install.

**APIs:** GRDB Database.makeStatement(sql:) / Statement.execute(arguments:) (GRDB checkout in build/SourcePackages (used by the scratch benchmark)); UserDefaults argument domain (launch argument -UITestsFixture) (Foundation, all iOS versions)

**Verifier reasons:** I re-ran the release build of the scratch benchmark (scratchpad/agents/fixture-bench/.build/release/seedbench): catalog 1686 ms (50,000 channels, 150,000 films, 40,000 series, 900 categories), guide of 480,000 rows 3649 ms, total about 5.3 s; prepared statements 1987 ms total; DELETE of the guide 405 ms plus the playlist cascade 381 ms; file 61.9 MB and 134.9 MB; COUNT check 3.85 ms; re-stamp 5.5 ms. These match the finding. I did not re-run the -Onone figures.

Code facts verified: seedIfNeeded runs synchronously in App.init (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:34), deletes the demo playlist (MockFixture.swift:28) and every child table cascades (Database/AppDatabase.swift: category, liveStream, vodStream, series, favorite, watchHistory, m3uChannel, downloadedItem, epgProgramme, epgChannel, epgSource all reference playlist with onDelete cascade). isActive (:9-16) is not compiled out. DEBUG is defined only for Debug (project.pbxproj:483); TestAction and Snapfile use Debug; ProfileAction and ArchiveAction use Release. restoreInitialTab (Views/DashboardView.swift:206-216) does shift a non-zero index down by one when the migration key is unset, so the second argument is needed. refreshTTL is 6 h (EPG/EPGConstants.swift:11).

Corrections: (1) 'would delete and rebuild it on every launch' describes a naive scale-up of the demo seeder; the orchestrator's scratch fixture already skips reseeding with a COUNT check (scratchpad/perf/harness/fixture_large.swift.txt). (2) The sketch omits two required pieces: lastPlaylistId is set to the demo id only (:38) and demoPlaybackURL answers only for demoPlaylistId (:189-194). (3) The scheme's LaunchAction is also Release, so with '#if DEBUG || PERF_FIXTURE' a launch from Xcode Run with -UITestsFixture scale silently falls back to the demo profile. (4) Storing the day in epgSource.url overloads a column the settings UI may read; a UserDefaults key or the playlist-name signature is cleaner.

**Corrected claim:** The repository has no scale fixture. Seeding 240,000 catalog rows plus a 480,000-row guide with today's per-row inserts takes about 5.3 s optimised on the dev Mac (2.0 s with prepared statements), and the current seeder's delete-and-reinsert pattern would repeat that on every launch if simply scaled up.

**Corrected fix:** As proposed (generate once, own playlist id, signature check, prepared statements, guide regenerated per day, lastSuccessAt re-stamped, '#if DEBUG || PERF_FIXTURE'), plus: set lastPlaylistId to the scale playlist id when the profile is scale; extend demoPlaybackURL to the fixture playlist ids; keep the guide day in a UserDefaults key rather than epgSource.url; document that Xcode Run and Profile are Release and need PERF_FIXTURE.

**API check:** GRDB Database.makeStatement(sql:) at GRDB/Core/Database+Statements.swift:36 and Statement.execute(arguments:) at GRDB/Core/Statement.swift:541 (found; the benchmark using them runs). UserDefaults argument domain: Foundation behaviour, already relied on by the '-UITests 1' launch argument.

**Regression risks:** The scale playlist stays in the shared database between runs, so the playlist list shows a second row and the simulator database grows to about 135 MB during functional tests; no existing UI test counts playlist rows. First launch blocks App.init for 5-15 s in Debug on the simulator. Demo seeding and store screenshots are unaffected if the demo path is untouched.

**How to verify:** Unit test at 1/100 scale on AppDatabase.empty(): counts, skewed category sizes, one on-air programme per guide channel. Second launch with -UITestsFixture scale: playlist row unchanged and no seeding time. 'strings' on a Release binary shows no 'Scale v1'. Launch with the scale profile opens the scale playlist, and Watch Now plays the demo stream.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-3 — The orchestrator needs one ordered list that says which run settles which unverified finding; the existing 120k baseline does not exercise guide data, uncached film metadata or failing image hosts

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort L · risk low
- Screens: All browse screens, TV Guide, Search, Player hand-off
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:157-160, 166-215, 653-668, 737-739`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:105-107, 278-315, 567-577`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:158-160, 615-627`, `Views/SearchView.swift:246-278`, `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-178`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:218-333`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. 79 of the 303 findings are marked partly or undecidable on performance grounds, or need a simulator or device run; without an order the cheap, decisive runs are mixed with the ones that cannot be decided on a simulator at all.

**Mechanism (finder):** The scratch baseline (scratchpad/perf/baseline-report.txt, 30k channels / 70k films / 20k series) already gives: one 100-170 ms main-thread stall at launch, phase 1 to phase 2 gap 0.43 s, scroll spikes up to 33 ms, tab switch 36-165 ms, film detail push 87-125 ms (first 255 ms), search settling 1.16 s after the last key. Its fixture (scratchpad/perf/harness/fixture_large.swift.txt) seeds epgChannelId nil, metadataLoaded true and images that always answer, so it says nothing about live-tv-browse-2, swiftui-invalidation-4, data-main-thread-6, swiftui-invalidation-6 or image-pipeline-3. Its control scenario (push of a trivial screen) shows 45-73 ms of main-thread stall, which is the simulator's floor: a predicted effect below that cannot be decided there.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Checklist, in order. Fixtures: demo = today's; rich, scale = proposed.
0. Calibration (demo). 0a: run one measure block with every metric and note which sub-measurements XCTest reports on the simulator. 0b: keep the control scenario as the noise floor. 0c: the four change-print probes (separate finding) -> swiftui-invalidation-2, 3; with rich also swiftui-invalidation-9, m3u-browse-14.
1. Demo fixture, no app change. 1a transitions-motion-10: record Movies and Live side by side (search activate and cancel, hide a category, category jump), then Movies with VODView.swift:160 removed in a scratch copy. 1b ios26-design-4 and navigation-architecture-10: A/B DashboardView.swift:243 on iOS 26 and on the installed 18.x runtime, at rest and scrolled. 1c onboarding-playlists-13, settings-ux-12, movies-browse-detail-14: iPad and iPhone-landscape screenshots. 1d player-handoff-miniplayer-6: type in Search, play, minimise, focus the field, tap the card, assert app.keyboards.count == 0. 1e player-handoff-miniplayer-8 and the tab-bar question: frames of 'miniPlayer.expand' and app.tabBars.firstMatch on iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, portrait and landscape, iOS 26 and 18.x. 1f accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-11: launch with -AppleLanguages (en) and app.selected_language = ar, screenshot set. 1g live-tv-browse-6: sort Z-A, play the first tile, next, compare the title with the second tile.
2. Rich fixture. 2a series-browse-detail-2, transitions-motion-8: season switch, chip frame.minY unchanged, no progress indicator. 2b movies-browse-detail-6, series-browse-detail-11: screenshot of the progress bar position. 2c live-tv-browse-2, scroll-perf-2, swiftui-invalidation-5: minY of the third shelf header at first paint and 5 s later. 2d scroll-perf-3, movies-browse-detail-10, transitions-motion-4: first category header frame at first paint and 3 s later. 2e series-browse-detail-5, transitions-motion-5, states-loading-empty-error-6, secondary-screens-9, data-main-thread-5: 60 fps screen recording of the pushes, count frames in the default state; add an 'EmptyState' signpost event in the empty views so a test can assert it never fired. 2f m3u-browse-6, 8, haptics-touch-feedback-8, 11. 2g ipad-adaptivity-13: landscape, shelf of 10+ items, x of the outermost poster pixels. 2h transitions-motion-12, 7 and native-reference-9 on a detail long enough to scroll. 2i with the panel stub: movies-browse-detail-1, transitions-motion-1, settings-ux-1, 4, swiftui-invalidation-1, data-main-thread-2, states-loading-empty-error-2 (pull to refresh returns one more channel; assert it appears without leaving the tab). 2j image-pipeline-1, 5, 6 with 150 ms image latency and Slow Animations; background and return, count gray tiles.
3. Scale fixture, optimised build. 3a launch (p01 plus the 'EmptyState' event): transitions-motion-2, data-main-thread-1, 4, states-loading-empty-error-1, live-tv-browse-1. 3b pagination: scroll-perf-1, movies-browse-detail-2, native-reference-1, series-browse-detail-10 (scroll 12 flings, open a cell, back, same cell hittable). 3c run counts from the HomeRecompute, GridRecompute and SearchScan signposts: scroll-perf-8, data-main-thread-7, search-ux-4, native-reference-6 (expect 3 per appearance today). 3d grid first paint with name sort stored: live-tv-browse-3, transitions-motion-3, states-loading-empty-error-5, series-browse-detail-4. 3e scrolling (p02, p03): scroll-perf-9, 6, image-pipeline-4, m3u-browse-1, 7. 3f search (p05): scroll-perf-5, search-ux-3, 4, data-main-thread-8. 3g detail (p06) with metadataLoaded false and the stub: data-main-thread-6, swiftui-invalidation-6, image-pipeline-6. 3h tabs (p04). 3i guide (p07): live-tv-browse-9, data-main-thread-10. 3j All Channels tap and Continue Watching tap with the PlayerPresent signpost: player-handoff-miniplayer-11, data-main-thread-14. 3k Back to Playlists with the CatalogUnload signpost: transitions-motion-14, onboarding-playlists-7. 3l category jump: transitions-motion-11. 3m rotate under the player on a 300-channel grid: player-handoff-miniplayer-4. 3n memory: data-main-thread-12, image-pipeline-10 (footprint heartbeat plus heap, see the open-questions finding). 3o image host that never answers for 20 % of the logos: image-pipeline-3; prefetch count 2 s after a fling: scroll-perf-6, image-pipeline-4. 3p playing in the mini card while scrolling All Series, and a running download in a long season: swiftui-invalidation-10, 8.
4. Device only. live-tv-browse-12 (ProMotion guide pan, SwiftUI and Hitches instruments); native-reference-8 (shelf snapping); transitions-motion-14 and data-main-thread-12 final numbers (memory warnings, jetsam); image-pipeline-7 on iPad; player-handoff-miniplayer-10 and accessibility-dynamic-type-rtl-9 (VoiceOver); secondary-screens-6; search-ux-4 step B and m3u-browse-1 final decision; every case where step 3 lands under the 45-73 ms floor.

**APIs:** OSSignposter.emitEvent(_:id:_:) (iOS 15.0 (os.swiftinterface:1944)); XCUIElement.frame / waitForExistence(timeout:) (XCUIAutomation, iOS 9.0+)

**Verifier reasons:** This is a test plan, not a defect, and its cross-references to 79 of 303 other findings cannot be checked from here. The factual base holds: scratchpad/perf/baseline-report.txt shows launch main-thread worst 101-171 ms, scroll worst 33 ms, tab switch worst 36-165 ms, film detail push 87-125 ms after a first 255 ms, search settled 1.16 s after the last key; scratchpad/perf/out/control/summary.tsv shows 45-75 ms main-thread stalls for a trivial push (first pushes 73 and 198 ms). The baseline fixture seeds epgChannelId nil and metadataLoaded true (scratchpad/perf/harness/fixture_large.swift.txt), so it cannot speak to guide, first-open detail or failing-image findings. An iOS 18.1 runtime (22B81) is installed, so the 18.x A/B steps are possible. I could not find the '0.43 s phase 1 to phase 2 gap' in the report.

Corrections: (1) Every signpost the plan names (CatalogLoad, HomeRecompute, GridRecompute, SearchScan, PlayerPresent, CatalogUnload, GuideBuildRows, GuideLayouts, EmptyState) is absent from the app; the only OSSignposter is in Networking/VideoPlayerController.swift:583, which is out of scope. Adding them is a prerequisite step, not listed in the order. (2) An 'EmptyState' signpost event cannot be asserted from a UI test: XCTOSSignpostMetric measures intervals, and XCTest has no API to assert that an event did not fire. Use the proposed 'empty.<screen>' identifier with a frame-by-frame recording, or an in-app counter read after the run. (3) With a 45-75 ms simulator floor and film detail at 87-125 ms, most of step 3 can only rank large effects; that limit should be stated per step rather than only at the end.

**Corrected claim:** The existing 120k baseline is real and reproducible but does not exercise guide data, uncached film metadata or failing image hosts, and its control scenario puts the simulator's noise floor at about 45-75 ms of main-thread stall per push. An ordered run list is useful, but it depends on fixtures, identifiers and signposts that do not exist yet.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the checklist, with a step before 0: add the interval signposts and identifiers and the rich and scale fixtures. Replace the 'EmptyState' signpost assertion with the 'empty.<screen>' identifier plus recording, or an in-app counter. Mark each step 3 item whose predicted effect is under about 75 ms as device-only from the start.

**API check:** OSSignposter.emitEvent(_:id:_:) found at os.swiftinterface:1944 and :1947. XCTOSSignpostMetric initWithSubsystem:category:name: found at XCTMetric.h:233; it measures intervals, not events. XCUIElement.frame and waitForExistence are in XCUIAutomation headers.

**Regression risks:** None for the app beyond added signposts and identifiers. The scratch-copy A/B steps (removing VODView.swift:160, changing DashboardView.swift:243) must stay in the scratch copy.

**How to verify:** Run step 0a first and record which sub-measurements each XCTest metric reports on the simulator; any metric that reports nothing moves its steps to the device list. Repeat the control scenario at the start of each session and treat differences below its spread as undecided.
