## gap-fixture-and-measurement-4 — The seven measure blocks can be written today against labels, but six accessibility identifiers they need do not exist outside the player

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movies home, All Movies, Tab bar, Search tab, Movie detail, TV Guide
- Code: `another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreensUITests.swift:49-58, 98-112, 230-244`, `another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:544-557`, `Views/VODView.swift:418-429, 448-467, 689-704`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:234-238`, `Views/SearchView.swift:149-245, 328-335`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift:47-56`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. Today a test can only find a poster by its title text and the Favorites link by the symbol name 'star.fill' (ScreensUITests.swift:52), which breaks with a synthetic catalog and with any label fix.

**Mechanism (finder):** grep for accessibilityIdentifier finds nine sites, all in the player and mini player (Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:596, 629, 654; Views/PlayerView.swift:3126-4616; Views/PlayerScrubBar.swift:205). Browse tests use labels: tab names, 'All Movies', 'TV Guide', 'Jump to category', 'Sort', 'Watch Now', film titles. Resolving an element by label inside a measured window makes the runner snapshot the app's accessibility tree on the app's main thread, which is why the scratch harness moved to an in-app driver (scratchpad/perf/harness/ZZBrowsePerfUITests.swift:4-6).

**Proposed fix (finder):** Code below type-checks against the Xcode 26.0.1 XCTest (swiftc -typecheck, iOS 18 simulator target; scratchpad/agents/fixture-bench/measure/BrowsePerformanceUITests.swift). Taps inside measured windows go to points resolved beforehand; waits are fixed sleeps, assertions sit outside the window.
```swift
import XCTest

@MainActor
final class BrowsePerformanceUITests: XCTestCase {
    private var app: XCUIApplication!

    private func signpost(_ name: String) -> XCTOSSignpostMetric {
        XCTOSSignpostMetric(subsystem: "dev.ogos.another-iptv-player", category: "PointsOfInterest", name: name)
    }
    private func hitches() -> [XCTMetric] {
        if #available(iOS 26, *) { return [XCTHitchMetric(application: app)] }
        return []
    }
    private func options(_ iterations: Int = 5, manual: Bool = true) -> XCTMeasureOptions {
        let options = XCTMeasureOptions()
        options.iterationCount = iterations
        if manual { options.invocationOptions = [.manuallyStart, .manuallyStop] }
        return options
    }
    /// tab: 0 Live TV, 1 Movies, 2 Series.
    private func arguments(tab: Int) -> [String] {
        ["-UITests", "1", "-UITestsFixture", "scale",
         "-dashboard_selected_tab", String(tab), "-dashboard_removed_home_tab_migration_v1", "YES",
         "-AppleLanguages", "(en)", "-AppleLocale", "en_US"]
    }
    private func launch(tab: Int) {
        app = XCUIApplication()
        app.launchArguments = arguments(tab: tab)
        app.launch()
        XCTAssertTrue(app.tabBars.buttons["Movies"].waitForExistence(timeout: 60))
        XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["home.shelf.header.0"].waitForExistence(timeout: 60))   // missing identifier
    }
    private func point(_ element: XCUIElement) -> XCUICoordinate {
        let frame = element.frame
        return app.coordinate(withNormalizedOffset: .zero).withOffset(CGVector(dx: frame.midX, dy: frame.midY))
    }
    private func fling(up: Bool, velocity: XCUIGestureVelocity = .fast) {
        let from = app.coordinate(withNormalizedOffset: CGVector(dx: 0.5, dy: up ? 0.75 : 0.30))
        let to = app.coordinate(withNormalizedOffset: CGVector(dx: 0.5, dy: up ? 0.25 : 0.80))
        from.press(forDuration: 0.02, thenDragTo: to, withVelocity: velocity, thenHoldForDuration: 0)
    }
    private func settle(_ seconds: TimeInterval) { Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: seconds) }

    override func tearDown() { app?.terminate(); app = nil; super.tearDown() }

    // 1. Cold launch to the first shelf
    func test_p01_coldLaunchToFirstShelf() {
        app = XCUIApplication()
        app.launchArguments = arguments(tab: 1)
        let metrics: [XCTMetric] = [XCTApplicationLaunchMetric(waitUntilResponsive: true),
                                    signpost("CatalogLoad"), signpost("HomeRecompute"),
                                    XCTMemoryMetric(application: app)]
        measure(metrics: metrics, options: options(5, manual: false)) {
            app.launch()
            XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["home.shelf.header.0"].waitForExistence(timeout: 30))   // missing identifier
            app.terminate()
        }
    }

    // 2. Vertical fling on Movies home
    func test_p02_moviesHomeVerticalFling() {
        launch(tab: 1)
        let metrics: [XCTMetric] = [XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric,
                                    XCTCPUMetric(application: app)] + hitches()
        measure(metrics: metrics, options: options()) {
            startMeasuring()
            for _ in 0..<3 { fling(up: true) }
            settle(1.5)
            stopMeasuring()
            for _ in 0..<4 { fling(up: false) }
            settle(1)
        }
    }

    // 3. Fling in All Movies
    func test_p03_allMoviesGridFling() {
        launch(tab: 1)
        app.buttons["All Movies"].firstMatch.tap()
        XCTAssertTrue(app.navigationBars["All Movies"].waitForExistence(timeout: 20))
        settle(3)
        let metrics: [XCTMetric] = [XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric,
                                    XCTMemoryMetric(application: app),
                                    XCTCPUMetric(application: app)] + hitches()
        measure(metrics: metrics, options: options()) {
            startMeasuring()
            for _ in 0..<5 { fling(up: true) }        // crosses several 90-cell pages
            settle(1.5)
            stopMeasuring()
            for _ in 0..<6 { fling(up: false) }
            settle(1)
        }
    }

    // 4. Switching between the three content tabs
    func test_p04_tabSwitching() {
        launch(tab: 1)
        let live = point(app.tabBars.buttons["Live TV"])
        let movies = point(app.tabBars.buttons["Movies"])
        let series = point(app.tabBars.buttons["Series"])
        live.tap(); settle(2); series.tap(); settle(2); movies.tap(); settle(2)   // first visits build the tabs
        let metrics: [XCTMetric] = [XCTCPUMetric(application: app), signpost("HomeRecompute")] + hitches()
        measure(metrics: metrics, options: options()) {
            startMeasuring()
            live.tap(); settle(1); series.tap(); settle(1); movies.tap(); settle(1)
            stopMeasuring()
        }
    }

    // 5. Typing a three-letter query in the Search tab
    func test_p05_searchTypingThreeLetters() {
        launch(tab: 1)
        app.tabBars.buttons["Search"].tap()
        let field = app.searchFields.firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(field.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
        field.tap()
        let metrics: [XCTMetric] = [signpost("SearchScan"), XCTCPUMetric(application: app)] + hitches()
        measure(metrics: metrics, options: options()) {
            startMeasuring()
            field.typeText("the")
            settle(3)                                  // debounce 0.25 s + scan + list diff
            stopMeasuring()
            XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label BEGINSWITH %@", "Movies (")).firstMatch.exists)
            field.typeText(String(repeating: XCUIKeyboardKey.delete.rawValue, count: 3))
            settle(1)
        }
    }

    // 6. Pushing and popping a movie detail
    func test_p06_movieDetailPushPop() {
        launch(tab: 1)
        let poster = app.buttons["poster.vod.0.0"]     // missing identifier: first card of the first shelf
        XCTAssertTrue(poster.waitForExistence(timeout: 20))
        let posterPoint = point(poster)
        posterPoint.tap(); settle(1.5)                 // unmeasured round: warms the detail, finds the back button
        let backPoint = point(app.navigationBars.buttons.element(boundBy: 0))
        backPoint.tap(); settle(1.5)
        let metrics: [XCTMetric] = [XCTOSSignpostMetric.navigationTransitionMetric,
                                    XCTCPUMetric(application: app)] + hitches()
        measure(metrics: metrics, options: options()) {
            startMeasuring()
            posterPoint.tap(); settle(1.5)
            backPoint.tap(); settle(1.5)
            stopMeasuring()
            XCTAssertTrue(poster.exists)
        }
    }

    // 7. Opening the TV guide
    func test_p07_openTVGuide() {
        launch(tab: 0)
        let guide = app.buttons["TV Guide"].firstMatch
        XCTAssertTrue(guide.waitForExistence(timeout: 20))
        let guidePoint = point(guide)
        guidePoint.tap(); settle(4)
        let backPoint = point(app.navigationBars.buttons.element(boundBy: 0))
        backPoint.tap(); settle(1.5)
        let metrics: [XCTMetric] = [XCTOSSignpostMetric.navigationTransitionMetric,
                                    signpost("GuideBuildRows"), signpost("GuideLayouts"),
                                    XCTMemoryMetric(application: app)] + hitches()
        measure(metrics: metrics, options: options()) {
            startMeasuring()
            guidePoint.tap(); settle(4)
            stopMeasuring()
            XCTAssertTrue(app.otherElements["epg.guide.grid"].exists)   // missing identifier
            backPoint.tap(); settle(1.5)
        }
    }
}
```
Existing handles used: tab buttons by title (ScreensUITests.swift:230-232), 'All Movies' (Views/VODView.swift:121), 'TV Guide' (Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:116), app.searchFields.firstMatch, the first navigation-bar button as Back (ScreensUITests.swift:108).
Missing identifiers, set on the Button or NavigationLink, outside its label: 'home.shelf.header.<index>' (VODView.swift:418-429 and the Series / Live twins); 'poster.<type>.<shelf>.<item>' on shelf cards (VODView.swift:451-462); 'cell.<type>.<index>' on grid cells (VODView.swift:691-704) for the pagination test; 'shelf.<type>.<categoryId>' on the horizontal ScrollView for the shelf-offset check; 'nav.favorites' (Views/DashboardView.swift:234-238, today 'star.fill'); 'search.results' and section headers without the count in the label (Views/SearchView.swift:245, 333); 'detail.primaryAction' and 'detail.favorite' (the label changes between Watch Now and Resume, UserFlowsUITests.swift:552-557); 'series.seasonChip.<n>' and 'episode.row.<n>'; 'epg.guide.grid'; 'empty.<screen>' on the hand-built empty states. Build the per-card strings only in fixture mode so normal scrolling does not pay for the interpolation.

**APIs:** XCTestCase.measure(metrics:options:block:) with XCTMeasureOptions.invocationOptions (iOS 13.0 (XCTest.apinotes:84-86, XCTMeasureOptions.h)); XCTOSSignpostMetric(subsystem:category:name:) (iOS 13.0 (XCTMetric.h:224-233)); XCTHitchMetric(application:) (iOS 26.0 (header says ios(19.0); swiftc reports 26.0)); XCUICoordinate.press(forDuration:thenDragTo:withVelocity:thenHoldForDuration:) (iOS 14.0 (already used in UserFlowsUITests.swift:404)); View.accessibilityIdentifier(_:) (iOS 14.0 (already used in MiniPlayerSupport.swift:596))

**Verifier reasons:** Verified: accessibilityIdentifier appears at nine sites, all in the player (Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift 3, Views/PlayerView.swift 5, Views/PlayerScrubBar.swift 1). Browse tests locate by label, including 'star.fill' for Favorites (ScreensUITests.swift:52). I re-ran the type-check of scratchpad/agents/fixture-bench/measure/BrowsePerformanceUITests.swift with swiftc (Swift 5 mode, arm64-apple-ios18.0-simulator, Xcode 26.0.1 XCTest): exit 0, no diagnostics.

Corrections: (1) 'Can be written today' means they compile. None of the seven would pass today: launch() asserts 'home.shelf.header.0', the arguments use '-UITestsFixture scale', and five signposts (CatalogLoad, HomeRecompute, SearchScan, GuideBuildRows, GuideLayouts) do not exist in the app. (2) The code uses three missing identifiers and the text lists about twelve patterns, not six. (3) Positional identifiers ('poster.<type>.<shelf>.<item>', 'home.shelf.header.<index>') need a shelf index passed into the Equatable shelf rows and an enumerated ForEach in the shelves; Views/VODView.swift:444-447 documents that copying a category per cell was removed on purpose. Content ids avoid that: 'poster.vod.<streamId>' and 'home.shelf.header.<categoryId>' are deterministic in the fixture. (4) test_p05 calls field.typeText inside the measured window, which is runner-driven accessibility traffic, contrary to the stated design; its CPU metric will include that. (5) app.tabBars does not exist on iPad with the sidebar-adaptable top bar (the tour's tab() helper at ScreensUITests.swift:296-301 works around this), so the class is iPhone-only as written. (6) The 10 % relative standard deviation target is optimistic given the 45-75 ms control spread.

**Corrected claim:** No accessibility identifier exists outside the player, so browse tests depend on visible labels and one SF Symbol name. The seven measure blocks compile against the Xcode 26.0.1 XCTest but cannot run until the scale fixture, the signposts and the identifiers exist.

**Corrected fix:** Add identifiers keyed by content id, not position: 'home.shelf.header.<categoryId>', 'poster.<type>.<streamId>', 'cell.<type>.<streamId>', plus 'nav.favorites', 'search.results', 'detail.primaryAction', 'detail.favorite', 'series.seasonChip.<n>', 'episode.row.<id>', 'epg.guide.grid', 'empty.<screen>'. Set them on the NavigationLink or Button without adding parameters to the Equatable shelf rows. Update the test file to those ids, move typing in p05 to an in-app driver or drop the CPU metric there, and state the iPhone-only limit. Land it after the fixture and signposts.

**API check:** XCTMeasureOptions.invocationOptions and iterationCount: XCTMeasureOptions.h:43, 51. XCTOSSignpostMetric initWithSubsystem:category:name: XCTMetric.h:233; navigationTransitionMetric :257; scrollingAndDecelerationMetric :269. XCTHitchMetric: XCTMetric.h:380-381, API_AVAILABLE(ios(19.0)), initWithApplication: at XCTMetric+UIAutomation.h:72; the '#available(iOS 26, *)' guard type-checks. XCUICoordinate pressForDuration:thenDragToCoordinate:withVelocity:thenHoldForDuration: XCUICoordinate.h:46. XCUIKeyboardKeyDelete: XCUIKeyboardKeys.h:17. View.accessibilityIdentifier already used in the app.

**Regression risks:** Positional identifiers would force index plumbing through the Equatable shelf rows and undo part of the earlier scroll work; content-id identifiers do not. String interpolation per cell is negligible but can be limited to fixture mode. Changing the Favorites toolbar item from 'star.fill' to an identifier breaks ScreensUITests.swift:52 unless updated together.

**How to verify:** After fixture and signposts land: run the class alone on the simulator and record, per metric, whether a value is reported and its spread over five iterations; compare the spread with the control scenario before using any number for a before/after claim. Run ScreensUITests and UserFlowsUITests to confirm no label-based query broke.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-5 — Every -UITests launch calls example.com and inherits UserDefaults from the previous run; that is where the 404 screens and the wrong-tab screenshots come from

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Series detail, Settings, Live TV home (guide refresh), Dashboard tab restore, Category and All grids (stored sort)
- Code: `Database/MockFixture.swift:28, 38, 41-50, 172`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:11, 131-137, 197-216`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:431-441`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:892-896`, `Views/VODView.swift:610`, `Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:14-19`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:206-216`, `another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:497-504`, `another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreenshotsUITests.swift:19-24`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. For the audit: iphone-light L01-L06 show the Series tab instead of Live TV (shots/README.txt), S03/S04 show an error page and T02 shows a failed account request. These are properties of the fixture, so they overstate how often a user meets those states and make runs depend on the network and on run order.

**Mechanism (finder):** (a) The demo playlist points at https://example.com (MockFixture.swift:45). The dashboard task calls epgStore.refreshIfStale after the catalog load (DashboardView.swift:131-137); the fixture's DELETE cascades to epgSource (MockFixture.swift:28; AppDatabase.swift:392-393), so no source row exists and EPGStore.swift:431-441 starts a real guide download on every launch. Series detail and Settings make their panel calls the same way and get HTTP 404. (b) Persisted UI state is not reset: dashboard_selected_tab (DashboardView.swift:11, 197), vod/series/live.sortOption (VODView.swift:610 and twins), hidden categories (HiddenCategoryStore.swift:14-19), epg.collapsedCategories (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:206-216), app.selected_language. A stored name sort changes which code path a grid takes (live-tv-browse-3), so before/after numbers can differ for that reason alone. (c) The same DELETE removes the demo playlist's watchHistory, favorite and downloadedItem rows at every launch, so a relaunch inside a test (UserFlowsUITests.swift:497-504) never sees the history the first launch wrote. (d) ScreenshotsUITests takes '01-Live' without selecting the Live tab (ScreenshotsUITests.swift:19-24); it is correct only because fastlane reinstalls the app (Snapfile reinstall_app true).

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. In fixture mode, before the first view is built, remove the browse UI keys: dashboard_selected_tab, vod.sortOption, series.sortOption, live.sortOption, the hidden-category keys of the fixture playlists (HiddenCategoryStore.removeAll(playlistId:)), epg.collapsedCategories.<id>. One block at the end of MockFixture.seedIfNeeded, next to line 38. Do not pin the sort keys through launch arguments: the argument domain shadows @AppStorage writes, so the sort menu would stop responding in tests that use it. Pinning the tab by argument is safe because the tab is copied into @State at init (DashboardView.swift:22).
2. Panel stub and guide stamp from the rich-fixture finding, so no launch leaves the machine: the URLProtocol on PanelURLSession and an epgSource row with lastSuccessAt = now.
3. Images through the fixture URLProtocol for the rich and scale profiles (separate finding); the demo profile keeps picsum.photos so store screenshots do not change.
4. Leave the per-launch reseed of the demo and rich profiles as it is (it is what makes the functional tests order-independent); only the scale profile is kept.

**APIs:** UserDefaults.removeObject(forKey:) (Foundation, all iOS versions); URLSessionConfiguration.protocolClasses (iOS 7.0 (Foundation NSURLSession.h:849))

**Verifier reasons:** Verified: (a) the demo playlist points at https://example.com (MockFixture.swift:45); the dashboard task calls epgStore.refreshIfStale (Views/DashboardView.swift:131-137); the fixture's DELETE (:28) cascades to epgSource (Database/AppDatabase.swift:392-393), so EPG/EPGStore.swift:431-441 finds no row and starts a real download through EPGDownloader on every launch; there is no MockFixture guard in the EPG code. Screenshots S04 and T02 show the resulting HTTP 404. (b) Nothing resets dashboard_selected_tab (DashboardView.swift:11), the three sort keys (Views/VODView.swift:610, Views/SeriesView.swift:580, Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:543), hidden categories (Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:14-19) or epg.collapsedCategories (Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:206-216). (c) favorite, watchHistory and downloadedItem cascade from playlist, so each launch wipes them. (d) ScreenshotsUITests.swift:19-24 takes '01-Live' without selecting a tab; Snapfile has reinstall_app(true). The argument-domain point about @AppStorage is correct, and pinning the tab by argument is safe because the tab is copied into @State at init (DashboardView.swift:22).

Corrections: (1) The wrong-tab attribution is not proven. iphone-light L01 and L03 do show the Series tab, but the tour taps 'Live TV' before its first shot (ScreensUITests.swift:310) and ignores a failed tap, so a restored Series tab alone does not explain it. It is a plausible contributor only. (2) Fix 2 conflicts with the companion finding's promise that the demo profile stays byte-for-byte unchanged: the existing UI tests all run the demo profile, so 'no launch leaves the machine' holds only if the stub and the epgSource stamp also apply to demo. That changes what Settings shows for the account, which may be visible in the 13-inch iPad store screenshot. (3) app.selected_language is named in the mechanism but missing from the removal list; a stored override beats -AppleLanguages.

**Corrected claim:** Every -UITests launch makes real requests to example.com (guide refresh, series info, account info) because the fixture has no stub and its cascade delete removes the guide bookkeeping row; browse UI state in UserDefaults survives between runs and can change the starting tab, the grid code path and the language. Whether this caused the wrong-tab screenshots is unproven.

**Corrected fix:** Step 1 as proposed, with app.selected_language added to the removed keys. For the demo profile, insert an epgSource row with lastSuccessAt = now in the seed so the guide refresh stops without any stub; this is one row and changes no browse screen. Apply the panel stub to the rich and scale profiles only, unless the owner decides the demo profile may change (decision needed: stubbed account data in Settings would alter the demo Settings screen). Keep per-launch reseed for demo and rich.

**API check:** UserDefaults.removeObject(forKey:): Foundation, already used at Models/HiddenCategoryStore.swift:52. HiddenCategoryStore.removeAll(playlistId:) exists at :46-56 and is main-actor isolated, which fits App.init. URLSessionConfiguration.protocolClasses: NSURLSession.h:849.

**Regression risks:** Resetting the tab and sort keys in fixture mode means restore-across-relaunch behaviour cannot be UI-tested under -UITests without an opt-out argument; no current test does so. An epgSource row in the demo profile may make the EPG settings section show a last-updated time with zero programmes. Stubbing the demo profile would change the App Store Settings screenshot if the account section is in view.

**How to verify:** Launch twice with -UITests after leaving the app on Series with a name sort and a non-system language: the second launch opens Live TV, default sort, argument language. With a proxy or the network off, a demo launch issues no xmltv.php request. Re-run the tour for iphone-light and check that L01 shows Live TV; if it still shows Series, the cause is the tap, not the stored tab.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-6 — Fixture artwork is fetched from picsum.photos; local file URLs would bypass Nuke's loader, a URLProtocol on the DataLoader configuration keeps the real loading path without a network

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort M · risk low
- Screens: All shelves and grids, Detail hero, Search rows, TV Guide logos
- Code: `Views/CachedImage.swift:13-38, 96-123`, `Database/MockFixture.swift:179-183`, `another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreenshotsUITests.swift:22-23`, `another_iptv_playerApp.swift:32-34`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. A perf run whose images come from the internet measures the network; one whose images arrive instantly never shows the gray placeholder phase that the image findings are about.

**Mechanism (finder):** posterURL builds https://picsum.photos/seed/... (MockFixture.swift:181-183) and ScreenshotsUITests sleeps 7 s for them (:22-23). Nuke 13.0.1 loads file and data URLs inline with Data(contentsOf:) and skips the data loader, its queue and the rate limiter (Nuke Sources/Nuke/Tasks/TaskFetchOriginalData.swift:27-34, ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:120-122), so file URLs exercise decode and resize but not the six loading slots, cancellation or failures. The scratch harness serves images from a Python server on 127.0.0.1:8765, which needs a helper process and cannot be reached from a phone. The app builds its own URLSessionConfiguration at Views/CachedImage.swift:19-24, which is the hook.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Fixture image URLs use a reserved host: https://img.fixture.invalid/<kind>/<id>.<ext>. Without the protocol they fail at DNS and never leave the machine.
```swift
#if DEBUG || PERF_FIXTURE
final class FixtureImageProtocol: URLProtocol {
    private var work: DispatchWorkItem?
    override class func canInit(with request: URLRequest) -> Bool { request.url?.host == "img.fixture.invalid" }
    override class func canonicalRequest(for request: URLRequest) -> URLRequest { request }
    override func startLoading() {
        guard let url = request.url else { return }
        let work = DispatchWorkItem { [weak self] in
            guard let self else { return }
            guard let data = FixtureImages.data(for: url) else {          // nil = 'dead' artwork
                self.client?.urlProtocol(self, didFailWithError: URLError(.cannotConnectToHost)); return
            }
            let response = HTTPURLResponse(url: url, statusCode: 200, httpVersion: "HTTP/1.1",
                                           headerFields: ["Content-Type": "image/jpeg"])!
            self.client?.urlProtocol(self, didReceive: response, cacheStoragePolicy: .notAllowed)
            self.client?.urlProtocol(self, didLoad: data)
            self.client?.urlProtocolDidFinishLoading(self)
        }
        self.work = work
        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .utility).asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + FixtureImages.latency(for: url), execute: work)
    }
    override func stopLoading() { work?.cancel() }
}
#endif
```
Views/CachedImage.swift, after line 23:
```swift
#if DEBUG || PERF_FIXTURE
if MockFixture.profile != .demo {
    urlConf.protocolClasses = [FixtureImageProtocol.self] + (urlConf.protocolClasses ?? [])
}
#endif
```
FixtureImages renders about 24 variants once with UIGraphicsImageRenderer into Caches (600x900 JPEG posters, 300x300 PNG logos with alpha, 480x120 wide logos) and maps a URL to a variant by hash; distinct URLs keep distinct Nuke cache keys, so decode, resize and memory pressure are real. Latency is a launch argument: 0 ms for scroll runs, 150 ms for pop-in checks, never-answer for a share of the logos to reproduce image-pipeline-3. cacheStoragePolicy .notAllowed keeps the URLCache out of it, so every run starts cold on disk. installAsShared runs before the seeder (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:32-34); MockFixture.profile reads only launch arguments, so the order is fine. The demo profile is not touched.

**APIs:** URLProtocol (canInit, startLoading, stopLoading, client) (iOS 2.0 (Foundation NSURLProtocol.h:163-220)); URLSessionConfiguration.protocolClasses (iOS 7.0 (Foundation NSURLSession.h:849)); UIGraphicsImageRenderer (iOS 10.0 (UIKit UIGraphicsImageRenderer.h:26)); Nuke DataLoader(configuration:) / DataLoader.defaultConfiguration (Nuke 13.0.1 (Sources/Nuke/Loading/DataLoader.swift:44-59))

**Verifier reasons:** Claim side verified. Database/MockFixture.swift:181-183 builds https://picsum.photos/seed/... and another-iptv-playerUITests/ScreenshotsUITests.swift:22-23 sleeps 7 s for it. Nuke 13.0.1 (checkout tag 13.0.1) really short-circuits local URLs: Sources/Nuke/Tasks/TaskFetchOriginalData.swift:27-35 does Data(contentsOf:) and returns before the rate limiter (:37-46) and dataLoadingQueue (:60); isLocalResource is scheme file|data (Internal/Extensions.swift:29-31); isLocalResourcesSupportEnabled defaults true (ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:122); dataLoadingQueue is 6 wide (:166). The hook exists: Views/CachedImage.swift:19-24 builds its own URLSessionConfiguration and hands it to DataLoader(configuration:). The scratch harness does use a Python server on 127.0.0.1:8765 (scratchpad/perf/image_server.py, run.sh). installAsShared runs before the seeder (another_iptv_playerApp.swift:32-34).

What needs correcting:
1. MockFixture.profile does not exist (grep: only isActive, demoPlaylistId, seedIfNeeded, posterURL, demoPlaybackURL). The snippet in CachedImage.swift does not compile until the scale-fixture finding of the same lens adds it; PERF_FIXTURE is not a defined compilation condition either (pbxproj:483 only defines DEBUG). This finding is not standalone.
2. The app target builds with SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor (pbxproj:393/415/578). I typechecked the snippet with swiftc -swift-version 5 -default-isolation MainActor against the iOS 26 simulator SDK: it compiles silently, but only because Swift 5 mode hides the mismatch; with -swift-version 6 every override errors ('main actor-isolated ... has different actor isolation from nonisolated overridden declaration'). The class and FixtureImages are implicitly @MainActor while CFNetwork calls them on its own threads. The repo's convention for this case is an explicit 'nonisolated' (PlayerCore/KSPlayerCrashGuards.swift:16 'nonisolated final class GuardedKSOptions: KSOptions', UIUtils/Log.swift:19).
3. Fidelity gap not mentioned: a custom URLProtocol never opens HTTP connections, so httpMaximumConnectionsPerHost = 4 (CachedImage.swift:20) is not exercised; the Python server did exercise it. Real single-host panels are throttled to 4, the URLProtocol fixture to Nuke's 6.
4. Client callbacks are issued from a global queue; this works with URLSession in practice but the documented contract is the loading thread, and stopLoading can race the work item (cancel does not stop a running block).
5. Flat UIGraphicsImageRenderer artwork compresses to a few KB and decodes faster than photographic posters (scratch images are 27-133 KB), so decode cost is understated unless noise/gradients are drawn.
Not user-facing, so severity is low.

**Corrected claim:** The demo fixture's artwork comes from picsum.photos (MockFixture.swift:181-183) and file/data URLs bypass Nuke's rate limiter, six-slot data queue and URLSession entirely (TaskFetchOriginalData.swift:27-35), so neither is suitable for image-pipeline measurements. A URLProtocol registered on the DataLoader's URLSessionConfiguration (CachedImage.swift:19-24) keeps Nuke's queueing, cancellation and failure paths without a network or helper process, but it does not model the 4-connections-per-host limit, and it depends on a fixture-profile switch that does not exist yet.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the URLProtocol approach, with these changes: (a) land it together with the scale-fixture finding that introduces the profile switch, or gate on a launch argument read directly (e.g. CommandLine.arguments.contains("-FixtureImages")) instead of the non-existent MockFixture.profile; drop PERF_FIXTURE or define it. (b) Declare 'nonisolated final class FixtureImageProtocol: URLProtocol' and 'nonisolated enum FixtureImages' (no @unchecked Sendable: swiftc warns the conformance is already unavailable). (c) Capture the loading thread's run loop in startLoading and deliver the client callbacks there (CFRunLoopPerformBlock + CFRunLoopWakeUp), guarded by a 'stopped' flag set in stopLoading. (d) To keep parity with production, cap concurrent in-flight fixture loads at 4 inside the protocol (a static semaphore or OperationQueue), or state in the report that the per-host limit is not modelled. (e) Draw noise or multi-stop gradients plus text into the generated posters so JPEG size and decode time are in the range of real artwork. (f) Factor the pipeline construction out of installAsShared into a function returning ImagePipeline so the unit test can build one without touching ImagePipeline.shared. Demo profile and fastlane screenshots stay on picsum.

**API check:** URLProtocol: Foundation NSURLProtocol.h:162-163 API_AVAILABLE(ios(2.0)); +canInitWithRequest: :220, -startLoading :258, -stopLoading :268, client :188. URLSessionConfiguration.protocolClasses: NSURLSession.h:849 '@property (nullable, copy) NSArray<Class> *protocolClasses' (header note: not available to background sessions; the image session is a default session). UIGraphicsImageRenderer: UIKit UIGraphicsImageRenderer.h API_AVAILABLE(ios(10.0)). Nuke 13.0.1 DataLoader.init(configuration:validate:) DataLoader.swift:44-45 and DataLoader.defaultConfiguration :55-59. Snippet typechecks in Swift 5 mode with -default-isolation MainActor; fails in Swift 6 mode unless marked nonisolated.

**Regression risks:** Touches Views/CachedImage.swift, where the image request tuning lives: the insertion must stay inside a DEBUG/launch-argument gate so the production session configuration (4 per host, 10/20 s timeouts, waitsForConnectivity false) is byte-for-byte unchanged. A protocol class left registered in Release would add a canInit call to every image request. Must not change the demo profile (App Store screenshots rely on picsum photos). Does not touch the tip-jar WIP (another_iptv_playerApp.swift is not edited).

**How to verify:** 1. swiftc -typecheck of the protocol file with -swift-version 6 -default-isolation MainActor must pass (proves the nonisolated annotation). 2. Unit test with the network off: a pipeline built from the fixture configuration loads img.fixture.invalid/vod/1.jpg, fails img.fixture.invalid/dead/1.png with the injected error, and a 'never-answer' URL fails after ~10 s (timeoutIntervalForRequest) and frees its slot. 3. Scale run with 150 ms latency: placeholders visible, then images; a proxy or 'nettop' shows zero outbound requests. 4. Compare one scroll scenario against the existing 127.0.0.1 server run: late-frame and hitch numbers should be within run-to-run noise; if the fixture is clearly smoother, the missing 4-connection cap is the reason. 5. Fastlane screenshot run unchanged.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-7 — The browse code has no signposts, so Instruments cannot attribute launch, recompute, search or guide time; eight intervals cover the estimates

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Launch, Live TV / Movies / Series home, Category and All grids, Search, TV Guide, Player hand-off, Back to Playlists
- Code: `Models/PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-159, 164-178, 183-190`, `Views/VODView.swift:166-215, 653-668, 838-854`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:220, 615-627`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:278-315, 567-577, 702-712`, `Views/SearchView.swift:251-278`, `EPG/EPGStore.swift:137-168`, `Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-278, 285-333`, `Networking/VideoPlayerController.swift:580-586`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. Today a 100-170 ms launch stall or a 1.16 s search delay is a number without an owner.

**Mechanism (finder):** The only signposter in the app belongs to the player (Networking/VideoPlayerController.swift:583-586, category pointsOfInterest, with the comment that it is measurement only). Nothing marks the catalog load phases, the recompute functions that every browse screen runs two or three times per appearance, the search scan or the guide build.

**Proposed fix (finder):** One shared signposter, same subsystem and category as the player's, local only (os_signpost never leaves the device, so the no-analytics rule holds):
```swift
// UIUtils/BrowseSignpost.swift
import os
nonisolated enum BrowseSignpost {
    static let signposter = OSSignposter(subsystem: Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier ?? "another-iptv-player",
                                         category: .pointsOfInterest)
}
// async span; an explicit id because three recomputes can overlap
let id = BrowseSignpost.signposter.makeSignpostID()
let state = BrowseSignpost.signposter.beginInterval("HomeRecompute", id: id, "vod")
defer { BrowseSignpost.signposter.endInterval("HomeRecompute", state) }
```
Intervals:
1. CatalogLoad around loadPlaylist (PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-159), with CatalogLoad.Categories for phase 1 (:128-137) and CatalogPublish for the main-actor assignments of phase 2 (:146-152). -> data-main-thread-1, 4; transitions-motion-2.
2. HomeRecompute in VODView.recomputeFilter (VODView.swift:166-215), SeriesView.recomputeFilter (SeriesView.swift:220) and LiveStreamsView.recomputeFilter (LiveStreamsView.swift:278-315). The count per appearance settles scroll-perf-8 and data-main-thread-7.
3. GridRecompute in VODCategoryContent.recompute (VODView.swift:653-668), SeriesCategoryContent.recompute (SeriesView.swift:615-627), LiveCategoryContent.recompute (LiveStreamsView.swift:567-577) and AllVODView.recompute (VODView.swift:838-854). -> scroll-perf-1, live-tv-browse-3, states-loading-empty-error-5.
4. SearchScan in SearchResultsView.runSearch (SearchView.swift:251-278), ending after the three assignments. -> search-ux-3, 4; scroll-perf-5; data-main-thread-8.
5. EPGTick around the read in EPGStore.tick (EPGStore.swift:150-152) and EPGPublish around :166-167. -> swiftui-invalidation-4, live-tv-browse-2.
6. GuideBuildRows around buildRows (EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-278, main actor) and GuideLayouts around rebuildLayouts (:285-333). -> live-tv-browse-9, data-main-thread-10.
7. ApplyVODMetadata (PlaylistContentStore.swift:164-178) and CatalogUnload (:183-190). -> data-main-thread-6, swiftui-invalidation-6, transitions-motion-14, onboarding-playlists-7.
8. PlayerPresent from the tap closure to playerOverlay.present returning in AllLiveView (LiveStreamsView.swift:702-712) and VODView.presentHistoryPlayer (VODView.swift:229-270). -> player-handoff-miniplayer-11, data-main-thread-14.
Plus one event, EmptyState, emitted from onAppear of the hand-built empty states (VODView.swift:53-60, 678-686 and twins), so a test can assert that no false empty state was shown.

**APIs:** OSSignposter(subsystem:category: OSLog.Category) (iOS 15.0 (os.swiftinterface:1927-1940)); OSSignposter.beginInterval(_:id:_:) / endInterval(_:_:) (iOS 15.0 (os.swiftinterface:1950-1970)); OSSignposter.makeSignpostID() (iOS 15.0 (os.swiftinterface:2027)); OSSignposter.emitEvent(_:id:_:) (iOS 15.0 (os.swiftinterface:1944))

**Verifier reasons:** Claim verified: grep for OSSignposter over the app sources returns one hit, Networking/VideoPlayerController.swift:583-586 (category .pointsOfInterest, comment 'Measurement only'). Nothing else emits signposts (Models/DownloadManager.swift only imports os.log). All cited sites exist as described: PlaylistContentStore.swift:100-159 (phase 1 :128-137, phase 2 assignments :146-152), :164-178, :183-190; VODView.swift:166-215 with three .task(id:) triggers at :157-159 (so three recomputes on first appearance is real), :653-668, :838-854; SeriesView.swift:220, :615-627; LiveStreamsView.swift:278-315, :567-577, :702-712; SearchView.swift:251-278 with three .task(id:) at :246-248; EPG/EPGStore.swift:137-168; Views/EPG/EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-278 (synchronous, main actor) and :285-333. The snippet (nonisolated enum, OSSignposter(subsystem:category: .pointsOfInterest), makeSignpostID, beginInterval/endInterval with defer inside an async function, emitEvent) typechecks against the iOS 26 simulator SDK with -default-isolation MainActor, target iOS 18.0. os_signpost is local, so the no-analytics rule holds, and no out-of-scope player file is edited.

Why not a plain 'confirmed': the mapping from intervals to the findings they are supposed to settle is partly wrong.
1. CatalogPublish (PlaylistContentStore.swift:146-152) and EPGPublish (EPGStore.swift:166-167) wrap @Published assignments. Those lines only swap array references and fire objectWillChange; the SwiftUI body re-evaluation and layout they cause runs later, in the run loop's commit. The interval will read close to zero and would wrongly suggest the publish is free; it cannot attribute a 100-170 ms launch stall.
2. HomeRecompute, GridRecompute, SearchScan, GuideLayouts and CatalogLoad span awaits on detached tasks / GRDB readers, so their duration is wall-clock, not main-thread time. They answer 'how many, how long until results' (useful for the three-recomputes-per-appearance and the 1.16 s search settle), not 'who blocked the main thread'.
3. XCTOSSignpostMetric with a custom name expects non-overlapping intervals; three concurrent HomeRecompute/SearchScan intervals of the same name inside one measure block make the reported duration ambiguous.
Severity: tooling, not user-facing, low.

**Corrected claim:** The browse code has no signposts (the only OSSignposter is the player's, VideoPlayerController.swift:583-586), so Instruments cannot count or time catalog load, the home/grid recomputes, the search scan or the guide build. Intervals can supply counts and wall-clock durations for the async work and true main-thread time only for the synchronous sites (buildRows, applyVODMetadata, unload, the tap-to-present closure); the cost of a @Published publish is not inside the assignment and needs a different measurement.

**Corrected fix:** Add UIUtils/BrowseSignpost.swift as proposed (nonisolated enum, same subsystem, .pointsOfInterest). Then: (1) async sites (CatalogLoad, HomeRecompute, GridRecompute, SearchScan, EPGTick read, GuideLayouts): begin/end with an explicit makeSignpostID() as proposed, and put the trigger in the message ("vod query", "vod streamsLoaded", "vod hidden") so the three overlapping runs can be told apart; read them as counts and time-to-result. (2) Synchronous main-actor sites (GuideBuildRows at EPGGuideViewModel.swift:249-278, ApplyVODMetadata, CatalogUnload, PlayerPresent): use withIntervalSignpost(_:around:) so the interval is exactly main-thread time. (3) Replace CatalogPublish and EPGPublish intervals with emitEvent markers placed right after the assignments, and attribute the stall that follows from the Hangs / Time Profiler track or the existing frame-gap log (scratchpad/perf/harness/HitchMonitor.swift) in the window after the marker. (4) Keep the EmptyState event. (5) For XCTOSSignpostMetric, measure only names that occur once per measured iteration (CatalogLoad, GuideBuildRows); count the others from the trace.

**API check:** os.swiftinterface (iPhoneSimulator26.0.sdk/usr/lib/swift/os.swiftmodule): 'public struct OSSignposter : @unchecked Sendable' @available(iOS 15.0) :1929-1930; init(subsystem: String, category: OSLog.Category) :1940; emitEvent(_:id:_:) :1944 and :1947; beginInterval(_:id:_:) -> OSSignpostIntervalState :1950/:1954; endInterval(_:_:) :1967/:1970; withIntervalSignpost(_:id:_:around:) :1973/:2004; makeSignpostID() :2027; OSLog.Category.pointsOfInterest :180. XCTOSSignpostMetric -initWithSubsystem:category:name: XCTMetric.h:233 (iOS 13.0). Snippet typechecked with swiftc, target arm64-apple-ios18.0-simulator, -default-isolation MainActor: no diagnostics.

**Regression risks:** Points-of-interest signposts are always enabled, also in Release; cost is sub-microsecond per call and none of the sites is per-cell or per-frame, so scrolling is unaffected, but nobody should later add one inside a card body or the per-item filter closures (that would undo the off-main filtering work). Edits land in PlaylistContentStore, the three home views, SearchView, EPGStore and EPGGuideViewModel: pure additions, but they must not reorder the 'guard !Task.isCancelled' / assignment sequences. No tip-jar file is touched.

**How to verify:** Instruments, Points of Interest + Hangs, optimised build, scale fixture: expect one CatalogLoad, three HomeRecompute per first tab appearance (messages query/streamsLoaded/hidden), three SearchScan per settled query. Check that the CatalogPublish marker is followed by the main-thread hang the baseline shows (99-171 ms 'worst' in first_8s_after_start of scratchpad/perf/baseline-report.txt). Re-run one scroll scenario with and without the signposts; late-frame counts must be within noise.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-8 — All requested XCTest metrics exist in Xcode 26.0.1; the hitch metric is iOS 26 only, and on the simulator only durations, counts and relative CPU and memory are trustworthy

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: UI test target
- Code: `another-iptv-playerTests/EPGGuidePerformanceTests.swift:9-28, 109-137`, `another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:506-521`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. It decides which numbers of the before/after comparison can be quoted.

**Mechanism (finder):** Read from /Applications/Xcode.app/.../iPhoneSimulator.platform/Developer/Library/Frameworks/XCTest.framework/Headers:
- XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric: XCTMetric.h:265-269, iOS 15.0, macOS 11.0.
- scrollDecelerationMetric: XCTMetric.h:271-275, iOS 14.0, marked to be deprecated with scrollingAndDecelerationMetric as replacement; scrollDraggingMetric the same (:277-281).
- navigationTransitionMetric: XCTMetric.h:253-257, iOS 14.0; customNavigationTransitionMetric :259-263, iOS 14.0.
- XCTApplicationLaunchMetric: XCTMetric.h:285-311, iOS 13.0; init(waitUntilResponsive:) iOS 14.0. The older XCTOSSignpostMetric.applicationLaunchMetric is deprecated (:247-251).
- XCTMemoryMetric :342-357 and XCTCPUMetric :313-340, iOS 13.0 (XCT_METRIC_API_AVAILABLE, XCTestDefines.h:80); init(application:) in XCTMetric+UIAutomation.h:12-40. XCTStorageMetric and XCTClockMetric likewise.
- XCTHitchMetric: XCTMetric.h:376-386, header availability ios(19.0), which the compiler reports as 'only available in iOS 26.0 or newer' (checked with swiftc against the SDK); only init(application:) exists (XCTMetric+UIAutomation.h:60-72).
- For animation intervals the signpost metric adds frame rate, frame count, hitch count, hitch duration and hitch ratio (XCTMetric.h:211-220).
The test targets contain no measure call today; EPGGuidePerformanceTests asserts counts, not time.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Simulator, meaningful as relative before/after on the same Mac: durations and counts of custom signpost intervals (CPU-bound work, same code), XCTApplicationLaunchMetric, XCTCPUMetric(application:), XCTMemoryMetric(application:) and the in-app frame-gap log of the scratch harness (scratchpad/perf/harness/HitchMonitor.swift), which already produced the baseline. Device only: hitch time ratio and frame rate from scrollingAndDecelerationMetric, navigationTransitionMetric and XCTHitchMetric (the simulator renders through the Mac's compositor at 60 Hz with no thermal or ProMotion behaviour), absolute launch time, image decode cost, memory warnings and jetsam. The headers do not say whether the animation sub-metrics are reported on a simulator at all, and nothing was run here: checklist step 0a records it, and until then the simulator numbers for hitches come from the frame-gap log.
Rules for the blocks: iterationCount 5 (the first extra iteration is discarded, XCTMeasureOptions.h); XCTHitchMetric behind 'if #available(iOS 26, *)' with the signpost metric as the iOS 18 fallback; resolve elements before startMeasuring, because a query inside the window snapshots the accessibility tree on the app's main thread; quote nothing below the control scenario's 45-73 ms floor.

**APIs:** XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric (iOS 15.0); XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollDecelerationMetric (iOS 14.0, to be deprecated); XCTOSSignpostMetric.navigationTransitionMetric (iOS 14.0); XCTApplicationLaunchMetric(waitUntilResponsive:) (iOS 14.0 (class iOS 13.0)); XCTMemoryMetric(application:) (iOS 13.0); XCTCPUMetric(application:) (iOS 13.0); XCTHitchMetric(application:) (iOS 26.0)

**Verifier reasons:** The API half is confirmed line by line in /Applications/Xcode.app/.../iPhoneSimulator.platform/Developer/Library/Frameworks/XCTest.framework/Headers (Xcode 26.0.1, build 17A400): XCTMetric.h:211-220 (animation sub-metrics), :233, :251 (applicationLaunchMetric deprecated), :257, :263, :269, :275, :281, :289-311, :317-340, :346-357, :380-386 (XCTHitchMetric ios(19.0)); XCTestDefines.h:80 (XCT_METRIC_API_AVAILABLE = iOS 13.0); XCTMetric+UIAutomation.h:12-72 (init(application:) for CPU, memory, storage, hitch); XCTMeasureOptions.h:46-50 (iterationCount default 5, block invoked count+1 times, first discarded). I compiled a test using all of them with swiftc for arm64-apple-ios18.0-simulator: everything typechecks except XCTHitchMetric, which reports "'XCTHitchMetric' is only available in iOS 26.0 or newer", exactly as stated. The test targets contain no measure call (grep for 'measure(' / XCTMetric / XCTOSSignpost in both test targets: none); EPGGuidePerformanceTests.swift:9-28 asserts counts with Swift Testing.

The second half of the title ('on the simulator only durations, counts and relative CPU and memory are trustworthy') is not established by anything on disk; the finding itself says nothing was run. Whether the scroll/navigation signpost metrics report hitch sub-metrics on a simulator, and whether XCTCPUMetric/XCTMemoryMetric(application:) report for a simulator-hosted app at all, can only be settled by the step-0a run. So that half is undecidable here, and CPU/memory should be on the step-0a list too rather than pre-declared trustworthy.

Two omissions that matter for the before/after comparison: (1) the scheme's test action builds Debug (-Onone); the baseline was only meaningful because scratchpad/perf/build.sh forces SWIFT_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL=-O and whole-module. The rules for the blocks must say so, otherwise filter/sort/search durations are several times inflated. (2) The existing harness deliberately drives scrolling from inside the app (PerfDriver.swift header: 'so no UI-test accessibility traffic lands on the main thread during a measured window'); programmatic scrolling emits no UIKit scroll signposts, so scrollingAndDecelerationMetric needs real XCUI swipes and is a separate, device-side measurement, not a drop-in for the frame-gap log.

**Corrected claim:** All listed XCTest metrics exist in Xcode 26.0.1 with the stated availability, and XCTHitchMetric is usable only behind #available(iOS 26, *) (compiler-verified). Which of them report meaningful values on the simulator is unverified: treat signpost interval durations/counts and the in-app frame-gap log as the simulator numbers, and treat hitch ratio, frame rate, CPU and memory from XCTest as 'to be confirmed by step 0a' on the simulator and as device metrics otherwise.

**Corrected fix:** Keep the proposed split and rules, plus: (1) run every measured build optimised (Release test configuration or the -O / wholemodule overrides from scratchpad/perf/build.sh); never quote a Debug number. (2) Step 0a records, per metric, the measurement names XCTest actually prints on the simulator, including XCTCPUMetric(application:) and XCTMemoryMetric(application:), before any of them is used. (3) Keep the in-app driver + frame-gap log as the simulator instrument; use scrollingAndDecelerationMetric / navigationTransitionMetric / XCTHitchMetric only with real XCUI gestures, measured with invocationOptions [.manuallyStart, .manuallyStop], on a device. (4) XCTHitchMetric(application:) behind 'if #available(iOS 26, *)', falling back to scrollingAndDecelerationMetric on iOS 18. (5) Custom XCTOSSignpostMetric only for interval names that occur once per iteration.

**API check:** XCTOSSignpostMetric.scrollingAndDecelerationMetric: XCTMetric.h:269 API_AVAILABLE(macos(11.0), ios(15.0)). scrollDecelerationMetric :275 and scrollDraggingMetric :281: ios(14.0, API_TO_BE_DEPRECATED), replacement scrollingAndDecelerationMetric. navigationTransitionMetric :257 and customNavigationTransitionMetric :263: ios(14.0). XCTApplicationLaunchMetric :289-311, class iOS 13.0, -initWithWaitUntilResponsive: ios(14.0). XCTCPUMetric :317, XCTMemoryMetric :346, XCTStorageMetric :363, XCTClockMetric :196: iOS 13.0; init(application:) in XCTMetric+UIAutomation.h:14-56. XCTHitchMetric :380 and (UIAutomation) :60-72: ios(19.0), init/new unavailable, only initWithApplication:; swiftc reports 'only available in iOS 26.0 or newer'. XCTMeasureOptions.iterationCount / invocationOptions: XCTMeasureOptions.h:16-50. All compiled in a scratch file for target iOS 18.0.

**Regression risks:** None for the app (test-target guidance only). Risk is to the audit's numbers: Debug-built or XCUI-polluted measurements would produce a wrong before/after verdict and could lead to reverting or keeping the wrong change. Adding measure blocks to the UI test target lengthens the UI test run; keep them in a separate test class that the normal scheme run skips.

**How to verify:** Step 0a on the simulator, optimised build: one measure block with [scrollingAndDecelerationMetric, XCTCPUMetric(application:), XCTMemoryMetric(application:), a custom signpost metric] around a single app.swipeUp(velocity: .fast); list the measurement names and units XCTest prints for each metric and whether hitch/frame-rate rows appear; compare any hitch figure with the frame-gap log of the same window. Repeat the identical block on a physical device (iOS 26 for XCTHitchMetric). Only metrics that print stable values (relative std dev under ~10% over 5 iterations) go into the before/after table.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-9 — The four SwiftUI assumptions behind the invalidation findings can each be confirmed or refuted with one temporary change print and one trigger

- Verdict: **partly** · severity low · effort S · risk low
- Screens: Dashboard root, Live TV home, Movies home, Series home, Player overlay host
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:9, 36`, `Views/SeriesView.swift:11, 37, 866`, `Views/LiveStreamsView.swift:9, 25, 63, 1221-1228`, `Views/DashboardView.swift:6-7, 46-50, 93-104`, `Views/Components/DownloadButton.swift:77`, `Views/M3UDashboardView.swift:24`

**What the user perceives:** Not user-facing. Nine of the eleven invalidation findings are 'partly' because their cost was estimated from these four assumptions without a run.

**Mechanism (finder):** The invalidation lens states its assumptions in its notes: (1) @EnvironmentObject / @ObservedObject invalidate a view whatever its body reads; (2) closure-valued environment entries never compare equal; (3) visited TabView tabs keep evaluating their bodies; (4) a @State whose default is a new class instance makes the view value unequal on every parent pass. No _printChanges call exists in the sources.

**Proposed fix (finder):** Add 'let _ = Self._printChanges()' as the first statement of the bodies named below, in a scratch copy, Debug build, demo fixture. For UI-test runs use Self._logChanges() instead, which writes to the unified log.
1. Observation without reading. Where: VODView.body (VODView.swift:36), SeriesDetailView.body (SeriesView.swift:866). Trigger: play a film, minimise, expand; no tab switch. Confirmed if each minimise and expand prints 'VODView: _playerOverlay changed.'; refuted if nothing is printed. Settles swiftui-invalidation-2.
2. Closure environment values. Where: a probe view, so the player file stays untouched: struct EnvProbe: View { @Environment(\.playerOverlayDismiss) var dismiss; var body: some View { let _ = Self._printChanges(); Color.clear } }, attached as .background(EnvProbe()) to item.root before the environment modifiers (DashboardView.swift:94-95). Trigger: with the mini card docked, switch between Settings and Search (re-evaluates DashboardView, publishes nothing else). Confirmed if every switch prints 'EnvProbe: _dismiss changed.'; refuted if silent. Control: a second probe reading only \.playerOverlayMode must stay silent. Settles swiftui-invalidation-3 (player part).
3. Visited tabs stay live. Where: SeriesView.body (SeriesView.swift:37) and LiveStreamsView.body (LiveStreamsView.swift:63). Trigger: launch on Movies, visit Series once, return to Movies, pull to refresh (publishes loadingMessage and loadError on the shared store even when the request fails). Confirmed if 'SeriesView: _contentStore changed.' appears while Movies is selected and the never-visited Live tab prints nothing; refuted if SeriesView prints only when its tab is selected again. Settles swiftui-invalidation-3 (tab part) and the cost side of scroll-perf-8.
4. Class instance as @State default. Where: LiveStreamsView.body (state at LiveStreamsView.swift:25, class at :1221-1228) with VODView.body as control. Trigger: something that re-evaluates DashboardView but publishes none of the two views' own objects: switch between Settings and Search, or wait for the guide's minute tick (DashboardView observes EPGStore, DashboardView.swift:7). Confirmed if LiveStreamsView prints '@self changed.' on each trigger and VODView prints nothing; refuted if both are silent. Settles the Live TV part of swiftui-invalidation-3.
Same technique, one line each: DownloadButton.body (DownloadButton.swift:77) during a download for swiftui-invalidation-8; SeriesCategoryContent.body (SeriesView.swift:634) during playback for swiftui-invalidation-10; M3UDashboardView.body (M3UDashboardView.swift:24) on a favourite toggle for m3u-browse-14.

**APIs:** View._printChanges() (iOS 15.0 (SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5699-5701)); View._logChanges() (iOS 17.1 (SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:14963-14969))

**Verifier reasons:** The technique and the code facts hold. View._printChanges() is in SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5699-5701 (iOS 15.0) and View._logChanges() in SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:14961-14969 (iOS 17.1); neither is used anywhere in the sources (grep empty). Cited sites match: VODView.swift:9 (@EnvironmentObject playerOverlay) and :36 (body); SeriesView.swift:11, :37, :866 (SeriesDetailView.body, env object at :800), :634; LiveStreamsView.swift:9, :25 ('@State private var playbackModelMemo = LivePlaybackModelMemo()'), :63, class at :1221-1228; DashboardView.swift:6-7 (observes PlaylistContentStore and EPGStore), :46-50, :93-104 (closure-valued environment entries recreated on every body pass); DownloadButton.swift:77; M3UDashboardView.swift:24. PlayerOverlayController publishes mode on minimize/expand (PlayerOverlayController.swift:22, :89-99), so trigger 1 is valid. A Settings<->Search switch writes only the @State selectedTab (DashboardView.swift:26-33; those tabs are not persisted), so it re-evaluates DashboardView and nothing else, which makes trigger 2 clean, and the mode-only control probe is a good control.

Corrections to the experiment design:
- Experiment 4 as written depends on experiment 3. LiveStreamsView and the VODView control are in non-selected tabs while the user toggles Settings/Search; if non-selected tabs are not updated (assumption 3 false), both stay silent and assumption 4 is wrongly 'refuted'. The minute-tick trigger is also unreliable on the demo fixture (EPGStore.tick returns early without an active playlist, EPGStore.swift:138).
- Experiment 3 says 'launch on Movies', but the fixture launches on Live (savedTab default, DashboardView.swift:11, restoreInitialTab :206-216), so Live is always 'visited' and the 'never-visited Live prints nothing' check cannot be observed without extra launch arguments.
- Assumption 1 is documented ObservableObject behaviour; the run is cheap but its outcome is not really in doubt, so it should not hold up the invalidation findings.
Nothing here is a defect in the app; it is a verification procedure. Outcomes themselves need the simulator.

**Corrected claim:** The four assumptions can each be settled with a temporary Self._printChanges() in a scratch Debug build, but experiment 4 must be run on the selected tab with a trigger that does not rely on assumption 3, and experiment 3 must account for the fixture launching on Live.

**Corrected fix:** Scratch copy only, as proposed, with these changes. Exp 1 unchanged (VODView.body and SeriesDetailView.body; play, minimise, expand; expect 'VODView: _playerOverlay changed.'). Exp 2 unchanged (EnvProbe as .background on item.root at DashboardView.swift:94, control probe reading \.playerOverlayMode; Settings<->Search with the card docked). Exp 3: launch normally (Live selected and therefore visited), open Movies, pull to refresh there; confirmed if 'LiveStreamsView: _contentStore changed.' prints while Movies is selected and the never-opened SeriesView prints nothing. (To start on Movies instead, pass '-dashboard_selected_tab 1 -dashboard_removed_home_tab_migration_v1 YES'.) Exp 4: stay on the Live tab and pull to refresh; confirmed if LiveStreamsView prints '@self' in its list ('@self, _contentStore changed.'), then do the same on Movies as control, where VODView must print only '_contentStore changed.'. Ignore the first print of each view (initial '@identity'). For unattended runs use Self._logChanges() and read subsystem com.apple.SwiftUI from the unified log. The three extra one-liners (DownloadButton, SeriesCategoryContent, M3UDashboardView) stand.

**API check:** SwiftUI.swiftinterface:5699-5701: '@available(iOS 15.0, ...) extension SwiftUICore.View { @MainActor @preconcurrency public static func _printChanges() }'. SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:14961-14969: '@available(iOS 17.1, macOS 14.1, ...) extension SwiftUICore.View { @MainActor @preconcurrency public static func _logChanges() }'. Both below the iOS 18.0 deployment target, no availability guard needed. Both are underscored debugging API and must not ship.

**Regression risks:** Only if a print is left in: per-body console output on every invalidation would itself cost frames on shelves. The grep gate (no _printChanges / _logChanges in the tree before commit) covers it. The EnvProbe .background on item.root changes the player subtree's view type; it must exist only in the scratch copy, never in the repo (DashboardView.swift:105-107 warns that restructuring around item.root remounts PlayerView).

**How to verify:** Debug run of the scratch copy on the simulator, demo fixture, console filtered per experiment as listed in corrected_fix. Record for each trigger the exact line printed (or silence). Exp 4's discriminator is the presence of '@self' for LiveStreamsView and its absence for VODView under the same trigger.

## gap-fixture-and-measurement-10 — Four open questions from the audit notes need a run, not a reading: shelf offset retention, memory after 200 shelves, blank frames in the category jump, and the iOS 26 tab bar under the docked card

- Verdict: **partly** · severity medium · effort M · risk low
- Screens: Movies / Series / Live TV home, Category picker jump, Mini player over the tab bar
- Code: `Views/VODView.swift:82-108, 160, 448-470`, `Views/CachedImage.swift:26-29, 75-80`, `Views/M3UChannelsView.swift:446-449`, `Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift:478, 596`, `another-iptv-playerUITests/UserFlowsUITests.swift:152-193, 679-706`

**What the user perceives:** If the answers are bad the user feels them directly: a shelf that forgets where it was scrolled, an app that is killed in the background after a long browse, a white flash when jumping to a category, a mini card sitting on the tab bar.

**Mechanism (finder):** Nothing in the code keeps a shelf's horizontal offset (no scrollPosition binding; VODView.swift:448-467), so it depends on whether LazyVStack keeps the row alive. Shelf and grid image cells never release their image on disappear (CachedImage.swift:75-80), so what realised cells hold is outside the 150 MB cache limit (:26-29). The jump animates scrollTo across lazy rows (VODView.swift:100-108) under a root that strips animations (:160). The docked card reserves a fixed 49 pt for the tab bar (MiniPlayerSupport.swift:478) and no screenshot shows it docked.

**Proposed fix (finder):** 1. Shelf offset. Scale fixture, Movies home. Fling the second shelf sideways three times, screenshot the shelf's rect, fling down ten times (about 40 shelves), return to the top (tap the status bar), screenshot the same rect and compare. Equal = retained. If it differs, the fix sketched by the scroll lens applies (ScrollPosition per category id in a non-observed holder, written from onScrollGeometryChange; both iOS 18.0). Repeat on Live TV. Simulator is enough.
2. Memory after 200 shelves. Scale fixture with fixture images. Record phys_footprint (the harness heartbeat) at rest, after a constant-speed scroll through 200 shelves, after 10 s idle and after returning to the top. On the simulator the app is a host process, so 'heap <pid>' gives the live counts of FetchImage and image objects and 'vmmap --summary <pid>' the image memory; compare with ImagePipeline.shared.cache totals. If footprint keeps growing with the number of shelves passed while the cache is at its limit, the cells are the holder. The jetsam consequence needs a device (Allocations, memory warnings).
3. Blank frames in the jump. Scale fixture, 300 categories. Choose the last category in the picker while recording the screen at 60 fps; step through the frames between sheet dismissal and rest and count frames in which the shelf area is empty background. Do it on Movies and on Live TV (Live has no animation-stripping transaction), and read the frame-gap log for the same window. Then count image requests started by the jump with Nuke's own signposts (ImagePipeline.Configuration.isSignpostLoggingEnabled).
4. Tab bar and docked card. Demo fixture; extend test_player_pullDownFromMiddle_minimizesToCard_tapExpands (UserFlowsUITests.swift:152-193): after docking, read the frame of 'miniPlayer.expand' and of app.tabBars.firstMatch, assert they do not intersect and the gap is at least 8 pt, and attach a screenshot. Matrix: iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, portrait and landscape, iOS 26.0 and the installed 18.x runtime; a pushed screen with the tab bar hidden (All Movies); the Search tab with the keyboard up. Geometry needs no playback, so the check does not depend on the demo stream.

**APIs:** ScrollPosition / View.scrollPosition(_:anchor:) (iOS 18.0 (named by the scroll lens; only relevant if step 1 fails)); XCUIElement.frame (XCUIAutomation, iOS 9.0+); ImagePipeline.Configuration.isSignpostLoggingEnabled (Nuke 13.0.1 (ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:154-157))

**Verifier reasons:** The four questions are real and the cited code is as described; none can be answered by reading. (1) No home shelf keeps its horizontal offset: VODView.swift:448-467 is a bare ScrollView(.horizontal) inside a LazyVStack row (:82-93); grep for scrollPosition/ScrollPosition finds it only in MovieDetailView and Views/EPG/EPGGuideView.swift, none in VODView, SeriesView or LiveStreamsView. (2) CachedImage.swift:75-80 documents that shelf/grid cells deliberately keep their request and image on disappear (.lowerPriority was tried and broke loading), while the cache is capped at 150 MB / 1500 entries (:26-29); M3UChannelsView.swift:446-449 states in its own comment that the lazy stack keeps thousands of cards alive, which supports the suspicion. (3) VODView.swift:100-108 animates proxy.scrollTo under '.transaction { $0.animation = nil }' at :160; SeriesView has the same pair (:104, :161); LiveStreamsView has the scrollTo (:253) and no such transaction. (4) MiniPlayerSupport.swift:478 hard-codes tabBarAllowance = 49; no file under scratchpad/shots (36 iphone-dark, 34 iphone-light, 6 ipad-light, re-listed at the end) shows a docked card. An iOS 18.1 runtime (iOS_22B81) and iOS 26.0 (iOS_23A343) are both installed under /Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Volumes, so the proposed matrix is runnable.

Corrections to the steps:
- Step 4 says geometry needs no playback, but the test it proposes to extend (UserFlowsUITests.swift:152-193) calls waitForPlaybackToStart() and asserts the 'Pause' label, so it does depend on the network stream. It also proposes app.tabBars.firstMatch.frame; on iOS 26 the bar is a floating capsule with a detached search button, and that frame is not a reliable proxy for what the card may cover.
- Step 1 compares screenshots of a shelf rect; pixels differ with image load state, so a retained offset can look 'different'. Lazy-row retention can also differ between iOS 18 and iOS 26, so one runtime is not enough.
- Step 3's result for Movies/Series depends on whether the root transaction strips scrollTo's animation at all; that should be recorded explicitly, because the fix differs (no animation vs blank frames).
- Any fix that step 4 leads to lives in Views/MiniPlayerSupport.swift, which is out of scope; any fix from step 2 must respect the deliberate no-onDisappear decision in CachedImage.swift.
Severity medium only because the questions gate user-visible findings; the finding itself changes nothing.

**Corrected claim:** Four open questions need a run: whether a home shelf keeps its horizontal offset after its row scrolls far away (iOS 18 and iOS 26 may differ), how much memory realised shelf cells hold beyond the 150 MB cache cap, whether the category jump shows blank frames (and whether it animates at all on Movies/Series), and whether the docked mini card clears the iOS 26 tab bar given the fixed 49 pt allowance. The code leaves each of them open; none is proven to be a defect yet.

**Corrected fix:** Run the four checks with these adjustments. 1) Shelf offset: after the sideways flings read the label/identifier of the first hittable card in that shelf, scroll away about 40 shelves and back, and compare the label (not pixels); run on both the 18.1 and 26.0 runtimes; repeat on Live TV. Only if it fails: ScrollPosition per category id held outside observed state, written from onScrollGeometryChange (both iOS 18.0, already used in EPGGuideView.swift:13, :138-189). 2) Memory: as proposed (phys_footprint at rest / after 200 shelves / after 10 s idle / back at top, plus heap and vmmap on the simulator host process, compared with ImagePipeline.shared.cache totals); report the simulator figure as relative, and leave jetsam to a device. Any remedy must not reintroduce onDisappear priority changes (CachedImage.swift:75-80). 3) Jump: 60 fps recording on Movies, Series and Live with 300 categories; first note whether the scroll animates on each screen, then count frames with an empty shelf area; enable ImagePipeline.Configuration.isSignpostLoggingEnabled in the scratch build to count requests started by the jump. 4) Mini card: add a separate geometry test that opens the player and pulls down without waitForPlaybackToStart, then asserts that the frame of 'miniPlayer.expand' does not intersect the frame of any tab button (the existing tabButton(named:) helper for Live TV, Movies, Series, Settings, Search) and keeps at least 8 pt clearance, with a screenshot attached; matrix as proposed (iPhone 17 Pro / Pro Max, portrait / landscape, 26.0 and 18.1, a pushed screen, Search with the keyboard up). Report the result to the mini-player owner; do not change MiniPlayerSupport.swift under this audit.

**API check:** ScrollPosition: SwiftUICore.swiftinterface:682-688 '@available(iOS 18.0, ...) public struct ScrollPosition : Sendable'. View.scrollPosition(_: Binding<ScrollPosition>, anchor: UnitPoint? = nil): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:22733-22734, iOS 18.0. View.onScrollGeometryChange(for:of:action:): SwiftUI.swiftinterface:13688-13689, iOS 18.0. XCUIElement frame: XCUIAutomation.framework/Headers/XCUIElementAttributes.h:38 '@property (readonly) CGRect frame'. Nuke 13.0.1 ImagePipeline.Configuration.isSignpostLoggingEnabled: 'public static var' at ImagePipeline+Configuration.swift:154-157. The finding listed ScrollPosition as unverified; it is present and already used by the app.

**Regression risks:** The steps are measurements, so the risk is in what they might trigger: a per-shelf ScrollPosition must not live in @State of the home view or an observed object (it would invalidate the Equatable shelf rows on every horizontal scroll); a memory remedy must not undo the deliberate 'no onDisappear for shelf/grid' image behaviour; a tab-bar clearance fix belongs to the out-of-scope mini-player file. The new UI test must not replace or weaken test_player_pullDownFromMiddle_minimizesToCard_tapExpands.

**How to verify:** 1) First-card label before/after on 18.1 and 26.0: equal = retained. 2) Footprint curve: if it keeps rising with shelves passed while the Nuke cache total sits at its limit, realised cells are the holder; confirm with 'heap <pid>' counts of FetchImage / image objects. 3) Number of recorded frames between sheet dismissal and rest in which the shelf area is plain background, per screen, plus the frame-gap log and Nuke signpost count for the same window. 4) Intersection and vertical gap between the 'miniPlayer.expand' frame and each tab button frame across the matrix, with attached screenshots; fail if any intersection or gap under 8 pt.
